source: Shi Qing became the Prime Minister of Qi State, and everyone in Qi State admired their family tradition, so Qi State was very stable without issuing decrees, so people built the Shixiang Temple in Shi Qing's honor. In the first year of Emperor Wu's Yuanshou, the emperor established the prince and selected people who could be the prince's teachers from among the ministers. Shi Qing was promoted from the post of Pei Taishou to the prince's tutor, and seven years later he was promoted to the imperial censor.
target: The lives of several officials from the Han Dynasty, focusing on their conduct and family traditions.

source: Wan Shijun's name was Fen, and his father was from the state of Zhao and his surname was Shi. After the fall of Zhao State, he moved to Wen County. Gaozu attacked Xiang Yu in the east and passed through Hanoi County. Shi Fen was fifteen years old at that time and was a minor official serving Gaozu. Emperor Gaozu talked with him and liked his respectful and cautious attitude. He asked him: Who are the people in your family? He replied: My mother is the only one in my family and unfortunately she is blind.
target: Wan Shijun, originally from Zhao, served under Emperor Gaozu and rose through ranks due to his respectful and cautious nature.

source: Emperor Gaozu talked with him and liked his respectful and cautious attitude. He asked him: Who are the people in your family? He replied: My mother is the only one in my family and unfortunately she is blind. The family is very poor. There is also a sister who can play the piano. Gaozu asked again: Can you follow me? He replied: I am willing to serve with all my strength. Therefore, Emperor Gaozu called his sister into the palace to be a beauty, and asked Shi Fen to be the official in charge of receiving documents and interviews from the ministers. He moved his family to the middle family in Chang'an because his sister had become a beauty. When Shi Fen served as an official until Emperor Xiaowen, he became a high-ranking official by accumulating merit. He didn't know much about Confucianism, but he was as respectful and cautious as anyone else. During the reign of Emperor Wen, Zhang Xiangru, Marquis of Dongyang, served as the Crown Prince and Tutor, but was later dismissed.
target: He became a tutor to the prince and later a high-ranking official, with his four sons also holding significant posts.

source: Therefore, Emperor Gaozu called his sister into the palace to be a beauty, and asked Shi Fen to be the official in charge of receiving documents and interviews from the ministers. He moved his family to the middle family in Chang'an because his sister had become a beauty. When Shi Fen served as an official until Emperor Xiaowen, he became a high-ranking official by accumulating merit. He didn't know much about Confucianism, but he was as respectful and cautious as anyone else. During the reign of Emperor Wen, Zhang Xiangru, Marquis of Dongyang, served as the Crown Prince and Tutor, but was later dismissed. Emperor Wen chose someone who could be the prince's tutor. Everyone recommended Shi Fen, and Shi Fen became the prince's tutor. When Emperor Jing came to the throne, he was appointed to the position of Jiuqing. Because he was too respectful and cautious and approached him, Emperor Jing was also afraid of him and made him the prime minister of the princes. His eldest son Shi Jian, his second son Shi Jia, his third son Shi Yi, and his fourth son Shi Qing all had official positions of two thousand shi because of their docile temperament, respect for their elders, and caution in doing things. So Emperor Jing said: "Shi Jun and his four sons all have official positions of two thousand shi, and the honor and glory of being ministers is concentrated in their family." He called Shi Fen the King of Wan Shi. In the last years of Emperor Jing's reign, Wan Shijun enjoyed the salary of a doctor and returned home in old age. When the imperial court held grand ceremonies and issued orders, he attended as a minister. When passing the palace gate, Wan Shijun must get out of the car and walk quickly to show respect. When seeing the emperor's driver, he must put his hand on the driver's chariot to express his greetings. When his descendants and grandchildren serve as minor officials and come home to visit him, Wan Shijun must wear court clothes to receive them and not call them by their names. When some of his descendants made mistakes, he would not scold them. Instead, he would sit on a side seat and face the table and refuse to eat. After this, other descendants will blame the person who made the mistake one after another, and then ask for mercy from the elders of the clan. They will bare their upper body to express their apology and resolutely correct themselves, and then they will agree to their request. When his adult children and grandchildren are around him, he must dress neatly and show a serious and tidy look, even if he is staying at home. His servants are also very respectful and cautious. Sometimes when the emperor would reward food and send it to his home, he would always kowtow and bow before eating it, just like in front of the emperor. When he was attending the funeral, he was very sad and mournful. Future generations will follow his teachings and do as he did. Wan Shijun's family was famous in all counties and vassal states for their filial piety and prudence. Even the simple Confucian scholars in Qi and Lu thought that they were inferior to them.
target: His family was renowned for filial piety and prudence, influencing even Confucian scholars. Wan Shijun’s strict household rules included requiring descendants to show respect, and he would refuse to eat if they erred. His son Shi Jian was notably filial, washing his father’s clothes secretly and being meticulous in his duties. Another son, Shi Qing, became prime minister but struggled during turbulent times, eventually dying in office. The family’s tradition declined after his death.

The emperor asked Shi De to be Shi Qing's heir and inherit the title of marquis. Later I did it too often. Because he violated the law and was sentenced to death, Namsu became an official and became a civilian after atonement. When Shi Qing was prime minister, thirteen of his descendants were promoted from minor officials to the rank of two thousand shi. After Shi Qing's death, he was gradually removed from office for different crimes, and the family tradition of filial piety and prudence also declined. Wei Wan, Marquis of Jianling, was a native of Daling, Daijun. Wei Wan became a Langguan by virtue of his driving skills and served Emperor Wen. He was promoted to Zhonglangjiang due to his continuous meritorious service. He had nothing but loyalty and prudence. When Emperor Jing was the crown prince, he invited the emperor's closest officials to a banquet, but Wei Wan refused to go because he was ill. When Emperor Wen was about to die, he told Emperor Jing: Wei Wan is a loyal man, you should treat him well. When Emperor Wen died and Emperor Jing came to the throne, Emperor Jing did not reprimand Wei Wan for more than a year. Wei Wan just performed his duties more cautiously day by day.
target: Wei Wan, Marquis of Jianling, served Emperors Wen and Jing with loyalty and prudence. He refused a banquet invitation from the future Emperor Jing, claiming illness, and kept six swords given by Emperor Wen unused.

When Emperor Jing became the crown prince, he appointed him as a minister. His accumulated merits gradually improved, and during the reign of Emperor Wen, he became a senior official in Taizhong. As soon as Emperor Jing succeeded to the throne, he appointed Zhou Ren as doctor. Zhou Ren was very reserved and did not reveal other people's words. He often wore shabby and patched clothes and underwear that could absorb urine, deliberately making his clothes unclean, so that the concubines would not come close to him, so he was favored by Emperor Jing. When Emperor Jing entered the palace and played obscenely with his concubines, Zhou Ren was often by his side. When Emperor Jing died, Zhou Ren was still serving as the doctor, but he never said anything.

source: King Wuzhu of Minyue was the same as King Yao of Yuedonghai. Their ancestors were all descendants of King Goujian of Yue, and their surname was Zou. After the Qin Dynasty annexed the world, they all had their royal titles abolished and became rulers, and their place was set up as Minzhong County. When the princes rebelled against the Qin Dynasty, Wu Zhuheyao led the Yue people to join Wu Rui, the magistrate of Poyang County, who was known as Pojun, and followed the princes to destroy the Qin Dynasty. At that time, Xiang Ji had the power to command the princes and did not make Wu Zhu and Yao kings. Therefore, they did not join the King of Chu. The King of Han attacked Xiang Ji, but Wu Zhu and Yao led the Yue people to assist the King of Han. In the fifth year of the Han Dynasty, Wu Zhu was re-established as the King of Minyue. He was proclaimed king in the original place of Minyue and established his capital in Dongye. In the third year of Emperor Hui of the Han Dynasty, he listed the contributions of the Yue people during the reign of Emperor Gao. The court believed that Lord Yao of Fujian had the most credit and his people were willing to join him, so Yao was appointed King of Donghai and established his capital in Dongou. The world called him King of Dongou. Several generations later, in the third year of Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty, King Wu Liu Bi rebelled and wanted Minyue to follow him to rebel against the Han Dynasty. Minyue was unwilling to follow, so only Dongou followed King Wu to rebel. When King Wu failed, Dong Ou accepted the heavy bribes from the Han Dynasty and killed King Wu Liu Bi in Dantu. Therefore, he was not killed and returned to his own country. Ziju, the son of King Wu Liu Bi, fled to Minyue. He resented Dongou for killing his father and often persuaded Minyue to attack Dongou. In the third year of the founding of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, Minyue sent troops to besiege Dongou. Dongou ran out of food and was in great distress. He was about to surrender, so he sent someone to ask for help from the Emperor of Han. The emperor asked Tian Fu about this, and Tian Fu replied: It is common for the Yue people to attack each other, and their attitudes are capricious. It is not worth bothering the Central Plains court to come to the rescue. From the Qin Dynasty, they began to abandon them and did not treat them as subordinate countries. So Zhuang Zhu, the Chinese doctor, questioned Tian Fu and said: "I am just worried that my strength is not enough to save them, and my kindness is shallow and cannot cover them. If you really have the ability to save them, why abandon them?" Moreover, the Qin State even abandoned the entire Xianyang, so how could it just abandon the Yue State? Nowadays, when small countries encounter difficulties and have no other choice, they come to the emperor for help. If the emperor does not come to rescue them, where will they go to complain and ask for help? How can the emperor raise and protect the people of all nations? The emperor said: The captain's opinion is not worthy of discussion. I had just ascended the throne, and I didn't want to take out the tiger talisman to mobilize troops from the county to fight. So he sent Zhuangzhu to Kuaiji with the talisman to mobilize troops for the expedition. The prefect of Kuaiji wanted to resist the order and refused to send troops to Zhuang Zhu for the expedition. Zhuang Zhu killed an army commander and clearly stated the emperor's will, and then the prefect of Kuaiji sent troops from the sea to rescue Dong Ou. Before the army reached Dongou, Minyue led his troops to evacuate. Dong Ou requested that the entire country be moved to areas that the imperial court could directly manage, so he led all the people to move here and live in the Jianghuai area.
target: The history of the Minyue and Dongou kingdoms, descendants of King Goujian of Yue, with the surname Zou. After the Qin Dynasty annexed their lands, they were demoted to rulers and their territory became Minzhong County. During the rebellion against Qin, Wu Zhu and Yao led the Yue people to join Wu Rui and helped destroy Qin, but Xiang Ji refused to make them kings, so they later supported the King of Han against Xiang Ji. In the fifth year of the Han Dynasty, Wu Zhu was reinstated as King of Minyue, with his capital at Dongye. In the third year of Emperor Hui's reign, Yao was made King of Donghai, known as King of Dongou, for his contributions. During Emperor Jing's reign, King Wu Liu Bi of Wu rebelled. Minyue refused to join, but Dongou followed. After Wu's defeat, Dongou killed him in Dantu under Han bribery and returned home. Liu Bi's son, Ziju, fled to Minyue and urged attacks on Dongou. In the third year of Emperor Wu's reign, Minyue besieged Dongou. Dongou sought Han aid; after debate, Zhuang Zhu was sent to mobilize troops from Kuaiji. Before the army arrived, Minyue withdrew. Dongou then relocated its people to the Jianghuai region.

id: 史记/七十列传/东越列传::group-001
article_path: 史记/七十列传/东越列传
source: The prefect of Kuaiji wanted to resist the order and refused to send troops to Zhuang Zhu for the expedition. Zhuang Zhu killed an army commander and clearly stated the emperor's will, and then the prefect of Kuaiji sent troops from the sea to rescue Dong Ou. Before the army reached Dongou, Minyue led his troops to evacuate. Dong Ou requested that the entire country be moved to areas that the imperial court could directly manage, so he led all the people to move here and live in the Jianghuai area. In the sixth year of Jianyuan, Fujian and Vietnam attacked South Vietnam. South Vietnam abided by the emperor's restrictions and did not dare to send troops to fight back without authorization, but reported the matter to the emperor. The emperor sent Wang Hui, a great general, to lead his troops from Yuzhang, and Han Anguo, a great farmer, from Kuaiji. They both served as generals. Before their army crossed the Yangshan Mountains, King Ying of Minyue sent troops to guard the dangerous place to fight against the Han army. Ying's younger brother Yu Shan discussed with the Prime Minister of Dongyue and the clan members and said: Our king sent troops to attack South Vietnam without authorization without asking the emperor for instructions, so the emperor sent troops to attack. Now that the Han Dynasty's army is numerous and powerful, if we can defeat them by luck now, the emperor will definitely send more troops in the future until our country is wiped out. Now if we kill the king and apologize to the emperor, if the emperor accepts our request, the war will be stopped and our country will be preserved intact. If the Emperor does not accept our apology, we will fight hard; if we cannot win, we will flee to the sea. Everyone said: Good attention! So he killed Ying with a spear and halberd, and sent an envoy with his head to Daxing Wang Hui. Wang Hui said: Our army came here to kill the King of Dongyue. Now that the head of the King of Dongyue has been delivered, Dongyue has also apologized. The disaster has been eliminated without fighting. There is no greater benefit than this. He stopped the military operation in a flexible and convenient way, informed Han Anguo of the situation, and sent an envoy to Chang'an with the head of the King of Dongyue to report to the emperor. The emperor issued an edict to stop the military operations of Wang Hui and Han Anguo's troops, saying: Wang Ying and others of Dongyue were the first to commit evil, and only Wu Zhu's grandson Yao Junchou did not participate in this conspiracy. The emperor then sent a lieutenant general to establish Chou as the king of Yue Yao to perform the sacrificial rituals to the king of Minyue. After Yu Shan killed Ying, his prestige spread throughout the country, and most of the people in the country belonged to him, so he secretly proclaimed himself king. King Yao could not correct the mistakes of his people and keep them on the right path. After the emperor heard this, he thought it was not worth raising troops for Yu Shan's cause, saying: "Yu Shan conspired with Ying many times to cause trouble, and later killed Ying first, so that the Han army could avoid hardship." So he appointed Yu Shan as the king of Dongyue and lived with King Yao at the same time. In the fifth year of Yuanding, South Vietnam rebelled. King Yu Shan of East Vietnam wrote to the Emperor of the Han Dynasty, requesting that he lead eight thousand soldiers to follow General Lou Chuan to attack Lu Jia and others.
target: In the sixth year of Jianyuan, Minyue attacked South Vietnam. The Han emperor sent generals Wang Hui and Han Anguo to intervene. King Ying of Minyue resisted, but his brother Yu Shan killed him and surrendered, ending the conflict. Yu Shan later proclaimed himself king, and the emperor appointed him King of Dongyue alongside King Yao. In the fifth year of Yuanding, Yu Shan feigned support for a Han campaign against South Vietnam but secretly aided the enemy. After the Han victory, General Yang Pu sought to attack Dongyue, but the emperor initially declined. In the sixth year of Yuanding, Yu Shan rebelled, attacked Han forces, and proclaimed himself emperor. The Han sent multiple generals to suppress him. Yu Shan was killed by his own people, including King Yao Jugu, who surrendered. The Han emperor then relocated the Dongyue population to the Jianghuai region, leaving the area empty. Tai Shigong reflects on the Yue kingdom's longevity, attributing it to ancestral merits and the legacy of Dayu, despite Yu Shan's treachery leading to its downfall.

source: Le Yi, his ancestor was named Le Yang. Leyang once served as the general of Wei Wenhou and once led troops to capture the Zhongshan Kingdom. Wei Wenhou gave Lingshou as a fief to Leyang. After Le Yang died, he was buried in Lingshou, and his descendants settled there. Later, Zhongshan was restored to the state, and it was destroyed by King Wuling of Zhao, and the descendants of the Le family gave birth to a famous man named Le Yi. Le Yi was a virtuous man who loved military affairs. The people of Zhao once recommended him to serve as an official. After King Wu Ling was besieged and starved to death in his palace in the sand dunes, he left Zhao and went to Wei. Later, he heard that King Yan Zhao was defeated by Qi due to the chaos in Yan State due to his son's rule. Therefore, King Yan Zhao hated Qi State and never forgot to take revenge on Qi State. The State of Yan was a weak country, located in a remote area, and its national power could not defeat the enemy, so King Zhao of Yan lowered his status and treated virtuous corporals. He first treated Guo Wei with thoughtful etiquette, so as to recruit more virtuous people. At this time, Le Yi came to Yan State as an envoy for King Zhao of Wei, and King Yan received him with the courtesy of a guest. Le Yi refused to give in, and finally presented a gift to King Yan Zhao to express his willingness to dedicate himself as a minister. King Yan Zhao appointed him as Yaqing, a position he held for a long time. At that time, King Min of Qi was very powerful. In the south, he defeated Chu Prime Minister Tang Wei at Chongqiu, and in the west, he defeated Wei and Zhao at Guanjin. He then united with Han, Zhao and Wei to attack Qin. He also helped Zhao to destroy Zhongshan and defeated Song, which increased Qi's territory by more than a thousand miles. He and King Zhao of Qin jointly fought for the title of emperor. Soon after, he canceled the title of Eastern Emperor on his own and still claimed the title of king. All the vassal states planned to desert Qin and submit to Qi. However, King Qi Min was very arrogant and arrogant, and the people could no longer tolerate it. King Yan Zhao thought that the opportunity to attack Qi had come, so he asked Le Yi about attacking Qi. Le Yi replied: Qi State was originally a hegemonic country and still retains its foundation. This country has a vast land and a large population. We cannot easily attack it alone. If the king must attack it, it is better to unite Zhao, Chu and Wei to attack it. So King Yan Zhao sent Le Yi to form an alliance and treaty with King Zhao Huiwen, and also sent envoys to unite Chu and Wei, and asked Zhao to persuade Qin with the benefit of attacking Qi. Because the princes believed that King Qi Min was arrogant and tyrannical, which would eventually be harmful to them, they all rushed to join forces with Yan to attack Qi. Le Yi came back to report on his mission. King Yan Zhao mobilized the country's troops and sent Le Yi as general. King Zhao Huiwen awarded Le Yi the seal of the Prime Minister. Le Yi then unified the armies of Zhao, Chu, Han, Wei, and Yan to attack Qi, and defeated the Qi army west of Jishui. At this time, the armies of various princes stopped attacking and retreated to their own countries. The Yan army, under the command of Le Yi, pursued the fleeing enemy alone until they reached Linzi, the capital of Qi.
target: Le Yi, a descendant of Le Yang who served Wei Wenhou and captured Zhongshan, was a virtuous man fond of military affairs. After King Wuling of Zhao died, Le Yi left Zhao for Wei. Hearing that King Yan Zhao sought revenge against Qi, Le Yi went to Yan as an envoy and became a minister. King Min of Qi grew arrogant and powerful, prompting King Yan Zhao to consult Le Yi about attacking Qi. Le Yi advised forming an alliance with Zhao, Chu, and Wei. King Yan Zhao sent Le Yi to forge alliances, and the allied forces defeated Qi at Jishui. The other states withdrew, but Le Yi’s Yan army pursued Qi to Linzi, capturing treasures and ritual objects. King Yan Zhao granted Le Yi the title of King of Chang Kingdom. Over five years, Le Yi captured over 70 Qi cities, leaving only Ju and Jimo unconquered.

source: At this time, the armies of various princes stopped attacking and retreated to their own countries. The Yan army, under the command of Le Yi, pursued the fleeing enemy alone until they reached Linzi, the capital of Qi. After King Min of Qi was defeated west of Jishui, he fled to Juyi and held the city. Le Yi stayed alone and led troops to patrol the occupied areas. All the cities in Qi State held fast and refused to surrender. Le Yi concentrated his forces to attack Linzi. After taking Linzi, he seized all the treasures and property of Qi and the ritual objects of the ancestral temple and transported them to Yan. King Yan Zhao was overjoyed and rushed to the shore of Jishui to express his condolences to the army. He rewarded and rewarded the soldiers with wine and meat. He granted the Chang Kingdom to Leyi and named him the King of Chang Kingdom. At that time, King Yan Zhao brought the spoils captured in Qi State back to Yan State, and asked Le Yi to continue to lead troops to attack the Qi State cities that had not yet been captured. Le Yi stayed in the Qi State for five years and patrolled and fought. He captured more than 70 cities and towns in the Qi State. They were all classified as counties and belonged to the Yan State. Only Ju and Jimo were not conquered. At this time, King Zhao of Yan died, and his son became King Hui of Yan. King Hui had been dissatisfied with Le Yi since he was the crown prince. After he came to the throne, Tian Dan of Qi State learned that he had conflicts with Le Yi, so he implemented counterintuitive tactics against Yan State and spread rumors that there were only two cities in Qi State that were not captured. The reason for the delay in conquering was said to be that Le Yi had a grudge against the new king of Yan State. Le Yi used troops intermittently to deliberately delay the time and stay in Qi State, preparing to proclaim himself king in Qi State. What the people of Qi were most worried about was that King Yan would send a general to replace Le Yi. At that time, King Yan Hui had already suspected Le Yi, and was provoked by Qi's counterintuitive plot, so he sent Qi Jie to replace Le Yi as general and recalled Le Yi. Le Yi knew in his heart that King Yan Hui had bad intentions in sending someone to replace him. He was afraid that he would be killed when he returned home, so he went west and surrendered to Zhao. The State of Zhao granted the place of Guanjin to Le Yi, with the title Wangzhujun. The State of Zhao respected Le Yi very much and used it as a favor to shock and intimidate the States of Yan and Qi. Tian Dan of the Qi State later fought against the Qi Jie, and he indeed set up a trap to confuse the Yan army. As a result, the Qi Jie army was defeated at the gate of Jimo City. He then chased the Yan army in many battles and chased north to the Yellow River. He recovered all the cities of the Qi State and welcomed King Xiang of Qi back to the capital Linzi from Juyi. King Yan Hui regretted that he sent cavalry to replace Le Yi, which caused the Yan army to be defeated and lost the captured land of Qi. However, he also resented Le Yi for surrendering to Zhao and worried that Zhao would use Le Yi to take advantage of Yan's defeat and fatigue to attack Yan. King Yan Hui sent someone to Zhao to blame Le Yi and apologize to him, saying: The late king entrusted the entire Yan State to the general. The general defeated Qi for the Yan State and avenged the late king. Everyone in the world was shocked. How can I dare to forget the general's achievements one day!
target: After King Yan Zhao died, King Yan Hui, who resented Le Yi, fell for Qi’s counterintelligence and replaced Le Yi with Qi Jie. Fearing execution, Le Yi surrendered to Zhao, which granted him Guanjin. Qi’s Tian Dan defeated Qi Jie, recovering all Qi cities. King Yan Hui regretted his actions and blamed Le Yi for defecting. Le Yi replied with a letter explaining his loyalty to the late king, his strategic advice, and his fear of unjust punishment. He compared himself to Wu Zixu, emphasizing the importance of preserving the late king’s achievements. King Yan Hui later appointed Le Yi’s son Le Jian as King of Chang State. Le Yi traveled between Zhao and Yan, dying in Zhao.

id: 史记/七十列传/乐毅列传::group-002
article_path: 史记/七十列传/乐毅列传
source: I am afraid that you believe the slanderous words of your servant and cannot understand the reason for my alienation from you. So I dedicate this letter to tell you my feelings. I hope the king will pay attention. So King Hui of Yan named Le Yi's son Le Jian the King of Chang State. Le Yi traveled between Zhao and Yan, and reestablished good relations with Yan. Both Yan and Zhao appointed him as a guest minister. Le Yi died in the state of Zhao. Lejian lived in the State of Yan for more than thirty years. The King of Yan liked to adopt the strategy of his prime minister Li Fu and planned to attack the State of Zhao, so he asked Lord Lejian of the State of Chang. Le Jian said: Zhao is a country at war with all sides. Its people are familiar with military affairs, so it is impossible to attack it. King Yan didn't like it, so he attacked Zhao. Lianpo of Zhao State fought back against the Yan army, defeated Lifu's army in Hadi, and captured Lifu and Lecheng. Lecheng and Lejian have the same ancestor. So Lejian fled to the State of Zhao, and the State of Zhao attacked the State of Yan. Yan State ceded a lot of land to Zhao State to seek peace. Only then did Zhao Jun relieve the siege and leave. King Yan regretted not listening to Yong Lejian's advice. Lejian was already in the state of Zhao, so he wrote a letter to Lejian saying: During the reign of King Zhou of Yin, Jizi was not appointed, but he dared to offend the king, spoke out and remonstrated without slacking off, hoping that King Zhou would listen; Shang Rong was demoted for admonishing King Zhou. He was humiliated, but he still hoped that King Zhou would change his ways. When the people's morale was weakened, the prisoners escaped one after another, and the country was beyond hope, then the two gentlemen resigned and lived in seclusion. Therefore, King Zhou had a bad reputation for being violent, but the two gentlemen did not lose their reputation as loyal and noble. Why is this? He did his best to worry about the king and the country. Although I am stupid now, I am not as violent as Yin Zhou; although the people of Yan State are unstable, they are not as serious as the people of Yin Dynasty. There is a saying that when there is a dispute within a family, one should not express one's own opinions, but tell one's neighbors. I think these two approaches are undesirable. Lejian and Lecheng resented the King of Yan for not following their plan, so they finally stayed in Zhao. Zhao Guo granted Lecheng the title of Lord Wuxiang. The next year, Lecheng and Lian Po besieged the Yan State for the Zhao State. The Yan State asked Zhao for peace with generous gifts, and the Zhao army began to besiege the Yan State. Five years later, King Zhao Xiaocheng died. King Mouxiang sent Lecheng to replace Lian Po's official position. Lian Po attacked Le Cheng, but Le Cheng fled, and Lian Po also fled to Wei. Sixteen years later, Qin destroyed Zhao. More than twenty years later, Emperor Gao of the Han Dynasty passed by the original territory of Zhao and asked the people there: "Does Le Yi have any descendants?" He replied: There is Uncle Le. Emperor Gao of the Han Dynasty gave him the title of Yueqing, and he was called Huachengjun. Hua Chengjun is Le Yi's grandson. The Le family also included Duke Le Xia and Duke Le Chen. They fled to Qi Gaomi when Zhao was about to be destroyed by Qin. Duke Lechen was good at studying the theories of Huangdi and Laozi. He was very famous in Qi State, and people called him a wise teacher.
target: Le Jian advised against attacking Zhao but was ignored. Zhao’s Lianpo defeated Yan, capturing Lifu and Lecheng. Le Jian fled to Zhao. King Yan regretted his decision. Later, Lecheng and Lian Po besieged Yan, forcing Yan to sue for peace. After King Zhao Xiaocheng died, Lecheng replaced Lian Po, but both fled. Qin eventually destroyed Zhao. Han Gaozu later granted Le Yi’s grandson, Uncle Le, the title of Huachengjun. The Le family also included Duke Le Xia and Duke Le Chen, who fled to Qi Gaomi. Duke Le Chen studied Huangdi and Laozi, becoming a renowned teacher. Sima Qian noted that reading Le Yi’s letter moved him to tears.

id: 史记/七十列传/伍子胥列传::group-000
article_path: 史记/七十列传/伍子胥列传
source: He heard that the prince was in Song Dynasty, so he went to follow him. When Wu She heard that Zixu had escaped, he said: "The kings and ministers of Chu will suffer from the war." When Wu Shang came to the capital of Chu, King Chu Ping killed Wu Shang and Wu She together. After Wu Zixu arrived in the Song Dynasty, he happened to encounter a rebellion by the Hua clan in the Song Dynasty, so he fled to the Zheng Kingdom with Prince Jian. The kings and ministers of Zheng were very friendly to them. Prince Jian went to the State of Jin again. Jin Qinggong said: Since the relationship between the Crown Prince and the State of Zheng is friendly, it means that the State of Zheng trusts the Crown Prince. If the Crown Prince can provide us with internal support, if we attack from the outside, we will definitely destroy the State of Zheng. After destroying the State of Zheng, we will entrust it to the Crown Prince. So the prince returned to Zheng. The time was not yet ripe for the incident, and the prince was planning to kill a person who followed him because of personal matters. This person knew his plan and told Zheng Guo about it. Zheng Dinggong and Zichan killed Prince Jian. Prince Jian had a son named Sheng. After the incident, Wu Zixu was frightened, so he fled to Wu with Sheng. When they arrived at Zhaoguan, the officers and soldiers of Zhaoguan wanted to arrest them, so Wu Zixu and Sheng each escaped on foot alone, and almost couldn't escape. The pursuers are behind. Wu Zixu fled to the river. There was a fisherman riding a boat on the river. Knowing that Wu Zixu was in danger, he crossed Wu Zixu across the river. After Wu Zixu crossed the river, he took off the sword he carried with him and said, "This sword is worth a hundred gold. I will give it to you, old man." The fisherman said: According to the law of Chu, whoever catches Wu Zixu will be rewarded with 50,000 dan of grain and the title of Zhigui. Is it a sword worth only a hundred gold? Refuse to accept it. Before Wu Zixu could escape to the capital of Wu State, he fell ill and had to stop on the way to beg for food. When he arrived at the capital of Wu, King Liao of Wu had just come into power and Prince Guang was the general. Wu Zixu asked to see the King of Wu through Gongzi Guang's relationship. After a long time, King Ping of Chu got so angry because Zhongli, a border town of Chu State, and Beiliang, a border town of Wu State, both raised silkworms, and the women from the two places fought each other over picking mulberry leaves, so that the two countries launched armies to attack each other. The state of Wu sent Prince Guang to attack the state of Chu, and after conquering Zhongli and Juchao of Chu state, they returned. Wu Zixu persuaded King Liao of Wu: Chu State can be conquered, and he hopes to send his son to attack Chu State again. Prince Guang said to the King of Wu: Wu Zixu's father and brother were killed by the Chu State, and I persuaded the king to attack the Chu State in order to avenge his personal revenge. Attacking Chu may not necessarily defeat it. Wu Zixu knew that Gongzi Guang had domestic ambitions and wanted to kill King Liao of Wu and establish himself as king. In this case, he could not persuade him with external military actions, so he recommended Zhuanzhu to Gongzi Guang, while he left the court and went to the countryside to farm with Prince Jian's son Sheng.
target: Wu Zixu, a native of Chu, was a famous official whose father Wu She and brother Wu Shang were killed by King Ping of Chu due to the slander of Fei Wuji. Fei Wuji, originally the young tutor of Prince Jian, manipulated King Ping into marrying the prince's intended bride from Qin, then slandered Prince Jian, leading to his exile. Wu She was imprisoned, and his sons were summoned under threat of death. Wu Shang chose to go and die with his father, while Wu Zixu escaped, vowing revenge. He fled to Song, then Zheng, and eventually to Wu after Prince Jian was killed in Zheng. Wu Zixu arrived in Wu, where he befriended Prince Guang and recommended Zhuanzhu to assassinate King Liao, allowing Prince Guang to become King Helu of Wu.

id: 史记/七十列传/伍子胥列传::group-001
article_path: 史记/七十列传/伍子胥列传
source: The hexagrams showed that it would be unlucky to hand over King Zhao to the Wu army, so he declined the offer and did not hand over King Zhao. At first, Wu Zixu and Shen Baoxu were close friends. When Wu Zixu escaped, he said to Baoxu: I must overthrow the state of Chu. Bao Xu said: I must save Chu State. When Wu soldiers invaded the capital of Ying, Wu Zixu searched for King Zhao but could not find him, so he dug up King Ping's grave, dragged out his body, and whipped him three hundred times before stopping. Shen Baoxu fled to the mountains and sent people to say to Wu Zixu: "You are going too far to take revenge like this!" I have heard: Although many people can conquer Heaven, God's anger can also destroy people. You were originally a minister of King Ping, and you personally served him as a minister, but now you have gone so far as to insult a dead man. Isn't this the height of cruelty? Wu Zixu said to the visitor: "Tell Shen Baoxu for me: I am old and have reached the end of my life." Because I am eager for revenge, I will act against the will and reason. So Shen Baoxu went to Qin to report the critical situation and asked Qin for help, but Qin refused. Shen Baoxu stood in the Qin court and cried day and night without interruption for seven days and seven nights. Duke Ai of Qin sympathized with him and said: Although the King of Chu is an unprincipled and ignorant king, how can he not preserve the Chu Kingdom with such ministers? So he sent 500 chariots to save Chu and attack Wu. In June, he defeated Wu's army in Jidi. Just when King Wu stayed in Chu for a long time to look for King Chu Zhao, Helu's younger brother Fugai fled back to the country and proclaimed himself king. When Helu heard the news, he abandoned Chu and rushed back to attack his brother Fugai. Fugai was defeated and fled to the state of Chu. King Zhao of Chu saw that there was an internal turmoil in the state of Wu, so he fought back to the capital of Ying and granted Tangxi to Fugai, calling him the Tangxi clan. The Chu State fought against the Wu Army again and defeated the Wu Army. The King of Wu returned to his country. Two years later, Helu sent Prince Fucha to lead an army to attack Chu and seize the territory. The Chu State was afraid of another large-scale attack by Wu's army, so it left Ying City and moved its capital to Pouyi. At this time, Wu State used the strategies of Wu Zixu and Sun Wu to defeat the powerful Chu State in the west, suppressed Qi and Jin in the north, and surrendered Yue in the south. Four years after Fu Chai attacked Chu and took over, Confucius became the Prime Minister of the State of Lu. Five more years later, the Wu army attacked Yue. King Gou Jian of Yue led his troops to fight, and defeated the Wu army in Gusu. He injured King Wu's toe in Helu, and the Wu army withdrew.
target: Under Helu, Wu Zixu became a key advisor, leading campaigns against Chu. In 506 BCE, Wu, with allies Tang and Cai, defeated Chu at the Battle of Boju, capturing the capital Ying. King Zhao of Chu fled. Wu Zixu, unable to find King Zhao, exhumed King Ping's corpse and whipped it 300 times in revenge. Shen Baoxu, a friend of Wu Zixu, sought aid from Qin, crying for seven days until Qin agreed to help. Qin forces defeated Wu, and internal strife forced Helu to return to Wu. Wu Zixu and Sun Wu's strategies made Wu dominant over Chu, Qi, Jin, and Yue.

id: 史记/七十列传/伍子胥列传::group-002
article_path: 史记/七十列传/伍子胥列传
source: I hope the king will give up Qi and attack Yue first; if not, it will be too late to regret now. The King of Wu did not listen to Wu Zixu's advice and sent him as an envoy to Qi. Before Zixu left, he said to his son: I have repeatedly warned the king, but the king did not listen. I have now seen the end of the Kingdom of Wu. It would be meaningless for you and the Kingdom of Wu to be destroyed. He entrusted his son to Bao Mu of Qi State and returned to Wu State to report to the King of Wu. The Grand Prime Minister of Wu State, Pi, had a quarrel with Wu Zixu for a long time, so he took the opportunity to speak ill of Wu Zixu in front of the King of Wu: Wu Zixu is a tough and vicious man, without friendship, jealous and vicious, and his resentment may lead to serious disasters. The last time the king wanted to attack Qi, Wu Zixu thought it was impossible. The king finally sent troops and won a major victory. Zixu felt ashamed that his strategy was not adopted, but he felt resentful. Now the king is about to attack Qi again, but Wu Zixu is too arbitrary and stubborn to stop him, corrupting and slandering the king's cause. He only hopes that Wu's defeat will prove his clever strategy. Now the king personally went on an expedition and mobilized all the armed forces of the country to attack Qi. However, Wu Zixu's advice was not accepted, so he stopped going to court and pretended to be ill and did not go with the king. Your Majesty, you must be on guard, as this can easily lead to disaster. Moreover, I sent people to investigate secretly. When he was on a mission to Qi, he entrusted his son to the Bao family of Qi. As a minister, he is not satisfied at home, and relies on the princes outside. He thinks that he is the adviser of the former king. Now he is not trusted, and he is often depressed and resentful. I hope your Majesty will find a solution to this matter as soon as possible. King Wu said: Without your words, I would have doubted him. He sent an envoy to give Wu Zixu the engraved sword and said: "You use this sword to commit suicide." Wu Zixu looked up at the sky and sighed: Alas! I slandered the villain Bo Pei and wanted to cause trouble, but the king came to kill me. I made your father king. Before you were confirmed as the heir to the throne, the princes were vying to be crown prince. I fought to the death in front of the late king and could hardly get the crown prince's position. After you became the crown prince, you also promised to give me a portion of the Kingdom of Wu, but I have no hope that you will repay me. But now you actually listened to the bad words of a flattering villain and killed your elders. So he told his close followers: You must plant a catalpa tree on my tomb so that it can grow up and make a coffin. Goug out my eyeballs and hang them on the east gate of Wu's capital to watch how the Yue invaders enter the capital and destroy Wu. So he committed suicide and died. When the king of Wu heard this, he was furious, so he put Wu Zixu's body in a leather bag and floated it in the river. The people of Wu State sympathized with him and built an ancestral hall for him by the river. Therefore, they named this place Xushan. After King Wu killed Wu Zixu, he attacked Qi. The Bao family of Qi killed their king, Duke Ai, and assisted Yang Sheng as king. King Wu planned to attack the Bao family, but he withdrew his troops before winning.
target: After Helu's death, his son King Fucha of Wu succeeded. Wu Zixu warned against sparing King Goujian of Yue after a victory, but Fucha, influenced by the corrupt official Bo Pi, accepted Yue's surrender. Wu Zixu repeatedly advised against attacking Qi, urging the elimination of Yue first, but was ignored. Fucha sent Wu Zixu as an envoy to Qi, where he entrusted his son to the Bao family, foreseeing Wu's doom. Bo Pi slandered Wu Zixu, leading Fucha to order his suicide. Wu Zixu, before dying, asked for his eyes to be hung on the eastern gate to watch Yue's invasion. Fucha, enraged, had his body placed in a leather bag and thrown into the river. The people of Wu built a shrine for him.

id: 史记/七十列传/伍子胥列传::group-003
article_path: 史记/七十列传/伍子胥列传
source: The people of Wu State sympathized with him and built an ancestral hall for him by the river. Therefore, they named this place Xushan. After King Wu killed Wu Zixu, he attacked Qi. The Bao family of Qi killed their king, Duke Ai, and assisted Yang Sheng as king. King Wu planned to attack the Bao family, but he withdrew his troops before winning. Two years later, King Wu summoned the kings of Lu and Wei to meet at Lugao for an alliance. The next year, he headed north and gathered the princes in Huangchi to give orders to the Emperor of Zhou. At this time, King Gou Jian of Yue attacked the state of Wu, killed the prince of the state of Wu, and defeated the army of the state of Wu. When King Wu heard the news, he returned to his country and sent envoys to negotiate peace with Yue with rich and valuable gifts. Nine years later, King Gou Jian of Yue finally destroyed the state of Wu, killed King Wu Fu Chai, and killed Dazai Pei because he was disloyal to his king, accepted valuable bribes from foreign countries, and secretly became close to the state of Yue. The son of Prince Jian of Chu, who had fled with Wu Zixu, lived in the state of Wu. When King Wu Fu Chai was in power, King Hui of Chu wanted to summon Sheng back to Chu. Ye Gongju advised: Sheng loves bravery and secretly seeks out warriors who dare to die. He may have selfish motives! King Hui didn't listen to his advice, so he finally called Sheng back and let him live in Yan, the border town of Chu. Known as Bai Gong. Three years after Duke Bai returned to Chu, King Wu killed Wu Zixu. Not long after Duke Bai returned to Chu State, he resented Zheng Guo for killing his father, so he secretly recruited warriors who dared to die to avenge Zheng Guo. After returning to Chu State for five years, he asked the King of Chu to attack Zheng State. Yin Zixi, the order of Chu State, agreed to his request. However, Jin had already sent troops to attack Zheng before it sent troops. Zheng sent people to Chu to ask for rescue. King Chu sent Zixi to rescue Zheng and made an alliance with Zheng before returning. Bai Gongsheng was angry and said: My enemy is not Zheng Guo, my enemy is Zixi! Bai Gongsheng sharpened the sword himself. Someone asked him: What do you use it for? Bai Gongsheng replied: "I want to use it to kill Zixi." When Zixi heard about this, he smiled and said: "Bai Gongsheng is like a bird's egg, what can he do!" Four years later, Bai Gongsheng and Shi Qi suddenly assassinated Ling Yin Zixi and Sima Ziqi in the court. Shi Qi said: "I can't do it without killing King Hui of Chu." So, King Hui of Chu was kidnapped and taken to Gaofu. Shi Qi's follower Qu Gu fled to the palace where Mrs. Zhao lived, carrying King Hui of Chu on his back. When Ye Gong heard that Bai Gongsheng was in trouble, he led his people to attack Bai Gongsheng. Bai Gongsheng and his group were defeated, and Bai Gongsheng fled to the mountains and committed suicide.
target: Years later, Yue destroyed Wu, fulfilling Wu Zixu's prophecy. Prince Jian's son, Bai Gong Sheng, returned to Chu but later rebelled, killing officials Zixi and Ziqi, and kidnapping King Hui. Ye Gong suppressed the rebellion, and Bai Gong Sheng committed suicide. Sima Qian commented on Wu Zixu's endurance and revenge, contrasting his fate with Bai Gong Sheng's failed rebellion.

id: 史记/七十列传/伯夷列传::group-000
article_path: 史记/七十列传/伯夷列传
source: Although there are many books that scholars have read, they still need to examine the authentic and trustworthy records in the Six Classics. Although the "Book of Songs" and "Shangshu" are incomplete, it can still be clearly examined from the texts recording the Yu and Xia dynasties. When Tang Yao was about to abdicate, he gave up the throne to Yu Shun. When Yu Shun gave up the throne to Xia Yu, princes from all over the world and the state pastors came to recommend him, and then he was placed in the position of emperor for inspection and trial. After presiding over the state affairs for decades and making outstanding achievements, the government was handed over to him. This means that the world is a very precious treasure, and the emperor is a very important leader, so the power is so solemn and prudent! However, it is said in Zhuzi's Miscellaneous Notes: Tang Yao wanted to cede the world to Xu You, but Xu You not only refused to accept it, but took it as a shame, so he ran away and lived in seclusion. In the Xia Dynasty, Bian Sui and Wuguang appeared again who did not accept Shang Tang's abdication. How does this glorify them? Tai Shigong said: I climbed Jishan Mountain and said that there might be Xu You's tomb on the mountain. Confucius discussed in turn the benevolent people, saints, and wise men in ancient times, such as Wu Taibo and Boyi, all in great detail. I think the virtues of Xu You and Wu Guang that I have heard are the noblest, but there is not even a rough written record in the scriptures. Why is this? Confucius said: Boyi and Shuqi do not remember their past hatred, so their resentment will be less. They pursue benevolence and get it, so why do they have any resentment? I deeply sympathized with Boyi's will, and I was surprised to see their poems that were not recorded in the scriptures. Their biographies say: Boyi and Shuqi are the two sons of Lord Guzhu. His father wanted to make Shuqi the king of the country. When his father died, Shuqi wanted to give up the throne to Boyi. Boyi said: This is my father's last wish! So he ran away. Shu Qi also refused to inherit the throne and ran away. The people of the country had no choice but to support Lord Guzhu's second son. At this time, Boyi and Shuqi heard that Xibochang could provide good support to the elderly, so they thought why not join him! But when they got there, Xibochang was already dead. His son, King Wu, honored Xibochang as King Wen, carried his wooden spiritual tablet on a chariot, and marched eastward to attack Yin Zhou. Boyi and Shuqi reined in King Wu's horse and remonstrated, saying: "If my father dies without being buried, then he starts a war. Can it be called filial piety?" Can it be said that killing a monarch as a minister is benevolent and righteous? The entourage around King Wu wanted to kill them. Taigong Lu Shang said: This is a man of integrity. So he helped them leave. When King Wu put down the rebellion of Shang Zhou, the whole world surrendered to the Zhou Dynasty, but Boyi and Shuqi thought it was a shame. They insisted on benevolence and righteousness, refused to eat the food of the Zhou Dynasty, and lived in seclusion on Shouyang Mountain, picking wild vegetables to satisfy their hunger. When I was about to starve to death, I composed a song with the words: Climb up the Western Mountain and pick the weeds there.
target: The authenticity of historical records, emphasizing the need to rely on trustworthy sources like the Six Classics, despite the incomplete state of the "Book of Songs" and "Shangshu." It recounts the abdication of Tang Yao to Yu Shun and Yu Shun to Xia Yu, highlighting the solemn and prudent transfer of power, as the world and emperor are precious. However, it contrasts this with accounts from Zhuzi's Miscellaneous Notes, where Xu You refused Tang Yao's abdication out of shame, and later Bian Sui and Wuguang similarly rejected Shang Tang's offer. The historian climbs Jishan Mountain, noting Xu You's possible tomb, and reflects on Confucius's discussions of ancient sages like Wu Taibo and Boyi, yet finds no scriptural record of Xu You and Wu Guang's virtues. The text then focuses on Boyi and Shuqi, sons of Lord Guzhu, who fled to avoid a succession dispute. They sought Xibochang but found him dead; his son King Wu marched against Yin Zhou. Boyi and Shuqi remonstrated against this, citing filial piety and righteousness, but were spared by Taigong Lu Shang. After the Zhou conquest, they refused to eat Zhou's food, starved on Shouyang Mountain, and composed a song expressing despair. The historian questions whether they felt resentment, given their fate.

id: 史记/七十列传/伯夷列传::group-001
article_path: 史记/七十列传/伯夷列传
source: When I was about to starve to death, I composed a song with the words: Climb up the Western Mountain and pick the weeds there. Exchange a tyrant minister for a tyrant, but you don't realize that it is a mistake. The peaceful and prosperous times of Shennong, Yu and Xia disappeared in a blink of an eye. Where is our destination? Alas, there is only death, such a bad fate! So he starved to death in Shouyang Mountain. From this poem, do they feel resentful or not? Some people say: Heaven is impartial and always helps good people. Should Boyi and Shuqi be said to be good people, or should they not be said to be good people? They accumulated benevolence and maintained noble conduct, but they finally starved to death! Besides, among Confucius's seventy proud students, only Yan Yuan was praised as a studious scholar. However, Yan Yuan was always poor and could not even eat poor food, and finally died prematurely. What is the reward of heaven for good people? Robber Zhi killed innocent people all day long, roasted people's hearts and livers and ate them as meat. He was cruel and indulgent, gathered thousands of gang members and ran rampant in the world, and he died a long life.
target: It further questions divine justice: Boyi and Shuqi, though virtuous, starved, while Yan Yuan, a studious disciple, died poor. In contrast, the cruel Robber Zhi lived long. Modern times show lawbreakers thriving while the righteous suffer. The historian is perplexed by this apparent lack of heavenly reward.

id: 史记/七十列传/伯夷列传::group-002
article_path: 史记/七十列传/伯夷列传
source: What kind of ethics does this follow? This is a great and remarkable thing. As for modern times, those who do not follow the right path and specifically break laws and regulations can live a life of ease and enjoyment, and live a wealthy and generous life for generations to come. But there are people who are willing to walk only when they choose a good place, who are willing to talk or walk only when the opportunity is right, and dare not go through small roads. They will never do anything that is not just and vigorous. There are countless people who are cautious and suffer disaster like this. I was deeply confused. If there is such a thing as the way of heaven, then is this the way of heaven, or not the way of heaven? Confucius said: People who have different ideas cannot discuss with each other. Only each person acts according to his own will. So he said: If wealth can be sought, I will do it even if I am a humble driver; if I cannot find it, I will still do it according to my own hobbies.  In the severe cold season, we realize that the pines and cypresses are the last to wither. When the whole society is chaotic and dirty, people with noble character will emerge. Isn't it because some people take wealth and happiness so seriously that other people take wealth and happiness so lightly? Confucius said: What a gentleman fears is not having his name mentioned until his death. Jia Yi said: Those who are greedy for money die for money, those who value righteousness over life sacrifice themselves for fame, those who are boastful and greedy for power die fighting for power, and ordinary people are greedy for life and hate death. The Book of Changes says: Things that are equally bright will reflect each other, and things that belong to the same category will naturally react to each other. The colorful clouds soar with the dragon's roar, the valley wind rises with the roar of the tiger, and the sage's description reveals the true nature of all things. Although Boyi and Shuqi were virtuous, their reputations only became more prominent when they were praised by Confucius. Yan Yuan was dedicated to learning, and it was only because he followed Confucius that his virtues became more remarkable. The hermits in the caves of Yanju are either well-known or unknown. This is sometimes the case. What a pity it would be for a person like this to have a buried reputation and not be praised! Scholars in remote areas must cultivate their virtues and establish a reputation. If they don't rely on people who are Delong and Wangzun, how can they be famous for future generations?
target: Confucius's sayings on differing paths and the value of virtue in chaotic times are cited. The text concludes that reputation depends on association with the virtuous, as Boyi and Shuqi were glorified by Confucius, and scholars in obscurity need such recognition to be remembered.

source: As the saying goes: If you work hard, it is better to have a good year; if you are good at being an official, it is better to have good luck in officialdom. This is not empty talk without basis. Not only did women use their beauty to flatter themselves to gain favor, but this also happened among scholars and eunuchs. In the past, many people used their beauty to gain favor. By the time the Han Dynasty was founded, Emperor Gaozu was extremely violent and upright, but he had children who were favored by flattery. During the reign of Emperor Xiaohui, there was a Hong child who was like this. These two people had no talent, but gained the favor of the nobles through their gentleness and flattery. They actually slept together with the emperor, and even the ministers had to go through them before they could make presentations to the emperor. Therefore, during the period of Emperor Xiaohui, the ministers and ministers all wore hats decorated with bird feathers, belts decorated with shells, and applied makeup and powder. This was the result of the influence of Hongru and Jiru. Later, Hong Ru and Ji Ru both moved their families to Anling.
target: How favoritism and flattery, rather than talent, often led to power and wealth in ancient China, particularly during the Han Dynasty. Both women and men, including scholars and eunuchs, used beauty and charm to gain imperial favor. During Emperor Gaozu's reign, flattery was common, and under Emperor Xiaohui, two favored individuals, Hongru and Jiru, gained such influence that ministers imitated their dress and behavior. They later moved to Anling.

id: 史记/七十列传/佞幸列传::group-001
article_path: 史记/七十列传/佞幸列传
source: Later, Hong Ru and Ji Ru both moved their families to Anling. During the reign of Emperor Xiaowen, the favored ministers in the palace included Deng Tong as a scholar and Zhao Tong and Beigong Bozi as eunuchs. Beigong Bozi was favored because he was a kind elder; Zhao Tong was favored because he was good at observing stars and fortune telling, and often served as Emperor Wen's companion; Deng Tong had no skills. Deng Tong was from Nan'an, Shu County. He became a Huangtou Lang because he was good at rowing. Emperor Xiaowen dreamed of ascending to heaven, but he couldn't go up. A yellow-headed man pushed him up to heaven from behind. He looked back and saw the man's clothes at the waist, and his belt was knotted behind his back. After waking up from the dream, Emperor Wen went to Jiantai and secretly looked for Huang Toulang who pushed him to heaven based on what he saw in his dream. Sure enough, he saw Deng Tong, his belt tied behind his back, just as he had seen in his dream. Emperor Wen summoned him and asked his name, and he replied that his surname was Deng Mingtong. Emperor Wen liked him and respected and favored him more and more day by day. Deng Tong was also honest and cautious, and did not like to interact with outsiders. Although the emperor granted him a vacation, he did not want to go out. At that time, the emperor rewarded him more than ten times, with a total of hundreds of millions of money, and his official position was promoted to senior doctor. Emperor Wen often visited Deng Tong's house to play and play. But Deng Tong had no other talents and could not recommend wise men. He was just cautious in doing things and trying to please the emperor. Once, the emperor asked a person who was good at fortune telling to look at Deng Tong. After the person looked at him, he said: Deng Tong will die of poverty and hunger. Emperor Wen said: I am the one who can make Deng Tong rich. How can I say that he will be poor? So Emperor Wen gave Deng Tong the Tongshan in Yandao, Shu County, and allowed him to mint his own money. From then on, "Deng's money" spread throughout the country. His wealth reached this level. Emperor Wen once suffered from carbuncle, and Deng usually sucked the pus and blood for him. Emperor Wen was unhappy and asked Deng Tong calmly: "Who in the world loves me the most?" Deng Tong said: There should be no one who loves you more than the prince. The prince came to see Emperor Wen's condition, and Emperor Wen asked him to suck the pus and blood. Although the prince sucked the pus and blood, his face showed embarrassment. Later, when the prince heard that Deng Tong sucked pus and blood for Emperor Wen, he felt ashamed and resented Deng Tong. When Emperor Wen died and Emperor Jing came to the throne, Deng Tong was dismissed and lived at home. Soon after, someone reported that Deng Tong had stolen coins minted from abroad.
target: Under Emperor Xiaowen, favored figures included Deng Tong, a boatman who became a high-ranking official after the emperor dreamed of a yellow-headed man pushing him to heaven, which matched Deng Tong's appearance. Deng Tong was rewarded generously, given a copper mountain to mint his own money, and even sucked pus from the emperor's carbuncle. However, after Emperor Jing ascended, Deng Tong was accused of minting coins abroad, his wealth was confiscated, and he died in poverty.

id: 史记/七十列传/佞幸列传::group-002
article_path: 史记/七十列传/佞幸列传
source: So the eldest princess ordered her subordinates to lend Deng Tong only the cost of food and clothing. After all, Deng Tong was not allowed to own a penny and lived in other people's homes until his death. During the reign of Emperor Xiaojing, there were no favored ministers in the palace, but only the Langzhong Ling Zhou Ren. He was the most favored, more favored than ordinary people, but still not deep. Today, the favored ministers and scholars in the palace of Emperor Wu of Han include Han Yan, the great-grandson of King Han, and the eunuch is Li Yannian. Han Yan is the concubine and grandson of Gong Gaohou Han Daidang. When the emperor was the king of Jiaodong, Han Yan and the emperor were calligraphy classmates and became friendly with each other. When the emperor became the prince, he became closer to Han Yan. Yan is good at riding horses and archery, and is good at flattery. When the emperor came to the throne, he wanted to attack the Huns, so Han Yan learned the weapons and formations of the Hu people in advance. For this reason, he became more and more distinguished, and his official position was promoted to a senior official. The emperor's rewards were comparable to those of Deng Tong. At that time, Han Yan often slept and woke up with the emperor.
target: During Emperor Xiaojing's reign, only Zhou Ren was favored, but not deeply. Under Emperor Wu, Han Yan, a calligraphy classmate, gained favor through flattery and military skills, often sleeping with the emperor.

id: 史记/七十列传/佞幸列传::group-003

source: King Jiangdu saw it from a distance and thought it was the emperor coming, so he asked his followers to stay away and he lay down by the roadside to pay his respects. However, Han Yan galloped past on horseback and did not see King Jiangdu. After Han Yan passed by, King Jiangdu was furious and cried to the Queen Mother: Please allow me to return the feudal state to the court and return to the palace as a guard on duty, just like Han Yan. The Queen Mother resented Han Yan. Han Yan served the emperor and was not prohibited from entering or leaving the residence of the concubines in Yongxiang. Someone reported the adultery to the empress dowager. The Empress Dowager was furious and sent an envoy to order Han Yan to commit suicide. Emperor Wu apologized and begged the Queen Mother on his behalf, but was ultimately not accepted and Han Yan committed suicide. Case Road Hou Han said that he was his younger brother, and he was favored because of his flattery. Li Yannian was from the Zhongshan Kingdom. His parents, him and his brothers and sisters were all singing and dancing artists. Li Yannian was castrated for breaking the law and then served in the Dog Prison. Princess Pingyang, the sister of Emperor Wu, told the emperor that Li Yannian's sister was good at dancing. The emperor summoned her and he liked her very much. After Li Yannian's sister was summoned to the palace, he also summoned Li Yannian to the palace to make him noble. Li Yannian was good at singing and composed new music. At this time, the emperor was building the Tiandi Temple and wanted to compose lyrics to accompany the music. Li Yannian was good at catering to the emperor's wishes and sang the new music to match the music. His sister was also favored by Emperor Wu and gave birth to a son. Li Yannian wore the official seal of two thousand stones, which was called "Xie Sheng Lv". He slept and rose with the emperor, and was very noble and favored, similar to the favor that Han Yan received. After a long time, Li Yannian gradually began to engage in lewd behavior with the palace maids, going in and out of the palace, becoming arrogant and indulgent. After the death of his sister, Mrs. Li, the emperor's favor with him waned, and eventually Li Yannian and his brothers were arrested and killed. From then on, most of the courtiers favored by the emperor in the palace were relatives of foreign relatives, but these people are not worth talking about. Wei Qing and Huo Qubing were also favored by dignitaries because of their relatives, but they were able to make contributions based on their own talents. Tai Shigong said: The timing of the emperor's favor and hatred is terrible! From Mi Zixia's experience, we can completely see the ending of the ungrateful people in future generations.
target: He was later accused of adultery with concubines and forced to commit suicide by the empress dowager. Li Yannian, a singer and dancer, rose to favor after his sister became Emperor Wu's concubine, but after her death, his arrogance led to his execution. The text concludes that most favored courtiers were relatives of the emperor, though Wei Qing and Huo Qubing achieved merit through talent. Tai Shigong reflects on the unpredictability of imperial favor, citing Mi Zixia as an example of ingratitude.

source: In the second year of the Zhongyuan period of Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty, Zhou Ju, the son of Zhou Jie, was granted the title of Marquis on his behalf. In the third year of Yuanding, Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, Zhou Ju was appointed as Taichang official. He committed a crime and was exempted from his fiefdom. Tai Shigong said: Fu Kuan, the Marquis of Yangling, and Jin She, the Marquis of Xinwu, both received high titles. They followed Emperor Gaozu and raised troops from Shandong, attacked Xiang Yu, killed famous generals, defeated dozens of enemy armies, and surrendered dozens of cities. They did not suffer setbacks or hardships. This is also a gift from God.
target: The military careers and titles of three Han Dynasty figures: Fu Kuan, Jin She, and Zhou Xie (Kuai Chenghou), as recorded in historical records.

id: 史记/七十列传/傅靳蒯成列传::group-001

source: Fu Kuan, the Marquis of Yangling, followed Pei Gong Liu Bang as a cavalry officer with the title of the fifth official of Wei State. He once served as a retainer and started an uprising in Hengyang. He followed Pei Gong to attack Anyang and Gangli, attacked Qin general Zhao Bi's army in Kaifeng, and defeated Qin general Yang Xiong's army in Quyu and Yangwu, capturing twelve enemy heads. Pei Gong granted him the title of Qing. Later he followed Pei Gong to Bashang. Peigong became the queen of Han Dynasty and gave Fu Kuan the title of Gongdejun. He followed the King of Han into the Hanzhong area and was promoted to the right cavalry general. Soon after, he followed the King of Han to pacify the Three Qin Dynasties, and the King of Han gave Diaoyin County as his seat. During the conflict between Chu and Han, he followed the King of Han to attack Xiang Yu, the overlord of Western Chu, and was ordered to meet the King of Han in Huai County. The King of Han gave him the title of Marquis of Tongde. When he followed the King of Han to attack Xiang Yu's generals Xiang Guan, Zhou Lan, and Long Qie, the soldiers he led captured an enemy cavalry general at the foot of Aocang Mountain, thus increasing his food supply. Fu Kuan was once under the command of Huaiyin Marquis Han Xin, and defeated Qi's garrison at Lixia and defeated Qi's general Tian Jie. Later, it came under the command of Cao Shen, the prime minister, and conquered Bo County of Qi State, adding more food towns. Because of his meritorious service in pacifying Qi, the king of Han divided the token in half and gave him half to show his credibility, so that his title could be passed down from generation to generation. He was granted the title of Marquis of Yangling, with a settlement of 2,600 households, and he was granted the title of a settlement before. Later, he served as the right prime minister of Qi State and stationed troops to guard against Tian Heng's rebellion. He served as prime minister of Qi for five years. In April of the eleventh year of Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty, he attacked Chen Xi, who rebelled against the Han and proclaimed himself king. He was under the command of Taiwei Zhou Bo, who replaced Fan Kuai, the prime minister of the Han Dynasty, and defeated Chen Xi. In January of the next year, he was transferred to Dai Guo Xiangguo and led troops to garrison the border counties. Two years later, he served as the prime minister of the country and continued to lead troops to garrison the border counties. Fu Kuan died in the fifth year of Emperor Hui of the Han Dynasty, and his posthumous title was Jinghou. His son Qinghou Fu Jing inherited the title, and his son Qinghou died after reigning for twenty-four years. Fu Jing's son, Gonghou Fu Ze, inherited the title and died after reigning for twelve years. Fu Ze's son Fu Yan inherited the title. In the thirty-first year, he was executed for treason with Liu An, King of Huainan, and his fiefdom was abolished.
target: Fu Kuan, Marquis of Yangling, began as a cavalry officer under Pei Gong (Liu Bang). He participated in numerous battles against Qin and Chu forces, including attacks on Anyang, Gangli, and Kaifeng, and defeating generals like Zhao Bi and Yang Xiong. After Liu Bang became King of Han, Fu Kuan was promoted to right cavalry general and granted Diaoyin County. He fought against Xiang Yu, capturing an enemy cavalry general at Aocang Mountain. Serving under Han Xin and later Cao Shen, he helped pacify Qi, earning a hereditary title as Marquis of Yangling with 2,600 households. He served as right prime minister of Qi for five years, guarded against Tian Heng’s rebellion, and attacked Chen Xi under Zhou Bo. Fu Kuan died in the fifth year of Emperor Hui’s reign, posthumously named Jinghou. His lineage continued until his descendant Fu Yan was executed for treason with Liu An, King of Huainan.

id: 史记/七十列传/傅靳蒯成列传::group-002
