source: Two years later, he served as the prime minister of the country and continued to lead troops to garrison the border counties. Fu Kuan died in the fifth year of Emperor Hui of the Han Dynasty, and his posthumous title was Jinghou. His son Qinghou Fu Jing inherited the title, and his son Qinghou died after reigning for twenty-four years. Fu Jing's son, Gonghou Fu Ze, inherited the title and died after reigning for twelve years. Fu Ze's son Fu Yan inherited the title. In the thirty-first year, he was executed for treason with Liu An, King of Huainan, and his fiefdom was abolished. Jin She, the Marquis of Xinwu, followed Pei Gong Liu Bang as an attendant official and raised troops in Wanqu. He once attacked Jiyang. Defeated the army of Qin general Li You. He also attacked the Qin army in the south of Bo County and northeast of Kaifeng. He killed one general with a thousand cavalry, captured fifty-seven heads, and captured seventy-three people. He received the title given by Pei Gong and was named Lord Linping. Later, they fought in the north of Lantian, killing two Qin army chariot commanders and one cavalry officer, beheading 28 heads and capturing 57 people. Then he led his army to Bashang. At that time, Peigong was the king of Han Dynasty and granted Jin She the title of Marquis of Jianwu and promoted him to the rank of Cavalry Commander. Jin She followed the King of Han and pacified the Three Qin Dynasties. In addition, he led his troops to march westward to attack Qin General Zhang Ping's army in Longxi, defeated the Qin army, and pacified six counties in Longxi. The soldiers he led killed four Qin army chariot commanders, four military commanders, and twelve cavalry officers. Later, he followed the King of Han to attack the Chu army eastward and reached Pengcheng. As a result, the Han army was defeated. Jin She defended Yongqiu, and then left Yongqiu to attack Wang Wu and others who rebelled against the Han. After seizing Liang, he led his troops to attack the Chu general Xing Shuo's army stationed in Shannan, and defeated Xing Shuo. He personally captured Xing Shuo's two captains, 12 Sima and junhou, and surrendered 4,180 enemy officers and soldiers. In addition, the Chu army was defeated in the east of Xingyang. In the third year of the reign of Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty, Jin She was given a city of 4,200 households. Jin She also led his troops to Hanoi and attacked the Zhao general Ben Hao who was stationed in Chaoge. He was defeated. The soldiers he led captured the two generals alive and captured 250 horses. He followed the King of Han to attack the area east of Anyang, reaching Jipu and capturing seven counties. He also led another troops to defeat Zhao's army, captured alive Zhao's two Sima soldiers and four military commanders, and recruited 2,400 Zhao officers and soldiers to surrender. He also followed the King of Han to conquer Handan. He led his troops to capture Pingyang alone, and personally beheaded Zhao's acting prime minister who was stationed in Pingyang. The soldiers he led beheaded the leading county guard and the county guard, forcing Ye to surrender.
target: Jin She, Marquis of Xinwu, served as an attendant under Pei Gong, raising troops in Wanqu. He defeated Qin forces under Li You and others, capturing numerous enemies and receiving the title Linping Lord. After Liu Bang became King of Han, Jin She was made Marquis of Jianwu and Cavalry Commander. He pacified the Three Qin Dynasties, defeated Zhang Ping in Longxi, and fought in the Chu-Han conflict, capturing Xing Shuo’s officers and surrendering 4,180 troops. He conquered Zhao forces, captured Pingyang, and forced Ye to surrender. He defeated Xiang Yu’s army at Chenggao and Lucheng, pacified Nanjun, and arrested Han Xin.

id: 史记/七十列传/傅靳蒯成列传::group-003
article_path: 史记/七十列传/傅靳蒯成列传
source: After that, he followed the King of Han to Chen County and arrested the evil Chu King Han Xin. The King of Han divided the talisman representing the voucher into two halves and gave one half to Jin She to show his credibility, so that his title could be passed down from generation to generation. He provided for 4,600 households in the settlement and was titled Xin Wuhou. Later, Jin She followed Emperor Gao as a cavalry captain to attack Dai Wang, defeated Dai Wang Han Xin at the foot of Pingcheng, and then led his army back to Dongyuan. Because of his meritorious service, he was promoted to general of chariots and cavalry, and then led the troops of Liang, Zhao, Qi, Yan, and Chu princes to attack Chen Xi's prime minister Hou Chang in separate groups, defeating him and forcing Qu Nicheng to surrender. Later, he followed Emperor Gaozu and made great achievements in attacking Tingbu. He was granted an additional 5,300 households with stipulated food settlements. In several important battles, Jin She beheaded 90 enemies and captured 132 people. He also defeated the enemy 14 times, surrendered 59 cities, pacified one county and one country, and 23 counties. He captured alive one person each from the princes, kings and Zhuguo, and 39 officials of different ranks ranging from less than 2,000 shi to 500 shi. In the fifth year of his reign, Jin She passed away and was given the posthumous title Suhou. His son Jin Ting inherited the title of Marquis. Twenty-one years later, in the third year of the reign of Emperor Wen of Han Dynasty, he was deprived of his title and exempted from the fiefdom because he drove the people beyond the regulations. Kuai Chenghou, named Gui, was from Peixian County and his surname was Zhou. He once served as Gaozu's bodyguard and followed Gaozu in rebellion as a retainer. He once accompanied Emperor Gaozu to Bashang, and then went west to enter the Shu and Han regions. Later, he returned with Emperor Gaozu and pacified the Three Qin Dynasties, and was granted the title of Chiyang as a food town. He was ordered to lead his troops eastward to cut off the enemy's transportation channels. Then he followed Gaozu on his expedition and crossed Pingyin Ferry to the east, meeting up with the troops of Huaiyin Marquis Han Xin in Xiangguo. At that time, the battles were sometimes won and sometimes defeated, and the situation was grim, but Zhou Ji never meant to deviate from Gaozu. Emperor Gaozu granted him the title of Marquis of Xinwu, with a settlement of 3,300 households. In the twelfth year of Emperor Gaozu's reign, Zhou Gui was granted the title of Marquis of Kuai Cheng, and at the same time, he was exempted from the original food fief. Emperor Gaozu once wanted to attack Chen Xi personally, but Marquis Kuai Cheng tried to dissuade him with tears: In the past, the King of Qin conquered the world without going out in person. Now you often go out in person. Doesn't this mean that you have no more people to dispatch? Emperor Gao believed that Zhou Xie sincerely cared for him, and made an exception to allow him to enter the palace without having to walk quickly. He would not be punished with death if he killed someone. In the fifth year of Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty, Zhou Hui died of old age and was given the posthumous title Zhenhou. His son Zhou Chang inherited the title of marquis, but was exempted from the fiefdom due to a crime. In the second year of the Zhongyuan period of Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty, Zhou Ju, the son of Zhou Jie, was granted the title of Marquis on his behalf. In the third year of Yuanding, Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, Zhou Ju was appointed as Taichang official. He committed a crime and was exempted from his fiefdom. Tai Shigong said: Fu Kuan, the Marquis of Yangling, and Jin She, the Marquis of Xinwu, both received high titles. They followed Emperor Gaozu and raised troops from Shandong, attacked Xiang Yu, killed famous generals, defeated dozens of enemy armies, and surrendered dozens of cities. They did not suffer setbacks or hardships. This is also a gift from God. The Marquis of Kuai Cheng and Zhou Jie were staunch and loyal, and were never doubted by anyone. Every time Gaozu went on an expedition, he never failed to shed tears. This can only be done by a person with a very painful heart. He can be said to be a loyal and kind gentleman.
target: He was titled Xinwuhou with 4,600 households, later increased to 5,300. Jin She died in the fifth year of his reign, posthumously named Suhou. His son Jin Ting inherited but lost the title in the third year of Emperor Wen’s reign. Zhou Xie, Marquis of Kuai Cheng, from Peixian, served as Gaozu’s bodyguard and retainer. He accompanied Gaozu to Bashang, entered Shu and Han, and pacified the Three Qin Dynasties, receiving Chiyang as a fief. He led troops eastward to cut enemy supply lines and joined Han Xin at Xiangguo. Gaozu granted him the title of Marquis of Xinwu with 3,300 households, later changed to Kuai Chenghou. He once tearfully dissuaded Gaozu from personally attacking Chen Xi, earning special privileges. Zhou Xie died in the fifth year of Emperor Wen’s reign, posthumously named Zhenhou. His son Zhou Chang inherited but lost the title due to crime. Zhou Ju, his grandson, was later granted the title but lost it in the third year of Emperor Wu’s reign. Sima Qian comments that Fu Kuan and Jin She received high titles, raised troops from Shandong, defeated dozens of enemy armies, and surrendered many cities without setbacks, attributing this to divine favor. Zhou Xie, loyal and unwavering, never doubted by Gaozu, wept during expeditions, showing a deeply loyal and kind heart.

id: 史记/七十列传/儒林列传::group-000
article_path: 史记/七十列传/儒林列传
source: Tai Shigong said: When I read the regulations for the imperial examination and selection of academic officials, and when I read that Guang Kai encouraged academic officials to start education, I could not help but put down the book and sigh, saying: Alas, the Zhou royal family has declined, and the poem "Guan Ju" that satirizes current affairs has appeared; Therefore, Confucius was worried about the decline of the royal way and the rise of evil ways, so he compiled "Poems" and "Books" and organized ritual music. When he went to Qi State and heard the wonderful music of "Shao", he became so addicted that he couldn't taste the delicious meat for three months. After he returned to Lu from Wei, he began to correct the music so that the songs of "Ya" and "Song" could be put into their proper places and in an orderly manner. Because the world was chaotic and dirty, no one could use him. Therefore, Confucius traveled around the country and asked more than 70 kings for officials, but he could not get any advice. He said with emotion: If someone is willing to use me, it will only take one year to manage the country's affairs. Someone hunted unicorns in the western suburbs of the state of Lu. Confucius lamented that his ideals could not be realized after hearing about it. So he wrote the Spring and Autumn Annals with the help of the existing historical records of the state of Lu, and used it to express the emperor's royal laws. Since the death of Confucius, more than seventy of his good students have dispersed to make friends with the princes. Those who have achieved great success have become teachers and ministers of princes and kings, while those who have achieved little success have made friends and taught scholars and officials, while some have lived in seclusion and are not serving as officials. Therefore, Zilu served as an official in the state of Wei, Zizhang served as an official in the state of Chen, Ziyu of Tantai lived in the state of Chu, Zixia taught in Xihe, and Zigong lived in Qi until his death. People like Tian Zifang, Duan Qianmu, Wu Qi, and Qin Huali were all trained by Zixia's generation, and then became teachers of princes and kings. At that time, only Wei Wenhou was the most humbly seeking advice from Confucianism. Later, Confucianism gradually declined until it suffered annihilation at the hands of Qin Shihuang. During the Warring States Period, when all the great powers in the world were fighting against each other, Confucianism had been squeezed out, but in the Qi and Lu areas, those who studied and studied it never abandoned it. During the reign of King Wei of Qi and King Xuan of Qi, Mencius, Xunzi and others all inherited Confucius' work and carried it forward, becoming famous in the world with their own theories. At the end of the Qin Dynasty, Qin Shihuang burned "Poems" and "Books" and killed Confucian scholars. The Six Arts of Confucian classics have been incomplete since then. Chen She rebelled against Qin and proclaimed himself king. The Confucian scholars in Lu went to him carrying Confucius' ancestral ritual vessels. So Kong Jia became Chen She's doctor and eventually died with him. Chen She started out as an ordinary citizen and led a group of rioters to guard the border. Within a month, he became the king of Chu, but within half a year he was destroyed again. His career was very small and shallow, but the scholar-bureaucrats carried Confucius's ritual vessels to follow and submit to him. Why? Because the Qin Dynasty burned their books and studies, they accumulated grudges, which forced them to seek refuge with King Chen to vent their anger. Until Emperor Gaozu killed Xiang Ji and led his troops to surround the state of Lu, the Confucian scholars in the state of Lu were still reciting scriptures and practicing rituals and music, and the sound of string songs was endless. Isn't this the legacy of the ancient saints? Isn't this a country that deeply loves rituals and music?
target: Tai Shigong reflects on the decline of the Zhou royal family, which led to the emergence of satirical poems like "Guan Ju." Confucius, troubled by the decay of the royal way and the rise of evil, compiled the "Poems" and "Books," organized ritual music, and became so captivated by the "Shao" music in Qi that he forgot the taste of meat for months. After returning to Lu from Wei, he corrected the music, restoring order to the "Ya" and "Song." Despite traveling to over seventy states seeking office, no one employed him. When a unicorn was hunted in Lu, Confucius lamented his unrealized ideals and wrote the "Spring and Autumn Annals" based on Lu's historical records to express imperial laws. After Confucius's death, his seventy-plus disciples dispersed, some becoming teachers to princes, others teaching scholars, and some living in seclusion. Zilu served in Wei, Zizhang in Chen, Ziyu in Chu, Zixia taught in Xihe, and Zigong died in Qi. Figures like Tian Zifang and Wu Qi were trained by Zixia's generation. Confucianism declined during the Warring States, squeezed out by warring powers, but persisted in Qi and Lu. Under Kings Wei and Xuan of Qi, Mencius and Xunzi advanced Confucius's work. The Qin dynasty burned books and killed scholars, leaving the Six Arts incomplete. Chen She's rebellion saw Lu Confucians carrying Confucius's ritual vessels to him, and Kong Jia became his doctor, dying with him. Despite Chen She's brief rule, scholars followed him due to resentment over Qin's book burning. Even when Han Gaozu besieged Lu, Confucians continued reciting scriptures and practicing rituals.

source: Because the Qin Dynasty burned their books and studies, they accumulated grudges, which forced them to seek refuge with King Chen to vent their anger. Until Emperor Gaozu killed Xiang Ji and led his troops to surround the state of Lu, the Confucian scholars in the state of Lu were still reciting scriptures and practicing rituals and music, and the sound of string songs was endless. Isn't this the legacy of the ancient saints? Isn't this a country that deeply loves rituals and music? So after Confucius traveled to the state of Chen, he said: Go back! Go back. The young people in our village have lofty aspirations and brilliant literary talent. I don’t know how to teach them. Qilu people attach great importance to cultural rituals. This has been the case since ancient times. This has become a natural trend. After the establishment of the Han Dynasty, Confucian scholars began to have the opportunity to re-study the classics, and they also taught and practiced the etiquette of shooting and drinking. After Shusun Tong formulated the etiquette of the Han Dynasty, he became a Taichang official. The Confucian disciples who formulated the etiquette with him were also elected as court officials, so people sighed and became interested in Confucianism. However, at that time, the war in the world had not yet ceased, and the emperor was busy pacifying the world and had no time to consider the establishment of schools.
target: After the Han dynasty's establishment, Confucian scholars revived their studies. Shusun Tong formulated Han rituals, becoming Taichang, and his disciples became court officials, sparking interest in Confucianism. However, wars delayed school establishment.

source: After Shusun Tong formulated the etiquette of the Han Dynasty, he became a Taichang official. However, at that time, the war in the world had not yet ceased, and the emperor was busy pacifying the world and had no time to consider the establishment of schools. When Emperor Xiaohui and Empress Lu were in power, the ministers were all highly skilled in martial arts and had outstanding military exploits. During the reign of Emperor Xiaowen, he briefly appointed Confucian scholars as officials, but Emperor Xiaowen originally only loved the theory of punishment names. When Emperor Xiaojing came to power, there was no need for Confucian scholars, and Empress Dowager Dou was fond of Taoist thought. Therefore, the doctorate positions were only reserved for officials waiting for imperial edicts. Until the emperor came to the throne today, Zhao Wan, Wang Zang and others had a deep understanding of Confucianism, and the emperor also yearned for it, so the imperial court ordered the recommendation of scribes and scholars who were virtuous, upright and proficient in Confucian classics. From then on, those who taught "Shi" included Shen Peigong in Lu, Yuan Yinsheng in Qi, and Han Taifu in Yan. Among those who talked about Shangshu was Jinan Fusheng. Among those who talked about "Li" was Gaotangsheng from Lu. Among those who taught "Spring and Autumn" were Hu Wusheng in Qi and Lu, and Dong Zhongshu in Zhao. After the death of Empress Dowager Dou, Tian Fu, Marquis of Wu'an, became the prime minister. He abandoned Taoism, Xing Mingjia and other hundreds of schools of thought, and invited hundreds of Confucian scholars to serve as officials in the court. However, Gongsun Hong rose through the ranks due to his proficiency in the "Spring and Autumn". From then on, students all over the world became fascinated and devoted themselves to studying Confucianism. Gongsun Hong once worshiped as a doctor. target: Under Emperors Xiaohui, Empress Lu, Xiaowen, and Xiaojing, Confucianism was sidelined, with only a few doctorates retained. When the current emperor ascended, Zhao Wan and Wang Zang promoted Confucianism, leading to the recommendation of virtuous scholars. Teachers of the "Shi" included Shen Peigong in Lu, Yuan Yinsheng in Qi, and Han Taifu in Yan. "Shangshu" was taught by Fusheng in Jinan, "Li" by Gaotangsheng in Lu, and "Spring and Autumn" by Hu Wusheng in Qi and Dong Zhongshu in Zhao. After Empress Dowager Dou's death, Tian Fu became prime minister, favoring Confucianism, and Gongsun Hong rose through his expertise in "Spring and Autumn," inspiring widespread study. Gongsun Hong, as prime minister, petitioned the emperor to promote education, citing ancient practices of village schools.

source: Therefore, we vigorously invite people with upright moral character and broad knowledge from all over the world to come and serve as officials in the dynasty. source: The emperor's instructions said: "It's accurate." From then on, there were many well-educated Confucian scholars among the officials and ordinary officials. Duke Shen is from the state of Lu. When Emperor Gaozu passed through the state of Lu, Duke Shen followed his teacher as a disciple to visit him in the Nangong of the state of Lu. During the period of Empress Dowager Lu, Shen Gong went to Chang'an to study and study, and he and Liu Ying studied under their teacher Fuqiu Bo. After graduation, Liu Ying was granted the title of King of Chu and asked Shen Gong to be the teacher of his crown prince Liu Wu. Liu Wu was not good at studying and hated Duke Shen. When Liu Ying, the king of Chu, died and Liu Wu became the king of Chu, he imprisoned Duke Shen. Duke Shen felt humiliated, so he returned to Lu and taught at home. He never left home for the rest of his life and refused all guests. He went only when Liu Yu, King Gong of Lu, invited him. More than a hundred disciples came from far away to study with him. Professor Shen Gong only explained the meaning of words in the Book of Songs, but did not elaborate on the meaning of the scriptures. If there were any doubts, he would leave them out and not forcefully teach them. After Wang Zang Xiangshen, a native of Lanling, studied "Poetry", he used it to serve Emperor Xiaojing and became the prince's young master. Later, he was dismissed and left the court. As soon as the emperor ascended the throne, Wang Zang wrote a letter requesting to enter the palace and serve as the emperor's guard. He was promoted continuously and became a doctor within a year. Zhao Wan, a native of Dai, also studied the Book of Songs from Duke Shen, and he became a royal censor. Zhao Wan and Wang Zang asked the emperor for instructions and wanted to build a bright hall to convene the princes to hold court meetings. They could not persuade the emperor to agree to this matter, so they recommended their teacher Shen Gong. So the emperor sent envoys carrying valuable gifts of silk and jade, driving horses and chariots to greet Duke Shen. Two disciples, Zhao Wan and Wang Zang, accompanied him in ordinary post cars. Duke Shen came to the capital to pay homage to the emperor. The emperor asked him about the security of the country. Shen Gong was already over eighty years old at the time. He was very old. He replied: People in power don't need to talk much, they just focus on how well they do their best. At this time, the emperor was fond of rhetoric and rhetoric. Shen Gong, over eighty, advised the emperor to focus on actions over words, but the emperor, fond of rhetoric, was displeased. After Empress Dowager Dou's interference led to Zhao Wan and Wang Zang's deaths, Shen Gong retired and died. His disciples became doctors and officials, praised for their integrity.

source: Although their explanations of the Book of Songs are different. But most of them follow Shen Gong's opinion. Yuan Gusheng, the Taifu of King Liu Cheng of Qinghe, was a native of Qi. Because of his study of the Book of Songs, he became a doctor during the reign of Emperor Xiaojing. He and Huang Sheng argued in front of Emperor Jing. Huang Sheng said: King Tang and King Wu did not succeed to the throne according to destiny, but committed regicide and usurped the throne. Yuan Gusheng retorted: No. In the Xia Dynasty, Jie and Yin Zhou were violent and confused, and the hearts of the people in the world all surrendered to Shang Tang and Zhou Wu. Shang Tang and Zhou Wu agreed with the wishes of the people and killed Jie and Zhou. The people of Jie and Zhou refused to serve them and turned to Tang and Wu. Tang and Wu had no choice but to establish themselves as emperors. What else is this but upholding the destiny of heaven? Huang Sheng said: Although the hat is old, it must be worn on the head; although the shoes are new, they must be worn on the feet. Why? This is why there is a difference between up and down. Although Jie and Zhou were immoral, they were in the upper position as monarchs; although Tang and Wu were sages, they were in the lower position as ministers. When the monarch makes a mistake, the ministers cannot directly advise and correct it to maintain the dignity of the emperor. Instead, they use the fault to kill the monarch and replace him as the king in the south. What is this if not regicide and usurpation of the throne? Yuan Gusheng replied: If we have to judge right and wrong according to your statement, then is it not right for Emperor Gao to replace Qin Dynasty as the emperor? Then Emperor Jing said: If you eat meat but not horse liver, it is not not ignorant of the delicious taste of meat; if a scholar does not talk about whether Tang and Wu are destined to succeed to the throne, it is not considered stupid. So the argument ceased. Since then, no scholar has dared to argue whether Tang and Wu were established by destiny or whether they exiled Jie and Zhou to usurp the monarchy. Empress Dowager Dou liked the book "Laozi" and summoned Yuan Gusheng to ask him about his experience in reading this book. Yuan Gusheng said: These are just ordinary people's remarks. Empress Dowager Dou said angrily: How can it compare with Confucian poetry and books that control prisoners! So he asked Yuan Gu to enter the animal pen and kill the wild boar. Emperor Jing knew that the Queen Mother was angry and Yuan Gu said she was not guilty, so he lent him sharp weapons. He went down to the animal pen to stab the wild boar, and hit it right in the heart. With one stab, the wild boar fell to the ground. The Queen Mother remained silent. There was no reason to punish him anymore, so she had to give up. Soon after, Emperor Jing believed that Yuan Gu was honest and upright, and worshiped him as the tutor of Liu Cheng, the king of Qinghe. After a long time, he was discharged from office due to illness. The current emperor has just ascended the throne and recruited Yuan Gu to join the court because of his virtuous character. Many Confucian scholars who liked to flatter Yuan Gu were jealous and slandered Yuan Gu, saying that Yuan Gu was old, so he was dismissed from office and sent home. Yuan Gu was already over ninety years old at this time. When he was recruited, Gongsun Hong from Xue Yi was also recruited, but he did not dare to face Yuan Gu.
target: Yuan Gusheng of Qi debated Huang Sheng before Emperor Jing about whether Tang and Wu usurped the throne. When Empress Dowager Dou questioned Yuan about "Laozi," he dismissed it as common talk, angering her. She ordered him to kill a wild boar, which he did with the emperor's help. Later, he became tutor to King Qinghe but retired due to illness. Recruited by the current emperor, he was slandered and sent home at over ninety, advising Gongsun Hong to uphold uprightness.

source: Fusheng was from Jinan County. I had previously been a doctor of Qin Dynasty. During the reign of Emperor Xiaowen, he wanted to find someone who could study "Shang Shu", but he searched all over the world and found no one. Later, he heard that Fu Shenghui taught it, so he planned to recruit him. Fu Sheng was already over ninety years old at that time. He was very old and could not walk, so Emperor Wen ordered Taichang to send his master Chao Cuo to Fu Sheng to learn from him. When the Qin Dynasty burned Confucian books, Fu Sheng hid "Shang Shu" in the wall. Later, when the war broke out, Fu Sheng went into exile. After the Han Dynasty pacified the world, he returned to look for the "Shang Shu" in his collection. He had lost dozens of articles and only got twenty-nine articles. So he taught the remaining "Shang Shu" in the Qilu area. Since then, scholars have become very good at explaining "Shang Shu", and all famous scholars east of Miaoshan have dabbled in "Shang Shu" to teach students. Fu Sheng taught Zhang Sheng and Ouyang Sheng from Jinan, and Ouyang Sheng taught Qiancheng Ren Kuan. After Kuan became proficient in "Shangshu", he participated in the county election based on his achievements in Confucian classics, went to study under a doctorate official, and studied under Kong Anguo. Erkuan's family was poor and had no resources, so he often worked as a kitchen worker for the students, and often went out to work secretly to earn money to provide for his own food and clothing needs. He often read the scriptures when he went out, and read and reviewed them aloud when he was resting. According to the ranking of the examination results, he filled the vacancy of Yan Weishi. At that time, Zhang Tangzheng was fond of Confucianism, so he asked Erkuan to be his agent and responsible for reporting the case. Erkuan judged difficult and major cases based on classics and ancient methods, so Zhang Tang favored him. Erkuan was gentle and kind-hearted, with integrity and intelligence. He was able to control his own words and deeds. He was also good at writing books and drafting memorials. He was agile in writing and thinking, but he was clumsy in speech and could not explain. Zhang Tang thought that he was a loyal person and praised him many times. When Zhang Tang became the imperial censor, he appointed Er Kuan as an official and recommended him to the emperor. After the emperor summoned Erkuan to inquire about him, he liked him very much. Six years after Zhang Tang's death, Erkuan became a royal official and died after nine years in office. Erkuan was one of the three princes. He had a long career as an official because of his gentle and kind temperament, his ability to obey the emperor's will, and his ability to mediate disputes. However, he did not correct the emperor's mistakes. During his tenure as an official, his subordinate officials looked down upon him and did not do their best for him. Zhang Sheng also became a doctoral officer. Fu Sheng's grandson was also recruited for studying "Shang Shu", but he could not clarify the meaning of "Shang Shu". From then on, Zhou Ba and Kong Anguo from Lu and Jia Jia from Luoyang were all good at teaching the contents of Shangshu. The Kong family had the Shangshu written in ancient pre-Qin script, and Kong Anguo re-copied and read them using the current official script font, thus giving rise to his own academic school. Kong Anguo obtained more than a dozen lost chapters in "Shang Shu", and the number of "Shang Shu" probably increased gradually from this time on.
target: Fusheng of Jinan, a former Qin doctor, hid "Shangshu" during the book burning. After the Han, he recovered twenty-nine chapters and taught them. He taught at home, and many people came to learn from him, so he could not teach them one by one in person. Instead, his disciples passed it on from generation to generation, and some of them had never even met him in person. Dong Zhongshu stayed at home and never visited the garden next to his house for three years. He was so dedicated to his studies. His appearance and behavior when he came in and out were all in line with etiquette. The students followed his example and respected him. After the current emperor ascended the throne, he served as the Prime Minister of Jiangdu. He deduced the reasons for the alternating movement of yin and yang based on the changes in natural disasters and special phenomena recorded in the Spring and Autumn Annals. Therefore, when praying for rain, he shut down all kinds of yang qi and released all kinds of yin qi, and when he stopped rain, he used the opposite method. This approach was implemented in Jiangdu State and all achieved the expected results. Later, he was demoted to a middle doctor and wrote "The Chronicle of Disasters" at home. At this time, a fire broke out in the Gaodi Temple in Liaodong. The master's father Yan was jealous of him, so he stole his book and wrote it to the emperor. The emperor summoned the Confucian scholars and showed them the book. The Confucian scholars believed that it contained accusations and ridicules of the government. Dong Zhongshu's student Lu Bushu didn't know that this was his teacher's work and thought it was extremely stupid. So he handed Dong Zhongshu over to the judge and sentenced him to death. However, the emperor issued an edict and pardoned him. Therefore, Dong Zhongshu never dared to talk about the theory of disasters. Dong Zhongshu is honest and upright. During this period, the imperial court was using troops to eliminate the intrusion of ethnic minorities inside and outside the four borders. Gongsun Hong's research on "Spring and Autumn" was not as successful as Dong Zhongshu's, but he was good at catering to the secular world, so he was able to occupy a high position and became a minister.

target: He was the most proficient in "Spring and Autumn" during the Han, teaching Gongyang studies. His disciples included Chu Da, Yin Zhong, and Lu Bushu, who judged cases fairly.

source: It's not that its kindness is too little, but that its situation is too weak. Now your Majesty has risen from Pei County, Fengyi, and gathered three thousand soldiers. He led them directly into battle and swept through the Shu and Han regions. He pacified the Three Qin Dynasties. He fought with Xiang Yu in Xingyang to compete for the danger of Chenggao. He fought seventy battles and forty small battles, causing the blood of the people of the world to flow on the earth. , the withered bones of father and son were exposed in the wilderness, countless corpses were scattered in the fields, miserable cries were heard endlessly, and people with injuries and disabilities were unable to move. However, this situation is compared with the prosperous period of King Cheng and King Kang of Zhou Dynasty. I privately think that this is not the same. Besides, Qin is covered by high mountains and surrounded by the Yellow River. The border fortresses on all sides can serve as a solid line of defense. Even if there is a sudden crisis, millions of soldiers can be ready for a battle. Relying on Qin's original management foundation and relying on fertile land, this is the so-called land of heaven with dangerous situation and abundant products. Your Majesty entered Hangu Pass and built the capital there. Even if there is trouble in Shandong, the original land of Qin can be preserved and occupied. When fighting with others, you cannot completely win without grabbing him by the throat and hitting him on the back. If your Majesty enters Hangu Pass and builds a capital, he will control the original areas of Qin. This is to grab the world by its throat and hit it on the back. Emperor Gao of the Han Dynasty sought the opinions of his ministers, who were all from the Shandong area. They argued one after another that the Zhou Dynasty established its capital in Luoyang and ruled the world for hundreds of years, while the Qin Dynasty established its capital in Guan Nei and perished after only two generations. It was better to establish its capital in the capital of the Zhou Dynasty. The emperor hesitated. After Zhang Liang, the remaining marquis, clearly explained the favorable conditions for entering Guanzhong and establishing the capital, the emperor took a car westward to establish the capital in Guanzhong that day. At that time, the emperor said: Originally it was Liu Jing who advocated establishing the capital in Qin, and Lou is Liu. So he changed Liu Jing's surname to Liu, granted him the official position of doctor, and gave him the title Fengchun Jun. In the seventh year of Emperor Gao of the Han Dynasty, King Xin of Han rebelled, and Emperor Gao of the Han Dynasty personally went to defeat him. When he arrived in Jinyang, he learned that Han Wangxin was colluding with the Xiongnu to attack the Han Dynasty. The emperor was furious and sent envoys to the Xiongnu. The Xiongnu hid their strong and capable soldiers and their fat cattle and horses, leaving only old and weak soldiers and thin livestock exposed. More than ten batches of envoys were sent back, and they all said that the Huns could attack. The emperor sent Liu Jing to go on an envoy to the Xiongnu again. He came back and reported: The two countries are at war, and it is time to show off their strengths.
target: Liu Jing, a native of Qi, advised Emperor Gao of Han against establishing the capital in Luoyang, arguing that the Han Dynasty's rise differed from the Zhou Dynasty's gradual accumulation of virtue over generations. He noted that the Zhou built Luoyang as a central capital during their peak, but their decline showed that a weak situation, not just virtue, led to loss of control. In contrast, the Han emerged from warfare, with countless battles and suffering, making it unsuitable to emulate the Zhou. Liu Jing advocated for capitalizing in Guanzhong, protected by mountains and the Yellow River, with fertile land and a strategic position to "grab the world by its throat." Despite opposition from ministers favoring Luoyang, Zhang Liang's support led Emperor Gao to establish the capital in Guanzhong, rewarding Liu Jing with a surname change to Liu, the title of doctor, and the name Fengchun Jun.

id: 史记/七十列传/刘敬叔孙通列传::group-001

source: In the seventh year of Emperor Gao of the Han Dynasty, King Xin of Han rebelled, and Emperor Gao of the Han Dynasty personally went to defeat him. When he arrived in Jinyang, he learned that Han Wangxin was colluding with the Xiongnu to attack the Han Dynasty. The emperor was furious and sent envoys to the Xiongnu. The Xiongnu hid their strong and capable soldiers and their fat cattle and horses, leaving only old and weak soldiers and thin livestock exposed. More than ten batches of envoys were sent back, and they all said that the Huns could attack. The emperor sent Liu Jing to go on an envoy to the Xiongnu again. He came back and reported: The two countries are at war, and it is time to show off their strengths. Now when I go there, I see only emaciated livestock and old and weak soldiers. This must be a deliberate attempt to show shortcomings and ambush surprise troops to win. I think the Huns cannot attack. By this time, the Han army had crossed Gouzhu Mountain, and an army of 200,000 soldiers had set out to fight. The emperor was very angry after hearing Liu Jing's words and scolded Liu Jing: "Qi is a coward!" I got the official position by relying on my words, but now I dare to stop me from sending troops by talking nonsense. Liu Jing was imprisoned in shackles and imprisoned in Guangwu County. Emperor Gao led his army to Pingcheng, and when they arrived at Pingcheng, the Huns unexpectedly sent out troops to siege Emperor Gao on Baishan Mountain. They were besieged for seven days before they were able to relieve the siege. When Emperor Gao returned to Guangwu County, he pardoned Liu Jing and said to Liu Jing: I didn't listen to your opinion, so I was besieged in Pingcheng. I have beheaded all the ten people who were approved by the Huns to attack. So Liu Jing was rewarded with a settlement of 2,000 households, and was granted the title of Marquis of Guannei, also known as Marquis of Jianxin. Emperor Gao of the Han Dynasty withdrew from Pingcheng and returned to the court, while King Xin of Han fled to Hu Di. At this time, Maodun was the Xiongnu Chanyu. He had a powerful army with 300,000 warriors and repeatedly invaded the northern border. The emperor was very worried about this situation and asked Liu Jing what to do. Liu Jing said: The Han Dynasty had just settled down, and the soldiers were tired of fighting. They could not use force to subdue the Xiongnu. Maodun killed his father and proclaimed himself a Chanyu, and took many of his father's concubines as his wives. He relied on force to establish his power, but he could not be persuaded by benevolence, righteousness, and morality. We can only make long-term plans to make his descendants surrender to the Han Dynasty, but I'm afraid your Majesty can't do it. The emperor said: If it is really feasible, why can't it be done? What to do? Liu Jing replied: If your majesty can marry the eldest princess born to the empress to Moton as his wife, and give him rich gifts. He knows that it is the daughter of the empress of the Han Dynasty who has sent rich gifts. The rough foreigners will definitely envy the use of Han women as Yan family members, and the son they will give birth to will definitely be the prince and will succeed the throne in the future. Why do this? Because the Xiongnu coveted the Han Dynasty's generous wealth and gifts. His Majesty repeatedly inquired about and presented gifts to the Han Dynasty that were superfluous throughout the year but rare to the Xiongnu. He also sent eloquent people to enlighten him with etiquette.
target: Later, in the seventh year of Emperor Gao, Liu Jing was sent to scout the Xiongnu before a campaign against the rebellious King Xin of Han. He warned that the Xiongnu's display of weak soldiers and livestock was a ruse to ambush the Han army, advising against attack. Emperor Gao ignored this, imprisoned Liu Jing, and marched to Pingcheng, where he was besieged for seven days. After escaping, he released Liu Jing, rewarded him with 2,000 households, and granted him the title of Marquis of Guannei. To address Xiongnu threats, Liu Jing proposed a peace marriage alliance, suggesting Emperor Gao marry his eldest princess to Maodun Chanyu to ensure future submission through kinship. Emperor Gao agreed but, due to Empress Lu's protests, sent a palace maid instead, with Liu Jing negotiating the treaty.

id: 史记/七十列传/刘敬叔孙通列传::group-002
article_path: 史记/七十列传/刘敬叔孙通列传
source: Why do this? Because the Xiongnu coveted the Han Dynasty's generous wealth and gifts. His Majesty repeatedly inquired about and presented gifts to the Han Dynasty that were superfluous throughout the year but rare to the Xiongnu. He also sent eloquent people to enlighten him with etiquette. When Maodun reigns, of course he is the son-in-law of the Han Dynasty; after his death, his grandson of the Han Dynasty is the monarch. Who has ever heard of a grandson who dared to stand up to his grandfather? The army could gradually make the Xiongnu surrender without going to war. If His Majesty cannot send the eldest princess, but lets a royal woman or a concubine pretend to be a princess, he will know about it and will not respect her and get close to her. There will be no good in that. After hearing this, Emperor Gao said: OK. He wanted to send the eldest princess to the Huns. When Empress Lu learned about it, she cried day and night and said to the emperor: I only have a prince and a daughter, how can I bear to abandon her to marry the Huns! After all, the emperor could not send the eldest princess, so he found a palace maid to marry Lord Moton as his wife in the name of the eldest princess. At the same time, Liu Jing was sent to conclude a peace and marriage alliance with the Xiongnu. When Liu Jing came back from the Huns, he said that the two tribes of the Huns in Henan, Aiyang and Loufan, were only 700 miles away from Chang'an, and light cavalry could reach the Guanzhong area in one day and one night. The Guanzhong area had just gone through the war and was still very depleted, with a sparse population, but the land was fertile and could be gradually enriched by immigrants. When the princes from all over the country raised armies to attack, they would not have prospered if it had not been for the participation of the Tian clan of Qi State and the Zhao, Qu and Jing clans of Chu State. Now, although His Majesty built the capital in Guanzhong, there is actually a lack of population. The north is close to the Huns and the enemy, and the east is the old nobles of the six countries. The clan power is very strong. If anything happens, your majesty cannot rest easy. I hope that your majesty will move the Tian clan of Qi State, the three major clans of Zhao, Qu and Jing of Chu State, the descendants of Yan, Zhao, Han, Wei and other countries, as well as the wealthy and famous people, to live in Guanzhong. If there is peace in the country, you can guard against the Xiongnu; if there is trouble in the vassal states, you can also lead them eastward to attack. This is a strategy to strengthen central power and weaken local power. The emperor said: Very good. So Liu Jing was sent to move more than 100,000 people to Guanzhong according to his own suggestions.
target: Upon returning, Liu Jing warned that Xiongnu tribes near Chang'an posed a threat and recommended strengthening Guanzhong's population by moving powerful clans from Qi, Chu, and other states, as well as wealthy families, to bolster defenses against both the Xiongnu and potential rebellions. Emperor Gao approved, and Liu Jing relocated over 100,000 people.

id: 史记/七十列传/刘敬叔孙通列传::group-003

source: Now that the world has become one, we have destroyed counties, cities, and cities, and sold all kinds of weapons to make it clear to the world that they will no longer use them. What's more, when a wise monarch reigns over the world and formulates complete laws and regulations for those below, so that everyone obeys the law and obeys their duties, and everyone from all directions submits to the court, how can anyone dare to rebel? This is just a group of thieves stealing, nothing to worry about. The county officials are hunting them down and punishing them, which is not worth worrying about. Qin Er said happily: "Okay." I asked every Confucian scholar again. Some Confucian scholars said they were rebels, and some said they were thieves. So Qin II ordered the censors to examine what every Confucian scholar said, and anyone who said they were rebels would be handed over to officials for punishment. Qin II believed that they should not say such things. Those who were said to be thieves were removed from their posts. But he gave Shusun Tong twenty pieces of silk, a set of clothes, and the title of doctorate. Shusun Tong walked out of the palace and returned to his residence. Some Confucian scholars asked: What flattering words did the master say? Shusun Tong said: You don’t know, I can hardly escape from the tiger’s mouth! So he fled the capital and arrived at Xue County. At that time, Xue County had surrendered to the Chu army. When Xiang Liang arrived in Xue County, Shusun Tong took refuge with him. Later, Xiang Liang died in battle in Dingtao, and Shusun Tong followed Xiong Xin, King Huai of Chu. King Huai was conferred the title of Righteous Emperor by Xiang Yu and moved to Changsha. Shusun Tong stayed behind to serve Xiang Yu. In the second year of Emperor Gao of the Han Dynasty, Liu Bang, the king of Han, led five princes and kings to attack Pengcheng, and Shusun Tong surrendered to the king of Han.
target: Shusun Tong, a scholar from Xue County, served under Qin II, where he flattered the emperor by dismissing a rebellion as mere thievery, earning rewards but fleeing after Qin II punished those who spoke truthfully. He later served Xiang Liang, King Huai of Chu, and Xiang Yu before surrendering to Liu Bang, the King of Han. Disliking Confucian robes, Shusun Tong adopted Chu-style short coats, pleasing the king. He recommended warriors over his own disciples, explaining that the king needed fighters, not scholars, during wartime.

id: 史记/七十列传/刘敬叔孙通列传::group-004
article_path: 史记/七十列传/刘敬叔孙通列传
source: Please wait for me, I won't forget you. The king of Han appointed Shusun Tong as a doctor and called him the Sijun of Ji. In the fifth year of Emperor Gao of the Han Dynasty, the world had been unified. The princes in Dingtao jointly honored the King of Han as the emperor, and Shusun Tong was responsible for formulating the rituals and etiquette. At that time, Emperor Gao of the Han Dynasty abolished all the strict etiquette regulations of the Qin Dynasty and only formulated some simple and easy-to-implement rules. However, the ministers were drinking and having fun in the court and arguing about merits. Some of them were shouting and screaming when they were drunk, and even drew their swords to chip away at the pillars of the court. Emperor Gao was troubled by this matter. Shusun Tong knew that the emperor was becoming more and more disgusted with such things, so he advised: It is difficult for those Confucian scholars to attack and capture for you, but they can help you preserve the results. I hope to recruit some Confucian scholars from Lu to work with my disciples to formulate court etiquette. Emperor Gao said: I'm afraid it will be as cumbersome and difficult as in the past, right? Shusun Tong said: The five emperors have different rituals, and the three kings have different rituals. Ritual is to formulate rules of moderation or modification for people according to the world's affairs and customs at that time. Therefore, we can understand this from the inheritance, deletion and addition of etiquette in the Xia, Yin and Zhou dynasties, which means that the etiquette in different dynasties is not repeated. I am willing to use some ancient etiquette and combine it with the etiquette of the Qin Dynasty to formulate new etiquette. The emperor said: You can try to do it, but make it easy to understand and consider what I can do. So Shusun Tong was ordered to recruit more than thirty Confucian scholars from Lu. There are two Confucian scholars in Lu who don't want to leave, saying: "You have served nearly ten monarchs, and they all gained closeness and authority through face-to-face flattery." Now that the world has just been peaceful, the dead have not yet been buried, and the disabled have not yet recovered, yet regulations on rituals and music must be formulated. Judging from the root cause of the establishment of rituals and music, it can only be popularized after a hundred years of accumulated merit.
target: After the Han unification, Emperor Gao abolished strict Qin rituals, leading to chaotic court behavior. Shusun Tong proposed creating a simplified court etiquette, blending ancient and Qin practices. He recruited 30 Confucian scholars, despite two refusing, and practiced for a month.

id: 史记/七十列传/刘敬叔孙通列传::group-005

source: So the emperor came out of the palace in a dragon chariot. Hundreds of officials raised flags to call for warning, and then guided officials at all levels from the princes to more than six hundred stones to respectfully salute and congratulate the emperor. All the officials below the princes and kings were not frightened and awed by this majestic ceremony. Wait until the ceremony is over, and then arrange a banquet. All the princes and officials sitting in the main hall held their breath and lowered their heads. They stood up in order of honor to congratulate and toast the emperor. After nine rounds of pouring wine, the visitor announced that the banquet was over. Finally, the supervisory officials enforced the etiquette regulations, identified those who did not comply with the etiquette regulations, and took them away. From the court to the banquet, no one dared to speak loudly or act inappropriately. After the ceremony, Emperor Gao said very proudly: Only today do I know the dignity of being an emperor. So he gave Shusun Tong the official position of Taichang and rewarded him with five hundred catties of gold. Shusun Tong took the opportunity to speak and said: My disciples, Confucian scholars, have been following me for a long time. They have worked with me to formulate court etiquette. I hope that your majesty will grant them official positions. Emperor Gao made them all officials.
target: In the seventh year, the Changle Palace ceremony impressed Emperor Gao, who remarked, "Only today do I know the dignity of being an emperor." Shusun Tong was made Taichang, rewarded with gold, and his disciples received official posts.

id: 史记/七十列传/刘敬叔孙通列传::group-006
article_path: 史记/七十列传/刘敬叔孙通列传
source: Shusun Tong took the opportunity to speak and said: My disciples, Confucian scholars, have been following me for a long time. They have worked with me to formulate court etiquette. I hope that your majesty will grant them official positions. Emperor Gao made them all officials. After Shusun Tong left the palace, he distributed five hundred kilograms of gold to various Confucian scholars. These Confucian scholars all said happily: Mr. Shusun is really a great sage who knows the important affairs of the day. In the ninth year of Emperor Gao of the Han Dynasty, Emperor Gao appointed his uncle Sun Tong as the crown prince and tutor. In the twelfth year of Emperor Gao of the Han Dynasty, Emperor Gao planned to let Zhao Wang Liu Ruyi replace the prince. Shusun Tong advised the emperor: In the past, Duke Xiang of Jin deposed the prince Shensheng because he favored Li Ji, and replaced him with Xi Qi. This caused the Jin Dynasty to be in chaos for decades, and was ridiculed by the people of the world. Because Qin Shihuang did not confirm Fusu as the crown prince early, he allowed Zhao Gao to use deception to establish Hu Hai, and ended up destroying himself. This is a fact that your Majesty has witnessed with your own eyes. Now everyone in the world knows that the prince is benevolent, righteous, loyal and filial; Empress Lu and Your Majesty have gone through hardships and lived together, and they are a couple who share weal and woe. How can they turn their backs on her? Your Majesty must abolish the eldest son and support the younger son. I would rather die first and let my blood stain the earth red. Emperor Gao said: Forget it, sir, I was just talking casually. Shusun Tong said: The prince is the foundation of the world. When the foundation is shaken, the world will shake. How can you use the foundation of the world as a joke? Emperor Gao said: I listen to your opinion. When the emperor set up a banquet to entertain the guests, he saw that the four senior scholars invited by Zhang Liang followed the prince into the palace to pay respects. The emperor had no idea of ​​replacing the prince anymore. When Emperor Gao of the Han Dynasty passed away and Emperor Xiaohui came to the throne, he said to Mr. Shusun: None of the officials are familiar with the etiquette of the late emperor's cemetery and ancestral temple. So he was appointed as Taichang and formulated the ceremonial regulations of the ancestral temple. After that, many ceremonial systems of the Han Dynasty were successively formulated, all of which were recorded and recorded by Shusun Tong when he was appointed Taichang. Emperor Xiaohui of the Han Dynasty wanted to go to the Changle Palace in the east to pay homage to the Empress Dowager Lu, and he often had small visits. Every time he went out, he had to clear the way. It was very annoying to block the passage, so he built a pavilion road just south of the arsenal of Weiyang Palace. Shusun Tong reported to Emperor Xiaohui about his work, and took the opportunity to ask for a confidential talk with the emperor: How could your Majesty build a flyover without authorization over the passage from Gaobin to Gaomiao every month? Gaodi Temple is the ancestral temple of the founder of the Han Dynasty. How can future generations be allowed to walk above the passage of the ancestral temple?
target: As crown prince tutor in the ninth year, Shusun Tong opposed Emperor Gao's plan to replace Crown Prince Liu Ying with Zhao Wang Liu Ruyi, citing historical disasters from such actions. He emphasized the prince's virtue and Empress Lu's shared hardships, threatening death if the change proceeded. Emperor Gao relented, especially after seeing four scholars supporting the prince. Under Emperor Xiaohui, Shusun Tong served as Taichang, formulating ancestral temple rituals. He advised against a pavilion road built over the Gaodi Temple passage, suggesting a new temple instead, and introduced cherry offerings to the temple. Sima Qian concluded that Liu Jing's strategic advice and Shusun Tong's adaptable ritual-making were crucial to the Han's stability, highlighting their unique contributions.

id: 史记/七十列传/刺客列传::group-000
article_path: 史记/七十列传/刺客列传
source: Cao Mo was from the state of Lu, and served Duke Zhuang of Lu with bravery and strength. Duke Zhuang loves brave people. Cao Mo served as the general of Lu and fought with Qi, being defeated many times and fled. Duke Zhuang of Lu was afraid, so he offered up Suiyi area to seek peace. But Cao Mo was still appointed as general. Duke Huan of Qi agreed to meet with Duke Zhuang of Lu in Ke Di and make an alliance. After Duke Huan and Duke Zhuang made an alliance on the altar, Cao Mo threatened Duke Huan with a dagger. No one in Duke Huan's bodyguard dared to move rashly. Duke Huan asked, "What are you going to do?" Cao Mo replied: Qi is strong and Lu is weak, so it would be too much to invade Lu with a big country. Now if the capital of Lu falls, it will hit the border of Qi. You need to consider this issue. So Duke Huan of Qi promised to return all the occupied land of Lu. After he finished speaking, Cao Mo dropped his dagger, walked down from the altar, and returned to where the courtiers were sitting, facing north, his expression unchanged, and his conversation calm as usual. Duke Huan was very angry and planned to break the covenant. Guan Zhong said: No. If you covet small profits for temporary pleasure, you will lose credibility in front of the princes and lose the support of the people in the world. It is better to return the land to Lu. So, Duke Huan of Qi returned the occupied land of Lu as agreed, and all the land that Cao Mo had lost in many battles returned to Lu. One hundred and sixty-seven years later, there were Zhuan Zhu's deeds in the state of Wu. Zhuanzhu was from Wu Guotang. When Wu Zixu fled Chu and went to Wu, he knew that Zhuan Zhu had skills. After Wu Zixu went to see King Liao of Wu, he persuaded him about the benefits of attacking Chu. Wu Gongziguang said: That Wu Yuan's father and brother were all killed by the Chu State. Wu Yuan just wanted to attack the Chu State. He did it to avenge his own personal revenge and did not really think about the Wu State.
target: The deeds of five assassins from ancient China, spanning over four centuries. Cao Mo of Lu, a general who, after military defeats against Qi, threatened Duke Huan of Qi with a dagger during a peace alliance. Cao Mo forced the duke to promise the return of all occupied Lu lands. Though the duke initially wanted to break the promise, his advisor Guan Zhong convinced him that keeping his word was crucial for maintaining credibility among the feudal lords, and the lands were returned.

id: 史记/七十列传/刺客列传::group-001
article_path: 史记/七十列传/刺客列传
source: One hundred and sixty-seven years later, there were Zhuan Zhu's deeds in the state of Wu. Zhuanzhu was from Wu Guotang. When Wu Zixu fled Chu and went to Wu, he knew that Zhuan Zhu had skills. After Wu Zixu went to see King Liao of Wu, he persuaded him about the benefits of attacking Chu. Wu Gongziguang said: That Wu Yuan's father and brother were all killed by the Chu State. Wu Yuan just wanted to attack the Chu State. He did it to avenge his own personal revenge and did not really think about the Wu State. The king of Wu no longer discussed the attack on Chu. Wu Zixu knew that Young Master Guang planned to kill King Liao of Wu, so he said: That Young Master Guang has an attempt to seize the throne at home, and we cannot persuade him to send troops abroad yet. So he recommended Zhuanzhu to Gongzi Guang. The father of Prince Guang was Zhufan, King of Wu. Zhufan had three younger brothers: in order of brotherhood, the eldest brother was called Yuji, the second brother was called Yimei, and the youngest brother was called Ji Zha. Zhufan knew that Ji Zha was a virtuous man, so he did not make his son the crown prince. Instead, he wanted to pass on the throne in the order of brothers, and finally pass the throne to Ji Zha. After Zhufan died, the throne was passed to Yuji. After Yuji's death, he passed it on to Yimei. After Yimei's death, it should have been passed down to Jiziza, but Jiziza avoided and refused to be made king, so the people of Wu made Yimei's son Liao their king. Prince Guang said: If the order of brothers is to be followed, the youngest son should be established; if it must be passed on to the son, then I am the real legitimate son, and I should be made the king. Therefore, he often secretly supported some wise people in order to obtain the throne with their help. After Prince Guang got Zhuanzhu, he treated him well like a guest. In the ninth year of King Liao of Wu, King Ping of Chu died. In the spring of this year, King Liao of Wu wanted to take advantage of the funeral of Chu State and sent his two younger brothers, Gongzi Gaiyu and Shuyong, to lead an army to surround the city of Ji of Chu State. He also sent the youngest son of Yanling to Jin State to observe the activities of various vassal states. The Chu State sent out its troops and cut off Wu generals Gaiyu and Shuyong's retreat. The Wu army could not return. At this time, Gongzi Guang said to Zhuan Zhu: This opportunity cannot be missed. If you don't fight for it, you will never get it! Besides, I am the true heir and should be made king. Even if Ji Zi comes back, he will not depose me. Zhuan Zhu said: Wang Liao can be killed. Mother and son were weak, so the two younger brothers led the army to attack the Chu State. The Chu State army cut off their retreat. At present, the Wu army is besieged by the Chu State outside, but there are no loyal ministers who are upright and outspoken in the country. What else can King Liao do to us? Gongzi Guang kowtowed his head and said: My Gongzi Guang's body is your body, and I will be responsible for everything after your death. On Bingzi day in April of this year, Gongzi Guang ambushed the warriors in armor in the basement and prepared a banquet for King Wu. King Liao sent guards to line up from the palace to Gongzi Guang's home. On both sides of the door and steps were King Liao's cronies.
target: One hundred and sixty-seven years later, Zhuan Zhu of Wu was recommended to Prince Guang by Wu Zixu. Prince Guang believed he was the rightful heir to the Wu throne, which had passed through brothers instead of to him. He plotted to kill King Liao of Wu. During a banquet, Zhuan Zhu hid a dagger inside a grilled fish and assassinated the king. Prince Guang's warriors then killed the king's guards, and Prince Guang became King Helu of Wu, rewarding Zhuan Zhu's son.

id: 史记/七十列传/刺客列传::group-002
article_path: 史记/七十列传/刺客列传
source: When he came to King Liao, Zhuan Zhu broke open the fish and stabbed King Liao with his dagger. King Liao died at that time. The guards also killed Zhuan Zhu, and King Liao's men were in chaos for a while. Prince Guang sent out an ambush of warriors to attack King Liao's men, and wiped them all out. He then proclaimed himself king, and became King Helu of Wu. Helu then granted Zhuanzhu's son the title of Shangqing. Over the next seventy years, Yurang's deeds were recorded in the state of Jin. Yu Rang was a native of Jin. He had served the Fan family and the Zhongxing family in the past, but he had no reputation. He left them to serve Zhibo, who respected and favored him very much. When Zhibo attacked Zhao Xiangzi, Zhao Xiangzi, Han and Wei jointly planned to destroy Zhibo. After Zhibo was destroyed, the three families divided his territory. Zhao Xiangzi hated Zhibo the most, so he painted his skull into a drinking vessel. Yurang fled to the mountains and said, "Oh! A man should die for someone who understands him, and a good woman should dress up for someone who loves her. Now that Uncle Zhi is my confidant, I will definitely avenge him and sacrifice my life to repay Uncle Zhi. Then even if I die, my soul will have nothing to be ashamed of. So he changed his name and surname, pretended to be a person who had been tortured, entered Zhao Xiang's womb to repair the toilet, and hid a dagger on his body, intending to use it to assassinate Zhao Xiangzi. Zhao Xiangzi went to the toilet, his heart palpitated, and he questioned the prisoner who was repairing the toilet, and found out that it was Yu Rang, with a sharp knife hidden in his clothes. Yu Rang said: "I want to avenge Zhibo!"
target: Seventy years later, Yu Rang of Jin sought to avenge his master Zhibo, who was killed by Zhao Xiangzi. Yu Rang first attempted assassination while disguised as a prisoner repairing a toilet, but was discovered and released. He then disfigured himself by painting his skin and swallowing charcoal to change his appearance.

id: 史记/七十列传/刺客列传::group-003
article_path: 史记/七十列传/刺客列传
source: Even his wife doesn't recognize him anymore. I met his friend on the road, recognized him, and said, "Aren't you Yu Rang?" Answered: It's me. His friend shed tears for him and said: With your talents, you will devote yourself to serving Zhao Xiangzi. Xiangzi will definitely be close to you and love you. Isn’t it easy to be close to you and do whatever you want? Why bother to mutilate your body and disfigure your appearance? Isn't it more difficult to achieve the purpose of revenge against Zhao Xiangzi in this way? Yurang said: "After entrusting yourself to serve someone, you then want to kill him. This is a monarch who serves him with a different intention." I know that it is very difficult to choose this approach, but the reason why I chose this approach is to make future generations of ministers in the world feel ashamed who serve the king with different intentions! After Yurang finished speaking, he left. Soon, Xiangzi was catching up to go out, and Yurang hid under the bridge that he must pass by. When Xiangzi came to the bridge, the horse was frightened. Xiangzi said: "This must be Yurang." I sent someone to check, and it turned out to be Yu Rang. So Xiangzi listed his sins and accused him, saying: Didn't you once serve the Fan family and the Zhongxing family? Zhibo wiped them all out, but instead of avenging them, you pretended to be Zhibo's retainer. Zhibo is dead, why are you so eager to avenge him? Yu Rang said: I serve the Fan family and the Zhongxing family, and they treat me as an ordinary person, so I repay them like an ordinary person. As for Zhibo, he treats me as a national scholar, so I repay him like a national scholar.
target: He hid under a bridge, but Zhao Xiangzi's horse was startled, revealing him. Zhao Xiangzi confronted him, and Yu Rang explained that Zhibo treated him as a national scholar, so he must repay him accordingly. He asked to stab Zhao Xiangzi's robe to fulfill his revenge, then committed suicide.

id: 史记/七十列传/刺客列传::group-004
article_path: 史记/七十列传/刺客列传
source: As for Zhibo, he treats me as a national scholar, so I repay him like a national scholar. Xiangzi sighed and said with tears: Oh, Mr. Yurang! You have become famous by avenging Uncle Zhi; and it is enough for me to forgive you. You should make your own plan, I can't let you go anymore! Order the soldiers to surround him. Yu Rang said: I have heard that a wise monarch does not bury the reputation of others, and loyal ministers are willing to die for their reputation. You forgave me before, and no one in the world did not praise your wisdom. I should have suffered the death penalty for what happened today, but I hope I can get your clothes and prick it a few times. This will fulfill my desire for revenge. Then, even if I die, I will have no regrets. I dare not expect you to agree to my request, but I still venture to speak my mind! So Xiangzi admired his chivalry very much and sent someone to bring his clothes to Yurang. Yu Rang pulled out his sword, jumped up and stabbed it many times, saying: "I can use it to repay Uncle Zhi for being under the Nine Springs!" So he committed suicide with his sword. On the day of his suicide, all the people with lofty ideals in Zhao State cried for him when they heard the news. More than forty years have passed since then, and there are stories of Nie Zheng in Zhi. Nie Zheng was a native of Shenjing, Zhiyi. In order to avoid killing people, he fled to Qi State with his mother and sister, and slaughtered livestock as a profession. After a long time, Yan Zhongzi of Puyang served Han Aihou and developed a grudge against Xia Lei, the Prime Minister of South Korea. Yan Zhongzi was afraid of being killed and ran away. He traveled around, looking for someone who could avenge Xia Lei on his behalf. When he arrived in Qi State, some people in Qi State said that Nie Zheng was a brave man because he avoided his enemies and hid among the butchers. Yan Zhongzi visited Nie Zheng's house and made many trips. Then he prepared a banquet and personally held a cup to toast Nie Zheng's mother. When he was very happy after drinking, Yan Zhongzi presented a hundred yi of gold to his mother Nie Zheng to celebrate her birthday.
target: More than forty years later, Nie Zheng of Zhi was sought out by Yan Zhongzi, who had a grudge against the Korean prime minister Xia Lei. Nie Zheng initially refused because his mother was alive, but after her death, he agreed. He went alone to the Korean court, killed Xia Lei, and then disfigured his own face before dying to protect his family. His sister Nie Rong identified his body, proclaiming his honor, and died of grief beside him.

id: 史记/七十列传/刺客列传::group-005
article_path: 史记/七十列传/刺客列传
source: After a long time, Jing Ke still showed no sign of taking action. At this time, Qin general Wang Jian had already broken through Zhao's capital, captured the king of Zhao, and incorporated all Zhao's territory into Qin's territory. The army advanced and seized land to the north until it reached the southern border of Yan State. Prince Dan was afraid, so he begged Jing Ke: The Qin army will cross Yishui sooner or later. Even if I want to serve you for a long time, how can I do it? Jing Ke said: Even if the prince does not say anything, I will ask for action. Now when I go to the Kingdom of Qin, if I don’t have anything to make the King of Qin trust me, then the King of Qin will not be able to approach me. As for General Fan, the King of Qin offered a reward of a thousand catties of gold and ten thousand households to buy his head. If I really get the head of General Fan and the map of Dukang of Yan State and present them to the King of Qin, the King of Qin will be happy to receive me, so that I can have the opportunity to serve you.
target: Two hundred and twenty years later, Jing Ke of Wei was recruited by Prince Dan of Yan to assassinate the King of Qin. Jing Ke gained the king's trust by presenting the head of a fugitive general and a map of Yan territory.

id: 史记/七十列传/刺客列传::group-006
article_path: 史记/七十列传/刺客列传
source: Jing Ke chased the King of Qin, and the King of Qin ran around the pillar. The ministers were in a daze with fright. Suddenly something unexpected happened and everyone lost their normal state. The laws of the Qin State stipulate that the ministers in the palace are not allowed to carry any weapons; the military attachés can only guard outside the palace in order with weapons, and they are not allowed to enter the palace without the emperor's order. At the critical moment, there was no time to summon the guards below, so Jing Ke was able to pursue the King of Qin. In a hurry, he was panic-stricken and had no weapons to attack Jing Ke, so he could only fight Jing Ke with his bare hands. At this time, the attendant medical officer Xia Wuqie hit Jing Ke with the medicine bag he was holding. Just as King Qin was running around the pillar, panicking and not knowing what to do, the attendants shouted: Your Majesty, push your sword behind your back! King Qin pushed his sword behind his back, then drew out his sword and attacked Jing Ke, cutting off his left leg. Jing Ke was crippled, so he raised his dagger and threw it directly at the King of Qin. He missed but hit the bronze pillar.
target: During the audience, he attempted to stab the king but failed, being wounded and killed. The king then attacked Yan, eventually destroying it. Jing Ke's friend Gao Jianli later attempted to assassinate the First Emperor with a weighted lute but also failed and was executed. The text concludes with the historian's commentary, affirming that despite varying outcomes, these assassins' intentions were clear and their reputations endure.

id: 史记/七十列传/匈奴列传::group-000
article_path: 史记/七十列传/匈奴列传
source: The ancestor of the Xiongnu was a descendant of the Xiahou family, named Chunwei. Before Yao and Shun of the Tang Dynasty, there were Shanrong, yangxu and Xunzhu, who lived in the wild land in the north and moved with the livestock activities. Most of their livestock are horses, cattle, and sheep, and their unique livestock are camels, donkeys, and mules? Fan Jun, Fan Dao. They migrated in pursuit of water and grass. They did not have permanent urban settlements or agricultural production, but they also had their own share of pasture land. There are no words or books, only words are used to restrain each other. A child can ride a sheep, draw a bow and shoot birds and mice; an older child can shoot foxes and rabbits for food.
target: The Xiongnu, whose ancestor was Chunwei, a descendant of the Xia dynasty, were a nomadic people living in the northern wilds. They moved with their livestock—horses, cattle, sheep, camels, and donkeys—in search of water and pasture, without permanent cities or agriculture. They had no written language, relying on oral agreements.

id: 史记/七十列传/匈奴列传::group-001
article_path: 史记/七十列传/匈奴列传
source: The men all had the strength to draw their bows, and they were all cavalry in armor. Their custom is that they nomadically roam at will and take hunting animals as their occupation; when the situation is urgent, everyone will practice combat and carry out invasions and conquests. This is their nature. Their long weapons were bows and arrows, and their short weapons were knives and small spears with iron handles. Attack when the situation is favorable, retreat when the situation is unfavorable, and do not be ashamed of running away. If you can get benefits, you don't know what etiquette is. From the king down, everyone eats the meat of livestock, wears the leather of livestock, and wears fur coats. Strong people eat rich food, and old people eat leftovers. Respect the strong and look down upon the old and the infirm. When the father dies, the son takes his stepmother as his wife; when the brother dies, the surviving brothers all take the wife of the deceased brother. Their customs are famous but not taboo, and they have no surnames or given names.
target: From childhood, they learned archery and riding, and all men were armored cavalry. Their customs prioritized warfare and plunder, favoring attack when advantageous and retreating without shame. They respected the strong and disdained the weak, practiced levirate marriage, and had no taboo against using personal names. Their leaders were called Chanyu, and they held seasonal gatherings for sacrifices and censuses. Laws were harsh, with punishments for murder and theft, and burial practices included human sacrifice for the Chanyu.

id: 史记/七十列传/匈奴列传::group-002
article_path: 史记/七十列传/匈奴列传
source: Their customs are famous but not taboo, and they have no surnames or given names. When the Xia Dynasty was in political decline, Gong Liu lost his position as Ji official, implemented reforms in Xirong, built a city in Bindi and settled there. More than 300 years later, the Rongdi tribe attacked Zhou Tai Wang Dan's father, and his father fled to the foot of Qishan. The people of Bindi followed his father to the foot of Qishan, built a city here, and established the Zhou Kingdom. More than a hundred years later, Jichang, Bo of the Western Zhou Dynasty, attacked the Yi clan. More than ten years later, King Wu of Zhou attacked King Zhou of Shang and built Luoyi. He returned to live in Fengjing and Haojing. He expelled the Rongyi to the north of Jingshui and Luoshui, and asked them to pay tribute to Zhou on time, which was called "Huangfu". Over the next two hundred years, when the Zhou Dynasty was in political decline, King Mu of Zhou conquered the Dog Rong and returned after obtaining four white wolves and four white deer. From then on, the Rong and Yi people in Huangfu no longer came to Haojing to pay tribute. So the Zhou Dynasty formulated the regulations of "Fu Xing". More than two hundred years after King Mu, King You of Zhou had a grudge against Marquis Shen because of his favor with Bao Si. The Marquis of Shen was angry, so he and Quan Rong attacked and killed King Zhou You under Mount Li. The Quan Rong captured the Jiaohuo land of the Zhou Dynasty, and the monarch invaded the Central Plains area along the Jing River and the Wei River. At this time, Qin Xianggong came to the rescue of the Zhou Dynasty, so King Zhou Ping left Fengjing and Haojing and moved eastward to Luoyi. At this time, Qin Xianggong attacked the Rong people and came to Qishan, and began to be named a prince. Sixty-five years later, Shan Rong crossed Yan State and attacked Qi State. Qi Ligong fought with Shan Rong outside the city of Qi State. Forty-four years later, Shanrong attacked Yan. The State of Yan appealed to the State of Qi, and Duke Huan of Qi went north to attack the Shan Rong, but the Shan Rong fled. More than twenty years later, Rong Di came to Luoyi and attacked King Xiang of Zhou Dynasty. King Xiang fled to Panyi of Zheng State. Initially, King Xiang of Zhou wanted to attack the State of Zheng, so he married a girl from Rong Di as his queen and joined forces with the soldiers of Rong Di to attack the State of Zheng. Soon, King Xiang deposed Queen Di, and Queen Di was resentful. King Xiang's stepmother was named Queen Hui, and she had a son named Zi Dai, who wanted to make him king. So Queen Hui, Queen Di, and Zi Dai acted as internal correspondents, and opened the city gate for Rong Di, so that Rong Di could enter the city, defeat the Zhou army, drive away King Xiang of Zhou, and make Zi Dai the emperor. So some people from Rong and Di lived in Luhun, and in the east they reached Weiguo. They invaded and tortured the people of the Central Plains, and the people of the Central Plains hated them. Therefore, the authors of the Classic wrote poems about attacking the Rong and Di. They attacked the wolves and arrived in Dayuan. They sent out military chariots and many war horses and built cities in the north. King Xiang of Zhou had been living abroad for four years, so he sent an envoy to ask for help from Jin. At that time, Duke Wen of Jin had just ascended the throne and wanted to establish hegemony, so he sent troops to attack and expel the Rong and Di, killed Zi Dai, and welcomed King Zhou Xiang back to live in Luoyi.
target: Historically, the Xiongnu and their predecessors, such as the Shanrong and Xunzhu, interacted with Chinese dynasties. During the Zhou dynasty, King Mu of Zhou campaigned against the Dog Rong, and later, King You of Zhou was killed by the Quanrong, leading to the Zhou capital's eastward move. The Qin dynasty, under Qin Shihuang, sent Meng Tian to drive the Xiongnu from the Ordos region and built the Great Wall. After Qin's fall, the Xiongnu regained strength under Chanyu Touman, who was killed by his son Modun. Modun, after training his troops with a signaling arrow, usurped power and expanded Xiongnu territory, defeating the Donghu, Yuezhi, and other tribes, and amassing over 300,000 cavalry. He established a hierarchical structure with left and right kings, generals, and officials, and his rule marked the Xiongnu's peak, making them a major threat to the Han dynasty.

id: 史记/七十列传/匈奴列传::group-003
article_path: 史记/七十列传/匈奴列传
source: Not long after, Chen Xi, a general of the Han Dynasty, rebelled and conspired with Han Xin to attack Daidi. The Han Dynasty sent Fan Kuai to stop them and re-captured Daijun, Yanmen and Yunzhong counties, but did not cross the border fortress. At this time, because some generals of the Han Dynasty came to surrender to the Xiongnu, Maodun often traveled to Dai to carry out intrusion and robbery activities.
