So the Han Dynasty was worried about this, and Emperor Gao sent Liu Jing to send the princess of the Han Dynasty royal family to the Chanyu family, and gave a certain amount of cotton wool, bamboo silk, wine, rice and food to the Xiongnu every year. Later, King Lu Wan of Yan rebelled and led thousands of his followers to surrender to the Huns. They traveled east of the Shanggu and caused suffering to the local people. After the death of Emperor Gaozu, during the period of Emperor Xiaohui and Empress Dowager Lu, the Han Dynasty had just settled down, so the Xiongnu seemed proud. Maodun wrote to the Empress Dowager Lu, talking nonsense. Empress Dowager Lu wanted to attack him, but the generals said: With Emperor Gao's wisdom and martial arts, he was besieged in Pingcheng. So Queen Mother Lu gave up her idea of ​​attacking and made peace with the Xiongnu. When Emperor Xiaowen just succeeded to the throne, he promoted the marriage plan. In May of the third year of Emperor Xiaowen's reign, King Youxian of the Xiongnu entered Henan to live, harassed and plundered the barbarians in the small border towns, and massacred and plundered the people. So Emperor Xiaowen ordered Prime Minister Guan Ying to dispatch 85,000 chariots and cavalry to Gaonu to attack King Youxian. King Youxian fled outside the wall. Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty came to Taiyuan in person. At this time, King Liu Xingju of Jibei rebelled. Emperor Wen returned to the capital and disbanded the army sent by the prime minister to fight the Huns. The next year, the Chanyu of the Xiongnu sent a letter to the Han Dynasty, saying: The Great Chanyu of the Xiongnu, appointed by heaven, respectfully wishes the emperor peace. Some time ago, the emperor said about the marriage, which was consistent with the meaning of the letter, and both parties were happy. The officials on the border of the Han Dynasty harassed and insulted King Youxian. King Youxian did not ask the Shanyu for instructions, but listened to the plot of Houyi Luhou Nan and others, resisted the Han Dynasty officials, severed the treaty between the Xiongnu and the Han emperor, and alienated the close brotherly relationship between the Han and the Xiongnu.
target: The Han dynasty, after its founding, faced constant Xiongnu raids. Emperor Gaozu was besieged at Pingcheng by Modun but escaped through bribery and a peace treaty involving marriage and tribute. Subsequent rulers, including Empress Dowager Lu and Emperor Wen, maintained this policy despite Xiongnu provocations. The Xiongnu, under Chanyu Laoshang and later Junchen, continued to raid border regions, while Han envoys like Zhonghang Yue, who defected to the Xiongnu, advised them to resist Han cultural influence. The Han dynasty alternated between appeasement and military campaigns, with Emperor Wu launching large-scale offensives led by generals Wei Qing and Huo Qubing, who defeated the Xiongnu in the Ordos and Gobi, capturing key territories and forcing them northward.

id: 史记/七十列传/匈奴列传::group-004
article_path: 史记/七十列传/匈奴列传
source: The Han army had agreed that after Shan Yu entered Mayi City, he would let his soldiers attack and kill him. Now the Chanyu has not arrived at Mayi, so the Han army has gained nothing. The Han Dynasty general Wang Hui's army came out of Daijun to attack the Xiongnu's baggage. He heard that the Chanyu army had returned and there were many soldiers, so he did not dare to attack. The Han Dynasty believed that Wang Hui was the one who planned the ambush but did not dare to attack, so he killed Wang Hui. From then on, the Xiongnu broke off their fraternal relations, attacked the frontier fortresses leading to important roads, and often invaded the Han Dynasty's borders to plunder, too many times to count. However, the Xiongnu were greedy and still liked to exchange customs and markets with the Han Dynasty. They liked the Han Dynasty's property very much. The Han Dynasty still maintained customs and market trade relations with the Xiongnu and catered to their wishes. In the autumn of the fifth year after the Mayi military campaign, the Han Dynasty sent Wei Qing and other four generals with 10,000 cavalry each to attack the Xiongnu near Guan City. General Wei Qing led his troops out of Shanggu County and arrived at Fucheng, where they killed and captured more than 700 Xiongnu people. Gongsun He led his troops out of Yunzhong County, but gained nothing. Gongsun Ao led his troops out of Daijun and was defeated by the Xiongnu, losing more than 7,000 people. Li Guang led his troops out of Yanmen County and was defeated by the Huns. The Huns captured Li Guang alive. Later, Li Guang was able to escape and return to the Han Dynasty. The Han Dynasty imprisoned Gongsun Ao and Li Guang. Gongsun Ao and Li Guang paid a ransom and became common people. This winter, the Xiongnu repeatedly broke into the border and plundered, and Yuyang suffered particularly badly. The Han Dynasty sent General Han Anguo to garrison Yuyang to defend against the Xiongnu. In the autumn of the next year, 20,000 Xiongnu cavalry invaded the Han Dynasty, killed the prefect of Liaoxi and took away more than 2,000 people. The Huns invaded Yuyang again, defeated more than a thousand troops of the Yuyang prefect, and besieged Han Anguo, the general of the Han Dynasty. At this time, Han Anguo's more than a thousand cavalry were about to be wiped out. King Yan's reinforcements happened to arrive, and the Huns left. The Xiongnu invaded Yanmen County again, killing and taking away more than a thousand people. So the Han Dynasty sent General Wei Qing to lead 30,000 cavalry out of Yanmen. Li Xi led his troops to force out of Dai County and attacked the Huns, killing and capturing thousands of them. The next year, Wei Qing went out to the west of Yunzhong County and the Longxi area in the west, and attacked Loufan and Aries Wang under the Xiongnu on the south bank of the Yellow River Hetao. He killed and captured thousands of people and obtained more than one million cattle and sheep. So the Han Dynasty captured the area on the south bank of the Yellow River Hetao, built Shuofang City, and repaired the pass built by Meng Tian of the Qin Dynasty in the past, relying on the Yellow River as a solid defense line. The Han Dynasty also gave up the twists and turns of Shanggu County and remote counties such as Zaoyang to the Xiongnu.
target: Despite these victories, the Xiongnu remained resilient. After Huo Qubing's death, the Han halted major campaigns, and the Xiongnu, under Chanyu Uwei and his successors, continued to raid and negotiate. The Han attempted to sow discord among Xiongnu leaders and used diplomacy with western states like Wusun to isolate them. However, internal strife and harsh winters weakened the Xiongnu. Later Chanyu, such as Er Chanyu and Huyan, faced rebellions and military defeats, including the capture of Han general Li Ling and the defection of Li Guangli. The Han built fortifications and expanded into the Hexi Corridor, but the Xiongnu persisted in their raids, leading to a prolonged stalemate.

id: 史记/七十列传/匈奴列传::group-005
article_path: 史记/七十列传/匈奴列传
source: Mao Dun said: How can we be stingy of a horse even though we are neighboring countries? So he gave the Chollima to Dong Hu. After a while, Dong Hu thought that Mao Dun was afraid of him, so he sent an envoy to Mao Dun to tell him that he wanted one of Shan Yu's clans. Mao Dun asked the ministers on the left and right again, and they all got angry and said: Donghu is unreasonable. He actually wants the Yan family. Please send troops to attack him. Mao Dun said: How can you be the leader of a country with someone else but begrudge a woman? So he gave his beloved Yan family to Donghu. King Donghu became more and more proud and invaded and invaded westward. There is an open space between the Donghu and the Xiongnu, which is more than a thousand miles away. No one lives in it. Both sides have built outposts on both sides of the open space. Donghu sent an envoy to Modu and said: You Xiongnu cannot go to the open space outside the border post between the Xiongnu and us. We want to occupy it. Mao Dun asked the officials for their opinions. Some of them said: This is an abandoned vacant land. You can give it to them or not. So Modu was furious and said: Land is the foundation of the country, how can we give it to them! Those who said they would give Donghu free space were killed. Maodun mounted his horse and ordered anyone in the country who retreated to be beheaded, so he headed east to attack Donghu. Donghu initially despised the Xiongnu and therefore did not take precautions. When Mao Dun arrived with his troops, he defeated Donghu as soon as the war started, wiped out the king of Donghu, captured the people of Donghu and plundered their livestock and property. After the Huns returned from Maodun, they defeated the Yuezhi in the west and annexed Loufan and the Aries Henan King in the south. And completely recovered the land that Meng Tian of the Qin faction had taken from the Huns, and the original Henan fortress was the boundary with the Han Dynasty, as far as Chao and Fushi, and then invaded Yan and Dai. At this time, the Han army was fighting against Xiang Yu's troops. The Central Plains area was exhausted by the war, so Maodun was able to become strong on his own, with an army of more than 300,000 people who could draw bows and shoot arrows. It was more than a thousand years from Chunwei to Touman. The power of the Xiongnu grew and fell, and they often dispersed and differentiated. Because of the long time, their lineages cannot be arranged in sequence. But when Maodun was the Chanyu, the Huns were the most powerful, making the northern barbarians completely submit to their rule and becoming an enemy of China in the south. After that, their lineage and national official titles could be recorded. The Huns set up official positions such as the left and right virtuous kings, the left and right kings of Guli, the left and right generals, the left and right captains, the left and right Danghu, and the left and right Guduhou. The Huns called virtuous people "Tu Qi", so they often made the prince the king of Zuo Tu Qi.
target: The historian Sima Qian notes that the Xiongnu's nomadic lifestyle and martial culture made them formidable adversaries. He criticizes Han officials for short-sighted policies and emphasizes the importance of selecting capable generals, as even wise rulers like Yao needed talented ministers to achieve success. The Xiongnu's lineage, from Chunwei to Modun, spanned over a thousand years, with their power fluctuating until Modun unified them. Their social structure, with hereditary titles and a focus on warfare, allowed them to dominate the northern steppes and challenge Chinese authority for centuries.

id: 史记/七十列传/司马相如列传::group-000
article_path: 史记/七十列传/司马相如列传
source: Sima Xiangru was born in Chengdu, Shu County, and his courtesy name was Changqing. When he was a boy, he liked to read and learn swordsmanship, so his parents named him Quanzi. After Sima Xiangru completed his studies, he admired Lin Xiangru's character and changed his name to Xiangru. Initially, due to his family's wealth, he was awarded the position of Langguan, guarded Emperor Xiao Jing, and became a regular servant of martial arts, but this was not his hobby. It happened that Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty did not like Ci Fu. At this time, King Liang Xiao came to the capital to see Emperor Jing. He was accompanied by people who were good at lobbying, including Zou Yang from Qijun, Meicheng from Huaiyin, and Mr. Zhuang Ji from Wuxian. Xiangru fell in love with these people when he saw them, so he resigned from his official position on the pretext of illness and lived in Liang State. King Liang Xiao asked Xiangru and other scholars to live together. Xiangru had the opportunity to get along with scholars and lobbyists for several years, so he wrote "Zixu Fu". Just when King Liang Xiao died, Xiangru had to return to Chengdu. However, his family was poor and he had no occupation that could support his life. Xiangru always got along well with Wang Ji, the magistrate of Linqiong County. Wang Ji said: Chang Qing, you have been away from home for a long time and are seeking an official position. It is not satisfactory. You can come to see me. So Xiangru went to Linqiong and lived in the capital pavilion in the city. The Linqiong County Magistrate pretended to be respectful and visited Xiangru every day. At first, Xiangru still met each other with courtesy. Later, he lied about being ill and asked his entourage to refuse Wang Ji's visit. However, Wang Ji was more cautious and respectful. There are many rich people in Linqiong County. For example, the Sun family of King Zhuo has 800 slaves, and the Cheng Zheng family has hundreds of people. The two discussed with each other and said: The county magistrate has a distinguished guest, and we are going to prepare a banquet for him. The county magistrate was also invited. When the county magistrate arrived at the Zhuo family, there were already hundreds of guests in the Zhuo family. At noon, I went to invite Sima Changqing, but he refused to come, saying that he was ill. Linqiong ordered to see Xiangru not come and did not dare to eat. He went to greet Xiangru himself. Xiangru had no choice but to come to Zhuo's house. All the guests were amazed and envious of his charisma. When the wine was in full swing, the Linqiong County Magistrate stepped forward, placed the harp in front of Xiangru, and said, "I heard that Chang Qing likes to play the harp very much, and I hope to listen to a piece of music to cheer you up." After thanking Xiangru, he played one or two pieces of music. At this time, Zhuo Wangsun had a daughter named Wenjun, who was newly widowed and loved music. So Xiangru pretended to respect each other with the county magistrate, and secretly aroused her love with the sound of the piano. When Xiangru came to Qiong, he was followed by carriages and horses. He was dignified in appearance, quiet and elegant, and very generous. When Zhuo Wang and Sun's family were drinking and playing piano music, Zhuo Wenjun secretly looked at him through the crack in the door. He was very happy and liked him very much, but he was afraid that he would not understand his feelings. After the banquet, Xiangru asked someone to reward Wenjun's waiter with a large sum of money to convey his admiration to her. So Zhuo Wenjun ran away from home at night and eloped with Xiangru. Xiangru and Wenjun hurried back to Chengdu. When I entered the house, I saw nothing but four walls.
target: Sima Xiangru, courtesy name Changqing, was born in Chengdu, Shu County. As a youth, he studied literature and swordsmanship, and later admired Lin Xiangru, changing his name accordingly. He initially served as a Langguan under Emperor Jing of Han due to family wealth, but disliked his post. When Emperor Jing showed little interest in rhapsodies (Ci Fu), Xiangru befriended scholars like Zou Yang and Mei Cheng during a visit from King Xiao of Liang. He resigned on pretence of illness and lived in Liang, where he wrote "Zixu Fu." After King Xiao's death, Xiangru returned to Chengdu impoverished. Xiangru's friend Wang Ji, magistrate of Linqiong, invited him to stay. Wang Ji feigned deference, but Xiangru eventually refused visits, feigning illness. Wealthy locals, including Zhuo Wangsun and Cheng Zheng, hosted a banquet for the magistrate. Xiangru initially declined but attended after the magistrate personally invited him. During the feast, Xiangru played the zither, captivating Zhuo Wangsun's newly widowed daughter, Wenjun, who secretly admired him. After the banquet, Xiangru bribed her attendants to convey his feelings, and Wenjun eloped with him to Chengdu, where they lived in poverty with only four walls.

id: 史记/七十列传/司马相如列传::group-001
article_path: 史记/七十列传/司马相如列传
source: So Zhuo Wenjun ran away from home at night and eloped with Xiangru. Xiangru and Wenjun hurried back to Chengdu. When I entered the house, I saw nothing but four walls. When Zhuo Wangsun learned about his daughter's elopement, he was furious and said: "My daughter is extremely unqualified. I can't bear to hurt her, but I won't give her a cent either." Some people tried to persuade Zhuo Wangsun, but he still refused to listen. After a long time, Wenjun felt unhappy and said: "Chang Qing, as long as you go to Linqiong with me, you can make a living by borrowing money from your brothers. Why have you made yourself so miserable?" Xiangru came to Linqiong with Wenjun, sold all his carriages and horses, and bought a hotel to sell wine. He also asked Wenjun to personally take charge of the wine shop business in Longqian, while he put on his calf-nosed trousers and worked with the employees, washing wine vessels in the busy city. When Zhuo Wangsun heard about this, he felt so ashamed that he stayed behind closed doors. Some brothers and elders talked to Zhuo Wangsun and said, "You have a son and two daughters. What the family lacks is not money." Now, Wenjun has become the wife of Sima Changqing. Changqing was tired of running away from home. Although he was poor, he was indeed a talent and could be completely relied on. Besides, he is a distinguished guest of the county magistrate, why do you despise him like this! Zhuo Wangsun had no choice but to give Wenjun 100 slaves, 1 million in money, clothes, bedding and various belongings when she got married.
target: Zhuo Wangsun was furious and refused to support them. Wenjun suggested they return to Linqiong, where they sold their possessions and opened a tavern. Wenjun managed the shop while Xiangru worked publicly in menial tasks. Ashamed, Zhuo Wangsun, persuaded by relatives, eventually gave them 100 slaves, money, and belongings, enabling them to become wealthy.

id: 史记/七十列传/司马相如列传::group-002
article_path: 史记/七十列传/司马相如列传
source: Now, Wenjun has become the wife of Sima Changqing. Changqing was tired of running away from home. Although he was poor, he was indeed a talent and could be completely relied on. Besides, he is a distinguished guest of the county magistrate, why do you despise him like this! Zhuo Wangsun had no choice but to give Wenjun 100 slaves, 1 million in money, clothes, bedding and various belongings when she got married. Wenjun returned to Chengdu with Xiangru, bought land and houses, and became a wealthy family. After a long period of time, Yang Deyi, a native of Shu County, served as a dog supervisor to serve the emperor. One day, Emperor Wu read "Zixu Fu" and thought it was well written. He said: "I cannot be at the same time as this author." Yang Deyi said: My fellow countryman Sima Xiangru claimed that he wrote this poem. Emperor Wu was very surprised and summoned Xiangru to ask. Xiangru said: There is such a thing. However, this Fu only describes the affairs of the princes and is not worth reading. Please ask me to write a poem about the emperor's hunting trip. After the poem is completed, I will present it to the emperor.
target: Later, Emperor Wu of Han read "Zixu Fu" and admired it. Yang Deyi informed him that Xiangru was the author. Summoned, Xiangru offered to write a grander rhapsody about the emperor's hunting grounds. He composed "Shanglin Fu," using fictitious characters—Zixu (Chu), Mr. Wuyou (Qi), and Wu Shigong (the emperor's perspective)—to contrast princely extravagance with imperial virtue.

id: 史记/七十列传/司马相如列传::group-003
article_path: 史记/七十列传/司马相如列传
source: However, the King of Qi was in the position of a prince and did not dare to talk about the joy of hunting and playing, and the vastness of the garden. Your husband is a guest who is being treated as a distinguished guest, so the King of Qi did not answer you with any words. How can you say that he is speechless? Wu Shigong smiled and said: Chu State is wrong, Qi State may not be right either. The reason why the emperor asked the princes to pay tribute was not for the sake of wealth, but to allow them to go to the court to state their performance of duties; therefore, the boundaries of the feudal state were divided not to guard the borders, but to prevent the princes from violating laws and regulations.
target: The rhapsody described vast landscapes, hunting scenes, and concluded with a call for frugality and benevolence. The emperor was delighted and appointed Xiangru as Langguan.

id: 史记/七十列传/司马相如列传::group-004
article_path: 史记/七十列传/司马相如列传
source: Xiangru served as Langguan for several years. At that time, Tang Meng was ordered to plunder and open up Yelang and Bozhong to the west. He recruited thousands of officials and soldiers from Ba and Shu counties, and more than 10,000 land and water transportation personnel from Xijun. He also used wartime laws to kill the commander, and the people of Ba and Shu were shocked and frightened. When the emperor heard about this situation, he sent Xiangru to blame Tang Meng and took the opportunity to tell the people of Ba and Shu that what Tang Meng did was not the emperor's original intention. The message said: Announcement to the governors of Ba and Shu: The barbarians have taken military power for themselves, disobeyed the imperial court, and have not been attacking for a long time. They often invade the borders and cause hardships to the scholar-bureaucrats.
target: Xiangru served as an envoy to blame Tang Meng for harsh policies in Ba and Shu, issuing an imperial proclamation reassuring the people. He later advocated for reopening southwestern territories, becoming Zhonglang General to pacify the region. Despite opposition, he succeeded, and the emperor was pleased.

id: 史记/七十列传/司马相如列传::group-005
article_path: 史记/七十列传/司马相如列传
source: Although the people are a little lazy, please allow us to set an example for them. The doctors were melancholy, retreated voluntarily, delayed for a while, and said goodbye. From then on, someone wrote a letter to accuse Xiangru of accepting bribes from others when he was on an envoy, and as a result, he lost his official position. He stayed at home for more than a year, and was called to the court as a Langguan. Xiangru stutters, but is good at writing articles.
target: However, accusations of bribery led to his dismissal, though he was later reinstated as Langguan. Xiangru suffered from diabetes and avoided court debates. He advised the emperor against dangerous hunting, writing a remonstrance. He also composed "Ode to the Immortals" and "Adult Fu," depicting celestial journeys.

id: 史记/七十列传/司马相如列传::group-006
article_path: 史记/七十列传/司马相如列传
source: After he married Zhuo Wenjun, he became very rich. When he held an official position, he was not willing to discuss national affairs with the ministers. Instead, he took advantage of his illness to stay at home and did not pursue the official title. He once followed the emperor to Changyang Palace for hunting. At this time, the emperor liked to personally kill bears and pigs, and chase wild beasts on horseback. Xiangru wrote a booklet to advise him. The booklet wrote: The ministers heard that although all living things are of the same kind, they have different abilities.
target: His final work, a treatise on the Feng and Shan sacrifices, urged the emperor to perform these rites. The emperor later conducted them after Xiangru's death.

id: 史记/七十列传/司马相如列传::group-007
article_path: 史记/七十列传/司马相如列传
source: The flexing and stretching yellow dragon ascends to heaven because of encountering holy virtues. The colors sparkle and shine. The appearance of the dragon body will surely awaken the people. It is recorded in the "Book of Changes·Tuan Zhuan" that this is the so-called chariot that the emperor was appointed to ride on. Tian Fu Rui has made it clear that there is no need to warn him again. It should be entrusted accordingly and tell the king to hold a Zen ceremony. Looking through the classics, we can see that there is a relationship between nature and human society, and the two inspire each other and are harmonious. The virtue of a wise king is to act conscientiously and cautiously. Therefore, we must consider decline when we are prosperous, and be aware of danger when we are peaceful and happy. Therefore, although King Tang of Shang and King Wu of Zhou were in the highest position, they still maintained the virtue of seriousness and respect. During the ceremony, Yu Shun still observed and reflected on his shortcomings and mistakes. That's the truth. Sima Xiangru had been dead for five years before the emperor began to worship the earth god. Eight years after his death, the emperor finally offered sacrifices to Zhongyue Mountain first, then to Mount Tai, and then to Liangfu Mountain and Zen Suran Mountain. Xiangru's other works, such as "The Book of the Marquis of Pingling", "The Dilemma with the Five Young Masters", and "The Book of Caomu" are not included, but his works that are particularly famous among public ministers are included. Tai Shigong said: "Spring and Autumn" can delve into the most subtle aspects of things, "Book of Changes" is originally subtle but can be explained in a simple way, "Daya" talks about the virtues of princes and the common people, "Xiaoya" ridicules the gains and losses of humble authors, but its rumors can affect court politics. Therefore, although the external manifestations of words are different, their gentle and enlightening effect is the same. Although the similar articles contain many false words and exaggerated statements, their main theme is frugality. How is this different from the satirical remonstrance in the Book of Songs? Yang Xiong believes that among Xiangru's gorgeous poems, there is a one hundred to one relationship between words that encourage luxury and words that advocate frugality. This is like playing the sounds of Zheng and Wei to your heart's content, but playing a little elegant music at the end of the piece.
target: Sima Qian noted that Xiangru's works, though ornate, promoted frugality, akin to the "Book of Songs." Yang Xiong criticized their imbalance between luxury and admonition, but Sima Qian defended their value.

id: 史记/七十列传/吴王濞列传::group-000
article_path: 史记/七十列传/吴王濞列传
source: King Wu Liu Bi was the son of Liu Zhong, the brother of Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty. Seven years after Emperor Gaozu pacified the world, he named Liu Zhong the acting king. Later, when the Xiongnu attacked Dai, Liu Zhong could not hold on, so he abandoned the country and fled. He took a small road to Luoyang and surrendered to the emperor. Because the emperor was a brother of flesh and blood, he could not bear to be punished according to law, so he only deposed the king and demoted him to be the Marquis of Heyang. In the autumn of the eleventh year of Emperor Gaozu, King Yingbu of Zhunnan rebelled, annexed the Jing territory to the east, hijacked the troops of the local princes, crossed the Huai River to the west, and attacked Chu State. Emperor Gaozu personally led the army to punish him. Liu Zhong's son, Peihou Liu Bi, was twenty years old and strong. As a cavalry commander, he followed Gaozu and defeated Yingbu's army at Huizhen in the west of Qixian County. Yingbu fled. King Liu Jia of Jing was killed by Yingbu and had no heirs. The emperor was worried that the people in Wu and Kuaiji were frivolous and aggressive, and there was no brave king to restrain them. His sons were young, so he made Liu Bi the king of Wu in Pei, with jurisdiction over three counties and fifty-three counties. After he had received his official seal, Emperor Gaozu asked Liu Bi to come and see him. After seeing him, he said: "You have a rebellious appearance." At the same time, he felt regret in his heart, but he had already appointed him, so he patted him on the back and warned him: "There will be a rebellion in the southeast in the fifty years after the founding of the Han Dynasty. Is it you?" However, everyone with the same surname is one family, so you must not rebel!
target: King Wu Liu Bi was the son of Liu Zhong, brother of Emperor Gaozu of Han. After Gaozu pacified the realm, he named Liu Zhong acting king, but Liu Zhong abandoned his post during a Xiongnu attack and was demoted to marquis. In the eleventh year of Gaozu, Yingbu rebelled, and Liu Bi, then twenty, served as a cavalry commander, helping defeat Yingbu. Gaozu, concerned about the unruly people of Wu and Kuaiji and lacking mature sons, appointed Liu Bi King of Wu over three counties. However, Gaozu noted Liu Bi's rebellious appearance and warned him against rebellion, which Liu Bi denied.

id: 史记/七十列传/吴王濞列传::group-001
article_path: 史记/七十列传/吴王濞列传
source: At the same time, he felt regret in his heart, but he had already appointed him, so he patted him on the back and warned him: "There will be a rebellion in the southeast in the fifty years after the founding of the Han Dynasty. Is it you?" However, everyone with the same surname is one family, so you must not rebel! Liu Bi kowtowed and said, "I don't dare." By the time of Emperor Xiaohui and Queen Gao, the world had just stabilized, and the princes of some counties were working hard to appease their own people. Wu State owned the copper mines in Yuzhang County, so Liu Bi recruited desperadoes from all over the world to mint money privately and boil seawater to make salt. Because of this, the state did not levy taxes and the state expenses were very abundant. During the reign of Emperor Xiaowen, the Crown Prince of Wu came to Beijing for an audience and was able to accompany the Crown Prince to drink and play chess. Prince Wu's teachers were both from Chu. They were frivolous, strong, and arrogant. When they were playing chess with the crown prince, they had an argument over the chess game and their attitude was disrespectful. The crown prince picked up the chessboard and threw the chessboard at Prince Wu, killing him. Afterwards, his body was sent back to Wu for burial. When they arrived at the state of Wu, King Wu said angrily: If a family with the same surname in the world died in Chang'an, they should be buried in Chang'an. Why should they be sent to the state of Wu for burial? The body was then sent to Chang'an for burial. From then on, the King of Wu gradually disobeyed the etiquette that his vassals should abide by, claiming to be ill and refusing to enter the court. The people in the capital knew that he claimed to be ill and refused to enter the court because his son had died. After questioning, he was indeed not ill. After that, when the envoys of the King of Wu came, they detained him, questioned him, and punished him. The King of Wu was frightened and even more actively planned rebellion. Later, the King of Wu sent someone to Beijing for the autumn invitation, and the emperor questioned the envoy again. The envoy told the emperor: The King of Wu is indeed not sick. The imperial court detained and punished several envoys, so he claimed that he was ill and could not come back. And there is such a thing: it is unlucky to see fish in a deep pool. Now the King of Wu began to pretend to be sick. When the court noticed and was severely questioned, he became more and more eager to conceal his behavior for fear that the emperor would kill him. The plan of claiming to be sick was out of helplessness. It is hoped that the emperor will put aside his past grudges and give King Wu a chance to start over. So the emperor pardoned Wu's envoys and allowed them to go back. He also gave King Wu a few swords and a staff, thinking that he was old and could not go to the capital to see him. The king of Wu was able to absolve him of his sins, and the rebellion was relaxed. However, the feudal state where he was located had no income from copper salt, so the people did not pay taxes. Soldiers are paid in lieu of service and the price is fair. At a certain time every year, they visit talented people and give rewards to common people. The king of Wu took in fugitives who were wanted by law officials from other counties and did not hand them over. After doing this for more than forty years, the king of Wu was able to control and utilize his people.
target: During Emperor Xiaohui and Queen Gao's reigns, Wu prospered by minting coins from copper mines and making salt from seawater, avoiding taxes and attracting desperadoes. Under Emperor Xiaowen, a chess dispute led to the Crown Prince of Wu's death at the hands of the Han crown prince. The King of Wu, angered, buried his son in Chang'an and began feigning illness to avoid court, gradually disobeying etiquette. The court detained Wu envoys, prompting the King of Wu to plan rebellion. Emperor Xiaowen later pardoned Wu's envoys and granted the king leniency, easing tensions. However, Wu continued to harbor fugitives and control its people for over forty years.

id: 史记/七十列传/吴王濞列传::group-002
article_path: 史记/七十列传/吴王濞列传
source: Although the emperor is now threatening and urgent, I am already guilty of capital punishment. How can I not support him? Ying Gao said: Chao Cuo, the imperial censor, deceived the emperor, invaded the princes, and blocked the loyal and virtuous people. All the ministers in the court felt hatred and resentment, and the princes all had the intention of betrayal. He has done his best to serve the people. Now comets appear and locust plagues continue to occur. This is the only opportunity that comes once in a lifetime, and the time of sorrow and labor is the era when saints are born. Therefore, the king of Wu wanted to use the crusade against Chao Cuo as an excuse at home, and follow the king's chariot outside, galloping around the world, making the places he faced surrender, and conquering the places pointed by his fingers. No one in the world dared to disobey. If your Majesty can promise me a word, then the King of Wu will lead the King of Chu to capture Hangu Pass, guard the grain of Aocang in Xingyang, and resist the Han soldiers. Build a house for the army to be stationed and wait for the arrival of the king. If the king really comes, then the world can be annexed. Isn't it also possible for two monarchs to divide and rule the world? King Jiaoxi said: OK. Ying Gao went back to report to the King of Wu. The King of Wu was still worried that the King of Jiaoxi would not participate in the rebellion, so he personally acted as an envoy to Jiaoxi and made an alliance with the King of Jiaoxi in person. Some of the officials in Jiaoxi learned about King Jiaoxi's rebellion plan and advised him: "Serving an emperor is the happiest thing." Now the king and the king of Wu are marching westward. If things succeed, the two masters will definitely have differences and disputes, and disaster will start from here. The land of the princes is less than two-tenths of the imperial counties, and betraying the imperial court will also worry the Queen Mother. This is not a long-term solution. King Jiaoxi refused to listen. So he sent envoys to join forces with the King of Qi, the King of Sichuan, the King of Jiaodong, the King of Jinan, and the King of Jibei. They all agreed and said: For the sake of justice, King Chengyang Jing will attack those surnamed Lu. Don't let him participate in the army. After the incident is completed, just give him some land. The princes were shocked and frightened by the recent punishment of reducing their land, and most of them resented Chao Cuo. When the documents to reduce the Wu Guoji and Yuzhang counties were sent to the state of Wu, the king of Wu first launched an army to rebel. On Bingwu of the first month, the king of Jiaoxi killed the officials sent by the court with less than 2,000 shi, as did the kings of Jiaodong, Sichuan, Jinan, Chu, and Zhao, so they marched westward. King Qi later regretted it and committed suicide by taking poison, violating the covenant. The King of Jibei's city wall was damaged and had not been repaired, so his lieutenant ordered him to be kidnapped and guarded so that he could not send troops. The King of Jiaoxi was the leader, and together with the King of Jiaodong, the King of Sichuan and the King of Jinan, they led troops to besiege Linyi. King Liu Sui of Zhao also rebelled and secretly sent envoys to the Xiongnu to discuss joint operations. When the Seven Kingdoms launched a rebellion, the King of Wu conscripted all his soldiers and ordered the whole country: I am sixty-two years old and personally command the army.
target: Chao Cuo, favored by Emperor Jing, repeatedly urged reducing Wu's territory, arguing that rebellion was inevitable. In the third year of Emperor Jing's reign, Chao Cuo reduced the lands of Chu, Zhao, Jiaoxi, and Wu. King Wu Liu Bi, fearing further losses, plotted rebellion. He sent Ying Gao to recruit King Jiaoxi, citing Chao Cuo's tyranny and promising joint action. King Jiaoxi agreed, and alliances formed with Qi, Sichuan, Jiaodong, Jinan, and Jibei. The Seven Kingdoms rebelled, with Wu conscripting over 200,000 men and gaining support from Dongyue. King Wu issued a letter to the princes, denouncing Chao Cuo and calling for a punitive campaign, offering rewards for capturing Han officials.

id: 史记/七十列传/吴王濞列传::group-003
article_path: 史记/七十列传/吴王濞列传
source: After the emperor was notified of the rebellion of the seven kingdoms, the emperor sent Taiwei Tiaohou Zhou Yafu to lead thirty-six generals to attack Wu and Chu; he sent Qu Zhouhou Liji to attack Zhao; general Luan Bu attacked Qi; General Dou Ying was stationed in Xingyang to monitor the armies of Qi and Zhao. When Wu Chu and other rebellious letters were heard, the Han Dynasty's army had not yet set off, and Dou Ying had not yet set out to praise Yuan An, the prime minister of the former King of Wu, to the emperor. Yuan Ang was relaxing at home at the time, and the emperor summoned him to see him. The emperor was planning the army and rations with Chao Cuo. The emperor asked Yuan Ang: "You once served as the prime minister of the King of Wu. Do you know the character of Wu's minister Tian Lubo?" Now that Wu Chu is rebelling, what do you think? Yuan Ang replied: It's not worth worrying about, we can defeat them immediately. The emperor said: The king of Wu relied on copper mines to mint coins, boil seawater to make salt, seduce the world's heroes, and raised his troops to rebel when his hair was gray. How could he launch a rebellion without a comprehensive plan? Why do you say he can't make a difference? Yuan Ang replied: It is true that the copper mines in Wu State are beneficial to boiling salt. Where can I get heroes and seduce them? If King Wu can really get heroes, he should help King Wu do what is reasonable, and he will not rebel. Those whom the King of Wu seduced were all scoundrels, treacherous men who fled to make money, so they seduced each other and rebelled. Chao Cuo said: Yuan An’s analysis is correct. The emperor asked: How can we come up with good countermeasures? Yuan An said: I hope to reject the people on the left and right. The emperor asked everyone around him to retreat, but Chao Cuo remained. Yuan An said: Even a minister cannot know what I say. So he dismissed Chao Cuo again. Chao Cuo hurried to the east chamber to escape, and was very angry about this. The emperor finally asked Yuan An again, and Yuan An replied: The letters exchanged between Wu and Chu said that the emperor Gaozu appointed the Liu family's children as kings and had their own enfeoffed lands. Now the traitor Chao Cuo has demoted and punished the princes without authorization, and deprived the princes of their land. In the name of rebellion, they jointly attacked to the west and jointly punished Chao Cuo. They would stop fighting when the original fiefdom was restored. The current strategy is to kill Chao Cuo, send envoys to pardon the sins of the seven kingdoms of Wu and Chu, and restore the original reduced fiefdoms. Then the war can be over without blood staining the weapons.
target: Emperor Jing responded by sending Zhou Yafu to attack Wu and Chu, and other generals against Qi and Zhao. Yuan An advised killing Chao Cuo to appease the rebels, and Chao Cuo was executed. Yuan An then attempted to negotiate with Wu, but King Wu refused, declaring himself the Eastern Emperor. Zhou Yafu, following a strategy to avoid direct confrontation, cut off Wu's food supplies. Wu's army, led by King Wu, failed to adopt effective strategies, such as a surprise attack on Wuguan or a swift march to Luoyang. After a prolonged siege of Liang, Wu's forces starved and scattered. King Wu fled to Dongyue but was assassinated by Dongyue forces bribed by Han. Other rebel kings, including those of Jiaoxi, Jiaodong, Sichuan, Jinan, and Zhao, were defeated or committed suicide, and their states were abolished. The rebellion lasted from January to March, with Zhao falling later. Emperor Jing reinstated some royal lines and granted Wu's territory to others.

id: 史记/七十列传/吴王濞列传::group-004
article_path: 史记/七十列传/吴王濞列传
source: Just committed suicide. The Queen Mother and the Prince also died. King Jiaodong, King Sichuan, and King Jinan also died successively, and the feudal state was abolished and returned to the Han Dynasty. General Li besieged the capital of Zhao for ten months before conquering it, and King Zhao committed suicide. Because the King of Jibei was kidnapped, he was not executed and was moved to the title of King of Sichuan. At the beginning, Wu King Liu Bi took the lead in the rebellion and led the Chu and Wu armies together, uniting the armies of Qi and Zhao. In the first month of the year, the army started a rebellion, and in March the whole army was defeated. Only Zhao State was finally conquered. Emperor Jing also named Pingluhou Liu Li, the youngest son of King Chu Yuan, as King of Chu, as the successor of King Chu Yuan. Liu Fei, the king of Runan who moved to Wu, took over the original fiefdom of Wu and became the king of Jiangdu. Tai Shigong said: King Wu Liu Bi was granted the title of King of Wu because his father was demoted. The King of Wu was able to exempt taxes and support the people because he had the convenience of copper mines and sea salt. The idea of ​​​​rebellion came from the death of his son. He got into trouble because of a chess dispute, and eventually his country was destroyed and he died; he got close to the foreign Yue people and murdered his fellow clan, and finally he died. Chao Cuo made great plans for the country, but disaster befell him instead. Yuan An was good at contingency lobbying. He was favored at first, but suffered humiliation in the end.
target: The historian concludes that Liu Bi's rebellion stemmed from his son's death and greed, while Chao Cuo's plans led to his own death, and Yuan Ang's strategies brought initial favor but eventual disgrace.

id: 史记/七十列传/商君列传::group-000
article_path: 史记/七十列传/商君列传
source: Lord Shang was the son of the concubine Ji of the Kingdom of Wei. His name is Yang Yang and his surname is Gongsun. His ancestor’s original surname was Ji. When he was young, Gongsun Yang was interested in the study of criminal names and magic. He served his uncle, the Prime Minister of Wei State, and served as the middle concubine. The uncle knew that he was a virtuous man, but he had not yet had time to recommend him to the king of Wei. Just when the uncle was sick, King Wei Hui went to visit him personally and said, "What will happen to the country if something unexpected happens to your illness?" The uncle replied: My bastard son Gongsun Yang is young, but he is talented. I hope that the king can hand over all the affairs of the country to him and let him govern. King Wei Hui was silent after hearing this. When King Hui of Wei was about to leave, the uncle withdrew his entourage and said: If the king does not use Gongsun Yang, he must be killed and not allowed to leave the country. King Wei agreed to his request and left. The uncle summoned Gongsun Yang and apologized: Just now, the king asked about people who could serve as prime minister, and I recommended you. Judging from the look on his face, the king will not agree with my suggestion. I must first be loyal to the king and then consider the position of the minister, so I advise the king that if Gongsun Martingale is not appointed, he should be killed. The king agreed to my request. You should leave quickly, otherwise you will be captured soon. Gongsun Yang said: Since the king cannot listen to you and appoint me, how can he listen to you and kill me? In the end, he did not leave Wei State. After King Hui left, he said to his attendants: "The uncle's illness is very serious, which is really sad. He wants me to hand over all the affairs of the country to Gongsun Yang, and after that, he persuades me to kill him. Isn't this very confusing?" Shortly after Gongshu Zuo's death, Gongsun Yang heard that Duke Xiao of Qin ordered to search for talented people throughout the country in order to restore the hegemony of Duke Mu of Qin and regain the lost territory in the east. He went west to enter the Qin State and relied on Duke Xiao's favored minister Jing Jian to seek an audience with Duke Xiao. Duke Xiao summoned Wei Yang and asked him to talk about state affairs for a long time. Duke Xiao fell asleep while listening and couldn't listen at all. Afterwards, Duke Xiao was angry with Jingjian and said: "Your guest is a bully. How can you appoint such a person?" Jing Jian again used Xiao Gong's words to blame Wei Yang. Wei Yang said: I used the methods of Yao and Shun to persuade the king, but his mind could not understand. A few days later, Jing Jian asked Duke Xiao to summon Wei Yang. When Wei Yang met with Duke Xiao, he explained the way of governing the country incisively and vividly, but it was not in line with Duke Xiao's wishes.
target: Lord Shang, originally named Gongsun Yang, was the son of a concubine of the Kingdom of Wei. As a youth, he studied criminal law and magic, serving under his uncle, the Prime Minister of Wei. When his uncle fell ill, King Wei Hui visited and asked about a successor. The uncle recommended Gongsun Yang, but the king remained silent. The uncle then privately advised the king to kill Gongsun Yang if he was not appointed, to prevent him from leaving the country. However, Gongsun Yang refused to flee, reasoning that the king would not heed advice to kill him if he ignored advice to appoint him. After his uncle's death, Gongsun Yang heard that Duke Xiao of Qin sought talented individuals to restore Qin's former glory. He entered Qin through the recommendation of Duke Xiao's favored minister, Jing Jian. Initially, Duke Xiao was unimpressed, falling asleep during discussions of ancient imperial methods. After several attempts, Gongsun Yang shifted to strategies for enriching the state and strengthening the army, which pleased Duke Xiao. Despite concerns about public opinion, Gongsun Yang convinced Duke Xiao to enact legal reforms, arguing that extraordinary actions often face criticism but are necessary for success. He was appointed as Zuo Shu Chang and implemented a new legal code, organizing households into mutual surveillance groups, rewarding military merit, punishing private disputes, and promoting agriculture.

id: 史记/七十列传/商君列传::group-001
article_path: 史记/七十列传/商君列传
source: Those who have military merit are distinguished and glorious, but those who do not have military merit cannot show glory even if they are very rich. The new law was ready but had not yet been announced. Worried that the people would not believe it, Wei Yang erected a three-foot-long log at the south gate of the market behind the capital, and recruited people who could move the log to the north gate and rewarded them with ten gold coins. The people thought this was strange and no one dared to touch it. He also announced that anyone who could move the wood to the north gate would be rewarded fifty gold. A man moved it away and immediately gave him fifty gold to show that he would do what he ordered and would never cheat. New laws were enacted afterwards. The new law was implemented among the people for a whole year. Thousands of people from Qin State came to the country and said that the new law was not suitable. At this time, the prince violated the new law. Wei Yang said: The new law cannot be implemented smoothly because the people at the top violate it. The prince will be punished according to the new law. The prince was the heir to the monarch and could not impose punishment, so he punished Gongzi Qian, the teacher who supervised his behavior, and Gongsun Jia, the teacher who imparted knowledge to him, with ink punishment. The next day, all the people of Qin implemented the new law. Ten years after the new law was implemented, the people of Qin were very happy. No one picked up other people's lost things on the road, there were no thieves in the mountains and forests, and every family was rich and sufficient.
target: To build trust, he erected a log at the market and rewarded a man who moved it, demonstrating his commitment to the law. The new law faced opposition, including from the crown prince. Gongsun Yang punished the prince's tutors, Qian and Gongsun Jia, with facial tattooing, after which the law was widely accepted. Over ten years, Qin prospered: lost items were not stolen, families became wealthy, and the people were courageous in public duty but avoided private conflicts. Gongsun Yang was promoted to Da Liang Zao and led campaigns against Wei, capturing Anyi.

id: 史记/七十列传/商君列传::group-002
article_path: 史记/七十列传/商君列传
source: After that, no one among the people dared to discuss the new law. So Wei Yang was appointed as Daliang Zao. He led the army to besiege Anyi of Wei State and forced them to surrender. Three years later, the Qin State built a palace city in Xianyang and moved the capital from Yongdi to Xianyang. It was ordered that fathers, sons, and brothers of the common people were not allowed to live in the same room. Sporadic towns and villages were merged into counties, and county magistrates and county magistrates were set up. A total of thirty-one counties were merged and divided. Abolish well fields and redraw the boundaries of farmland, encourage the reclamation of wasteland, and balance taxes. Unify the national weights and measures system. After four years of implementation, Gongzi Qian violated the new law again and was sentenced to death. Five years later, when the Qin state became prosperous and powerful, the Emperor of Zhou gave the sacrificial meat to Duke Xiao of Qin, and princes from all over the world came to congratulate him. The next year, Qi's army defeated Wei's army in Maling, captured Wei's crown prince Shen, and killed general Pang Juan. Another year later, Wei Yang persuaded Qin Xiaogong: The relationship between Qin and Wei is like a person suffering from a heart disease. Either Wei annexes Qin, or Qin annexes Wei.
target: He later oversaw the construction of Xianyang, reorganized territories into counties, abolished well-fields, and standardized weights and measures. After further victories, Gongsun Yang persuaded Duke Xiao to attack Wei, exploiting Wei's recent defeat by Qi. He tricked Wei's general, Gongzi Yan, into a meeting, captured him, and defeated the Wei army.

id: 史记/七十列传/商君列传::group-003
article_path: 史记/七十列传/商君列传
source: King Wei Hui's army was defeated by Qi and Qin many times, leaving the country empty. Wei was getting weaker day by day. King Wei Hui was very panicked, so he sent envoys to cede the Hexi region to Qin in order to seek reconciliation. Wei then evacuated Anyi and moved its capital to Daliang. King Wei Hui said: I really regret not taking the advice of Gongshu Zuo. After Wei Yang returned from defeating the Wei army, Qin Xiaogong granted him fifteen cities in the Yu and Shang areas, with the title Lord Shang. Lord Shang served as Prime Minister of Qin for ten years, and many princes and nobles resented him.
target: King Wei Hui ceded land and regretted not heeding the uncle's advice. Gongsun Yang was granted fifteen cities and titled Lord Shang. As prime minister for ten years, he faced resentment from nobles.

id: 史记/七十列传/商君列传::group-004
article_path: 史记/七十列传/商君列传
source: None of these things are popular. As soon as you go out, dozens of vehicles are following behind you. The vehicles are all armored guards. Strong men serve as personal guards. People with spears and halberds run close to your vehicle. If you lack any of these defenses, you will definitely not dare to go out. "Shangshu" says: Prosperity depends on virtue, and destruction depends on force. Your situation is as dangerous as the morning dew that will soon disappear. Do you still plan to prolong your life? Then why not return Shang's fiefdom of fifteen cities to the State of Qin, go to remote and desolate places to water gardens and cultivate their own land, and persuade the King of Qin to reuse those talents who live in seclusion in the mountains and forests to support the elderly and raise orphans, so that father and brother can respect each other, rank according to merit, and respect virtuous people. Only in this way can peace be guaranteed. You also want to covet Shang Yu's wealth, take monopolizing the political and religious affairs of Qin as an honor and favor, and arouse the resentment of the people. Once the king of Qin abandons his guests and cannot be in power, how many people will Qin want to arrest you? The day of your death will come as quickly as you lift your feet. But Shang Jun did not follow Zhao Liang's advice. Five months later, Qin Xiaogong died and the prince ascended the throne. Gongzi Qian and his gang reported that Shang Jun wanted to rebel, and the monarch sent people to arrest Shang Jun. Shang Jun fled to the border crossing and wanted to stay in a hotel. The owner of the inn did not know that he was Lord Shang, and said: Lord Shang has an order, and the owner of the hotel will jointly and severally sentence the people staying in the hotel without documents. Shang Jun sighed longly and said: Alas! The legacy of enacting new laws has reached such an extent! He left Qin and fled to Wei. The people of Wei resented him for deceiving the young master Yan and defeating the Wei army, and refused to take him in. Shang Jun plans to go to other countries. The people of Wei said: Lord Shang is a fugitive from Qin. Qin is powerful, but its fugitive comes to Wei. It is impossible not to return him. So he sent Lord Shang back to Qin. After Lord Shang returned to Qin, he fled to his fiefdom of Shang. He and his subordinates mobilized the soldiers in the city to attack Zheng in the north to seek a way out. Qin sent troops to attack Lord Shang and killed him in Lingchi of Zheng. King Hui of Qin divided Shang Jun into five pieces and showed it to the public, saying: Don't rebel like Shang Yang! So he killed the whole clan of Lord Shang. Tai Shigong said: Mr. Shang is a cruel and merciless person by nature. It should be considered that when he used the way of an emperor to persuade Duke Xiao, he relied on pretentious talk and it was not his own qualifications. Besides, relying on the recommendation of the king's favorite minister Jing Jian, when he was appointed, he punished the prince Qian, deceived the Wei general, the prince Xian, and refused to listen to Zhao Liang's advice, which is enough to prove that Lord Shang was cruel and ungrateful. I once read a book about Shang Jun's Kasai farming campaign, and the content is similar to his own actions. But in the end, he got a bad reputation in Qin State for treason. There is a reason for this!
target: Zhao Liang warned him of his dangerous position, criticizing his reliance on harsh methods and lack of virtue, but Lord Shang ignored the advice. Five months after Duke Xiao's death, the new prince ascended. Gongzi Qian accused Lord Shang of rebellion. Lord Shang fled but was turned away by innkeepers due to his own laws requiring identification. He escaped to Wei, but the Wei people, angry over his deception, returned him to Qin. He attempted to raise troops in his fiefdom but was captured and executed by dismemberment. His entire clan was killed. Sima Qian concluded that Lord Shang's cruel and ungrateful nature, reliance on deceit, and refusal to heed wise counsel led to his downfall.

id: 史记/七十列传/大宛列传::group-000
article_path: 史记/七十列传/大宛列传
source: Dawan was discovered by Zhang Qian. Zhang Qian was from Hanzhong and served as a Langguan during the Jianyuan reign of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty. At this time, the emperor asked the surrendered Huns. They all said that the Huns attacked and defeated King Yuezhi and used his skull as a drinking vessel. The Yuezhi fled and often resented the Huns, but they had no friends to fight with them. At this time, the Han Dynasty was about to attack the Xiongnu. After hearing these statements, it wanted to send an envoy to Yuezhi to contact them. But to go to Yuezhi, you have to pass through the Xiongnu, so you recruited people who could be sent as envoys. Zhang Qian responded to the call as a Langguan and was sent as an envoy to the Yuezhi. He left Longxi with a former Huns slave named Ganfu from Tangyi. When passing by the Huns, he was captured by the Huns and handed over to the Chanyu. The Chanyu retained Zhang Qian and said, "The Yueshi are to the north of us. How can the Han Dynasty send envoys there?" If we want to send an envoy to South Vietnam, will the Han Dynasty allow us? He detained Zhang Qian for more than ten years, married him, and gave birth to children. However, Zhang Qian kept the talisman of the Han Dynasty envoy and did not lose it. Zhang Qian stayed with the Xiongnu, and the Xiongnu's care for him gradually relaxed. As a result, Zhang Qian and his followers fled to the Yueshi, and ran westward for dozens of days until they arrived in Dawan. Dawan heard that the Han Dynasty was rich in money and wanted to communicate with the Han Dynasty, but failed. Now that I saw Zhang Qian, I felt happy and asked Zhang Qian: "Where do you want to go?" Zhang Qian said: I sent an envoy to the Yuezhi for the Han Dynasty, but the Huns blocked my way. Now that we have escaped from the Huns, I hope the king will send someone to guide and escort us to Yuezhi. If we can really reach Yuezhi, we can return to the Han Dynasty. The wealth that the Han Dynasty presented to the king cannot be described in words. Dawan believed that Zhang Qian's words were true, so he asked Zhang Qian to set off and sent him a guide and translator to reach Kangju. Kangju transferred him to Dayuezhi again. At this time, the king of Dayuezhi had been killed by the Xiongnu, and his prince was appointed king.
target: Zhang Qian, a Langguan from Hanzhong during the Jianyuan reign of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, discovered Dawan. The emperor, learning from surrendered Xiongnu that the Yuezhi had been defeated by the Xiongnu and sought allies, recruited envoys to contact the Yuezhi. Zhang Qian responded, leaving Longxi with Ganfu, a former Xiongnu slave. Captured by the Xiongnu, he was detained for over ten years, married, and had children, but kept his envoy's talisman. Eventually, he escaped westward to Dawan. Dawan, eager to connect with the wealthy Han Dynasty, welcomed Zhang Qian and provided guides to Kangju, then to Dayuezhi.

id: 史记/七十列传/大宛列传::group-001
article_path: 史记/七十列传/大宛列传
source: Now that we have escaped from the Huns, I hope the king will send someone to guide and escort us to Yuezhi. If we can really reach Yuezhi, we can return to the Han Dynasty. The wealth that the Han Dynasty presented to the king cannot be described in words. Dawan believed that Zhang Qian's words were true, so he asked Zhang Qian to set off and sent him a guide and translator to reach Kangju. Kangju transferred him to Dayuezhi again. At this time, the king of Dayuezhi had been killed by the Xiongnu, and his prince was appointed king. This king had conquered Bactria and settled here. The land here is fertile and fertile, and there are few enemies to invade it, so the mood is comfortable and happy. I also thought that I was far away from the Han Dynasty and had no intention of revenge against the Huns. Zhang Qian arrived in Daxia from the Yueshi, but after all he did not get the clear attitude of the Yueshi towards uniting the Han to attack the Huns. Zhang Qian lived in Yueshi for more than a year and returned home. He traveled along the Nanshan Mountains and wanted to return to Chang'an from where the Qiang people lived, but he was captured by the Huns again. He lived with the Xiongnu for more than a year. When the Chanyu died, King Zuoguli of the Xiongnu attacked the prince and proclaimed himself the Chanyu. The country was in chaos. Zhang Qian took the opportunity to escape back to the Han Dynasty with his Hu wife and Tangyi father. In the Han Dynasty, Zhang Qian was granted the title of Taizhong Dafu, and Tang Yifu was granted the title of Envoy Lord.
target: The Yuezhi king, having conquered Bactria, was content and unwilling to attack the Xiongnu. After over a year, Zhang Qian returned via the Nanshan Mountains but was recaptured by the Xiongnu. He escaped during internal Xiongnu chaos, returning to the Han Dynasty with his Hu wife and Ganfu. He was granted the title Taizhong Dafu.

id: 史记/七十列传/大宛列传::group-002
article_path: 史记/七十列传/大宛列传
source: Zhang Qian was strong, powerful, broad-minded, honest and trustworthy, and all the barbarians liked him. Tangyi's father was a Huns and was good at archery. Whenever he was in poverty and danger, he would shoot birds and animals for food. Initially, Zhang Qian had more than a hundred followers when he was sent as an envoy. Thirteen years after leaving the Han Dynasty, only he and Gan Fu returned to the Han Dynasty. Zhang Qian visited Dayuan, Dayuezhi, Daxia, and Kangju. Legend has it that there were five or six big countries next to these countries. He stated the situation to the Emperor of Han one by one, saying: Dayuan is southwest of the Xiongnu, due west of the Han Dynasty, about 10,000 miles away from the Han Dynasty. The local custom is to settle in one place, cultivate the fields, and grow rice and wheat. Produces wine. There are many good horses. The horses are sweating and bloody. Their ancestors are the sons of Tianma. There are city walls and houses there, and there are more than 70 large and small towns under its jurisdiction, with about hundreds of thousands of people. The weapons of Dawan are bows and spears, and people ride horses and shoot arrows.
target: Zhang Qian reported on Dawan and neighboring states: Dawan, southwest of the Xiongnu, had settled agriculture, wine, and fine horses. It had over 70 towns and hundreds of thousands of people.

source: People tilled the fields and grew rice. There arose a great bird whose eggs were as big as an urn. The old people in Anxi said that there was Weushui and Queen Mother of the West in Tiaozhi State, but they had never seen them. Daxia is located south of the Guishui River, more than 2,000 miles southwest of Dawan. The local custom is that people settle in one place, with towns and houses. The custom is the same as that of Dawan. There is no grand governor, instead each town has a small governor. The country's military is weak and afraid of war. People are good at doing business. When the Da Yuezhi moved westward, they defeated Da Xia and ruled the entire Da Xia. There are many people in Daxia, about one million. Its capital is called Lanshi City. There is a trade market here. Sells various items. There is a poisonous country in the southeast of Daxia.

They drew horizontal lines on the leather as text. To the west is Tiaozhi, to the north are Yancai and Lixuan. The branches are thousands of miles west of Parthia, near the Western Sea. The weather there is hot and humid. People tilled the fields and grew rice. There arose a great bird whose eggs were as big as an urn. With a large population, some places often had small princes, and Parthian servants governed them. Think of it as a peripheral country. The people of Tiaozhi are good at magic. Daxia is located south of the Guishui River, more than 2,000 miles southwest of Dawan. The local custom is that people settle in one place, with towns and houses. The custom is the same as that of Dawan. There is no grand governor, instead each town has a small governor. The country's military is weak and afraid of war. People are good at doing business. When the Da Yuezhi moved westward, they defeated Da Xia and ruled the entire Da Xia. There are many people in Daxia, about one million.
target: Anxi, a large settled state with towns and trade, used silver coins. Tiaozhi, near the Western Sea, was hot and humid. Daxia, south of the Guishui River, had weak military but strong commerce, ruled by the Yuezhi.

id: 史记/七十列传/大宛列传::group-005
article_path: 史记/七十列传/大宛列传
source: People are good at doing business. When the Da Yuezhi moved westward, they defeated Da Xia and ruled the entire Da Xia. There are many people in Daxia, about one million. Its capital is called Lanshi City. There is a trade market here. Sells various items. There is a poisonous country in the southeast of Daxia. Zhang Qian said: When I was in Daxia, I saw Qiong bamboo sticks and Shu cloth, so I asked them: Where did they get these things? People from the Daxia Kingdom said: Our merchants bought it from the Shendu Kingdom. Shendu Country is about several thousand miles southeast of Daxia. The custom there is for people to settle in one place, which is roughly the same as in Daxia, but the terrain is low and humid and the weather is hot. Its people fought on elephants. It is near a flood. I estimate that Daxia is twelve thousand miles away from the Han Dynasty and is in the southwest of the Han Dynasty. Shendu Country is located thousands of miles southeast of Daxia and has products from Shu County, which means that it is not far from Shu County. Nowadays, if an envoy is sent to Daxia, if he passes through the Qiang residential area, the terrain is dangerous and the Qiang people hate it; if he goes slightly north, he will be captured by the Huns. The road from Shu should be straight and free from intruders. The emperor has heard that Dawan, Daxia, Anxi, etc. are all big countries that produce many strange things. The people live in one place and their lives are quite similar to those of the Han Dynasty. However, their armies are weak and they value the property of the Han Dynasty. There are countries such as Dayuezhi and Kangju in the north. Their armies are powerful, but you can use gifts and benefits to induce them to come to pay homage to the Emperor of Han. And if we can really get them and make them our own with morality, then we can expand the territory of thousands of miles, and through many translations, attract people with different customs, so that the prestige and kindness of the emperor of the Han Dynasty can be spread all over the world. Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty was happy and thought Zhang Qian's words were right, so he ordered Zhang Qian to send secret envoys from Shu County and Jianwei County to set off in four groups at the same time: one from Zhan, one from Ran, one from Qi, and one from Qionbo, each traveling one or two thousand miles. As a result, the northern route was blocked by Di and Zuo, and the southern route was blocked by Xi and Kunming. Countries like Kunming had no rulers and were good at robbing and stealing. They often killed and robbed the Han Dynasty envoys, but the Han Dynasty envoys failed to pass. However, I heard that more than a thousand miles west of Kunming, there was a country called Dianyue where the people rode elephants. Some of the merchants from Shu County who smuggled goods out of the country had been there, so the Han Dynasty began to communicate with the Dian Kingdom because they wanted to find a way to Daxia. At first, the Han Dynasty wanted to open up the southwestern barbarians, but it wasted a lot of money and the road was not opened, so they gave up. When Zhang Qian said that it was possible to connect to Daxia from the southwestern barbarians, the Han Dynasty resumed the work of opening up the southwestern barbarians. Zhang Qian followed the general Wei Qing to attack the Xiongnu as a captain. Because he knew where there were water and grass, the army could not be exhausted. The emperor named Zhang Qian the Marquis of Bowang. This happened in the sixth year of Yuanshuo, Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty. The next year, Zhang Qian became a guard and set out from Youbeiping with General Li Guang to attack the Xiongnu.
target: Zhang Qian noted that in Daxia, he saw Qiong bamboo sticks and Shu cloth, bought from Shendu (India), suggesting a route from Shu. The emperor, intrigued by these wealthy states, sent envoys from Shu, but they were blocked by tribes like Kunming. Zhang Qian later joined General Wei Qing against the Xiongnu, earning the title Marquis of Bowang. After a failed campaign with Li Guang, he was reduced to commoner status.

id: 史记/七十列传/大宛列传::group-006
article_path: 史记/七十列传/大宛列传
source: Birds flew to him with meat in their mouths and fed him; wolves came and fed him. The Chanyu felt strange and thought he was a god, so he took him in and let him grow up. When he came of age, he was asked to lead troops in battles. After many meritorious service, the Shanyu gave him his father's people and ordered him to stay in the Western Regions for a long time. Kunmo adopted his people and attacked nearby small towns. Gradually, he had tens of thousands of soldiers who could draw bows and fight, and they were familiar with the skills of offensive warfare. After Shanyu's death, Kunmo led his people to move far away, maintaining their independence and refusing to worship the Huns. The Xiongnu sent a commando to attack Kunmo, but failed to win. They believed that Kunmo was a god and stayed away from him. They restrained and controlled him instead of launching a major attack on him. Now Shan Yugang was very tired after being beaten by the Han Dynasty, and the place controlled by King Hunxie was unguarded. The custom of the barbarians is to covet the property of the Han Dynasty. If Wusun can be gifted with rich property at this time to attract him to move eastward, live in the place formerly controlled by King Hunxie, and become brothers with the Han Dynasty, Kunmo should be able to accept it according to the situation. If he accepts this arrangement, then it will be like cutting off the right arm of the Huns. After uniting Wusun, Daxia and other countries to its west can be recruited as foreign vassals. Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty believed that Zhang Qian was right and appointed him as Zhonglang General. He led 300 people, each with two horses, tens of thousands of cattle and sheep, and carried money, cloth and silk worth tens of millions. He also appointed many deputy envoys holding talismans. If the road could be opened, he would send them to neighboring countries. Zhang Qian had arrived at Wusun, and King Kunmo of Wusun received the envoys of the Han Dynasty with the same etiquette as he treated the Xiongnu Chanyu. Zhang Qian felt ashamed in his heart. He knew that the barbarians were greedy, so he said: The emperor gives gifts, and if the king does not thank him, the gifts will be returned.
target: The emperor, seeking to ally with Wusun, sent Zhang Qian as Zhonglang General with 300 men, gifts, and deputy envoys. Wusun's king, Kunmo, was hesitant due to Xiongnu influence and internal divisions. Zhang Qian dispatched deputies to various states. Wusun sent envoys to the Han Dynasty, impressed by its wealth. Zhang Qian died as Daxing, a high official.

id: 史记/七十列传/大宛列传::group-007
article_path: 史记/七十列传/大宛列传
source: The local custom respects women. When a woman speaks, her husband will resolutely comply and dare not violate it. There is no silk or lacquer everywhere, and they don't know how to make money or utensils. When the fugitive soldiers of the Han Dynasty envoys surrendered to them, they were taught to forge weapons and utensils. When they got gold and silver from the Han Dynasty, they used it to make vessels, not coins. More and more envoys from the Han Dynasty went to the Western Regions. Most of those who had been envoys since their youth reported to the emperor the situation they were familiar with, saying: "There is a good horse in Dayuan. In Ershi City, they hid it and refused to give it to the envoys of the Han Dynasty." The emperor already liked Dawan's horses. When he heard the news, he felt very happy and sent his warriors Cha Ling and others with a thousand pieces of gold and golden horses to ask the king of Dawan to exchange for the fine horses from Ershi City. Dawan already had many things from the Han Dynasty. King Wan and his ministers discussed with each other and said: The Han Dynasty is far away from us, and there are frequent deaths in our country through the salt lake. If you come from the north, there will be Xiongnu intrusion, and if you come from the south, there will be a lack of water and grass. There are often no towns and food is scarce. Envoys from the Han Dynasty came in groups of several hundred people each time, but often more than half of them died due to lack of food. How could they send a large army in such a situation? There is nothing they can do to us, and besides, the second master’s horse is a BMW from Dawan.
target: Subsequently, the Han Dynasty established ties with Western Regions states, though envoys faced challenges from Xiongnu and local resistance. The emperor launched campaigns against Dawan for its horses, leading to two expeditions under Li Guangli. The first failed due to lack of supplies, but the second succeeded with a large army, capturing Dawan and securing horses. The Han Dynasty expanded its influence, setting up commanderies and protecting trade routes.

id: 史记/七十列传/太史公自序::group-000
article_path: 史记/七十列传/太史公自序
source: Tai Shigong studied astronomy from Tang Du, the Book of Changes from Yang He, and Taoist theory from Huang Zi. Tai Shigong was an official from Jianyuan to Yuanfeng. He was worried that scholars could not understand the essence of each school and what they learned was contradictory, so he discussed the essence of the six schools of Yin and Yang, Confucianism, Mohism, Ming, Dharma and Taoism: "Zhouyi·Xici Zhuan" says: People all over the world pursue the same thing, but their specific plans are diverse; they achieve the same goal, but the methods they take are different. Yin-Yang, Confucianism, Mohism, Mingjia, Legalism and Taoism are all schools dedicated to how to achieve peace and order in the world, but the doctrines they follow are not the same, some are explicit and some are not. I have studied the art of Yin and Yang in private, and found that it focuses on the omens of good and bad luck, and has many taboos, which makes people restrained and fearful. However, the Yin and Yang family's principles on the order of the four seasons of the year cannot be discarded. Confucianism is extensive but rarely grasps the essentials. It takes effort but has little effect. Therefore, it is difficult to fully comply with the ideas of this school. However, it enshrines the etiquette of monarch, minister, father and son, and the distinction between husband and wife, elder and younger, which cannot be changed. The Mohist school is frugal and difficult to follow, so all the ideas of this school cannot be followed, but its idea of ​​emphasizing the power of this school cannot be discarded. Legalism advocates harsh punishments but unkindness, but its idea of ​​correcting the status of kings and ministers cannot be changed. Famous scholars make people constrained and easily lose their authenticity; but the relationship between the rectification of names and reality must be carefully examined. Taoism makes people's minds focused and their actions consistent with the invisible Tao, making all things abundant.
target: He noted that while all sought peace and order, their doctrines differed. Yin-Yang focused on good and bad omens with many taboos, making people fearful, but its principles on the four seasons could not be discarded.

id: 史记/七十列传/太史公自序::group-001
article_path: 史记/七十列传/太史公自序
source: Confucianism uses the "Six Arts" such as "Poetry", "Book", "Yi", "Li", "Spring and Autumn", and "Music" as its formula, and there are tens of millions of texts and interpretations of the "Six Arts". Several generations have not been able to understand their knowledge, and they will not be able to exhaustively study their etiquette in their lifetimes. Therefore, Confucianism is said to be broad but rarely grasps the essentials, and it takes effort but has little effect.
target: Confucianism was broad but rarely grasped essentials, taking much effort with little effect, yet its etiquette on君臣父子 relationships could not be changed.

id: 史记/七十列传/太史公自序::group-002

source: They eat with Tao Gui, drink soup with Tao Gui, and eat wild vegetable soup made from brown rice and quinoa. Wear Gebu clothes in summer and deerskin fur in winter. The Mohist family made only a three-inch-thick Paulownia wood coffin for the funeral of the deceased. The mourners could not fully express their grief but wept. Teaching people funeral rites must be a unified standard for all people. Suppose everyone in the world did this. Then there is no difference between high and low. Generations are different, times are changing, and people may not necessarily do the same things, so Mohism is said to be frugal and difficult to follow.
target: Mohism was frugal and difficult to follow, but its emphasis on utility could not be discarded.

source: The Mohist school is frugal and difficult to follow, so all the ideas of this school cannot be followed, but its idea of ​​emphasizing the power of this school cannot be discarded. Legalism advocates harsh punishments but unkindness, but its idea of ​​correcting the status of kings and ministers cannot be changed. The meaning is concise and concise and easy to grasp, with less effort and more effects. This is not the case with Confucianism.
target: Legalism advocated harsh punishments without kindness, but its correction of status relationships could not be changed. Famous scholars made people constrained and lost authenticity, but the relationship between names and reality required examination. Taoism made minds focused and actions consistent with the invisible Tao, absorbing strengths from other schools and adapting to times and changes.
