source: If the spirit is overused, it will fail; if the body is overworked, it will be exhausted; if the body and spirit are separated, death will occur. The dead cannot be resurrected, and the spirit and form cannot be reunited after being separated, so saints attach great importance to this issue. From this point of view, spirit is the foundation of human life, and body is the support of life. Without first stabilizing one's mind and body, but talking about how to govern the world, what can I rely on? The official position of Taishi is in charge of astronomy and does not care about civil affairs. Taishi Gong had a son named Qian. Sima Qian was born in Longmen and lived a life of farming and animal husbandry in the north of the Yellow River and south of Longmen Mountain. When he was only ten years old, he already learned to recite ancient Chinese prose. At the age of 20, he began to travel south to the Jiang and Huai areas, climbed Mount Kuaiji, explored the Yu Cave, visited Mount Jiuyi, and rafted on the Yuan River and Xiang River. He crossed north to Wenshui and Sishui, studied learning in the cities of Qi and Shandong, investigated the legacy of Confucius, and performed the ritual of shooting in Zouxian and Yishan. He was trapped in Po, Xue, and Pengcheng, and returned to his hometown through the land of Liang and Chu. So Sima moved out to serve as a doctor, and was ordered to go west to conquer the south of Bashu. He went south through Qiong, Zuo and Kunming, and returned to the court to return his orders. In this year, the emperor began to hold the Han Dynasty's Zen ceremony, but Tai Shigong was stranded in Zhounan and could not participate in the ceremony. Therefore, he was so angry that he fell ill and was about to die.
target: Tai Shigong had a son named Qian. Sima Qian was born in Longmen, farming and herding north of the Yellow River. At ten, he learned ancient prose. At twenty, he traveled south to Jiang and Huai, climbed Kuaiji, explored Yu Cave, visited Jiuyi, rafted on Yuan and Xiang rivers, crossed north to Wenshui and Sishui, studied in Qi and Shandong, investigated Confucius's legacy, performed shooting rituals in Zou and Yi, was trapped in Po, Xue, and Pengcheng, and returned through Liang and Chu. He then served as a doctor, went west to conquer south of Bashu, traveled south through Qiong, Zuo, and Kunming, and returned to report. That year, the emperor began the Han Zen ceremony, but Tai Shigong was stranded in Zhounan and could not participate, becoming ill and near death.

id: 史记/七十列传/太史公自序::group-005
article_path: 史记/七十列传/太史公自序
source: Sima Qian was born in Longmen and lived a life of farming and animal husbandry in the north of the Yellow River and south of Longmen Mountain. When he was only ten years old, he already learned to recite ancient Chinese prose. At the age of 20, he began to travel south to the Jiang and Huai areas, climbed Mount Kuaiji, explored the Yu Cave, visited Mount Jiuyi, and rafted on the Yuan River and Xiang River. He crossed north to Wenshui and Sishui, studied learning in the cities of Qi and Shandong, investigated the legacy of Confucius, and performed the ritual of shooting in Zouxian and Yishan. He was trapped in Po, Xue, and Pengcheng, and returned to his hometown through the land of Liang and Chu. So Sima moved out to serve as a doctor, and was ordered to go west to conquer the south of Bashu. He went south through Qiong, Zuo and Kunming, and returned to the court to return his orders. In this year, the emperor began to hold the Han Dynasty's Zen ceremony, but Tai Shigong was stranded in Zhounan and could not participate in the ceremony. Therefore, he was so angry that he fell ill and was about to die. His son Sima Qian happened to return from a mission and visited his father between the Yellow River and Luoshui. Taishi Gong held Sima Qian's hand and cried and said: Our ancestor was Taishi of the Zhou Dynasty. As far back as the ancient Yu and Xia Dynasties, he had gained fame and was responsible for astronomical affairs. Will the decline of future generations be cut off in my hands today? If you continue to be Taishi, you will continue the work of our ancestors. Now the emperor has inherited the great cause of the thousand-year unification of the Han Dynasty and is holding a Zen ceremony in Mount Tai, but I cannot accompany him. This is fate, it is fate! After I die, you must become Taishi; when you become Taishi, don't forget the writings I want to write. Furthermore, filial piety begins with serving parents, then serves the emperor, and finally establishes one's reputation. It is the greatest filial piety to make one's name known to future generations to show off one's parents. The world praises the Duke of Zhou, saying that he can expound and praise the merits of King Wen and King Wu, promote the customs of Zhou and Shao, understand the thoughts of Taiwang and Wang Ji, and even the achievements of Gong Liu, and respect the ancestor Hou Ji. After King You and King Li of Zhou Dynasty, the royal way declined and the rituals and music declined. Confucius studied and sorted out the old classics, repaired and revitalized the abandoned and destroyed rituals and music, discussed the "Book of Songs" and "Book of Books", and wrote "Spring and Autumn", which scholars still use as a guideline. In the more than four hundred years since Confucius wrote the Spring and Autumn Annals, the princes have merged with each other and all the history books have been discarded. Nowadays, the rise of the Han Dynasty, the unification of the country, the Ming Dynasty, the wise king, the loyal ministers, and the righteous people, I, as the Taishi, have not been able to comment on and record it, cutting off the world's history-making tradition. I am very scared about this, you must keep it in mind! Sima Qian lowered his head and shed tears and said: "Although my son is stupid, I will detail the historical news compiled by my ancestors and dare not make any omissions." Three years after Sima Tan's death, Sima moved to the post of Taishi Ling and began to collect historical books and archives collected by the state. In the fifth year of Sima Qian's appointment as Taishi Ling, which was the first year of Taichu in the Han Dynasty, during the winter solstice on Jiazishuo day in November, the Han Dynasty's calendar began to use Xia Zheng, that is, the first month of the lunar calendar was the first month. The emperor held a ceremony to implement the new calendar in the Mingtang, and all the gods received auspiciousness. Tai Shigong said: The ancestors said: Confucius came into being five hundred years after the death of Duke Zhou. Five hundred years after the death of Confucius, is there anyone who can inherit the Qingming Dynasty, correct the "Yi Zhuan", continue the "Spring and Autumn", and interpret the "Poetry", "Book", "Ritual" and "Music"? That's the purpose, that's it! How dare I refuse. The doctor Hu Sui asked: Why did Confucius write the Spring and Autumn Annals in the past? Tai Shigong said: I heard Dong Sheng say: The kingship of the Zhou Dynasty declined and became derelict. Confucius served as the military commander of the Lu State. The princes were jealous of him and the ministers and officials obstructed him. Confucius knew that his opinions were not accepted and his political ideas could not be implemented, so he praised and criticized the rights and wrongs of the two hundred and forty-two years as the standard for judging right and wrong in the world. He belittled the emperor who was unrighteous, reprimanded the princes who were wrong, and denounced the officials who were in chaos, just to make the country's political affairs clear. Confucius said: Instead of setting out empty sermons, it would be better for me to cite the actions of those in power to see what is right and wrong, whether good or bad, so that it becomes more profound. "Spring and Autumn" is a book that explains the governance of the three kings, distinguishes the rules of personnel, distinguishes suspicion, distinguishes right from wrong, decides on indecision, praises the good and hates the evil, respects the virtuous, and despises the unworthy. It allows the ruined country to exist and the severed lineage to continue. It repairs the decline and revitalizes the neglected industry. This is the greatest royal way.
target: When Sima Qian visited his father between the Yellow River and Luoshui, Tai Shigong held his hand and wept, saying their ancestor was Taishi of Zhou, responsible for astronomical affairs since Yu and Xia. He urged Sima Qian to continue as Taishi and not forget the writings he wanted to complete. He emphasized that filial piety begins with serving parents, then the emperor, and finally establishing one's reputation. He cited the Duke of Zhou for expounding King Wen and King Wu's merits, and Confucius for studying old classics, writing the Spring and Autumn Annals. He lamented that for over four hundred years since Confucius, history had been discarded, and with the Han rise, he feared cutting off the historical tradition. Sima Qian wept and promised to detail the historical news compiled by their ancestors without omission. Three years after Sima Tan's death, Sima Qian became Taishi Ling and began collecting historical books. In the first year of Taichu, the Han calendar began using Xia Zheng with the first month as the new year. Tai Shigong reflected on Confucius appearing five hundred years after the Duke of Zhou, and wondered if someone would now inherit the Qingming, correct the Yi Zhuan, and continue the Spring and Autumn. He discussed with Doctor Hu Sui why Confucius wrote the Spring and Autumn Annals, explaining that when Zhou kingship declined, Confucius praised and criticized 242 years of history as a standard for judging right and wrong, belittling unrighteous emperors, reprimanding wrong princes, and denouncing chaotic officials. The Spring and Autumn Annals explained the governance of three kings, distinguished personnel rules, and allowed ruined countries to exist and severed lineages to continue.

article_path: 史记/七十列传/太史公自序
source: Since the founding of the Han Dynasty, to this day, the wise emperor has met Fu Rui, held a Zen ceremony, revised the calendar, changed the color of his clothes, and received orders from heaven. His favor has spread endlessly, and countless people from overseas countries with different customs have come to China's borders through multiple interpretations, requesting to pay homage. The officials tried their best to praise the emperor's merits, but they still could not fully express their feelings. Besides, it is a shame for a king to be a capable scholar but not appointed; it is the fault of the officials concerned that the monarch is a wise and sage but his merits cannot be spread widely so that everyone knows about them. Moreover, I once held the position of Taishi Ling. If I abandon the emperor's saintly wisdom and virtues without recording them, bury the achievements of meritorious officials, aristocratic families, and wise officials without recording them, and violate my father's last words, the sin will be too great. The retelling of old events and the compilation of family biographies of relevant people I am talking about are not so-called works. And if you compare it with "Spring and Autumn", you are wrong. Then began to discuss the documents and materials obtained from the compilation. In the seventh year, Tai Shigong suffered a disaster from Li Ling and was imprisoned. So he sighed and said: This is my sin! This is my sin! There is no use in mutilating the body. He stood back and thought deeply: "Poems" and "Books" have subtle meanings and simple words. They are the authors who want to express their aspirations and emotions. In the past, King Wen of Zhou Dynasty was imprisoned in Youli, and he deduced the "Book of Changes"; Confucius encountered the difficulties of Chen and Cai, and wrote "Spring and Autumn"; Qu Yuan was exiled and wrote "Li Sao"; Zuo Qiuming was blind, so he compiled "Guoyu", and his grandson suffered a leg injury After the death penalty, he discussed the art of war; Lu Buwei was demoted to Shu County, and only "Lü Lan" was spread in the world; Han Fei was imprisoned in the Qin State, and then he wrote "Speaking of Difficulties" and "Lonely Anger"; most of the 300 "Poetry" were written by saints and wise men to express their anger. These people are depressed and sad in their hearts, and their ideals and ideas cannot be realized, so they recall the past and consider the future. So I finally made up my mind to record the history from the Tao and Tang Dynasties to the year of Emperor Wu Huolin, starting from the Yellow Emperor.
target: Sima Qian then began compiling documents. In the seventh year, he suffered disaster from Li Ling and was imprisoned. He sighed that this was his sin, but reflected that King Wen deduced the Book of Changes while imprisoned, Confucius wrote the Spring and Autumn Annals when distressed, Qu Yuan wrote Li Sao when exiled, and others wrote when frustrated. He finally resolved to record history from the Tao and Tang dynasties to Emperor Wu's Huolin year, starting from the Yellow Emperor. He organized his work into twelve basic annals, ten tables, eight books, thirty hereditary houses, and seventy biographies, totaling 130 chapters and 526,500 words, called "Tai Shi Gong Shu." He stored it in a famous mountain and left a copy in Kyoto for future sages and gentlemen to see.

id: 史记/七十列传/孙子吴起列传::group-000
article_path: 史记/七十列传/孙子吴起列传
source: Sun Tzu, named Wu, was from the state of Qi. Because he was proficient in the art of war, he was received by King Wu in his house. Helu said: I have read all thirteen of your military books. Can you use them to try to command the army on a small scale? Sun Tzu replied: Yes. Helu said: Can it be tested on women? Answer: Yes. So Helu agreed to his experiment and called out the beauties in the palace, a total of about one hundred and eighty people. Sun Tzu divided them into two teams, and asked King Wu's two most beloved concubines to serve as captains of each team respectively. He also asked all the beauties to hold a halberd.
target: Sun Tzu, from Qi, demonstrated his military expertise to King Helu of Wu by training 180 palace women. After repeated orders failed due to laughter, he executed the two favorite concubines serving as captains, despite the king's plea.

id: 史记/七十列传/孙子吴起列传::group-001
article_path: 史记/七十列传/孙子吴起列传
source: He hurriedly sent an envoy to convey the order and said: I already know that the general is good at using troops. If I don't have these two concubines, my food will not taste sweet. I hope you won't kill them. Sun Tzu replied: I have accepted the order as a general, and the general is in the army. It is not necessary to accept some orders from the king. So he killed two captains in public. Then the second person from the two teams was appointed as the captain in order, and then the drums were beaten to give orders. Whether the women moved left or right, forward or backward, kneeled or stood up, they all complied with the orders and discipline requirements. No one dared to speak out. So Sun Tzu sent an envoy to report to the King of Wu: The team has been drilled in order. Your Majesty, you can come down and inspect their drills. You can use them however you want, even if you ask them to go through fire and water. King Wu replied: Let the general stop the drill and go back to the hotel to rest. I don't want to go down and take a look. Sun Tzu sighed and said: Your Majesty only appreciates my military theory, but cannot let me put it into practice. From then on, King Wu Helu knew that Sun Tzu was really good at using troops, and finally appointed him as a general. Later, Wu State defeated the powerful Chu State in the west, conquered the capital of Ying, and shocked Qi and Jin in the north. It became famous among the princes and countries. During this period, Sun Tzu not only participated, but also contributed a lot.
target: The drill then succeeded perfectly. Helu later appointed Sun Tzu as general, leading Wu to defeat Chu, capture Ying, and intimidate Qi and Jin.

id: 史记/七十列传/孙子吴起列传::group-002
article_path: 史记/七十列传/孙子吴起列传
source: After the death of the grandson, another Sun Bin appeared after more than a hundred years. Sun Bin was born in Acheng and Juancheng, and he was also a descendant of Sun Wu. He once studied the art of war with Pang Juan. After Pang Juan served the Wei State, he became a general of King Wei Hui, but he knew that his talents were not as good as Sun Bin. So he secretly found Sun Bin. When Sun Bin arrived, Pang Juan was afraid that he was more talented than himself and hated him, so he cut off his feet on the pretext of being guilty and tattooed his face, hoping that he would hide him and not dare to show his face. The envoy of Qi State came to Daliang, and Sun Bin secretly met with the envoy of Qi as a prisoner to lobby. The envoys of Qi State thought that he was a rare talent, so they secretly drove him back to Qi State. General Qi Tian Ji not only appreciated him but also treated him like a guest. Tian Ji often raced horses with the nobles of Qi State and placed huge bets. Sun Bin found that their horses had almost the same foot power and could be divided into three grades: upper, middle and lower. So Sun Bin said to Tian Ji: Just place a big bet and I can make you win. Tian Ji believed this and placed thousands of gold bets in a competition with the King of Qi and the nobles. When the game came, Sun Bin said to Tian Ji: Now use your low-grade horses against their high-grade horses, your high-grade horses against their medium-grade horses, and your medium-grade horses against their low-grade horses. After three games, Tian Ji lost once and won twice, and finally won the Qi King's daughter's bet. So Tian Ji recommended his grandson to King Wei of Qi. After King Wei asked him about the art of war, he regarded him as his teacher. Later, Wei State attacked Zhao State. Zhao State was in a critical situation and asked Qi State for help. King Qi Wei planned to appoint Sun Bin as a general, but Sun Bin declined and said: "A person who has been tortured cannot be a general." So he appointed Tian Ji as the commander-in-chief and Sun Bin as the military adviser. They sat in a car with a tent and planned secretly. Tian Ji wanted to lead the reinforcements to Zhao, but Sun Bin said: Those who want to untie the tangled threads should not clench their fists and pull forcefully; those who are rescuing a fight should not get involved in random fights. To seize the vital points of the combatants, the combatants have to untie themselves due to the constraints of the situation. Now that Wei and Zhao are attacking each other, Liang's elite troops will be exhausted abroad, and the old, weak and remnant troops will be exhausted at home. You might as well lead the army to advance towards Daliang quickly, occupy its main transportation routes, and attack its empty areas. Wei will definitely abandon Zhao and return to save itself. In this way, we saved the siege of Zhao State in one fell swoop, and at the same time reaped the effects of Wei State's own defeat. Tian Ji listened to Sun Bin's advice. Sure enough, the Wei army left Handan and returned to the army. They fought in Guiling and were severely defeated. Thirteen years later, Wei and Zhao jointly attacked South Korea, and South Korea asked Qi for help.
target: Over a century later, Sun Bin, a descendant, studied warfare with Pang Juan. Jealous of Sun Bin's talent, Pang Juan had his feet cut off and face tattooed. Sun Bin secretly met Qi envoys, who smuggled him to Qi. Advising General Tian Ji, Sun Bin used clever horse-racing tactics to win bets, impressing King Wei of Qi, who made him a teacher. When Wei attacked Zhao, Sun Bin proposed attacking Daliang to force Wei's retreat, leading to victory at Guiling. Years later, when Wei and Zhao attacked Han, Sun Bin feigned weakness by reducing camp stoves daily. Pang Juan, believing Qi soldiers deserted, pursued with light troops to Maling, where Sun Bin ambushed him. Pang Juan, seeing a carved tree, lit a torch and was killed by arrows, saying, "This boy has made his name!" Sun Bin's fame spread.

id: 史记/七十列传/孙子吴起列传::group-003
article_path: 史记/七十列传/孙子吴起列传
source: Pang Juan knew that there was nothing he could do and defeat was inevitable, so he drew his sword and killed himself. Before he died, he said: "It has made this boy famous!" The Qi army took advantage of the victory to pursue it, completely defeated the Wei army, and captured Wei Crown Prince Shen back to the country. Sun Bin also became famous all over the world, and his "Art of War" was circulated in later generations. Wu Qi was a native of Wei and was good at using troops. He once studied with Zengzi and served the king of Lu. The army of Qi State attacked Lu State. Lu Jun wanted to appoint Wu Qi as a general. However, Wu Qi's wife was from Qi State, so Lu Jun was suspicious of him. At that time, Wu Qi wanted to become famous, so he killed his wife to show that he was not close to Qi. Lu Jun finally appointed him as a general, led the army to attack Qi, and defeated the Qi army. Some people in the State of Lu slandered Wu Qi and said: Wu Qi is a suspicious and cruel man.
target: Wu Qi, from Wei, served Lu after killing his Qi wife to gain trust, defeating Qi. Slandered for cruelty, he fled to Wei, where Marquis Wen appointed him general.

id: 史记/七十列传/孙子吴起列传::group-004
article_path: 史记/七十列传/孙子吴起列传
source: When he was young, his family had a thousand gold in savings. He went out to seek official positions in vain and squandered all his family property. People in his hometown and neighbors laughed at him, so he killed more than thirty people who laughed at him. Then he escaped from the east gate of Weiguo. When he said goodbye to his mother, he bit his arm and said harshly: "I, Wu Qi, will never return to Weiguo unless I become prime minister." So he worshiped Zengzi as his teacher. Soon, his mother died, and Wu Qi did not go back to attend the funeral.
target: He shared soldiers' hardships, even sucking pus from a soldier's sore, causing the soldier's mother to weep, recalling her husband's similar fate.

id: 史记/七十列传/孙子吴起列传::group-005
article_path: 史记/七十列传/孙子吴起列传
source: Wu Qi said: "Command the three armies so that the soldiers are willing to fight to the death for the country and the enemy does not dare to plot against Wei. Who is better between you and me?" Tian Wen said: Not as good as you. Wu Qi said: "How can you and I manage the civil and military officials, keep the people attached to them, and enrich the treasury?" Tian Wen said: Not as good as you. Wu Qi said: If the Qin army refuses to defend the Xihe River and does not dare to invade the east, South Korea and Zhao will surrender. Who can compare with me? Tian Wen said: Not as good as you. Wu Qi said: You are inferior to me in these aspects, but your position is above mine. Why? Tian Wen said: The king of Wei is still young, the people of the country are worried, the ministers are not friendly, and the people do not trust me. At this time, should I entrust the political affairs to you or to me? Wu Qi was silent for a long time, and then said: "I should leave it to you." Tian Wen said: This is why my position is higher than yours. Only then did Wu Qi realize that he was inferior to Tian Wen in this aspect. After Tian Wen's death, his uncle became the prime minister and married Wei Jun's daughter, but he was afraid of Wu Qi. The uncle's servant said: "It is not difficult to drive Wu Qi away." The uncle asked: What should I do? The servant said: Wu Qi is a man of character and loves fame and prestige. You can find an opportunity to say to Marquis Wu first: Wu Qi is a virtuous man, but your country is too small and borders the powerful Qin State. I am privately worried that Wu Qi has no plans to stay in Wei State for a long time. Marquis Wu would say: What should we do? You take the opportunity to say to Wu Hou: Please test him by marrying the princess. If Wu Qi has the intention to stay in Wei for a long time, he will definitely agree to marry the princess. If Wu Qi does not have the intention to stay in Wei for a long time, he will definitely refuse. This method can be used to infer his will. You find an opportunity to invite Wu Qi to go home with you, deliberately making the princess angry and despising you in person. Seeing that the princess despises you like this, Wu Qi will definitely not marry the princess. At that time, Wu Qi saw how the princess despised the prime minister, so he politely declined the offer to Marquis Wu of Wei. Marquis Wu doubted Wu Qi and no longer trusted him. Wu Qi was afraid of causing disaster, so he left Wei and immediately went to Chu. King Chu Mourning had always heard that Wu Qi was a capable person, so he appointed him as the prime minister as soon as he arrived in Chu. He made the law clear, acted in accordance with the law, enforced his orders, eliminated and reduced unnecessary redundant personnel, stopped alienating the royal family's regular supplies, and raised the warriors. Committed to strengthening the military and exposing the lobbyists who come and go. So he went south to pacify Baiyue; he went north to annex Chen and Cai, and repelled the attacks of Han, Zhao and Wei; and he went west to conquer Qin. The princes and countries were worried about Chu's power. The estranged royal families whose supplies were stopped by Wu Qi in the past all wanted to murder Wu Qi. After Duke Mourning died, the royal ministers launched a riot and attacked Wu Qi. Wu Qi fled to the place where King Chu's body was buried and hid on the body of King Mourning.
target: Wu Qi governed Xihe, resisting Qin and Han. He advised Marquis Wu that state security relies on benevolence, not terrain. After Tian Wen became prime minister, Wu Qi felt slighted but accepted Tian Wen's reasoning about political stability. Later, a plot by the new prime minister made Marquis Wu suspect Wu Qi, who fled to Chu. King Mourning made him prime minister; he reformed laws, cut redundancies, and strengthened the military, pacifying Baiyue and defeating Qin and Han. After the king's death, nobles attacked Wu Qi, who hid on the king's corpse, causing arrows to strike both.

id: 史记/七十列传/孙子吴起列传::group-006
article_path: 史记/七十列传/孙子吴起列传
source: The princes and countries were worried about Chu's power. The estranged royal families whose supplies were stopped by Wu Qi in the past all wanted to murder Wu Qi. After Duke Mourning died, the royal ministers launched a riot and attacked Wu Qi. Wu Qi fled to the place where King Chu's body was buried and hid on the body of King Mourning. The group of people attacking Wu Qi took the opportunity to shoot Wu Qi with arrows, and also hit King Mourning's body. After the mourning king was buried, the prince ascended the throne. He ordered Ling Yin to execute all those who shot Wu Qi and also shot King Mourning's body. More than seventy people were exterminated because of the shooting of Wu Qi. Tai Shigong said: Those who praise military warfare in society all praise the Thirteen Chapters of "Sun Tzu" and Wu Qi's "The Art of War". These two books are widely circulated in society, so I will not discuss them and will only comment on the situations involved in their lives. As the saying goes: Those who can do may not be able to speak, and those who can speak may not be able to do. Sun Bin's military action against Pang Juan was wise, but he himself could not avoid the torture of having his feet cut off in advance.
target: The new prince executed over seventy families for this. Sima Qian notes Sun Tzu and Wu Qi's writings are famous, but Sun Bin couldn't avoid mutilation, and Wu Qi's harshness led to his death.

id: 史记/七十列传/孟尝君列传::group-000
article_path: 史记/七十列传/孟尝君列传
source: Mengchangjun's surname is Tian Mingwen. Tian Wen's father is Jingguo Jun Tian Ying. Tian Ying is the youngest son of King Qi Wei and the younger brother of King Qi Xuan's concubine. Tian Ying has been in power since he was King Wei. He once led troops with Chenghou Zou Ji and Tian Ji to rescue South Korea and attack Wei. Later, Chenghou and Tian Ji competed for the favor of King Qi and had a deep rift. As a result, Chenghou betrayed Tian Ji. Tian Ji was very frightened, so he launched a surprise attack on the city on the border of Qi. He failed to capture it and ran away. At this time, King Wei of Qi passed away and King Xuan came to the throne. King Xuan knew that it was Chenghou who framed Tian Ji, so he recalled Tian Ji and made him a general. In the second year of King Xuan of Qi, Tian Ji, Sun Bin and Tian Ying attacked the state of Wei, defeated the state of Wei in Maling, captured the prince Shen of the state of Wei, and killed the general Pang Juan of the state of Wei. In the seventh year of King Xuan, Tian Ying was ordered to go to South Korea and Wei as an envoy. After some of his activities, South Korea and Wei were surrendered to Qi. Tian Ying accompanied Han Zhaohou and King Wei Hui to meet with King Qi Xuan in Dong'anan. The three countries formed an alliance and signed a treaty before leaving. The next year, King Xuan met with King Hui of Liang again in Zhendi. This year, King Hui of Liang passed away. In the ninth year of King Xuan's reign, Tian Ying became prime minister of Qi. King Xuan of Qi and King Xiang of Wei respected each other as kings at the Xuzhou League. After King Chu Wei learned about this incident, he was very angry with Tian Ying and thought that he was the one who planned it. The next year, Chu attacked Qi and defeated the Qi army in Xuzhou, so they sent people to hunt down Tian Ying. Tian Ying sent Zhang Chou to persuade King Chu Wei, and King Chu Wei finally gave up. Tian Ying served as prime minister of Qi for eleven years. King Xuan died and King Min came to the throne. Three years after King Min came to the throne, he granted Tian Ying the title of "Xue Yi". At first, Tian Ying had more than forty sons. One of his concubines gave birth to a son named Wen. Tian Wen was born on May 5th. Tian Ying told Tian Wen's mother: Don't raise him. But Tian Wen's mother still secretly raised him. When he grew up, his mother introduced Tian Wen to Tian Ying through Tian Wen's brother. When Tian Ying saw the child, he angrily said to his mother: I asked you to throw this child away, but you dared to feed him. Why? Before Tian Wen's mother could answer, Tian Wen immediately kowtowed and then asked Tian Ying: "Why are you not allowed to raise a child born in May?" Tian Ying replied: A child born in May will be disadvantageous to his parents when he grows to be as tall as the door. Tian Wen said: Is human destiny granted by God? Or is it awarded by the portal?
target: Mengchangjun, whose surname was Tian and given name Wen, was the son of Jingguo Jun Tian Ying. Tian Ying, the youngest son of King Qi Wei, served as a general and later as prime minister of Qi, leading campaigns against Wei and forming alliances with Han and Wei. He had over forty sons, but Tian Wen was born on May 5th, a date considered inauspicious. Tian Ying ordered the child abandoned, but his mother secretly raised him. When Tian Wen grew up, he confronted his father, arguing that fate was determined by heaven, not by the doorframe, and criticized Tian Ying for accumulating wealth while neglecting the state's welfare. Impressed, Tian Ying made Tian Wen his heir.

id: 史记/七十列传/孟尝君列传::group-001
article_path: 史记/七十列传/孟尝君列传
source: The number of guests kept coming and going, and Tian Wen's reputation spread to all the vassal states. All the vassal states sent people to ask Tian Ying to make Tian Wen the crown prince, and Tian Ying agreed. After Tian Ying's death, he was given the posthumous title of Jing Guojun. As expected, Tian Wen inherited Tian Ying's title in Xue Yi. This is Lord Mengchang. Lord Mengchang was in Xue Yi, soliciting guests from various vassal states and people who had committed crimes and fled. Many people joined Lord Mengchang. Lord Mengchang was willing to give up his family fortune and give them generous treatment, so scholars from all over the world came here to admire his reputation. He has thousands of diners, and all are treated the same as Tian Wen, regardless of high or low. Whenever Mr. Mengchang receives guests and sits and talks with them, he always arranges an attendant behind the screen to record the conversation between Mr. Mengchang and the guests, as well as the residence of the guests' relatives. As soon as the guests left, Lord Mengchang sent envoys to the homes of the guests' relatives to comfort them and offer them gifts. Once, Meng Changjun entertained guests for dinner, and someone blocked the light. The guest was very annoyed, thinking that the quality of the food must be unequal, so he put down his bowls and chopsticks and was about to say goodbye. Lord Mengchang immediately stood up and compared his own food with his. The guest was so ashamed that he cut his neck and committed suicide as an apology. Therefore, many of the wise men were willing to join Lord Mengchang. Mr. Mengchang warmly accepted all the guests who came to his door, without being picky or familiar, and gave them all generous treatment. Therefore, everyone among the guests thought that Lord Mengchang was close to them. When King Zhao of Qin heard that Lord Mengchang was a virtuous man, he first sent Lord Jingyang to Qi as a hostage and asked to see Lord Mengchang. Lord Mengchang was about to go to Qin, but the guests did not approve of his trip and tried to persuade him, but he refused to listen and insisted on going.
target: After Tian Ying's death, Tian Wen inherited the title of Lord Mengchang in Xue Yi. He generously hosted thousands of guests, treating them equally regardless of status. He recorded their conversations and sent gifts to their relatives. Once, a guest suspected unequal treatment, but Lord Mengchang compared his own meal to prove fairness, leading the guest to commit suicide in shame. Lord Mengchang accepted all guests without discrimination, earning their loyalty.

id: 史记/七十列传/孟尝君列传::group-002
article_path: 史记/七十列传/孟尝君列传
source: If it really rains and the water rushes towards you, I don’t know where it will take you. Today's Qin State is a country as fierce as a tiger or a wolf. If you insist on going there, if you cannot come back, will you not be laughed at by the local puppets? After hearing this, Lord Mengchang realized the truth and stopped preparing for the trip. In the twenty-fifth year of King Min of Qi, he finally sent Lord Mengchang to Qin. King Zhao of Qin immediately appointed Lord Mengchang as the prime minister of Qin. Someone among the officials persuaded the King of Qin: Lord Mengchang is indeed a virtuous man, but he is a member of the Qi clan and now serves as the prime minister of the Qin State. When planning things, he must first plan for the Qi State and then consider the interests of the Qin State. This will put the Qin State in danger. So King Zhao of Qin dismissed Lord Mengchang from his position as prime minister. He imprisoned Lord Mengchang and wanted to kill Lord Mengchang. Lord Mengchang knew that the situation was critical, so he sent someone to see King Zhao's concubine to ask for help. The concubine made a condition and said: I hope to get Lord Mengchang's white fox fur. When Lord Mengchang came, he brought with him a white fox fur, which was worth thousands of gold. There was no second one in the world. When he arrived in Qin, he presented it to King Zhao, and there was no other fur. Lord Mengchang was worried about this matter. He asked all the guests, but no one could think of a solution. There was a man who was not very capable but could steal things in dog skins. He said: I can get that white fox fur. So that night, he disguised himself as a dog, went into the warehouse of the Qin Palace, took out the fox white fur that was presented to King Zhao, and took it back and presented it to King Zhao's concubine. After getting the concubine, she interceded with King Zhao on behalf of Lord Mengchang, and King Zhao released Lord Mengchang. After Mengchangjun was released, he immediately fled by express train, changed his exit certificate, changed his name and escaped from the city pass. We arrived at Hangu Pass at midnight. King Zhao regretted releasing Lord Mengchang and sent people to look for him again. When he found that he had escaped, he immediately sent people to chase him. Mengchangjun and his party arrived at Hangu Pass. According to the customs law, guests can only be let out when the rooster crows. Mengchangjun was worried that his pursuers would arrive. Among the guests, there was a person who was of low rank but could imitate the rooster's crow. As soon as he imitated the rooster's crow, the nearby chickens also crowed, and he immediately showed his documents and escaped from Hangu Pass. After about a meal after leaving the pass, Qin's pursuers arrived at Hangu Pass, but fell behind Lord Mengchang, so they had to go back. When Lord Mengchang accepted these two people as guests, the guests all felt ashamed and disgraced. When Lord Mengchang suffered a disaster in Qin, he finally relied on these two people to escape.
target: King Zhao of Qin, hearing of Lord Mengchang's virtue, invited him to Qin and appointed him prime minister. However, officials warned that Lord Mengchang, being a Qi noble, would prioritize Qi's interests, so King Zhao imprisoned him. Lord Mengchang's concubine demanded his white fox fur as a bribe for her intercession. A guest skilled in thievery disguised himself as a dog, stole the fur from the palace, and gave it to the concubine, who secured Lord Mengchang's release. As he fled, another guest imitated a rooster's crow to open the Hangu Pass gates before pursuers arrived. Though initially ashamed of these lowly guests, Lord Mengchang's reliance on them earned admiration for his inclusive recruitment.

id: 史记/七十列传/孟尝君列传::group-003
article_path: 史记/七十列传/孟尝君列传
source: You send your army to Hangu Pass but do not attack. Let the Western Zhou Dynasty tell King Zhao of Qin your feelings and say that Duke Xue will definitely not attack Qin to strengthen the power of Han and Wei. His purpose in attacking Qin was just to ask the king to instruct Chu to cede the Eastern Kingdom to Qi, and to ask you to release King Huai of Chu to reach a reconciliation. You asked the Western Zhou Dynasty to use this method to benefit Qin. Qin could not be attacked and used Chu's territory to protect itself. Qin must want to do this. If the King of Chu could be released, he would definitely be grateful to the State of Qi. The Qi State will naturally become stronger and stronger after acquiring the Dong Kingdom, and Xue Yi will be free from worries for generations. Qin will not be overly weakened, and it is located to the west of South Korea and Wei. South Korea and Wei must rely on Qi. After hearing this, Lord Mengchang immediately said: "Okay." So Han and Wei were asked to congratulate Qin, which prevented a military disaster. Qi, Han, and Wei no longer sent troops to attack, and Qi stopped borrowing weapons and rations from the Western Zhou Dynasty. At this time, King Huai of Chu had already arrived in Qin, and Qin detained him, so Lord Mengchang must ask Qin to release him. But Qin did not do this. When Mengchang Jun was the prime minister of Qi, his attendant Wei Zi went to collect the tax from the feudal city for him. He made three trips back and forth, but he never got the tax back once. Lord Mengchang asked him what was the reason for this, and Wei Zi replied: There is a virtuous man. I donated the tax to him privately in your name, so I did not take it back. After hearing this, Lord Mengchang became angry and dismissed Wei Zi. A few years later, someone spread rumors about Lord Mengchang to King Min of Qi, saying that Lord Mengchang was about to launch a rebellion. When Tian Junjia kidnapped King Min, King Min suspected that it was Master Mengchang who planned it, and fled to avoid disaster. The sage who had received food as a gift from Wei Zi heard about this and wrote to King Min to state that Lord Mengchang would not cause rebellion and asked for his own life as a guarantee. He then cut his neck and committed suicide at the gate of the palace to prove Lord Mengchang's innocence. King Min was shocked, so he investigated and inquired about the actual situation. As expected, Lord Mengchang had no rebellion conspiracy, so he recalled Lord Mengchang. Lord Mengchang therefore excused himself from illness and asked to resign and return to Xue Yi to retire. King Min agreed to his request. After that, Qin's fugitive general Lu Li came to Qi to serve as Qi's prime minister. He wanted to put Su Dai in trouble. Su Dai said to Lord Mengchang: Zhou Zui was extremely loyal to the King of Qi, but the King of Qi expelled him and listened to the advice of his relatives and made Lu Li the prime minister. The reason was that he planned to unite with Qin. If Qi and Qin unite, then Qin Fu and Lu Li will be reused. If they are used in important positions, Qi and Qin will definitely despise you. You might as well march north quickly, attack Zhao Zhao to make Qin and Wei make peace, and recruit Zhou Zui to show your kindness. You can also restore the reputation of King Qi and prevent the world's current situation from changing. If the State of Qi does not rely on the State of Qin, then all the princes will join the State of Qi, and their relatives will inevitably flee. In this case, who else can the King of Qi rule the country with besides you? So Lord Mengchang followed Su Dai's plan, so Lu Li was jealous and wanted to murder Lord Mengchang.
target: Later, Lord Mengchang became Qi's prime minister and planned to attack Qin with Han and Wei. Su Dai advised him to avoid strengthening Han and Wei, instead using the Western Zhou to negotiate with Qin for Chu's eastern territory and the release of King Huai of Chu. Lord Mengchang agreed, averting war. When dismissed as prime minister due to slander, he retired to Xue Yi. After Qin's general Lu Li became Qi's prime minister, Lord Mengchang, following Su Dai's advice, marched north to secure alliances, causing Lu Li to flee. When King Qi Min grew proud and sought to eliminate him, Lord Mengchang fled to Wei, became prime minister, and allied with Qin and Zhao to attack Qi, leading to King Min's death. King Xiang of Qi later reconciled with Lord Mengchang, who remained neutral among the states. After his death, his sons fought over the title, and Qi and Wei destroyed Xue Yi, ending his lineage.

id: 史记/七十列传/孟尝君列传::group-004
article_path: 史记/七十列传/孟尝君列传
source: At the banquet, when everyone was drinking and enjoying themselves, Feng Chen walked up to the banquet with the deeds and checked them one by one. Those who could pay the interest would be given a time limit; those who were too poor to pay the interest would take back their deeds and burn them in public. Then he said to everyone: The reason why Lord Mengchang asked everyone for loans was to provide funds for people without funds to engage in industrial production; the reason why he asked everyone for debts was because he had no money to support the guests. Nowadays, the rich and wealthy can repay their debts on the agreed date, while the poor and unable to repay their debts burn the deeds and cancel all debts. Please enjoy your drink. With such a fiefdom master, how could we turn our backs on him in the future? Everyone sitting there stood up and knelt down twice in a row. When Lord Mengchang heard that Feng Chen had burned the deed, he was very angry and immediately sent someone to recall Feng Chen. As soon as Feng Chen arrived, Lord Mengchang asked: "I have three thousand diners, so I lend money in Xue Yi." My fiefdom is small to begin with, but the people still do not repay the interest on time, and the guests are afraid that they will not have enough to eat, so I asked you, sir, to collect the debts. I heard that after receiving the money, my husband held a banquet of wine and meat and burned the deed. Why is this? Feng Xuan replied: Yes. If there is no way to gather all the debtors together without throwing a feast of wine and meat, there will be no way to know who is rich and who is poor. If he is wealthy, he will be given a set date to repay his debts. The poor will not be able to repay their debts even if they are detained for ten years. The longer the time, the higher the interest. If you are too hasty, they will not be able to repay you in the end. On the one hand, you will be thought to be greedy for small profits and not caring for the people. On the other hand, the people will have a reputation of abandoning the emperor and relying on debts. This is not a way to encourage scholars and people and show your reputation. I burned the useless IOUs and discarded the nominal account books to make the common people of Xue Yi trust you and promote your good reputation for kindness. What else do you have to doubt? After hearing this, Lord Mengchang clapped his hands and thanked him repeatedly. The King of Qi was bewitched by the slanderous remarks of Qin and Chu, and believed that Lord Mengchang's reputation was higher than his own and that he would monopolize the power of Qi, so he dismissed Lord Mengchang from his official position. When the guests saw that Lord Mengchang had been dismissed, they all left him.
target: Feng Chen, a poor scholar, joined Lord Mengchang's household. Initially placed in low-class quarters, he sang about lacking fish, a carriage, and means to support his family, prompting Lord Mengchang to upgrade his status. When Lord Mengchang needed to collect debts in Xue Yi, Feng Chen was sent. Instead of collecting, he burned the deeds of the poor, arguing that this would earn the people's trust and enhance Lord Mengchang's reputation. Though initially angry, Lord Mengchang later thanked him.

id: 史记/七十列传/孟尝君列传::group-005
article_path: 史记/七十列传/孟尝君列传
source: Feng Chen replied: Your Majesty also knows that the State of Qi has dismissed Lord Mengchang from his position, right? King Qin said: I heard about this. Feng Xuan said: The person who made Qi respected by the world was Lord Mengchang. Now that the king of Qi has listened to the slander and dismissed Lord Mengchang, Lord Mengchang is extremely resentful and will definitely betray Qi. If he betrays Qi and enters Qin, then the national conditions of Qi and the situation in the court, from the king to the officials, will be under the control of Qin. You will get the entire land of Qi, and you will be more than just the hero! Hurry up and send an envoy with gifts to meet Lord Mengchang secretly. Don't miss this opportunity. If King Qi comes to his senses and appoints Lord Mengchang again, then it is impossible to predict who will win or lose. The King of Qin was very happy after hearing this, and sent ten carriages carrying a hundred yi gold to meet Lord Mengchang. Feng Xuan said goodbye to the King of Qin and rushed to the State of Qi ahead of the envoy. When he arrived at the State of Qi, he persuaded the King of Qi: The lobbyists from all over the world who drive east to Qi State all want to make Qi strong and make Qin weak; those who ride west to Qin State all want to make Qin strong and make Qi weak. Qin and Qi are equally superior and inferior. If Qin is strong, Qi must be weak. These two countries will inevitably not be able to dominate at the same time. Now I heard privately that the Qin State has sent an envoy with ten carriages carrying a hundred yi gold to greet Lord Mengchang. It's fine if Lord Mengchang doesn't go west. If he goes west and serves as the prime minister of Qin, then the world will belong to Qin. If Qin becomes the lord, Qi will have no choice but to succumb to it. Then Linzi and Jimo will be in danger. Why didn't the king quickly restore Mengchang to his official position and increase his fiefdom to apologize to him before the Qin envoy arrived? If this is done, Lord Mengchang will be happy and willing to accept it. Although Qin is a powerful country, how can it arbitrarily go to other countries to welcome other people's prime ministers? It is necessary to thwart Qin's conspiracy and cut off its plan to seek strength and hegemony. After hearing this, King Qi immediately understood and said: OK. So he sent people to the border to wait for the Qin envoy. As soon as the Qin envoy's car entered the Qi border, the Qi envoy at the border immediately changed his car and drove back to report the situation. The King of Qi recalled Mengchang Jun and restored his position as prime minister. At the same time, he also gave him the land of the original fiefdom and added a thousand households to him. When the envoy from Qin heard that Lord Mengchang had restored his position as prime minister of Qi, he changed his carriage and went back. Since the King of Qi dismissed Lord Mengchang because of the slander, all the guests have left him. Later, the King of Qi recalled and restored Lord Mengchang to his official position, and Feng Chen went to greet him.
target: When Lord Mengchang was dismissed as prime minister, his guests abandoned him. Feng Chen went to Qin, convincing King Zhao to send gifts to recruit Lord Mengchang. He then urged King Qi to restore Lord Mengchang's position before the Qin envoy arrived, which King Qi did. When Lord Mengchang expressed bitterness toward his former guests, Feng Chen explained that people naturally flock to the wealthy and abandon the poor, advising him to forgive them. Lord Mengchang accepted this counsel.

id: 史记/七十列传/孟尝君列传::group-006
article_path: 史记/七十列传/孟尝君列传
source: Feng Xuan said: I'm not apologizing for the guests, it's because your words were wrong. Generally speaking, everything has its inevitable end, and everything in the world has its routine. Do you understand the meaning of this sentence? Lord Mengchang said: I don’t understand what you mean. Feng Xuan said: All living things will die at some point. This is the inevitable result of living things. Rich people have many guests, while poor people have few friends. This is how it is. Don't you see people rushing to the market? At dawn, people crowded into the market, squaring their shoulders to get in; after sunset, people passing by the market waved their arms without even looking back. It's not that people like morning and hate evening, but because what they expected is no longer available in the East and West markets. Now that you have lost your official position and all your guests have left, you cannot resent your guests and cut off their access to you. I hope you treat your guests like you used to. Lord Mengchang bowed down twice and said, "I respectfully follow your advice." Listen to your teacher, do you dare to accept instruction without respect? Tai Shigong said: I once passed through Xuedi, where the folk customs were very different from those in Zoudi and Lu. I asked the people there what was the reason for this, and they said: Lord Mengchang once attracted many righteous people from all over the world, and there were probably more than 60,000 people who violated laws and regulations and entered Xuedi alone. It is said that Mr. Mengchang was very proud of his pleasure in entertaining guests, and his reputation was indeed well-deserved.
target: Sima Qian noted that Xue's unique customs stemmed from Lord Mengchang's hospitality, which attracted over sixty thousand lawbreakers, affirming his well-deserved reputation for entertaining guests.

id: 史记/七十列传/屈原贾生列传::group-000
article_path: 史记/七十列传/屈原贾生列传
source: Qu Yuan, named Ping, has the same surname as the Chu king's family. Served as the left disciple of King Huai of Chu. Qu Yuan was well-informed, had a strong memory, understood the principles of national stability and turmoil, and was good at rhetoric. When Qu Yuan was at court, he discussed state affairs with King Huai of Chu in order to issue orders; when outside the court, he received guests and dealt with the affairs of the marquis. King Huai of Chu trusted him very much. The official Shangguan had the same position as Qu Yuan. In order to gain the favor of King Huai, he was very jealous of Qu Yuan's talents. Once, King Huai ordered Qu Yuan to formulate a national law. Qu Yuan had just finished writing the draft but had not yet completed the final revision. When Shangguan saw it, he wanted to take it for himself, but Qu Yuan refused to give it to him. He spoke ill of Qu Yuan to King Huai of Chu: Your Majesty, you asked Qu Yuan to make a decree. No one at the top or bottom did not know about it. Every time a decree was issued, Qu Yuan boasted of his achievements, saying that no one could make it except me. King Huai was very angry after hearing this, so he alienated Qu Yuan. Qu Yuan felt extremely sad that King Huai was unable to distinguish right from wrong, that his vision was blinded by flatterers and unable to distinguish truth from falsehood, that evil harmed justice, and that upright people were not tolerated by the court. Therefore, he wrote "Li Sao" with deep sorrow and deep thought. The so-called "Li Sao" means encountering sorrow. God is the origin of man; parents are the foundation of man. When people are in a difficult situation, they have to remember their roots. Therefore, when the fatigue and hardship are extreme, there is no one who does not call God; when the pain is unbearable, there is no one who does not call for the parents. Qu Yuan insisted on notarization, acted upright, was loyal to the king, and used his talents to the best of his ability. However, he was provoked by villains, and his situation could be said to be extremely embarrassing. How can one not feel grief and indignation when one is doubted by the king because one is sincere for the country, and one is slandered by villains because one is loyal to the master? Qu Yuan wrote "Li Sao" precisely to express this feeling of grief and indignation. Although "The Book of Songs: Guofeng" contains many works describing the love between men and women, it is not chaotic; although "The Book of Songs: Xiaoya" reveals the people's slander and resentment against the government, it does not advocate open rebellion. Qu Yuan's "Li Sao" can be said to have the advantages of both. In "Li Sao", Qu Yuan traced the deeds of Emperor Ku upwards, praised Qi Huan's great achievements in modern times, and described the virtues of Shang Tang and Zhou Wu in the middle to criticize current affairs.
target: Qu Yuan, named Ping, shared the same surname as the Chu royal family and served as a left disciple under King Huai of Chu. He was knowledgeable, had a strong memory, understood statecraft, and was skilled in rhetoric. King Huai trusted him deeply, but the official Shangguan, jealous of Qu Yuan's talents, slandered him by claiming Qu Yuan boasted about his own decrees. King Huai believed this and alienated Qu Yuan. Grief-stricken by the king's inability to discern truth from falsehood, Qu Yuan wrote "Li Sao," a work expressing his sorrow and indignation. The text praises "Li Sao" for combining the virtues of "The Book of Songs: Guofeng" and "Xiaoya," using metaphors like vanilla to symbolize noble character, and comparing Qu Yuan's purity to the sun and moon.

id: 史记/七十列传/屈原贾生列传::group-001
article_path: 史记/七十列传/屈原贾生列传
source: Qu Yuan had been demoted. After that, Qin planned to attack Qi, and Qi and Chu joined forces to have a blind date. King Qin Hui was worried about this, so he sent Zhang Yi to pretend to leave Qin and bring rich gifts to serve Chu. He said: Qin hates Qi very much. King Huai of Chu greedily listened to Zhang Yi's words, broke off diplomatic relations with Qi, and sent envoys to Qin to accept the land. Zhang Yi deceived the envoy of the Chu State and said: I, Zhang Yi, agreed with King Huai of Chu to be six miles, but I have never heard of six hundred miles. The Chu envoy left Qin angrily and returned to report to King Huai of Chu. King Huai of Chu was angry and raised troops to attack Qin. The Qin State sent troops to attack the Chu army, and defeated the Chu army in the Danshui and Xishui areas. It killed 80,000 Chu soldiers, captured the Chu general Qu, and took advantage of the situation to seize the Hanzhong area of ​​the Chu state. King Huai of Chu dispatched all the troops from across the country to attack Qin and fought in Lantian. When Wei heard the news, he sent troops to attack Chu and penetrated as far as Deng Yi. The Chu army was frightened, so they withdrew from Qin and returned home. However, the state of Qi finally refused to rescue the state of Chu because of anger, and the state of Chu was in great distress. The next year, Qin proposed to cede the land in Hanzhong to make peace with Chu, but King Huai of Chu said: I don't want to get the land, I just want Zhang Yi and I will be content. When Zhang Yi heard this, he said: "I, Zhang Yi, can come to Hanzhong and ask the king to allow me to go to Chu." After Zhang Yi arrived in Chu State, he gave generous gifts to Jin Shang, the powerful minister of Chu State, and used sweet words to deceive King Huai's concubine Zheng Xiu. King Huai actually listened to Zheng Xiu's words and let Zhang Yi run away again. At this time, Qu Yuan had been alienated and no longer held important official positions. He had just been sent as an envoy to Qi State. After returning, he admonished King Huai and said: Your Majesty, why don't you kill Zhang Yi? King Huai felt very regretful and sent people to chase him, but it was too late. After that, all the vassal states jointly attacked the Chu State, defeated the Chu army, and killed the Chu general Tang Wei. At that time, King Zhao of Qin was married to Chu and wanted to meet King Huai of Chu. King Huai of Chu wanted to go. Qu Yuan advised him: Qin is a greedy and violent country like tigers and wolves. It cannot be trusted, so it is better not to go. But King Huai's youngest son Zilan persuaded King Huai to go, saying: "Why do you want to cut off King Qin's good intentions?" King Huai finally went. But as soon as he entered Wuguan, the Qin Dynasty's ambush cut off his return and detained King Huai in order to make him agree to cede the land. King Huai was furious and refused to agree. He fled to the State of Zhao, but the State of Zhao refused to accept him. Then he came to the State of Qin and finally died in the State of Qin. His body was transported back to the State of Chu for burial.
target: After Qu Yuan's demotion, Qin, fearing the Qi-Chu alliance, sent Zhang Yi to deceive Chu. King Huai, swayed by greed, broke ties with Qi and was tricked into believing Qin would cede six hundred miles of land, only to receive six. Enraged, King Huai attacked Qin but suffered a devastating defeat, losing 80,000 soldiers and the Hanzhong region. Wei also attacked Chu, and Qi refused aid. Later, Qin proposed peace, but King Huai demanded Zhang Yi. Zhang Yi bribed Chu officials and King Huai's concubine, Zheng Xiu, to secure his release. Qu Yuan, then an envoy to Qi, urged King Huai to kill Zhang Yi, but it was too late. Subsequently, vassal states defeated Chu, killing General Tang Wei. King Zhao of Qin invited King Huai for a meeting; Qu Yuan warned against it, but King Huai's son Zilan persuaded him to go. King Huai was captured, refused to cede land, fled to Zhao (which rejected him), and died in Qin. His body was returned to Chu.

id: 史记/七十列传/屈原贾生列传::group-002
article_path: 史记/七十列传/屈原贾生列传
source: King Huai finally went. But as soon as he entered Wuguan, the Qin Dynasty's ambush cut off his return and detained King Huai in order to make him agree to cede the land. King Huai was furious and refused to agree. He fled to the State of Zhao, but the State of Zhao refused to accept him. Then he came to the State of Qin and finally died in the State of Qin. His body was transported back to the State of Chu for burial. King Huai's eldest son, King Qingxiang, succeeded to the throne and appointed his younger brother Zilan as Ling Yin. Zilan persuaded King Huai to enter Qin and eventually died in Qin. People in Chu blamed Zilan for this. Qu Yuan also hated Zilan very much for what he did. Although he was exiled, he was still attached to the Kingdom of Chu, missed King Huai, and always thought about returning to the court. He always hoped that the king would suddenly wake up and change his bad customs. He always remembered the king, revived the country, and reversed the situation, so he expressed this feeling many times in a work. However, there was nothing he could do, so it was impossible to return to the court. This also shows that King Huai did not wake up in the end. As a king, no matter he is smart or stupid, talented or not, he hopes to find loyal ministers and wise men to assist him in governing the country. However, the destruction of the country and the destruction of the family continue to happen, but the sage king and the peaceful country have not been seen for many generations. The fundamental reason is that the so-called loyal ministers are not loyal, and the so-called wise men are not wise. Because King Huai did not know the duties of a loyal minister, he was deceived by Zheng Xiu internally and deceived by Zhang Yi externally. He alienated Qu Yuan and trusted Shangguan officials and Ling Yin Zilan. As a result, the army was defeated miserably, the country was invaded, and the territory of six counties was lost. He also lived in a foreign country, died in Qin, and was ridiculed by the people of the world. This is a disaster caused by ignorant people. "Book of Changes" says: It is sad that the well has been dredged but no one comes to drink water. If the king is wise, everyone can be happy. And King Huai is so ignorant, how can he deserve happiness? Ling Yin Zilan was furious when he heard the above situation, and finally asked Shangguan officials to speak ill of Qu Yuan to King Qingxiang. King Qingxiang banished Qu Yuan when he was angry. Qu Yuan came to the riverside, his hair disheveled and walking on the grass in the wilderness, groaning in sorrow and indignation. His face was haggard and his body was thin. When a fisherman saw him, he asked: "Aren't you Dr. Sanlu?" Why come here?
target: King Qingxiang succeeded King Huai and appointed Zilan as Ling Yin. Qu Yuan, exiled but still loyal, blamed Zilan for King Huai's death and hoped for reform. However, Zilan and Shangguan slandered Qu Yuan to King Qingxiang, leading to his banishment. Qu Yuan wandered by the river, disheveled and gaunt. A fisherman asked why he was exiled; Qu Yuan replied that he alone was pure in a corrupt world. The fisherman advised adapting to the times, but Qu Yuan refused to taint his integrity, preferring to die in the river. He wrote "Huaisha," expressing his resolve to maintain his principles despite injustice. He then drowned himself in the Miluo River.

id: 史记/七十列传/屈原贾生列传::group-003
article_path: 史记/七十列传/屈原贾生列传
source: Heavy sadness and long sigh, sighing and mourning forever. The world is turbid and there are few close friends. People's hearts are unpredictable and difficult to guess. You must die in this world, so don't cherish your own life too much. Tell this clearly to the world, gentlemen, that I will always be a role model for others. So Qu Yuan threw himself into the Miluo River with stones in his arms and committed suicide. After Qu Yuan's death, there were Song Yu, Tang Le, Jing Cha and others in the Chu State. They all loved literature and were famous for their good poetry and poetry. But they all only learned the euphemistic and implicit side of Qu Yuan's speech, and in the end no one dared to express his advice as bluntly as Qu Yuan did. After that, the Chu State became weaker and weaker day by day, and was finally eliminated by the Qin State decades later. More than a hundred years after Qu Yuan sank into the river and died, there was a man named Jia Sheng in the Han Dynasty who passed by the Xiang River when he was serving as the Prince of Changsha. He wrote a poem and threw it into the river to pay homage to Qu Yuan. Jia Sheng's name is Jia Yi, and he is from Luoyang. At the age of eighteen, he became famous locally for reciting poetry and writing articles. When Wu Tingwei was serving as the governor of Henan County, he heard that Jia Yicai had excellent academic performance, so he summoned him to serve in the Yamen and regarded him very highly. When Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty first came to the throne, he heard that Wu Gong, the governor of Henan Province, had outstanding political achievements and was ranked first in the country. He was from the same hometown as Li Si and had learned from Li Si, so he recruited him as a court captain. Wu Tingwei recommended that Jia Yi was young and talented, and could be proficient in the knowledge of hundreds of schools of thought. In this way, Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty recruited Jia Yi to serve as a doctor. At that time, Jia Yi was more than 20 years old and the youngest among the Ph.D. Every time Emperor Wen ordered the doctors to discuss some issues, the older gentlemen had nothing to say, but Jia Yi could answer them one by one, and everyone felt that they had said what they wanted to say. Doctors all believed that Jia Sheng's talent was outstanding and unparalleled. Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty also liked him very much and promoted him to Taizhong doctor within a year. Jia Yi believed that it had been more than twenty years since the founding of the Western Han Dynasty and Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty had reached peace in the world. It was the time to correct the calendar, change the colors of clothes, establish systems, determine official names, and revitalize rituals and music. So he drafted various rituals, advocating yellow, following the theory of the five elements, and creating official names, which completely changed the old laws of the Qin Dynasty. Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty had just ascended the throne and was too modest to make concessions in time. However, subsequent changes in various laws and regulations, as well as the fact that princes must go to the fiefdom to take office, were all Jia Yi's ideas. So Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty discussed with his ministers and wanted to promote Jia Yi to the position of public minister. However, Jianghou Zhou Bo, Guan Ying, Dongyang Hou, Feng Jing and others were jealous of him, so they slandered Jia Yi and said: This Luoyang man is young and has little knowledge. He only wants to monopolize power and make political affairs a mess. After that, Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty alienated Jia Yi, no longer adopted his opinions, and appointed him as the Grand Tutor of Changsha.
target: After Qu Yuan's death, Chu scholars like Song Yu imitated his style but lacked his boldness. Chu weakened and was conquered by Qin decades later. Over a century later, Jia Yi of the Han Dynasty, while serving as Grand Tutor of Changsha, wrote a poem to honor Qu Yuan. Jia Yi, a talented young scholar from Luoyang, was favored by Emperor Wen of Han but slandered by officials like Zhou Bo, leading to his demotion.

id: 史记/七十列传/屈原贾生列传::group-004
article_path: 史记/七十列传/屈原贾生列传
source: The big fish that dominates the world will eventually be controlled by ants. In Jia Yi's third year as the Prince of Changsha, an owl flew into his residence and landed next to his seat. The people of Chu called the owl Fu. Jia Yi originally came to Changsha because he was demoted, and Changsha has a low-lying terrain and a humid climate, so he thought that his life would not be long, and he was sad and sad, so he wrote a poem to comfort himself. The poem reads: In the early summer of April of the Dingmao year, when the sun was setting on Gengzi Day, an owl flew into my house. It stopped next to the seat, looking so relaxed and at ease.
target: He wrote "Ode to the Birds" to console himself, reflecting on the cyclical nature of fortune and the futility of worldly concerns.

id: 史记/七十列传/屈原贾生列传::group-005
article_path: 史记/七十列传/屈原贾生列传
source: More than a year later, Jia Yi was recalled to the capital to meet the emperor. At that time, Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty was sitting in the propaganda room, receiving blessings from God. Because Emperor Wen was interested in ghosts and gods, he asked Jia Yi about the origin of ghosts and gods. Jia Yi took the opportunity to explain in detail the various situations that led to the occurrence of ghosts and gods. By midnight, Emperor Wen was so absorbed in listening that he unconsciously moved towards Jia Yi in his seat. After listening, Emperor Wen sighed: I haven't seen Jia Yi for a long time. I thought I could surpass him, but now it seems I'm still not as good as him. Soon after, Emperor Wen appointed Jia Yi as the Taifu of King Lianghuai. King Lianghuai was the youngest son of Emperor Wen of Han Dynasty. He was favored by Emperor Wen and liked to read, so he asked Jia Yi to be his teacher. Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty also granted the title of Liehou to the four sons of King Li of Huainan. Jia Yi advised him, believing that the rise of national disasters would start from here. Jia Yi appealed to the emperor many times, saying that some princes had too many fiefdoms, even covering several counties, which was inconsistent with the ancient system, and their power should be gradually weakened, but Emperor Wen of Han refused to listen. A few years later, King Liang Huai fell off his horse and died due to careless riding, leaving no descendants. Jia Yi believed that he had failed to fulfill his responsibilities as a tutor. He was very sad and cried for more than a year before he died. He was only thirty-three years old when he died. Later, Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty passed away and Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty ascended the throne and promoted Jia Yi's two grandsons to serve as county guards. Among them, Jia Jia was the most eager to learn. He inherited Jia Yi's family business and had exchanges of letters with me. By the time of Emperor Zhao of the Han Dynasty, he held the post of Jiuqing. Tai Shigong said: After reading "Li Sao", "Heavenly Questions", "Calling the Soul" and "Ai Ying", I felt very sorry for Qu Yuan's ambition. When I came to Changsha and visited the place where Qu Yuan drowned himself in the river, I couldn't help but shed tears and miss him as a person. After reading Jia Sheng's poem in memory of Qu Yuan, I privately blamed Qu Yuan for his talent. If he went to lobby the princes, which country would not tolerate him? And actually put himself in such a situation! After reading "Ode to the Birds", I realized that life and death were treated equally, and the ups and downs of one's life experience were not taken seriously. I couldn't help but feel at a loss.
target: Later, he served as tutor to King Liang Huai, who died in a riding accident. Jia Yi, blaming himself, died of grief at age 33. The historian Sima Qian, after reading Qu Yuan's works and Jia Yi's poems, initially criticized Qu Yuan for not seeking refuge elsewhere but later, after reading "Ode to the Birds," understood his equanimity toward life and death.

id: 史记/七十列传/平原君虞卿列传::group-000

source: Zhao Sheng, Lord of Pingyuan, was a young master of the State of Zhao. Among the many princes, Zhao Sheng was the most virtuous and talented. He was hospitable and cultivated scholars. There were about thousands of guests who came to his sect. Lord Pingyuan served as the prime minister of King Zhao Huiwen and King Xiaocheng. He left the position of prime minister three times and was reinstated three times. His fiefdom was in Dongwu City. Mr. Pingyuan's house has a tall building facing the houses below. There was a lame man in the house who always limped out to fetch water. A beautiful concubine of Mr. Pingyuan lived upstairs. One day she looked down and saw the lame man fetching water, and she burst out laughing. The next day, the cripple came to Lord Pingyuan's house and asked: "I heard that you love scholars. The reason why scholars are not afraid of traveling thousands of miles to join your family is because you value scholars and despise concubines." I was unfortunately ill and disabled, but your concubine was laughing at me from a high building. I wanted to get the head of the person who laughed at me. Mr. Pingyuan smiled and replied: "Okay."
target: Zhao Sheng, Lord of Pingyuan, was a virtuous and talented young master of the State of Zhao, known for hosting thousands of scholars. He served as prime minister under Kings Huiwen and Xiaocheng, leaving and returning to the position three times, with his fief in Dongwu City. A crippled man fetching water near his home was laughed at by one of Lord Pingyuan’s concubines. The cripple demanded her head, but Lord Pingyuan initially refused, causing many scholars to leave. He later killed the concubine and apologized to the cripple, regaining his guests.

id: 史记/七十列传/平原君虞卿列传::group-001
article_path: 史记/七十列传/平原君虞卿列传
source: I didn't kill that person after all. More than a year later, more than half of the guests and diners on errands left one after another. Mr. Pingyuan felt very strange about this situation and said: I, Zhao Sheng, never dare to be rude in all aspects of my treatment of gentlemen, but why are so many people leaving me? A retainer stepped forward and replied: Because you did not kill the concubine who laughed at the cripple, everyone thought that you liked beauty and despised the scholars, so the scholars left one after another. So Lord Pingyuan cut off the head of the concubine who laughed at the cripple. He personally visited the lame man's house and offered it to him, and took the opportunity to apologize to him. From then on, the original guests came back one after another. At that time, Qi State had Lord Mengchang, Wei State had Lord Xinling, and Chu State had Lord Chunshen. They were all hospitable to scholars, so they competed to be more courteous to scholars than others in order to attract more talents to themselves. When the Qin State besieged Handan, King Zhao sent Lord Pingyuan to ask for help. At that time, he planned to recommend Chu as the leader of the alliance and make a joint alliance to fight against Qin. Lord Pingyuan agreed to go to Chu State with twenty of his followers who were brave, resourceful, and capable of both civil and military affairs. Mr. Pingyuan said: It would be best if we can succeed through polite negotiations. If the negotiation fails to succeed, then the king of Chu will be coerced to confirm the alliance in public, and he must confirm the alliance before returning home. The civil and military people who are going with me don’t have to look outside. It’s enough to choose from the diners under my sect. In the end, nineteen people were selected, and there was nothing left to choose from. There was no way to gather twenty people. At this time, a man named Mao Sui among the diners walked up to the front and recommended himself to Lord Pingyuan: I heard that you are going to Chu State, and let Chu State be the leader of the alliance to make an alliance. You also agreed to go with twenty diners, and no one will go outside to search. There is still one person missing now, I hope you can use me to recharge and go together. Mr. Pingyuan asked: How many years has it been since Mr. Wang stayed with me? Mao Sui replied: It has been three years now. Mr. Pingyuan said: A talented wise man living in the world is like an awl placed in a pocket, its sharp edge will be revealed immediately. It has been three years since your husband has been under my care for three years now. None of my close ministers have ever praised or recommended you, and I have never heard of you. This is because your husband has no expertise. Sir, you can't go. Sir, please stay. Mao Sui said: I just want to put it in my pocket today. If I had been placed in the pocket, the entire cone would have been exposed, not just the tip. Lord Pingyuan finally agreed to let Mao Sui go with him. The nineteen people winked at each other and laughed at Mao Sui secretly, but did not make a sound. When Mao Sui arrived in Chu, he discussed and argued with the nineteen people about the situation in the world. All nineteen people admired him. The Lord of Pingyuan negotiated with the King of Chu to establish a joint alliance. They repeatedly stated their interests. They negotiated from morning until noon until no decision was made. The nineteen people encouraged Mao Sui and said: "Sir, please come to the court."
target: When Qin besieged Handan, Lord Pingyuan sought help from Chu to form an alliance. He needed twenty followers but could only find nineteen. Mao Sui, a retainer for three years, volunteered. Lord Pingyuan doubted his abilities, but Mao Sui argued that if placed in a pocket, the entire awl would show, not just its tip. Mao Sui joined and impressed the others. In Chu, negotiations stalled until Mao Sui confronted the King of Chu, threatening him and highlighting Chu’s past defeats by Qin. The king agreed to the alliance, and Mao Sui sealed it with a blood oath. Lord Pingyuan later praised Mao Sui as more powerful than an army.

id: 史记/七十列传/平原君虞卿列传::group-002

source: If the Qin army breaks Zhao, how can you have these things? If the State of Zhao can be preserved, why would you worry about not having these things? Now you can really order all the members below the wife to be organized into the soldiers, and they will be responsible for the labor of guarding the city, and distribute all the things in the house for the soldiers to enjoy. When the soldiers are in crisis and hardship, it is easy to be grateful. So Pingyuan Jun adopted Li Tong's advice and got 3,000 soldiers who dared to risk their lives. Li Tong joined a team of 3,000 people and rushed to the Qin army for a decisive battle. As a result, the Qin army was pushed back thirty miles. At this time, it happened that reinforcements from Chu and Wei arrived, and the Qin army withdrew, and Handan was preserved. Li Tong was killed in battle with the Qin army, and his father was granted the title of Marquis Li. Yu Qing wanted to request additional fiefdoms for Lord Pingyuan on the grounds that Lord Xinling sent troops to save Zhao and saved Handan. When Gongsun Long heard the news, he drove overnight to see Lord Pingyuan and said: I heard that Yu Qing wanted to ask for additional fiefs on your behalf on the grounds that Lord Xinling sent troops to save Zhao and saved Handan. Is this true? Mr. Pingyuan replied: Yes. Gongsun Long said: This is very inappropriate. It is said that the monarch appointed you as the prime minister of Zhao State, not because your intelligence and talent are unique to Zhao State and no one else has them. The title of Dongwu City is granted to you not because of your meritorious deeds, but because you are a close relative of the monarch. You didn't refuse to accept the seal because you were incompetent, and you didn't refuse to accept the title because you had no merit. It was also because you considered yourself a close relative of the monarch. Now Lord Xinling has sent troops to save Handan and you ask for an increase in the number of fiefs. This is because you accepted the fiefs as close relatives when you had no merit, but when you did meritorious service, you asked for rewards based on ordinary people's merits. This is obviously very inappropriate. Moreover, Yu Qing holds the initiative on both sides of success and failure.
