If the thing succeeds, he will ask for compensation like a deed to collect debt; if the thing does not succeed, he will use the false name of claiming credit for you to make you grateful to him. You must not listen to his advice. Lord Pingyuan then rejected Yu Qing's suggestion. Lord Pingyuan died in the fifteenth year of King Zhao Xiaocheng's reign. Lord Pingyuan's descendants inherited his title from generation to generation, and his descendants were finally cut off when the Zhao Kingdom was destroyed.
target: After returning, Chu and Wei sent reinforcements, but Handan remained in danger. Li Tong advised Lord Pingyuan to mobilize his household and distribute resources to the people, gaining 3,000 volunteers. Li Tong died in battle, pushing Qin back thirty miles, and Handan was saved when reinforcements arrived. Yu Qing sought additional fiefs for Lord Pingyuan, but Gongsun Long argued against it, noting Lord Pingyuan’s position and fief were due to kinship, not merit, and that Yu Qing’s proposal was self-serving. Lord Pingyuan rejected the request. Lord Pingyuan died in the fifteenth year of King Xiaocheng’s reign, and his descendants held the title until Zhao’s fall.

id: 史记/七十列传/平原君虞卿列传::group-003
article_path: 史记/七十列传/平原君虞卿列传
source: Lord Pingyuan then rejected Yu Qing's suggestion. Lord Pingyuan died in the fifteenth year of King Zhao Xiaocheng's reign. Lord Pingyuan's descendants inherited his title from generation to generation, and his descendants were finally cut off when the Zhao Kingdom was destroyed. Lord Pingyuan treated Gongsun Long very kindly. Gongsun Long was good at debating the "Li Jian Bai" proposition. When Zou Yan visited Zhao State, he discussed the most upright principles and refuted Gongsun Long's famous debate proposition. After that, Lord Pingyuan dismissed Gongsun Long. Yu Qing was a talented person who was good at lobbying. He wore straw sandals and an umbrella on his shoulders and came all the way to lobby King Zhao Xiaocheng. When he visited King Zhao for the first time, King Zhao gave him a hundred yi of gold and a pair of white jade. When he visited King Zhao for the second time, he became the minister of Zhao, so he was called Yu Qing. Qin and Zhao fought in Changping. Zhao was unfavorable in the first battle and lost one captain. King Zhao summoned Lou Chang and Yu Qing to discuss the situation and said: "Our army did not go well in the first battle and the captain died in battle. I will roll up my armor and go to the enemy to fight the Qin army. What do you think?" Lou Chang said: If there is no benefit, it is better to send important envoys to seek peace. Yu Qing said: The reason why Lou Chang advocated for peace was that he believed that if he did not seek peace, our army would be defeated. But the initiative to control the peace talks lies with Qin.
target: He treated Gongsun Long well but dismissed him after Zou Yan refuted his debates. Yu Qing, a skilled lobbyist, advised King Zhao against ceding land to Qin after the Changping defeat, proposing instead to ally with Qi. King Zhao initially agreed but later followed Lou Huan’s advice to cede land, leading to further conflict. Yu Qing eventually fled to Daliang, where he wrote “Yu’s Spring and Autumn Annals,” criticizing political failures.

id: 史记/七十列传/平原君虞卿列传::group-004
article_path: 史记/七十列传/平原君虞卿列传
source: The current situation is that Wei is willing to bear the disaster as a small country, but you refuse to enjoy the fruits as a big country. So I say that the king is wrong, and the state of Wei is also wrong. I personally think that a vertical alliance is beneficial. King Zhao said: OK. So he made an alliance with Wei State. Because of Wei Qi, the Prime Minister of Wei State, Yu Qing preferred to abandon the title of Marquis of Wanhu and the Prime Minister's seal, and fled from a small road with Wei Qi. Finally, he left Zhao State and was trapped in Daliang of Wei State. After Wei Qi's death, Yu Qing became even more dissatisfied. He wrote a book, collected historical facts from "Spring and Autumn", observed the modern world situation, and wrote a total of eight articles: "Jieyi", "Title", "Speculation" and "Political Strategy". It is used to criticize the success and failure of national politics. It has been circulated in the world and is called "Yu's Spring and Autumn Annals". Tai Shigong said: Mr. Pingyuan is a handsome and talented son in troubled times, but he cannot understand the overall situation. As the saying goes: greed for personal gain will lead to loss of reason. Lord Pingyuan believed in Feng Ting's heresy and coveted the Shangdang he gave, which led to the Zhao State's defeat in Changping, more than 400,000 Zhao soldiers were killed, and the Zhao State was almost destroyed. Yu Qing analyzed the affairs, speculated on the situation, and made suggestions for the State of Zhao. How thoughtful and ingenious he was! In the end, I couldn't bear to watch Wei Qi being hunted down, and finally found himself in trouble in Daliang. Ordinary people knew they couldn't do this, let alone talented people. But if Yu Qing had not been poor and sad, he would not have been able to write books and make his reputation known to the world and pass on to future generations.
target: Tai Shigong noted that Lord Pingyuan, though talented, failed to grasp the bigger picture, leading to Zhao’s defeat at Changping and the loss of 400,000 soldiers. Yu Qing’s plans were thoughtful, but his inability to avoid trouble in Daliang highlighted his flaws, though his writings ensured his legacy.

id: 史记/七十列传/平津侯主父列传::group-000
article_path: 史记/七十列传/平津侯主父列传
source: Prime Minister Gongsun Hong was from Xue County, Sichuan State, Qi Prefecture, and his cousin's name was Ji. When he was young, he worked as a prison officer in Xue County, but was dismissed due to his crimes. His family was poor and had to go to the beach to herd pigs. It wasn’t until he was in his forties that he studied the Spring and Autumn Annals and various works explaining the Spring and Autumn Annals. He raised his stepmother with filial piety and prudence. In the first year of Emperor Wu's founding, as soon as the emperor came to the throne, he recruited virtuous and literary people. At this time, Gongsun Hong was sixty years old. He was recruited to Beijing as a virtuous person and became a doctor. He was ordered to go on a mission to the Huns and reported the situation to Emperor Wu when he came back. The situation did not suit the emperor's wishes. The emperor was angry and thought Gongsun Hong was incompetent, so Gongsun Hong was excused from his post and returned home on the pretext of illness. In the fifth year of Emperor Yuanguang's reign, the emperor issued an edict to recruit literature, and the Sichuan Kingdom recommended Gongsun Hong. Gongsun Hong refused to give in to the people and said: I have gone west to the capital to accept the emperor's appointment, but I resigned from office because of incompetence and returned. Hope to change the recommended candidate. However, the people of the country resolutely recommended Gongsun Hong, and Gongsun Hong went to Taichang. Taichang asked the more than 100 Confucian scholars recruited to make countermeasures respectively, and Gongsun Hong's countermeasures articles were ranked last. All countermeasure articles were sent to the emperor, and Emperor Wu promoted Gongsun Hong's countermeasure article to first place. Gongsun Hong was summoned to see the emperor. Emperor Wu saw that he was very beautiful and made him a doctor. At this time, the Han Dynasty opened a road to the southwestern Yi and set up counties and counties there. The people of Bashu felt poor about this, and the emperor ordered Gongsun Hong to inspect it.
target: Prime Minister Gongsun Hong, from Xue County in Qi Prefecture, began his career as a prison officer but was dismissed due to crimes. His family was poor, and he herded pigs until his forties, when he studied the Spring and Autumn Annals. He raised his stepmother with filial piety. At age sixty, during Emperor Wu's reign, he was recruited as a virtuous person and became a doctor. After a mission to the Xiongnu displeased the emperor, he was dismissed and returned home. In the fifth year of Yuanguang, he was recommended again, despite initial reluctance, and his countermeasure essay was promoted to first place by Emperor Wu, who made him a doctor. He inspected the southwestern Yi region but advised against further development, which the emperor ignored.

id: 史记/七十列传/平津侯主父列传::group-001
article_path: 史记/七十列传/平津侯主父列传
source: Gongsun Hong returned from his inspection and reported to the emperor that it was useless to try his best to slander the southwestern barbarians. The emperor did not adopt his opinions. Gongsun Hong was a majestic and strange man with extensive knowledge. He often said that the fault of the master is that he is not broad-minded, and the fault of the minister is that he is not frugal. Gongsun Hong covered himself with a quilt and did not eat more than two kinds of meat or vegetables when eating. When his stepmother died, he stayed in mourning for three years.
target: Gongsun Hong was known for his frugality, covering himself with a quilt and eating simple meals.

id: 史记/七十列传/平津侯主父列传::group-002
article_path: 史记/七十列传/平津侯主父列传
source: When his stepmother died, he stayed in mourning for three years. Every time he went to court to discuss political affairs with everyone, he always stated various things at the beginning and let the emperor make his own decisions. He refused to refute him face to face or argue in court. So the emperor observed him and found that he was honest in character, good at talking, familiar with documents, laws and official affairs, and he could also use Confucian views to embellish him. The emperor liked him very much. Within two years, he was promoted to Zuo Neishi. Gongsun Hong reported matters to the emperor, but sometimes they were not accepted and he did not argue in the court. He once asked the emperor to meet him in his spare time with his lord lieutenant Ji An. Ji An first asked the emperor a question, and Gongsun Hong then explained the problem clearly, and the emperor was often very happy. Everything he said was accepted. From then on, Gongsun Hong became closer to the emperor day by day, and his status became more prominent. He had made an agreement in advance with the ministers about the issues he wanted to discuss with the emperor, but when he came before the emperor, he broke the agreement and obeyed the emperor's will. Ji An rebuked Gongsun Hong at the court and said: Most of the people in Qi are deceitful and have no true feelings. He made this suggestion with us at the beginning, but now they have all violated it and are not loyal. The emperor asked Gongsun Hong, and Gongsun Hong apologized and said: People who know me think I am loyal, people who don't know me think I am disloyal. The emperor agreed with Gongsun Hong's statement. The favored ministers around the emperor often slandered Gongsun Hong, but the emperor treated Gongsun Hong more and more favorably. In the third year of Emperor Wu's Yuanshuo reign, Zhang Ou was dismissed from office, and the emperor appointed Gongsun Hong as the imperial censor. At this time, the Han Dynasty was opening up the southwestern barbarians, setting up Canghai County in the east and Shuofang County in the north. Gongsun Hong repeatedly advised the emperor, believing that these practices were exhausting China and running useless places, and hoped to stop doing these things. Therefore, Emperor Wu asked Zhu Maichen and others to use the favorable situation of setting up Shuofang County to question Gongsun Hong. Zhu Maichen and others asked ten questions, but Gongsun Hong couldn't answer any of them. Gongsun Hong apologized and said: I am a humble person from Shandong. I didn't know the benefits of building Shuo County. I hope to stop connecting with the southwestern Yi and setting up Canghai County, and concentrate on running Shuofang County.
target: He mourned his stepmother for three years. In court, he avoided direct confrontation, letting the emperor decide. He was promoted to Zuo Neishi within two years. He often agreed with the emperor's will, even breaking prior agreements with ministers, leading to accusations of deceit from Ji An. Gongsun Hong apologized, claiming loyalty was misunderstood. Despite slander, the emperor favored him. In the third year of Yuanshuo, he became imperial censor. He advised against expanding into the southwestern barbarians and Canghai County, focusing on Shuofang County instead. When questioned by Zhu Maichen, he couldn't answer and apologized.

id: 史记/七十列传/平津侯主父列传::group-003
article_path: 史记/七十列传/平津侯主父列传
source: I have the noble status of the Three Lords but I cover myself with a blanket. It is indeed a clever deception in an attempt to gain a good reputation. Moreover, I heard that Guan Zhong was the prime minister of Qi and had three residences. His luxury was comparable to that of the king of Qi. Duke Huan of Qi relied on Guan Zhong to dominate, which was also an act of disrespect for the superior king. Yan Ying was the prime minister of Qi Jinggong. He did not eat more than two kinds of meat and vegetables during meals, and his concubines did not wear silk clothes. Qi State was governed very well. This is because Yan Ying looked after the people below. Now that I am a royal censor, I am covered with a quilt. This means that there is no distinction between high and low among officials from Jiuqing and below, just like what Ji An said. Besides, without Ji An's loyalty, how could His Majesty hear these words! Emperor Wu thought that Gongsun Hong was humble and courteous, so he treated him more favorably. Finally, he made Gongsun Hong the prime minister and granted him the title of Marquis of Pingjin. Gongsun Hong was suspicious and jealous, magnanimous on the outside, but deep inside. Those who had enmity with Gongsun Hong, although Gongsun Hong got along well with them on the surface, he secretly caused trouble to others and took revenge. It was Gongsun Hong's idea to kill his father Yan and reassign Dong Zhongshu to Jiaoxi as prime minister. He only ate a meat dish and shelled coarse rice for each meal. His old friends and his favorite hangers-on all relied on him to provide food and clothing. Gongsun Hong's salary was used to provide for them, and the family had no money left.
target: Ji An accused him of fraud for his frugality, but Gongsun Hong defended himself, citing historical examples. The emperor made him prime minister and Marquis of Pingjin. Gongsun Hong was outwardly magnanimous but inwardly vengeful, causing harm to enemies like Dong Zhongshu. He supported old friends with his salary, leaving no savings.

id: 史记/七十列传/平津侯主父列传::group-004
article_path: 史记/七十列传/平津侯主父列传
source: I was lucky enough to inherit the throne in the past, but I was afraid of being unrest and wanted to rule the world together with all the ministers. You should know this. Gentlemen like kind people and hate ugly people. If you act carefully, you can always stay by my side. Unfortunately, you are suffering from frost, dew, wind and cold. Why worry about not being cured? You actually submitted a letter to Hou Yin, resigned and returned home. This is to show my immorality! Now that things are a little less complicated, you should reduce your thoughts, concentrate, and use medical assistance for treatment. Therefore, Emperor Wu allowed Gongsun Hong to continue his leave and gave him cattle, wine and various cloths. After a few months, Gongsun Hong's condition improved greatly, and he began to deal with political affairs. The year before last, Gongsun Hong fell ill and eventually died as prime minister. His son Gongsun Du inherited the title of Marquis of Pingjin. Gongsun Du had been the governor of Shanyang for more than ten years, but he lost his title as a marquis for breaking the law. Zhu Fuyan was a native of Linyi, Qidi. He studied the theories of political advisors during the Warring States Period. In his later years, he began to study the Zhouyi, Spring and Autumn Annals, and the theories of hundreds of schools of thought. He traveled among many scholars in Qi, but no one was willing to treat him favorably. Many scholars in Qi State rejected him together, making it impossible for him to stay in Qi State. His family was poor and he couldn't borrow money from others, so he went to Yan, Zhao and Zhongshan in the north to study. No one in any place treated him favorably, so it was difficult to be a guest. In the first year of Emperor Xiaowu's Yuanguang year, he thought that all the vassal states were not worthy of study tours, so he went west to Hanguguan to meet General Wei Qing. General Wei Qing recommended him to the emperor many times, but the emperor refused to summon him. The money he brought had been spent, and he had been staying in Chang'an for a long time. The guests of the princes hated him, so he wrote to the emperor. In the morning he presented the memorial, and in the evening the emperor summoned him.
target: During the Huainan and Hengshan rebellions, he fell ill and wrote to the emperor, citing his inadequacy and offering to resign. The emperor refused, granting him leave and gifts. He recovered but eventually died as prime minister. His son Gongsun Du inherited the title but lost it for breaking the law. Zhu Fuyan, from Linyi, studied political theories and later the Zhouyi and Spring and Autumn Annals. Poor and rejected by scholars, he traveled to various states without success. In Yuanguang's first year, he sought an audience with General Wei Qing, who recommended him, but the emperor ignored him. After spending his money, he wrote a memorial, which led to an immediate summons. His advice included warnings against war with the Xiongnu, citing Qin and Han failures. He advocated for frugality and caution, referencing historical precedents.

id: 史记/七十列传/平津侯主父列传::group-005
article_path: 史记/七十列传/平津侯主父列传
source: Xu Le and Yan An's memorials were sent to the emperor. The emperor summoned his father Yan, Xu Le and Yan An and said to them: "Where are you all?" Why did we meet so late? So Emperor Wu appointed the three of them as doctors. Master Fu Yan visited the emperor many times and discussed political affairs. The emperor ordered him to be appointed as an emissary, and he was promoted to a senior official. In one year, Zhu Fuyan's position was promoted four times.
target: The emperor appointed him and others as doctors, and Zhu Fuyan was promoted four times in a year.

id: 史记/七十列传/平津侯主父列传::group-006
article_path: 史记/七十列传/平津侯主父列传
source: Gongsun Hong said: During the Qin Dynasty, 300,000 people were mobilized to build the city north of the Yellow River, but it was not completed and was soon abandoned. Zhufu Yansheng thought it was beneficial, but the emperor actually adopted Zhufu Yan's strategy and established Shuofang County. In the second year of Yuanshuo, the master's father Yan told the emperor about Qi King Liu Cijing's promiscuous and eccentric behavior in the palace, and the emperor appointed him as the prime minister of Qi. The master's father came to the state of Qi, summoned his brothers and guests, distributed five hundred gold to them, and scolded them: "When I was poor at first, my brothers did not give me food and clothing, and my guests did not let me in. Now that I have made a formal appearance, some of the kings have gone thousands of miles away to welcome me." I have severed all relations with you. Please do not enter my master's father's house again! So he sent someone to touch King Qi with the adultery between King Qi and his sister. King Qi thought that he could not escape the blame after all, and was afraid of being sentenced to death like King Yan Liu Dingguo, so he committed suicide. The official in charge reported the matter to the emperor. When Zhufu Yan first became a commoner, he traveled to Yan and Zhao. When he became a high official, he exposed the secrets of King Yan. The King of Zhao was afraid that he would become a scourge to the State of Zhao, and wanted to write to the emperor to tell his secrets, because his father was buried in the court and he did not dare to expose it. When he became the Prime Minister and walked out of Hangu Pass, the King of Zhao sent a letter to accuse his father Yan of accepting bribes from the princes. Therefore, many of the princes' sons were made princes for this reason. When the King of Qi committed suicide, the emperor was furious when he heard about it. He thought that the master father Yan had threatened his king to commit suicide, so he handed it over to the officials for interrogation. Zhu Fuyan admitted to accepting bribes from the princes, but actually did not threaten the King of Qi to commit suicide. The emperor did not want to kill Zhufu Yan. At this time, Gongsun Hong, the imperial censor, said to the emperor: The King of Qi committed suicide and had no descendants. The feudal state was abolished and turned into a county and returned to the imperial court. Zhufu Yan is the chief culprit in this matter. Your Majesty will not be able to explain it to the people of the world unless he kills Zhufu Yan. So the emperor killed everyone in the father's family. When the master's father Yan was being favored by dignitaries, there were thousands of guests. When he was exterminated and died, no one collected his body. Only Kongche, a man from Mixian County, collected his body and buried him. The emperor later heard about this and thought that Kong Che was an elder. Tai Shigong said: Although Gongsun Hong's moral behavior is beautiful, it is also because he encountered a good opportunity. It has been more than eighty years since the founding of the Han Dynasty. The emperor was advocating Confucianism and recruiting talents with outstanding talents to develop Confucianism and Mohism. Gongsun Hong was the selected person. Master Fu Yan was in an important position, and all the high-ranking officials in the court praised him. But when his reputation was ruined and he was killed, the scholars were all vying to talk about his bad qualities. How sad! The Empress Dowager Wang Zhengjun issued an edict to the Grand Situ Ma Palace and the Grand Sikong Zhenfeng: I heard that the way to govern a country is to first make the people rich; the key to making the people rich is frugality.
target: Zhu Fuyan advised dividing the territories of princes to weaken their power, which the emperor adopted. He also suggested moving powerful families to Maoling. He exposed secrets of King Yan and King Qi, leading to their deaths. Accused of bribery, he was executed after Gongsun Hong argued his guilt. His guests abandoned him, but Kong Che buried him. Tai Shigong noted Gongsun Hong's success due to timing and Zhu Fuyan's tragic end. Empress Dowager Wang Zhengjun praised Gongsun Hong's frugality and virtue, citing his example as a model for officials. His descendants were granted titles and lands.

id: 史记/七十列传/廉颇蔺相如列传::group-000
article_path: 史记/七十列传/廉颇蔺相如列传
source: Lian Po was an outstanding general of Zhao State. In the sixteenth year of King Zhao Huiwen, Lian Po led the Zhao army to conquer Qi, defeated the Qi army, captured Yangjin, and was named Shangqing by King Zhao. He was famous among the princes and countries for his bravery in battle. Lin Xiangru was a native of the State of Zhao and a retainer of the family of the eunuch Ling Muxian of the State of Zhao. During the reign of King Zhao Huiwen, he obtained the Heshi Bi from Chu State. When King Zhao of Qin heard about this, he sent a letter to King Zhao, expressing his willingness to exchange fifteen cities for He's Bi. King Zhao discussed with General Lian Po and his ministers: If he gave the jade to Qin, it would be impossible for Qin's cities to be obtained and they would be deceived in vain; if he didn't give it, he would be afraid that the Qin army would attack Zhao immediately. The countermeasures were not discussed, and I tried to find an envoy who could be sent to Qin to reply, but I couldn't find one. The eunuch ordered Miao Xian to say: "My retainer Lin Xiangru can go to Qin as an envoy."
target: Lian Po, a renowned general of Zhao, conquered Qi and captured Yangjin, earning the title of Shangqing. Lin Xiangru, a retainer of eunuch Miao Xian, was sent as an envoy to Qin after King Zhao of Qin offered fifteen cities for the He's Bi jade. Lin Xiangru successfully returned the jade intact to Zhao after King Qin failed to honor the exchange. Later, at the Mianchi meeting, Lin Xiangru forced King Qin to play a fou, maintaining Zhao's dignity. For his efforts, he was named Shangqing, ranking above Lian Po.

id: 史记/七十列传/廉颇蔺相如列传::group-001
article_path: 史记/七十列传/廉颇蔺相如列传
source: He also threatened: If I meet Lin Xiangru, I will definitely humiliate him. After hearing this, Xiangru refused to meet him. Whenever Lin Xiangru went to court, he often used illness as an excuse to hide at home, unwilling to compete with Lian Po for ranking. Not long after, Xiangru went out, and Lin Xiangru went out in a carriage. He saw Lian Po from a distance, and Lin Xiangru quickly asked someone to turn the car around to avoid it. So Xiangru's disciples came together to express their admonition, saying: "The reason why we leave our relatives to serve you is because we admire your noble integrity." Now you and Lian Po have the same official position. Mr. Lian speaks evil words, but you are afraid to hide from him. Your fear is too much. A mediocre person is ashamed, let alone a general! We people have no talent, please let us say goodbye! Lin Xiangru resolutely persuaded them to stay and said: Who do you think is more powerful than General Lian or the King of Qin? He replied: General Lian cannot compare with King Qin. Xiangru said: With the power of the King of Qin, I dare to scold him in the court and humiliate his ministers. Although I, Lin Xiangru, are incompetent, can I be afraid of General Lian? But I thought that the reason Qiang Qin did not dare to use troops against Zhao was because of the two of us. Now that the two tigers are fighting, they will inevitably not be able to coexist. The reason why I was so tolerant was to put the country's emergencies first and my personal grievances behind. When Lian Po heard these words, he took off his shirt, exposed his upper body, carried a thorn stick on his back, and was led by the guests to Lin Xiangru's door to apologize. He said: I am a rough and humble person, but I never thought that you, General, are so generous! The two finally reconciled and became friends through life and death. This year, Lian Po attacked Qi eastward and defeated one of its troops.
target: Lian Po, resentful of Lin Xiangru's higher rank, threatened to humiliate him. Lin Xiangru avoided conflict, prioritizing national unity over personal grievances. When Lian Po learned of this, he apologized, and the two became close friends. Lian Po later led successful campaigns against Qi and Wei.

id: 史记/七十列传/廉颇蔺相如列传::group-002
article_path: 史记/七十列传/廉颇蔺相如列传
source: When he was collecting taxes, Pingyuan Jun's family refused to pay. Zhao She punished him according to law and killed nine people in charge of Pingyuan Jun's family. Lord Pingyuan was furious and wanted to kill Zhao She. Zhao She took the opportunity to persuade and said: "You are a noble son in the State of Zhao. If you allow your retainers to disobey the government's laws now, the laws will be weakened. If the laws are weakened, the country will be weak. When the country is weak, the princes will send troops to invade. If the princes send troops to invade the Zhao country, it will perish. How can you keep this wealth?" With your status and honor, being able to abide by the law will make the country fair, and fairness will make the country strong. When the country is strong, the Zhao family's regime will be stable. As a noble relative of the Zhao country, will you be despised by the world? Lord Pingyuan thought he was very talented and recommended him to King Zhao. King Zhao appointed him in charge of the country's taxation. The country's taxation was very fair and reasonable, the people lived a prosperous life, and the national treasury was also very full.
target: Zhao She, a tax official, gained King Zhao's favor after punishing Lord Pingyuan's family for tax evasion. He was appointed to oversee national taxation, which prospered the people and treasury.

id: 史记/七十列传/廉颇蔺相如列传::group-003
article_path: 史记/七十列传/廉颇蔺相如列传
source: 军队离开邯郸三十里，赵奢就在军中下令说： 有谁来为军事进谏的就处以死刑。 The Qin army was stationed to the west of Wu'an. The sound of the Qin army beating drums and shouting for military training shook the roof tiles in Wu'an city. A scout in Zhao's army asked for urgent help from Wu'an, and Zhao She immediately beheaded him. Zhao Jun held on to the camp and stayed for twenty-eight days without advancing. Instead, he built more fortresses.
target: During the Qin siege of Yanyu, Zhao She led a daring rescue, defeating the Qin army and earning the title of Ma Fujun.

id: 史记/七十列传/廉颇蔺相如列传::group-004
article_path: 史记/七十列传/廉颇蔺相如列传
source: King Zhao said: Just put this matter aside. I have already decided. Zhao Kuo's mother then said: You must send him to lead the army. If he is incompetent, can I not be implicated? King Zhao agreed. After Zhao Kuo replaced Lian Po, he changed all the original rules and regulations and replaced the original military officials. When Qin general Bai Qi heard about this, he dispatched a surprise force, pretended to be defeated and fled, then cut off the Zhao army's food transport road, split the Zhao army in half, and separated the Zhao soldiers. After more than forty days, the Zhao army was hungry. Zhao Kuo sent out elite soldiers to fight the Qin army personally. The Qin army shot Zhao Kuo to death. Zhao Kuo's army was defeated, and hundreds of thousands of troops surrendered to the Qin army. The Qin army buried them all alive. From the beginning to the end of the Battle of Changping, Zhao State suffered a total of 450,000 losses. The next year, the Qin army surrounded Handan. The siege lasted for more than a year. Zhao could hardly survive. It was only through the rescue of the Chu and Wei armies that the siege of Handan was lifted. King Zhao finally did not implicate Zhao Kuo's mother because of her words.
target: After King Zhao Huiwen's death, King Xiaocheng ascended. In the Changping campaign, Lian Po initially held defensive positions against Qin. King Xiaocheng replaced him with Zhao Kuo, despite warnings from Lin Xiangru and Zhao Kuo's mother. Zhao Kuo's arrogance led to a disastrous defeat, with 450,000 Zhao soldiers killed. The Qin army later besieged Handan, which was relieved by Chu and Wei forces.

id: 史记/七十列传/廉颇蔺相如列传::group-005
article_path: 史记/七十列传/廉颇蔺相如列传
source: King Zhao finally did not implicate Zhao Kuo's mother because of her words. Five years after the siege of Handan was relieved, the Yan State adopted Li Fu's strategy. It was said that all the mature men of the Zhao State died in the Battle of Changping, and their orphans were not yet adults, so the King of Yan sent troops to attack Zhao. King Zhao sent Lian Po to lead the troops to counterattack, defeated the Yan army in Hacheng, killed Li Fu, and surrounded the capital of Yan. Yan State ceded five cities and asked for peace, and King Zhao agreed to a truce. King Zhao gave Wei Wen the title of Lord Xinping to Lian Po, and appointed him as acting prime minister. Lian Po was dismissed from his post in Changping and returned home. When he lost power, all his original followers left him.
target: Lian Po later defeated Yan, earning the title of Lord Xinping. After King Xiaocheng's death, Lian Po fled to Wei following a conflict with Lecheng.

id: 史记/七十列传/廉颇蔺相如列传::group-006
article_path: 史记/七十列传/廉颇蔺相如列传
source: Lian Po was furious and attacked Lecheng, but Lecheng escaped. Lian Po then fled to Daliang in Wei. The next year, Zhao State attacked Yan State with Li Mu as general and captured Wu Sui and Fangcheng. Lian Po had lived in Daliang for a long time, and Wei could not trust him. Since the State of Zhao was besieged by Qin soldiers many times, the King of Zhao wanted to use Lian Po as a general again, and Lian Po also wanted to be appointed by the State of Zhao again. King Zhao sent envoys to visit Lian Po to see if he could still be employed. Lian Po's enemy Guo Kai bribed the envoy with a large amount of money, asking him to speak ill of Lian Po when he came back. After the Zhao envoy met Lian Po, Lian Po ate a bushel of rice and ten kilograms of meat in front of him. He also put on his armor and mounted his horse, indicating that he could still be employed. The envoy from the State of Zhao went back and reported to King Zhao: Although General Lian is old and still has a good appetite, he pooped three times in a short period of time while sitting with me.
target: Zhao attempted to recall him, but a bribed envoy falsely reported his frailty, and he was not reinstated. Lian Po died in Chu.

id: 史记/七十列传/廉颇蔺相如列传::group-007
article_path: 史记/七十列传/廉颇蔺相如列传
source: So Li Mu prepared 1,300 carefully selected chariots, 13,000 selected war horses, 50,000 warriors who dared to charge into battle, and 100,000 soldiers who were good at shooting, and organized them all for training and combat. At the same time, large numbers of livestock were allowed to graze everywhere, and the entire wilderness was filled with people grazing. When a small group of Huns invaded, Li Mu pretended to be defeated. Li Mu deliberately abandoned thousands of people to the Huns. When Chanyu heard about this situation, he led a large number of troops to invade. Li Mu ambushed many strange soldiers, spread out his left and right wings to outflank the enemy and counterattacked, defeating the Xiongnu and killing more than 100,000 horses. He destroyed Xiu, defeated Donghu, surrendered Linhu, and Shanyu fled. For more than ten years after that, the Huns no longer dared to approach the border towns of Zhao. In the first year of King Zhao Daoxiang, after Lian Po had fled to Wei State, Zhao State sent Li Mu to attack Yan State and captured Wu Sui and Fangcheng. Two years later, Pang Nuan defeated the Yan army and killed Ju Xin. After another seven years, the Qin army defeated and killed the Zhao general Hu Zou at Wu Sui, and killed 100,000 Zhao soldiers. The State of Zhao then appointed Li Mu as its general, attacked the Qin army in Yi'an, defeated the Qin army, and drove away the Qin general Huan Jue. Li Mu was named Lord Wu'an. Three years later, the Qin army attacked Fanwu. Li Mu defeated the Qin army and moved south to resist South Korea and Wei. In the seventh year since King Zhao moved, the State of Qin sent Wang Jian to attack the State of Zhao, and the State of Zhao sent Li Mu and Sima Shang to resist the Qin army. The State of Qin bribed King Zhao's favored minister Guo Kai with a lot of money to let him carry out counterintuitive schemes and spread rumors that Li Mu and Sima Shang were going to rebel. The king of Zhao sent Zhao Cong and Qi general Yan Ju to replace Li Mu, but Li Mu refused to accept the order. King Zhao sent people to secretly arrest Li Mu, killed him, and removed Sima Shang from his official position. Three months later, Wang Jian took the opportunity to attack the State of Zhao, defeated the Zhao army, killed Zhao Cong, captured Zhao Wangqian and his general Yan Ju, and finally destroyed the State of Zhao.
target: Li Mu, a capable general, defended Zhao's northern border against the Xiongnu. Initially perceived as timid, he later ambushed and defeated the Xiongnu, securing peace for over a decade. He also achieved victories against Qin, earning the title of Lord Wu'an. However, King Zhao, influenced by rumors, executed Li Mu and removed Sima Shang. Three months later, Qin destroyed Zhao.

id: 史记/七十列传/廉颇蔺相如列传::group-008
article_path: 史记/七十列传/廉颇蔺相如列传
source: Tai Shigong said: If you know you are about to die and are not afraid, you must be very courageous; death is not difficult, but how to deal with this death is difficult. When Lin Xiangru held up a treasure and squinted at the court pillars, and scolded the King of Qin's attendants, considering the situation in front of him, the most he could do was to be killed. However, ordinary scholars often did not dare to behave like this because they were timid and cowardly. Once Xiangru inspired his courage, his power was unleashed to overwhelm the enemy. Later, he humbly gave in to Lian Po. His reputation was more important than Mount Tai. The wisdom and courage he showed in doing things can be said to be both!
target: Tai Shigong praised Lin Xiangru's courage and wisdom, noting his ability to intimidate enemies and later yield to Lian Po, prioritizing the state's interests.

id: 史记/七十列传/张丞相列传::group-000
article_path: 史记/七十列传/张丞相列传
source: Zhou Chang is simple, strong and upright, and he is as stubborn as wood and stone. Ren Ao was reused because of his kindness to Empress Lu in the past. Shen Tujia can be said to be a man of uprightness, perseverance, and noble moral character, but he neither understands power nor is knowledgeable. Compared with senior prime ministers such as Xiao He, Cao Shen, and Chen Ping, he is probably inferior. There were many prime ministers during the reign of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, so I will not name them one by one, nor record their origins, place of origin, dates of birth and death, conduct, deeds, etc. For the time being, I will record the prime ministers since Emperor Wu Zhenghe's reign.
target: The lives and careers of several prominent officials in the early Han Dynasty, focusing on their roles, achievements, and interactions with emperors.

id: 史记/七十列传/张丞相列传::group-001
article_path: 史记/七十列传/张丞相列传
source: Prime Minister Zhang Cang is from Yangwu. He likes books, music and calendars very much. During the Qin Dynasty, he served as the censor and was in charge of various documents and files in the palace. Later, because of the crime, he ran away and went home. When Pei Gong conquered the city and passed Yangwu, Zhang Cang followed Pei Gong as a guest to attack Nanyang. Later, Zhang Cang should be beheaded for breaking the law. When he took off his clothes and leaned on the instrument of torture, he was tall and big, with skin as plump and fair as gourd seeds. Wang Ling happened to see him and marveled at how good Zhang Cang was. Therefore, Wang Ling interceded with Pei Gong and pardoned his death penalty. In this way, Zhang Cang followed Pei Gong westward into Wuguan and arrived at Xianyang. Pei Gong was established as the king of Han, entered Hanzhong, and soon returned to pacify the Three Qin Dynasties. Chen Yu defeated Zhang Er, the king of Changshan, and Zhang Er surrendered to the king of Han. The king of Han appointed Zhang Cang as the governor of Changshan. He also followed Han Xin to attack Zhao, and Zhang Cang captured Chen Yu. After Zhao Di was pacified, the king appointed Zhang Cang as the Prime Minister of the country to guard against border enemies. Soon after, he was transferred to Zhao Guo Xiangguo to assist Zhao Wang Zhang Er. After Zhang Er died, he assisted Zhao Wang Zhang Ao. Then he was transferred to Dai Guo Xiangguo to assist Dai Wang. When King Zang Tu of Yan rebelled, Emperor Gaozu led troops to attack. Zhang Cang followed Emperor Gaozu as the acting prime minister for his meritorious service in attacking Zang Tu. In the sixth year of Emperor Gaozu's reign, he was granted the title of Marquis of Beiping, with a settlement of 1,200 households. Later, Zhang Cang was promoted to the position of Prime Minister in charge of financial management. Instead, he served as chief accountant as Liehou, a position he held for four years. At this time, Xiao He was serving as the prime minister, and Zhang Cang had been serving as the historian since the Qin Dynasty. He was very familiar with the world's books and various books. In addition, he was proficient in calculations, music and calendars, so he was ordered to stay in the prime minister's mansion as a prince and be responsible for managing the accounting books handed over by various counties. When Yingbu failed to rebel and fled, Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty appointed his son Liu Chang as king of Huainan and ordered Zhang Cang to assist him as prime minister. Fourteen years later, Zhang Cang was promoted to the imperial censor.
target: Prime Minister Zhang Cang, from Yangwu, was a scholar of books, music, and calendars. After serving as a Qin censor, he fled home due to a crime. He later joined Pei Gong (Emperor Gaozu) and was saved from execution by Wang Ling, who was impressed by his appearance. Zhang Cang served in various posts, including governor and prime minister of several states, and was granted the title of Marquis of Beiping. He became chief accountant and later imperial censor. As prime minister, he revised music and calendars, adhering to the Qin calendar and the virtue of water.

id: 史记/七十列传/张丞相列传::group-002
article_path: 史记/七十列传/张丞相列传
source: The emperor issued an edict to hand over the proposal to Zhang Cang for review. Zhang Cang thought it was not the case and threw the matter aside. But later Huanglong actually appeared in Chengji County, Tianshui County, so Emperor Wen summoned Gongsun Chen to the court and appointed him as a doctor, making him responsible for drafting a calendar system that conformed to Tu De. At the same time, the first year was changed. Prime Minister Zhang Cang therefore retired on his own, claiming that he had been ill for many years and would no longer go to court.
target: He lived to over a hundred years old, relying on wet nurses in his old age.

id: 史记/七十列传/张丞相列传::group-003
article_path: 史记/七十列传/张丞相列传
source: At this time, Xiao He was serving as the prime minister, and Zhang Cang had been serving as the historian since the Qin Dynasty. He was very familiar with the world's books and various books. In addition, he was proficient in calculations, music and calendars, so he was ordered to stay in the prime minister's mansion as a prince and be responsible for managing the accounting books handed over by various counties. When Yingbu failed to rebel and fled, Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty appointed his son Liu Chang as king of Huainan and ordered Zhang Cang to assist him as prime minister. Fourteen years later, Zhang Cang was promoted to the imperial censor. Zhou Chang was a native of Peixian County. He and his cousin Zhou Ke both served as soldiers of Surabaya during the Qin Dynasty. When Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty raised an army in Pei County, he defeated the governor and eunuch of Sishui County. In this way, the two brothers Zhou Chang and Zhou Ke followed Pei Gong with their qualifications as soldiers. Pei Gong appointed Zhou Chang to be in charge of the flag, and Zhou Ke was temporarily a guest in his tent. Later, they all followed Pei Gong into the Pass and overthrew the rule of Qiang Qin. Pei Gong was granted the title of King of Han, and the King of Han appointed Zhou Ke as Yushi Dafu and Zhou Chang as Lieutenant. In the fourth year of the Han Dynasty, the Chu army surrounded the Han Dynasty in Xingyang. The situation was urgent. The Han Dynasty quietly escaped and ordered Zhou Ke to stay in Xingyang City. The Chu army conquered Xingyang and wanted to appoint him as a general. Zhou Ke scolded him: You people should surrender to the king of Han quickly, otherwise you will be prisoners soon! Xiang Yu was furious after hearing this and immediately cooked and killed Zhou Ke.
target: Zhou Chang, from Peixian, served as a soldier under Pei Gong and became a lieutenant. After his cousin Zhou Ke was killed by Xiang Yu for refusing to surrender, Zhou Chang became imperial censor.

id: 史记/七十列传/张丞相列传::group-004
article_path: 史记/七十列传/张丞相列传
source: You really have no choice but to go away for me! So Zhou Chang, the imperial censor, was transferred to the position of Prime Minister of the State of Zhao. After Zhou Chang left, a long time passed. Gaozu held the official seal of the imperial censor in his hand, gently caressed it and said: Who is the most suitable candidate for the imperial censor? Then he looked at Zhao Yao carefully and said: No one is more suitable than Zhao Yao. In this way, Zhao Yao was appointed as the imperial censor. Zhao Yao also had military merits and food in the past. When he followed the imperial censor to attack Chen Xi and made meritorious service, he was named the Marquis of Jiangyi. After the death of Emperor Gaozu, Empress Dowager Lu sent an envoy to summon King Zhao to the court. Prime Minister Zhou Chang asked King Zhao to say that he was not in good health and could not go. The envoy went back and forth three times, but Zhou Changdu always insisted not to send King Zhao to Beijing. So Empress Lu was very worried and sent an envoy to summon Zhou Chang to the capital. After Zhou Chang came to Beijing, he met with Empress Lu. Empress Lu scolded him very angrily: Don't you know that I hate Mrs. Qi very much? But you didn't let King Zhao enter the capital, why? After Zhou Chang was summoned to the capital, Empress Lu sent an envoy to summon King Zhao. Soon, King Zhao came to the capital. More than a month after he arrived in Chang'an, he was forced to drink poison and died. Therefore, Zhou Chang claimed that he was recovering from illness and no longer went to court to see the Queen Mother. Three years later, he too died. Five years later, Gao Hou heard that the imperial censor Zhao Yao, the Marquis of Jiangyi, had made a plan to protect King Zhao Ruyi during the reign of Emperor Gaozu, so he removed his title of Marquis of Jiangyi to compensate for his crime, and made Ren Ao, Marquis of Guang'a, the censor. Ren Ao turned out to be a jailer in Peixian County. When Emperor Gaozu was still an ordinary citizen, he avoided lawsuits. The jailers could not find Emperor Gaozu himself, so they captured Empress Lu and disrespected her. Ren Ao, who had always been close to Emperor Gaozu, was very angry when he saw this, so he wounded the jailer who was detaining Empress Lu. When Emperor Gaozu began to raise troops, Ren Ao followed him as a guest, and later served as censor, stationed in Fengyi for two years. Emperor Gaozu established himself as King of Han, marched eastward to attack Xiang Yu, and promoted Ao to the post of governor of Shangdang County. When Chen Kui rebelled, Ren Ao held on to the city and was not captured by the rebels. For his meritorious service, he was granted the title of Marquis of Guang'a, with a settlement of 1,800 households. When he was in high school, he served as the imperial censor. Three years later, he was dismissed and appointed Pingyang Marquis Cao Cheng as the imperial censor. After the death of Empress Gao, Cao Cheng and his ministers jointly killed Lu Lu and others. Afterwards, he was removed from his official position and appointed Zhang Cang, the prime minister of the King of Huainan, as the imperial censor. Zhang Cang, Jianghou Zhou Bo and others jointly honored Dai Wang as Emperor Xiaowen. In the fourth year of Emperor Wen's reign, Prime Minister Guan Ying passed away and Zhang Cang succeeded him as Prime Minister.
target: He was known for his bluntness, once comparing Emperor Gaozu to tyrants. He opposed the emperor's plan to depose the crown prince, earning gratitude from Empress Lu. Later, he was appointed prime minister of Zhao to protect the young King Ruyi, despite his reluctance. After Gaozu's death, Empress Lu summoned King Zhao to court, leading to his death. Zhou Chang then feigned illness and died three years later. Zhao Yao, a young censor, advised Gaozu to appoint Zhou Chang as Zhao's prime minister. He later became imperial censor and was named Marquis of Jiangyi. After Gaozu's death, Empress Lu stripped him of his title for his role in protecting King Zhao. Ren Ao, a former jailer who aided Empress Lu, succeeded him as censor and was named Marquis of Guang'a. He was later dismissed, and Cao Cheng briefly served as censor before Zhang Cang was reappointed.

id: 史记/七十列传/张丞相列传::group-005
article_path: 史记/七十列传/张丞相列传
source: Zhang Lei, the son of Marquis Kang, succeeded to the throne. Eight years later, the titles and fiefdoms were revoked because he was guilty of disrespecting the princes after attending their funerals. In the past, Zhang Cang's father was less than five feet tall. After giving birth to Zhang Cang, Zhang Cang was eight feet tall. He was named a marquis and became a prime minister. Zhang Cang's son was also very tall, but his grandson Zhang Lei was a little over six feet tall. He lost his title because of a violation of the law. After Zhang Cang was dismissed as prime minister, he was already very old and had no teeth in his mouth. He could only live by sucking milk and used young women as his wet nurses. He had many wives and concubines, numbering around a hundred, and anyone who had ever given birth to a child was no longer favored. Zhang Cang finally lived to be more than a hundred years old before passing away. Prime Minister Shen Tujia was from Liang. As a warrior who could draw strong bows and crossbows, he followed Emperor Gao to attack Xiang Yu, and was promoted to a minor official called Duiliu due to his military exploits. When he followed Emperor Gao to attack the Yingbu rebels, he was promoted to captain.
target: Shen Tujia, from Liang, was a warrior who followed Emperor Gaozu and became prime minister under Emperor Wen.

id: 史记/七十列传/张丞相列传::group-006
article_path: 史记/七十列传/张丞相列传
source: Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty once went to his house to drink and have fun, which shows how much the emperor loved him. At that time, the Prime Minister Shen Tujia went to the court to pay homage to the emperor, but Deng Tong stood beside the emperor and neglected his etiquette. After Shen Tujia finished his speech, he continued: Your Majesty, you love your favorite and you can make him rich, but as for the etiquette in the court, you must take it seriously. The emperor said: Please stop talking, I just have a preference for Deng Tong. Shen Tujia came back from the court and sat in the Prime Minister's Mansion. He issued an order asking Deng Tong to come to the Prime Minister's Mansion. If he didn't come, Deng Tong would be beheaded. Deng Tong was very frightened and went to the palace to tell Emperor Wen. Emperor Wen said: "It's okay for you to go. I will send someone to summon you to the palace immediately." Deng Tong came to the Prime Minister's Mansion, took off his hat and shoes, kowtowed to Shen Tujia and apologized. Shen Tujia sat there casually, deliberately not treating him with courtesy, and at the same time scolded him: "The court is the court of Emperor Gaozu." You, Deng Tong, are just a minor minister, but you dare to play in the main hall. You are guilty of disrespect and should be beheaded. Whoever comes, execute it now and kill him! Deng Tong kowtowed and his head was bleeding, but Shen Tujia still didn't say spare him. Emperor Wen estimated that the prime minister had made Deng Tong suffer a lot, so he sent an envoy to summon Deng Tong into the palace with the emperor's official certificate. He apologized to the prime minister and said: "This is my dear minister, please spare him!" After Deng Tong returned to the palace, he cried and said to Emperor Wen: The prime minister almost killed me! Five years after Shen Tujia served as prime minister, Emperor Xiaowen died and Emperor Xiaojing ascended the throne. In the second year of Emperor Jing's reign, Chao Cuo served as internal historian. Because he was favored by the emperor, he had a high status and great power. He petitioned the emperor to change many laws and regulations. At the same time, they also discussed how to use demotion and punishment to weaken the power of the princes. Prime Minister Shen Tujia also felt that what he said was not adopted, so he hated Chao Cuo. Chao Cuo served as the internal historian. The gate of the internal historian's mansion originally led out of the palace from the east, which made it inconvenient for him to get in and out. So he took it upon himself to build a wall door to lead out to the south. The wall cut through the door to the south was the outer wall of the Taishang Emperor's ancestral temple. After Shen Tujia heard about it, he wanted to use Chao Cuo's unauthorized cutting of the ancestral temple wall as a door to punish Chao Cuo and petition the emperor to kill him.
target: He was known for his honesty and strict adherence to court etiquette. He once ordered the execution of the favored courtier Deng Tong for disrespect, but Emperor Wen intervened. As prime minister, he clashed with Chao Cuo, who changed laws and cut through a temple wall. Shen Tujia sought to execute Chao Cuo but was thwarted by Emperor Jing. He died of anger after being outmaneuvered.

id: 史记/七十列传/张丞相列传::group-007
article_path: 史记/七十列传/张丞相列传
source: If someone is guilty of a serious crime and should be beheaded, Xiao Zhi will rationally let him commit suicide. His teachings spread throughout the world, and his reputation was known far and near. Emperor Xiaoxuan specially issued a document for this purpose, saying: Huang Ba, the prefect of Yingchuan, used propaganda laws to govern the people, so no one picked up relics on the road, men and women went their own way, and there were no prisoners who committed serious crimes in the prison. The title of Marquis of Guannei is specially given and one hundred catties of gold. In this way, he was recruited by the emperor to the capital as Jing Zhaoyin, and later became prime minister. During his tenure as prime minister, he still governed the country with etiquette and justice, and finally died of illness while serving as prime minister. After his death, his son inherited the title and was later made a prince. After Prime Minister Huang died, the emperor appointed Yu Dingguo, the imperial censor, to take his place. Prime Minister Yu Dingguo already has a biography of Tingwei, which is included in the biography of "Zhang Tingwei". After Prime Minister Yu resigned, Wei Xuancheng, the imperial censor, took over his position. Prime Minister Wei Xuancheng is the son of the Prime Minister Wei Xian mentioned earlier.
target: The text also lists later prime ministers, including Che Qianqiu, Wei Xian, Wei Xiang, Bing Ji, Huang Ba, Yu Dingguo, Wei Xuancheng, and Kuang Heng.

id: 史记/七十列传/张丞相列传::group-008
article_path: 史记/七十列传/张丞相列传
source: At the same time, both father and son became prime ministers. Both father and son were prime ministers, and people talked about it well at that time. Isn't this destiny? The person meeting you knew in advance that something like this would happen. After the death of Prime Minister Wei, Kuang Heng, the imperial censor, took over his position. Prime Minister Kuang Heng was from Donghai. He loves reading and once studied the Book of Songs with a doctor. Because his family was poor, he had to work for others to make ends meet. His talent was low and he took the court's talent selection exam many times, but failed. He only managed to pass the C-level exam at the ninth time. As for the scriptures, he was very familiar with them because he failed many examinations. Later, he became a candidate for Pingyuan County Literature and History. After several years, no one in the county respected him. At this time, the imperial censor summoned him to Beijing, and as a candidate for the Baishi official, he was recommended as a Langguan, a supplementary doctor, and was worshiped as the prince's young master to serve Emperor Xiaoyuan. Emperor Xiaoyuan liked the Book of Songs, so he promoted Kuang Heng to the rank of Guang Luxun, and asked him to serve as a teacher in the palace, teaching the emperor's courtiers. The emperor also sat next to him and listened to the lectures, and admired him very much. Therefore, his status became more and more noble day by day. Zheng Hong, the imperial censor, was dismissed from office for breaking the law, and Mr. Kuang Heng succeeded him as the censor. More than a year later, Prime Minister Wei Xuancheng passed away, and Mr. Kuang succeeded him as Prime Minister and was named Marquis of Le'an. In ten years, he rose to the rank of prime minister without leaving the city gate of Chang'an. Isn't this a good opportunity and destiny? Tai Shigong said: I have thought over and over again that scholars travel all over the world in order to obtain high-ranking officials and generous salaries, but there are too few people who can get the title of marquis! Most people will step down after reaching the position of imperial censor. These people have already become censors and are one step away from the position of prime minister. They hope in their hearts that the prime minister will die immediately so that they can take his place. There are also people who engage in conspiracy and conspiracy, secretly slandering and slandering, hoping to gain power. But some people wait for a long time but don't get it; while some people don't wait long and get promoted to the throne and are named princes: this may be really destiny!
target: Many were scholars who rose through official ranks, with some losing their titles for crimes like riding into temples. The historian notes that while some achieved high office through fate, others schemed in vain, and many talented individuals remained unrecognized.

id: 史记/七十列传/张仪列传::group-000
article_path: 史记/七十列传/张仪列传
source: Zhang Yi is a native of Wei. At first, he and Su Qin studied under Mr. Gui Guzi and learned the art of lobbying. Su Qin thought that he was not as talented as Zhang Yi. After Zhang Yi completed his studies, he went to lobby the princes. He once drank with Prime Minister Chu. During the dinner, Prime Minister Chu lost a piece of jade. The guests suspected Zhang Yi and said, "Zhang Yi is poor and has bad conduct. He must have stolen the prime minister's jade." So, everyone arrested Zhang Yi and tortured him hundreds of times. Zhang Yi never admitted it and had to release him. His wife said sadly and hatefully: Alas! If you had never gone to study and lobby, how could you have suffered such humiliation? Zhang Yi said to his wife: Look, is my tongue still there? His wife smiled and said: The tongue is still there. Zhang Yi said: This is enough. At that time, Su Qin had persuaded King Zhao to agree to form a vertical alliance with the other six countries except Qin, but he was afraid that Qin would take the opportunity to attack the vassal states and the alliance would be destroyed before it was even concluded. He also considered that there was no suitable person to send to Qin, so he sent someone to secretly guide Zhang Yi and said: "You and Su Qin had a good relationship at the beginning. Now that Su Qin is in power, why don't you make friends with him to realize your wish of success?" So Zhang Yi went to Zhao State, submitted a famous invitation, and requested to meet Su Qin. Su Qin warned his disciples not to inform Zhang Yi, and kept him from leaving for several days.
target: Zhang Yi, a native of Wei, studied lobbying under Guiguzi alongside Su Qin, who acknowledged his own inferiority to Zhang Yi. After completing his studies, Zhang Yi faced humiliation when he was falsely accused of stealing a jade during a dinner with the Prime Minister of Chu, resulting in torture. Despite his wife's lament, Zhang Yi remained undeterred, noting that his tongue—his tool for persuasion—was still intact. Su Qin, having secured a vertical alliance against Qin, secretly aided Zhang Yi by provoking him through public humiliation, which spurred Zhang Yi to seek fortune in Qin. Su Qin provided Zhang Yi with resources, enabling him to gain favor with King Hui of Qin and become a guest minister. Zhang Yi later realized Su Qin's strategy and refrained from attacking Zhao, honoring their unspoken pact.

id: 史记/七十列传/张仪列传::group-001
article_path: 史记/七十列传/张仪列传
source: Please thank Mr. Su for me. As long as Mr. Su is in power, how can I, Zhang Yi, dare to talk about attacking Zhao? After Zhang Yi became the prime minister of Qin, he wrote a letter to warn the prime minister of Chu: When I drank with you, I didn't steal your jade, but you whipped me. You have to protect your country well, I will steal your city soon! Ba and Shu attacked each other, and they went to Qin for help. King Hui of Qin wanted to send out troops to attack Shu, but he also believed that the road was dangerous, narrow and difficult to reach. At this time, South Korea came to invade Qin again. King Qin Hui wanted to attack South Korea first, and then attack Shu, which might be disadvantageous; he wanted to attack Shu first, but he was worried that South Korea would take advantage of the fatigue of the long battle to launch a sneak attack, so he hesitated and could not make a decision. Sima Cuo and Zhang Yi argued endlessly in front of King Hui. Sima Cuo advocated attacking Shu, but Zhang Yi said: It is better to attack South Korea first. King Hui said: I am willing to hear your respective reasons. Zhang Yi said: We will first have a blind date with the Wei State and be friendly with the Chu State, and then march to Sanchuan to block the pass of Shigu and block the main road of Tunliu. In this way, the passage from Wei to Nanyang was cut off, allowing the Chu State to send troops to approach Nanzheng. The Qin army attacked Xincheng and Yiyang, approaching the suburbs of the Western Zhou and Eastern Zhou Dynasties to attack the king of Zhou for his crimes, and then captured the lands of Chu and Wei.
target: As Qin's prime minister, Zhang Yi advised King Hui on military strategy, initially advocating an attack on Han to seize the Nine Tripods and control the Zhou emperor, while Sima Cuo argued for conquering Shu to expand territory and enrich the state. King Hui chose Sima Cuo's plan, capturing Shu and strengthening Qin. Zhang Yi later persuaded Wei to ally with Qin, leading to Wei ceding territory and Zhang Yi becoming Qin's prime minister.

id: 史记/七十列传/张仪列传::group-002
article_path: 史记/七十列传/张仪列传
source: So he severed relations with Qi, abolished the alliance, and sent a general to follow Zhang Yi to Qin to take over the land. Zhang Yi returned to Qin State and pretended not to hold on to the rope of the carriage. He fell off the carriage and was injured. He did not go to court for three months. When the King of Chu heard about this, he said, "Isn't Zhang Yi because I have not completely severed ties with Qi State?" He sent warriors to the Song Dynasty, borrowed Song's talisman, and went to the northern Qi State to insult the King of Qi. The Qi King was angry, cut off the talisman, and aggrievedly made friends with Qin. Qin and Qi established diplomatic relations, and Zhang Yi came to court. He said to the envoy of the Chu State: I have a six-mile fiefdom granted by the King of Qin, and I am willing to dedicate it to the King of Chu. The envoy from the Chu State said: I am here to take over Shang Yu's land of six hundred miles under the order of the King of Chu. I have never heard of six miles. The envoy reported back to the King of Chu. The King of Chu was so angry that he immediately sent out troops to attack Qin. Chen Zhen said: Can I open my mouth and speak? Instead of attacking Qin, it is better to cede land to bribe Qin and join forces with him to attack Qi. We will take back the land we ceded to Qin and take it back from Qi as compensation. In this way, your country can still survive. The King of Chu refused to listen and finally sent out his army and general Qu Gai to attack Qin. Qin and Qi jointly attacked Chu, killing 80,000 officers and soldiers, and Qu Gai, and then seized the lands of Danyang and Hanzhong. The State of Chu sent more troops to attack the State of Qin. They went to Lantian and launched a large-scale battle. The Chu army was defeated, so the State of Chu ceded two more cities and made peace with Qin. Qin threatened Chu and wanted to get the land in Guizhou, and wanted to exchange it for land outside Wuguan. The King of Chu said: I am not willing to exchange land. As long as I get Zhang Yi, I am willing to give up the central Guizhou area. The King of Qin wanted to send Zhang Yi away, but he couldn't bear to say it. Zhang Yi asked to go. King Hui said: "The King of Chu is angry that your husband broke his promise to give Shang land, and he is deliberately retaliating against you." Zhang Yi said: Qin is strong and Chu is weak. I have a good relationship with Jin Shang, the official of Chu. Jin Shang can flatter Zheng Xiu, the wife of Chu, and the king of Chu will obey all Zheng Xiu's words. Besides, I was sent as an envoy to the State of Chu on the order of the king. How dare the king of Chu kill me? If you kill me and obtain the land in central Guizhou for Qin, this is also my highest wish. So he went to Chu as an envoy. King Huai of Chu imprisoned Zhang Yi as soon as he arrived, intending to kill him.
target: Zhang Yi's diplomatic efforts extended to Chu, where he promised 600 li of land in exchange for Chu severing ties with Qi. King Huai of Chu agreed, but Zhang Yi reneged, offering only six li. This led to war, with Qin and Qi defeating Chu, seizing Danyang and Hanzhong. Zhang Yi later returned to Chu as an envoy, narrowly escaping execution through the intercession of Zheng Xiu, and convinced King Huai to ally with Qin.

id: 史记/七十列传/张仪列传::group-003
article_path: 史记/七十列传/张仪列传
source: The reason why King Wei valued Zhang Yi was because he wanted to obtain the land of Korea. Besides, Nanyang in South Korea has been occupied. Why don't you entrust some political affairs to Gongsun Yan and ask him to go to the King of Wei to ask for credit? Then the exchanges between Qin and Wei will stop. If this is the case, then Wei must seek to conquer Qin and abandon Zhang Yi, make friends with South Korea, and let Gongsun Yan serve as prime minister. The uncle thought this was beneficial, so he entrusted political affairs to Xishou and asked him to contribute. As expected, Xishou became the prime minister of Wei, and Zhang Yi left Wei. Lord Yiqu came to pay homage to King Wei. Xishou heard that Zhang Yi had become the prime minister of Qin again, and he was very jealous. Xishou said to Mr. Yiqu: "Your country is far away. Today we are parting ways. It will be difficult to meet here again. Please allow me to tell you something." He continued: If all the countries in the Central Plains do not unite to attack Qin, Qin will burn and plunder your country. If all the countries in the Central Plains unite to attack Qin, Qin will send lightly-armed envoys with valuable gifts to serve your country. After that, the five kingdoms of Chu, Wei, Qi, Han, and Zhao jointly attacked Qin. Just then, Chen Zhen said to the king of Qin: Lord Yiqu is a wise monarch among the barbarian countries. It is better to give him money to appease his aspirations. King Qin said: OK.
target: Zhang Yi also lobbied Han, Qi, Zhao, and Yan to submit to Qin, emphasizing Qin's military superiority and the futility of resistance. Each state eventually agreed to serve Qin, but after King Hui's death, King Wu of Qin distrusted Zhang Yi, leading to his departure to Wei, where he died as prime minister.

id: 史记/七十列传/张仪列传::group-004
article_path: 史记/七十列传/张仪列传
source: The King of Chu sent people to eavesdrop, but Zhuang Shun still spoke in the Yue accent. Now, even if I am abandoned and run to Chu, will I lose the Qin accent? King Hui said: Well said. Now Korea and Wei are at war, which has not been resolved for a whole year. Some people say to me that it is beneficial for them to reconcile, and some people say it is beneficial for them not to reconcile. I cannot make a decision. I hope that besides making suggestions for your monarch, you can also give me some advice. Chen Zhen replied: Has anyone ever told the king about Bian Zhuangzi's murder of a tiger? Zhuangzi was about to kill the tiger, but a boy in the hotel stopped him and said: Two tigers are eating cows. When they get the taste of the cow, they will definitely fight. Once they fight, the big one will be injured and the small one will die. If you chase the injured tiger and assassinate it, you will definitely gain the reputation of assassinating both tigers. Bian Zhuang thought what he said made sense, and stood aside to wait for them. Soon, the two tigers fought. As a result, the older one was injured and the younger one died. Zhuangzi caught up with the injured tiger and killed it. As expected, he got the credit for killing both tigers. Nowadays, the war between Han and Wei cannot be resolved for a year. This will inevitably damage the big country and perish the small country. If you pursue the injured country and attack it, this crusade will definitely gain two fruits of victory. This is like Zhuangzi killing a tiger. What is the difference between me advising for my king and advising for the king? King Hui said: Well said. Finally they were not reconciled. As expected, the big countries were hurt and the small ones were in danger. Qin took the opportunity to send troops to attack them and defeated them. This was Chen Zhen's strategy. Xishou was from the Yin and Jin Dynasties of the Wei State. His name is Yan and his surname is Gongsun. She has a bad relationship with Zhang Yi.
target: Chen Zhen, a rival strategist, defended his loyalty to Qin against Zhang Yi's slander and later advised King Hui on the Han-Wei conflict, using the parable of Bian Zhuangzi killing two tigers to advocate non-intervention until both sides were weakened. This strategy succeeded, allowing Qin to attack and defeat both states.

id: 史记/七十列传/张仪列传::group-005
article_path: 史记/七十列传/张仪列传
source: In the tenth year of King Hui's reign, he sent his sons Hua and Zhang Yi to lead an army to besiege Puyang of Wei and surrendered it. Zhang Yi took the opportunity to persuade King Qin to return it to Wei, and sent his son Yao to Wei as a hostage. Zhang Yi took the opportunity to persuade the king of Wei: "Qin is so generous to Wei, and Wei must reciprocate with courtesy." Therefore, Wei State dedicated Shangjun and Shaoliang to Qin State to thank King Qin Hui. King Hui appointed Zhang Yi as his prime minister and renamed Shaoliang Xia Yang. Zhang Yi served as the Prime Minister of Qin for four years and officially supported King Hui as king.
target: Xishou, another strategist, undermined Zhang Yi's influence in Wei by aligning with Han, eventually becoming Wei's prime minister and forcing Zhang Yi's departure. After Zhang Yi's death, Xishou served as Qin's prime minister and led a five-state alliance.

id: 史记/七十列传/张仪列传::group-006
article_path: 史记/七十列传/张仪列传
source: He and Zhang Yi served King Hui of Qin together, and they were both highly regarded and distinguished, and they competed with each other for the favor of King Qin. Zhang Yi slandered Chen Zhen in front of the King of Qin and said: Chen Zhen freely traveled between Qin and Chu with generous gifts, and he should be working for the country's diplomacy. Now the Chu State has not become more friendly to the Qin State but is friendly to Chen Zhen. This shows that Chen Zhen has more plans for himself and less for the king.
target: Sima Qian concluded that Zhang Yi's actions were inferior to Su Qin's, but both were cunning figures whose strategies shaped the era.

id: 史记/七十列传/张耳陈馀列传::group-000
article_path: 史记/七十列传/张耳陈馀列传
source: Zhang Er was a native of Daliang, Wei State. When he was young, he was a guest at the gate of Wei Gongzi Wuji. Zhang Er was once expelled from the local register and fled to Waihuang. There was a daughter of a wealthy family in Waihuang. She was very beautiful, but she married a stupid and mediocre husband. She therefore ran away from her husband and went to live with her father's old friend. Her father's friend knew Zhang Er well, so he said to the woman: If you must marry a talented husband, marry Zhang Er. The woman listened to his advice, finally severed her relationship with her husband, and remarried Zhang Er. At this time, Zhang Er was freed from his embarrassment and began to travel extensively. The bride's family provided Zhang Er with generous supplies, so Zhang Er could attract guests from thousands of miles away. So Huang became the county magistrate outside Wei. His reputation grew. Chen Yu was also a native of Daliang in Wei State. He loved Confucianism and had visited Kuxing in Zhao State many times. A very wealthy Gongcheng family married his daughter to him because he knew that Chen Yu was not an ordinary mediocre person. When Chen Yu was young, he served Zhang Er like his father, and the two established a friendship through adversity that they would never regret. When the Qin Dynasty destroyed Daliang, Zhang Er's family lived in Waihuang. When Han Emperor Gaozu was still an ordinary commoner, he had many contacts with Zhang Er and lived in Zhang Er's family for several months at a time. A few years after the fall of the Qin State and the Wei State, it was heard that these two men were famous people in the Wei State, and a reward was offered for their arrest. Anyone who captured Zhang Er would be rewarded with a thousand gold coins, and whoever captured Chen Yu would be rewarded with a reward of five hundred gold coins. Zhang Er and Chen Yu changed their names and fled to Chendi together, where they worked as guards to support themselves. They lived opposite each other. A minor official once whipped Chen Yu for a minor offense. Chen Yu was about to resist, but Zhang Er quickly stepped on him to signal him not to move and accept the whipping. After the minor official left, Zhang Er took Chen Yu under the mulberry tree and scolded him: "What did I tell you in the first place?" Now that I have suffered a little humiliation, am I going to die at the hands of an official? Chen Yu thought he was right. The State of Qin issued an order proclamation, offering a reward for the arrest of the two of them. They also used their status as Li Zhengwei to convey the order to the residents of Lizhong. Chen She revolted in Qizhou and when he invaded Chen, his army had expanded to tens of thousands. Zhang Er and Chen Yu asked to see Chen She. Chen She and his cronies had heard that Zhang Er and Chen Yu were talented many times, but they had never met them, and they were very happy after meeting them. The heroes and elders of Chendi persuaded Chen She: "The general wears strong armor and holds sharp weapons. He leads the soldiers to attack the tyrannical Qin State, reestablishes the power of Chu State, revives the destroyed country, and continues the extinct heirs. Such merits should be called the king." Moreover, we have to supervise and lead all the generals in the world. It is impossible not to call ourselves kings. I hope that the generals will be established as kings of Chu. Chen She asked Chen Yu and Zhang Er for their opinions on this, and they replied: The Qin State is unethical and has occupied other people's countries, destroyed their country, cut off their descendants, and plundered the people's property. The general's eyes widened with anger, he let go of his courage and risked his life, just to eliminate cruelty and cruelty in the world. Now he has just conquered Chen Di and proclaimed himself king, showing his selfishness in front of everyone in the world. I hope the general will not become king. He quickly led his troops to the west and sent people to support the descendants of the Six Kingdoms as his own party members to increase the hostility to Qin.
target: Zhang Er, a native of Daliang in Wei State, was once a guest of Wei Prince Wuji. After being expelled from the local register, he fled to Waihuang, where a wealthy woman left her foolish husband to marry him on the advice of her father's friend. With her family's support, Zhang Er traveled widely and gained fame, eventually becoming a county magistrate. Chen Yu, also from Daliang, was a Confucian scholar who married into a wealthy family. He served Zhang Er like a father, and they formed a close bond. After Qin destroyed Wei, both men became wanted fugitives. They changed their names and worked as guards in Chendi. When a minor official whipped Chen Yu, Zhang Er restrained him from resisting, advising patience. When Chen She rebelled, Zhang Er and Chen Yu advised him not to proclaim himself king too early but to restore the Six Kingdoms to weaken Qin. Chen She ignored them and made himself king. They then helped Wu Chen lead an army to conquer Zhao, where they persuaded him to declare himself King of Zhao. Chen Yu became general, and Zhang Er became prime minister.

id: 史记/七十列传/张耳陈馀列传::group-001
article_path: 史记/七十列传/张耳陈馀列传
source: Zhang Er and Zhao Wangxie fled into Julu City, where they were surrounded by Qin general Wang Li. Chen Yu gathered tens of thousands of Changshan's remaining troops in the north and stationed them north of Julu City. Zhang Han's army was stationed in Jiyuan, south of Julu City. A corridor was built to connect with the Yellow River to transport military supplies to Wang Li. Wang Li's troops had plenty of food and they rushed to attack Julu. The food in Julu City was exhausted and the troops were very weak. Zhang Er sent people to call Chen Yu many times to come to the rescue. Chen Yu considered that his troops were insufficient and could not defeat the Qin army, so he did not dare to go. After several months of stalemate with no reinforcements, Zhang Er was furious and resentful of Chen Yu. He sent Zhang Xiao and Chen Ze to rebuke Chen Yu, saying: "You and I formed a life-and-death friendship at the beginning, but now King Zhao and I may die overnight, and you have tens of thousands of troops and refuse to rescue us. Where is the friendship of life and death?" If you want to keep your promise, why don't you fight the Qin army to the death? There may still be a 1/20 chance of winning. Chen Yu said: I consider that even if we advance forward, not only will we not be able to save Zhao, but our entire army will be wiped out in vain. Besides, I don’t go and die together because I want to avenge King Zhao and Jun Zhang from Qin in the future. Now we must die together, just like giving meat to a hungry tiger. What is the benefit? Zhang Xian and Chen Ze said: The matter is imminent. We need to die together to establish integrity. How can we care about the future? Chen Yu said: I have no regrets about dying, it is just that it will be useless, but I will definitely do what you two said. So he sent 5,000 troops under the leadership of Zhang Xian and Chen Ze to attack the Qin army. When they reached the front line, the entire army was wiped out. At this time, Yan, Qi, and Chu heard that Zhao was in danger and came to rescue him. Zhang Ao also gathered more than 10,000 troops from Daidi to the north. They all set up camp next to Chen Yu and did not dare to attack the Qin army. Xiang Yu's army cut off Zhang Han's tunnel many times, and Wang Li was short of military supplies. Xiang Yu led all his troops across the Yellow River and defeated Zhang Han. Zhang Han led his troops to retreat, and then the armies of various princes dared to attack the Qin army that besieged Julu, and finally captured Wang Li. Qin general Shejian committed suicide. In the end, it was the State of Chu that saved the giant deer. At this time, King Zhao Xie and Zhang Er were able to leave Julu City to thank the princes from all over the world. When Zhang Er and Chen Yu met, they blamed Chen Yu for refusing to save Zhao and asked about the whereabouts of Zhang Xu and Chen Ze.
