Chen Yu said angrily: Zhang Xu and Chen Ze blamed me for dying together. I sent them to lead five thousand troops to try to attack the Qin army first. As a result, the entire army was wiped out and no one was spared.
target: When Qin forces besieged Julu, Zhang Er and King Zhao Xie were trapped inside. Chen Yu, with insufficient troops, hesitated to rescue them. Zhang Er sent messengers to rebuke him, but Chen Yu's cautious approach led to a rift. After Xiang Yu defeated Qin at Julu, Zhang Er blamed Chen Yu for the deaths of his messengers. Chen Yu angrily offered his seal, which Zhang Er accepted, deepening their enmity.

id: 史记/七十列传/张耳陈馀列传::group-002
article_path: 史记/七十列传/张耳陈馀列传
source: However, because Chen Yu did not follow him into Guanzhong, and because Xiang Yu heard that Chen Yu was in Nanpi, he granted him the three counties around Nanpi, moved King Zhao Xie's capital to Dai County, and changed his title to Dai Wang. When Zhang Er went to his feudal state, Chen Yu became even more angry and said, "Zhang Er and I have equal merits. Zhang Er can be granted the title of king, but I can only be granted the title of marquis. This is unfair to Xiang Yu." When King Tian Rong of Qi betrayed Chu, Chen Yu sent Xia Yuan to persuade Tian Rong: Xiang Yu, as the ruler of the world, is unfair. He enfeoffs good places to generals to be kings, and moves those who were kings to bad places. Now he has moved King Zhao to Dai County! I hope your Majesty will lend me your troops and use Nanpi as a shield for your defense. Tian Rong planned to establish a faction in Zhao State to oppose Chu State, so he sent troops to follow Chen Yu's command. Therefore, Chen Yu mobilized all the troops from his three counties to attack Changshan King Zhang Er. Zhang Er was defeated and fled. He thought that there was no one among the princes who could defect to him, so he said: Although the King of Han has an old friendship with me, Xiang Yu's power is strong, and he entrusted me, so I want to defect to Chu. Duke Gan said: When the king of Han entered the pass, the five stars gathered in the Jingsu sky area. Jingsutian District is the branch star of Qin State. Whoever arrives first will definitely succeed. Even if Chu is strong now, it will definitely belong to Han in the future. Therefore, Zhang Er decided to go to Han. The King of Han also returned to pacify the Three Qin Dynasties, and was besieging Zhang Han's army in Feiqiu. Zhang Er came to see the King of Han, who received him with great courtesy. After Chen Yu defeated Zhang Er, he recovered all the land of Zhao State, brought King Zhao back from Dai County, and became the king of Zhao State. King Zhao was grateful to Chen Yu and made Chen Yu the king of Dai. Because King Zhao was weak and the domestic situation had just stabilized, Chen Yu did not go to the feudal state and stayed to assist King Zhao, while he sent Xia Yue to garrison Daiguo as the prime minister. In the second year of the Han Dynasty, the king of Han attacked the Chu State eastward and sent an envoy to inform the State of Zhao that he would attack Chu together with the State of Zhao. Chen Yu said: As long as the king of Han kills Zhang Er, Zhao will obey. So the king of Han found a man who looked similar to Zhang Er and beheaded him, and sent someone to take the head to Chen Yu. Chen Yu then sent troops to help Han. The King of Han was defeated west of Pengcheng. Chen Yu realized that Zhang Er was still alive, so he betrayed the King of Han. In the third year of the Han Dynasty, not long after Han Xin pacified Wei, he sent Zhang Er and Han Xin to break through Jingxing of Zhao State, kill Chen Yu on the banks of the Sashui River, and pursue Xiang State to kill Zhao Wangxie. The Han Dynasty granted Zhang Er the title of King of Zhao. In the fifth year of the Han Dynasty, Zhang Er died, and his posthumous title was King Jing. Zhang Er's son Zhang Ao succeeded his father as King of Zhao, and Princess Lu Yuan, the eldest daughter of Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty, married King Ao of Zhao and became his queen.
target: Xiang Yu enfeoffed Zhang Er as King of Changshan but gave Chen Yu only three counties. Chen Yu, resentful, allied with Qi to attack Zhang Er, who fled to Han. Han Xin helped Zhang Er defeat and kill Chen Yu, and Zhang Er was made King of Zhao. He died in the fifth year of Han, succeeded by his son Zhang Ao.

id: 史记/七十列传/张耳陈馀列传::group-003
article_path: 史记/七十列传/张耳陈馀列传
source: Now that all three of my clans have been sentenced to death because of this incident, will I sacrifice my relatives for the sake of King Zhao? But King Zhao did not resist, only we people participated. He explained in detail his original intention to murder the emperor and the situation that King Zhao did not know the inside story. So Duke Xie went to the palace and reported in detail what he had learned, and the emperor pardoned King Zhao. The emperor appreciated Guangao as a man of faith, so he sent Duke Xie to tell him about the pardon of King Zhao, saying: King Zhao has been released from imprisonment. Therefore, Guan Gao was also pardoned. Guan Gao said happily: Is our King Zhao really released? Xie Gong said: Yes. Duke Xie said again: The emperor praised you, so he pardoned you. Guan Gao said: The reason why I survived being beaten to death was to prove that King Zhang Ao did not commit rebellion. Now that King Zhang Ao has been released, my responsibility has been remedied, and I will not regret it even if I die. Besides, if a minister has a reputation of usurping, how can he have the dignity to serve the emperor again? Even if the emperor does not kill me, am I not ashamed in my heart? So he raised his head and cut his throat and died. By this time, he was already famous throughout the world. Not long after Zhang Ao was released, he was named Marquis of Xuanping because he married Princess Lu Yuan. Therefore, the emperor praised Zhang Ao's guests. All the guests who followed King Zhang into the pass as slaves were all princes, ministers, and county guards. Until the time of Xiaohui, Gaohou, Emperor Wen, and Xiaojing, the descendants of King Zhang's guests had become high-ranking officials with a salary of two thousand stone. Zhang Ao died in the sixth year of high school. Zhang Ao's son Zhang Yan was named King of Lu Yuan.
target: Zhang Ao married Princess Lu Yuan, daughter of Emperor Gaozu. When Gaozu treated him arrogantly, Zhang Ao's retainers Guan Gao and Zhao Wu plotted to assassinate the emperor. The plot was discovered, and Zhang Ao was arrested. Guan Gao took full responsibility, enduring torture to prove Zhang Ao's innocence. Gaozu eventually pardoned Zhang Ao, and Guan Gao committed suicide. Zhang Ao was later made Marquis of Xuanping. His descendants held high offices until the Lu clan's downfall led to their demotion, though some were later restored.

id: 史记/七十列传/张耳陈馀列传::group-004
article_path: 史记/七十列传/张耳陈馀列传
source: This is my strategy for pacifying a land thousands of miles away with just one order. Wu Xinjun followed his plan and sent Kuai Tong to give Fan Yanglinghou's seal. After the Zhao people heard the news, more than thirty cities surrendered without a fight. When they arrived at Handan, Zhang Er and Chen Yu heard that Zhou Zhang's troops had entered Guanzhong and were defeated again in the water-playing area. They also heard that the generals who had conquered the city for King Chen were often slandered, convicted and executed. They also resented King Chen for not adopting their strategy and promoting them to generals, instead making them captains.
target: The historian comments that Zhang Er and Chen Yu, once loyal friends, became bitter enemies over power and territory, revealing that their bond was rooted in self-interest rather than true virtue.

id: 史记/七十列传/张释之冯唐列传::group-000
article_path: 史记/七十列传/张释之冯唐列传
source: Tingwei Zhang Shizhi was from Duyang, with the courtesy name Ji. Lives with his brother Zhong. Because his family had a lot of money, he became a knight and served Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty. He was not promoted within ten years and became unknown. Zhang Shizhi said: Being a Langguan for a long time has depleted my brother's wealth and made people uneasy. I want to resign and go home. The lieutenant general Yuan Ang knew that he had both political integrity and talent, and regretted his departure. He asked Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty to appoint him as a visitor. After Zhang Shizhi met with Emperor Wen, he stepped forward to state the big plans and policies that would benefit the country and the people. Emperor Wen said: Talk about things close to real life, don't talk lofty words, what you say should be implemented now. So Zhang Shizhi talked about the Qin and Han Dynasties again, and talked for a long time about the reasons for the demise of the Qin Dynasty and the prosperity of the Han Dynasty. Emperor Wen admired him very much and appointed him as an emissary. Once, Zhang Shizhi followed Emperor Wen of Han Dynasty on a trip to the tiger enclosure. Emperor Wenwen of Han Dynasty asked about the status of various animals registered in the book. He asked more than a dozen questions. Lieutenant Shang Lin could only look here and there, but could not answer any of them. The stingy man who was in charge of the tiger enclosure answered the questions raised by the emperor on behalf of Lieutenant Lin, and he answered them very comprehensively. I want to use this to show that I answer questions like a voice response and that I can't answer questions.
target: Zhang Shizhi, a Tingwei from Duyang, served Emperor Wen of Han but remained unknown for a decade. Yuan Ang recommended him as a visitor. Zhang advised the emperor on practical governance, discussing Qin's fall and Han's rise. Emperor Wen appointed him as an emissary. During a visit to a tiger enclosure, a keeper answered questions fluently while the Shanglin Lieutenant faltered.

id: 史记/七十列传/张释之冯唐列传::group-001
article_path: 史记/七十列传/张释之冯唐列传
source: May your Majesty understand clearly. After a long time, the emperor said: Ting Wei's sentence is correct. Later, someone stole the jade ring in front of the throne of Gaozu Temple and was caught. Emperor Wen was angry and handed it over to Tingwei for punishment. Zhang Shizhi reported to the emperor the crime of stealing the ancestral temple's clothing and equipment according to the law and was sentenced to death. The emperor was furious and said: "This man has acted so lawlessly that he stole the artifacts from the temple of the late emperor. I handed him over to the Tingwei for trial and wanted to punish him with genocide, but you blindly reported the punishment to me in accordance with the provisions of the law. This is not my original intention to respect and flatter the ancestral temple."
target: The emperor wanted to promote the keeper, but Zhang warned against valuing eloquence over substance, citing Qin's decline due to such practices. The emperor agreed and canceled the promotion.

id: 史记/七十列传/张释之冯唐列传::group-002
article_path: 史记/七十列传/张释之冯唐列传
source: Now that Your Majesty has promoted a stingy man to a higher level because of his sharp tongue, I am afraid that people all over the world will follow this trend and rush to use their rhetorical skills without pursuing reality. Moreover, people in lower positions are influenced by those in higher positions as quickly as shadows follow the body and respond to sounds. Your Majesty must not be irrational in anything you do! Emperor Wen said: OK! Therefore, the original plan was cancelled, and Shifu was no longer appointed as Shanglin Ling. Emperor Wen got into the car and asked Zhang Shizhi to ride beside him. The car moved forward slowly. Emperor Wen asked Zhang Shizhi about the shortcomings of Qin's government, and Zhang Shizhi told him truthfully. When he arrived at the palace, Emperor Wen appointed Zhang Shizhi as the bus commander. Soon, the prince and King Liang entered the court in the same car, and they did not get off the car when they arrived at Simamen outside the palace. At that time, Zhang Shizhi stepped forward to stop the prince and King Liang from entering the palace. They also reported to the emperor that they had committed the crime of "disrespect" by not getting out of the car outside the palace gate. When Empress Dowager Bo learned about this, Emperor Wen took off his hat and said, "I blame my lax teaching of my son." Empress Dowager Bo also sent envoys with her edict to pardon the sins of Prince Liang, so that Prince Liang and Prince Liang could enter the palace. From this, Emperor Wen even more saw Zhang Shizhi's uniqueness and appointed him as a middle doctor. After some time, Zhang Shizhi was promoted to Zhonglang General. Following the emperor to Ba Ling, Emperor Wen of Han stood on the north side of Ba Ling and looked out. At this time, Mrs. Shen also followed. The emperor showed her the road to Xinfeng with his hand and said: This is the road to Handan. Then, he asked Mrs. Shen to play the harp, and Emperor Wen of Han Dynasty sang to the melody of the harp himself. He felt very miserable and sad, and turned back to the ministers and said: Alas! Use the stone from Beishan to make a coffin, fill the gaps in the stone coffin with chopped ramie silk wadding, and then apply paint on it. How can it still be opened? The attendants around me all said: That’s right. Zhang Shizhi stepped forward and said: If there is something inside that can cause people to be greedy, even if the coffin is made of Nanshan, there will still be gaps; if there is nothing inside that can cause people to be greedy, even if there is no stone coffin, there will be no need to worry! Emperor Wen praised him for speaking well. Later he was appointed Tingwei.
target: Zhang later stopped the prince and King Liang from entering the palace without dismounting, reporting them for disrespect. The empress dowager pardoned them, and Emperor Wen promoted Zhang to Zhonglang General. At Ba Ling, the emperor lamented about his coffin, but Zhang argued that greed, not the coffin, determines security. The emperor praised him.

id: 史记/七十列传/张释之冯唐列传::group-003
article_path: 史记/七十列传/张释之冯唐列传
source: Later he was appointed Tingwei. Shortly thereafter, when the emperor was on patrol and passed the Zhongwei Bridge in the north of Chang'an City, a man suddenly ran out from under the bridge. The horse that the emperor was driving was frightened. So he ordered the knights to capture the man and hand him over to Ting Wei Zhang Shizhi. Zhang Shizhi interrogated that person. The man said: I am a countryman from Chang'an County. I hid under the bridge when I heard the order to close the Qingdao Road. After a long time, I thought the emperor's team had passed by, so I came out from under the bridge. I saw the emperor's motorcade and started running immediately. Then the Tingwei reported to the emperor the punishment that the man deserved, saying that he had violated the prohibitions of Qingdao and should be fined. Emperor Wen was angry and said: This man frightened my horse. Fortunately, my horse is tame and gentle. If it had been another horse, it might have injured me, but it was the Tingwei who sentenced him to a fine! Zhang Shizhi said: The law is something that the emperor and the people of the world should abide by. Now the law stipulates this, but the punishment must be increased, so the law cannot win the trust of the people. At that time, your Majesty, you can just ask someone to kill him immediately. Now that this person is handed over to Tingwei, who is the leader of fair law enforcement in the world, if there is a slight deviation, the law enforcers in the world will be arbitrarily light or heavy, won't the people be at a loss? May your Majesty understand clearly. After a long time, the emperor said: Ting Wei's sentence is correct. Later, someone stole the jade ring in front of the throne of Gaozu Temple and was caught. Emperor Wen was angry and handed it over to Tingwei for punishment. Zhang Shizhi reported to the emperor the crime of stealing the ancestral temple's clothing and equipment according to the law and was sentenced to death. The emperor was furious and said: "This man has acted so lawlessly that he stole the artifacts from the temple of the late emperor. I handed him over to the Tingwei for trial and wanted to punish him with genocide, but you blindly reported the punishment to me in accordance with the provisions of the law. This is not my original intention to respect and flatter the ancestral temple." Zhang Shizhi took off his hat, kowtowed and apologized, saying: "This punishment is enough according to the law." Moreover, when the charges are the same, the severity of the crime must also be distinguished. Now if he steals the artifacts from the ancestral temple, he will be punished with genocide. If a stupid person digs up a handful of earth from Changling, what punishment will your Majesty use to punish him? After some time, Emperor Wen and Empress Dowager Bo discussed the matter and agreed to Tingwei's verdict.
target: As Tingwei, Zhang judged a man who startled the emperor's horse. The emperor wanted severe punishment, but Zhang insisted on the legal fine, stating the law must be trusted. The emperor relented. When someone stole from Gaozu Temple, the emperor demanded execution of the entire family, but Zhang argued the law prescribed only death for the thief. The emperor agreed after consulting the empress dowager.

id: 史记/七十列传/张释之冯唐列传::group-004
article_path: 史记/七十列传/张释之冯唐列传
source: At that time, Lieutenant Tiaohou Zhou Yafu and Liang Guoguo's Prime Minister Shandu Hou Wang Tiankai saw Zhang Shizhi's impartiality in enforcing the law and became close friends with him. Zhang Shizhi was praised by people all over the world. Later, Emperor Wen died and Emperor Jing ascended the throne. Zhang Shizhi was frightened and pretended to be sick. He wanted to resign and leave, but he was worried that he would be executed. He wanted to apologize to Emperor Jing in person, but he didn't know what to do. After using Wang Sheng's strategy, he finally saw Emperor Jing apologize and apologize, but Emperor Jing did not blame him. Wang Sheng is a virgin who likes Huang Lao's theory. Once he was called into the court, where all the three princes and nine ministers were standing. Wang Sheng, an old man, said: My garter is loose. He turned around and said to Zhang Tingwei: Kie the garter for me! Zhang Shizhi knelt down and tied his garters. Afterwards, someone asked Wang Sheng: Why did he humiliate Zhang Tingwei in the court and make him kneel to tie his garters? Wang Sheng said: I am old and of low status. I expected that I would not be able to benefit Zhang Tingwei in the end. Zhang Tingwei is a famous official in the world. I deliberately humiliated Zhang Tingwei and made him kneel down to tie his garters, hoping to use this method to strengthen his reputation. After hearing this, all the ministers praised Wang Sheng's virtue and respected Zhang Tingwei. Zhang Tingwei served Emperor Jing for more than a year and was demoted to the position of Prince of Huainan. This was because he had offended Emperor Jing in the past. After some time, Zhang Shizhi died. His son's name was Zhang Zhi, named Changgong. His official position was until he was a doctor, and he was later dismissed.
target: After Emperor Wen's death, Zhang feared Emperor Jing and sought Wang Sheng's advice. Wang humiliated Zhang in court by asking him to tie his garters, which elevated Zhang's reputation. Zhang later served Emperor Jing but was demoted and died.

id: 史记/七十列传/张释之冯唐列传::group-005
article_path: 史记/七十列传/张释之冯唐列传
source: Later, when Zhao Wangqian came to the throne, his mother was a singing woman. As soon as he came to the throne, he listened to Guo Kai's slander and eventually killed Li Mu and replaced him with Yan Ju. As a result, the army was defeated and captured and destroyed by the Qin people. Now I heard that Wei Shang was the governor of Yunzhong County. He used all the taxes from the military market to reward the soldiers. He also used his personal money to kill an ox every five days, entertain guests and military officials, and get close to the people around him. Therefore, the Huns stayed far away and did not dare to approach the border fortress of Yunzhong County. The Huns once invaded, and Wei Shang led his army to attack and killed many enemy troops. Those soldiers were all children of ordinary families who came from the countryside to join the army. How did they know the laws and regulations such as the ruler's registration and the five-year-old talisman? They only know how to fight hard all day long, kill the enemy and capture prisoners, and go to the shogunate to report their merits. As long as one sentence is not consistent with the actual situation, the judge will punish them with the law. The reward you deserve cannot be honored, but the judge will pursue it according to the law. I foolishly thought that His Majesty's laws were too strict, the rewards too light, and the punishments too severe. Moreover, Wei Shang, the governor of Yunzhong County, was only guilty of falsely reporting that he had killed six more enemies. Your Majesty handed him over to the judge, deprived him of his title, and sentenced him to one year in prison. From this point of view, even if His Majesty gets Lian Po and Li Mu, he cannot reuse them. I am indeed stupid, I have violated a taboo, I deserve the death penalty, I deserve the death penalty! Emperor Wen was very happy and asked Feng Tang to go on a Hanjie envoy that day to pardon Wei Shang and re-appoint him as the governor of Yunzhong County. He appointed Feng Tang as the chariot and cavalry captain, in charge of the lieutenants and the chariot warriors of each county. In the seventh year after Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty, Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty came to the throne and asked Feng Tang to be the prime minister of Chu State. He was soon dismissed. When Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty came to the throne, he was looking for virtuous people, and everyone recommended Feng Tang. Feng Tang was already over ninety years old and could no longer serve as an official, so he appointed his son Feng Sui as Lang Guan.
target: Feng Tang, known for filial piety, served Emperor Wen. He compared Zhao generals Li Qi, Lian Po, and Li Mu, stating the emperor could not use them due to strict laws. He cited Wei Shang, a governor punished for minor errors despite his success against the Xiongnu. Emperor Wen pardoned Wei Shang and appointed Feng Tang as chariot and cavalry captain. Under Emperor Jing, Feng became prime minister of Chu but was dismissed. Under Emperor Wu, he was recommended but too old to serve; his son Feng Sui became an official.

id: 史记/七十列传/张释之冯唐列传::group-006
article_path: 史记/七十列传/张释之冯唐列传
source: They also reported to the emperor that they had committed the crime of "disrespect" by not getting out of the car outside the palace gate. When Empress Dowager Bo learned about this, Emperor Wen took off his hat and said, "I blame my lax teaching of my son." Empress Dowager Bo also sent envoys with her edict to pardon the sins of Prince Liang, so that Prince Liang and Prince Liang could enter the palace. From this, Emperor Wen even more saw Zhang Shizhi's uniqueness and appointed him as a middle doctor. After some time, Zhang Shizhi was promoted to Zhonglang General. Following the emperor to Ba Ling, Emperor Wen of Han stood on the north side of Ba Ling and looked out.
target: The historian comments that Zhang Shizhi's integrity and Feng Tang's insights on generalship are admirable, aligning with the principle of impartial governance.

id: 史记/七十列传/循吏列传::group-000
article_path: 史记/七十列传/循吏列传
source: Tai Shigong said: Laws are used to guide people to do good, and punishments are used to prevent people from doing evil. When the grammar and criminal laws were incomplete, kind-hearted people still exercised self-restraint and self-cultivation with fear, because the officials behaved well and never violated the rules and regulations. As long as officials fulfill their duties and act according to principles, they can use it as an example to govern the world. Why must we use severe punishments? Sun Shuao was a hermit from Chu State. The Prime Minister Yu Qiu recommended him to King Zhuang of Chu, hoping that he would succeed him. Sun Shuao was promoted to the state minister in three months after he became an official. He administered politics and taught the people, which made the officials and people harmonious and united, and the customs were very pure and beautiful. His administration was lenient and not harsh, but he always stopped prohibitions. Officials did not do evil or deceitful things, and there were no thieves among the people. In autumn and winter, he encouraged people to go into the mountains to cut trees, and in spring and summer, he used the rising river water to transport the wood out of the mountains. The people all have convenient ways to make a living and live happily. King Zhuang believed that the original coins of Chu State were too light, so he ordered the small coins to be minted into large coins. It was very inconvenient for the people to use them, and they gave up their own business one after another. The chief executive in charge of the market reported to Prime Minister Sun Shuao: The market is in chaos, no one can do business there with peace of mind, and the order is very unstable.
target: Tai Shigong observed that laws guide people toward good, while punishments deter evil. Even when legal codes were incomplete, virtuous people exercised self-restraint because officials upheld rules. He argued that if officials fulfill their duties with integrity, severe punishments are unnecessary. Sun Shuao, a hermit from Chu, became prime minister after three months. His lenient yet effective governance fostered harmony, pure customs, and no deceit among officials or theft among people. He encouraged seasonal woodcutting and river transport, improving livelihoods. When King Zhuang replaced small coins with large ones, causing market chaos, Sun Shuao advised restoring the old currency, which stabilized the market within three days.

id: 史记/七十列传/循吏列传::group-001
article_path: 史记/七十列传/循吏列传
source: King Zhuang agreed and issued the order for three days, and the market returned to its original state. The people of Chu State liked to ride in low carriages. The King of Chu thought that low carriages were not convenient for driving horses, so he wanted to order the low carriages to be raised. Sun Shuao, the Prime Minister of the State, said: It is not good to issue government orders repeatedly, leaving the people at a loss as to what to do. If you definitely want to raise the height of your car, I would like to ask the villagers to raise the threshold. The passengers are all respectable gentlemen. They cannot get out of the car frequently just to pass the threshold, so naturally the base of the car will be made higher. The king of Chu agreed to his request. After half a year, people took the initiative to raise the height of their cars.
target: To address low carriages, he suggested raising thresholds instead of issuing decrees; within half a year, people voluntarily raised their carriages.

id: 史记/七十列传/循吏列传::group-002
article_path: 史记/七十列传/循吏列传
source: After half a year, people took the initiative to raise the height of their cars. This is why Sun Shuao naturally obeyed his teachings without giving orders to control the people. People around him saw his words and deeds with their own eyes and imitated him. People who were far away watched the changes in the people around him and imitated him. Therefore, Sun Shuao was not complacent in being in the position three times, because he understood that he had achieved it with his talents; he had no regrets in leaving the position three times, because he knew that he was not at fault.
target: Sun Shuao remained humble in office and unregretful in dismissal, knowing his abilities and lack of fault.

id: 史记/七十列传/循吏列传::group-003
article_path: 史记/七十列传/循吏列传
source: Zichan was a senior official in the state of Zheng. When Zheng Zhaojun was in power, he appointed his favorite Xu Zhi as the prime minister of the country. The government was in chaos, the officials and the people were not in harmony, and the father and son were not harmonious. Dagong Ziqi told Zheng Zhaojun about these situations, and Zhaojun appointed Zichan as the prime minister. After Zichan was in power for one year, the libertines no longer played frivolously, the elderly no longer had to carry heavy loads, and the children no longer had to work in the fields. After two years, transactions in the market will be fair and high prices will no longer be reserved.
target: Zichan, a senior official in Zheng, became prime minister under Zheng Zhaojun after prior mismanagement. In one year, frivolity ceased, elders and children were relieved of burdens. In two years, market transactions became fair.

id: 史记/七十列传/循吏列传::group-004
article_path: 史记/七十列传/循吏列传
source: After Zichan was in power for one year, the libertines no longer played frivolously, the elderly no longer had to carry heavy loads, and the children no longer had to work in the fields. After two years, transactions in the market will be fair and high prices will no longer be reserved. Three years later, people did not close their homes at night and did not pick up lost items on the road. Four years later, farmers will not have to take their farm tools home after work. Five years later, men will not need to perform military service. In case of a funeral, they will consciously perform funeral rites. Zichan passed away in the twenty-sixth year of his rule in Zheng. The young men cried bitterly, and the old people wept like children, saying: "Zichan has left us and died. Who will the people rely on in the future?"
target: In three years, people left doors unlocked and returned lost items. In four years, farmers left tools in fields. In five years, military service was unnecessary, and funerals were conducted properly. After 26 years, Zichan died; young and old mourned, lamenting the loss of their reliance.

id: 史记/七十列传/循吏列传::group-005
article_path: 史记/七十列传/循吏列传
source: Four years later, farmers will not have to take their farm tools home after work. Five years later, men will not need to perform military service. The young men cried bitterly, and the old people wept like children, saying: "Zichan has left us and died. Who will the people rely on in the future?" Gongyixiu was a doctor from the state of Lu. Because of his outstanding talent and learning, he became the prime minister of the state of Lu. He obeyed the laws and acted according to the principles without changing the regulations at all, so the officials behaved themselves in a correct manner. He ordered officials not to compete for interests with the people, and high officials not to take advantage.
target: Gongyixiu, prime minister of Lu, upheld laws without alteration, ensuring officials behaved correctly. He forbade officials from competing with people for profit. When offered fish, he refused, fearing dismissal would end future gifts.

id: 史记/七十列传/循吏列传::group-006
article_path: 史记/七十列传/循吏列传
source: Now that I am the Prime Minister, I can afford fish. If I am dismissed from office because I accepted your fish today, who will be willing to give me fish in the future? So I can't accept it. Gongyixiu ate the vegetables and thought they tasted good, so he pulled out all the mallow vegetables in his home and threw them away. When he saw that the cloth he had woven was good, he immediately kicked his wife out of the house and burned the loom. He said: Are we going to leave farmers and weavers with nowhere to sell the goods they produce? Shi She was the Prime Minister of King Zhao of Chu. He was strong, upright, honest and just. He was neither flattering nor timid. On a trip to inspect various counties, a murderer happened to kill someone on the way. He pursued the murderer, who turned out to be his own father. He let his father go and imprisoned himself when he returned. He sent someone to tell King Zhao: The murderer is my father. If you punish your father to establish political achievements, this is unfilial; if you abandon the law and condone crime, it is disloyal; therefore, I deserve the death penalty.
target: He discarded tasty vegetables and burned his wife’s loom to avoid harming farmers and weavers. Shi She, prime minister of Chu, pursued a murderer who was his father. He released his father and imprisoned himself, stating that punishing his father was unfilial and condoning crime disloyal. Despite King Zhao’s pardon, he committed suicide to uphold duty.

id: 史记/七十列传/循吏列传::group-007
article_path: 史记/七十列传/循吏列传
source: So Shi She refused to obey the king of Chu's order and cut his neck to death. Li Li was a judge of Duke Wen of Jin. He heard that the case was wrong and the murder was in vain. When he found out, he imprisoned himself and sentenced him to death. Duke Wen said: Official positions vary, and punishments vary in severity. This is the fault of your officials, not your fault. Li Li said: My official position is that of a senior official, and I have never given up my high position to my subordinates. I have received a lot of official salary, and I have never given any benefits to them. Now, I have made mistakes in investigating the case and a life was wasted, but I have to shift the blame to my subordinates. I have never heard of such a theory. He refused to accept Duke Wen's order. Duke Wen said: If you think you are guilty, am I guilty too? Li Li said: There are laws and regulations for judges to decide cases. If you are wrongly sentenced, you will be punished personally, and if you are wrongly killed, you will be punished with death. You made me a judge because I can listen to subtle details and decide difficult cases. Now I heard the case wrongly and killed someone in vain, so I should be sentenced to death. So he refused to accept Duke Wen of Jin's pardon and committed suicide with his sword. Tai Shigong said: Sun Shuao said something, and the market order in Yingdu was restored. Zichan died of illness, and the people of Zheng State burst into tears. When Gongyixiu saw that his wife had finished weaving the cloth, he drove her out of the house. Shi She let his father go and committed suicide to take the blame, which established King Zhao of Chu's reputation. Li Li was wrongly convicted of murder and died with his sword, helping Duke Wen of Jin to rectify the country's laws.
target: Li Li, a judge of Jin, discovered a wrongful execution. He imprisoned himself and sentenced himself to death. Duke Wen offered pardon, but Li Li insisted on accountability, refusing to shift blame. He committed suicide to uphold legal integrity. Tai Shigong concluded that Sun Shuao restored market order, Zichan’s death moved Zheng, Gongyixiu drove out his wife, Shi She’s suicide honored King Zhao, and Li Li’s death rectified Jin’s laws.

id: 史记/七十列传/扁鹊仓公列传::group-000
article_path: 史记/七十列传/扁鹊仓公列传
source: Bian Que was from Miao, Bohai County. His surname was Qin and his name was Yue. When he was young, he was the manager of a guesthouse. A guest named Chang Sang came to the guest house. Only Bian Que thought he was a strange person and always treated him respectfully. Chang Sangjun also knew that Bian Que was not an ordinary person. He had been coming and going for more than ten years. One day, he asked Bian Que to sit with him and quietly said to Bian Que: I have a secret medical prescription. I am old and I want to pass it on to you. Please don't leak it. Bian Que said: "I respectfully obey my orders." Then he took out the medicine in his arms and gave it to Bian Que, and said: Take this medicine with the dew on the grass and trees, and you will know many things in thirty days. Then he took out all his secret recipes and gave them to Bian Que. Suddenly the person disappeared, maybe he was not a mortal. Bian Que took the medicine as he said for thirty days, and he could see the people on the other side of the wall. Therefore, when diagnosing other people's diseases, you can see all the symptoms in the five internal organs, but on the surface, you are still taking the patient's pulse. Sometimes he practiced medicine in the state of Qi, and sometimes he practiced medicine in the state of Zhao.
target: Bian Que, a physician from Bohai County, was originally named Qin Yue. As a young innkeeper, he met a mysterious guest named Chang Sang, who recognized his potential and gave him a secret medical prescription. After taking the medicine for thirty days, Bian Que gained the ability to see through walls and diagnose illnesses internally. He practiced medicine in Qi and Zhao, where he became known as Bian Que.

id: 史记/七十列传/扁鹊仓公列传::group-001
article_path: 史记/七十列传/扁鹊仓公列传
source: Then he took out all his secret recipes and gave them to Bian Que. Suddenly the person disappeared, maybe he was not a mortal. Bian Que took the medicine as he said for thirty days, and he could see the people on the other side of the wall. Therefore, when diagnosing other people's diseases, you can see all the symptoms in the five internal organs, but on the surface, you are still taking the patient's pulse. Sometimes he practiced medicine in the state of Qi, and sometimes he practiced medicine in the state of Zhao. When he was in Zhao State, his name was Bian Que. During the reign of Duke Zhao of Jin, the power of many officials was strong but the power of the monarch was weak. Zhao Jianzi was a doctor, but he was in charge of state affairs alone. Zhao Jianzi fell ill and was unconscious for five days. The doctors were very worried and summoned Bian Que. Bian Que came into the room to examine the patient and walked out. Doctor Dong Anyu asked Bian Que about his condition. Bian Que said: "His blood is normal, why should you be surprised!" Once upon a time, Duke Mu of Qin was in this situation and fell into a coma for seven days before he woke up. The day he woke up, he told Gongsun Zhi and Ziyu: I am very happy when I arrive at the Emperor of Heaven. The reason why I stayed there for such a long time was that the Emperor of Heaven wanted to teach me. The Emperor of Heaven told me that the Jin Kingdom was about to be in chaos and that the Five Dynasties would not be able to live in peace. Then someone will become the overlord, and he will die soon after becoming the overlord. The sons of overlords will make their country's men and women promiscuous. Gongsun Zhi wrote down these words and kept them. Later, the history books of Qin recorded this matter. You have heard of the promiscuity of Duke Xian of Jin, the dominance of Duke Wen of Jin, and the indulgence of Duke Xiang of Jin after defeating the Qin army in Miao Mountain. You have heard of these. Now your lord's illness is the same as his, and he will be cured in less than three days. He will definitely say something after he recovers. After two and a half days, Zhao Jianzi woke up and told the doctors: I was very happy when I went to the Emperor of Heaven. I played with the gods in the center of the sky, where various musical instruments played many music and dances were performed. It was not like the music and dance of the three ancient times. The music was heart-stirring.
target: During the reign of Duke Zhao of Jin, Zhao Jianzi fell unconscious for five days. Bian Que diagnosed him, noting his blood was normal, and predicted he would recover in three days, similar to a past episode involving Duke Mu of Qin. Zhao Jianzi indeed woke up after two and a half days, recounting a vision of the Emperor of Heaven. He rewarded Bian Que with 40,000 acres of land.

id: 史记/七十列传/扁鹊仓公列传::group-002
article_path: 史记/七十列传/扁鹊仓公列传
source: People told Zhao Jianzi what Bian Que had said, and Zhao Jianzi gave Bian Que 40,000 acres of land. Later, Bian Que passed through Guo State. When the prince of the Guo Kingdom died of illness, Bian Que came to the gate of the palace of the King of Guo and asked a concubine who was fond of medicine: What disease did the prince have? Why did the capital hold rituals to ward off evil spirits and diseases more than many other things? The concubine said: The prince's disease is caused by the irregular circulation of blood and qi, the intertwining of yin and yang and the inability to drain it. It violently breaks out on the surface of the body, but in fact the internal organs are damaged. The human body's righteous energy cannot stop the evil energy, and the evil energy accumulates and cannot be released. Therefore, the yang energy weakens and the yin evil becomes strong, so the person suddenly faints and dies. Bian Que asked: When did he die? The concubine replied: From the time the rooster crows to now. Asked again: Has it been buried? He replied: Not yet, he died less than half a day ago. Please inform Mr. Guo that I am a Qinyue native of Bohai County, and my home is in Midi. I was unable to look up to the king's majesty and pay homage to him. I heard that the prince passed away unfortunately and I can revive him. The concubine said: Sir, are you not talking nonsense? Why do you say the prince can be resurrected! I heard that in ancient times, there was a doctor named Yu Fu. He did not use decoctions, medicinal wine, trowels, needles, needles, guides, massages, medicinal irons, etc. He could identify the location of the disease as soon as he undressed and examined the acupoints of the five internal organs, then cut the skin and muscles, dredged the meridians, and tied them Tendons, massage the brain, touch the bones, straighten the diaphragm, cleanse the stomach, cleanse the five internal organs, cultivate the essence, and change the expression and complexion. If the gentleman's medical skills can be like this, then the prince can be reborn; if he can't do this, but you want to resurrect him, you can't deceive the baby who just learned to laugh.
target: In Guo State, Bian Que encountered a prince who had seemingly died. He explained the prince suffered from "corpse disease," caused by an imbalance of yin and yang, and was not truly dead. Using acupuncture and medicinal applications, Bian Que revived the prince, though he insisted he could not resurrect the dead, only help those who could recover.

id: 史记/七十列传/扁鹊仓公列传::group-003
article_path: 史记/七十列传/扁鹊仓公列传
source: Bian Que then asked his disciple Ziyang to sharpen the needle stone and use Sanyang and Wuhui to inject needles. After a while, the prince woke up. He also asked his disciple Zi Bao to prepare a medicinal iron that could penetrate into the body for five minutes, and then mix and boil the medicine with eight prescriptions, and then apply it alternately under the two flanks. The prince was able to sit up. After further harmonizing the yin and yang, my body returned to the same as before after just taking the decoction for twenty days. Therefore, people all over the world believe that Bian Que can resurrect the dead. Bian Que said, "I can't resurrect the dead. He should live. All I can do is help him recover." When Bian Que arrived in Qi, Marquis Huan of Qi treated him as a guest. He went to the court to pay homage to Marquis Huan and said, "You have a small illness between your skin and muscles. If it is not treated, it will go deep into your body." Marquis Huan said: I am not sick. After Bian Que walked out of the palace, Huan Hou said to the people around him: Doctors love utilitarianism and want to attribute the cure of people to their own merits. Five days later, Bian Que went to see Huan Hou again and said, "Your disease is already in your blood. If you don't treat it, it may go deep into your body." Marquis Huan said: I am not sick. After Bian Que went out, Marquis Huan was unhappy. Five days later, Bian Que went to see Huan Hou again and said, "Your disease is already in the intestines and stomach. If it is not treated, it will invade deeper into the body." Marquis Huan refused to answer. After Bian Que went out, Marquis Huan was unhappy. Five days later, Bian Que went there again. When he saw Huan Hou, he backed away and ran away. Marquis Huan sent someone to ask him why he ran away. Bian Que said: If the disease is between the skin and flesh, decoctions and medicinal irons can cure it; if the disease is in the blood, acupuncture and stone can cure it; if the disease is in the intestines and stomach, medicinal wine can cure it; if the disease enters the bone marrow, even the God in charge of life can do nothing. Now that the disease has entered the bone marrow, I dare not ask for treatment. Five days later, Marquis Huan fell seriously ill and sent for Bian Que. Bian Que had already fled Qi. Marquis Huan fell ill and died. If Marquis Huan could know in advance the hidden symptoms and let good doctors diagnose and treat them as early as possible, then the disease could be cured and his life could be saved.
target: When visiting Qi, Bian Que warned Marquis Huan of a minor illness between his skin and muscles. The marquis ignored him, and over successive visits, the disease progressed to his blood, then intestines and stomach, and finally to his bone marrow, where it became incurable. Marquis Huan died five days after Bian Que fled, illustrating the importance of early treatment.

id: 史记/七十列传/扁鹊仓公列传::group-004
article_path: 史记/七十列传/扁鹊仓公列传
source: Five days later, Marquis Huan fell seriously ill and sent for Bian Que. Bian Que had already fled Qi. Marquis Huan fell ill and died. If Marquis Huan could know in advance the hidden symptoms and let good doctors diagnose and treat them as early as possible, then the disease could be cured and his life could be saved. People worry that there are too many diseases, and doctors worry that there are too few treatments. Therefore, there are six types of illness that cannot be cured: those who are arrogant, indulgent and unreasonable are the first incurable; those who despise the body and value money are the two incurable; those who dress inappropriately and eat improperly are the three incurable; those who have Yin and Yang disorder and the five internal organs are not functioning properly are the four incurable; those who are very weak and unable to take medicine are the five incurable; those who are superstitious in witchcraft and do not believe in medical skills are the six incurable. It is very difficult to cure a situation like this. Bian Que's reputation spread throughout the world. When he arrived in Handan, he heard that the local people respected women, so he became a doctor to treat women's diseases; when he arrived in Luo, he heard that Zhou people respected the elderly, so he became a doctor specializing in treating deafness, blindness, limbs, and pain; when he arrived in Xianyang, he heard that Qin people loved children, so he became a doctor to treat children's diseases; he changed the scope of his treatment according to the customs of various places. Li Xi, the imperial physician of Qin, knew that his medical skills were not as good as Bian Que's, so he sent someone to assassinate Bian Que. Up to now, people all over the world who talk about pulse diagnosis methods follow Bian Que's theory and practice.
target: Bian Que's fame spread, and he adapted his practice to local customs—treating women in Handan, the elderly in Luo, and children in Xianyang. However, Li Xi, the Qin imperial physician, jealous of his skills, had him assassinated. Despite this, Bian Que's methods in pulse diagnosis endured.

id: 史记/七十列传/扁鹊仓公列传::group-005
article_path: 史记/七十列传/扁鹊仓公列传
source: Bian Que's reputation spread throughout the world. When he arrived in Handan, he heard that the local people respected women, so he became a doctor to treat women's diseases; when he arrived in Luo, he heard that Zhou people respected the elderly, so he became a doctor specializing in treating deafness, blindness, limbs, and pain; when he arrived in Xianyang, he heard that Qin people loved children, so he became a doctor to treat children's diseases; he changed the scope of his treatment according to the customs of various places. Li Xi, the imperial physician of Qin, knew that his medical skills were not as good as Bian Que's, so he sent someone to assassinate Bian Que. Up to now, people all over the world who talk about pulse diagnosis methods follow Bian Que's theory and practice. This man in Taicang was the chief officer in charge of the granary in the capital of Qi State. He was from Lingan, his surname was Chunyu, and his given name was Yi. Young but fond of medical skills. Eight years after Han Gao's death, he once again studied medicine with Gongcheng Yangqing from Yuanli in the same county. At this time, Yang Qing was over seventy years old and had no descendants who could inherit the medical skills, so he asked Chunyu Yi to put aside all the medical prescriptions he had learned before, and then gave him all the secret recipes he had mastered. He also taught him the pulse books of Huangdi and Bian Que, and the method of diagnosing diseases by observing different colors on the face, so that he could know the patient's life and death in advance, determine difficult diseases, judge whether they could be cured, and the theory of pharmaceuticals. After studying for three years, he cured people's illnesses, predicted death and life, and accomplished many things. However, he traveled among the vassal states to practice medicine and study, and did not take care of his family. Sometimes he refused to treat others, so many patients resented him. In the fourth year of Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty, someone wrote to the court to accuse him. According to the criminal law, he had to be escorted to Chang'an in a carriage. Chunyu Yi had five daughters who followed him and cried.
target: The text then shifts to Chunyu Yi, a Taicang official from Qi, who studied medicine under Gongcheng Yangqing. Yangqing taught him the pulse books of Huangdi and Bian Que, along with diagnostic methods. After three years, Chunyu Yi became skilled but faced legal trouble in the fourth year of Emperor Wen's reign.

id: 史记/七十列传/扁鹊仓公列传::group-006
article_path: 史记/七十列传/扁鹊仓公列传
source: However, he traveled among the vassal states to practice medicine and study, and did not take care of his family. Sometimes he refused to treat others, so many patients resented him. In the fourth year of Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty, someone wrote to the court to accuse him. According to the criminal law, he had to be escorted to Chang'an in a carriage. Chunyu Yi had five daughters who followed him and cried. He got angry and cursed: If you don't give birth to a boy, there will be no one available at the critical moment! So the youngest daughter Tiying was very sad after hearing her father's words, so she followed her father westward to Chang'an. She wrote to the court and said: My father is an official of the court. The people of Qi State praise him for his integrity and justice. Now he has violated the law and been sentenced. I am very sad that people who are executed cannot regenerate, and those who are disabled by torture cannot recover. Even if they want to change their ways, there is no way to do it, and in the end they cannot do so. I would rather join the government and become a slave to atone for my father's sins and give him a chance to reform. Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty read Tiying's petition, felt compassion for her, and pardoned Chunyu Yi, and abolished corporal punishment that year.
target: His daughter Tiying petitioned the emperor, offering to become a slave to atone for his crimes. Moved by her plea, the emperor pardoned Chunyu Yi and abolished corporal punishment.

According to the pathology, when the disease invades the body surface, the yang energy on the body surface is exhausted, and the yin energy will invade. When Yin Qi invades and becomes aggressive, the cold Qi will flow up and the hot Qi will flow down, causing a person's chest to feel full. When a person is lying on the ground while sweating, his pulse will be cold and cold. For people with a cold and yin pulse, disease pathogens will inevitably invade the inside. During treatment, the yin and coldness should be caused to flow out with sweat. The wife of Sikong Chu in the Beigong of Qi State was ill. Then she was given gunpowder decoction. After three days, the hernia disappeared and the disease was cured. Once upon a time, the wet nurse of the King of Jibei said that she had fever in the soles of her feet and felt depressed in her chest. I told her: It was a fever syndrome. Three acupoints were pricked on each sole of her foot. When the needles were removed, they were used to hold the acupoints to prevent blood from flowing out. The disease was quickly cured. This means that theory only summarizes the general situation and puts forward general principles. If mediocre doctors fail to learn and understand deeply, they will make mistakes in identifying the yin and yang principles. When the King of Qi was a Marquis of Yang Deficiency, he was seriously ill, and many doctors thought it was a serious illness. I diagnosed his pulse and thought it was paralysis. The root of the disease was in the lower part of the right side of the body. It was as big as a clasped cup, making the person breathless, with rising negative Qi and unable to eat. I gave him gunpowder porridge, and after six days, the Qi went down. Then I asked him to take pills, and after about six days, the disease was cured. His illness was caused by improper sexual intercourse. When I diagnosed his pulse, I couldn't identify which meridian had the disease, but I could roughly tell where the disease was. I once diagnosed and treated a man named Cheng Kaifang in Wudu, Anyang. He said he was not sick, but I said he would suffer from tracheitis. In three years, his limbs would no longer be under his control, and he would become mute and unable to make a sound, and he would die at this time. Now I heard that he can no longer move his limbs. Although he is mute, he is not dead yet. His illness was caused by wind evil after drinking alcohol many times. The reason why I knew about his illness was because when I took his pulse, I found that his pulse condition was in line with the teachings of "Qi Ke Shu": If the internal qi is opposite, death will occur. Cut his pulse and get the pulse pattern of kidney qi counteracting lung qi. According to this principle, he will die in three years. A Gongchen named Xiang Chu in Anling Ban was ill. I diagnosed his pulse and said, "This is male hernia." Hernia is a disease that occurs under the chest septum and connects to the lungs. It is caused by sexual intemperance. I said to him: You must not do anything that requires strenuous effort. If you do such things, you will vomit blood and die. Later, Xiang Chu went to play Cuju. As a result, his waist became cold, he sweated a lot, and he vomited blood.

The King of Qi, as Marquis of Yangxu, had paralysis from sexual intercourse, cured with gunpowder porridge. Cheng Kaifang developed tracheitis from drinking and wind, becoming paralyzed and mute. source: The medical skills I am good at are all neglected. My compatriots who live in Linyi are good at medical skills, but I am not as good as him. Gao Ming and Wang Yu, the imperial doctors sent by the King of Jibei, asked me for advice. I taught them the distribution of meridians up and down and the connection positions of abnormal meridians. I often discussed the location of acupoints and the direction of evil and good and reverse when the energy of the meridians circulates. id: 史记/七十列传/日者列传::group-000
article_path: 史记/七十列传/日者列传
source: Since ancient times, only those who have received destiny can become kings, and the rise of kings does not depend on destiny through divination! This situation was particularly prevalent in the Zhou Dynasty and can still be seen in the Qin Dynasty. When the kings of the Han Dynasty came to Beijing to inherit the throne, they were also left to the fortune tellers. As for the emergence of diviners, they began to appear since the rise of the Han Dynasty. Lord Sima Ji is from Chu State. He was doing divination in the east city of Chang'an. At this time, Song Zhong was appointed as a doctor, and Jia Yi was appointed as a doctor. One day, the two of them went out to the court to take a bath and take a break. While walking, they discussed and learned the governance methods of the previous kings and saints, and extensively explored the world and human affairs. The two looked at each other and sighed. Jia Yi said: I heard that ancient saints, if they were not officials in the court, must be among the ranks of diviners and doctors. Now, I have seen the three princes, nine ministers and the sergeants and officials of the court, and I can know their talents, learning and character. Let’s try to observe the soothsayer’s style. The two of them went to the city in the same car and visited the divining restaurant. It had just rained, and there were very few people on the road. Lord Sima Ji was sitting leisurely in the pavilion, with three or four disciples accompanying him, explaining the principles of heaven and earth, the movement of the sun and the moon, and the origin of good and bad luck in yin and yang. The two doctors bowed twice to Lord Sima Ji. Master Sima Ji looked at their appearance and saw that they seemed to be knowledgeable people, so he returned the courtesy and asked his disciples to lead them to sit down. After sitting down, Sima Jizhu re-explained what he had said before, analyzed the origin and end of heaven and earth, the movement of the sun, moon and stars, distinguished the differences between benevolence and righteousness, listed the signs of good and bad luck, and talked about thousands of words, all of which were logical. Song Zhong and Jia Yi were surprised and understood. They adjusted their crowns and belts, straightened their clothes, sat respectfully, and said, "I see your appearance and listen to your conversation. I have never seen anything like this in the world of today." But why is your current status so low and why is your career so dirty? Sima Jizhu laughed loudly and said: "It seems that the two doctors are people with Taoism. How could they say such superficial words and use such crude words now?" What kind of person do you think a sage is? Who do you think is a noble person? Why do you regard me, an elder, as humble and dirty? Song Zhong and Jia Yi said: Noble official positions and generous salaries are valued by the world, and worthy people enjoy them. The position your husband is in now is not that kind of status, so he is considered to be in a lowly position. What is said is not true, what is done is not effective, and what is taken is inappropriate, so it is dirty. Diviners are despised by the world.
target: The role of divination in ancient China, particularly during the Zhou and Han dynasties. Kings historically received destiny without relying on divination, but by the Han dynasty, diviners had emerged. Lord Sima Ji, a diviner from Chu, practiced in Chang'an's east city. Two officials, Song Zhong and Jia Yi, visited him after discussing governance and saints. They questioned why Sima Ji, despite his wisdom, held a lowly position. Sima Ji defended divination, contrasting it with corrupt officials who exploit power for personal gain. He argued that diviners follow moral principles, aiding people through predictions and advice, unlike officials who engage in deceit and greed. He cited historical figures like Fuxi and King Wen of Zhou to highlight divination's value in governance. Sima Ji criticized the hypocrisy of those who judge diviners while ignoring their own ethical failings. He emphasized that diviners serve society by promoting virtue and preventing harm, often without recognition.

id: 史记/七十列传/日者列传::group-001

source: Today's diviners answer people's questions and educate people's ignorance. How can those who are ignorant and confused become wise with just one sentence! Therefore, never tire of talking. Therefore, the Qiji cannot ride in the same carriage as the tired donkey, the phoenix does not flock with the swallows and the sparrows, and the sage does not ride with the unworthy. Therefore, a gentleman always stays in a humble and inconspicuous position to avoid the public, hides himself to avoid the shackles of human relations, secretly observes the moral conformity of the world, eliminates all kinds of harm, shows the nature of God, helps God to nurture living beings, and hopes for more benefits without seeking any status or honor. You two are just casual commentators, how can you know the truth of the elders! Song Zhong and Jia Yi were in a daze and seemed to be lost after hearing this. They were at a loss, looked melancholy, and could not speak. So he got up and dressed, bowed twice and said goodbye to Lord Sima Ji. The two of them walked without knowing the difference between east, west, north and south. When they went out, they had to get into the car by themselves, lying on the railing, not daring to raise their heads, and could never catch their breath. Three days later, Song Zhong saw Jia Yi outside the palace gate, and took him away from everyone to talk about it. He said with emotion: The higher the morality, the safer it is, and the higher the power, the more dangerous it is. In a prominent position, death is imminent. Even if the divination does not work, it will not be deprived of the refined rice that it deserves; if the advice for the king is not thorough, there will be no place for him to stand. The two are too different, just like the sky and the earth are completely different. This is just as Lao Tzu said: Namelessness is the origin of all things in the world. Ha! The sky and the earth are vast and boundless, and all things are prosperous and happy. Some are safe and some are dangerous. No one knows where he should live. How qualified are you and I to comment on them? The longer they live, the happier they will be. Even Zhuangzi's ideas are not different from this. After a long time, Song Zhong went on a mission to the Xiongnu but returned before he arrived, and was therefore convicted of a crime. Jia Yi was the tutor of King Huai of Liang. King Huai of Liang accidentally fell off his horse and died. Jia Yi took the blame and went on a hunger strike and died with hatred.
target: The officials were humbled by his words. Later, Song Zhong and Jia Yi faced personal misfortunes—Song was convicted for a failed mission, and Jia Yi died after a student's accident. The text concludes with reflections on diviners' wisdom and their role in society, noting that many skilled individuals, like Sima Ji, remain unrecognized. It advises that elders should nurture children's talents and that diverse skills, including divination, are valuable. The narrative underscores the tension between worldly status and moral integrity, advocating for humility and the pursuit of virtuous living.

source: Chun Shenjun is a native of Chu State, his name is Xie and his surname is Huang. He once traveled around to learn from his teachers, gained profound knowledge, and served King Qingxiang of Chu. King Qingxiang thought Huang Xie was eloquent and asked him to go on a mission to Qin. At that time, King Zhao of Qin sent Bai Qi to attack Hanhe, defeated Han and Wei in Huayang, and captured Wei general Mang Mao. Han and Wei surrendered to Qin and served Qin. King Zhao of Qin had ordered Bai Qi to attack Chu with South Korea and Wei, but the Qin army had not yet set off. At this time, King Chu sent Huang Xie to Qin by chance and heard about Qin's plan. At this time, the State of Qin had occupied a large area of ​​Chu State, because before this King Qin had sent Bai Qi to attack the State of Chu, captured Wu County, Qianzhong County, captured the capital of Yancheng and Ying, and marched eastward to Jingling. King Qingxiang of Chu had to move the capital eastward to Chen County. Huang Xie saw that King Huai of Chu was lured by Qin and went to Qin's court for negotiation. As a result, he was deceived, detained and died in Qin. King Qingxiang was the son of King Huai of Chu, and the state of Qin did not pay attention to him at all. Huang Xie was worried that the state of Chu would perish if a war started. So he wrote a letter to persuade King Qin: Among the princes in the world, no one is more powerful than Qin and Chu. Now I heard that your Majesty is going to conquer Chu State, which is like two tigers fighting each other. When two tigers fight each other and the inferior dog takes advantage of it, it is better to be friendly with Chu. Please allow me to state my opinion: I have heard that when things develop to their peak, they will inevitably go to the opposite direction, as is the case with the changes between winter and summer; when things accumulate to extremely high levels, they will be dangerous, as is the case with stacked chess pieces. Now the land of Qin occupies the western and northern borders of the world. This has never been the case since the beginning of mankind, not even the territory of the emperor.
target: Chun Shenjun, a native of Chu named Huang Xie, served King Qingxiang of Chu. He was sent to Qin after King Qingxiang recognized his eloquence. At that time, Qin, under King Zhao, had been attacking Chu's allies, and Huang Xie learned of Qin's plan to invade Chu. Worried for Chu's survival, he wrote to King Zhao, arguing that Qin and Chu, as the two strongest states, should not fight each other, as this would benefit weaker states like Han and Wei. He warned that Qin's past victories had made it powerful, but attacking Chu would strengthen its enemies and lead to future trouble. Citing historical examples, he advised Qin to ally with Chu instead.

id: 史记/七十列传/春申君列传::group-001
article_path: 史记/七十列传/春申君列传
source: After reading Chun Shenjun's letter, King Zhao said: "It's really good." So he stopped Bai Qi from going on an expedition and resigned from Han and Wei. At the same time, he sent envoys to send generous gifts to Chu, and Qin and Chu formed an alliance to become friendly countries. Huang Xie accepted the alliance and returned to Chu State. The King of Chu sent Huang Xie and Prince Wan to Qin State as hostages. Qin State detained them for several years. Later, King Qingxiang of Chu fell ill, but Prince Wan was unable to return to Chu. However, the prince had a very good personal relationship with the Qin Prime Minister Ying Hou, so Huang Xie persuaded Ying Hou: Prime Minister, are you really very good to the prince of Chu? Ying Hou said: Yes. Huang Xie said: Now the King of Chu may be ill, so it would be better for Qin to let the prince go back. If the prince can be established as king, he will definitely serve the Qin State deeply and be grateful to the Prime Minister for his kindness that will never be exhausted. This is not only an expression of goodwill and friendship between the countries, but also retains an ally of a great country for the future. If he is not allowed to go back, then he will be just a commoner in Xianyang City at best; Chu State will establish a new crown prince, and he will definitely not serve Qin State by then. That would lose the trust of friendly countries and cut off the allies of a powerful country. This is not the best policy. I hope you, Xiangguo, will consider this matter carefully. Ying Hou Fan Ju reported what Huang Xie said to the King of Qin. The King of Qin said: Let the teacher of the Prince of Chu go back to inquire about King Chu's condition first, and then make a plan after he comes back. Huang Xie made plans for the prince of Chu and said: The purpose of Qin detaining the prince is to obtain benefits. Now the prince is powerless to benefit Qin. I am very worried about you. Moreover, Yang Wenjun's two sons are both in the Chu Kingdom. If the king unfortunately dies and the prince is not in the Chu Kingdom, Yang Wenjun's son will definitely be his successor, and the prince will not be able to enjoy the country. It is better to flee Qin and go out with the envoy; please let me stay and bear the consequences of this with my life. The Prince of Chu changed his clothes and pretended to be the driver of an envoy from the Chu State to get out of the customs. Huang Xie stayed in the guest house, always refusing to receive guests on the pretext that the Prince was ill. It was estimated that the prince had gone far and Qin could not catch up, so Huang Xie took the initiative to report to King Zhao of Qin: The prince of Chu has gone back and is far away. I deserve death, please grant me death. King Zhao was very angry and wanted to allow Huang Xie to commit suicide. Ying Hou said: "As a minister, Huang Xie sacrificed his life for his master. If the prince is established as the king of Chu, he will definitely use Huang Xie in an important position. Therefore, it is better to spare him the death penalty and let him return to his country to show his goodwill towards the Chu country." The King of Qin listened to the advice of Marquis Ying and sent Huang Xie back to his country. Three months after Huang Xie returned to Chu, King Qingxiang of Chu passed away, and Prince Wan was appointed King of Chu. This was King Kaolie. In the first year of King Kaolie's reign, Huang Xie was appointed prime minister, granted the title Lord Chunshen, and was rewarded with twelve counties in Huaibei.
target: King Zhao agreed, halted the attack, and formed an alliance with Chu. Huang Xie returned with Prince Wan of Chu as a hostage in Qin. When King Qingxiang fell ill, Huang Xie persuaded the Qin prime minister to let Prince Wan return, arguing it would secure Chu's loyalty. When Qin hesitated, Huang Xie helped Prince Wan escape disguised as a charioteer, staying behind to face punishment. King Zhao initially wanted to execute him but, on advice, spared him and sent him back. Three months later, King Qingxiang died, and Prince Wan became King Kaolie of Chu, appointing Huang Xie as prime minister and granting him the title Lord Chunshen with twelve counties.

id: 史记/七十列传/春申君列传::group-002
article_path: 史记/七十列传/春申君列传
source: Three months after Huang Xie returned to Chu, King Qingxiang of Chu passed away, and Prince Wan was appointed King of Chu. This was King Kaolie. In the first year of King Kaolie's reign, Huang Xie was appointed prime minister, granted the title Lord Chunshen, and was rewarded with twelve counties in Huaibei. Fifteen years later, Huang Xie proposed to the King of Chu: The area north of the Huaihe River is close to the State of Qi. The situation there is urgent. Please classify this area as a county to make governance more convenient. At the same time, he offered twelve counties in Huaibei and asked for the seal to be transferred to Jiangdong. King Kaolie agreed to his request. Chun Shenjun built cities in the old capital of Wu and made them his own capital. Chun Shenjun has already served as the prime minister of the Chu State. At this time, Qi State has Mengchang Lord, Zhao State has Pingyuan Lord, and Wei State has Xinling Lord. They are all vying to treat virtuous corporals, attract guests, compete with each other for wise men, and assist the king in controlling the state affairs. In the fourth year when Chun Shenjun served as the prime minister of Chu, Qin defeated and killed more than 400,000 Zhao Changping garrison. In the fifth year, Handan, the capital of Zhao State, was surrounded. Handan asked for help from the Chu State. Chu State sent Chun Shenjun to lead troops to rescue Handan. After the Qin army retreated, Chun Shenjun led his troops back to Chu State. In the eighth year when Chun Shenjun served as the prime minister of Chu State, he marched northward for Chu State, destroyed Lu State, and appointed Xunqing as the magistrate of Lanling County. At this time, the Chu State became prosperous and powerful again. Once, Lord Pingyuan of the State of Zhao sent envoys to visit Lord Chunshen, and Lord Chunshen arranged for them to stay in a first-class guesthouse. The envoy of the State of Zhao wanted to show off the wealth of the State of Zhao to the State of Chu, so he specially put a tortoise shell hairpin in his crown, showed off his sword scabbard decorated with pearls and jade, and asked to invite the guests of Lord Chun Shen to meet him. The distinguished guests of Lord Chun Shen all came to see the envoy of the State of Zhao wearing shoes made of pearls, which made the envoy of the State of Zhao feel ashamed. In the fourteenth year of Chun Shenjun's tenure as prime minister, King Zhuang Xiang of Qin came to the throne, appointed Lu Buwei as Prime Minister of Qin, and granted him the title of Marquis Wenxin. Captured the Eastern Zhou Dynasty. In the 22nd year of Chun Shenjun's appointment as prime minister, the princes of various countries were worried that Qin's conquests would be endless and unstoppable, so they made an alliance with each other to crusade against Qin in the west. The king of Chu served as the leader of the six-nation alliance, leaving Chun Shenjun in charge. After the Allied Forces of the Six Nations arrived at Hangu Pass, the Qin army came out to fight. The Allied Forces of the Six Nations were defeated and fled.
target: As prime minister, Chun Shenjun governed effectively, moving his fief to Jiangdong and building a capital in the old Wu city. He competed with other lords in attracting talented guests. In his fifth year, he led Chu forces to relieve the siege of Handan, Zhao's capital. In his eighth year, he conquered Lu for Chu, restoring Chu's strength. However, in his twenty-second year, a six-state alliance against Qin, led by Chu, was defeated at Hangu Pass, leading to his alienation by King Kaolie.

source: Now I know I'm pregnant, but no one else knows. I have only been favored by you for a short time. If you offer me to the King of Chu based on your noble status, the King of Chu will definitely favor me. I rely on God's blessing to give birth to a son. This will mean that your son will become the King of Chu, and the whole country of Chu will be yours. How is this compared with the unexpected disaster you suffer? Chun Shenjun thought that what he said was very right, so he sent Li Yuan's sister away from home, arranged her in a strict residence, and then told the King of Chu that he wanted to donate Li Yuan's sister. The King of Chu summoned Li Yuan's sister into the palace and favored her very much. He gave birth to a son, made him a prince, and made Li Yuan's sister a queen. The King of Chu valued Li Yuan, so Li Yuan participated in the government affairs. Li Yuan sent his sister to the palace, made her a queen, and made her son a prince. Worried that Lord Chun Shen would reveal his secret and become more arrogant, he secretly raised an assassin. He planned to kill Lord Chun Shen to silence him, and some people in the capital knew about it. In the twenty-fifth year of Chunshenjun's tenure as prime minister, King Kaolie of Chu fell seriously ill. Zhu Ying said to Chun Shenjun: There are unexpected blessings and unexpected disasters in the world. Now that you are in a world where life and death are uncertain, and you serve a moody monarch, how can you not have people come unexpectedly? Chun Shenjun asked: What is unexpected blessing? Zhu Ying replied: You have been the prime minister of Chu for more than 20 years. Although you are the prime minister in name, you are actually the king of Chu. Now the king of Chu is seriously ill and is about to die. You assist the young king and control the state affairs on his behalf, just like Yi Yin and Zhou Gong. When the king grows up and then hand over the power to him, doesn't it mean that you go south to claim the king and occupy the Chu country? This is what is called unexpected blessings. Chun Shenjun asked again: What is an unexpected disaster? Zhu Ying replied: Li Yuan is your enemy if he is not in charge of national affairs. He has been raising assassins for a long time without caring about the military. As soon as the King of Chu is born, Li Yuan will definitely enter the palace first to seize power and kill you to silence you. This is what is called an unexpected disaster. Chun Shenjun then asked: What do you mean by someone who comes unexpectedly? Zhu Ying replied: If you arrange for me to be the doctor, when the King of Chu is born, Li Yuan will be the first to enter the palace. I will kill Li Yuan for you. This is what is called an unexpected person. After hearing this, Chun Shenjun said: "You have to give up this plan." Li Yuan is a weak person, and I am very friendly to him. Besides, how could he get to this point! Zhu Ying knew that his suggestions were not adopted, and he was afraid that disaster would affect him, so he ran away. Seventeen days later, King Chu Kaolie passed away. As expected, Li Yuan entered the palace first and ambushed the assassin at Thorny Gate. When Chun Shenjun entered the Thorny Gate, the assassins raised by Li Yuan caught him from both sides and killed him. He cut off his head and threw it outside the Thorny Gate. At the same time, he sent officials to kill everyone in Chunshenjun's family. Li Yuan's sister was favored by Lord Chun Shen and became pregnant. Then she entered the palace and was favored by Queen Chu Kaolie. The son born to her was established as King of Chu. This was King Chu You. This year, Qin Shihuang has been on the throne for nine years. Lao Ai also had an affair with the Queen Mother of Qin. After being discovered, the three tribes were destroyed by the barbarians, and Lu Buwei was deposed because of his involvement. Taigong Shi said: I went to the Chu region and visited Chun Shenjun's old city. The palace buildings were very magnificent! At that time, Chun Shenjun persuaded King Qin Zhao and risked his life to send people to send the Prince of Chu back to Chu State. What a smart and brilliant move it was! But later he was controlled by Li Yuan and became confused. As the saying goes: If you fail to make a decision when you should make a decision, you will suffer disaster in turn. It means Chun Shenjun lost Zhu Ying's opportunity to kill Li Yuan, right?
target: Chun Shenjun later became involved with Li Yuan, who presented his pregnant sister to him. She convinced Chun Shenjun to offer her to the childless King Kaolie, ensuring his son would become king. The king favored her, and she bore a son, who became prince. Li Yuan, fearing Chun Shenjun would reveal the secret, secretly raised assassins. When King Kaolie fell ill, a guest named Zhu Ying warned Chun Shenjun of Li Yuan's plot, but he dismissed it. Seventeen days after the king's death, Li Yuan ambushed and killed Chun Shenjun at the palace gate, then massacred his family. Li Yuan's sister's son became King You of Chu. The historian comments that Chun Shenjun's early wisdom in persuading Qin and risking his life for the prince was admirable, but he later fell victim to Li Yuan's schemes, failing to act on Zhu Ying's advice, which led to his downfall.
