source: King Weiman of North Korea was originally from the state of Yan. Initially, when the Yan Kingdom was in its heyday, it conquered Zhenfan and North Korea, made them belong to the Yan Kingdom, appointed officials for them, and built defensive castles at the border fortresses. Later, the Qin State destroyed the Yan State, and North Korea became a border country outside Liaodong County. After the founding of the Han Dynasty, because North Korea was far away and difficult to defend, the previous passes in Liaodong County were renovated until they were bounded by the Xishui River, which was under the jurisdiction of the State of Yan. Later, King Lu Wan of Yan rebelled and went to the Huns. Weiman also went into exile, gathered more than a thousand of his companions, wore cone-shaped buns and barbarian clothes, walked out of the Great Wall in the east, crossed the Xu River, and lived in the original empty land of Qin called Shangxiazhang. During the time of Emperor Hui and Queen Gao of the Han Dynasty, when the world had just stabilized, the governor of Liaodong County agreed that Wei Man would be the foreign minister of the Han Dynasty to protect the barbarians outside the border fortresses and not allow them to come to the border to harass and plunder. The barbarian leaders wanted to see the emperor from the Han Dynasty and did not prohibit it. The governor of Liaodong reported this situation to the emperor, who agreed to the condition. Therefore, Weiman was able to use his military power and wealth to invade and surrender the small countries around him. Zhenfan and Lintun both surrendered and belonged to Weiman. The area under his control was thousands of miles in radius. Weiman passed the rule to his son, and then to his grandson Youqu. During this period, more and more refugees from the Han Dynasty were lured to North Korea, and Youqu never went to see the emperor of the Han Dynasty. Many small countries around Zhenfan wanted to submit letters requesting an audience with the Emperor of the Han Dynasty, but were blocked from letting the Emperor know about their request. In the second year of Yuanfeng, the Han Dynasty sent He He to blame and inform Youqu, but Youqu refused to accept the Han Dynasty's edict.
target: King Weiman of North Korea, originally from the state of Yan, settled in the empty region of Shangxiazhang after Yan's fall and Lu Wan's rebellion. During the reigns of Emperor Hui and Queen Gao of Han, the Liaodong governor appointed Weiman as a foreign minister to protect border barbarians, allowing him to use military power to subdue nearby states like Zhenfan and Lintun, expanding his territory. Weiman's rule passed to his son and grandson Youqu, who lured Han refugees and blocked smaller states from contacting the Han emperor. In the second year of Yuanfeng, the Han sent Shehe to reprimand Youqu, but Youqu rejected the edict.

Facing the Xu River, he sent a driver to assassinate the North Korean Pi Xiaowang who was escorting Shehe. Then he immediately crossed the river, galloped back, and entered the Han Dynasty border fortress. So he returned to the capital and reported to the emperor: I killed a North Korean general. The emperor believed that he had a good reputation for killing Korean generals, so he no longer pursued his fault, but awarded him the official position of captain of eastern Liaodong. North Korea resented Shehe and dispatched troops to make a surprise attack and killed Shehe. The emperor of the Han Dynasty ordered the recruitment of prisoners whose crimes had been pardoned to attack North Korea. In the autumn of the second year of Yuanfeng, the Han Dynasty sent general Yang Pu of Louzhou to cross the Bohai Sea by boat with an army of 50,000 people. General Xunshe of the left led his troops out of Liaodong County to attack Youqu. Youqu mobilized troops to defend strategic locations to resist the Han army. General Zuo's pawn named Duo was the first to lead the Liaodong troops to attack the enemy. As a result, the team failed and became separated. Most of them ran back and were executed for violating military law. General Lou Chuan led 7,000 soldiers from Qi to arrive at Wangxian City first. Youqu was guarding the city and heard the news that General Lou Chuan's army was small, so he went out to attack General Lou Chuan. General Lou Chuan's army failed and fled in all directions. General Yang Pu lost his army and fled to the mountains to hide for more than ten days. He gradually recovered his scattered soldiers and reunited them. General Xun Shen of the left attacked the Korean army stationed west of the Xu River, but failed to break through the enemy from the front.
target: Shehe assassinated a Korean general on his return, earning a promotion but provoking a Korean attack that killed him. The Han emperor then recruited pardoned prisoners to attack Korea. In autumn, General Yang Pu led 50,000 troops by sea, while General Xun She led forces from Liaodong. Youqu defended strategic points. Yang Pu's initial assault on Wangxian City failed, and his army scattered. Xun She also failed to break through Korean defenses.

target: The emperor sent Weishan to negotiate, and Youqu agreed to surrender, sending his prince with tribute.

source: General Zuo thought about General Lou Chuan's fault for losing the battle in the past. Now he was secretly friendly with the North Korean minister, but North Korea refused to surrender, so he suspected that General Lou Chuan had a rebellion conspiracy, but he did not dare to take action. The emperor said that the general was incompetent. Not long ago, I sent Weishan to tell Youqu to surrender. Youqu sent the prince to apologize, but Weishan, the messenger, could not handle the matter decisively and made mistakes in his plans with General Zuo, which finally broke the agreement of North Korea's surrender.
target: However, suspicions arose between the Han envoys and the Korean prince, leading to a breakdown. Weishan was executed for mishandling the situation.

The prince also suspected that the Han envoys and General Zuo wanted to deceive and kill him, so he stopped crossing the river and led the Korean people back. Weishan returned to the capital and reported to the emperor, who killed Weishan. General Zuo defeated the North Korean army on the Haishui River and then advanced until he reached the foot of Wangxian City and surrounded the northwest of the city.
target: Xun She then defeated the Korean army at Haishui River and besieged Wangxian City, joined by Yang Pu. The two generals disagreed on strategy: Xun She favored aggressive attack, while Yang Pu sought peaceful surrender. This discord prolonged the siege.

id: 史记/七十列传/朝鲜列传::group-005
article_path: 史记/七十列传/朝鲜列传
source: Gongsun Sui, the governor of Jinan, was sent to correct their mistakes. If there is a convenient and favorable opportunity, he can handle the affairs on his own at any time. After Gongsun Sui arrived in North Korea, General Zuo said: North Korea could have been captured long ago. There is a reason why it has not been captured yet. He also told Gongsun Sui that he had agreed with General Lou Chuan on the date of march, but General Lou Chuan did not come to join forces. He also told Gongsun Sui that he had always suspected General Lou Chuan of treason, and said, "If we don't arrest him now, I'm afraid it will be a big harm. Not only will General Lou Chuan rebel, but he will also unite with North Korea to destroy our army." Gongsun Sui also thought that this was the case, so he used the talisman to summon General Lou Chuan to General Zuo's camp to discuss the matter. He ordered General Zuo's men to capture General Lou Chuan on the spot, merge his troops under General Zuo, and then reported the incident to the Emperor of the Han Dynasty. The emperor killed Gongsun Sui. General Zuo merged the two armies and tried his best to attack North Korea. Korean Prime Minister Lu Ren, Prime Minister Han Yin, Prime Minister Nixi, and General Wang Xi discussed with each other: At first, General Lou Chuan was wanted to surrender, but now General Lou Chuan has been arrested, and only General Zuo leads the combined army. The war is becoming more and more urgent. We may not be able to persist, and the king refuses to surrender. Han Yin, Wang Yi, and passers-by all fled to the Han army and surrendered to the Han Dynasty. Passers-by died on the road. In the summer of the third year of Yuanfeng, Nixi Xiangcan sent people to kill the Korean king Youqu and surrendered to the Han Dynasty. Before Wang Xiancheng was captured, Cheng Si, the former minister of Youqu, rebelled again and attacked the Korean officials who did not rebel with him.
target: The emperor sent Gongsun Sui to mediate, but Xun She convinced him to arrest Yang Pu on suspicion of treason. Gongsun Sui complied, but the emperor later executed him. Xun She merged the armies and intensified the attack. Korean officials, fearing defeat, killed King Youqu and surrendered.

Therefore, the Han Dynasty finally pacified Korea and established four counties. The emperor of the Han Dynasty granted Shen the title of Marquis of Qingqing, Han Yin as the Marquis of Diju, Wang Xi as the Marquis of Pingzhou, and Chang demoted them to Jihou. Lu Zui was named Marquis of Wenyang because of his meritorious service after his father died. General Zuo was recalled to the capital. He committed the crime of competing for merit, becoming jealous of each other, and violating the battle plan, and was publicly executed. General Lou Chuan was also sentenced to death because he committed the crime of attacking the enemy first without authorization when his troops arrived at Lukou. He should have waited for General Zuo, resulting in many casualties. He atone for his crime with money, was exempted from the death penalty, and became a civilian. Tai Shigong said: King Youqu of Korea relied on the rugged terrain and the country was wiped out. She He's deception to gain credit became the beginning of sending troops to attack North Korea. General Lou Chuan acts with a narrow mind and suffers disaster when in danger. I regretted that I had failed in the capture of Panyu, but was suspected of rebelling. Xun Zhen and Gong Sun Sui were both beheaded as they fought for merit. The two armies of Yang Pu and Xun Shen who conquered Korea suffered humiliation, and the generals were not granted the title of marquis.
target: The Han established four counties, granting titles to defectors. Xun She was executed for rivalry and violating battle plans, while Yang Pu was reduced to civilian status after paying a fine. The historian notes that Korea's reliance on terrain led to its fall, and the generals' conflicts caused their downfall.

id: 史记/七十列传/李将军列传::group-000
article_path: 史记/七十列传/李将军列传
source: General Li Guang was a native of Chengji County, Longxi County. His ancestor was Li Xin, a general of the Qin State who captured Prince Dan of Yan. His home was originally in Huaili County, but later moved to Chengji. The art of archery has been passed down from generation to generation in Li Guang's family. In the fourteenth year of Emperor Wen's reign, the Huns invaded Xiaoguan with great force. Li Guang joined the army to fight against the Huns as a son of a good family. Because he was good at riding and archery, and killed many enemy heads, he was appointed Zhonglang. Li Guang's cousin Li Cai was also appointed as Zhonglang. Both of them were appointed as regular servants of the martial arts, with an annual salary of 800 shi of food. Li Guang once traveled with the emperor, often charging into battle, resisting enemies, and killing ferocious beasts. Emperor Wen said: What a pity! You haven't encountered a good opportunity. If you catch up with the Emperor Gaozu's era and be granted the title of Marquis of Ten Thousand Households, what's the point? After Emperor Jing came to the throne, Li Guang was appointed as the Captain of Longxi, and then as the Cavalry General. During the rebellion of the seven kingdoms of Wu and Chu, Li Guang served as the captain of Xiaoqi and followed the Taiwei Zhou Yafu to fight back against the Wu and Chu rebels. He captured the enemy's flag at the foot of Changyi City and became famous. However, because King Xiao of Liang privately awarded Li Guang the General's Seal, the court did not reward him after he returned to the court. He was appointed as the governor of Shanggu, and the Huns came to fight every day. Sun Kunxie, the Duke of Dian, cried to the emperor and said: Li Guang's talent is unparalleled in the world. He relies on his talent to fight the enemy head-on many times. I'm afraid he will lose this good general. So he was appointed as the prefect of Shangjun. Later, Li Guang was transferred to the prefecture of the border counties, and then to the prefecture of Shangjun. He served as the prefect of Longxi, Beidi, Yanmen, Daijun, and Yunzhong, and was famous for his vigorous fighting. The Huns invaded Shangjun in a large scale, and the emperor sent a eunuch to study military affairs with Li Guang and fight against the Huns. The eunuch led dozens of cavalry on horseback. When they encountered three Huns, they fought with them. The three Huns turned around and fired arrows, wounding the eunuch and almost killing all his cavalry. The eunuch fled back to Li Guang. Li Guang said: "This must be a Xiongnu expert in shooting vultures." Li Guang then took a hundred cavalry to chase the three Huns. The three men had no horses and traveled on foot. After walking for dozens of miles, Li Guang ordered his cavalry to spread out to the left and right and outflank them in two directions. He personally shot the three men, shot two to death and captured one alive. As expected, it was the Huns' eagle shooter. After tying him onto his horse, he saw thousands of Huns cavalry in the distance. When they saw Li Guang, they thought he was a cavalryman luring the enemy. They were surprised and ran up the mountain to set up their formation.
target: General Li Guang, a native of Chengji County, Longxi, descended from Li Xin, a Qin general. Skilled in archery from a young age, he joined the army during Emperor Wen's reign, distinguishing himself against the Xiongnu and becoming a Zhonglang. Emperor Wen lamented his unlucky timing, suggesting he would have been a marquis in Emperor Gaozu's era. Under Emperor Jing, Li Guang served as a cavalry general, capturing enemy flags during the Rebellion of the Seven States but receiving no reward due to a private seal from the King of Liang. He later governed several border commanderies, earning fame for his fierce fighting. During a Xiongnu invasion of Shangjun, Li Guang, with only a hundred cavalry, encountered thousands of Xiongnu.

id: 史记/七十列传/李将军列传::group-001
article_path: 史记/七十列传/李将军列传
source: A Hun general riding a white horse came out to guard his soldiers. Li Guang immediately mounted his horse and galloped with more than a dozen cavalry. He shot the Hun general riding a white horse to death. Then he returned to his cavalry team, took off the saddle, and asked the soldiers to let go of their horses and lie down casually. It was dusk at this time, and the Xiongnu army always felt strange and did not dare to attack. In the middle of the night, the Xiongnu soldiers thought that the Han Dynasty had an ambush nearby and wanted to sneak up on them at night, so the Xiongnu troops retreated. The next morning, Li Guang returned to his army camp. The army did not know where Li Guang was going, so they were unable to respond later. Several years later, Emperor Jing died and Emperor Wu ascended the throne. All the ministers on the left and right thought that Li Guang was a famous general, so Li Guang was transferred from the prefect of Shangjun to the chief of the imperial guard of Weiyang Palace, and Cheng Bushi also came to be the chief of the imperial guard of Changle Palace. Cheng Bushi and Li Guang both served as governors of border counties and were also in charge of military garrison. When it came time to attack the Xiongnu, Li Guang marched without strict formations and formations. He stationed troops near places with abundant water and lush grass, and set up camps and lodgings, which was convenient for everyone. He did not call for self-defense at night. The shogunate simplified various documents and books, but he placed sentries far away, so he did not encounter danger. Cheng Bushi had strict requirements on the organization of the troops, marching columns, and garrison formations. He kept watch at night, and the military clerks had to wait until dawn to process performance appraisals and other official documents and books. The troops had no rest, but they never encountered danger. Cheng Bushi said: Li Guang's army is simple and easy, but if the enemy suddenly attacks him, he will be unable to stop him; but his soldiers are comfortable and happy, and they are willing to die for him. Although my army is busy with military affairs, the enemy does not dare to invade me. At that time, Li Guang and Cheng Bushi at the border of the Han Dynasty were both famous generals, but the Huns were afraid of Li Guang's strategy, and most of the soldiers were willing to follow Li Guang and suffered the hardship of following Cheng Bushi. During the reign of Emperor Jing, Cheng Bushi was awarded the title of Taizhong Dafu because he repeatedly spoke out and remonstrated. He was an honest man and strictly abided by the court documents and laws. Later, the Han Dynasty used the city of Mayi to lure Chanyu and sent a large army to ambush in the valley near Mayi. Li Guang was appointed as the general of Xiaoqi and was controlled by the guard general Han Anguo.
target: He cleverly dismounted and unsaddled his men, feigning a lure, which deterred the enemy from attacking. At night, the Xiongnu retreated, suspecting an ambush. Under Emperor Wu, Li Guang became a palace guard chief alongside Cheng Bushi. While Cheng's army was strict and disciplined, Li Guang's was simple and flexible, earning soldiers' loyalty. The Xiongnu feared Li Guang's strategy, though his lax approach sometimes led to danger. Li Guang was captured by the Xiongnu but escaped by feigning death, stealing a horse, and shooting pursuers.

id: 史记/七十列传/李将军列传::group-002
article_path: 史记/七十列传/李将军列传
source: The law enforcement officer ruled that Li Guang had suffered too many casualties, and he himself was captured alive by the enemy and should be beheaded. Li Guang used money and materials to atone for his death penalty and reduced his position to serve the people. In the blink of an eye, Li Guang has been living at home for several years. Li Guang's family and Guan Qiang, the grandson of the late Yingyin Hou Guanying, live in seclusion in Lantian and often go hunting in Nanshan. One night he went out with an entourage on horseback and drank with others in the fields.
target: He was sentenced to death for losses but redeemed himself with money, becoming a commoner.

id: 史记/七十列传/李将军列传::group-003
article_path: 史记/七十列传/李将军列传
source: When he came back, he walked to Ba Ling Pavilion. Ba Lingwei was drunk and shouted loudly, prohibiting Li Guang from passing. Li Guang's entourage said: This is the former General Li. Tingwei said: The current general is not allowed to pass, let alone his predecessor! So he detained Li Guang and asked him to stay under Ba Ling Pavilion. Not long after, the Xiongnu invaded and killed the prefect of Liaoxi and defeated General Han. General Han moved to Youbeiping. So the emperor summoned Li Guang and appointed him as the right governor of Beiping. Li Guang immediately asked to send Lieutenant Ba Ling to join him, and he was killed when he arrived in the army. Li Guang was stationed in Youbeiping. When the Xiongnu heard about it, they called him the "Flying General of the Han Dynasty" and avoided him for several years, not daring to invade Youbeiping. Li Guang went out hunting and saw a stone in the grass. He thought it was a tiger and shot at it. Then he ejaculated again, but after all, he couldn't ejaculate anymore.
target: Later, as Right Beiping governor, he killed a disrespectful Ba Ling guard and was called the "Flying General of Han," causing the Xiongnu to avoid him for years. He once mistook a stone for a tiger and shot it, but could not repeat the feat.

id: 史记/七十列传/李将军列传::group-004
article_path: 史记/七十列传/李将军列传
source: Then he ejaculated again, but after all, he couldn't ejaculate anymore. Li Guang had been stationed in various counties. When he heard about tigers, he often went to shoot them himself. When he was stationed in Youbeiping, he went to shoot the tiger again. The tiger jumped up and injured Li Guang. Li Guang also shot the tiger to death in the end. Li Guang was an upright official, and he distributed rewards to his subordinates. He always shared food and drink with the soldiers. From his life to his death, Li Guang served as an official with a salary of two thousand stone for more than forty years. He had no extra property in his family and never talked about family property.
target: Li Guang was generous, sharing rewards and food with soldiers, and lived simply despite decades of high office.

id: 史记/七十列传/李将军列传::group-005
article_path: 史记/七十列传/李将军列传
source: Not long after, Shi Jian passed away, so the emperor summoned Li Guang and asked him to succeed Shi Jian as Lang Zhongling. In the sixth year of Yuanshuo, Li Guang was appointed as the rear general. He followed General Che Weiqing's army out of Dingxiang to conquer the Xiongnu. Many generals were made marquises for their military merits because they killed the enemy's heads in compliance with the prescribed amount, but Li Guang's army had no military merits.
target: In the sixth year of Yuanshuo, Li Guang joined General Wei Qing's campaign but had no military merits.

id: 史记/七十列传/李将军列传::group-006
article_path: 史记/七十列传/李将军列传
source: Two years later, Li Guang, who held the title of Langzhongling, led 4,000 cavalry from Youbeiping. Bowang Marquis Zhang Qian led 10,000 cavalry to join Li Guang in two separate routes. After marching for several hundred miles, King Zuoxian of the Xiongnu led 40,000 cavalry and surrounded Li Guang. Li Guang's soldiers were very frightened, so Li Guang sent his son Li Gan to ride towards the Xiongnu army. Li Gan galloped alone with dozens of cavalry, passed through the Xiongnu cavalry formation, and protruded from its left and right wings. He came back and reported to Li Guang: "The enemy Huns are very easy to deal with!" The soldiers felt relieved. Li Guang formed a circular formation, facing outward. The Huns attacked fiercely, and arrows rained down. More than half of the Han soldiers were dead, and their arrows were all used up. Li Guang ordered the soldiers to draw their bows fully and not to release arrows. Li Guang personally used the big yellow crossbow to shoot at the Huns' lieutenants, killing several of them, and the Huns army gradually dispersed. It was getting late at this time, and the officers and soldiers were all expressionless, but Li Guang looked calm and paid more attention to rectifying the army. From then on, everyone in the army admired his bravery. The next day, they went to fight hard again. Bowang Hou's army also arrived, and the Huns retreated. The Han army was very tired and could not pursue him. At that time, Li Guang's army was almost completely wiped out, so he had to withdraw his troops and return to the court. According to the laws of the Han Dynasty, if Bowang Hou marched slowly and delayed the deadline, he should be sentenced to death, use money to atone for his crime, and be reduced to a civilian. Li Guang's merits and demerits were equal to each other, so he was not rewarded. At first, Li Guang's cousin Li Cai and Li Guang served Emperor Wen together. By the time of Emperor Jing, Li Cai had accumulated merit and obtained an official position with an annual salary of two thousand dan. During the reign of Emperor Wu, he served as the prime minister of the country.
target: Two years later, he was surrounded by 40,000 Xiongnu with 4,000 cavalry. His son Li Gan's bravery calmed the troops, and Li Guang's personal archery killed several enemy officers, forcing a retreat. Despite heavy losses, Li Guang's calmness earned admiration. His cousin Li Cai, though less talented, became a marquis and prime minister, while Li Guang remained unenfeoffed. Astrologer Wang Shuo attributed this to Li Guang's past massacre of 800 surrendered Qiang rebels.

id: 史记/七十列传/李将军列传::group-007
article_path: 史记/七十列传/李将军列传
source: Wang Shuo said: There is no greater disaster than killing those who have surrendered. This is why generals cannot be made marquises. Two years later, General Wei Qing and General Huo Qubing led a large-scale expedition against the Xiongnu. Li Guang personally requested several times to accompany them. The emperor thought that he was old and did not agree. It took a long time before he allowed him to go and made him a former general. This year is the fourth year of Yuanshou. Li Guang soon followed the general Wei Qing on an expedition against the Huns. After leaving the border fortress, Wei Qing captured the enemy soldiers and knew where the Shan Yu lived. He led his elite troops to chase the Shan Yu and ordered Li Guang to merge with the troops of General You and attack from the east. The east road is somewhat circuitous, and the army is walking in a place where there is a lack of water and grass, so it is inevitable that they will not be able to march together. Li Guang personally requested: "My position is a former general, but now the general ordered me to send troops from the east route. Besides, I have been fighting against the Xiongnu since I was a boy, and I have only got a chance to confront the Shanyu today. I am willing to be a vanguard and fight to the death with the Shanyu first." General Wei Qing was secretly warned by the emperor, thinking that Li Guang was old and had a bad fate, so he should not let him confront the Chanyu, as he might not be able to realize his wish to capture the Chanyu. At that time, Gongsun Ao had just lost his title of Marquis and was appointed lieutenant general, accompanying the general on the expedition. The general also wanted Gongsun Ao to fight against Shanyu with him, so he deliberately transferred former general Li Guang away. Li Guang also knew the inside story at the time, so he insisted on asking the general to withdraw the transfer order. The general did not agree to his request, and ordered the chief historian to write a document and send it to Li Guang's shogunate, and said to him: Hurry up to the right general's chariot troops and follow the document. Li Guang set off without saying goodbye to the general. He was very angry and went to the military headquarters. He led his troops and joined forces with Zhao Shiqi, the right general of the chariot army, and set off from the east road. The army has no guide and sometimes loses its way and ends up falling behind the general. The general fought with Shanyu, but Shanyu fled, and Wei Qing had no choice but to return his troops. The general traveled south across the desert and met the former general and the right general. After Li Guang paid an audience with the general, he returned to his army. The general sent Chang Shi to bring dry food and wine to Li Guang. The envoy asked Li Guang and Zhao Shiqi about the situation of losing their way. Wei Qing wanted to write a letter to the emperor reporting detailed military information. Li Guang didn't answer. The general sent Chang Shi to urgently order the personnel of Li Guang shogunate to go for trial and confrontation. Li Guang said: The captains are not guilty. It was me who lost my way. Now I will personally go to the shogunate to be tried and confronted. When he arrived at the shogunate of the general, Li Guang said to his subordinates: I have fought more than seventy battles with the Xiongnu since I was a boy, and now I have the honor to follow the general on an expedition to fight the Shanyu army. However, the general sent my troops to take a circuitous and long road, and they lost their way. Isn't it God's will? Besides, I am already over sixty years old. After all, I can no longer bear the insults of those swordsmen and pen officials.
target: In the fourth year of Yuanshou, Li Guang, now a former general, joined Wei Qing's campaign against the Xiongnu. Wei Qing, warned by the emperor about Li Guang's age and bad luck, ordered him to take a circuitous eastern route. Li Guang protested but was overruled, leading to his army losing its way. After the campaign, Wei Qing demanded an inquiry. Li Guang, refusing to face humiliation, declared, "I have fought over seventy battles. Now, at over sixty, I cannot bear the insults of clerks," and committed suicide. His death caused widespread mourning.

id: 史记/七十列传/李将军列传::group-008
article_path: 史记/七十列传/李将军列传
source: Li Guang said: The captains are not guilty. It was me who lost my way. Now I will personally go to the shogunate to be tried and confronted. When he arrived at the shogunate of the general, Li Guang said to his subordinates: I have fought more than seventy battles with the Xiongnu since I was a boy, and now I have the honor to follow the general on an expedition to fight the Shanyu army. However, the general sent my troops to take a circuitous and long road, and they lost their way. Isn't it God's will? Besides, I am already over sixty years old. After all, I can no longer bear the insults of those swordsmen and pen officials. So he drew his sword and killed himself. All the soldiers in Li Guang's army cried bitterly. When the people heard the news, whether they knew him or not, whether they were old or young, they all shed tears for Li Guang. The right general Zhao Shiqi was handed over to the law enforcement officials alone, and he should be sentenced to death. He should use property to atone for his crime and be reduced to a civilian. Li Guang had three sons named Danghu, Jiao and Gan, all of whom were appointed Langguan. Once the emperor was playing with the jester Han Yan, and Han Yan acted a little wanton. Li Danghu went to beat Han Yan, but Han Yan ran away, so the emperor thought Danghu was brave. Li Danghu died early, and Li Jiao was named the prefect of Daijun. Both of them died before Li Guang. Li Danghu had a posthumous son named Li Ling. When Li Guang died in the army, Li Gan was following the hussar general Huo Qubing. In the second year after Li Guang's death, Li Cai used his position as prime minister to occupy the open space on both sides of the road in front of Emperor Jing's mausoleum. He was convicted and should be sent to law officials for investigation. However, Li Cai did not want to be tried and confronted and committed suicide. His feudal state was abolished. Li Gan served as a school lieutenant and accompanied General Hussar to attack King Zuoxian of the Huns. He fought hard, captured King Zuoxian's war drums and flags, and beheaded many enemies. As a result, he was granted the title of Marquis of Guannei and granted 200 households in the city. He succeeded Li Guang as Langzhongling. Soon, Li Gan resented the general Wei Qing for causing his father to die of hatred, so he wounded the general. The general concealed the incident and did not make it public. Not long after that, Li Gan followed the emperor to Yong County and went hunting in Ganquan Palace. General Huo Qubing was related to Wei Qing, so he shot Li Gan to death. Huo Qubing was a noble and favored man at the time, so the emperor concealed the truth and said that Li Gan was killed by a deer.
target: Li Guang's sons—Danghu, Jiao, and Gan—served as officials. Danghu died young, and Jiao became a prefect. Li Gan, a marquis, wounded Wei Qing in revenge but was later killed by Huo Qubing, who claimed it was a deer accident. Li Guang's grandson Li Ling, a skilled archer, led 5,000 infantry against 80,000 Xiongnu, killing over 10,000 before surrendering due to lack of supplies. The Han executed his family, ending the Li family's reputation. The historian concluded that Li Guang's honest character, like peach and plum trees, naturally drew people to him, despite his lack of eloquence.

id: 史记/七十列传/李斯列传::group-000
article_path: 史记/七十列传/李斯列传
source: Li Si was a native of Shangcai, State of Chu. When he was young, he worked as a minor official in the county. He saw rats eating dirty things in the toilet near his office. Whenever someone or a dog came near, he would be frightened and run away. Later, Li Si walked into the granary and saw the rats in the granary eating the stored grain and living under the big house without having to worry about being disturbed by people or dogs. So Li Si sighed with emotion: A person's talent or incompetence is determined by his environment, just like a mouse. So Li Si learned from Xunzi how emperors governed the world. After completing his studies, Li Si estimated that the King of Chu was not worthy of serving, and that the six kingdoms were already weak and there was no hope of making contributions to them, so he wanted to go west to Qin. Before leaving, he said goodbye to Xunzi: I heard that if a person encounters an opportunity, he should not slack off. Nowadays, all the vassal states are striving for opportunities so that lobbyists can make meritorious deeds and gain real power. Now that the King of Qin wants to annex other countries and proclaim himself emperor to govern the world, this is a good time for political activists and lobbyists from civilian backgrounds to travel around and express their ambitions. Being in a humble position and not thinking about seeking fame and wealth is like an animal. It only wants to eat meat when it sees it. It only has a human face but can barely walk. Therefore, the greatest shame is humble status, and the greatest sorrow is poverty. Being in a humble position and difficult situation for a long time, yet still criticizing society, hating fame and wealth, and slandering oneself as uncontested is not the original wish of a scholar. So I am going west to lobby the King of Qin. After Li Si arrived in Qin, just as King Zhuangxiang of Qin passed away, Li Si asked to be a retainer of Lu Buwei, the prime minister of Qin. Lu Buwei appreciated him very much and appointed him Lang Guan. As a result, Li Si got the opportunity to lobby. He said to the King of Qin: Mediocre people often lose opportunities, but those who can achieve great achievements are those who can take advantage of opportunities and be ruthless.
target: Li Si was a native of Shangcai in the State of Chu. As a young county official, he observed rats in the toilet fleeing from people and dogs, contrasting them with granary rats that ate stored grain undisturbed. This led him to conclude that a person's competence depends on their environment. He studied under Xunzi to learn the art of governing an empire. Afterward, deeming the King of Chu unworthy and the six kingdoms too weak for him to achieve merit, he decided to go west to Qin. He told Xunzi that opportunity must be seized, and that the King of Qin's ambition to unify the world was a perfect chance for a commoner to gain fame and wealth. He considered humble status the greatest shame and poverty the greatest sorrow, rejecting the notion of a scholar who claims to be above worldly pursuits.

id: 史记/七十列传/李斯列传::group-001
article_path: 史记/七十列传/李斯列传
source: Therefore, the greatest shame is humble status, and the greatest sorrow is poverty. Being in a humble position and difficult situation for a long time, yet still criticizing society, hating fame and wealth, and slandering oneself as uncontested is not the original wish of a scholar. So I am going west to lobby the King of Qin. After Li Si arrived in Qin, just as King Zhuangxiang of Qin passed away, Li Si asked to be a retainer of Lu Buwei, the prime minister of Qin. Lu Buwei appreciated him very much and appointed him Lang Guan. As a result, Li Si got the opportunity to lobby. He said to the King of Qin: Mediocre people often lose opportunities, but those who can achieve great achievements are those who can take advantage of opportunities and be ruthless. In the past, although Duke Mu of Qin dominated the world, he did not move eastward and annex the six kingdoms of Shandong. What was the reason? The reason was that the number of princes was still large and the prestige of the Zhou Dynasty had not completely declined. Therefore, the five hegemons emerged alternately and successively promoted the Eastern Zhou royal family. Since Qin Xiaogong, the royal family of the Eastern Zhou Dynasty has been weak and weak, and the princes have merged with each other. The area east of Hangu Pass has been transformed into six kingdoms. Qin State took advantage of the victory to gradually conquer the six kingdoms. It has been about six generations now. Nowadays, the princes obey Qin just like the counties obey the imperial court. With the power of Qin and the wisdom of the king, just like sweeping away the dust on the stove, it is enough to wipe out the princes, achieve the emperor's cause, and realize the unification of the world. This is the only opportunity that comes once in a lifetime. If we are slack now and do not take action on this matter, when the princes become stronger again and enter into alliance alliances, even if they are as capable as Huang Di, they will not be able to annex them. Qin Shihuang appointed Li Si as the chief historian, followed his plan, and secretly sent counselors to various countries with gold and jade treasures to lobby. If famous figures from various countries can be bribed, they will be bribed with gifts; if they cannot be bribed, they will be killed with sharp swords. These are all strategies to alienate the relationship between the princes and their ministers. Then, the King of Qin sent good generals to attack later. The King of Qin appointed Li Si as his guest minister. At this time, the Korean Zheng Guo came to Qin as a spy in the name of building channels, and was soon discovered. The royal family and ministers of the State of Qin all said to the King of Qin: Most of the people who come from various vassal states to serve the King of Qin are lobbying for their king, just to alienate the State of Qin. They ask the King to expel all the guests. Li Si was also among the guests planned to be expelled. So Li Si wrote a letter saying: I heard that officials were talking about expelling guest guests. I privately thought that this was wrong. In the past, Duke Mu of Qin recruited talented people, and he obtained Yu Yu from Xirong, Baili Xi from the garden of Chu in the east, Uncle Jian from Song, and Pi Bao and Gongsun Zhi from Jin. None of these five people were born in Qin, but Duke Mu of Qin used them to annex more than 20 countries, and then dominated Xirong. Qin Xiaogong adopted Shang Yang's new method and changed customs. As a result, the people prospered and the country became rich and powerful. The people were willing to serve the country and the princes sincerely submitted. He defeated the armies of Chu and Wei and captured thousands of miles of land. To this day, the country is politically stable and strong.
target: Upon arriving in Qin, Li Si became a retainer of Prime Minister Lü Buwei, who appointed him as a Lang official. He then advised the King of Qin that while Duke Mu of Qin had dominated the world, he could not annex the six kingdoms because the Zhou dynasty's prestige had not yet declined. Since Duke Xiao of Qin, the Zhou had weakened, and the six kingdoms had formed. Now, with Qin's power and the king's wisdom, the time was ripe to unify the world. He warned that hesitation would allow the princes to strengthen and form alliances, making conquest impossible. The King of Qin appointed Li Si as Chief Historian, following his plan to bribe or assassinate key figures in other states to alienate them from their rulers, followed by military attacks. Li Si was later made a Guest Minister. When the Korean spy Zheng Guo was discovered, Qin's nobles urged the king to expel all foreign guests, including Li Si. Li Si wrote a letter arguing against this. He cited Duke Mu of Qin, who used five non-Qin officials to dominate Xirong; Duke Xiao, who used Shang Yang to make Qin rich and powerful; King Hui, who used Zhang Yi to expand territory and break up alliances; and King Zhao, who used Fan Sui to strengthen the royal house. He argued that these four rulers relied on guest ministers. He then compared the king's love for foreign treasures, music, and women to his rejection of foreign talent, stating this was not the way to unify the world. He concluded that expelling guests would weaken Qin and aid its enemies. The king abolished the expulsion order, restored Li Si's position, and later promoted him to Tingwei. Over twenty years, Qin unified the world, and Li Si became Prime Minister.

id: 史记/七十列传/李斯列传::group-002
article_path: 史记/七十列传/李斯列传
source: After more than twenty years, he finally unified the world and honored the king as "Emperor". The emperor also appointed Li Si as prime minister. They also demolished the city walls of counties and counties in various countries, destroyed weapons in various places, and stated that they would no longer be used. The Qin State did not have an inch of enfeoffed land, nor did it make the emperor's sons or brothers kings, nor did it confer meritorious officials as princes, so that the country would never have the scourge of war from now on. In the thirty-fourth year of Qin Shi Huang's reign, he held a banquet in Xianyang Palace to entertain officials. Dr. Zhou Qingchen and others praised Qin Shi Huang's military might and virtue. Chun Yuyue, a native of Qi State, advised: I heard that the Yin, Shang and Zhou dynasties ruled for more than a thousand years, and they enfeoffed clan members and heroes as their own auxiliary forces. And now, although Your Majesty has unified the world, your children are still common people. If there is a disaster like Tian Chang and Liu Qing seizing power and usurping the throne, and there are no strong assistant ministers in the court, who will come to rescue them? I have never heard of a dynasty that could maintain a long-term rule without learning from ancient experience. Now Zhou Qingchen and others are flattering you in person to aggravate your mistake. They are not loyal. The First Emperor handed over this memorial to Li Si. Li Si thought this argument was absurd, so he discarded it, and wrote to the emperor: In ancient times, the world was scattered and chaotic, and they did not obey each other, so the princes rose up together. General public opinion praised the ancient times for denying the present and decorating some exaggerated words to disturb the reality of society. People thought that their own school had the best knowledge to deny the emperor's policies and decrees.
target: In the 34th year of Qin Shi Huang's reign, Dr. Zhou Qingchen praised the emperor, but Chun Yuyue advised enfeoffing clan members, warning that without strong assistants, the dynasty could not last. The First Emperor asked Li Si, who dismissed the argument. Li Si wrote that in ancient times, scholars used the past to criticize the present, undermining the emperor's authority.

id: 史记/七十列传/李斯列传::group-003
article_path: 史记/七十列传/李斯列传
source: Now His Majesty has unified the world, distinguished right from wrong, and made the emperor a common person in the country. However, hundreds of schools of thought have come together to criticize the imperial court's laws and regulations. When they heard that the imperial court issued an order, they immediately discussed it from the viewpoint of their own school. If this continues without prohibition, the power and prestige of the monarch above will decline, and private gangs will form below. Therefore, it is better to ban it. I request that all the "Poems", "Books" and works of various schools of thought be swept away. Thirty days after the order is issued, if anyone still disobeys, he will be sentenced to tattoos and hard labor in building the city. Not included in the purge are books on medicine, divination, planting, etc. If anyone wants to learn the law, he should take officials as his teachers. Qin Shihuang approved his suggestion and confiscated the "Book of Songs", "Shangshu" and the works of various schools of thought, in order to make the people ignorant and make it impossible for people in the world to use ancient events to criticize the current court. The revision of the legal system and the formulation of laws and regulations all started with Qin Shihuang. Unified the writing system and built villas throughout the country. The next year, the First Emperor went on inspection tours and pacified the ethnic minorities in all directions. Li Si made a lot of efforts in these measures. Li Si's eldest son Li You served as the governor of Sanchuan County. His sons all married Qin princesses, and his daughters all married Qin royal family members.
target: He requested that all "Poems," "Books," and works of the hundred schools be banned, with punishment for those who disobeyed, except for books on medicine, divination, and planting. The emperor approved, confiscating these texts to make the people ignorant. Li Si also contributed to unifying the writing system and building imperial villas. His sons married Qin princesses, and his daughters married Qin royalty.

id: 史记/七十列传/李斯列传::group-004
article_path: 史记/七十列传/李斯列传
source: The youngest son Hu Hai was very favored and asked to accompany him, and the First Emperor agreed. None of the other sons followed. In July of this year, Qin Shihuang arrived at Shaqiu and was very ill. He ordered Zhao Gao to write an edict to his son Fusu, saying: Hand over the army to Meng Tian, ​​hurry to Xianyang to attend the funeral, and then bury him. The letters were sealed, but before they were delivered to the envoy, Qin Shihuang passed away. The letters and seals were all in the hands of Zhao Gao. Only his youngest son Hu Hai, Prime Ministers Li Si and Zhao Gao, and five or six trusted eunuchs knew about the death of the First Emperor. The rest of the officials did not know. Li Si believed that the emperor died outside and the crown prince had not been officially established, so he kept it a secret and placed the body of the First Emperor in a car that could both keep warm and ventilate and cool him. The officials performed their duties and presented food and drinks as usual, so the eunuch pretended to ask the emperor to approve the reports from the car. Therefore, Zhao Gao withheld the edict given by the First Emperor to Fusu, and said to his son Hu Hai: The emperor has passed away, and there is no edict to make all his sons kings. He only gave an edict to his eldest son Fusu. When the eldest son arrives, he ascends the throne and becomes emperor, but you don’t even have a fief of any size. What should you do? Hu Hai said: That’s how it is. I have heard that a wise monarch knows his ministers best, and a wise father knows his son best. When my father died, he did not issue an order to divide the princes, so what else could he say? Zhao Gao said: Not so. The power in the world today, no matter who's life or death, is in the hands of you, me and Li Si!
target: At a banquet, Li Si lamented that his wealth and status had reached their peak, and he feared the decline that must follow. In the 37th year, the First Emperor died at Shaqiu. Li Si, Zhao Gao, and Hu Hai kept his death secret. Zhao Gao withheld the emperor's edict to Fusu and persuaded Hu Hai to usurp the throne, arguing that power was in their hands and that great deeds required decisive action. Hu Hai agreed, and Zhao Gao convinced Li Si by warning that Fusu would replace him with Meng Tian, leading to his death.

id: 史记/七十列传/李斯列传::group-005
article_path: 史记/七十列传/李斯列传
source: Li Si looked up to the sky and sighed with tears: Alas! Unfortunately, we are in troubled times, and since I can no longer remain loyal to death, where will I place my destiny? So Li Si obeyed Zhao Gao. Zhao Gao then reported back to Hu Hai and said: I was sent to inform Prime Minister Li Si on your order, Crown Prince. How dare he disobey the order? So they discussed together and forged an edict from Qin Shihuang to Prime Minister Li Si, making Hu Hai the crown prince. He also forged an edict to his eldest son Fusu, saying: I travel around the world, praying and offering sacrifices to the gods of famous mountains in various places for longevity. Now Fusu and General Meng Tian have led hundreds of thousands of troops to garrison the border for more than ten years. They have been unable to advance, and the soldiers have suffered many casualties. They have not made any achievements. Instead, they have written many times to bluntly slander what I have done. Because they cannot be dismissed and returned to Beijing to become the prince, they are resentful and dissatisfied day and night. Fusu was unfilial as a human son and committed suicide with a sword! General Meng Tian was out with Fusu. If he didn't correct his mistake, he should have known about his plan. As a minister, he was not loyal, so he was ordered to commit suicide and handed over the army to the deputy general Wang Li. He sealed the edict with the emperor's jade seal and asked Hu Hai's retainers to take the edict to Shangjun and hand it over to Fusu. After the messenger arrived, Fusu opened the letter, cried, and entered the inner room to commit suicide. Meng Tian stopped Fusu and said: "Your Majesty is away and has not established a prince. He has sent me to lead an army of 300,000 to guard the border. The prince will serve as the supervisor. This is an important task in the world."
target: Li Si wept but complied. They forged an edict making Hu Hai crown prince and another ordering Fusu and Meng Tian to commit suicide. Fusu obeyed, but Meng Tian was imprisoned. Hu Hai became the Second Emperor, and Zhao Gao gained great power.

id: 史记/七十列传/李斯列传::group-006
article_path: 史记/七十列传/李斯列传
source: Zhao Gao said: This can be done by a wise monarch, but it should be taboo by a confused monarch. I took the liberty to say something that I am not afraid of beheading, so please pay more attention to your majesty. All the princes and ministers are suspicious of Sha Qiu's conspiracy, and these princes are all your brothers, and these ministers were appointed by the late emperor. Now that Your Majesty has just ascended the throne, these people are indignant and resentful, fearing that they will cause trouble. What's more, although Meng Tian is dead, Meng Yi is still leading troops outside. The reason why I am worried is just that I am afraid that there will be bad results. Your Majesty, how can you enjoy this? The second said: What can we do?
target: The Second Emperor wanted to indulge his desires, but Zhao Gao warned that the princes and former ministers were suspicious and might rebel.

id: 史记/七十列传/李斯列传::group-007
article_path: 史记/七十列传/李斯列传
source: The second said: What can we do? Zhao Gao said: Implement strict laws and cruel punishments, kill all those who break the law and those who are implicated, until the entire clan is exterminated, kill the ministers of the dynasty and alienate your brothers and sisters, make the formerly poor people rich, and make the formerly humble people noble. Eliminate all the former emperor's old ministers, re-appoint those you trust and keep them by your side. In this way, they will be grateful to you from the bottom of their hearts, eradicate harm and put an end to treachery. No one in the group will not receive your favor and accept your kindness. Your Majesty, you can sit back and relax and enjoy yourself. There is no better idea than this. The Second Emperor believed that Zhao Gao's words were correct, so he revised the law. So the ministers and princes were found guilty and handed over to Zhao Gao, who ordered him to be interrogated and brought to justice. Minister Meng Yi and others were killed, ten princes were beheaded in the streets of Xianyang, and twelve princesses were also cut into pieces and executed in Du County. Their property was confiscated and returned to the emperor, and countless others were jointly punished. Young Master Gao wanted to escape for his life, but he was afraid of being executed by the whole family, so he wrote a letter saying: When the late emperor was alive, I would give him food when he entered the palace and give him a ride when he left the palace. The clothes in the emperor's palace were given to me by the late emperor; the horses in the stables in the palace were also given to me by the late emperor. I should have died with the late Emperor but failed to do so. This is my unfilial piety as a son of man and my disloyalty as a minister. There is no reason for a disloyal person to live in this world. Please allow me to die with the late emperor, hoping to bury me at the foot of Mount Li.
target: He advised implementing harsh laws, killing all opponents, and replacing them with loyalists. The Second Emperor agreed, revising the law. Many princes and ministers were executed, including ten princes beheaded in Xianyang and twelve princesses dismembered. Prince Gao requested to die with the First Emperor, which the Second Emperor approved.

id: 史记/七十列传/李斯列传::group-008
article_path: 史记/七十列传/李斯列传
source: The clothes in the emperor's palace were given to me by the late emperor; the horses in the stables in the palace were also given to me by the late emperor. I should have died with the late Emperor but failed to do so. This is my unfilial piety as a son of man and my disloyalty as a minister. There is no reason for a disloyal person to live in this world. Please allow me to die with the late emperor, hoping to bury me at the foot of Mount Li. I just ask the emperor to pity me and agree to it. After the book was presented, Hu Hai was very happy. He called Zhao Gao and showed him the book, saying: "This can be said to be embarrassing and helpless, right?" Zhao Gao said: How can you plot a rebellion when the ministers are worried all day long that they will die before it is too late! Hu Hai agreed to Gongzi Gao's request and gave him 100,000 yuan for burial. At that time, the laws and punishments became more and more cruel day by day. Everyone among the ministers was in danger, and there were many people who wanted to rebel. The second generation also built the Epang Palace, straight roads and galloping roads, taxes became heavier and heavier, and military service was endless. So Chen Sheng, Wu Guang and others, who were recruited from Chu to guard the border, rebelled and raised troops to the east of Xiaoshan. Heroes and heroes swarmed up, proclaimed themselves princes and rebelled against the Qin Dynasty. Their troops attacked until Hongmen before retreating. Li Si wanted to find opportunities to remonstrate many times, but the second emperor did not allow him. Instead, the Second Emperor blamed Li Si and said: I have an opinion that I heard from Han Feizi. He said that when Yao ruled the world, the palace was only three feet high, the oak rafters were used without cutting them, and the thatched roofs were made without trimming. Even the accommodation conditions in the hotels were not more difficult than this. Wearing deerskin coats in winter and linen clothes in summer, making coarse rice for rice and wild vegetables for soup, eating from earthen pots and drinking water from earthen bowls, even a janitor's life cannot be more miserable than this. Xia Yu opened the dragon gate, opened the Great Xia Waterway, dredged many rivers, built many dikes in twists and turns, and channeled the stagnant water into the sea. There was no white meat on the thighs, no hair on the calves, thick calluses on the palms and soles, and a dark face. In the end, he died of exhaustion and was buried on Kuaiji Mountain. Even a slave's labor would not be worse than this. However, does the purpose of those who regard ruling the world as a noble thing just want to worry about it, live in a dormitory like a hotel, eat the food of a janitor, and do the work of a slave? These things are done by people with low talents, not by wise people. When those wise people rule the world, they just use everything in the world to satisfy their own desires. This is why they regard ruling the world as nothing noble.
target: Laws grew crueler, taxes heavier, and corvée endless, leading to rebellions like that of Chen Sheng and Wu Guang. Li Si tried to remonstrate but was blamed by the Second Emperor, who argued that a ruler should use the world to satisfy his own desires, not labor like Yao or Yu.

id: 史记/七十列传/李斯列传::group-009
article_path: 史记/七十列传/李斯列传
source: Li Si was very frightened, and he valued his title and salary very seriously. He didn't know what to do, so he listened to Ashun II's wishes and asked for forgiveness, so he wrote a letter to reply to Ashun II: A wise monarch must be one who is able to fully grasp the way to be a monarch and exercise the skills to govern his subordinates. If the subordinates are strictly supervised and supervised, the ministers will not dare not do their best to serve the monarch.
target: Li Si, fearing for his position, wrote a letter flattering the Second Emperor, advocating strict supervision and severe punishments to ensure the ruler's absolute power and pleasure.

id: 史记/七十列传/李斯列传::group-010
article_path: 史记/七十列传/李斯列传
source: Isn't it also appropriate to say that Yao and Yu regarded the world as their "shackles"? This is a fault that cannot be blamed. So Mr. Han Fei said that a loving mother will raise a prodigal son, but a strict master will not have strong slaves in his family. Why? This is the inevitable result of being able to impose severe punishments. Therefore, Shang Yang's new law stipulates that anyone who spreads ashes on the road will be sentenced. Sprinkling ashes on the road is a minor offense, but adding punishment to it is a severe penalty. Only a wise monarch can severely punish misdemeanors. If you are severely punished for a misdemeanor, how much more serious crimes?
target: He cited Shen Buhai, Han Fei, and Shang Yang, arguing that harsh penalties for minor crimes prevent greater offenses.

id: 史记/七十列传/李斯列传::group-011
article_path: 史记/七十列传/李斯列传
source: In this way, it can be said that one has mastered the emperor's ruling skills, and can also be said to have understood the method of controlling his ministers. Even if Shen Buhai and Han Fei are resurrected, they cannot go beyond that. After the answer was submitted, the second generation was very happy after reading it. So we implemented supervision and responsibilities more strictly, and the more taxes we collected from the people, the wiser the officials became. The Second Emperor said: Only in this way can one be said to be good at supervising and punishing people. Half of the pedestrians on the road are prisoners. The corpses of newly killed people are piled up every day in the market, and the more people kill, the more loyal they become. The Second Emperor said: Only in this way can we be called to practice supervision. At first, when Zhao Gao was serving as Lang Zhongling, he killed many people and framed many people for personal revenge. He was afraid that the ministers would expose him to the Second Emperor when he came to court, so he persuaded the Second Emperor: The reason why the emperor is noble is that the ministers can only hear his voice but not see his face, so they call themselves "I". Moreover, Your Majesty is still very young and may not know everything. Now that you are sitting in the court, if the punishments and rewards are inappropriate, your shortcomings will be exposed to the ministers, and you will not be able to show your wisdom to the world. Your Majesty might as well stay in the palace, stay with me and the servants who are familiar with the law, and wait for the minister to submit the official report. Once the official document is submitted, we can study and make a decision. In this way, ministers will not dare to report difficult matters, and people in the world will call you the Lord of Sage. The Second Emperor followed Zhao Gao's advice and no longer sat in the court to receive ministers, but lived deep in the palace. Zhao Gao always serves the emperor and all official affairs are decided by Zhao Gao. Zhao Gao heard that Li Si was dissatisfied with this, so he went to Li Si and said: There are many thieves in the area east of Hangu Pass, but now the emperor is stepping up his efforts to send laborers to build Afang Palace and collect dogs, horses and other useless playthings. I want to remonstrate, but my position is humble. But it's really your prime minister's business, why don't you give me advice? Li Si said, "It's true. I've wanted to talk for a long time." But now the emperor does not come to court to listen to the government, but always lives in the palace. Although I have something to say, it is inconvenient for others to convey it. I want to see the emperor but I have no chance. Zhao Gao said to him: If you can really advise me, please allow me to inquire for you. As soon as the emperor is free, I will inform you immediately. So Zhao Gao took advantage of the fact that the second son was living and entertaining, and the beautiful woman was in front of him, and sent someone to tell the prime minister: The emperor is free and can come to the palace to report something. Prime Minister Li Si went to the palace gate to ask for an audience, which happened three times in a row.
target: The Second Emperor was pleased and intensified supervision and taxation, leading to half the population being prisoners and corpses piled in the markets. Zhao Gao, fearing exposure, persuaded the Second Emperor to stay in the palace and not meet ministers, allowing Zhao Gao to control all affairs. Zhao Gao then tricked Li Si into seeking an audience during the emperor's leisure, angering the Second Emperor. Zhao Gao accused Li Si of involvement in the Shaqiu conspiracy and of colluding with rebels through his son Li You. The Second Emperor ordered an investigation.

id: 史记/七十列传/李斯列传::group-012
article_path: 史记/七十列传/李斯列传
source: In addition, I lost my father at a young age and have little knowledge and do not know how to manage people. And you are old, so I am worried that you will be isolated from the people of the world. If I don't entrust the state affairs to Zhao Gao, who else should I use? Besides, Mr. Zhao is a shrewd and honest man, he does his best, understands the people's conditions below, and adapts to my wishes above, please don't doubt it. Li Si said: Not so. Zhao Gao used to be a humble man who didn't understand the truth, was greedy and constantly seeking profit. His status and power were second only to His Majesty, but his desire for status and power was endless, so I say it was very dangerous. The second son had believed Zhao Gao in the morning and was worried that Li Si would kill him, so he secretly told Zhao Gao these words. Zhao Gao said: The prime minister is only worried about me, Zhao Gao. After my death, the prime minister can do what Tian Chang did. So the Second Emperor said: Let Li Si be handed over to you, the doctor, to investigate and deal with it! Zhao Gao investigates Li Si. After Li Si was arrested, he was put on a torture device and imprisoned in prison. He looked up to the sky and sighed: Oh! How sad! How can the ignorant and foolish king advise him! In the past Xia Jie killed Guan Longfeng, Shang Zhou killed Prince Bigan, and Wu Wang Fucha killed Wu Zixu. Are these three ministers disloyal? However, death was inevitable. Although they died loyally, it was a pity that they were not loyal to the people they were. Now my wisdom cannot keep up with these three people, and the cruelty and cruelty of the second generation exceeds that of Jie, Zhou, and Fu Cha. It is right for me to die because of my loyalty. Besides, isn’t it nonsense to govern the country in the second generation? Not long ago, he killed his brother and established himself as the emperor. He also killed loyal people, reused lowly people, built the Epang Palace, and levied tyrannical taxes on the people of the world. It's not that I don't give advice, it's that he doesn't listen to me. All ancient sages and emperors had a certain degree of restraint in their diet, a certain number of vehicles, horses, and utensils, and a certain limit in their palaces. They issued orders and did things, and prohibited anything that increased expenses and was not conducive to the people, so that long-term peace and stability could be achieved. Now the second generation is using unnatural and cruel methods on his brothers, without considering what disasters will happen. He persecutes and kills loyal ministers without considering what disasters will happen. He vigorously builds palaces, increases taxes on the people of the world, and does not hesitate to spend money. After these three measures were implemented, the people of the world did not obey. Now the rebels have accounted for half of the people in the world, but the second generation has not yet awakened in his heart, and actually appointed Zhao Gao as his assistant. I will definitely see the thieves invade Xianyang and turn the court into a place where elk roam. So the Second Emperor sent Zhao Gao to examine the prime minister's case, punish him, inquire about Li Si and his son Li You's rebellion, and arrest all his guests and family members. Zhao Gao punished Li Si and tortured him more than a thousand times. Li Si could not bear the painful torture and unjustly confessed.
target: Li Si wrote to expose Zhao Gao's ambition, comparing him to usurpers like Tian Chang. The Second Emperor defended Zhao Gao, but Li Si warned of his greed. The Second Emperor told Zhao Gao, who accused Li Si of plotting rebellion. Li Si was arrested and tortured into confessing. In prison, he lamented that the Second Emperor was worse than Jie and Zhou, killing brothers and loyal ministers, building the Epang Palace, and overtaxing the people. He wrote a letter listing his seven crimes, which were actually achievements, but Zhao Gao suppressed it. When the Second Emperor sent investigators, Li Si, fearing torture, did not change his confession. He was sentenced to five punishments and executed in the Xianyang market, along with his entire clan.

id: 史记/七十列传/李斯列传::group-013
article_path: 史记/七十列传/李斯列传
source: Zhao Gao presented the verdict to the emperor, and the second emperor said happily: Without Zhao Jun, I was almost betrayed by the prime minister. By the time the envoy from the Second Sect arrived in Sanchuan to investigate Li You, Xiang Liang had already killed him. When the envoy returned, just as Li Si had been handed over to the custody of the jailers, Zhao Gao fabricated a whole set of charges against Li You for treason. In July of the second year of the Second Emperor's reign, Li Si was sentenced to five punishments and sentenced to be cut in half in the Xianyang market. When Li Si was released from prison, he was escorted together with his second son. He turned around and said to his second son: I want to go out to Cai Dongmen with you and lead the yellow dog to hunt and chase cunning rabbits, but how can we do it? So the father and son cried bitterly to each other, and all the people of the three tribes were executed. After Li Si's death, the second emperor appointed Zhao Gao as the prime minister. Zhao Gao made all the decisions, no matter how big or small. Zhao Gao knew that he had too much power, so he offered a deer and called it a horse. The Second Emperor asked his attendants: Is this a deer? Everyone said: It's a horse. The second generation panicked, thinking that he was confused, so he summoned the fortune teller and asked him to calculate a divination. Taibu said: Your Majesty goes to the countryside to offer sacrifices in the spring and autumn, and worships the ghosts and gods of the ancestral temple. He is not pious when fasting, and that is why he is like this. You can fast again sincerely according to the appearance of a sage monarch. So the second generation went to Shanglin Garden to fast. He spent the whole day playing hunting in Shanglin Garden. Once a pedestrian walked into Shanglin Garden, and he shot him to death with his own hands. Zhao Gao asked his son-in-law Yan Le of Xianyang to come forward to impeach, saying that someone unknown killed the person and moved the body into Shanglin Garden. Zhao Gao advised the Second Emperor to say: The emperor kills innocent people for no reason. This is not allowed by God, and ghosts and gods will not accept your sacrifice. God will bring disasters, and you should stay away from the palace to pray for relief. The second generation left the palace and went to live in Wangyi Palace. The Second Emperor stayed in Wangyi Palace for three days. Zhao Gao pretended to be the Second Emperor's order and asked the guards to wear white clothes and face the palace with weapons in hand. He entered the palace and told the Second Emperor: Bandits from all walks of life in Shandong are coming in large numbers! The Second Emperor went to the balcony to watch and saw the guards heading into the palace with weapons. He was very frightened. Zhao Gao immediately forced the Second Emperor to commit suicide. Then he took the jade seal and carried it with him. None of the civil and military officials around him followed him. When he ascended the hall, it seemed to collapse several times. Zhao Gao knew that God would not grant him the position of emperor, and the officials would not agree, so he called the younger brother of Qin Shihuang's younger brother and handed the jade seal to him. After Ziying came to the throne, he was worried that Zhao Gao would cause trouble again, so he pretended to be ill and did not go to court to handle government affairs. He discussed with the eunuch Han Tan and his son how to kill Zhao Gao. Zhao Gao came to see him and asked about his condition. Ziying summoned him to the palace and ordered Han Tan to assassinate him and annihilate his three clans. Three months after Ziying came to the throne, Liu Bang's army invaded from Wuguan and arrived in Xianyang. All civil and military officials revolted against Qin and did not resist Pei Gong. Ziying, his wife and children all tied ribbons around their necks and went to Zhidao Pavilion to surrender. Liu Bang handed them over to the custody of his subordinate officials. Xiang Yu killed them after arriving in Xianyang, and Qin lost the world. Tai Shigong said: As a commoner in an alley, Li Si traveled to the princes, entered the customs to serve the Qin State, seized the opportunity, assisted Qin Shihuang, and finally completed the great cause of unification. Li Si occupies the position of the Three Officials and can be said to be very important. Li Si knew the gist of the Confucian "Six Classics", but he did not devote himself to political clarity to make up for the emperor's faults. Instead, relying on his noble status, he flattered and followed at will, implemented harsh methods of torture, listened to Zhao Gao's heresy, abolished his legitimate son Fusu and established his concubine Hu Hai. When rebellions broke out in various places, Li Si wanted to directly advise him. Isn't this too stupid? People think that Li Si was so loyal that he died of five punishments. However, when I carefully examined the truth of the matter, I found it was different from the popular view. Otherwise, Li Si's achievements would really be comparable to Duke Zhou and Duke Zhao.
target: After Li Si's death, Zhao Gao became Prime Minister. He tested his power by presenting a deer and calling it a horse, which all officials affirmed. The Second Emperor, confused, went to fast in Shanglin Garden, where he killed a pedestrian. Zhao Gao advised him to leave the palace to pray, then forced him to commit suicide. Zhao Gao tried to take the throne but failed, so he installed Ziying, a younger brother of the First Emperor. Ziying, fearing Zhao Gao, feigned illness and had him assassinated, annihilating his clan. Three months later, Liu Bang's army entered Xianyang, and Ziying surrendered. Xiang Yu later killed them, and Qin fell. The Grand Historian commented that Li Si, though a commoner, achieved great success but failed to correct the emperor's faults, instead flattering him and implementing harsh laws. He listened to Zhao Gao, deposed the rightful heir, and when rebellions arose, his belated advice was foolish. His loyalty was questionable, and his achievements, while great, were not comparable to those of the Duke of Zhou.

id: 史记/七十列传/樊郦滕灌列传::group-000
article_path: 史记/七十列传/樊郦滕灌列传
source: Wuyang Hou Fan Kuai was a native of Peixian County. He made a living by killing dogs and selling their meat. He once hid in the countryside with Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty. At first, Fan Kuai followed Gaozu and raised troops in Fengyi and captured Peixian County. When Emperor Gaozu was the Duke of Pei, he used Fan Kuai as his servant. He followed Pei Gong to attack Huling and Fangyu, then returned to guard Fengyi. He attacked the army of the Sishui County Supervisor in Fengyi and defeated them. Then he went east to pacify Peixian County, and defeated the army of Sishui County Governor to the west of Xue County.
target: Fan Kuai, a native of Peixian County, initially made a living by killing dogs and selling meat. He joined Liu Bang (later Emperor Gaozu of Han) in raising troops, capturing Peixian, and serving as a servant.

source: Following Pei Gong, he defeated Yang Xiong's army in Quyu. When attacking Wanling, Fan Kuai took the lead in ascending the city, beheaded eight people and captured 44 people. Peigong gave him the title of Xian Chengjun. He followed Pei Gong to attack Changshe and Sheyuan, blockaded the Yellow River ferry, went east to attack the Qin army in Shixiang, and went south to attack the Qin army in Taoyi. Defeat Lu , the governor of Nanyang County, in Yangcheng. When attacking Wancheng to the east, Fan Kuai took the lead in ascending the city. Arriving at Li County in the west, Fan Kuai repelled the enemy, beheaded 24 of them and captured 40, and was rewarded by Pei Gong with an increase in rank and salary. Attacked Wuguan, and when they reached Bashang, they killed one captain, beheaded ten people, captured 146 people, and surrendered 2,900 enemy soldiers. Xiang Yu garrisoned under the stage and prepared to attack Peigong. Pei Gong sent more than a hundred cavalry with him to meet Xiang Yu through Xiang Bo, and stated that he had not blocked the pass. Xiang Yu held a banquet in honor of the army lieutenants. While they were drinking heavily, Yafu wanted to murder Pei Gong. He sent Xiang Zhuang to draw his sword and perform a dance in front of the banquet, hoping to take the opportunity to assassinate Pei Gong. However, Xiang Bo repeatedly protected Pei Gong. At that time, only Pei Gong and Zhang Liang could enter the camp and sit down. Fan Kuai stayed outside the camp. Hearing that Pei Gong's situation was urgent, he entered the camp with an iron shield. The guards of the military camp stopped Fan Kuai, but Fan Kuai ran straight in and stood under the tent. Xiang Yu looked at him with his eyes and asked him who he was. Zhang Liang said: "It's Fan Kuai who is accompanying Duke Pei." Xiang Yu said: Strong man! He gave him a cup of wine and a pig's leg. After Fan Kuai drank the wine, he drew his sword, cut the meat, and ate it all. Xiang Yu asked: Can I drink again? Fan Kuai said: If I die, I will not refuse, let alone just drink a glass of wine! Besides, Pei Gong first entered the Pass to pacify Xianyang and camped in Bashang to wait for the king. As soon as the king arrived today, he listened to the villain's slander and had a problem with Pei Gong. I am worried that the world will be divided and the people will doubt the king. Xiang Yu remained silent. Pei Gong went to the toilet and called Fan Kuai out. After coming out, Pei Gong left behind his carriage and rode only one horse. He followed Fan Kuai and four other men on foot and took a small path down the mountain to escape back to Bashang's military camp, leaving Zhang Liang to say goodbye to Xiang Yu. Xiang Yu also had his way, so he had no intention of killing Pei Gong. On this day, if Fan Kuai hadn't broken into the camp and condemned Xiang Yu, Pei Gong's situation would have been in danger. The next day, Xiang Yu entered the city and bloodbathed Xianyang, and made Peigong the king of Han. The king of Han also made Fan Kuai a prince, called Linwuhou.
target: Throughout numerous battles, Fan Kuai consistently demonstrated valor, often leading assaults on cities and beheading enemy soldiers. His military exploits included defeating Qin forces at Puyang, Chengyang, and Kaifeng, among others, earning him successive titles and promotions from Pei Gong (Liu Bang). A pivotal moment occurred at the Hongmen Banquet, where Xiang Yu plotted to kill Pei Gong. Fan Kuai, stationed outside, burst into the camp with an iron shield, confronted Xiang Yu, and condemned his actions, ultimately saving Pei Gong's life. Following Xiang Yu's defeat, Fan Kuai continued to serve Gaozu, suppressing rebellions by Zang Tu, Han Xin, Chen Xi, and Lu Wan, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wuyang with 5,400 households.

source: So Emperor Gaozu gave Fan Kuai an additional 1,300 households, confirming that he would be the Marquis of Wuyang with a total of 5,400 households. When Fan Kuai followed Gaozu in the battle, he beheaded 176 enemies and captured 188 enemy soldiers. He led the troops to fight alone, defeated seven enemy armies, captured five cities, pacified six counties and fifty-two counties, and captured one enemy prime minister, 12 generals, and 11 officials ranging from 2,000 to 300 shi. Because Fan Kuai married Empress Lu's sister Lu Xu and gave birth to a son, Mr. and Mrs. Fan, Gaozu was closer to Fan Kuai than other generals. During the Yingbu rebellion, Gaozu was very ill and hated seeing people. He lay in the palace confinement and ordered the gatekeepers not to let the officials in to see him.
target: He married Empress Lü's sister, Lü Xu, and remained close to Gaozu. During Gaozu's illness, Fan Kuai boldly entered the palace to urge him to attend to state affairs.

id: 史记/七十列传/樊郦滕灌列传::group-003
