source: And now that the world has settled down, how exhausted you are! Besides, you are seriously ill, the ministers are panicking, and you are unwilling to meet us to discuss state affairs. Do you just want to decide with a eunuch? Besides, haven't you seen anything about Zhao Gao? After hearing this, Emperor Gaozu smiled and got up from the bed. Later, Lu Wan rebelled, and Gaozu ordered Fan Kuai to attack Yan as prime minister. At this time, Emperor Gaozu was very ill again. Some people slandered Fan Kuai and the Lu family for forming a party. If the emperor died one day, Fan Kuai would lead his troops to kill Madam Qi and King Zhao Ruyi. When Emperor Gaozu heard about it, he became furious and immediately ordered Chen Ping to drive Jianghou Zhou Bo in a chariot to replace Fan Kuai, and immediately beheaded Fan Kuai in the army. Because Chen Ping was afraid of Empress Lu, he did not carry out Gaozu's order, but sent Fan Kuai to Chang'an. When they arrived in Chang'an, Gaozu had passed away, so Empress Lu released Fan Kuai and restored his title and fiefdom. In the sixth year of Emperor Hui of the Han Dynasty, Fan Kuai passed away, and his posthumous title was Marquis Wu.
target: Later, slandered for conspiring with the Lü clan, Gaozu ordered his execution, but Chen Ping delayed, and after Gaozu's death, Empress Lü released him. Fan Kuai died in the sixth year of Emperor Hui's reign, posthumously titled Marquis Wu. His descendants held the title until it was revoked in Emperor Jing's time due to legal transgressions.

source: Li Shang, the Marquis of Quzhou, was from Gaoyang. When Chen Sheng rebelled against Qin, he gathered a group of young people and recruited thousands of people. Peigong attacked the city and captured the territory and came to Chenliu. More than six months later, Li Shang led more than 4,000 soldiers to Qitou and returned to Peigong. He followed Pei Gong to attack Changshe and took the lead in ascending the city. Pei Gong conferred a title on him and named him Xinchengjun. Following Pei Gong, he attacked the Feng family, blocked the Yellow River ferry, and defeated the Qin army east of Luoyang. Following Pei Gong, he captured Wan and Rang, and also pacified seventeen counties. He led an army to attack Xunwu alone and pacified Hanzhong. After Xiang Yu destroyed Qin, he established Peigong as King of Han. The King of Han bestowed upon Li Shangxin the title of Lord and made him the Captain of Longxi with the rank of general. Li Shang led his army alone to pacify Beidi and Shangjun. They defeated the army led by King Yong Zhanghan at Yanshi, defeated the army led by Zhou Lei at Yiyi, and defeated the army led by Su Zao at Niyang. So the king of Han gave Li Shang 6,000 households in Wucheng County as his food town. As the captain of Longxi, he followed the Duke of Pei to attack Xiang Yu's army for five months. He sent troops to Juye and fought with Zhong Limei. For his meritorious service in the fierce battle, the Duke of Pei granted him the seal of Liang Guoxiang and granted him 4,000 additional households. During the battle of Longtuo, Li Shang charged into the battle, took the lead in ascending the city, and defeated Zang Tu's army in Yixia. Because of his meritorious service in killing the enemy, he was promoted to the right prime minister, and was given the title of a lord. Like other princes, he cut the talisman as a letter, and it will never be extinguished from generation to generation. He took the five thousand households in Zhuoyi as his food town and was titled Zhuohou. As prime minister on the right, he led troops to pacify Shanggu alone, and then attacked Dai. Gaozu granted him the seal of the prime minister of Zhao. As the Prime Minister of the Right and the Prime Minister of the State of Zhao, he led his troops, together with Jianghou Zhou Bo and others, to pacify Dai Heyanmen, and captured alive the Prime Minister of Dai Cheng Zong, the Prime Minister Guo Tong, and a total of 19 officials ranging from generals to 600 shi. After the victory, he served as the bodyguard of the Supreme Emperor as a general for one year and seven months. Then he used his position as Prime Minister You to attack Chen Xi and destroy the Dongyuan city wall. As Prime Minister of the Right, he followed Emperor Gao to attack the rebellious Yingbu. Li Shang led his troops to storm the enemy's forward positions and captured two positions, allowing the Han army to defeat Yingbu's army. Emperor Gao changed his fiefdom to Quzhou, increasing it to 5,100 households, and took back the food fiefdoms he had previously granted. In total, Li Shang defeated three enemy armies, surrendered and pacified six counties and seventy-three counties, and captured the prime minister, the prime minister, one general each, two junior generals, and nineteen officials ranging from 2,000 shi to 600 shi. Li Shang was serving Xiaohui. When he was a queen, he was unable to take care of political affairs due to poor health. His son Li Ji was very close to Lu Lu. In this year, Li Shang passed away, and his posthumous title was Jinghou. His son Li Ji succeeded to the throne, and everyone in the world said that he had betrayed his friends.
target: Li Shang, from Gaoyang, initially gathered followers during Chen Sheng's rebellion and later joined Pei Gong with over 4,000 soldiers. He distinguished himself in battles, capturing cities like Changshe and Wan, and was appointed Lord of Xincheng and later Captain of Longxi. Li Shang fought against Xiang Yu, defeated forces of Yong King Zhanghan, and pacified regions including Beidi and Shangjun. He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhuoxian with 5,000 households, later serving as Right Prime Minister and leading campaigns against Chen Xi and Yingbu. His fief was changed to Quzhou with 5,100 households. Li Shang served under Emperor Xiaohui but was unable to govern due to illness. His son Li Ji succeeded but was executed for treason during the Rebellion of the Seven States. Another son, Li Jian, continued the lineage until it was eventually revoked for legal violations.

source: After the death of Miao Jinghou Li Jian, his son Kanghou Li Suicheng succeeded to the throne. After Li Suicheng died, his son Huaihou Li Shizong succeeded to the throne. After the death of Li Shizong, his son Li Zhonggen inherited the throne and served as Taichang. Later, the feudal state was revoked because of breaking the law. Xia Houying, Marquis of Ruyin, was from Peixian County. He began to take charge of horse breeding and driving in the stable of Peixian County. Whenever he drove back after seeing off envoys or guests, he would go to Sishang Pavilion in Peixian County to chat with Gaozu, and they would chat for most of the day. Later, Xia Houying served as a probationary county official and became closer to Gao Zu. Once, Gaozu accidentally injured Xia Houying because of a joke, and was reported to the government. At that time, Gaozu was the chief of the pavilion, and he had to be severely punished if he hurt someone. Therefore, Gaozu complained that he had not harmed Xia Houying, and Xia Houying also proved that he had not been harmed. Later, the case was reversed. Xia Houying was imprisoned for more than a year because of Gao Zu's involvement, and received hundreds of slaps. However, Gao Zu was eventually exempted from punishment. When Gaozu led his disciples to attack Pei County, Xia Houying contacted Gaozu as a subordinate official of the county magistrate. On the day Gaozu surrendered to Peixian County, Gaozu made him Duke of Pei, gave Xia Houying the title of Seventh Doctor, and appointed him as his imperial servant. When following Gaozu to attack Hu Ling, Xia Houying and Xiao He surrendered to Sishui County Supervisor Ping. Ping handed over Hu Ling and surrendered. Gaozu gave Xia Houying the title of fifth doctor. He followed Gaozu to attack the Qin army east of Dang County, attacked Jiyang, captured Hufu, and defeated Li You's army in the Yongqiu area. During the battle, he drove a chariot to attack quickly and fought bravely. Gaozu gave him the title of silk guard. Xia Houying also used his position as a servant to command chariots and follow Gaozu to attack Zhang Han in Dong'a and Puyang. During the battle, he drove chariots to attack Zhang Han quickly. He fought bravely and defeated the Qin army. Gaozu gave him the title of Zhigui. He also commanded military chariots to follow Emperor Gaozu in attacking Zhao Ben's army in Kaifeng, and in Quyu he attacked Yang Xiong's army. During the battle, Xia Houying captured 68 people, surrendered 850 soldiers, and seized a box of gold seals. Then he commanded military chariots to follow Gaozu to attack the Qin army east of Luoyang. He drove into the battle and fought hard, and Gao Zu granted him the title of Duke Teng. Then he commanded the chariots to follow Gaozu to attack Nanyang. In the battles at Lantian and Zhiyang, he drove the chariots to fight bravely and fought bravely until he reached Bashang. After Xiang Yu entered the Pass, he destroyed the Qin Dynasty and made Peigong King of Han. The King of Han bestowed upon Xiahou Ying the title of Marquis of Zhaoping. He also took the position of Taiwen and followed the King of Han into the Shu and Han regions. Later, the King of Han returned to pacify the Three Qin Dynasties, and Xia Houying followed the King of Han to attack Xiang Yu's army.
target: Xiahou Ying, from Peixian, began as a stable hand and befriended Gaozu, even taking a false imprisonment for him. He joined Gaozu's uprising, serving as a chariot commander and fighting in key battles such as Dong'a and Kaifeng. After Xiang Yu's defeat, Xiahou Ying rescued Gaozu's children during a retreat and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Ruyin with 6,900 households. He served as a servant under Gaozu, Xiaohui, and Empress Lü, and played a role in welcoming Emperor Wen to the throne.

id: 史记/七十列传/樊郦滕灌列传::group-006
article_path: 史记/七十列传/樊郦滕灌列传
source: Xia Houying followed Emperor Gao to raise troops in Peixian County and served as a servant for a long time until Emperor Gao's death. Later, he served Emperor Xiaohui as a royal servant. Emperor Xiaohui and Empress Lu were very grateful to Xia Houying for rescuing Emperor Xiaohui and Princess Lu Yuan on the road to Xiayi, so they gave him a first-class mansion close to the north of the palace, named "near me", which meant that he could be closest to me, and expressed their special respect for Xia Houying. After the death of Emperor Xiaohui, he served the Empress Gao as a servant. When Empress Gao passed away and King Dai came to the capital, Xia Houying went to the palace as a servant to clean up the palace together with Dongmou Hou Liu Xingju, deposed the young emperor, and used the emperor's method to drive to the palace of King Dai to welcome King Dai. Together with the ministers, he established King Dai as Emperor Xiaowen. He died eight years later and was given the posthumous title Wenhou. His son Yihou Xiahou Zao succeeded to the throne and died seven years later.
target: He died posthumously titled Wenhou. His descendants held the title until it was revoked for adultery.

source: When Fan Kuai returned to Xingyang, the king of Han added 2,000 households in Pingyin as his settlement, and asked him to guard Guangwu as a general. A year later, Xiang Yu led his troops eastward, and Fan Kuai followed Gaozu to attack Xiang Ji, occupy Yangxia, and captured 4,000 soldiers of General Zhou of Chu. They surrounded Xiang Ji in Chen County and defeated him. Bloodbath in Hu Ling. After Xiang Yu's death, the King of Han became the emperor. Because of Fan Kuai's meritorious service in holding on to the city and attacking in battles, he granted 800 households a new enfeoffment. Fan Kuai followed Gaozu to attack the rebellious King of Yan Zang Tu, captured Zang Tu, and pacified the Yan territory. King Han Xin of Chu launched a rebellion. Fan Kuai followed Gaozu to Chen County, arrested Han Xin, and pacified Chu. Emperor Gaozu changed Fan Kuai's title to that of a noble prince and established a trustworthy relationship with the princes, so that they could be passed down from generation to generation. Emperor Gaozu removed Fan Kuai's former food town and gave him food in Wuyang, naming him Marquis of Wuyang. Later, Fan Kuai followed Gaozu to Daidi as a general to attack the rebellious King Xin of Han. From the Huo people to Yunzhong, Fan Kuai, Jianghou Zhoubo and others jointly pacified it, so an additional 1,500 households were added. Later, Fan Kuai led his troops to attack the armies of the rebels Chen Xi and Manqiuchen, and fought in Xiangguo. When he captured Bairen County, he took the lead in ascending the city. He also surrendered and pacified twenty-seven counties in Qinghe and Changshan counties, and destroyed Dongyuan County. He was promoted to Prime Minister Zuo for his merits. In Wujing and Guangchang, he defeated the armies of Qi Wuyan and Yin Pan and captured them alive. In the south of Daidi, the army led by the Hu general Wang Huang under Chen Xi was defeated. Then, he marched to join forces and attacked Han Wangxin's army. Fan Kuai's men killed Han Wangxin. In Henggu, Chen Xi's Hu cavalry troops were defeated, general Zhao Ji was killed, and ten people including the Prime Minister Han Liang, the governor Sun Fen, the general Wang Huang, Tai Pu Xie and the general were captured. Together with the generals, he pacified seventy-three villages and towns in Dai. After that, King Lu Wan of Yan rebelled. Fan Kuai led the army to attack Lu Wan as prime minister, defeated the army led by Prime Minister Lu Wan in the south of Jixian County, and pacified a total of 18 counties and 51 townships in Yan. So Emperor Gaozu gave Fan Kuai an additional 1,300 households, confirming that he would be the Marquis of Wuyang with a total of 5,400 households. When Fan Kuai followed Gaozu in the battle, he beheaded 176 enemies and captured 188 enemy soldiers. He led the troops to fight alone, defeated seven enemy armies, captured five cities, pacified six counties and fifty-two counties, and captured one enemy prime minister, 12 generals, and 11 officials ranging from 2,000 to 300 shi. Because Fan Kuai married Empress Lu's sister Lu Xu and gave birth to a son, Mr. and Mrs. Fan, Gaozu was closer to Fan Kuai than other generals. During the Yingbu rebellion, Gaozu was very ill and hated seeing people. He lay in the palace confinement and ordered the gatekeepers not to let the officials in to see him. Among the officials, such as Jianghou Zhou Bo, Guan Ying and others did not dare to enter the palace.
target: Guan Ying, a silk merchant from Suiyang, joined Pei Gong and fought in numerous campaigns, including against Qin forces and Xiang Yu. He distinguished himself as a cavalry commander, defeating Chu forces and capturing key figures like Zhou Lan. After Xiang Yu's death, Guan Ying pursued and killed him, leading to his enfeoffment as Marquis of Yingyin with 5,000 households. He later suppressed rebellions by Zang Tu, Han Xin, Chen Xi, and Yingbu. During the Lü clan crisis, he feigned support but secretly allied with Zhou Bo to establish Emperor Wen, becoming Taiwei and later Prime Minister. He died in office, posthumously titled Yihou. His descendants held the title until it was revoked for bribery. Sima Qian notes that these figures, originally humble commoners, rose to prominence and established lasting legacies through their service to the Han dynasty.

source: Ji An, whose courtesy name is Changru, was born in Puyang County. His ancestors were favored by the king of the ancient Wei Kingdom. By the time he was the seventh generation, he had been serving as ministers and officials in the court for generations. Ji An relied on his father's recommendation. During the reign of Emperor Xiao Jing, Ji An became the prince Xima. He was respected by others because he was a serious man. When Emperor Jing died, the prince succeeded to the throne and appointed him as the official of the audience. There was an attack between the Minyue and Ouyue people in East Vietnam, and the emperor sent Ji An to inspect. Before he reached Dongyue, he turned back when he reached Wuxian and reported: The Dongyue people are attacking each other because the local folk customs are so aggressive that it is not worth bothering the emperor's envoys to inquire. A fire broke out in Hanoi County, burning more than a thousand households. The emperor sent Ji An to inspect. He came back and reported: Ordinary people there accidentally catch fire. Because the houses are densely packed, the fire spreads, so there is no need to worry. When I passed through Henan County, I saw that the local poor were suffering from floods and droughts. There were more than ten thousand families affected by the disaster, and some even went as far as father and son eating each other. So I took advantage of the talisman I held and ordered the distribution of grain stored in the official warehouse of Henan County to provide relief to the local victims.
target: Ji An, courtesy name Changru, was born in Puyang County, with ancestors serving as ministers for seven generations. During Emperor Xiao Jing's reign, he became a prince Xima through his father's recommendation and was respected for his seriousness. After Emperor Jing's death, the new emperor appointed him as an official of the audience. Sent to inspect conflicts between the Minyue and Ouyue peoples, he turned back at Wuxian, deeming the local aggression unworthy of imperial attention. Similarly, after a fire in Hanoi County burned over a thousand households, he reported it as an accident due to dense housing. While passing through Henan County, he saw severe flood and drought suffering, with over ten thousand families affected and reports of cannibalism.

There were more than ten thousand families affected by the disaster, and some even went as far as father and son eating each other. So I took advantage of the talisman I held and ordered the distribution of grain stored in the official warehouse of Henan County to provide relief to the local victims. Now I request that the talisman be returned and bear the responsibility of falsely preaching the imperial edict. The emperor believed that Ji An was a virtuous person, so he was exempted from guilt and was transferred to Xingyang County Magistrate. Ji An thought it was a shame to be a county magistrate, so he resigned and returned home claiming illness. When the emperor heard the news, he summoned Ji An to serve as a senior official in the imperial court. Because he repeatedly expressed his opinions to the emperor, he was still not allowed to stay in the court for a long time and was released as the prefect of Donghai County.
target: Using his talisman, he distributed grain from official stores for relief, then returned the talisman and accepted responsibility for falsely preaching the imperial edict. The emperor, considering him virtuous, exempted him from guilt and transferred him to Xingyang County Magistrate. Ji An, ashamed of the role, resigned claiming illness. The emperor then summoned him as a senior official in the imperial court, but due to his frequent outspoken opinions, he was released as the prefect of Donghai County.

source: Ji An admired Taoism, managed the government and handled civil affairs. He liked to be clean and tidy, and entrusted all matters to the capable county magistrates and book historians he selected. When he manages county affairs, he just supervises his subordinates to act in accordance with general principles and does not pay attention to details. He was frail and sickly and often lay indoors without going out. In more than a year, Donghai County became very peaceful and peaceful, and people praised him very much. After the emperor learned about it, he summoned Ji'an back to the capital to serve as the Lord Commander, and he was treated similarly to Jiu Qing's treatment. He strives to govern by doing nothing, and promotes the big ideas without adhering to the legal provisions. Ji An is very arrogant when dealing with others, does not pay attention to etiquette, contradicts people in person, and cannot tolerate other people's mistakes. He would be close to and friendly to those who were congenial to him; he would be impatient to meet those who were incompatible with him, and therefore the scholars would not want to rely on him. But Ji An was eager to learn and good at doing chivalry, and he paid great attention to his ambition and integrity. He usually lives at home and has good and pure conduct; when he enters the court, he likes to speak out and give advice, repeatedly offending the emperor's face, and often admires the conduct of Fu Bai and Yuan An. He had good relations with Guan Fu, Zheng Shi and Zong Zheng and Liu Qi. They were also unable to stay in their official positions for a long time because of their repeated remonstrances. Just when Ji An was appointed Lord Commander and Lieutenant-in-Chief, the Queen Mother's younger brother Wu'anhou Tianfu became prime minister. When high-ranking officials with an annual salary of two thousand dan came to visit him, they all knelt down and bowed down, but Tian Fu actually refused to return the courtesy.
target: Ji An admired Taoism, managed affairs cleanly, and delegated to capable subordinates, focusing on general principles rather than details. Despite frail health, he often stayed indoors, and within a year, Donghai County became peaceful and praised. The emperor recalled him as Lord Commander, treating him similarly to Jiu Qing. He governed by doing nothing, promoting big ideas without strict legal adherence. Arrogant and blunt, he contradicted people openly, befriending only those congenial to him and shunning others, causing scholars to avoid him. Yet he was eager to learn, chivalrous, and principled, often speaking out in court and offending the emperor, admiring figures like Fu Bai and Yuan An. He associated with Guan Fu, Zheng Shi, Zong Zheng, and Liu Qi, who also faced demotions for remonstrance. When Wu'anhou Tianfu became prime minister, high-ranking officials knelt to him, but Ji An only bowed.

id: 史记/七十列传/汲郑列传::group-003
article_path: 史记/七十列传/汲郑列传
source: He had good relations with Guan Fu, Zheng Shi and Zong Zheng and Liu Qi. They were also unable to stay in their official positions for a long time because of their repeated remonstrances. Just when Ji An was appointed Lord Commander and Lieutenant-in-Chief, the Queen Mother's younger brother Wu'anhou Tianfu became prime minister. When high-ranking officials with an annual salary of two thousand dan came to visit him, they all knelt down and bowed down, but Tian Fu actually refused to return the courtesy. But when Ji An asked to see Tian Fu, he never bowed down and often bowed to him. At this time, the emperor was recruiting literary scholars and Confucian scholars, saying what I wanted, Ji An replied: "Your Majesty has many desires in his heart and only practices benevolence and righteousness on the surface. How can he truly imitate the political achievements of Tang Yao and Yu Shun!" The emperor was silent, angry in his heart, and then stopped courting with a sudden change of expression. The ministers were all frightened and worried about Ji An. After the emperor retired from the court, he said to the ministers around him: This is too much, Ji An is too stupid and straightforward! Someone among the ministers blamed Ji An, and Ji An said: Is it true that the emperor appointed ministers such as public ministers and hundreds of officials to be submissive and flattery, and put the monarch in a dilemma that goes against the right path? What's more, I am already in the position of Jiuqing. Even though I cherish my life, what if I harm the important affairs of the court? Ji An was sick and had been ill for three months. The emperor had repeatedly granted him leave to recuperate, but his illness never recovered. The last time he was very ill, Zhuang Zhu asked for leave on his behalf. The emperor asked: How is Ji An? Zhuang Zhu said: There is nothing extraordinary about letting Ji An become an official and deacon. However, he can assist the young monarch, stick to the established cause, use inducements to prevent him from coming, use threats to prevent him from leaving. Even if someone claims to be as brave as Meng Ben and Xia Yu, he cannot regret his integrity. The emperor said: Yes. In ancient times, there were so-called loyal ministers who ensured peace and security, and Ji An was very similar to them. General Wei Qing entered the palace, and the emperor sat beside the bed to see him. Prime Minister Gongsun Hong usually asked to see him for something, but the emperor sometimes didn't even wear his hat. As for Ji An's visit, the emperor would not receive him without wearing a good hat. The emperor was once sitting in a majestic military tent. When Ji An came to report on official business, the emperor was not wearing a hat. When he saw him, he hurriedly hid in the tent and sent a close servant to approve his memorial. Ji An was respected and respected by the emperor to this extent. As soon as Zhang Tang became a court official by changing the criminal law, Ji An repeatedly questioned and accused Zhang Tang in front of the emperor, saying: As a minister, you are unable to carry forward the achievements of the late emperor, and you are unable to curb the evil desires of the people in the world. Safeguarding the country and enriching the people, and keeping the prisons empty of criminals are neither of these two things.
target: The emperor, recruiting literary scholars, was rebuked by Ji An for having many desires while feigning benevolence. The emperor grew angry, and ministers feared for Ji An. Later, the emperor remarked on Ji An's stupidity, but Ji An defended his integrity, stating he would not harm court affairs. Ill for three months, Ji An's condition persisted. Zhuang Zhu, requesting leave on his behalf, told the emperor that Ji An could assist a young monarch steadfastly, unswayed by inducements or threats. The emperor agreed, comparing Ji An to ancient loyal ministers. General Wei Qing entered the palace with the emperor seated by his bed, while Prime Minister Gongsun Hong sometimes saw the emperor without a hat. For Ji An, the emperor always wore a hat, once hiding in a tent when unprepared.

source: Ji An served as the internal history of You for several years. During his tenure, his political affairs were in order and never neglected. The general Wei Qing has become more and more noble. His sister Wei Zifu became the queen, but Ji An still treated him as an equal. Someone advised Ji An: "The emperor wanted all the officials to be subordinate to the general. Now that the general is respected and valued by the emperor, his status is even more noble. You must kneel down and worship him." Ji An replied: "Because the general has guests who bow his hands and salute, does that make him disrespected?" When the general heard what he said, he thought Ji An was even more virtuous. He asked him many times for advice on difficult matters in the country and the court, and regarded him better than people he had always known. Liu An, the king of Huainan, conspired to rebel and was afraid of Ji An. He said: "Ji An loves to speak out and give advice. He sticks to his integrity and is willing to die for justice. When today the emperor has conquered the Xiongnu many times and achieved great success, and Ji An advocated making peace with the foreigners without raising troops to conquer, he would not listen even more. When Ji An was enjoying the treatment of Jiuqing, Gongsun Hong and Zhang Tang were just ordinary petty officials. When Gongsun Hong and Zhang Tang became more prominent and equaled Ji An in official positions, Ji An again accused and slandered them. Soon, Gongsun Hong was promoted to prime minister and was granted the title of Marquis of Pingjin; Zhang Tangguan was promoted to Yushi Dafu; the former county magistrates and book historians under Ji An were also at the same level as Ji An, and some were re-employed and even surpassed him in status. Ji An was narrow-minded and impetuous, and it was impossible not to complain at all. When he met with the emperor, he stepped forward and said: Your Majesty appoints ministers like a pile of firewood, and the later ones are piled on top. The emperor remained silent. After a while Ji An retreated, and the emperor said: A person cannot be without knowledge. After listening to Ji An's words, his stupidity became more and more serious.
target: General Wei Qing's status rose, but Ji An treated him as an equal. When advised to kneel, Ji An replied that bowing did not diminish respect. As Ji An enjoyed Jiuqing treatment, Gongsun Hong and Zhang Tang rose to equal ranks, then surpassed him. Ji An complained to the emperor about later officials being piled on top, but the emperor dismissed his stupidity.

id: 史记/七十列传/汲郑列传::group-006
article_path: 史记/七十列传/汲郑列传
source: The emperor remained silent. After a while Ji An retreated, and the emperor said: A person cannot be without knowledge. After listening to Ji An's words, his stupidity became more and more serious. Not long after, King Hunxie of the Xiongnu led his troops to surrender to the Han Dynasty, and the court conscripted 20,000 vehicles to pick them up. The government had no money, so they borrowed horses from the people. Some people hide their horses so that they cannot gather them together. The emperor was furious and wanted to kill the magistrate of Chang'an. Ji An said: The magistrate of Chang'an County is not guilty. As long as he kills me, the people will be willing to sacrifice their horses. Moreover, if the Xiongnu generals betrayed their monarch and surrendered to the Han Dynasty, the court could slowly ask the counties along the way to prepare chariots and horses to pick them up in order. Why would it disturb the whole country and make our people exhausted to serve the surrendered soldiers of the Xiongnu generals? The emperor was silent. When King Hunxie arrived with his troops, more than 500 merchants were sentenced to death for doing business with the Huns.
target: When King Hunxie of the Xiongnu surrendered, the court borrowed horses from the people, causing unrest. Ji An defended the magistrate of Chang'an, suggesting gradual preparations. Later, over 500 merchants were sentenced to death for trading with the Huns.

id: 史记/七十列传/汲郑列传::group-007
article_path: 史记/七十列传/汲郑列传
source: Even if this is not possible now, and King Hunxie leads tens of thousands of people to surrender, he should not spend all the property in the official treasury to reward them, recruit honest and dutiful people to serve them, and treat them like darlings. How could the ignorant people know that if they allowed the Huns to buy goods in Chang'an City, they would be regarded as illegally smuggling property out of the customs by law enforcement officers who are obsessed with legal provisions and be sentenced? Even though Your Majesty cannot seize the Huns' supplies to comfort the people of the world, you still have to use harsh laws to kill more than 500 ignorant people. This is the so-called practice of "protecting the leaves and damaging the branches." I privately think that Your Majesty's move is undesirable. The emperor was silent and disagreed, and then said: I haven't heard Ji An's words for a long time. Today he talked nonsense again. A few months later, Ji An was convicted of violating a minor law. When the emperor granted him amnesty, he was only dismissed from office. So Ji An retired to the countryside.
target: Ji An argued against harsh laws, but the emperor disagreed. Months later, Ji An was convicted of a minor law, dismissed, and retired.

id: 史记/七十列传/汲郑列传::group-008
article_path: 史记/七十列传/汲郑列传
source: I now summon and appoint you. Due to the tense relationship between the local government and the people in Huaiyang, I have no choice but to use your authority and ask you to stay at home and manage it. After Ji An said goodbye to the emperor, he went to visit Li Xi, the great minister. He said: I was abandoned in a foreign county and can no longer participate in the affairs of the imperial court. However, Zhang Tang, the imperial censor, was clever enough to block other people's criticism, and cunning enough to cover up his own mistakes. He used clever flattery words and strong arguments to find faults. He refused to speak uprightly for the people of the world, and devoted himself to catering to the emperor's thoughts. If the emperor didn't want it, he would slander it; if the emperor wanted it, he would take the opportunity to praise it. He likes to cause trouble and fiddle with laws and regulations. In court, he is deeply treacherous to cater to the Lord's will, and outside the court, he blackmails officials who harm society to strengthen his power. You are the ninth minister. If you don't advise the emperor as soon as possible, both you and him will be killed. Li Xi was afraid of Zhang Tang and never dared to remonstrate with the emperor. Ji An managed the county affairs as he had in the past, and the politics of Huaiyang County became clear. Later, Zhang Tang was indeed ruined. After the emperor learned what Ji An had said to Li Xi, he found Li Xi guilty and ordered Ji An to enjoy the salary treatment of the princes and ministers and still be in charge of Huaiyang County. Ji An died seven years later. After Ji An's death, because of Ji An's relationship, the emperor appointed his younger brother Ji Ren to be promoted to the rank of Jiu Qing, and his son Ji Yan to be promoted to the minister of the princes and states. Ji An's aunt's son Sima An was also the prince Xima when he was young. He was good at juggling legal provisions and was skillful in serving as an official. His official position reached Jiuqing four times, and he died while serving as the governor of Henan County. Because of him, ten of his brothers were promoted to the rank of two thousand shi at the same time. Duan Hong from Puyang initially served Gaihou Wang Xin. Wang Xin recommended Duan Hong, and Duan Hong was promoted to Jiuqing twice. But the officials in Puyang's hometown all respected Ji An and were content to live under him.
target: Years later, the emperor appointed Ji An as prefect of Huaiyang County due to private coin minting. Ji An declined but was forced to accept. He managed the county well, and after Zhang Tang's ruin, the emperor ordered Ji An to enjoy princes' salary while governing Huaiyang. Ji An died seven years later. His brother Ji Ren and son Ji Yan were promoted, and his aunt's son Sima An reached Jiuqing four times. Duan Hong from Puyang also rose to Jiuqing, but officials respected Ji An more.

Zheng was born in Chen County with a courtesy name of Zhuang. His ancestor Zheng Jun once served as a general under Xiang Ji. Soon after Xiang Ji died, he belonged to the Han Dynasty. Emperor Gaozu ordered all Xiang Ji's former subordinates to call him by his first name when referring to Xiang Ji. Zheng Jun alone refused to accept the edict. Emperor Gaozu decreed that those who were willing to address Xiang Ji by his first name would be worshiped as senior officials, and Lord Zheng was driven away. Zheng Jun died during the reign of Emperor Xiaowen. Zheng Zhuang took pleasure in being a chivalrous man and rescuing Zhang Yu from danger, and his reputation spread throughout Liang and Chu. During the reign of Emperor Xiaojing, he served as Prince Sheren. During every five-day holiday, he often bought horses in the suburbs of Chang'an, rode on horseback to visit old friends, invited and thanked guests and friends, and stayed up all night long, always worrying about omissions. Zheng Zhuang loves Taoism and admires elderly and virtuous people. His affection is as intense as if he is afraid that he will never see them again. He is young and has a humble official position, but his close friends are all from his grandfather's generation and are famous people in the world. After Emperor Wu came to the throne, Zhengzhuang was promoted step by step from the lieutenant of Lu State, the prefect of Jinan Qun, and the prime minister of Jiangdu to the right internal history of Jiuqing. Due to his improper opinions on the dispute between Wu'an Hou Tianfan and Wei Qihou Dou Ying, he was demoted to Zhan Shi and was later transferred to Da Nong Ling. When Zheng Zhuang was doing the internal history of You, he warned his subordinate officials: If there are visitors, no matter they are noble or lowly, they are not allowed to wait at the door. He respects the host's hospitality and subordinates himself to the guests with his noble status. Zheng Zhuang was an upright person and did not purchase any private property. He only relied on his official salary and rewards to provide for his elderly friends. The gifts he gave to others were only a few meals in bamboo utensils.
target: Zheng Zhuang, courtesy name Zhuang, was born in Chen County. His ancestor Zheng Jun served under Xiang Ji and refused to address him by his first name, as ordered by Emperor Gaozu, leading to his dismissal. Zheng Zhuang was chivalrous, rescuing Zhang Yu, and gained fame in Liang and Chu. During Emperor Xiao Jing's reign, he served as Prince Sheren, often visiting friends and hosting guests. He loved Taoism, admired elders, and was humble. Under Emperor Wu, he rose to Right Internal History of Jiuqing but was demoted for improper opinions. As Right Internal History, he treated visitors equally, was upright, and had no private property, using his salary to support friends.

id: 史记/七十列传/汲郑列传::group-010
article_path: 史记/七十列传/汲郑列传
source: Zheng Zhuang was an upright person and did not purchase any private property. He only relied on his official salary and rewards to provide for his elderly friends. Whenever he goes to court and has the opportunity to give advice to the emperor, he will be praised by the most respected people in the world. He recommended scholars and his subordinates, prime ministers and officials, and talked about them with great interest. He often praised them as more capable than himself. He never addressed the officials by their first names, and when talking to his subordinates, he was so humble as if he was afraid of hurting them. When I heard that others had good ideas, I recommended them to the emperor for fear of delaying the matter. Therefore, scholars and well-known elders in the vast area east of Miao Mountain all praised his virtues. Zheng Zhuang was sent to inspect the breach of the Yellow River, and he asked for five days to prepare his luggage. The emperor said: I heard that Zheng Zhuang traveled thousands of miles without food. Why did he ask for time to prepare his luggage?
target: He recommended scholars, praising them as better than himself, and was praised by elders east of Miao Mountain. Sent to inspect the Yellow River breach, he asked for five days to prepare, but the emperor noted his reputation for traveling without food.

source: In his later years, the Han Dynasty conquered the Xiongnu and recruited ethnic minorities in various places. The world spent a lot of money and the country's financial and material resources were even more scarce. The people recommended by Zheng Zhuang and their guests were responsible for transportation for the great peasant order, and they owed a lot of money. Sima An was appointed as the prefect of Huaiyang County and reported the matter. Zheng Zhuang was held responsible for this. After atonement, he was demoted to a civilian. Soon, he entered the Prime Minister's Mansion and held the temporary post of chief historian. The emperor thought that he was old and asked him to be the governor of Runan County. A few years later, he died in office. Zheng Zhuang and Ji An were originally ranked among the nine ministers. They were honest in government and had pure conduct at home. Both of them were dismissed from office during the process, their families were poor, and their guests gradually declined. When he became a county magistrate, there was no property left in his family after his death. Because of him, as many as six or seven of Zheng Zhuang's brothers and descendants have reached the rank of two thousand shi. Tai Shigong said: Because Ji An and Zheng were so virtuous at that time, when they were powerful, the number of guests would be ten times greater, but when they were powerless, the situation was completely the opposite. If they were like this, let alone ordinary people! Zhai Gong of Xiajun County once said that when he first served as a court official, his house was full of guests; but when he lost his official position, the outside became so deserted that people could gather to catch birds. After he was reinstated, the guests wanted to see him again, so Zhai Gong wrote on the gate: "One death and one life are all friendships." One is poor and the other is rich, which is a state of acquaintance. One is noble and the other is humble, friendship is about seeing each other. Ji An and Zhengzhuang also had this misfortune, how sad!
target: In later years, due to debts from recommended guests, he was demoted to civilian, then served as governor of Runan County until death. Zhai Gong of Xiajun County wrote on his gate: "One death and one life show friendship; one poor and one rich show acquaintance; one noble and one humble show friendship." Ji An and Zheng Zhuang suffered this misfortune, which was sad.

id: 史记/七十列传/淮南衡山列传::group-000

source: Liu Chang, King Li of Huainan, was the youngest son of Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty. His mother was the concubine of Zhang Ao, the former king of Zhao. In the eighth year of Emperor Gaozu's reign, Emperor Gao passed by Zhao from Dongyuan County, and King Zhao dedicated King Li's mother to him. She was favored by the emperor and became pregnant. From then on, King Zhao Zhang Ao did not dare to let her live in the palace, so he built another palace for her to live in. The following year, the imperial court discovered that Zhao Xiangguan and others were plotting to kill Emperor Gaozu in Bairen County. King Zhao was also arrested and charged. His mother, brothers and concubines were all arrested and imprisoned in the Hanoi County government. King Li's mother said to the jailer in prison: I am favored by the emperor and am pregnant. The jailer reported truthfully that the emperor was angry because of King Zhao's incident and ignored the complaint of King Li's mother. Zhao Jian, the younger brother of King Li's mother, asked Piyang Hou Shenshi to inform Empress Lu. Queen Lu was jealous and refused to plead with the emperor, so Piyang Hou stopped trying to persuade him. King Li's mother was resentful after giving birth to Queen Li, so she committed suicide. The jailer carried King Li to the emperor. The emperor regretted it and ordered Queen Lu to raise him and bury King Li's mother in Zhending County. Zhending is the hometown of King Li's mother, and her ancestors lived there. In July of the eleventh year of Emperor Gaozu, King Yingbu of Huainan rebelled, so the emperor appointed his son Liu Chang as King of Huainan, putting him in charge of the four counties and fiefdoms that were formerly under Yingbu's territory. The emperor personally led an army to go out and annihilated Yingbu, so King Li took the throne of Huainan. King Li lost his mother when he was young and grew up dependent on Empress Lu. Therefore, he was able to avoid political disasters during the reign of Emperor Xiaohui and Empress Lu. However, he always resented Marquis Piyang in his heart and did not dare to take action. When Emperor Xiaowen came to the throne, King Huainan considered himself the closest to the emperor. He was arrogant and arrogant, and repeatedly violated laws and disciplines. The emperor thought of his brother-sister relationship and often tolerated and pardoned his faults. In the third year of Emperor Xiaowen's reign, King Huainan professed his own country and entered the dynasty. His attitude was very arrogant. He followed the emperor to the imperial garden for hunting, rode in the same car with the emperor, and often called the emperor "big brother". King Li was talented and brave, and could lift a heavy cauldron with all his strength, so he went to the mansion of Piyang Hou to seek an audience. When Marquis Piyang came out to see him, he took out an iron mallet from his sleeve and struck Marquis Piyang, and ordered his attendant Wei Jing to cut off Marquis Piyang's head. Afterwards, King Li galloped to the palace and apologized to the emperor, saying: "My mother should not have been convicted of Zhao's rebellion. At that time, if Marquis Piyang had tried his best to save her, he would have been able to get help from Empress Lu, but he did not try hard. This was the first crime." King Zhao Ruyi and his son were not guilty. Empress Lu deliberately killed them, but Marquis Piyang did not try to dissuade them. This was the second crime. Empress Lu made a relative of the Lu family king, intending to threaten the Liu family, and Marquis Piyang did not stand up to fight. This is the third crime. I killed the treacherous minister Piyanghou for the people of the world, and avenged my mother. I came to the court to kneel down and plead guilty. The emperor's desire to pity King Li, and out of brotherly love, did not punish him and pardoned him. During this period, the Empress Dowager Bo, the Crown Prince, and all the ministers were all afraid of King Li. Therefore, King Li became more arrogant and unruly after returning to the country. He did not act in accordance with the court decrees. He issued orders to warn Qingdao when entering and leaving the palace. He also called the orders he issued "zhi" and made laws by himself, imitating the emperor.
target: Liu Chang, King Li of Huainan, was the youngest son of Emperor Gaozu of Han. His mother, a concubine of the former King of Zhao, was favored by Emperor Gaozu and became pregnant. After the King of Zhao was implicated in a plot against the emperor, she was imprisoned and, despite being pregnant, her pleas for help were ignored due to the emperor's anger and Empress Lü's jealousy. After giving birth to Liu Chang, she committed suicide. The emperor regretted this and had Empress Lü raise the child. Liu Chang was later made King of Huainan after suppressing a rebellion. Growing up under Empress Lü's protection, Liu Chang escaped political disasters but harbored resentment against Marquis Piyang for not helping his mother. After Emperor Xiaowen ascended, Liu Chang became arrogant, calling the emperor "big brother" and violating laws. He eventually killed Marquis Piyang in revenge, claiming three crimes against him. The emperor pardoned him out of brotherly love, but Liu Chang grew more unruly, imitating imperial decrees and plotting rebellion.

id: 史记/七十列传/淮南衡山列传::group-001
article_path: 史记/七十列传/淮南衡山列传
source: In the sixth year of Emperor Xiaowen's reign, King Li asked seventy men without official titles to discuss with Chai Qi, the son of Chai Wu, Marquis of Jipu, and planned to use forty large trucks to rebel in Gukou County, and sent envoys to Minyue and Xiongnu to contact various places. The imperial court found out about this, punished the rebels, and sent envoys to summon King Huainan to the capital. King Huainan came to Chang'an. Prime Minister Zhang Bao, Dian Kechen Feng Jing, Imperial Censor Shizong Zhengchenyi, Tingwei Chenhe, and the thief Lieutenant Chenfu risked death. They reported: Huainan King Liu Chang abandoned the grammar of the late emperor, disobeyed the emperor's edict, and engaged in non-compliance with the law in daily life. He made his own chariot with a yellow satin umbrella that the emperor rode.
target: In the sixth year of Emperor Xiaowen's reign, Liu Chang conspired with seventy men to rebel, contacting Minyue and Xiongnu. The plot was discovered, and he was summoned to Chang'an.

id: 史记/七十列传/淮南衡山列传::group-002
article_path: 史记/七十列传/淮南衡山列传
source: Chen Cang, Chen Jing, Chen Yi, Chen Fu, and Chen He reported the crime of risking death: I have discussed it with forty-three people including the princes, the officials Chen Ying, and the two thousand stone officials. Everyone said that Liu Chang did not obey the law and the emperor's edict. He secretly recruited party members and conspirators, and treated those who were guilty and fled, out of evil intentions. The ministers and others decided that Liu Chang should be punished according to law. The emperor's instructions said: I cannot bear to punish King Huainan according to law. I should pardon his death penalty and dethrone him. Chen Cang and others committed the crime of risking death: Liu Chang was guilty of committing a crime of death. His Majesty could not bear to punish him according to law, so he graciously pardoned him and deposed him from the throne.
target: Officials reported his numerous crimes, including forging imperial chariots, appointing unauthorized officials, harboring fugitives, and killing innocents. The emperor, unable to bear punishing him, deposed him and exiled him to Shu County.

id: 史记/七十列传/淮南衡山列传::group-003
article_path: 史记/七十列传/淮南衡山列传
source: The emperor said: I just let him taste the pain, and I will let him come back. Those who were escorting King Huainan from various counties along the way did not dare to open the door of the prison car, so King Huainan said to his servant: Who said you, me, and I are brave men? How can I still be brave! I ended up in this predicament because I was too arrogant to hear my own faults. How can one endure such depression in this life! So he went on a hunger strike and died. When the prison car arrived at Yong County, the county magistrate opened the sealed door and reported the news of Liu Chang's death to the emperor.
target: Liu Chang went on a hunger strike and died en route. The emperor later posthumously honored him as King Li and enfeoffed his sons.

id: 史记/七十列传/淮南衡山列传::group-004
article_path: 史记/七十列传/淮南衡山列传
source: King Huainan is the same as before. Liu An, the king of Huainan, liked reading and playing the piano, but he didn't like shooting and letting dogs and horses race. He also wanted to do good deeds secretly to appease the people and spread his good name throughout the world. He often complained about the death of King Li and often wanted to rebel against the court, but he had no chance. In the second year of Emperor Xiaowu's founding, King Huainan went to Beijing to see the emperor. Tianfan, the Marquis of Wu'an, who had always been good friends with him, was serving as a Taiwei at that time. Tian Fu greeted King Huainan at Bashang and told him: Now the emperor has no prince. Your Majesty, you are the grandson of Emperor Gao. Your benevolence and righteousness are known to everyone in the world. If the emperor dies one day, who should succeed him if not you? The King of Huainan was very happy and gave Marquis Wuan a generous gift of gold, silver, money, and items. The king of Huainan secretly made friends with guests, appeased the people, and planned rebellion. In the sixth year of Jianyuan, a comet appeared, and the king of Huainan felt strange. Someone advised the King of Huainan: In the past, when the Wu army rose up, the comet appeared only a few feet long, but the battle was still bloody for thousands of miles. Now that the comets have grown all over the sky, there will be a great war in the world. The King of Huainan thought that the emperor had no crown prince, and if something happened in the world, all the princes and kings would fight for the throne together, so he stepped up his efforts to organize weapons and offensive equipment, and accumulated gold and money to bribe the county guards, princes, lobbyists and talented people. All the eloquent and eloquent people gave advice to the King of Huainan, but they all made up absurd and heresies to flatter the King of Huainan. The king of Huainan was very happy and rewarded them with a lot of money, but he was even more interested in rebellion. The King of Huainan has a daughter named Liu Ling. She is smart and eloquent.
target: Liu Chang's son, Liu An, became King of Huainan. He was cultured and sought to win over the people, but he resented his father's death and plotted rebellion. He befriended guests, accumulated weapons, and bribed officials.

id: 史记/七十列传/淮南衡山列传::group-005
article_path: 史记/七十列传/淮南衡山列传
source: So the King of Huainan ordered his slaves to enter the palace and forged the emperor's seal, the prime minister, the imperial censor, the general, the military historian, Zhong Erqian Shi, the official seals of the various officials in the capital and county magistrates, the official seals of the prefects and captains of neighboring counties, and the official hats worn by the court envoys and judges, all planning to act according to Wu Qui's plan. The King of Huainan also sent people to pretend to be convicted and escape from the Huainan Kingdom and go west to Chang'an to serve the general and the prime minister. He intended to have them assassinate the general Wei Qing immediately if an army broke out, and then persuade the prime minister to surrender. It would be as easy as removing a covering cloth.
target: His daughter, Liu Ling, spied in Chang'an. The king's advisor, Wu Bei, warned against rebellion, citing the failures of Wu and Chu and the stability of the Han dynasty. Despite this, Liu An continued preparations, forging seals and planning to assassinate officials.

id: 史记/七十列传/淮南衡山列传::group-006
article_path: 史记/七十列传/淮南衡山列传
source: Liu An's crime was more serious than the rebellion, and his rebellion was a foregone conclusion. I have seen clear evidence of his forged documents, talismans, seals, maps and other treasonous and immoral facts. His crime is extremely treasonous and immoral, and he should be executed according to law. As for the officials in the Huainan Kingdom with an official rank of more than 200 shi and less than 200 shi, as well as the favored ministers of the clan who have not violated the law, if they cannot fulfill their duties to correct the Huainan King and prevent the rebellion of the King of Huainan, they should be removed from their posts, have their titles reduced, and be demoted to soldiers, and they will not be allowed to serve as officials again in the future. Those other criminals who are not officials can use two pounds and eighty taels of gold to pay for the death penalty. The imperial court should publicly expose Liu An's crimes so that everyone in the world will clearly understand the way of being a minister and will not dare to have evil ambitions to betray the emperor. Prime Minister Gongsun Hong, Tingwei Zhang Tang and others reported everyone's opinions, and the emperor sent Zongzheng holding a talisman to judge the Huainan King. Before Zongzheng arrived in Huainan, King Liu An of Huainan had committed suicide in advance. Queen Tu, Prince Liu Qian and all those who collaborated in the rebellion were all killed. When the emperor of Huainan, Liu An, was dissuaded from rebelling because of Wu, his words were elegant and upright. He said a lot of good things about the government and wanted not to kill him. Ting Wei Zhang Tang said: Wu Ban was the first to plot a rebellion for the King of Huainan, and his crime cannot be forgiven. So Wu Bei was killed.
target: The plot was exposed when Liu An's grandson, Liu Jian, informed on the prince. The court investigated, and Liu An, fearing exposure, hesitated to act. His advisor Wu Bei again urged caution, but Liu An persisted. Eventually, the court arrested the conspirators, and Liu An committed suicide before his arrest. His queen and prince were executed, and Huainan was reduced to a commandery.

id: 史记/七十列传/淮南衡山列传::group-007
article_path: 史记/七十列传/淮南衡山列传
source: If you send troops when the time is not ripe, I am afraid you will not succeed. I am willing to go to the court to be arrested. King Huainan also secretly wanted to give up, so he agreed to the prince's request. So the prince cut his neck and committed suicide, but he did not die. Wu Ban went to the law enforcement officials alone and reported his participation in the Huainan King's rebellion, and gave all the details of the rebellion. The legal officials therefore arrested the prince and the queen, surrounded the palace, searched and arrested all the guests of King Huainan who participated in the rebellion, and also found the utensils of the rebellion, and then reported the matter to the emperor. The emperor handed the case to the ministers for trial. The case implicated several thousand princes, two thousand stones, and local tycoons who had conspired with the Huainan King. They were all sentenced to death according to the severity of the crime. Liu Ci, the king of Hengshan, was the younger brother of the king of Huainan. He was found guilty of the same crime and should be arrested. The official responsible for handling the case requested the arrest of the king of Hengshan. The Emperor said: Each prince and king regards his own feudal state as the foundation of his life and should not involve each other. You, together with the princes and princes, go to meet with the prime minister to discuss. After discussion, forty-three people including King Pengzu of Zhao and Cao Xiang, the princes of Lieutenant, all said: King Liu An of Huainan is extremely treasonous and immoral. His crime of rebellion is clear and he should be punished without mercy. Liu Duan, the king of Jiaoxi, expressed his opinion: Liu An, the king of Huainan, ignored the king's law and did evil things. He was deceitful, disrupted the world, confused the people, betrayed his ancestors, and spread heresy. "Spring and Autumn" once said that ministers should not lead the people to cause chaos, and they should be killed if they lead the people to cause chaos. Liu An's crime was more serious than the rebellion, and his rebellion was a foregone conclusion.
target: Liu An's brother, Liu Ci, King of Hengshan, also plotted rebellion. He feuded with his brother and prepared for war, forging documents and building weapons. His internal conflicts, including disputes over succession and adultery, led to his downfall. After his son Liu Xiao surrendered and revealed the plot, Liu Ci committed suicide. His kingdom was also abolished.
