target: Sima Qian comments that despite their noble status, the kings of Huainan and Hengshan failed in their duties and plotted rebellion, leading to their ruin. Their faults were compounded by the influence of unruly subordinates and local customs.

id: 史记/七十列传/淮阴侯列传::group-000
article_path: 史记/七十列传/淮阴侯列传
source: Han Xin, the Marquis of Huaiyin, was from Huaiyin. When he was a commoner, he was poor, had no good character, could not be elected to be an official, and could not make a living by doing business. He often lived in other people's homes and had nothing to do, so most people hated him. I went to the countryside many times to have a casual meal at the pavilion in Nanchang. For several months, the pavilion chief's wife was worried about Han Xin, so she made breakfast in advance and took it to the bed in the inner room to eat. When it was time to eat, Han Xin went, but no food was prepared for him. Han Xin also understood their intentions. In a rage, he actually left and never came back. Han Xin was fishing under the city, and there were several old ladies rinsing the silk cotton. One of them saw that Han Xin was hungry, so she gave Han Xin food to eat. This continues for dozens of days until rinsing is complete. Han Xin was very happy and said to the aunt: I will repay you heavily in the future. The aunt said angrily: "A man can't support himself. I give you food out of pity for you, the young master. Do I hope you will repay me?" A young man among the Huaiyin butchers insulted Han Xin and said: Although you are tall and like to carry a sword, you are actually a coward. He insulted him in public and said: If you are not afraid of death, stab me with a sword; if you are afraid of death, crawl under my crotch. So Han Xin looked at him carefully, lowered himself to the ground, and crawled under his crotch. People all over the street laughed at Han Xin and thought he was timid. When Xiang Liang led his army across the Huaihe River, Han Xin followed him with a sword, but he had no reputation among Xiang Liang's men. Xiang Liang was defeated, and Han Xin was subordinated to Xiang Yu, who made him a doctor. He repeatedly offered suggestions to Xiang Yu in order to be reused, but Xiang Yu did not adopt them. Liu Bang, the king of Han, entered Shu, and Han Xin left the Chu army and submitted to the king of Han. Because he had no reputation, he only served as a minor official receiving guests. Later, he was sentenced to beheading for breaking the law, and all thirteen people who were accomplices in the crime were killed. When it was Han Xin's turn, he looked up and happened to see Teng Gong and said: Doesn't the King of Han want to achieve the feat of unifying the world? Why do you want to kill the strong man? Teng Gong felt that his words were extraordinary and saw that he was handsome, so he let him go.
target: Han Xin, the Marquis of Huaiyin, was a native of Huaiyin. In his youth, he was poor, lacked good character, and could not secure an official position or make a living through business. He often relied on others for meals, which made him disliked. He frequently ate at a pavilion in Nanchang, but the pavilion chief's wife, annoyed by his presence, began eating breakfast early in the inner room. When Han Xin arrived, no food was prepared for him. Angered, he left and never returned. While fishing under the city, an old woman rinsing silk cotton pitied his hunger and fed him for dozens of days. Han Xin promised to repay her heavily, but she rebuked him, saying she did not expect repayment. A young butcher insulted Han Xin, calling him a coward and challenging him to either stab him or crawl under his crotch. Han Xin chose to crawl, and the crowd mocked him for his timidity. When Xiang Liang led his army across the Huai River, Han Xin followed but gained no reputation. After Xiang Liang's defeat, he served under Xiang Yu as a doctor, offering suggestions that were ignored. He then joined Liu Bang, the King of Han, but was only made a minor official.

id: 史记/七十列传/淮阴侯列传::group-001
article_path: 史记/七十列传/淮阴侯列传
source: When Xiang Liang led his army across the Huaihe River, Han Xin followed him with a sword, but he had no reputation among Xiang Liang's men. Xiang Liang was defeated, and Han Xin was subordinated to Xiang Yu, who made him a doctor. He repeatedly offered suggestions to Xiang Yu in order to be reused, but Xiang Yu did not adopt them. Liu Bang, the king of Han, entered Shu, and Han Xin left the Chu army and submitted to the king of Han. Because he had no reputation, he only served as a minor official receiving guests. Later, he was sentenced to beheading for breaking the law, and all thirteen people who were accomplices in the crime were killed. When it was Han Xin's turn, he looked up and happened to see Teng Gong and said: Doesn't the King of Han want to achieve the feat of unifying the world? Why do you want to kill the strong man? Teng Gong felt that his words were extraordinary and saw that he was handsome, so he let him go. Talked with Han Xin, admired him very much, and reported the matter to the King of Han, who appointed Han Xin as the Commander-in-Chief of Su Su. But the king of Han did not see that he had any special talents. Han Xin talked to Xiao He many times, and Xiao He thought he was a genius. When they arrived at Nanzheng, dozens of generals from all walks of life fled on the way. Han Xin speculated that Xiao He and others had recommended him to the King of Han many times, but the King of Han did not use him and ran away. Xiao He heard that Han Xin had escaped and had no time to report to the King of Han, so he chased him personally. Someone reported to the King of Han that: Prime Minister Xiao He has escaped. The king of Han was furious because losing Xiao He was like losing his right and left hands. A day or two later, Xiao He came to see the King of Han. The King of Han was both angry and happy. He scolded Xiao He and said: Why did you run away? Xiao He said: I don't dare to run away, I will chase the escaping person. The king of Han said: Who are you chasing? He replied: It’s Han Xin. The King of Han cursed again: Dozens of generals from all walks of life have fled, but you did not chase anyone; but you chased Han Xin, which is a lie. Xiao He said: Those generals are easy to get. As for outstanding figures like Han Xin, there is no second person in the world.
target: Sentenced to death for breaking the law, he caught the attention of Teng Gong, who spared him after a bold speech. Teng Gong recommended him to Liu Bang, who appointed him as a commander, though without recognizing his talents. Han Xin frequently conversed with Xiao He, who considered him a genius. When Han Xin fled due to lack of recognition, Xiao He chased him personally. Liu Bang initially suspected Xiao He of desertion but learned he was pursuing Han Xin. Xiao He argued that Han Xin was unparalleled and essential for Liu Bang's ambitions to conquer the world. Liu Bang agreed to make Han Xin a general, and after a formal ceremony, Han Xin was appointed.

id: 史记/七十列传/淮阴侯列传::group-002
article_path: 史记/七十列传/淮阴侯列传
source: Although he was the hegemon in name, he actually lost the support of the people in the world. Therefore, his advantages can easily be turned into disadvantages. Now the king can really do the opposite: appointing the brave and capable talents in the world, what can't be punished? If all the cities in the world are given to meritorious ministers, who wouldn't be convinced? As a righteous teacher, obeying the soldiers' wish to return eastward, what kind of enemy cannot be defeated? Moreover, the three kings that Xiang Yu enfeoffed were all generals of the Qin Dynasty. They led the children of Qin to fight for several years, and many of them were killed and escaped. They also deceived their subordinates to surrender to the princes. Upon arriving at Xin'an, King Xiang cunningly buried alive more than 200,000 Qin troops who had surrendered. Only Zhang Han, Sima Xin, and Dong Yi survived. The fathers and brothers of Qin hated these three men to their bones. Now, relying on his power, Xiang Yu forcibly made these three kings, and no one in Qin loved them. When the king entered Wuguan, Qiu did not commit any crime. He abolished the harsh laws of the Qin Dynasty and made a three-part agreement with the people of Qin. All the people of Qin did not want the king to be king in Qin. According to the agreement made by the princes, the king should be the king in Guanzhong. The people in Guanzhong all know this. The king lost the title he deserved and entered Hanzhong. The people of Qin all regretted it. Now that the king has mobilized his army to advance eastward, the Sanqin fiefdom can be pacified with just one document. So the King of Han was very happy, thinking that it was too late to get Han Xin. Just follow Han Xin's plan and deploy various generals to attack targets. In August, the King of Han sent troops to advance eastward through Chencang and pacified the Three Qin Dynasties. In the second year of the Han Dynasty, troops went out of Hangu Pass and subdued the king of Wei and the king of Henan. The king of Han and Yin also surrendered one after another. The king of Han then joined forces with the king of Qi and the king of Zhao to attack the Chu army. In April, when they arrived at Pengcheng, the Han army was defeated and returned in disarray. Han Xin gathered the scattered troops and met the King of Han in Xingyang, and defeated the Chu army between Jingxian and Suoting. Therefore, the Chu army was never able to advance westward. After the Han army was defeated in Pengcheng, King Sima Xin of Sai and King Dong Yi of Zhai rebelled against Han and surrendered to Chu. Qi and Zhao also rebelled against Han and reconciled with Chu. In June, King Bao of Wei asked for leave to return to his hometown on the pretext of visiting his mother's illness. As soon as he arrived in the feudal state, he immediately cut off the main transportation road at Linjin Pass at the Yellow River ferry, rebelled against the king of Han, and made peace with the Chu army. The king of Han sent Li Sheng to lobby Wei Bao, but failed. In August of this year, the King of Han appointed Han Xin as Prime Minister Zuo to attack King Bao of Wei. The king of Wei stationed the main force in Puban and blocked Linjin Pass, the Yellow River ferry. Han Xin added more suspects and deliberately arranged warships to pretend to cross the river at Linjin. However, the hidden troops used wooden basins to float across the river from Xia Yang and attacked Anyi. King Bao of Wei panicked and led his army to attack Han Xin. Han Xin captured Wei Bao, pacified Wei and reorganized it into Hedong County.
target: Han Xin analyzed Xiang Yu's weaknesses, such as his inability to delegate, his reluctance to reward subordinates, and his harsh rule, which alienated the people. He advised Liu Bang to adopt the opposite approach, emphasizing the loyalty of the Qin people due to Liu Bang's merciful policies. Liu Bang followed Han Xin's plan, and in August, they advanced eastward through Chencang, pacifying the Three Qin regions. In the second year of the Han Dynasty, they subdued the kings of Wei and Henan. However, in April, the Han army was defeated at Pengcheng. Han Xin regrouped and met Liu Bang at Xingyang, defeating the Chu army. Later, King Bao of Wei rebelled, and Han Xin captured him, pacifying Wei. He then attacked Zhao with Zhang Er, defeating a 200,000-strong Zhao army at Jingxing by using a river-backed formation and a surprise cavalry attack. Han Xin spared Li Zuoche, who advised him to subdue Yan and Qi through diplomacy rather than force. Han Xin followed this advice, and Yan surrendered.

id: 史记/七十列传/淮阴侯列传::group-003
article_path: 史记/七十列传/淮阴侯列传
source: The Qi and Chu armies fought on their own land, and the soldiers easily escaped. It is better to have a deep trench and a high base, unable to hold on. Let the King of Qi send his trusted ministers to pacify the cities that have fallen. If the officials and people of these cities know that their king is still there and the Chu army comes to rescue them, they will definitely rebel against the Han army. The Han army lives two thousand miles away, and the people in Qi's cities and towns rise up to rebel against them. They will inevitably lose food, which will force them to surrender without a fight. Long Qie said: I have always understood Han Xin's character and it is easy to deal with him. Moreover, I rescued Qi and made Han Xin surrender without a fight. What credit do I have for that? Now that I have defeated him, half of Qi's land can be entrusted to me. Why not fight? So he decided to start a war and set up a battle array with Han Xin across the Weishui River. Han Xin ordered more than 10,000 bags to be made overnight, filled with sand and soil, blocked the upper reaches of the Weishui River, led half of the army across the river, attacked Long Qie, pretended to be defeated, and ran back. Long Qie said happily: "I have known that Han Xin is timid." So he crossed the Weishui River to pursue Han Xin. Han Xin ordered the sandbags blocking the Weishui River to be excavated. The river surged forward, and more than half of Long Qie's army had not yet crossed the river. Han Xin immediately returned to the army and counterattacked fiercely, killing Long Qie. Long Qie's troops on the east bank of the Weishui River that had not yet crossed the river scattered and fled. King Tian Guang of Qi also fled. Han Xin pursued the defeated troops as far as Chengyang and captured all the Chu soldiers. In the fourth year of the Han Dynasty, Han Xin surrendered and pacified the entire Qi State. He sent someone to write to the King of Han, saying: Qi is cunning and capricious, and its southern border borders Chu. If a temporary acting king is not set up to pacify it, the situation will not be stable. In order to facilitate the current situation, I hope that I will be allowed to temporarily act as King Qi. At this time, the Chu army was tightly besieging the King of Han in Xingyang. Han Xin's envoy arrived. The King of Han opened the letter and read it. He became furious and cursed: I am besieged here and I am waiting for you to help me day and night, but you want to make yourself king! Zhang Liang and Chen Ping secretly stepped on the King of Han's feet, leaned into the King of Han's ear and said: "The Han army is currently in a disadvantageous situation. How can we prevent Han Xin from becoming king?" It is better to take the opportunity to make him king, treat him well, and let him guard Qi by himself. Otherwise, an accident may occur. The King of Han woke up and deliberately cursed again: Since a man has conquered the feudal lords, he must be the real king. Why should he be a temporary acting king? He sent Zhang Liang to appoint Han Xin as King of Qi and mobilized his army to attack the Chu army. After the Chu army lost Long Qi, King Xiang was frightened and sent Wu She from Xuyi to persuade King Han Xin of Qi, saying: "The people of the world have suffered from Qin's tyranny for a long time, so we all work together to attack it."
target: Han Xin requested that Zhang Er be made King of Zhao, which Liu Bang approved. The Chu army besieged Liu Bang at Xingyang, but he escaped and seized Han Xin's troops. Han Xin was ordered to attack Qi, and despite Liu Bang's envoy Li Shiqi persuading Qi to surrender, Han Xin, urged by Kuai Tong, attacked and conquered Qi. Chu sent Long Qie to aid Qi, but Han Xin defeated him by damming the Wei River and then releasing the water, killing Long Qie. Han Xin then requested to be made acting King of Qi. Liu Bang, initially furious, was persuaded by Zhang Liang and Chen Ping to grant the title to secure Han Xin's loyalty. Kuai Tong later advised Han Xin to rebel and divide the world into three parts, but Han Xin refused, citing Liu Bang's generosity. Despite Kuai Tong's warnings about the dangers of his position, Han Xin hesitated and ultimately remained loyal.

id: 史记/七十列传/淮阴侯列传::group-004
article_path: 史记/七十列传/淮阴侯列传
source: So Han Xin was given torture instruments. When he arrived in Luoyang, he pardoned Han Xin's sins and changed his title to Marquis of Huaiyin. Han Xin knew that the king of Han was afraid of his own abilities and often excused himself from attending court meetings and attending court meetings due to illness. From then on, Han Xin was resentful day and night, unhappy at home, and felt ashamed of being in the same position as Jianghou and Guan Ying. Han Xin once visited General Fan Kuai. Fan Kuai knelt down to greet him and called himself a minister. Said: How come the king is willing to come?
target: After Xiang Yu's defeat, Liu Bang demoted Han Xin to King of Chu and later, fearing his influence, arrested him during a visit to Yunmeng. Han Xin was pardoned but reduced to Marquis of Huaiyin.

id: 史记/七十列传/淮阴侯列传::group-005
article_path: 史记/七十列传/淮阴侯列传
source: Han Xin discussed with his retainers and falsely issued an edict at night to pardon the criminals and slaves serving in various government offices, intending to mobilize them to attack Empress Lu and the prince. The deployment is completed and we are waiting for news from Chen Xi. One of his retainers offended Han Xin, who imprisoned him and planned to kill him. His younger brother wrote a letter of rebellion and reported to Empress Lu that Han Xin was preparing to rebel. Empress Lu planned to summon Han Xin, but was afraid that he would not submit, so she conspired with Xiao Xiangguo to pretend that Chen Xi was coming from the emperor, saying that Chen Xi had been captured and executed, and all the princes and ministers came to congratulate him. Xiao Xiangguo deceived Han Xin and said: Even if he is ill, he must work hard to go to the palace to congratulate him. When Han Xin entered the palace, Empress Lu ordered the warriors to tie Han Xin up and kill him in the bell chamber of Changle Palace. When Han Xin was about to be executed, he said: I regret that I did not adopt Kuai Tong's plan and was deceived by women and boys. Isn't it God's will? So he killed the three Han and Xin tribes. Emperor Gaozu returned to the capital from the army that suppressed Chen Xi's rebellion. When he saw that Han Xin was dead, he was happy and pitied him, and asked: What did Han Xin say before he died? Queen Lu said: Han Xin said he regretted not adopting Kuai Tong's plan. Emperor Gaozu said: That man is a lobbyist of Qi State. He ordered Qi to capture Kuai Tong. Kuai Tong was brought, and the emperor said: "Did you instigate the Marquis of Huaiyin to rebel?" Answer: Yes. I did teach him that the boy would perish by not following my plan. If that kid adopts my plan, how can Your Majesty destroy him? The emperor said angrily: "Cook him." Kuai Tong said: Oh, boil me to death, it is unfair! The emperor said: You instigated Han Xin to rebel. What injustice is there? Kuai Tong said: When the laws of the Qin Dynasty were corrupted and the political power collapsed, the six kingdoms of Shandong were in chaos. The princes from all walks of life revolted one after another. For a time, the heroes of the world gathered like crows. The Qin Dynasty lost its throne, and all the heroes in the world came to snatch it, so those with high intelligence and quick actions were the first to get it. Zhi's dog barked at Yao. Yao was not unkind, just because he was not the owner of the dog. At this time, I only knew that there was Han Xin, but not His Majesty. Moreover, there are too many people in the world who are sharpening their weapons and holding sharp knives in their hands who want to do what Your Majesty is doing, but they are just not up to the task. How can you cook them all to death? Emperor Gaozu said: Let him go. Kuai Tong's sins were forgiven. Tai Shigong said: When I went to Huaiyin, the Huaiyin people told me that even when Han Xin was a commoner, his ambition was different. His mother passed away and the family was too poor to bury her, but he still looked for a high and spacious cemetery where thousands of families could be placed next to the tomb. I looked at his mother's grave and it was true.
target: He grew resentful and avoided court. When Chen Xi rebelled, Han Xin conspired with him but was betrayed by a retainer. Empress Lu and Xiao He tricked Han Xin into the palace, where he was executed. Before his death, he regretted not following Kuai Tong's advice. Kuai Tong was captured but spared after arguing that he only served his master. The historian comments that Han Xin's early ambition was evident, but his failure to remain humble and his eventual rebellion led to his downfall.

id: 史记/七十列传/滑稽列传::group-000
article_path: 史记/七十列传/滑稽列传
source: Confucius said: The Six Classics have the same role in governing the country. "Li" is used to regulate people's words and deeds, "Music" is used to promote people's harmony, "Book" is used to record past deeds and regulations, "Poetry" is used to express emotions, "Yi" is used to spy on the magical changes of heaven and earth, and "Spring and Autumn" is used to understand the meaning of subtle words and weigh the right and wrong. Tai Shigong said: The truth in the world is vast and boundless, isn't it great! If the words can be slightly to the point, it can also resolve a lot of troubles. Chunyu Kun was a son-in-law of Qi State. Less than seven feet tall, he is funny and eloquent. He has been on many missions to the princes and has never been humiliated. When King Wei of Qi was in power, he liked to talk in argot, feast all night long, indulge in excessive drinking, ignored state affairs, and entrusted political affairs to the officials. The civil and military officials are dissolute and indulgent, and the princes and countries invade and invade. The country is in danger and is in danger in a matter of seconds. None of the ministers around King Qi dared to give advice. Chunyu Kun used argot to admonish and admonish King Wei of Qi, saying: There is a big bird in the capital that landed in the king's courtyard. It has not flown or screamed for three years. Does the king know what happened to this bird? King Wei of Qi said: If this bird does not fly, it will go straight to the sky; if it does not scream, it will amaze people. So he ordered all the chiefs of the seventy-two counties in the country to come to the court to report. They rewarded one person and killed another. They also sent troops to defend against the enemy. The princes and states were shocked and returned the occupied land to Qi. Qi's prestige lasted for thirty-six years. All these things are recorded in "Tian Wan Family". In the eighth year of King Wei of Qi's reign, the State of Chu sent a large army to invade its borders. The King of Qi sent Chunyu Kun as an envoy to the State of Zhao to request reinforcements, and asked him to carry a gift of a hundred catties of gold and ten four-horse carriages.

Tai Shigong remarked on the vastness of truth, noting that concise words can resolve many troubles. Chunyu Kun, a short, witty son-in-law of Qi, often served as an envoy without disgrace. During King Wei of Qi's reign, the king neglected state affairs, indulging in feasting and drinking, leading to invasions and national peril. No minister dared to advise. Chunyu Kun used an allegory of a great bird that neither flew nor cried for three years.

id: 史记/七十列传/滑稽列传::group-001
article_path: 史记/七十列传/滑稽列传
source: King Wei of Qi said: If this bird does not fly, it will go straight to the sky; if it does not scream, it will amaze people. So he ordered all the chiefs of the seventy-two counties in the country to come to the court to report. They rewarded one person and killed another. They also sent troops to defend against the enemy. The princes and states were shocked and returned the occupied land to Qi. Qi's prestige lasted for thirty-six years. All these things are recorded in "Tian Wan Family". In the eighth year of King Wei of Qi's reign, the State of Chu sent a large army to invade its borders. The King of Qi sent Chunyu Kun as an envoy to the State of Zhao to request reinforcements, and asked him to carry a gift of a hundred catties of gold and ten four-horse carriages. Chunyu Kun looked up to the sky and laughed so hard that the string holding his hat broke. King Wei said: Sir, do you think the gift is too little? Chunyu Kun said: How dare you think too little! King Wei said: Then you laugh, do you have any excuse? Chunyu Kun said: Today I came from the east and saw a man worshiping the God of the Fields by the roadside. He held a pig's trotter and a glass of wine and prayed: "The grain harvested in the highlands fills the bonnet, and the crops harvested in the low fields fill the vehicles; the grains are lush and ripe, and the rice grains are piled up in the warehouse." I saw that he brought few sacrifices and prayed for many things, so I laughed at him. So King Wei of Qi increased the gifts to a thousand pieces of gold, ten pairs of white jade stones, and a hundred four-horse carriages. Chunyu Kun said goodbye and set off for the Kingdom of Zhao. King Zhao allocated him 100,000 elite soldiers and 1,000 leather-wrapped chariots. When the Chu State heard the news, they withdrew their troops overnight. King Qi Wei was very happy. He set up wine and food in the harem, summoned Chunyu Kun and gave him wine to drink. Ask him: How much wine can you drink before you get drunk? Chunyu Kun replied: I can get drunk even if I drink a dou of wine, and I can get drunk even if I drink a stone of wine. King Wei said: "Sir, you will get drunk after drinking one measure. How can you drink one stone?" Can you tell me this truth? Chunyu Kun said: The king gave me wine in front of me, with the law enforcement officer standing beside me and the censor standing behind me. I was frightened, bowed my head and drank on the ground. I was drunk after not even one bucket. If my parents have distinguished guests, I roll up my sleeves, sit down on my knees, and serve wine to the guests. The guests reward me with residual wine from time to time, and I raise my glass to toast many times to socialize, and I get drunk after less than two cups. If friends are traveling together, they have not seen each other for a long time, and suddenly they meet again. They happily reminisce about the past and talk about their hearts. They will become drunk after drinking about five or six buckets.
target: King Wei understood, summoned all county chiefs, rewarded one, executed another, and repelled invaders, restoring Qi's prestige for 36 years. Later, when Chu invaded, Chunyu Kun was sent to Zhao for reinforcements with modest gifts. He laughed at a farmer praying for abundant harvests with meager offerings, prompting King Wei to increase the gifts. Zhao then sent 100,000 elite troops, causing Chu to withdraw. King Wei asked Chunyu Kun about his drinking capacity. Chunyu Kun explained that his drunkenness varied by context: fear made him drunk after one measure, while joy allowed him to drink eight measures.

source: As for gatherings in the countryside, men and women sit together, toast each other, and there is no time limit. They also play games such as Liubo and Hu Tou. They call friends and invite pairs. Shaking hands and talking happily are not punished, and flirting is not prohibited. There are fallen earrings in front of me and lost hairpins behind my back. At this time, I am happiest. I can drink eight measures of wine, and I am only two or three points drunk. It was getting dark and the wine was almost finished. We put the remaining wine together and everyone sat down together, men and women sharing the same table. Shoes and clogs were mixed together. Cups and plates were in a mess. The candles in the main room had been extinguished. Therefore, if you drink too much, you will easily get into trouble, and if you are extremely happy, something sad will happen. This is true of all things. This statement means that no matter what happens, it should not be taken to extremes. If it reaches extremes, it will decline. Chunyu Kun used this to tactfully persuade King Qi Wei. King Wei said: OK. So King Wei stopped drinking and drinking every night, and appointed Chunyu Kun as the guest official to receive guests from the princes.
target: He warned against excess, as it leads to decline. King Wei ceased nightly drinking and appointed Chunyu Kun as a guest official.

id: 史记/七十列传/滑稽列传::group-003
article_path: 史记/七十列传/滑稽列传
source: The royal family of the King of Qi held banquets, and Chunyu Kun often accompanied them. More than a hundred years after Chunyu Kun, Yu Meng came out of the Chu State. You Meng was originally a singing and dancing artist from Chu State. He was eight feet tall and very eloquent. He often used jokes to persuade the king of Chu. During the reign of King Zhuang of Chu, he had a favorite horse. He dressed it in brocade clothes, kept it in a magnificent house, slept on a bed without a curtain, and fed it candied dried dates. The horse became ill and died because of obesity. King Zhuang of Chu sent his ministers to hold a funeral for the horse. They wanted to bury it in a coffin and bury it according to the etiquette of a doctor. King Zhuang's ministers on the left and right quarreled with each other to advise him on this matter, thinking that it should not be done. King Zhuang issued an order: Anyone who dares to remonstrate with the matter of burying a horse will be sentenced to death. When Youmeng heard this, he walked into the palace gate and cried to the sky. King Zhuang was surprised and asked him why he was crying. Youmeng said: "The horse is the king's favorite thing. With a country as powerful as Chu, there is nothing that can't be done, but burying it with the etiquette of a doctor is too rude. Please bury it with the etiquette of a king." King Zhuang asked: What should we do? You Meng replied: I requested that the coffin be made of beautiful jade with carved patterns, the cover of fine catalpa wood, and the coffin blocks made of valuable woods such as urin, maple, hemp, and camphor. I sent soldiers to dig a grave for it, and asked the elderly and children to carry earth to build the tomb. When the princes heard this, they all knew that the king despised people and valued horses. King Zhuang said: "Has my fault reached this level?" What to do about it? Umeng said: Please allow me to bury it in the same way as an animal: pile an earth stove on the ground as a set, use a large copper pot as a coffin, use ginger and dates to season, use spices to relieve the smell, use rice as a sacrifice, use fire as clothes, and bury it in the human belly. So King Zhuang sent someone to give the horse to the eunuch in charge of the palace's meals, so that the people in the world would not spread the matter for a long time. Sun Shuao, the prime minister of Chu, knew that Youmeng was a wise man and treated him well. When Sun Shuao was seriously ill and about to die, he told his son: After I die, you will definitely be poor. At that time, you go to see Youmeng and say that I am Sun Shuao's son. A few years later, Sun Shuao's son was indeed so poor that he had to rely on firewood to survive. Once I met Youmeng on the road, he said to Youmeng: I am Sun Shuao's son.
target: Over a century later, You Meng, a tall Chu performer, used humor to advise King Zhuang. When the king wanted to bury his beloved horse with grand rites, You Meng suggested an even grander burial to expose the king's folly. King Zhuang relented and had the horse cooked. Later, You Meng impersonated the deceased prime minister Sun Shuao to advise King Zhuang. He highlighted Sun Shuao's poverty despite his integrity, leading the king to grant Sun's son land and households for ancestral worship.

id: 史记/七十列传/滑稽列传::group-004

source: It’s really not worth being an upright official! So King Zhuang expressed his apology to You Meng, and immediately summoned Sun Shuao's son and granted him the city of Qiuqiu with 400 households for the purpose of worshiping Sun Shuao. Since then, there has been no interruption for ten generations. It can be said that Youmeng's intelligence was just right and he seized the opportunity to display it. More than two hundred years after You Meng, Qin State gave birth to You Zhan. Youzhan is a singing and dancing artist from the Qin State. He is very short. He is good at telling jokes, but they all make sense. During the reign of Qin Shihuang, a banquet was held in the palace. It was raining, and the guards standing guard under the palace steps were all wet with rain and cold. When Youzhan saw them, he felt very sorry for them and said to them: "Do you want to rest?" The guards all said: Very much so. Youzhan said: If I call you, you must answer me quickly. After a while, people in the palace toasted Qin Shihuang and shouted long live the emperor. Youzhan approached the railing and shouted loudly: Guard! The guard replied: Yes. Youzhan said: Although you are tall, what good is it? I was lucky enough to stand in the open air and get soaked in the rain. Although I am short, I am lucky enough to rest here. Therefore, Qin Shihuang allowed the guards to reduce their duty by half and take over in turns. Qin Shihuang once planned to expand the hunting area to Hangu Pass in the east and Yong County and Chencang in the west. Youzhan said: OK. Keep more animals inside. If the enemy invades from the east, it will be enough to let the elk use their horns to resist them. After hearing this, Qin Shihuang stopped his plan to expand the hunting grounds. Emperor Qin II came to the throne and wanted to paint the city walls with paint.
target: Two centuries later, You Zhan, a short Qin performer, used wit to aid others. During a rainstorm, he joked about guards being wet while he was dry, leading Qin Shihuang to halve their duty. He also dissuaded the emperor from expanding hunting grounds and Qin Ershi from painting city walls, using humor to highlight impracticality.

id: 史记/七十列传/滑稽列传::group-005

source: To accomplish this, it is easy to paint, but what is difficult is to find a big house, put the painted city wall in it, and let it dry in the shade. The second emperor laughed and canceled the plan. Soon, the second emperor was killed, Youzhan surrendered to the Han Dynasty, and died a few years later. Tai Shigong said: Chunyu Kun looked up to the sky and laughed, and King Wei of Qi followed his example throughout the world. You Meng shook his head and sang, and those who carried firewood for a living were rewarded. Youzhan leaned on the railing and shouted, so the guards holding shields under the palace steps were able to reduce their duty by half and take turns to rest. Aren’t these all great and praiseworthy! Mr. Chu Shaosun said: I am fortunate to be a doctor because I am proficient in Confucian classics. I also like to read historical biographies other than the Six Classics. I couldn't be humble and conceding, so I wrote six more chapters of funny stories and compiled them at the back of Tai Shigong's original work. It can be read and expanded, so that it can be passed on to future generations who are not afraid of troubles to read, so as to relax their minds and alert them to listen. It is specially attached to the back of the three funny stories of Tai Shigong above. During the reign of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, there was a favored artist named Guo. Although his speeches were not reasonable, he could make the emperor feel happy after listening to them. When Emperor Wu was young, the mother of Marquis Dongwu nursed him. When Emperor Wu grew up, he called her the "Big Wet Nurse". I visit the DPRK about twice a month. Every time the notification of entering the court was sent in, the imperial edict would send the favored minister Ma Youqing to reward the wet nurse with fifty pieces of silk and prepare food to support her.
target: Tai Shigong praised these three for their clever advice. Mr. Chu Shaosun added six more tales, including that of Guo Sheren, who helped a wet nurse avoid exile by prompting her to show reluctance, moving Emperor Wu to pity. Dongfang Shuo, a learned scholar, used humor to gain favor with Emperor Wu, often receiving rewards but spending them on marriages. He defended his behavior as "court reclusion" and advised against slander on his deathbed.

source: Its teeth are the same from front to back and are equal in size without big teeth, so it is called Zou fang. About a year later, King Hunxie of the Xiongnu came and surrendered to the Han Dynasty with 100,000 people. Emperor Wu then rewarded Dongfang Shuo with a lot of money. In old age. When Dongfang Shuo was dying, he advised Emperor Wu: "The Book of Songs" says that flies flying around will fall on the fence. Kind and kind gentleman, don't listen to slander. There is no end to the slander, and there is no peace for neighboring countries on all sides. I hope that your Majesty will stay away from those who flatter people with clever words and rebuke their slander. Emperor Wu said: Why do Dongfang Shuo mostly make good remarks today? Be amazed by this. Soon after, Dongfang Shuo died of illness. Ancient books say: When a bird is dying, its cry is particularly sad; when a person is dying, its words are very kind. That's what I mean. During the reign of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, General Wei Qing was the elder brother of Queen Wei and was granted the title of Marquis of Changping. He led the army to attack the Xiongnu and chased them to the Yuwu River before returning. He killed a large number of enemy soldiers and captured many prisoners. He made great achievements in battle and returned victorious. Emperor Wu ordered a reward of a thousand catties of gold. When the general came out of the palace gate, Mr. Dong Guo, a native of Qi, was waiting at the carriage house as an alchemist. He stopped General Wei's carriage and horse on the road, paid homage and said: "I have something to report to the general." General Wei stopped in front of the car, and Mr. Dong Guo said beside the car: Mrs. Wang has recently been favored by the emperor, and her family is poor. Now that the general has received a thousand catties of gold, if he uses half of it to give to Mrs. Wang's parents, the emperor will be very happy to know it. This is what is called a clever and convenient strategy. General Wei thanked him and said: Fortunately, sir, you told me this convenient strategy. I will definitely follow the advice. So General Wei used five hundred kilograms of gold as a gift to Mrs. Wang's parents. Mrs. Wang told Emperor Wu about this. Emperor Wu said: The general does not know how to do this. When Wei Qing was asked where he got the strategy, he replied: "I got it from Mr. Dongguo who was on duty." So he ordered Mr. Dongguo to be summoned and appointed him as the county captain. Mr. Dongguo has been waiting for work at the bus station for a long time. He is poor, hungry and cold. His clothes are shabby and his shoes are not intact. When walking in the snow, the shoes have sides but no soles, and the feet are all on the ground.
target: Mr. Dong Guo advised General Wei Qing to gift gold to Empress Wang's parents, earning himself an official post. Other tales include a clever envoy who lost a swan but gained rewards, a prefect coached by a drunkard to credit the emperor for peace, and Ximen Bao, who stopped the practice of sacrificing girls to the River God by throwing the corrupt priests into the river, then dug irrigation canals that benefited the people for generations.
