article_path: 史记/七十列传/田儋列传
source: Tian Dan was a native of Di County and a sibling of the Tian family, King of Qi during the Warring States Period. Tian Dan's cousin and Tian Rong's younger brother Tian Heng was a powerful figure in the local area, and his clan was strong and very popular. When Chen She began to raise troops and claim to be the King of Chu, he sent Zhou Shi to capture and pacify the Wei region, and then marched north to Di County, which was defended. Tian Dan pretended to tie up his own slave and led his young men to the county government, claiming to kill the guilty slave after meeting with the county magistrate. When they saw the magistrate of Di County, they took the opportunity to kill him, and then summoned powerful officials and young people to say: "The princes from all over the country have rebelled against Qin and established themselves. Qi is a country established in ancient times, and I, Tian Dan, am a member of Qi Wang Tian's clan and should be the king." So Tian Dan proclaimed himself King of Qi and raised troops to attack Zhou City. After Zhou Shi's army withdrew, Tian Dan took the opportunity to lead his troops eastward, seize and pacify the land of Qi. Qin general Zhang Han led his troops to besiege King Jiu of Wei in Linji. The situation was urgent, and King Wei sent people to Qi to ask for rescue. King Tian Dan of Qi led the army to rescue Wei. Zhang Han let his soldiers and horses hold the coins in their mouths at night, and took advantage of the cover of night to launch a sneak attack. He defeated the Qi and Wei coalition forces and killed Tian Dan at the foot of Linji City. Tian Dan's cousin Tian Rong gathered the remaining troops of Tian Dan and fled eastward to Dong'a. After the people of Qi heard the news that Tian Dan had died in battle, they supported Tian Jia, the younger brother of the former King of Qi Tian Jian, as King of Qi, Tian Jiao as prime minister, and Tian Jian as general, in order to resist the princes. When Tian Rong fled to Dong'a, Zhang Han pursued and intercepted him. Xiang Liang heard that Tian Rong was in critical condition, so he led his troops to Dong'a City and defeated Zhang Han in one fell swoop. Zhang Han fled to the west, while Xiang Liang took advantage of the victory to pursue him. However, Tian Rong was very angry about the fact that the Qi people made Tianjie the king of Qi, so he led his troops back and attacked and chased Qi King Tianjie. Tianjie fled to Chu State, and Prime Minister Tian Jiao fled to Zhao State. Tian Jiao's younger brother Tian Jian had gone to Zhao State for help before, so he stayed in Zhao State and did not dare to go back. Tian Rong then made Tian Dan's son Tian Shi the king of Qi and appointed himself prime minister. Tian Heng was made a general and the land of Qi was pacified. After Xiang Liang pursued Zhang Han, Zhang Han's army became increasingly powerful, so Xiang Liang sent envoys to inform Qi and Zhao, asking the two countries to jointly send troops to attack Zhang Han. Tian Rong said: If Chu kills Tianjia and Zhao kills Tianjiao and Tianjian, we will send troops. King Huai of Chu said: Tianjia is the king of our ally. He came to us when we were desperate. It is unethical to kill him. Zhao State was also unwilling to trade with Qi State by killing Tian Jiao and Tian Jian Lai. The people of Qi said: If the hand is bitten by a viper, the hand must be cut off; if the foot is bitten by the viper, the foot must be cut off. Why? Because if not, it will harm the whole body. But now Tianjia, Tianjiao, and Tianjian are not flesh and blood relatives to Chu and Zhao. Why not kill them?
target: Tian Dan, a member of the Qi royal family, proclaimed himself King of Qi during the Warring States period after killing the Di County magistrate. He raised troops but was later killed by Qin general Zhang Han at Linji. His cousin Tian Rong gathered the remnants and fled east. After Tian Dan's death, the Qi people installed Tian Jia as king, but Tian Rong, angered by this, attacked and drove Tian Jia and his ministers into exile. Tian Rong then made Tian Dan's son Tian Shi king and appointed himself prime minister, with Tian Heng as general.

id: 史记/七十列传/田儋列传::group-001
article_path: 史记/七十列传/田儋列传
source: Why? Because if not, it will harm the whole body. But now Tianjia, Tianjiao, and Tianjian are not flesh and blood relatives to Chu and Zhao. Why not kill them? Moreover, if the Qin Dynasty succeeds in conquering the world, not only will we be humiliated, but even our ancestors' graves may have to be dug up. Neither Chu nor Zhao were willing to obey Qi, and Qi was very angry and eventually refused to send troops to rescue. Zhang Han indeed defeated the Chu army and killed Xiang Liang. The Chu army fled eastward, and Zhang Han took the opportunity to cross the Yellow River and besiege Zhao's Julu. Xiang Yu went to rescue Zhao State, and therefore resented Tian Rong very much. Xiang Yu had already protected Zhao State and surrendered Zhang Han and other generals of the Qin Dynasty, so he went west to Xianyang to kill, destroyed the Qin Dynasty, and then divided the princes and kings among themselves. So he changed the title of King Qi Tianshi to King Jiaodong and ruled in Jimo. Qi general Tian Du followed Xiang Yu to rescue Zhao and then marched into Guanzhong. Therefore, Xiang Yu made Tian Du the king of Qi and ruled in Linzi. Tian An, the grandson of Tian Jian, the former Qi king, captured many cities in Jibei one after another when Xiang Yu was crossing the river to rescue Zhao, and then led his troops to surrender to Xiang Yu. Xiang Yu therefore made Tian An the king of Jibei, and his seat was Boyang. Because Tian Rong disobeyed Xiang Yu and refused to send troops to assist Chu and Zhao in attacking the Qin Dynasty, he could not be crowned king; Zhao general Chen Yu was also not crowned king because of his dereliction of duty. Both of them resented Xiang Yu. After Xiang Yu returned to Chu, the feudal princes also returned to their own fiefdoms. Tian Rong sent troops to help Chen Yu and asked him to rebel against Xiang Yu in Zhao. Tian Rong himself also sent troops to fight against Tian Du, who fled to Chu. Tian Rong detained Qi Wang Tianshi and refused to allow him to go to the administrative office of Jiaodong. Tian Shi's men said: Xiang Yu is powerful and ferocious, and as the king of Qi, you should go to your own kingdom of Jiaodong. If you don't go, there will be danger. Tian Shi was very frightened, so he ran away to Jiaodong. When Tian Rong learned about it, he was furious and led his men to chase King Qi Tianshi and killed him in Jimo. When he came back, he attacked Tian'an, the king of Jibei, and killed him. Therefore, Tian Rong proclaimed himself the king of Qi and occupied all the lands of Sanqi. After Xiang Yu heard the news, he was very angry, so he launched an army to attack Qi in the north. King Tian Rong of Qi was severely defeated and fled to Pingyuan. The people of Pingyuan killed Tian Rong. Afterwards, Xiang Yu burned and leveled the walls of Qi's capital, and massacred everyone he passed. The people of Qi couldn't bear it, so they all gathered to rebel against him. Tian Rong's younger brother Tian Heng gathered Qi's scattered soldiers and obtained tens of thousands of troops to counterattack Xiang Yu in Chengyang. At this time, Liu Bang, king of Han, led the army of the princes to defeat the Chu army and entered Pengcheng. After Xiang Yu heard the news, he let go of the Qi army and went back, launching an attack on the Han soldiers in Pengcheng. Then there were many battles with the Han army, and they were locked in a stalemate in Xingyang.
target: When Xiang Liang requested Qi's aid against Zhang Han, Tian Rong demanded the execution of the exiled Qi leaders as a condition, which Chu and Zhao refused. Qi withheld support, and Zhang Han subsequently defeated and killed Xiang Liang. Later, Xiang Yu, after defeating Qin, divided the territories, demoting Tian Shi to King of Jiaodong and installing Tian Du as King of Qi. Tian Rong, resentful at being excluded, attacked and killed Tian Du and Tian An, proclaiming himself King of Qi. Xiang Yu retaliated, defeating and killing Tian Rong. Tian Heng then gathered forces, regained Qi territory, and installed Tian Rong's son Tian Guang as king, with himself as de facto ruler.

id: 史记/七十列传/田儋列传::group-002
article_path: 史记/七十列传/田儋列传
source: King Tian Rong of Qi was severely defeated and fled to Pingyuan. The people of Pingyuan killed Tian Rong. Afterwards, Xiang Yu burned and leveled the walls of Qi's capital, and massacred everyone he passed. The people of Qi couldn't bear it, so they all gathered to rebel against him. Tian Rong's younger brother Tian Heng gathered Qi's scattered soldiers and obtained tens of thousands of troops to counterattack Xiang Yu in Chengyang. At this time, Liu Bang, king of Han, led the army of the princes to defeat the Chu army and entered Pengcheng. After Xiang Yu heard the news, he let go of the Qi army and went back, launching an attack on the Han soldiers in Pengcheng. Then there were many battles with the Han army, and they were locked in a stalemate in Xingyang. Therefore, Tian Heng was able to regain the large and small cities of Qi again, and established Tian Guang, Tian Rong's son, as the king of Qi. Tian Heng assisted him as prime minister and arbitrarily ruled the country. All political affairs, no matter how big or small, were decided by Tian Heng. Three years after Tian Heng pacified Qi, King Liu Bang of Han sent Li Shiqi to Qi to lobby Qi King Tian Guang and Prime Minister Tian Heng to submit to the Han Dynasty. Tian Heng believed that this was feasible, so he lifted Qi's defense against the Han army in Lixia. Han Xin, the general of the Han Dynasty, was going to attack Qi State eastward. At first, Qi State sent troops led by Hua Wushang and Tian Jie to station in Lixia to resist the Han army. When the Han envoys arrived, they abandoned their war preparations to defend the city, allowed the soldiers to drink, and sent envoys to make peace with the Han Dynasty. However, after the Han general Han Xin pacified Zhao and Yan, he used Kuai Tong's strategy to cross the plains and make a sudden attack, defeating the Qi garrison stationed in Lixia, and then invaded Linzi. When Qi King Tian Guang and Prime Minister Tian Heng saw the sudden appearance of the Han army, they were very angry. They thought they had been betrayed by Li Sheng and immediately cooked and killed Li Sheng. King Tian Guang of Qi fled east to Gaomi, Prime Minister Tian Heng fled to Boyang, Prime Minister Tian Guang fled to Chengyang, and General Tian Ji led the army to garrison in Jiaodong. At this time, Chu State sent Long Qie to lead the army to rescue Qi State. Qi Wang Tian Guang and Long Qie met in Gaomi. Han generals Han Xin and Cao Shen defeated the Qi-Chu coalition forces in Gaomi, killed Chu general Long Qie, and captured Qi King Tian Guang. Han general Guan Ying continued the pursuit and captured Tian Guang, the prime minister of Qi. Guan Ying continued to march and arrived at Boyang. When Tian Heng heard that King Qi Tian Guang was dead, he proclaimed himself King of Qi and turned to fight Guan Ying. Under Yingxia, Tian Heng's army was severely defeated by Guan Ying. Tian Heng fled to Liangdi and surrendered to Pengyue. At this time, Peng Yue supported the army and remained neutral between Chu and Han, as if for the king of Han and for the king of Chu. After Han Xin killed Chu General Long Qie, he ordered Cao Shen to continue marching to Jiaodong, where he defeated Tian Ji and killed him in battle. Han Xin also ordered Guan Ying to pursue Qi General Tian Sui, defeat him in Qiancheng and kill him. In this way, Han Xin pacified Qi and wrote to Liu Bang, asking him to make himself the false king of Qi. Liu Bang also took advantage of the situation and made Han Xin the king of Qi. More than a year later, Liu Bang, king of Han, destroyed Xiang Yu, proclaimed himself emperor, and made Pengyue King of Liang.
target: Years later, Han king Liu Bang sent Li Shiqi to negotiate Qi's submission. Tian Heng agreed and lifted defenses, but Han general Han Xin launched a surprise attack, capturing Linzi. Believing Li Shiqi had betrayed them, Tian Guang and Tian Heng executed him. Han forces defeated Qi and Chu allies, killing General Long Qie and capturing Tian Guang. Tian Heng then proclaimed himself king but was defeated by Han forces and fled to Liang. After Liu Bang became emperor, Tian Heng, fearing execution, fled to an island with 500 followers. Summoned by the emperor, Tian Heng committed suicide near Luoyang, ashamed to serve under Liu Bang after having killed Li Shiqi.

id: 史记/七十列传/田儋列传::group-003
article_path: 史记/七十列传/田儋列传
source: When the envoy came back to report, Emperor Gaozu immediately issued an edict to Weiwei Li Shang: King Tian Heng of Qi is about to arrive in Beijing. Anyone who dares to touch his entourage will be executed immediately! Then he sent an envoy with a talisman to inform Tian Heng of the imperial edict issued by the emperor to tell Li Shang's situation exactly as it was. He also said: "If Tian Heng comes to Beijing, the largest one can be made a king and the smallest one can be made a marquis; if he does not come, an army will be sent to kill him." Tian Heng and his two retainers took the stage carriage to Luoyang.
target: His two retainers and later the 500 followers also died, demonstrating his ability to inspire loyalty.

id: 史记/七十列传/田儋列传::group-004
article_path: 史记/七十列传/田儋列传
source: Thirty miles away from Luoyang, there is a place called Corpse Township. On this day, Tian Heng and others came to this inn. Tian Heng said to the Han envoy: As a human minister, you should take a refreshing bath before paying homage to the emperor. So he stayed. Tian Heng said to his disciples: At first, I, Tian Heng, and the King of Han were both lonely kings in the south. But now that the King of Han has become the emperor, I, Tian Heng, have become a slave of the subjugated country. It would be a great shame to have to serve him in the north. What's more, I killed someone's elder brother and then served the same master side by side with his younger brother. Even though he was afraid of the emperor's order and did not dare to touch me, wouldn't I feel ashamed in my heart?
target: The historian Sima Qian praised Tian Heng's virtue, noting that despite his death, no painter has depicted his story.

id: 史记/七十列传/白起王翦列传::group-000
article_path: 史记/七十列传/白起王翦列传
source: In this year, Ranghou served as the prime minister of Qin. He appointed Ren Bi as the governor of Hanzhong County. The next year, Bai Qi was granted the title Zuogeng, attacked the allied forces of Han and Wei, fought in Yique, killed 240,000 enemies, captured their general Gongsun happy, and captured five cities. Bai Qi was promoted to captain of the country. He led his troops across the Yellow River and captured a large area of ​​land east of Anyi in South Korea up to Wadi River. In the third year, Bai Qi was granted the title of Daliangzao again. Defeated the Wei army and captured sixty-one cities, large and small. In the fourth year, Bai Qi and Ke Qing attacked Yuan City by mistake and captured it immediately. In the fifth year after that, Bai Qi attacked Zhao and captured Guanglang City. In the seventh year after this, Bai Qi attacked Chu and occupied five cities including Yan and Deng. The next year, he attacked Chu again, captured Ying, the capital of Chu, burned the tombs of the Chu kings, and headed east to Jingling. The king of Chu fled the capital of Ying and fled eastward, moving his capital to Chen. The Qin State established Yingdi as Nanjun. Bai Qi was named Lord Wu'an. He took advantage of the situation to attack Chu and pacified Wu and Qianzhong counties. In the thirty-fourth year of King Zhao, Bai Qi attacked Wei and captured Huayang, causing Mangmao to flee. He also captured the generals of Zhao and Wei and killed 130,000 enemies. At that time, Bai Qi fought with Zhao's general Jia Yan and sank 20,000 Zhao soldiers into the Yellow River. In the forty-third year of King Zhao, Bai Qi attacked Xingcheng in South Korea, captured five cities, and killed 50,000 enemies. In the forty-fourth year, Bai Qi attacked Nanyang Taihang Road in South Korea and blocked this passage. In the forty-fifth year of King Zhao, Bai Qi sent troops to attack the Yewang City in South Korea. The Yewang surrendered, cutting off the connection between Shangdang County in South Korea and South Korea. Feng Ting, the governor of Shangdang County, planned with the people and said: The road to the capital Zheng is cut off, and South Korea will definitely not be able to control us. The Qin army is advancing day by day, and South Korea cannot rescue it, so it is better to surrender Shangdang to Zhao. If Zhao State accepts us, Qin State will be angry and will definitely attack Zhao State. Zhao State was attacked by force and must be close to South Korea. If Han and Zhao unite, they can resist Qin. So he sent someone to inform Zhao State. King Zhao Xiaocheng studied this matter with Pingyang Jun and Pingyuan Jun. Pingyang Jun said: It is better not to accept it. The consequences of accepting it will be far greater than the benefits. Lord Pingyuan expressed his dissent and said: "I got a county for nothing, it would be beneficial to accept it." As a result, King Zhao accepted Shangdang and named Feng Ting Lord of Huayang. In the forty-sixth year of King Zhao, the Qin State captured Goushi and Linyi in South Korea. In the forty-seventh year of King Zhao, the State of Qin sent Wang Lu, the chief of the left concubine, to attack South Korea and capture Shangdang. The people of Shangdang fled to Zhao State one after another. The State of Zhao stationed troops in Changping to support the people of Shangdang. In April, Wang Lu used this opportunity to attack Zhao. The State of Zhao sent Lian Po to lead the army.
target: Bai Qi, a skilled military commander from Yidi, served King Zhao of Qin. His early campaigns included victories against Han, Wei, and Zhao, capturing cities and killing tens of thousands of enemies. He was promoted through ranks, eventually becoming Lord Wu'an after conquering Chu's capital Ying and burning its royal tombs. His most notable battle was against Zhao at Changping in the 47th year of King Zhao's reign. After initial setbacks, Zhao replaced General Lian Po with Zhao Kuo. Bai Qi used deception, cutting off Zhao's supply lines and surrounding their army. After 46 days without food, Zhao Kuo was killed, and 400,000 Zhao soldiers surrendered. Bai Qi, fearing rebellion, ordered them buried alive, shocking Zhao. Following this, Qin planned to besiege Handan, but Su Dai, sent by Han and Zhao, persuaded Prime Minister Yinghou to halt, arguing that Bai Qi's growing fame threatened Yinghou's position. King Zhao agreed to a truce, but Bai Qi's resentment toward Yinghou grew. When Qin later attacked Handan under Wang Ling, Bai Qi refused to lead, citing the army's exhaustion and the risk of allied reinforcements. Despite King Zhao's orders, Bai Qi feigned illness. After Qin's defeat, Bai Qi's remarks angered the king, who demoted him and ordered his exile. Accused of discontent, Bai Qi was forced to commit suicide in the 50th year of King Zhao's reign.

id: 史记/七十列传/白起王翦列传::group-001
article_path: 史记/七十列传/白起王翦列传
source: Lord Wu'an died innocently, and the people of Qin sympathized with him, so they worshiped him in both urban and rural areas. Wang Jian was from Dongxiang, Pinyang. He was fond of military affairs when he was young, and later served Qin Shihuang. In the eleventh year of the First Emperor's reign, Wang Jian led troops to attack Yanyu of Zhao State. Not only did he capture it, but he also captured nine cities in a row. In the eighteenth year of the First Emperor's reign, Wang Jian led troops to attack Zhao. In just over a year, the State of Zhao was captured, King Zhao surrendered, and all parts of the State of Zhao were pacified and set up as counties. The next year, the State of Yan sent Jing Ke to the State of Qin to murder the King of Qin, and the King of Qin sent Wang Jian to attack the State of Yan. King Yan fled to Liaodong, and Wang Jian finally pacified Ji, the capital of Yan State, and returned victorious. The King of Qin sent Wang Jian's son Wang Ben to attack Chu, but the Chu army was defeated. He turned around and attacked Wei again. The king of Wei surrendered, and finally all parts of Wei were pacified. Qin Shihuang destroyed the three kingdoms of Han, Zhao, and Wei, drove away King Xi of Yan, and defeated the Chu army many times. Qin general Li Xin was young, energetic, brave and mighty. He once led thousands of soldiers to pursue Prince Dan of Yan to Yanshui, and finally defeated the Yan army and captured Prince Dan. Qin Shihuang believed that Li Xinxian was brave. One day, Qin Shihuang asked Li Xin: I plan to attack Chu State. How many people do you think the general can mobilize? Li Xin replied: No more than 200,000 people. Qin Shihuang asked Wang Jian again, and Wang Jian replied: "We must have 600,000 people." Qin Shihuang said: General Wang, how cowardly you are! General Lee was really decisive and brave, and what he said was right. So he sent Li Xin and Meng Tian to march south with 200,000 troops to attack Chu. Wang Jian's words were not accepted, so he excused himself from illness and returned to his hometown in Pinyang for retirement. Li Xin attacked Pingyu, and Meng Tian attacked Xinyi, defeating the Chu army. Li Xin then attacked Yanying and captured it again, so he led his troops to move west to meet Meng Tian at Chengfu. In fact, the Chu army was tracking and pursuing them for three days and three nights. As a result, they defeated Li Xin's troops, invaded two military camps, and killed seven captains. The Qin army was defeated and fled. When Qin Shihuang heard the news, he was furious and rushed to Pinyang by express train. When he saw Wang Jian, he apologized and said: Because I did not adopt your strategy, Li Xin really brought shame to the Qin army. Now I heard that the Chu army is advancing westward every day. Although the general is sick, can he have the heart to abandon me? Wang Jian declined and said: "The old minister is sick, tired, faint and incompetent. I hope the king will choose another good general." Qin Shihuang apologized again and said, "Okay, general, don't say anything more!" Wang Jian said: Your Majesty must appoint me, and you must have 600,000 people. Qin Shihuang said: Just follow the general's advice. So Wang Jian set off with an army of 600,000 men, and Qin Shihuang personally went to Bashang to see him off. When Wang Jian set out, he asked for many fertile fields, beautiful houses, gardens, ponds, etc. Qin Shihuang said: Although the general is on the road, why should he worry about the hard life at home?
target: Wang Jian, from Pinyang, served Qin Shihuang. He conquered Zhao, Yan, and other states, often requesting 600,000 troops for campaigns. After Li Xin's failed attack on Chu with 200,000 men, Wang Jian was recalled. He led 600,000 troops, avoided direct engagement, and waited for Chu's army to weaken before striking, defeating them and capturing King Chu. Wang Jian's son Wang Ben and Li Xin later conquered Yan and Qi, unifying China. Wang Jian's grandson Wang Li, a third-generation general, was captured by Xiang Yu during Chen Sheng's rebellion, fulfilling a saying that general families often fail by the third generation due to accumulated killings.

id: 史记/七十列传/白起王翦列传::group-002
article_path: 史记/七十列传/白起王翦列传
source: Soon after, Xiang Yu rescued Zhao and attacked the Qin army. As expected, Wang Li was captured, and Wang Li's army surrendered to the princes' army. Tai Shigong said: As the saying goes, sometimes a ruler is short and an inch is sometimes long. Bai Qi's scheming against his enemies was famous for his ability to adapt to changing circumstances, endless tricks, wonderful changes, and fame throughout the world. However, he was unable to deal with the disasters Yinghou created for him. As a general of the Qin State, Wang Jian had outstanding achievements in pacifying the six kingdoms. He was worthy of being a veteran general at the time, and Qin Shihuang respected him as his teacher. However, he could not assist Qin Shihuang in establishing a moral government to consolidate the foundation of the country, but he only catered to and pleased his master until his death.
target: Sima Qian noted Bai Qi's strategic brilliance but inability to avoid Yinghou's schemes, and Wang Jian's military success but failure to promote moral governance, leading to his grandson's capture.

id: 史记/七十列传/管晏列传::group-000
article_path: 史记/七十列传/管晏列传
source: Guan Zhong, whose name was Yiwu, was from Yingshang. When he was young, he often interacted with Bao Shuya, and Bao Shuya knew that he was wise and talented. Guan Zhong's family was poor and he often took advantage of Bao Shuya, but Bao Shuya was always very kind to Guan Zhong and had no complaints because of these things. Soon, Bao Shuya served the young master Xiaobai of Qi State, and Guan Zhong served the young master Jiu. After Xiaobai came to the throne and was established as Duke Huan of Qi, Duke Huan asked the state of Lu to kill Prince Jiu and Guan Zhong was imprisoned. So Bao Shuya recommended Guan Zhong to Duke Huan of Qi. After Guan Zhong was appointed, he came to power in Qi. Duke Huan relied on Guan Zhong to dominate, and as the overlord, he united with the princes many times to bring the world into unity. This was all achieved through Guan Zhong's wisdom. Guan Zhong said: When I was poor, I used to do business together with Bao Shuya. When we shared the profits, I always asked for more. Bao Shuya did not think that I was greedy for money. He knew that my family was poor. I once planned things for Bao Shuya, but it made him even more difficult and embarrassed. Bao Shuya didn't think I was stupid, because he knew that there were good times and bad times in fortune. I had served as an official many times and was expelled by the king many times. Bao Shuya did not think that I had no talent. He knew that I had not met a good opportunity. I have run away from many battles. Bao Shuya doesn't think I'm timid. He knows that I have an old mother at home who needs support. Prince Jiu failed in the struggle for the throne of the king, Zhaohu died for him, and I was imprisoned and suffered humiliation. Bao Shuya did not think that I was a shameless person, because he knew that I was not ashamed of small mistakes, but felt ashamed of not being famous in the world. It was my parents who gave birth to me, and it was Bao Shuya who really understood me. After Bao Shuya recommended Guan Zhong, he was willing to work under Guan Zhong. His descendants have enjoyed salaries in Qi for generations, and more than a dozen generations have received fiefs, most of whom are famous officials. Therefore, people in the world did not praise Guan Zhong's talents, but praised Bao Shuya for his ability to recognize talents. After Guan Zhong became the Prime Minister of Qi, he relied on the conditions of the small Qi State on the seaside to circulate goods and accumulate wealth, making the country rich and powerful, and sharing the same likes and dislikes with the people. Therefore, he said in his book "Guanzi": Only when the warehouses are full of food can the people understand etiquette; when food and clothing are abundant, can the people distinguish between honor and disgrace; only when the king's actions are in line with the law can the six relatives be stable; if etiquette, justice and integrity are not promoted and carried forward, the country will perish.
target: Guan Zhong, also known as Yiwu, was from Yingshang. In his youth, he frequently interacted with Bao Shuya, who recognized his wisdom and talent. Despite Guan Zhong's poverty and tendency to take advantage of him, Bao Shuya remained kind and without complaint. Bao Shuya later served Prince Xiaobai of Qi, while Guan Zhong served Prince Jiu. After Xiaobai became Duke Huan of Qi, he had Prince Jiu killed and imprisoned Guan Zhong. Bao Shuya then recommended Guan Zhong to Duke Huan. Appointed to power, Guan Zhong helped Duke Huan become an overlord, uniting the princes and bringing order to the realm through his wisdom. Guan Zhong reflected that Bao Shuya never judged him harshly: when Guan Zhong took more profit in their business, Bao Shuya understood his poverty; when his plans failed, Bao Shuya knew fortune's ups and downs; when he was dismissed from office, Bao Shuya saw missed opportunities; when he fled battles, Bao Shuya recognized his duty to his mother; when he endured imprisonment, Bao Shuya knew he valued fame over minor shame. Guan Zhong declared, "My parents gave me life, but Bao Shuya truly understands me." After recommending Guan Zhong, Bao Shuya served under him. Their descendants received fiefs for generations, producing many famous officials. The world praised Bao Shuya's ability to recognize talent over Guan Zhong's abilities. As Prime Minister, Guan Zhong enriched Qi by circulating goods and accumulating wealth, aligning with the people's desires. He wrote that ample food leads to understanding etiquette, and abundant clothing allows distinction between honor and disgrace.

id: 史记/七十列传/管晏列传::group-001
article_path: 史记/七十列传/管晏列传
source: Government decrees issued by the state are like the source of flowing water, flowing down the minds of the people. Therefore, government orders can be easily implemented if they are consistent with the situation. Whatever the people want, give it to them; whatever the people object to, abolish it. When Guan Zhong was in power, he was good at turning disaster into good fortune and failure into success. He pays attention to the priorities of things and carefully weighs the pros and cons of things. Duke Huan of Qi actually resented Shaoji's remarriage and wanted to attack Cai. Guan Zhong took this opportunity to attack Chu and blamed it for not paying tribute to the Zhou royal family. Duke Huan actually wanted to send troops to the north to attack Shanrong, but Guan Zhong took the opportunity to let Yan rebuild the political and religious system of the Zhaogong period. During the alliance meeting at Ke, Duke Huan wanted to break the treaty that Cao Mo had forced him to make, but Guan Zhong followed the situation and persuaded him to abide by the treaty, and the princes therefore submitted to Qi. Therefore, it is said: Knowing that giving is just for getting, this is the magic weapon for governing the country. Guan Zhong's wealth was comparable to that of the monarch, and he had a gorgeous Sangui Terrace and banquet facilities for the monarch, but the people of Qi did not think that he was extravagant and arrogant. After Guan Zhong's death, Qi still followed his policies and was often stronger than other vassal states. More than a hundred years later, Yan Ying came out of Qi State. Yan Pingzhong, named Ying, was a Yiwei native of Lai, Qi State. He assisted three generations of Qi Dukes Linggong, Zhuanggong and Jinggong. He was respected by people in Qi because of his frugality and hard work. When he became the prime minister of Qi, he did not eat more than two kinds of meat at each meal, and his wives and concubines did not wear silk clothes.
target: He emphasized that government decrees should flow like water, easily implemented when consistent with circumstances. He turned disaster into fortune and failure into success, such as using Duke Huan's desire to attack Cai as an opportunity to blame Chu for not paying tribute to Zhou, or persuading Duke Huan to honor a treaty at Ke, winning the princes' submission. Guan Zhong's wealth rivaled a monarch's, but the people did not consider him extravagant. After his death, Qi followed his policies and remained strong. More than a century later, Yan Ying, also known as Yanzi, emerged from Qi. He served Dukes Ling, Zhuang, and Jing, respected for his frugality and hard work. As prime minister, he ate no more than two meats and his family wore no silk. He acted honestly in court and followed orders when the ruler was righteous.

id: 史记/七十列传/管晏列传::group-002
article_path: 史记/七十列传/管晏列传
source: In the court, if the king's words involve him, he should express his opinions honestly; if the king's words do not involve him, he should act honestly. If the king can do the right thing, he should follow his orders. If he can't do the right way, he can act according to his orders. Therefore, during the three generations of Qi Linggong, Zhuanggong and Jinggong, his reputation was well-known among the princes of various countries. Yue Shi's father is a talented man who is being imprisoned and serving hard labor. Yanzi went out and met him on the road. He untied the horse on the left side of the carriage, ransomed him, and then drove him home. After leaving Taoism, Yan Zi went into the inner room without saying goodbye to Yue Shi's father. After a long time, Yue Shi's father asked to break off the relationship with Yan Zi. Yanzi was shocked, and hurriedly packed his clothes and apologized, saying: Even though I can't be said to be kind and generous, I finally helped you get out of your predicament. Why did you ask to break off the relationship so quickly? Father Yue Shi said: That's not the case. I heard that a gentleman will be wronged by people who don't understand him, but his will will be upheld in front of people who understand him. When I was in captivity, those people didn't understand me. Since you have been moved and awakened, and bought me out, this means you understand me; if you understand me but do not treat me politely, it is better to let me continue to be imprisoned and serve as a slave. So Yanzi invited him into the house and treated him as an honored guest. When Yanzi was the prime minister of Qi, he was going out in a carriage. The coachman's wife secretly looked at her husband through the crack in the door. He saw his husband driving the car for the prime minister, with a big umbrella covering his head, waving a whip and driving four horses, looking very proud and proud. Soon after returning home, his wife asked to leave him. The coachman asked her why she left. The wife said: Yanzi was only six feet tall, but he became the prime minister of Qi State and his reputation was famous in various countries. I saw that when he went out, his ambitions and thoughts were very deep, and he often had the attitude of being inferior to others. Now you are eight feet tall and can only be a coachman. Judging from your expression, you think you are quite satisfied, so I beg you to let me leave. From then on, the coachman became humble and respectful. Yanzi noticed his change and felt strange, so he asked him about it, and the driver told him the truth. Yanzi recommended him to become a doctor. Tai Shigong said: I have read Guan Zhong's "Herdsmen", "High Mountains", "Riding Horses", "Light and Heavy", "Jiufu" and "Yanzi Chunqiu". These books are really written in too much detail! After reading their works, I also wanted people to know about their deeds, so I wrote biographies for them in turn. As for their works, there are already many in the society, so I will not discuss them here, but only record their unknown things. Guan Zhong is what the world calls a virtuous minister, but Confucius despises him. Is it because the Zhou Dynasty's rule is declining? Since Huan Gong is a virtuous minister, Guan Zhong does not encourage him to practice the royal way but assists him to become the overlord? An old saying goes: It is necessary to take advantage of the situation to help cultivate a gentleman's virtues and correct his mistakes, so that the monarch, his ministers and the people can be close to each other. This is probably Guan Zhong, right? When Yan Zi lay on the body of Duke Zhuang and cried bitterly, completed the etiquette and then left, was it a sign that people said that if you don't do something just when you encounter something just, you have no courage? As for Yanzi who spoke out and dared to offend the majesty of the monarch, this is what people call a person who thinks of being loyal when advancing and thinks of making up for his mistakes when retreating!
target: Yanzi once ransomed Yue Shi's father from imprisonment. When Yue Shi's father criticized Yanzi for not treating him politely after understanding him, Yanzi apologized and honored him as a guest. Yanzi's coachman, initially proud, became humble after his wife threatened to leave him for his arrogance compared to Yanzi's modesty. Yanzi recommended the coachman to become a doctor. Tai Shigong noted that he read Guan Zhong's and Yanzi's works but focused on their unknown deeds. He questioned whether Confucius despised Guan Zhong for not encouraging Duke Huan to practice the kingly way, instead assisting him as an overlord. He praised Yanzi for crying over Duke Zhuang's body and daring to offend the monarch, expressing a wish to serve Yanzi if he were alive.

id: 史记/七十列传/老子韩非列传::group-000
article_path: 史记/七十列传/老子韩非列传
source: I am a native of Qurenli, Li Township, Kuxian County, Chu State. His surname was Li, his given name was Er, and his courtesy name was Dan. He was a historian in charge of the library in the Zhou Dynasty. Confucius went to the capital of Zhou and wanted to ask Laozi about etiquette. Lao Tzu said: The etiquette you are talking about, the person and the bones of the person who advocated it have rotted away, only his words remain. Moreover, a gentleman will drive his car and go out to be an official when his fortune comes. If he is born at the wrong time, he will be blown away by the wind like a fluffy grass. I have heard that people who are good at business hide their goods as if they were nothing. A gentleman has a noble character, but his appearance is as humble as a dull person. Abandon your arrogance and excessive desires, abandon your artificial moods and unrealistic ambitions, these are not good for yourself. That's all I can tell you. After Confucius left, he said to his disciples: I know birds are good at flying; fish, I know they are good at swimming; animals, I know they are good at running. Those that can run can weave a net to catch it, those that can swim can be made into silk thread to catch it, and those that can fly can shoot it with arrows. As for the dragon, I don't know what to do. It is said that it rides the wind and soars into the sky. The Lao Tzu I saw today probably looks like a dragon! Lao Tzu studied moral knowledge, and his teachings aimed at concealing traces and not seeking to be heard. He lived in Zhoudu for a long time. Seeing that the Zhou Dynasty was declining, he left Zhoudu. When he arrived at Hangu Pass, Guan Ling Yinxi said to him: You are going to live in seclusion and try your best to write a book for us. So I wrote a book, divided into two parts, expounding the original meaning of morality, with a total of more than 5,000 words. Then I left. No one knows where he went in the end. Some people say: Lao Laizi was also from the Chu state. He wrote fifteen books on how to apply Taoist knowledge. He was a contemporary of Confucius. It is said that I lived for more than 160 years, and some people say that I lived for more than 200 years. This is because he can cultivate his mind and live a long life. One hundred and twenty-nine years after the death of Confucius, historical records record that when Taishi Dan of Zhou met with Duke Xiang of Qin, he prophesied: When the Qin State and the Zhou Dynasty were united, they were united for five hundred years and then separated. After seventy years of separation, there will be people who will become kings and hegemons. Some people say that Taishi Dan is Lao Tzu, and some people say that he is not. No one in the world knows which statement is correct. In short, I am a true hidden gentleman. Lao Tzu's son is called Li Zong. He served as a general of Wei State and his fiefdom was in Duanqian. Li Zong's son is called Li Zhu, Li Zhu's son is called Li Gong, and Li Gong's great-great-grandson is called Li Jie. Li Jie served as an official during the reign of Emperor Wen of Han Dynasty. Li Jie's son Li Jie served as the Taifu of Jiaoxi King Liu Xuan, so the Li family settled in Qidi. Anyone in the world who studies Laozi's knowledge will disparage Confucian thought and doctrine; and those who study Confucianism will also disparage Laozi's doctrine. People with different opinions cannot agree with each other. Is this the case?
target: A biographical account of Laozi, a native of Chu State who served as a Zhou dynasty librarian. When Confucius sought his advice on etiquette, Laozi dismissed the topic, noting that its proponents had long since perished, and advised Confucius to abandon arrogance and excessive desires. Confucius later likened Laozi to a dragon, elusive and transcendent. Laozi, observing Zhou's decline, wrote a book of over 5,000 words on morality at the request of a gatekeeper before disappearing. Some claim he lived over 160 years, while others identify him with the historian Taishi Dan, who prophesied about Qin and Zhou's future. Laozi's son, Li Zong, became a Wei general, and his descendants served in Han times. The text contrasts Laozi's philosophy of non-action with Confucianism, noting mutual criticism between followers.

id: 史记/七十列传/老子韩非列传::group-001
article_path: 史记/七十列传/老子韩非列传
source: Li Zong's son is called Li Zhu, Li Zhu's son is called Li Gong, and Li Gong's great-great-grandson is called Li Jie. Li Jie served as an official during the reign of Emperor Wen of Han Dynasty. Li Jie's son Li Jie served as the Taifu of Jiaoxi King Liu Xuan, so the Li family settled in Qidi. Anyone in the world who studies Laozi's knowledge will disparage Confucian thought and doctrine; and those who study Confucianism will also disparage Laozi's doctrine. People with different opinions cannot agree with each other. Is this the case? Lao Tzu believes that if you govern by doing nothing, the people will naturally become corrupt; if you are quiet and do nothing, the people will naturally return to righteousness. Zhuangzi was a native of Mengyi, and his name was Zhuangzhou. He once served as a minor official in Mengdi Lacquer Garden, and was a contemporary of King Hui of Liang and King Xuan of Qi. source: He lobbied the princes and wanted to serve the king of Wei, but his family was very poor and had no way to raise funds, so he first went to serve Xu Jia, a senior official in the state of Wei. Once, Xu Jia went to Qi State as an envoy for King Zhao of Wei, and Fan Ju also went with him. They stayed in Qi for several months, but were unable to complete their mission. At that time, King Qi Xiang learned that Fan Ju was very eloquent, so he sent a special person to give Fan Ju gifts such as ten pounds of gold, beef and wine, but Fan Ju repeatedly refused and did not dare to accept. When Xu Jia found out about this, he was very angry. He thought that Fan Ju must have sold the secrets he knew about Wei to Qi, so he got such a gift. So he asked Fan Ju to accept food such as beef, wine, and return the gold. After returning to the state of Wei, Xu Jia was angry and jealous of Fan Ju, so he reported the matter to the prime minister of the state of Wei. The prime minister of Wei State is one of the sons of Wei State, named Wei Qi. Wei Qi was furious after hearing this, and ordered his ministers to beat Fan Ju with boards and thorns, breaking Fan Ju's ribs and teeth. At that time, Fan Ju pretended to be dead, so Wei Qi sent someone to roll him up in a mat and threw him in the toilet. He also made the guests at the banquet drunk and took turns urinating on Fan Ju, deliberately humiliating him to punish the police and prevent people from revealing state secrets. Fan Ju, who was wrapped in the mat, said to the guard: "If you let me go, I will thank you very much in the future." The guard wanted to let Fan Ju go, so he asked Wei Qi for instructions to throw the dead people out of the mat. Wei Qi was already very drunk at this time, so he agreed smoothly and said: "Okay." Fan Ju was able to escape. Later Wei Qi regretted it and sent people to search for Fan Ju again. Zheng Anping, a native of Wei, heard about this, so he ran away with Fan Ju. They hid, and Fan Ju changed his name to Zhang Lu. At this time, King Zhao of Qin sent his envoy Wang Jizheng to Wei. Zheng Anping pretended to be a servant and served Wang Ji.
target: Fan Ju, a man of eloquence, initially sought to serve the King of Wei but was too poor to fund his journey. He first served under Xu Jia, a senior official in Wei. When Xu Jia was sent as an envoy to Qi, Fan Ju accompanied him. King Qi Xiang, impressed by Fan Ju's eloquence, sent him gifts of gold, beef, and wine, which Fan Ju refused. Xu Jia suspected Fan Ju had betrayed Wei secrets to Qi and reported this to the Wei prime minister, Wei Qi. Wei Qi had Fan Ju beaten severely, breaking his ribs and teeth, then wrapped him in a mat and threw him in a toilet, where drunken guests urinated on him. Fan Ju convinced a guard to let him escape, and later hid with the help of Zheng Anping, changing his name to Zhang Lu.

source: Wang Ji asked him: "Would any of the talented people in Wei State be willing to travel with me to the Qin State in the west?" Zheng Anping replied: There is a Mr. Zhang Lu in my hometown who would like to see you and discuss world affairs with you. However, he has enemies and dare not come out to meet you during the day. Wang Ji said: You should come with him at night. Zheng Anping brought Zhang Lu to visit Wang Ji at night. Before the two of them finished talking, Wang Ji realized that Fan Ju was a talented person, so he said to him: Sir, please wait for me south of Santang Gang. Fan Ju and Wang Ji made a private appointment to meet and left. After Wang Ji said goodbye to Wei and went on the road, when he passed the south of Sanding Gang, he loaded up Fan Ju and quickly entered the border of Qin. When the car arrived at Huyi, we saw a group of carriages and horses galloping from the west. Fan Ju asked: "Who is coming over there?" Wang Ji replied: That was when Ranghou, the Prime Minister of Qin State, went to the east to inspect the counties and cities. As soon as Fan Ju heard that it was Ranghou, he said: I heard that Ranghou has monopolized the power of the Qin State. He hates accepting lobbyists from various countries. I am afraid that such a meeting will insult me. I would rather hide in the car for a while. After a while, Marquis Rang arrived as expected. After greeting Wang Ji, he stopped the car and asked, "How has the situation in Guandong changed?" Wang Ji replied: No. Marquis Rang said to Wang Ji again: "Isn't it possible that the envoy came to Qin with the lobbyists from the princes?" Such people are not good to Qin and will only disturb other people's countries. Wang Ji quickly replied: "I don't dare." The two then said goodbye and left. Fan Ju said to Wang Ji: I heard that Ranghou is a wise man and has many doubts about how to deal with things. Just now he suspected that there was someone hiding in the car, but he forgot to search it. So Fan Ju jumped out of the car and walked on foot, saying: "Ranghou will not let this matter go. He will regret not searching the car." After walking for about ten miles, Marquis Rang sent cavalry to chase and search the car. No one was found, so he gave up. Wang Ji then entered Xianyang City with Fan Ju. After Wang Ji reported the envoy situation to the King of Qin, he took the opportunity to say: There is a Mr. Zhang Lu in Wei State. This man is a rare eloquent person in the world. He said that King Qin's country is in danger, just like stacking eggs one on top of another. If King Qin can get and reuse me, it will make the country safe. But he needed to be interviewed in person and could not be conveyed by letter, so I brought him to Qin. The King of Qin did not believe what Fan Ju said, so he only let Fan Ju live in a guest house and gave him poor food. In this way, Fan Ju waited for more than a year to be received by King Qin. At that time, King Qin Zhao had been on the throne for thirty-six years. The State of Qin captured the important towns of Yan and Ying of the State of Chu in the south. King Huai of Chu was imprisoned in the State of Qin and finally died in the State of Qin. He conquered Qi in the east. Previously, King Qi Min once called himself the Eastern Emperor, but soon canceled this title. Qin also besieged Han, Zhao and Wei many times and expanded its territory. King Zhao of Qin was a man of great martial arts, so he hated those lobbyists and did not believe what they said. Ranghou and Huayangjun are the younger brothers of King Zhao's mother, Queen Mother Xuan, while Lord Jingyang and Lord Gaoling are both brothers of King Zhao. Marquis Rang served as the prime minister, and Lord Huayang, Lord Jingyang, and Lord Gaoling served as generals. They all had their own fiefdoms. Due to the protection of Queen Mother Xuan, their private wealth even exceeded that of the country.

On the way, they encountered Marquis Rang, the powerful Qin prime minister, but Fan Ju hid to avoid detection. Once in Qin, Wang Ji recommended Fan Ju to King Zhao, but the king was skeptical and housed Fan Ju poorly for over a year. During this time, Qin had expanded its territory significantly, but the king distrusted lobbyists. Marquis Rang and other relatives of the queen mother held immense power, with private wealth exceeding the state's.

source: A wise doctor can know the life and death of his patients, and a wise monarch can discern the success or failure of state affairs. source: Fan Ju knew that he could not escape the blame, so he knelt on the straw mat and begged for punishment. According to the laws of the State of Qin, if an official is recommended and the recommended official commits a crime, then the recommender will also be punished according to the crime of the recommended official. In this way, Fan Ju should be sentenced to the crime of arresting his father, mother, and wife. However, King Qin Zhao was worried about hurting Fan Ju's feelings, so he ordered that anyone in the capital who dared to discuss Zheng Anping's affairs would be punished according to Zheng Anping's crimes. At the same time, Fan Ju, the prime minister, was rewarded with richer food to make Fan Ju feel at ease. In the next two years, Wang Ji served as the governor of Hedong County. Later, one day, King Zhao of Qin kept sighing when he went to court. Fan Ju stepped forward and said: I heard that it is a shame for the ministers to worry about the monarch, and it is a capital crime for the ministers to be humiliated. Today, the king is so worried about government affairs. I beg to be punished for my crime. King Zhao said: I heard that Chu’s iron swords are sharp but their singing and dancing skills are poor. If the country's iron sword is sharp, its soldiers will be brave; if its singing and dancing skills are poor, its monarch's plans will be far-reaching. Commanding brave soldiers with far-reaching strategies in mind, I am worried that Chu is planning how to attack Qin. If you don't prepare in advance, you won't be able to cope with sudden changes. King Zhao of Qin said this to inspire and encourage Fan Ju. But Fan Ju felt frightened after hearing this and couldn't think of anything to do. I heard that saints are not judged by their appearance, so I am probably talking about Mr. Cai Ze knew that Tang Ju was joking with him, so he said, "I already have wealth. Cai Ze smiled and expressed his gratitude and walked away. source: Meng Tian, ​​his ancestor was from Qi State. Meng Tian's grandfather, Meng Ao, came to Qin from Qi to serve King Qin Zhao, and became a high official. In the first year of King Zhuangxiang of Qin, Meng Ao served as the general of the Qin State, attacked South Korea, occupied Chenggao and Xingyang, and established Sanchuan County. In the second year of King Zhuang Xiang's reign, Meng Ao attacked Zhao and captured thirty-seven cities. In the third year of Qin Shihuang's reign, Meng Ao attacked South Korea and captured thirteen cities. In the fifth year of the First Emperor's reign, Meng Ao attacked Wei, captured twenty cities, and established Dongjun. In the seventh year of the First Emperor's reign, Meng Ao passed away. Meng Ao's son was named Meng Wu, and Meng Wu's son was named Meng Tian. Meng Tian once worked in prison litigation records and was responsible for managing relevant documents and prison litigation files. In the 23rd year of the First Emperor of Qin, Meng Wu served as a general of the Qin State. He and Wang Jian attacked the Chu State, defeated the Chu army and killed Xiang Yan. In the twenty-fourth year of the First Emperor's reign, Meng Wu attacked Chu State again and captured the King of Chu. Meng Tian's younger brother is called Meng Yi. In the twenty-sixth year of the First Emperor of Qin, Meng Tian became a general of the Qin State because of his background. He led his troops to attack the Qi State and defeated the Qi army. He was given the official position of internal history. After the Qin State annexed the world, it sent Meng Tian to lead a huge army of 300,000 people to drive away the Rong and Di to the north and recover the land south of the Yellow River. The Great Wall was built, taking advantage of the geographical situation, and setting up fortresses, stretching from Lintao in the west to Liaodong in the east, stretching for more than 10,000 miles. So he crossed the Yellow River, occupied Yangshan Mountain, and extended zigzag to the north. In the scorching sun, frost, wind and rain, I have been stationed in Shangjun for more than ten years. At this time, Meng Tian's reputation shocked the Xiongnu. Qin Shihuang particularly respected and admired the Meng family, trusting and appreciating their talents. Therefore, he became close to Meng Yi and became the highest official. When he went out, he would ride in the same carriage with the First Emperor, and when he returned to the court, he would serve the king. Meng Tian was responsible for military responsibilities outside the country, while Meng Yi often made suggestions in the court and was known as a loyal minister. Therefore, even other generals did not dare to compete with them for favor. Zhao Gao is an estranged relative of King Zhao's family. The Zhao Gao brothers were all castrated at birth and became eunuchs. His mother was also punished for breaking the law, so her status was low for generations. When the King of Qin heard that Zhao Gao was very capable and proficient in criminal and prison laws, he promoted him to the post of Zhongche Mansion Order. Zhao Gao then served his son Hu Hai privately and taught him how to decide lawsuits. Zhao Gao committed a serious crime, and King Qin asked Meng Yi to punish him in accordance with the law. Meng Yi did not dare to bend the law. According to the law, he should be sentenced to death and deprived of his official status.
target: Meng Tian, a Qin general, hailed from Qi through his grandfather Meng Ao, who served Qin under King Zhao and later as a general under King Zhuangxiang and the First Emperor, conquering territories in Han, Zhao, and Wei before his death in 7 BCE. Meng Tian’s father, Meng Wu, also a general, defeated Chu alongside Wang Jian. Meng Tian began as a legal clerk, became a general in 26 BCE, and led 300,000 troops to expel northern nomads, reclaim land south of the Yellow River, and construct the Great Wall from Lintao to Liaodong. He garrisoned Shangjun for over a decade, intimidating the Xiongnu. His brother Meng Yi served as a trusted advisor to the First Emperor.

When the King of Qin heard that Zhao Gao was very capable and proficient in criminal and prison laws, he promoted him to the post of Zhongche Mansion Order. Zhao Gao then served his son Hu Hai privately and taught him how to decide lawsuits. Zhao Gao committed a serious crime, and King Qin asked Meng Yi to punish him in accordance with the law. Meng Yi did not dare to bend the law. According to the law, he should be sentenced to death and deprived of his official status. The First Emperor pardoned Zhao Gao because of his diligence and hard work. His original official position was restored. The First Emperor planned to tour the world, passing through Jiuyuan County and going directly to Ganquan Palace. He sent Meng Tian to open a road for him, from Jiuyuan to Ganquan, opening up the mountains and filling in the deep valleys, a total length of 1,800 miles. However, the passage was not completed. In the winter of the thirty-seventh year of the First Emperor's reign, the royal chariot went out on a tour of Kuaiji, leaning on the sea, heading north to Langye. He got seriously ill halfway through, so Meng Yi turned back to pray to the gods of mountains and rivers. Before Meng Yi could return, the First Emperor walked to the sand dunes and died. The news of the death of the First Emperor was blocked, and none of the civil and military officials knew about it. At this time, Prime Minister Li Si, Prince Hu Hai, and Zhao Gao, the magistrate of CRRC, often served Qin Shihuang. Zhao Gao usually received Hu Hai's favor and planned to appoint Hu Hai to inherit the throne. However, he resented Meng Yi for punishing him according to the law instead of protecting him, so he wanted to kill him. He secretly planned with Prime Minister Li Si and Prince Hu Hai to make Hu Hai the crown prince. After the crown prince was established, he sent envoys to fabricate charges and prepare the death penalty for Prince Fusu and Meng Tian. After Fusu committed suicide, Mengtian became suspicious and asked for an appeal.
target: Zhao Gao, a eunuch of Zhao royal descent, rose to favor due to legal expertise, teaching Prince Hu Hai. When Zhao Gao committed a serious crime, Meng Yi sentenced him to death, but the First Emperor pardoned him. During the First Emperor’s fatal illness in 37 BCE, Meng Yi was sent to pray; after the emperor’s death, Zhao Gao conspired with Li Si and Hu Hai to install Hu Hai as crown prince, fabricating charges against Fusu and Meng Tian. Fusu committed suicide; Meng Tian was imprisoned. Zhao Gao, fearing the Meng family’s resurgence, falsely accused Meng Yi of opposing Hu Hai’s appointment, leading to his imprisonment in Dai. After Hu Hai became the Second Emperor, Zhao Gao slandered the Mengs daily. Ziying advised against killing them, warning of past disasters from killing loyal ministers, but Hu Hai ignored him.

source: After the crown prince was established, he sent envoys to fabricate charges and prepare the death penalty for Prince Fusu and Meng Tian. After Fusu committed suicide, Mengtian became suspicious and asked for an appeal. The envoy handed Meng Tian over to the officials in charge, and sent someone else to take over his duties. Hu Hai used Li Si's retainers as military guards. When the envoy came back to report, Hu Hai had heard the news of Fusu's death and immediately planned to release Meng Tian. Zhao Gao was afraid that the Meng family would become powerful again and resented them. Meng Yi returned after praying to the gods of the mountains and rivers. Zhao Gao took the opportunity to express his loyalty to Hu Hai and wanted to eradicate the Meng brothers, so he said to Hu Hai: I heard that the late emperor selected talents and made you the crown prince a long time ago, but Meng Yi tried to dissuade him and said: No.
target: Meng Yi was ordered to commit suicide; he defended his loyalty and criticized unjust executions, citing historical examples, but was killed. Meng Tian, ordered to die, declared his innocence and loyalty, recounting the Duke of Zhou’s story to urge the emperor to reconsider. The envoy refused to relay his words.

id: 史记/七十列传/蒙恬列传::group-003
article_path: 史记/七十列传/蒙恬列传
source: Starting from Lintao and continuing to Liaodong, the Great Wall was built and trenches were dug for more than 10,000 miles. Is there no place where the earth's veins are cut off in the middle? This is my sin. So he swallowed poison and committed suicide. Tai Shigong said: I went to the northern border and returned from the straight road. Along the way, I observed the Great Wall and frontier fortresses built by Meng Tian for the country. He excavated mountains, filled deep valleys, and connected the straight road. I originally did not pay attention to the people's manpower and material resources. When the Qin State had just wiped out the other princes, the people of the world had not yet settled down, and the wounds had not yet healed. As a famous general, Meng Tian did not try his best to admonish and relieve the people's emergencies, provide care for the elderly, raise orphans, and devote himself to the work of making the people live a stable life. Instead, he catered to the wishes of the First Emperor and built the Great Wall on a large scale. Isn't it natural that their brothers were killed? Where is the sin of digging up the earth's veins?
target: Meng Tian lamented his sin of cutting earth’s veins while building the Great Wall and poisoned himself. Sima Qian criticized Meng Tian for failing to counsel the First Emperor to aid the people after conquests, instead building the Great Wall, which led to his and his brother’s deaths.

id: 史记/七十列传/袁盎晁错列传::group-000

source: Yuan Ang is from Chu, and his courtesy name is Si. His father once worked with bandits and later moved to Anling. During the period of Empress Lu, Yuan An once served as Lu Lu's retainer. When Emperor Wen of Han came to the throne, Yuan An's brother Yuan Kuai recommended him to be the lieutenant. Jianghou Zhou Bo became the prime minister. After the pilgrimage, he hurried out of the court, very satisfied with his ambitions. The emperor was very respectful to him and often sent him off in person. Yuan Ang remonstrated and said: What kind of person do you think Prime Minister Jianghou is? The emperor said: He is an important minister of the country. Yuan An said: Jianghou is what is usually called a hero, not an important minister of the country. The important ministers of the country can live and die with the emperor. When Empress Lu was in power, the Lu family was in power and granted the title of king without authorization. As a result, the Liu family's world was barely held together like a thin ribbon and was almost severed. During this period, Jianghou Zhou Bo was the Taiwei and held military power, but could not correct the collapse of the Han Dynasty. After Empress Lu died, the ministers jointly opposed the Lu family. The Taiwei took control of the military and happened to have the opportunity to succeed, so he was what is usually called a hero, not an important official of the country. If the Prime Minister shows a proud look towards the Emperor, but His Majesty humbly gives in, both the minister and the Lord are violating etiquette. I privately think that Your Majesty should not adopt this attitude. Later in the court meeting, the emperor gradually became more majestic, and the prime minister gradually became more awe-inspiring. Soon after, the prime minister resented Yuan Ang and said: I have a relationship with your brother Yuan Kuai, but now you are slandering me in the court! Yuan An also did not apologize to him. When Jianghou was dismissed from his position as prime minister and returned to his feudal state, someone in the feudal state wrote a letter accusing him of treason, so Jianghou was summoned to Beijing and imprisoned in prison. Some princes in the royal family did not dare to speak for him. Only Yuan Ang declared that Jianghou was not guilty.
target: Yuan Ang, courtesy name Si, was from Chu and later moved to Anling. He served as a retainer under Lü Lu during Empress Lü’s reign and was recommended as a lieutenant by his brother after Emperor Wen ascended. Yuan Ang remonstrated with Emperor Wen about his excessive respect for Prime Minister Zhou Bo, arguing that Zhou Bo was a “hero” rather than a true “important minister” for failing to prevent the Lü clan’s usurpation. The emperor heeded his advice, and Zhou Bo later resented Yuan Ang but reconciled after Yuan Ang defended him when Zhou Bo was imprisoned for treason.

id: 史记/七十列传/袁盎晁错列传::group-001
article_path: 史记/七十列传/袁盎晁错列传
source: It was difficult for Zeng Shen to do this as a poor man, but now His Majesty has practiced it as a king, which is much better than Zeng Shen's filial piety. When Zhu Lu was in power, ministers acted arbitrarily, but Your Majesty rode six inferior horse-drawn carriages from Dai to the capital where disaster and fortune were unpredictable. Even brave men like Meng Ben and Xia Yu could not compare with Your Majesty. His Majesty arrived at Dai Guo's guest house in the capital. He resigned to the throne of emperor twice while facing west, and resigned to the throne of emperor three times while sitting facing south. Xu You resigned to the world only once, but His Majesty resigned to the world five times, which was more than Xu You's four times. Besides, Your Majesty demoted the King of Huainan to make him suffer some hardship and make him correct his mistakes. However, because the officials were not cautious in protecting him, he died of illness. Then the emperor felt relieved and said: What should we do in the future? Yuan Ang said, "The King of Huainan has three sons. It's just up to your Majesty's arrangement." So Emperor Wen made all three sons of King Huainan kings. As a result, Yuan Ang became famous in the court. Yuan An often praised righteousness and spoke impassionedly. Because the eunuch Zhao Tong was favored by the emperor more than once, he often secretly hurt Yuan Ang, which made Yuan Ang worried. Yuan An's nephew Yuan Zhong served as an attendant knight, guarding the emperor with talismans. Yuan Zhong persuaded Yuan Ang: "Fight with him and insult him in the court, so that his slanderous words will have no effect." Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty went on a tour, and Zhao Tong accompanied him in the car. Yuan Ang lay in front of the car and said: I heard that the people who accompany the emperor on the tall chariot are all heroes in the world. Although the Han Dynasty lacks talents today, why does Your Majesty only want to ride in the same carriage with people who have been cut by swords and saws? So the emperor smiled and asked Zhao Tong to get off, and Zhao Tong got out of the car with tears in his eyes. Emperor Wen went up the mountain from Baling and planned to run down the steep slope in the west. Yuan An was riding a horse, leaning against the car and holding the horse's reins.
target: Yuan Ang advised against indulging Liu Chang, the King of Huainan, whose arrogance led to rebellion and exile. When the king died en route, Yuan Ang consoled the grieving emperor by citing his three virtuous acts: filial piety to his mother, bravery during the Lü crisis, and humility in refusing the throne. The emperor later made the king’s three sons rulers. Yuan Ang’s outspokenness caused friction with eunuch Zhao Tong, whom he publicly humiliated to prevent him from riding in the emperor’s carriage. He also dissuaded the emperor from reckless chariot racing and corrected seating arrangements that favored a concubine over the queen.

id: 史记/七十列传/袁盎晁错列传::group-002

source: The terrain in the south is low-lying and humid, so you'd better drink wine every day, don't care about anything, and just persuade King Wu from time to time not to rebel. This way you might just get away with it. Yuan An adopted Yuan Zhong's strategy, and the King of Wu treated Yuan An favorably. When Yuan An asked for leave to go home, he met the Prime Minister Shen Tujia on the road and got out of the car to worship him. The Prime Minister only expressed his gratitude from the car. When Yuan An returned home, he felt ashamed in front of his subordinate officials, so he went to the Prime Minister's house and asked to see the Prime Minister. It took a long time for the prime minister to come out to see him, so Yuan Ang knelt down and said, "I hope others will avoid him and meet him alone." The prime minister said: If what you are talking about is a public matter, please go to the official office to discuss it with the chief minister, and I will report your opinion; if it is a private matter, I will not accept private conversations. Yuan Ang knelt down and persuaded him: "As prime minister, please weigh yourself. How do you compare with Chen Ping and Jianghou?" The prime minister said: I am not as good as them. Yuan Ang said: Well, you even said you are not as good as them. Chen Ping and Jianghou assisted in protecting Gaozu, pacifying the world, becoming generals, killing Zhu Lu, and preserving the Liu family. You only used the bow and crossbow to become a low-level warrior, and then promoted to captain. You accumulated merit and became the governor of Huaiyang. You did not come up with any strange tricks, and made military exploits in attacking cities and seizing land, and fighting in the wild. Besides, His Majesty came from Dai. Every time he went to court and Lang Guan submitted a memorial, he never stopped to listen to their opinions. If the opinions could not be adopted, he would put them aside. If the opinions were acceptable, he would adopt them. No one would not praise and praise them. What is this for? He wanted to use this method to attract the wise scholar-bureaucrats in the world. Every day the emperor hears things he has never heard before, understands truths he has never understood before, and becomes wiser and wiser day by day; now that you have closed the mouths of the people in the world, you are becoming more stupid day by day. If you use a wise monarch to supervise a foolish prime minister, the day when you will suffer disaster is not far away! The prime minister then bowed twice and said: I am a vulgar and vulgar person, but I am not smart. Fortunately, I have been taught by the general. Shen Tujia invited Yuan An into the inner room to sit with him and treated him as an honored guest.
target: Transferred to Longxi, Yuan Ang won soldiers’ loyalty through kindness. As prime minister of Wu, he followed his nephew’s advice to avoid conflict by drinking daily and persuading the king not to rebel. He later confronted Prime Minister Shen Tujia for arrogance, warning that closing off advice would lead to disaster. Shen Tujia apologized and treated him as an honored guest.

source: Someone told Yuan Ang about this. Yuan Ang was afraid and went to see Dou Ying overnight to explain to him the reasons for King Wu's rebellion, hoping to confront him personally in front of the emperor. Dou Ying went to the palace to report to the emperor, and the emperor summoned Yuan Ang to the palace to meet him. Chao Cuo was right in front of him. When Yuan An asked the emperor to meet him alone without others, Chao Cuo retreated, feeling very resentful. Yuan Ang explained in detail that the King of Wu rebelled because of Chao Cuo. Only by killing Chao Cuo immediately to apologize to the King of Wu could the Wu army stop. These words of his are all recorded in "The Biography of Wu Wangbi". The emperor appointed Yuan An as Taichang and Dou Ying as general. The two men have always been friends. When the King of Wu rebelled, the prestigious people living in the mausoleums and the wise officials in Chang'an City were vying to attach themselves to the two of them, and hundreds of cars followed behind them every day. After Chao Cuo was executed, Yuan Ang went to Wu as an envoy as Taichang. The King of Wu wanted him to serve as a general, but Yuan Ang refused. The king of Wu killed him and sent a captain to lead 500 men to surround Yuan Ang in the army. When Yuan An was the Prime Minister of the State of Wu, a Cong Shi secretly had an affair with Yuan An's maid. Yuan An knew about it but did not reveal it, and treated Cong Shi as before. Someone told Cong Shi that Yuan Ang knew about his affair with his maidservant, and Congshi fled home. Yuan Ang chased Congshi in his car, and gave him his maidservant, still calling him Congshi. When Yuan An was sent as an envoy to Wu and was besieged, Sima happened to be the captain who besieged Yuan An. Sima sold all the belongings he carried and used the money to buy two loads of strong-flavored wine. It happened to be cold and the besieging soldiers were hungry and thirsty. They drank too much wine and the soldiers guarding the southwest corner of the city were drunk. Sima Cheng led Yuan An up at night and said: You can go, the King of Wu expects to kill you tomorrow. Yuan Ang didn't believe it and said, "What do you do?" Sima said: I am the one who originally had an affair with your maid in the history. Yuan Ang then thanked him in surprise and said: "You are lucky to have your parents here, I can't let you get in trouble because of this." Sima said: Just leave. I will run away and hide my parents. Why should you worry? So he cut the tent of the military camp open with a knife and led Yuan Ang out of the road blocked by the drunken soldiers. Sima and Yuan Ang parted ways and went in opposite directions. Yuan Ang took off his knot and carried it in his arms. He leaned on his staff and walked for seven or eight miles. At dawn, he encountered Liang's cavalry and fled on horseback. Finally, he returned to the court to report. The Wu-Chu rebels had been defeated, and the emperor changed the title of Pingluhou Liu Li, the son of King Chu Yuan, to the king of Chu, and Yuan An became the prime minister of Chu. Yuan Ang once wrote a letter to make suggestions, but they were not accepted. Yuan Ang was exempted from official duties due to illness and lived at home, hanging out with the villagers and playing cockfighting and dog racing games with them. Ju Meng, a native of Luoyang, once visited Yuan An, who received him warmly. A rich man from Anling said to Yuan An: I heard that Ju Meng is a gambler. Why do you want to associate with him?
target: Yuan Ang clashed with Chao Cuo, who investigated him for accepting bribes from the King of Wu, leading to his demotion. When Wu rebelled, Yuan Ang blamed Chao Cuo and urged his execution to appease the rebels. After Chao Cuo’s death, Yuan Ang was sent as an envoy to Wu but was besieged. A former subordinate, whom Yuan Ang had forgiven for an affair with his maid, helped him escape. Yuan Ang later served as prime minister of Chu but retired due to illness, living humbly and befriending gambler Ju Meng despite criticism. He opposed making the King of Liang the emperor’s heir, prompting assassination attempts. Warned by an assassin who spared him, Yuan Ang was eventually killed by Liang’s agents outside Anling.

id: 史记/七十列传/袁盎晁错列传::group-004
