source: During the reign of Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty, there was no one in the world who studied "Shangshu". I only heard that Mr. Fu from Jinan was a doctor from the original Qin Dynasty and had studied "Shangshu". He was too old to answer the call, so Emperor Wen ordered Taichang to send people to study with him. Taichang sent Chao Cuo to Mr. Fu to study Shangshu. After he came back from his studies, he took the opportunity to report to the emperor things that benefited the country and the people, and quoted and explained "Shang Shu". Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty issued an edict and appointed Chao Cuo as the prince's family minister, family official, and prince's family magistrate. Chao Cuo won the favor of the prince with his eloquence, and the prince's family called him "the wise man". During the reign of Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty, Chao Cuo wrote many times about reducing the power of the princes and amending the laws. After dozens of petitions, Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty did not accept them, but he believed that he had unique talents and was promoted to a middle doctor. At that time, the prince praised Chao Cuo's strategy, but Yuan Ang and most of the other great heroes did not like Chao Cuo. After Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty succeeded to the throne, he appointed Chao Cuo as his internal historian. Chao Cuo repeatedly requested the emperor to discuss political affairs with him alone. Emperor Jing always obeyed and favored him more than Jiu Qing. Chao Cuo revised many laws.
target: Chao Cuo, from Yingchuan, studied Legalist doctrines and Shangshu under Master Fu. He gained favor as a prince’s tutor during Emperor Wen’s reign, advocating for reducing princely power. Emperor Jing promoted him, and he revised laws, angering nobles. His father warned him of danger but Chao Cuo insisted on centralizing authority.

id: 史记/七十列传/袁盎晁错列传::group-005
article_path: 史记/七十列传/袁盎晁错列传
source: After the death of Chao Cuo, Duke Deng of Yezhe Pushe served as a school captain. When he attacked Wu Chu's army, he served as a general. After returning to the capital, he wrote a letter reporting the military situation and went to see the emperor. The emperor asked: "You came from the army and heard that Chao Cuo was dead. Did Wu Chu's army retreat?" Deng Gong said: The King of Wu has been deliberately rebellious for decades. He was angry because you reduced his fiefdom, so in the name of killing Chao Cuo, his original intention was not Chao Cuo. Besides, I'm worried that all the scholars in the world will shut up and never dare to speak out again. The emperor said: Why? Deng Gong said: Chao Cuo was worried that the princes would become too powerful and could not be subdued, so he asked to reduce the fiefdoms of the princes in order to favor the court. This is the benefit of all generations. The plan had just started to be implemented, but he was actually killed, which blocked the mouths of loyal ministers internally, and avenged the princes externally. I privately think that it is not advisable for your Majesty to do this. At this time Emperor Jing was silent for a long time and said: "What you said is right. I also regret this."
target: The Wu-Chu rebellion used his execution as a pretext. After his death, Deng Gong argued that Chao Cuo’s policies were for the empire’s benefit, and Emperor Jing regretted the execution. Deng Gong later became a high official but retired.

id: 史记/七十列传/袁盎晁错列传::group-006
article_path: 史记/七十列传/袁盎晁错列传
source: So Deng Gong was appointed as the lieutenant of Chengyang. Deng Gong was from Chenggu and had many unexpected ideas. During the Jianyuan period, the emperor recruited virtuous people, and the ministers all recommended Deng Gong. At that time, Deng Gong was dismissed from office, and he became the ninth minister from his leisure time at home. A year later, he resigned and returned home, claiming to be ill. His son Deng Zhang was very famous among the court ministers for studying the theories of Huangdi and Laozi. Tai Shigong said: Although Yuan Ang is not easy to learn, he is good at understanding and understanding. He takes benevolence as his essence and often praises righteousness and is impassioned.
target: Tai Shigong commented that Yuan Ang, though unlearned, was benevolent and outspoken, but his fame-seeking led to downfall.

id: 史记/七十列传/袁盎晁错列传::group-007
article_path: 史记/七十列传/袁盎晁错列传
source: The current situation was constantly changing. When Wu Chu rebelled, he proposed to kill Chao Cuo. Although his suggestions were adopted and implemented, he was no longer used by the court. People who love fame and show off their talents end up getting into trouble because of their pursuit of fame. When Chao Cuo was making the prince's family orders, he made many suggestions but they were not adopted. Later, he took power and revised many laws of the country. The princes launched a rebellion, but Chao Cuo was not eager to correct the crisis, but wanted to avenge himself, which resulted in his death. As the saying goes: If you change the ancient laws and mess up the routine, you will either die or escape. Are you talking about people like Chao Cuo?
target: Chao Cuo, despite his talents, failed to adapt and died due to his rigidity, as the saying goes: altering ancient laws brings ruin.

id: 史记/七十列传/西南夷列传::group-000
article_path: 史记/七十列传/西南夷列传
source: The people of these Yi countries wear their hair in buns, cultivate fields, and live together in towns and villages. The places outside them, from Tongshi in the west to Yiyu in the north, are called Xi and Kunming. The people here put their hair on their heads and move around with the grazing livestock. They have no fixed place of residence and no commander. They move for thousands of miles. Going northeast from Wei, there are so many rulers that one can count them by ten, among which Yi and Zuo are the most powerful. Going northeast from Zuo, there are so many rulers that one can count them by ten, among which Ran Zhen is the most powerful. Their custom is that some are indigenous people and some are immigrants, all in the west of Shu County. Going northeast from Ranjun, there are so many kings that you need to count them by ten. Among them, Baima is the most powerful, and they are all of the same kind as the Di tribe. These are all barbarians outside Bajun and southwest of Shujun. When King Wei of Chu was king, he sent General Zhuang Qi to lead his army up the Yangtze River and captured the areas west of Bajun, Shujun and Qianzhong County. Zhuang Qi is a descendant of the former King Zhuang of Chu. Zhuang Qi arrived at Dianchi Lake, which has a radius of three hundred miles, is surrounded by flat land, and is fertile and rich for thousands of miles. Zhuang Qi relied on the power of his army to pacify the place and made it subordinate to the Chu State. Zhuang Qi wanted to return to Chu State to report the situation, but just as Qin State attacked and captured Bajun and Qianzhong County of Chu State, the road was blocked and could not pass, so he returned to Dianchi Lake and became the king of Dian with the help of his army. He changed his clothes and obeyed local customs, so he became the ruler of the Dian people.
target: Various Yi tribes and their customs. Some wear hair in buns, cultivate fields, and live in towns, while others, like the Xi and Kunming, move with livestock and have no fixed residence or commander. From Wei northeast, many rulers exist, with Yi and Zuo being most powerful, followed by Ran Zhen. These are barbarians outside Bajun and southwest of Shujun. King Wei of Chu sent General Zhuang Qi, a descendant of King Zhuang of Chu, to capture areas west of Bajun, Shujun, and Qianzhong County. He reached Dianchi Lake, a fertile area, and pacified it for Chu. Unable to return due to Qin's capture of Bajun and Qianzhong, he became king of Dian, adopting local customs.

id: 史记/七十列传/西南夷列传::group-001
article_path: 史记/七十列传/西南夷列传
source: Zhuang Qi is a descendant of the former King Zhuang of Chu. Zhuang Qi arrived at Dianchi Lake, which has a radius of three hundred miles, is surrounded by flat land, and is fertile and rich for thousands of miles. Zhuang Qi relied on the power of his army to pacify the place and made it subordinate to the Chu State. Zhuang Qi wanted to return to Chu State to report the situation, but just as Qin State attacked and captured Bajun and Qianzhong County of Chu State, the road was blocked and could not pass, so he returned to Dianchi Lake and became the king of Dian with the help of his army. He changed his clothes and obeyed local customs, so he became the ruler of the Dian people. During the Qin Dynasty, Chang Yan briefly opened the Five Feet Road and set up some officials in these countries. After more than ten years, the Qin Dynasty perished. When the Han Dynasty was established, these countries were abandoned, and the original boundaries of Shu County were used as fortresses. Some people from Bajun and Shujun secretly went out to trade in exchange for horses from Zuo, boy servants and yaks from Bo. Therefore, Bajun and Shujun were particularly wealthy. In the sixth year of the founding of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, Wang Hui of Daxing attacked Dongyue. The Dongyue people killed Ying, the king of Dongyue, and reported to the Han Dynasty. Wang Hui relied on his military power to send Fan Yang to Tang Meng to tactfully inform South Vietnam of the Han Dynasty's intention to send troops. Nanyue gave Tang Meng some wolfberry sauce produced in Shu County. Tang Meng asked where it came from. Nanyue said: It came via the Zoke River in the northwest. The Zoke River is several miles wide and flows under Panyu City. Tang Meng returned to Chang'an and asked the merchants in Shu County. The merchants said: Only Shu County produces wolfberry sauce, and many people secretly take it out to make deals with Yelang. Yelang is close to the Zoke River. The river is hundreds of paces wide and can be used for boating. Nanyue wanted to use property to make Yelang belong to him, but his power reached directly to his fellow soldiers in the west, and he could not use Yelang like his subordinates. Tang Meng wrote to the emperor and said: The King of Nanyue rides in the yellow house's carriage, with the flag of Zuohu flying on the carriage. His land is more than 10,000 miles from east to west. In name, he is a foreign minister, but in fact he is the lord of a state. Nowadays, most of the waterways from Changsha and Yuzhang County are blocked, making it difficult to move forward. I have privately heard that Yelang has more than 100,000 elite soldiers. He can take boats down the Zoko River and attack them while they are not paying attention. This is a wonderful trick to subdue South Vietnam. If we can really use the power of the Han Dynasty and the wealth of Bashu to open the road to Yelang and set up officials there, it will be very easy. Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty agreed with Tang Meng's proposal and appointed him Lieutenant General Lang. He led a thousand troops and more than 10,000 people in charge of food and baggage. He entered Yelang from Bafu Pass and met Yelang Hou Duotong.
target: During Qin, Chang Yan briefly opened the Five Feet Road and set officials. After Qin's fall, Han abandoned these areas, using Shu County's boundaries as fortresses. Bajun and Shujun grew wealthy through secret trade with Zuo, Bo, and others. In Emperor Wu's sixth year, Wang Hui attacked Dongyue, and Tang Meng learned from Nanyue about wolfberry sauce from Shu, traded via Yelang and the Zoke River. Tang Meng proposed using Yelang's elite troops to attack Nanyue, and Emperor Wu agreed. Tang Meng entered Yelang, made agreements, and established Qianwei County. Roads were built, but difficulties and rebellions led to temporary cessation of development.

id: 史记/七十列传/西南夷列传::group-002
article_path: 史记/七十列传/西南夷列传
source: After several years, the road was not repaired. The soldiers were tired, hungry, and suffered from dampness, and many died. The southwestern barbarians rebelled many times, dispatching troops to attack, spending money and manpower, but there was no commotion. The emperor was worried about this, so he sent Gongsun Hong to observe and inquire in person. Gongsun Hong returned to Beijing to report to the emperor, claiming that it was unfavorable. When Gongsun Hong became the censor, the Han Dynasty was building Shuofang County in order to use the Yellow River to expel the Huns. Gongsun Hong took the opportunity to repeatedly state the harm of developing the southwestern barbarians, so he could temporarily stop development activities and concentrate on dealing with the Xiongnu. The emperor ordered the cessation of activities against the Western Yi, and only set up two counties and one captaincy in Yelang, Nanyi. He ordered Qianwei County to protect itself and gradually improve its county system. In the first year of Yuanshou, Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, Bowang Hou Zhang Qian returned from his mission to Daxia. He said that when he was in Daxia, he had seen cloth produced in Shu County and bamboo sticks from Qiongdu. He asked people about the origin of these things. The person who answered said: They were obtained from the Shendu Kingdom in the southeast. The road from here to there is thousands of miles, and you can do business with merchants in Shu. Some people heard that there was a country called Shendu about two thousand miles west of Qiongdi. Zhang Qian took the opportunity to talk about how Daxia was in the southwest of the Han Dynasty, admired China, and was worried that the Xiongnu would block their main transportation routes with China. If a road to Shu could be opened, the road to Shendu would be convenient and short, which would be beneficial and harmless to the Han Dynasty. So Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty ordered Wang Ranyu, Bai Shichang, Lu Yueren and others to find a shortcut from the west of Xiyi to find the Shendu Kingdom. When they arrived in the Dian Kingdom, King Changqiang of Dian stayed with them and sent more than ten groups of people to the west to find a way for them. More than a year later, all those who were looking for a way were blocked by the Kunming Kingdom and could not reach the Shendu Kingdom. The King of Dian said to the envoys of the Han Dynasty: Which one is bigger, the Han Dynasty or our Dian Kingdom? When the Han Dynasty envoy arrived at Yelang, Yelang also raised such a question.
target: Later, Zhang Qian reported seeing Shu cloth and Qiong bamboo sticks in Daxia, suggesting a route to Shendu. Emperor Wu sent envoys to find Shendu via Dian, but they were blocked by Kunming. Dian and Yelang kings, unaware of Han's size, questioned its magnitude.

id: 史记/七十列传/西南夷列传::group-003
article_path: 史记/七十列传/西南夷列传
source: When the Han Dynasty envoy arrived at Yelang, Yelang also raised such a question. This is because the roads are impassable. Each of them thought he was the master of a state and did not know the vastness of the Han Dynasty. When the envoys of the Han Dynasty returned to the capital, they tried their best to say that Dian was a great country and worthy of getting close to them and joining the Han Dynasty. Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty paid attention to this matter. When the South Vietnamese rebelled, the emperor sent Marquis Chiyi to dispatch the Nanyi troops in the name of Jianwei County. Qie Lanjun was afraid that after his army traveled far, neighboring countries would take the opportunity to plunder his old and weak people, so he rebelled with his army and killed the Han Dynasty envoys and the prefect of Jianwei County. The Han Dynasty mobilized eight captains from Bajun and Shujun who originally wanted to attack South Vietnam, and led the criminals who had been pardoned to join the army to attack Qielan and pacify it. Just as South Vietnam had been conquered, the eight lieutenants of the Han Dynasty had not yet moved south along the Zangke River, so they led their troops to withdraw and killed Tou Lan during the march. Toulan was a country that often blocked the transportation routes between the Han Dynasty and the Dian Kingdom. After Toulan was pacified, Nanyi was pacified and Zoke County was established there. Yelanghou began to rely on Nanyue. After Nanyue was destroyed, just as the Han army came back to kill the rebels, Yelanghou went to the capital of the Han Dynasty to meet the emperor. Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty named him King Yelang. After the destruction of Nanyue, and the execution of Lord Qielan and Lord Qiong by the Han Dynasty, as well as the death of Marquis Zhe, Ran and Zhen were shocked and panicked, and they asked the Han Dynasty to become ministers and appoint officials for them. In the Han Dynasty, Qiongdu was set up as Yuesi County, Zhedu was set up as Shenli County, Ran and Zhan were set up as Lunshan County, and Baima in the west of Guanghan was set up as Wudu County.
target: When Nanyue rebelled, Qielan rebelled and killed Han envoys. Han forces conquered Qielan and Nanyue, establishing Zoke County. Yelanghou submitted and was named king. Other tribes, shocked, requested Han officials. Han set up Yuesi, Shenli, Lunshan, and Wudu counties.

id: 史记/七十列传/西南夷列传::group-004
article_path: 史记/七十列传/西南夷列传
source: After the destruction of Nanyue, and the execution of Lord Qielan and Lord Qiong by the Han Dynasty, as well as the death of Marquis Zhe, Ran and Zhen were shocked and panicked, and they asked the Han Dynasty to become ministers and appoint officials for them. In the Han Dynasty, Qiongdu was set up as Yuesi County, Zhedu was set up as Shenli County, Ran and Zhan were set up as Lunshan County, and Baima in the west of Guanghan was set up as Wudu County. The emperor sent Wang Ranyu to use the military power of destroying Nanyue and killing the Nanyi rulers to tactfully persuade the Dian king to come to see the emperor. The King of Dian had an army of tens of thousands. Next to him in the northeast were Lao Jin and Mi Mo. They both had the same surname as the King of Dian. They relied on each other and refused to listen to advice. Lao Jin and Mi Mo repeatedly offended Han Dynasty envoys and officers and soldiers. In the second year of Yuanfeng reign of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, the emperor mobilized the troops from Bajun and Shujun to attack and destroy Laojin and Mimo, and the army approached the Dian Kingdom. The King of Dian had good intentions towards the Han Dynasty from the beginning, so he was not executed. The King of Dian then left Xiyi, led the country to surrender to the Han Dynasty, requested to appoint officials for them, and went to Beijing to meet Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty. So the Han Dynasty established the Dian Kingdom as Yizhou County, gave the Dian King a royal seal, and still ruled over his people. There were hundreds of princes in southwestern Yi, but only the princes of Yelang and Dian accepted the royal seal. Dian is a small country that was most favored by the Han Dynasty. Tai Shigong said: Did the ancestors of Chu have a salary and position given by God? During the Zhou Dynasty, their ancestor Wan Xiong became the teacher of King Zhou Wen. Later, Xiong Yi was granted the title of King Zhou Cheng to the land of Chu barbarians and established his country. By the time the Zhou Dynasty declined, the territory of Chu State was known as five thousand miles. The Qin State destroyed its princes, and only the descendants of the Chu State still had the King of Dian. The Han Dynasty killed the southwestern barbarians, and most of the countries there were wiped out. Only the King of Dian was favored by the Emperor of Han. But the beginning of the pacification of Nanyi was the sight of Gojiang in Panyu and the sight of Qiong Bamboo Staff in Daxia. Xiyi was later divided into the west and south, and was finally divided into seven counties by the King of Han.
target: The Dian king, with tens of thousands of troops, initially refused to submit. After Han destroyed Laojin and Mimo, Dian surrendered, becoming Yizhou County. The Dian king received a royal seal, favored by Han. Tai Shigong noted that Chu's descendants, including the Dian king, survived Qin's destruction. Han pacified southwestern barbarians, with Dian favored. The pacification began with sightings of Gojiang in Panyu and Qiong bamboo sticks in Daxia, leading to the division of Xiyi into seven counties.

id: 史记/七十列传/郦生陆贾列传::group-000
article_path: 史记/七十列传/郦生陆贾列传
source: Li Shiqi was from Gaoyang, Chenliu. He likes to study very much, but his family is poor and destitute. He doesn't even have a property that can afford to clothe and feed himself, so he has to work as a lowly clerk looking after the inner door. But despite this, the wise men and powerful men in the county did not dare to use him casually. People in the county called him "Kangsheng". When Chen Sheng, Xiang Liang and others rebelled against the Qin Dynasty, dozens of generals passed through Gaoyang when they attacked the city. However, Li Shiqi heard that these people were narrow-minded, liked trivial etiquette, were self-willed, and could not listen to open-minded words. So he lived in seclusion and hid himself, not to cater to these people. Later, he heard that Pei Gong led troops to capture the city and came to the outskirts of Chenliu. One of Pei Gong's cavalrymen happened to be the son of an old friend of Li Shi's neighborhood. Pei Gong often asked him about the wise men and heroes in his hometown. One day, when the cavalry came home, Li Shiqi saw him and said to him: I heard that Pei Gong was arrogant and looked down upon others, but he had many far-reaching strategies. This is the person I really want to follow, but I have no one to introduce him to him. When you see Pei Gong, you can say this to him: There is a Mr. Li in my hometown who is over sixty years old and eight feet tall. People call him a crazy person, but he himself says that he is not a crazy person.
target: Li Shiqi, a learned man from Gaoyang, Chenliu, lived in poverty and worked as a lowly clerk. Despite his humble status, local elites dared not employ him casually, calling him "Kangsheng." During the rebellions against Qin, he avoided serving narrow-minded generals until he heard of Pei Gong (Liu Bang). Through a cavalryman, he arranged a meeting.

id: 史记/七十列传/郦生陆贾列传::group-001
article_path: 史记/七十列传/郦生陆贾列传
source: When you see Pei Gong, you can say this to him: There is a Mr. Li in my hometown who is over sixty years old and eight feet tall. People call him a crazy person, but he himself says that he is not a crazy person. The cavalryman replied: Pei Gong does not like Confucian scholars. Many people came to see him wearing Confucian scholar hats. He immediately took off their hats and urinated in them. When he talked to people, he often cursed. So you'd better not lobby him as a Confucian scholar. Li Shiqi said: Just say it like I taught you. After the knight returned, he told Pei Gong according to Li Sheng's instructions. Later, Pei Gong came to Gaoyang, stayed in an inn, and sent someone to summon Li Shiqi to come and see him. When Li Sheng came to the hotel, Pei Gong sat on the bed with his legs spread apart and asked two women to wash his feet. He called Li Sheng to see him. Li Sheng went in, only made a long salute without leaning down to worship, and said: "Do you want to help Qin attack the princes, or do you want to lead the princes to destroy Qin?" Pei Gong scolded: You Confucian scholar! The people of the world have been suffering from the Qin Dynasty for a long time, so the princes have raised armies to resist the violent Qin one after another. How can you help the Qin Dynasty attack the princes? Li Sheng said: If you are determined to gather the people and call for volunteers to overthrow the tyrannical and cruel Qin Dynasty, you should not receive the elders in such a arrogant and disrespectful manner. So Pei Gong immediately stopped washing his feet, tidied his clothes, invited Li Sheng to the guest's seat, and apologized to him. Li Sheng talked about the strategy used by the six kingdoms to unite vertically and horizontally. Pei Gong was very happy and ordered people to bring rice for Li Sheng to eat. Then he asked: "Then how do you think we should formulate our strategy today?" Li Sheng said: If you gather the rabble and scattered soldiers, the total is less than 10,000 people. If you use this to directly confront the powerful Qin, it will be what people often say is exploring the tiger's mouth. Chenliu is an important transportation thoroughfare in the world, extending in all directions. Now there is a lot of grain in the city. I am very close to the magistrate of Chenliu. Please send me to him to ask him to surrender to you. If he doesn't obey, you can send troops to attack the city again, and I can act as an internal response in the city. So Pei Gong sent Li Sheng there and followed closely with his own troops. In this way, he captured Chenliu and gave Li Sheng the title of Lord of Guangye. Li Sheng recommended his younger brother Li Shang to lead thousands of people to follow Pei Gong to the southwest to capture the city. Li Sheng himself often served as a lobbyist and traveled among the princes as an envoy. In the autumn of the third year of the Han Dynasty, Xiang Yu attacked the Han Dynasty and captured Xingyang City. The Han soldiers fled to defend Gong and Luo. Soon after, the people of Chu heard that Han Xin, the Marquis of Huaiyin, had conquered Zhao and that Peng Yue had rebelled many times in Liang, so they sent a group of troops to rescue him. Han Xin, the Marquis of Huaiyin, was attacking Qi to the east. The King of Han was besieged by Xiang Yu many times in Xingyang and Chenggao, so he wanted to give up the territory east of Chenggao and stationed troops in Gong and Luoyi to confront the Chu army.
target: When they met, Pei Gong was washing his feet with two women, but Li Shiqi criticized his disrespect, prompting Pei Gong to apologize. Li Shiqi advised capturing Chenliu for its strategic location and grain stores, offering to persuade the magistrate to surrender. Pei Gong agreed, and with Li Shiqi's help, Chenliu was taken. Li Shiqi was titled Lord of Guangye and later recommended his brother Li Shang to serve Pei Gong.

id: 史记/七十列传/郦生陆贾列传::group-002
article_path: 史记/七十列传/郦生陆贾列传
source: Therefore, all the scholars in the world have surrendered to the King of Han, and the King of Han can command them from his seat. The King of Han led the army of Shu Han to pacify the Three Qin Dynasties, occupied a large area of ​​land outside the Xihe River, led the elite troops of the Shangdang who surrendered, captured Jingxing, and killed Lord Cheng'an; he defeated Wei Bao of Hebei and occupied thirty-two cities: just like the invincible Chi You's army, it did not rely on human strength, but was the result of God's blessing. Now the king of Han has seized the grain of Aocang, blocked the dangerous fortress of Chenggao, guarded the White Horse Ferry, blocked the main road of Daxing, and guarded the Fehu Pass. If the princes of the world want to surrender in the end, they will be destroyed first. If you surrender to the King of Han quickly, the state of Qi can still be preserved; if you do not surrender to the King of Han, the moment of peril will come soon. Tian Guang believed that Li Sheng's words were right, so he obeyed Li Sheng, removed all military defense and war preparations, and drank and had fun with Li Sheng every day. Han Xin, the Marquis of Huaiyin, heard that Li Sheng had made a trip in the car without any effort, and had captured more than 70 cities in Qi State with his sharp tongue. He was very unconvinced, so he took advantage of the cover of night to lead his troops across the plains to secretly attack Qi State. King Tian Guang of Qi heard that the Han soldiers had arrived and thought that Li Sheng had betrayed him, so he said to Li Sheng: If you can stop the Han army from attacking, I will let you live. If not, I will cook you to death! Li Sheng said: People who do great things do not stick to trivial matters, and people with great virtues are not afraid of others' criticism. Your father will not lobby Han Xin on your behalf! In this way, the King of Qi killed Li Sheng and led his troops to escape eastward. In the twelfth year of Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty, Li Shang, the Marquis of Quzhou, led troops to attack Yingbu in his capacity as prime minister. When Emperor Gaozu was enfeoffing feudal princes and attacking his ministers, he missed Li Shiqi very much. Li Shiqi's son Li Shi led troops to fight many times, but his military exploits did not reach the level of a marquis. The emperor made Li Shi a Marquis of Gaoliang because of his father. Later, the place of residence was changed to Wusui, and the title was passed down to three generations. In the first year of Yuanshou, Li Ping, Marquis of Wu Sui, defrauded King Hengshan of one hundred kilograms of gold by falsely claiming the emperor's order. The crime he committed should have been executed on the street, but at this time, he died of illness and the fiefdom was revoked. Lu Jia was a native of the Chu State. He followed Emperor Gaozu to pacify the world as a guest of staff. People at that time called him a very eloquent lobbyist, so he accompanied Emperor Gaozu and often traveled to various vassal states as envoys. When Emperor Gaozu had just pacified the Central Plains, Wei Ta also pacified South Vietnam and established himself as king there. Emperor Gaozu considered that the world had been settled for the first time, so he did not execute Wei Ta. He also sent Lu Jia with the seal of the King of South Vietnam given to Wei Ta to appoint him. When Lu Sheng arrived in South Vietnam, he wore his hair in an awl-like bun popular in the area, sat with his legs spread like a dustpan, and met Lu Sheng.
target: During the Chu-Han conflict, Li Shiqi advised the King of Han to hold Aocang's grain and key fortresses instead of retreating. He then volunteered to persuade the King of Qi to submit to Han. The King of Han agreed. Li Shiqi convinced King Tian Guang of Qi that the world's hearts turned to Han due to Han's generosity and Xiang Yu's failures. Tian Guang surrendered and removed defenses. However, Han Xin, jealous of Li Shiqi's success, attacked Qi by night. Tian Guang, believing Li Shiqi betrayed him, threatened to boil him alive. Li Shiqi refused to lobby Han Xin and was executed. Later, Emperor Gaozu enfeoffed Li Shiqi's son as Marquis of Gaoliang, a title passed for three generations until it was revoked. Lu Jia, a Chu native and eloquent lobbyist, served Emperor Gaozu as an envoy. He was sent to appoint Wei Tuo as King of South Vietnam. Lu Jia criticized Wei Tuo's barbarian customs and warned that Han could destroy him. Wei Tuo apologized, acknowledged Han's superiority, and submitted. Lu Jia returned, was appointed Taizhong doctor, and wrote "New Speech" at the emperor's request, discussing statecraft.

id: 史记/七十列传/郦生陆贾列传::group-003
article_path: 史记/七十列传/郦生陆贾列传
source: Chen Ping used his strategy and gave 500 gold to Jianghou Zhou Bo to celebrate his birthday, and prepared a grand singing and dancing banquet to entertain him; Taiwei Zhou Bo also repaid Chen Ping in the same way. In this way, Chen Ping and Zhou Bo established a very close relationship, and Lu's conspiracy to usurp power became even more difficult to realize. Chen Ping also gave Lu Sheng 100 slaves, 50 chariots and horses, and 5 million yuan as food expenses. Lu Sheng used these expenses to lobby among the ministers of the Han Dynasty, and became very famous. After Zhu Lu was killed and Emperor Xiaowen ascended the throne, Lu Sheng contributed a lot to this. After Emperor Xiaowen came to the throne, he wanted to send envoys to South Vietnam. Prime Minister Chen Ping and others recommended Lu Sheng as the Taizhong doctor, sent him as an envoy to South Vietnam, and ordered the South Vietnamese king Wei to cancel the Yellow House title system and other Vietnamese rituals, and let him adopt the same etiquette and rituals as other princes. After Lu Sheng went on his mission, he acted accordingly and the emperor's requirements were met, so Emperor Wen was very satisfied. The specific plot of this matter is recorded in "Biographies of South Vietnam". Lu Sheng finally died of old age. Pingyuan Marquis Zhu Jian was a native of Chu. At first, he served as the state minister of Huainan King Yingbu, but he left because of his guilt. Later, he worked under Ying Bu again. When Ying Bu wanted to rebel, he asked Zhu Jian what he thought of the matter, and Zhu Jian strongly opposed it. But Yingbu did not listen to his advice, but did what Liang Fuhou said, so he rebelled. After the Han Dynasty put down the rebellion and killed Yingbu, I heard that Zhu Jian, the king of Pingyuan, had advised Yingbu not to rebel. At the same time, he did not participate in the conspiracy of rebellion, so he did not kill Zhu Jian. This matter is recorded in "The Biography of Qingbu". Zhu Jian, Lord of Pingyuan, was eloquent and eloquent. At the same time, he was upright and adhered to the integrity and selfless integrity. Home is in Chang'an. He never agrees casually with his words or deeds, adheres to moral principles and refuses to bend to please others. Piyanghou Shenshi's behavior was not upright, and he won the favor of Empress Dowager Lu through flattery. At that time, Marquis Piyang wanted to be on good terms with Lord Pingyuan, but Lord Pingyuan refused to see him. When Pingyuanjun's mother passed away, Lu Sheng and Pingyuanjun had always been very close, so they went to express their condolences. Mr. Pingyuan was from a poor family and did not even have the money to pay for his mother's funeral. He was about to borrow money to buy funeral supplies, but Lu Sheng told Mr. Pingyuan to just pay for the funeral without borrowing money. Then Lu Sheng went to Piyanghou's home and congratulated him, saying: Pingyuanjun's mother passed away. Marquis Piyang said in confusion: Mr. Pingyuan's mother is dead, why do you congratulate me? Lu Sheng said: "You have always wanted to be on good terms with Mr. Pingyuan before, but he was a moral person and refused to associate with you. This was because of his mother." Now that his mother has passed away, if you give him generous gifts for his mother's funeral, then he will definitely be willing to work desperately for you. So Piyanghou sent a generous gift worth one hundred gold to Pingyuanjun.
target: During Empress Dowager Lü's reign, he retired, distributed wealth to his sons, and traveled. He later advised Chancellor Chen Ping to ally with General Zhou Bo against the Lü clan, using gifts to secure their cooperation. After the Lü clan's fall, Lu Jia was sent to South Vietnam again, succeeding in enforcing Han rituals. He died of old age. Pingyuanjun (Zhu Jian), a Chu native, served Yingbu but opposed his rebellion. After Yingbu's defeat, he was spared. He was upright, refusing to associate with the corrupt Piyanghou. When Pingyuanjun's mother died, Lu Jia advised Piyanghou to give generous funeral gifts, winning his favor. Later, when Piyanghou was imprisoned, Pingyuanjun persuaded the emperor's favorite Hong Jiru to intercede, securing his release. After Empress Dowager Lü's death, Pingyuanjun helped save Piyanghou again. Under Emperor Wen, Pingyuanjun was implicated in Piyanghou's crimes and committed suicide to protect his family. His son was appointed Taizhong doctor but died on a mission to the Xiongnu.

id: 史记/七十列传/郦生陆贾列传::group-004
article_path: 史记/七十列传/郦生陆贾列传
source: After hearing this, Li Sheng's eyes widened, holding a sword, he scolded the messenger and said: Hurry up! Go and tell Pei Gong again that I am a drunkard of Gaoyang, not a Confucian scholar. When the messenger saw this, he was so frightened that he dropped his business card on the ground. Then he knelt down to pick it up, quickly turned around and ran in, and reported to Pei Gong again: The guest outside is truly a hero in the world. Pei Gong immediately wiped his feet, held his spear in his hand and said: Invite the guests in! After Li Sheng entered, he bowed to Pei Gong with equal etiquette and said: "Pei Gong, you have been working outside for many years with your clothes exposed. It is very hard. You led the troops and the Chu army to conquer the tyrannical and cruel Qin Dynasty, but Pei Gong, why don't you respect yourself at all?"
target: An alternate account describes Li Shiqi's earlier meeting with Pei Gong, where he insisted on being called a "drunkard" rather than a scholar, criticized Pei Gong's disrespect, and again advised capturing Chenliu. He killed the magistrate at night, enabling Pei Gong to take the city and raise troops. Sima Qian notes that later accounts misplace Li Shiqi's role, but he confirms the details through his friendship with Pingyuanjun's son.

id: 史记/七十列传/酷吏列传::group-000
article_path: 史记/七十列传/酷吏列传
source: Confucius said: Use political laws to guide the people, and use punishments to restrain the people. The people can avoid committing crimes, but they will have no shame. If you use morality to guide the people and use etiquette to restrain the people, then the people will feel ashamed and change their ways. Laozi said: People with high morals do not show formal virtue, so they have virtue; people with low morals stick to formal virtue, so they have no actual virtue.  The more stringent the laws, the more thieves there are. Tai Shigong said: These words are credible! Han Ling is a tool of politics, not the source of political turmoil. In the past, the legal net in the world was very tight, but evil and deceitful things began to occur. When the situation reached its most serious state, officials and people actually deceived each other, reaching the point where the country was in ruins. At this time, the management of government affairs by officials is like putting out fires with salary and quelling the boiling water. How can they be competent and happy without strong and powerful people and strict laws and regulations? If people who advocate morality are allowed to do these things, they will definitely be derelict in their duties. Therefore, Confucius said: When it comes to hearing lawsuits, I am the same as everyone else; if there must be a difference, then let people stop lawsuits. Lao Tzu said: Stupid and superficial people will laugh when they hear moral words. These words are not false. After the establishment of the Han Dynasty, the square ones were destroyed and replaced by round ones, and major changes were made to the laws of the Qin Dynasty, just like cutting off the external carvings to reveal the simple and natural essence. The laws were changed from complicated to lenient and simple, just like a fishing net that could catch the fish that swallowed the boat. However, the officials' performance was pure and prosperous, and they would not do evil things, and the people were safe. It can be seen from this that the beauty of national politics lies in the generosity of the king, not in the harshness of the law. In the High Empress era, the only cruel officials were Hou Feng, who harshly oppressed the royal family, violated and humiliated meritorious ministers. After Zhu Lu's complete defeat, the court killed Hou Feng's entire family. During the reign of Emperor Xiaojing, Chao Cuo was harsh and cruel, and used magic to display his talents. As a result, the seven kingdoms of Wu, Chu, and others rebelled and vented their anger on Chao Cuo, who was killed. After that, there were people like Zhidu and Ningcheng. Zhi was a native of Yang County and served Emperor Xiaowen as a Langguan. During the reign of Emperor Jing, Zhi Du became a lieutenant general. He dared to speak out and give advice to the court, and convinced people in person at the court.
target: Laozi adds that strict laws increase theft. Tai Shigong affirms these views, noting that harsh legal nets in the past led to deceit and ruin. He observes that after the Han Dynasty simplified Qin laws, officials became honest and people peaceful, concluding that good governance relies on the ruler’s generosity, not legal severity. The narrative then details cruel officials from the Han era. During Empress Gao’s reign, Hou Feng oppressed the royal family and was executed after the Lu clan’s fall. Under Emperor Jing, Chao Cuo’s harshness sparked the Rebellion of the Seven Kingdoms, leading to his death.

id: 史记/七十列传/酷吏列传::group-001
article_path: 史记/七十列传/酷吏列传
source: Zhi was a native of Yang County and served Emperor Xiaowen as a Langguan. During the reign of Emperor Jing, Zhi Du became a lieutenant general. He dared to speak out and give advice to the court, and convinced people in person at the court. He once followed the emperor to Shanglinyuan. When Jia Ji went to the toilet, a wild boar suddenly broke into the toilet. The emperor signaled Zhidu with his eyes, but Zhidu refused to act. The emperor wanted to save Jia Ji with weapons in person. Zhi Du knelt in front of the emperor and said: If you lose a concubine, another concubine will come into the palace. Is there a shortage of people like Jia Ji in the world?
target: Zhi Du, a lieutenant, was known for his bravery and integrity. He refused to save a concubine from a boar, earning the Empress Dowager’s favor. As governor of Jinan, he executed a powerful clan, ending crime. He was fair, refused bribes, and prioritized duty over family.

id: 史记/七十列传/酷吏列传::group-002
article_path: 史记/七十列传/酷吏列传
source: King Linjiang wrote a letter of apology to the emperor and committed suicide. When Empress Dowager Dou heard the news, she became angry and used severe methods to slander Zhidu. Zhidu was dismissed from office and returned home. Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty sent an envoy with a talisman to appoint Zhidu as the governor of Yanmen, and asked him to take the road directly to Yanmen to take office and handle political affairs independently according to the actual situation. The Huns had always heard that Zhi Du had a moral integrity, and now he was guarding the border. Therefore, the Huns led their troops and left the Han Dynasty border. They did not dare to approach Yanmen until Zhi Du died. The Huns even made puppets that looked like Zhidu and asked the cavalry to run and shoot. No one could hit them, and they were so afraid of Zhidu. The Huns regarded Zhidu as a disaster. Empress Dowager Dou finally used the laws of the Han Dynasty to slander Zhidu. Emperor Jing said: Zhidu are loyal ministers. Want to free him. Queen Mother Dou said: Isn't King Linjiang a loyal minister? So they killed all Zhi. Ning Cheng was a native of Rang County and served Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty as a bodyguard. He is competitive, and when he is someone else's junior official, he must bully his superiors; when he is someone else's superior, he is as easy to control as tying wet sticks. He was cunning, cruel, willful and powerful, and gradually rose to the rank of captain of Jinan. At this time, Zhi was also the prefect of Jinan. Before this, several captains walked into the prefect's mansion, conveyed it through the lower-level officials, and then went to see the prefect, just like the county magistrate meeting the prefect. They were afraid of Zhidu and this was the way. When Ning Cheng came, he crossed Zhidu and reached his superior position. Zhidu had always heard of his reputation, so he treated him well and formed a friendly relationship with him. After a long time, Zhidu died. Later, many people in the royal family near Chang'an committed violent crimes, so the emperor summoned Ning Cheng to become a lieutenant. His governance methods were imitated by Zhidu. His integrity was not as good as Zhidu, but everyone in the royal family was afraid of the powerful. When Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty came to the throne, Ning Cheng was appointed internal historian. Relatives often slandered Ning Cheng's shortcomings, and he was punished according to law by shaving his hair and binding his neck with iron. At this time, Jiu Qing was executed for crimes that deserved death, and rarely received ordinary punishments, but Ning Cheng suffered extremely heavy punishments. He said: "If you can't be a high-ranking official of two thousand dan in office, and you can't make 10 million gu of money in business, how can you compare with others?" So he borrowed money to buy more than a thousand hectares of irrigated land and rented it out to poor people. Thousands of families worked for him and were enslaved. A few years later, I encountered amnesty. He already has several thousand kilograms of gold in his family. He specializes in fighting injustices and grasping the shortcomings of officials. When he goes out, he is followed by dozens of people on horseback.
target: He later arrested King Linjiang, who committed suicide, leading to Zhi Du’s dismissal and eventual execution by Empress Dowager Dou. Ning Cheng, a captain, was cunning and cruel, bullying superiors and subordinates alike. He imitated Zhi Du but lacked his integrity, though he intimidated the royal family. Under Emperor Wu, he was punished but later became wealthy through land rental, wielding influence over officials.

source: A few years later, I encountered amnesty. He already has several thousand kilograms of gold in his family. He specializes in fighting injustices and grasping the shortcomings of officials. When he goes out, he is followed by dozens of people on horseback. His authority to drive the people was greater than that of the county governor. Zhou Yangyou, his father Zhao Jian was named Zhou Yanghou as the uncle of Huainan King Liu Chang, so his surname was Zhou Yang. Zhou Yang was appointed Lang Guan because he was a relative, serving Emperor Xiaowen and Emperor Xiaojing. During the reign of Emperor Jing, Zhou Yangyou became a Langguan. After Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty came to the throne, officials handled political affairs and advocated following the law and acting prudently. However, Zhou Yangyou was the most tyrannical, cruel, proud and indulgent among the officials of the two thousand stone level. If someone he likes commits a capital crime, he will bend the law to make that person live; if he hates someone, he will bend the law to kill him. Whichever county he serves as an official, he must eliminate the wealthy families in that county. When he was the prefect of the county, he regarded the captain as the county magistrate. As a captain, he would definitely bully the prefect and usurp his power. He and Ji An were both ruthless people, and Sima An was good at using laws and regulations to harm others, and both were officials with two thousand stones. However, Ji An, Sima Anruo, and Zhou Yangyou did not dare to share the seats and rails with Zhou Yangyou in the same carriage. Zhou Yangyou later became the captain of Hedong County. He often fought for power with the prefect Shentu Gong and complained to each other. As a result, Shen Gong was found guilty. However, he insisted on morality and refused to accept the punishment and committed suicide. Zhou Yangyou was sentenced to abandoning the market. After Ning Cheng and Zhou Yang You, political affairs became more complicated, and the people used cunning and deceptive means to deal with the law. Most officials managed government affairs just like Ning Cheng and Zhou Yang You. Zhao Yu was a native of Zhuxian County. He was appointed as an official in the capital government as an assistant historian. Because of his integrity, he was promoted to an official historian and served Zhou Yafu. Zhou Yafu became the prime minister, and Zhao Yu became the prime minister. Everyone in the prime minister's house praised him for his integrity and fairness. But Zhou Yafu did not reuse him and said: I know that Zhao Yu has outstanding talents, but he enforces the law very harshly and cannot be an official in the upper-level government. During the reign of Emperor Wu, Zhao Yu accumulated merit due to his clerical work and was gradually promoted to censor. The emperor thought he was talented and was promoted to Taishi doctor. He and Zhang Tang jointly formulated various laws and made "knowledge laws" to allow officials to monitor and report each other. The laws in the Han Dynasty became increasingly strict, probably starting from this time. Zhang Tang is from Du County.
target: Zhou Yangyou, a relative of the Huainan king, was tyrannical, bending laws to favor friends and kill enemies. He clashed with the governor Shentu Gong, leading to Shentu’s suicide and Zhou’s execution. Zhao Yu, a censor, co-created strict laws with Zhang Tang, increasing legal severity. Zhang Tang, from Du County, showed early talent in legal cases. He befriended powerful figures and rose to censor, crafting laws to control officials. He was cunning, pretending to admire Confucianism while using harsh methods. He handled major rebellions, minted coins, and monopolized salt and iron, draining state resources. His arrogance led to his downfall: after conflicts with officials and accusations of corruption, he committed suicide, leaving minimal wealth. His mother refused a lavish burial, and the emperor later executed his accusers.

source: The few criminals who were not caught fled to nearby counties. When they were hunted down and captured, it was spring. Wang Wenshu stamped his feet and sighed: Alas! If winter lasts another month, my business will be done. This is how he likes to kill and show his power and does not care for the people. The emperor heard this and thought he had talent, so he was promoted to lieutenant. He still followed Hanoi's approach in governing political affairs, and brought in famous evildoers and cunning officials to work with him, including Yang Jieyu and Ma Wu in Hanoi, and Yang Gan and Cheng Xin in Guanzhong. Because Yi Zong was the internal historian, Wang Wenshu was afraid of him, so he did not dare to implement harsh policies arbitrarily. After Yi Zong died and Zhang Tang failed, Wang Wenshu was promoted to Tingwei and Yin Qi became lieutenant. Yin Qi was a native of Chiping, Dongjun. He was promoted from a clerk to a censor. Serving Zhang Tang, Zhang Tang repeatedly praised him for his integrity and bravery, and assigned him to supervise the arrest of thieves. The people he wanted to kill did not avoid powerful and royal relatives. He was promoted to captain of the pass and his reputation surpassed that of Ning Cheng. The emperor thought he had talent and promoted him to lieutenant, while the lives of officials and civilians became even more difficult. Yin Qi was rigid in doing things and did not pay attention to etiquette. The strong and vicious officials were hidden, and the kind officials could not handle political affairs effectively on their own, so most of the political affairs were neglected and sentenced. The emperor changed Wang Wenshu's position to lieutenant, and Yang Pu became the lord captain by virtue of his harshness and cruelty. Yang Pu was from Yiyang and became a minor official as a thousand-year-old man.
target: Yi Zong, a former robber, became a harsh official, executing hundreds in Dingxiang and terrorizing Nanyang. Wang Wenshu, a tomb robber, rose to governor, using informants and brutal tactics to eliminate thieves, boasting he needed more winter days to kill. He later became lieutenant, flattering the powerful while crushing the weak. He committed suicide after corruption charges. Yin Qi, a rigid official, killed without mercy, dying in poverty.

source: However, the scattered soldiers escaped and gathered into a party again, occupying dangerous mountains and rivers to cause trouble, often living in groups, and there was nothing they could do. So the imperial court promulgated the "Senior Law", which said that a group of thieves occurred but the officials did not notice it, or they discovered it but did not capture the prescribed amount, and the relevant officials from two thousand dan to the smallest should be put to death. After that, petty officials were afraid of being executed. Even if there were thieves, they did not dare to report them. They were afraid that they would not be caught, and they would be sentenced for breaking the law and incriminate the higher-level officials. The higher-level officials also asked them not to report it. Therefore, there are more thieves, hiding from each other, playing with words, and evading legal sanctions.
target: The text concludes with a surge in banditry, leading to the “Senior Law” punishing officials for failing to catch thieves, which ironically increased crime.

source: He was dismissed from office midway, and later became You Fufeng. Because he was resentful of his subordinate Chengxin, Chengxin fled and hid in Shanglin Garden. The magistrate of Yi County was sent to kill Chengxin. When officials and soldiers shot Chengxin, they shot at the gate of Shanglinyuan. Jiaxuan was handed over to the judge for sentencing. The judge believed that he had committed treason and sentenced him to genocide, so Jiaxuan committed suicide. Du Zhou was appointed. Du Zhou was a native of Du Yan, Nanyang. Yi Zong became the governor of Nanyang and regarded Du Zhou as his right assistant and recommended him to be the official of the imperial court. He served Zhang Tang. Zhang Tang repeatedly said that he was extremely talented and his official position was promoted to censor. He was assigned to examine the cases of deserted border soldiers, and many of them were sentenced to death. The things he reported were in line with the emperor's wishes, and he was appointed. He was succeeded by Tongjiaxuan, and was appointed Zhongcheng for more than ten years. Du Zhou's management of political affairs was similar to that of reducing propaganda, but he was cautious in handling affairs, slow in making decisions, loose in appearance, and deep in heart. Jia Xuan became Zuo Neishi, and Du Zhou became Tingwei. He imitated Zhang Tang in governing political affairs, and was good at spying on the emperor's intentions. If the emperor wants to exclude someone, he will take advantage of the opportunity to frame him; if the emperor wants to release him, he will imprison him for a long time pending trial and secretly reveal his grievances. Some of the disciples scolded Du Zhou, saying: "I decided the case fairly for the emperor. I did not follow the five-foot law, but decided the case based on the emperor's will."
target: Jiaxuan and Du Zhou continued harsh practices, with Du Zhou justifying decisions based on the emperor’s will rather than law. Tai Shigong reflects that while some cruel officials like Zhi Du were principled, others like Du Zhou were sycophantic, leading to legal decay and corruption.

source: King Han Xin of Han was the concubine grandson of the original King Xiang of Han. He was eight feet five inches tall. When Xiang Liang supported King Chu Huai, the descendant of King Chu, Yan, Qi, Zhao, and Wei had already established their own kings. Only South Korea had no successor, so Hancheng, Lord Hengyang among the Korean princes, was made King of Han, hoping to appease the land of the original South Korea. Xiang Liang was defeated and died in Dingtao, and Han Cheng defected to King Huai of Chu. When Pei Gong led the army to attack Yangcheng, he ordered Zhang Liang to surrender the original territory of South Korea as the Korean Situ. He obtained Han Xin and appointed him as the general of South Korea. He led his army to follow Pei Gong into Wuguan. Pei Gong was appointed as the king of Han. Han Xin followed Pei Gong into Hanzhong and persuaded the king of Han: "Xiang Yu has sealed all his subordinates in the areas near the Central Plains, but you, the king, are in this far away place. This is tantamount to demotion!" The soldiers under your command are all from the east of Mount Laoshan. They stand on tiptoe, eager to return to their hometown, so that while they are strong and strong, they can march eastward and compete for the world. When the King of Han returned to pacify the Three Qin Dynasties, he agreed to make Han Xin the King of Han. He first appointed him as Taiwei Han to lead troops to capture the old land of Korea. The princes and kings granted by Xiang Yu all went to their respective fiefdoms. King Han Cheng of Han did not follow Xiang Yu in the battle and had no military exploits, so he was not sent to the fiefdom and instead made him a prince. When he heard that the king of Han sent Han Xin to attack Han, he ordered Zheng Chang, the magistrate of Wu County when he was traveling in Wu, to be the king of Han to resist the Han army. In the second year of Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty, Han Xin pacified more than a dozen cities in Korea. When the King of Han arrived in Henan, Han Xin violently attacked King Zheng Chang of Han in Yangcheng. When Zheng Chang surrendered, the King of Han made Han Xin the King of Han, and he often led the Korean army to follow the King of Han. In the third year of Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty, the King of Han withdrew from Xingyang, and King Han Xin, Zhou Ke and others guarded Xingyang. When the Chu army conquered Xingyang, Han Xin surrendered to the Chu army, escaped soon, and surrendered to the King of Han. The King of Han again made him King of Han, and finally followed the King of Han to defeat Xiang Yu and pacify the world. In the spring of the fifth year of Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty, Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty cut the talisman with Han Xin as a letter and officially named him King of Han, with the fiefdom in Yingchuan. In the spring of the next year, Emperor Gaozu thought that Han Xin was strong and brave, and his fief Yingchuan was close to Gongxian and Luoyang in the north, Wanxian and Yexian in the south, and the important town of Huaiyang in the east. These were all strategic places in the world, so he issued an edict and ordered Han Xin, the king of Han, to move to the north of Taiyuan to prepare for resistance to the Xiongnu and establish Jinyang as his capital.
target: King Han Xin of Han, a concubine grandson of the original King Xiang of Han, was a tall man. Initially, after Xiang Liang's defeat, Han Cheng was made King of Han to appease the region. Han Xin later served under Pei Gong (future Emperor Gaozu), persuading him to march eastward. He was eventually made King of Han after capturing Korean cities and defeating rival King Zheng Chang. However, fearing execution due to suspicions of betrayal, Han Xin allied with the Xiongnu, rebelled, and attacked Taiyuan. Emperor Gaozu personally defeated him, and Han Xin fled to the Xiongnu. He continued to lead Xiongnu forces against Han until General Chai killed him in battle. His descendants later surrendered to Han and were granted marquisates, though some titles were eventually revoked.

source: Last spring, the Han Dynasty executed the entire family of Huaiyin Marquis Han Xin, and in the summer, they killed Peng Yue. This was Empress Lu's plan. Now the emperor was seriously ill and handed over all state affairs to Queen Lu. And Queen Lu was a woman who always wanted to find an excuse to kill princes, kings with different surnames and ministers with high achievements. So Lu Wan still refused to go to Beijing, claiming to be ill. Lu Wan's subordinates and ministers all fled and hid. But some of Lu Wan's words leaked out. Marquis Piyang heard about it and reported all this to the emperor, who became even more angry. Later, the Han Dynasty got some surrendered Huns and said that Zhang Sheng had fled to the Huns and was the envoy of King Yan. So the emperor said: Lu Wan has really rebelled! He sent Fan Kuai to attack Yan. King Lu Wan of Yan settled all his family members and thousands of cavalry under the Great Wall, waiting for an opportunity, hoping that after the emperor recovered from his illness, he would come to Beijing to apologize in person. In April, Emperor Gaozu passed away, and Lu Wan led his men to flee to the Huns, who named him King of Donghulu. Lu Wan was invaded and plundered by the Huns, and always wanted to return to the Han Dynasty. More than a year later, Lu Wan died in Xiongnu. When he was the Queen of Gao, Lu Wan's wife and children escaped from the Xiongnu and returned to the Han Dynasty. Just as the Queen of Gao was seriously ill and could not see each other, they lived in King Yan's palace in Beijing and planned to hold a banquet to see each other after they recovered from the illness. But Empress Gao passed away unexpectedly and could not meet. Lu Wan's wife also died of illness. In the sixth year of Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty, Lu Tazhi, the grandson of Lu Wan, surrendered to the Han Dynasty as King of Donghu and was named Marquis of Yagu. Chen Xi was from Wanqu, and he didn't know why he followed Gaozu in the first place. In the winter of the seventh year of Emperor Gaozu, King Han Xin of Han rebelled and fled to the Xiongnu. The emperor returned to Pingcheng and made Chen Xi a marquis. As the prime minister of Zhao State, he led the border defense troops of Zhao State and Dai State. The troops guarding the border in this area were under his jurisdiction. Chen Xi once asked for leave to return home. When passing through the State of Zhao, Zhou Chang, the Prime Minister of Zhao State, saw that Chen Xi's accompanying guests had more than a thousand cars and filled all the official residences in Handan. Chen Xi treated his guests with the same etiquette among common people, and he was always humble and respectful, and he treated others with humility. When Chen Xi returned to Dai, Zhou Chang asked to come to Beijing to see him. After meeting the emperor, he told the whole story that Chen Xi had many guests and had been in sole control of the military for several years. He was afraid that something might happen. The emperor ordered people to investigate Chen Xi's guests for their violations of laws and regulations regarding property and property, many of which implicated Chen Xi. Chen Xi was very frightened and secretly sent guests to Wang Huang and Manqiu Chen to inform them. In July of the tenth year of Emperor Gaozu, the Supreme Emperor passed away. The emperor sent someone to summon Chen Wei to Beijing, but Chen Wei said that his condition was serious. In September, he rebelled with Wang Huang and others, proclaimed himself the king of Dai, and plundered Zhao and Dai two places. After the emperor heard about it, he pardoned all Zhao and Dai officials who were implicated by Chen Xi and committed plunder. The emperor went there in person and said happily after arriving at Handan: "Chen Xi will not occupy Zhangshui in the south and guard Handan in the north. From this we know that he will not do anything." Zhao Xiangguo submitted a memorial requesting that the governors and lieutenants of Changshan be beheaded, saying: Changshan had a total of twenty-five cities, but Chen Xi rebelled and lost twenty of them. The emperor asked: Have the county guards and county lieutenants rebelled? Zhao Xiangguo replied: No rebellion. The emperor said: This is because of insufficient troops. They were pardoned and their duties as captains were restored. The emperor asked Zhou Chang: Does Zhao still have generals who can lead troops to fight?
target: Lu Wan, a close childhood friend and neighbor of Emperor Gaozu, was exceptionally favored, serving as a general and Taiwei. After the empire was pacified, he was made King of Yan, the most favored among non-Liu princes. During Chen Xi's rebellion, Lu Wan sent Zhang Sheng to the Xiongnu, who secretly aided Chen Xi. Lu Wan later realized this and continued to prolong the war. When Emperor Gaozu discovered Lu Wan's collusion with Chen Xi and the Xiongnu, he sent Fan Kuai to attack Yan. Lu Wan fled to the Xiongnu, becoming King of Donghulu, but always wished to return. After Gaozu's death, Lu Wan died among the Xiongnu. His family later returned to Han, but his wife died before meeting Empress Gao. His grandson eventually surrendered and was made a marquis. Chen Xi, a marquis and prime minister of Zhao, commanded border troops. Suspected by Zhou Chang, he feared investigation and rebelled with Wang Huang, proclaiming himself King of Dai. Emperor Gaozu personally campaigned, pardoning many officials and rewarding Zhao generals. The Han army defeated Chen Xi's forces, killing his generals and eventually Chen Xi himself in Lingqiu.

source: In the winter of the eleventh year of Emperor Gaozu's reign, the Han army attacked and killed Chen Xi's generals Hou Chang and Wang Huang at Quni City. They also defeated Chen Xi's general Zhang Chun in Liaocheng, killing more than 10,000 people. Taiwei Zhou Bo marched and pacified Taiyuan and Daijun. In December, the emperor personally led an army to attack Dongyuan, but failed to capture it. The rebel soldiers insulted the emperor. Soon Dongyuan surrendered. All soldiers who insulted the emperor were beheaded, and other soldiers who did not insult were sentenced to tattoos and tattoos on their foreheads. Change Dongyuan's name to Zhending. All Wang Huang and Manqiuchen's men who were offered rewards were captured alive, so Chen Xi's army was completely defeated. The emperor returned to Luoyang. The emperor said: Daijun is located to the north of Changshan Mountain, but Zhao Guo controls it from the south of the mountain. It is too far away. So he named his son Liu Yuan the king of Dai, made Zhongdu the capital, and Daijun and Yanmen were all subordinate to Daiguo. In the winter of the twelfth year of Emperor Gaozu's reign, Fan Kuai's soldiers chased Chen Kuai to Lingqiu and beheaded him. Tai Shigong said: Han Xin and Lu Wan were not a family that had always accumulated good deeds. Instead, they were lucky enough to improvise and succeeded through deception and violence. Just as the Han Dynasty was just established, they were able to divide the territory and make the south the king. Internally, it was suspected because of its strong power, and externally, it relied on foreigners for assistance. Therefore, he was increasingly alienated by the emperor, found himself in danger, had no choice but to surrender to the Huns. Isn't it sad? Chen Xi was a native of Liang. When he was young, he always praised and admired Wei Gongzi Xinlingjun. Later, he led the army to guard the border, gathered guests, and treated virtuous corporals, and his reputation exceeded his actual status. Zhou Chang doubted him, and many mistakes occurred from here. Fearing that disaster would come, the treacherous villain took the opportunity to speak again, and finally fell into a treasonous situation. Oh, how sad! It can be seen from this that the maturity and success or failure of the plan have a profound impact on a person!
target: The Grand Historian comments that Han Xin and Lu Wan, lacking accumulated virtue, succeeded through deception and violence during the Han's founding. Suspected internally and relying on foreigners, they were alienated and forced to surrender to the Xiongnu—a tragic fate. Chen Xi, admiring Lord Xinling, gathered guests and exceeded his reputation. Zhou Chang's suspicions, fear of disaster, and treacherous whispers led to his rebellion. Thus, the success or failure of plans profoundly impacts a person's destiny.

source: Han Anguo, the imperial censor, was a native of Cheng'an County, Liang State, and later settled in Suiyang. I once studied "Han Feizi" and the doctrines of Zajia from Mr. Tian in Zouxian County. He served King Xiao of Liang and served as a middle official. When the Seven Kingdoms of Wu and Chu rebelled, King Xiao of Liang sent Han Anguo and Zhang Yu as generals to resist the Wu army on the eastern front. Because Zhang Yu fought hard and Han Anguo defended firmly, the Wu army could not cross Liang's defense line. The Wu Chu rebellion was put down, and the reputations of Han Anguo and Zhang Yu became prominent. King Xiao of Liang was the half-brother of Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty. Empress Dowager Dou liked him very much and allowed him to have the power to nominate the Prime Minister of Liang and two thousand stone-level officials. The scene of his coming in and out and playing games was more like that of an emperor than that of a minister. When Emperor Jing heard about it, he was very unhappy. Empress Dowager Dou knew that Emperor Jing was dissatisfied, so she became angry with the envoys sent by Liang Guo and refused to receive them. Instead, she asked them about what King Liang had done. At that time, Han Anguo was the envoy of the Liang Kingdom, so he went to see the eldest princess and cried: Why can't the Queen Mother clearly understand the filial piety of the Liang King as a son and the loyalty as a minister?
target: Han Anguo, a native of Liang State and a student of Han Feizi and Zajia, served as a middle official under King Xiao of Liang. During the Rebellion of the Seven Kingdoms, he and Zhang Yu defended Liang’s eastern front, preventing the Wu army from crossing. After the rebellion, their reputations grew. King Xiao of Liang, favored by Empress Dowager Dou, acted with imperial-like grandeur, angering Emperor Jing. As Liang’s envoy, Han Anguo pleaded with the eldest princess, explaining King Liang’s filial piety and loyalty during the rebellion, and his use of imperial gifts to display the emperor’s favor. The empress dowager relented, and Emperor Jing reconciled, rewarding Han Anguo generously.

id: 史记/七十列传/韩长孺列传::group-001
article_path: 史记/七十列传/韩长孺列传
source: Why was the King of Liang filial as a son and loyal as a minister, but the Queen Mother showed no mercy? The eldest princess told Queen Mother Dou these words in detail, and Queen Mother Dou happily said: I will tell the emperor these words for him. After telling the story, the knot in Emperor Jing's heart was relieved. He took off his hat and confessed his mistake to the Queen Mother, saying: We brothers cannot advise each other, which actually adds sorrow to the Queen Mother. So he received all the envoys sent by King Liang and rewarded them heavily. From then on, King Liang became even more favored. Empress Dowager Dou and Princess Dachang rewarded Han Anguo with property worth about a thousand gold. As a result, his reputation became prominent and he became connected with the imperial court. Later, Han Anguo was convicted of breaking the law, and Meng County jailer Tian Jia insulted Han Anguo. Han Anguo said: Will the ashes of death not resurface? Tian Jia said: If it burns again, just urinate to put it out. Soon after, the position of domestic history of Liang was vacant. The Han court sent envoys to appoint Han Anguo as domestic history of Liang. He started as a prisoner and served as an official with a rank of 2,000 stone. Tian Jia abandoned his official position and ran away. Han Anguo said: If Tian Jia doesn't come back and take office, I will destroy your clan. Tian Jia took off his clothes and exposed his chest to apologize. Han Anguo smiled and said: You can pee now! Do people like you deserve my punishment? Finally treat him nicely. When the internal history of Liang was vacant, King Xiao of Liang had just recruited Gongsun Gui from Qi. He liked him very much and planned to request his appointment as internal history. Queen Mother Dou heard this and ordered King Xiao of Liang to appoint Han Anguo as internal history. Gongsun Gui and Yang Sheng lobbied King Xiao of Liang and asked him to ask Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty to be the heir to the throne and increase the fiefdom. They were afraid that the court ministers would not agree and secretly sent people to assassinate the advisors in power. Even after Yuan Ang, the former Prime Minister of Wu State, was killed, Emperor Jing heard about the plans of Gongsun Gui, Yang Sheng and others, so he sent envoys to capture Gongsun Gui and Yang Sheng. More than a dozen groups of Han sent envoys to the Liang State, and a nationwide search was conducted from Liang State Prime Minister down, but still no one was caught for more than a month.
target: Later, Han Anguo was imprisoned for a crime but became Liang’s domestic history after a jailer’s insult. He forgave the jailer. When Liang’s internal history post opened, the empress dowager ordered King Liang to appoint Han Anguo. Gongsun Gui and Yang Sheng plotted to make King Liang heir, assassinating Yuan Ang. Emperor Jing sent envoys to capture them, but they hid in King Liang’s palace. Han Anguo warned King Liang of the dangers, citing historical precedents, and the king surrendered the conspirators, who committed suicide. This resolved the crisis, and Han Anguo gained favor. After King Xiao’s death, Han Anguo lost his post but later became a chief minister.
