source: Why is this so? Because in governing the world, public affairs cannot be compromised by private affairs. If you want to say: Even if you are your biological father, how do you know that he will not turn into a tiger? How do even brothers know he won't turn into a wolf? Now, Your Majesty, you are among the princes, but you listened to the false words of an evil minister, violated the emperor's prohibition, and obstructed the sage's law. Because of the Queen Mother, the Emperor cannot bear to use laws against you.
target: During the Xiongnu peace debate, he argued against war, favoring peace. The emperor agreed.

id: 史记/七十列传/韩长孺列传::group-003
article_path: 史记/七十列传/韩长孺列传
source: The Tingwei judged him that he should be beheaded as he walked to avoid the enemy and waited. Wang Hui secretly gave Tian Fu a thousand gold coins. Tian Fu did not dare to plead with the emperor, but said to the Queen Mother: Wang Hui first proposed the plan of Mayi to lure the enemy, but now it failed and he killed Wang Hui. This was to avenge the Huns. When the emperor met with the Queen Mother, the Queen Mother told the emperor what the prime minister had said. The emperor said: The person who first proposed the Mayi plan was Wang Hui, so he mobilized hundreds of thousands of soldiers from all over the world to follow his words and attack the Huns. Besides, even if the Chanyu cannot be captured this time, if Wang Hui's troops attack the Huns' military supplies, they may still gain something, which can comfort the hearts of the soldiers.
target: In the Mayi incident, Nie Wengyi lured the Xiongnu, but the plan failed when the Chanyu retreated. Wang Hui, who proposed the plan, was executed despite pleas.

id: 史记/七十列传/韩长孺列传::group-004
article_path: 史记/七十列传/韩长孺列传
source: Now I cannot apologize to the people of the world without killing Wang Hui. When Wang Hui heard this, he committed suicide. Han Anguo was a man of great strategy, and his intelligence was enough to cater to the world, but he did so out of a loyal heart. He is greedy for money. Those he recommended were all honest scholars who were more worthy than himself. In the Liang Kingdom, Hu Sui, Zang Gu, and Zhi Ta were recommended, and they were all famous scholars in the world. The scholars also praised and admired him very much, and even the emperor thought that he was a talented person in governing the country. Han Anguo served as the imperial censor for more than four years. When the Prime Minister Tian Fu passed away, Han Anguo acted as the prime minister. He fell off the car while guiding the emperor's car and became lame.
target: Han Anguo, known for strategy and loyalty but greedy, recommended many scholars. He served as imperial censor for four years, then as lieutenant and guard.

id: 史记/七十列传/韩长孺列传::group-005
article_path: 史记/七十列传/韩长孺列传
source: More than a year later, he was transferred to the rank of guard. The chariot general Wei Qing attacked the Xiongnu, marched from Shanggu County, and defeated the Xiongnu in Longcheng. General Li Guang was captured by the Xiongnu and escaped; Gongsun Ao's soldiers suffered heavy casualties; they all deserved beheading, but later paid for their sins and became commoners. The next year, the Xiongnu invaded the border and killed the governor of western Liaoning. When they invaded Yanmen, they killed and took thousands of people captive. The chariot and cavalry general Wei Qing sent troops to pursue them and marched out of Yanmen County. Weiwei Han Anguo served as general Caiguan and was stationed in Yuyang. Han Anguo captured prisoners, who confessed that the Huns had gone far away. Han Anguo immediately wrote to the emperor saying that it was the farming season and requested that the army be temporarily suspended. After stopping their military garrison for more than a month, the Xiongnu invaded Shanggu and Yuyang on a large scale.
target: After Wei Qing’s campaigns, Han Anguo was stationed in Yuyang but was deceived by prisoners, leading to Xiongnu raids.

id: 史记/七十列传/韩长孺列传::group-006
article_path: 史记/七十列传/韩长孺列传
source: The Huns captured more than a thousand people, livestock and property and left. After the emperor heard the news, he was very angry and sent an envoy to blame Han Anguo. Tiaohan Anguo moved further east and stationed in Youbeiping. Because at that time the prisoners of the Huns confessed that they wanted to invade the east. Han Anguo initially served as a royal censor and a general protecting the army, but was gradually ostracized and alienated, demoted and demoted; while the newly favored young generals Wei Qing and others had military merits and were even more favored by the emperor. After being alienated, Han Anguo felt very frustrated; he led troops to garrison and was bullied by the Xiongnu. He suffered many losses and casualties, and felt very guilty. He hoped to return to the court, but he was even transferred to the east to garrison, and he felt depressed. A few months later, he fell ill and vomited blood and died. Han Anguo died in the second year of Yuanshuo. Tai Shigong said: Hu Sui and I reviewed the calendar and observed Han Changru's behavior. Judging from Hu Sui's deep and reserved kindness, the world said that Liang Guo has many loyal and loyal elders. This is indeed true! Hu Sui did his best as an official, and the emperor was about to rely on him to become the prime minister of the Han Dynasty, but Hu Sui died again.
target: Demoted and alienated, he died of illness in 123 BCE. Sima Qian praised his loyalty and the integrity of Liang’s elders.

id: 史记/七十列传/魏公子列传::group-000
article_path: 史记/七十列传/魏公子列传
source: Mr. Wei's name is Wuji, he is the youngest son of King Wei Zhao and the half-brother of King Wei Anli. After the death of King Zhao, King Anli came to the throne and named the son Lord Xinling. At that time, Fan Sui fled from Wei to Qin and served as Qin Prime Minister. Because he was resentful that Wei Qi Qu beat him almost to death, he sent Qin troops to besiege Daliang and defeated the Wei troops stationed in Huayang, causing Wei general Mang Mao to flee in defeat. The king of Wei and his son were very anxious about this matter. The prince was kind, generous, courteous and virtuous. Regardless of whether the scholars had talent or talent, he interacted with them courteously. He never dared to look down on the scholars because of his wealth. Therefore, scholars from thousands of miles around rushed to join him, and he attracted 3,000 diners. At that time, the princes and states did not dare to invade Wei for more than ten years because of the virtuous son and the large number of guests.
target: Lord Xinling, named Wei Wuji, was the youngest son of King Wei Zhao and half-brother of King Wei Anli. After King Zhao's death, King Anli enfeoffed him as Lord Xinling. Fan Sui, who fled to Qin and became prime minister, resented Wei's mistreatment and led Qin forces to besiege Daliang, defeating Wei troops at Huayang. The king and lord were deeply troubled. The lord was generous, humble, and virtuous, attracting three thousand retainers from across the realm. For over a decade, no feudal lords dared invade Wei due to his reputation.

id: 史记/七十列传/魏公子列传::group-001
article_path: 史记/七十列传/魏公子列传
source: At that time, the princes and states did not dare to invade Wei for more than ten years because of the virtuous son and the large number of guests. One time, the young master and the King of Wei were playing chess, and an alarm came from the northern border, saying that Zhao State was sending troops to invade and would enter the border. The king of Wei immediately put down his chess pieces and summoned the ministers to discuss countermeasures. The prince dissuaded the king of Wei and said: "The king of Zhao is just hunting, not invading the border." Then he continued to play chess with King Wei as if nothing had happened. But the king of Wei was frightened and did not focus on playing chess at all. After a while, news came from the north saying: King Zhao is just hunting, not invading the border. King Wei was greatly surprised when he heard this and asked: How did the young master know this? The young master replied: One of my diners can go deep into the secrets of King Zhao. If King Zhao takes any action, he will report it to me immediately, so I know about it. From then on, the king of Wei was afraid of the young master's talents and did not dare to use him to handle national affairs. There was a hermit named Hou Ying in the state of Wei. He was seventy years old and came from a poor family. He was the gatekeeper of the east gate of Daliang City. When the prince heard about this man, he sent someone to see him and wanted to give him a generous gift. But Hou Ying refused to accept it, saying: I have cultivated my moral character and insisted on integrity for decades, but after all, I cannot accept the prince's financial gift because I am a poor janitor.
target: Once, while playing chess with the king, a false alarm about a Zhao invasion arose. The lord correctly identified it as a hunting expedition, revealing he had a spy in Zhao's court. This frightened the king, who thereafter feared the lord's abilities and refused him state affairs.

id: 史记/七十列传/魏公子列传::group-002
article_path: 史记/七十列传/魏公子列传
source: From then on, the king of Wei was afraid of the young master's talents and did not dare to use him to handle national affairs. There was a hermit named Hou Ying in the state of Wei. He was seventy years old and came from a poor family. He was the gatekeeper of the east gate of Daliang City. When the prince heard about this man, he sent someone to see him and wanted to give him a generous gift. But Hou Ying refused to accept it, saying: I have cultivated my moral character and insisted on integrity for decades, but after all, I cannot accept the prince's financial gift because I am a poor janitor. The young master then held a banquet and entertained the guests. After everyone came and sat down, the young master took the carriage, horses and entourage, vacated the left seat in the carriage, and went to the east gate in person to greet Mr. Hou. Mr. Hou tidied up his shabby clothes and hats, then got into the car and sat in the distinguished seat vacated by the young master. He had no intention of being humble at all, and wanted to observe the young master's attitude. But the young master held the horse's reins more respectfully. Mr. Hou said to the young master again: I have a friend who is in the slaughterhouse in the market. I would like to give him a ride and take me to visit him. The young master immediately drove to the market. Mr. Hou got out of the car and went to meet his friend Zhu Hai. He squinted at the young master and deliberately stood there for a long time, chatting with his friend and secretly observing the young master. The young master's face became more cheerful. At this time, the generals, prime ministers, clan ministers and distinguished guests from Wei State were all sitting in the hall, waiting for the young master to raise their glasses to start the banquet. Everyone in the market saw the young master holding the reins and driving the car for Mr. Hou. The young master's entourage secretly scolded Mr. Hou. Mr. Hou saw that the young master's expression remained unchanged, so he said goodbye to his friend and got into the car. After arriving home, the young master led Mr. Hou to sit on the upper seat and introduced Mr. Hou to all the guests with praise. All the guests in the hall were surprised. When everyone was drunk, the young master stood up and walked to Mr. Hou to toast his birthday. Mr. Hou took the opportunity and said to the young master: Today I, Hou Ying, have made things difficult for the young master. I am just a man who holds the gate and locks it at the east gate of the city, but the young master has resigned himself to carriages and horses and personally welcomes me in the public. I should not visit my friend again, but today the young master condescends to accompany me to visit him. But I also wanted to make the young master famous, so I deliberately stopped the young master's carriage and horse in the market for a long time, and used the opportunity to visit friends to observe the young master. As a result, the young master became more humble. People in the market thought that I was a villain, but they thought that the young master was a noble person who could treat the corporal with courtesy. After the banquet ended, Mr. Hou became the prince's distinguished guest. Mr. Hou said to the young master: The butcher Zhu Hai I visited is a virtuous man, but people don't understand him, so he is hidden among the butchers.
target: The lord befriended Hou Ying, a seventy-year-old gatekeeper, by personally driving his carriage to fetch him for a banquet. Hou Ying tested the lord's humility by sitting in the honored seat and visiting a friend, Zhu Hai, in the market. The lord remained respectful, winning Hou Ying's loyalty. Hou Ying later recommended Zhu Hai as a capable man.

id: 史记/七十列传/魏公子列传::group-003
article_path: 史记/七十列传/魏公子列传
source: I am just a man who holds the gate and locks it at the east gate of the city, but the young master has resigned himself to carriages and horses and personally welcomes me in the public. I should not visit my friend again, but today the young master condescends to accompany me to visit him. But I also wanted to make the young master famous, so I deliberately stopped the young master's carriage and horse in the market for a long time, and used the opportunity to visit friends to observe the young master. As a result, the young master became more humble. After the banquet ended, Mr. Hou became the prince's distinguished guest. Mr. Hou said to the young master: The butcher Zhu Hai I visited is a virtuous man, but people don't understand him, so he is hidden among the butchers. The young master went to visit Zhu Hai many times, but Zhu Hai deliberately refused to pay his respects and thank him. The young master thought this person was strange. In the 20th year of King Anli of Wei, King Zhao of Qin had defeated the Zhao army in Changping, and then marched to besiege Handan. The young master's sister is the wife of King Zhao Huiwen's brother Pingyuan Jun. She has sent letters to the King of Wei and the young master many times, asking for reinforcements from Wei. The king of Wei sent General Jin Bi to lead an army of 100,000 people to rescue Zhao. After King Zhao of Qin learned the news, he sent an envoy to warn King Wei: I am about to capture Zhao. It is only a matter of time. Who among the princes dares to save Zhao will definitely mobilize troops to attack it first after capturing Zhao. The King of Wei was very frightened, so he sent people to stop Jin Bi from advancing further. He left the army to camp in Yecheng, nominally to save Zhao, but in fact he adopted a two-sided strategy to wait and see how the situation would develop. The envoys of Lord Pingyuan came to Wei one after another, and they were often in urgent need. They blamed Mr. Wei and said: "The reason why I, Zhao Sheng, voluntarily rely on Wei to marry with Wei is because you have noble moral principles and can enthusiastically help others out of danger."
target: In the twentieth year of King Anli's reign, Qin besieged Handan, Zhao's capital. The lord's sister, married to Zhao's Lord Pingyuan, begged Wei for aid. King Wei sent General Jin Bi with 100,000 troops but halted at Ye, fearing Qin's threats. Despite the lord's pleas, the king refused to advance. Determined to die with Zhao, the lord gathered retainers and chariots to attack Qin.

id: 史记/七十列传/魏公子列传::group-004
article_path: 史记/七十列传/魏公子列传
source: Because the King of Wei was afraid of Qin, he always refused to listen to the prince's opinion. The prince estimated that he would not be able to obtain the consent of the King of Wei to send troops after all, so he decided that he could not let Zhao fall while alive, so he invited guests, gathered more than a hundred chariots, and planned to rush to the battlefield with the guests to fight to the death with the Qin army and die together with the Zhao people. When the young master led the convoy through the east gate, he went to see Mr. Hou and told Mr. Hou everything about his plan to fight the Qin army to the death.
target: Passing through the east gate, the lord informed Hou Ying, who offered no farewell. Suspicious, the lord returned.

id: 史记/七十列传/魏公子列传::group-005
article_path: 史记/七十列传/魏公子列传
source: Mr. Hou asked the others to leave and talked secretly with the young master, saying: I heard that Jin Bi's military talismans are often placed in the King of Wei's bedroom. Among the wives and concubines, Ru Ji is the most favored. I also heard that Ru Ji's father was killed. Ru Ji's desire for revenge had been building up for three years. All the ministers from the King of Wei on down wanted to avenge Ru Ji, but they failed. For this reason, Ruji once cried to the prince, and the prince sent a retainer to cut off the enemy's head and present it to Ruji respectfully. If Ru Ji wanted to die for the young master, she had no choice but to do so, but she just had no chance to act. If the young master really asks Ru Ji for help, Ru Ji will definitely agree, and then he will be able to obtain the tiger talisman and seize the military power of Jin Bi. The north can save the Zhao State, and the west can resist the Qin State. This is the achievement of the Five Hegemons of the Spring and Autumn Period. The young master followed Hou Ying's plan and asked Ruji for help. Sure enough, Ruji stole Jin Bi's military talisman and gave it to the young master. The young master got the military talisman and was about to go on the road. Mr. Hou said: When a general is fighting abroad, he has the power to make decisions. He may not accept some of the king's orders in order to benefit the country. When the young master arrives there, even if the two numbers match and are verified to be correct, Jin Bi still refuses to hand over the military power to the young master and instead asks the King of Wei for instructions. Then things will be in danger. My friend the butcher Zhu Hai can go with you. This man is a strong man. If Jin Bi obeys, that would be the best; if he doesn't obey, Zhu Hai can kill him.
target: Hou Ying explained the futility of a direct assault and proposed stealing Jin Bi's military tally from the king's favored concubine, Ruji, whom the lord had previously helped. The lord obtained the tally through Ruji. Hou Ying also advised taking Zhu Hai to kill Jin Bi if he resisted. The lord wept, foreseeing Jin Bi's death.

id: 史记/七十列传/魏公子列传::group-006
article_path: 史记/七十列传/魏公子列传
source: So he set out on the road with the young master. The young master went to say goodbye to Mr. Hou. Mr. Hou said: I should have gone with you, but I am too old to make the trip. Please allow me to calculate the date of your journey. On the day you arrived at the Jinbi Military Headquarters, I faced the north and cut my neck to death to express my loyalty to see the young master off. The young master then set out on the road. When he arrived at Yecheng, the young master took out his military talisman and pretended to send an order from King Wei to replace Jin Bi as the general. Jin Bi combined the military talisman and verified that it was correct, but he still doubted the matter. He raised his hand and stared at the young master and said: Now I command an army of one hundred thousand troops stationed on the border. This is an important task related to the fate of the country. Today you come to replace me alone. What's going on? About to refuse to accept the order. At this time, Zhu Hai took out the forty kilograms of iron vertebrae hidden in his sleeves and killed Jin Bi with one vertebrae. The young master then took command of Jin Bi's army.
target: At Ye, Jin Bi verified the tally but refused to surrender command. Zhu Hai killed him with a hidden iron mallet.

id: 史记/七十列传/魏公子列传::group-007
article_path: 史记/七十列传/魏公子列传
source: About to refuse to accept the order. At this time, Zhu Hai took out the forty kilograms of iron vertebrae hidden in his sleeves and killed Jin Bi with one vertebrae. The young master then took command of Jin Bi's army. Then he organized the troops and issued an order to the army: If father and son are in the army, the father should go home; if brothers are in the army, the eldest brother should go home; and if the only son has no brothers, he should go home to support his parents. After reorganization and selection, 80,000 elite soldiers were obtained. Kaiba attacked the Qin army on the front line. The Qin army broke up the siege and retreated, so Handan was saved and Zhao was saved. King Zhao and Lord Pingyuan came to the suburbs to greet the young master. Mr. Pingyuan led the way, carrying a pouch full of arrows for the young master.
target: The lord reorganized the army, sending home fathers, elder brothers, and only sons, then led 80,000 elite troops to break the Qin siege, saving Handan. Hou Ying fulfilled his promise by cutting his own throat.

id: 史记/七十列传/魏公子列传::group-008
article_path: 史记/七十列传/魏公子列传
source: King Zhao drank with the young master until evening. He was still embarrassed to talk about the conferment of five cities because the young master always blamed himself for giving in. The young master finally stayed in Zhao State. King Zhao rewarded the prince with the city of Haoyi. At this time, the king of Wei also returned the city of Xinling to the prince. The young master is still in the state of Zhao. The young master heard that there were two talented and virtuous people in Zhao who were not engaged in politics. One was Mao Gong who was hiding among the gamblers, and the other was Xue Gong who was hiding in the hotel. The young master wanted to see these two people, but the two men hid and refused to see the young master. When the young master found out where they were hiding, he walked quietly to interact with these two people. They both enjoyed their acquaintance and were very happy. Lord Pingyuan learned about this situation and said to his wife: At first I heard that my wife's brother Wei Gongzi was an unparalleled sage, but now I heard that he was doing random things and associating with the gang of gamblers and hotel clerks. The young master is just an ignorant and reckless person. Lord Pingyuan's wife told the young master these words. After hearing this, the young master said goodbye to his wife and prepared to leave, saying: "I heard that Lord Pingyuan was virtuous, so I betrayed King Pingyuan and rescued Zhao State, which satisfied Lord Pingyuan's request." Now I know that Mr. Pingyuan's interactions with others are just a bold act to show his wealth. He is not looking for wise men and talents.
target: Fearing the king's wrath, the lord remained in Zhao. King Zhao offered five cities, but the lord, humbled by a retainer's rebuke, refused credit. He later befriended recluses Mao Gong and Xue Gong, angering Lord Pingyuan, who deemed them unworthy. The lord defended his actions, causing many of Pingyuan's retainers to defect to him.

id: 史记/七十列传/魏公子列传::group-009
article_path: 史记/七十列传/魏公子列传
source: The young master was still worried that the King of Wei would be angry with him, so he warned his guests: "Anyone who dares to deliver the message for the envoys of the King of Wei will be put to death." Since all the guests had deserted Wei and came to Zhao, no one dared to persuade the young master to return to Wei. At this time, Duke Mao and Duke Xue went to see the young master and said: The reason why the young master is respected in Zhao and famous among the princes is just because of the existence of Wei. Now the Qin State is attacking the Wei State. The Wei State is in danger, but the young master does not care. If the Qin State breaks through the beams and razes the ancestral temple of your ancestors, how can the young master still have the face to live in the world? Before he finished speaking, the young master's expression immediately changed and he told the driver to quickly hitch up the carriage and go back to rescue Wei Guo.
target: After ten years, Qin attacked Wei. The king begged the lord's return. Mao and Xue convinced him to go back.

id: 史记/七十列传/魏公子列传::group-010
article_path: 史记/七十列传/魏公子列传
source: Now the Qin State is attacking the Wei State. The Wei State is in danger, but the young master does not care. If the Qin State breaks through the beams and razes the ancestral temple of your ancestors, how can the young master still have the face to live in the world? Before he finished speaking, the young master's expression immediately changed and he told the driver to quickly hitch up the carriage and go back to rescue Wei Guo. When the King of Wei saw the young master, the two of them couldn't help but shed tears. The King of Wei gave the young master the seal of general, and the young master officially assumed the highest position of commanding the army, the general. In the thirtieth year of King Anli of Wei, the prince sent envoys to inform various princely states of his appointment as general. When the princes learned that the young master had become the general, they all dispatched their own troops and generals to rescue Wei. The young master led the armies of the five vassal states and defeated the Qin army south of the Yellow River, causing the Qin general Meng Ao to flee. Then they took advantage of the victory and pursued it as far as Hangu Pass, trapping the Qin army in Hangu Pass, so that they did not dare to leave the pass again. At that time, the reputation of the young master shocked the world, and guests from various princely states presented their art of war. The young master put them together and signed his name, so it is commonly known as "Wei Gongzi's Art of War" in the world.
target: The lord became general, rallied five allied states, and defeated Qin at the Yellow River, pursuing them to Hangu Pass. His fame spread, and he compiled "Wei Gongzi's Art of War.".

id: 史记/七十列传/魏公子列传::group-011
article_path: 史记/七十列传/魏公子列传
source: The young master will also take this opportunity to decide to become king. The princes are afraid of the young master's power and prestige, and are planning to come together to support him as king. The Qin State carried out rebellion many times, using the spies of the Wei State in the Qin State, pretending not to know anything and asking them to congratulate the young master and ask if he had been established as the king of Wei. The king of Wei heard these slanderous words about the young master every day and could not help but believe them. Later, he actually sent someone to replace the young master as general. The prince himself knew that he was being deposed for slander again, so he excused himself from going to court because he was ill. He feasted with the guests at home all night long, drank hard liquor, and often hung out with women. He spent four years having fun day and night, and finally died of illness due to excessive drinking. In this year, King Wei Anli also passed away. When the King of Qin received the news that the young master was dead, he sent Meng Ao to attack Wei, captured twenty cities, and began to establish Dongjun. From then on, Qin gradually invaded Wei's territory like eating mulberry leaves. After eighteen years, it captured Wei Wangjia, massacred the soldiers and civilians of Daliang, and destroyed the capital.
target: Qin bribed slanderers to claim the lord aimed for kingship. The king believed them and replaced him. The lord feigned illness, indulged in wine and women, and died four years later. King Anli died the same year. Qin then conquered twenty Wei cities and eventually destroyed Wei.

id: 史记/七十列传/魏公子列传::group-012
article_path: 史记/七十列传/魏公子列传
source: When Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty was in a low status, he heard many times that Mr. Wei was virtuous and talented. After he ascended the throne and became emperor, he often went to worship the prince every time he passed by Daliang. In the twelfth year of Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty, he returned from the front line where he defeated the rebel general Yingbu. When he passed through Daliang, he settled five families for the young master to guard his tomb and let them worship the young master according to the four seasons every year from generation to generation. Tai Shigong said: When I passed by the ruins of Daliang, I looked for the so-called Yimen. It turns out that Yimen is the east gate of Daliang City. There are indeed many gentlemen in the world who are hospitable and like people, but only Lord Xinling can make friends with those people who are hidden in every corner of society. It makes sense that he does not feel ashamed to make friends with the lower class. His reputation far exceeds that of the princes, and it is indeed true. Therefore, every time Gaozu passed through Daliang, he ordered the people to offer sacrifices to him without interruption.
target: Emperor Gaozu of Han, who admired the lord, ordered five families to guard his tomb and offer seasonal sacrifices. Sima Qian noted the lord's unique ability to befriend humble folk, ensuring his lasting renown.

id: 史记/七十列传/魏豹彭越列传::group-000
article_path: 史记/七十列传/魏豹彭越列传
source: Wei Bao was originally the son of the Wei Kingdom during the Six Kingdoms period. His elder brother is Wei Jiu, who was named Lord Ningling when he was in Wei State. After the Qin State destroyed the Wei State, he was exiled to other places and became a commoner. Chen Sheng rebelled and proclaimed himself king, and Wei Jiu followed him. King Chen sent Zhou Shi, a native of Wei, to lead troops to seize the land of Wei. After Wei was captured, everyone discussed with each other and wanted to make Zhou Shi the king of Wei. Zhou Shi said: Only when the world is in chaos can loyal ministers be revealed. Now that the whole world is rebelling against Qin, morally speaking, we must support the descendants of King Wei. Qi and Zhao each sent fifty chariots, hoping to establish Zhoushi as the king of Wei. Zhou Shi refused to accept the offer and sent people to Chen County to meet Wei Jiu. After five trips in total, King Chen agreed to send Wei Jiu back and establish him as King of Wei. Not long after Zhang Han defeated King Chen, he marched to Linji to attack King Wei. King Wei sent Zhou Shi to Qi and Chu to request reinforcements. Qi and Chu sent Xiang Ta and Tian Ba ​​to lead the army to follow Zhou City to rescue Wei. Zhang Han actually defeated the reinforcements, killed Zhou Shi, and surrounded Linji. Wei Jiu proposed conditions for surrender for the sake of the soldiers and people in the city. After the negotiation was successful, Wei Jiu set himself on fire and died. Wei Bao fled to Chu. King Huai of Chu gave Wei Bao thousands of troops and went back to capture Wei. By this time Xiang Yu had defeated the Qin army and surrendered to Zhang Han. Wei Bao captured more than 20 cities one after another. Xiang Yu made Wei Bao King of Wei. Wei Bao led his elite troops and followed Xiang Yu into the pass. In the first year of the Han Dynasty, Xiang Yu divided the princes among the feudal lords. He planned to occupy the Liang land, so he moved King Bao of Wei to Hedong, established his capital in Pingyang, and named him King of the Western Wei Dynasty. The King of Han returned to pacify the Three Qin Dynasties and led his troops across the Yellow River from Linjin. Wei Bao surrendered the entire country to the King of Han and followed the King of Han to Pengcheng to attack the Chu army. The king of Han was defeated and returned to Xingyang. Wei Bao asked for leave and went home to visit his mother's condition. After returning home, he immediately cut off the crossing of the Yellow River and betrayed the King of Han. Although the King of Han heard the news of Wei Bao's rebellion, he was worried about the Chu State in the east. He had no time to attack him, so he said to Li Sheng: Go and persuade Wei Bao for me. If you can persuade him, I will make you the Marquis of Wanhu. Li Sheng went to lobby Wei Bao. Wei Bao politely refused and said: Life is as short as the shadow of the sun passing through the crack in the wall. Now the King of Han is arrogant and insults others at will. He scolds the princes and ministers as if they were slaves. He has no etiquette at all. I can't bear to see him. So the King of Han sent Han Xin to attack Wei Bao, captured Wei Bao in Hedong, and escorted him to Xingyang in a post car, and changed Wei Bao's original territory into three counties. The King of Han ordered Wei Bao to garrison Xingyang. When the Chu army tightened its siege, Zhou Ke killed Wei Bao. Peng Yue was from Changyi, with the courtesy name Zhong.
target: Wei Bao, son of the Wei Kingdom during the Six Kingdoms period, had his elder brother Wei Jiu named Lord Ningling. After Qin destroyed Wei, Wei Bao became a commoner. When Chen Sheng rebelled, Wei Jiu followed him. Chen Sheng sent Zhou Shi to seize Wei land; after capturing it, others wanted Zhou Shi as king, but he insisted on supporting Wei descendants. Qi and Zhao sent chariots to back Zhou Shi, who refused and fetched Wei Jiu from Chen County. Chen Sheng agreed, making Wei Jiu King of Wei. Zhang Han defeated Chen Sheng, attacked Wei, and killed Zhou Shi. Wei Jiu surrendered to save his people, then set himself on fire. Wei Bao fled to Chu, received troops from King Huai of Chu, and captured over 20 cities. Xiang Yu made Wei Bao King of Wei, then moved him to Hedong as King of Western Wei. Wei Bao surrendered to the King of Han, followed him to attack Chu, but later betrayed him by cutting off the Yellow River crossing. The King of Han sent Li Sheng to persuade him, but Wei Bao refused, citing the King of Han's arrogance. Han Xin captured Wei Bao, who was later killed by Zhou Ke during a Chu siege.

id: 史记/七十列传/魏豹彭越列传::group-001
article_path: 史记/七十列传/魏豹彭越列传
source: Chen Sheng and Xiang Liang rose up, and a young man said to Peng Yue: Many heroes are rushing to raise banners to resist the violent Qin Dynasty. You can stand up, and we will follow their example. Peng Yue said: Now is the time for the two dragons to fight, so let's wait. More than a year later, more than a hundred young people from Zezhong gathered to follow Peng Yue and said, "Please be our leader." Peng Yue refused and said: I don't want to work with you. The young people persisted in their request, and he agreed. Make an appointment with them to gather when the sun rises the next day, and those who are late will be beheaded. When the sun came up the next day, more than ten people were late, and the last one didn't come until noon. At that time, Peng Yue said apologetically: I am old and you insist on making me the leader. Now, if there are many people late at the appointed time, we cannot behead all of them, but only the last person to come. Order the captain to kill him. Everyone laughed and said: "Why bother? I just don't dare to be late again from now on." So Peng Yue took the last person who arrived and killed him. Set up an earthen altar, use human heads to offer sacrifices, and give orders to everyone who belongs to them. Everyone was shocked and afraid of Peng Yue. No one dared to look up at him. So he led everyone to seize the land and collected more than a thousand soldiers who had fled from the princes. Peigong went north from Dang to attack Changyi, and Peng Yue assisted him. Changyi was not captured, so Pei Gong led the army to march west. Peng Yue also led his troops to garrison in Juye Ze to collect the fleeing soldiers of Wei. Xiang Ji entered Guanzhong and divided the feudal lords, and then returned. Peng Yue's army had grown to more than 10,000 people, but he had no one to belong to. In the autumn of the first year of Han Dynasty, King Tian Rong of Qi betrayed King Xiang, so he sent someone to give General Peng Yue a seal and asked him to march to Jiyin to attack the Chu army. The Chu army ordered Xiao Gongjiao to lead his troops to attack Peng Yue, but was severely defeated by Peng Yue. In the spring of the second year of the Han Dynasty, the King of Han, King Bao of Wei and various princes went east to attack Chu. Peng Yue led more than 30,000 troops to join the King of Han in Waihuang. The King of Han said: General Peng has recovered more than a dozen cities in Wei and is eager to support the descendants of King Wei. Today, King Bao of Wei is the cousin of King Jiu of Wei and a descendant of the real King of Wei. He appointed Peng Yue as the Prime Minister of Wei State, monopolizing military power and pacifying the Liang Dynasty. After the King of Han was defeated in Pengcheng, he retreated westward. At this time, Peng Yue abandoned all the cities he had captured and led his army alone to the north to station along the Yellow River. In the third year of the Han Dynasty, Peng Yue often traveled and sent troops on behalf of the Han Dynasty, attacked the Chu army, and cut off their supply of food and grass in Liang. In the winter of the fourth year of the Han Dynasty, King Xiang and King Han were at a stalemate in Xingyang, and Peng Yue captured seventeen cities including Suiyang and Waihuang. When King Xiang heard the news, he sent Cao Jiu to garrison Chenggao, and he led his army eastward to recover the cities that Pengyue had conquered, returning them to Chu.
target: Peng Yue, from Changyi, fished and robbed in Juye Lake. After Chen Sheng and Xiang Liang rose, youths urged him to lead, but he delayed. Over a year later, over a hundred youths insisted, and he agreed, executing a latecomer to enforce discipline. He gathered followers and assisted Peigong (Liu Bang) in attacking Changyi. After Xiang Ji divided the lords, Peng Yue's army grew to over 10,000. In the first year of Han, Qi's King Tian Rong gave him a seal to attack Chu. Peng Yue defeated Chu's Xiao Gongjiao. In the second year, he joined the King of Han with 30,000 troops and was made Prime Minister of Wei. After the King of Han's defeat, Peng Yue stationed along the Yellow River, harassing Chu's supply lines. In the fourth year, he captured 17 cities, but Xiang Ji recovered them. In the fifth year, he seized grain for the King of Han. Following Zhang Liang's advice, the King of Han promised Peng Yue land to become king, leading him to join the Han army at Gaixia, defeating Chu. Peng Yue was made King of Liang. In the tenth year, Chen Xi rebelled; Peng Yue feigned illness, angering Emperor Gao.

id: 史记/七十列传/魏豹彭越列传::group-002
article_path: 史记/七十列传/魏豹彭越列传
source: It would be better to send troops to rebel. The king of Liang did not listen to his advice and still said that he was ill. King Liang was very angry with his servant and planned to kill him. The servant hurriedly fled to Emperor Gao of the Han Dynasty and accused King Liang and Hu Zou of conspiring to rebel. So the emperor sent envoys to attack King Liang unexpectedly. King Liang was unaware of this, so he arrested King Liang and imprisoned him in Luoyang. After trial by the officials in charge, they believed that he had sufficient evidence for treason and requested the emperor to sentence him according to law. The emperor pardoned him, deposed him as a commoner, and exiled him to Qingyi County, Shu. When Peng Yue was escorted west to Zheng County, Empress Lu happened to be coming from Chang'an and was going to Luoyang. On the way, she met King Peng. King Peng cried to Empress Lu and personally told her that she was not guilty and hoped to return to her hometown Changyi. Empress Lu agreed and went east to Luoyang with him. Queen Lu stated to the emperor: King Peng is a heroic and brave man. Now that he is exiled to Shu, he will bring trouble to himself. It is better to kill him. So, I brought him back with me. Therefore, Empress Lu asked Peng Yue's retainers to accuse him of plotting to rebel again. Tingwei Wang Tiankai submitted a petition to kill Peng Yue's family, and the emperor approved it, so Peng Yue was killed, his family was killed, and his feudal state was abolished. Tai Shigong said: Although Wei Bao and Peng Yue were born in poverty, they occupied thousands of miles of vast land like rolled mats and became kings in the south. They followed the enemy's bloodstains to pursue victory, and their fame grew day by day. With a rebellious intention, when he failed, he failed to kill himself to become famous, but he was willing to be a prisoner, and even himself was killed. Why? People with average intelligence and above are ashamed of their behavior, let alone those who are kings! The reason why they endured the humiliation was for no other reason than because their wisdom and strategy were superior to others, and they were only worried about not being able to save their own lives.
target: Accused of conspiracy, he was arrested, pardoned to commoner status, and exiled. Empress Lu, fearing his influence, had him executed and his family exterminated. Tai Shigong comments: Though Wei Bao and Peng Yue rose from poverty to become kings, their failure to die for honor and willingness to be prisoners led to their deaths. Their endurance of humiliation stemmed from superior strategy and fear for their lives, hoping to seize power as circumstances changed.

id: 史记/七十列传/鲁仲连邹阳列传::group-000
article_path: 史记/七十列传/鲁仲连邹阳列传
source: Lu Zhonglian was a native of Qi. He is good at analyzing unique, grand and extraordinary strategies, but he is unwilling to serve as an official and is willing to maintain high integrity. He once visited Zhao State. When Zhao Xiaocheng was king, King Zhao of Qin sent Bai Qi to lead an army to defeat Zhao Changping's army, killing more than 400,000 people in total. As a result, Qin's army advanced eastward and besieged Handan, the capital of Zhao.
target: Lu Zhonglian, a native of Qi, was skilled in grand strategies but refused to serve as an official, valuing integrity.

id: 史记/七十列传/鲁仲连邹阳列传::group-001
article_path: 史记/七十列传/鲁仲连邹阳列传
source: When Zhao Xiaocheng was king, King Zhao of Qin sent Bai Qi to lead an army to defeat Zhao Changping's army, killing more than 400,000 people in total. As a result, Qin's army advanced eastward and besieged Handan, the capital of Zhao. King Zhao was very afraid, and no one from the reinforcements from the vassal states dared to attack the Qin army. King Anli of Wei sent General Jin Bi to lead troops to rescue Zhao. However, he was afraid of the Qin army and stationed in Tangyin and did not dare to advance. The king of Wei sent his guest general Xinyuan Yan into Handan through a hidden path, and met with the king of Zhao through Pingyuan Jun. He said: The reason why the Qin army is eager to besiege Zhao is because it used to compete with King Qi Min to become emperor, and soon King Qi Min revoked the title of emperor. If Zhao can send envoys to honor King Qin Zhao as emperor, King Qin will be very happy and will withdraw his troops.
target: During the siege of Handan by Qin, Zhao sought aid. Wei sent General Jin Bi, who hesitated, and envoy Xinyuan Yan proposed Zhao honor King Zhao of Qin as emperor to secure peace. Pingyuan Jun hesitated.

id: 史记/七十列传/鲁仲连邹阳列传::group-002
article_path: 史记/七十列传/鲁仲连邹阳列传
source: At this time, Lu Zhonglian traveled to the State of Zhao and caught up with the Qin army to besiege Handan. He heard that the State of Wei wanted Zhao to honor King Qin Zhao and proclaim himself emperor, so he went to Jin to see Lord Pingyuan and said: "What are we going to do about this?" Mr. Pingyuan said: How dare we talk about such a big event in our country! Not long ago, 400,000 troops were lost abroad, and now they are surrounded by the Qin army in Handan, and they cannot make them retreat. The King of Wei sent the guest general Xinyuan Yan to ask the State of Zhao to honor King Qin Zhao as emperor. This man is still here. How dare I talk about such a big thing! Lu Zhonglian said: I used to think that you were the most virtuous son in the world, but today I know that you are not the most virtuous son in the world. Where is Wei Guo's guest Xinyuan Yan? I will blame him for you and send him back. Mr. Pingyuan said: I would like to introduce you to Mr. Pingyuan. So Mr. Pingyuan met Xinyuan Yan and said: "There is a Mr. Lu Zhonglian in Qi State. He is here now. Please let me introduce him to you so that he can get to know the general and make friends." Xinyuan Yan said: I heard that Mr. Lu Zhonglian is a noble person in Qi State. I am a minister of the King of Wei, and I have been ordered to be an envoy and bear my responsibilities. I do not want to see Mr. Lu Zhonglian. Mr. Pingyuan said: I have revealed the news that you are here. Niiguan Yan had no choice but to agree. Lu Zhonglian saw Xinyuan Yan but said nothing. Xinyuan Yan said: I think those who stay in this besieged city are all people who seek help from Lord Pingyuan. But now, I don’t think Mr.’s appearance looks like someone who wants help from Lord Pingyuan. Why do you stay in this besieged city for a long time and not leave? Lu Zhonglian said: The world thinks that Bao Jiao committed suicide because of his narrow-mindedness. This view is completely wrong. Most people don't understand his shame in living in a troubled world, and think he just has personal agenda. The Qin State was a country that abandoned etiquette and only valued military merit. It treated its soldiers with power and deceit and enslaved its people like slaves. If it were allowed to proclaim itself emperor without restraint and rule the world, I would rather jump into the East China Sea and die than be its obedient citizen. The reason why I came to see the general was to help Zhao.
target: Lu Zhonglian confronted Xinyuan Yan, arguing that submitting to Qin would bring disaster. He cited historical examples, such as King Wei of Qi’s humiliation by Zhou and the fates of Jiuhou and Ehou under Yin Zhou, to illustrate the dangers of imperial ambition. Lu declared he would rather die than serve Qin. Xinyuan Yan was convinced and withdrew his proposal. The Qin army retreated after Wei’s Prince Wuji rescued Zhao. Pingyuan Jun offered Lu a reward, but he refused, stating that a worthy person resolves conflicts without seeking payment, and left forever.

id: 史记/七十列传/鲁仲连邹阳列传::group-003
article_path: 史记/七十列传/鲁仲连邹阳列传
source: If the Qin State is greedy enough and finally proclaims itself emperor, then the ministers of the princes will be replaced. He will depose those he deems unworthy and replace them with those he deems worthy; he will depose those he deems unworthy and replace them with those he loves. How could the King of Wei live a peaceful life when his children and troublemaking concubines were also allowed to be married to princes as concubines and live in the palace of Wei? And how can you, general, gain your original favor? At this time, Xinyuan Yan stood up, bowed to Lu Zhong twice and apologized, saying: "At first I thought you were an ordinary person, but today I know that you are a wise man in the world." I will leave Zhao State and no longer dare to talk about King Qin proclaiming himself emperor. When the Qin army general heard the news, he withdrew his army fifty miles. It happened that Wei Gongzi Wuji seized the military power of Jin Bi and led the army to rescue Zhao and attack the Qin army, so the Qin army withdrew from Handan and returned. Lord Pingyuan wanted to reward Lu Zhonglian, but Lu Zhonglian repeatedly refused and refused to accept. Lord Pingyuan held a banquet in honor of him. When his ears were full of wine, Lord Pingyuan stood up and offered a thousand pieces of gold as a reward to Lu Zhonglian. Lu Zhonglian said with a smile: The reason why outstanding people are respected by people in the world is because they can eliminate troubles, eliminate disasters, and resolve disputes without asking for compensation. If you ask for remuneration, it will become a businessman's behavior. I, Lu Zhonglian, cannot bear to do that. So I bid farewell to Lord Pingyuan and left, never to see each other again for the rest of our lives. More than twenty years after this incident, a Yan general captured Qi State's Liaocheng. Someone in Liaocheng spoke ill of General Yan in front of King Yan. General Yan was afraid of being executed, so he stayed in Liaocheng and did not dare to go back. Qi Guotian attacked Liaocheng alone for more than a year. Many soldiers died, but he could not capture Liaocheng. Lu Zhonglian wrote a letter, tied it to an arrow and shot it into the city to General Yan.
target: Over twenty years later, a Yan general held Qi’s Liaocheng. Lu Zhonglian wrote him a letter, urging him to choose wisely: return to Yan or surrender to Qi. He argued that clinging to a besieged city was unwise, citing Guan Zhong and Cao Mo as examples of those who overcame disgrace to achieve greatness. The general, torn between fear of execution and shame, committed suicide, leading to Qi’s capture of Liaocheng. Qi’s king offered Lu a title, but he fled to the seaside, preferring poverty to serving others.

id: 史记/七十列传/鲁仲连邹阳列传::group-004
article_path: 史记/七十列传/鲁仲连邹阳列传
source: When he returned, he reported Lu Zhonglian's affairs to the King of Qi. The King of Qi wanted to knight him. After hearing this, Lu Zhonglian fled to the seaside and lived in seclusion. He said: Instead of being rich and serving others, it is better for me to be poor and despise the world and let my own ambitions go. Zou Yang is from Qi State. When he traveled to Liang State, he interacted with Zhuang Ji, a native of Wu State, and Mei Cheng, a native of Huaiyin. He wrote a letter of self-recommendation and was a disciple of King Liang Xiao among Yang Sheng and Gongsun Gui.
target: Zou Yang, also from Qi, served King Xiao of Liang but was slandered by rivals and imprisoned.

id: 史记/七十列传/鲁仲连邹阳列传::group-005
article_path: 史记/七十列传/鲁仲连邹阳列传
source: In the past, Bian He offered jade, and the king of Chu chopped off his feet; Li Si tried his best to be loyal, but Hu Hai had him executed. So Jizi pretended to be crazy and took his father into seclusion to hide from the world. They were all afraid of suffering such a disaster. I hope your Majesty will carefully examine the sincerity of Bian He and Li Si, and don't believe in slander like King Chu and Hu Hai, and don't let me be ridiculed by Ji Zi and Jie Yu. I heard that Bigan was disemboweled and Wu Zixu's body was put into a leather bag and thrown into the river. I didn't believe it at first, but now I know that such a thing happened. I hope your Majesty will examine it carefully and show me a little mercy! As the saying goes: Some people are strangers even after getting along with them for a long time, while some people feel like old friends as soon as they stop and talk. What is this wish for? It lies in knowing one's heart and not knowing one's heart. Therefore, in the past, Fan Yuqi fled from Qin to Yan, and lent his head to Jing Ke to carry out Yan Dan's mission of assassinating the King of Qin; Wang She left Qi for Wei, and committed suicide on the city wall to retreat the Qi army and protect Wei.
target: From prison, he wrote a letter defending his loyalty, citing historical figures like Bian He, Li Si, and Bigan, who suffered unjustly. He argued that true understanding between ruler and subject transcends slander, as seen with Su Qin and Yan, or Baili Xi and Duke Mu of Qin.

id: 史记/七十列传/鲁仲连邹阳列传::group-006
article_path: 史记/七十列传/鲁仲连邹阳列传
source: Therefore, a sage monarch governs the country like a potter's fortune, with his own laws and regulations to educate the world, and will not be swayed by despicable opinions or changed by everyone's tongue. Therefore, Qin Shihuang listened to the words of his concubine Meng Jia and believed Jing Ke's lies. Jing Ke was able to take out the dagger secretly and assassinate people unprepared. King Wen of Zhou was hunting in the Jing and Wei areas and carried him back to Lu Shang in a chariot, so that he could become the king of the world. Therefore, King Qin listened to his ministers and was almost killed; King Wen of Zhou unexpectedly became king of the world. Why is this? Because King Wen of Zhou could transcend the restraints of the left and right, get rid of the restrained discussions of the world, and independently see the broad and bright road. Nowadays, the king is indulged in flattery and flattery, surrounded by concubines and attendants, causing outstanding scholars to be mixed up with horses and old oxen. This is the reason why Bao Jiao is resentful of the world and has no nostalgia for wealth. I heard that those who go to court solemnly and strictly will not be greedy for profit and moral integrity; those who pursue fame will not indulge their selfish desires and corrupt their character. Therefore, the county is called Shengmu, but Zengzi will not enter; the city is called Chaoge, and Mozi returns to his carriage and leaves. Nowadays, if people with lofty ideals are frightened by the mighty power, suppressed by the high position, and deliberately use evil faces and dirty conduct to serve the flattering villains in order to get close to the king, then the ambitious people will die in the caves of old age. How can they be willing to follow the king with all their loyalty and faith? This letter was presented to King Xiao of Liang, who sent someone to release Zou Yang from prison, and finally became King Xiao of Liang's honored guest. Tai Shigong said: Even if the main purpose of Lu Zhonglian's discussion is not righteous, I applaud him for being a common man, free and easy, not yielding to the princes, commenting on the current world, but he has convinced the powerful ministers and prime ministers. Even though Zou Yang's words are not modest enough, his comparisons between similar things are indeed touching. He can also be said to be frank, honest and unyielding, so I attach him to this biography.
target: He warned that listening to flattery leads to ruin, as with Lu and Song. King Xiao released him, and Zou became his honored guest. Sima Qian comments that while Lu Zhonglian’s arguments may not be entirely righteous, his independence and ability to sway powerful figures are admirable. Zou Yang’s words, though immodest, are sincere and compelling, earning him a place in this biography.

id: 史记/七十列传/黥布列传::group-000
article_path: 史记/七十列传/黥布列传
source: Qingbu is from Liuxian County and his surname is Ying. During the Qin Dynasty, he was a common man. When he was a child, a guest showed him a fortune and said: After being tortured, I will be king. When he reached his prime, he broke the law and was sentenced to tattoo. Tingbu smiled happily and said: Someone showed me a picture and said that I should be king after being tortured. Now, this is probably the situation, right? Everyone who heard him say this laughed at him. Not long after his conviction, Yingbu was sent to Lishan for hard labor. There were hundreds of thousands of prisoners in Lishan. When Chen Sheng rebelled, Ying Bu went to see Wu Rui, the magistrate of Fan County, and rebelled against the Qin Dynasty with his men, gathering a team of several thousand people. Magistrate Fan even married his daughter to him. After Zhang Han eliminated Chen Sheng and defeated Lu Chen's army, Yingbu led his troops north to attack Qin's left and right schools, defeated them at Qingbo, and then led his troops to advance eastward. Yingbu heard that Xiang Liang had pacified Kuaiji in the east of the Yangtze River and crossed the Yangtze River to march west. Chen Ying led his army to Xiang Liang because Xiang had been the general of the Chu State for generations, and crossed the Huai River southward. Generals Yingbu and Pu also led their troops to join Xiang Liang. Xiang Liang led his troops across the Huaihe River and marched westward. In the battles against Jingju, Qin Jia and others, Qingbu was brave and good at fighting and was always ranked first among the troops. Xiang Liang arrived in Xuedi and heard that King Chen was indeed dead, so he supported King Huai of Chu. Xiang Liang was called Wu Xinjun, and Yingbu was called Dangyang Lord. Xiang Liang was defeated and died in Dingtao. King Huai of Chu moved his capital to Pengcheng, and the generals and Yingbu also gathered in Pengcheng to guard it. At this time, the Qin army stepped up its siege on Zhao State, and Zhao State repeatedly sent people to ask for help. King Huai of Chu sent Song Yi as the top general, Fan Zeng as the last general, Xiang Ji as the second general, Yingbu and Pu as generals, all under Song Yi's command, to rescue Zhao State in the north. When Xiang Ji killed Song Yi on the bank of the Yellow River, King Huai took advantage of the situation and appointed Xiang Ji as general, and all generals were under Xiang Ji's control. Xiang Ji sent Yingbu to take the lead in crossing the Yellow River to attack the Qin army. Yingbu had the advantage due to his repeated military exploits. Xiang Ji led all his troops across the Yellow River and fought in coordination with Yingbu. They defeated the Qin army and forced Zhang Han and others to surrender. The Chu army won many battles and conquered all the princes. The reason why the armies of various princes can gradually surrender to Chu is because Yingbu can command the army to defeat many with less, which is impressive! Xiang Ji led his troops westward to Xin'an, and sent Yingbu and others to attack at night and bury more than 200,000 Zhang Han's subordinates alive. When they arrived outside Hangu Pass and could not enter, they sent Yingbu and others to take a small path to attack the defenders under the pass before entering the pass and reaching Xianyang City. Yingbu often served as a pioneer. King Xiang granted titles to the generals, named Yingbu the King of Jiujiang, and made six counties his capital.
target: Yingbu, a commoner from Liuxian County with the surname Ying, was predicted in his youth to become a king after being tortured. After being sentenced to tattooing for breaking the law, he laughed at the prophecy's fulfillment. Sent to hard labor at Lishan, he later rebelled against the Qin Dynasty with Wu Rui, the magistrate of Fan County, gathering thousands of troops. Yingbu joined Xiang Liang, proving himself brave in battle, and was titled Dangyang Lord. After Xiang Liang's death, he served under Xiang Ji (Xiang Yu), leading attacks that defeated the Qin army and forced Zhang Han's surrender. Yingbu buried over 200,000 Qin soldiers alive and helped Xiang Yu enter Xianyang. He was named King of Jiujiang and later killed the Righteous Emperor on Xiang Yu's orders.

id: 史记/七十列传/黥布列传::group-001
article_path: 史记/七十列传/黥布列传
source: Sui He rushed in, sat on the table of Chu's envoys, and said, "The king of Jiujiang has surrendered to the king of Han. Why should Chu let him send troops?" Yingbu looked surprised. The envoy from Chu State stood up to leave. Sui He took the opportunity to persuade Yingbu: "The important thing has been accomplished. We can kill the Chu envoy immediately. We cannot let him go back. Let's move closer to the Han Dynasty and fight together." Yingbu said: Just follow your instructions and send troops to attack Chu. So he killed the envoy and sent troops to attack Chu. Chu State then sent Xiang Sheng and Long Qie to attack Huainan, while King Xiang stayed to attack Xiayi. The war lasted for several months, and Long Qie defeated Yingbu's army in the battle of Huainan. Yingbu wanted to lead his troops to retreat to Han, but he was afraid that Chu's army would intercept and kill him, so he and Suihe fled back to Han through a hidden trail. When King Huainan arrived, the King of Han was sitting on the bed washing his feet, so he asked Yingbu to see him. When Yingbu saw this, he was so angry that he regretted coming and wanted to commit suicide. When he exited and came to the hotel prepared for him, Yingbu was overjoyed again when he saw that the curtains, utensils, food, and attendant officials were as luxurious as those of the King of Han. So he sent people to Jiujiang. At this time, the King of Chu had sent Xiang Bo to recruit Jiujiang's troops and killed Yingbu's wife and children. The people sent by Yingbu found Yingbu's friends and close subordinates, and took thousands of people to defect to the king of Han. The king of Han gave Yingbu more troops and went north with him to recruit troops at Chenggao. In July of the fourth year of Han Dynasty, the king of Han granted Yingbu the title of King of Huainan, and together with him he attacked Xiang Ji. In the fifth year of the Han Dynasty, Yingbu sent people into Jiujiang and captured several counties. In the sixth year of the Han Dynasty, Yingbu and Liu Jia entered Jiujiang and lured the great Sima Zhou Yin to surrender. After Zhou Yin rebelled against the Chu State, he mobilized the Jiujiang army and the Han army to jointly attack the Chu State and defeated the Chu army in Gaixia. After Xiang Ji's death, the world was at peace. The emperor held a banquet, but belittled Sui He's achievements, saying that Sui He was a pedantic, conservative, and out-of-date scholar. How could such a person be used to govern the world.
target: During the Chu-Han conflict, Yingbu feigned illness to avoid aiding Xiang Yu, who grew resentful. The Han king, valuing Yingbu's talents, sent Sui He to persuade him to defect. Sui He argued that Chu was weak and unjust, while Han was strong, promising Yingbu land and titles. Yingbu agreed, killed the Chu envoy, and attacked Chu. After being defeated by Long Qie, he fled to Han with Sui He. Initially angered by the Han king's casual reception, he was pleased by the luxurious treatment. The Han king granted him the title King of Huainan, and Yingbu helped defeat Xiang Yu at Gaixia. After peace, Yingbu grew fearful upon seeing the execution of Han Xin and Peng Yue.

source: The emperor said: Which strategy will Yingbu choose? Ling Yin replied: Choose the next best thing. The emperor said: Why did he give up the best policy or the middle policy and choose the worst policy? Ling Yin said: Yingbu was originally a prisoner of Lishan, and he worked hard to become the master of ten thousand chariots. This was all for his own wealth, without caring about the current people or future generations, so he chose the wrong strategy. The emperor said: Well said. Grant Xue Gong the title of Marquis of Thousand Households. The prince Liu Chang was canonized as King of Huainan. The emperor mobilized the army and personally led the eastward attack on Yingbu. At the beginning of the rebellion, Yingbu said to his generals: The emperor is old and hates fighting. He must not be able to lead troops in person and send generals. The generals are only afraid of Huaiyin and Peng Yue. Now that they are dead, the other generals have nothing to fear. So rebelled. As Duke Xue expected, he went east to attack Jing State. King Liu Jia of Jing fled and died in Fuling. Yingbu hijacked all his troops and crossed the Huaihe River to attack Chu. The state of Chu mobilized its troops to fight Yingbu between Xu and Tong. The state of Chu divided its troops into three groups and tried to adopt a strange strategy of mutual rescue. Someone advised the Chu general: Yingbu is good at using troops to fight, and the people have always been afraid of him. Moreover, the Art of War says: When princes fight the enemy in their own territory, once the soldiers are in danger, they will flee. Now the troops are divided into three groups. As long as they defeat one of our troops, the rest will run away. How can they rescue each other? The Chu general did not listen to the advice. Sure enough, Yingbo defeated one of the armies, and the other two armies fled in all directions. Yingbu's army advanced westward and met the emperor's army at Huizhen, west of Qixian County. Yingbu's army was very elite, so the emperor hid in the fortress of Yongcheng and could not get out. When he saw that Yingbu's formation was just like Xiang Ji's army, the emperor was very disgusted with him. Seeing Yingbu from a distance, he said to Yingbu from a distance: Why bother to rebel? Yingbu said: I want to be the emperor! The emperor was furious and scolded him, and then the two armies fought. Yingbu's army was defeated and fled, crossing the Huaihe River. They stopped and fought several times, but all failed, so they had to flee to the south of the Yangtze River with more than a hundred people. Yingbu was originally married to the magistrate of Fan County. Therefore, King Ai of Changsha sent someone to trick Yingbu into fleeing to South Vietnam. Yingbu believed him and followed him to Fanyang. The Fanyang people killed Yingbu in the houses of the people in Zixiang and finally destroyed Yingbu. The emperor appointed Prince Liu Chang as the King of Huainan, and granted Benhe the title of Marquis of Si. Most of the generals were rewarded for their military exploits. Tai Shigong said: Yingbu, are his ancestors the descendants of the British and Six Kingdoms Gaotao who were destroyed by the Chu Kingdom as recorded in the "Spring and Autumn"? He himself was tattooed, so why could he rise to prominence so quickly? Xiang killed thousands of people and buried them alive, and Yingbu was often the culprit. His merits were ranked highest among the princes, so he was able to become king, but he could not avoid suffering the greatest humiliation in the world.
target: Ben He fled to Chang'an and reported Yingbu's rebellion. Despite initial disbelief, Yingbu killed Ben He's family and rebelled. The emperor consulted Xue Gong, who predicted Yingbu would choose a poor strategy—attacking Wu and Chu but fleeing to Changsha. Yingbu indeed attacked Jing and Chu, defeating them, but was routed by the emperor's army at Huizhen. He fled south with a hundred men, was tricked by King Ai of Changsha, and killed by Fanyang people. The emperor made Prince Liu Chang King of Huainan. The historian notes Yingbu's rise from tattooing to kingship, his role in massacres, and his downfall due to jealousy over a concubine.

How can they not respect the use of divination to help achieve good deeds? It is impossible to record what happened before Tang Yao and Yu Shun. Judging from the rise of the Xia, Shang and Zhou dynasties, they were all based on auspicious omens from divination. When the king decided on difficult matters, he would refer to the results of divination made with the turtle to make the final decision. This was an unchanging traditional procedure. Although the Barbarians, Barbarians, Di and Qiang did not have the Chinese-style hierarchy of monarchs and ministers, they also had the custom of divination for making decisions and doubts. Some use gold and stone, some use plants and trees, and divination customs vary from country to country. But they can all be used to guide war operations, research, and achieve victory in wars. Each worships the gods of divination to predict future events. In the Zhou Dynasty, diviners always collected yarrow and tortoise shells for later use. In addition, who is more intelligent and who is less intelligent? When using Turtleweed, which one comes first and which one comes last? Every dynasty has different values. But in summary, the purpose of using turtle divination methods to help people predict the future is the same. Some people believe that there was never a time when the Holy King was undecided when encountering something; there was never a time when the Holy King lacked insights when solving problems. The reason why they set up the method of praying to gods and asking for divination is because they are worried that future generations will decline and decline. Foolish people will not learn from smart people. Everyone will be satisfied with their own knowledge. Differences in education will arise. The big principles will be broken into pieces and cannot be grasped. Therefore, they push the physical and emotional affairs to the most subtle realm, that is, the gods, and seek purity in the spirit. Some people also think that what the tortoise is good at, the saint cannot catch up with. It judges good and bad, distinguishes right from wrong, and is often more accurate than human predictions. After Emperor Gaozu succeeded to the throne, he followed the system of the Qin Dynasty and established diviners. At that time, the country had just been unified and the war had not stopped. As for Emperor Xiaohui, his reign was short, Empress Lu was the heroine, and Emperor Xiaowen and Emperor Xiaojing just followed the old system and did not have time to study the divination in depth. Therefore, although fortune-telling has been passed down from father to son and passed down from generation to generation, many of its subtle and profound principles and methods have been lost. Now that the emperor has ascended the throne, he has opened up the path for talented people to advance, and has recruited various scholars. Anyone who is proficient in a certain skill will have the opportunity to contribute, and those with outstanding skills will receive preferential treatment. He is pragmatic and has no partiality. In the past few years, the Taibu official office has gathered many talents.
target: Tai Shigong observed that since ancient times, sage kings establishing states and accepting heaven's mandate have always respected divination to aid good deeds. Evidence from Xia, Shang, and Zhou dynasties shows their rises were based on auspicious divination omens: Dayu's marriage to the Tushan daughter was auspicious, leading to Xia Qi's dynasty; Jian Di swallowing a swallow's egg brought favorable predictions for Yin's rise; Houji's agricultural skill brought auspiciousness for Zhou kingship. Kings consulted turtle divination for difficult decisions as an unchanging tradition. Even barbarian tribes without Chinese hierarchy had divination customs using various materials like gold, stone, plants, and wood, all guiding warfare and predicting events. During Xia and Yin, yarrow and turtle shells were discarded after divination, but Zhou collectors preserved them. Different dynasties valued divination differently, but all used it to predict the future. Some believed holy kings never lacked insights but established divination to guide future generations who might decline in wisdom. Others thought turtles' judgment surpassed human predictions. After Emperor Gaozu succeeded, he followed Qin's system to establish diviners, but the country's unification and ongoing wars prevented deep study. source: From this point of view, isn’t it great! So can we disrespect the Turtles? There was an old man in the south who used a turtle support to prop up the foot of his bed. More than twenty years later, the old man died and someone else moved the bed, but the turtle was still alive. Turtles can move Qi and guide it. Someone asked: The turtle is such a god, but when the diviner gets a live turtle, why does he always kill it and pick off its plastron? A few years ago, someone along the Yangtze River got a famous turtle and raised it, making his family very rich. He discussed with others and wanted to release the turtle and leave. Someone taught him to kill the turtle and not release it. If he released the turtle, his family would be destroyed. The turtle told him in a dream: Send me back to the water, don't kill me. The family eventually killed it. After killing the turtle, the owner will die and the family will be unlucky. The common people and the monarch have different principles. When the common people get the name of turtle, it seems that it is not suitable to kill them. According to past stories, the ancient Ming King and Holy Lord always killed turtles and used them. When the kings of Song and Yuan Dynasties got a turtle, they killed it and made use of it. I would like to record this incident in succession below, so that people with good intentions can appreciate and choose from it. In the second year of the reign of Emperor Song and Yuan Dynasty, the God of the Yangtze River sent a divine turtle to the Yellow River. When they arrived in Quanyang, a fisherman cast a net to catch the turtle, imprisoned it and put it in a cage. In the middle of the night, Gu Lai entrusted a dream to King Song and Yuan, saying: I went on a mission to the Yellow River for the River God, but the fishnet blocked my way. Yuqie of Quanyang has got me, and I can't leave. In times of trouble, there is no one to turn to. The king is virtuous, so he came here to tell you. King Yuan woke up in surprise. So he summoned Dr. Wei Ping and asked him: Tonight I dreamed of a man with stretched out neck and long head, wearing black embroidered clothes, riding a carriage. He came to me in the dream and said: I am on a mission to the Yellow River for the River God, but the fishnet blocks my way. Yuqie of Quanyang has got me, and I can't leave. In times of trouble, there is no one to turn to. The king is virtuous, so he came here to tell you. What kind of character is this? Wei Ping took the divination tool and stood up, looked up at the sky, observed the light of the moon, observed the direction of the handle of the Big Dipper, and deduce the position of the sun in the sky. Use compasses and square rulers as auxiliary tools, plus weighing hammers and weighing rods. The four corners of southeast, northeast, southwest and northwest have been determined. Qian, Kun, Zhen, Xun, Kan, Li, Gen and Dui Bagua are in their respective positions and face each other. Observe the good and bad signs among them, and the armored insect appears first. Wei Ping then said to King Yuan: Last night on the day of Ren, the sun was in the Altair constellation.

source: Yu Qie said: At midnight, I cast a net and caught a turtle. The messenger asked: Where is the turtle now? He hesitated to answer: In a cage. The messenger said: The king knows that you have this turtle, so he sent me to ask for it. Yuqie said: OK. The turtle was immediately tied up, taken out of the cage, and presented to the messenger. The messenger carried the turtle and left the gate of Quanyang City. Suddenly it was broad daylight and nothing could be seen. It was stormy and dark. Clouds cover the top of the turtle car, showing green and yellow colors; thunder and rain are coming, and the wind is accompanying it. Entering the end gate of the palace, Gui came to see King Yuan in the east side hall. The body of the turtle is like running water, moist and shiny. When the turtle saw King Yuan, it stretched out its neck and crawled forward. After crawling for three steps, it stopped, retracted its neck and retreated back to its original position. When King Yuan saw this, he was surprised and asked Wei Ping: "When the turtle saw me, it stretched its neck and crawled forward. Why did it look up?" He shrunk his neck and returned to his original position. What does this mean? Wei Ping replied: The turtle was in trouble and was imprisoned all night. The king was virtuous and sent people to rescue it. Now it stretches its neck and crawls forward to express its gratitude, and then shrinks its neck and retreats, hoping to leave quickly. King Yuan said: How wonderful! Has the turtle's spirit reached such an extent? Don't keep it for a long time, drive the turtle to it as soon as possible, don't let it delay the deadline. Wei Ping replied: The tortoise is the most precious thing in the world. The first person to get the tortoise will become the emperor, and he will be able to win ten times in ten battles. The turtle was born in the abyss and grew up in the loess. It knows the way of heaven and understands the people and affairs of ancient times. It has traveled for three thousand years without exceeding the area where it lives. The tortoise is peaceful and peaceful, its energy is calm and upright, and it moves without any effort. Longevity covers the world, and no one knows its limit. It changes with everything, changing color with the seasons. It lives and hides itself, lying down without eating food. It is cyan in spring, yellow in summer, white in autumn and black in winter. Turtles can clearly distinguish between yin and yang, examine punishments and virtues, foresee benefits and harms, and carefully examine misfortunes and blessings.
