He concluded by detailing the fates of the kings: Liu Xu plotted rebellion and committed suicide, and Liu Dan also conspired and died, leading to the abolition of their states.

id: 史记/三十世家/五宗世家::group-000
article_path: 史记/三十世家/五宗世家
source: A total of thirteen sons of Emperor Xiaojing were named kings. These thirteen were born to five mothers, and those born to the same mother were clan relatives. The sons born to Li Ji are Liu Rong, Liu De and Liu Yanyu. The sons born to Cheng Ji are Liu Yu, Liu Fei and Liu Duan. The sons born to Jia Fu are Liu Pengzu and Liu Sheng. The son born to Tang Ji was Liu Fa. Mrs. Wang's sons, Liu Yue, Liu Ji, Liu Cheng, and Liu Shun, were born to her. Liu De, the king of Hejian, was named the king of Hejian as a prince in the second year of Emperor Xiaojing's reign. He likes Confucian learning, and he dresses and behaves like a Confucian scholar. Most of the Confucian scholars in Shandong attached themselves to him. He died after reigning for twenty-six years and was succeeded by his son, Prince Gong Liu Buhu. Liu Buhui died after four years on the throne, and his son Liu Ji, King Gang, succeeded him. Liu Ji died in his 12th year on the throne, and his son Liu Shu, King of Qing, succeeded him. Linjiang Ai Wang Liu Yan was named Linjiang King as a prince in the second year of Emperor Xiaojing's reign. He died after reigning for three years. Because he had no descendants to inherit the throne, the feudal state was abolished and changed to counties.
target: Emperor Xiaojing had thirteen sons by five mothers, all named kings. Li Ji bore Liu Rong, Liu De, and Liu Yanyu; Cheng Ji bore Liu Yu, Liu Fei, and Liu Duan; Jia Fu bore Liu Pengzu and Liu Sheng; Tang Ji bore Liu Fa; and Mrs. Wang bore Liu Yue, Liu Ji, Liu Cheng, and Liu Shun. Liu De, King of Hejian, was a Confucian scholar who attracted many followers. He reigned 26 years, succeeded by his son and grandson.

id: 史记/三十世家/五宗世家::group-001
article_path: 史记/三十世家/五宗世家
source: Linjiang Ai Wang Liu Yan was named Linjiang King as a prince in the second year of Emperor Xiaojing's reign. He died after reigning for three years. Because he had no descendants to inherit the throne, the feudal state was abolished and changed to counties. Linjiang Min King Liu Rong was established as the crown prince in the fourth year of Emperor Xiaojing's reign. Four years later, he was deposed and was named Linjiang King as the original prince. In the fourth year of his reign, he was convicted of occupying the open space outside the ancestral temple wall to expand the palace, and the emperor conscripted him. Liu Rong responded to the call and set out to worship the god of travel at the north gate of Jiangling. After getting in the car. The axle is broken and the car is useless. The Jiangling elders thought this was an ominous sign, and cried and whispered: Our king may not be able to come back! Liu Rong arrived in the capital and went to the Lieutenant's Mansion for interrogation. Lieutenant Zhi questioned him and he died out of fear of committing suicide. Buried in Lam Tin. Tens of thousands of swallows placed earth in their mouths on his tomb, and the people pitied him. Liu Rong was the oldest among the sons of Emperor Jing. After his death, he had no sons to inherit the throne. The feudal kingdom was abolished and the fiefdom was merged into the imperial court and became Nanjun. The first kings of the above-mentioned Three Kingdoms were all sons of Li Ji. Liu Yu, King of Lu Gong, was named King of Huaiyang as a prince in the second year of Emperor Xiaojing's reign. In the second year, after the rebellion of the seven kingdoms of Wu and Chu was put down, he was renamed King of Lu in the third year of Emperor Xiaojing's reign. He likes to build palaces and gardens and raise dogs and horses. In his later years, he loved music, but he was not good at speaking and had a stutter. He died in the twenty-sixth year of his reign, and his son Liu Guang succeeded him as king. Liu Guang also liked music, carriages and horses at first, but in his later years he became stingy, fearing that his property would not be enough. Liu Fei, King of Yi of Jiangdu, was named King of Runan as a prince in the second year BC of Emperor Xiaojing. When the seven kingdoms of Wu and Chu rebelled, Liu Fei was fifteen years old. He was brave and resourceful. He wrote to the emperor and volunteered to lead troops to attack Wu. Emperor Jing gave him the seal of general and ordered him to attack the state of Wu. After the state of Wu was defeated, he was renamed King of Jiangdu the next year and governed the original fiefdom of the state of Wu. Because of his military merits, he was awarded the emperor's banner. In the fifth year of Yuanguang reign of Emperor Xiaowu, the Huns invaded the Han territory and became bandits. Liu Fei wrote a letter volunteering to attack the Huns, but the emperor did not agree. Liu Fei liked to use his strength, build palaces, recruit heroes and knights from all over the world, and was extremely arrogant and extravagant. He died in his twenty-sixth year on the throne, and his son Liu Jian succeeded him as king. Liu Jian committed suicide after seven years in office. When Huainan and Hengshan rebelled, Liu Jian had some idea of ​​their plans. He believed that his kingdom was close to Huainan, and he was afraid that it would be annexed by the king of Huainan if the incident happened, so he secretly made weapons, and often wore the general's seal given to his father by the emperor, and carried the emperor's banner on patrols.
target: Liu Rong, once crown prince, was deposed and later died by suicide after being convicted of expanding his palace onto temple grounds. His kingdom was abolished. Liu Yu, King of Lu, built palaces and loved music but stuttered. Liu Fei, King of Jiangdu, was a brave military leader who defeated Wu in the Rebellion of the Seven Kingdoms. His son Liu Jian committed suicide after plotting rebellion, adultery, and witchcraft. Liu Duan, King of Jiaoxi, was cruel and impotent, often killing officials who followed Han laws. He died without heirs, and his kingdom was abolished.

id: 史记/三十世家/五宗世家::group-002
article_path: 史记/三十世家/五宗世家
source: Therefore, although Jiaoxi is a small country, there are many officials with the rank of 2,000 stone killed and injured. Liu Duan died after reigning for forty-seven years. In the end, because he had no son to inherit the throne, the feudal state was abolished and the feudal land was merged into the imperial court and became Jiaoxi County. The first kings of the above-mentioned three kingdoms were all sons of Cheng Ji. King Liu Pengzu of Zhao was named King of Guangchuan as a prince in the second year of Emperor Xiaojing's reign. After King Zhao rebelled and was defeated, Peng Zu was named King of Guangchuan. In the fourth year of his reign, he was renamed King Zhao. In the fifteenth year of his reign, Emperor Xiaojing passed away. Peng Zu was a deceitful and sycophantic man, humble and flattering. On the surface, he was humble and respectful, but he was mean and vicious in his heart. He likes to play with the law and slander others with sophistry. Peng Zu had many beloved concubines and descendants. If the prime minister and officials of the 2,000-stone level want to govern political affairs according to the laws of the Han Dynasty, they will harm the interests of King Zhao. For this reason, whenever the Prime Minister or a 2,000-stone-level official arrived, Liu Pengzu would dress in black cloth and pretend to be a slave, go out to greet him personally, clean the residence where the 2,000-stone-level official stayed, and create more confusion to attract the other party. Once the 2,000-stone-level official made inappropriate remarks and violated the court's taboos, he would write it down.
target: Liu Pengzu, King of Zhao, was deceitful and manipulative, causing many officials to be dismissed or executed. He amassed wealth through monopolies but spent it on concubines.

id: 史记/三十世家/五宗世家::group-003
article_path: 史记/三十世家/五宗世家
source: Liu Yue, King Hui of Guangchuan, was named King of Guangchuan as a prince in the second year of Emperor Xiaojing's reign. Liu Yue died in the 12th year of his reign, and his son Liu Qi succeeded him as king. Liu Qi had a favored minister Sang Ju. Later, Sang Ju committed a crime, and Liu Qi wanted to kill Sang Ju, but Sang Ju escaped, and Liu Qi captured and exterminated his clan. Sang Ju resented Liu Qi because of this, so he wrote a letter to accuse Liu Qi of committing adultery with his compatriot sisters. From then on, in order to protect himself, Liu Qi repeatedly wrote letters to accuse the Han Dynasty officials and favored ministers such as Suo Zhong and others for their crimes. Liu Ji, King Kang of Jiaodong, was named King of Jiaodong as a prince in the second year of Emperor Xiaojing's reign. He died after reigning for twenty-eight years. When the King of Huainan was planning a rebellion, Liu Ji secretly heard about it, so he secretly made bows and arrows, prepared for war and defense, and waited for the King of Huainan to rebel. Later, when the officials interrogated the King of Huainan for his rebellion, this incident was exposed in his confession. Liu Ji had the closest relationship with the emperor. He felt guilty and grieved for participating in the rebellion. He died of an illness and did not dare to pass it on to his successor. Later, the emperor learned about this situation. Liu Ji's eldest son was named Xian, but his mother was not favored; his younger son was named Qing, and his mother was favored. Liu Ji once wanted to appoint Liu Qing as his successor, but because it was not in line with the inheritance order and because of his own sins, he finally dared not say anything. The emperor took pity on him and made Liu Xian King of Jiaodong and the successor of King Kang. Liu Qing was granted the title of King of Liu'an in the former fiefdom of King Hengshan. King Liu Xian of Jiaodong died in the fourteenth year of his reign and was given the posthumous title of King Ai. His son Liu Qing succeeded to the throne as king. In the second year of Yuanshou, Liu Qing, the king of Liu'an, was named the king of Liu'an as the son of King Kang of Jiaodong. Liu Cheng, the Ai King of Qinghe, was granted the title of King Qinghe as a prince in the third year of Zhongyuan Period by Emperor Xiaojing. He died after reigning for 12 years. Because he had no sons, the feudal state was abolished and the land belonged to the imperial court and became Qinghe County. Liu Shun, the Xianwang of Changshan, was named the King of Changshan as a prince in the fifth year of Emperor Xiaojing's reign. Liu Shun was the favorite youngest son of Emperor Jing. He was arrogant and lazy, engaged in many promiscuous affairs, and repeatedly violated laws and regulations. The emperor often pardoned him. Liu Shun died in the thirty-second year of his reign, and his prince Liu Bo succeeded him as king.
target: Liu Sheng, King of Zhongshan, indulged in wine and women, fathering over 120 children. Liu Fa, King of Changsha, was born to a maid and ruled a small, poor kingdom. Liu Yue, King of Guangchuan, died after 12 years. Liu Ji, King of Jiaodong, prepared for a rebellion but died of illness. His son Liu Xian succeeded him. Liu Cheng, King of Qinghe, died heirless, and his kingdom was abolished. Liu Shun, King of Changshan, was favored but arrogant. His son Liu Bo was deposed after misconduct, and the kingdom was divided.

id: 史记/三十世家/五宗世家::group-004
article_path: 史记/三十世家/五宗世家
source: More than a month later, the emperor noticed that King Xian was his favorite youngest son, so he issued an edict to the officials: King Xian of Changshan died early, the queen and her concubines were at odds with each other, and the concubines fabricated charges against each other and fought with each other. As a result, they fell into injustice and the country was destroyed. I pity him very much. Liu Ping, the son of King Xian, has 30,000 households and is the true king; Liu Shang, the son of King Xian, has 30,000 households and is the king of Sishui. In the fourth year of Yuanding, Liu Ping, the king of Zhending, was named the king of Zhending as the son of Prince Xian of Changshan. Liu Shang, the Si Wang of Surabaya, was named the King of Surabaya as the son of Prince Changshan Xian in the fourth year of Yuanding. He died after reigning for eleven years and was succeeded by his son Liu Anshi, King Ai. King Ai died after eleven years of reigning without any sons. The emperor took pity on the Queen of Surabaya and appointed Liu Anshi's younger brother Liu He as the King of Surabaya. The first kings of the four kingdoms mentioned above were all the sons of Mrs. Wang Erjiao. Later, the Han Dynasty added the title of King of Liu'an and King of Sishui to his descendants. In total, there are six kings of Erjiao's descendants. Tai Shigong said: When Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty was on the throne, all the taxes of the princes belonged to the princes and kings, and they could appoint officials below the level of internal history. The court only sent prime ministers to them and awarded them gold seals. The vassal kings appointed censors, court officials, and doctors on their own, similar to the emperor. Since the rebellion of Wu, Chu and other countries, during the era when the Five Sects were kings, the imperial court sent 2,000 stone-level officials to them, removed the "prime minister" and replaced them with "prime minister". The princes and kings could only enjoy the taxes within the fiefdom, and their power was deprived of their power by the court. After that, the poor among the princes and kings could only ride on bullock carts.
target: Sima Qian noted that after the Rebellion of the Seven Kingdoms, the power of princes was reduced; they only collected taxes, and the court appointed officials. Some princes became so poor they rode oxcarts.

id: 史记/三十世家/卫康叔世家::group-000
article_path: 史记/三十世家/卫康叔世家
source: Uncle Kang of Wei State was named Feng, and he was the half-brother of King Wu of Zhou Dynasty. They also had a younger brother named Ran Ji, who was the youngest. After King Wu of Zhou defeated Yin Zhou, he granted the remnants of Yin Zhou to King Zhou's son Wu Geng Lufu, making him the same as the princes, so that they could worship their ancestors and pass them on from generation to generation. Because Wu Geng had not fully obeyed, King Wu was worried that Wu Geng had rebellious intentions, so he sent his younger brothers Guan Shu and Cai Shu to monitor and assist Wu Geng's father to appease the people. After King Wu died, King Cheng was young and still in his infancy. Zhou Gongdan took charge of state affairs instead of King Cheng. Uncle Guan and Uncle Cai suspected Zhou Gongdan, so they launched a rebellion with Wu Genglu's father to attack Chengzhou. Zhou Gongdan asked King Cheng to organize an army to attack the state of Yin, killed Wu Genglu's father and Guan Shu, exiled Cai Shu, and granted Wu Geng Yin's remnants to Kang Shu, making him the king of Wei. He lived between the Yellow River and Qishui River, which was the ancient capital of the Shang Dynasty, Yinxu. Zhou Gongdan was worried that Uncle Kang was young and would have difficulty maintaining his rule, so he repeatedly warned Uncle Kang: You must find talented, prestigious, and experienced people in the Yin Dynasty, and learn from them the history of the rise and fall of the Yin Dynasty, and you must care for and care for your own people. He also warned Kang Shu that the reason for Zhou's demise was that he drank excessively, indulged in pleasure, and indulged in female sex. Therefore, the chaos in the reign of King Zhou began from here. Zhou Gongdan also wrote "Zi Cai" in accordance with the principle that craftsmen must use rules when making woodenware, as a guideline for rulers to follow. Therefore, it was called "Kang Gao", "Jiu Gao" and "Zicai", and was used to teach Uncle Kang. Uncle Kang used these principles to govern the feudal country, stabilize and harmonize his people, and the people were very happy. After King Cheng came of age, he personally took charge of the political power, appointed Uncle Kang as the Sikou of the Zhou Dynasty, and gave him many treasures and sacrificial vessels to commend Uncle Kang's virtues. After Uncle Kang's death, his son Kang Bo became the king.
target: Uncle Kang of Wei, named Feng, was the half-brother of King Wu of Zhou. After King Wu defeated the Shang dynasty, he granted the remnants of Yin to Wu Geng, King Zhou's son, but worried about rebellion. He sent Guan Shu and Cai Shu to monitor Wu Geng. After King Wu's death, King Cheng was young, and Zhou Gongdan ruled as regent. Guan Shu and Cai Shu, suspecting Zhou Gongdan, rebelled with Wu Geng. Zhou Gongdan suppressed the rebellion, killed Wu Geng and Guan Shu, exiled Cai Shu, and granted the Yin remnants to Kang Shu, making him ruler of Wei. Zhou Gongdan warned Kang Shu to learn from Yin's history, avoid excessive drinking and pleasure, and wrote "Kang Gao," "Jiu Gao," and "Zi Cai" as guidelines. Kang Shu governed well, and the people were content. After King Cheng came of age, he appointed Kang Shu as Sikou and honored him.

id: 史记/三十世家/卫康叔世家::group-001
article_path: 史记/三十世家/卫康叔世家
source: After Kaobo's death, his son Sibo became the king. After the death of Sibo, his son Boli became the king. After Bo's death, his son Jing Bo became the king. After the death of Jingbo, his son Zhenbo became the king. After the death of Zhenbo, his son Qinghou was established as the king. Because the Marquis of Qing bribed the King of Zhou Yi with generous gifts, the King of Yi ordered the King of Wei to be named Marquis. Qinghou died in the twelfth year after he became the king, and his son Lihou became the king. In the thirteenth year of Lihou's reign, King Li of Zhou fled to the land of Hu, and Duke Zhao and Duke of Zhou took charge of the political power together, which was named "Republican Administration". In the twenty-eighth year of Lihou, King Xuan of Zhou was established as the emperor. In the forty-second year, Marquis Li died, and Prince Gong Boyu became the king. Gongbo's younger brother He Zeng was favored by Marquis Li. Marquis Li gave He a lot of property. He then used these properties to bribe warriors and attacked Gongbo Yu in Lihou's cemetery. Gongbo was forced to flee to the tomb of Lihou and commit suicide. The people of Wei buried Gongbo next to Lihou's tomb and called him Gongbo. They established He as the king of Wei, and he was named Wu Gong. After Duke Wu came to the throne, he reorganized Uncle Kang's government affairs, and the people lived in peace and harmony. In the 42nd year, Quan Rong killed King You of Zhou. Duke Wu personally commanded the generals to assist the Emperor of Zhou in quelling the invasion of Quan Rong and established military exploits. King Ping of Zhou ordered Duke Wu to declare himself duke. In the fifty-fifth year, Duke Wu passed away, and his son Zhuang Gongyang became the king. In the fifth year of Duke Zhuang's accession to the throne, he married a daughter of the State of Qi as his wife. The daughter of Qi was beautiful but childless. Duke Zhuang then married Chen Guonv, who gave birth to a son who died in infancy. Chen Nu's sister was also favored by Duke Zhuang and gave birth to a son named Wan. After Wan's mother passed away, Duke Zhuang asked his wife Qi to raise Wan and made Wan the prince. Duke Zhuang also had a beloved concubine who gave birth to a son named Zhouxu. In the eighteenth year of Duke Zhuang, Zhouxu grew up and liked military affairs, so Duke Zhuang appointed him as a general in the army. Shi Jue, the high minister of the Wei State, kindly came to admonish Duke Zhuang and said, "My son is fond of military affairs. Please make him a general. From now on, troubles will arise." Duke Zhuang refused to listen. In the twenty-third year, Duke Zhuang passed away and the crown prince was established as the king. This is Duke Huan. In the second year of Duke Huan, his younger brother Zhou Xu was arrogant and extravagant. Duke Huan deposed him and Zhou Xu fled abroad. In the thirteenth year, Duan, Zheng Bo's younger brother, attacked his elder brother but failed to win and fled. Zhouxu asked for friendship with him. In the 16th year, Zhouxu gathered the fugitives of Weiguo to attack and kill Duke Huan. Zhouxu himself established himself as the king of Weiguo. Because Zheng Bo's brother Duan wanted to attack the state of Zheng, Zhouxu asked Song, Chen, and Cai to jointly support Duan, and the three countries all agreed to this request.
target: After Kang Shu's death, his descendants ruled Wei for generations. Qinghou bribed King Yi of Zhou to have the ruler of Wei titled Marquis. During Lihou's reign, King Li of Zhou fled, and the "Republican Administration" began. Later, Gongbo Yu was forced to commit suicide by his brother He, who became Duke Wu. Duke Wu reformed governance, and the people prospered. He assisted King Ping of Zhou against Quan Rong and was declared duke. After his death, Duke Zhuang succeeded him. Duke Zhuang married a Qi woman who was childless, then married a Chen woman who bore a son who died. Another Chen woman bore Wan, who was made prince. Duke Zhuang also had a son, Zhouxu, who loved military affairs. Minister Shi Que warned Duke Zhuang, but he ignored him. After Duke Zhuang's death, Prince Wan became Duke Huan. Zhouxu, arrogant and extravagant, was deposed and fled. Later, Zhouxu gathered fugitives, killed Duke Huan, and declared himself ruler. He sought to support Zheng Bo's brother Duan, but the people hated him for killing Duke Huan. Shi Que conspired with Chen Hou to kill Zhouxu and established Duke Huan's brother Jin as Duke Xuan.

id: 史记/三十世家/外戚世家::group-000
article_path: 史记/三十世家/外戚世家
source: Since ancient times, the founding emperors who were appointed by heaven and the monarchs who inherited the orthodox and abided by the laws of the late emperors were not only intrinsically noble in character, but also mostly had the help of their relatives. The rise of the Xia Dynasty was due to the daughter of the Tushan family, and Xia Jie's exile was also related to Moxi. The rise of the Yin Dynasty also relied on the Nu family, and the murder of King Zhou of Shang was also related to his favoring Daji. The rise of the Zhou Dynasty also relied on Jiang Yuan and Tai Ren, and the capture of King You was also related to his fornication with Bao Si. Therefore, the "Book of Changes" is based on the two hexagrams "Qian" and "Kun", the "Book of Songs" begins with "Guan Ju", the "Shang Shu" praises Yao for marrying his daughter to Shun, and the "Spring and Autumn" ridicules those who marry their wives without going to meet them in person. The relationship between husband and wife is the most important ethical relationship in human nature. In the application of etiquette, only marriage is the most cautious. When music harmonizes the four seasons, it becomes harmonious. The changes of yin and yang are the rulers of the growth and change of all things. How can we not be cautious?
target: The crucial role of marriage and imperial consorts in the rise and fall of dynasties. Founding emperors and orthodox monarchs often relied on their relatives for support. The Xia Dynasty rose through the Tushan family's daughter and fell with Moxi; the Yin Dynasty rose through the Nu family and fell due to Daji; the Zhou Dynasty rose through Jiang Yuan and Tai Ren, while King You's downfall involved Bao Si. The text emphasizes that husband-wife relationships are the most important ethical bond, and marriage is the most cautious ritual application.

id: 史记/三十世家/外戚世家::group-001
article_path: 史记/三十世家/外戚世家
source: Indeed, a king cannot get the love of his spouse from his ministers, nor can a father get it from his son, let alone those of low status! After couples get together, some are unable to produce children and grandchildren; after they are able to produce children, some cannot find a good home. Isn't this destiny? Confucius rarely talked about the destiny of heaven, probably because it was difficult to explain clearly. If we cannot understand the changes of yin and yang, how can we understand the principles of human nature and destiny? Tai Shigong said: The situation before Qin was too ancient, and the details could not be recorded. After the establishment of the Han Dynasty, Lu Ehuang became the empress of Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty, and her son was the prince. In her later years, her appearance deteriorated and she fell out of favor. As Mrs. Qi gained favor, her son Ruyi almost replaced the prince several times. After the death of Emperor Gaozu, Empress Lu executed the Qi family and killed King Zhao Ruyi. However, the concubines in Emperor Gaozu's harem could only be safe if they were not favored and alienated. Empress Lu's eldest daughter was the wife of Zhang Ao, the Marquis of Xuanping, and Zhang Ao's daughter was the queen of Emperor Hui. Because of their close relationship, Empress Dowager Lu tried every means to try to get her to have a child, but she never had a child. She had to bring someone else's son from the harem and falsely claimed it was her son. After the death of Emperor Xiaohui, the world had just stabilized and the person who would succeed the throne was not yet clear. So he raised the status of his relatives, made the Lu brothers kings as assistants, and made Lu Lu's daughter the queen of the young emperor, hoping to make the foundation stronger, but it was of no use. Empress Lu died and was buried in Changling with Gaozu. Lu Lu, Lu Chan and others were afraid of being killed, so they plotted to cause trouble. The ministers conquered them, and heaven guided the Han family's imperial line, and finally eliminated the Lu family.
target: The narrative then details several Han Dynasty empresses and their families. Empress Lu, wife of Emperor Gaozu, lost favor in her later years as Lady Qi gained prominence. After Gaozu's death, Empress Lu executed the Qi family and killed Prince Ruyi. She tried to secure succession through her daughter's child but failed, eventually elevating her Lu relatives. After her death, the Lu clan plotted rebellion but were eliminated by ministers, who installed Emperor Xiaowen.

id: 史记/三十世家/外戚世家::group-002
article_path: 史记/三十世家/外戚世家
source: So he raised the status of his relatives, made the Lu brothers kings as assistants, and made Lu Lu's daughter the queen of the young emperor, hoping to make the foundation stronger, but it was of no use. Empress Lu died and was buried in Changling with Gaozu. Lu Lu, Lu Chan and others were afraid of being killed, so they plotted to cause trouble. The ministers conquered them, and heaven guided the Han family's imperial line, and finally eliminated the Lu family. Only Queen Xiaohui was placed in the North Palace. The minister ushered the king into the throne, who was Emperor Xiaowen, and he enshrined the ancestral temple of the Han family. Isn't this destiny? If it were not destiny, who could take on this important task? Empress Dowager Bo, whose father was a Wu man and whose surname was Bo, had an affair with Wei Wei, a woman from the original Wei king's clan during the Qin Dynasty, and gave birth to Bo Ji. Bo Ji's father died in Shanin and was buried there. When the princes rebelled against the Qin Dynasty, Wei Bao proclaimed himself King of Wei, and Wei sent her daughter to the palace of the King of Wei. Wei Lao went to Xu Fu's place to see her fortune teller and asked him to see Bo Ji. Xu Fu said that she would definitely be able to give birth to the emperor. At that time, Xiang Yu and Liu Bang, the king of Han, were fighting over the world in Xingyang, and it was not yet certain who would own the world. Wei Bao initially joined the King of Han in attacking the King of Chu, but when he heard Xu Negi's words, he felt happy alone, so he betrayed the King of Han, first remaining neutral, and then allied with the King of Chu. The king of Han sent Cao Shen and others to attack and imprison King Bao of Wei, changed the Gui land he occupied into a county, and sent Bo Ji to Zhizao mansion where criminals were housed. After the death of King Bao of Wei, the King of Han once entered the Zhizao Mansion and saw Bo Ji's beautiful appearance. He issued an edict to take her into the harem, but she was not favored for more than a year. When Bo Ji was young, she was very close to Mrs. Guan and Zhao Zier. The three of them made a vow: Whoever gets rich first will not forget the others. Later, Mrs. Guan and Zhao Zier were both favored by the King of Han. One time when the King of Han was sitting on the Chenggao Platform in the Henan Palace, the two beauties laughed at each other as they talked about their vows with Bo Ji. When the King of Han heard about it, he asked them why, and they both told the King of Han the truth. The king of Han felt a little sad and felt sorry for Bo Ji, so he summoned her and stayed with her that day. Bo Ji said: Last night I dreamed of a blue dragon occupying my belly. Emperor Gaozu said: This is a sign of a noble person. Let me fulfill it for you. Fortunately, a boy was born, and he became the king. After that, Bo Ji rarely saw Gaozu. After the death of Emperor Gaozu, Empress Dowager Lu was very resentful of the concubines such as Mrs. Qi and others who were favored to serve as Emperor Gaozu's bedtime, so she imprisoned them all and were not allowed to leave the palace. Because Bo Ji rarely saw Gaozu, she was able to leave the palace and follow her son to the Kingdom of Dai, becoming the Queen Mother of Dai. The Queen Mother's younger brother Bo Zhao also followed him to Dai.
target: Empress Dowager Bo's story follows. Her mother had an affair with a Wei clan member during Qin times, producing Bo Ji. A fortune-teller predicted she would bear an emperor. Wei Bao, hearing this, betrayed the King of Han but was defeated. Bo Ji entered the harem but remained unfavored for over a year. Through friends' intervention, she gained the king's favor, dreamed of a blue dragon in her belly, and bore a son. After Gaozu's death, because she was rarely favored, she escaped Empress Lu's persecution and followed her son to the Kingdom of Dai, becoming Queen Mother of Dai. After Empress Lu's death, ministers chose her son as Emperor Xiaowen.

id: 史记/三十世家/外戚世家::group-003
article_path: 史记/三十世家/外戚世家
source: Only one person in the Bo family was granted the title of Marquis. Empress Dowager Bo died two years later than Emperor Wen, in the second year of Emperor Jing's reign, and was buried in Nanling. Since Empress Lu was buried with Emperor Gaozu in Changling, she specially built a separate mausoleum for herself, close to Emperor Xiaowen's Ba Mausoleum. Empress Dowager Dou was a native of Guanjin County, Qinghe County, Zhao State. During the reign of Queen Mother Lu, Concubine Dou was selected from a good family to serve the Queen Mother in the palace. Later, the Queen Mother sent the maids out of the palace and gave them to the princes and kings, five for each king. Dou Ji was among these maids. Dou Ji's family was in Qinghe. Thinking that Zhao State was close to her home, she asked the eunuch in charge of the deportation: "My name must be put on the list of people going to Zhao State." The eunuch forgot about this and mistakenly put her on the list of people going to Dai. The roster was read, the edict said it was okay, and it was time to set off. Dou Ji burst into tears and complained that the eunuch didn't want to go, so he forced her to leave before she was willing to leave. When he arrived in the Kingdom of Dai, the King of Dai only favored Concubine Dou, and gave birth to a daughter called Prostitute, and later gave birth to two boys. The queen gave birth to four boys. The queen died before the king entered the court and became the emperor. When the king became the emperor, the four boys born to the queen also died of illness one after another. A few months after Emperor Xiaowen came to the throne, the ministers requested the establishment of a prince. Dou Ji's eldest son was the oldest and was established as the prince. Dou Ji was also made the queen, and her daughter Liu Piao was the eldest princess. The next year, he established his youngest son Liu Wu as the acting king, and soon moved to Liang State. This was King Xiao of Liang. Queen Dou's parents had died long ago and were buried in Guanjin. At this time, Empress Dowager Bo issued an edict to relevant officials to honor Empress Dou's father as Marquis Ancheng and his mother as Mrs. Ancheng. He ordered a garden town of 200 households to be set up in Qinghe, which was served and guarded by the local chief minister. Everything was done in accordance with the practices of Lingwen Garden. Queen Dou's elder brother is Dou Changjun, and his younger brother is Dou Guangguo, also known as Shaojun.
target: Empress Dowager Dou was selected for palace service during Empress Lu's reign. When palace maids were distributed to princes, she wanted to go to Zhao but was mistakenly sent to Dai. There, the King of Dai favored her, and she bore two sons. After the queen and her sons died, Dou Ji's eldest son became crown prince, and she became empress. Her brother Dou Guangguo, sold as a child, later identified himself through shared memories and was reunited with her. The Dou family received honors, and Empress Dowager Dou promoted Huang-Lao teachings.

id: 史记/三十世家/外戚世家::group-004

source: He left an edict and gave all the money and property in the East Palace to the eldest princess Liu Piao. The Queen Mother is from Huaili, and her mother's name is Zang'er. Zang'er is the granddaughter of Zang Tu, the original king of Yan. Zang'er first married Wang Zhong of Huaili and gave birth to a son named Xin and two daughters. Later, Wang Zhong died, and Zang'er remarried to the Tian family in Changling and gave birth to sons Tian Fu and Tian Sheng. Zang'er's eldest daughter married Jin Wangsun and gave birth to a daughter. Zang'er considered her children a title, and it turned out that her two daughters were both noble people. So she wanted to rely on her two daughters, so she forcibly took her daughter back from the Jin family's home. Jin was very angry and refused to break up with his wife, so Zang'er sent his daughter to the prince's womb. The prince loved her very much and gave birth to three daughters and one son. When the boy was still pregnant, Beauty Wang dreamed that the sun fell into her arms. She told the prince about this dream, and the prince said: This is a sign of great wealth. Emperor Xiaowen died before he was born. After Emperor Xiaojing came to the throne, Mrs. Wang gave birth to the boy. Previously, Zang'er sent her youngest daughter Erjiao to the palace, and Erjiao gave birth to four boys. When Emperor Jing was crown prince, Empress Dowager Bo chose a woman from the Bo family to be his concubine. When Emperor Jing came to the throne, this concubine was made Queen Bo. The queen had no children and was not favored. As soon as Queen Mother Bo died, Queen Bo was deposed. Liu Rong, the eldest son of Emperor Jing, and his mother was Li Ji. Li Ji is from Qi. Liu Rong was established as the prince. The eldest princess Liu Piao has a daughter who plans to be the prince's concubine. Li Ji was jealous, and it was only through the eldest princess that the beauties of Emperor Jing met Emperor Jing. They received more honor and favor than Li Ji. Li Ji was resentful every day, so she declined the eldest princess's request and refused to marry. The eldest princess wanted to betroth her daughter to Mrs. Wang's son, and Mrs. Wang agreed.
target: The text also covers Empress Wang, whose mother Zang'er forcibly took her daughter from her husband Jin Wangsun and sent her to the prince's womb. She dreamed of the sun falling into her arms and bore a son who became Emperor Wu. Lady Li Ji, mother of the eldest son, refused the eldest princess's marriage proposal for her daughter, leading to conflict. Through manipulation, Mrs. Wang's son became crown prince instead.

id: 史记/三十世家/外戚世家::group-005
article_path: 史记/三十世家/外戚世家
source: Tian Fu and Tian Sheng are greedy people and good at using words and arguments. Wang Zhong died early and was buried in Huaili. He was honored as Gonghou and established a garden of 200 households. When Lord Pingyuan died, he was buried in Changling together with the Tian family. The cemetery set up had the same specifications as the Gonghou Cemetery. The Queen Mother died sixteen years later than Emperor Xiao Jing, in the fourth year of Yuanshuo, and was buried with Emperor Jing in Yangling. A total of three people in the Queen Mother's family were granted the title of marquis. Queen Wei, also known as Zifu, came from a humble background. Probably her family was called the Wei family and was within the Pingyang Marquis fiefdom. Zifu is the singer of Princess Pingyang. Emperor Wu newly came to the throne and had no sons for several years. Princess Pingyang selected a dozen girls from good families, dressed them up and stayed at home. Emperor Wu came back from participating in the ceremony to eliminate disasters and pray for good fortune in Bashang, and stopped by Princess Pingyang's house. The princess asked all the beauties serving her to come out to see Emperor Wu, but Emperor Wu didn't like it. After drinking, the singer came in. When Emperor Wu saw her, he only liked Wei Zifu. On this day, Emperor Wu got up to change his clothes. Zifu served in the emperor's clothes carriage and was honored by his relatives. Emperor Wu returned to his seat, very happy, and gave Princess Pingyang a thousand catties of gold. The princess took the opportunity to ask Wei Zifu to be sent to the palace. After Zifu got in the car, Princess Pingyang stroked her back and said: Let's go, eat well and work hard! If you are noble, don't forget me. Zihu had been in the palace for more than a year, but he never received Emperor Wu's favor again. Emperor Wu singled out the useless palace servants and asked them to leave the palace and go home. Wei Zifu was then able to see Emperor Wu, and she cried and asked to leave the palace. The emperor loved her and favored her again, so she became pregnant and became more respected and favored day by day. Emperor Wu summoned her elder brother Wei Changjun and younger brother Wei Qing to serve as ministers. Later, Zifu became very favored by Emperor Wu and gave birth to three daughters and one son. The son's name was Zhu. When Emperor Wu was still the crown prince, he married the eldest princess's daughter as his concubine. When he ascended the throne as emperor, the concubine was made empress, with the surname Chen, and she had no children. The emperor can inherit the throne, and the eldest princess has contributed a lot, so Queen Chen is arrogant and arrogant. Hearing that Wei Zifu was favored by Emperor Wu, he was very angry and sought death many times. The emperor also became even more angry. Empress Chen used women's witchcraft to deceive people. Emperor Wu was quite aware of this, so he deposed Empress Chen and made Wei Zifu the empress.
target: Wei Zifu, a singer from Princess Pingyang's household, caught Emperor Wu's attention. After initial neglect, she became pregnant and gained favor, eventually becoming empress after Empress Chen was deposed for witchcraft. Her brother Wei Qing became a general, and her family produced five marquises.

id: 史记/三十世家/外戚世家::group-006
article_path: 史记/三十世家/外戚世家
source: After Prince Wei was deposed, there was no new crown prince. And King Liu Dan of Yan wrote a letter, willing to return to the capital and join the palace as a guard. Emperor Wu was very angry and immediately beheaded the envoy of King Yan in Beique. The emperor lived in Ganquan Palace and called a painter to draw a picture of Zhou Gong carrying the king on his back. So the officials knew that Emperor Wu wanted to make his youngest son the prince. A few days later, Emperor Wu condemned Mrs. Gou Yi. The lady took off her hairpin and earrings and kowtowed to apologize. Emperor Wu said: Take her away and send her to Yeting Prison! The lady looked back and saw Emperor Wu saying: "Go quickly, you can't live!" The lady died in Yunyang Palace. When he died, a storm blew up the dust, and the people were very sad. The messenger took the coffin to the burial site at night and marked the burial place. Afterwards, Emperor Wu asked around him in his spare time: "What do people say about this matter?" The left and right replied: People say that since her son is to be established, why do they need to get rid of his mother? Emperor Wu said: Yes. This is beyond the understanding of children and fools. In the past, the reason why the country was in trouble was because the monarch was young and his mother was in her prime. When a woman lives alone, she will become arrogant, arrogant and indulgent, and no one can stop her. Haven't you heard about Queen Lu? Therefore, all the mothers who gave birth to children for Emperor Wu, whether male or female, were not condemned and executed. Can we say that they are not sages? Such a clear vision and careful consideration for future generations are not within the reach of those ignorant and ignorant Confucians.
target: The text concludes with Emperor Wu's later consorts and his controversial execution of Lady Gou Yi, mother of his youngest son. He explained that young monarchs with living mothers caused chaos, citing Empress Lu as an example. All mothers of Emperor Wu's children were executed to prevent such problems.

article_path: 史记/三十世家/孔子世家
source: Confucius was born in Zouyi, Changping Township, Lu State. His ancestor was from the Song Dynasty, named Uncle Kong Fang. Uncle Fang gave birth to Bo Xia, and Bo Xia gave birth to Shu Liang He. Shu Lianghe and Yehe, a woman named Yan, gave birth to Confucius. They got Confucius after they went to Niqiu Mountain to pray to the gods. Confucius was born in the 22nd year of Duke Xiang of Lu. The top of his head was concave when he was born, so he was named Qiu. The courtesy name is Zhongni and the surname is Kong. Shortly after Confucius was born, his uncle Liang He died and was buried in Fangshan. Fangshan was in the east of Lu State, so Confucius could not know for sure where his father's tomb was. His mother did not tell him where his father was buried. When Confucius was a child, he played games, often setting up various sacrificial vessels and learning the ritual movements of sacrificial offerings. After Confucius's mother died, she temporarily placed her coffin in the Five Fathers' Road without burying her. This was out of prudent consideration. The mother of Wan's father, who was from Zouyi, told him the burial place of Confucius's father, and then Confucius moved his mother to Fangshan to be buried with his father.
target: Confucius was born in Zouyi, Changping Township, Lu State, to Shu Lianghe and a woman named Yan after they prayed at Niqiu Mountain. His head was concave at birth, so he was named Qiu, with the courtesy name Zhongni and surname Kong. His father died shortly after his birth and was buried in Fangshan, but his mother did not reveal the location. As a child, Confucius played at setting up sacrificial vessels and learning ritual movements. After his mother died, he temporarily placed her coffin at the Five Fathers' Road until a neighbor told him his father's burial place, allowing him to bury them together.

id: 史记/三十世家/孔子世家::group-001
article_path: 史记/三十世家/孔子世家
source: After Confucius's mother died, she temporarily placed her coffin in the Five Fathers' Road without burying her. This was out of prudent consideration. The mother of Wan's father, who was from Zouyi, told him the burial place of Confucius's father, and then Confucius moved his mother to Fangshan to be buried with his father. When Confucius was mourning with a filial piety belt tied around his waist, Ji Sun held a banquet to entertain celebrities, and Confucius went to attend. Ji Sun's retainer Yang Hu stopped him and said: "Ji's family is entertaining celebrities, but you are not invited." Confucius withdrew because of this. When Confucius was seventeen years old, Lizi, a senior official in the state of Lu, was critically ill. Before his death, he warned his son Yizi: Confucius is a descendant of a saint, and his ancestors perished in the Song Dynasty. His ancestor Fufu He was supposed to succeed as the king of Song Dynasty, but he gave way to his younger brother Li Gong. When another of his ancestors, Zheng Kao's father, assisted Song Dai Gong, Song Wu Gong, and Song Xuangong in three dynasties, he was more respectful every time he was given orders. Therefore, the inscription on Zheng Kao's father's tripod says: The first appointment was received with a bow, the second appointment was received with a bow, and the third appointment was bowed and received. When I walked, I avoided the middle of the road and walked against the wall, and no one dared to bully me. I just made batter and porridge in this cauldron to survive. His frugality has reached this point. I heard that although the descendants of saints may not necessarily become kings and govern, there will definitely be people with outstanding talents and virtues. Now Confucius is young and courteous. Isn't he a man of outstanding talents and virtue? If I die, you must take him as your teacher. After Meng Lizi died, Meng Yizi and Nangong Jingshu, a native of Lu, went to Confucius to learn etiquette. This year, Ji Wuzi died, and Pingzi succeeded to the throne. Confucius' family was poor and of low status. When he came of age, he worked as a clerk in charge of the Ji family's warehouse, and he was a cashier who could calculate money and grain fairly and accurately. He also worked as a clerk in charge of pastures, and he was able to breed livestock well. Therefore, he was promoted to Sikong in charge of construction projects. Not long after, he left the state of Lu, was ostracized in the state of Qi, was expelled in the states of Song and Wei, was besieged between the states of Chen and Cai, and finally returned to the state of Lu. Confucius was nine feet six inches tall. People called him "The Long Man" because they thought he was different from ordinary people. The State of Lu was still very kind to him, so he returned to the State of Lu. Nangong Jingshu, a native of Lu, said to Duke Zhao of Lu: Please allow me to go on a mission to Zhou with Confucius. Duke Zhao of Lu gave him a carriage, two horses, and a boy servant, and set off with him to the Kingdom of Zhou to learn etiquette and pay a visit to Lao Tzu.
target: At seventeen, Meng Lizi, a senior official, warned his son Yizi that Confucius, a descendant of saints, should be taken as a teacher. After Lizi's death, Yizi and Nangong Jingshu learned etiquette from Confucius. Confucius' family was poor and of low status. He worked as a clerk managing the Ji family's warehouse and pastures, where he was fair and efficient, leading to his promotion to Sikong. He later left Lu, was ostracized in Qi, expelled in Song and Wei, besieged between Chen and Cai, and finally returned to Lu. At nine feet six inches tall, he was called "The Long Man." Nangong Jingshu requested Duke Zhao of Lu to allow Confucius to travel to Zhou to learn etiquette from Lao Tzu, who advised him to avoid speaking of others' faults and to act without selfish motives. After returning, Confucius gained many disciples.

id: 史记/三十世家/孔子世家::group-002
article_path: 史记/三十世家/孔子世家
source: Not long after, he left the state of Lu, was ostracized in the state of Qi, was expelled in the states of Song and Wei, was besieged between the states of Chen and Cai, and finally returned to the state of Lu. Confucius was nine feet six inches tall. People called him "The Long Man" because they thought he was different from ordinary people. The State of Lu was still very kind to him, so he returned to the State of Lu. Nangong Jingshu, a native of Lu, said to Duke Zhao of Lu: Please allow me to go on a mission to Zhou with Confucius. Duke Zhao of Lu gave him a carriage, two horses, and a boy servant, and set off with him to the Kingdom of Zhou to learn etiquette and pay a visit to Lao Tzu. When they were saying goodbye, Lao Tzu came out to see them off and said: I heard that wealthy people give gifts with property, and people with noble moral character give gifts with words. I am not a wealthy person, so I can only steal the name of a noble person and send you off with words. These sentences are: A wise and thoughtful person is often threatened with death because he likes to talk about others; a knowledgeable, eloquent and insightful person is often in trouble and endangers himself, because he likes to expose the sins of others. Children should not have selfish motives, and ministers should not think only of themselves but the monarch. After Confucius returned to the state of Lu from Zhou Dynasty, more and more disciples followed him. At this time, Jin Pinggong was promiscuous and immoral, and the six ministers of the Han, Zhao, Wei, Zhonghang, Fan, and Zhi families controlled the state affairs and constantly sent troops to attack the feudal states in the east. King Ling of Chu had a strong army and often invaded other countries in the Central Plains; Qi was a big country and close to Lu. The state of Lu was small and weak. If it surrendered to the state of Chu, it would anger the state of Jin. If it surrendered to the state of Jin, it would cause the state of Chu to attack. If it did not serve Qi well, Qi's army would invade the state of Lu. Lu Zhaogong was twenty years old and Confucius was thirty years old. Duke Jinggong of Qi and Yan Ying came to the state of Lu. Duke Jinggong asked Confucius: "In the past, Duke Qin's country was small and remote. Why was he able to dominate?" Confucius replied: Although the Qin State is small, its ambitions are great; although its location is remote, its governance is very appropriate. Duke Mu of Qin personally pulled Baili Xi, who had been redeemed with five black ram skins, and awarded him the title of a great official. As soon as he was released from detention, Qin Jun discussed with him for three days, and then let him take charge of the state affairs.
target: At thirty, Confucius advised Duke Jing of Qi that Qin's success came from its ambitious governance and use of talents like Baili Xi. At thirty-five, after political turmoil in Lu, Confucius went to Qi, where he studied music and advised Duke Jing on governance, emphasizing proper roles and frugality. However, Yan Ying dissuaded the duke from employing Confucius, criticizing Confucian rituals as impractical. Confucius left Qi and returned to Lu.

id: 史记/三十世家/孔子世家::group-003
article_path: 史记/三十世家/孔子世家
source: In the ninth year of Duke Dinggong of Lu, Yang Hu failed in his rebellion and fled to Qi. At this time, Confucius was fifty years old. Gongshan Buxuan used Philadelphia to rebel against the Ji family, and he sent people to summon Confucius to help. Confucius has been exploring the way to govern the country for a long time, but he was depressed and had nowhere to apply it. No one could use him, so he said: In the beginning, King Wen and King Wu of Zhou arose from Feng and Hao and established the royal industry. Although Philadelphia is small now, it should be about the same! Confucius wanted to go, but Zilu was unhappy and stopped Confucius. Confucius said: If they invite me to go, will my trip be in vain? If I am reused, I will establish a dynasty like Zhou Dynasty in the East! However, it didn't happen in the end. Later, Duke Dinggong of Lu appointed Confucius as the governor of the central capital. A year later, all places followed his example. Confucius was promoted from the chief of Zhongdu to Sikong, and from Sikong to the great Sikou.
target: At fifty, Confucius was appointed governor of Zhongdu, then promoted to Sikong and later to Grand Sikou.

id: 史记/三十世家/孔子世家::group-004
article_path: 史记/三十世家/孔子世家
source: So the officials in charge cut them in half according to law and ordered them to live apart. Qi Jinggong was greatly frightened and deeply touched. He knew that it was difficult to rival Lu in terms of morality. After returning home, he was very panicked and told his ministers: Lu uses the principles of a gentleman to assist their king, but you only teach me the methods of Yi Di, causing me to offend the king of Lu. What should I do? The official in charge stepped forward and replied: When a gentleman makes a mistake, he uses practical actions to apologize to others and admits his mistake; when a villain makes a mistake, he uses sweet words to cover it up. If you feel sad, take concrete actions to express your apology. So Qi Jinggong returned the land of Yun, Wenyang, and Guiyin of Lu State that he had invaded in the past, in order to apologize and repent to Lu State. In the summer of the thirteenth year of Duke Dinggong of Lu, Confucius said to Duke Dinggong: Weapons cannot be stored in the homes of ministers, and city walls one foot high and three hundred feet long cannot be built in the fiefdom of officials. So he sent Zhong Yu to serve as Ji's retainer, intending to demolish the city walls of Ji Sun, Meng Sun and Shu Sun. At this time, Shusun first demolished the city wall of Liyi. The Jisun family was also preparing to demolish the city wall of Feiyi. Gongshan Buxuan and Shusunsu led Feiyi's people to attack Lu.
target: In the tenth year of Duke Ding of Lu, he organized a meeting at Jiagu between Lu and Qi, where he confronted Qi's disruptive performances and had performers executed. Qi returned invaded lands to Lu. In the thirteenth year, Confucius ordered the demolition of the city walls of Ji, Meng, and Shu families to curb their power, but the Meng family resisted, and the city of Cheng could not be captured.

id: 史记/三十世家/孔子世家::group-005
article_path: 史记/三十世家/孔子世家
source: Then the city was ready to be demolished. Meng Sun's retainer Gong Lian Chufu told Meng Sun: "If the city wall of Cheng Yi is demolished, the people of Qi will definitely advance to our north gate." Moreover, Chengcheng is also a barrier for your Meng family. Without Chengcheng, there is no Meng family. I'm not going to tear it down. In December, Lu Dinggong led his troops to surround Chengcheng but could not capture it. In the fourteenth year of Lu Dinggong, Confucius was fifty-six years old. He acted as the chief minister in the affairs of the prime minister, with a look of joy on his face. His disciples said: I heard that a gentleman will not be afraid when a great disaster comes, nor will he be overjoyed when a great blessing comes. Confucius said: There is this saying, but isn't there another saying: "Being in a high position and treating the virtuous but a lowly person is content with yourself?" So Confucius killed the official Shaozhengmao who was disturbing the state affairs. Three months after Confucius participated in state affairs, merchants selling pigs and sheep no longer dared to ask for high prices; men and women walked separately; no one picked up things dropped on the road; travelers from all over the country came to the cities of Lu, and they did not need to ask for favors or gifts from officials, they could get what they needed and go back satisfied. When the Qi State heard the news, they became frightened and said: "As long as Confucius is in power in the Lu State, he will definitely dominate. Once the Lu State becomes hegemonic, we are the closest and will definitely take the lead in annexing us."
target: At fifty-six, Confucius acted as chief minister, killing the official Shaozhengmao. Within three months, Lu's markets became honest, men and women walked separately, and lost items were not taken.

id: 史记/三十世家/孔子世家::group-006
article_path: 史记/三十世家/孔子世家
source: Why not give them some land first? Li Kuan said: Let's try to stop them first. If that doesn't work, then give them the land. Is it too late? So he selected 80 beautiful women from Qi, put them all in gorgeous clothes, taught them how to dance "Kangle", and gave them to Lord Lu together with 120 horses with patterns on their bodies. First, place the female musicians and the patterned horse float outside the high gate in the south of Lucheng. Ji Huanzi wore casual clothes and went to watch it again. He planned to accept it, so he told Jun Lu that he would go out to inspect various places. He would take the opportunity to go to the south gate all day long to watch the beauties and horses of Qi State. He didn't even bother to manage the political affairs of the country. Seeing this, Zilu said to Confucius: Teacher, we can leave here. Confucius said: The State of Lu is about to hold a suburban ceremony. If the barbecue after the ceremony can be distributed to the officials according to the law, then I can stay here. Ji Huanzi finally accepted the women's band sent by Qi State and did not attend to government affairs for three days. After the suburban sacrifice, he violated common etiquette and did not give the sacrificial meat and the ritual utensils used in the suburban sacrifice to the doctor.
target: Qi, fearing Lu's rise, sent eighty beautiful women and 120 horses to Lu. Ji Huanzi accepted them, neglecting state affairs.

id: 史记/三十世家/孔子世家::group-007
article_path: 史记/三十世家/孔子世家
source: So Confucius left the state of Lu and stayed in the camp overnight that day. A musician named Shi Ji from the state of Lu came to see him off and said, "Sir, you are not at fault." Confucius said: Can I sing a song? So he sang: Those women's mouths can drive away ministers and cronies; approaching those women can cause people to ruin their affairs. Being leisurely and comfortable is the only way I can spend my time! After Master Ji returned, Huanzi asked him: What did Confucius say? Master, tell me the truth. Huanzi sighed and said, "Sir, you blame us for accepting that group of female musicians from Qi State!" Confucius then went to Weiguo and stayed at the home of Yan Zhuozou, the brother of Zilu's wife. Duke Linggong of Wei asked Confucius: How much salary did you receive in Lu? Confucius replied: Sixty thousand dou of salary. Weiguo also gave him a salary of 60,000 dou. Not long after, someone slandered Confucius in front of Duke Linggong of Wei. Duke Linggong of Wei sent Gongsun Yu to use troops to monitor Confucius' coming and going. Confucius was afraid of being punished here, so he stayed in Weiguo for ten months and then left Weiguo. Confucius was about to go to the state of Chen and passed a place called Kuang. His disciple Yan Ke drove his chariot for him. Yan Ke pointed his horse whip at Kuang and said, "I have entered this city through that gap before." When the people of Kuang heard about the arrival of their friends, they mistakenly thought that Yang Hu from the state of Lu was coming. Yang Hu had once killed the Kuang people, so the Kuang people besieged Confucius. Confucius looked very much like Yang Hu, so he was trapped there for five days. Yan Yuan arrived later, and Confucius said: I thought you were dead.
target: Confucius left Lu after the suburban sacrifice was mishandled, traveling to Wei, where he received a salary of 60,000 dou but left after slander. He was besieged in Kuang, mistaken for Yang Hu, but escaped. He returned to Wei, met Nanzi, and left after Duke Linggong's behavior disgusted him.

id: 史记/三十世家/孔子世家::group-008
article_path: 史记/三十世家/孔子世家
source: Confucius swore: If what I say is not true, God will hate me! Let God abandon me! After living in Weiguo for more than a month, Duke Linggong and his wife Nan rode in a carriage together. The eunuch Yongqu accompanied him on the right side of the carriage. After leaving the palace, he asked Confucius to sit in the second carriage and follow him, walking through the market in a swaggering manner. Confucius said: I have not seen him as fond of virtue as he is fond of beauty. So he was disgusted with what Wei Linggong did, so he left Wei State and went to Cao State. This year, Lu Dinggong passed away. Confucius left the State of Cao and arrived in the State of Song, where he practiced etiquette with his disciples under a big tree. Sima Huan of the Song Dynasty wanted to kill Confucius, so he cut down the tree. Confucius had no choice but to leave this place. The disciples urged: We can leave quickly. Confucius said: Since God has given me the mission of preaching morality, what can Huan Miao do to me? When Confucius arrived in the state of Zheng, he became separated from his disciples. Confucius stood alone at the east gate of the outer city. When the people of Zheng saw it, they said to Zigong: There is a man at the east gate. His forehead is like Yao, his neck is like Gaotao, and his shoulders are like Zheng Zichan. But from the waist down, he is three inches shorter than Yu. He looks embarrassed and listless, really like a lost dog. When Zigong met, he told Confucius the truth. Confucius said happily: He may not be right when he describes my appearance, but he is absolutely right when he says that I look like a lost dog! Absolutely right. Confucius then arrived in the state of Chen and stayed at the home of Sadako in Sicheng. More than a year later, King Wu Fucha came to attack Chen State and captured three cities before retreating. Zhao Yang attacked Chaoge. Chu State surrounded Cai State, and Cai State moved to Wu. The state of Wu defeated King Gou Jian of Yue in Kuaiji. One day, many falcons fell down and died in the palace of Chen State. They were pierced by arrows made of falcon wood. The arrowheads were made of stone and were one foot and eight inches long. Chen Minggong sent an envoy to ask Confucius for advice. Confucius said: These falcons flew from a very far away place. They are arrows from the Sushen tribe.
target: Confucius traveled to Song, where Sima Huan tried to kill him, then to Zheng, where he was described as a lost dog. In Chen, he identified arrows from the Sushen tribe.

id: 史记/三十世家/孔子世家::group-009
article_path: 史记/三十世家/孔子世家
source: Those birds and beasts know how to avoid unjust behavior, let alone me, Confucius! So he returned to his hometown, Zouxiang, and composed the music "Zou Cao" to mourn the two sages Dou Mingdu and Shunhua. Then he returned to Weiguo and stayed at Zang Boyu's house. One day, Duke Linggong of Wei asked Confucius about the formation of troops for battle. Confucius replied: I have heard about sacrifices, but I have never learned about arranging troops. The next day, when Wei Linggong was talking to Confucius, he saw wild geese flying in the sky. He just raised his head and looked up, but his expression was not on Confucius. Confucius then left the state of Wei and went to the state of Chen. In the summer of this year, Wei Linggong died, and his grandson was appointed as the king. This was Wei Chugong. In June, Zhao Yang took the exiled Prince Kuai Kuai to Qi. Yang Hu asked the prince Kuai Kuai to put on mourning clothes, and asked eight people to wear mourning clothes. They pretended to be coming from Weiguo to pick up the prince and go back to attend the funeral. Weeping, he entered Qicheng and lived there. In winter, Cai Guo moved his capital to Zhou Lai. This year was the third year of Duke Ai of Lu, and Confucius was sixty years old. The state of Qi helped the state of Wei to surround Qicheng because the crown prince of Wei, Kuai Kuai, was there. In the summer of that same year, the temples of Duke Huan and Duke Li of Lu were set on fire. Uncle Nangong Jing went to put out the fire. When Confucius heard the news in the state of Chen, he said: The fire must be in the temples of Duke Huan and Duke Li, right? It was soon confirmed that it was indeed what he said. In the autumn of this year, Ji Huanzi, who was seriously ill, saw Lucheng in his chariot. He sighed with emotion and said: In the past, this country was almost prosperous, but it did not prosper because I offended Confucius. He turned back and said to his heir Ji Kangzi: If I die, you will definitely take over the power of Lu and serve as the king; after you serve as the king, you must recall Confucius. A few days later, Ji Huanzi died and Ji Kangzi succeeded him. After the funeral was over, I thought I would return to Confucius. Dafu Gongzhiyu said: In the past, our country Lu Dinggong once appointed him, but he failed to follow through and was ridiculed by the princes. Now if you use him again, if he doesn't end well, he will be ridiculed by the princes again.
target: After three years, he left due to invasions. At Pu, he was detained but escaped after a covenant. He returned to Wei, but Duke Linggong did not use him. He considered going to Jin but turned back after learning of the deaths of two virtuous officials. He returned to Wei, then left for Chen after Duke Linggong ignored him.

id: 史记/三十世家/孔子世家::group-010
article_path: 史记/三十世家/孔子世家
source: After the funeral was over, I thought I would return to Confucius. Dafu Gongzhiyu said: In the past, our country Lu Dinggong once appointed him, but he failed to follow through and was ridiculed by the princes. Now if you use him again, if he doesn't end well, he will be ridiculed by the princes again. Ji Kangzi said: Who should I call? Gong Zhiyu said: We must summon Ranqiu. So he sent someone to recall Ran Qiu. Ran Qiu was about to get up and go, but Confucius said: This time the State of Lu summoned Ran Qiu back, he will not be used lightly, he should be used in a big way. On this day, Confucius said: Go back, go back!
target: At sixty, Confucius was in Chen. After Ji Huanzi's death, Ji Kangzi recalled Ran Qiu, and Confucius hoped to return.

id: 史记/三十世家/孔子世家::group-011
article_path: 史记/三十世家/孔子世家
source: Chang Ju said: Who is the man holding the reins of the horse? Zilu replied: It is Confucius. Chang Ju asked again: "Is he Confucius from Lu?" Zilu said: Yes. Chang Ju said: Then he should know where the ferry is. Jie Dong asked Zi Lu again: "Who are you?" Zilu said: I am Zhong Yu. Jie Dun said: Are you a disciple of Confucius? Zilu said: Yes. Jie Dun said: The world is in turmoil everywhere, and who can change this situation? Besides, instead of running around with those who are fleeing from the rioters, why not follow those of us who are fleeing from the troubled times? After saying that, he continued to plow the fields non-stop. Zilu told Confucius this, and Confucius said disappointedly: We can't live in the mountains and forests with the birds and beasts. If the world were peaceful, I wouldn't have to run around trying to change this situation. One day, when Zi Lu was walking alone, he met an old man carrying a weeding tool on his shoulder. Zilu asked him: Have you seen my teacher? The old man said: You people are not diligent in your limbs and cannot distinguish the grains. How can I know who your teacher is? After saying that, he went to pull weeds on crutches. Later, Zilu told Confucius what happened. Confucius said: This is a hermit. I asked Zilu to look there again, but the old man was gone. Three years after Confucius moved to the state of Cai, the state of Wu attacked the state of Chen.
target: He moved to Cai, then to Ye, where he advised on governance. He met hermits Chang Ju and Jie Ni, who criticized his efforts.

id: 史记/三十世家/孔子世家::group-012
article_path: 史记/三十世家/孔子世家
source: I asked Zilu to look there again, but the old man was gone. Three years after Confucius moved to the state of Cai, the state of Wu attacked the state of Chen. The State of Chu rescued the State of Chen, and the army was stationed in Chengfu. Hearing that Confucius lived on the border of Chen and Cai, Chu sent people to hire Confucius. Confucius was about to go to see and accept the betrothal gift. The officials of Chen and Cai discussed and said: Confucius is a talented and virtuous man, and what he criticizes and satirizes are all about the shortcomings of the princes. Now we have been stuck between Chen and Cai for a long time. The administration and actions of the officials are not in line with Zhongni's wishes. Today's Chu State is a big country, but it came to hire Confucius. If Confucius is reused in Chu State, then our officials in power in Chen and Cai will be in danger. So both sides sent some laborers to besiege Confucius in the wild. Confucius and his disciples were unable to move and their food supply was cut off. The disciples who followed him were sick from hunger and could not stand up. But Confucius continued to give lectures, recite poems, sing, and play the piano to everyone.
target: He was besieged between Chen and Cai, running out of food, but continued teaching. His disciples questioned their plight, but Confucius maintained his principles.

id: 史记/三十世家/孔子世家::group-013
article_path: 史记/三十世家/孔子世家
source: So he sent Zigong to the state of Chu. King Zhao of Chu mobilized his army to meet Confucius, and this disaster was avoided. King Zhao of Chu wanted to grant Confucius a 700-mile land with household registration. Zixi, the envoy of Chu State, stopped him and said: "Among the envoys sent by your Majesty to the various vassal states, are there people like Zigong?" King Zhao said: No. Zixi asked again: "Are there any of the king's assistant ministers like Yan Hui?" King Zhao said: No.
target: King Zhao of Chu planned to grant him land, but Zixi dissuaded him, and the king died soon after. Confucius returned to Wei, then to Lu after fourteen years.

id: 史记/三十世家/孔子世家::group-014
article_path: 史记/三十世家/孔子世家
source: After examining the additions and deletions made by the Yin Dynasty to the Xia Dynasty in the etiquette system, Confucius said: Even after a hundred years in the future, the increases and decreases can be predicted, because one kind of emphasis is on literary talent, and the other is on simplicity. The etiquette system of the Zhou Dynasty was formulated based on the Xia Dynasty and the Yin Dynasty. It is so rich and colorful. I advocate using the etiquette of the Zhou Dynasty. Therefore, "Shu Zhuan" and "Book of Rites" were both compiled by Confucius. Confucius once said to the music official Taishi of Lu: Music can be understood. At the beginning of the performance, they should cooperate with each other, and continue to have a harmonious rhythm, clear and continuous sound, until the whole piece of music is completed. Confucius also said: After I returned to Lu from Wei, I began to correct the poetry and music, restoring the original tunes of "Ya" and "Song". There are more than 3,000 poems handed down from ancient times. At the time of Confucius, he deleted the repetitive ones and selected those that were consistent with the meaning for etiquette education. The earliest ones traced the ancestors of Yin, Qi, and the ancestors of Zhou, Houji. The second ones described the prosperity of the Yin and Zhou dynasties, until the political absence of King Zhou You and King Li of Zhou. The beginning was a poem describing the relationship and feelings between men and women, so it is said: The movement "Guan Sui" is the first chapter of "Guofeng", "Lu Ming" is the first chapter of "Xiao Ya", "King Wen" is the first chapter of "Daya", and "Qing Temple" is the first chapter of "Ode". Confucius was able to play and sing the three hundred and five poems in order to match the tunes of the music "Shao", "Wu", "Ya" and "Song". From then on, the music system of the former kings was restored to the old view and could be described. The king's way was complete, and Confucius also completed the compilation of "Poetry", "Book", "Yue", "Yi" and "Spring and Autumn" which are known as the "Six Arts". In his later years, Confucius liked to study "The Book of Changes". He explained in detail the "Yun Ci", "Xici", "Gua", "Classic Chinese", etc. Confucius read the "Book of Changes" so diligently that he broke the cowhide rope that woven the slips through many times. He also said: If I live a few more years, I will be able to fully understand the diction and meaning of "The Book of Changes". Confucius used "Poems", "Books", "Li" and "Music" as teaching materials to educate his disciples. There were about 3,000 disciples studying there, and 72 of them were proficient in the six skills of etiquette, music, archery, charioteering, arithmetic, and shu. As for people like Yan Zhuozou, there are even more disciples who were taught by Confucius in many aspects but were not formally naturalized. Confucius educated his disciples in four aspects: knowledge, words and deeds, loyalty and forgiveness, and faith. Set four prohibitions for disciples: don’t speculate, don’t be arbitrary, don’t be stubborn, and don’t be self-righteous. Things that he believed should be handled with special caution were: fasting, war, and disease. Confucius rarely talked about profit. If he did, it was associated with fate and benevolence.
target: In Lu, Confucius was not appointed to office. He compiled the "Shu Zhuan" and "Book of Rites," corrected poetry and music, and studied the "Book of Changes," wearing out the binding cords. He taught about 3,000 disciples, with 72 mastering the six arts. He educated in knowledge, conduct, loyalty, and faith, avoiding profit unless linked to fate and benevolence. He was humble in his hometown but eloquent in court. He avoided spoiled food and improper seating, and showed sympathy to mourners and the blind.

id: 史记/三十世家/孔子世家::group-015
article_path: 史记/三十世家/孔子世家
source: Confucius said: If you don't lower your ambitions and don't let your personality be insulted, only Boyi and Shuqi Bing can do it! He also said: Liu Xiahui and Shaolian lowered their ambitions and insulted their personalities. It is also said that Yu Zhong and Yi Yi lived in seclusion, did not talk about worldly affairs, behaved in a noble and pure manner, and abandoned themselves in a contingency manner. He also said: I am different from them. I neither lower my ambitions or humiliate myself in order to make progress, nor do I live in seclusion and escape from the world. There is no absolute can and no absolute can't. Confucius said: No, no! The most worrying thing for a gentleman is that he will not leave a good reputation after his death. If my ideas cannot be implemented, what should I leave to future generations? So he made the Spring and Autumn Annals based on the history books of the Lu State, starting from the first year of Lu Yin to the fourteenth year of Lu Aigong, and included a total of twelve monarchs of the Lu State. The narrative is centered on the state of Lu, respects the royal family of Zhou as the orthodoxy, uses the ancient traditions of the Yin and Shang Dynasties as a reference, and extends the legal tradition of Xia, Shang and Zhou Dynasties. The writing is simple and the purpose is broad. Therefore, the people of Wu and Chu who claimed to be kings were still derogated as viscounts in the Spring and Autumn Annals; Duke Wen of Jin actually summoned King Xiang of Zhou to join the alliance in Jiantu, but the Spring and Autumn Annals avoid saying that the Emperor of Zhou came to Heyang on a hunting tour. By analogy, "Spring and Autumn" used this principle to praise and criticize various events at that time. Later, some kings praised and promoted it, so that the justice and law of "Spring and Autumn" prevailed in the world, and the rebellious officials and traitors in the world became afraid.
target: In his later years, Confucius compiled the "Spring and Autumn Annals" based on Lu's history, covering twelve rulers. He used subtle writing to praise and criticize, making rebellious officials fearful.

id: 史记/三十世家/孔子世家::group-016
article_path: 史记/三十世家/孔子世家
source: After that, Confucius died. Confucius was seventy-three years old and died on Ji Chou day in April of the sixteenth year of Duke Ai of Lu. Duke Ai of Lu wrote a eulogy for him and said: God is not kind and refuses to keep this old man. He leaves me alone and I am lonely and hurt. ah! How painful! Nifu, there is no one who can serve as a role model for me to learn from! Zigong said, "Master of Lu, can't he stay in Lu forever?" The teacher said: Loss of Dharma will lead to confusion, and loss of status will lead to faults. If you lose your will, you will become confused; if you lose your ability, you will make mistakes. You cannot use the teacher while he is alive, but it is not appropriate to mourn him after he is dead. It is inappropriate to call him "Yu Yiren" as a prince. After his death, Confucius was buried on the shore of Surabaya, north of Lucheng. His disciples mourned him in their hearts for three years.
target: He died at seventy-three in the sixteenth year of Duke Ai of Lu. Duke Ai mourned him, but Zigong criticized the eulogy.

id: 史记/三十世家/孔子世家::group-017
article_path: 史记/三十世家/孔子世家
source: If you lose your will, you will become confused; if you lose your ability, you will make mistakes. You cannot use the teacher while he is alive, but it is not appropriate to mourn him after he is dead. It is inappropriate to call him "Yu Yiren" as a prince. After his death, Confucius was buried on the shore of Surabaya, north of Lucheng. His disciples mourned him in their hearts for three years. After three years of mourning, when everyone said goodbye and left, they all cried to each other and mourned each other; some even stayed. Only Zigong lived in a small room next to the tomb and guarded the tomb for a total of six years before leaving. His disciples and others from the state of Lu led more than a hundred people who lived near the tomb. So this place was named Kongli. It has been passed down from generation to generation in the State of Lu that they regularly visit Confucius's tomb every year to worship. Confucian scholars also come here at this time to learn etiquette, go to the countryside for academic examinations, have drinking ceremonies, and perform archery competitions and other ceremonies. Confucius's tomb is an area of ​​one hectare. The main hall of Confucius's former residence and the inner rooms where his disciples lived were later converted into temples to store the clothes, hats, musical instruments, cars, books, etc. that Confucius wore during his lifetime. Until the Han Dynasty, it was not abandoned for more than 200 years. Emperor Liu Bang of Gao Dynasty passed through the land of Lu and sacrificed Confucius with Tailao, which was equipped with cattle, sheep and pigs.
target: Confucius was buried north of Lucheng. Disciples mourned for three years, with Zigong staying six years. His tomb became a site of annual worship, and his former residence was turned into a temple, preserved for over 200 years. Emperor Liu Bang of Han sacrificed to him.

id: 史记/三十世家/孔子世家::group-018
article_path: 史记/三十世家/孔子世家
source: His disciples and others from the state of Lu led more than a hundred people who lived near the tomb. So this place was named Kongli. It has been passed down from generation to generation in the State of Lu that they regularly visit Confucius's tomb every year to worship. Confucian scholars also come here at this time to learn etiquette, go to the countryside for academic examinations, have drinking ceremonies, and perform archery competitions and other ceremonies. Confucius's tomb is an area of ​​one hectare. The main hall of Confucius's former residence and the inner rooms where his disciples lived were later converted into temples to store the clothes, hats, musical instruments, cars, books, etc. that Confucius wore during his lifetime. Until the Han Dynasty, it was not abandoned for more than 200 years.
