When princes, ministers, officials, and prime ministers arrive at their posts, they often visit the tomb of Confucius before taking office and handling government affairs. Confucius gave birth to a carp, named Boyu. Boyu died at the age of fifty, before Confucius. Boyu gave birth to Ji, whose name was Zisi. Guo was sixty-two years old. Once trapped in the Song Dynasty. Zisi wrote "The Doctrine of the Mean".
target: Confucius' descendants continued his lineage, including his son Boyu, who died before him, and grandson Zisi, who wrote "The Doctrine of the Mean." The historian concluded that Confucius, though a commoner, became the supreme sage, with his teachings enduring for generations.

id: 史记/三十世家/宋微子世家::group-000
article_path: 史记/三十世家/宋微子世家
source: Wei Zikai was the eldest son of Emperor Yi of the Yin Dynasty and the half-brother of King Zhou. After Shang Zhou came to the throne, his rule was dark, he did not care about the affairs of the country, he was licentious and extravagant, and his followers repeatedly came to the throne, but King Zhou did not listen. When Zuyi destroyed Xu due to Zhou Xibochang's virtuous governance, Weizi was worried that disaster would befall the Yin Dynasty, so he repeatedly advised King Zhou. But King Zhou said: Wasn't it my destiny to be in Gastrodia when I was born? Who can do anything to me? Wei Zi then expected that King Zhou would not listen to his advice until his death, and planned to die or leave King Zhou. But he could not make a decision, so he went to ask the Taishi and Shaoshi, saying: The Yin Dynasty no longer has clear politics and cannot govern the four directions well.
target: Wei Zikai, eldest son of Emperor Yi of Yin and half-brother of King Zhou, repeatedly advised King Zhou against his dark, licentious rule but was ignored. Fearing Yin's downfall, Wei Zi consulted the Grand Master and Junior Master, who advised him to leave when the kingdom became irredeemable. He then departed.

id: 史记/三十世家/宋微子世家::group-001
article_path: 史记/三十世家/宋微子世家
source: The Grand Master followed suit and said: Prince, the Emperor of Heaven has brought disaster and destroyed the Yin Dynasty, but King Zhou is not afraid of the punishment of Heaven, nor does he listen to the advice of his elders. Now, the subjects of the Yin Dynasty actually violated and falsely accused the gods of their will. Now, if the Yin Dynasty can really be saved and the country is well managed, even if he dies, there will be no resentment left. I'm afraid that even if you die for the country, the country still can't be governed, so it's better to go far away. So Wei Zi left the Yin Dynasty. Jizi is a relative of King Zhou. When King Zhou first made ivory chopsticks, Jizi lamented: If he makes ivory chopsticks now, he will definitely make jade cups in the future; if he makes jade cups, he will definitely want to take possession of rare treasures from far away. The luxury of carriages, horses and palaces will definitely start from here, and the country will definitely not be able to revitalize. Because of King Zhou's excessive sexual behavior, Jizi came to remonstrate with him, but King Zhou still refused to listen. Someone said: You can leave now. Jizi said: When a minister remonstrates with the monarch, the monarch ignores him and then leaves him. This is to publicize the monarch's evil deeds and to flatter the people by grandstanding. I cannot bear to do this. So Jizi disheveled his hair, pretended to be crazy and became a slave. He lived in seclusion and masturbated by playing the piano, so people praised his song as "Ji Zi Cao". Prince Bigan was also a relative of King Zhou. When he saw that Jizi was admonishing, but the monarch did not listen and became a slave, he said: "The monarch has sins, and if he cannot persuade him directly with death, the people will suffer, and what crime do the people have?" So, he bluntly remonstrated with King Zhou. King Zhou was furious and said: I heard that the saint's heart has seven orifices. Is this true? So King Zhou killed Bigan and dug out his heart to verify. Wei Zi said: Father and son are connected by flesh and blood, while ministers and ministers are connected by morality. Therefore, if a father is at fault and his son refuses to listen to his advice over and over again, he should cry accordingly; if a minister refuses to listen to his advice after repeated advice, then morally speaking, the minister can leave the king. So, the Grand Master and the Young Master advised Wei Zi to leave, and Wei Zi left. King Wu of Zhou attacked King Zhou and defeated the Yin Dynasty. Weizi came to King Wu's military gate with his sacrificial weapon in hand. He exposed his right arm and tied his hands behind his back. He had someone on the left holding the sheep and someone on the right holding a straw. He knelt on the ground and went forward to beg King Wu. So King Wu released Wei Zi and restored his original title. King Wu made Wu Geng, the son of Shang Zhou, his father and asked him to inherit the sacrifices of the Yin Dynasty. He also sent Uncle Guan and Uncle Cai to assist him. After King Wu destroyed the Yin Dynasty, he went to visit Jizi. King Wu said: Alas! God silently stabilizes the people so that they can live and work in peace and contentment, but I don't know the common order of God's order for the people. Jizi replied: Once upon a time, Gun blocked the flood and disturbed the laws of the Five Elements of Heaven, so God was angry and did not give him the nine great laws of heaven to govern the country. Gun was killed, and Yu succeeded him. God then gave Yu Tianda nine kinds of great laws, and the ethical laws were thus ordered. Of these nine great laws, one is called the Five Elements, the second is called the Five Matters, the third is called the Eight Political Rules, the fourth is called the Five Disciplines, the fifth is called Emperor Ji, the sixth is called Three Virtues, the seventh is called suspicion, the eighth is called Concubine Zheng, the ninth is called Appointment and Five Blessings, and people are afraid of using the Six Extremes.
target: Jizi, a relative of King Zhou, lamented King Zhou's extravagance with ivory chopsticks, foreseeing ruin. After King Zhou ignored his remonstrations, Jizi feigned madness and became a slave rather than publicize the king's evil. Prince Bigan, another relative, bluntly admonished King Zhou, who killed him and ripped out his heart to check for seven orifices. Wei Zi concluded that ministers may leave a king who refuses repeated advice. King Wu of Zhou defeated Yin, and Wei Zi surrendered, bearing sacrificial vessels. King Wu restored Wei Zi's title and appointed Wu Geng, son of Shang Zhou, to continue Yin sacrifices, with Guan Shu and Cai Shu as assistants. King Wu visited Jizi, who explained the nine great laws of heaven: the Five Elements, Five Matters, Eight Political Rules, Five Epochs, Imperial Principles, Three Virtues, Divination, Various Signs, and Five Blessings with Six Extremes. King Wu granted Jizi Korea, no longer treating him as a subject. Jizi later composed a poem mourning Yin's ruins.

id: 史记/三十世家/宋微子世家::group-002
article_path: 史记/三十世家/宋微子世家
source: The so-called boy is King Zhou. When the people of Yin saw this poem, they all cried for it. After King Wu died and King Cheng was still young, Zhou Gongdan took charge of the state power as an acting administrator. Uncle Guan and Uncle Cai suspected Zhou Gongdan, so they started a rebellion with Wu Geng and wanted to attack King Cheng and Duke Zhou. Zhou Gong borrowed the order from King Cheng to kill Wu Geng and Guan Shu, and banished Cai Shu. He also asked Wei Zikai to take charge of Yin in Wu Geng's place to continue the sacrifice of Yin's ancestors. He also warned him with the "Wei Zi's Order" and sealed Wei Zi in the Song Dynasty. Weizi was originally benevolent, righteous and capable. After replacing Wu Geng, the people in the old land of the Yin Dynasty loved him very much. After Wei Zikai died, he made his younger brother Yan the king of the country. This is Wei Zhong. After Weizhong's death, his son Song Gongji came to the throne. After the death of Song Gongji, his son Ding Gongshen came to the throne. After the death of Ding Gongshen, his son Min Gong came to the throne. After Min Gong died, his younger brother Yang Gongxi came to the throne. After Duke Yang ascended the throne, Min Gong's son Yusi killed Duke Yang and seized the throne, and announced: "I should ascend the throne." This is Duke Li. After Li Gong died, his son Li Gongju came to the throne. In the seventeenth year of Ligong's reign, King Li of Zhou fled to pig. In the twenty-eighth year, after Duke Li died, his son Hui Gong came to the throne. In the fourth year of Duke Hui, King Xuan of Zhou came to the throne. In the thirtieth year, Duke Hui passed away and Duke Ai came to the throne. Ai Gong died in the first year, and his son Dai Gong came to the throne. In the twenty-ninth year of Dai Gong, King You of Zhou was killed by Quan Rong, and Qin began to be classified as a vassal state. In the thirty-fourth year, Duke Dai died, and his son Wu Gong came to the throne empty. Duke Wu gave birth to a daughter, who later became the wife of Duke Hui of Lu and gave birth to Duke Huan of Lu. In the eighteenth year, Duke Wu died and his son Xuan Gongli came to the throne. Xuan Gong's prince's name is Yi.
target: After King Wu's death, Zhou Gongdan, acting as regent, suppressed a rebellion by Guan Shu, Cai Shu, and Wu Geng. He killed Wu Geng, exiled Cai Shu, and appointed Wei Zikai to rule Yin, later enfeoffing him in Song. Wei Zi's benevolent rule endeared him to the people. His successors included Wei Zhong, Song Gongji, Ding Gongshen, Min Gong, Yang Gongxi, Li Gong, Li Gongju, Hui Gong, Ai Gong, Dai Gong, Wu Gong, Xuan Gongli, and Mu Gong. Mu Gong, honoring his brother Xuan Gong's wish, passed the throne to Xuan Gong's son Yi (Duke Shang) instead of his own son.

id: 史记/三十世家/宋微子世家::group-003
article_path: 史记/三十世家/宋微子世家
source: In this year, the people of Lu killed their own king Yin Gong. Ten years later, Governor Hua killed Kong's father and took away his wife. Duke Shang was very angry, so Governor Hua killed Duke Shang, and brought Feng Mu's son back from Zheng and made him king. This is Duke Zhuang. In the first year of Zhuang Gong, Governor Hua became prime minister. In the ninth year, he arrested Zheng Zhong's Ji Zhong and threatened him to become the king of Zheng. Ji Zhong agreed and finally made Tu Tu the king. In the 19th year, Duke Zhuang passed away and his son Min Gongjie came to the throne. In the seventh year of Duke Min, Duke Huan of Qi came to the throne.
target: Duke Shang's reign saw turmoil: Hua Du killed Kong's father and Duke Shang, installing Duke Zhuang. Subsequent rulers included Min Gong, Huan Gong, Xiang Gong, Cheng Gong, Zhao Gong, Wen Gong, Gong Gong, Ping Gong, Yuan Gong, Jing Gong, Zhao Gong, Duke Du, Xiu Gongtian, Pi Gong, Ticheng, and Yan.

source: In the ninth year, Duke Zhao was ignorant and immoral, and the people did not rely on him. Duke Zhao's younger brother Bao Ge was very virtuous and courteous to the corporal. Once upon a time, Mrs. Xianggong wanted to have an affair with her son Bao, but failed, so she helped Bao do favors to the people. With the help of doctor Hua Yuan, he was elected as the right master. When Zhaogong went hunting, his wife Wang Ji asked Wei Bo to kill Zhaogong Chujiu. Zhaogong's younger brother Bao Ge came to the throne. This was Duke Wen. In the first year of Emperor Wen's reign, the Jin State led its princes to attack the Song State and condemned the Song State for killing its king Chujiu.
target: Yan, known as "Jie Song," indulged in cruelty and debauchery, shooting advisors. The princes allied with Qi to attack Song, killing Yan and dividing its territory in his forty-seventh year.

source: When King Yan of the Song Dynasty came to the throne forty-seven years, King Min of Qi joined forces with Wei and Chu to attack the Song State, killed Yan, destroyed the Song State, and divided the Song State's territory. Tai Shigong said: Confucius said: Weizi left, Jizi became a slave, Bigan was killed when he came to remonstrate, and there were three benevolent people in the Yin Dynasty. "Spring and Autumn" ridiculed that the turmoil in the Song Dynasty began when Duke Xuan deposed the prince and allowed his younger brother to take the throne. The country was unstable for ten generations. When Duke Xiang was in power, he practiced benevolence and righteousness and wanted to be the leader of the alliance. In order to praise him, his doctor Zheng Kaofu traced the reasons for the prosperity of the Yin Dynasty in the Qi, Tang and Gaozong periods and wrote "Ode to Shang". Song Xianggong was defeated at Hongshui, but some gentlemen still thought he was worthy of praise. This was because the gentlemen lamented that the countries in the Central Plains region lacked etiquette at that time, so they commended him because Song Xianggong had a spirit of courtesy.
target: Tai Shigong concluded that Confucius recognized three benevolent men of Yin: Wei Zi, Jizi, and Bigan. The "Spring and Autumn" noted Song's instability began when Duke Xuan deposed the prince for his brother. Duke Xiang's benevolent attempts at leadership were praised, though he was defeated at Hongshui; gentlemen commended his adherence to ritual propriety amidst the era's lack of etiquette.

source: So the Jin people made Aihou's son Xiaozi their king, and he became Xiaozihou. In the first year of Xiaozi's reign, Duke Wu of Quwo ordered Han Wan to kill the captured Jin Aihou. Quwo became more and more powerful, and Jin had nothing to do with it. In the fourth year of Jin Xiaozi's reign, Quwo Wu Gong deceived Jin Xiaozi and killed him. King Huan of Zhou sent Guo Zhong to attack Duke Wu of Quwo. Duke Wu fled back to Quwo, and Marquis Ai of Jin's younger brother Min was made Marquis of Jin. In the fourth year of Jin Houmin's reign, the Song Dynasty arrested Zheng Zhong's Ji Zhong and forced him to establish Tu as the king of Zheng. In the 19th year of the Marquis of Jin, the Qi people Guan Zhifu killed his own monarch Qi Xianggong. In the twenty-eighth year of the Marquis of Jin, Duke Huan of Qi began to dominate. Duke Wu of Quwo attacked Jin Hou Min, destroyed Jin, and dedicated all the treasures of Jin to King Zhouli. King Li appointed Duke Wu of Quwo as the king of Jin and listed him as a prince, so Duke Wu annexed the entire land of Jin and made it his own. Duke Wu of Quwo had been on the throne for thirty-seven years before he changed his title to Duke Wu of Jin. Duke Wugong of Jin began to move to the capital of Jin State, including the previous accession to the throne in Quwo, for a total of thirty-eight years. Duke Wu claimed to be the great-grandson of the late king Muhou of Jin and the grandson of Uncle Huan Quwo. Uncle Huan was the first to be granted the title of Quwo. Duke Wu is the son of Uncle Zhuang. It was a total of sixty-seven years from the time when Uncle Huan was first granted the title of Quwo to the time when Duke Wu destroyed the state of Jin. Duke Wu finally replaced the state of Jin and became a vassal. Duke Wu died in the second year after he replaced the king of Jin. Including his reign in Quwo, he died in a total of thirty-nine years. His son Xian Gong Gui Zhu came to the throne. In the first year of Xian AD, King Hui of Zhou's brother Tuan attacked King Hui. King Hui fled and lived in Liyi of Zheng State.
target: The conflict between Quwo and Jin continued for generations. Quwo Zhuangbo killed Xiaohou, and later Quwo Wugong killed Aihou and Xiaozi. Finally, in the 28th year of Hou Min, Duke Wu of Quwo destroyed Jin, presented its treasures to King Li of Zhou, and was appointed ruler of Jin. Duke Wu had reigned 37 years in Quwo before becoming Duke Wu of Jin. He died two years after replacing the Jin ruler, and his son Xian Gong succeeded.

source: Duke Wu died in the second year after he replaced the king of Jin. Including his reign in Quwo, he died in a total of thirty-nine years. His son Xian Gong Gui Zhu came to the throne. In the first year of Xian AD, King Hui of Zhou's brother Tuan attacked King Hui. King Hui fled and lived in Liyi of Zheng State. In the fifth year, Duke Xian of Jin attacked Li Rong and obtained Li Ji and Li Ji's sister, whom he loved very much. In the eighth year of the Jin Dynasty, many princes from Jin State had fled to Guo State. Therefore, Guo Gong once again attacked Jin State, but failed to win. In the tenth year of Xiangong's reign, Jin wanted to attack Guo, but Shi Jiang said: Let's wait until it has its own civil strife! In the twelfth year, Li Ji gave birth to Xi Qi. Duke Xian planned to depose the prince, so he said: Quwo is the place where the ancestral temple of our ancestors is located, while Pu is close to Qin and Qu is close to Zhai. If the princes are not allowed to guard those places, I will be worried. So Duke Xian asked Prince Shen Sheng to garrison Quwo, Prince Chong'er to garrison Pu, and Prince Yiwu to garrison Qu. Xi Qi, the son of Duke Xian and Li Ji, lived in Jiang, the capital of the country. Therefore, the people of Jin knew that the prince would not be able to ascend the throne. Prince Shen Sheng's mother was Qi Huangong's daughter, named Qi Jiang, who had died long ago. Shen Sheng's half-sister is Mrs. Mu Gong of Qin. Chong'er's mother was a woman of the Hu family in Zhai. Yiwu's mother is the sister of Chong'er's mother. Duke Xian had eight sons in total. Prince Shen Sheng, Chong'er, and Yi Wu were all virtuous and of high moral character. After Duke Xiang had Li Ji, he alienated his three sons. In the 16th year, Duke Xiang of Jin established two armies. Xian Gong commanded the upper army, Prince Shen Sheng commanded the lower army, Zhao Su drove the chariot, and Bi Wan served as the right guard. They successively conquered and destroyed Huo, Wei, and Geng. After the whole army returned to Jin, Xian Gong helped the prince build a city in Quwo, gave the land of Geng to Zhao Su, and gave the land of Wei to Bi Wan, making them officials.
target: Duke Xian attacked Li Rong, obtained Li Ji and her sister, and favored them greatly. Li Ji gave birth to Xi Qi. Duke Xian planned to depose Crown Prince Shen Sheng, sending him to garrison Quwo while sending Chong'er and Yiwu elsewhere. Li Ji falsely accused Shen Sheng of poisoning food meant for Duke Xian. Unable to prove his innocence, Shen Sheng committed suicide. Chong'er and Yiwu fled in fear. Duke Xian sent troops against them, and Chong'er escaped to Di while Yiwu fled to Liang.

source: Xun Xi said: I cannot break my promise to the late king. In October, Rick killed Xi Qi in the mourning place. At that time, Duke Xian had not yet been buried. Xun Xi planned to die, but someone suggested that he should make Xi Qi's younger brother mourn his son and assist him. Xun Xi then made a mourning son and buried Duke Xian. In November, Rick killed his mourning son in the court, and Xun Xi also committed suicide. The gentleman said: "The Book of Songs" says that if a white stone has spots, it can be polished, but if it is wrong, it cannot be saved. This is Xun Xi! Xun Xi did not break his promise. At the beginning, when Duke Xian was about to attack Li Rong, Turtle Bu said, "Slanderous words can cause harm." After defeating Li Rong and getting Li Ji, Duke Xian doted on her so much that he actually caused chaos in the Jin Kingdom. Rick and others have killed Xi Qi and Dao Zi, and sent people to Zhai State to welcome the young master Chong'er, intending to support him. Chong'er thanked him and said: "I escaped from Jin against my father's orders. After my father passed away, I couldn't attend the funeral according to the etiquette of a son. How could I dare to return to my country and take the throne? Please ask the doctor to appoint someone else instead." The person sent came back to report to Rick, who sent someone to Liang Kingdom to meet Yi Wu. Yiwu wanted to return to Jin, but Lu Sheng and Cherui said: "It is hard to believe that there are still young masters in the country who can ascend the throne, but they go abroad to find them." I guess it would be very dangerous not to go to Qin in order to use the power of a powerful country to return to Jin. So Yiwu asked Cherui to bribe Qin with generous gifts, and agreed: If I can return to Jin, I am willing to dedicate Hexi of Jin to Qin. Yiwu also wrote a letter to Rick saying: If I can really ascend the throne, I am willing to seal the city of Fenyang to you. Duke Mu of Qin sent troops to escort Yi Wu back to Jin. When Duke Huan of Qi heard about the civil strife in Jin, he also led the princes to Jin. The Qin army and Yi Wu also arrived at the Jin State at this time. The Qi State asked Peng Peng to join the Qin State in sending Yi Wu back to the Jin State and made him the king of Jin. This is Hui Gong. Duke Huan of Qi returned to Qi after arriving at Gaoliang of Jin. In the first year of Yiwu, Hui Gong sent Pi Zheng to apologize to the King of Qin and said: I promised you the land of Hexi. Now I am fortunate to return to the country and become the king. The minister said: The land was left by the ancestors. You are on the run, so why should you arbitrarily grant it to Qin? My efforts were in vain, so I apologized to Qin. At the same time, Yiwu did not grant Fenyang City to Rick, but instead took away his power. In April, King Zhou Xiang sent Duke Zhou's father-in-law to meet the officials of Qi and Qin to visit Duke Hui of Jin. Because Chong'er was on the run, Duke Hui was afraid that Rick would launch a coup, so he ordered Rick to die and said to him: Without you Rick, I cannot ascend the throne.
target: After Duke Xian died, Li Ke killed Xi Qi and his brother, then invited Chong'er to return, but he refused. Yiwu was brought back with Qin's help and became Duke Hui. He broke promises to grant land to Qin and reward Li Ke, instead forcing Li Ke to commit suicide. When Qin suffered famine, Jin refused aid and attacked Qin instead. Duke Hui was captured at the Battle of Han Yuan but later released. After Duke Hui died, his son Duke Huai succeeded but was killed by Qin forces escorting Chong'er back.

source: Besides, I have already expressed my complaint and will never eat his salary. Mother said: How about letting Mr. Wen know about your situation? Jie Zitui replied: Words are flower decorations on everyone's body. The body wants to be hidden, so why use flower decorations anymore? Putting on floral decorations is about showing yourself off. Jie Zitui's mother said, "Can I do what you said?" Then I'll hide with you. Mother and son never showed up again until their deaths. Jie Zitui's followers felt pity for him, so they hung a sign at the entrance of the palace, which read: If a dragon wants to go to heaven, it needs the help of five snakes. The dragon has gone deep into the clouds, and the four snakes have each entered their own palaces. Only one snake is sad and resentful alone, and ultimately cannot find its own place. When Duke Wen came out of the palace, he saw these words and said: This is Jie Zitui. I was worried about the royal family and had not yet been able to consider his merits. So Duke Wen sent someone to call Jie Zitui, but Jie Zitui had already escaped. Duke Wen asked about Jie Zitui's residence and heard that he had entered Mianshang Mountain. So, Duke Wen sealed the entire Mianshang Mountain to Jie Zitui, and called it Jie Tui Field as his fief, and named it Jieshan, in order to record my sins and commend talented people. Uncle Hu, an incompetent man who fled with Duke Wen, said: Your Majesty, you have rewarded the meritorious officials three times but it has not been my turn. May I ask what I am guilty of? Duke Wen reported back: Teach me with benevolence and righteousness, advise me with morality and kindness, and you should be highly rewarded. Assisting me with actions finally brought me success, which deserves a lesser reward. He took on the danger of bows and arrows and made great contributions to me, which should be rewarded again. If you only use your labor to serve me without making up for my mistakes, you should be rewarded again. After these three rewards are over, it will be your turn. The people of Jin were very happy when they heard Duke Wen's words. In the spring of the second year, the Qin army was stationed by the Yellow River and was about to escort the King of Zhou back to Beijing. Zhao Shui said: If you want to become the overlord, it is better to escort the King of Zhou back to the capital and respect the King of Zhou. Zhou and Jin have the same surname. If Jin does not escort King Zhou back to the capital first and falls behind Qin, it will not be able to issue orders in the world. Today, respecting the king of Zhou is the capital of Jin's dominance. On the first day of the third month, Jin sent troops to Yangfan, surrounded Wen, and escorted King Xiang of Zhou to the capital of Zhou. In April, Jin killed Wang Zidai, the younger brother of King Xiang. King Zhou Xiang gave the land of Hanoi and Yangfan to the State of Jin. In four years, King Chu Cheng and other princes surrounded Song State. Gongsun Gu of Song State rushed to Jin State to ask for help.
target: Chong'er, Duke Wen, had fled for 19 years, traveling through Di, Qi, Cao, Song, Zheng, Chu, and finally Qin. He returned at age 62 and was welcomed by most Jin people. After securing his position, he rewarded followers but initially forgot Jie Zitui, who hid in Mianshang Mountain and died there. Duke Wen later granted the mountain to Jie Zitui's memory. Duke Wen became hegemon after assisting King Xiang of Zhou and defeating Chu at Chengpu. After his death, his son Duke Xiang succeeded.

source: Qin sent Suihui to Wei, so he captured Suihui and brought him back to Jin. In the eighth year, King Qing of Zhou passed away. Due to the vying for power among the officials, no obituary was issued to the various vassal states. The Jin State sent Zhao Dun to lead 800 chariots to quell the chaos in the Zhou Dynasty and support King Kuang. This year, King Zhuang of Chu just ascended the throne. In ten years, the people of Qi killed their own king Yigong. In the fourteenth year, Duke Ling grew up and became very extravagant. He plundered people's wealth and used color paintings to decorate the palace walls. Shooting people from a high platform and having fun watching people avoid the projectiles. When the cook failed to boil the bear's paws, Duke Lin became angry and killed the cook. He asked the women to carry the body of the cook and throw it out past the court. Zhao Dun and others went to the meeting to give advice many times, but Duke Linggong didn't listen at all. Later, they saw the dead man's hand again, so they went to give advice again. Suihui went to persuade him first, but Duke Ling didn't listen. Duke Linggong was very worried and asked Chu Qi to assassinate Zhao Dun.
target: The text continues through many generations of Jin rulers, including Duke Ling (who was killed for his tyranny), Duke Cheng, Duke Jing, Duke Li, and Duke Mourning. The power of the six ministerial families grew while the ducal house weakened.

source: The king of Jin only occupied Jiang and Quwo, and the rest were merged into the three Jins. In the fifteenth year, Wei Wenhou ascended the throne. In the eighteenth year, Duke You raped a woman and went out of the city at night, where he was killed by bandits. Marquis Wen of Wei sent troops to quell the civil strife in Jin, and appointed Duke You's son Zhi, who was Duke Lie. In the nineteenth year of Duke Lie, King Weilie of Zhou granted the states of Zhao, Han, and Wei the title of prince, and made them all princes. In the twenty-seventh year, Lie Gong passed away, and his son Xiao Gongqi came to the throne. In the ninth year of Duke Xiao's reign, Marquis Wu of Wei had just ascended the throne and attacked Handan. He failed to win and left. In the seventeenth year, Duke Xiao passed away and his son, Duke Jing, came to the throne. This year is the first year of King Qi Wei. In the second year of Jinggong, Marquis Wu of Wei, Marquis Han Ai, and Marquis Zhao Jing destroyed the Jin Kingdom and divided the Jin land into three parts. Jinggong became a commoner, and the state of Jin stopped offering sacrifices.
target: Eventually, Zhao, Han, and Wei divided Jin among themselves. In the second year of Duke Jing, these three families destroyed Jin, reduced the duke to commoner status, and ended the state's sacrifices.

source: Cao Shen, Marquis of Pingyang, was born in Peixian County. During the Qin Dynasty, Cao Shen served as the warden of Peixian County, and Xiao He was the chief official. They were already well-known officials in the county. When Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty was the Duke of Pei, Cao Shen followed him as Zhongjuan. Cao Shen led his army to attack Huling and Fangyu, and attacked the Qin Dynasty's county supervisors' army, greatly defeating the enemy. He took Xuexian County to the east and attacked the army of the Sishui County Governor to the west of the outer city of Xuexian County. Then he attacked Huling and successfully captured it. Cao Shen led his army to move to guard Fang Yu. Fang Yu had rebelled and surrendered to the king of Wei, so Cao Shen attacked Fang Yu. Fengyi also rebelled and surrendered to the king of Wei, and Cao Shen went to attack Fengyi again. Duke Pei bestowed upon Cao Shen the title of Seventh Doctor. Cao Shen attacked Qin Dynasty Sima Yí's army east of Dang County, defeated him, and captured Shanzhiyi in Dang County, Hufu County, and Qi County. Cao Shen then attacked the area west of Xiayi, as far as Yu County, and attacked Zhang Han's army. When attacking Yuan Qi and Kang Fu, Cao Shen was the first to climb the tower. Cao Shen was promoted to the fifth official position. He went north to rescue Dong'a, attacked Zhang Han's army, captured Chen County, and pursued to Puyang. He attacked Dingtao and captured Linji. He went south to rescue Yongqiu, attacked Li You's army, defeated it, killed Li You, and captured one of the Qin Dynasty's military commanders. At this time, Qin general Zhang Han defeated Xiang Liang's army and killed Xiang Liang. Pei Gong and Xiang Yu led their troops back east. King Chu Huai appointed Pei Gong as the governor of Dang County and commanded the army of Dang County. Peigong granted Cao Shen the title of Silk Holder and was known as Jiancheng Lord. Later, Cao Shen was promoted to the magistrate of Yuanqi County and was subordinate to Dang County. From there, Cao Shen followed Pei Gong to attack the army of the prefect of Dongjun and defeated the enemy south of Chengwu. They attacked Wang Li's army in the south of Chengyang and fought Wang Li's army in Gangli, defeating them severely. Chasing the fleeing enemy troops, he went west to Kaifeng, attacked Zhao Bi's army, defeated it, and surrounded Zhao Bi in the city of Kaifeng. Going west, he encountered the Qin Dynasty general Yang Xiong's army in Qu, defeated it, and captured one of the Qin Dynasty's Sima and Yushi. Cao Shen was promoted to Zhigui and followed Pei Gong to attack Yangwu, captured the Yuan and Feng clans, blocked the Yellow River ferry, returned to attack Zhao Ben's army, and defeated it to the north of Xixiang. Following Pei Gong, he went south to attack Jiyi, and fought with Lu Xun, the governor of Nanyang County, east of the outer city of Yangcheng. He broke through Lu Xun's army, captured Wan County, captured Lu Xun, and completely pacified Nanyang County. Following Pei Gong, he went west to attack Wuguan and Yaoguan, and captured these two passes. He first attacked the Qin army in the south of Lantian, and then attacked the north of Lantian at night, defeating the Qin army. Then he reached Xianyang and destroyed the Qin Dynasty. After Xiang Yu came to Guanzhong, he named Liu Bang King of Han. The king of Han granted Cao Shen the title of Marquis of Jiancheng.
target: Cao Shen, Marquis of Pingyang, was born in Peixian County and served as a warden there during the Qin Dynasty. He followed Emperor Gaozu of Han (then Duke of Pei) as a Zhongjuan, leading military campaigns against Qin forces, including attacks on Huling, Fangyu, Xuexian, and Dang County. He defeated generals such as Zhang Han, Li You, and Wang Li, capturing cities and officials. After Xiang Yu named Liu Bang King of Han, Cao Shen was granted the title Marquis of Jiancheng and later promoted to general. He helped pacify the Three Qin Dynasties, capturing territories like Xiabian and Yongxian, and besieged Zhang Han in Feiqiu.

source: By this time, Han Xin had defeated the State of Zhao, became prime minister, and attacked Qi State in the east. Cao Shen, serving as Prime Minister Zuo, subordinated to Han Xin, defeated Qi Lixia's army and captured Linyi. The returning army pacified Jibei County and attacked the counties, Luoyin, Pingyuan, Li County and Lu County. Soon after, Han Xin followed Han Xin to attack Long Qie's army, defeated the enemy, killed Long Qie, and captured his general Zhou Lan. The state of Qi was pacified and more than seventy counties were obtained in total. They captured the Prime Minister Tian Guang of the former Qi King Tian Guang, Xu Zhang who stayed behind in place of the Prime Minister, and the former Qi State Jiaodong General Tian Ji. Han Xin became the king of Qi, led his troops to Chen County, joined the king of Han, and defeated Xiang Yu together, while Cao Shen stayed to pacify the unconquered areas of Qi. Xiang Yu was dead, the world was at peace, the King of Han became emperor, Han Xin was renamed King of Chu, and the state of Qi was divided into counties. Cao Shen returned the seal of the Han Prime Minister. Emperor Gao made his eldest son Liu Fei the King of Qi and appointed Cao Shen as the Prime Minister of Qi. In the sixth year of Emperor Gaozu's reign, the titles of the princes were enfeoffed. The imperial court and the princes cut the talismans as proof, so that the titles of the enfeoffed persons could be passed down from generation to generation without being extinguished. Emperor Gaozu granted Cao Shen 10,630 households in Pingyang as a fiefdom, with the title Marquis of Pingyang, and took back the fiefdoms previously entrusted to Cao Shen. As the Prime Minister of Qi, Cao Shen led troops to attack Chen Xi's general Zhang Chun's army and defeated the enemy. Yingbu rebelled. As the Prime Minister of Qi, Cao Shen followed Qi Hui King Liu Fei and led 120,000 troops. Together with Gaozu, he attacked Yingbu's army and defeated the enemy. They marched southward to Qi County, then returned to the army and pacified Zhuyi, Xiangxian, Xiaoxian and Liuxian. Cao Shen's achievements: he conquered two vassal states and 122 counties in total; captured two vassal kings, three prime ministers of the vassal states, six generals, and one each of the county guard, Sima, military marquis, and censor. In the first year of Emperor Xiaohui's reign, he abolished the decree of establishing a prime minister's state in the vassal states and appointed Cao Shen as the prime minister of Qi. When Cao Shen was the prime minister of Qi, there were seventy cities in Qi. At that time, the world had just been peaceful, and King Huihui was very young. Cao Shen summoned the elderly and scholars to ask for ways to appease the people. But there were hundreds of scholars in Qi State, and they had different opinions. Cao Shen didn't know how to make a decision. He heard that there was a Duke Gai in Jiaoxi who studied Huang Lao's theory intensively, so he sent someone to invite him with generous gifts. After meeting Gai Gong, Gai Gong told Cao Shen that the most important way to govern the country is to be pure and inactive, allowing the people to settle down on their own. He recommended similar things in this regard and stated them all to Cao Shen. Cao Shen then gave up his main hall and let Gai Gong live in it. From then on, Cao Shen's method of governing the country was to adopt Huang Lao's teachings, so he served as the prime minister of Qi for nine years. The country of Qi was stable, and people greatly praised him as a wise prime minister. In the second year of Emperor Hui's reign, Xiao He passed away. When Cao Shen heard the news, he told his disciples to pack their bags quickly and said: I am going to the court to become the prime minister.
target: Cao Shen served as acting Prime Minister Zuo, suppressing rebellions by King Bao of Wei and others, capturing Wei and Zhao territories. He followed Han Xin to defeat Qi, pacifying over seventy counties. After Xiang Yu's death, Cao Shen became Prime Minister of Qi under King Liu Fei, governing with Huang Lao principles of purity and inaction for nine years, stabilizing the state. When Xiao He died, Cao Shen succeeded him as Han Prime Minister, adhering strictly to Xiao He's laws without changes. He selected steady officials, dismissed those seeking reputation, and spent his time drinking, avoiding interference in minor affairs.

id: 史记/三十世家/曹相国世家::group-002
article_path: 史记/三十世家/曹相国世家
source: Cao Shen said: Your Majesty, do you think my talents are better than those of Xiao He? Emperor Hui said: You are probably not as good as Xiao He. Cao Shen said: What your Majesty said is correct. Emperor Gao and Xiao He have brought peace to the world, and the laws have been made clear. Now His Majesty has lowered his clothes and handed over his hands. Isn't it enough for us to abide by our respective responsibilities, follow the original laws and not change them at will? Emperor Hui said: OK. Take a rest! Cao Shen served as the Prime Minister of the Han Dynasty for three years. After his death, he was posthumously named Yihou. Cao Shen's son, Cao Cheng, succeeded his father as the marquis. The common people praised Cao Shen's deeds and said: Xiao He formulated laws that were clear and consistent; Cao Shen succeeded Xiao He as prime minister and abided by Xiao He's laws without changing them. Cao Shen implemented his pure and inactive approach, and the people were peaceful and undisturbed. Cao Cheng, Marquis of Pingyang, was the imperial censor at that time. Emperor Xiaowen ascended the throne and was dismissed as a marquis. Cao Cheng died after 29 years as a marquis, and his posthumous title was Jinghou. Cao Cheng's son Cao Qi took over the throne and died after seven years of service. His posthumous title was Marquis Jian. Cao Qi's son Cao Shi succeeded him. Cao Shi married Princess Pingyang and gave birth to a son, Cao Xiang. Cao Shi got sick and returned to the feudal country. Cao Shi died in his 23rd year as a Marquis, and his posthumous title was Yihou. Cao Shi's son Cao Xiang succeeded him. Cao Xiang married Princess Wei Chang and had a son, Cao Zong. Cao Xiang died in his sixteenth year as a marquis, and his posthumous title was Gonghou. Cao Xiang's son Cao Zong succeeded him.
target: When Emperor Hui questioned his governance, Cao Shen argued that following the established laws of Emperor Gaozu and Xiao He was sufficient. Cao Shen served as Prime Minister for three years, dying with the posthumous title Yihou. His descendants inherited the title until Cao Zong was executed for involvement in a mutiny, ending the feudal state. The people praised Cao Shen for maintaining Xiao He's clear laws and allowing peace through non-interference.

source: In October of the 29th year, King Xiao of Liang came to Beijing to meet Emperor Jing. Emperor Jing sent an envoy to hold the talisman and drive the emperor's horse-drawn carriage to the pass to greet King Liang. After meeting Emperor Jing, he submitted a memorial requesting to stay in the capital, and was allowed to do so because the Queen Mother loved Prince Xiao very much. When King Xiao entered the palace, he accompanied Emperor Jing on a chariot. When he left the palace, he went hunting with the chariot and went to Shanglin Garden to shoot birds and beasts. Liang Guo's ministers, Langguan, and visitors only need to register their names in the name book so that they can enter and leave the emperor's palace, no different from the officials of the imperial court. In November, the emperor deposed Prince Li, and Empress Dowager Dou wanted to make Prince Xiao his successor. The ministers, Yuan An and others dissuaded Emperor Jing, and Empress Dowager Dou's motion was blocked. From then on, she no longer mentioned the matter of making Prince Liang his successor. Because this matter is very secret, no one in the world knows about it. The King of Liang then bid farewell to the court and returned to the feudal state. In April of this summer, the emperor made King Jiaodong the crown prince. The King of Liang resented Yuan An and the ministers who participated in the heir discussion, so he planned with Yang Sheng, Gongsun Gui and others to secretly assassinate Yuan An and more than ten other ministers who participated in the heir discussion. The court searched for the murderer, but failed to find it. So the emperor suspected King Liang and captured the murderer, who was indeed the mastermind. So Emperor Jing sent envoys constantly on the road to Liang State, where they repeatedly conducted inspections and arrested Gongsun Gui and Yang Sheng. Gongsun Gui and Yang Sheng were hiding in the harem of King Liang. The envoy was urgent to question the officials of Erqianshi. Liang Xiangxuan Qiu Bao and Nei Shi Han Anguo came to admonish the king of Liang. The king of Liang ordered Yang Sheng and Gongsun Gui to commit suicide, and then handed them over. The emperor resented King Liang for this. The King of Liang was frightened, so he sent Han Anguo to confess to the Queen Mother through the eldest princess and ask for forgiveness, and then he was forgiven. The emperor's anger gradually dissipated, and King Liang wrote a letter requesting an audience. After arriving at Hangu Pass, Mao Lan persuaded King Liang to take a cloth chariot and bring only two cavalry to the capital, hiding in the eldest princess's garden. The imperial court sent envoys to welcome King Liang, but King Liang had already entered the pass. All his entourage, chariots and horses were outside the pass, and he did not know where he was. The Queen Mother cried: Your Majesty killed my son!
target: In October of the 29th year, King Xiao visited Emperor Jing, who sent an imperial carriage to greet him. He requested to stay in the capital, which was granted due to the Queen Mother's love. He accompanied the emperor in chariots and hunted at Shanglin Garden. Liang's ministers could enter the palace freely. In November, after the prince was deposed, the Queen Mother wanted King Xiao as successor, but ministers like Yuan An dissuaded Emperor Jing, blocking the motion. The matter remained secret. King Xiao then returned to his state. In April, the emperor made King Jiaodong the crown prince. Resentful, King Xiao plotted with Yang Sheng and Gongsun Gui to assassinate Yuan An and over ten other ministers. The court failed to find the murderer initially but eventually suspected King Xiao. After capturing the assassins, the emperor sent envoys to Liang, arresting Gongsun Gui and Yang Sheng, who hid in the harem. Liang's officials urged the king to have them commit suicide, which he did. The emperor remained resentful, but after Han Anguo pleaded for forgiveness through the eldest princess, King Xiao was forgiven. He later entered the capital in disguise, hiding in the eldest princess's garden, causing the Queen Mother to weep, thinking the emperor had killed him. King Xiao then confessed, and brotherly relations were restored, though the emperor gradually alienated him.

id: 史记/三十世家/梁孝王世家::group-001
article_path: 史记/三十世家/梁孝王世家
source: Then the officials accompanying King Liang were summoned into the pass. However, Emperor Jing gradually alienated King Liang and no longer rode with him in chariots. In the winter of the thirty-fifth year, King Liang went to Beijing again to see the emperor. He submitted a memorial requesting to retain the capital, but the emperor did not agree. After King Liang returned to his feudal state, he felt confused and depressed. When he went hunting in the Liangshan Mountains in the north, someone offered him a cow. The cow's feet were long on his back. King Xiao was disgusted by it. In mid-June, King Liang fell ill with fever and died six days later. His posthumous title is King Xiao. King Xiao of Liang was very filial. Every time he heard that the Queen Mother was ill and couldn't eat or sleep well, he often wanted to stay in Chang'an to serve the Queen Mother. The Queen Mother also loved him. When she learned that King Liang had died, Empress Dowager Dou cried very sadly and refused to eat or drink, saying: Your Majesty really killed my son! Emperor Jing was sad and worried about it, and didn't know what to do. Emperor Jing discussed with the eldest princess and divided the Liang Kingdom into five kingdoms. All five sons of King Xiao were granted the title of king, and all five daughters were also granted the title of Tang Muyi to them. After reporting these measures to the Queen Mother, the Queen Mother became happy and added an extra meal because of Emperor Jing's treatment. The eldest son of King Liang Xiao, Liu Mai, inherited the throne and was named the King of Gong; the second son, Liu Ming, was named the King of Jichuan; the third son, Liu Pengli, was named the King of Jidong; the fourth son, Liu Ding, was named the King of Shanyang; and the youngest son, Liu Bushi, was named the King of Jiyin. Before the death of King Xiao of Liang, his property amounted to hundreds of millions and was incalculable. After his death, there were still more than 400,000 kilograms of gold left in his treasury, and other properties were also equivalent to this.
target: In the winter of the 35th year, King Xiao visited again but was denied permission to stay. After returning, he became depressed. While hunting, a cow with feet on its back disgusted him. He fell ill with fever in mid-June and died six days later, posthumously titled King Xiao. He was filial, often wanting to serve the Queen Mother when she was ill. Her grief was immense, but Emperor Jing divided Liang into five kingdoms, granting all five sons and five daughters titles, which pleased her. King Xiao's eldest son, Liu Mai, inherited as King Gong; others became kings of Jichuan, Jidong, Shanyang, and Jiyin. His wealth was immense, with over 400,000 kilograms of gold left after death.

id: 史记/三十世家/梁孝王世家::group-002
article_path: 史记/三十世家/梁孝王世家
source: After his death, there were still more than 400,000 kilograms of gold left in his treasury, and other properties were also equivalent to this. In the third year of Liang Gong's reign, Emperor Jing died. King Gong died after reigning for seven years and was succeeded by his son Liu Xiang, who became King Ping. In the fourteenth year of Liang Ping King Liu Xiang's reign, Liang Ping King's mother was the Queen Mother Chen. The mother of King Gong is Queen Mother Li. Queen Mother Li is the biological grandmother of Prince Ping. King Ping's queen's surname was Ren, and she was called Queen Ren. Queen Ren was very favored by King Ping Liu Xiang. At first, when King Xiao was still alive, he had a bottle worth thousands of gold. King Xiao warned his descendants to take good care of the bottle and not give it to others. After Queen Ren heard about it, she wanted to get the bottle. The Queen Mother Li, the grandmother of King Ping, said: The late king had a will not to give away the bottles to others.
target: King Gong died after seven years, succeeded by his son Liu Xiang as King Ping. A dispute over a valuable bottle led to conflict between King Ping, his grandmother Queen Mother Li, and Queen Ren. Queen Ren took the bottle despite Queen Mother Li's objections. Queen Mother Li later died, with Queen Ren neglecting her in illness and death.

id: 史记/三十世家/梁孝王世家::group-003
article_path: 史记/三十世家/梁孝王世家
source: Even if other things are worth hundreds of millions, you can take them for yourself. Queen Ren insisted on getting this bottle. King Ping Liu Xiang directly asked people to open the treasury to get the bottles and gave them to Queen Ren. Empress Dowager Li was furious. The imperial envoy came to the Liang Kingdom. Empress Dowager Li wanted to tell the envoy personally about the matter. King Ping Liu Xiang and Queen Ren stopped her and closed the door. Empress Dowager Li struggled to open the door, and her fingers were caught in the crack of the door. Finally, she could not see the envoy from the imperial court. Empress Dowager Li secretly committed adultery with the Chief Food Officer and the doctor Yin Ba, so King Ping and Queen Ren sent people to dissuade Empress Dowager Li with this hint. Empress Dowager Li gave up because of her lewd behavior. Later, Queen Mother Li died of illness. When she was ill, Queen Ren did not ask for her health; after her death, she did not pay homage to her. During the Yuanshuo period, there was a Suiyang man named Lei Anfan. Someone insulted his father. This man went out in the same car with the retainer of the Huaiyang prefect. The prefect's retainer got out of the car and left. Lei Anfan killed his enemy in the car and ran away.
target: A man named Lei Anfan, seeking revenge, revealed palace secrets to the court. Investigations confirmed Queen Mother Li's adultery and King Ping's mismanagement.

id: 史记/三十世家/梁孝王世家::group-004
article_path: 史记/三十世家/梁孝王世家
source: Officials with less than 2,000 dan were very urgent to arrest the rebels, so they arrested the relatives of the rebels. Lei Lian knew the secrets in Liang's palace, so he reported to the court in detail the events surrounding the dispute between King Ping and his grandmother over the Lei Zun. At that time, officials below the prime minister knew about this incident and wanted to use it to attack the senior officials of Liang State, so they submitted a petition to the emperor. The emperor handed the matter over to the officials for investigation and interrogation, and it was indeed true. The minister asked the emperor to depose King Ping Liu Xiang and make him a commoner. The Emperor said: Empress Dowager Li committed adultery, and Liang Wang Liu Xiang did not have a good master, so she fell into such an unjust situation. So the fiefdoms of eight cities in Liang were reduced, and Queen Ren was beheaded in the city. There are still ten cities left in the Liang Kingdom. Liu Xiang died in the 39th year of his reign and was posthumously named King Ping. His son Liu Wushang was established as King of Liang. King Liu Ming of Jichuan was the second son of King Xiao of Liang. In the sixth year of Emperor Xiaojing's reign, he was granted the title of King of Jichuan by the Marquis of Huanyi. Seven years later, due to the crime of shooting the lieutenant, the relevant officials in the court petitioned to kill King Jichuan. The emperor could not bear to kill him, so he deposed Liu Ming as a civilian and demoted him to Fangling. The fiefdom belonged to the court and became a county. King Liu Pengli of Jidong was the son of King Xiao of Liang. He was named King of Jidong in the sixth year of Emperor Xiaojing's reign. Twenty-nine years later, Liu Pengli was arrogant and fierce, without the demeanor of a human king. He secretly went out at night with dozens of his slaves and desperate youths to rob, kill, and plunder other people's property for fun. More than a hundred people were found to have been killed by him. The whole country knew about it and no one dared to go out at night. The son of the man he killed wrote a letter to report. Relevant officials in the imperial court petitioned to have him executed. The emperor couldn't bear it and deposed him as a commoner and demoted him to Shangyong. The fiefdom belonged to the imperial court and became Dahe County. Liu Ding, the Ai King of Shanyang, was the son of Liang Xiaozi. He was named King of Shanyang in the sixth year of Emperor Xiaojing's reign. After reigning for nine years, he died without a son. The feudal state was abolished and the land belonged to the imperial court and became Shanyang County. Liu Bushi, the Ai King of Jiyin, was the son of King Xiao of Liang. He was named King of Jiyin in the sixth year of Emperor Xiaojing's reign. He died after one year in office without any sons. The feudal state was abolished and the land belonged to the imperial court and became Jiyin County.
target: The emperor reduced Liang's fiefdom by eight cities and executed Queen Ren. Liu Xiang died after 39 years, succeeded by his son Liu Wushang. Other sons of King Xiao faced fates: Liu Ming was deposed for shooting a lieutenant; Liu Pengli was deposed for robbery and murder; Liu Ding died without an heir; Liu Bushi died after one year without an heir. Their fiefdoms became counties. Tai Shigong noted that King Xiao's wealth and splendor, though due to his position and the prosperous times, constituted transgression.

id: 史记/三十世家/梁孝王世家::group-005
article_path: 史记/三十世家/梁孝王世家
source: Tai Shigong said: Although King Xiao of Liang was granted the title of king in a fertile land because he was the brother of the emperor and the beloved son of the queen mother, he also coincided with the prosperity of the country and the prosperity of the people, so he was able to accumulate wealth, expand the palace, and his carriages, horses and clothing were similar to those of the emperor. However, doing so would also constitute an act of transgression. Mr. Chu Shaosun said: When I was a Langguan, I heard about the deeds of King Liang Xiao from the old Langguan who liked to gossip in the palace. I privately believe that the trouble that made King Xiao of Liang resentful and dissatisfied, and wanted to be emperor was caused by the imperial court. The Queen Mother at that time was the heroine of the country. Because she loved her youngest son, she wanted Prince Liang to be the crown prince. The ministers of the DPRK do not promptly tell the reason why they cannot do this, but instead just flatter the Queen Mother, talk about trivial things, and privately please the Queen Mother in order to get rewards. This is not a loyal minister! If ministers could speak openly and honestly like Wei Qihou and Dou Ying, how could there be any subsequent disasters?
target: Chu Shaosun added that the trouble stemmed from the court's failure to properly address succession issues, with ministers like Yuan Ang and Dou Ying providing wise counsel.

source: After hearing this, King Liang quickly declined. Although he knew that what Emperor Jing said was not true, he was secretly happy. The Queen Mother was equally happy. That spring, the seven kingdoms of Wu, Chu, Qi, and Zhao rebelled. Wu and Chu first attacked Liang's Jibi and killed tens of thousands of people. King Xiao of Liang guarded Suiyang City and appointed Han Anguo, Zhang Yu and others as generals to resist the troops of Wu and Chu. Wu and Chu were blocked by Liang and did not dare to cross the Liang Kingdom to march westward. They had a stalemate with Taiwei Yafu and others for three months. Wu and Chu were destroyed, and the number of Wu and Chu troops killed and captured by Liang was roughly as many as the imperial court. The following year, the imperial court established a prince.
