source: Because of this, "Spring and Autumn" accused Song Xuangong of this. After Song Xuangong died, he passed the throne to his younger brother instead of having a son. After his brother succeeded to the throne and died, the throne was given to his elder brother's son. His younger brother's son fought for the throne and thought he should succeed his father, so he killed Xuangong's son. So the country was in chaos. Disasters continue. Therefore, "Spring and Autumn" says: A gentleman respects and follows the right path, and the chaos in the Song Dynasty was caused by Duke Xuan. The ministers and others asked to see the Queen Mother to explain this truth. Yuan An and others went to the palace to see the Queen Mother and said: The Queen Mother said that she would establish King Liang. So, who will be established after King Liang dies?
target: The Queen Mother's desire to make King Xiao heir was ultimately thwarted by ministers citing historical precedents, such as the chaos in Song caused by Duke Xuan. After the assassination of Yuan An, the case was handled by officials who burned evidence, preserving King Xiao's reputation and calming the Queen Mother.

source: The ancestors of the Chu State came from Gaoyang, Emperor Zhuanxu. Gao Yang is the grandson of Huangdi and the son of Changyi. Gao Yang gave birth to Cheng, Cheng gave birth to Juan Zhang, and Juan Zhang gave birth to Chong Li. Chongli became the Huozheng of Emperor Ku's Gaoxin family. He was very meritorious and could illuminate the world. Emperor Ku gave him the title of Zhu Rong. The Gonggong clan launched a civil strife, and Emperor Ku asked Chong Li to kill the rebels, but he did not kill them all. Emperor Ku killed Chongli on the day of Gengyin, and asked his younger brother Wu Hui to succeed Chongli and also take up the post of Huozheng, still called Zhurong. Wu Hui gave birth to Lu Zhong. Lu Zhong had six sons, all born by caesarean section. The eldest son is called Kunwu, the second son is called Shenhu, the third son is called Pengzu, the fourth son is called Huiren, the fifth son is named Cao, the sixth son is named Jilian, and Jilian's surname is Mi. He is the ancestor of the Chu king's family. Kunwu once served as Hou Bo during the Xia and Shang Dynasties, but was destroyed by Tang during the Jie Dynasty. Peng Zu once served as Hou Bo during the Yin Dynasty. At the end of the Yin Dynasty, Peng Zu was destroyed. Ji Lian gave birth to Fuju, and Fuju gave birth to Cave Bear. His descendants declined midway. Some were in the Central Plains, and some were in barbarians, and history books failed to record their lineages. During the reign of King Wen of Zhou Dynasty, there was a descendant of Ji Lian called Wan Xiong. Wu Xiong served King Wen like a son and died young.
target: The ancestors of the Chu State originated from Gaoyang, Emperor Zhuanxu, who was the grandson of Huangdi. The lineage passed through several generations to Chongli, who served as Huozheng under Emperor Ku and was granted the title Zhurong. After Chongli failed to completely suppress the Gonggong rebellion, Emperor Ku executed him and appointed his younger brother Wu Hui as his successor. Wu Hui fathered Luzhong, who had six sons by caesarean section. The youngest son, Jilian, whose surname was Mi, became the ancestor of the Chu royal family. Jilian's descendants included Yuxiong, who served King Wen of Zhou like a son but died young.

source: His descendants declined midway. Some were in the Central Plains, and some were in barbarians, and history books failed to record their lineages. During the reign of King Wen of Zhou Dynasty, there was a descendant of Ji Lian called Wan Xiong. Wu Xiong served King Wen like a son and died young. His son's name is Xiong Li. Xiong Li gave birth to Xiong Kuang, and Xiong Kuang gave birth to Xiong Yi. Xiong Yi was in the era of King Cheng of Zhou Dynasty. King Cheng wanted to use the descendants of the heroes of King Wen and King Wu, so he granted Xiong Yi the title of baron in Chu Man. His surname was Mi and he lived in Danyang. Xiong Yi, the son of Chu, served the king together with Bo Qin, the Duke of Lu, Zi Mou, the uncle of Wei Kang, Xie, the Marquis of Jin, and Lu Ji, the prince of Qi. Xiong Yi gave birth to Xiong Ai, Xiong Ai gave birth to Xiong Ai, and Xiong Ai gave birth to Xiong Sheng. Xiong Sheng made his younger brother Xiong Yang his successor. Xiong Yang gave birth to Xiong Qu. Xiong Qu has three sons. During the reign of King Zhou Yi, the Zhou royal family declined. Some princes refused to pay homage to the emperor, and the princes attacked each other. Xiong Qu won the support of the people along the Yangtze River and Han River, so he sent troops to attack Yong and Yang Yue, all the way to Hubei. Xiong Qu said: I am located in a barbarian land, so I don’t have to have the same names and posthumous titles as those of other countries in the Central Plains. So he named his eldest son Xiong Kang King of Judan, his second son Xiong Hong as King of E, and his youngest son Xiong Zhizhen as King of Yue Zhang, all in the Chuman area along the Yangtze River. When King Li of Zhou came to power, Xiong Qu was worried that King Li would attack Chu due to his violent temper, so he removed his title as king. Xiong Qu's successor was his eldest son Xiong Wukang, who died early.
target: During King Cheng of Zhou's reign, Yuxiong's descendant Xiong Yi was granted the title of baron in the Chu Man region with Danyang as his residence. Xiong Yi served the Zhou king alongside other noble descendants. The lineage continued through several generations until Xiong Qu, who gained support from people along the Yangtze and Han Rivers. He conquered territories including Yong and Yangyue, and declared his three sons kings of various regions in the Chu Man area. When King Li of Zhou ascended, Xiong Qu removed his kingly title out of fear.

source: Xiao Ao died in the sixth year of his reign, and his son Xiong Zhen came to the throne. This is Fimao. In the thirteenth year of Fu Mao's reign, the state of Jin began to be in turmoil because of Quwo. Fu Mao died in the seventeenth year of his reign. Fu Mao's younger brother Xiong Tong killed Fu Mao's son and ascended the throne. This was King Wu of Chu. In the seventeenth year of King Wu's reign, Prince Quwo of Jin State killed Jin Xiaohou, the king of the suzerain state. In the nineteenth year, Zheng Bo's younger brother Duan provoked civil strife. In the twenty-first year, Zheng Guo invaded the emperor's fields. In the twenty-third year, the people of Wei killed their king Huan Gong. In the twenty-ninth year, the people of Lu killed their king Yin Gong. In the thirty-first year of the Song Dynasty, Hua Du, the governor of the Song Dynasty, killed his own monarch Shang Gong. In the thirty-fifth year, the Chu State attacked Sui State. Sui Guojun said: I have no sin. The King of Chu said: I am in a barbarian area. Today, all the princes have betrayed the royal family, invaded and killed each other. I have an army and want to use it to participate in the political affairs of the Central Plains. I request the Zhou royal family to respect my name. The people of Sui went to the Zhou royal family to ask for a title on his behalf, but the Zhou royal family refused, so the people of Sui came back and reported to Chu. In the thirty-seventh year, Chu Xiongtong said angrily: My ancestor Wu Xiong was the teacher of King Wen, but it was a pity that he died early. King Zhou Cheng promoted my late grandfather, but only gave him the land with the title of baron and let him live in the Chu region. Now the barbarian tribes are submissive, but King Zhou still does not grant him a title, so I have no choice but to claim my title! So he called himself King Wu and made an alliance with the people of Sui before withdrawing his troops. From then on, he began to cultivate Pu land and occupy it. In the fifty-first year, the king of Zhou summoned Sui Hou and scolded him for supporting the king of Chu to become king. King Wu of Chu was very angry and thought that Sui Hou had betrayed him, so he attacked Sui. King Wu died of illness on the march, and Chu State stopped its march. King Wu's son King Wen Xiong Yu came to the throne, and the Chu State began to move its capital to Ying.
target: After several successions and internal conflicts, Xiong Tong killed his nephew and ascended the throne as King Wu of Chu. He declared himself king after the Zhou royal family refused to grant him a higher title, stating that his ancestor had served King Wen and that the Zhou had only given his family a baron's title in the Chu region. King Wu attacked Sui and died of illness during the campaign. His son King Wen Xiong Yu moved the capital to Ying. Under King Wen, Chu attacked Shen, Cai, and Deng, becoming powerful and intimidating smaller states in the region.

source: In the eleventh year, Duke Huan of Qi began to dominate, and the state of Chu also began to become powerful. In the twelfth year, the Chu State attacked the Deng State and destroyed the Deng State. In the thirteenth year, King Wen passed away and his son Xiong Jin came to the throne. This is Zhuang Ao. In the fifth year of Zhuang Ao's reign, he wanted to kill his younger brother Xiong Yun. Xiong Yun fled to Sui, attacked and killed Zhuang Ao with his followers, and became king. In the first year of the reign of King Cheng Yun, as soon as he came to the throne, he extended kindness and morality to the people and restored the old friendly relations among the princes.
target: King Cheng Xiong Yun extended kindness to the people and restored relations with other states.

source: So the Chu State expanded to a thousand miles in radius. In the 16th year, Duke Huan of Qi sent troops to invade the state of Chu, all the way to Xingshan. King Cheng of Chu asked General Qu Wan to lead his army to resist, and made an alliance with Duke Huan of Qi. Duke Huan scolded King Chu Cheng for not paying tribute to the Zhou royal family. King Chu Cheng agreed and he withdrew his troops from Chu. In the eighteenth year, King Cheng led his army to attack the state of Xu in the north. The king of Xu State took off his shirt and exposed his arms to plead guilty, and King Cheng of Chu released him. In the twenty-second year, Chu State attacked Huang State. In the twenty-sixth year, Chu State destroyed Britain. In the thirty-third year, Duke Xianggong of the Song Dynasty wanted to form an alliance with the princes and summoned King Cheng of Chu to attend. The King of Chu said angrily: "How dare you summon me? I will go with a friendly attitude, and then take the opportunity to attack and insult him." So the King of Chu sent troops to Yu, arrested and humiliated Song Xianggong, and soon let him return to his country. In the thirty-fourth year, Zheng Wengong went south to pay homage to the King of Chu. King Chu Cheng went north to attack the Song Dynasty, defeated the Song army at Hongshui, and shot and wounded Song Xianggong. Xianggong died of the arrow wound soon after. In the thirty-fifth year of the Jin Dynasty, Chong'er, the prince of Jin Dynasty, passed through the state of Chu. King Cheng entertained Chong'er according to the etiquette of entertaining guests from princes, gave Chong'er many gifts, and escorted him to the state of Qin. In the 39th year, Duke Xi of Lu asked Chu State to send troops to attack Qi State. Chu State sent Marquis Shen to lead an army to attack Qi State, captured the valley, and settled Qi Huangong's son Yong in the valley. The seven sons of Duke Huan of Qi all fled to the State of Chu, and all of them in the State of Chu worshiped them as senior officials. The Chu State destroyed Kui because Kui did not sacrifice to Zhu Rong and Wan Xiong. In the summer, Chu State attacked Song State. Song State asked Jin State for help. Jin State sent troops to rescue Song State. King Chu Cheng had to give up and return to Chu State. General Ziyu asked to continue fighting, and King Cheng said: Chong'er has been on the run for many years and finally returned to Jin. God is blessing him and cannot stop him. Ziyu resolutely asked for a battle, so King Chu Cheng left with only a small army. As expected, Jin defeated Ziyu in Chengpu. King Chu Cheng was very angry and killed Ziyu. In the forty-sixth year, at first, King Cheng planned to establish Shang Chen as the crown prince and told Ling Yin Zishang. The Master said: Your Majesty is still young, and you have many lovely wives and concubines. If you establish the crown prince now, he may be deposed in the future, and the country will be in trouble. The crown prince of Chu State is often born to his young son. Moreover, the merchant's eyes were like poisonous bees and his voice was like that of a jackal. He was an extremely cruel person and it was not suitable for him to be crown prince. The King of Chu refused to listen and finally appointed Shang Chen. Later, the King of Chu wanted to establish the position of son, and abandoned the prince and merchant. Shang Chen heard some rumors but had not confirmed it, so he told his teacher Pan Chong: How can we get the real situation?
target: He expanded Chu's territory to a thousand miles in radius. When Duke Huan of Qi invaded Chu, King Cheng made an alliance with him. King Cheng later captured and humiliated Duke Xiang of Song, attacked Song, and entertained the Jin prince Chong'er. After Chong'er returned to Jin, Chu's general Ziyu was defeated at Chengpu, and King Cheng executed him. King Cheng initially established Shang Chen as crown prince despite warnings about his cruel nature. When King Cheng planned to replace him, Shang Chen surrounded the palace, and King Cheng hanged himself.

source: Later, the King of Chu wanted to establish the position of son, and abandoned the prince and merchant. Shang Chen heard some rumors but had not confirmed it, so he told his teacher Pan Chong: How can we get the real situation? Pan Chong said: Treat Jiang Miji, whom King Cheng loves, but do not respect her. The merchants followed his plan. Jiang Mi said angrily: The king wants to kill you and make you the crown prince. The merchant told Pan Chong: The king really wants to depose me and replace me with another official. Pan Chong asked: Can you serve? The merchant replied: No! Can you escape from here? The merchant replied: No. Can you do what it takes to kill a king? The merchant replied: Yes. In October of winter, the merchants asked the palace guards to surround King Cheng. King Cheng asked to eat bear paws before dying, but the merchants refused. On the day of Ding Wei, King Cheng hanged himself. Shang Chen came to the throne, and this was King Mu. After King Mu ascended the throne, he gave Pan Chong his royal palace and made him the grand master to preside over state affairs. In the third year of King Mu, Chu State was destroyed by Jiang State. In four years, the Chu State destroyed the Six Kingdoms and the Liao Kingdom. 6. The king of Liao is a descendant of Gaotao. In the eighth year, Chu State attacked Chen State. In the twelfth year, King Mu passed away. His son Zhuang Wanglu came to the throne. King Zhuang has been on the throne for three years. He has never issued any political orders to the country. He has had fun day and night. He also issued an edict to the country: Anyone who dares to remonstrate will be killed! Wu Ju entered the palace to admonish him. King Zhuang holds Zheng Ji in his left hand and Yue Nu in his right hand, sitting among the singers and dancers. Wu Ju said: I hope to give you a hidden word. Then he said: There was a bird that landed on the mountain. It did not fly or sing for three years. What kind of bird was it? King Zhuang said: If you don't fly for three years, you will soar into the sky; if you don't sing for three years, you will become a blockbuster. Go down, I know what you mean. After a few months, King Zhuang became even more lewd and indulgent. Su Cong, the doctor, went to the palace to give advice. King Zhuang of Chu said: Didn't you hear my edict? Su Cong replied: It is my long-cherished wish to sacrifice myself to make you wise. The king of Chu then stopped his lewdness and pleasure and began to handle government affairs. He killed hundreds of criminals, promoted hundreds of meritorious ministers, and appointed Wu Ju and Su Cong to manage government affairs, which was supported by the whole country. At that time, the state of Chu was destroyed. In six years, Chu State attacked Song State and obtained 500 chariots. In the eighth year, the Chu State attacked Lu Hunrong and arrived at Luo, where they held a military parade on the outskirts of the Zhou capital. King Zhou Ding sent Wang Sunman to reward King Chu. The King of Chu asked Wang Sunman about the size of the tripod. Wang Sunman replied: Ruling a country depends on whether the government is virtuous, not on the size of the tripod.
target: King Mu Shang Chen ascended and destroyed several states. His son King Zhuang Lu initially indulged in pleasure but reformed after remonstrance from Wu Ju and Su Cong. King Zhuang attacked Lu Hunrong, paraded troops near the Zhou capital, and asked about the Nine Tripods. Wang Sunman replied that ruling depends on virtue, not tripods, and that the Zhou dynasty's mandate was difficult to change. King Zhuang withdrew. He later attacked Chen, captured it, but restored it after Shen Shu's advice. He besieged Zheng, accepted its surrender, and defeated Jin at the Yellow River. He besieged Song for five months until its people resorted to cannibalism, then withdrew.

source: So King Ling wanted to enter Yan City by boat. You Yin estimated that King Ling would never listen to his advice, and feared that he would be killed together with King Ling, so he left King Ling and ran away. The Spirit King then wandered alone in the mountains, and no villagers dared to take him in. On the way, King Ling met Juan Ren who had been in the palace and said to him: "Please find something to eat for me. I have been hungry for three days." Juan said: The new king has just issued an edict to kill any of the three tribes who dare to give you food and flee with you, not to mention there is no food to be found here. The Ling King then fell asleep with his head on his lap. Juanren replaced it with a clod of earth, pulled out his legs and ran away. After King Ling woke up, he could not find Juan Ren. He was so hungry that he could not sit up. Shen Hai, the son of Shen Wuyu, the local magistrate of Tudi, said: My father violated the king's law twice, but King Ling pardoned him both times. There is no greater kindness than this! So he searched everywhere for the Spirit King, and finally found the hungry and fainting Spirit King in Lize, and served the Spirit King all the way to his own home. On the day of Guichou in the fifth month of summer, King Ling passed away at Shen Hai's house. Shen Hai had two women buried in sacrifice and buried King Ling. At this time, although the Chu State had already elected Prince Bi as King of Chu, it was afraid that King Ling would return again and had not heard the news of King Ling's death. Therefore, Guan Cong said to the new prince Bi: If you don't kill Qiji, even if you own the entire country, you will still suffer disaster. The king of Chu said: I can't bear to kill him. Guan Cong said: Others can't bear to kill you. The new king did not obey, so Guan Cong left. After Qi Ji returned to the capital, the people in the capital were frightened every night, saying: King Ling has entered the city. On the night of Yimao day, Qiji asked the boatmen to run along the bank of the Yangtze River and shout: "The King of Spirits is coming!" People in the capital were even more frightened. Qiji then asked Man Chengran to tell the new prince Bi and his ling Yin Zixi: King Ling is here! The people in the capital will kill you, Sima is coming! You should think of a solution as soon as possible and don't insult yourself. The anger of the people is like floods and fires, which cannot be saved. The new king and Zixi committed suicide. On Bingchen day, Qiji ascended the throne and became the king of Chu, and changed his name to Xiong Ju. He was the king of Ping. King Ping used deception to kill two kings and ascended the throne. He was afraid that the people in the capital and the princes would betray him, so he extended favors to the people.
target: King Gong Shen was defeated by Jin at Yanling and shot in the eye. After several successions, King Ling Xiong Wei gathered the princes, built Zhanghua Terrace, and asked about obtaining the Zhou tripod. He became arrogant but faced rebellion when his brother Qiji conspired with Guan Cong. King Ling's soldiers abandoned him, and he died of starvation at Shen Hai's house. Qiji ascended as King Ping, who deceived and killed two kings to gain the throne. He extended favors to the people, returned territories, and improved governance.

source: He enjoys the throne, doesn’t he deserve it? In the past, our Duke Wen was the son of Hu Jiji and was favored by Duke Xian. He is eager to learn. At the age of only seventeen, he made friends with five talented people, including the former great masters Ziquan and Zifu as his confidants, Wei Ji and Jia Tuo as his right-hand men, Qi, Song, Qin and Chu as foreign aids, and Luan, Que, Hu and Xian as internal responders. Duke Wen had been on the run for nineteen years, and his ambition to return was very firm. Because Hui Gong and Huai Gong lost the support of the people, the people all followed each other and turned to Wen Gong. In this way, shouldn't it be appropriate for Wen Gong to enjoy the country? Zibi had nothing to give to the people, and he received no foreign aid. When he left Jin, the Jin people did not escort him; when he returned to Chu, the Chu people did not welcome him. Why do you enjoy the country? As expected, Zibi's reign as king did not last long, and it was Qiji who finally ascended the throne, just as Shu Xiang predicted. In the second year of King Ping's reign, Fei Wuji was sent to the State of Qin to marry Prince Jian. This woman was extremely beautiful. Before she could reach the capital of Chu, Wuji hurried back and encouraged King Ping: "The woman of Qin is as beautiful as the king. You can stay here and find another one for the prince." King Ping listened to Wuji's persuasion and finally married Qin's daughter and gave birth to Xiong Zhen. He married another woman for the prince. At that time, Wu She was the prince's tutor and Wuji was the young tutor. Wuji was not favored by the prince and often slandered and slandered the prince Jian. Prince Jian was fifteen years old at the time. His mother was a woman from Cai State, and was not favored by King Ping. King Ping gradually became more distant from Prince Jian. In the sixth year, King Ping asked the prince to live with his father in the city and guard the border. Wuji again slandered Prince Jian in front of King Ping day and night, saying: Ever since I sent the Qin women to your harem, the Prince has resented me very much, and it is impossible not to have resentment towards you. You should also be careful. Moreover, the prince lives in the city father, monopolizes military power, makes friends with foreign princes, and always wants to invade the capital. King Ping called Tai Fu Wu She to scold him. Wu She knew that this was the result of Wuji's rumors, so he said: Your Majesty, why have you alienated your own flesh and blood because of a villain? Wuji said to King Ping: If you don't punish Wu She today, you will regret it in the future. So King Ping imprisoned Wu She. Let Sima Fenyang summon Prince Jian back and want to kill the Prince. The prince heard the news and fled to Song Dynasty. Fei Wuji said: Wu She has two sons. If they are not killed, they will become a disaster to the Chu State.
target: King Ping listened to Fei Wuji's slander against Prince Jian, imprisoned Wu She, and forced Prince Jian to flee. Wu She's son Wu Zixu escaped to Wu. King Ping married the woman intended for Prince Jian and fathered Xiong Zhen, who became King Zhao. Fei Wuji's slander caused Prince Jian's exile and Wu She's execution. King Zhao fled when Wu invaded, and Wu Zixu desecrated King Ping's tomb. King Zhao eventually returned with Qin's help.

source: Twenty years later, Bai Qi, the general of Qin State, captured Xiling of Chu State. In the 21st year, Bai Qi, the general of Qin State, captured Ying of Chu State and burned Yiling, the tomb of the late king. King Chu Xiang's army was defeated and could no longer fight, so he retreated to the northeast and defended Chencheng. In the 22nd year, Qin State captured Wu County and Qianzhong County of Chu State. In the twenty-third year, King Xiang gathered the soldiers from the east, a total of more than 100,000 people, and went west to capture the fifteen cities on the Yangtze River that Qin had captured, and divided them into counties to resist Qin. In the twenty-seventh year, Chu sent 30,000 men to help the Three Jins attack Yan. Chu made peace with Qin again and asked the prince to serve as a hostage in Qin. The state of Chu asked Zuo Tu to serve the prince in the state of Qin. In the thirty-sixth year, King Qingxiang fell ill, and the prince fled back to Chu. In autumn, King Qingxiang died, and prince Xiong Yuan came to the throne. This was King Kaolie. King Kaolie appointed Zuo Tu as his Ling Yin and granted him the title of Lord Chunshen of Wu. In the first year of King Kaolie's reign, he gave the state to Qin in order to make peace with Qin. At this time, the state of Chu was getting weaker and weaker. In the sixth year, the State of Qin surrounded Handan. The State of Zhao asked the State of Chu for help. The State of Chu sent the late general Jingyang to rescue the State of Zhao. In seven years, Chu State invaded Xinzhong. The Qin army left. In the twelfth year, King Zhao of Qin passed away, and the King of Chu asked Chun Shenjun to come to Qin to express his condolences. In the 16th year, King Zhuangxiang of Qin passed away, and King Zhao Zheng of Qin came to the throne. In the twenty-second year, the Chu State and the vassal states jointly attacked the Qin State, failed in the battle and withdrew their troops. The Chu State moved its capital eastward to Shouchun, which was called Ying. In the twenty-fifth year, King Kaolie passed away, and his son You Wanghan came to the throne. Li Yuan killed Chun Shenjun. In the third year of King You, Qin and Wei attacked Chu. Lu Buwei, the prime minister of Qin, passed away. In the ninth year, Qin destroyed South Korea. In the tenth year, King You passed away, and his younger half-brother, You, came to the throne. This was King Ai. More than two months after King Ai came to the throne, the gangsters of King Ai's brother, Fu Chu, attacked and killed King Ai, and made Fu Chu king of Chu. At that time, Qin captured Zhao Wangqian. In the first year of Wang Fuchu's reign, Prince Dan of Yan sent Jing Ke to assassinate the King of Qin. In the second year, Qin sent generals to attack Chu, defeated the Chu army and captured more than ten cities. In three years, Qin State destroyed Wei State. In the fourth year, the Qin general Wang Jian defeated the Chu army in Qi and killed the general Xiang Yan. In the fifth year, the Qin generals Wang Jian and Meng Wu invaded the capital of Chu, captured the Chu king Fu Chu, destroyed the Chu state, and established three counties in Chu. Tai Shigong said: When King Ling of Chu gathered the princes in Shen, killed Qi Qingfeng, built Zhanghua Terrace, and asked for the nine tripods of the Zhou royal family, he had lofty ambitions and looked down on the world. When he died of starvation at Shenhai's house, he was ridiculed by the people of the world.
target: King Hui was kidnapped by Bai Gongsheng but rescued by Ye Gong. After several more successions, King Huai was deceived by Zhang Yi into breaking relations with Qi, then attacked Qin and was defeated. He was later tricked into meeting King Zhao of Qin, who detained him. King Huai died in Qin, causing Chu to break relations with Qin. King Qingxiang moved the capital eastward as Qin captured Chu territories. The Chu state continued to weaken, eventually moving its capital to Shouchun. Qin generals Wang Jian and Meng Wu captured the Chu king, destroyed the state, and established three commanderies in Chu territory.

id: 史记/三十世家/燕召公世家::group-000
article_path: 史记/三十世家/燕召公世家
source: Zhao Gongxi has the same surname as the Zhou royal family, Ji. After King Wu of Zhou destroyed King Zhou of Shang, he granted Duke Zhao a title in Northern Yan. When King Cheng of Zhou was on the throne, Duke Zhao was in charge of the three Dukes: from the west of Shaanxi, Duke Zhao was in charge; from the east of Shaanxi, Duke Zhou was in charge. At that time, King Cheng was still young, and Duke Zhou presided over the affairs of state on his behalf and held the power of the country, just like the emperor. Duke Zhao was suspicious of Duke Zhou's actions, so Duke Zhou wrote an article "Jun Shi" to express his confession. Duke Zhao was still very dissatisfied with Duke Zhou. Duke Zhou then praised the relevant historical facts of the Yin and Shang Dynasties and said: During the reign of Shang Tang, there was Yi Yin, whose merits reached heaven; during Taiwu's reign, there were people like Yi Zhi and Chen Hu, whose merits reached heaven, and Wu Xian managed the government; during Zu Yi's reign, there were people like Wu Xian; during Wu Ding's era, there were people like Gan Ban: these ministers all had the merit of assisting the king and presiding over governance, and the Yin Dynasty was governed and stabilized. After hearing these words, Duke Zhao became happy. Duke Zhao governed the western region and was deeply loved by the people. When Zhao Gong went to inspect villages and towns, he saw a Tangli tree, and he judged lawsuits and handled political affairs under the tree. From marquises, counts to civilians, everyone has been properly accommodated, and there has been no neglect of duty. After the death of Duke Zhao, the people missed his political achievements and the time when Duke Zhao handled political affairs under the Tangli tree. They were reluctant to cut down the trees and praised Duke Zhao, writing a poem called "Gantang". After Zhao Gong, it was passed down to Huihou through nine generations. The reign of Yan Huihou coincided with the time when King Zhou Li fled to Pig, and when Zhou Dinggong and Zhaomu Gong were in power together. Huihou died and his son Lihou came to the throne. This year, King Zhou Xuan had just ascended the throne. In the 21st year of Lihou, Duke Huan of Zheng was granted the title of Zheng. In the thirty-sixth year, Lihou died and his son Qinghou came to the throne. In the 20th year of Qinghou's reign, King You of Zhou committed adultery and was killed by Quan Rong. Qin State began to be classified as vassals at this time. Qinghou died in the twenty-fourth year of his reign, and his son Aihou came to the throne. Marquis Ai died after reigning for two years, and his son Marquis Zheng came to the throne. Zheng Hou died in the thirty-sixth year of his reign, and his son Miao Hou came to the throne. The seventh year of Yan Muhou's reign was the first year of Lu Yin's reign. Marquis Mu of Yan died in the eighteenth year of his reign, and his son Marquis Xuan came to the throne. Xuanhou died in the thirteenth year of his reign, and his son Huanhou came to the throne. Huan Hou died after reigning for seven years, and his son Zhuang Gong came to the throne. In the twelfth year of Duke Zhuang, Duke Huan of Qi began to dominate. In the 16th year, Yan State, Song State, and Wei State jointly attacked King Hui of Zhou. King Hui fled to Wendi. The three kingdoms supported King Hui's younger brother Decai as King of Zhou. In the seventeenth year, Zheng Guo arrested Yan Zhongfu and escorted King Hui of Zhou back to Zhou Guo. In the twenty-seventh year, the Shan Rong invaded the Yan State. Duke Huan of Qi went to rescue the Yan State, so he led his troops north to attack the Shan Rong and then returned home. Duke Zhuang of Yan sent Duke Huan of Qi out of the country, and Duke Huan of Qi ceded the place where Duke Zhuang of Yan went to the state of Yan. He asked Duke Zhuang of Yan and the princes to pay tribute to the emperor of Zhou, just like Duke Zhao of Yan during the reign of King Cheng of Zhou.
target: The history of the Yan state, beginning with its founder, Zhao Gongxi, a member of the Zhou royal family granted the title in Northern Yan by King Wu. During King Cheng's reign, Zhao Gong governed west of Shaanxi, while the Duke of Zhou governed the east. Suspicious of the Duke of Zhou's regency, Zhao Gong was appeased by the Duke's historical references to virtuous Yin ministers. Zhao Gong governed the western region with great popularity, famously adjudicating under a Tangli tree, which the people later honored in the poem "Gantang" after his death. The succession of Yan rulers is then detailed, from Huihou through numerous generations, with key events interspersed: the flight of King Zhou Li, the rise of Qin as vassals, and the reign of King Xuan. The narrative covers Yan's interactions with other states, including attacks on King Hui of Zhou, invasions by Shan Rong (aided by Duke Huan of Qi), and participation in alliances against Qin. Internal strife emerges under King Kuai, who ceded power to his minister Zizhi, leading to chaos, Qi's invasion, and the death of King Kuai. King Zhao of Yan restored stability by recruiting talents like Le Yi, Zou Yan, and Ju Xin, leading to a prosperous period and a successful campaign against Qi, capturing its capital Linzi.

id: 史记/三十世家/燕召公世家::group-001
article_path: 史记/三十世家/燕召公世家
source: When the Yan army arrived at Songzi, Zhao sent Lian Po to lead his troops and defeated Li Fu at Cha. Le Cheng also defeated Qing Qin in Dai Di. Lejian fled to Zhao State. Lian Po pursued Yan for more than five hundred miles and surrounded the capital of Yan. The people of Yan requested peace talks, but the people of Zhao refused, so they had to ask General Qu to come forward to preside over the peace talks. The State of Yan appointed General Qu as prime minister and went to preside over the peace talks. The State of Zhao listened to General Qu's request and lifted the siege of the State of Yan. In the sixth year of King Yan's reign, the Qin State destroyed the Eastern Zhou Dynasty and established Sanchuan County. In seven years, Qin State captured 37 cities including Yulin of Zhao State and established Taiyuan County. In the ninth year, King Qin Yingzheng had just ascended the throne. In the tenth year, the State of Zhao sent Lian Po to lead an army to attack Fanyang of the State of Wei and occupied it. At this time, King Zhao Xiaocheng passed away and King Mouxiang came to the throne. King Mouxiang sent Lecheng to take over Lianpo's command, but Lianpo refused to obey orders and attacked Lecheng. Lecheng escaped, and Lianpo also fled to Daliang, the capital of Wei. In the twelfth year, Zhao State sent Li Mu to attack Yan State and captured Wu Sui and Fangcheng. When Ju Xin lived in the State of Zhao, he was very close to Pang Nuan, but later fled to the State of Yan. King Yan saw that Zhao was besieged by Qin soldiers many times and Lian Po left Zhao. At this time, Pang Nuan was leading the army to fight, so he wanted to take advantage of Zhao's fatigue to attack it. King Yan asked Ju Xin at this time, and Ju Xin said: Pang Nuan is easy to deal with. The King of Yan sent Ju Xin to lead an army to attack the State of Zhao. The State of Zhao sent Pang Nuan to fight, captured 20,000 Yan troops, and killed Ju Xin. At this time, Qin State captured twenty cities of Wei State and established Dongjun. In the 19th year, Qin State captured nine cities including Ye of Zhao State. King Zhao Daoxiang passed away. In the twenty-third year, Prince Dan of Yan was sent to Qin as a hostage, but he escaped back to Yan. In the twenty-fifth year, Qin captured Han Wangan, destroyed Han, and established Yingchuan County. In the twenty-seventh year, Qin captured Zhao Wangqian and destroyed Zhao. Prince Jia of the State of Zhao established himself as acting king. The monarchs and ministers of the Yan State saw that the Qin State was about to destroy the six countries. The Qin army had already reached Yishui, and disaster was about to befall the Yan State. Prince Dan of Yan secretly supported twenty warriors. At this time, he sent Jing Ke to present the map of Dukang to the King of Qin and took the opportunity to assassinate the King of Qin. The King of Qin found out, killed Jing Ke, and sent General Wang Jian to attack Yan. In the 29th year, the Qin army captured Ji, the capital of Yan State. King Yan fled and later moved to Liaodong. He killed Prince Dan and presented his head to Qin State. Thirty years later, Qin destroyed Wei. In the thirty-third year, the Qin army captured Liaodong, captured King Xi of Yan, and finally destroyed the Yan state. This year, Qin general Wang Ben also captured Dai Wangjia. Tai Shigong said: Zhao Gongxi can be called a virtuous person! That Tangli tree is still missed by the people, let alone Zhao Gong himself?
target: After King Zhao's death, King Hui's distrust of Le Yi led to Qi's recovery under Tian Dan. Subsequent rulers faced defeats by Zhao, including a failed attack advised by Ju Xin, resulting in heavy losses. The state weakened as Qin expanded, destroying Han and Zhao. Prince Dan of Yan's failed assassination attempt on Qin's king via Jing Ke prompted Qin's invasion, capturing Ji and forcing King Yan to flee to Liaodong. Eventually, Qin captured Liaodong, ending the Yan state. The historian concludes that Yan's survival for eight or nine hundred years, despite external pressures and near destruction, was due to Zhao Gong's virtuous legacy.

id: 史记/三十世家/留侯世家::group-000
article_path: 史记/三十世家/留侯世家
source: Liu Hou Zhang Liang, his ancestors were Koreans. His grandfather served as the prime minister of Han Zhaohou, King Xuanhui and King Xiangai in Kaidi. His father, Zhang Ping, served as prime minister to King Li and King Tuohui. In the twenty-third year of King Hui's reign, his father Zhang Ping passed away. Twenty years after Zhang Liang's father died, the Qin State destroyed South Korea. Zhang Liang was young at the time and had not been an official in Korea. After the fall of Korea, Zhang Liang's family had 300 servants. When Zhang Liang's younger brother died, he was not buried well. He used all his property to find warriors to assassinate the King of Qin and avenge Korea. This was because his grandfather and father had served as the kings of Korea for five generations. Zhang Liang once studied etiquette in Huaiyang and went to the East to meet Lord Canghai. He found a strong man and made a hammer weighing 120 kilograms. Qin Shihuang went on a tour to the East. Zhang Liang and Hercules attacked Qin Shihuang at Bolangsha, and accidentally hit the auxiliary car. Qin Shihuang was furious and launched a massive search across the country, hoping to catch the assassin quickly. This was exactly what Zhang Liang had caused. Zhang Liang then changed his name and surname, fled to Xiapi and hid. Zhang Liang was wandering on the Xiapi Bridge in his spare time. He met an old man wearing coarse clothes. He walked up to Zhang Liang and deliberately threw his shoes under the bridge. He looked at Zhang Liang and said to him: Boy, go down and pick up the shoes! Zhang Liang was a little surprised and wanted to beat him, but seeing that he was old, he reluctantly endured it and went down to pick up the shoes.
target: Zhang Liang, also known as Liu Hou, was a descendant of Korean nobility. His grandfather and father served as prime ministers to five generations of Korean kings. After Qin destroyed Korea, Zhang Liang, though young and never an official, used his family's wealth to hire an assassin to attack Qin Shi Huang at Bolangsha, but mistakenly struck an auxiliary carriage. Forced to flee, he changed his name and hid in Xiapi.

id: 史记/三十世家/留侯世家::group-001
article_path: 史记/三十世家/留侯世家
source: Zhang Liang was wandering on the Xiapi Bridge in his spare time. He met an old man wearing coarse clothes. He walked up to Zhang Liang and deliberately threw his shoes under the bridge. He looked at Zhang Liang and said to him: Boy, go down and pick up the shoes! Zhang Liang was a little surprised and wanted to beat him, but seeing that he was old, he reluctantly endured it and went down to pick up the shoes. The old man said: Put on my shoes! Since Zhang Liang had picked up the shoes for him, he knelt down and put them on for him. The old man stretched out his feet and put on his shoes, smiled and left. Zhang Liang was very surprised and followed the old man's figure and stared at him. The old man left for about a mile, then returned and said, "You, my boy, can teach." Meet me here at dawn five days later. Zhang Liang thought this was strange, knelt down and said, "Yeah." At dawn five days later, Zhang Liang went there. The old man was already there first and said angrily: "I date an old man, but I arrive late. Why?" The old man left and said: Come and meet early in five days. Five days later, when the rooster crows, Zhang Liang goes. The old man was there first and said angrily: "I'm late again. Why is this?" The old man left and said: Come back early in five days. Five days later, Zhang Liang left before midnight. After a while, the old man also came and said happily: It should be like this. The old man took out a book and said: After reading this book, you can become the emperor's teacher. There will definitely be some development in ten years. Thirteen years later, when your boy comes to Jibei to meet me, the yellow stone at the foot of Gucheng Mountain will be me. After saying that, he left without leaving anything else, and he never saw the old man again. At dawn, I looked at the book given by the old man and found it was "Tai Gong's Art of War". Zhang Liang felt that this book was extraordinary and often studied and recited it. When Zhang Liang lived in Xiapi, he was a chivalrous and righteous man.
target: While wandering on a bridge in Xiapi, Zhang Liang encountered an old man who tested him by throwing his shoes and demanding Zhang Liang retrieve and put them on. After passing this test, the oldman gave him the "Tai Gong's Art of War," declaring Zhang Liang would become the emperor's teacher. Zhang Liang studied the book diligently.

id: 史记/三十世家/留侯世家::group-002
article_path: 史记/三十世家/留侯世家
source: Thirteen years later, when your boy comes to Jibei to meet me, the yellow stone at the foot of Gucheng Mountain will be me. After saying that, he left without leaving anything else, and he never saw the old man again. At dawn, I looked at the book given by the old man and found it was "Tai Gong's Art of War". Zhang Liang felt that this book was extraordinary and often studied and recited it. When Zhang Liang lived in Xiapi, he was a chivalrous and righteous man. Xiang Bo once killed someone and hid with Zhang Liang. Ten years later, Chen She and others rebelled against Qin, and Zhang Liang also gathered more than a hundred young people. Jing Ju established himself as the acting King of Chu and stationed in Liu County. Zhang Liang planned to follow him, but met Pei Gong on the way. Peigong led thousands of men to seize the area west of Xiapi, and Zhang Liang joined him. Pei Gong appointed Zhang Liang as the stable general. Zhang Liang offered suggestions to Pei Gong based on "Tai Gong's Art of War" many times. Pei Gong appreciated him and often adopted his strategies. Zhang Liang taught "Tai Gong's Art of War" to others, but no one could understand it. Zhang Liang said: Pei Gong was probably bestowed on earth by heaven. So Zhang Liang followed Pei Gong instead of joining Jingju. When Pei Gong arrived at Xuedi, he met with Xiang Liang. Xiang Liang supported King Huai of Chu. Zhang Liang then persuaded Xiang Liang: "You have already supported the descendants of the King of Chu, and Han Cheng, Lord of Hengyang among the Korean princes, can be made king and increase the strength of his allies." Xiang Liang sent Zhang Liang to find Han Cheng and made him king of Han. Appointed Zhang Liang as the Situ of South Korea, and led more than a thousand people to the west to attack South Korea's original territory with the King of Han, and captured several cities. The Qin army soon recaptured them, and the Han army only conducted guerrilla operations in the Yingchuan area. When Pei Gong passed through the Sheyuan Mountain south from Luoyang, Zhang Liang led his troops to follow Pei Gong, captured more than ten cities in Han, and defeated Yang Xiong's army.
target: During the rebellions against Qin, Zhang Liang gathered followers and joined Pei Gong (Liu Bang), becoming his trusted advisor. He used strategies from the Art of War to advise Pei Gong, who appreciated his counsel. Zhang Liang persuaded Xiang Liang to restore Han Cheng as King of Han, and Zhang Liang served as his Situ. He later rejoined Pei Gong, advising him against attacking the Qin army at Yao Pass directly, instead suggesting bribery and deception, leading to Qin's surrender.

id: 史记/三十世家/留侯世家::group-003
article_path: 史记/三十世家/留侯世家
source: Then Pei Gong arrived in Xianyang, and Qin Prince Ying surrendered to Pei Gong. Pei Gong entered the Qin Palace. There were thousands of palaces, tents, dogs and horses, precious treasures, and beautiful women. Pei Gong's intention was to stay in the palace. Fan Kuai advised Pei Gong to go out and live there, but Pei Gong refused to listen. Zhang Liang said: The Qin Dynasty was tyrannical and immoral, so Pei Gong was able to come here. To eradicate cruel tyranny from the world, we should be honest and simple. Now that we have just invaded the capital of Qin, we have to enjoy it in peace. This is what people say, "helping Jie to do harm." Moreover, good advice is unpleasant to the ear but beneficial to action, and good medicine is bitter to the mouth and beneficial to the patient. I hope Pei Gong will listen to Fan Kuai's opinion. Only then did Pei Gong return to his carriage and stop at Bashang. Xiang Yu came to Hongmen and wanted to attack Pei Gong. Xiang Bo rushed to Pei Gong's camp overnight and met with Zhang Liang privately, hoping that Zhang Liang would leave with him. Zhang Liang said: I am escorting Pei Gong on behalf of the King of Han. Now the situation is urgent and it is unethical to escape. So he told Pei Gong everything. Pei Gong was very surprised and said: "What will we do about this?" Zhang Liang said: Does Pei Gong really want to betray Xiang Yu? Pei Gong said: "The ignorant villain taught me to block Hangu Pass and prevent the princes from entering. He said that in this way the land of the Qin Dynasty could be completely controlled, so I followed this advice." Zhang Liang said: Pei Gong thinks for himself, can he defeat Xiang Yu? Pei Gong was silent for a while and then said, "It shouldn't be possible. What should we do now?" Zhang Liang then firmly invited Xiang Bo to see Pei Gong. Xiang Bo met with Pei Gong. Pei Gong drank with Xiang Bo, toasted and blessed him, and married him. Pei Gong asked Xiang Bo to explain to Xiang Yu in detail that Pei Gong did not dare to betray Xiang Yu. The reason why Pei Gong blocked Hangu Pass was to prevent other bandits. After Pei Gong met with Xiang Yu, the two parties reached a reconciliation, which was recorded in "The Notes of Xiang Yu". In the first month of the first year of the Han Dynasty, Peigong became the king of Han and ruled the Bashu region. The king of Han rewarded Zhang Liang with a hundred yi of gold and two measures of pearls. Zhang Liang gave them all to Xiang Bo. Therefore, the King of Han asked Zhang Lianghou to give Xiang Bo a gift, so that Xiang Bo asked King Xiang to allocate the Hanzhong area to him on his behalf. King Xiang agreed to the request of the King of Han, and the King of Han obtained the Hanzhong area. The King of Han went to Fengguo, Zhang Liang sent the King of Han to Baozhong, and the King of Han asked Zhang Liang to return to Korea. Zhang Liang then advised the King of Han: "Why don't you burn down the plank road you pass by to express your determination not to come back to the world, so as to stabilize King Xiang's heart?" The king of Han then asked Zhang Liang to return to Korea. When the king of Han was marching, he burned down the plank road he passed.
target: After entering Xianyang, Zhang Liang convinced Pei Gong to leave the Qin palace and avoid luxury, warning it would harm his cause. At the Hongmen Banquet, Zhang Liang helped Pei Gong reconcile with Xiang Yu. When Pei Gong became King of Han, Zhang Liang advised burning the plank road to show no intention of returning east, stabilizing Xiang Yu. He later recommended using Yingbu, Peng Yue, and Han Xin to defeat Chu.

id: 史记/三十世家/留侯世家::group-004
article_path: 史记/三十世家/留侯世家
source: Now your Majesty has re-divided the descendants of the Six Kingdoms and established the descendants of Han, Wei, Yan, Zhao, Qi and Chu as princes and kings. The wanderers in the world have returned to serve their monarchs, reunite with their long-lost relatives, and return to their old friends and hometowns where their ancestral graves are. Who will your Majesty go with to conquer the world? This is the eighth reason why the descendants of the Six Kingdoms cannot be enfeoffed. Moreover, the Chu State is currently invincible in the world. The descendants of the six kingdoms you have re-enfranchised will all surrender to the Chu State. What method can your Majesty have to make them surrender? If your majesty really adopts the diner's plan, your majesty's great affairs will be ruined. The King of Han stopped eating, spit out the food in his mouth, and cursed: This ignorant person almost ruined my big event! Immediately ordered the seal to be destroyed immediately. In the fourth year of the Han Dynasty, Han Xin wanted to proclaim himself king of Qi after conquering Qi, but the king of Han was furious. Zhang Liang advised the King of Han, and the King of Han sent Zhang Liang to grant Han Xin the seal of King Xin of Qi. This matter was recorded in the "Biography of the Marquis of Huaiyin". In the autumn of this year, the king of Han pursued the Chu army to the south of Yangxia. Because of the defeat in the battle, he held fast to the Guling camp. The princes did not come on the appointed day. Zhang Liang proposed a plan to the king of Han, and the king of Han adopted his plan, and all the princes came. This incident is recorded in "The Chronicles of Xiang Yu". In the first month of the sixth year of Han Dynasty, Emperor Gao rewarded the meritorious officials. Zhang Liang had no military exploits. Emperor Gao said: "It is the contribution of Zifang to make plans in the camp and decide the victory or defeat thousands of miles away." Zhang Liang was asked to select 30,000 households from Qi State as fiefdoms. Zhang Liang said: When I started an uprising in Xiapi and met Your Majesty in Liu County, it was God who handed me over to Your Majesty. Your Majesty adopted my strategy, and luckily my prediction turned out right. I only wanted to be granted a county seal, and I did not dare to bear 30,000 households. So Zhang Liang was granted the title of Liuhou, along with Xiao He and others.
target: Zhang Liang opposed enfeoffing descendants of the six kingdoms, arguing it would undermine Liu Bang's support. He convinced Liu Bang to grant Han Xin the title of King of Qi. After the Han dynasty was established, Liu Bang praised Zhang Liang's strategic contributions and offered him 30,000 households, but Zhang Liang accepted only a county, becoming Marquis of Liu.

id: 史记/三十世家/留侯世家::group-005
article_path: 史记/三十世家/留侯世家
source: The four people finished toasting and blessing, and walked away quickly. The emperor watched them off, summoned Mrs. Qi, pointed to the four people, and said, "I want to replace the prince. The four of them will assist him. The prince's wings have already been formed and it is difficult to change them." Queen Lu is truly your master. Qi Fu began to cry, and the emperor said: You dance Chu dances for me, and I sing Chu songs for you. The emperor sang: The swan flies high, fluttering its wings for thousands of miles. The wings are ready, soaring all over the world. Soaring all over the world, there is nothing you can do! Although there are short arrows, where can I use them? The emperor sang several times, and Mrs. Qi sobbed and shed tears. The emperor got up and left, and the banquet was over. The emperor did not replace the prince in the end. It was originally Liuhou who caused the influence of these four people. Liuhou followed the emperor to attack the country of Dai, made a clever plan under the city of Mayi, and persuaded the emperor to appoint Xiao He as the prime minister. He and the emperor usually talked about many things in the world casually, but because they were not important matters related to the survival of the country, they were not recorded. Liuhou declared: My family has been the prime minister of Korea for generations. When Korea was destroyed, I spared no expense on my family wealth to avenge Korea against the powerful Qin. The world was shocked by this. Now with my three-inch tongue, I am the emperor's commander, granting tens of thousands of households, and ranking among the nobles. This is supreme for a commoner. I, Zhang Liang, am very satisfied. I am willing to abandon the things in this world and plan to travel with Chisongzi. Zhang Liang then learned the science of bigu and practiced the Tao to lead the way of lightening one's body. When Emperor Gao died, Empress Lu was grateful to Liu Hou, so she tried her best to let him eat, saying: "In this life, time flies as fast as a fleeting moment, why do you have to be so ascetic?" Liu Hou had no choice but to eat as ordered. Eight years later, Liuhou died, and his posthumous title was Wenchenghou. His son Zhang Busuo was granted the title of Marquis. Zhang Zifang first met the father-in-law who gave him "Tai Gong's Art of War" on the Xiapi Bridge. Thirteen years after their departure, he passed through Jibei with Emperor Gao. Sure enough, he saw the yellow stone at the foot of Gucheng Mountain, so he took it back and worshiped it as a treasure. Liuhou died and Huangshi was buried together. From then on, whenever Zhang Liang was worshiped during tomb sweeping and winter and summer festivals, Huangshi was also worshiped at the same time.
target: Zhang Liang advised moving the capital to Guanzhong for its strategic advantages. When Liu Bang wanted to depose the crown prince, Zhang Liang suggested inviting four reclusive sages to support the prince. Their presence convinced Liu Bang the prince's position was secure. Zhang Liang later practiced Taoist techniques, abstained from grain, and sought to travel with the immortal Chisongzi. He died eight years after Liu Bang, posthumously named Wencheng Hou. His son inherited the title but lost it due to misconduct.

source: Guan Shuxian and Cai Shudu were both sons of King Wen of Zhou and younger brothers of King Wu of Zhou. There were ten brothers from the same mother of King Wu of Zhou. Their mother's name was Taisi, who was King Wen's wife. Her eldest son is Boyikao, followed by Wu Wangfa, Guan Shuxian, Zhou Gongdan, Cai Shudu, Cao Shuzhenduo, Cheng Shuwu, Huo Shuchu, Kang Shufeng, and the youngest is Ran Jizai. Among the ten brothers, only Wu Wangfa and Zhou Gongdan were highly virtuous and talented, and they were the right-hand men to assist King Wen. Therefore, King Wen did not establish Boyikao, but made his second son Fa the crown prince. After King Wen died, Prince Fa came to the throne and became King Wu. Boyikao had passed away before this. After King Wu defeated King Zhou of Yin and pacified the world, he granted great titles to his heroes and brothers. So he enfeoffed the administrative land to Shuxian and the Cai land to Shudu; and made them ministers to the father of Wu Genglu, the son of Zhou, to govern the remnants of the Yin people together. He enfeoffed the land of Lu to Shu Dan, and at the same time made Shu Dan the prime minister of the Zhou Dynasty, so he was called Zhou Gong. Shu Zhenduo was granted the title of Cao Di, Shu Wu was granted the title of Cheng Di, and Shu Chu was granted the title of Huo Di. Uncle Kang and Ran Jizai were young at that time, so they were not awarded the title. After King Wu died, King Cheng succeeded to the throne at a young age, and Duke Zhou took control of the country. Uncle Guan and Uncle Cai suspected that Duke Zhou's actions were not conducive to becoming king, so they supported Wu Geng in the rebellion. Zhou Gongdan conquered the rebels according to the decree of King Cheng, executed Wu Geng, killed Guan Shu and exiled Cai Shu. During the exile, Cai Shu was only given a carriage and seventy prisoners as his entourage.
target: The lineage and history of the sons of King Wen of Zhou, focusing on Guan Shuxian and Cai Shudu, younger brothers of King Wu. King Wu had ten brothers from the same mother, Taisi. Among them, only King Wu and Zhou Gongdan were virtuous and talented, leading King Wen to make Fa (King Wu) crown prince. After King Wu conquered the Yin, he enfeoffed lands to his brothers: Shuxian received Guan, Shudu received Cai, and they were made ministers to Wu Geng, son of the Yin king. Zhou Gongdan was enfeoffed in Lu and served as prime minister. Other brothers received Cao, Cheng, and Huo. Kang Shu and Ran Jizai were too young for titles.

id: 史记/三十世家/管蔡世家::group-001

source: In the fourth year of Marquis Cheng, the Song State destroyed the Cao State. In the tenth year, Tian Chang of Qi State killed his king, Duke Jian of Qi State. In the thirteenth year, Chu State destroyed Chen State. In the 19th year, Chenghou died and his son Shenghou Chan succeeded to the throne. Shenghou died in the fifteenth year, and his son Yuanhou succeeded to the throne. Yuan Hou died in the sixth year, and his son Hou Qi succeeded to the throne. In the fourth year of Hou Qi's reign, King Hui of Chu destroyed the State of Cai, and Hou Qi of Cai fled. From then on, the sacrifices of the State of Cai were cut off, and the country was destroyed, thirty-three years later than the State of Chen. Boyikao's descendants don't know where they were sealed. The descendant of Wu Wangfa was Zhou Wang, which is recorded in "Benji". Guan Shuxian rebelled and was killed, leaving no descendants. The descendants of Zhou Gongdan were the monarchs of Lu State, which are recorded in "Shijia". The descendants of Cai Shudu are the monarchs of Cai State, which are recorded in "Guan Cai Family". The descendants of Cao Shu Zhenduo are the monarchs of Cao State, which are recorded in "Guan Cai Family". The whereabouts of Cheng Shuwu's descendants are unknown. The descendants of Huo Shuchu were enfeoffed in Huo Di and were later destroyed by Duke Xian of Jin. The descendants of Kang Shufeng are the monarchs of Wei State, which are recorded in "Wei Kangshu Family". The whereabouts of Ran Jizai's descendants are unknown. Tai Shigong said: There is nothing worth recording about the rebellion of Uncle Guan and Uncle Cai. However, after King Wu of Zhou died and King Cheng was young, everyone in the world doubted Duke Zhou. It was only with the help of Cheng Shu, Ran Ji and ten other people, including his mother and brothers, that all the princes in the world respected the Zhou family, so their deeds were appended to the "Aristocratic Family". Cao Shu Zhenduo was the younger brother of King Wu of Zhou. After King Wu defeated Shang Zhou, he enfeoffed the land of Cao to Shu Zhenduo. Shu Zhenduo died, and his son Taibo Pi succeeded to the throne. Tai Bo died and his son Zhong Junping came to the throne. Zhong Junping died, and his son Xian Bohou succeeded to the throne. When Xian Bohou passed away, his son Xiao Boyun succeeded him. Xiao Boyun died, and his son Yi Boxi succeeded him. In the twenty-third year of Yibo, King Li of Zhou fled to the land of pigs. Yi Bo died in the 30th year, and his younger brother You Boqiang succeeded to the throne. In the ninth year of Youbo's reign, his younger brother Su killed Youbo and established himself as the king of the country. He was Daibo. In the first year of Dai Bo, King Zhou Xuan had been on the throne for three years. Thirty years later, Dai Bo died and his son Hui Boyi succeeded him. In the twenty-fifth year of Huibo's reign, King You of Zhou was killed by Quan Rong. The royal family moved eastward and became increasingly weak. The princes betrayed the royal family one after another. Qin State began to be classified as a vassal state in this year. In the thirty-sixth year, Hui Bo died and his son Shi Fu succeeded to the throne. His younger brother Wu killed Shi Fu and made himself king, namely Duke Mu. Duke Mu died after reigning for three years, and his son Duke Huan succeeded him for life.
target: After King Wu died, King Cheng succeeded as a child, and Zhou Gongdan ruled as regent. Guan Shu and Cai Shu, suspecting Zhou Gong's intentions, rebelled with Wu Geng. Zhou Gong crushed the rebellion, executing Wu Geng and Guan Shu, and exiling Cai Shu. Cai Shu died in exile, but his son Hu reformed and was later enfeoffed in Cai by Zhou Gong's recommendation. The text then traces the succession of Cai rulers through generations, including conflicts with Chu and Qi. Key events include Cai Aihou's capture by Chu, Cai Miao Hou's conflict with Duke Huan of Qi over a marriage dispute, and Cai's eventual destruction by King Hui of Chu after 33 years. The text also covers the lineage of Cao Shu Zhenduo, another brother, whose descendants ruled Cao until its destruction by Song. It notes that Guan Shu left no descendants, while Zhou Gongdan's descendants ruled Lu, and Kang Shu's descendants ruled Wei. The historian concludes that Guan and Cai's rebellion was unremarkable, but Zhou Gong's regency stabilized the Zhou dynasty. The dream of a Cao man predicting the state's fall is recounted, ending with Cao's destruction due to poor governance under Boyang and Gongsun Qiang.
