If the monarch wants to make a profit, then the officials also want to make a profit; if the officials want to make a profit, then the people also want to make a profit. If everyone from top to bottom strives for profit, the country will be in danger. As a monarch of a country, it is enough to be benevolent and righteous. Why should we be concerned about profit? In the thirty-sixth year of King Hui's reign, he met King Qi again in Zhenyi.
target: Meng Ke advised the king that a ruler should focus on benevolence and righteousness rather than profit.

source: If the Wei State gets South Korea as a county, Wei, Daliang, and Hewai will definitely be able to stabilize. If Korea is not preserved, the East and West Zhou and Anling will be in danger. After the defeat of Chu and Zhao, Wei and Qi are very afraid. The days when all the princes in the world rush west to Qin to pay homage to Qin are not long. In the 20th year of King Anli's reign, the Qin army besieged Handan. Wuji, the king of Xinling, falsely conveyed the king's order to seize the army of General Jin Bi to rescue the Zhao State. The Zhao State was preserved, and Wuji therefore stayed in the Zhao State. In the twenty-sixth year, King Zhao of Qin passed away. In the 30th year of King Anli, Wuji returned to Wei and led the armies of the five countries to attack Qin. He defeated the Qin army outside the river and drove away Qin general Meng Ao. At that time, Prince Zeng of Wei State was a hostage in Qin State. The King of Qin was angry and wanted to imprison Prince Zeng of Wei State. Someone said to the King of Qin on behalf of Prince Zeng: Gongsun Xi originally said to the Prime Minister of Wei: Please use the Wei army to attack Qin quickly. When the King of Qin is angry, he will definitely imprison Prince Zeng. This will make King Wei angry and attack Qin again. Qin will definitely hurt Prince Zeng. Now the king wants to imprison Prince Zeng. This is Gongsun happy's plan. Therefore, it is better to treat Prince Zeng favorably and have good relations with Wei, and let Qi and South Korea doubt Wei. Only then did King Qin cancel his plan to imprison Prince Zeng. In the thirty-first year of King Anli's reign, King Qin began to ascend the throne. In the thirty-fourth year of King Anli, King Anli died, and Prince Zeng ascended the throne. This was King Jingmin. Xinlingjun Wuji passed away. In the first year of King Jingmin, the Qin army captured 20 cities in the Wei State and established them as the East Commandery of the Qin State. In the second year, the Qin army captured Chaoge of Wei State. Weiguo moved to Yewang. In three years, the Qin army captured Jiyi in the state of Wei. In five years, the Qin army captured Wei's Yuandi, Puyang, and Yanyi. In the fifteenth year, King Jingmin died, and his son King Wei assumed the throne. In the first year of King Wei's holiday, Prince Dan of Yan sent Jing Ke to assassinate King Qin, but King Qin discovered it. Three years after King Jie of Wei, the Qin army flooded Daliang and captured King Jie of Wei. Finally, the state of Wei was destroyed and established as prefectures and counties. Tai Shigong said: I have been to the old city site of Daliang. The people there said: The Qin army conquered Daliang by diverting water from the chasm to flood Daliang. After three months, the city was destroyed, and the King of Wei asked for surrender, thus destroying the Wei state. Those who discussed it all said that because King Wei did not reuse Lord Xinling, the country was weakened and even destroyed. I don't think so. God's will is for the Qin State to pacify the sea, but its achievements have not yet been completed. Even if the Wei State is assisted by wise ministers like A Heng, what is the use?
target: The later reigns of King Xiang, King Ai, King Zhao, King Anli, King Jingmin, and King Wei saw Wei's gradual decline. The Qin state repeatedly attacked Wei, capturing cities and territories. Despite efforts by figures like Lord Xinling Wuji, who successfully led a coalition of five states against Qin, Wei continued to lose ground. In the third year of King Wei's reign, the Qin army diverted water from the chasm to flood Daliang, capturing King Wei and destroying the Wei state, which was then established as prefectures and counties. The Grand Historian concluded that while some blamed King Wei's failure to employ Lord Xinling for Wei's destruction, he believed the Qin state was destined by Heaven to unify the realm, and even wise ministers could not have prevented Wei's fall.

id: 史记/三十世家/鲁周公世家::group-000
article_path: 史记/三十世家/鲁周公世家
source: Duke Dan of Zhou was the younger brother of King Wu of Zhou. When King Wen was still alive, Dan, as his son, was very filial, loyal and kind, better than his other brothers. When King Wu came to the throne, Dan often assisted King Bi Wu and handled many government affairs. In the ninth year of King Wu's reign, he personally marched eastward to Mengjin, and Duke Zhou accompanied the army to assist him. In the eleventh year, King Wu crusaded against Yin Zhou and the army reached Muye. Duke Zhou assisted King Wu and issued the "Oath of Mu" to mobilize the battle. The Zhou army broke through the capital of Yin and entered the palace of Yin. After killing Yin Zhou, Duke Zhou held a big axe, and Duke Zhao held a small axe. They flanked King Wu on their left and right, held the ceremony of provoking the community, and announced King Zhou's guilt to heaven and the people of Yin Dynasty. Release the imprisoned Jizi. Wu Genglu, the son of King Zhou, was granted the title of Father, and ordered Uncle Guan and Uncle Cai to assist him in order to continue the sacrifices of Yin. After that, he was awarded the title of meritorious officials and relatives of the Zhou royal family. The Duke of Zhou was granted the title of Duke of Lu in Qufu, Shaohao's former ruins. However, Duke Zhou was not allowed to go to his own kingdom, but stayed in Chaoyan to assist King Wu.
target: Duke Dan of Zhou, younger brother of King Wu of Zhou, was known for his filial piety and virtue. He assisted King Wu in military campaigns, including the conquest of Yin Zhou at Muye. After Yin Zhou's death, Duke Zhou participated in ceremonies announcing King Zhou's guilt, released the imprisoned Jizi, and helped grant territories to various nobles. Though granted the title of Duke of Lu in Qufu, he remained in the capital to assist King Wu.

id: 史记/三十世家/鲁周公世家::group-001
article_path: 史记/三十世家/鲁周公世家
source: King Fa of Zhou was not as versatile as Dan and could not serve ghosts and gods. But King Fa of Zhou was ordered by Heaven to help the whole world, and to enable your descendants to live peacefully in the world. People everywhere will respect him. He can ensure that the heaven-given treasures are preserved for a long time, and our late king can be enshrined forever. Now I obey the orders of the late king through the divination turtle. If you can agree to my request, I will offer the jade and obey your orders. If you don't agree, I will hide the jade. After Zhou Gong ordered the historian to write a book to congratulate King Tai, Wang Ji, and King Wen that he would replace King Wu with his own body, he went to the altar of the three kings to divine fortune. People in fortune-telling said it was auspicious. When I opened the omen book, I found that it was indeed auspicious. Duke Zhou was very happy, so he opened the lock and looked at the divination book hidden in the cabinet, which was also an auspicious sign. The Duke of Zhou immediately entered the palace to congratulate King Wu and said: "You are not in trouble. I have just accepted the orders of the three ancestors, so that you only need to consider the long-term plan of the Zhou Dynasty and the world, and have nothing else to worry about." This is what is called God’s thoughtful consideration for the Emperor. Duke Zhou put the scroll into a gold-wired cabinet and sealed it, warning the keepers not to leak it. The next day, King Wu suddenly recovered. Later, King Wu died and King Cheng was still in his infancy. Duke Zhou was worried that people in the world would betray the court when they heard about King Wu's death, so he ascended the throne to handle government affairs on behalf of King Cheng and preside over the power of the country. Guan Shu and his brothers spread rumors in the country: Duke Zhou will be detrimental to the king. The Duke of Zhou then told Taigong Wang and Zhao Gongsi: The reason why I do not avoid suspicion and act in the affairs of the country is because I am afraid that the people in the world will betray the Zhou family and cannot explain to our ancestors Taiwang Taiwang, Wang Ji and King Wen. The three ancestors have worked hard for the cause of the world for a long time, and they have just succeeded. King Wu died young and King Cheng was young. I only did this to complete the great cause of stabilizing the Zhou Dynasty. So he eventually assisted in becoming king, and ordered his son Boqin to go to the State of Lu to be granted a title on his behalf. Zhou Gong warned Bo Qin: I am the son of King Wen, the younger brother of King Wu, and the uncle of King Cheng. My status among the people in the world is not low. But I had to pull up my hair three times once I washed my hair, spit out the food I was chewing three times after eating a meal, and got up to receive the wise men. Even so, I was afraid of missing out on the wise men in the world. After you arrive in Lu, don't be arrogant because you have a land. Sure enough, Guan Shu, Cai Shu, Wu Geng and others led Huaiyi to launch a rebellion. The Duke of Zhou followed the orders of King Cheng, raised his troops to march eastward, and wrote the "Great Edict". So Guan Shu was executed, Wu Geng was killed, and Cai Shu was exiled.
target: When King Wu fell ill, Duke Zhou offered himself as a sacrifice to the ancestral spirits, praying to die in King Wu's place. He performed divination, received auspicious signs, and King Wu recovered. After King Wu's death, with King Cheng still an infant, Duke Zhou assumed regency to prevent rebellion. His brothers Guan Shu and Cai Shu spread rumors that he would harm the young king. Duke Zhou explained his actions were to preserve the Zhou legacy, and eventually suppressed a rebellion led by Guan Shu, Cai Shu, and Wu Geng, executing Guan Shu and exiling Cai Shu.

id: 史记/三十世家/鲁周公世家::group-002
article_path: 史记/三十世家/鲁周公世家
source: Collect the remnants of Yin, grant Kang Shu to Wei, and Wei Zi to Song, and let him perform Yin's sacrifices. It took another two years to pacify Huaiyi and other areas in the east. The princes all followed the Zhou Dynasty. God sent blessings, and Uncle Tang received two stalks of millet and one ear, which he dedicated to King Cheng. King Cheng ordered Uncle Tang to go to the eastern part of the garrison where Duke Zhou's army was stationed and present it to Duke Zhou, and wrote "Feeding Grain". After Zhou Gong accepted it, he expressed gratitude and praised the emperor's order and wrote "Jiahe". After the East became stable, Duke Zhou reported back to King Cheng and wrote a poem as a gift to King Cheng. His poem was called "Owl". King Cheng did not dare to blame Duke Zhou. On the last day of February in the seventh year of King Cheng, King Cheng went to Haojing to pay homage to Wuwang Temple, and then walked to Fengjing to pay homage to Wenwang Temple. He ordered Taibao Zhaogong to go to Luoyi first to survey the terrain. In March, Duke Zhou went to Luoyi to build the capital city of Zhou and conducted divination. The results showed good luck, so he made Luoyi the capital. King Cheng grew up and was able to handle state affairs. So Zhou Gong returned the political power to King Cheng, who came to the court to listen to the government. In the past, when the Duke of Zhou replaced King Cheng in governing the world, he faced the south and his back to the wall to accept the worship of the princes. Seven years later, when King Cheng returned the throne, Duke Zhou faced north and stood in the position of a minister, still cautious and respectful as if he were walking on thin ice. When King Cheng was young, he fell ill once. Duke Zhou cut off his fingernails and sank them into the river. He prayed to the gods and said: "The king has no opinions when he is young, and he offends the gods." He also hid the blessing notice in the secret palace, and the illness of King Cheng was indeed cured. After King Cheng came to the throne, some people said bad things about Duke Zhou, so Duke Zhou fled to the state of Chu. King Cheng opened the secret palace and found the prayer book written by Duke Zhou. He was moved to tears and immediately invited Duke Zhou back. After Zhou Gong returned to the country, he was afraid that the young king would indulge in debauchery while governing the country, so he wrote "Toast" and "Wuyi". "Wu Yi" says: As parents, it is extremely difficult to start a business for a long time. Their descendants are arrogant and extravagant and forget the hardships of their ancestors, ruining the family business. Sons of man must be cautious! Therefore, in the past, King Zhongzong of Yin solemnly and respectfully feared the mandate of heaven, was strict with himself when governing the people, competed in the industry and did not dare to neglect his career for his own pleasure, so Zhongzong owned the country for seventy-five years.
target: Duke Zhou governed for seven years, then returned power to King Cheng when the king came of age. He wrote admonitions including "Wu Yi" and "Toushi" to warn King Cheng against indulgence, citing examples of Yin Dynasty rulers who prospered through diligence or fell through decadence. After Duke Zhou's death, King Cheng buried him beside King Wen. When a storm destroyed crops, King Cheng opened the golden-bound cabinet containing Duke Zhou's prayer to die for King Wu, realized his virtue, and performed ceremonies that restored the harvest.

id: 史记/三十世家/鲁周公世家::group-003
article_path: 史记/三十世家/鲁周公世家
source: Ji Pingzi walked barefoot in common clothes and apologized to the six ministers. Liuqing spoke for Ji Pingzi and said: Although Jin supports Duke Zhao, the people of Lu are unwilling. Jin Jun gave up. In the thirty-second year, Duke Zhao died in Qianhou. The people of Lu jointly established Zhaogong's younger brother Song as their king, who was named Dinggong. After Duke Ding was established, Zhao Jianzi asked Shi Mo: Will the Ji family perish? Shi Mo replied: It will not perish. Ji You made great contributions to the state of Lu, and was granted the title of Shangqing in Eyi. He continued to expand his business through generations until Wenzi and Wuzi. After Duke Wen of Lu passed away, Dongmen killed his legitimate son and made his concubine the king of Lu. The king of Lu lost his political power. The national affairs are controlled by the Ji family, and so far there have been four monarchs. The people don't know their king. How does the king control the administrative power of the country? Because of this, the monarch should treat the country's vehicles, equipment, titles and titles with caution, and should not give them to others easily. In the fifth year of Duke Dinggong's reign, Ji Pingzi died. Yang Hu had private resentment, imprisoned Ji Huanzi, and made a covenant with him before releasing him. In the seventh year, the Qi army attacked the state of Lu, captured Yunyi, made it a fiefdom for Yanghu of the state of Lu, and allowed him to participate in political affairs. In eight years, Yang Hu wanted to kill all the direct heirs of San Huan and replace the direct heirs with concubines who were closely related to him. Yang Hu drove Ji Huanzi in a car and took the opportunity to kill him, but Huanzi used deception to escape.
target: The state of Lu continued through successive dukes. Duke Boqin, Duke Zhou's son, governed Lu and suppressed rebellions. The state experienced periods of stability and turmoil, with conflicts over succession and the growing power of the Three Huan families (Mengsun, Shusun, Jisun). Duke Zhao was forced into exile after attacking the Ji family, dying in Qianhou. The state declined as the Three Huan families grew increasingly powerful, reducing subsequent rulers to figureheads.

id: 史记/三十世家/鲁周公世家::group-004
article_path: 史记/三十世家/鲁周公世家
source: When Gong Gong died in the 22nd year, his son Tun succeeded to the throne and became Kang Gong. Kang Gong died in the ninth year, and his son Jinggong succeeded to the throne. Jinggong died in the 29th year, and his son succeeded him, namely Pinggong. At this time, all the six countries claimed to be kings. In the 12th year of Ping Gong, King Hui of Qin passed away. Twenty years later, Duke Ping died, and his son Jia succeeded him as Duke Wen. In the first year of Emperor Wen's reign, King Huai of Chu died in Qin. In the twenty-third year, Duke Wen passed away, and his son, Qing Gong, succeeded him. In the second year of Qinggong, Qin conquered the capital of Chu State, Ying, and King Qing of Chu moved his capital eastward to Chen. In the 19th year, Chu defeated Lu, and the war zone was Xuzhou. In the twenty-fourth year, King Kaolie of Chu conquered Lu. Qinggong fled, moved to a small town outside the capital, and became a commoner. The sacrifices of the state of Lu were extinct. Qinggong died in Keyi. The state of Lu had thirty-four generations in total, from Duke Zhou to Duke Qing. Tai Shigong said: I heard that Confucius once said that the morality of the state of Lu was really in decline! People in Zhushui and Surabaya argued and argued endlessly. Look at how chaotic the state of Lu was when Qingfu, Shuya and Min Gong came to the throne! The succession of Duke Huan and Duke Yin occurred; Xiang Zhong killed his legitimate concubine; Meng Sun, Shu Sun, and Ji Sun were ministers, but they personally attacked Zhao Gong, causing Zhao Gong to flee. Although they have always followed the etiquette of courtesy, their actual behavior is so contrary to this!
target: The state of Lu lasted for thirty-four generations from Duke Zhou to Duke Qing, when King Kaolie of Chu conquered Lu. The historian Sima Qian noted that despite Lu's reputation for ritual propriety, its actual history was marked by chaos, including the murder of legitimate heirs and ministers attacking their rulers, revealing a contradiction between their ceremonial observance and political reality.

id: 史记/三十世家/齐太公世家::group-000
article_path: 史记/三十世家/齐太公世家
source: Taigong looked at Lu Shang, who was from the East China Sea. His ancestors once served as officials in the Four Mountains, assisting Xia Yu in water management and made great contributions. Shun and Yu were granted the title of Lu, and some were granted the title of Shen, with the surname Jiang. During the Xia and Shang dynasties, some places in Shen and Lu were granted to descendants of other branches, and some descendants became commoners. Lu Shang is their descendant. Lu Shang's original surname was Jiang. Because he took the name of his fiefdom, he was called Lu Shang. Lu Shang was once very famous. When he was old, he took the opportunity of fishing to ask to see Zhou Xibo. Before going out hunting, Xibo made a divination, and the hexagram said: The prey obtained is neither a dragon nor a chi, nor a tiger nor a bear; what he obtains is the assistant minister who will become the overlord. So Xibohou went out hunting, and sure enough he met Taigong on the north bank of the Wei River. After talking with Taigong, Xibo was overjoyed and said: I have long heard the Taigong, the ancestor of our country, say: A saint will definitely come to Zhou, and Zhou will prosper. That's you, right? Our grandpa has been waiting for you for a long time. So he called Lu Shang "Tai Gong Wang", and the two of them rode back together and respected him as military advisor. Some people say that Taigong was very knowledgeable and once assisted King Zhou of Shang Dynasty. Because King Zhou was unruly, Taigong left. He went around lobbying the princes of various countries, but failed to find a king, so he finally went west to join Zhou Xibo. Some people say that Lu Shang was a scholar who lived in seclusion by the sea. When Zhou Xibo was imprisoned in Youli by King Zhou, Xibo's ministers San Yisheng and Hong Yao knew about Lu Shang, so they asked him to come out. Lu Shang also said this: I heard that Xibo was virtuous and always respected and cared for the elderly. Why not go there? In order to rescue Uncle Xi, these three people searched for beautiful women and rare treasures, and presented them to King Zhou to redeem Uncle Xi. As a result, Xibo was released and returned to Zhou. Although there are different legends about Lu Shang's return to the Zhou Dynasty, the general consensus is that he was the teacher and assistant minister of King Wen and King Wu. After Zhou Xibochang escaped from Youli and returned to the country, he and Lu Shang secretly planned how to implement virtue and overthrow the rule of the Shang Dynasty. Many of them were military tactics and cunning tactics. Therefore, future generations who talked about military tactics and the secret power of the Zhou Dynasty all respected the basic strategies of the Grand Duke. Zhou Xibo was upright and peaceful. Especially after the territorial dispute between the Yu and Rui kingdoms, he was praised as King Wen who was destined to receive the destiny. Xibo also conquered Chongguo, Mixu and Quanyi, and built Fengyi on a large scale. Two-thirds of the princes in the world turned their hearts to the Zhou Dynasty, which was mostly the result of the Taigong's planning. After King Wen died, King Wu came to the throne. In the ninth year, King Wu wanted to continue to complete King Wen's great cause and campaigned eastward against Shang Zhou to see if the princes gathered to respond. When the army was leaving, Lu Shang, who was respectfully called "Master Shangfu", held a yellow ax in his left hand and a Bingbai jade in his right hand, swearing to be the master, and said: Cang Si Cang Si, command the troops, assemble the ships, and behead those who are late. So the army arrived at Mengjin. There were as many as eight hundred princes who came without being summoned. The princes all said: It is time to conquer Shang Zhou. King Wu said: Not yet. He returned as a teacher and wrote "Tai Oath" with Tai Gong. Two years later, Shang Zhou killed Prince Bigan and imprisoned Jizi. King Wu was preparing to conquer the Shang Dynasty again, and a divination revealed that the tortoise sign was unlucky, with a sudden storm coming. The ministers were frightened, and only Taigong persuaded King Wu to march, so King Wu led his troops to fight.
target: Taigong Wang, originally named Lu Shang and surnamed Jiang, was a descendant of officials who assisted Yu in flood control during ancient times. In his old age, he met Zhou Xibo (later King Wen of Zhou) while fishing on the Wei River. Xibo, having received a divination that he would find an assistant to become overlord, recognized Lu Shang as the sage his ancestors had predicted would come to Zhou. He called him "Taigong Wang" and respected him as military advisor. Some accounts say Lu Shang had previously served King Zhou of Shang but left due to his unruliness, while others claim he was a recluse recruited by Xibo's ministers to help rescue Xibo from imprisonment. Regardless of the legends, all agree he became teacher and assistant to both King Wen and King Wu. Taigong secretly planned with King Wen to implement virtue and overthrow Shang rule, employing military tactics that later generations would honor. After King Wen's death, King Wu succeeded him. In the ninth year of King Wu's reign, he campaigned eastward with Taigong as his commander, gathering eight hundred princes at Mengjin. Two years later, despite unfavorable divination and a storm, Taigong persuaded King Wu to march. They defeated Shang Zhou at Muye, and King Zhou was killed. King Wu then distributed Shang's wealth to the poor, honored loyal ministers, and established Zhou governance—all following Taigong's advice.

id: 史记/三十世家/齐太公世家::group-001
article_path: 史记/三十世家/齐太公世家
source: He moved the Jiuding, which symbolizes the highest power in the world, to the Zhou Dynasty, fixed the government affairs of the Zhou Dynasty, and started to create a new era together with the people of the world. Most of the above-mentioned matters were based on the advice of Master Shangfu. At this time, King Wu had pacified Shang Zhou and became the king of the world, so he awarded the title of Yingqiu of Qi State to his master Shangfu. Master Shangfu went east to his own feudal country, living and traveling at a very slow pace. The people in the guest house said to him: I heard that opportunities are hard to come by but easy to lose. This guest slept so peacefully, I'm afraid he didn't go to the feudal country to take up his post. After hearing this, the Grand Duke dressed up overnight and set out on the road, arriving at his own kingdom at dawn. Just when Laihou led his troops to attack, he wanted to compete with Taigong for the camp. Yingqiu is adjacent to Laiguo. The Lai people were a Yi tribe. They took advantage of the chaos of Shang and Zhou and the Zhou Dynasty had just settled down. There was no time to pacify the remote areas, so they competed with Taigong for territory. After Taigong arrived in his feudal country, he straightened political affairs, followed its customs, simplified etiquette, opened up industry and commerce, and developed the advantages of fishery and salt industry. As a result, more people joined Qi State, and Qi State became a great power. When King Cheng of Zhou came to the throne at a young age, Uncle Guan and Uncle Cai rebelled, and Huaiyi also rebelled against the Zhou Dynasty. King Cheng sent Zhao Kanggong and ordered Tai Gong to say: From the sea in the east, to the Yellow River in the west, to Muling in the south, and to Wudi in the north, the five-level princes here are guarded by local officials. If there is any crime, I order you to attack. Therefore, Qi can conquer other countries and form a great country, with its capital at Yingqiu. Taigong was already more than a hundred years old when he died, and his son Dinggong Lu Ji succeeded to the throne.
target: King Wu enfeoffed Taigong with the state of Qi at Yingqiu. When Taigong traveled slowly to his fief, a lodging house keeper warned him that opportunities are easily lost. He immediately hurried and arrived just as the Lai people attacked for the territory. Taigong governed by simplifying customs, opening commerce, and developing fishery and salt industries, making Qi a great power. King Cheng later granted Taigong authority to conquer any rebellious nobles within vast territories. Taigong died over one hundred years old.

id: 史记/三十世家/齐太公世家::group-002
article_path: 史记/三十世家/齐太公世家
source: The Lai people were a Yi tribe. They took advantage of the chaos of Shang and Zhou and the Zhou Dynasty had just settled down. There was no time to pacify the remote areas, so they competed with Taigong for territory. After Taigong arrived in his feudal country, he straightened political affairs, followed its customs, simplified etiquette, opened up industry and commerce, and developed the advantages of fishery and salt industry. As a result, more people joined Qi State, and Qi State became a great power. When King Cheng of Zhou came to the throne at a young age, Uncle Guan and Uncle Cai rebelled, and Huaiyi also rebelled against the Zhou Dynasty. King Cheng sent Zhao Kanggong and ordered Tai Gong to say: From the sea in the east, to the Yellow River in the west, to Muling in the south, and to Wudi in the north, the five-level princes here are guarded by local officials. If there is any crime, I order you to attack. Therefore, Qi can conquer other countries and form a great country, with its capital at Yingqiu. Taigong was already more than a hundred years old when he died, and his son Dinggong Lu Ji succeeded to the throne. When Ding Gong died, his son Yi Gong succeeded him. When Duke Yi died, his son Gui Gong and his loving mother succeeded him. When Duke Gui passed away, his son Aigong Buchen succeeded him. When Duke Ai was in power, the Marquis of Ji framed Duke Ai to the king of Zhou. The king of Zhou boiled Duke Ai to death in a big cauldron, and appointed Duke Ai's younger brother Jing as the king of Qi, namely Duke Hu. Duke Hu moved the capital to Bogu during the reign of King Zhou Yi. Shan, the younger brother of Duke Ai, resented Duke Hu, so he and his followers led the people from Yingqiu to attack and kill Duke Hu, and established themselves as Duke Xian of Qi. In the first year of Xian's reign, they all expelled Hu Gong's disciples and took the opportunity to move the capital from Bogu to Linzi. In the ninth year, Duke Xian died and his son, Duke Wu, succeeded him. In the ninth year of Duke Wu, King Li of Zhou fled and lived in Sheyi. Ten years later, the Zhou royal family was in chaos, and the ministers presided over the state affairs, which was known as the "Republic". In the twenty-fourth year, King Zhou Xuan ascended the throne. In the twenty-sixth year, Duke Wu died and his son Li Gong Wuji succeeded him. Duke Li was ruthless and wreaking havoc, so Duke Hu's son returned to Qi. The people of Qi wanted to make Duke Hu's son their king, so they attacked and killed Duke Li together. Hu Gong's son also died in the battle. The people of Qi then appointed Chi, the son of Duke Li, as Duke Wen of Qi. He killed more than seventy people who attacked and killed Duke Li. Duke Wen died in the 12th year, and his son Cheng Gongtu succeeded to the throne. Chenggong died in the ninth year, and his son Zhuang Gonggu succeeded to the throne. In the twenty-fourth year of Duke Zhuang, Quan Rong killed King You, and the Zhou royal family moved its capital eastward to Luoyi.
target: The succession continued through Dinggong, Yigong, Guigong, and Aigong, whom the Marquis of Ji falsely accused, leading to his execution by boiling. His brother Jing became Duke Hu but was killed by Aigong's brother Shan, who became Duke Xian and moved the capital to Linzi. Subsequent rulers included Duke Wu, Duke Li (killed by the people for his tyranny), Duke Wen, Duke Cheng, and Duke Zhuang. During Duke Zhuang's reign, the Zhou royal family moved east to Luoyi after Quan Rong killed King You.

id: 史记/三十世家/齐太公世家::group-003
article_path: 史记/三十世家/齐太公世家
source: In the fourth year, Duke Huan of Lu and his wife came to Qi. Duke Xiang of Qi had an affair with Mrs. Lu in the past. Mrs. Lu is the sister of Duke Xiang. She married Duke Huan of Lu as his wife during the reign of Duke Li of Qi. This time she came to Qi with Duke Huan of Lu and committed adultery with Duke Xiang. When Duke Huan of Lu found out about this, he scolded his wife angrily, and she told Duke Xiang of Qi. Duke Xianggang of Qi hosted a banquet for Duke Huan of Lu, got him drunk, and sent his strongman Peng Sheng to carry Duke Huan of Lu into the chariot. He then broke Duke Huan's ribs and killed Duke Huan. Duke Huan was already dead when he got out of the car. The people of Lu blamed Qi for this, and Qi Xianggong killed Peng Sheng to apologize to Lu and atone for his sins. In the eighth year, Qi State conquered Ji State, and Ji State was forced to move its capital. In the twelfth year, Duke Xiang sent Lian Cheng and Guan Zhifu to garrison in Kuiqiu. They agreed to go there when the melons ripened in July, and sent someone to replace them when the melons ripened the next year. They went to garrison for a year, but after the ripening period passed, Duke Xiang still did not send anyone to replace them. Someone asked Duke Xiang to send someone to replace them, but Duke Xiang refused. So the two were angry and planned a rebellion through Gongsun Wuwu. Lian said that he had a cousin who was not favored in the palace of Duke Xiang, so he asked her to spy on Duke Xiang secretly and said to her: "When the matter is completed, I will let you be Gongsun Wuzhi's wife."
target: Duke Li was succeeded by Duke Xiang, who had conflicts with his cousin Wuzhi and committed adultery with his sister, Lady Lu of Lu. When Duke Huan of Lu discovered this, Duke Xiang had him killed. Later, Duke Xiang was killed by Wuzhi and conspirators after failing to replace garrison troops as promised. Wuzhi was then killed by the people of Yonglin.

id: 史记/三十世家/齐太公世家::group-004
article_path: 史记/三十世家/齐太公世家
source: Bao Shuya said: I am honored to follow you, and you finally became the king. I can no longer help you improve your exalted status. If you only want to govern Qi, Gao Xi and I will be enough. If you want to become an overlord, don't worry about Yiwu. The country where Yiwu lives must be strong and cannot lose this talent. So Duke Huan listened to this. He pretended to recall Guan Zhong to take revenge, but in fact he wanted to let him rule. Guan Zhong knew it, so he asked for Qi to be returned. Bao Shuya welcomed Guan Zhong. As soon as he arrived at Tangfu in Qi State, he removed Guan Zhong's shackles and asked him to fast, bathe and see Duke Huan. Duke Huan rewarded him with generous gifts and appointed Guan Zhong as a doctor to preside over government affairs. After Duke Huan got Guan Zhong, he worked with Bao Shu, Xi Peng, and Gao Xi to manage the political affairs of Qi State, implemented the military service system with five families as the basic units, developed the advantages of commercial circulation, fishery and salt industry, used them to relieve the poor, reward the capable people, and everyone in Qi State was happy. In the second year of Duke Huan, Qi conquered and destroyed Tan, and the king of Tan fled to Ju. When Duke Huan fled in the early years, he visited the country of Tan. The king of Tan was rude to Duke Huan, so he attacked him. Five years later, the Lu army was defeated. Duke Zhuang of Lu asked for the city of Sui to be used for peace, and Duke Huan agreed to make an alliance with the Lu people in Ke. When the oath was about to be made, Cao Mo of Lu kidnapped Duke Huan of Qi with a dagger on the altar and said: "Return the occupied land of Lu!" Duke Huan agreed. Then Cao Mo threw away the dagger and returned to his seat of ministers facing north. Duke Huan regretted not returning the occupied territory of Lu and had Cao Mo killed. Guan Zhong said: If you agree to someone else's request when you are kidnapped, and then break your promise and kill someone, you are satisfied with a small pleasure, but you have lost your trust among the princes, and you have lost the support of the people in the world. You cannot do this. Duke Huan then returned all the territory that Cao Mo had lost after three defeats to Lu. When the princes heard about it, they all believed that Qi was trustworthy and were willing to surrender. In the seventh year, the princes and Duke Heng of Qi met in Zhendi for an alliance. From then on, Duke Huan of Qi became the overlord of the princes in the world. In the fourteenth year, Chen Ligong's son Chen Wan, named Jingzhong, fled to Qi. Duke Huan of Qi wanted to appoint him as a minister, but he humbly declined; so he was appointed Gongzheng in charge of hundreds of works.
target: After Duke Xiang's death, his brothers competed for the throne. Prince Xiaobai, with support from the Gao and Guo families, returned first and became Duke Huan of Qi. He initially wanted to kill Guan Zhong, but Bao Shuya convinced him that Guan Zhong was essential for becoming overlord. Duke Huan appointed Guan Zhong as minister, and together with Bao Shu, Xi Peng, and Gao Xi, they reformed Qi's government, implemented military systems, developed commerce and fisheries, and relieved the poor, bringing happiness to the people.

id: 史记/三十世家/齐太公世家::group-005
article_path: 史记/三十世家/齐太公世家
source: When the oath was about to be made, Cao Mo of Lu kidnapped Duke Huan of Qi with a dagger on the altar and said: "Return the occupied land of Lu!" Duke Huan agreed. Then Cao Mo threw away the dagger and returned to his seat of ministers facing north. Duke Huan regretted not returning the occupied territory of Lu and had Cao Mo killed. Guan Zhong said: If you agree to someone else's request when you are kidnapped, and then break your promise and kill someone, you are satisfied with a small pleasure, but you have lost your trust among the princes, and you have lost the support of the people in the world. You cannot do this. Duke Huan then returned all the territory that Cao Mo had lost after three defeats to Lu. When the princes heard about it, they all believed that Qi was trustworthy and were willing to surrender. In the seventh year, the princes and Duke Heng of Qi met in Zhendi for an alliance. From then on, Duke Huan of Qi became the overlord of the princes in the world. In the fourteenth year, Chen Ligong's son Chen Wan, named Jingzhong, fled to Qi. Duke Huan of Qi wanted to appoint him as a minister, but he humbly declined; so he was appointed Gongzheng in charge of hundreds of works. This is the ancestor of Tian Chengzi and Tian Chang. In the twenty-third year, Shan Rong invaded Yan State, and Yan asked Qi State for help. Duke Huan of Qi sent troops to rescue Yan, and then attacked Shanrong. He only returned to Guzhu after arriving at Guzhu. King Yanzhuang sent Duke Huan into the territory of Qi again. Duke Huan said: Except for the emperor, the princes cannot send each other out of their own borders. I cannot be rude to Yan. So the territory of Qi State where Yan Jun went was divided with ditches and given to Yan State, so that Yan Jun could rebuild the government of Zhao Gong and pay tribute to the Zhou royal family, just like in the days of King Cheng and King Kang of Zhou. After the princes heard about it, they all obeyed Qi. In the twenty-seventh year, Duke Min of Lu's mother was called Ai Jiang, and she was the sister of Duke Huan of Qi. Aijiang had an affair with Qingfu, the son of Lu Gong, and Qingfu killed Duke Min. Aijiang wanted to make Qingfu the king, but the Lu people instead made Duke Li. Duke Huan called Ai Jiang back to Qi and killed him. In the twenty-eighth year, Duke Wen of Wei was invaded by the Di people and asked Qi for help. The state of Qi led the princes to build a city in Chuqiu and placed the king of Wei there. In the twenty-ninth year, Duke Heng and his wife Cai Ji took a boat trip. Cai Ji was familiar with the nature of water, so she rocked the boat and jolted Duke Huan. Duke Huan was afraid and ordered her to stop, but she still did not stop. After getting off the boat, Duke Huan was angry and sent Cai Ji back to Cai State, but he did not break off the marriage. The king of Cai State was also very angry, so he married Cai Ji to someone else. After hearing this, Duke Huan became even more angry and raised troops to attack Cai Guo. Thirty years ago in the spring, Duke Huan of Qi led the princes to attack Cai State, and Cai State was defeated. Duke Huan continued to attack Chu. King Chu Cheng led his troops to meet the enemy and asked: "Why did you enter my country?" Guan Zhong replied: In the past, Duke Kang ordered me to be the first king of Taigong: "You have the right to conquer the fifth-level princes and guard the officials in various places to assist the Zhou Dynasty."
target: Duke Huan became the first overlord of the Spring and Autumn period. He kept his promise to return territory to Lu after Cao Mo's kidnapping, earning trust among princes. He rescued Yan from Shanrong, gave Yan territory, and restored Zhao Gong's governance. He defended Wei against Di invaders and built a city for them. He attacked Cai and Chu for failing to pay tribute, though he eventually made peace with Chu. He convened multiple alliances, including the famous Kuiqiu meeting, where King Xiang of Zhou rewarded him. Despite Guan Zhong's opposition, Duke Huan wanted to perform the fengshan sacrifices but eventually abandoned the idea.

id: 史记/三十世家/齐太公世家::group-006
article_path: 史记/三十世家/齐太公世家
source: After Guan Zhong fell seriously ill, Duke Huan of Qi asked him: After your death, who among the ministers can be the prime minister? Guan Zhong said: There is nothing better than a wise minister like a king. Duke Huan said: "How is Yi Ya?" He replied: He killed his own son to please the king, which is unkind and cannot be used. Duke Huan asked: "How is this person doing?" He replied: He abandoned his parents to cater to the king, which is unkind and unapproachable. Duke Huan said: "How is this man Shudao?" He replied: Castrating yourself to please the king is unkind and cannot be trusted. After Guan Zhong's death, Duke Huan did not listen to Guan Zhong's words, but still closely appointed these three people, who had exclusive power. In the forty-second year, the Rong people attacked Zhou, and Zhou asked Qi for help. Qi ordered all the princes to send troops to defend the Zhou royal family. In this year, Prince Chong'er of Jin came to Qi, and Duke Huan of Qi married his daughter to Chong'er. Forty-three years. At first, Duke Huan of Qi had three wives: Wang Ji, Xu Ji, and Cai Ji. None of them gave birth to a son. Duke Huan was lustful and had many favored concubines, among whom there were six concubines with the same status as his wives: Changwei Ji, born to Wu Gui; Shao Wei Ji, born to Hui Gong; Zheng Ji, born to Xiao Gong Zhao; Ge Ying, born to Xiao Gong Pan; Mi Ji, born to Yi Gong Shang; Song Huazi, born to Gongzi Yong. Duke Huan of Qi and Guan Zhong once entrusted Duke Xiao Gong Zhao to Duke Xiang of Song Dynasty and established him as the crown prince. Yi Ya was favored by Duke Huan's eldest son, Wei Ji, and through the eunuch Shu Diao, he gave generous gifts to Duke Huan, so he was also favored by Duke Huan. Duke Huan agreed to make Yi Ya the crown prince.
target: After Guan Zhong's death, Duke Huan ignored his advice and appointed Yi Ya, Shu Diao, and Kaifang, who seized power. Duke Huan had six favored concubines bearing sons, and after his death, his sons fought for succession.

id: 史记/三十世家/齐太公世家::group-007
article_path: 史记/三十世家/齐太公世家
source: Yi Ya was favored by Duke Huan's eldest son, Wei Ji, and through the eunuch Shu Diao, he gave generous gifts to Duke Huan, so he was also favored by Duke Huan. Duke Huan agreed to make Yi Ya the crown prince. After Guan Zhong's death, the five princes all asked to be crown princes. On the day of Yihai in the tenth month of winter, Duke Huan of Qi died. Yi Ya entered the palace, and Shu Dao killed the officials with the help of his favored ministers, and established the young master Wu Gui as the king of Qi. Prince Zhao fled to the Song Dynasty. When Duke Huan was seriously ill, the five princes each formed a party and demanded to be crowned prince. After Duke Huan died, they fought against each other, so that no one in the palace dared to bury Duke Huan in the coffin. Duke Huan's body lay on the bed for sixty-seven days, and all the maggots on the body crawled outside the door.
target: His body lay unburied for sixty-seven days, with maggots crawling outside the door. Five of his sons eventually became rulers: Wugui, Xiaogong, Zhaogong, Yigong, and Huigong.

id: 史记/三十世家/齐太公世家::group-008
article_path: 史记/三十世家/齐太公世家
source: In May of the 19th year, Duke Zhao died, and his son She was made King of Qi. She's mother was not favored by Duke Zhao, so no one in Qi was afraid of him. Duke Zhao's younger brother, Merchant, failed to become king after Duke Huan's death. He secretly befriended wise men and cared for the people, so he was very popular among the people. After the death of Duke Zhao, his son She succeeded to the throne, but he was weak. The merchants and others killed Qi Junshe in front of Zhaogong's grave in October. The merchants established themselves as kings, namely Duke Yigong. Duke Yi was the son of Duke Huan, and his mother's name was Miji. In the spring of the fourth year of Duke Yi, when he was still a son, Duke Yi and Bingrong's father hunted together and competed with each other for the prey, but Duke Yi failed to win. After he came to the throne, Duke Yi cut off Bingrong's father's foot and asked Bingrong to drive for him. Yongzhi's wife was very beautiful, so Duke Yi snatched her into the palace and made Yongzhi his companion. In the fifth month, Duke Yi was playing in Shenchi. Bingrong and Yongzhi were joking with each other while taking a bath. Yongzhi said that Bingrong was the son of the man who cut off his feet, while Bingrong said that Yongzhi was the husband who had his wife taken away from him. Both of them were ashamed of these words and hated Duke Yi together. So the two of them planned for Yi Gong to go to the bamboo forest to play. They killed Yi Gong in the car, threw the body in the bamboo forest and escaped. After Yigong came to the throne, he became arrogant and arrogant, and the people did not join him. The people of Qi deposed the son of Duke Yi and welcomed the prince Yuan from Wei to return to Qi. He made him the king of the country, namely Duke Hui. Duke Hui was the son of Duke Huan. His mother was a daughter of Wei State named Shao Wei Ji. She fled to Wei State to avoid civil strife in Qi. In the second year of Duke Hui, Chang Zhai came to Qi. Prince Chengfu attacked and killed Chang Zhai and buried him at the north gate. Zhao Chuan, the official of Jin State, killed the king of Jin Linggong. In ten years, Duke Hui died, and his son Qinggong Wuye succeeded him. At first, Cui Zhu was favored by Duke Hui. After Hui Gong's death, the Gao family and the Guo family were afraid of being coerced by him, so they expelled Cui Zhu from the country, and Cui Zhu fled to Weiguo. In the first year of Qing AD, King Zhuang of Chu became stronger and conquered the State of Chen. In the second year, the State of Chu besieged the State of Zheng. Zheng Bo surrendered and soon restored Zheng Bo. In the spring of the sixth year, the state of Jin sent Choke as envoy to the state of Qi. Qi Qinggong asked his mother to sit behind the curtain and watch. When Choke went up the stairs, his wife saw that he was hunchbacked and laughed at him.
target: The state experienced continued turmoil through various rulers. Duke Yi was killed by Bingrong and Yongzhi after mutilating them. Duke Hui was established after Yigong's death. Duke Qing faced invasion from Jin after his mother laughed at Jin envoy Chuke. Duke Zhuang was killed by Cui Zhu for adultery with his wife. Cui Zhu and Qingfeng then controlled the government until the Tian family rose to power.

id: 史记/三十世家/齐太公世家::group-009
article_path: 史记/三十世家/齐太公世家
source: Who among us with the surname Tian cannot be the patriarch of the Tian family? If you cowardly run away without caring about everyone, my ancestors will not spare you unless I kill you. Tian Changcai stayed. The supervisor ran home and gathered his disciples to attack all the gates of the palace, but without success, he fled. The Tian clan members were in hot pursuit. Someone in Fengqiu caught Jianzhi and reported it, and Tian killed Jianzhi at Guomen. Tian Chang wanted to kill Dalu Zifang, but Tian Ni interceded for him and was pardoned. In the name of Mr. Jian, he stopped the car on the road and drove out of Yongmen. Tian Bao gave him the car, but he didn't want it, saying: "Tian Ni interceded for me. If Tian Bao gave me the car, people would think that I have a personal relationship with Mr. Tian." I am a retainer who is in charge of prison, but I have secretly colluded with his enemies. How can I run away to meet the scholars of Lu and Wei? On Gengchen day, Tian Chang arrested Duke Jian in Chuzhou. Duke Jian said: If I had listened to Tian Yang's words earlier, I would not be in the situation I am today. On the day of Jiawu, Tian Chang killed Duke Jian in Chuzhou. Tian Chang appointed Ao, the younger brother of Duke Jian, as Lord of Qi, which was called Duke Ping. After Ping Gong came to the throne, Tian Chang became the prime minister, specializing in the power of Qi State, and divided the vast land east of Anping of Qi State into the territory of the Tian family. In the eighth year of Ping Gong's reign, the State of Yue destroyed the State of Wu. In the twenty-fifth year of the reign of Emperor Pinggong, his son Xuan Gongji succeeded him. In the fifty-first year of Xuangong's reign, Xuangong died and his son Kang Gongdai succeeded to the throne. Tian Hui rebelled in Linqiu. In the second year of Kanggong's reign, Han, Zhao and Wei began to become princes. In the 19th year, Tian Chang's great-grandson Tian He began to become a prince and exiled Kang Gong to the seaside. In the twenty-sixth year, Duke Kang passed away, and the Lu family stopped offering sacrifices. The Tian family finally took possession of the Qi State, and when King Qi Wei was king, he became the lord of the world. Tai Shigong said: When I arrived in Qi, I saw that the land of Qi starts from Mount Tai in the west, connects Langye in the east, and reaches the sea in the north. There are two thousand miles of fertile land in between. Its people are broad-minded and deep and wise. This is their nature. Because of Taigong's sage, he established the foundation of the country, and because of Huangong's virtue, he implemented good governance, so he summoned the princes to form an alliance and became the overlord. Isn't it logical?
target: Tian Chang eventually killed Duke Jian and established Duke Ping, becoming prime minister and dividing Qi's territory for the Tian family. The Tian family ultimately took full possession of Qi, and when Tian He became a prince, the state continued under the Tian clan until King Wei of Qi ruled as a hegemon. Sima Qian observed that Qi's fertile land and broad-minded people, combined with Taigong's foundation and Duke Huan's virtuous governance, naturally led to its position as overlord among the princes.

id: 史记/三十世家/齐悼惠王世家::group-000
article_path: 史记/三十世家/齐悼惠王世家
source: Liu Fei, King Hui of Qi Dynasty, was the eldest son of Emperor Gaozu. His mother was Gaozu's former mistress, whose surname was Cao. Six years ago, Emperor Gaozu granted Liu Fei the title of King of Qi and granted him seventy cities. All people who spoke the Qi language belonged to the King of Qi. King Qi is the elder brother of Emperor Xiaohui. In the second year of Emperor Xiaohui's reign, King Liu went to Beijing to see the emperor. Emperor Hui and the King of Qi had a banquet, and the two treated each other with the same etiquette as family members and brothers. Empress Dowager Lu was angry about this and wanted to kill King Qi. The King of Qi was afraid that he would not be able to avoid disaster, so he adopted the strategy of his internal historian Xun and donated Chengyang County as Tang Muyi to Princess Lu Yuan. Empress Dowager Lu was very happy, and King Qi was able to resign and return to Qi. Thirteen years after King Hui ascended the throne, he died in the sixth year of Emperor Hui. His son Liu Xiang came to the throne and became King Ai. In the first year of King Ai, Emperor Xiaohui passed away, and Empress Dowager Lu began to take charge of the government. All affairs in the world were decided by Empress Lu. In the second year, Empress Gao conferred the title of King Lu on her brother's son Lihou Lutai, and set up Jinan County in Qi State as the fiefdom of King Lu. In the third year of King Ai's reign, his younger brother Liu Zhang entered the Han Palace for guard duty. Empress Dowager Lu named him Zhu Xuhou and married Lu Lu's daughter to him.
target: Liu Fei, King Hui of Qi, was Emperor Gaozu's eldest son, granted the title of King of Qi with seventy cities. In the second year of Emperor Xiaohui's reign, he visited the capital and dined with the emperor as equals, angering Empress Dowager Lu, who sought to kill him. Following his internal historian Xun's advice, he donated Chengyang County to Princess Lu Yuan, appeasing the empress dowager and allowing his safe return to Qi. He died thirteen years into his reign, succeeded by his son Liu Xiang, King Ai.

id: 史记/三十世家/齐悼惠王世家::group-001
article_path: 史记/三十世家/齐悼惠王世家
source: Thirteen years after King Hui ascended the throne, he died in the sixth year of Emperor Hui. His son Liu Xiang came to the throne and became King Ai. In the first year of King Ai, Emperor Xiaohui passed away, and Empress Dowager Lu began to take charge of the government. All affairs in the world were decided by Empress Lu. In the second year, Empress Gao conferred the title of King Lu on her brother's son Lihou Lutai, and set up Jinan County in Qi State as the fiefdom of King Lu. In the third year of King Ai's reign, his younger brother Liu Zhang entered the Han Palace for guard duty. Empress Dowager Lu named him Zhu Xuhou and married Lu Lu's daughter to him. Four years later, Empress Dowager Lu granted Liu Zhang's younger brother Xingju the title of Marquis of Dongmou, and both of them served as guards in Chang'an Palace. In the eighth year of King Ai's reign, Empress Gao divided Langxie County of Qi State and named Liu Ze, Marquis of Yingling, as King Langxie. The next year, King Zhao Liuyou entered the court and was imprisoned in his mansion and died. The three Zhao kings were deposed one after another. After Gao, the descendants of the Lu family were granted the title of King of Yan, King of Zhao, and King of Liang, and they monopolized power and arbitrarily ruled the government. When Zhu Xuhou Liu Zhang was twenty years old, he was a man of great courage and bravery. He was angry because the Liu family could not get a position. He once served the banquet of the Queen of Gao, who ordered Zhu Xuhou and Liu Zhang to serve as wine stewards. Liu Zhang personally requested: "I am a descendant of a military general. Please allow me to supervise the behavior at the banquet in accordance with military law." Empress Gao said: Yes. When the wine was in full swing, Liu Zhang performed songs and dances to add to the fun. Then he said: Please let me sing a plowing song for the Queen Mother. The queen treated him as a child and said with a smile: "I think your father knows about farming. You were born as a prince, how could you know about farming?" Liu Zhang said: I know. The Queen Mother said: "Try to tell me about farming." Liu Zhang said: If you plow deeply and plant densely, you will leave sparse seedlings. They are not the same kind, so you must shovel and hoe them resolutely. Queen Lu was silent after hearing this. After a while, one of the Lu clan members got drunk and ran away from the banquet. Liu Zhang chased him, drew his sword and beheaded him. Then he came back and reported: "There is a man who escaped from the banquet. I would like to kill him according to military law." The Queen Mother and her officials were greatly surprised. Since he had been allowed to act in accordance with military law, he could not be punished. The banquet also ended. From then on, everyone in the Lu family was afraid of Zhu Xuhou, and even the ministers obeyed Zhu Xuhou. Liu's momentum gradually became stronger again. The next year, Queen Gao died. King Lu Lu of Zhao was appointed as the general, and King Lu Chan was appointed as the prime minister. Both of them lived in Chang'an City. They gathered troops to threaten the ministers and wanted to launch a rebellion. Because his wife was Lu Lu's daughter, Zhu Xuhou Liu Zhang knew about their plot, so he sent someone to sneak out of Chang'an to report to his brother King Qi, hoping that he would send troops to the west. Zhu Xuhou and Dongmuhou acted as internal correspondents in order to kill the Lu clan and take the opportunity to make King Qi the emperor.
target: During King Ai's reign, Empress Dowager Lu took control, appointing Lu family members as kings and dividing Qi's territories. Liu Zhang, Marquis of Zhuxu and King Ai's younger brother, boldly challenged the Lu clan's power. At a banquet, he used a farming song to criticize their rule and later executed a drunken Lu clan member under military law, instilling fear in the Lu family and reviving Liu clan influence. After Empress Dowager Lu's death, Lu Lu and Lu Chan plotted rebellion. Liu Zhang, aware of their plans, urged his brother King Qi to raise troops westward while he and Dongmou Hou served as internal allies. King Qi mobilized forces, detaining King Langxie to command his troops, and sent letters to princes condemning the Lu clan's usurpation. However, General Guan Ying, sent to intercept Qi, halted at Xingyang and allied with Qi instead.

id: 史记/三十世家/齐悼惠王世家::group-002
article_path: 史记/三十世家/齐悼惠王世家
source: When the court heard that the King of Qi was sending troops to march westward, Prime Minister Lu Chan sent General Guan Ying to lead his troops eastward to intercept the Qi troops. When Guan Ying arrived at Xingyang, he thought in his mind: Zhu Lu led his troops to gather in Guanzhong, intending to harm the Liu family and establish himself as emperor. If I defeat Qi and return to the DPRK to report victory, it will be equivalent to increasing the capital of the Lu family. So he ordered the army to stop and garrison in Xingyang, and sent envoys to inform the king of Qi and the princes that they were willing to unite with each other and wait for Lu's rebellion to be executed together. After the King of Qi heard about this, he marched westward to recapture their hometown of Jinan County, and stationed troops on the western border of Qi State to wait for the fulfillment of the alliance. Lu Lu and Lu Chan wanted to rebel in Guanzhong. Zhu Xuhou Liu Zhang, Taiwei Zhou Bo, and Prime Minister Chen Ping killed them. Zhu Xuhou first beheaded Lu Chan, and then Taiwei Zhou Bo and others were able to kill all the Lu clan members. King Langxie also happened to come to Chang'an from Qi. The ministers discussed letting King Qi succeed the emperor, but King Langxie and some ministers said: King Qi's mother-uncle Sijun is ferocious and cruel, like a tiger wearing a hat. We almost caused chaos in the world just now because of the Lu family, and now we want to establish the King of Qi because we want another Lu family to appear. Dai Wang's mother's family, the Bo family, is upright and loyal. Moreover, Dai Wang is the biological son of Emperor Gao. He is still alive and is the eldest. From the perspective of parents and children, it is justified; from the perspective of a kind family, ministers will feel relieved. So the ministers planned to welcome the king as the emperor, and sent Zhu Xuhou to tell the King of Qi that Zhu Lu had been killed and asked him to withdraw his troops. Guan Ying was in Xingyang. He heard that Wei Bo originally instigated the rebellion of the King of Qi. After the Lu family was killed, Qi also withdrew its troops. Guan Ying sent someone to summon Wei Bo to question him. Wei Bo said: When there is a fire in a house, where do you have time to tell your parents first and then go to put out the fire? After saying that, he stood aside, his legs trembling, as if he was too frightened to speak, and he didn't say anything else until the end. General Guan looked at him for a long time and said with a smile: People say that Wei Bo is brave, but in fact he is just a mediocre and incompetent man. How can he accomplish anything? So he was removed from his post but not punished. Wei Bo's father met Emperor Qin because he was good at playing the piano. When Wei Bo was young, he wanted to meet Cao Shen, the Prime Minister of Qi. Since his family was poor and he did not have the financial resources to smooth things over in person, he often went to clean the door of Prime Minister Qi's attendants alone in the middle of the night. The attendant was very strange and thought it was some kind of monster, so he waited secretly and finally caught Wei Bo. Wei Bo said: I want to see the Prime Minister, but there is no way, so I came to clean up for you in order to ask for an audience. So this attendant led Wei Bo to visit Cao Shen, and Cao Shen asked him to become an attendant. Once he was driving for Cao Shen and asked for his opinions on some matters. Cao Shen thought he was talented and recommended him to King Qi Huihui.
target: Liu Zhang, along with Taiwei Zhou Bo and Prime Minister Chen Ping, killed Lu Chan and Lu Lu in Guanzhong, ending the Lu clan's threat. The ministers debated succession; King Langxie and others opposed King Qi due to his cruel maternal uncle, Sijun, and instead chose Dai Wang, Emperor Gaozu's son with the virtuous Bo family, as Emperor Xiaowen. King Qi withdrew his troops. Wei Bo, who had instigated Qi's rebellion, was spared but dismissed after Guan Ying deemed him incompetent. Wei Bo's background included serving Cao Shen, who recommended him to King Huihui.

id: 史记/三十世家/齐悼惠王世家::group-003
article_path: 史记/三十世家/齐悼惠王世家
source: Wei Bo said: I want to see the Prime Minister, but there is no way, so I came to clean up for you in order to ask for an audience. So this attendant led Wei Bo to visit Cao Shen, and Cao Shen asked him to become an attendant. Once he was driving for Cao Shen and asked for his opinions on some matters. Cao Shen thought he was talented and recommended him to King Qi Huihui. King Huihui summoned Wei Bo and appointed him as internal history. At first, King Huihui had the right to appoint officials with a salary of two thousand stone. After King Ai Hui passed away and King Ai Hui came to the throne, Wei Bo was arbitrary in political affairs and had more power than Qi Prime Minister. After King Qi withdrew his troops and returned to his country, Dai Wang came to Chang'an and took the throne as emperor. This was Emperor Xiaowen. In the first year of Emperor Xiaowen's reign, Chengyang, Langye and Jinan counties, which were separated from Qi during the reign of Emperor Gao, were all returned to Qi. King Langye was renamed King of Yan, and Marquis Zhuxu and Marquis Dongmou were granted the title of 2,000 households each. In this year, King Ai of Qi died, and Prince Liu Ze came to the throne. This was King Wen of Qi. In the first year of King Wen of Qi, the imperial court granted the Chengyang County of Qi to Zhu Xuhou Liu Zhang, making him King of Chengyang; and the Jibei County of Qi to Dongmou Liu Xingju, making him the King of Jibei. In the second year of King Wen of Qi, King Jibei rebelled, and the imperial court sent troops to kill him, and his fiefdom was returned to the imperial court. Two years later, Emperor Xiaowen conferred the title of marquis on seven people, including King Qi Hui's son Ba Pí Jun. King Wen of Qi died fourteen years after he took the throne. He had no sons, the title of his country was abolished, and the fiefdom was transferred to the imperial court. A year later, Emperor Xiaowen divided the land of Qi and made several sons of King Hui Hui originally named kings. General Lu of King Xiao of Qi was promoted to King of Qi as Yang Xuhou, the son of King Hui Hui. It turned out that all other counties in the Qi State were entrusted to the sons of King Huihui as kings: Liu Zhi was the King of Jibei, Liu Biguang was the King of Jinan, Liu Xian was the King of Sichuan, Liu Xian was the King of Jiaoxi, Liu Xiongqu was the King of Jiaodong, and together with the King of Chengyang and the King of Qi, they were seven kings in total.
target: In Emperor Xiaowen's first year, Qi regained Chengyang, Langye, and Jinan counties. Liu Zhang was made King of Chengyang, and Liu Xingju King of Jibei. King Ai of Qi died, succeeded by his son Liu Ze, King Wen. King Wen died without heirs, and his territory reverted to the court. Emperor Xiaowen then divided Qi among King Huihui's sons: Liu Zhi as King of Jibei, Liu Biguang as King of Jinan, Liu Xian as King of Sichuan, Liu Xian as King of Jiaoxi, Liu Xiongqu as King of Jiaodong, alongside the King of Chengyang and King of Qi, totaling seven kings.

id: 史记/三十世家/齐悼惠王世家::group-004
article_path: 史记/三十世家/齐悼惠王世家
source: King Wen of Qi died fourteen years after he took the throne. He had no sons, the title of his country was abolished, and the fiefdom was transferred to the imperial court. A year later, Emperor Xiaowen divided the land of Qi and made several sons of King Hui Hui originally named kings. General Lu of King Xiao of Qi was promoted to King of Qi as Yang Xuhou, the son of King Hui Hui. It turned out that all other counties in the Qi State were entrusted to the sons of King Huihui as kings: Liu Zhi was the King of Jibei, Liu Biguang was the King of Jinan, Liu Xian was the King of Sichuan, Liu Xian was the King of Jiaoxi, Liu Xiongqu was the King of Jiaodong, and together with the King of Chengyang and the King of Qi, they were seven kings in total. In the eleventh year of King Xiao of Qi, King Liu Bi of Wu and King Liu Wu of Chu rebelled. They raised their troops and marched westward, telling the princes: We are going to kill the traitor Chao Cuo of the Han Dynasty to stabilize the country. The kings of Jiaoxi, Jiaodong, Sichuan, and Jinan all sent troops without authorization in response to the actions of the kings of Wu and Chu. They also wanted to unite with Qi State, but King Xiao of Qi was hesitant and always defended the city and did not listen to them. The armies of the three countries jointly surrounded Qi. The King of Qi sent Dr. Lu Zhong to report to the emperor, and the Emperor asked Dr. Lu Zhong to go back and tell the King of Qi: "Hold on, the troops I sent have now defeated Wu and Chu." On the way, the doctor returned to Qi State. The armies of the Three Kingdoms surrounded Linzi heavily, and the doctors on the road were unable to enter the city. The generals of the Three Kingdoms kidnapped the doctor in Luzhong and made an alliance with him, saying: You turn around and say that the Han court has been breached, and Qi should surrender to the Three Kingdoms as soon as possible, otherwise it will be massacred. The doctor on the way had no choice but to agree to them, and when he came to the city, he saw the King of Qi from a distance and said: The imperial court has sent millions of troops, and sent Lieutenant Zhou Yafu to defeat the Wu Chu rebels. He is leading troops to rescue Qi State. Qi State must hold on and not surrender!
target: In King Xiao of Qi's eleventh year, the Rebellion of the Seven Kingdoms erupted, with Wu and Chu leading the revolt. Kings of Jiaoxi, Jiaodong, Sichuan, and Jinan joined, besieging Qi. King Xiao hesitated but defended the city. Dr. Lu Zhong, sent to the emperor, returned with orders to hold out, but was captured by the rebels.

id: 史记/三十世家/齐悼惠王世家::group-005
article_path: 史记/三十世家/齐悼惠王世家
source: The doctor on the way had no choice but to agree to them, and when he came to the city, he saw the King of Qi from a distance and said: The imperial court has sent millions of troops, and sent Lieutenant Zhou Yafu to defeat the Wu Chu rebels. He is leading troops to rescue Qi State. Qi State must hold on and not surrender! The generals of the Three Kingdoms killed the doctor on the road. When the state of Qi was first besieged and reached a critical stage, it secretly contacted the three kingdoms. The alliance had not yet been concluded. Just when they heard that Dr. Lu Zhong had returned from the court, the king of Qi was very happy, and the ministers once again advised the king of Qi not to surrender to the three kingdoms. Soon after, the troops led by Han generals Luan Shi and Pingyang Hou Caoqi came to Qi State, defeated the armies of the three countries, and lifted the siege of Qi State. Soon, the emperor heard that Qi had conspired with the Three Kingdoms at first, and wanted to move troops to attack Qi. King Xiao of Qi was afraid and committed suicide by taking poison. After Emperor Jing heard about it, he thought that Qi was the best. It was not his fault that he conspired with the Three Kingdoms because he was threatened by persecution. So Liu Shou, the prince of King Xiao, was made King of Qi. This was King Yi, who continued the descendants of King Qi. The King of Jiaoxi, King of Jiaodong, King of Jinan and King of Sichuan were all executed, and their territories were all assigned to the Han court. Moved the King of Jibei to Suichuan and became the king. In the twenty-second year of King Qi Yi's reign, his son Cijing came to the throne. This was King Li. King Qi Li, his mother is Queen Mother Ji. The Queen Mother married her brother Ji's daughter to King Li as his queen. King Li did not like Ji's daughter. The Queen Mother wanted the Ji family to be favored for generations to come, so she let her eldest daughter Ji Wengzhu enter the palace to straighten out the order in the harem and not allow the maids to approach King Qi. She wanted King Li to like Ji's daughter. King Li took the opportunity to commit adultery with his sister Wengzhu. There was a eunuch named Xu Jia from the State of Qi who entered the court to serve the Empress Dowager of Han Dynasty. The Empress Dowager has a beloved daughter, whose title is Xiuchengjun. Xiuchengjun is not from the Liu family, but the Empress Dowager loves her. Xiuchengjun had a daughter named E, and the Queen Mother wanted to marry her off to the princes. The eunuch Xu Jia asked to be sent to Qi as an envoy, saying that he would let the King of Qi write a letter asking for E to be his queen. The Queen Mother was very happy and sent Xu Jia to Qi State. At that time, the leader of the Qi State, Fu Yan, knew that Xu Jia was on a mission to the State of Qi to marry the queen. He also took the opportunity to say to Xu Jia: If the matter succeeds, I hope you can tell the boss that my daughter is willing to serve in the Queen of Qi's harem. After Xu Jia arrived in Qi State, he first spread the matter secretly. When the Queen Mother Ji heard this, she was furious and said, "The King of Qi already has a queen, and all the concubines in the harem are ready." Moreover, Xu Jia was originally a poor man from Qi State. He became an eunuch after he was extremely poor. He entered the court to serve the Han Palace. He did not get any benefits. He also wanted to disturb our royal family of Qi State! As for who the master father Yan is? He actually wants his daughter to enter the harem! Xu Jia was very embarrassed and returned to the court to report to the Empress Dowager: King Qi is willing to marry E as his queen, but there is a problem, maybe like King Yan. The King of Yan had just been sentenced to death for committing adultery with his daughters and sisters, and the feudal country was destroyed, so Xu Jia deliberately used the story of King Yan to offend the Queen Mother. The Queen Mother said: "Don't talk about marrying your granddaughter to Qi anymore." The matter gradually spread to the emperor's ears. From then on, the master father Yan also had a gap with the King of Qi.
target: He falsely reported the Han court's defeat to the city but secretly urged resistance, leading to his execution. Qi held until Han forces under Luan Bu and Cao Qi defeated the rebels and lifted the siege. Suspected of collusion, King Xiao committed suicide, but Emperor Jing later cleared his name, making his son Liu Shou King Yi of Qi. The rebel kings were executed, and their territories annexed. King Yi reigned for twenty-two years, succeeded by his son Liu Ci, King Li. King Li's mother, Queen Mother Ji, arranged his marriage to her niece, but he disliked her. She then had her daughter Wengzhu oversee the harem, leading to an incestuous relationship. Eunuch Xu Jia, sent by Empress Dowager to propose a marriage for her granddaughter E, was rebuffed by Queen Mother Ji. Xu Jia later slandered Qi, comparing it to the fallen King of Yan. Master Father Yan, favored by the emperor, accused Qi of rebellion and incest, becoming prime minister to investigate.

After Master Yan came to Qi State, he stepped up the interrogation of the eunuchs in Queen Qi's harem who helped King Qi reach the residence of his sister Wengzhu, and ordered them to implicat King Qi in their confessions and circumstantial evidence. source: Gongsun Hong said: The king of Qi died of melancholy and had no descendants. The land has been transferred to the imperial court. It is impossible to eliminate the resentment of the people of the world without killing the master father Yan. Finally, he killed his father Yan. King Qi Li died in the fifth year of his reign and had no descendants. The fiefdom was transferred to the Han Dynasty. The descendants of King Hui of Qi also owned two countries, namely Chengyang and Suichuan. The land of Fengchuan is close to the state of Qi. The emperor took pity on the State of Qi, and because the cemetery of King Hui Hui was in the county town, he assigned all the cities east of Linzi surrounding the cemetery of King Hui Hui to the State of Sichuan in order to worship King Hui Hui. Liu Zhang, King of Chengyang Jing, was the son of King Hui Hui. He relied on his status as Zhu Xuhou and his ministers to kill Zhu Lu, and Liu Zhang personally beheaded the property of King Lu of the Prime Minister in Weiyang Palace. After Emperor Xiaowen came to the throne, he granted Liu Zhang the title of 2,000 households in his territory and rewarded him with a thousand catties of gold.
target: King Hui of Qi's descendants also ruled Chengyang and Suichuan. Liu Zhang, King of Chengyang Jing, was rewarded for killing Lu Chan.
