source: Thirteen years later, in the sixteenth year of Emperor Wen's reign, he granted the title of King of Jibei to Anduhou Liu Zhi, the son of King Hui Hui of Qi. Eleven years later, when Wu and Chu rebelled, Liu Zhi always stood firm in the city and did not conspire with the princes of the seven countries to cause rebellion. After the Wu and Chu rebellions were put down, the emperor changed the title of Liu Zhi to King Sichuan. Jinan King Liu Biguang, the son of King Qi Hui, was named King of Jinan in the 16th year of Emperor Xiaowen's reign as a Lehou. Eleven years later, he rebelled with the kings of Wu and Chu. The Han army defeated the rebels, killed Liu Piguang, made Jinan a county, and transferred the fiefdom to the Han court. Liu Xian, King of Sichuan, was the son of King Hui of Qi. In the 16th year of Emperor Wen's reign, he was named King of Sichuan by Wucheng Hou Jin. Eleven years later, he rebelled with the kings of Wu and Chu. The Han army defeated the rebels and killed Liu Xian. The emperor therefore moved and granted the title of King of Jibei, Liu Zhi, as King of Sichuan. Liu Zhi was also the son of King Qi Hui, and the emperor named him King of Jibei from the Marquis of Andu. Liu Xian, the king of Sichuan, rebelled and had no descendants, so he changed the title of King Jibei to King Sichuan. King Sichuan died after reigning for thirty-five years, and his posthumous title was King Yi. His son Liu Jian succeeded to the throne and became King Jing. King Jing died after reigning for twenty years, and his son Liu Yi succeeded to the throne. He was King Qing. King Qing died in his thirty-sixth year, and his son Liu Zhonggu came to the throne. This was King Si. King Si died in the twenty-eighth year of his reign, and his son Liu Shang came to the throne. This was King Xiao. King Xiao died in the fifth year of his reign, and his son Liu Heng ascended the throne. He died in the eleventh year of his reign in the third year of Jianshi. King Liu Xing of Jiaoxi was the son of King Hui of Qi. In the 16th year of Emperor Wen's reign, he was granted the title of King of Jiaoxi by the Marquis of Changping. Eleven years later, he rebelled with the kings of Wu and Chu. The Han army defeated the rebels and killed Liu Xian. The fiefdom was transferred to the Han court and renamed Jiaoxi County. Liu Xiongqu, King of Jiaodong, was the son of King Qi Mouhui. In the 16th year of Emperor Wen's reign, he was granted the title of King of Jiaodong by the Marquis of Baishi. Eleven years later, he rebelled with the kings of Wu and Chu. The Han army defeated the rebels and killed Xiongqu. The fiefdom was transferred to the Han court and changed to Jiaodong County. Tai Shigong said: Among the princes, no one in the great country surpasses King Qi Yuhui. Since the world had just been pacified and the Liu family had fewer children, the emperor of the Han Dynasty felt that the Qin Dynasty did not grant large-scale land to clan members, so he enfeoffed people with the same surname in large numbers to calm the hearts of the people. It was only natural that it was later split into several countries.
target: His lineage continued through several generations. Liu Xingju, King of Jibei, rebelled after feeling slighted by Emperor Wen, who reduced his promised territory. He was defeated and committed suicide. Later, Liu Zhi, King of Jibei, remained loyal during the Seven Kingdoms Rebellion and was renamed King of Sichuan. Other sons of King Huihui—Liu Biguang, Liu Xian, Liu Xian, and Liu Xiongqu—were made kings but rebelled and were killed, their territories becoming counties. Sima Qian noted that King Hui of Qi's domain was the largest among princes, initially granted to stabilize the realm after the Qin dynasty's failure to support clan members, though it was later divided.

id: 史记/十二本纪/五帝本纪::group-000
article_path: 史记/十二本纪/五帝本纪
source: Huangdi is a descendant of the Shaodian tribe, and his surname is Gongsun and Xuanyuan. He was born with great spirituality. He was good at speaking at a very young age. He was clever and alert as a child. He was honest and agile when he grew up. He was wise and judicious as an adult. When Xuanyuan was in power, the descendants of the Shennong clan had declined. The princes fought against each other and abused the people with violence, but the Shennong clan had no power to conquer them. So Xuanyuan practiced military training and went to conquer those princes who did not come to pay tribute. Only then did all the princes come to submit. Chiyou was the most violent among the princes, and no one could conquer him. Emperor Yan wanted to attack and oppress the princes, and all the princes came to Xuanyuan. So Xuanyuan practiced virtue, rectified his army, studied the changes in the four seasons, planted grains, appeased the people, measured the land in all directions, trained bears, 罴, 貔, 貅, 貲, tigers and other beasts, and fought with Emperor Yan in the countryside of Banquan. After several battles, he conquered Emperor Yan and won as he wished. Chiyou launched a rebellion and refused to obey Huangdi's orders. So Huang Di mobilized the troops of the princes and fought with Chi You in the suburbs of Zhuolu, and finally captured and killed him. In this way, the princes all respected Xuanyuan as the emperor, replacing Shennong. This was the Yellow Emperor. When there were disobedient people in the world, the Yellow Emperor went to conquer them. After pacifying a place, he left, splitting mountains and clearing roads along the way, and never lived in peace anywhere. Huang Di went east to the East China Sea and climbed Mount Maru and Mount Tai. Went west to Kongtong and climbed to Jitou Mountain. Went south to the Yangtze River and climbed Xiong Mountain and Xiang Mountain. He expelled the Hunzhou tribe to the north, came to Busan, signed the talisman contract with the princes, and built a city at the foot of Zhulu Mountain. The Yellow Emperor moved around and had no fixed residence. Wherever he led his troops, he set up military camps for self-defense.
target: Huangdi (Yellow Emperor), a descendant of the Shaodian tribe with the surname Gongsun and name Xuanyuan, displayed remarkable intelligence from birth. During his rise to power, the Shennong clan had declined, and princes were fighting violently. Xuanyuan trained his army, conquered rebellious princes, and eventually all submitted except the violent Chiyou. After Emperor Yan attacked the princes, they turned to Xuanyuan, who cultivated virtue, organized his forces, and defeated Emperor Yan at Banquan. He later captured and killed Chiyou at Zhuolu, after which the princes recognized him as emperor, replacing Shennong. The Yellow Emperor traveled extensively—east to Mount Tai, west to Kongtong, south to the Yangtze River, and north驱逐 the Hunzhou tribe. He had no fixed residence, establishing military camps wherever he went.

id: 史记/十二本纪/五帝本纪::group-001
article_path: 史记/十二本纪/五帝本纪
source: Went west to Kongtong and climbed to Jitou Mountain. Went south to the Yangtze River and climbed Xiong Mountain and Xiang Mountain. He expelled the Hunzhou tribe to the north, came to Busan, signed the talisman contract with the princes, and built a city at the foot of Zhulu Mountain. The Yellow Emperor moved around and had no fixed residence. Wherever he led his troops, he set up military camps for self-defense. All the official positions granted by the Yellow Emperor were named after Yun, and the army was called Yunshi. He set up left and right supervisors to supervise the various vassal states. At this time, all countries were in peace, so since ancient times, the number of people offering sacrifices to ghosts and gods in mountains and rivers was the highest during the Yellow Emperor's time. The Yellow Emperor received the tripod given by God, so he observed the movement of the sun, used yarrow for divination to calculate the calendar, and predicted the solar terms and dates. He appointed Fenghou, Limu, Changxian, Dahong and others to govern the people. The Yellow Emperor complied with the laws of the four seasons of heaven and earth, speculated on the changes of yin and yang, explained the principles of life and death, and discussed the causes of existence and death. He sown grains and grasses according to the seasons, domesticated birds, beasts, and silkworms, measured the sun, moon and stars to determine the calendar, collected earth, stone, gold, and jade for civilian use. When he was the emperor, he had the auspicious sign of the attribute of earth. The earth was yellow in color, so he was called the Yellow Emperor. Huangdi had twenty-five sons, fourteen of whom established their own surnames. The Yellow Emperor lived in Xuanyuan Mountain and married a daughter of the Xiling Kingdom, who was Leizu. Leizu was the Yellow Emperor's concubine and had two sons. Their descendants all ruled the world: one was named Xuanxiao, also known as Qingyang. Qingyang was named a prince and settled in Jiangshui; the other was named Changyi, who was also named a prince and settled in Ruoshui. Changyi married a daughter of the Shushan clan, named Changpu, and gave birth to Gao Yang, who had the character of a saint. After the death of Huangdi, he was buried in Qiaoshan. His grandson, Changyi's son Gaoyang, ascended the throne and became Emperor Zhuanxu. Emperor Zhuanxu Gaoyang was the grandson of Huangdi and the son of Changyi.
target: He appointed officials named after clouds, created supervisory positions, and received a divine tripod for calendar-making. He observed celestial movements, calculated seasons, and appointed ministers to govern. Following the laws of heaven and earth, he studied yin and yang, explained life and death, cultivated grains, domesticated animals, and collected resources for public use. Because of the earth attribute's auspicious sign, he was called the Yellow Emperor. He had twenty-five sons, fourteen of whom established surnames. After his death, his grandson Gaoyang ascended as Emperor Zhuanxu.

id: 史记/十二本纪/五帝本纪::group-002
article_path: 史记/十二本纪/五帝本纪
source: Emperor Zhuanxu Gaoyang was the grandson of Huangdi and the son of Changyi. He is calm, steady, resourceful, and knowledgeable. He raised various crops and livestock to make full use of the soil, calculated the four seasons to conform to nature, followed the ghosts and gods to formulate etiquette and justice, straightened out the energy of the four seasons and the five elements to educate the people, and purified the body and mind to sacrifice to the ghosts and gods. He went north to Youling, south to Jiaozhi, west to Liusha, and east to Panmu. All kinds of animals and plants, big gods and small gods, wherever the sun and moon shine, are all pacified, and there is no one who does not submit.
target: Emperor Zhuanxu Gaoyang was calm, resourceful, and knowledgeable. He cultivated crops, calculated seasons, followed ghosts and gods to establish rituals, and educated the people. His domain extended north to Youling, south to Jiaozhi, west to Liusha, and east to Panmu, pacifying all creatures.

source: All kinds of animals and plants, big gods and small gods, wherever the sun and moon shine, are all pacified, and there is no one who does not submit. The son born to Emperor Zhuanxu was called Qiongchan. After Zhuan Xu's death, Xuan Xiao's grandson Gao Xin came to the throne and became Emperor Ku. Emperor Ku Gaoxin was the great-grandson of the Yellow Emperor. Gao Xin's father was called Xiuji, Xiuji's father was named Xuanxiao, and Xuanxiao's father was Huangdi. Neither Xuan Xiao nor Xiu Ji ascended to the throne of God, and they did not ascend to the throne of God until Gaoxin. Gao Xin was Zhuanxu's nephew. Gao Xin was born with great aura and called out his name as soon as he was born. He generally bestows favor on everyone but not himself. He is smart and intelligent, can understand long-term situations, and can discern subtle things. He complies with the will of God and understands the concerns of the people. Be benevolent and dignified, be gentle and trustworthy, cultivate yourself, and the world will obey you.
target: After his death, his nephew Gao Xin became Emperor Ku. Gao Xin was born with great aura, benevolent and dignified, understanding both divine will and people's concerns.

id: 史记/十二本纪/五帝本纪::group-004
article_path: 史记/十二本纪/五帝本纪
source: He is smart and intelligent, can understand long-term situations, and can discern subtle things. He complies with the will of God and understands the concerns of the people. Be benevolent and dignified, be gentle and trustworthy, cultivate yourself, and the world will obey you. He collects the products of the land and uses them frugally; he caresss and educates the people and teaches them all kinds of useful things; he calculates the movements of the sun and the moon to determine the solar terms of the year, and respectfully welcomes the coming and going of the sun and the moon; he knows the ghosts and gods clearly and serves them carefully. He has a dignified appearance and high moral character. His actions are in keeping with the times and his actions are like those of a scholar. The emperor governs the people as impartially as rainwater irrigates farmland, all over the world, wherever the sun and moon shine, wherever the wind and rain go, no one disobeys and submits. Emperor Ku married Chen Feng's daughter and gave birth to Fangxun. Marry the daughter of the Qozi clan and give birth to Zhi. After Emperor Ku's death, Zhi took over the throne. After Emperor Zhi ascended the throne, he did not achieve any political achievements, so his younger brother Fangxun ascended the throne. This is Emperor Yao. Emperor Yao was a man of honor. He is as kind as heaven and as wise as God. Being close to him warms the heart like the sun; looking up to him is like clouds covering the earth. He is rich but not proud, noble but not indulgent. He wears a yellow hat, black clothes, a scarlet chariot and a white horse. He can respect virtuous people and make nine generations of the same clan love each other. Since the people of the same clan were at peace, they went to inspect the officials. All officials have outstanding achievements, and all princes and states can live in harmony. Emperor Yao ordered the Xi family and the He family to follow the will of God, draw up a calendar based on the appearance and appearance of the sun and the moon, and the position of the stars, and carefully teach the people the production seasons.
target: He governed impartially, and all under heaven submitted. After his death, his son Zhi ruled without achievement, so his brother Fangxun became Emperor Yao. Emperor Yao was kind as heaven and wise as God, rich but not proud. He united his clan, inspected officials, and ordered the Xi and He families to create a calendar based on celestial observations. He appointed officials to oversee spring, summer, autumn, and winter farming, establishing a 366-day year with leap months.

source: Yao said: Who can inherit my career? Fang Qi said: Your son Danzhu is a master of affairs. Yao said: Hum! Danzhu, he is stupid, vicious and cannot be used. Yao asked again: Then who else can? Huandou said: Gonggong has gathered people extensively and made achievements, which can be used. Yao said: Gonggong likes to talk nice words, but his intentions are not right. When he speaks, he seems to be very respectful, but his heart is absent and cannot be used. Yao asked again: Alas, the Four Mountains, now the floods are surging and mighty, surrounding the mountains and covering the hills. The people are extremely miserable. Who can be sent to control them? Everyone said Gun could do it. Yao said: Gun violated the destiny of heaven and destroyed his own people, so he cannot be used. The four mountains all said: Just use him. If it doesn't work, then remove him. Yao therefore followed Siyue's advice and appointed Gun. Gun controlled the flood for nine years without achieving any results. Yao said: Alas! Dear leaders, I have been on the throne for seventy years. Which of you can follow the destiny and succeed me as emperor? Siyue replied: Our virtues are very despicable and we are not worthy of being on the throne of God. Yao said: "Then let's recommend him from among all the ministers near and far with the same surname and different surnames, as well as those who live in seclusion. Everyone said to Yao: There was a single man living among the people, named Yu Shun. Yao said: Yes, I have heard of him. What is he like? Siyue replied; He is the son of a blind man. His father was fierce and stubborn, his mother was stupid and stubborn, and his brother was arrogant, but Shun was able to live in harmony with them, practice filial piety, and manage the family business with virtue to prevent them from going evil.
target: When Yao sought a successor, his son Danzhu was deemed unworthy, and Gonggong was rejected for insincerity. Despite warnings, Gun was appointed to control floods but failed after nine years.

source: From Qiongchan to Emperor Shun, the intervening generations had low status and were all commoners. Shun's father, Gusou, was blind. After Shun's biological mother died, Gusou married another wife and gave birth to Xiang, who was unruly. Gusou liked his second wife's son and often wanted to kill Shun, but Shun escaped. If he made a little mistake, he would be severely punished. Shun served his father, stepmother and stepmother's brother respectfully, becoming more respectful every day without slacking off at all. Shun was from Jizhou. Shun plowed fields in Lishan, fished in Leize, made pottery on the bank of the Yellow River, made various household utensils in Shouqiu, and did business in Fuxia. Shun's father Gusou was fierce and stubborn, his mother was arrogant, and his brother Xiang was unruly. They all wanted to kill Shun. Shun, however, behaved respectfully and never violated the principles of being a son, loving his brothers and being filial to his parents. They wanted to kill him, but they never succeeded; and when they needed him for something, he was always by their side. When Shun was twenty years old, he became famous for his filial piety. When he was thirty years old, Emperor Yao asked who could govern the world. All the four mountains recommended Yu Shun, saying that this man could do it. So Yao married his two daughters to Shun to observe his conduct at home, and let his nine sons live with him to observe his behavior outside.
target: The Four Mountains recommended Yu Shun, a filial man living among commoners. Yao tested Shun by marrying his daughters to him, observing his virtue, and assigning him various duties, which Shun performed excellently.

source: On the first day of the first lunar month, Shun accepted Yao's abdication in Wenzu Temple. Wenzu was also the Taizu of Yao. At this time, Yao was already old and asked Shun to act as the emperor's political agent, so as to observe whether Shun was in line with God's will as emperor. Shun then used instruments for observing astronomical phenomena to locate the sun, the moon, and the five stars of metal, wood, water, fire, and earth. He then held temporary ceremonies to offer sacrifices to heaven. He used the ritual of burning sacrifices on fire to worship the four seasons of heaven and earth.
target: Shun accepted Yao's abdication and began governing. He established rituals, standardized measurements, and conducted inspections every five years.

People in the world hate him and call him the four evils together with the three evils mentioned above. target: He divided the world into twelve states, dredged rivers, and implemented a penal system with reduced punishments. He exiled the four evil ministers—Gonggong, Huandou, Sanmiao, and Gun—satisfying the world.

source: They also divided and disintegrated the Sanmiao tribe. Each of these twenty-two people achieved great achievements: Gao Tao served as Dali, in charge of criminal law, and settled cases impartially, and people believed that he sought truth from facts; Boyi presided over etiquette, and was courteous and courteous in both high and low positions; Chui served as engineer, in charge of all workers, and all workers could do their jobs well; Yi served as Yu, in charge of Shanze , the mountains, forests, lakes and swamps were all developed; he was abandoned as Ji, in charge of agriculture, and all the grains grew luxuriantly according to the seasons; Qi was in charge of Situ, in charge of education, and the people were close and harmonious; Long was in charge of receiving guests, and tribes from far away came to join them; Shun appointed the twelve prefectures for pastoral work, and no one in the nine prefectures appointed by Yu disobeyed. Among them, Yu had the greatest contribution. He opened nine mountains, dredged nine lakes, regulated nine rivers, and delineated the boundaries of the nine states. All places paid tribute according to the amount they should pay, and there was no violation of the regulations. The territory spanning five thousand miles was pacified, all the way to the remote and remote areas farthest from the capital. At that time, the south pacified Jiaozhi and Beifa, the west pacified Rong, Xizhi, Qusui, Di, and Qiang, the north pacified Shanrong, Fa, and Xishen, and the east pacified Chang and Niaoyi. All four seas jointly praised Emperor Shun's merits. So Yu composed the music "Nine Moves" to praise Shun's merits, which attracted auspicious things, and the phoenix also flew in, circling and dancing with the music. The Qingming Dynasty and its virtues all started from the time of Yu and Shun. Shun was famous for his filial piety when he was twenty years old. He was appointed by Yao when he was thirty years old. Thirty-nine years after he ascended the throne, he toured the south and died in the Cangwu countryside in the south. Buried in Jiuyi Mountain on the south bank of the Yangtze River, this is Lingling. After Shun ascended the throne, he rode in a car with the emperor's flag to pay homage to his father Gusou. He behaved humbly and cautiously and followed the principles of being a son. He also made his younger brother Xiang a prince. Shun's son Shangjun was also unqualified, so Shun recommended Yu to heaven in advance.
target: The territory expanded five thousand miles, and all regions submitted. Shun died while touring south and was buried at Jiuyi Mountain. His son Shangjun being unworthy, Shun recommended Yu to heaven. After Shun's death, Yu ascended the throne, continuing the pattern of abdication.

source: From the Yellow Emperor to Shun and Yu, they all had the same surname, but they had different national titles in order to highlight their respective bright virtues. Therefore, Huangdi was named Youxiong, Emperor Zhuanxu was named Gaoyang, Emperor Ku was named Gaoxin, Emperor Yao was named Taotang, and Emperor Shun was named Youyu. Emperor Yu's title was Queen of Xia, and he was given another surname, Si. The descendants of Qi founded Shang, with the surname Zi. The descendants of Qi founded the Zhou Dynasty, and their surname was Ji. Tai Shigong said: Many scholars refer to the Five Emperors, and the Five Emperors have been around for a long time. "Shangshu" only records historical facts since Yao; while each school's description of the Yellow Emperor is rough and not typical, and it is difficult for the scholar-officials to explain clearly. Some scholars do not pass on the "Zaiyu Asks the Virtues of the Five Emperors" and "Emperor Lineage Surnames" handed down by Confucius. I once went to Kongtong in the west, Zhuolu in the north, the sea in the east, and crossed the Yangtze River and Huai River in the south. Wherever I went, I went to places where old people praised the deeds of the Yellow Emperor, Yao, and Shun. Although the customs and teachings were different, the statements that were consistent with ancient records were relatively credible. I have studied "Spring and Autumn" and "Guoyu", and their explanations of "Five Emperors' Virtues" and "Emperor's Lineage" are very clear, but people have not studied them in depth. In fact, their descriptions are not false theories. "Shangshu" is incomplete and intermittent, but scattered anecdotal records can often be found in other books. If you are not eager to learn and think deeply, and truly understand their meaning in your heart, it will definitely be difficult to explain it to those who have shallow knowledge and limited knowledge. I reviewed and sorted these materials, selected those with particularly elegant and correct writing, and wrote this chapter as the first chapter of the book.
target: The historian notes that while records of the Five Emperors are ancient and sometimes unclear, careful study of various texts and oral traditions confirms their authenticity. This account selects the most elegant and correct materials as the first chapter of the historical record.
