source: Empress Dowager Lu was Gaozu's humble wife and gave birth to Emperor Xiaohui and his daughter, Empress Dowager Lu Yuan. When Emperor Gaozu became the king of Han, he found Qi Ji in Dingtao. He loved her very much and gave birth to King Ruyi of Zhao Yin. Emperor Xiaohui was kind and weak, but Gaozu thought he was not like him, so he often wanted to depose the prince and make Qi Ji's son Ruyi, thinking that Ruyi was similar to himself. Qi Ji was favored and often followed Emperor Gaozu to Guandong. She cried day and night and wanted to make her son the crown prince to replace the original crown prince. Empress Lu was getting older and often stayed behind. She rarely saw Gaozu, and their relationship became increasingly estranged. Ruyi was granted the title of Queen Zhao, and almost replaced the prince many times. Fortunately, the ministers' remonstrances and Liu Hou's strategy prevented the prince from being abolished. Empress Lu was a strong and resolute person. She assisted Emperor Gaozu in pacifying the world and killing ministers, mostly thanks to Empress Lu. Empress Lu had two older brothers, both of whom were generals. The eldest brother Zhou Luhou died in the line of duty, and his sons Lu Tai were granted the title of Lihou, Lu Chan was granted the title of Jiaohou; the second brother Lu Shizhi was granted the title of Jiancheng Marquis. On April 25, the twelfth year of Emperor Gaozu's reign, he died in Changle Palace. The prince inherited the title of Emperor Gaozu and succeeded him as emperor. At this time, Emperor Gaozu had eight sons: the eldest son Liu Fei, who was the brother of Emperor Xiaohui and had a different mother than Emperor Xiaohui, was named King of Qi; the rest were younger brothers of Emperor Xiaohui. Liu Ruyi, the son of Qi Ji, was named King of Zhao, Mrs. Bo's son Liu Heng was named King of Dai, the other sons of Ji's concubines were Liu Huifeng, King of Liang, Liu Youfeng, King of Huaiyang, Liu Changfeng, King of Huainan, and Liu Jianfeng, King of Yan. Gaozu's younger brother Liu Jiao was granted the title of King of Chu, and his elder brother's son Liu Bi was granted the title of King of Wu. Wu Chen, the son of Fan Jun Wu Rui, a hero who was not a descendant of the Liu family, was granted the title of King of Changsha. Empress Lu resented Madam Qi and her son King Zhao the most, so she ordered Madam Qi to be imprisoned in Yongxiang, and summoned King Zhao to the capital. The envoy went back and forth several times. Zhao Xiang Jianpinghou Zhou Chang said to the envoy: Emperor Gao entrusted King Zhao to me. King Zhao is still young. I heard that the Queen Mother resented Mrs. Qi and wanted to summon King Zhao to kill him together. I dare not send King Zhao away. Moreover, King Zhao was also ill and could not go there according to the imperial edict.
target: Empress Dowager Lu was the humble wife of Emperor Gaozu and mother of Emperor Xiaohui and Princess Lu Yuan. Gaozu favored Concubine Qi, who bore King Ruyi of Zhao, and often considered deposing the kind and weak Crown Prince Xiaohui in favor of Ruyi. Empress Lu, growing estranged from Gaozu, was resolute and assisted in pacifying the realm and killing ministers. After Gaozu's death in 195 BCE, Xiaohui succeeded him. Empress Lu resented Concubine Qi and King Ruyi. She imprisoned Concubine Qi and summoned Ruyi to the capital. Emperor Xiaohui protected Ruyi, but during a hunt, the Queen Mother poisoned Ruyi. She then mutilated Concubine Qi, calling her a "human pig." Xiaohui, horrified, fell ill and abandoned court affairs, dying in 188 BCE. During his funeral, the Queen Mother cried without tears until ministers, following advice, appointed Lu family members as generals, securing her power.

id: 史记/十二本纪/吕太后本纪::group-001
article_path: 史记/十二本纪/吕太后本纪
source: It is against the oath to make a descendant of the Lu family king now. The Queen Mother was very unhappy. Ask Zuo Prime Minister Chen Ping and Jianghou Zhou Bo. Zhou Bo and others replied: Emperor Gao brought peace to the world and made his children kings. Now that the Queen Mother is in charge of the court, she can make her brothers and the children of the Lu family kings. There is nothing wrong with that. The Queen Mother became happy and returned to the palace. Wang Ling scolded Chen Ping and Jianghou, saying: Were you not present when we made a blood oath with Emperor Gao? Now that Emperor Gao is dead, the Queen Mother comes to court as a heroine and intends to make the children of the Lu family kings. Even if you want to flatter and break your oath, how can you have the face to go to Jiuquan to see Emperor Gao after your death? Chen Ping and Jianghou said: "Today we openly oppose in front of the Queen Mother and fight hard in the court, we are not as good as you; when it comes to protecting the country and stabilizing the kingship of Liu's descendants, you are not as good as us." Wang Ling was speechless. In November, the Queen Mother wanted to depose Wang Ling, so she made him the emperor's tutor and deprived him of his powers as prime minister. Therefore, Wang Ling claimed that he was ill and was dismissed from office and returned home. Then Chen Ping, the prime minister of the left, was made the prime minister of the right, and Marquis Piyang Shenshi was made the prime minister of the left. Prime Minister Zuo did not manage government affairs and asked him to supervise the affairs of the palace, just like a doctor. Therefore, Shen Shiqi was favored by the Queen Mother and often made decisions on government affairs. The ministers relied on him to decide important matters. Then he pursued Li Hou's father as the King of Wuwu, intending to use this as the beginning of making the Lu family's children kings. In April, the Queen Mother planned to make the children of the Lu family a marquis, so she first made Feng Wuze, a great minister of the Great Ancestor, the Marquis of Bocheng. Princess Lu Yuan died and was given the posthumous title of Queen Mother Lu Yuan. Her son was named King of Lu. The father of King Lu was Zhang Ao, Marquis of Xuanping. Liu Zhang, the son of King Hui of Qi, was granted the title of Zhu Xuhou, and Lu Lu's daughter was married to him. Prime Minister Qi Shou was granted the title of Marquis of Pingding. Yang Chengyan of Shaofu was granted the title of Wuhou. Then they named Lu Zhong as Peihou, Lu Ping as Fuliuhou, and Zhang Mai as Nangonghou. The Queen Mother wanted to make Lu's children kings, so she first made Liu Qiang, the son of Emperor Xiaohui's harem, the King of Huaiyang, Liu Buyi the King of Changshan, Liu Shan the Marquis of Xiangcheng, Liu Chao the Marquis of Zhi, and Liu Wu the Marquis of Huguan. The Empress Dowager signaled to the ministers in a low voice, and the ministers requested that Li Hou Lutai be granted the title of King Lu, and the Empress Dowager agreed. After the death of Lu Shizhi, Marquis of Kang in Jiancheng, his son who had inherited the title was found guilty and was deposed. His younger brother Lu Lu was granted the title of Marquis of Huling and succeeded Kang Marquis. In the second year, King Changshan died, and his younger brother Liu Shan, Marquis of Xiangcheng, was appointed King of Changshan and his name was changed to Yi. In November, King Lu Tai died. He was posthumously named King Su, and Prince Lu Jia was made king on his behalf.
target: The Queen Mother then ruled as regent, intending to make Lu family members kings. She consulted ministers; Wang Ling opposed, citing Gaozu's oath, while Chen Ping and Zhou Bo supported her. She deposed Wang Ling and promoted Chen Ping. She made Lu Tai King of Lu, and after his death, Lu Jia succeeded. She also made several of Xiaohui's sons kings, though they were not his biological children. The Queen Mother deposed and killed a young emperor who threatened rebellion, replacing him with Liu Yi, renamed Hong.

id: 史记/十二本纪/吕太后本纪::group-002
article_path: 史记/十二本纪/吕太后本纪
source: King Zhao came to the capital and placed him in his official residence. He did not receive him and ordered his guards to surround him and deny him anything to eat. Some of his subordinates secretly brought him food, and they were arrested and tried for crimes. King Zhao was hungry, so he sang: "Zhu Lu has the power, the Liu family is in danger; you are coercing the princes, forcing me to marry the Lu family's daughter as my concubine." My concubine is jealous and slanders me for committing a crime; she slanders my daughter and brings chaos to the country, but the emperor doesn't understand. I have no loyal ministers, otherwise why would I lose my feudal kingdom? In the wilderness of suicide, Heaven must uphold justice in its affairs! Alas, I have no regrets. I would rather kill myself as soon as possible. I starve to death for the sake of the king, who has mercy on me? Lu is unreasonable and has no choice but to ask God to avenge me. On the 18th, King Zhao was imprisoned and died, and he was buried next to the graves of the people of Chang'an using the etiquette of ordinary people. On the 30th, there was a solar eclipse and the day was dark. The Queen Mother was disgusted and unhappy, so she said to the attendants: "It must be because of me." In February, Liu Hui, the king of Liang, became the king of Zhao. King Lu Lu Chan moved to the throne and became King Liang. King Liang did not go to the feudal state to take office, but stayed in the capital as the emperor's tutor. The emperor's son Liu Tai, Marquis of Changping, was made King Lu. Liang was renamed Lu, and Lu was renamed Jichuan. The Queen Mother's sister Lu Yu had a daughter who was the wife of Liu Ze, the Marquis of Yingling, who was a general. The Empress Dowager conferred the title of king on a descendant of the Lu family. She was afraid that General Liu would cause chaos after her death, so she named Liu Ze King Langxie to comfort him.
target: The Queen Mother continued to consolidate Lu power, killing or deposing several Zhao kings, including Liu You, who starved to death after opposing the Lu family. She made Lu Lu King of Zhao and Lu Chan King of Liang. In 180 BCE, she fell ill and warned Lu Chan and Lu Lu to control the army, fearing rebellion. She died, leaving edicts for rewards and amnesty.

id: 史记/十二本纪/吕太后本纪::group-003
article_path: 史记/十二本纪/吕太后本纪
source: The loyal ministers gave advice, but the empress was confused and refused to accept it. Now that Empress Gao has passed away, the emperor is still young and cannot govern the world, so he can only rely on ministers and princes. However, the Lu family prides itself on its position, gathers troops, uses its majesty to intimidate the loyal ministers of the princes, and orders the world under the pretext of imperial edicts. Therefore, the Liu family's ancestral temple is in danger. I led the army to the court to eliminate those who should not be king. When the Han court heard the news, Prime Minister Lu Chan and others sent Yingyin Marquis Guanying to lead an army to attack the King of Qi. When Guan Ying arrived in Xingyang, he discussed with others that the Lu family had taken control of the army in Guanzhong and wanted to eliminate the Liu family and establish themselves as emperor. If I defeat Qi's army now and go back to resume my life, this will further strengthen the Lu family's power. So Guan Ying stationed troops in Xingyang and sent envoys to inform the king of Qi and the princes of other countries. We must unite with them, wait for Lu's rebellion, and get rid of Lu together. After the King of Qi heard the news, he withdrew his army to the western border of Qi State, waited for the news, and acted as agreed. Lu Lu and Lu Chan wanted to launch a rebellion in Guanzhong, but they were afraid of Suihou, Zhu Xuhou and others internally, and externally they were afraid of the armies of Qi and Chu. They were also worried about Guan Ying's rebellion, so they planned to wait until Guan Ying's army fought with Qi's army before launching a rebellion. At this time, King Liu Tai of Jichuan, King Liu Wu of Huaiyang, King Liu Chao of Changshan, and King Lu Yuan, grandson of Empress Lu, who were nominally younger brothers of the Young Emperor, all did not return to the country due to their young age and lived in Chang'an. Zhao Wang Changlu and Liang Wang Lu Chan each commanded troops and lived in the Northern and Southern Army. They were both from the Lu family. No one among the princes and ministers felt that they would be able to save their lives. Taiwei Jianghou Zhou Bo could not enter the military camp to take control of the army. The Marquis of Qu Zhou, Li Shang, was old and sick, and his son Li Ji was friendly with Lu Lu.
target: After her death, the Lu family plotted rebellion. King Qi of Liu led forces against them, and ministers like Zhou Bo and Chen Ping conspired to remove the Lu. Zhou Bo, using deception, gained command of the Northern Army, and the soldiers supported the Liu family. Lu Lu surrendered his command, and Lu Chan was killed. The Lu family was exterminated, including Lu Lu and Lu Yu.

id: 史记/十二本纪/吕太后本纪::group-004
article_path: 史记/十二本纪/吕太后本纪
source: Report to the king: The palace has been cleaned up. King Dai entered Weiyang Palace that night. There were ten visitors holding halberds guarding the main entrance and saying, "The emperor is here, what are you doing in there?" Dai Wang told the Taiwei about the situation. The Taiwei went to explain, and all ten of the visitors put down their weapons and walked away. The king then entered the palace to listen to political affairs. At night, the officials separately killed King Liang, King Huaiyang, King Changshan and the young emperor in the official residence. On behalf of the king, he was established as the emperor. He died in the 23rd year of his reign and was posthumously named Emperor Xiaowen. Tai Shigong said: During the period of Emperor Xiaohui and Empress Gao, the people were freed from the suffering of the Warring States Period. The emperor and ministers all wanted to recuperate and rule by doing nothing. Therefore, Emperor Xiaohui dropped his clothes and handed over his clothes. Empress Gao used the heroine to act as the emperor. Political affairs did not go out of the door, and the world was peaceful. Punishment was rarely used and the number of sinners was few. The people are diligent in farming and have more food and clothing. When Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty first started to rebel, Lu Pheasant became his wife. After the world was pacified, Empress Lu began to dominate and prosper secretly. Empress Lu was a stoic person with a cruel and suspicious personality. She poisoned King Liu Fei of Qi with poisoned wine, and cruelly cut off Concubine Qi's hands and feet and called her a human pig. When Emperor Hui died, Empress Lu pretended to cry and was not sad. He appointed his relatives with the same surname to rule the world privately. Kill the ministers, cut off the Liu family's queens and their heirs, harm the people, and make them miserable.
target: The ministers, fearing the young emperor was not truly Xiaohui's son, chose Liu Heng, King of Dai, as emperor due to his maturity and virtue. He became Emperor Xiaowen, reigning for 23 years. The historian notes that during Empress Lu's rule, the people recovered from war, punishments were rare, and agriculture flourished, despite her cruelty and nepotism.

source: Hou Ji, the ancestor of the Zhou Dynasty, was named Qi. His mother was a woman of Tai family named Jiang Yuan. Jiang Yuan was the emperor's concubine. Jiang Yuan went out to the countryside and saw a giant footprint. He was so happy that he wanted to step on it. When he stepped on it, he felt his body vibrating as if he was pregnant. When they were ten months old, they gave birth to a son. Jiang Yuan thought that the child was unlucky, so he threw him into a narrow alley, but horses and cows passed by him and avoided stepping on him, so he threw him in the woods. There were many people in the woods, so he moved to another place. Jiang Yuan thought this was so magical, so he took him back and raised him as a human being. Since I wanted to throw him away at first, I named him Abandoned. When Qi was a child, he had the lofty ambitions of a great man.
target: Hou Ji, ancestor of the Zhou Dynasty, was named Qi. His mother Jiang Yuan, a concubine of the emperor, became pregnant after stepping on a giant footprint. She bore a son but tried to abandon him multiple times. Miraculously, animals protected him, so she raised him and named him "Abandoned." As a child, Qi showed great ambition, excelling at planting crops.

source: Since I wanted to throw him away at first, I named him Abandoned. When Qi was a child, he had the lofty ambitions of a great man. When he was playing games, he liked to plant hemp and beans, and the hemp and beans he planted grew very luxuriantly. When he grew up, he liked farming. He could observe the characteristics of the land and choose suitable grains to plant. The people followed his example. When Emperor Yao heard about these things, he appointed Qi as a farmer to teach people how to grow crops. People all over the world benefited from this, and he made great contributions. Emperor Shun said: "Sir, the people were suffering from hunger, thanks to you being the Houji to sow all kinds of grains." Therefore, the enfeoffment was abandoned in Tai, known as Houji, and Ji was the surname. Hou Ji is famous because during the Tao, Tang, Yu, and Xia generations, this family was very virtuous. After Hou Ji died, his son Buchu succeeded to the throne. In Buchu's later years, the Xia Hou family's state affairs declined, and they gave up the official post of Houji and no longer paid attention to agriculture. Buchu fled to the Rongdi area because he lost his official position. After Bucheng died, his son Ju succeeded to the throne. After Ju's death, his son Gong Liu succeeded to the throne. Although Gong Liu was in the Rong and Di, he resumed the business of repairing Houji's foundation, engaged in farming, and planted crops according to the cultivation characteristics of the land. He crossed the Wei River from Qishui and Ju Rivers, felled and obtained timber for use, so that those who went out had travel expenses, those at home had savings, and the people's lives improved thanks to him. The people were grateful and loved him, and many moved to join him. The great prosperity of Zhou Dynasty's statecraft started from here, so poets composed poems and music to praise and commemorate his kindness. After Gong Liu died, his son Qingjie succeeded to the throne and established the capital in Bin. After Qingjie's death, his son Huangpu succeeded to the throne. After the death of the imperial servant, his son Chafu succeeded to the throne. After Chafu's death, his son Ruihe succeeded to the throne. After the death of Ruihe, his son Gongfei succeeded to the throne. After Gong Fei's death, his son Gao Yu succeeded to the throne. After Gao Yu's death, his son Ya Yu succeeded to the throne. After Yayu's death, his son Gongshu Zulei succeeded to the throne. After the death of Gongshu Zulei, his son Gu Gongdanfu succeeded to the throne. Gu Gongdanfu re-established the foundations of Houji and Gongliu, accumulated virtues, and spread benevolence and righteousness. The people in the capital all supported him. Xunyu and other Rongdi tribes came to attack them and wanted to plunder their property, so Gu Gong and Danfu gave it to them. Soon after, the Rongdi tribe came to attack again, wanting to get the land and people. The people were very angry and wanted to go out and fight. Gu Gong said: The people support the monarch because they want him to seek benefits for everyone. Now Rong and Di are coming to invade, with the purpose of wanting my land and people. What difference does it make if the people follow me or follow them? The people went to war because of me and relied on fathers, sons and brothers who sacrificed the people to be the monarch. I really couldn't bear to do this. So Gu Gongdanfu and his relatives left Bin, crossed Qishui and Jushui, crossed Liangshan, and settled at the foot of Qishan. And all the people in Bindi brought their old and young to the foot of Qishan Mountain, and all returned to Gu Gong's side. Nearby countries heard that the ancient Duke was benevolent, and many people came to follow him. So Gu Gong abandoned the customs of Rong and Di, built cities and houses, and set up towns for the people to settle down.
target: When he grew up, he became skilled at farming, observing land characteristics to choose suitable grains. Emperor Yao appointed him as a farmer to teach agriculture, and Emperor Shun enfeoffed him in Tai, calling him Hou Ji, with Ji as his surname. After Hou Ji died, his son Buchu succeeded. During Buchu's later years, the Xia dynasty declined and abandoned agriculture. Buchu fled to the Rongdi region. His descendant Gong Liu revived Hou Ji's agricultural practices, crossing rivers to obtain timber, improving people's lives. Many people moved to join him, marking the beginning of Zhou's prosperity. Gong Liu's descendant Gu Gongdanfu further accumulated virtues and benevolence. When Rongdi tribes attacked, seeking land and people, Gu Gong refused to fight, saying he could not bear sacrificing people for his own sake. He moved with his relatives to the foot of Qishan Mountain, where many people followed him. He built cities, established towns, and created five official positions.

source: And all the people in Bindi brought their old and young to the foot of Qishan Mountain, and all returned to Gu Gong's side. Nearby countries heard that the ancient Duke was benevolent, and many people came to follow him. So Gu Gong abandoned the customs of Rong and Di, built cities and houses, and set up towns for the people to settle down. Five official offices were established: Situ, Sima, Sikong, Sushi, and Sikou. The people composed poems and music to praise him and praise his kindness. The eldest son of Duke Gu was called Taibo, and the second son was called Yu Zhong. Taijiang gave birth to a younger son, Ji Li, who married Tairen. Both Taijiang and Tairen were virtuous wives. Tairen gave birth to a prosperous son, which was a sign of sagehood. Gu Gong said: My descendants will achieve great things, probably Chang, right? The eldest son Taibo and Yu Zhong knew that Gu Gong wanted to establish Ji Li so that he could pass on to Chang in the future, so they fled to Jingman, got tattoos on their bodies, cut their hair short, and gave way to Ji Li. After the death of Gu Gong, Ji Li succeeded to the throne and became Gong Ji. Gong Ji practiced the way of governing the country left by the ancient Duke and resolutely implemented benevolence and righteousness, and the princes all obeyed him. After Gong Ji died, his son Chang succeeded to the throne and became Xibo. Xibo was called King Wen. He inherited the cause of Hou Ji and Gong Liu, followed the laws of Gu Gong and Gong Ji, practiced benevolence and righteousness, respected the elderly, and was kind to the young. He treated the wise men with courtesy. In order to receive the wise men, he sometimes did not bother to eat at noon, so the scholars all attached themselves to him. Boyi and Shuqi were in Guzhu country. They heard that Xibo was very respectful and took care of the elderly, so they went together to join Xibo. Tai Dian, Hong Yao, San Yisheng, Huan Zi, Xin Jia and other officials also went to submit to him. Chonghou Hu spoke ill of Xibo in front of King Zhou of Yin: Xibo has accumulated virtues and done good deeds, and all the princes have submitted to him, which will be detrimental to you.
target: Gu Gong's eldest son Taibo and second son Yu Zhong fled to Jingman, giving way to their younger brother Ji Li, whose son Chang (King Wen) would achieve greatness. King Wen inherited the legacy of Hou Ji and Gong Liu, practicing benevolence, respecting elders, and treating wise men with courtesy. Many scholars and officials submitted to him.

source: He treated the wise men with courtesy. In order to receive the wise men, he sometimes did not bother to eat at noon, so the scholars all attached themselves to him. Boyi and Shuqi were in Guzhu country. They heard that Xibo was very respectful and took care of the elderly, so they went together to join Xibo. Tai Dian, Hong Yao, San Yisheng, Huan Zi, Xin Jia and other officials also went to submit to him. Chonghou Hu spoke ill of Xibo in front of King Zhou of Yin: Xibo has accumulated virtues and done good deeds, and all the princes have submitted to him, which will be detrimental to you. So Yin Zhou imprisoned Xibo in Youli. Hong Yao and others were very worried about Xi Bo, and tried their best to find beauties from the Xin family, colorful horses from the Lirong region, nine carriages from the Xiong Kingdom, and various other rare treasures, and presented them to King Zhou through Fei Zhongjin, a favored minister of the Yin Shang Dynasty. King Zhou was very happy and said: "Anything in this is enough for me to free Xibo, not to mention there are so many other good things!" So he pardoned Count Xi and gave him bows, arrows, axes and axes, giving him the right to conquer the neighboring princes. King Zhou told Xibo: The person who framed Xibo was Chonghou Hu. After Xibo returned home, he offered the land west of Luoshui and asked Zhou to abolish the criminal law of Paoluo. Zhou agreed to him. Xibo secretly did good deeds, and the princes came to ask him to judge right and wrong. At that time, people from Yu and Rui had lawsuits that could not be adjudicated, so they went to Zhou. They entered the realm of Zhou and saw that those who farmed fields gave way to each other, and the people regarded humility as a virtue. Before the people of Yu and Rui saw Xibo, they felt ashamed and said to each other: "What we are fighting for is what the people of Zhou are ashamed of. Why are we going to do it? We are just bringing shame on ourselves." So they returned and left with humility to each other. When the princes heard about it, they all said: Xibo must be a monarch who has received orders from heaven.
target: Chonghou Hu slandered him to King Zhou of Yin, who imprisoned him in Youli. Officials presented rare treasures to King Zhou, who freed King Wen and gave him the right to conquer neighboring princes. King Wen secretly did good deeds, and when people from Yu and Rui came to him with disputes, they saw the humility of Zhou's people and felt ashamed, resolving their conflicts peacefully.

source: The next year, he conquered Chonghou Hu. Fengyi was built and the capital was moved from Qixia to Feng. The next year, Uncle Xi died, and Prince Fa ascended the throne, becoming King Wu. Siebo reigned for about fifty years. When he was imprisoned in Youli, he probably increased the eight hexagrams in "Yi" to sixty-four. Judging from the praise of Count Xi by the author of "Poetry", it was probably in that year that Count Xi was appointed king and adjudicated the lawsuits between Yu and Rui. He died ten years later, and his posthumous title was King Wen. He once changed the legal system of Yin and formulated the calendar. Zeng Zhui respected Gu Gong as the Taiwang, and Gongji as the Wangji: It probably means that the auspicious sign of the emperor began from the time of the Taiwang. When King Wu came to the throne, Taigong Wang was appointed as Grand Master, Duke Zhou became assistant prime minister, and Duke Zhao and Duke Bi assisted King Wu and followed King Wen's legacy. In the ninth year of King Wu's appointment, King Wu first offered sacrifices to King Wen in Bi, and then went to the east to hold a military parade and arrived at Mengjin. Let King Wen's wooden master be carried on a cart and placed in the central army's tent. King Wu claimed to be Prince Fa, indicating that he was conquering in the name of King Wen and did not dare to act arbitrarily. He declared to Sima, Situ, Sikong and other officials who were ordered by the king to hold the talisman festival: Be careful and do what you say! I am an ignorant person, but because my ancestors were virtuous, I inherited their achievements. Various reward and punishment systems have now been established to ensure that the achievements of ancestors are completed. So he sent troops. Master Shi Shangfu ordered: Gather your men and take advantage of the oars. Anyone who is late will be killed. King Wu crossed the Yellow River, and when the boat reached the middle of the river, a white fish jumped into King Wu's boat. King Wu leaned over and picked it up for sacrifice. After crossing the river, a ball of fire fell from the sky and landed on King Wu's roof. It solidified into the shape of a crow, was red in color, and made a soulful cry. At that time, eight hundred princes came to Mengjin to form an alliance. The princes all said: Zhou can be defeated. King Wu said: You don't understand the destiny of heaven, not yet. So he led the army back. Two years later, I heard that Zhou was more chaotic and violent than before, so he killed Prince Bigan and imprisoned Jizi. Tai Shizhen and Shao Shiqiang took their musical instruments and fled to the state of Zhou. At this time, King Wu announced to all the princes: King Yin has committed serious crimes and must work together to defeat him! So he followed King Wen's decree and led 300 chariots, 3,000 warriors, and 45,000 armored warriors to march eastward to defeat Zhou. On the Wuwu day of the twelfth month of the eleventh year, all the troops crossed Mengjin, and all the princes came to join them. King Wu said: "You must be diligent and don't slack off!" King Wu therefore wrote the "Tai Oath" and announced to everyone: Now King Zhou of Yin actually listened to the words of his wives and concubines, cut himself off from heaven, violated the movements of the sun, moon, and Beidou, alienated his brothers from the same ancestor, abandoned the music of his ancestors, and dared to use promiscuous music to modify elegant music to please his wives and concubines.
target: King Wen conquered several states and moved the capital to Feng. After his death, his son King Wu ascended. In the ninth year of his reign, King Wu marched eastward to Mengjin, where eight hundred princes formed an alliance. Two years later, hearing of Yin Zhou's increasing tyranny, King Wu led 300 chariots, 3,000 warriors, and 45,000 armored soldiers eastward. At Muye, he swore an oath condemning King Zhou for listening to women, abandoning ancestors, and oppressing the people. Although King Zhou's army numbered 700,000, they had no will to fight and turned their weapons against him. King Zhou fled to the Deer Platform and burned himself to death. King Wu shot arrows at his corpse and beheaded him.

source: King Wu granted the remaining people of Yin to Lu Fu, the son of Shang Zhou. King Wu sent his younger brothers Guan Shuxian and Cai Shudu to assist Lu's father in governing Yin because the world had just settled down and was not yet peaceful and harmonious. Then he ordered Duke Zhao to release Jizi from prison. Bi Gong was ordered to release the imprisoned people from prison and commend the people in Shangronglu Lane. Nangong Kuo was ordered to distribute the money gathered in Lutai and the food in Juqiao to help the poor savages and untouchables. Nangong Kuo and Shi Yi were ordered to remove the Jiuding and Baoyu belonging to the Yin people. Hongyao was ordered to build soil and repair Bigan's tomb. Zongzhu was ordered to offer sacrifices to the fallen soldiers in the army. Then withdrew troops back to the west. Along the way, King Wu visited various vassal states, recorded political affairs, and wrote the "Wucheng" chapter, announcing the achievement of Wu's victory over Yin. He divided the feudal princes and rewarded them with the sacrificial vessels of the Yin ancestral temple. He wrote the chapter "Dividing the Vessels of Yin" to record his orders and the vessels obtained by the feudal princes. King Wu recalled the ancient saint kings, so he honored the descendants of Shennong in Jiao, the descendants of Yellow Emperor in Zhu, the descendants of Emperor Yao in Ji, the descendants of Emperor Shun in Chen, and the descendants of Dayu in Qi. Then he was awarded the title of hero and counselor, and Master Shangfu was the first one to be awarded the title. King Wu granted his father the title of Qi in Yingqiu. His younger brother Tong Gongdan was granted the title of Qufu, and his country was named Lu. He was granted the title of Duke Zhao and died in Yan. His younger brother Shu Xian was granted the title of Guan, and his younger brother was granted the title of Du in Cai. Others were also sealed in turn. King Wu summoned the chief officials of Jiuzhou, climbed to the high ground of Bin, and looked at the capital of Shang in the distance. King Wu returned to Zhou Dynasty and could not sleep at night.
target: After conquering Yin, King Wu released prisoners, distributed wealth to the poor, repaired Bigan's tomb, and divided feudal territories. He honored descendants of ancient sage kings and granted lands to his brothers and officials. King Wu could not sleep at night, worrying about stabilizing the kingdom. He planned to build Zhou city in Luoyi.

source: They raised horses in the south of Huashan Mountain and cattle in the Taolin area, ordered the army to lay down their weapons, rectified the army and then disbanded the army: to express to the people of the world that they would no longer use troops. Two years after King Wu defeated the Yin Dynasty, he asked Jizi about the reasons for the demise of the Yin Dynasty. Jizi couldn't bear to talk about the crimes of the Yin Dynasty, so he told King Wu about the survival of the country. King Wu also felt embarrassed, so he turned to Tiandao. King Wu was seriously ill. At this time, the world was not yet unified, and all the ministers were afraid and performed divination. Therefore, Duke Zhou broke the fast and volunteered to be a substitute, hoping to bear the disaster for King Wu. King Wu's illness gradually improved. Later, King Wu died, and Prince Song inherited the throne and became the king. When King Cheng was young, Zhou had just brought peace to the world. Duke Zhou was worried that the princes would betray Zhou, so he managed government affairs on behalf of King Cheng and presided over state affairs. Uncle Guan, Uncle Cai and other brothers suspected that Duke Zhou had usurped the throne and joined forces with Wu Geng to launch a rebellion and betray Zhou. On the orders of King Cheng, Duke Zhou had Wu Geng and Uncle Guan killed, and Uncle Cai was exiled.
target: Two years after defeating Yin, King Wu fell ill and died. His young son King Cheng ascended, with Duke Zhou acting as regent. Guan Shu and Cai Shu rebelled with Wu Geng, but Duke Zhou suppressed the rebellion, killed Wu Geng and Guan Shu, and exiled Cai Shu.

source: Now what Wang is studying is to monopolize financial profits. How can this be allowed? If an ordinary person monopolizes wealth and profits, it can be called "stealing". If a king does this, there will be very few people willing to join him. If Duke Rongyi was reused, the Zhou Dynasty would definitely decline. King Li refused to listen, and finally appointed Rongyi Gong as a minister and asked him to preside over national affairs. King Li was tyrannical, extravagant and arrogant, and the people of the country openly discussed his faults. Duke Zhao remonstrated: The people can no longer stand your decree. King Li was furious and found a sorcerer who was defending the country and sent him to monitor those who criticized the king. Anyone reported to have committed this crime will be killed. In this way, the criticism was reduced, and the princes no longer came to see him. In the thirty-fourth year, King Li became even more strict. No one in the country dared to speak anymore, and they could only exchange glances when meeting on the road. King Li was very proud and told Duke Zhao: I can quell people's criticism so that they dare not even speak. Duke Zhao said: "This is because you have blocked their mouths." Blocking people's mouths is more dangerous than blocking water. If the water is blocked, the embankments will burst and flood, which will definitely hurt a lot of people, including the people. Therefore, those who manage water must channelize the water, and those who manage the people must let them speak freely. Therefore, in order to understand the situation, the emperor asked everyone from the ministers to the nobles to contribute poems, blind musicians to present music, historians to present books, masters to give instructions, blind people without eyes to narrate, blind people with eyes to recite, and all craftsmen to Let the common people talk in the streets, let the ministers admonish, let the relatives correct mistakes, let the blind musicians and historians teach, let the old people admonish, and then let the emperor consider it, so that political affairs can be carried out without violating reason. The people have mouths, just like the land has mountains and rivers, which are the source of wealth, and just like the land has plains and fertile fields, which are the source of food and clothing. Let people speak freely, and good and bad things can be reflected. Doing good deeds and guarding against bad deeds is the true source of wealth, food and clothing. The people consider it in their hearts and speak it out with their mouths, and then do it after the matter is decided. How can it last long if their mouths are blocked? The king refused to listen. Therefore, no one in the country dared to speak. Three years later, they rebelled and attacked King Li. King Li fled to Pig. King Li's prince was hiding quietly in Duke Zhao's house. When the people of the country found out, they surrounded Zhao Gong's house. Duke Zhao said: "I have warned the king many times before, but the king did not listen, which led to such a disaster."
target: King Cheng and King Kang's reigns saw peace for over forty years without using punishments. The Zhou royal family declined during King Zhao's reign. King Mu, who ascended at age fifty, restored order but foolishly attacked the Quanrong, causing distant states to stop paying tribute. King Li was greedy and tyrannical, suppressing criticism by killing those who spoke out. Duke Zhao warned him that blocking people's mouths was more dangerous than blocking water, but King Li refused to listen. After three years, the people rebelled and King Li fled. The country was governed by two dukes during the Republic period.

source: In order to make Bao Si laugh, King You of Zhou lit the beacon fire. When the princes saw the beacon fire, they all rushed over. When they arrived, there were no enemies. Bao Si laughed out loud as expected. King You liked this method and raised beacons for Bao Si many times. Later, losing trust, the princes gradually stopped coming. King You appointed Guo Shifu as a minister to preside over the affairs of the country. People in the capital were very angry. Guo Shi's father was a eloquent man who liked flattery and was greedy for wealth, but King You put him in high regard. In addition, he deposed Empress Shen and removed the prince. Marquis Shen was very angry and joined forces with Zhen and Quan Rong, who belonged to Xiyi, to attack King You. King You raised beacon fire to recruit the armies of the princes, but none of them came. Marquis Shen killed King You at the foot of Mount Li, captured Bao Si, and took away all Zhou's treasures before leaving. At that time, all the princes came to Shenhou to jointly establish Yijiu, the prince of the former Youwang, as Pingwang, in order to maintain the Zhou Dynasty's sacrificial tradition. King Ping ascended the throne and moved the capital east to Luoyi to avoid the invaders. During the reign of King Ping, the Zhou royal family declined, and powerful states annexed weak ones. Qi, Chu, Qin, and Jin began to become powerful, and political orders often came from the hegemonic monarch.
target: King Xuan restored Zhou's prestige, but King You foolishly lit beacon fires to amuse his concubine Bao Si, causing the princes to lose trust. He deposed his queen and prince, provoking Marquis Shen to join with Quanrong to attack and kill King You. King Ping moved the capital east to Luoyi. The Zhou royal family declined as powerful states like Qi, Chu, Qin, and Jin grew strong. Over subsequent generations, Zhou kings lost authority, with political orders coming from hegemonic monarchs. Eventually, Qin conquered the Western Zhou, obtaining the sacred nine tripods. Seven years later, Qin destroyed the Eastern Zhou, ending the Zhou Dynasty's sacrificial traditions.

source: Xia Yu's name was Wen Ming. Yu's father was Gun, Gun's father was Emperor Zhuanxu, Zhuanxu's father was Changyi, and Changyi's father was Huangdi. Yu is the great-great-grandson of Huangdi and the grandson of Emperor Zhuanxu. Neither Yu's great-grandfather Changyi nor his father Gun ascended to the throne, but served as ministers to the emperor. When Emperor Yao was in power, the floods were so powerful that they surrounded the mountains and covered the hills. The people were very worried about this. Yao was looking for someone who could control the floods, and all the ministers in the four mountains said that Gun could do it. Yao said: Gun, a man who disobeyed the destiny and destroyed his own people, is of no use. The four mountains all said: In comparison, among the ministers, no one is stronger than him. I hope you will let him try. So Yao followed Siyue's advice and appointed Gun to control the flood. Nine years later, floods are still raging and water control has not achieved any results. At this time, Emperor Yao asked someone else to control the floods, and he found Shun again. Shun was appointed to take charge of the emperor's government affairs and visited all directions. During his inspection, Shun saw that Gun was ineffective in controlling the floods, so he killed Gun at Yushan. Everyone in the world believed that Shun's punishment of Gun was correct. Shun also promoted Gun's son Yu to continue his father Gun's career in flood control. After Yao's death, Emperor Shun asked Siyue: Is there anyone who can fulfill Yao's cause well and hold an official position?
target: Xia Yu, also known as Wen Ming, was the great-great-grandson of Huangdi and grandson of Emperor Zhuanxu. His father Gun and great-grandfather Changyi served as ministers rather than emperors. During Emperor Yao's reign, devastating floods surrounded mountains and covered hills, causing great distress. Yao sought flood control experts, and despite his reservations about Gun's character, appointed him based on ministers' recommendations. After nine years of failed efforts, Shun, who had been appointed to manage government affairs, executed Gun at Yushan—a decision widely approved—and appointed Gun's son Yu to continue the work.

source: Therefore, he appointed Yu and said: Go and calm down the water and soil, and work hard! Yu bowed his head and thanked him, and humbly gave way to Qi, Houji and Gaotao. Shun said: You'd better go and handle your affairs quickly! Yu was smart, quick-witted, and diligent. He abided by morality and was kind and amiable. His speech was honest and trustworthy, his voice was in tune, his behavior was in line with the law, and the standards of weighing were set by Yu. He is diligent and serious, and is a model for all officials. Yu accepted Emperor Shun's order and took office together with Yi and Hou Ji. He ordered the princes and officials to recruit civilians to carry out water and soil control work. He set up signs along the way and measured the appearance of mountains and rivers. Yu was saddened by the fact that his father Gun was killed for failing to control the floods. Therefore, regardless of fatigue and exhaustion, Yu did not dare to enter his house even after passing by his house several times for thirteen years.
target: Yu, described as intelligent, diligent, and morally upright, accepted Shun's appointment alongside Yi and Hou Ji. Grieving his father's execution, Yu worked tirelessly for thirteen years, passing his home multiple times without entering. He lived frugally, invested resources in water conservancy, and used various transportation methods to survey terrain.

source: He lived simply in food and clothing, and tried his best to worship ghosts and gods. They lived in simple houses and spent their money on water conservancy projects such as building canals and digging ditches. He traveled by car on land, took a boat by water, rode a sled on muddy roads, and wore toothed shoes when walking on mountain roads. He holds a yardstick and a rope in his left hand, a rule and a rule in his right hand, and also carries instruments for measuring the four seasons and determining directions, which he uses to develop Kyushu, open up roads to Kyushu, build embankments of Kyushu lakes, and measure the veins of mountains in Kyushu. He asked Boyi to distribute rice seeds and teach the people to plant them in low-lying and humid places. Later, Houji was asked to provide relief to the people who could not ensure food and clothing. In places where food is scarce, some regions are allowed to transfer their surplus grain to food-deficient areas, so that all princes have food to eat within their borders. Yu also inspected the unique products of various places to determine their tribute, and also inspected the convenient transportation conditions of mountains and rivers in various places. Yu's journey to supervise flood control began in Jizhou. Jizhou: Hukou has been controlled, and Liangshan and its branches will be controlled next. After managing Taiyuan, it was then repaired to the south of Taiyue Mountain. After controlling Qinhuai, they continued to the Hengshui and Zhangshui areas. The soil in Jizhou is white and soft. The taxes here belong to the upper class, that is, the first class, sometimes mixed with the second class. The fields belong to the middle class, that is, the fifth class. The Changshui and Weishui rivers have been dredged, and the land around Daluze can be cultivated. The Tori tribe in the northeast paid tribute to the nobles for the skins of exotic animals. They followed the sea route to pay tribute, and when sailing south along the coast, they saw the Jieshi at the right corner, so they turned west and sailed straight into the Yellow River channel. Between Jishui and the Yellow River is Yanzhou: the nine rivers in this area have been unblocked, Leixia has accumulated into a large lake, and Yongshui and Jushui will also flow into this lake. Mulberries are planted on the land and silkworms are raised, so the people can live in the flatlands from the highlands where they moved to avoid floods. The soil of Yan is black and fertile, the vegetation on it is lush and the trees are tall. The fields here are listed in the sixth class, and the taxes are in the ninth class. After thirteen years of farming, we can be like other states. The soil here is white and fertile, the seashore is wide and contains alkali, and the fields are mostly saline-alkali land. The fields belong to the upper and lower classes, that is, the third class, and the taxes belong to the middle and upper classes, that is, the fourth class. The tributes in this area include salt, fine kudzu cloth, seafood, and stones for grinding jade, as well as silk, hemp, lead, pine, and jade-like stones from the Tai Valley. The Laiyi area can be used for grazing, so livestock products are tribute there, as well as baskets containing tussah silk used to make piano strings. Its tribute route was shipped directly from Wenshui to Jishui. The area between the coast in the east, Mount Tai in the north, and Huai River in the south is Xuzhou. The Huai River and Yishui River in this area have been controlled, and crops can be grown in Mengshan and Yushan. Ohnozawa has accumulated into a lake, the water in the Dongyuan area has receded, and the land has leveled off. The soil here is red, sticky and fertile, and the vegetation growing here is very lush. The fields were ranked in the second class, and the taxes were in the fifth class.
target: Yu distributed rice seeds, provided relief to the needy, and facilitated food transfers between regions. His flood control journey began in Jizhou, where he managed rivers and lakes, classified soil types, and established tax and tribute systems based on land fertility. Yu's efforts spanned nine provinces, each with distinct characteristics. In Jizhou, white soft soil was taxed at upper-first class with middle-fifth class fields. Yanzhou featured black fertile soil with sixth-class fields and ninth-class taxes. Xuzhou had red sticky fertile soil with second-class fields and fifth-class taxes. Yangzhou's moist soil ranked ninth-class fields with seventh-class taxes. Jingzhou's moist soil had lower-middle eighth-class fields and upper-lower third-class taxes. Yuzhou's soft fertile soil featured upper-middle fourth-class fields and upper-middle second-class taxes. Liangzhou's blue-black soil had lower-upper seventh-class fields and lower-middle eighth-class taxes. Yongzhou's yellow soft fertile soil had upper-first class fields and middle-lower sixth-class taxes. Each province contributed specific tributes, including metals, fabrics, stones, and exotic goods, transported via designated waterways.

source: Starting from Wenshan, the Yangtze River is channeled, branching off to the east as a tributary called Tuoshui River, then going east to reach Lishui River, passing through Jiujiang, and arriving at Dongling. It flows diagonally eastwards to the north, meets the water of Penglize, and continues eastward to become Zhongjiang River, and finally flows into the sea. It diverts the Dian River and flows eastward to become the Jishui River. It flows into the Yellow River. When the two rivers meet, they overflow into the Yingze River. It passes eastward through the north of Taoqiu, continues eastward to Heze River, and then flows northeastward to join the Wenshui River, and then flows northward into the sea. Starting from Tongbai Mountain, the Huai River is channeled eastward to join the Sishui River and Yishui River, and then flows eastward into the sea. The channel of the Wei River starts from Niaoshu Tongxing Mountain, goes east to join the Feng River, then east to join the Jing River, then east through Qishui and Ju River, and flows into the Yellow River. The Luoshui River is diverted from Xiong'er Mountain to the northeast to join the Jianshui River and the Xishui River, and then to the east to join the Yishui River, and then to the northeast to flow into the Yellow River. All the mountains, rivers and rivers have been tamed. From then on, the nine states were unified and everyone within the four borders could live. Roads were opened in the nine mountains, the water sources were dredged in the nine rivers, and embankments were built in the nine lakes. The princes from all over the world could come to the capital for alliance and pilgrimage.
target: Yu opened nine mountain roads and channeled nine major rivers, including the Yellow River, Yangtze River, Huai River, and Wei River, directing waters to the sea. This unified the nine provinces, enabling peaceful habitation, road construction, and tributary systems.

source: Each tax official has his or her own responsibilities, and taxes must be collected in various places. Taxes must be collected with caution and based on the fertility of the land, and must be collected within the nine states of China. He divided the princes among the nine states, gave them land and surnames, and ordered: "You must respect my virtues first, and you must not violate my various measures." The area five hundred miles away from Suifu is the key service, that is, the area that is bound and obeyed by the emperor: within three hundred miles of Suifu, one must abide by the teachings and live in peace; the area within two hundred miles away is the place where prisoners are exiled. The area five hundred miles away should be conquered as desolate areas, that is, the remote areas on the far side were guarded by the emperor; the areas within three hundred miles closer should be conquered as desolate and backward, where people could come and go without restriction; and the area within two hundred miles further away would be the place where prisoners were exiled. In this way, with the sea to the east, the desert to the west, and from north to south, the emperor's prestige and education reached the remote frontiers in all directions. So Emperor Shun gave Yu a piece of black jade representing the color of water in recognition of his merits in flood control, announcing to the world that the flood control was successful. The world will be peaceful and stable from now on. Gaotao held the official position of law enforcement sergeant and governed the people. When Emperor Shun went to court, Yu, Boyi, and Gaotao talked together in front of Emperor Shun. Gao Tao expressed his opinion and said: If you follow morality unswervingly, you can achieve wise strategies and unite your ministers. Yu said: That’s right, but what should we do?
target: Emperor Shun recognized Yu's achievements by granting him a black jade symbol. Yu, Boyi, and Gaotao discussed governance before Shun, with Gaotao emphasizing moral cultivation, understanding people, and appeasing the populace through nine virtues. Yu recounted his diligent efforts in flood control, food distribution, and land management. Shun stressed the importance of capable ministers and moral leadership, warning against decadence like Danzhu's. Yu noted his own sacrifices, including marrying Tushan's daughter and leaving his son Qi unraised, to complete water control.

source: Gao Tao therefore respected Yu's merits and ordered the world to learn from Yu. Those who disobey orders will be punished. Therefore, Shun's moral education was further developed. At this time, Kui played music, the spirits of the ancestors came to appreciate it, the princes showed courtesy to each other, birds and beasts flew and danced around the palace, and after playing "Xiao Shao" nine times, the phoenix was summoned. All the beasts danced, and all the officials were loyal and harmonious. Emperor Shun then sang: "Follow the mandate of heaven, implement virtuous government, comply with the times of heaven, and act with caution and prudence." He also sang: The ministers are high-spirited, the emperor is working hard, and the careers of all officials are prosperous! Gao Taozuo bowed his head and said loudly: You must remember to take the lead and work hard to do your duty, be careful about your laws, and handle all kinds of affairs seriously! So he continued to sing: The emperor is wise and wise, the ministers are all virtuous, and everything in the world is prosperous! He also sang: The emperor has no big ideas, the ministers are slack, and everything in the world is ruined! Emperor Shun paid homage and said, "Yes!" We will all work hard to handle our respective affairs from now on! At this time, the world respected Yu for his expertise in scale and music, and respected him as the Lord of the Gods of Mountains and Rivers, meaning an emperor who could issue orders on behalf of the Gods of Mountains and Rivers. Emperor Shun recommended Yu to heaven as the heir to the throne. Seventeen years later, Emperor Shun died. After three years of mourning, Yu took refuge in Yangcheng in order to give up the throne to Shun's son Shangjun. But all the princes in the world did not go to worship Shang Jun and came to worship Yu. Only then did Yu inherit the throne of the Son of Heaven, and he accepted the worship of all the princes from the south. His country name was Queen of Xia, and his surname was Si. After Emperor Yu established himself as emperor, he appointed Gao Tao as his successor, recommended him to heaven, and entrusted him with state affairs. However, Gao Tao died without succeeding him. Yu sealed the descendants of Gaotao in Ying and Liu, and some in Xu. Later, he used his benefits and granted him state affairs. Ten years later, Emperor Yu visited the east and arrived at Kuaiji, where he died. Spread benefit to the world. After three years of mourning, Yi gave up the throne to Yu's son Qi and went to the south of Jishan Mountain to escape. Yu's son became virtuous, and all the people in the world turned to him. When Yu died, although he passed the throne of emperor to Yi, because Yi had not been assisting Yu for long, the world did not obey him. Therefore, all the princes left Yi and went to pay homage to Qi, saying: "We will make Emperor Yu's son king." So Qi inherited the position of emperor, and this was Emperor Qi of Xia. Emperor Qi of the Xia Dynasty was the son of Yu, and his mother was a daughter of the Tushan clan. After Qi ascended the throne, some members of the Hu clan did not come to join him, so Qi went on an expedition and fought a battle at Gandi. Before the battle began, Qi made an oath called "Gan's Oath" and summoned the generals of the six armies for admonishment. Qi said: Sigh!
target: After Shun's death, Yu initially yielded to Shun's son Shangjun but ascended the throne when all princes paid homage to him, establishing the Xia dynasty with the surname Si. Yu appointed Gaotao as successor, but Gaotao died before inheriting. Yu later granted state affairs to Yi. Ten years into his reign, Yu died during an eastern inspection at Kuaiji. Yi yielded to Yu's son Qi, who became Emperor Qi of Xia after gaining universal support. Qi suppressed the Youhu clan's rebellion, issuing the "Gan's Oath" to enforce discipline. Subsequent Xia rulers included Taikang, who lost his country due to neglect; Zhongkang; and others down to Jie, the final emperor. Jie's tyranny led to his defeat by Tang, who replaced the Xia dynasty. Tang enfeoffed Xia descendants, who later received Qi in the Zhou dynasty. Sima Qian noted Yu's surname Si, with descendants adopting various clan names, and Confucius' correction of the Xia calendar. Yu's burial site at Kuaiji Mountain, meaning "accounting," commemorates his assessment of princes' merits.

source: Emperor Xiaojing was the eldest son of Emperor Xiaowen. His mother is Queen Mother Dou. When Emperor Xiaowen was in Daiguo, the former queen gave birth to three boys. When Empress Dowager Dou became favored, the former queen died, and her three sons also died one after another, so Emperor Xiaojing could succeed to the throne. On April 22, the first year of Emperor Jing's reign, a general amnesty was granted to the whole world. On the Yisi day, the people were given the first rank of nobility. In May, half of farmers’ land rent will be reduced. The Taizong Temple was built for Emperor Xiaowen. Order ministers not to congratulate him on his accession to the throne. The Xiongnu were allowed to enter the land of Dai and signed a peace treaty with the Xiongnu. In the spring of the second year, Xiao Xi, the grandson of Xiao He, the original Prime Minister, was ennobled as Marquis of Wuling, and it was stipulated that men should be registered in the book when they were twenty years old.
target: Emperor Xiaojing, eldest son of Emperor Xiaowen and Queen Mother Dou, succeeded to the throne after the former queen and her three sons died. In his first year, he granted amnesty, reduced land rent, built Taizong Temple, and signed a peace treaty with the Xiongnu. In the second year, he ennobled Xiao He's grandson and set the age of registration for men at twenty.
