source: On April 25, Queen Mother Xiaowen passed away. The kings of Guangchuan and Changsha both went to their respective kingdoms. Prime Minister Shen Tujia passed away. In August, Kaifeng Hou Taoqing, the imperial censor, was appointed prime minister. The comet appears in the northeast. In autumn, hailstorms hit Hengshan Mountain like rain. The largest hailstones were five inches long and the deepest ones were two feet deep. Yinghuo moved backwards, approaching Beichen's position, and the moon appeared in the middle of Beichen. The year star moves in reverse direction in heaven. The emperor established Nanling, Neishi and Qiyi as counties. On the twenty-second day of the first month of the third year, a general amnesty was granted to the whole world. A comet with a long ray appears in the west. The sky fire burned down the main hall and tower of Luoyang East Palace. King Liu Bi of Wu, King Liu Wu of Chu, King Liu Sui of Zhao, King Liu Xian of Jiaoxi, King Liu Biguang of Jinan, King Liu Xian of Zichuan, and King Liu Xiongqu of Jiaodong launched a rebellion and sent troops to the west. The emperor executed Chao Cuo because of this incident and sent Yuan Ang to inform the seven kingdoms. However, the seven kingdoms still did not stop their march and continued to besiege Liang State to the west. Therefore, the emperor sent General Dou Ying and Taiwei Zhou Yafu to lead troops to attack them and finally eliminated them. On June 25, the emperor pardoned the defeated soldiers and those who participated in the rebellion, including Liu Pei, the son of King Chu Yuan. The general Dou Ying was granted the title of Marquis of Wei. He established Pingluhou Liu Li, the son of King Yuan of Chu, as King of Chu.
target: Queen Mother Dou died, and officials like Shen Tujia passed away. Comets, hailstorms, and celestial anomalies occurred. In the third year, a rebellion by seven kings, including Wu and Chu, was suppressed after executing Chao Cuo. The emperor appointed Dou Ying and Zhou Yafu to lead troops, defeating the rebels. He then established new kings and marquises.

id: 史记/十二本纪/孝景本纪::group-002
article_path: 史记/十二本纪/孝景本纪
source: Prince Liu Duan was made King of Jiaoxi, and Prince Liu Sheng was made King of Zhongshan. Liu Zhi, the king of Jibei, was renamed the king of Zichuan, Liu Yu, the king of Huaiyang, was the king of Lu, and Liu Fei, the king of Runan, was the king of Jiangdu. The king of Qi, Liu Jianglu, and the king of Yan, Liu Jia, both died. In the summer of four years, the crown prince was established. The prince Liu Che was granted the title of King of Jiaodong.
target: In the fourth year, the crown prince was established, and Liu Che was made King of Jiaodong.

id: 史记/十二本纪/孝景本纪::group-003
article_path: 史记/十二本纪/孝景本纪
source: In the summer of four years, the crown prince was established. The prince Liu Che was granted the title of King of Jiaodong. On June 29th, a general amnesty was granted to the whole world. In leap September, Geyang was changed to Yangling. Checkpoints were also set up at ferries and passes, and entry and exit were based on talismans. In winter, the state of Zhao was renamed Handan County. In March of the fifth year, Yangling and Wei Bridge were built. In May, two hundred thousand coins were allocated to recruit people from all over the country to move to Yangling.
target: Reforms included setting up checkpoints at ferries. In the fifth year, Yangling was built, and people were recruited to move there.

id: 史记/十二本纪/孝景本纪::group-004
article_path: 史记/十二本纪/孝景本纪
source: In March of the fifth year, Yangling and Wei Bridge were built. In May, two hundred thousand coins were allocated to recruit people from all over the country to move to Yangling. The Jiangdu area encountered a big storm from the west, destroying twelve feet of the city wall. On the 28th, the emperor conferred the title of Longluhou on the son of the eldest princess. The title of King Guangchuan was changed to King Zhao. In the spring of the sixth year, Lieutenant Wei Wan was granted the title of Marquis of Jianling, Prime Minister Cheng Jia of Jiangdu was granted the title of Marquis of Jianping, Grand Administrator Gongsun Hunxie of Longxi County was granted the title of Marquis of Pingqu, Prime Minister Su Jia of Zhao was granted the title of Marquis of Jiangling, and the original general Luan Bu was granted the title of Marquis of Tuan. King Liang and King Chu both died. In leap September, the trees along the Chi Road were cut down and the orchid pond was filled in. In the winter of the seventh year, Prince Li Liu Rong was deposed and was granted the title of King of Linjiang. On the last day of November, there was a solar eclipse. In the spring, the prisoners and slaves who built Yangling were pardoned. Prime Minister Tao Qing was dismissed from his post. On February 16, Taiwei Tiaohou Zhou Yafu was appointed prime minister.
target: In the sixth year, several officials were ennobled. In the seventh year, Prince Li was deposed, and Zhou Yafu became prime minister.

id: 史记/十二本纪/孝景本纪::group-005
article_path: 史记/十二本纪/孝景本纪
source: On February 16, Taiwei Tiaohou Zhou Yafu was appointed prime minister. On April 17, the mother of King Jiaodong was made queen. On the 29th, King Jiaodong was established as the crown prince. The crown prince's name is Toru. In the first year of the Zhongyuan Dynasty, Zhou Ping, the grandson of the original censor Zhou Ke, was granted the title of Shenghou, and Zhou Zuoche, the grandson of the original censor Zhou Chang, was granted the title of Anyanghou. On April 23, a general amnesty was granted to the people, and the people were given first-class titles.
target: The crown prince was renamed Toru. In the first year of Zhongyuan, amnesty was granted, and restrictions on merchants and criminals were lifted.

id: 史记/十二本纪/孝景本纪::group-006
article_path: 史记/十二本纪/孝景本纪
source: The prohibition against merchants and bridal sons-in-law being allowed to serve as officials, and the prohibition against officials who have committed crimes being allowed to serve as officials again, were abolished. There was an earthquake. There was hail in Hengshan and Yuandu, with the largest diameter being one foot and eight inches. In February of the second year of the Zhongyuan Dynasty, the Xiongnu invaded Yan territory, so they no longer made peace with the Xiongnu. In March, he ordered King Linjiang to be summoned to the capital for questioning. Soon King Linjiang died in the Lieutenant's Mansion. In the summer, Prince Liu Yue was made King of Guangchuan, and Prince Liu Ji was made King of Jiaodong. Four princes were enfeoffed. On September 30, there was a solar eclipse. In the winter of the third year of Zhongyuan, the official position of Yushi Zhongcheng in the princely kingdoms was abolished. In the spring, the two kings of the Xiongnu came and surrendered with their tribes, and they were both named princes. The prince Liu Fangcheng was made King of Qinghe. In March, the comet appears in the northwest. Prime Minister Zhou Yafu was dismissed from his post and Taohou Liu She, the imperial censor, was appointed as prime minister. In April, there was an earthquake. On the last day of September, there was a solar eclipse. Troops were stationed outside the Dongdu Gate of the capital. In March of the fourth year of Zhongyuan, Deyang Palace was built. A serious locust plague occurred. In autumn, the prisoners who built Yangling were pardoned. In the summer of the fifth year of Zhongyuan, Prince Liu Shun was made King of Changshan. Ten people were enfeoffed as marquises. On June 29th, a general amnesty was granted to the people, and the common people were given first-class titles. Severe waterlogging occurred across the country. Change the name of the prime minister of the vassal kingdom to prime minister. In the fall, there was an earthquake. On February 25, the sixth year of Zhongyuan, the emperor came to Yong County to worship the Five Emperors in the suburbs.
target: Earthquakes and hail occurred. In the second year, the Xiongnu invaded, and King Linjiang died. In the third year, Xiongnu kings surrendered, and Zhou Yafu was dismissed. In the fourth year, Deyang Palace was built, and locusts plagued the land. In the fifth year, severe flooding led to renaming officials. In the sixth year, the emperor worshipped the Five Emperors, and the Liang Kingdom was divided. Official titles were reformed.

id: 史记/十二本纪/孝景本纪::group-007
article_path: 史记/十二本纪/孝景本纪
source: The official rank of Ouchi was determined to be two thousand stones, and the left inner officer and the right inner officer were set up to make them subordinate to Ouchi. On July 29, there was a solar eclipse. In August, the Huns invaded Shangjun. In the winter of the first year of Houyuan, he was renamed Zhongdafu Ling as Weiwei. On March 19, a general amnesty was granted to the people, and the people were given the title of first class. Officials with two thousand shi and the prime ministers of the princely states were given the title of right concubine.
target: In the first year of Houyuan, officials were renamed, and amnesty was granted. Earthquakes and solar eclipses occurred.

id: 史记/十二本纪/孝景本纪::group-008
article_path: 史记/十二本纪/孝景本纪
source: On May 9, there was an earthquake, and there was another earthquake during breakfast. The Shangyong earthquake lasted for twenty-two days and destroyed the city wall. On July 29, there was a solar eclipse. Prime Minister Liu She was dismissed from his post. In August, Wei Wan, the imperial censor, was appointed prime minister and granted the title of Marquis of Jianling. In the first month of the next two years, three earthquakes occurred in one day. General Zhi led his troops to attack the Xiongnu. The people were allowed to gather and feast for five days.
target: In the second year, General Zhi attacked the Xiongnu, and restrictions on grain and clothing were imposed.

id: 史记/十二本纪/孝景本纪::group-009
article_path: 史记/十二本纪/孝景本纪
source: General Zhi led his troops to attack the Xiongnu. The people were allowed to gather and feast for five days. Neishi County was ordered not to feed the horses with grain, but to return the horses to the government. Criminals and slaves were required to wear only the most coarse clothing. It is forbidden to use horses to pound rice. Due to the poor harvest that year, the people of the world were prohibited from eating the food harvested that year in advance within one year. Reduce the number of princes in the capital and send them to their own fiefdoms. In March, the Huns invaded Yanmen. In October, the cultivated land around Changling, the mausoleum of Emperor Gaozu, was rented to farmers. A severe drought occurred. The plague spread among the people of Hengshan Kingdom, Hedong County, and Yunzhong County. In October of the third year of AD, a solar and lunar eclipse occurred. The sun and moon were red for five consecutive days. On the last day of December, there was a thunderstorm. The sun appears purple. The five stars are retrograde and invade Taiweiyuan. The moon crosses the sky. On the seventeenth day of the first lunar month, Crown Prince Liu Che held a coronation ceremony.
target: Drought and plague spread. In the third year, celestial anomalies appeared, and Crown Prince Liu Che was crowned.

id: 史记/十二本纪/孝景本纪::group-010
article_path: 史记/十二本纪/孝景本纪
source: The plague spread among the people of Hengshan Kingdom, Hedong County, and Yunzhong County. In October of the third year of AD, a solar and lunar eclipse occurred. The sun and moon were red for five consecutive days. On the last day of December, there was a thunderstorm. The sun appears purple. The five stars are retrograde and invade Taiweiyuan. The moon crosses the sky. On the seventeenth day of the first lunar month, Crown Prince Liu Che held a coronation ceremony. On the 27th, Emperor Xiaojing passed away. The imperial edict granted everyone from the princes to the common people who were his father's heirs a first-class title, and each household in the world received one hundred coins. Release the palace maids and let them return to their homes, exempting them from taxes and corvee for life. The prince ascended the throne and became Emperor Xiaowu. In March, Tian Fu, the younger brother of the Empress Dowager, was granted the title of Marquis of Wu'an, and Tian Sheng was granted the title of Marquis of Zhou Yang. Yangling was set up as the mausoleum of Emperor Jing. Tai Shigong said: After the rise of the Han Dynasty, Emperor Xiaowen extended his kindness and kindness, and the people of the world were grateful and at peace. By the time of Emperor Xiaojing, there was no longer any need to worry about the rebellion of princes and kings with different surnames. However, Chao Cuo deprived the princes and kings of the same surname of their fiefdoms, causing the seven kingdoms to rebel together and jointly attack the imperial court in the west. This is because the power of the princes and kings is too strong, and Chao Cuo did not gradually weaken it when taking action. It was not until Zhufu Yan made suggestions that the power of the princes and kings weakened, and the country was finally stabilized.
target: Emperor Xiaojing died, granting titles and coins to the people, releasing palace maids. Prince ascended as Emperor Xiaowu. Tai Shigong noted that Emperor Xiaojing faced the seven kingdoms' rebellion due to strong princely power, which was later stabilized by Zhufu Yan's strategies.

id: 史记/十二本纪/孝武本纪::group-000
article_path: 史记/十二本纪/孝武本纪
source: Emperor Xiaowu was the middle son of Emperor Xiaojing, and his mother was the Queen Mother. In the fourth year of Xiaojing's reign, Emperor Wu was granted the title of King of Jiaodong as a prince. In the seventh year of Xiaojing's reign, Prince Li was deposed as King Linjiang and King Jiaodong was established as Crown Prince. Emperor Xiaojing died after reigning for sixteen years, and the prince ascended the throne, becoming Emperor Xiaowu. When Emperor Xiaowu came to the throne, he paid special attention to worshiping ghosts and gods. In the first year of Jianyuan, the Han Dynasty had been established for more than sixty years, and the world was peaceful and peaceful. Officials all hoped that the emperor would hold a Zen ceremony and change the new year-end kimono color system. The emperor also believed in Confucian scholarship and recruited talented people. Zhao Wan, Wang Zang and others were granted the title of minister because of their knowledge. They wanted to imitate ancient times and suggested that the emperor build a Mingtang in the south of the city to clarify politics and religion, and use it as a place for princes to meet the emperor. The plans they drafted for hunting tours, conferring Zen, and reforming the calendar and uniforms have not yet been completed. Encountering that Empress Dowager Dou liked the teachings of Huangdi and Laozi, but disliked Confucian scholarship, she sent people to secretly observe Zhao Wan and others' illegal profit-seeking deeds, and summoned Zhao Wan and Wang Zang to investigate the case. Zhao Wan and Wang Zang committed suicide, and many of the measures they proposed were abolished. Six years later, Queen Mother Dou died. The next year, the emperor recruited Gongsun Hong and others, who were knowledgeable people. In the second year, the emperor came to Yong County for the first time and held a suburban sacrifice in Wujie. From then on, the Suburban Festival was often held every three years. At that time, the emperor invited a divine monarch to enshrine her in the Tishi Temple in Shanglin Garden. This divine king was actually a woman from Changling who died of grief over the death of her son. After her death, the spirit appeared in her sister-in-law Wanruo. It was as if he worshiped her in his own home, and later many people went to worship her.
target: Emperor Xiaowu, the middle son of Emperor Xiaojing, ascended the throne after his father's sixteen-year reign. Upon becoming emperor, he showed particular devotion to worshipping ghosts and gods. During the early years of his reign, the Han Dynasty had enjoyed over sixty years of peace, and officials hoped the emperor would perform the Feng and Shan sacrifices to heaven and earth. The emperor, favoring Confucian scholarship, recruited talented individuals like Zhao Wan and Wang Zang, who proposed building a Mingtang for political and religious clarification. However, Empress Dowager Dou, who favored Huang-Lao teachings, opposed Confucianism, leading to Zhao Wan and Wang Zang's suicides and the abandonment of their plans. After the empress dowager's death six years later, the emperor recruited Gongsun Hong and others, and began performing suburban sacrifices every three years. The emperor invited a divine spirit, originally a woman from Changling who died grieving for her son, to be worshipped in the Shanglin Garden.

id: 史记/十二本纪/孝武本纪::group-001
article_path: 史记/十二本纪/孝武本纪
source: At that time, the emperor invited a divine monarch to enshrine her in the Tishi Temple in Shanglin Garden. This divine king was actually a woman from Changling who died of grief over the death of her son. After her death, the spirit appeared in her sister-in-law Wanruo. It was as if he worshiped her in his own home, and later many people went to worship her. The emperor's maternal grandmother Pingyuan Jun also went to worship the country, and her descendants became prominent officials. After Emperor Wu came to the throne, he invited her to the palace with generous gifts to worship her in the temple. But I could only hear her voice, but couldn't see her person. At that time, Li Shaojun came to see the emperor because he knew how to bring good fortune to the ancestral stove, eat grains instead of fire, guide spiritual energy and achieve immortality. The emperor respected him very much. Li Shaojun was recommended by the late Marquis Shenze to manage the alchemy affairs. He concealed his true age and place of birth. He often said that he was seventy years old and could drive ghosts and make people immortal. He traveled everywhere and relied on his alchemy skills to make friends with princes. He has no wife or children. People heard that he could drive away ghosts and make people immortal, so they rushed to give him gifts, so he had a lot of money, silk fabrics, clothes and food. Everyone thought that he was rich without managing the property, and did not know where he was from, so they believed in him even more and rushed to serve him. Li Shaojun is good at alchemy and is good at guessing hidden things and telling some secrets of the target person. He once had a banquet with Wu'an Hou Tianfan. There was an old man in his nineties sitting with him. Li Shaojun then said that he and the old man's grandfather visited an archery place. The old man had been with his grandfather when he was a child and recognized the place. This surprised all the guests. One time, Li Shaojun met the emperor. The emperor had an old copperware hidden in his possession and asked Shaojun. Shaojun said: This bronze vessel was displayed on the cypress bed in the tenth year of Duke Huan of Qi. Then he looked at the words engraved on the bronze vessel and found that it was indeed from the era of Duke Huan of Qi. Everyone in the palace was very surprised, thinking that Shaojun was a god and a person who was hundreds of years old. Shaojun said to the emperor: By worshiping the stove, you can attract the gods and turn the cinnabar into gold. After the gold is refined, it can be used to make eating utensils. Using these utensils can prolong your life. When you live longer, you can see the immortals on Penglai Mountain in the sea. After meeting the immortals, you can hold a Zen ceremony and you can live forever. This is what the Yellow Emperor did.
target: He also honored Li Shaojun, an alchemist who claimed to be seventy years old and capable of driving ghosts and making people immortal. Li Shaojun demonstrated his powers by identifying an ancient bronze vessel and advised the emperor to worship the stove, turn cinnabar into gold, and seek immortals on Penglai Mountain to achieve immortality. The emperor followed his advice, worshipping the stove and sending alchemists to the sea. After Li Shaojun's death, the emperor believed he had ascended to immortality and continued seeking alchemists.

id: 史记/十二本纪/孝武本纪::group-002
article_path: 史记/十二本纪/孝武本纪
source: So he conferred the title of General Wencheng on the young man, rewarded him with many things, and received him with the etiquette of receiving guests. General Wencheng said: If the emperor wants to communicate with the gods, the palace, bedding and other daily necessities are different from those used by the gods, and the gods will not come. So they made cars with clouds painted on them, and drove cars of different colors on different days to drive away evil spirits. They also built Ganquan Palace. In the middle of the palace was a stage room with paintings of many gods such as Tianyi, Earthly One, and Taiyi. Sacrificial utensils were placed to attract the gods. More than a year later, the young man's alchemy became less and less effective, and the god never came. General Wencheng wrote some words on a piece of silk and let the cow eat it. He pretended that he didn't know anything about it, and told others that there was something strange in the belly of the cow. He killed the cow and looked at it, and got the silk book. The words in the book were very weird. After that, white beam platforms, copper pillars and dew-bearing cactus were built. In the second year after Wencheng's death, the emperor became seriously ill in Dinghu Palace. The witch doctors used all kinds of prescriptions, but they could not cure his illness. A man named You Shui Fagen wrote a letter saying: There was a wizard in Shangjun, and the ghosts and spirits possessed him when he was ill. The emperor summoned him and placed him in Ganquan Palace. When the wizard gets sick, he sends someone to ask the god. Shenjun said: The emperor does not need to worry about his illness. When the illness is better, please cheer up and meet me in the sweet spring. So the emperor's illness improved a lot. He went to Ganquan Palace to offer sacrifices in person, and his illness was completely cured. The emperor granted pardon to the whole world and placed the divine king in the longevity palace. The most noble among the gods is Taiyi, and his assistants are Da Jin, Siming, etc., who all follow him. The appearance of these gods is invisible, but their voices can be heard, just like human voices.
target: Various alchemists presented methods for worshipping gods, including Bo Youji's teachings on Taiyi, the most noble god. The emperor built altars and performed sacrifices accordingly. Later, a young man named General Wencheng claimed to summon spirits and was rewarded, but his methods eventually failed, and he was executed after being caught deceiving the emperor. The emperor fell ill but recovered after consulting a wizard in Ganquan Palace, where he built the Longevity Palace and continued worshipping gods.

id: 史记/十二本纪/孝武本纪::group-003
article_path: 史记/十二本纪/孝武本纪
source: Three years later, the official in charge suggested that the year name should be named with the auspiciousness sent from heaven, instead of counting one or two. The first year of the era is called Jianyuan, the second year of Jianyuan is called Yuanguang because of the long star flowing in the sky, and the third era is called Yuanshou because of the unicorn captured during the suburban festival. In the winter of the next year, the emperor went to the outskirts of Yong County to offer sacrifices. He discussed with the ministers and said: Now I personally offer sacrifices to heaven in the outskirts of Yong County, but I have not yet worshiped Hou Tu, the God of Earth. This is inconsistent with etiquette. The officials in charge discussed with Taishi Ling Sima Tan, ancestral official Kuanshu and others: The horns of the calf used to offer sacrifices to heaven and earth should be as small as silkworm cocoons and chestnuts. Now your majesty personally offers sacrifices to Hou Tu. Hou Tu should build five altars on the circular high ground in the middle of the lake. Each altar should use a small ox to sacrifice to Dalao. After the sacrifice, all the sacrifices must be buried, and those who accompany the sacrifice must also wear yellow clothes. So the emperor drove eastward, and in accordance with the method agreed upon by Kuan Shu and others, he erected the Houtu Temple on the high hill of Fenyin. The emperor personally looked at the Houtu and worshiped it, which was the same etiquette as offering sacrifices to heaven.
target: The emperor adopted year names based on auspicious signs, such as Yuanguang and Yuanshou. He performed the Hou Tu sacrifice at Fenyin and inspected various counties.

id: 史记/十二本纪/孝武本纪::group-004
article_path: 史记/十二本纪/孝武本纪
source: Queen Kang had promiscuous behavior and was at odds with the new king. They used laws to harm each other. After Kang Hou heard that General Wencheng was dead, he wanted to please the emperor, so he sent Luan Da to rely on his relationship with Marquis Lecheng to see the emperor to discuss alchemy. Ever since the emperor killed Marquis Wencheng, he regretted letting him die so early because his alchemy skills were not fully passed down. When he saw Luan Da, the emperor was very happy. Luan Da is tall and handsome, speaks thoughtfully and strategically, dares to speak boldly, and looks calm. He said: I once traveled to and from the sea and saw immortals such as An Qisheng and Xianmen. But they all thought I was of low status and didn't believe me. He also believed that King Kang was just a prince and was not worthy of being given alchemy. I have made suggestions to King Kang several times, but King Kang refused to appoint me. My teacher once said: Gold can be made, river banks can be blocked when they break, medicine of immortality can be obtained, and immortals can be summoned. I'm just afraid of ending up like Wen Cheng. Then all methods will be silent, how dare you talk about alchemy!
target: Luan Da, recommended by Marquis Lecheng, claimed to have met immortals and was granted high honors, including marriage to a princess. However, his methods also failed, leading to his execution.

id: 史记/十二本纪/孝武本纪::group-005
article_path: 史记/十二本纪/孝武本纪
source: Since the emperor has enshrined Zen in Mount Tai and has not encountered wind and rain disasters, the locals said that the sacred mountains in Penglai will also be found. The emperor was very happy and thought that he might be able to meet the gods, so he went eastward to the seaside to look at the Penglai Immortal Island. At this time, Huo Zihou, the captain of Fengche, suddenly fell ill and died that day. The emperor then left, along the coast, heading north to Jieshi, and then patrolled from western Liaoning, passing through the northern border, to Jiuyuan. In May, the emperor returned to Ganquan Palace. The official in charge proposed that the year when Baoding appeared should be designated as Yuan Ding. Since the Fengchan ceremony was held this year, the year name should be designated as Yuanfeng, and this year would be the first year of Yuanfeng.
target: The emperor continued seeking immortals, building temples and altars, and eventually performed the Feng and Shan sacrifices at Mount Tai in the first year of Yuanfeng.

id: 史记/十二本纪/孝武本纪::group-006
article_path: 史记/十二本纪/孝武本纪
source: The emperor also put on yellow clothes and personally offered sacrifices to heaven according to the ceremony. Gong Yingdai said: Although the Yellow Emperor held a ceremony for conferring Zen in Mount Tai, Feng Hou, Feng Ju and Qi Bo asked the Yellow Emperor to confer sacrifices on Mount Tai in the East and set up a place to offer sacrifices in Mount Fan to match Fu Rui, so that they could live forever. The emperor ordered the preparation of sacrificial utensils, and when he came to Dongtai Mountain, he saw that Dongtai Mountain was short and incompatible with its reputation, so he ordered the ancestral officials to worship according to the etiquette and not hold a Zen ceremony. Later, the public servants were ordered to offer sacrifices there and wait for the gods. In the summer, the emperor returned to Mount Tai and held the five-year Zen ceremony. The etiquette was the same as before, with the addition of the etiquette of worshiping the land at Shilu Mountain. Shilu Mountain is located to the south of the foot of Mount Tai. Many alchemists said that this is where immortals live, so the emperor personally worshiped it. Five years later, the emperor went to Mount Tai to offer sacrifices, and on his way back he also offered sacrifices to Mount Chang. When the emperor built the temples Taiyi and Houtu, the emperor himself would offer sacrifices in the suburbs every three years. The Han family's Zen system established by the emperor would be held every five years. Bo Youji also petitioned to build five shrines, Taiyi, Sanyi, Mingyang, Maxing and Chixing, and the temple official Kuanshu held sacrificial ceremonies according to the prescribed time.
target: The emperor established a system of suburban sacrifices every three years and Feng and Shan ceremonies every five years.

id: 史记/十二本纪/孝武本纪::group-007
article_path: 史记/十二本纪/孝武本纪
source: These five temples, together with Taiyi and Houtu Temples, total six temples, all of which are managed by Taizhu. As for the shrines of gods such as the Eight Gods and other famous mountains and rivers such as Next Year and Fanshan, worship was performed when the emperor passed by and stopped after he left. The gods built by the alchemists each presided over the sacrifices. When the person died, the sacrifices stopped. The ancestral officials were no longer in charge of the sacrifices. Other temples were handled according to the original regulations. Now that the emperor has enshrined Zen, he will look back in the next twelve years and worship all the five mountains and four mountains. The alchemists waited and offered sacrifices to the gods, and went to the sea to visit Penglai, but to no avail. But Gongsun Qing and other alchemists who were waiting for the immortal used the giant's footprints as an excuse, but it had no effect. The emperor was getting tired of the magicians' strange and profound discussions, but he always wanted to win over them, hoping to meet the real immortals. Since then, alchemists have talked more about offering sacrifices to gods, but the effect can be seen. Tai Shigong said: I followed the emperor on his tour, worshiped the gods of heaven and earth and famous mountains and rivers, and participated in the Zen ceremony. I entered the Shrine of the Shougong Palace and listened to the blessings of sacrifices to the gods. I observed and studied the remarks of the alchemists and ancestral officials. Then I sat down and described in chronological order the things that have been done to worship ghosts and gods since ancient times, specifically revealing its superficial phenomena and inner actual conditions. People who have knowledge in the future should be able to see the situation at that time from here. As for the details of Zu Dougui, jade, coins, and the etiquette of offering sacrifices to the gods, there are specific regulations from the officials in charge.
target: Despite numerous efforts by alchemists to find immortals, none succeeded. The emperor grew tired of their claims but continued hoping to meet real immortals. Taishi Gong, who accompanied the emperor on his tours, recorded these events to reveal the true nature of the worship practices, noting that specific details of rituals were handled by the responsible officials.

source: Yin Qi's mother's name was Jian Di. She was the daughter of the You'u family and the second concubine of Emperor Ku. Jian Di and three other people went to the river to take a bath. When they saw an egg dropped by a black bird, Jian Di picked it up and swallowed it. As a result, she became pregnant and gave birth to Qi. When Qi grew up, he assisted Yu in flood control. Emperor Shun then made an appointment deed and said: Now the common people are not in harmony and the relationship between the five ethics is not smooth. If you are to serve as Situ, you must respectfully promote the education of the five ethics and take generosity as the foundation. The deed was sealed in Shang Land and given the surname Zi. Qi arose in the era of Tang Yao, Yu Shun, and Xia Yu. Its achievements were outstanding in the hearts of the people, and the people lived a stable life as a result. After Qi's death, his son Zhaoming succeeded to the throne. After Zhaoming's death, his son Xiangtu succeeded to the throne. After Xiangtu died, his son Changruo succeeded to the throne. After Chang Ruo died, his son Cao Yu succeeded to the throne. After Cao Yu's death, his son Ming succeeded to the throne. After Ming's death, his son Zhen succeeded to the throne. After Zhen died, his son Wei succeeded to the throne. After Wei's death, his son Baoding succeeded to the throne. After Baoding died, his son Baoyi succeeded him. After Bao Yi died, his son Bao B succeeded to the throne. After Bao Bing died, his son Zhu Ren succeeded to the throne. After the death of Zhu Ren, his son Zhu Gui succeeded to the throne. After Zhugui died, his son Tianyi succeeded to the throne. This is the soup. Chengtang, from Qi to Tang, had moved its capital eight times. Chengtang wrote the "Emperor's Edict" for this purpose, reporting to Emperor Ku on the situation of moving the capital. Chengtang was Fangbo in the Xia Dynasty and had the power to conquer the princes. Ge Bo did not offer sacrifices to ghosts and gods, so Cheng Tang conquered him first. Chengtang said: I have said this: People can see their own appearance from the water, and the state of governance of the country can be known from the mental outlook of the people. Yi Yin said: How wise! Only when good words are heard can moral progress be made. To govern the country and nurture the people, all those who are virtuous and do good deeds should be appointed as officials of the court. Work hard, work hard! Chengtang said to Ge Bo: If you cannot respect the destiny of heaven, I will punish you severely without mercy. So he wrote "Tang Zheng", recording the situation of Zheng Ge. Yiyin's name is Aheng. A Heng wanted to meet Cheng Tang but had no way, so he went to serve as a married servant of the Youshen family. He carried a rice pot and chopping board and used the opportunity of talking about the taste of cooking to advise Cheng Tang and persuade him to practice the royal way. Some people also say that Yi Yin was originally a hermit who was talented and virtuous but refused to be an official. Cheng Tang sent someone to hire him. After five trips, he agreed to follow Tang and tell Cheng Tang what the ancient emperors and the nine types of monarchs had done. Chengtang then appointed him to manage the state affairs. Yi Yin once left Shang Tang and went to the Xia capital. Because he saw the ugliness of the Xia Dynasty's lack of justice, he returned to Bo, the Shang capital. When he entered the city from the north gate, he met Nu Jiu and Nv Fang, the virtuous ministers of Shang Tang, so he wrote "Nv Jiu" and "Nv Fang" to describe his feelings when he left the Xia Dynasty and returned to the Shang capital. Chengtang went out and saw someone in the wild with a net set up on all sides. The person setting up the net prayed and said: May everything from heaven, everything from the earth, and everything from the four directions enter my net! Chengtang heard this and said: Hey, this way we can catch all the animals! So he asked the man to remove the three-sided net, and asked the person who set up the net to pray: If you want to go to the left, go to the left, and if you want to escape to the right, run to the right. Anyone who disobeys orders will enter my snare. When the princes heard about this, they all said: Tang Zhen is so kind and virtuous that even animals have been favored by him. At that time, Xia Jie implemented a tyrannical rule and was immoral and immoral, and the princes Kunwu and his family were in trouble again. Shang Tang then raised his troops and led the princes to conquer, and Yi Yin followed Tang. Shang Tang personally held a big ax to attack Kunwu, and then went to attack Xia Jie. Shang Tang said: You people, come here and listen to me. It's not that I dare to raise troops to cause trouble, it's because Xia Jie's crimes were extremely heinous. I also heard you say that Xia Jie was guilty. I am afraid of God and dare not not conquer.
target: Yin Qi's mother, Jian Di, was the daughter of the You'u family and the second concubine of Emperor Ku. While bathing in a river with three others, she swallowed an egg dropped by a black bird, became pregnant, and gave birth to Qi. Qi grew up to assist Yu in flood control. Emperor Shun appointed him as Situ to promote the education of the five ethics, sealed him in Shang Land, and gave him the surname Zi. Qi's achievements during the eras of Tang Yao, Yu Shun, and Xia Yu brought stability to the people. After his death, his descendants succeeded him in a long lineage, culminating in Chengtang (Tang), who moved the capital eight times. Chengtang, a Fangbo under the Xia Dynasty, first conquered Ge Bo for failing to offer sacrifices. He wrote "Tang Zheng" to record this. Yi Yin (Aheng) served Chengtang, either as a married servant or after being hired following five invitations. Yi Yin advised Chengtang on governance, left for the Xia capital, and returned to Bo, writing "Nv Jiu" and "Nv Fang." Chengtang's kindness was shown when he ordered a net set on all sides to be reduced to three, allowing animals to escape, which impressed the princes. Xia Jie's tyranny led Chengtang to raise troops, with Yi Yin following. Chengtang issued the "Tang Oath," defeated Xia Jie at Mingtiao, and conquered Sanke. He replaced the Xia social god but wrote "Xia She" to explain why it was not replaced. After the princes submitted, Chengtang ascended the throne, wrote "Tang Gao" to warn the princes, and revised the calendar to favor white.

source: He also said: If any of you does something unethical and moral, then you will not be allowed to govern the people in the country. Then you should not resent me. Tang warned the princes with these words. Yi Yin wrote "Xian Yi De", explaining that monarchs and ministers should have pure moral character; Jiu Shan wrote "Ming Ju", which talked about the laws that the people should abide by. Shang Tang then revised the calendar, changed the color of clothing, advocated white, and held court meetings during the day. After the death of Shang Tang, the prince Taiding died before he ascended the throne, so Taiding's younger brother Waibing was made emperor. This was Emperor Waibing. Emperor Waibing ascended the throne for three years. After his death, he made Waibing's younger brother Zhongren the emperor. This was Emperor Zhongren. Four years after Zhongren ascended the throne, after his death, Yiyin supported Taiding's son Taijia as emperor. Taijia, the eldest grandson of Chengtang, is Emperor Taijia. In the first year of Taijia, Yi Yin wrote "Yi Xun", "Si Ming", and "Xu Hou", which stated what should be done according to the political and religious laws. Emperor Taijia reigned for three years. His politics were unclear, his behavior was tyrannical, he did not abide by King Tang's laws, and his morals were corrupted. So Yi Yin exiled him to Tong Palace, where Tang is buried. In the next three years, Yi Yin handled government affairs on behalf of the emperor, presided over state affairs, and accepted visits from princes. Taijia lived in Tonggong for three years, reflected on and repented of his mistakes, and tried to be good again. So Yiyin welcomed Emperor Taijia back to the court and handed over the power to him. Emperor Taijia practiced virtuous government, and the princes came to submit to the Yin and Shang Dynasties, and the people were peaceful. Yi Yin admired Emperor Taijia very much, so he wrote three chapters of "Taijia Xun" to praise Emperor Taijia and called him Taizong. After Taizong's death, his son Woding succeeded to the throne. During the reign of Woding, Yi Yin passed away. Yi Yin was buried in Bodi, so Jiu Shan wanted to use Yi Yin's deeds to instruct future generations, so he wrote "Woding". When Woding died, his younger brother Tai Geng succeeded to the throne. This was Emperor Tai Geng. After Taigeng died, his son Xiaojia came to the throne; after Emperor Xiaojia passed away, his younger brother Yongji succeeded to the throne, and this was Emperor Yongji. At this time, the power of the Yin Dynasty had declined, and some princes stopped coming to court. After Yong's death, his younger brother Taiwu came to the throne. This is Emperor Taiwu. Taiwu appointed Yi Zhi as his prime minister. At that time, there was a strange phenomenon of mulberry and mulberry trees growing together in the court hall in the capital, and they grew as thick as two hands together overnight. Emperor Taiwu felt very scared and went to ask Yi Zhi. Yi Zhi said: I once heard that monsters cannot defeat virtuous people. Could it be that there are some flaws in your governance? I hope you will still improve your moral character. Taiwu followed Yi Zhi's advice, and the strange mulberry tree withered and disappeared. Yi Zhi praised Wu Xian and told him about it. Wu Xian was effective in managing the royal family's affairs. He wrote "Xianai" and "Taiwu", which recorded his achievements in governing the government and praised Emperor Taiwu's obedience and virtue.
target: After Chengtang's death, his son Taiding died before ascending, so Waibing and then Zhongren ruled briefly. Yi Yin then supported Taijia, Chengtang's grandson. Taijia's tyranny led Yi Yin to exile him to Tong Palace for three years, during which Yi Yin governed. Taijia repented, returned to power, and practiced virtuous government, earning the title Taizong. After Taizong's death, Woding succeeded, and Yi Yin died. Subsequent rulers like Tai Geng, Yong Ji, and Tai Wu saw decline, but Tai Wu's appointment of Yi Zhi and response to a strange mulberry tree event revived Yin, earning him the title Zhongzong. Later rulers like Zhong Ding, Wai Ren, He Dan Jia, and Zu Yi saw further decline and revival, with Wu Xian playing a key role.

source: After Emperor Zuyi came to the throne, Yin prospered again. Minister Wu Xian was appointed to an important position. After the death of Zu Yi, his son Emperor Zu Xin came to the throne. After the death of Emperor Zuxin, his younger brother Wojia came to the throne. This was Emperor Wojia. After Wo Jia's death, Zu Ding, the son of Wo Jia's brother Zu Xin, came to the throne. This was Emperor Zu Ding. After the death of Zuding, his younger brother Wojia's son Nangeng ascended the throne. This was Emperor Nangeng. After the death of Emperor Nangeng, Emperor Zuding's son Yangjia came to the throne. This was Emperor Yangjia. When Emperor Yangjia was on the throne, Yin's country was weak. Since the time of Emperor Zhongding, the legitimate sons have been deposed and replaced by brothers and brothers' sons. Their brothers and their sons sometimes fight with each other to obtain the throne. There has been chaos for nine consecutive generations, so the princes have not come to court again. After the death of Emperor Yangjia, his younger brother Pan Geng succeeded to the throne. This was Emperor Pan Geng. When Pan Geng was in power, the Yin Dynasty had established its capital in Amadi, north of the Yellow River. Pan Geng crossed the Yellow River and settled in Bo, Chengtang's former residence, south of the Yellow River. So far, this is the fifth time the capital has been moved, and there has never been a fixed capital. Everyone in the Yin Dynasty sighed and complained, unwilling to move again. Pan Geng then told the princes and ministers: "The great former king Chengtang and your ancestors worked together to bring peace to the world, and their laws and regulations should be abided by." If we give up and do not work hard to pursue it, how can we achieve virtue? So he crossed the Yellow River to the south bank, managed and repaired it, and obeyed and implemented Chengtang's decree. After that, the people were able to stabilize and the Yin Dynasty prospered again. The princes also came to see him one after another. This was because Pan Geng followed Cheng Tang's moral policy. After the death of Emperor Pan Geng, his younger brother Xiao Xin came to the throne. This is Emperor Xiao Xin. When Xiao Xin was in power, Yin became weak again. The people missed Pan Geng, so they wrote three chapters of "Pangeng". After Emperor Xiao Xin passed away, his younger brother Xiao Yi came to the throne. This was Emperor Xiao Yi. After the death of Emperor Xiao Yi, his son Wu Ding came to the throne. After Emperor Wu Ding came to the throne, he wanted to revive the Yin Dynasty, but there was no suitable minister to assist him. Wu Ding did not publish any political opinions for three years. Political matters were decided by Tsukasa, and he carefully observed the country's atmosphere. Wu Ding dreamed of a saint named Shuo at night. He observed the ministers and officials according to the appearance of the saint he saw in his dream, but none of them looked like the man in the dream. So he sent hundreds of officials to search among the people, and finally found him in Fu Xian. At that time, it was said that he was a slave working in Fuxian building roads. The official brought the story to Wu Ding, and Wu Ding said it was this person. After finding out the story, Wu Ding talked with him and found that he was really a sage, so he appointed him as the prime minister of the country, and the Yin country prospered in peace. Therefore, the place name Fu Xian was used as the surname of Fu Shuo, and it became Fu Shuo. Wu Ding offered sacrifices to the soup. The next day, a pheasant flew up and crowed on the ears of the tripod. Wu Ding was very frightened.
target: From Zhong Ding onward, succession disputes among brothers and sons caused nine generations of chaos, weakening Yin. Pan Geng moved the capital to Bo, Chengtang's former residence, and revived Yin by following Chengtang's decrees. After Pan Geng's death, Xiao Xin and Xiao Yi ruled weakly. Wu Ding, seeking to revive Yin, dreamed of a sage named Shuo, found him as a slave in Fu Xian, and appointed him prime minister, bringing prosperity. A pheasant crowing on a tripod during a sacrifice led Zu Ji to advise Wu Ding on morality, further strengthening Yin. Wu Ding was later called Gaozong.

source: When evil comes, good will lead to slander and slander, so the princes became more and more alienated from King Zhou. When Xibo returned to the capital, he secretly practiced virtuous governance and performed good deeds. Many people among the princes betrayed Zhou and came to join Xibo. Xibo's power became stronger and stronger, and King Zhou gradually lost his power. Prince Bigan came forward to persuade Zhou, but Zhou refused to listen. Shang Rong was a talented and virtuous man, and the people respected and loved him very much, but Zhou deposed him. When Xibo attacked the hungry country and destroyed it, Zuyi, the minister of Zhou, heard about it and resented Zhou. He was very frightened and went to Zhou to report: God has cut off the longevity of our Yin country. People who know good and bad luck use big tortoises for divination, but there are no good omens. It’s not that the late king didn’t protect our descendants, but that you, the great king, were licentious and tyrannical and cut yourself off from heaven. Therefore, God abandoned us, so that we can’t live in peace of mind. If we don’t understand God’s will, we can’t follow the ordinary laws. As a result, the people of our country all hope that the Yin Kingdom will perish. They say: Why doesn’t God show its majesty? Why haven’t God’s orders come yet? Your Majesty, what do you want to do now? Zhou said: Wasn't it that I was blessed by heaven when I was born? After Zuyi returned home, he said: Zhou can no longer be persuaded! After the death of Xibochang, King Wu of Zhou led his army to the east. When they arrived at Mengjin, the princes betrayed Yin and Zhou and came to join King Wu from eight hundred countries. The princes all said: It's time to attack Zhou! King Wu of Zhou said: You don’t know the destiny of heaven. So the class teacher returned to China. Zhou became even more promiscuous and had no end. Wei Zi repeatedly advised Zhou, but Zhou refused to listen. Wei Zi discussed with the Grand Master and the Young Master and left Yin. Bigan said: As a minister, I have to risk my life to advise. So he tried his best to persuade Zhou. Zhou was furious and said: I heard that the saint's heart has seven holes. So he cut open Bigan's chest and took out his heart to see. Jizi was frightened when he saw it, so he pretended to be crazy and became a slave. Zhou imprisoned Jizi again. The grand masters and young masters of Yin State took the sacrificial vessels and musical instruments and fled to Zhou State in a hurry. King Wu of Zhou led the princes to attack Yin Zhou. Zhou also sent troops to resist the Zhou army in Muye. On the day of Jiazi, Zhou's army was defeated. Zhou fled into the city, climbed to the deer platform, put on his precious jade clothes, ran to the fire and burned himself to death. King Wu of Zhou cut off Zhou's head and hung it on a white flagpole. King Zhou Wu executed Daji again, released the imprisoned Jizi, repaired Bigan's tomb, and commended Shang Rong's alleys. He also enfeoffed Zhou's son Wu Geng and his father, allowing him to continue to worship Yin's ancestors and order him to implement Pan Geng's virtuous government. The people of Yin were very happy. So King Wu of Zhou became the emperor. Because descendants of the Yin and Shang dynasties devalued the title of emperor, he was called king. King Wu of Zhou made the descendants of Yin princes and subordinated them to Zhou.
target: After Wu Ding's death, Zu Geng and Zu Jia ruled, with Zu Jia's promiscuity causing decline. Subsequent rulers like Lin Xin, Geng Ding, and Wu Yi saw further decline. Wu Yi's cruelty, including making a puppet and shooting a blood-filled pouch, led to his death by lightning. His son Tai Ding and then Yi ruled, with Yi's son Xin (Zhou) succeeding. Zhou was talented but tyrannical, indulging in debauchery with Daji, increasing taxes, and inventing the Pao Ge torture. He killed Jiu Hou and E Hou, imprisoned Xibo (later King Wen), who was released after bribes. Xibo practiced virtuous governance, attracting princes. Zhou's minister Bigan was killed for advising, and Jizi was imprisoned. King Wu of Zhou led a revolt, defeated Zhou at Muye, and Zhou burned himself to death. King Wu executed Daji, released Jizi, and enfeoffed Zhou's son Wu Geng. Later, Wu Geng rebelled, and King Cheng made Wei Zi the king of Song to continue Yin's lineage.

id: 史记/十二本纪/秦始皇本纪::group-000
article_path: 史记/十二本纪/秦始皇本纪
source: The First Emperor of Qin was the son of King Zhuangxiang of Qin. When King Zhuang Xiang was a hostage of Qin in Zhao, he saw Lu Buwei's concubine and liked her very much, so he married her and gave birth to the first emperor. The First Emperor was born in Handan in the first month of the forty-eighth year of King Zhao of Qin. When he was born, he was named Zheng and his surname was Zhao. At the age of thirteen, King Zhuang Xiang died, and Zheng succeeded him as King of Qin. At that time, the Qin State had annexed Ba, Shu, and Hanzhong, crossed Wan, occupied Ying, and established Nanjun; went north to the east of Shangjun, and occupied Hedong, Taiyuan, and Shangdang counties; east to Rongyang, eliminated the Western Zhou and Eastern Zhou Dynasties, and established Sanchuan County. Lu Buwei became prime minister, granted a fief of 100,000 households, and was named Marquis Wenxin. Recruiting guests and tourists, intending to annex the world. Li Si was Shiren, and Meng Ao, Wang Jue, Hegong and others were generals. The King of Qin was young and in the early days of his accession to the throne, state affairs were left to the ministers. Jinyang rebelled, and in the first year of Qin Wangzheng's reign, General Meng Ao put down the rebellion. In the second year, Duke He led his army to attack Juanyi and killed 30,000 people. In three years, Meng Ao attacked South Korea and captured thirteen cities.
target: The First Emperor of Qin, son of King Zhuangxiang of Qin, was born Zheng in Handan in the first month of the forty-eighth year of King Zhao of Qin. At thirteen, he succeeded as King of Qin after his father's death. The Qin state had already expanded significantly, annexing territories like Ba, Shu, Hanzhong, and establishing commanderies. Lu Buwei served as prime minister, with Li Si as a retainer and Meng Ao, Wang Jue, and others as generals. Due to the king's youth, state affairs were managed by ministers. In the early years of his reign, Qin faced rebellions and military campaigns. Meng Ao suppressed a revolt in Jinyang and later attacked Wei, capturing twenty cities.

id: 史记/十二本纪/秦始皇本纪::group-001
article_path: 史记/十二本纪/秦始皇本纪
source: The envoys from Qi and Zhao came to prepare a banquet with wine. Mao Jiao, a native of Qi State, advised the King of Qin: The State of Qin is taking running the world as its own responsibility, and the King has the reputation of banishing his mother and the Queen Mother. I am afraid that the princes of various countries will hear about this and rebel against the State of Qin. The King of Qin went to Yongdi to welcome the Queen Mother, returned to Xianyang, and asked her to live in Ganquan Palace again. The King of Qin carried out large-scale raids and expelled guests from the vassal states. Li Si wrote a letter to dissuade him, and the King of Qin revoked the order to expel the guests. He took the opportunity to advise King Qin. He first conquered Korea and made other vassal states fearful. So King Qin sent Li Si to attack South Korea.
target: The king faced challenges including a locust plague, famine, and a coalition attack from five states.

id: 史记/十二本纪/秦始皇本纪::group-002
article_path: 史记/十二本纪/秦始皇本纪
source: It was because he attacked Longyi, Guyi and Qingdu, and then returned to attack Jiyi. The comet appeared in the west for another sixteen days. Queen Mother Xia is dead. In the eighth year, Zhao Chengyu, the younger brother of King Zhao Zheng of Qin, led an army to attack Zhao. Tunliu rebelled. As a result, all his officers were killed and the people there were moved to Lintao. The general who came to attack Cheng Xi died, and the soldier Pu Hao who stayed in the camp rebelled again and died in battle. After his death, he was tortured by whipping his body. Fish from the Yellow River rushed to the shore in large numbers, and people drove carriages to the east to find food. Lao Ai was granted the title of Marquis Changxin. Give him the Shanyang region to live in. There are no restrictions on Lao Ai in terms of palaces, carriages and horses, clothing, gardens, and hunting. All matters, big or small, are decided by Lao Ai. Hexi and Taiyuan counties were also changed into feudal states of Lao Ai. In the ninth year, a comet appeared, sometimes shining brightly into the sky. Attack Yuanyi and Puyang of Wei State. In April, King Qin stayed in Yongdi. In Jiyou, the King of Qin held a crown ceremony and wore a sword. The conspiracy of Changxin Hou Lao Ai to cause rebellion was discovered, so she fraudulently used the seals of the King of Qin and the Queen Mother to mobilize the army and guards of the county, national cavalry, Rong Zhai leaders, and She people, planning to attack Qinian Palace and launch a rebellion. When the King of Qin learned of the news, he sent his prime ministers Changping Jun and Changwen Jun to mobilize soldiers to attack Lao'ai. In the battle at Xianyang, hundreds of people were killed and all received titles. Eunuchs who participated in the battle also received first-class titles. Lao Ai and others were defeated and fled. The King of Qin then issued an order throughout the country: Anyone who captured Lao Ai alive would be rewarded one million; anyone who killed Lao Ai would be rewarded five hundred thousand. Lao Ai and others were all captured. Twenty people, including Wei Wei Jie, Nei Shisi, Zuo Yi Jie, and Zhongda Fu Ling Qi, were all beheaded and hung. They also cut their bodies into pieces and paraded them around, wiping out their clans. Lao Ai's family members were punished for minor crimes by serving as ghost slaves. More than 4,000 people who had their titles removed and moved to Shu lived in Fangling. It's so cold this month that some people freeze to death. Yang Duanhe attacked Yanshi. The comet appeared in the west and then in the north, following the Beidou as it moved southward for eighty days. Ten years later, the Prime Minister Lu Buwei was convicted of Lao Ai's involvement and was removed from the post of Prime Minister.
target: In the eighth year, Lao Ai was granted the title of Marquis Changxin and given extensive authority. The following year, his conspiracy to rebel was discovered, leading to a battle in Xianyang. Lao Ai was captured, and his followers were executed or exiled. Lu Buwei was removed as prime minister due to his involvement.
