source: The King of Qin carried out large-scale raids and expelled guests from the vassal states. Li Si wrote a letter to dissuade him, and the King of Qin revoked the order to expel the guests. He took the opportunity to advise King Qin. He first conquered Korea and made other vassal states fearful. So King Qin sent Li Si to attack South Korea. The King of Han was very worried and discussed with Han Fei to weaken Qin's power. Wei Liao, a native of Daliang, came to Qin and advised the king of Qin: With the great power of Qin, the princes are like the monarchs of a county. But I am worried that the princes will unite and attack Qin by surprise. This is why Zhibo, Fucha and King Min perished.
target: The king implemented policies to strengthen Qin, including expelling guest officials, though Li Si's counsel led to the revocation of this order. Wei Liao advised bribing enemy officials, a strategy the king adopted.

id: 史记/十二本纪/秦始皇本纪::group-004
article_path: 史记/十二本纪/秦始皇本纪
source: An earthquake occurs. In September of the 16th year, troops were sent to take over the Nanyang area of ​​South Korea, and Teng temporarily acted as the county governor. Men were ordered to register their age. Wei State donated land to Qin State. Qin established Liyi. In the seventeenth year, Neishiteng attacked South Korea, captured Han Wangan, annexed all South Korean territory, and set up a county in its territory, named Yingchuan. An earthquake occurs. Queen Mother Huayang died. The people suffered from severe famine. In the eighteenth year, a large number of troops were sent to attack the State of Zhao. Wang Jian led the soldiers from Shangdi to capture Jingxing. Yang Duanhe led the Hanoi soldiers, Qiang Yu also led his army to attack Zhao, and Yang Duanhe besieged Handan City. In the 19th year, Wang Jian and Qiang You all captured and pacified the Dongyang area of ​​​​Zhao and captured the king of Zhao. He led his troops to prepare to attack Yan State and stationed his troops in Zhongshan. When the King of Qin came to Handan, he killed all those who had a grudge against his mother's family when he was born in the State of Zhao. The King of Qin returned to Qin from Taiyuan and Shangjun. The Empress Dowager, the mother of the First Emperor, passed away. Prince Jia of the State of Zhao led several hundred people from his clan to Dai, proclaimed himself King of Dai, and united with the army of the State of Yan eastward, stationed in Shanggu.
target: Military campaigns continued, with Wang Jian and others attacking Zhao and capturing cities. In the seventeenth year, Qin conquered Han, establishing Yingchuan Commandery. The conquest of Zhao followed, with the king personally executing those who had wronged his mother's family in Handan.

id: 史记/十二本纪/秦始皇本纪::group-005
article_path: 史记/十二本纪/秦始皇本纪
source: Prince Jia of the State of Zhao led several hundred people from his clan to Dai, proclaimed himself King of Dai, and united with the army of the State of Yan eastward, stationed in Shanggu. A severe famine occurred during this year. Twenty years ago, Crown Prince Dan of Yan State was worried about Qin's army coming to Yan State. He was panic-stricken and sent Jing Ke to assassinate the King of Qin. The King of Qin noticed this, dismembered Jing Ke's body and paraded it to the public, and sent Wang Jian and Xin Sheng to attack Yan. Yan and Dai sent troops to attack the Qin army, and the Qin army defeated the Yan army west of Yishui. In the twenty-first year, Wang Ben attacked Jingdi. He dispatched more soldiers to Wang Jian's army, defeated Prince Yan's army, captured Jicheng of Yan State, and obtained Prince Dan's head. King Yan went east to gather troops from Liaodong and proclaimed himself king there. Wang Jian excused himself from illness and retired to his hometown. Xinzheng rebelled. Lord Changping moved to Yingdi. It snowed heavily, the snow was two feet five inches deep. In the 22nd year, Wang Ben attacked Wei and dug ditches to divert water from the river to flood Daliang. The city wall of Daliang was destroyed. King Wei asked for surrender, and Qin occupied all Wei territory. In the twenty-third year, the King of Qin recruited Wang Jian again, insisted on using him, and sent him to lead the army to attack Jing State. They captured the area from the south of Chendi to Pingyu and captured King Jing. The king of Qin arrived at Yingchen on his parade. Jing general Xiang Yan established Lord Changping as King of Jing and raised troops south of the Huai River to rebel against Qin.
target: The assassination attempt by Jing Ke of Yan failed, leading to Qin's attack on Yan. Wang Jian and others captured Yan's capital and obtained Prince Dan's head. Wei was conquered by diverting rivers to flood Daliang. Jing (Chu) was attacked, with Wang Jian capturing King Jing. Xiang Yan's rebellion was suppressed, and by the twenty-fifth year, Yan, Dai, and Qi were all conquered, unifying China.

id: 史记/十二本纪/秦始皇本纪::group-006
article_path: 史记/十二本纪/秦始皇本纪
source: The King of Qin said: Remove the word "Tai" and leave the word "huang". Use the ancient word "emperor" to express status and title, and call it "emperor". Other opinions as agreed. Give the order and say: OK. Pursuing King Zhuang Xiang as the Supreme Emperor. The emperor issued an order and said: I heard that in ancient times, there were titles but no posthumous titles. In the Middle Ages, there were titles. Posthumous titles were determined after death based on the deeds during life. Doing this means that the son will talk about his father and the ministers will talk about the king. This is very meaningless. I will not adopt this approach. From then on, the posthumous law was abolished. I am the First Emperor. Counting the descendants, from the second and third generations to the ten thousand generations, the inheritance will be endless. The First Emperor deduced based on the order of succession of the five virtues, and believed that the Zhou Dynasty obtained the fire virtue, and the Qin Dynasty replaced the fire virtue of the Zhou Dynasty. Following the law of the victory of the five elements, the water virtue should now be the beginning. At the beginning of October, the first month of the new year, a group of ministers came to the court to celebrate. Clothes, banners, and festival flags are all black. Six is ​​used as the standard for number, the talisman and the dharma crown are all six inches, the chariot is six feet wide, the steps are six feet, and the chariot is driven by six horses. The river was renamed Deshui as the beginning of water virtue. Being tough and decisive in politics, being violent and harsh, deciding everything in accordance with the law, being harsh and severe, without kindness, kindness, warmth and morality, this is in line with the principles of the evolution of the Five Virtues.
target: The king declared himself the First Emperor, abolishing posthumous titles and establishing a system of succession for ten thousand generations. He adopted water virtue, with black as the color, six as the standard, and harsh laws.

id: 史记/十二本纪/秦始皇本纪::group-007
article_path: 史记/十二本纪/秦始皇本纪
source: It is not appropriate to create feudal lords. The First Emperor said: The world is suffering from endless wars because of the princes and kings. Relying on the spirit of the ancestral temple, we have just pacified the world and then established the princely states. This is creating enemies for ourselves, and seeking peace is not very difficult! Tingwei's suggestion is correct. Divide the country into thirty-six counties, with guards, lieutenants, and prisons in each county. The people renamed it Qianshou. The whole world gathers and feasts. Collected weapons from all over the world, concentrated them in Xianyang, and cast them into bells. They also cast twelve bronze figures, each weighing a thousand stones, and placed them in the palace. Unify the legal system and standards of weights and measures. It is stipulated that the distance between the two wheels of the car is the same. Writing uses a unified script. The country's territory extends from the sea and Korea in the east, to Lintao and Qiangzhong in the west, to the area where the gate opens to the north in the south, with the Yellow River as a barrier to the north, and along the Yinshan Mountains to Liaodong. Moved 120,000 wealthy families in the world to Xianyang. The mausoleums, Zhangtai and Shanglin gardens of the kings of Qin are all on the south bank of the Wei River. Every time the Qin State eliminated a vassal state, it imitated its palace and built it on the northern slope of Xianyang, adjacent to the Wei River in the south, and from the east of Yongmen to the confluence area of ​​​​the Jing River and the Wei River. Palace rooms, sky plank roads and winding pavilion roads were continuous. The beauties, bells and drums captured from the princely states were all placed inside. In the twenty-seventh year, the First Emperor visited Longxi and Northland and came to Jitou Mountain, passing by on his way back to Central China. So Xin Palace was built south of the Weishui River, and soon the Xin Palace was renamed Ji Temple, symbolizing the Tianji Star.
target: The empire was divided into thirty-six commanderies, with unified laws, weights, measures, and writing. Wealthy families were moved to Xianyang, and palaces were built imitating those of conquered states.

id: 史记/十二本纪/秦始皇本纪::group-008
article_path: 史记/十二本纪/秦始皇本纪
source: Now the emperor has unified the four seas and divided the country into counties and counties. The world is peaceful and harmonious. Carrying forward the mighty spirit of the ancestral temple, adhering to the truth, spreading kindness widely, and worthy of the title of emperor. The ministers praised the emperor's merits together and engraved them on gold and stone as a model for future generations. The inscriptions on the stone had been completed, and people from Qi such as Xu Shi wrote a letter saying that there were three sacred mountains in the sea, named Penglai, Fangzhang, and Yingzhou, where immortals lived. I hope to fast and bathe, and to seek the three sacred mountains with boys and girls. So he sent Xu Shi to select thousands of boys and girls to search for immortals in the sea. When the First Emperor returned, he passed by Pengcheng, fasted and prayed, and wanted to salvage Zhou Ding from Surabaya. Thousands of people were asked to dive into the water to look for it, but could not find it.
target: The First Emperor toured extensively, erecting stone tablets praising his achievements. He sought immortality, sending Xu Shi with boys and girls to find the elixir.

id: 史记/十二本纪/秦始皇本纪::group-009
article_path: 史记/十二本纪/秦始皇本纪
source: All affairs in the world, no matter how big or small, depended on the emperor. The emperor even used scales to weigh documents. There was a certain amount in a day, and no rest was allowed until the amount was reached. If you are greedy for power to this extent, you cannot find a magic medicine for him. So he ran away. When the First Emperor heard about the escape of Hou Sheng and Lu Sheng, he was very angry and said: I used to collect books from all over the world and burned them all if they were not suitable for the time. Many literary and alchemists were recruited to bring peace to the country. These alchemists planned to refine elixirs and obtain strange medicines. Now I heard that Han Zhong never came back after leaving. Xu Shi and others spent tens of thousands of dollars, but in the end they still didn't get the elixir, but there were some rumors about profiteering every day. I have great respect for Lu Sheng and others, and have received generous rewards. Now they are slandering me to aggravate my unkindness. I sent people to investigate some Confucian scholars in Xianyang, and some of them created weird and heresies to confuse the people.
target: He burned books and buried Confucian scholars alive, enforcing strict laws. The construction of the Epang Palace and the Lishan tomb involved hundreds of thousands of workers.

id: 史记/十二本纪/秦始皇本纪::group-010
article_path: 史记/十二本纪/秦始皇本纪
source: The officials reported state affairs as before, and the eunuchs approved what they reported from their carriages. Only the First Emperor's sons Hu Hai, Zhao Gao and five or six close eunuchs knew that the First Emperor was dead. Zhao Gao used to teach Hu Hai writing and prison laws, and Hu Hai was very close to him in private. Zhao Gao conspired with Prince Hu Hai and Prime Minister Li Si to defeat the imperial edict sealed by the First Emperor and sent it to Prince Fusu. At the same time, he falsely claimed that Prime Minister Li Si was in the sand dunes to accept the imperial edict from the First Emperor and make his son Hu Hai the crown prince. He also wrote another edict to the young masters Fusu and Mengtian, listing their crimes and ordering them to commit suicide. These things are recorded in "The Biography of Li Si". Hu Hai and others continued to move forward, so they arrived at Jiuyuan from Jingxing. Just in time for the hot weather, the First Emperor's carriages started to smell bad, so he ordered the officials to load each carriage with a stone of abalone to mix up the stench of the First Emperor's body. Hu Hai and others returned to Xianyang from Zhidao and announced the death of the First Emperor. Prince Hu Hai succeeded to the throne and became the second emperor.
target: The emperor's death was concealed, and a forged edict made Hu Hai the Second Emperor, forcing Fusu to commit suicide.

id: 史记/十二本纪/秦始皇本纪::group-011
article_path: 史记/十二本纪/秦始皇本纪
source: Yan Le still refused. The Second Emperor said: I hope to become common people with my wife and children, just like those young men. Yan Le said: I was ordered by the Prime Minister to execute you on behalf of the people of the world. Although you said a lot, I dare not report it to the Prime Minister. Yan Le directed his soldiers to attack forward. The second commits suicide. Yan Le came back to report to Zhao Gao, who summoned all the ministers and princes and told them about the killing of the second son. Zhao Gao said: Qin was originally a kingdom of vassals, and the first emperor ruled the world, so he was called the emperor. Now that the six countries have established their own political power, Qin's territory is shrinking day by day, but it is still claiming the title of emperor in vain. This is unacceptable. It is more appropriate to be king as in the past. He made the son of his second brother, Gong Ziying, the king of Qin. The second generation was buried in Yichun Garden in the south of Du County with common people's rites. Zhao Gao asked Ziying to fast, visit his ancestors in the ancestral temple, and receive the seal of King Qin. After fasting for five days, Ziying discussed with his two sons: Prime Minister Zhao Gao killed the second son in Wangyi Palace. He was afraid that the officials would punish him, so he pretended to make me king in the name of righteousness. I heard that Zhao Gao made an agreement with Chu that he would destroy the Qin clan and become king in Guanzhong. Now they ask me to fast and visit the ancestral temple. They want to kill me while I am in the ancestral temple. I told him that if he didn't go away if he was ill, the prime minister would come to me personally and kill him when he came. Zhao Gao sent people several times to invite Ziying, but Ziying refused to go. Zhao Gao came in person and said, "Visiting the ancestral temple is a big event. Why doesn't the king go?" Ziying stabbed Zhao Gao to death in the fasting palace, executed all three members of Zhao Gao's family, and showed them to the public in Xianyang. Ziying was the king of Qin for forty-six days. The Chu general Pei Gong defeated the Qin army, entered Wuguan, came to Bashang, and sent people to ask Ziying to surrender. Ziying tied his neck with a ribbon, rode on a white horse, held the emperor's seal and talisman, and surrendered beside Zhi Road. So Pei Gong entered Xianyang, closed the official offices and treasury, and returned to the army. More than a month passed. The armies of various princes arrived, and Xiang Yu, the leader of the alliance, killed Ziying and the clan of Prince Qin. Xianyang was massacred, the palaces were burned, the sons and women of Qin were captured, the treasures were plundered, and the princes divided them among themselves. After the Qin State was eliminated, its land was divided into three parts, named King Yong, King Sai, and King Zhai, known as the Three Qins. Xiang Yu was the overlord of Western Chu and was responsible for dividing the world's princes and kings. The Qin Dynasty finally perished. Five years later, the Han Dynasty unified the country.
target: The Second Emperor's reign was marked by cruelty and rebellion. Chen She's uprising spread, and Zhang Han suppressed it with convicts. Zhao Gao gained power, killing officials and princes. The Second Emperor was eventually forced to commit suicide by Zhao Gao's agents. Ziying, made king, killed Zhao Gao but soon surrendered to Liu Bang. Xiang Yu killed Ziying and the Qin clan, burning Xianyang. The Qin dynasty ended after 610 years from Duke Xiang to the Second Emperor.

source: The ancestor of Qin was the granddaughter of a descendant of Emperor Zhuanxu, named Nuxiu. While the nun was weaving, a swallow dropped an egg. The nun swallowed it and gave birth to a son. Daye married a daughter of the Shaodian tribe, named Nuhua. Nuhua gave birth to Dafei, who assisted Xia Yu in managing the soil and water. After the flood control was successful, Emperor Shun gave Yu a black jade gui in recognition of his contribution. Yu accepted the reward and said: "I can't control the floods alone, and it's also because I have a lot of money to serve as an assistant." Emperor Shun said: Ah! Dafei, you helped Yu successfully control the flood! I will give you a black flag pendant. Your descendants will prosper. Therefore, the beautiful woman named Yao was given to him as his wife. Da Fei worshiped and accepted the reward, and helped Shun tame birds and beasts. Many birds and beasts were tamed, and this person was Bai Yi. Shun gave him the surname Ying. Da Fei had two sons: one was named Dalian, the ancestor of the Niaosu family; the other was named Ruomu, the ancestor of the Fei family. Ruomu's great-great-grandson was called Fei Chang. Some of his descendants lived in the Central Plains and some in Yidi. When Fei Changsheng was Xia Jie, he left Xia and went to Shang. He drove for Shang Tang and defeated Xia Jie at Mingtiao. Dalian's great-great-grandsons were named Meng Xi and Zhong Yan. Zhong Yan looked like a bird and could speak human language. When Emperor Taiwu heard about it, he asked someone to divine it, and the result was that he would be lucky to drive the car for him, so he invited him to drive the car and marry him a wife. Since Taiwu, the descendants of Zhongyan have served the Yin State for generations, so many of the Ying surnames have become famous in the world and have become princes. Zhong Yan's great-great-grandson was named Zhong Yan, who lived in the Xirong area and defended Xicui. Feilian was born in Zhongyi. Feilian was born evil. When evil comes, he has great strength, but Fei is honest and good at running. Father and son both serve King Zhou of Yin with their bravery. King Wu of Zhou defeated Zhou and killed the evil ones together. Feilian went to the north as an envoy to Zhou. When he came back, because Zhou was dead and there was no place to report, he built an altar in Huotai Mountain to report to King Zhou. During the sacrifice, he received a stone coffin with an inscription that said: The angel Chufu survived the rebellion of the Yin Dynasty and gave you the stone coffin to glorify the clan. After Feilian died, he was buried in Huo Taishan.
target: The ancestor of Qin originated from Nuxiu, a granddaughter of Emperor Zhuanxu's descendant. While weaving, Nuxiu swallowed a swallow's egg and gave birth to Daye. Daye married Nuhua, who gave birth to Dafei. Dafei assisted Yu in flood control, and Emperor Shun rewarded him, granting him the surname Ying and a wife. Dafei's descendants included Feilian and Elai, who served King Zhou of Yin. When King Wu of Zhou defeated Zhou, Elai was killed, while Feilian died later and was buried on Huotai Mountain.

source: Feilian also had a son named Ji Sheng. Ji Sheng gave birth to Meng Zeng. Meng Zeng was favored by King Zhou Cheng and was entrusted to Gaolang. Meng Zeng gave birth to Father Heng. Hengfu gave birth to Zaofu. Zaofu was favored by King Mu of Zhou because he was good at driving. King Mu of Zhou obtained horses named Chiji, Pirates, Hualiu, Luo'er, etc., and drove them to the west for inspections. He was so happy that he never returned. When King Xu Yan rebelled, Zaofu drove King Mu for a long time, traveling thousands of miles in a day, and rushed back to Zhou to put down the rebellion. King Mu granted the city of Zhao to Zaofu, and the Zaofu family was called the Zhao family from then on. From the fifth generation of Ji Shengzhuan, the birth of Feilian, he came to Zaofu and began to live in Zhaocheng separately. Zhao Shuai is his descendant. Erelaige was Feilian's son and died young. He has a son named Nvfang. Nüfang gave birth to Pang Gao, Pang Gao gave birth to Tai Ji, Tai Ji gave birth to Da Luo, and Da Luo gave birth to Feizi. They were all favored by Zaofu and lived in Zhaocheng with the surname Zhao. Feizi lived in Quanqiu. He loved horses and other livestock and was good at raising and breeding them. The people in Quanqiu told King Xiao of Zhou about this, and King Xiao summoned Feizi and asked him to manage the horses between the Mihe and Weihe rivers. Horses were bred in large numbers. King Xiao wanted Feizi to be Daluo's heir. Marquis Shen's daughter was Da Luo's wife. She gave birth to a son, Cheng, who became his heir. Marquis Shen said to King Xiao: "In the past, my ancestor was the daughter of Lishan. She became the wife of Xuxuan, the great-grandson of Zhongyan of the Xirong tribe, and gave birth to Zhongyi. Because she was in love with the Zhou Dynasty, she joined the Zhou Dynasty and guarded the western border. Therefore, the western border was harmonious and peaceful." Now I will marry my daughter to Da Luo and give birth to an heir. The Marquis of Shen and Da Luo marry again, and all the Xirong tribe submits. Only in this way can you be crowned king. I hope you will consider it. Then King Xiao said: In the past, Boyi was in charge of livestock for Emperor Shun, and his livestock multiplied a lot, so he was granted a land grant and given the surname Ying. Now his descendants are also taming and breeding horses for me, and I will also give them land as a vassal state. He was given the land of Qin as a fief, and asked him to take over the sacrifices of the Ying family, known as Qin Ying. But he did not abolish the son born from the daughter of Marquis Shen as the heir of Daluo, so as to reconcile with Xirong. Qin Ying gave birth to Qin Hou. The Marquis of Qin died after ten years in office. The Marquis of Qin gave birth to an uncle. The uncle died after three years in office. The uncle gave birth to Qin Zhong. In the third year of Qin Zhong's reign, King Li of Zhou was immoral, and some princes rebelled. Xirong also rebelled against the royal family and destroyed the Daluo clan who lived in Quanqiu. After King Xuan of Zhou ascended the throne, he appointed Qin Zhong as a doctor to attack Xirong. Xirong killed Qin Zhong. Twenty-three years after Qin Zhong ascended the throne as Houwang, he died in the hands of Xirong. Qin Zhong had five sons, the eldest son was named Zhuang Gong.
target: Feilian's son Jisheng began a lineage that produced Zaofu, who was favored by King Mu of Zhou for his driving skills. Zaofu drove King Mu westward and later rushed back to suppress a rebellion, earning the city of Zhao as his fief, establishing the Zhao family. Feizi, a descendant, lived in Quanqiu and excelled at raising horses. King Xiao of Zhou appointed him to manage horses, and later granted him the land of Qin as a vassal state, known as Qin Ying. Qin Ying's descendants included Qin Hou, Qin Zhong, and Zhuang Gong. Qin Zhong was killed by Xirong, but his son Zhuang Gong, with Zhou's help, defeated Xirong. Zhuang Gong's son Xiang Gong succeeded him.

source: King Xuan of Zhou summoned the five Zhuang Gong brothers and gave them 7,000 soldiers. He ordered them to attack Xirong and defeated Xirong. King Xuan of Zhou then rewarded Qin Zhong's descendants again, including the fiefdom of their ancestor Daluo, Quanqiu, and appointed them as officials of Xicui. Zhuang Gong lived in Quanqiu, Xixi, Daluo's hometown. He had three sons. The eldest son was called Shifu. Shifu said: Xirong killed my grandfather Qin Zhong. I will never enter the city until I kill the king of Rong. So he led his troops to attack Xirong and gave up the position of heir to his younger brother Xiang Gong. Therefore, Duke Xiang was established as the crown prince. Duke Zhuang died in his forty-fourth year, and Prince Xiang Gong came to the throne. In the first year of Xiang AD, Duke Xiang married his sister Miao Ying to King Feng as his wife. In the second year of Duke Xiang, the Xirong besieged Quanqiu. Shifu fought against him and was finally captured by the Rong. After more than a year, the Rong people released Shifu again. In the spring of the seventh year, King You of Zhou appointed Bao Si as his queen, deposed him as the crown prince, and instead appointed Bao Si's son as the crown prince. He broke trust with the princes many times, so the princes rebelled. Quan Rong of Xirong and Shen Hou attacked the Zhou Dynasty together and killed King You at the foot of Mount Li. Qin Xianggong led his troops to rescue the Zhou Dynasty, fought effectively and achieved military exploits. In order to avoid the harassment of dog soldiers, King Ping of Zhou moved the capital eastward to Luoyi. Duke Xiang led troops to escort King Ping of Zhou. King Ping of Zhou made Duke Xiang a prince and gave him the land west of Qishan. King Ping said: Xirong is unjust and has invaded our lands in Qishan and Fengshui. If Qin can drive Xirong away, the land of Xirong will belong to Qin. King Ping made an oath with him, granted him a fiefdom, and awarded him a title. Only then did Duke Xiang make Qin a vassal state, exchange envoys with other vassal states, and send gifts of invitation and greetings to each other. They also used three black-maned and naked ponies, three oxen, and three rams to sacrifice to the Emperor of Heaven in the Western Border. In the twelfth year, Duke Xiang attacked Xirong and reached Qi, where he died. Born Wen Gong. In the first year of Wen Gong, Wen Gong lived in Xicui Palace.
target: Duke Xiang rescued the Zhou dynasty from Quan Rong attacks and escorted King Ping of Zhou eastward to Luoyi. King Ping granted Duke Xiang the title of prince and the land west of Qishan, making Qin a vassal state. Duke Xiang died in battle against Xirong. His son Wen Gong expanded territory, built cities, established rituals, and set up historians. Wen Gong's descendants included Ning Gong, Wu Gong, De Gong, Xuan Gong, Cheng Gong, and Mu Gong.

source: So Duke Mu crossed the river from Maojin, buried the corpses in Mt. Confucius, and mourned for them for three days. Duke Mu issued an oath to the entire army and said: Hey, soldiers! Listen, don't make any noise, I swear to you. I want to tell you that the ancients listened humbly to the opinions of the elderly, so they made no mistakes. Duke Mu once again reflected on his fault for not following Uncle Jian and Baili Xi's plan, so he made this oath to let future generations remember his fault. When the gentlemen heard about this, they all shed tears and said: Ah! Duke Mu of Qin was so considerate to others that he was finally blessed with the victory of Meng Ming and others. In the thirty-seventh year, Qin adopted Youyu's strategy to attack the Rong king, annexed twelve countries, opened up thousands of miles of land, and finally dominated Xirong. The emperor sent Duke Zhao to give Duke Mu a golden drum to express his congratulations. In the thirty-ninth year, Duke Mu died and was buried in Yong. A total of 177 people were buried with him. Three virtuous ministers of Qin, belonging to the Ziyu family, named Yanxi, Zhongxing, and Zhenhu, were also among the martyrs. The people of Qin mourned and wrote the poem "Yellow Bird" for him. The gentleman said: Duke Mu of Qin expanded his territory and united the country, defeated the powerful Jin in the east, and dominated the Rong and Yi in the west. However, it is appropriate that he should not be the leader of the princes and allies. After death, he did not cherish his subjects, but even took his virtuous ministers to be buried with him. After the death of the late king, it is necessary to leave behind good morals and institutions, let alone good people and virtuous ministers who win the sympathy of the people? This shows that Qin could not conquer the east. Duke Mu had forty sons, and his crown prince named him as Duke Kang. The first year of Kanggong. The previous year, when Duke Mu passed away, Duke Xianggong of Jin also died; Duke Xianggang of Jin's younger brother was named Yong, who was born to a daughter of Qin and lived in Qin. Zhao Dun, the Qing of Jin, wanted to make him king and sent a retinue to pick him up. The Qin State sent troops to escort Yong to Linghu. However, the Jin State had already established the son of Duke Xiang, but he came to attack the Qin Army. The Qin Army was defeated and fled to the Qin State. In the second year, Qin attacked Jin and occupied Wucheng to retaliate for the Battle of Linghu. In the fourth year, Jin conquered Qin and occupied Shaoliang. In the sixth year, Qin attacked Jin and occupied Jima. The two armies fought at Hequ and defeated the Jin army.
target: Duke Mu of Qin was a notable ruler. He married a daughter of Jin, captured the virtuous minister Baili Xi, and appointed him along with Jian Shu. During a famine, Qin aided Jin despite previous betrayals. When Jin attacked Qin, Duke Mu was nearly captured but was rescued by 300 men who had previously eaten his horse and been forgiven. Duke Mu captured Jin's ruler but released him after negotiations. He later helped Chong'er become Duke Wen of Jin. Duke Mu attacked Zheng but withdrew after learning of Zheng's preparedness. The Qin army was defeated by Jin at Miao Mountain. Duke Mu later adopted Youyu's strategies, attacked the Rong king, annexed twelve countries, and dominated Xirong. He died and was buried with 177 people, including three virtuous ministers.

source: Jin occupied Wucheng. In the twenty-fourth year, there was civil strife in Jin, Zhibo was killed, and his territory was divided among the three kingdoms of Zhao, Han, and Wei. In the twenty-fifth year, Zhikai and the people in Zhishi's fiefdom fled to Qin. In the thirty-third year, he attacked Yiqu and captured the king of Yiqu. In the thirty-fourth year, a solar eclipse occurred. Duke Li died and his son Duke Cao ascended the throne. In the second year of Cao Gong's reign, Nan Zheng rebelled. In the thirteenth year, Yiqu came to attack Qin and arrived in Weinan. In the fourteenth year, Duke Cao died and his younger brother, Duke Huai, succeeded him. In the fourth year of Duke Huai's reign, the concubine Chao and his ministers besieged Duke Huai, who committed suicide. The prince Huai Gong's name was Zhaozi. He died early, so the ministers made Zhaozi's son king, who was Duke Ling. Duke Ling is the grandson of Duke Huai. In the sixth year of Linggong, the Jin State built a city in Shaoliang, and the Qin army attacked the Jin State. In the thirteenth year, the Qin State built a city in Jigu. When Duke Linggong died, his son Xiangong failed to succeed him, so the uncle of Duke Linggong was appointed to mourn his son. This was Duke Jian. Duke Jian is the younger brother of Zhaozi and the son of Duke Huai. In the sixth year of Duke Jian's reign, he issued an order to allow lower-level officials to carry swords. The embankments of Luoshui were cut and built, and the walls of Chongquan City were built. After his death in the sixteenth year, his son Hui Gong came to the throne. In the twelfth year of Duke Hui's reign, his son Chuzi was born. In the thirteenth year, he attacked Shu and occupied Nanzheng. Duke Hui died and his son came to the throne. In the second year after the birth of his son, the concubine Zhang Jun took Duke Linggong's son Xiangong back from Hexi and established him as the king. Kill the son and his mother and sink them into the abyss. In the past period, the state of Qin frequently changed its monarchs, and the status of monarchs and ministers was reversed. Therefore, the state of Jin became stronger again and took away Qin's land west of the Yellow River. In the first year of Xian AD, burials with people were abolished.
target: After Duke Mu, his descendants included Kang Gong, Gong Gong, Huan Gong, Jing Gong, Ai Gong, Hui Gong, Dao Gong, Li Gong, Cao Gong, Huai Gong, Ling Gong, Jian Gong, Hui Gong, Chu Zi, and Xian Gong. During this period, Qin frequently changed rulers, and Jin grew stronger, taking Qin's land west of the Yellow River.

source: In the past period, the state of Qin frequently changed its monarchs, and the status of monarchs and ministers was reversed. Therefore, the state of Jin became stronger again and took away Qin's land west of the Yellow River. In the first year of Xian AD, burials with people were abolished. In the second year, the city wall of Yueyang City was built. In the first month of the fourth year, Gengyin, Duke Xiao was born. In the eleventh year, Zhou Taishi Danjin met with Duke Xiang and said: Zhou used to be one with Qin, but later they separated. After five hundred years of separation, they will merge again. In seventeen years together, there will be an overlord. In the sixteenth year, the peach trees bloomed in winter. In the eighteenth year, it rained gold in the oak sun. In the 21st year, he fought with Jin at Shimen and beheaded 60,000 people. The emperor gave Fu Fu as a congratulation. In the twenty-third year, he fought with the state of Wei in Shaoliang and captured Wei general Gongsun Cuo. In the twenty-fourth year, Duke Xian died, and his son, Duke Xiao, came to the throne at the age of twenty-one.
target: Duke Xian abolished live burials and built cities. His son Duke Xiao ascended the throne at age 21.

source: I feel sad every time I think of your late king's wishes. If any of the guests and ministers can come up with clever ideas to make Qin strong, I will make them high officials and give them land. Then he sent troops to surround Shaanxi City in the east and kill King Xian of the Rong tribe in the west. When Wei Yang heard that this order had been issued, he came to Qin from the west and asked to see Duke Xiao through the introduction of Jingjian. In the second year, the emperor rewarded King Qin with sacrificial meat. In the third year, Wei Yang persuaded Duke Xiao to implement reforms, formulate punishments, promote agriculture internally, strictly enforce rewards and punishments externally, and encourage soldiers to fight hard and fight to the death. Duke Xiao expressed his appreciation.
target: Duke Xiao issued an order to recruit talents to strengthen Qin. Wei Yang (Shang Yang) came from Wei and implemented reforms, establishing laws, promoting agriculture, and enforcing strict rewards and punishments.

source: In the 22nd year, Wei Yang attacked Wei and captured Wei Gongzi Yan. Wei Yang was enfeoffed as a lord, known as "Shang Jun". In the twenty-fourth year, he fought with Jin at Yanmen and captured the enemy general Wei Cuo. When Duke Xiao died, his son Hui Wenjun came to the throne. 此年，处死卫鞅。 Wei Yang had just implemented a new law in the Qin State, but the new law could not be implemented. First of all, the prince violated the law.
target: Despite opposition, the new laws were adopted. Qin built Xianyang, established counties, and expanded territory. Duke Xiao died, and his son Huiwen Jun executed Wei Yang.

source: Qin captured Wei's Ancheng and marched to Daliang. Yan and Zhao rescued Wei. The Qin army retreated. Wei Ran was dismissed as prime minister. In twenty-five years, two Zhao cities were captured. The King of Qin and the King of Han met in Xincheng, and the King of Wei met in Xinmingyi. In the twenty-sixth year, the criminals were pardoned and moved to Rang, and Ranghou was appointed prime minister again. In the twenty-seventh year, Sima Cuo attacked Chu. The criminals were pardoned and moved to Nanyang. Bai Qi attacked Zhao and occupied the Guanglang City of Dai. He also sent Sima Cuo to send troops to Longxi County to attack Chu's Qianzhong County via Shu and captured it. In the twenty-eighth year, Daliang Zaobai attacked Chu, occupied Yan and Deng, and pardoned the criminals and moved to that place. In the 29th year, Daliang Zaobai attacked Chu, occupied Ying and established it as Nanjun. The king of Chu fled. Zhou Jun came to congratulate. The King of Qin and the King of Chu met in Xiangling. Bai Qi was named Lord Wu'an. In the 30th year, Zhang Ruo, the governor of Shu County, attacked Chu, occupied Wu County and Jiangnan, and established it as Qianzhong County. In the thirty-first year, Bai Qi attacked Wei and captured two cities. The Chu people rebelled in the land south of the Yangtze River occupied by our country. In the 32nd year, Prime Minister Ranghou attacked Wei and reached Daliang. He defeated Baoyuan's army and beheaded 40,000 people. Baoyuan was defeated and fled, and Wei ceded three counties to seek peace. In the thirty-third year, Hu Yang, the guest minister, attacked Juan, Caiyang, and Changshe of Wei State and occupied them. Attacked Mangmao in Huayang, defeated the enemy army, and beheaded 150,000 people. Wei ceded Nanyang to seek peace. In the thirty-fourth year, Qin merged Wei, Han and Shangyong into one county, and moved the pardoned criminal officials of Nanyang to this place. Thirty-five years later, he helped Han, Wei, and Chu defeat Yan. Nanyang County was established. In the thirty-sixth year, Ke Qingzao attacked Qi, occupied Gang and Shou, and granted Ranghou. In the thirty-eighth year, Zhong Geng Hu Shang attacked Zhao Yu and failed to capture it. Forty years later, the crown prince died in Wei and was buried in Zhiyang. In the summer of the 41st year, he attacked Wei and occupied Xingqiu and Huai. In the forty-second year, An Guojun was established as the prince. In October, Empress Dowager Xuan died and was buried in Lishan Mountain in Zhiyang. In September, Marquis Rang left the court and returned to Taodi. Forty-three years. Wu'an Junbai attacked Han, captured nine cities, and beheaded 50,000 people. In the forty-fourth year, he attacked Han Nanyang and occupied it. In the forty-fifth year, Ben, the fifth official, attacked Han and captured ten cities. Ye Yangjun's son Kui ran away to his feudal country, but died before he arrived. In the forty-seventh year, Qin attacked Han's Shangdang County. Shangdang County surrendered to Zhao. Qin attacked Zhao again. Zhao sent troops to meet Qin. The two armies were at a stalemate. Qin sent Bai Qi, Lord Wu'an, to attack and defeated the Zhao army in Changping. All 400,000 surrendered soldiers were killed.
target: Huiwen Jun's reign saw further expansion. Zhang Yi served as prime minister. Qin attacked Shu, captured Hanzhong, and defeated Chu. King Wu succeeded Huiwen Jun but died after a weightlifting accident. His half-brother Zhaoxiang Wang became king, with Queen Mother Xuan as regent. Zhaoxiang Wang's reign was marked by extensive military campaigns. Bai Qi defeated Han and Wei at Yique, killing 240,000. Qin attacked Chu, occupied Ying, and established Nanjun. Bai Qi defeated Zhao at Changping, killing 400,000 surrendered soldiers. Qin attacked the Western Zhou, whose king surrendered. The nine tripods were moved to Qin, and the Zhou dynasty was destroyed.

source: Wei fell last, so Qin sent generals to attack Wei and captured Wucheng. The king of Han came to see him; the king of Wei also entrusted the country to Qin to obey his orders. In the fifty-fourth year, the King of Qin worshiped the Emperor of Heaven in the southern suburbs of Yongcheng. In the autumn of the fifty-sixth year, King Zhaoxiang died, and his son King Xiaowen came to the throne. The eighth son of the Tang Dynasty was respected as the Empress Dowager of the Tang Dynasty and was buried with King Zhaoxiang. The King of Han put on mourning clothes to express his condolences. The princes also sent their generals to express their condolences and attend the funeral. In the first year of King Xiaowen's reign, criminals were granted amnesty, the former king's meritorious officials were still reused, clan relatives were given preferential treatment, and the royal family's gardens were opened to the public. King Xiaowen's period of mourning expired and he ascended the throne on Jihai day in October. He died on Xinchou day in just three days, and his son King Zhuang Xiang came to the throne. In the first year of King Zhuang Xiang's reign, he granted a general amnesty to criminals. He still reused the heroes of the previous king, extended benevolence, treated relatives favorably, and extended grace to the people. The king of Eastern Zhou and the princes planned to attack Qin. Qin sent Prime Minister Lu Buwei to attack him and merge all his lands into Qin's territory. However, Qin did not interrupt his sacrificial tradition and gave the land of Yangren to Zhou Jun, allowing him to continue his sacrificial rituals. He sent Meng Ao to attack Han, and Han sacrificed Cheng Gao and Gong. Qin's territory expanded to Daliang, and Sanchuan County was established. In the second year, he sent Meng Ao to attack Zhao and pacify Taiyuan. In the third year, Meng Ao attacked Wei's Gaodu and Ji and captured them. Meng Ao also attacked Yuci, Xincheng and Langmeng of Zhao State, capturing thirty-seven cities. A solar eclipse occurs in April. Wang Lu attacked Shangdang and began to establish Taiyuan County. Wei general Wuji led the troops of the five countries to counterattack the Qin army, and the Qin army retreated to the south of the Yellow River. Meng Ao lost the battle, got rid of the siege and evacuated. On Bingwu in the fifth month, King Zhuang Xiang died, and his son Ying Zheng ascended the throne, becoming the first emperor of Qin. In the twenty-sixth year after King Yingzheng of Qin came to the throne, he began to unite the world and establish thirty-six counties, known as the First Emperor. The First Emperor died at the age of fifty-one, and his son Hu Hai ascended the throne and became the second emperor. In the third year of the Second Emperor's reign, the princes rebelled against the Qin Dynasty one after another. Zhao Gao killed the Second Emperor and made Ziying emperor. More than a month after Ziying took the throne, the princes killed him again, and the Qin Dynasty was destroyed. The detailed description can be found in "The Chronicles of Qin Shihuang". Tai Shigong said: The ancestors of Qin were named Ying. His descendants were divided into various places and took the feudal country as their surname. They include the Xu family, the Tan family, the Ju family, the Zhongli family, the Yunxiang family, the Tuqiu family, the Jiangliang family, the Huang family, the Jiang family, the Xiuyu family, the Baiming family, the Feilian family, and the Qin family. However, Qin was granted the title of Zhao City because of his ancestor Zaofu, who was also called the Zhao family.
target: Zhaoxiang Wang died, and his son Xiaowen Wang reigned only three days before dying. Zhuang Xiang Wang succeeded him, attacking Eastern Zhou and merging its lands. He died, and his son Ying Zheng became king, later known as Qin Shi Huang. He united the world, established thirty-six counties, and became the First Emperor. After his death, his son Hu Hai became the Second Emperor. In the third year of the Second Emperor's reign, princes rebelled. Zhao Gao killed the Second Emperor and made Ziying emperor. Ziying was killed by princes, and Qin was destroyed. The Grand Historian noted that Qin's ancestors were surnamed Ying, with descendants scattered across various states, taking their fiefs as surnames. Qin was granted Zhao City due to Zaofu, so they were also called the Zhao family.

id: 史记/十二本纪/项羽本纪::group-000
article_path: 史记/十二本纪/项羽本纪
source: Zhao's army was defeated, and Qin's army was stronger. What opportunity could there be to take advantage of exhaustion! Moreover, the Chu army had been defeated recently, and the king was restless, so he concentrated all the troops in the country under the general's command. The safety of the country was at stake. Nowadays, we do not care about the soldiers, but only seek selfish interests. This is not a minister who shares the same interests with the country. Xiang Yu met General Song Yi in the morning, cut off Song Yi's head in his tent, and came out to give orders to the army: Song Yi and Qi State conspired against Chu, and the King of Chu secretly ordered me to kill him. At this time, the generals were all afraid and surrendered, and no one dared to resist. It is said that the generals and their families founded the State of Chu. Now it was the general who executed the rebels again. The generals jointly elected Xiang Yu as acting general. He sent people to chase Song Yi's son, and caught up with him in Qi State and killed him. Xiang Yu sent Huan Chu to report to King Huai of Chu. King Huai of Chu made Xiang Yu the general, and both Dangyang Jun and General Pu belonged to Xiang Yu. Xiang Yu had killed the champion of Qingzi, which shocked the Chu country and became famous among the princes. He sent Lord Dangyang and General Pu to lead 20,000 soldiers across the river to rescue Julu. After the war was somewhat successful, Chen Yu asked Xiang Yu for more troops. Xiang Yu led his entire army across the river, scuttled the ships, smashed the cooking utensils, burned the camps, and carried three days of rations to show that the soldiers fought to the death and no one had any intention of coming back alive. As soon as the army arrived, they surrounded Wang Li, encountered the Qin army, fought nine battles, cut off the Qin army's corridors, and defeated the Qin army. Killed Su Jiao and captured Wang Li. Shejian refused to surrender to the Chu army and burned himself to death. At that time, the Chu army was famous among the princes. At that time, the various princes who came to rescue Zhao had more than a dozen large camps, but they did not dare to send troops easily. When the Chu army attacked, the princes and generals were watching the battle on the camp. The soldiers of the Chu army were all equal to ten. The shouts of the Chu soldiers shook the sky, and the soldiers of the princes were frightened. Having defeated the Qin army, Xiang Yu summoned all the princes and generals. They entered the camp gate and walked forward on their knees, not daring to look up. From then on, Xiang Yu became the general of the princes' armies, and all the princes surrendered to him. Zhang Han was stationed at Jiyuan and Xiang Yu was stationed at the south bank of Zhangshui River. The two armies were in a stalemate and there was no fighting. The Qin army retreated many times, and the Second Emperor sent someone to punish Zhang Han. Zhang Han was frightened and sent Chief Shi Simaxin to ask for instructions. When he arrived in Xianyang, he waited outside the door for three days. Zhao Gao did not receive him, which was a sign of distrust.
target: After Xiang Liang's death, King Huai of Chu appointed Song Yi as supreme general to rescue Zhao, with Xiang Yu as second-in-command. Song Yi stalled at Anyang for 46 days. Xiang Yu killed him for incompetence and took command, leading the army across the river after sinking ships and burning camps. They defeated the Qin army at Julu, killing Su Jiao and capturing Wang Li. The Chu army's victory made Xiang Yu the commander of all allied forces. Zhang Han, facing pressure from Zhao Gao, surrendered to Xiang Yu after negotiations. Xiang Yu appointed Zhang Han as King Yong but later executed over 200,000 Qin soldiers at Xin'an due to fears of rebellion.

id: 史记/十二本纪/项羽本纪::group-001
article_path: 史记/十二本纪/项羽本纪
source: Hangu Pass is guarded by soldiers and cannot enter. When he heard that Pei Gong had conquered Xianyang, Xiang Yu was furious and sent Dangyang Lord and others to attack the pass. Xiang Yu then entered Hangu Pass and reached the west bank of the water. Pei Gong garrisoned Ba Shang, but was unable to meet Xiang Yu. Cao Wushang, the minister on the left of Pei Gong, sent someone to tell Xiang Yu: Pei Gong wants to claim the title of King of Guanzhong, make Ziying his prime minister, and possess all the treasures. Xiang Yu was so angry that he said: "Tomorrow morning, if we feast our soldiers, we will defeat Pei Gong's army!" At this time, Xiang Yu had 400,000 troops stationed at Xinfenghongmen, and Peigong had 100,000 troops stationed at Bashang. Fan Zeng advised Xiang Yu: When Pei Gong was in Shandong, he was greedy for money, lustful and fond of beautiful women. Now that he has entered the pass, he does not accept property or get close to women. From this, it seems that his ambition is not small. I asked people to observe the clouds in the sky above him. They were all shaped like dragons and tigers, and were colorful. This was the spirit of the emperor. Attack quickly and don't miss the chance. Xiang Bo, Zuo Yin of the Chu State, was Xiang Yu's uncle and had always been friendly with Liu Hou Zhang Liang. Zhang Liang was following Pei Gong at this time, and Xiang Bo rode to Pei Gong's camp at night. He met Zhang Liang in private, told what happened, and planned to ask Zhang Liang to leave with him. He said: Don't die with them. Zhang Liang said: I was ordered by the King of Han to escort Pei Gong. Now that Pei Gong is encountered, it would be unethical to escape, so I have to tell him. Zhang Liang went in and told Pei Gong everything. Pei Gong was shocked and said, "What should we do?" Zhang Liang said: Who gave the king this idea? Pei Gong said: A boy advised me to guard Hangu Pass and not let the princes' troops come in. I can take all the land of Qin as my own and call myself the king here. I took him at his word.
target: Xiang Yu entered Hangu Pass and camped at Hongmen, where Pei Gong (Liu Bang) had already taken Xianyang. Fan Zeng urged Xiang Yu to kill Pei Gong, but Xiang Bo warned Pei Gong, who apologized at the Hongmen feast. Xiang Zhuang's sword dance failed to assassinate Pei Gong, who escaped with Fan Kuai's help. Xiang Yu later entered Xianyang, killed Ziying, burned the Qin palace, and collected treasures. He divided the empire, making Pei Gong King of Han and himself Hegemon-King of Western Chu. He moved Emperor Yi to Chen County and had him killed. Conflicts arose as Tian Rong rebelled in Qi and Chen Yu attacked Changshan. The King of Han conquered the Three Qins and marched east, leading to a prolonged war with Xiang Yu.

id: 史记/十二本纪/项羽本纪::group-002
article_path: 史记/十二本纪/项羽本纪
source: When they arrived at Xingyang, the defeated armies from all walks of life gathered together. Xiao He also recruited all the old and weak who had no residence in Guanzhong and came to Xingyang, and the momentum was revived. The Chu army set out from Pengcheng, often taking advantage of the victory to pursue defeated troops, and fought with the Han army between Jing and Suo south of Xingyang. The Han army defeated the Chu army, so the Chu army could not cross Xingyang and advance westward. King Xiang rescued Pengcheng and chased the King of Han to Xingyang. Tian Heng took the opportunity to regain the state of Qi and made Tian Rong's son Tian Guang the king of Qi.
target: The war saw numerous battles, including the Han defeat at Pengcheng and the siege of Xingyang.

id: 史记/十二本纪/项羽本纪::group-003
article_path: 史记/十二本纪/项羽本纪
source: When King Xiang heard that Long Qie's army had collapsed, he panicked and sent Wu She from Xutai to persuade the Marquis of Huaiyin. The Marquis of Huaiyin refused to obey. At this time, Peng Yue rose up against Chu again and captured Liang, cutting off the Chu army's food routes. King Xiang said to Cao Jiu, the chief minister of Haichunhou, and others: Guard Chenggao carefully. Even if the Han army challenges it, do not fight it, just do not let it advance eastward. I will definitely kill Peng Yue in fifteen days, pacify the Liang region, and then join the general. So King Xiang led his army eastward and attacked Chenliu and Waihuang during the march. Waihuang was not captured. A few days later, Waihuang surrendered. King Xiang was very angry and ordered all men over fifteen years old to go to the east of the city to prepare to kill them. The son of a retainer in Waihuang, who was only thirteen years old, went to advise King Xiang: Peng Yue used force to force the people of Waihuang. The people of Waihuang were very scared, so they temporarily surrendered and waited for the arrival of the king. When the king arrives, he traps and kills them. Do the people still want to submit? From here to the east, more than ten cities in the Liang region were fearful and no one was willing to surrender. King Xiang agreed with his words and pardoned those who were supposed to be killed by Waihuang. Everyone from Waihuang to Suiyang rushed to surrender to King Xiang after hearing the news. As expected, the Han army challenged the Chu army many times, but the Chu army did not come out to challenge. The Han army sent people to insult the Chu army in front of the battle line. They insulted the Chu army for five or six days. The great Sima was very angry and asked the soldiers to cross the Si River. The soldiers had just crossed the halfway point when the Han army attacked, defeated the Chu army and captured all the supplies of the Chu state. The great Sima Cao Jiu and the Chang Shi Xin both committed suicide on the Si River. The chief minister, Cao Jiu, was originally the warden of Qixian County, and the chief minister, Sima Xin, was originally the warden of Yueyang. They had been kind to Xiang Liang, so King Xiang trusted them. At that time, King Xiang was in Suiyang. When he heard that Haichunhou's army had failed, he led his army back. The Han army was besieging Zhongli Mei in the east of Xingyang. As soon as King Xiang arrived, the Han army was afraid of the Chu army and all retreated to dangerous areas. At this time, the Han army had many soldiers and sufficient food, but King Xiang's soldiers were exhausted and had no food. The King of Han sent Lu Jia to persuade King Xiang to release the Grand Duke, but King Xiang did not agree. The king of Han sent Duke Hou to persuade King Xiang, and King Xiang made an agreement with Han to divide the world equally, dividing the west of the chasm to go to Han, and the east of the chasm to Chu.
target: Xiang Yu's forces were weakened by defections and food shortages. After a stalemate at Guangwu, Xiang Yu agreed to divide the empire at the Hong Canal, releasing the King of Han's family. However, the King of Han broke the treaty and pursued Xiang Yu. At Gaixia, Xiang Yu's army was surrounded, and hearing Chu songs, he realized defeat was imminent. He fled with 800 cavalry, but only 28 remained at Dongcheng. After killing hundreds of Han soldiers, he committed suicide, refusing to cross the Wu River. His body was divided among five Han officers for rewards. The city of Lu surrendered only after seeing his head, and he was buried with the rites of a duke. The Han king did not kill the Xiang clan, granting some titles. Sima Qian noted Xiang Yu's rise from obscurity to dominance in three years but criticized his arrogance, abandonment of Guanzhong, and failure to learn from the past, attributing his downfall to his own faults rather than divine will.

id: 史记/十二本纪/高祖本纪::group-000
article_path: 史记/十二本纪/高祖本纪
source: He wanted to rebel again, so he executed three of his clansmen. His son Liu Hui was named King of Liang, and his son Liu You was named King of Huaiyang. In autumn and July, King Yingbu of Huainan rebelled and annexed the land of Liu Jia, King of Jing, to the east, and crossed the Huai River to the north. Liu Jiao, King of Chu, fled to Xue County. Emperor Gaozu personally went to attack him and named his son Liu Chang the King of Huainan. In October of the twelfth year, Emperor Gaozu defeated Yingbu's army in Huizhen, and Yingbu fled. Gaozu ordered other generals to pursue him. Emperor Gaozu led his army back, passed by Peixian County, and stopped.
target: Emperor Gaozu, born Liu Ji in Peixian County, was the son of Taigong and Liu Yu.

id: 史记/十二本纪/高祖本纪::group-001
article_path: 史记/十二本纪/高祖本纪
source: Gaozu was born in Zhongyangli, Fengyi, Peixian County. The surname is Liu and the courtesy name is Ji. The father's name is Taigong, and the mother's name is Liu Yu. Previously, Lady Liu had rested on the shore of the Great Lake and met God in her sleep. At this time, there were thunder and lightning, and the sky was dark and the earth was dark. Grandpa Gong went to see Lady Liu and saw a dragon on her body. Later Lady Liu became pregnant and gave birth to Gaozu. Gaozu had a high nose, a plump forehead like a dragon, a beautiful beard, and seventy-two black moles on his left leg.
target: His mother became pregnant after dreaming of meeting a god while resting by a lake, during which a dragon appeared on her body. Gaozu possessed distinctive physical features including a high nose, dragon-like forehead, beautiful beard, and seventy-two black moles on his left leg.

id: 史记/十二本纪/高祖本纪::group-002
article_path: 史记/十二本纪/高祖本纪
source: They often have lofty ambitions and do not engage in ordinary people's production operations. When he reached his prime, he tried to be an official and became the chief of the Sishui Pavilion. Every official in the court was familiar with him and was teased by him. He likes drinking and women. He often borrowed wine from Wang Lao and Wu Fu and slept drunk. Wu Fu and Wang Lao often saw a dragon above him and felt very strange. Every time Emperor Gaozu came to buy wine and stayed in the hotel to drink, the wine in the hotel sold several times more than usual.
target: He was generous, charitable, and broad-minded, with lofty ambitions that set him apart from ordinary people. As an adult, Gaozu served as the chief of Sishui Pavilion, where he became familiar with local officials and enjoyed drinking and women. He frequently borrowed wine from local establishments, where shopkeepers observed a dragon above him when he was drunk.

id: 史记/十二本纪/高祖本纪::group-003
article_path: 史记/十二本纪/高祖本纪
source: He often borrowed wine from Wang Lao and Wu Fu and slept drunk. Wu Fu and Wang Lao often saw a dragon above him and felt very strange. Every time Emperor Gaozu came to buy wine and stayed in the hotel to drink, the wine in the hotel sold several times more than usual. When a strange phenomenon was discovered, at the end of the year, these two hotels often wrote off the credit debts of Gao Zu. Emperor Gaozu once went to Xianyang to perform corvées and allowed people to watch. When he saw Qin Shihuang, he sighed and said: Ah, a real man should look like this! Lu Gong, a single father, was friendly with the magistrate of Peixian County. In order to avoid his enemies from visiting the magistrate's house, he moved his family to Peixian County.
target: During a corvée trip to Xianyang, he saw Qin Shihuang and expressed his desire to achieve similar greatness.

id: 史记/十二本纪/高祖本纪::group-004
article_path: 史记/十二本纪/高祖本纪
source: Lu Gong was a good person, so when he saw Gaozu's appearance, he respected him especially and led him to sit in the hall. Xiao He said: Liu Ji originally talked a lot but rarely achieved anything. Emperor Gaozu then teased the guests in the hall and sat at the top of the table, showing no humility. The banquet was about to end, and Duke Lu signaled Gao Zu not to leave with his eyes. Gaozu finished his drink and stayed behind. Lu Gong said: I have been good at meeting people since I was young. I have met many people, but none of them is as noble as you, Liu Ji. I hope you, Liu Ji, take care of yourself. I have a biological daughter who is willing to be your wife, Liu Ji, who holds a broom and sweeps. After the banquet, Mrs. Lu was angry with Mr. Lu and said: "At first you always wanted to make this daughter different and marry her to a noble man." Pei Ling was friendly with you and asked to marry your daughter, but you didn't agree. Why did you arbitrarily decide to marry Liu Ji? Lu Gong said: This is not what you women and children can understand. So he married his daughter to Liu Ji. The daughter of Duke Lu was Empress Lu, who gave birth to Emperor Xiaohui and Princess Lu Yuan. When Emperor Gaozu was the director of the pavilion, he once asked for leave to go home. Queen Lu and her two children were weeding in the field. An old man passed by and asked for some water. Queen Lu gave him some food.
target: Lu Gong, impressed by Gaozu's appearance at a gathering, married his daughter to him despite his wife's objections. This daughter became Empress Lu, mother of Emperor Xiaohui and Princess Lu Yuan.

id: 史记/十二本纪/高祖本纪::group-005
article_path: 史记/十二本纪/高祖本纪
source: Lu Gong said: This is not what you women and children can understand. So he married his daughter to Liu Ji. The daughter of Duke Lu was Empress Lu, who gave birth to Emperor Xiaohui and Princess Lu Yuan. When Emperor Gaozu was the director of the pavilion, he once asked for leave to go home. Queen Lu and her two children were weeding in the field. An old man passed by and asked for some water. Queen Lu gave him some food. The old man met Empress Lu and said, "My wife is a noble person in the world." Empress Lu asked him to read the faces of the two children. The old man looked at Xiaohui and said: Madam, the reason why she is so noble is because of this child. After seeing Lu Yuan, he was also a noble prime minister. The old man had already left, and Gaozu happened to come to the field from someone else's house. Empress Lu told him that a guest was passing by and showed our faces to mother and son, saying that we would both be noble people in the future. Gaozu asked where my father was, and Empress Lu said: "It's not far away." Gaozu caught up with the old man and asked him. The old man said: I met my wife and children just now, and they are all similar to you. Your appearance is beyond words. Emperor Gaozu thanked me and said: If it is true as my father said, I will never forget your kindness to me. When Emperor Gaozu became famous, he didn't even know where the old man was. When Emperor Gaozu was the director of the pavilion, he used bamboo skin as a hat. This hat was made by a thief he sent to Xue County, and he often wore it. When he became a distinguished person, he still often wore it. The so-called "Liu's crown" refers to this kind of hat. Emperor Gaozu served as the pavilion chief and sent servants to Mount Li for the county. Many of the servants fled on the way. He estimated that by the time they reached Lishan Mountain, everyone would have fled. He went to the swamp area west of Fengyi and stopped to drink. At night, Gaozu released the slaves he had escorted.
target: While serving as pavilion chief, Gaozu encountered an old man who predicted that Empress Lu and their children would become noble, and that Gaozu's own appearance was beyond description. When escorting servants to Mount Li, many fled, so Gaozu released the remaining servants and became a fugitive.

id: 史记/十二本纪/高祖本纪::group-006
article_path: 史记/十二本纪/高祖本纪
source: He estimated that by the time they reached Lishan Mountain, everyone would have fled. He went to the swamp area west of Fengyi and stopped to drink. At night, Gaozu released the slaves he had escorted. Emperor Gaozu said: "Everyone, let's go. I'm running away from now on!" Among the servants, there were more than ten young and strong men who were willing to follow Gaozu. Emperor Gaozu was drunk, so he took a small road through the swamp that night and sent a man to explore the way. The person who went out to explore the road came back and reported: There is a big snake lying across the road ahead. Please go back. Emperor Gaozu was drunk and said: "When a hero walks, there is nothing to be afraid of!" So he stepped forward, drew his sword and struck the snake, cutting it into two pieces, and the road was opened. After walking for a few miles, he got drunk and lay down to sleep. The people behind came to the place where the snake was killed and saw an old lady crying at night. People asked why she was crying. The old lady said: Someone killed my son, so I cried. People said again: Old lady, why was your son killed? The old lady said: My son, the son of the White Emperor, turned into a snake and was lying on the road. Now he was killed by the son of the Red Emperor, so I cried. People thought the old lady was dishonest and wanted to give her a hard time. The old lady suddenly disappeared. Those who were left behind arrived at the place where Gaozu was resting, and Gaozu had already woken up. They told Gaozu what had just happened. Gaozu was secretly happy and felt arrogant. Those who followed him grew in awe of him.
target: Drunk one night, he killed a large snake blocking his path. An old woman later claimed the snake was the son of the White Emperor, killed by the son of the Red Emperor, which made Gaozu secretly proud and increased his followers' awe of him.

id: 史记/十二本纪/高祖本纪::group-007

source: When some of the children in Pei County heard about this, many wanted to join him. In the autumn of the first year of Qin II, Chen Sheng and others revolted in Qixian County and established themselves as kings in Chenxian County, known as Zhang Chu. Most of the counties and counties killed their chiefs in response to Chen Sheng. The magistrate of Peixian County was frightened and wanted to respond to Chen Sheng with Peiju. The chief official Xiao He and the jailer Cao Shen said to him: As an official of the Qin Dynasty, you are now rebelling against Qin and leading the children of Peixian County. I am afraid they will not obey your orders. I hope you can gather hundreds of people who are fleeing outside. Use this power to intimidate the masses, and they will not dare to disobey your orders. The county magistrate sent Fan Kuai to summon Liu Ji. Liu Ji's team already numbered nearly a hundred people. So Fan Kuai followed Liu Ji to Peixian County. The magistrate of Peixian County regretted it again. Fearing that something might happen to Liu Ji, he closed the city gates and sent people to defend him, intending to kill Xiao He and Cao Shen. Xiao He and Cao Shen were frightened and climbed over the city wall to attach themselves to Liu Ji. Liu Ji wrote a letter on silk and sent it to the city, telling the elders of Peixian County: The world has been suffering from the tyranny of the Qin Dynasty for a long time.
target: During the Qin II period, Chen Sheng's rebellion inspired the magistrate of Peixian County to consider revolt. Following advice from Xiao He and Cao Shen, Fan Kuai was sent to summon Liu Ji. After the magistrate reneged, the elders killed him and welcomed Liu Ji, who became Duke of Pei after initially declining.

id: 史记/十二本纪/高祖本纪::group-008
article_path: 史记/十二本纪/高祖本纪
source: The flags are all red, because the snake Liu Ji killed was the son of the White Emperor, and the one who killed the snake was the son of the Red Emperor, so he respected red. So the young men and powerful officials, such as Xiao He, Cao Shen, Fan Kuai and others, recruited soldiers for Pei Gong. They gathered two to three thousand people to attack Hu Ling and Fang Yu, and then returned to defend Fengyi. In the second year of Qin II, General Chen Sheng led Zhou Zhang's army to the west to play in the water and return. Yan, Zhao, Qi, and Wei all established themselves as kings. Xiang Liang and Xiang Yu raised troops in Wu. Qin Ping, the governor of Sishui County, led his troops to surround Feng. Two days later, Peigong sent troops to fight and defeated the Qin army. Duke Pei ordered Yong Chi to guard Fengyi and led his troops to Xue. Zhuang, the governor of Sishui County, was defeated in Xue and fled to Qi. Pei Gongzuo Sima captured Zhuang, the governor of Sishui County, and killed him. Pei Gong returned to the army to fight against his father. When he arrived, there was no fighting. King Chen Sheng of Chen sent Wei people to Zhoushi to attack the city and seize the territory. The envoy from Zhoushi said to Yong Chi: "Feng, it turns out that King Liang once moved here." Now Wei has captured dozens of cities. If you, Yongchi, surrender to Wei, Wei will make you Yongchi a marquis and still garrison Fengyi. If you don't surrender, Fengyi will be slaughtered with blood. Yong Chi was originally very reluctant to submit to Pei Gong. When Wei Guo surrendered, he betrayed Pei Gong and defended Fengyi for Wei Guo. Duke Pei led his troops to attack Feng, but failed to capture it.
target: They raised two to three thousand soldiers, attacked nearby areas, and returned to defend Fengyi. When Yong Chi betrayed Pei Gong by surrendering to Wei, Pei Gong failed to recapture Fengyi and sought help from Xiang Liang, who provided additional troops.

id: 史记/十二本纪/高祖本纪::group-009
article_path: 史记/十二本纪/高祖本纪
source: In the third year of Qin II, King Huai of Chu saw that Xiang Liang's army was defeated. He was frightened, moved away from Xutai, established his capital in Pengcheng, merged the armies of Lu Chen and Xiang Yu, and took command personally. Peigong was appointed as the governor of Dang County and was granted the title of Marquis of Wu'an, commanding the army of Dang County. Xiang Yu was granted the title of Marquis of Chang'an and his title was Duke of Lu. Lu Chen was appointed Situ, and his father Lu Qing was appointed Ling Yin. Zhao requested rescue many times, so King Chu Huai sent Song Yi as his general, Xiang Yu as his second general, and Fan Zeng as his junior general, and went north to rescue Zhao. He ordered Pei Gong to march west and invade Guanzhong. An agreement was made with the generals: whoever conquers Guanzhong first will be crowned king in Guanzhong. At this time, the Qin army was strong and often took advantage of the victory to pursue, but the generals did not think it was advantageous to enter the pass first. Only Xiang Yu hated Qin for defeating Xiang Liang's army, and was so angry that he was willing to enter the pass with Peigong west. King Huai's veterans all said: Xiang Yu is agile but fierce, cunning and cruel. Xiang Yu once attacked Xiangcheng, but no one was left alive in Xiangcheng. They were all buried alive. Wherever they passed, they were slaughtered and destroyed. Moreover, the Chu army attacked and conquered many times, and King Chen and Xiang Liang failed before. It is better to send another kind-hearted elder to march westward with the call of justice and explain the truth clearly to Qin's father and brothers. Qin's father and brothers have suffered from their monarch's rule for a long time. Now if they can really get a generous elder to go to Guanzhong without bullying and tyranny, they should be able to win Guanzhong. Now Xiang Yu is so fierce that he cannot be dispatched. Only Pei Gong, who has always been a tolerant elder, can be dispatched. In the end, King Huai did not agree to Xiang Yu's request and sent Peigong to the west to attack Qin. Collecting the scattered troops of King Chen and Xiang Liang, they passed through Dang and arrived at Chengyang. They faced off against the Qin army in Gangli and defeated the two Qin troops. The Chu army sent troops to attack Wang Li and severely defeated his army. Peigong led his troops to the west, met Peng Yue in Changyi, and joined him to attack the Qin army. The battle was not won. Returning to Li County, I met Marquis Gangwu and captured his army, about 4,000 people, and merged them together. Peigong, together with the troops of Wei General Huang Xin and Wei Shentu Wu Pu, jointly attacked Changyi, but Changyi was not captured. Passing through Gaoyang on the way west. Li Shiqi was the prison gate and said: "There are many generals passing by here. I think Pei Gong is a big man, with the demeanor of a kind and elder man." So he went to seek an audience and lobby Pei Gong.
target: Pei Gong joined forces with Xiang Yu, and together they achieved military successes while suffering setbacks. After Xiang Liang's death, King Huai of Chu appointed Pei Gong as governor of Dang County and ordered him to march west into Guanzhong, promising kingship to whoever entered first. Despite Xiang Yu's desire to join, King Huai's advisors favored Pei Gong's reputation as a tolerant elder. Pei Gong collected scattered troops, defeated Qin forces, and through strategic decisions including sparing the governor of Nanyang County, gained widespread surrenders.

id: 史记/十二本纪/高祖本纪::group-010
article_path: 史记/十二本纪/高祖本纪
source: When Zhao Gao had killed Qin II, he sent people to see Pei Gong and wanted to make an agreement to carve up Guanzhong and claim the throne. Pei Gong thought it was a fraud, so he adopted Zhang Liang's strategy and sent Li Sheng and Lu Jia to lobby the Qin generals. They lured them with their own interests and took the opportunity to attack Wuguan and break the pass. He also fought with the Qin army in the south of Lantian. He added more suspects and planted more flags. No looting was allowed in the places he passed. The people of Qin were very happy. The Qin army collapsed and the Qin army was defeated. They fought again in the north of Lantian and defeated the Qin army again. Taking advantage of the victory, he pursued and completely defeated the Qin army. In October of the first year of the Han Dynasty, Pei Gong's army arrived at Bashang before the princes. The Prince of Qin rode on a plain carriage with a white horse, tied his neck with a ribbon, sealed the emperor's seal and talisman, and surrendered beside Zhi Road. Some generals advocated killing the King of Qin. Pei Gong said: King Huai of Chu sent me originally because I can be tolerant. Besides, it is unlucky to kill someone after they have already surrendered.
target: Pei Gong's army arrived at Bashang in October of the first Han year, where the King of Qin surrendered. After initially wanting to rest in the palace, Pei Gong heeded advice to seal the treasures and return to camp.

id: 史记/十二本纪/高祖本纪::group-011
article_path: 史记/十二本纪/高祖本纪
source: Pei Gong wanted to stay in the palace to rest, but after being persuaded by Fan Kuai and Zhang Liang, he sealed off the valuable treasures, property and storehouses in the Qin Palace and returned to the army. He summoned the elders and heroes from each county and said: "The elders have suffered from the harsh punishments of the Qin Dynasty for a long time. Those who slander the government will be exterminated, and those who gather to discuss will be beheaded in the streets."
target: He established the three-chapter law code, abolished harsh Qin laws, and won the people's support by refusing their offerings.

id: 史记/十二本纪/高祖本纪::group-012
article_path: 史记/十二本纪/高祖本纪
source: I plan to get a reward for this. Yafu advised Xiang Yu to attack Peigong. At that time, Xiang Yu feasted his soldiers and prepared for the battle tomorrow. At this time, Xiang Yu had 400,000 troops, which was said to be one million. Pei Gong had 100,000 troops, which he claimed were 200,000, but he was no match for Xiang Yu. It happened that Xiang Bo wanted to save Zhang Liang and went to see him at night. He persuaded Xiang Yu with reason, and Xiang Yu canceled his plan to attack Peigong. Pei Gong brought more than a hundred cavalry and rode to Hongmen to see Xiang Yu and express his apology. Xiang Yu said: This is what your Pei Gongzuo Sima Cao Wushang told me. Otherwise, why would I, Xiang Yu, do such a thing? Peigong was able to escape and return because of Fan Kuai and Zhang Liang.
target: When Xiang Yu's forces approached, Pei Gong's subordinate Cao Wushang informed Xiang Yu of his intentions, but Xiang Bo's intervention and Pei Gong's apology at Hongmen prevented conflict.

source: When they arrived at Nanzheng, many of the generals and soldiers fled back on the way. The soldiers all sang songs and wanted to return to the east. Han Xin advised the King of Han: Xiang Yu made the meritorious generals kings, while the king was made alone in Nanzheng. This was actually demoting him. The officers and soldiers in the army were all from the east of Mount Laoshan, and they were eager to return home day and night. If you take advantage of them when they are strong, you can achieve great success. When the world is at peace and everyone naturally feels at ease, it can no longer be exploited. It is better to decide to march eastward and fight for the power of the world. Xiang Yu left Hangu Pass and sent people to move to Emperor Yi. Said: In ancient times, emperors ruled over thousands of miles of land and had to live upstream. He sent envoys to move Emperor Yi to Chen County in Changsha and urged him to leave quickly. The ministers gradually betrayed Emperor Yi, so Xiang Yu secretly asked the kings of Hengshan and Linjiang to attack him and kill Emperor Yi in the south of the Yangtze River. Xiang Yu resented Tian Rong and made Qi general Tian Du the king of Qi. Tian Rong was angry and proclaimed himself king of Qi. He killed Tian Du and rebelled against Xiang Chu. He gave the general's seal to Peng Yue and asked him to raise troops in Liang to rebel against Chu. Chu sent Xiao Gongjiao to attack Peng Yue, and Peng Yue defeated Xiao Gongjiao. Chen Yu resented Xiang Yu for not making him king, so he sent Xia Sui to lobby Tian Rong and borrow troops to attack Zhang Er. Qi lent troops to Chen Yu and defeated Zhang Er, king of Changshan. Zhang Er fled and joined the king of Han. Chen Yu took King Zhao Xie back from Dai and established him as King of Zhao. King Zhao then named Chen Yu the Dai King. Xiang Yu was furious and sent troops north to attack them. In August, the King of Han used Han Xin's strategy to return from the old route and attack King Yong Zhanghan. Zhang Han met the Han army in Chencang, but King Yong was defeated and retreated. He stopped to engage in battle at Haozhen, but failed again and fled to Feiqiu. The king of Han immediately pacified Yongdi. He went east to Xianyang, led his army to besiege King Yong in Feiqiu, and sent generals to capture Longxi, Beidi and Shangjun. He sent generals Xue Ou and Wang Xiu out of Wuguan, and with the help of Wang Ling's troops stationed in Nanyang, they met the Taigong and Empress Lu in Peixian County. When Chu heard the news, he sent troops to block Yangxia so that the Han army could not advance.
target: Xiang Yu later broke the agreement, making Pei Gong King of Han in Ba, Shu, and Hanzhong. The King of Han used Han Xin's strategy to march eastward, attacking and defeating King Yong Zhanghan. Over subsequent years, the Han and Chu forces engaged in prolonged warfare with shifting fortunes. The King of Han survived assassination attempts, built alliances, and eventually defeated Xiang Yu at Gaixia, where Xiang Yu's forces heard Chu songs and were routed.

id: 史记/十二本纪/高祖本纪::group-014
