source: Haixi is Da Qin, and the southwest of Shan State leads to Da Qin. On the New Year's Day of the next year, Emperor An met with his ministers and asked him to perform music in the palace. He appointed Yong Youtiao as the Han Dynasty Commander-in-Chief, and gave him seals and ribbons as well as various amounts of gold, silver and colored silk. Qiongdu Yi was developed by Emperor Wu, who designated it as Qiongdu County. After a while, the ground sank and turned into a slop, so it was called Qiongchi, and people in the south called it Qionghe River. Later, the Qiongdu Yi rebelled again. In the sixth year of Yuanding, Han soldiers crossed the Jun River to conquer the Qiongdu Yi and made it Yue Mao County. The land in Boguo is flat and there are rice fields. On Yutong Mountain in Qingxie County, there are the Golden Horse Society and the Bade God, where light and shadow often appear. The custom in Nahuo is that most people have fun and debauchery, but they also like to sing, which is roughly similar to the people of Pangke. The Qiongdu Yi chieftains were very indulgent and it was difficult to control them. During the reign of Wang Mang, the governor of the county, Mei Gen, recruited a noble from Qiondu and appointed him as a military marquis. In the second year of Gengshi, Changgui led his tribe to attack and killed Meigen, and established himself as King of Qiong Valley, exercising the power of prefect. Later he surrendered to Gongsun Shu. After Gongsun Shu failed, Guangwu granted Changgui the title of King of Qiong Valley. In the fourteenth year of Jianwu's reign, Changgui sent an envoy to present three years' accounting records to the court. Guangwu immediately awarded Changgui the seal and ribbon of the Yuelun Prefect. In the 19th year, General Liu Shang of Wuwei attacked Yizhou Yi and passed through Yuelun. After Changgui learned about it, he suspected that once Liu Shang pacified the south, authoritarian laws would be implemented, and he could not indulge at will. So he gathered people to build a fortress, called the leaders of various ministries, and brewed a large amount of poisonous wine. He wanted to use the poisonous wine to comfort the army first, and then took the opportunity to attack Liu Shang. Liu Shang knew Chang Gui's plan, and immediately dispatched troops to occupy Qiongdu, then suddenly attacked Chang Gui, killed him, and moved his family to Chengdu. In the first year of Yongping, Gu Fuyi rebelled again. The governor of Yizhou sent troops to conquer, defeated Gu Fuyi, killed Ding and their leader, and sent their heads to the capital. Later, Zhang Xi, a native of Bajun, was the prefect. His political affairs and education were clean and fair, and he made the barbarians harmonious. Zhang Xi had been the governor for seventeen years. When he died, the Yi people loved and admired him as if they had lost their parents. More than 200 elderly people from Suqi County brought cattle and sheep to mourn Zhang Xi's birthplace, Anhan County, to build a tomb to worship him. The emperor issued an edict to praise Zhang Xi and built an ancestral hall for him. In the third year of Emperor An's reign, eight tribes including Dayang and other Yi people outside the Yue Mao border, with a total of 31,000 households and 167,620 people, admired virtue and righteousness and submitted. At that time, there were many taxes in counties and counties. In the fifth year of the Yuan Dynasty, Zhuanyi Danniu Zhong Fengli and others rebelled and killed Sui Jiuling.
target: The Qiongdu Yi were developed by Emperor Wu. During Wang Mang's reign, Changgui killed the prefect and later submitted to Gongsun Shu. Guangwu made him king, but Liu Shang killed him in Jianwu's nineteenth year. During Emperor An's reign, eight Yi tribes submitted. In Yuan's fifth year, Feng Li rebelled, and Zhang Qiao sent Yang Song to defeat him. The Yi capital was developed by Emperor Wu. During Yongping, Zhu Fu pacified over 100 countries including Bailang, with over 6 million people submitting.

In the second year of Emperor Huan Yongshou's reign, the barbarians from Shu commanderies rebelled, killing and plundering officials and people. In the second year of Yanxi, three Xiangyi people from Shu County invaded Canling and killed the county officials. In the fourth year, barbarians from the Jianwei Kingdom invaded the county. Shan Yu, the governor of Yizhou, defeated them and killed 1,400 people. The rest were disintegrated and disintegrated. source: Ran Chiyi was developed by Emperor Wu. In the sixth year of Yuanding, this area was designated as Wenshan County. In the third year of Dijie, the Yi people felt that the taxes in this county were too heavy, so Emperor Xuan eliminated Wenshan County and merged it with Shu County as the northern governor. In the mountainous area of ​​Nahuo there are six tribes of Yi people, seven tribes of Qiang people, and nine tribes of Di people, each with its own tribe. Their princes knew a lot of writing, but the laws were strict. They respect women and are matriarchal. After death, the body is burned. The climate there is mostly cold, and the ice that forms in midsummer still does not melt. Therefore, in order to avoid the cold in winter, the Yi people go to Shu County to work as servants, and in summer they escape the heat and return to their own villages. They all live close to the mountains and build houses with stones. The houses are more than ten feet high and are called "Qiong Cong". The land there is hard and salty, and does not produce grain, millet, hemp, or beans. They only rely on wheat to survive, but it is suitable for raising livestock and grazing. There is a kind of hornless cow, also called a child cow, which weighs up to a thousand kilograms and its hair can be made into ornaments. That bundle produces famous horses. There are antelopes, which can cure poisoning. There is another kind of deer that eats medicine. The feces in the intestines of pregnant young deer can also treat poisoning. There are also five-horned sheep, musk deer, felt ducks with light feathers, and livestock. People there can make woolen fabrics such as felt, banchu, qington, soap felt, and woolen fabrics. There are a wide variety of medicinal materials in that package. The ground is covered with salty soil, which can be boiled to make salt. The dogs, sheep, cows, and horses all grow very fat. To the west of Yisu there are Sanyihui and Biwanglu, and to the north are Tongshi, Beidi and Lushuihu. Outside of this is the border. During the reign of Emperor Ling, the northern part of Shu County was divided to establish Wenshan County. Zhiwuya was developed by Genyou in the sixth year of Yuan Gu. It was divided into the western part of Lulian County and combined to form Wudu County.

source: During the reign of Emperor Ling, the northern part of Shu County was divided to establish Wenshan County. Zhiwuya was developed by Genyou in the sixth year of Yuan Gu. It was divided into the western part of Lulian County and combined to form Wudu County. The terrain is dangerous and isolated, and there are hemp fields, which produce famous horses, cattle, sheep, lacquer, and honey. Di people are brave, stupid, and have no scruples. They are greedy for money and die for gain. They live in Hechi, also called Qiuchi, which has a radius of one hundred hectares and is steep and dangerous on all sides. The Di people invaded the border many times, and counties and counties conquered them, so they relied on the difficult terrain to guard it. In the third year of Yuanfeng, the Di people rebelled. The imperial court sent troops to defeat the Di people and moved them to Jiuquan County. In the first year of Emperor Zhao Yuanfeng's reign, the Di people rebelled again. The imperial court sent Jinwu Ma Shijian, Longluo Hou Han Zeng, and Dahong Lu Tian Guangming to lead the criminals under the control of Sanfu and Taichang to defeat the Di people. When Wang Mang usurped the throne and started rebellion, his people also rebelled. In the early years of Jianwu, all the Di people returned to Long and Shu. After Wei Xiao was destroyed, the leader of the Di people betrayed Gongsun Shu and surrendered to the Han Dynasty. Ma Yuan, the governor of Longxi, wrote a letter to restore the princes and leaders of the Di people, and the court gave them seals and ribbons. Later, Kai Mao, a kinsman of Kai Xiao's, rebelled and killed the governor of Wudu. Qi Zhongliu, the great leader of the Di people, was respected and trusted by the people in the tribe. His prestige convinced many leaders. He and the county prime minister Kong Fen attacked Wei Mao, defeated and killed him. Later, the Di people also invaded from time to time and were conquered and defeated by the counties. The argument goes: Liu Mo's expedition against Rong and Di and his use of troops in remote areas generally began and ended with the emperor's achievements. Sometimes the border was lost, the army was destroyed, and the generals were defeated. But within a year, they were finally able to open up the lands of the barbarians from all directions and make the races with different customs submit. As for the places moistened by documents and covenants, and affected by weathering and prestige, it almost extends to all areas where the sun rises and sets. Classics, starting from Shan Jing and Shui Zhi, also briefly mention this aspect. Although the Yi people from all over the world surrendered and rebelled erratically, and the prestige and favor of the imperial court were often interrupted, as long as the education was implemented, whether it was a tribe with lop-eared eagle feet or a tribe that lived like wild beasts and spoke like a raven, they all submitted to the Central Plains as an entire tribe. Therefore, their names are recorded in the official offices of Zhonglang General and Xiaowei, and their numbers are included in the official lists of meritorious officials under the Duhufu, Buduwei, and Prefectures. The population is often calculated in millions. As for the divine objects hidden deep in the mountains, hidden under the sea, and the treasures buried in sand and stone and inhabiting the land, they all showed strange and gorgeous features and were decorated in the palace curtains. Tributes such as warnings, fire orders, domesticated birds and tall beasts were gathered in the imperial treasury; arts with completely different sound and rhythm, such as Yi people's songs and Bayu dances, were displayed outside the palace gate. Is the way of submission complete at this point? However, it can also be said that it has attracted the submission of races from far away. Although the barbarians lived on the mountains, rocks and valleys, most of them lived in certain areas, connected to Jingzhou and Jiaozhou areas, and were distributed and guarded outside Bajun and Yong. It is impossible to calculate their number. However, the barbarians were ferocious and cunning and slightly weaker than the Qiang and Di, so the harm caused by their plundering and cruelty could not go far. The barbarians outside the southwest border are especially weak. Therefore, setting up a garrison in Yongchang was initially to guard against the barbarians from far away. Later, it opened up the land and made the people self-reliant. Now it has become a city. Zan said: The area inhabited by various barbarians is very small, but it is spread all over the four borders. Sculpted bodies, wearing straw clothes, relying on the deep and rugged mountain life. There are also some Yi people living in the border areas of Shu County. The scattered tribal villages have turned to Zhou Qi's path of morality and justice. Once they gained trust by going to teach, the barbarians changed their clothes and brought treasures, which led the imperial court to establish Yongchang County and include the barbarians in household registers along with hundreds of millions of people in the mainland.

source: Wu Hanzi Ziyan was born in Wan County, Nanyang County. His family was poor and he worked as the county pavilion chief. In Wang Mang's last years, because his guests broke the law, he took off his name and fled to Yuyang. Due to lack of funds, he made a living by selling horses. He traveled between Yan and Ji, and made friends with heroes wherever he went. Gengshi ascended the throne and sent envoy Han Hong to Hebei to recruit surrender. Someone said to Han Hong, "Wu Ziyan is a wonderful man. You can discuss matters with him." Han Hong summoned Wu Han and was very happy. He appointed him as the magistrate of Anle County according to the emperor's order. Coinciding with the rise of Wang Lang, Beizhou was disturbed and confused. Wu Han had always heard that Guangwu was an elder, and he wanted to return to Guangwu. He told the prefect Peng Chong: The cavalry in Yuyang and Shanggu that attack the enemy are famous all over the world. Why don't you gather the elites from the two counties and join Liu Gong to attack Handan? This is a rare achievement. Peng Chong thought it was right, but the officials below all wanted to join Wang Lang, and Peng Chong could not take away his ambition. Wu Han then resigned and stayed in the outer pavilion, trying to blackmail everyone, but he still couldn't figure out a way. Seeing a man who looked like a Confucian scholar on the road, Wu Han sent people to summon him, provided him with food, and asked him what he had heard. Therefore, Confucian scholars said that wherever Liu Gong went, all counties and counties were devoted to him; the man in Handan who arrogantly claimed the title was indeed not a member of the Liu family. Wu Han was overjoyed, so he pretended to be a letter written by Guangwu himself, and sent it to Yuyang. He sent a Confucian scholar to Peng Chong and asked him to convince Peng Chong of what he had heard. Wu Han also followed him to Yuyang. Peng Chong was very satisfied. So Wu Han was sent to lead his troops and the generals from Shanggu to the south, killing General Wang Lang wherever they went. After chasing Guangwu in Guang'a, he worshiped Wu Han as a partial general. After conquering Handan, he was given the title of Marquis Jiance. Wu Han was a man of loyal nature but lacked literary talent and could not express his thoughts in words in a hurry. Deng Yu and other generals knew him well and recommended him many times. When he was summoned, Guangwu trusted him and often lived under his door. General Guang sent troops to Youzhou and summoned Deng Yu at night to ask who could take on the task. Deng Yu said: I have talked with Wu Han many times. He is brave and resourceful. Few generals can match him. That is to say, Wu Han was appointed as the general and ordered to carry the talisman to the north to attack the enemy's cavalry from ten counties. Gengshi Youzhou Mu Miao once heard that he secretly mobilized troops and ordered the counties not to send troops accordingly. Wu Han led twenty horses and galloped to the end.
target: Wu Han, courtesy name Ziyan, was born into poverty in Wan County, Nanyang County, and served as a county pavilion chief. During Wang Mang's final years, he fled to Yuyang after his guests broke the law, supporting himself by selling horses and befriending heroes throughout Yan and Ji regions. When Gengshi ascended the throne, envoy Han Hong appointed Wu Han as magistrate of Anle County. During Wang Lang's uprising, Wu Han sought to join Guangwu, attempting to persuade Prefect Peng Chong to ally with Guangwu against Handan. When officials favored Wang Lang, Wu Han fabricated a letter from Guangwu and sent a Confucian scholar to convince Peng Chong, who ultimately agreed. Wu Han led troops south, killing Wang Lang's generals, and after pursuing Guangwu to Guang'a, was appointed partial general. Following the conquest of Handan, he was made Marquis Jiance.

source: Guangwu ascended the throne, worshiped Wu Han as Grand Sima, and was granted the title of Marquis of Wuyang. In the spring of the second year of Jianwu, Wu Han led the general Wang Liang, the general Zhu You of Jianyi, the general Du Mao, the Jin Wu Jiafu, the Yanghua general Jian Tan, the partial general Wang Ba, the cavalry captain Liu Long, Ma Wu, and Yinshi. They attacked the Tanxiang bandits on the Zhang River in the east of Ye. They defeated the bandits and more than 100,000 people surrendered. The emperor sent envoys to seal Wu Han as the Marquis of Guangping, with four counties in total: Guangping, Kuizhang, Quzhou and Guangnian. Wu Han again led his generals to attack the bandits Li Boxing and others in the western mountains of Ye, and pursued them to Hanoi Wu, where they defeated all the bandits' gatherings. Guangwu personally came to express his condolences. Wu Han was sent back to march into Nanyang County, attack Wan, Nie, Yang, Li, Rang and Xinye cities, and captured them all. He led his troops to the south, fought with Qin Feng on the Huangyou River, and defeated Qin Feng. He and the partial general Feng Yi attacked Zhang Wen and others on the fifth floor of Changcheng. They also attacked Bronze Horse and Five Flags in Xin'an, and defeated them all. In the spring of the next year, Wu Han led Jianwei General Geng Yan and Huya General Gai Yan to attack Qingdu in the west of Zhejiang, defeating him and forcing him to surrender. He also led the hussar general Du Mao, the strong crossbow general Chen Jun and others to surround Su Mao in Guangle. Liu Yong recruited Zhou Jian and gathered more than 100,000 people to rescue Guangle. Wu Han sent Qingqi to fight with him, but was unfavorable. He fell from his horse and injured his knee. When he returned to camp, Zhou Jian led his troops into the city. The generals said to Wu Han: The enemy is in front, but the Duke is lying down due to his wounds, and everyone is afraid. Wu Hannai became angry, changed his color, wrapped up his knee wound, and rose up, killing cattle and feasting on the soldiers. He ordered the army to say: Although there are many thieves, they are just a group of robbers. When they win, they will not give in, and when they lose, they will not save each other. They are not loyal and willing to die for righteousness. Today is a good opportunity to make meritorious deeds and become a lord, please give me more encouragement. The sergeant was enraged and his morale doubled. Early in the morning, Zhou Jian and Su Mao sent troops to surround Wu Han. Wu Han selected four elite soldiers, including Huangtou Wu He and others, as well as more than 3,000 Wuhuan cavalry, and advanced together with great noise. Zhou Jianjun was defeated and ran back to the city. Wu Han pursued them with a long drive, fought for the gate and entered with all their strength, and greatly defeated Jian and Mao's army. Su Mao and Zhou Jian broke through and left. Wu Han left Du Mao, Chen Jun and others to guard Guangle, and led his own troops to help Gai Yan encircle Liu Yong in Suiyang. At that time, Nan Danyu and Wu Huan came to surrender, and there was nothing happening on the border. The people had just gotten rid of the military revolution. They were young and had enough money. Zhang Chun believed that the holy king built schools to promote etiquette and righteousness and to provide education on the basis of enriching the people. So in accordance with the prophecies of the Seven Classics, the Mingtang Picture, Hejian's "Gu Piyong Ji", and Xiaowu Taishan Mingtang system, Emperor Heping discussed it in detail and wanted to start it in detail. It was not submitted, but it happened that Dr. Huan Rong wrote a letter suggesting the establishment of Piyong and Mingtang. The memorial was sent to Sangong and Taichang. Zhang Chun's opinion was the same as Huan Rong's, so the emperor agreed. On the 30th year, Zhang Chun submitted a memorial that should hold a Zen ceremony. The memorial said: Since ancient times, those who have been appointed as emperors by fate must have the ceremony of Zen ceremony to declare their success in a time of peace. id: 后汉书/列传/张曹郑列传::group-004
article_path: 后汉书/列传/张曹郑列传
source: ◆Cao Bao Biography, Cao Bao, courtesy name Shutong, was born in Xue, Lu State. His father, Cao Chong, insisted on studying the "Qingshi Rites". During the Jianwu period, he became a doctor. He followed the emperor on a hunting trip to Mount Tai and established the Zen Rite. After returning, he was ordered to establish etiquette such as Qijiao, Sanyong, Dashe, and Elderly Care. After Xianzong came to the throne, Cao Chong said: If the Han Dynasty receives the mandate of heaven again, there will still be a matter of enshrining Zen, but the rituals and music are incomplete and cannot be used as an example for future generations. The five emperors did not inherit each other's music, and the three kings did not follow each other's old rituals. The great Han should make his own rituals and use them as examples for generations of descendants. The emperor asked: How to make rituals and music? Chong replied: "He Tu Kuo Di Xiang" says: "Elegance in rituals and music emerged in the Han Dynasty." "Shang Shu·Ji Qian" says: There was an emperor who came out of the Han Dynasty. He was virtuous and happy, and his name was Yu. The emperor appreciated it very much and issued an edict: Now the official name of Taiyue will be changed to Taiyule, and he will sing poems and perform music, and wait for future gentlemen to supplement it. He worshiped Cao Chong as his servant. It was difficult to argue chapters and sentences, so "Qingshi Xue" came out. Cao Bao was ambitious and generous when he was young. When he was twenty, he inherited his father's studies. He was knowledgeable and especially fond of etiquette. He often felt that the imperial system was incomplete and envied Shusun Tong for establishing etiquette for the Han Dynasty, so he studied it morning and night and concentrated on thinking. He held the letters in his arms when sleeping and recited the documents while walking. When he was so fascinated by his thoughts, he forgot which way he should go. Cao Bao was first promoted to Xiaolian, and then to the magistrate of Yuxian County. He used etiquette to govern people and virtue to change customs.
target: Cao Bao, courtesy name Shutong, was from Xue in Lu State. His father Cao Chong studied the "Qingshi Rites" and became a doctor during Jianwu, establishing various rituals. After Xianzong ascended, Cao Chong discussed ritual and music matters with the emperor, who appreciated his views and appointed him as servant. Cao Bao was ambitious and generous, inheriting his father's studies at twenty. He was knowledgeable and fond of etiquette, often feeling the imperial system was incomplete. He studied morning and night, even forgetting directions while walking. He was first promoted to Xiaolian, then magistrate of Yuxian County, governing with etiquette.

source: Cao Bao was first promoted to Xiaolian, and then to the magistrate of Yuxian County. He used etiquette to govern people and virtue to change customs. At that time, five thieves from other counties came into Yuxian County and were captured by the officials. Ma Yan, the prefect of Chenliu, was very angry after hearing this and ordered to go to the county to kill them. Cao Bao said to the officials: Those who cut off human life will be cut off by God. It is said that Gaotao did not enact the death penalty for thieves, but Guan Zhong was promoted to a public minister when he met a thief. Now to kill them according to the order from above is to violate God's will and obey the governor, and the punishment is too severe. If I can save the life of the thief and let me be punished, I am willing. So he didn't kill those five people. Ma Yan reported that Cao Bao was weak and dismissed him from his post. He returned to the county and became a meritorious Cao Cao. Later, Cao Bao was recruited to become a doctor.
target: When five thieves were captured, he refused to kill them despite orders, saving their lives. He was dismissed for this but later recruited as a doctor.

id: 后汉书/列传/张曹郑列传::group-006
article_path: 后汉书/列传/张曹郑列传
source: I was very awed in the morning and evening. I could not praise the late emperor's meritorious service to my superiors, and I could not take care of the spiritual creatures. When the Han Dynasty succeeded the Qin Dynasty, the rituals and music were incomplete, and there was no benefit in continuing to do things as usual. If anyone has knowledge in this area, please do your best. Cao Bao thought about his intention, and then sighed and said to everyone: "In the past, Xi Si sang about Lu, and Kaofu praised the Shang Dynasty." It is a virtue for ministers to honor the monarch and commend the emperor according to the great righteousness. It’s my duty to do so, why should I refuse? So he went on to explain the fundamentals of rituals and music and the meaning of system reform. The emperor then appointed Cao Bao as a doctor, and followed the emperor on a tour to the south. After returning, he handed over the matters concerning the etiquette to the Three Dukes. Before he had time to report, he summoned Xuanwu Sima Bangu to ask about changes to the etiquette system and other matters. Ban Gu said: There are many Confucian scholars in the capital, and most of them are good at talking about etiquette. We should recruit them widely to discuss the pros and cons together. The Emperor said: As the saying goes: It will take three years to build a house next to the road. When we gather at the house for ceremony, it is superficially a discussion, but in reality it is mutual suspicion, and we are delayed in writing. In the past, Emperor Yao used a minister named Kui to compose the Great Chapter. In the first month of the first year of Zhanghe, he summoned Cao Bao to Jiademen and ordered Xiaohuangmen to take the twelve chapters of "Han Yi" written by Shu Suntong, which Ban Gu had attended, and ordered Cao Bao to say: "This Han Yi is very loose and inconsistent with the meaning of the scriptures. Some modifications should be made now to make it practical." You can concentrate on your work in Nangong and Dongguan. After receiving the order, Cao Bao arranged the order of etiquette, based on the old scriptures, mixed with the prophecies of the Five Classics, and wrote out the system of etiquette from the emperor to the common people, including the good and bad luck of weddings, etc., a total of 150 articles, written on two-foot-four-inch bamboo sketches, and memorialized in December of that year. The emperor thought that it was difficult for everyone to agree on the opinions, so he only accepted them and no longer asked the officials to comment. When the emperor died and Emperor He ascended the throne, Cao Bao wrote chapters and sentences, and the emperor put the two chapters of "New Rites" at the top. Cao Bao was promoted to supervise Yulin Zuoqi. In the fourth year of Yongyuan's reign, he was promoted to the rank of Colonel Shesheng. Later, Taiwei Zhang Youfu, Shangshu Zhang Min and others complained that he had made the "Han Rites" without authorization and that he should be beheaded if he broke the sacred law. Although the emperor put down the memorial, the "Han Rites" was not implemented.
target: When Suzong wanted to formulate rituals and music, Cao Bao presented a memorial. The emperor appointed him as doctor. Later, the emperor ordered him to work on "Han Yi" in Nangong and Dongguan. Cao Bao wrote 150 articles on ritual systems from emperor to commoners. After the emperor died, Cao Bao was promoted to various positions. Some officials complained about his "Han Rites," which was not implemented.

His eighth-generation ancestor Zheng Chong was the minister of public affairs at the time of Emperor Ai of the Han Dynasty. When Zheng Xuan was a boy, he worked as a small official in the countryside in charge of litigation and tax collection. Whenever he went home on vacation, he always had to go to school and was not happy to be a small official. His father was angry many times but could not stop him. So he went to study at Taixue in Beijing, where he became a teacher under Wu Yuanxian, a native of Jingzhao, and then he became proficient in "Jingshi Yi", "Gongzhu Chunqiu", "Santong Calendar" and "Nine Chapters of Arithmetic". He also studied "Zhou Guan", "Book of Rites", "Zuo Shi Chun Qiu", "Han Shi" and "Guwen Shangshu" from Zhang Gongzu of Dongjun. Because there was no one in Shandong who could question him, he went west and entered the customs. After being introduced by Lu Zhi of Zhuojun, he became his disciple Fufeng Ma Rong. Ma Rong had more than 400 students, and only about 50 people were taught by Ma Rong personally. Ma Rong was an arrogant person, and Zheng Xuan had not seen him for three years under his tutelage. Ma Rong just sent his senior disciples to tutor Zheng Xuan. Zheng Xuan studied day and night and never slackened off. One day, Ma Rong summoned his students to study Tuwei. Hearing that Zheng Xuan was proficient in arithmetic, he summoned him upstairs. Zheng Xuan took this opportunity to ask Ma Rong many difficult questions. After asking, he said goodbye to Ma Rong and returned to his hometown in Shandong. Ma Rong said to his students with emotion: Now that Zheng Sheng has left me, my teachings will spread eastward. Since Zheng Xuan went out to study, it took more than ten years before he returned to his hometown. His family was poor and he went to Donglai to work as a farmer. There are hundreds of students studying with him. When the disaster of party imprisonment occurred, more than 40 people including Zheng Xuan and Sun Song from the same county were imprisoned. So he immersed himself in studying the classics and stayed behind closed doors.

source: When the disaster of party imprisonment occurred, more than 40 people including Zheng Xuan and Sun Song from the same county were imprisoned. So he immersed himself in studying the classics and stayed behind closed doors. At that time, He Xiu, a native of Rencheng, loved the theory of "Gongyang", so he wrote "Gongyang Mo Shou", "Zuo Shi's Death" and "Gu Liang's Failed Disease". Zheng Xuan wrote articles refuting "Mo Shou", "Gao Ming" and "Fei Ji". He Xiu saw it and sighed: Zheng Kangcheng walked into my house, picked up my spear, and came to attack me! In the early years of the Eastern Han Dynasty, Fan Sheng, Chen Yuan, Li Ming, and Jia Kui were debating ancient and modern theories. Later, Ma Rong replied to Liu Mo and Zheng Xuan, the prefect of the North. He Xiu said that because of the profound research on doctrine and theory, the ancient classics became prosperous from then on. In the last years of Emperor Ling of the Han Dynasty, the party ban was lifted, and the general He Jin heard of Zheng Xuan's reputation and recruited him. The prefectures and counties believed that He Jin was a powerful nobleman and did not dare to go against his wishes, so they forced Zheng Xuan to obey the call. Zheng Xuan had no choice but to go and answer the imperial edict. He Jin set up several canes for him and treated him very generously. Zheng Xuan did not accept the court robes, but came to see He Jin in Confucian attire wearing a turban. He stayed one night and then escaped. Zheng Xuan was already sixty years old at that time, and his students came from far away places, such as Zhao Shang from Hanoi, and there were thousands of them. target: He refuted He Xiu's theories, impressing He Xiu. When the party ban was lifted, General He Jin recruited him, but Zheng Xuan escaped after one night. At sixty, he had thousands of students. He declined various official positions.

source: At this time, General Yuan Shao was commanding the army in Jizhou. He sent an envoy to invite Zheng Xuan as a guest. Zheng Xuan arrived last, and Yuan Shao invited him to his seat. Zheng Xuan was tall, could drink a handful of wine, had fine features, handsome appearance, and was gentle and majestic. Most of Yuan Shao's guests were handsome, talented, and good at debating. They saw that Zheng Xuan was a Confucian scholar and thought that he was not a knowledgeable person. So everyone rushed to imagine some tricky and weird questions, and various schools of thought put forward their opinions one after another. Zheng Xuan answered and responded according to the orthodox Confucian views, and the content exceeded the scope of the question. Everyone gained knowledge that they had never heard of before, and no one did not admire and admire Zheng Xuan. At this time, Ying Shao from Runan also joined Yuan Shao, so he introduced himself: Ying Zhongyuan, the former governor of Qinshan, would you like to call me your disciple from the north? How about it? Zheng Xuan smiled and said: Confucius's students had to take exams in four subjects: morality, speech, political affairs, and literature. Students like Yan Yuan and Zigong never claimed their official titles or family status. Ying Shao felt ashamed after hearing this. Therefore, Yuan Shao recommended Zheng Xuan as Maocai, and the above table recommended him as Zuo Zhonglang General. Zheng Xuan did not take office.

At that time, more than a thousand people who had been students under Zheng Xuan's sect, including county magistrates and officials, came to the funeral in solemn mourning clothes. Zheng Xuan's students co-wrote Zheng Xuan's answers to questions raised by his disciples from the "Five Classics" during his lifetime, and compiled it into "Zheng Zhi" in eight chapters according to the style of "The Analects of Confucius". In total, the books that Zheng Xuan annotated include "The Book of Changes", "Shangshu", "Mao Shi", "Ritual", "Book of Rites", "The Analects", "The Book of Filial Piety", "Shangshu Da Zhuan", "Zhonghou", and "Cheqi Xiangli". Zheng Xuan's self-authored books include "Seven Political Treatises on Astronomy", "The Comprehensive Theory of Lu Li and Emperor Xuan", "Six Art Theory", "Mao Shi Pu", "Refutation of the Different Meanings of Xu Shen's Five Classics", and "Reply to the Difficulty of Lin Xiao and Preserving Zhou Rites", with a total of more than one million words. Zheng Xuan strived to be simple and realistic in his interpretation of classics. Many knowledgeable people ridiculed this approach as too cumbersome. As for his rich understanding of classics' annotations, he may be called a pure Confucian. People in Qilu respect him as their master. His students, Xi Luguan from Shanyang, Wang Quan from Donglai, and Cui Yan from Qinghe were all famous in the local area.
target: The imperial court conscripted him as chief minister of agriculture, but he requested to return home due to illness. He was respected as a master in Qilu, and his students became famous in their regions.

Zhang Hao withdrew from the imperial court and wrote: "In the past, Jiang Chong, a traitor, made slanderous rumors and rebels, causing the military garden to raise troops, and finally disaster occurred."

So he studied yin and yang, became proficient in astronomy and calendar, made an armillary sphere, and wrote "Lingxian" and "Suanwang Lun", which were very detailed and clear. In the early years of the emperor's reign, he was transferred again and became the Taishi Order. Zhang Heng did not envy the fame and wealth of his time, and the official positions he held were often not promoted for many years. He left his post as historian and returned to his original post five years ago. So he set up an objective question and wrote "Yingwen" to express his thoughts. In the first year of Yangjia, another wind and earth motion instrument was created. It is made of fine copper, with a diameter of eight feet, a protruding top cover, shaped like a wine bottle, and decorated with images of turtles, birds and beasts in seal script. There is a big pillar in the middle, with eight paths running beside it, which is used to shut down the engine. There are eight dragons outside, each holding a copper pill in its mouth, and a toad underneath, opening its mouth to receive the pill. The teeth are ingeniously made and are hidden in the bottle, covering them thoroughly and without gaps. If the earth moves, the bottle will cause the dragon to shake, and the dragon will spit out pills, which will go into the toad's mouth and make an exciting sound, so the guardian will know that the ground is shaking.
target: Zhang Heng, styled Pingzi, was a native of Xi'e County, Nanyang. His grandfather, Zhang Kan, served as the prefect of Shu County. Zhang Heng excelled in writing from a young age, studied in Sanfu and the Imperial Academy, and mastered the Five Classics and Six Arts. Despite his exceptional talent, he remained humble and indifferent, avoiding interactions with common people. During the Yongyuan period of Emperor He, he was recommended as a Xiaolian but declined multiple government recruitments. Observing the extravagance of the time, he spent ten years composing "Ode to Two Capitals" as a satire, inspired by Ban Gu's work. General Deng Zhi admired his talent but Zhang Heng ignored his summons. Skilled in mechanics, astronomy, yin-yang, and calendar calculation, Zhang Heng admired Yang Xiong's "Tai Xuan Jing." Emperor An appointed him as a doctor and later as Taishi Ling, where he studied yin-yang, built an armillary sphere, and wrote "Lingxian" and "Suanwang Lun." In the first year of Yangjia, he created a seismoscope made of fine copper, eight feet in diameter, with eight dragons holding copper balls and toads beneath them. When an earthquake occurred, a dragon would release a ball into a toad's mouth, indicating the direction.

source: After testing, it was in accordance with the established system, and it was as good as God. This has never happened since there were records in books. Once upon a time, a dragon's plan came out and the earth did not move, and the scholars in the capital blamed it for not believing it. A few days later, the messenger came, and sure enough, there was an earthquake in Longxi, so they all admired its miracle. From then on, historians were ordered to record the place where the earthquake occurred. At that time, political affairs were gradually declining and power was controlled by subordinates. Zhang Heng then went to the court to explain the matter. Said: The emperor is smart and wise, and he upholds the destiny. Unfortunately, when he became the prince, he was deposed as the king of Jiyin and his virtue was not promoted.
target: This device proved accurate, even detecting a distant earthquake in Longxi that others initially doubted. As political affairs declined, Zhang Heng advised the emperor against sharing power with subordinates, warning that disasters stemmed from moral failings.

source: What was said before is confirmed later, so smart people value this. It's called a prophecy. The prophecies became popular, but not many people knew about them. Since the Han Dynasty replaced the Qin Dynasty, it can be said that it is a great event to use military force to fight and achieve great success. At this time, no one was predicting. For example, Xia Housheng, Mu Meng, etc. were famous for their Taoism, but there are no prophecies in their writings. Liu Xiang and his son were the school secretaries, and they approved the ninth stream, but there was no record of the prophecy. It was only after Cheng and Ai that people began to hear about prophecies.
target: He criticized prophecies as false, noting they emerged only after the Cheng and Ai periods and contradicted classical texts. He urged their suppression to prevent confusion.

source: Prophecies should be collected and not popular, so that there will be no confusion between right and wrong, and there will be no bad books. After he was promoted to a servant, the emperor led him into the palace and satirized him. I once asked Zhang Heng what the world hates. There were also many powerful people who gathered together to cause trouble. When Zhang Heng took office, he established his authority, rectified the laws, secretly found out the names of traitors, and arrested them at once. He was awe-inspiring from top to bottom, and he was known for his political integrity.
target: Later, as Prime Minister of Hejian, Zhang Heng curbed the king's arrogance and lawlessness, earning a reputation for integrity.

source: After serving for three years, he submitted a letter requesting to retire and return home. Ask for help from the minister. He died in the fourth year of Yonghe's reign at the age of sixty-two. Cui Yuan, who wrote "Exegesis of Zhou Officials", believed that there was no difference between him and other Confucian scholars. He also wanted to follow Confucius's "Yi" to correct the defects of "彖" and "Xiang", but it was never completed. He has written poems, fu, inscriptions, seven words, "Lingxian", "Yingjian", "Qibian", "Xungao" and "Xuantu", a total of thirty-two articles.
target: After three years, he requested retirement and died at sixty-two. He authored thirty-two works, including poems and essays.

source: He also wanted to follow Confucius's "Yi" to correct the defects of "彖" and "Xiang", but it was never completed. In An Diyong Junior High School, the visitor Pushe Liu Zhen, the school secretary Liu Mayu and others wrote Dongguan and compiled the "Han Ji". When Liu Zhen and Liu Mayu passed away, Zhang Heng sighed and wanted to complete the matter. As a servant, Shangshu asked him to go to Dongguan to collect and inspect the remaining documents and make every effort to repair them. There are also more than ten things recorded by the superiors Ma Qian and Ban Gu that are inconsistent with the classics. He also believed that the original biography of Wang Mang should only record the usurpation of the throne. As for chronicling the years and recording disasters and auspiciousness, it should be compiled into the "Benji of the Empress of the Yuan Dynasty". He was appointed again, and the people had no objections. Guangwu was his general at the beginning, and he came to the throne later. The title of Gengshi should be built before Guangwu. I submitted the letter several times, but it was not accepted. Later writings were mostly unknown in classics, which was a pity for the people at the time. The historian commented: Cui Yuan praised Pingzi and said: The art of numerology explores the mysteries of heaven and earth, and the craftsmanship works together with nature. Can you talk about this kind of attainment? When it comes to his study of heaven and earth, the spiritual energy of heaven and earth is immeasurable; if he is mechanically diligent, no one can match his wisdom. Therefore, people's profound thoughts have reached the pinnacle of intellectual thinking. "Book of Rites" says: Virtue comes first, and skill comes down.
target: He also sought to correct historical records, arguing that Wang Mang's biography should focus on usurpation and that Gengshi's title should precede Guangwu's, but his proposals were not accepted. The historian praised his profound wisdom and mechanical ingenuity, noting that his virtue was not diminished by his skills.

source: The emperor sighed and said: You are right. After arriving in Wuwei, Tian Cang, the commander of the army at that time, was a prominent family in the county. His nephews and guests harmed the people. Ren Yan arrested Tian Cang, and five or six of his father, son and guests were executed. Tian Xiang's youngest son, Tian Shang, gathered hundreds of dissolute and frivolous people, called themselves generals, and attacked the county government at night.
target: Emperor Guangwu, having risen from the common people, understood the hardships of farming and the suffering of the people.

source: In the beginning, Guangwu was born among the people. He knew the truth of the world very well and witnessed the hardships of farming and the diseases of the people. Therefore, after the world was settled, he strived for peace, eliminated the complicated methods of Wang Mang's period, and restored the lenient methods of the Han Dynasty. He wears rough clothes without a second color. Guang Wu's ears do not listen to the sound of Mi Mi, his hands do not play with pearls and jade, there is no preference in the harem, and the ministers near him are not treated differently. In the thirteenth year of Jianwu's reign, foreign countries presented famous horses that could run thousands of miles in a day, and also presented swords, which were worth hundreds of kilograms of gold. The edict ordered the chariots to be driven by horses and drums, and swords were given to the knights. They also reduced the number of officials in Shangzheng Garden and abolished things like traveling and hunting. The handwritten letters given by the emperor to localities and vassal states are all in ten lines and written in small characters. The atmosphere of diligence and frugality prevailed in the imperial court. The emperor repeatedly asked ministers and generals to sit on the throne. He visited extensively to inquire about the sufferings of the people and collected folk songs. Therefore, no one inside or outside the court dared to slack off, and the people got a rest. The local governors competed for their efforts. For example, Du Shi served as the governor of Nanyang and was called "Du Mu". Ren Yan and Xiguang changed the customs in the border areas. These are the people with the most remarkable political achievements. There are also Wu Lun, Song Jun and others, who also have many things worthy of praise. However, during the Jianwu and Yongping years, political affairs were too strict and detailed, and local governors were replaced many times based on rumors and one-sided remarks. Therefore, Zhu Fu wrote many times and put forward sharp opinions. Zhong Zhengtong and others also repeatedly gave advice. They spoke as loyal and generous elders, but they were not adopted. Therefore, Mosaic during the ZTE period still had shortcomings. Since Emperor Zhang and Emperor He, some officials with outstanding political achievements have continued to appear. For example, Lu Gong, Wu You, Liu Kuan and the four county magistrates of Tichuan all used their benevolence, faith, loyalty and honesty to prevent people from cheating; Wang Tang and Chen Chong appointed virtuous and talented people, and political affairs were naturally managed: these can move all things and promote education. Bian Feng and Yan Du successively served as Jing Zhaoyin, and people compared them to Zhao Guangmo and Zhang Chang. In addition, Wang Huan and Ren Jun served as the Luoyang Order, publicly punishing bad people and bad things, and the officialdom improved, and what was forbidden was naturally prohibited. Although there were some imperfections in terms of morality and etiquette, they were still good officials at that time.
target: After unifying the realm, he pursued peace, abolished the complex policies of Wang Mang's era, and restored the lenient Han methods. He reduced officials, abolished hunting expeditions, and wrote imperial letters in small characters, fostering an atmosphere of diligence and frugality. He frequently consulted ministers and visited the people to learn of their grievances, leading to diligent governance and rest for the populace. From the reigns of Emperor Zhang and Emperor He onward, officials like Lu Gong, Wu You, and Liu Kuan used benevolence and integrity to prevent deceit, while Wang Tang and Chen Chong appointed virtuous talents, promoting education. Others like Wang Huan and Ren Jun, as Luoyang magistrates, punished evil and improved officialdom, though they had imperfections in morality and etiquette.

Wei Sa came from a poor family but loved learning. He studied with a teacher but had no food, so he often relied on work to survive.
target: Wei Sa, from a poor family, studied diligently and served as a magistrate and prefect.

source: Wei Sa came from a poor family but loved learning. He studied with a teacher but had no food, so he often relied on work to survive. During the reign of Wang Mang, he served as the governor of Yuzhou. In the second year of Jianwu's reign, he went to serve in the mansion of Grand Situ Deng Yu. He was appointed as an imperial censor and a magistrate of Xiangcheng for recommending talented people to handle heavy official duties. He had a good reputation and achievements in politics, and was promoted to the prefect of Guiyang. Guiyang borders Jiaozhou and is greatly influenced by Jiaozhou. The people do not know etiquette. After Wei Sa took office, he built schools, rectified education, and formulated marriage etiquette.
target: In Guiyang, he built schools, established marriage rites, and transformed local customs. He constructed roads and inns, reducing corvée labor, and regulated iron smelting, increasing annual revenue. He governed with consideration for the people, maintaining peace for ten years. Ren Yan, a learned scholar, served as a young prefect of Kuaiji, where he hired virtuous men and supported the poor. In Jiuzhen, he taught farming, established marriage regulations, and civilized the people, leading to prosperity and admiration from barbarian tribes. He later governed Wuwei, where he executed corrupt officials, defended against invaders, built irrigation systems, and promoted education, leaving a lasting legacy.

source: In the second year of Yongping, the emperor summoned him to school and then appointed him as the governor of Hanoi. He served for nine years and died of illness. His youngest son Ren Kai was very successful in his official career. ◆Wang Jingzhuan, Wang Jing, courtesy name Zhongtong, was born in Lelang, Jiahan. His eighth generation ancestor, Wang Zhong, was originally from Langxie. Wang Zhong likes Taoism and understands celestial phenomena. When Zhu Lu was in rebellion, King Ai of Qi Liu Xiang planned to send troops and asked Wang Zhong for advice many times. When Liu Xingju, the king of Jibei, rebelled, he wanted him to serve as military advisor. Wang Zhong was afraid of disaster, so he took a boat across the sea and fled to Lelang Mountain, where he settled down.
target: Wang Jing, a scholar of the *Book of Changes* and other subjects, was summoned to control floods.

source: And because he had managed Junyi, he was given the "Book of Mountains and Seas", "Book of Rivers and Canals", "Pictures of Tribute to Yu" as well as coins, cloth, clothing and items. In the summer, the imperial court finally mobilized hundreds of thousands of troops and sent Wang Jing and Wang Wu to build channels and embankments. It was more than a thousand miles from Rongyang to Qiancheng Haikou. Wang Jing then measured the terrain, opened up the mountains, cleared the sand and gravel from the water, directly cut off the deep ditches, built dams at key points, and dredged and guided the blocked water flow. He built a sluice every ten miles so that the water could flow back and forth without causing the danger of bursting.
target: He successfully built canals and embankments over a thousand miles, using sluices to manage water flow, saving costs and preventing disasters.

source: Qin Peng's sixth ancestor Qin Xi served as Ying! There are five people who hold the position of two thousand stones at the same time, so they are called the Wanshi Qin family in the Sanfu area. Qin Peng's sister entered the palace as a noble during the reign of Emperor Xianzong and was very favored. In the seventh year of Yongping, as the elder brother of Peng Guiren, Qin Peng was promoted to Kaiyang City Gate Marquis along with Xiaohou, a relative of the fourth surname. In the fifteenth year, he was awarded the position of Captain of Cavalry and helped Captain Geng Bingbei to conquer the Xiongnu. In the first year of Jianchu's reign, Qin Peng was promoted to Shanyang Prefect. He educated the people with etiquette and justice without punishment. He respected Confucianism and advocated education. Every time during the Spring and Autumn period when people were eating and drinking, he would always revise the etiquette of ascending and descending, as well as the courtesy of guests and hosts. He formulated four precepts for the people to determine the etiquette between father and son, brothers, husband and wife, elder and younger. Anyone who abides by the teachings will be promoted to the third elder of the village, and he will often be given wine and meat as encouragement in August. When an official commits a crime or fault, he or she should be removed from his official position and sent away without humiliation. As a result, the people all had benevolent hearts, and no one deceived or violated each other. He cultivated thousands of hectares of rice fields. Every farming season, Qin Peng personally measured the acres of land, classified the fertile and barren land, classified them into three grades, recorded them in official books, and stored them in the township and county. In this way, cunning officials dare not act rashly and cannot hide their evil deeds. Qin Peng then wrote to the court, saying that it would be best to implement this system throughout the country. The edict distributed the provisions he listed to the three governments and issued them to the prefectures and counties. Qin Peng served for six years and was transferred to Yingchuan Prefecture. There are often auspicious signs such as phoenixes, unicorns, particularly strong rice crops, sweet rain and dew, appearing everywhere in the county. Suzong went out for inspections and when he came to Yingchuan again, he always rewarded him with money and food, and was particularly fond of him. He died in the second year of Zhanghe. Qin Peng's younger brothers Qin Dun and Qin Guo served as captains of Shesheng together. ◆Biography of Wang Huan, Wang Huan, courtesy name Zhizi, was from Zheng County, Guangmo. Wang Huan's father, Wang Shun, served as the governor of Anding. Wang Huan has been fond of chivalry and advocating martial arts since he was a child. He has interacted with strong and agile young men many times. Later, he changed his conduct, paid attention to Confucianism, studied "Shangshu", recited the law, and was able to roughly grasp its main meaning. He served as the meritorious officer of the prefect Chen Chong, and he dared to make decisions regardless of the powerful. Chen Chong's reputation for political governance spread widely, and he served as chief agricultural officer in the capital.
target: He later served as a prefect in Xuzhou and Lujiang, where he taught cattle plowing, reclaimed land, and guided sericulture, engraving laws for the people. Qin Peng, from a prominent family, governed Shanyang with etiquette and education, establishing moral precepts and agricultural classifications. He cultivated rice fields and implemented a grading system to prevent official corruption, later serving in Yingchuan with auspicious signs. Wang Huan, initially chivalrous, later studied Confucianism and served as a magistrate, eliminating cunning criminals and ensuring peace.

source: A few years later, he was recruited by the imperial court and granted the position of Shi Yushi. In the fifteenth year of Yongyuan, Wang Huan followed the emperor to the south for inspection and served as the Luoyang order after returning. Wang Huan was upright in his conduct and could be lenient and strict in his administration. For those unjust and doubtful cases that have been litigated for a long time, which have not been resolved by several county magistrates, and which are difficult to judge based on legal basis, Wang Huan can skillfully clarify the truth of the case and eliminate everyone's doubts. He can also use his uncanny skills to discover hidden bad guys and evil deeds. The people in the capital all praised and marveled, thinking that Wang Huan had a wonderful plan.
target: As Luoyang magistrate, he resolved difficult cases and uncovered hidden evils, earning widespread praise. After his death, the people built a shrine for him, and even Emperor Huan later preserved it.

source: The enemy helped Xu Jing up and said, "You are praised as a virtuous person in the county. How dare we be rude to you?" So let it go. Xu Jing's reputation became even more prominent. The prefect Huang Jing recommended him as Xiaolian. During the reign of Emperor He, Xu Jing was gradually promoted to the prefect of Guiyang. Guiyang is close to Nanzhou, and its customs and customs are very frivolous and do not understand knowledge and morality. Xu Jing made a wedding and funeral system for them to let the people know the etiquette, justice, laws and prohibitions. He once visited Moyang County in the spring. There was a man named Jiang Jun. Brothers accused each other of fighting over property. Xu Jing faced the two brothers and sighed: I bear the important responsibility of the country, but the education has not been implemented. The responsibility lies with me, the prefect. So he turned around and asked the officials around him to write to the court to explain the situation and request to be punished by the court captain.
target: Xu Jing, as Guiyang prefect, established wedding and funeral rites and resolved a property dispute between brothers by taking responsibility himself, leading to their repentance.

source: Due to illness, he wrote to the court, and was summoned and appointed as an admonishment official. He died in office. People in Guiyang built a temple and a monument for him. Xu Jing's grandson Xu Jian served as Taiwei during the reign of Emperor Ling. ◆Biography of Mengchang, Mengchang, courtesy name Bozhou, was born in Shangyu, Kuaiji. His ancestors served as county officials for three generations, and they all died in the chaos.
target: Mengchang, known for his integrity, cleared a widow's wrongful conviction, ending a drought. As Hepu prefect, he reformed pearl collection, restoring the pearl trade and reviving the local economy.

source: Mengchang lived in seclusion in a remote swamp and farmed by himself. Scholars and people in neighboring counties admired Mengchang's virtues, and more than a hundred people moved to live with him. During the reign of Emperor Huan, Yang Qiao, a native of the same county as Shangshu, wrote to recommend Meng Chang, saying: I have written seven times to recommend Meng Chang, the former prefect of Hepu, but he was so indifferent that he was never considered.
target: He retired to farming, and despite recommendations, was never hired, dying at seventy. The Fifth Fang, a grandson of a former minister, governed Zhangye during a famine by opening granaries without awaiting orders, saving the people.

source: So he took out food and distributed it to the people. Emperor Shun issued the fifth interview of the Shaoshu Commendation. The people of the whole county were saved. More than a year later, there were enough officials and people, and no treachery or robberies occurred in the county. Later he was transferred to Nanyang Prefecture. After leaving office, he was awarded the post of Colonel Protecting Qiang, and people in the border areas were convinced of his authority. The fifth visit died in office. ◆Biography of Liu Chong, courtesy name Zurong, a native of Mouping County, Donglai County. Qi mourned the descendants of King Hui.
target: He later served in Nanyang and as Colonel Protecting Qiang. Liu Chong, a descendant of royalty, governed with kindness, removing oppressive rules.

source: Liu Chong learned from his father when he was young. Because he was proficient in Confucian classics, he was promoted as Xiaolian and appointed as the magistrate of Dongpingling County. He was loved by the officials and people because of his kindness and kindness to the people. My mother was ill and left her official position to return home. The people sent him off, but even the road was blocked and the car could not move forward, so he ran back in civilian clothes. Later, he was promoted to the post of Yuzhang Prefect four times and to Kuaiji Prefect three times. Some people in the mountains are simple and reserved, but some have never been to a city since they were young, and are often deceived by officials. Liu Chong removed those cumbersome rules and regulations and prohibited his subordinates from disturbing the people and other illegal behaviors. The county was in order and the people lived and worked in peace and contentment. He will be appointed as a minister. There were five or six old men in Shanyin County, their eyebrows and hair were all gray, who came out of the Ruoxie Valley, and each of them gave Liu Chong a hundred coins. Liu Chong comforted them and said, "Elders, why are you doing this?" He replied: The ignorant people in the valley have never seen the governor. In the past, when the prefect was in office, he would send officials to the people to search for property day and night. Sometimes dogs barked all night, and the people had no peace. Since you took office, no dogs can be heard barking at night, and the common people cannot see the officials. It is rare for us in our old age to enjoy this peaceful time. Now I heard that you are leaving office, so we are here to send you a gift. Liu Chong said: How can my politics be what your elders say? Thank you for your hard work! He picked a big one from each person's money and accepted it.
target: When leaving Kuaiji, elders gave him coins, but he accepted only one from each. He held high offices but remained frugal, dying at home.

source: When he was young, he was a scholar, simple and silent, and no one in the village knew about him. When he was forty years old, the county government called him to serve as a supplementary official and he was promoted to chief of Pu Pavilion. Advise the people to manage production and formulate regulations and laws to ensure that there are as many fruits and vegetables as there are chickens and hogs. After the farm work is finished, the children are gathered together to study in school. Those who were idle and doing evil were made to farm and cultivate mulberry trees, and were strictly disciplined. He personally managed funerals for the people and helped the poor and widowed. Within a year, the education was widespread. When Qiu Lan arrived at the pavilion, there was a man named Chen Yuan who lived alone with his mother. His mother went to Qiu Lan to accuse Chen Yuan of being unfilial. Qiu Lan said in surprise: "I passed by your house recently. The courtyard is neat and cultivated on time." He is not a bad person, maybe it is because my education is not up to standard. The mother is widowed and has worked hard to raise orphans until she grows old. Why does she want to cause her son to be unjust when she gets angry? The mother was moved after hearing this, regretted it, and went back in tears. Qiu Lan personally went to Chen Yuan's house to have a drink with his mother and son. He talked to them about human ethics and filial piety, and warned them about the dangers and benefits. Chen Yuan finally became a filial son.
target: Qiu Lan, a quiet scholar, governed as a pavilion chief, promoting agriculture and education. He resolved a filial piety dispute by counseling a mother and son, transforming the son into a filial child.

source: ◆Tong Hui's biography, Tong Hui's courtesy name was Han Zong, and he was a native of Gumu Mu, Langfu County. His father, Tong Zhongyu, encountered a period of severe famine and used all his family property to provide relief. Hundreds of people from the nine tribes and the village relied on him to survive. Tong Zhongyu died very early. When Tong Hui was young, he worked as an official in the state and county. Situ Yangci knew that he was fair in enforcing the law, so he recruited him. When Yang Ci was impeached and should be removed from office, all his subordinates abandoned him and left. Only Tong Hui went to the court to argue for Yang Ci. Yang Ci's case was vindicated, and all his subordinates came back, but Tong Hui drove away. Therefore, public opinion praised him. He was then conscripted into the government, but was not given the order. County officials and the people should be educated at any time if they break the law; if the officials are competent and if some of the people have done good deeds, they will be rewarded with food and wine to encourage and dissuade them. There are regulations for farming, textile and other production undertakings. The whole place is quiet, and the prison has been empty for years without a single prisoner. The exiled population from neighboring counties came to join us, and more than 20,000 households moved there. The common people were often harmed by tigers. They set up fences to catch tigers and captured two tigers alive.
target: He later entered the Imperial College but avoided frivolous talk, maintaining strict personal conduct. Tong Hui, known for fairness, argued for his superior Yang Ci when others abandoned him. As a magistrate, he educated offenders, rewarded good deeds, and captured tigers harming people, executing one and releasing another. His governance led to peace and an influx of refugees.

source: ◆The biography of Du Du, named Jiya, was born in Duling, Jingzhao. The great ancestor was Du Yannian, who served as a censor during the reign of Emperor Xuan. When Du Du was young, he was very knowledgeable and did not practice small things. The people in the village did not treat him well. He lived in Meiyang and had good relations with Meiyang Ling. He asked him to do things for him many times, but Meiyang Ling didn't do it for him and hated him. In anger, Meiyang Ling arrested Du Du and sent him to the capital. When the great Sima Wu Han passed away, Guangwu ordered all the Confucian scholars to express condolences. Du Du wrote an edict in prison with elegant speech. Guangwu praised him for his good writing and gave him silk and exempted him from punishment. Du Du believed that the mountains inside Guanzhong and the river outside were the former capital of the late emperor, and Luoyi should not be rebuilt, so he wrote a "Fu on the Capital" and presented it to the emperor. Du Du later became an official in the county literature department, but due to eye disease, he did not go to the capital for more than 20 years.
target: Du Du, styled Jiya, was from Duling, Jingzhao. His great ancestor was Du Yannian, a censor under Emperor Xuan. Though knowledgeable, Du Du was not well-regarded locally. After a conflict with Meiyang Ling, he was arrested and sent to the capital. While imprisoned, he wrote an edict for Guangwu, who praised his writing, gave him silk, and pardoned him. Du Du later argued against rebuilding Luoyi, writing a "Fu on the Capital." He served as a county literary official but did not go to the capital for over twenty years due to eye disease.

source: Du Du's maternal great-grandfather, Po Qiang general Xin Wuxian, was famous for his military strategies. Du Du often sighed and said: Du's civilization is good at politics, but Du Du is not appointed as an official. Xin's upright and martial, but Du is timid and afraid of getting into trouble. The change has come and cannot be prevented. The officials and the people should be called to prepare early. The governor refused to listen, so Wen Gong prepared a big boat alone. Some people heard about it, and some took precautions. When the drought was at its worst, Wen Gong hurriedly moved away and sent someone to report to the governor, who laughed it off. The sun was about to hit the middle of the day, clouds started to rise in the north, and soon it rained heavily. By evening, the water suddenly rose by more than ten feet, destroying houses and injuring thousands of people. Duke Wen became famous for his divination skills. He was called Sikong Peng. Emperor Ping ascended the throne and returned home claiming to be ill. After Wang Mang usurped the throne, Duke Wen knew that a great chaos was coming, so he trained his family members to carry hundreds of kilograms of stuff and run around the house dozens of times a day. source: ◆Zhu You Biography Zhu You, courtesy name Zhongxian, was a native of Wan County, Nanyang County. When the young man lost his father, he returned to the home of his maternal grandparents Liu in Fuyang County and traveled to and from Chongling. Shizu and Bosheng were both dear to him. After Bo Sheng paid homage to the Chief Situ, he appointed Zhu You as his guard. Shizu was the Grand Sima, and when he conquered Hebei, he appointed Zhu You as his army guard. He often met his relatives and stayed there. Zhu You accompanied the banquet and said calmly: Chang'an is in political chaos and the public has the status of an emperor. This is a destiny sent from heaven. Shizu said: Summon assassins to arrest you, the guardian! Zhu You didn't dare to say anything anymore. He followed the expedition to Hebei and often fought hard to break the formation. He made Zhu You a partial general and was granted the title of Marquis of Anyang. Shizu ascended the throne and was worshiped as General Jianyi. In the second year of Jianwu's reign, Yanghou was blocked. In winter, he and his generals attacked Deng Feng in Yuyang, Zhu You was defeated and captured by Deng Feng. The next year, Deng Feng was defeated, and Rouqi and Zhu You surrendered. The emperor restored Zhu You's position and generously rewarded him with condolences. He was sent to attack Xinye and Suixian, and they were all pacified. Since Yancen was defeated by Rang, he joined Qin Feng's general Zhang Cheng. Zhu You led the conquering general Ji Zun to fight Yancen in Dongyang, defeated Yancen, and beheaded Zhang Cheng before the battle. Yancen was defeated and returned to Qin Feng. Zhu You received ninety-seven seals and ribbons. Attacked Huangyou, Huangyou surrendered and rewarded Zhu You with thirty kilograms of gold. In the fourth year of Jianwu's reign, he led general Hou Jin and general Geng Zhi to attack the south and besieged Qin Feng in Liqiu, defeated his general Zhang Kang in Caiyang and beheaded Zhang Kang. The emperor personally came to Liqiu and sent Li You, the censor Zhongcheng, with a seal to recruit Qin Feng to surrender. Qin Feng made bad words and refused to surrender. The emperor returned and gave Zhu You strategies, and Zhu You tried his best to besiege. In the summer of the next year, the city was impoverished, so Qin Feng led his mother and his wife, Jiurenzuchou, to surrender. Zhu You took Qin Feng to Luoyang in a prison car and beheaded him. The Grand Sima Wu Han impeached Zhu You for abolishing the imperial edict and accepting surrender, which violated the general's mission, and the emperor did not punish him. After Zhu You returned, he joined forces with the Cavalry Commander Zang Gong to attack Yancen Yu and the bandits in Yin County, Zanhuang County and Zhuyang County, and they were all put down. Zhu You was a simple and upright man who liked Confucianism. Leading a large number of soldiers, accepting more surrenders, taking the ability to stabilize the city as the foundation, and not pursuing the merit of indiscriminate beheading. The soldiers were also strictly prohibited from plundering the people. The soldiers were happy to indulge themselves, and they often complained about Zhu You. In the ninth year of Jianwu, troops were stationed south to the Tang Dynasty to resist the Xiongnu. In the thirteenth year of Jianwu's reign, the number of fiefs was increased, and the title of Lihou was established, with 7,300 households living in the fiefs. In the fifteenth year of Jianwu's reign, he went to the capital and presented the seal and ribbon of the general, because he stayed in the capital to serve the imperial invitation.
target: **Zhu You**, courtesy name Zhongxian, was from Wan County, Nanyang. Orphaned young, he lived with his maternal grandparents in Fuyang and traveled to Chongling, where Shizu and Bosheng held him dear. Bosheng appointed him guard, and Shizu later made him army guard during the Hebei campaign. Zhu You once suggested that Chang'an's chaos indicated heaven-sent destiny for Shizu, who threatened him. He fought bravely in Hebei, became a partial general, and was named Marquis of Anyang. After Shizu ascended, Zhu You became General Jianyi. He attacked Deng Feng but was captured; after Deng Feng's defeat, Zhu You surrendered, was restored, and pacified Xinye and Suixian. He defeated Yancen, beheading Zhang Cheng, and received ninety-seven seals. He besieged Qin Feng in Liqiu, who surrendered after a year. Wu Han impeached Zhu You for accepting surrender against orders, but the emperor did not punish him. Zhu You, simple and upright, liked Confucianism, stabilized cities, and prohibited plundering, though soldiers complained. He later resisted the Xiongnu, increased his fief to 7,300 households, and suggested changing kings to dukes, which the emperor adopted. He died in Jianwu 24.

Following the pacification of Hebei, he paid homage to the Wild King's order, and together with Kou Xun, the prefect of Hanoi, rejected Luoyang in the south and guarded Tianjing Pass in the north. Zhu Jun and others did not dare to send troops. Shizu thought it was Wang Liang's contribution. When he came to the throne, it was discussed to elect the Great Sikong, and "Chi Fu Fu" said that Wang Liang's main guard was Xuanwu. The emperor thought that Ye Wang was the emigration of Wei Yuanjun, Xuanwu was the name of the water god, and Sikong was the official of water and earth, so he promoted Wang Liang to be the Great Sikong and granted him the title of Wu Qianghou. In the second year of Jianwu, he and the Grand Sima Wu Han and others attacked Tanxiang together. The imperial edict was that all military affairs should belong to the Grand Sima. However, Wang Liang launched the wild king's troops without authorization. The emperor refused to obey the edict and ordered him to stop operations in the county where he was located, and Wang Liang marched without authorization. The emperor was furious because Wang Liang had disobeyed orders before and after, and sent Minister Zong Guang to hold the talisman to kill Wang Liang in the army. Zong Guang couldn't bear it, so he took Wang Liang back to the capital in a prison car. After arriving in Beijing, the emperor pardoned him. After more than a month, he was appointed as Zhonglang General and also in charge of Jinwu affairs. Guard Jiguan in the north, attack Chimei Biejiao and surrender. In the spring of the third year, he attacked the five schools, pursued Xindu and Zhao State, and defeated them. All the settlements were pacified. In winter, an envoy was sent to hold the talisman festival to worship Wang Liang as the former general. In the spring of the fourth year of Jianwu's reign, he attacked Feicheng and Wenyang and captured them both. Jin and the hussar generals Du Mao attacked Jiaopi and Su Mao between Chu and Pei, and captured Daliang and Lisang. The captured general Ma Wu and the partial general Wang Ba also went their separate ways, and they were all put down in more than a year. In the fifth year of Jianwu's reign, he followed to rescue Taocheng, defeat Pang Meng and others. Wang Liang fought particularly effectively. He became the prefect of Shanyang, guarded and comforted the new converts, and led the troops as before. A few months later, he was recruited to Beijing and replaced Ouyang She as Henan Yin. Wang Liang opened a canal to divert the valley water into the city of Luoyang, then poured it eastward into Gongchuan River. When the canal was completed, the water stopped flowing. In the seventh year of Jianwu's reign, an impeachment report was issued. Wang Liang was frightened and wrote a letter requesting to resign. The emperor issued an edict saying: Wang Liang once led troops to conquer, and everyone praised him as a virtuous man, so he was promoted to the capital. It is suggested to open a canal to benefit others, but all efforts have been made, but the success has not been achieved. The people complained and slandered, and the talkers made a loud noise.
target: **Wang Liang**, courtesy name Junyan, from Yuyang, was a county official under Prefect Peng Chong. He led troops south to Shizu, became a partial general, and Marquis of Guannei. He pacified Hebei, guarded Tianjing Pass, and Shizu credited him. After ascension, prophecies favored Wang Liang for Grand Sikong, which he received. He disobeyed orders by launching troops without authorization; the emperor sent Zong Guang to execute him, but Zong Guang brought him to the capital instead. The emperor pardoned him, made him Zhonglang General, and later Former General. He captured Feicheng and Wenyang, pacified regions with Du Mao, and rescued Taocheng. As Henan Yin, he dug a canal diverting water to Luoyang, but it failed. He resigned, became Jinan prefect, and died in Jianwu 14.

source: In the 14th year of Jianwu's reign, he died in officialdom. Prince Yu succeeded to the throne. When Yu died, his son Wang Jianshi succeeded him. Wang Jianshi was investigated because his father Wang Yu and his younger brother Wang Ping participated in the rebellion of Chu King Liu Ying. At first, he returned to Guangwu in Hebei and became a backbone general, often accompanying him on expeditions. Dongfang had been pacified, and in the seventh year of Jianwu's reign, Du Mao was ordered to lead troops northward to garrison Jinyang and Guangwu to guard against Hu invaders. In the ninth year of Jianwu, Guo Liang, the prefect of Yanmen, attacked Yin Yufan County, the general of Lu Fang. Jia Lan, the general of Lu Fang, led more than 10,000 Hu cavalry to rescue him. Du Mao fought with him, but the army was defeated and led into Loufan County. At this time, Lu Fang occupied Gaoliu, joined forces with the Xiongnu soldiers, and invaded the border people many times, which made the emperor very worried. In the twelfth year of Jianwu's reign, the emissary Duan Zhong was dispatched to distribute the prisoners who had been released from the shackles to Du Mao in each county to guard the north. He then mobilized the border soldiers to build pavilions and repair beacon fires. He also mobilized the transportation of gold, silk and silk to supply the sergeants and give them to the border residents. The officials kept looking at each other. Du Mao also built farmland and used horse-drawn carts to transport the goods. First, Jia Dan, Huo Kuang, Xie Sheng and others from Yanmen were plundered by Yin You. Yin You took them as generals and guarded Pingcheng with Yin You. When Jia Dan and others heard that Lu Fang had failed, they killed Yin You with Huo Kuang, Xie Sheng and others to see Guo Liang. Guo Liang reported the situation and made them all princes. The emperor ordered that the transportation of gold and silk be given to Du Mao, Guo Liang's military officials and the people who surrendered in Pingcheng. From then on, Lu Fang's cities gradually surrendered. Guo Liang killed the members of his powerful family, the Xun family, to appease the old and weak. Within a month, Yanmen was temporarily peaceful, and Lu Fang fled to the Xiongnu.
target: **Du Mao**, courtesy name Zhugong, from Nanyang, joined Shizu in Hebei as a backbone general. After ascension, he became General and Marquis of Lexiang, later Marquis of Kuxing. He pacified bandits in Weijun, Qinghe, and Dongjun. As Hussar General, he attacked Peijun and captured Mangxian. He fought Lu Fang's general Jia Lan but was defeated. He built fortifications and beacon fires, transported supplies, and pacified Yanmen after Lu Fang fled to the Xiongnu. His fief increased, but he was dismissed for a soldier-killing incident, reduced to Marquis of Shenzang Township. He died in Jianwu 19.
