source: Jianwu died in the 19th year. His son Du Yuan succeeded him. In the 14th year of Yongping, because he was involved in a rebellion with King Dongping and others, his death was reduced by one degree, and the feudal state was abolished. In the seventh year of Yongchu, Mrs. Deng later granted Du Maosun and Du Feng the title of Marquis of Anleting. ◆Biography of Ma Cheng Ma Cheng, whose courtesy name is Junqian, was born in Jiyang, Nanyang County. He was a county official when he was young. Shizu conquered Yingchuan, used his horse to become an Jidu, and transferred him to the magistrate of Jiaxian County. When Shizu launched a crusade against Hebei, Ma Cheng abandoned his official post and went on foot to catch up with him in Puyang. He used Ma Cheng as a Qi gate to follow the expedition. Shizu ascended the throne and moved to the guard of the army. In the fourth year of Jianwu, he was promoted to General Yangwu and supervised the execution of General Liu Long, General Zhenwei Song Deng, and Shesheng Xiaowei Wang Shang. He sent soldiers from Kuaiji, Danyang, Jiujiang, and Lu'an to attack Li Xian. At that time, the emperor came to Shouchun and set up a mandala to offer sacrifices according to ancestral rites. Encircling Li Xian in Shu, he ordered all armies to dig deep ditches and fortify themselves. Li Xian challenged him many times, but Ma Cheng stood firm and refused to fight. He defended the area for more than a year. In the spring of the sixth year of Jianwu, the city was depleted of food, so they attacked the city, massacred the residents of Shucheng, beheaded Li Xian, pursued his followers, and pacified the Jianghuai area. In the summer of the seventh year of Jianwu, he was granted the title of Pingshuhou. In the eighth year, he followed the expedition and defeated Weixiao. He became the prefect of Tianshui with his horse and commanded the army as before. In winter, the army was summoned to the capital. In the ninth year of Jianwu, Dai Lai She was in charge of Zhonglang General, and led Wuwei General Liu Shang and others to conquer Hechi County and pacify Wudu County. In the second year, Grand Sikong Li Tong resigned from office and appointed Ma Cheng as his deputy. He lived in Grand Sikong Mansion and performed his duties faithfully. He paid homage to General Yangwu again for several months. In the 14th year of Jianwu's reign, troops were stationed in Changshan and Zhongshan to guard the northern border, and he led the troops of General Zhu You of Jianyi. He also built fortifications on behalf of General Du Mao of the Hussars. From Xihe to Weiqiao, from Heshang to Anyi, from Taiyuan to Jingxing, from Zhongshan to Ye, he built forts, set off beacons, and built a lookout post ten miles away. After five or six years of service, the emperor recognized Ma Cheng's hard work and summoned him back to Beijing. Many people from the frontier wrote letters begging him to return to the border, so the emperor sent Ma Cheng back to the camp. When Nandan was at peace in the fortress and the north was at peace, he worshiped Ma and became the governor of Zhongshan, presented the general's seal and ribbon, and continued to lead the troops as before. In the 24th year of Jianwu's reign, he attacked the barbarians in Wuxi Valley in the south. Before he achieved military success, he presented himself with the seal and ribbon of the prefect. In the twenty-seventh year of Jianwu's reign, he was granted the title of Marquis of Quanjiao and returned to the country.
target: **Ma Cheng**, courtesy name Junqian, from Nanyang, was a county official. Shizu made him Jidu and Jiaxian magistrate. He abandoned his post to join Shizu in Puyang, becoming Qi gate. He was named Marquis of Pingshu, defeated Weixiao, and became Tianshui prefect. He later guarded the northern border, building forts and beacons from Xihe to Ye. After five or six years, he returned to the capital but was sent back due to border petitions. He became Zhongshan governor, attacked Wuxi Valley barbarians, and died in Jianwu 32.

In the thirteenth year of Jianwu's reign, the number of towns increased and he was granted the title of Marquis of Jingling. In the fifteenth year of Jianwu's reign, the prefectures and counties were ordered to inspect and verify land reclamation. However, the governors and governors were unevenly distributed. They might give fine and fertile land to powerful families, while exploiting and exploiting the weak common people. The common people complained and filled the roads with howls and cries.
target: **Liu Long**, courtesy name Boyuan, from Nanyang, survived a family purge under Wang Mang. He studied in Chang'an, became Cavalry Captain, and joined Shizu in Hanoi. Li Yi killed his family. He became General Who Kills Captives, attacked Li Xian, and garrisoned Wudang. As Nanyang governor, he presented his general's seal. His fief increased to Marquis of Jingling. During land surveys, officials favored powerful families, causing complaints. Liu Long was imprisoned for fraud, demoted to commoner, later restored as Marquis of Fule Township.

Liu Long also defeated their army at the entrance of Jinxi Valley, captured their commander Zheng Er, beheaded more than a thousand people, and surrendered more than 20,000 people. After returning to Beijing, he was granted the title of Marquis of Changping. After the death of the Grand Sima Wu Han, Liu Long became the Hussar General and acted as the acting general for the Grand Sima. Liu Long followed the law and guarded himself, and took charge of the affairs for eight years. He presented the seal and ribbon of the general, dismissed from office, and was given cattle and ten bottles of wine, and was invited by the princes. In the 30th year of Jianwu's reign, he was granted the title of Marquis Shen. He died in the second year of Zhongyuan, and his posthumous title was Jinghou. His son Liu An succeeded him. ◆Fu Jun's biography Fu Jun's courtesy name was Ziwei, and he was a native of Xiangcheng, Yingchuan County. Shizu captured Xiangcheng, and Fu Jun greeted the Han army as the county pavilion chief and worshiped him as a school captain. Xiangcheng arrested his mother, brother, and clan, and executed them all. Follow and defeat Wang Xun and others, with Fu Jun as the partial general. Another attack on Jing and Mi was defeated. He was sent back to Yingchuan to collect and bury his family members. When Shizu was conquering Hebei, Fu Jun and more than ten guests pursued him northward. They caught up with him at Handan and paid a visit to Shizu. Shizu asked him to lead the Yingchuan troops and often follow him in the expedition. Shizu ascended the throne and took Fu Jun as his attendant. In the second year of Jianwu, he was granted the title of Marquis of Kunyang. In the third year of Jianwu's reign, he appointed Fu Jun as General Jinu, and together with Cen Peng, the general who conquered the south, defeated Qin Feng, so he led his troops to conquer Jiangdong and pacified all of Yangzhou. He died in the seventh year of Jianwu and was given the posthumous title of Weihou.
target: He attacked Jiaozhi barbarians, beheading over a thousand. After Wu Han's death, he became Hussar General and acting Grand Sima for eight years. He died in Zhongyuan 2, posthumously named Jinghou. **Fu Jun**, courtesy name Ziwei, from Yingchuan, greeted the Han army as pavilion chief. Xiangcheng executed his family. He became a partial general, defeated Wang Xun, and collected his family's remains. He joined Shizu in Hebei, leading Yingchuan troops. After ascension, he became attendant, Marquis of Kunyang, and General Jinu. He defeated Qin Feng with Cen Peng, pacified Yangzhou, and died in Jianwu 7, posthumously named Weihou.

source: In the second year of Jianwu, he was granted the title of Marquis of Kunyang. In the third year of Jianwu's reign, he appointed Fu Jun as General Jinu, and together with Cen Peng, the general who conquered the south, defeated Qin Feng, so he led his troops to conquer Jiangdong and pacified all of Yangzhou. He died in the seventh year of Jianwu and was given the posthumous title of Weihou. His son Fu Chang succeeded to the throne and was granted the title of Marquis of Wuhu. During the early years of the founding of the People's Republic of China, his mother was bereaved, so he wrote a letter saying that Wuhu was poor and unwilling to go to the country, and asked for a grant of 500,000 yuan to be made a Marquis of Guannei. Suzong was angry and demoted Fu Chang to the title of Marquis of Guannei, but refused to reward him with money. In the seventh year of Yongchu's reign, Empress Dowager Deng restored the title of Fu Tie, Fu Chang's son, to the title of Gaozhitinghou. ◆Jiantan's biography Jiantan's courtesy name is Zidanji, a native of Xiangcheng, Yingchuan. As a county official. When Shizu was campaigning against Hebei, someone recommended Jiantan, so Shizu summoned him. Because of his ability to serve as a county official, he was appointed as the chief bookkeeper. He also worshiped as a partial general and followed him to pacify Hebei. He also defeated the big gun Yu Lunu. When Shizu ascended the throne, he worshiped Jiandan as General Yanghua and granted him the title of Qianghou of Xuyin. He and other generals attacked Luoyang, while Zhu Tuna's generals guarding the east city acted as counterattacks and made a private agreement to open the east gate in the early morning. Jiantan and Jianyi General Zhu You took the opportunity to enter and fought with Zhu Tuna in Kuxia, killing many people. The fighting did not cease until breakfast, and Zhu Tun surrendered. He attacked Neihuang again and calmed down. In the second year of Jianwu, he and his right general Wan captured the counties of Nanyang, while Dong Jinjin, a native of Duxiang, built in Wancheng and captured Liu Ma, the prefect of Nanyang. Jiantan then led his troops to Wan, and selected his own suicide squad to climb the city tower at night and cut through the pass. Dong Jinjin abandoned the city and returned to Duxiang. Deng Feng built another army in Xinye and defeated Wu Han. At this time, Wan died of illness, and Jiandan was alone and helpless. Deng Feng was blocked from the south, and Dong Tanjin was blocked from the north. For a year, the roads were blocked and food supplies were cut off. Jiantan ate only vegetables and worked hard with the soldiers. Whenever he encounters a battle, he often acts as a target and is wounded in three places on his body, in order to save his troops. When the emperor conquered Nanyang and defeated Dong Yujin and Deng Feng, he appointed Jiantan as his left cao and often followed him on expeditions. In the sixth year of Jianwu, he was granted the title of Marquis of Hefei. Jianwu died in the twenty-sixth year of his reign. Zijianhong succeeded to the throne. Jianhong died, and Zijian succeeded to the throne. Jianfu died, and Zijianya succeeded to the throne. ◆The biography of Ma Wu Ma Wu was named Zizhang and was a native of Huyang, Nanyang County. When he was young, he lived in Jiangxia to avoid hatred. In the last years of Wang Mang's reign, the three elders of Jingling and Xiyang raised troops at the county border. Ma Wu also participated. Later, they entered the green forest and joined the Han army. When Gengshi was established, he appointed Ma Wu as his minister, and together with his ancestor Po Wang Xun and others, he worshiped him as General Zhenwei, and together with Shangshu Ling Xie Gong attacked Wang Lang. Shizu conquered Handan and invited Xie Gong, Ma Wu and others to hold a grand cocktail party in an attempt to kill Xie Gong, but failed. After the reception, Shizu and Ma Wu climbed up the Congtai alone and calmly said to Ma Wu: I have obtained the Yuyang and Shanggu assault cavalry and want you to command them. How about it? Ma Wu said: I am dull, cowardly and have no strategy. Shizu said: "A general has been a general for a long time and has a deep knowledge of military affairs. Is it the same as my history?" From this, Ma Wu returned to Shizu in his heart. After Xie Gong was executed, Ma Wu rushed to She Quan and surrendered. Shizu was very happy to see him and led him to his side. Every time he held a condolence banquet with the generals, Ma Wu often got up and considered it before him. Shizu was very happy. Then he asked Ma Wu to lead his troops to Ye. Ma Wu kowtowed and refused, saying that he was unwilling. Shizu praised his intention even more, and asked Ma Wu to follow him to attack the bandits. Shizu attacked You Lai, Wu Ban and others, but failed at Shenshui. Ma Wu, the only rear army in the palace, returned to attack the enemy's position, so the rebels did not dare to catch up. Entering Anci and Xiaoguangyang, Ma Wuchang was the vanguard and fought vigorously forward. All the generals led their troops to follow. Therefore, they defeated the rebels and pursued them to Pinggu and Junmi counties before returning to the army. When Shizu ascended the throne, he appointed Ma Wu as the Shizhong, Qi Duwei, and the Shandu Marquis. In the fourth year of Jianwu, he and Huya General Gai Yan and others attacked Liu Yong. Mawu attacked Jiyin separately, captured Chengwu and Chuqiu, and captured the general. The next year, Pang Meng made an attack on Taocheng. Ma Wu fought with him first and defeated Pang's army. Just as the emperor's chariot arrived, Pang Meng was defeated. In the summer of the sixth year of Jianwu, he and Gengxi, the general of Jianwei, attacked Weixiao. The Han army was disadvantaged and led the army to Long. Wei Xiao pursued him urgently. Ma Wu selected his best cavalry to return to the army to resist Wei Xiao. He wore armor and held a painted halberd and charged at him, killing thousands of people. Only then did Wei Xiao's troops retreat, and all the troops had to return to Chang'an.
target: **Jian Tan**, courtesy name Zidanji, from Yingchuan, was a county official. Shizu summoned him, made him chief bookkeeper and partial general. He pacified Hebei and defeated Yu Lunu. After ascension, he became General Yanghua and Marquis of Xuyin. He attacked Luoyang, opening the east gate with Zhu You, and fought Zhu Tuna until surrender. He pacified Neihuang, captured Nanyang counties, and fought Deng Feng while besieged for a year, eating only vegetables. He was wounded three times saving his troops. He became Marquis of Hefei in Jianwu 6 and died in Jianwu 26. **Ma Wu**, courtesy name Zizhang, from Nanyang, joined the Green Forest Army and later the Han. Gengshi made him General Zhenwei. Shizu invited him to command Yuyang and Shanggu cavalry, and Ma Wu secretly turned to Shizu. After Xie Gong's execution, Ma Wu surrendered. Shizu made him Shizhong, Qi Duwei, and Shandu Marquis. He attacked Liu Yong, captured Chengwu, defeated Pang Meng, and fought Wei Xiao, charging with a painted halberd to save the army. He became Marquis of Yu, guarded against Xiongnu, and was known for drinking and speaking frankly. The emperor tolerated his faults. He attacked Wuling barbarians and later Western Qiang, beheading 4,600. He died in Yongping 4.

source: They fought again in the Luodu Valley and were defeated by the Qiang soldiers, killing more than a thousand people. The Qiang then led the crowd out of the fortress, and Ma Wu pursued them to the east and west Han, where they defeated the Qiang soldiers, beheading 4,600 people and capturing 1,600 alive. The rest either surrendered or dispersed. Ma Wu reorganized his army and returned to the capital, adding 700 new households to the city, bringing the total to 1,800 households in total. He died in the fourth year of Yongping. Zima Tan succeeded to the throne, but because he was involved in the rebellion between his brother Bo Ji and Chu King Liu Yingdang and Yan Zhong, the feudal state was abolished. In the seventh year of Yongchu, Mrs. Deng subsequently granted Ma Wu and Sun Ma Zhen the title of Marquis of Ting. When Ma Zhen died, Zima succeeded him. The historian commented: The twenty-eight generals of Zhongxing were thought to correspond to the twenty-eight constellations in the sky in their previous lives, and they were not examined in detail. But they can feel the changes in current affairs, use their wisdom and courage, and are called assistant ministers. They are really ambitious and capable people. Most of the reviewers had a negative attitude towards the fact that Guangwu did not serve as a meritorious official, and even abandoned those handsome men who had achieved great achievements. However, it turns out that such a move was made out of foresight. As for the decline of royal power and the decline of domineering virtues, officials can still be appointed based on their merits and virtues. For example, Guan Zhong and Zan Xianpeng were successively promoted in the Qi Huan Dynasty, and Xian Zhen and Zhao Shanzhi were both listed in the Jin Wen Dynasty. It can be said that they are both connected. In the Qin and Han Dynasties, the world valued force, and the rise of warriors was the reason for helping kings' fortunes. There are also some cunning people who sell bamboo poles to butcher dogs, and some are rewarded by connecting the city, or they are entrusted with the task of leveling the land on which the world depends. Therefore, if the power is doubtful, gaps will arise, and if the forces are equal, disasters will occur. Xiao He and Fan Kouhui were still in prison, and Han Xin and Peng Yue were eventually executed. Isn't it like this? From then on, as for Xiaowu, the ministers and assistants of the fifth generation were all served by princes and nobles.
target: The historian comments that the twenty-eight Zhongxing generals were thought to correspond to constellations. Guangwu's policy of not appointing meritorious officials to high positions was foresighted, avoiding the disasters of Han Xin and Peng Yue. He rewarded heroes with fiefs but kept them from state affairs, maintaining peace.

source: Therefore, in view of the deviation from the past, Guangwu had ambitions to make things right. Although Kou Xun and Deng Yu had great achievements, and Geng and Jia Fu had great achievements, they could only enclose a few large counties, and they only added special advances and invitations from the court. Examining his policy during the period of peace, assessing his duties and holding his faults accountable, he is exactly the kind of person who is said to be able to guide people through government and coordinate them through punishment. If you act according to the law, it will definitely hurt them. Why? If you act according to the law, you will lose personal favors and old friendships; if you are forgiving in the first place, you will violate prohibitions and punishments; if you choose virtues and talents, you do not have to have great merits; if you recommend merits, people will not necessarily be virtuous; if you participate in the office, it will be difficult for the public to be satisfied; if the merits and talents are appointed side by side, the ills of the great ancestor will not be far away. One has to assess whether one is competent or not, that is, weighing the facts. Therefore, high-ranking officials rewarded their heroes with generous salaries, harsh laws and strict decrees, and ordered officials to perform their duties. In the era of Jianwu, there were more than a hundred people who were feudal lords, but only a few people such as Deng Yu, Jia Fu, and Li Tong participated in state affairs. The blame was shared equally, and the rest were treated favorably with generous laws, and their fiefdoms and salaries were improved, and all of them continued to benefit their descendants with their fame. In the past, Zhang Liang thought that all Liu Bang used were the old stories of Xiao He and Cao Shen, while Guo Qianji also ridiculed Nanyang for having too many dignitaries, and Zheng Xing advised him not to use only meritorious officials. Giving partial favor to others can easily lead to the disadvantages of selfish indulgence. If everyone is favored by the public, they will surely recruit talents from all over the world. Isn't it like this when you think about it? In Yongping, Xianzong recalled the heroes of his previous life, so he drew pictures of twenty-eight generals and hung them on the cloud platform of Nangong. In addition, there were Wang Chang, Li Tong, Dou Rong, and Zhuo Mao, a total of thirty-two people. Here it is appended to the end of the chapter according to its original order to indicate the ranking of the meritorious officials. source: ◆The biography of Li Gu, whose courtesy name was Zijian, was from Nanzheng, Hanzhong, and the son of Situ Li Hui. Li Hui's deeds are in "The Biography of Fang Shu". The statue of Li Gu has a peculiar appearance. There are bones on the head that protrude like a tripod foot, which rise into the hairline, and there are turtle inscriptions on the feet. When he was young, he was eager to learn and often traveled thousands of miles to find teachers on foot. So I read many ancient books and made friends with many wise men. People with lofty ideals from all over the world envy his style and come to learn from him. Everyone in the capital admired and said: This is the second Mr. Li again. Both Sili and Yizhou ordered the county governors to promote Li Gu as Xiaolian and call him Sikongpu, but they did not take office. In the second year of Yangjia, there were earthquakes, landslides, fires and other changes. The ministers recommended Li Gu to take countermeasures. The emperor issued an edict specifically asking him about the shortcomings of the contemporary era and what he should do for government. Li Gu replied: "I heard that the king regards heaven as his father and earth as his mother, and possesses the treasures of mountains and rivers." If the royal way works, then Yin and Yang will be harmonious; if politics is disobedient, landslides and earthquakes will become disasters.

source: The punishment cannot be reinstated, and the deeds will become bad as a result. This is the order of the world and the current urgent task. Your Majesty should open the book in the golden cabinet in the stone chamber, display the books, and recruit a group of Confucian scholars to ask questions about the gains and losses of government, criticize changes, and seek God's will. What they say makes sense, they implement it immediately, select their people, and commend those who are capable. Then holy virtues are heard every day, and loyal ministers use their wisdom. The eunuchs should also be dismissed, their authority should be removed, and two regular servants should be appointed, upright and virtuous people, and let them inspect the affairs on the left and right; five people from Xiaohuangmen, who are intelligent and elegant, should be allowed to work in the palace. In this way, the people who talk about it will become tired of it, and a peaceful world will come. The reason why I dare to state foolish words and take the liberty to report to you is that if the emperor wants to enlighten your majesty, your majesty should consider your words carefully and have mercy on me and pardon my death penalty. Emperor Shun saw the above countermeasures and adopted many of them. He immediately asked his mother to move back to his younger brother's house. All the regular servants kowtowed and apologized, and the court's political discipline was solemn. He also appointed Li Gu as his minister, but the eunuchs around his mother hated Li Gu for being too outspoken, so they fabricated crimes to frame Li Gu, and everything went from bad to worse. The chief minister Huang Shang and others asked the general Liang Shang, and the servant Huang Qiong investigated Li Gu's case. It took a long time before he was appointed as Yilang. Li Gu went out to become the magistrate of Luo County in Guanghan. When he arrived at Baishui Pass, he removed his seal and ribbon, returned to Hanzhong, and closed his door to avoid interacting with others. For half a year, Liang Shang asked Li Guzuo to work as a lieutenant. Liang Shang assisted the government as his father, but he was meek and defensive, unable to rectify the situation. Disasters occurred many times, and the power below him became increasingly powerful. Li Gu wanted to ask Liang Shang to rectify his morals first and resign from his position as Gao Man, so he wrote a memorial to Liang Shang: "Spring and Autumn" praises Yi father to open up the path of righteousness, and blames Wu Hao to close the door of benefit. When the way of righteousness is closed, the door of profit is opened; when the door of profit is opened, the way of righteousness is blocked. The former Emperor Xiao'an appointed Borong, Fan Feng and others internally, and Zhou Guang, Xie Yun and others were appointed externally. They accepted bribes and hired people improperly. There was a lot of discussion in the world and the voice of resentment was everywhere. When the imperial court was first established, it was relatively quiet. Within a few years, it gradually deteriorated. As the party advances, people are promoted every day, and those who stick to the good path are at the end of their rope, without any way to correct their shortcomings and establish righteousness. After taking the throne for more than ten years, the crown prince has not yet been established, and everyone is looking forward to it. The number of concubines in the palace can be reduced, and people of low status but suitable for having children can be selected to join the emperor and help God's will.
target: He advised against enfeoffing the emperor's grandmother, citing the danger of excessive power for relatives, and warned against the influence of the Liang family and eunuchs. He urged the emperor to select virtuous officials, dismiss eunuchs, and follow the laws of sages. Emperor Shun adopted many of his suggestions, but eunuchs framed Li Gu, leading to his dismissal. He later became a magistrate but resigned and returned home. Liang Shang asked Li Gu to be a lieutenant. Li Gu wrote to Liang Shang, criticizing the corruption of previous reigns and urging him to rectify morals, reduce palace concubines, and establish a crown prince.

source: However, building a new ancestral hall requires hundreds of millions of labor and is not to show virtue or frugality. Over the past few years, disasters have appeared many times, and it has not rained for many consecutive years, but it has been gloomy and cloudy. There must be a conspiracy within the palace. Confucius said: A wise man thinks of punishment when he sees a change, but a fool hides his name when he sees something strange. There is no distinction between closeness and distance in the way of heaven, which can be respected. The recent lunar eclipse has been on the side of Duanmen. Moon, the symbol of the minister. Generally speaking, if it is too high, it will be dangerous; if it is too full, it will overflow; if the moon is full, it will be short; and if the sun is at noon, it will shift. These four items are natural numbers. In the heart of heaven and earth, blessings should be modest and should not be prosperous. Therefore, virtuous people will retire after success, preserve their reputation, and live their lives well, without fear or worry. If Wang Gang is kept intact, his conduct is loyal, Ming Gong follows the path of Bo Gao, and his immortal reputation is preserved, is it the same as these mediocre relatives who enjoy a good position? I am a foolish person who is ignorant of the general situation. I secretly feel that the ancients repaid a favor with a meal. How much more can I not do my best to receive care and preferential treatment? Liang Shang did not listen.
target: He warned against building new ancestral halls and noted that disasters and eclipses indicated conspiracies within the palace. Liang Shang did not listen.

During the Yonghe period, bandits arose in Jingzhou and could not be pacified for many years, so the imperial court appointed Li Gu as the governor of Jingzhou. After Li Gu took office, he sent officials to visit the territory to express condolences, pardon the bandits' previous crimes, and start over with them. So the bandit leader Xia Mi and others recruited more than 600 of their gang members, tied themselves up, and came to surrender. Li Gudu forgave them and asked them to go back, so that they could gather among themselves and start a demonstration. Within half a year, all the thieves surrendered, and the state was at peace ever since. Li Gu reported to Nanyang Governor Gao Ci and others about their corrupt behavior. Gao Ci and others were afraid of being punished, so they jointly bribed the general Liang Ji with a large sum of money. Liang Ji sent the message thousands of miles for them, but Li Gu held on tighter. Liang Ji then ordered Li Gu to be appointed as the prefect of Taishan. At this time, the bandits in Taishan had been gathering for many years. There were often thousands of soldiers in the county, and they could not be suppressed by pursuit. After Li Gu took office, he dismissed all the county soldiers and went back to farm. He only selected more than a hundred people with fighting ability to stay and used their kindness to lure the thieves to surrender. Within a year, the thieves had all fled.
target: During the Yonghe period, Li Gu was appointed governor of Jingzhou, where he pardoned bandits and pacified the region within half a year. He reported corrupt officials, who bribed Liang Ji, leading to Li Gu's transfer to Taishan. There, he dismissed most soldiers and used kindness to subdue bandits within a year.

source: Li Gu also spoke to Guang Luxun and Liu Xuan: "In recent elections of pastoral guards, most of them are incompetent and even act unethically and infringe on the rights and interests of the people." Also, Your Majesty, you should stop having fun and play, and concentrate on your government. The emperor adopted their opinions and issued an edict to the various states to impeach officials below the prefect and county magistrate. Those who behaved improperly and were not good for the people should be removed from their official positions; those who committed treachery and serious crimes were sent to prison. Later, Emperor Chong came to the throne and appointed Li Gu as the Taiwei, who participated in the affairs of the Shangshu with Liang Ji. The emperor died the next year. The Empress Dowager Liang thought that the thieves in Yangzhou and Xuzhou were strong and she was afraid of causing chaos. She sent an imperial edict to Li Gu and others, hoping to wait until all the princes and princes summoned arrived before mourning. Li Gu replied: Although the emperor is young, he is still the father of the world. Today's collapse, people and gods are moved, how can any ministers rebel against the Communist Party and hide it? In ancient times, the First Emperor of Qin died in a sand dune. Hu Hai and Zhao Gao concealed his death and did not announce the mourning. They killed Fusu and even destroyed the country. Recently, the Marquis of Beixiang died, and the Yan brothers, Jiang Jing and others also concealed the secret, so Sun Cheng committed murder. This is a taboo in the world and must not be done. The Queen Mother obeyed and held mourning that night. Li Gu believed that Liu Suan, the king of Qinghe, was old and virtuous, and wanted to make him the emperor. He said to Liang Ji: To establish an emperor today, we should choose someone who is old and virtuous, and who is responsible for personal affairs. He hopes that the general will carefully review the plan and learn from Zhou Bo's approach to establishing Emperor Wen and Huo Guang's approach to establishing Emperor Xuan, instead of taking advantage of the weak monarchs like Empress Dowager Deng and Empress Dowager Yan. Liang Ji refused to listen, so he appointed Liu Zuan, the son of King Le'an, who was just eight years old, as Emperor Zhi. At this time, Emperor Chong took the Beibu Mountain Mausoleum as the burial site, and Li Gu suggested: Today there are bandits everywhere, so the military expenses will be doubled. If the emperor is still young, his tomb can be built in the Kuanling Tomb. According to the Kangling system of Emperor Shang, the cost can be reduced by one-third. So he followed Li Gu's advice. At this time, the Empress Dowager appointed prime ministers because of her repeated misfortunes. Li Gu's corrective opinions were obeyed every time, and those Huangmen eunuchs were all dismissed. The world hoped for peace, but Liang Ji guessed and hated each other. At first, many of the officials appointed during Emperor Shun's reign were not in order. When Li Gu was in charge, he dismissed more than a hundred people. This group of people were both resentful and wanted Liang Ji's help, so they jointly wrote an urgent memorial to slander Li Gu. The memorial said: "I heard that the king does not act according to heaven, so I cannot accept the destiny of heaven; I do not tell the past, and I cannot serve the king." In ancient times, after Yao's death, Shun admired him for three years. When he sat down, he saw Yao by the wall, and when he was eating, he saw Yao beside the soup.
target: Li Gu was promoted and recommended several scholars. He later became Taiwei under Emperor Chong. When the emperor died, Li Gu insisted on immediate mourning, opposing the Empress Dowager's delay. He advocated for establishing an older, virtuous emperor, but Liang Ji appointed the young Liu Zuan as Emperor Zhi. Li Gu reduced burial costs for the emperor. He dismissed over a hundred improperly appointed officials, who then slandered him to Liang Ji, accusing him of nepotism, extravagance, and lack of mourning. The Empress Dowager spared Li Gu from death. Liang Ji later poisoned Emperor Zhi. Li Gu cried over the emperor's body. When establishing a new emperor, Li Gu advocated for Liu Lian, the King of Qinghe, but Liang Ji, persuaded by eunuchs, chose Liu Zhidang (Emperor Huan) instead. Liang Ji later falsely accused Li Gu of plotting to make Liu Lian emperor and imprisoned him. Despite public support, Liang Ji had Li Gu killed at age 54. Before death, Li Gu wrote to Hu Guang and Zhao Jie, blaming them for following Liang Ji and causing the decline of the Han dynasty.

source: Who would have thought that once Liang was confused, you would just follow suit and turn good things into bad things, and success into failure? The decline of the Han Dynasty began from then on. You have received generous rewards from the Lord, but you subvert rather than support, and overturn national affairs. Will the good history of future generations tolerate your selfishness? My body is gone, but I still gain something in terms of righteousness, so what else can I say? Hu Guang and Zhao Jie felt sad and ashamed after receiving the letter, and they both sighed and shed tears. The prefecture and county arrested Li Gu's two sons, Li Ji and Lizi, and both died in prison. The youngest son Li Xie escaped with his life. Liang Ji sealed the official positions of Hu Guang and Zhao Jie, exposed Li Gu's body on a traffic thoroughfare, and ordered that those who dared to approach would be punished with additional penalties. Li Gu's disciple Runan Guo Liang, who had just grown up and studied in Luoyang, went to the court with a memorial ax and ax in his left hand and a husband's pledge in his right hand, requesting that Gu's body be collected. He was not allowed to do so, so he went to cry and made his speeches in front of him, then stayed in mourning and refused to leave.
target: His sons died in prison, and his body was exposed. His disciple Guo Liang and others mourned him, and the Empress Dowager eventually allowed his burial.

source: From then on, the two became famous, and the three princes recruited him. Dong Ban then disappeared and disappeared. Li Gu wrote a total of eleven articles including chapters, tables, memorials, discussions, teachings, countermeasures, notes and inscriptions. Disciple Zhao Cheng and others could not stop lamenting, so they discussed Li Gu's remarks and deeds and wrote an article "Virtue". ◆The biography of Du Qiao, named Shu Rong, was born in Linli, Hanoi. When he was young, he was a Zhusheng and was conscripted into Situ Yang Zhen's mansion. Gradually he was promoted to the prefect of Nanjun, transferred to the prime minister of the East China Sea, and became a servant in the imperial court. In the first year of Han'an, Du Qiao acted for Dr. Guanglu and sent him to inspect Yanzhou. The above table reports that Li Gu, the prefect of Taishan, has the best political performance in the world; Liang Rang, the prefect of Chenliu, Si Gong, the prefect of Jiyin, and Cui Yuan, the prefect of Jibei, etc. embezzled more than ten million. Liang Rang is the uncle of General Liang Ji, and Bangong and Cui Yuan are Liang Ji's cronies. Returning to Beijing, he was awarded the title of Crown Prince and Tutor, and was promoted to Minister of Agriculture.
target: Du Qiao, courtesy name Shurong, was from Linli, Hanoi. He served as a prefect and later as a servant. He reported that Li Gu had the best political performance and that others, including Liang Ji's relatives, had embezzled money. He was promoted to Minister of Agriculture.

source: The above table reports that Li Gu, the prefect of Taishan, has the best political performance in the world; Liang Rang, the prefect of Chenliu, Si Gong, the prefect of Jiyin, and Cui Yuan, the prefect of Jibei, etc. embezzled more than ten million. Liang Rang is the uncle of General Liang Ji, and Bangong and Cui Yuan are Liang Ji's cronies. Returning to Beijing, he was awarded the title of Crown Prince and Tutor, and was promoted to Minister of Agriculture. At this time, the five descendants of Liang Ji and the ministers of Zhongchang had no merit and were granted the title. Du Qiao wrote a letter to remonstrate: The emperor comes from the vassals, Long Fei ascends the throne, heaven and man return, and all nations rely on them. However, instead of appointing loyal and virtuous people, they first appoint the left and right confidants. This harms good people, is harmful to virtue, and encourages the trend of flattery. I heard that in ancient times, wise kings were rewarded for their merits and punished for their faults; the declining kings were dim and incompetent, and rewards and punishments were all based on selfish motives. Nowadays, the Liang family, the eunuchs and evil sons, all wear seals and ribbons with no merit, and the fiefdoms for their hard work and merit are given to them. How can we fully explain the perverseness and disorder of this practice. Merits are not rewarded, and good deeds are not rewarded as they should be; no one cares about treacherous people, allowing them to do evil and cause disaster. Therefore, people are not afraid of the murderous butcher's knife placed in front of them, and conferring titles and titles will not serve as a reward. If this continues for a long time, is it just harmful to political integrity? It is enough to cause chaos and ruin the country. It is worthy of vigilance! Please play, your Majesty does not need it. Yizhou governor Zhongfan impeached Yongchang prefect Liu Junshi and sent a golden snake to Liang Ji. When the incident was discovered, he sent the golden snake to Sinong. Liang Ji asked Du Qiao to borrow it for a look, but Du Qiao refused, and Liang Ji began to hold a grudge. Du Qiao was promoted to Dahonglu. At this time, Liang Ji's daughter died, and all the officials went to attend the funeral. Du Qiao could not go alone, and Liang Ji hated him even more. Du Qiao was promoted to Guang Luxun. In the first year of Jianhe, Hu Guang was appointed Taiwei on his behalf. Emperor Huan planned to accept Liang Ji's sister as his queen. Liang Ji wanted to welcome his sister with generous gifts, but Du Qiao refused to listen to him according to the old regulations. Liang Ji asked Du Qiao to appoint Si Gong as minister. Du Qiao believed that Si Gong was guilty of embezzlement and refused to use it. This greatly contradicted Liang Ji's wishes. First, Li Gu was deposed, and everyone inside and outside the court was dejected. All the ministers were afraid and trembling. Only Du Qiao was serious and did not dare to offend. Therefore, the whole country sighed for him, and both the government and the public looked at him and worried about him. After a few months in office, he was dismissed from office due to an earthquake. Eunuchs Tang Heng, Zuo and others jointly framed Du Qiao in front of Emperor Huan, saying: When the emperor ascended the throne, Du Qiao and Li Gu objected, saying that the emperor was not worthy of enshrining the ancestral temple of the Han Dynasty and inheriting the throne. Emperor Huan also hated him. After the Qinghe King incident occurred, Liang Ji suggested that the supervisor should impeach Du Qiao and Li Gu for colluding with Liu Tuna, and ask for their arrest and prosecution. The Empress Dowager Liang always knew that Du Qiao was loyal, so she only dismissed him from office. Liang Ji became even more angry and sent someone to threaten Du Qiao, saying: "If you commit suicide early, your wife will be saved." Duccio refused. The next day Liang Ji sent cavalry to his house, but when he heard no cries, he arrested him and died in prison.
target: He remonstrated against granting titles to Liang Ji's relatives and eunuchs without merit, warning it would cause chaos. He refused Liang Ji's requests to borrow evidence and attend his daughter's funeral, earning Liang Ji's hatred. As Guang Luxun, he opposed lavish gifts for Liang Ji's sister becoming queen and refused to appoint a corrupt official. After Li Gu was deposed, Du Qiao remained serious and unyielding. He was dismissed due to an earthquake. Eunuchs and Liang Ji framed him for opposing the emperor's ascension and colluding with Li Gu. He was arrested and died in prison.

source: Liang Ji became even more angry and sent someone to threaten Du Qiao, saying: "If you commit suicide early, your wife will be saved." Duccio refused. The next day Liang Ji sent cavalry to his house, but when he heard no cries, he arrested him and died in prison. The wife went back to her hometown. The bodies of Du Qiao and Li Gu were exposed in the north of the city, and their families and friends did not dare to look at them. Du Qiao's old subordinate Chen Liu and Yang Kuang heard about it and rushed to Luoyang wailing at night. Wearing his original red turban, he pretended to be a Xiamen Pavilion official, guarding the corpse and driving away flies and mosquitoes for a total of twelve days. The governor captured him and reported to the court. Empress Dowager Liang believed that people with loyalty should not care about their sins. Yang Kuang then took Tie to the court to submit a letter and requested that the bodies of Li Gu and Du Qiao be collected. The Queen Mother agreed to his request. The funeral was carried out with ceremonial etiquette, and Du Qiao was sent home for his funeral. After the funeral, he lived in seclusion and did not serve as an official.
target: His body was exposed, but his former subordinate Yang Kuang mourned him and requested burial, which the Empress Dowager granted. The historian commented that Li Gu and Du Qiao sacrificed their lives for righteousness, unlike Hu Guang and Zhao Jie.

source: Li Tong, whose courtesy name was Ciyuan, was from Wan County, Nanyang County. He has been famous for doing business for generations. His father, Li Shou, was nine feet tall and his appearance was very different from ordinary people. He was serious and resolute, and his home was as if he were in a court. At first, he worked with Liu Xin. He was fond of astronomical calculations and prophecies for predicting bad luck. He became Wang Mang's disciple. Li Tong also worked for General Wuwei, and later became the magistrate of Wu County, with a reputation for being capable. In the last years of Wang Mang's reign, the people were worried and resentful. Li Tong once heard his father's prophecy about the revival of the Liu family and the Li family as an assistant, and he often thought about it. Because his family was very wealthy and ranked first in the township, he did not want to be an official, so he voluntarily resigned and returned home. Later, Wang Chang's Xiajiang soldiers and Wang Kuang's Xinshi soldiers rose up, causing turmoil in Nanyang. Li Tong's cousin Li Yi, who had always been a good person, discussed together and said: Now that there is chaos from all directions, Wang Mang's regime is about to collapse, and the Han Dynasty should rise.
target: Li Tong, courtesy name Ciyuan, was from Wan County, Nanyang. His family was renowned for business, and his father Li Shou was a tall, imposing man who served Wang Mang. Li Tong worked for General Wuwei and later became magistrate of Wu County, known for his competence. During Wang Mang's late reign, Li Tong heard his father's prophecy about the Liu family's revival with the Li family as assistants. Wealthy and disinclined to serve, he resigned and returned home.

source: Guang Wuchu admired Li Tong because he was a gentleman, so he went to thank him. When they met, the two talked for a long time and shook hands happily. Li Tong told all the prophecies, and Guangwu started to have a big surprise, saying that he didn't dare to take it seriously. At this time, Li Shou was in Chang'an. Guangwu looked at Li Tong secretly and said, "In this case, what should your father do?" Li Tong said: I already have a solution. So he stated his plan in detail to Guangwu. Since Guangwu was well aware of Li Tong's intentions, he made an agreement with Li Tong and made a plan to take advantage of the capital's knight test on the first day of autumn to kidnap Zhen Fu, a senior official in the front team, and Qiuci, a subordinate of Zhengliang, so he ordered the public to declare an uprising. He sent Guangwu and Li Yi back to Chongling and raised their troops accordingly. He sent his cousin's son Li Ji to Chang'an to tell Li Shou the plan. Li Ji died of illness on the road. Li Shou knew the secret and wanted to flee back. Li Shousu was friendly with Huang Xian, a fellow villager. Huang Xian was then the Zhonglang General. When he heard the news, he said to Li Shou: "The gates are now tightly guarded. Your appearance is special. Where will you go?" It is better to go to the court and ask for your return. At this time, Zhen Fu from the front team wrote another letter stating the situation of Li Tong's army. Wang Mang was angry and prepared to kill Li Shou. Gengshi sent Li Tong back to Jingzhou to guard Jingzhou, so Li Tong married Guangwu's sister Boji, who was Princess Ningping. Guangwu ascended the throne and recruited Li Tong as a guard. target: When rebellions erupted in Nanyang, Li Tong and his cousin Li Yi discussed joining Liu Boxheng (Liu Yan) and his brother Guangwu (Liu Xiu) to restore the Han. Li Tong sent Li Yi to greet Guangwu, and they formed a pact. They planned to kidnap officials Zhen Fu and Liang Qiuci to spark an uprising. Li Tong sent his cousin's son Li Ji to inform Li Shou in Chang'an, but Li Ji died en route. Li Shou, learning the secret, tried to flee but was advised by Huang Xian to request leave. The plot was discovered; Wang Mang arrested Li Shou and, despite Huang Xian's pleas, executed both and Li Shou's family in Chang'an. Nanyang also killed sixty-four of Li Tong's clan members. Li Tong joined Guangwu and Li Yi in Jiyang, attacking and killing Zhen Fu and Liang Qiuci. Under Gengshi, Li Tong became General of Zhuguo and later King of Xiping. He married Guangwu's sister, Princess Ningping. After Guangwu ascended, Li Tong served as Grand Minister of Agriculture, guarding the capital during campaigns. In Jianwu 5-6, he led troops against Hanzhong bandits and Gongsun Shu, defeating them. As peace prevailed, Li Tong sought to retire due to illness, but Guangwu refused. He became Grand Sikong but remained humble, often taking sick leave. Guangwu favored him, granting his son Li Xiong a marquisate. Li Tong died in Jianwu 18, posthumously titled Gonghou. His lineage continued, and he alone among his kin lived with honor.

When his teacher Zhu Pu passed away, Huan Rong went to Jiujiang to attend the funeral. He carried the soil to build his teacher's grave, so he stayed to teach and had hundreds of disciples. Wang Mang failed and the world was in chaos. Huan Rong took the scriptures and fled into the valley with his students. Although he was often hungry, he continued to lecture on scriptures and treatises. Later, he taught in the Jianghuai area. In the 19th year of Jianwu's reign, when Huan Rong was over sixty years old, he was awarded the post of Grand Situ. At that time, Xianzong had just been established as the crown prince, and he chose to seek Ming scriptures. He promoted Huan Rong's student Yuzhang Hetang to be the general of Huben Zhonglang, and taught the prince in the Book of Documents. Shizu calmly asked He Tang who his master was, and He Tang replied: Huan Rong of Pei State. The emperor immediately summoned Huan Rong and ordered him to explain "Shang Shu". He thought it was very good. He worshiped Huan Rong as Yilang, gave him one hundred thousand yuan, and allowed him to enter the palace and teach the prince. At every court meeting, Huan Rong was often asked to explain the scriptures in front of the ministers. source: ◆The Legend of Huan Tan Huan Tan, whose courtesy name is Junshan, was born in Xiangxian County, Peiguo County. His father was Tai Leling when he became emperor. Huan Tan was appointed as a minister due to his father's relationship, so he loved music and was good at drums and harp. He is very knowledgeable, has read all the Five Classics, and can explain the great meanings of ancient books. Distinguish sentences without leaving chapters. He wrote good articles, and especially loved ancient learning. He repeatedly analyzed difficult and different meanings through debates between Liu Xin and Yang Xiong. He also loved miscellaneous dramas. He was a simple man and did not put on official airs. He liked to slander secular Confucian scholars, so he was often ostracized and attacked. During the reigns of Emperor Ai and Emperor Ping, his status was only that of a man. Queen Fu's father, Fu Yan, the Marquis of Kongxiang, thought highly of Huan Tan. At that time, Gao'an Hou Dong Xian was favored by the emperor, and his sister was named Zhaoyi. The emperor became increasingly alienated from Empress Fu, and Fu Yan was silently dissatisfied. Huan Tan said to Fu Yan: In the past, Emperor Wu wanted to appoint Wei Zifu, and secretly collected Empress Chen's faults. Empress Chen was finally deposed, and Wei Zifu was actually appointed. Now Dong Xian is favored and his sister is especially favored. There may be another change of "Wei Zihu". Don't you worry? Fu Yan was alarmed and said: Yes, what should we do? Huan Tan said: Punishment cannot be imposed on innocent people, and evil spirits cannot defeat righteous people in vain. A scholar serves his master with his intelligence, and a woman seeks his master with a charming way. The queen is young and has not experienced many hardships. There are people who are driving witch doctors inside, seeking magic skills outside, and practicing evil ways. We must be on guard against these. Moreover, because the king is respected as the father of the queen, he communicates with the guests. The guests will definitely use this to enhance their power, which will attract people's ridicule. Why don't you thank the guests and send the disciples away? You must be humble and cautious. This is the way to cultivate yourself and your family to avoid disaster. Fu Yan said: OK. So he dismissed the guests and went to the palace to tell the queen, just as Huan Tan said. Later, Dong Xian indeed hinted to the imperial physician Ling Zhenqin to collect the Fu family's crimes and arrest Fu Xi, Empress Fu's younger brother. During the interrogation, no evidence of guilt was found, and the case was eliminated, so the Fu family was finally saved during the reign of Emperor Ai. Later, Dong Xian became the Grand Sima. Hearing about Huan Tan's reputation, he wanted to make friends with him. Huan Tan first wrote to Dong Xian, saying that Dong Xian could not use the method of assisting the country and protecting himself, so Huan Tan would not have any contact with him. When Wang Mang was regent and usurped Emperor Ping, the intellectuals at that time all praised Wang Mang. Or they described auspicious signs to create public opinion to please Wang Mang, but Huan Tan kept his innocence and remained silent.
target: Huan Tan, courtesy name Junshan, was from Xiangxian County, Peiguo. He was appointed as a minister through his father's connections. He was knowledgeable in the Five Classics, wrote excellent essays, and favored ancient learning. He debated with Liu Xin and Yang Xiong, and enjoyed criticizing secular Confucian scholars, which led to his ostracism. During the reigns of Emperor Ai and Emperor Ping, his status remained low. Fu Yan, Marquis of Kongxiang, valued Huan Tan. When Emperor Ai favored Dong Xian and his sister Zhaoyi over Empress Fu, Huan Tan warned Fu Yan of potential danger, advising him to dismiss guests and remain humble. Fu Yan followed this advice, and when Dong Xian later attempted to incriminate the Fu family, no evidence was found, saving them. Dong Xian later sought Huan Tan's friendship, but Huan Tan refused, criticizing Dong Xian's inability to protect himself through proper governance. During Wang Mang's usurpation, Huan Tan remained silent while others praised Wang Mang. After Emperor Guangwu (Shizu) ascended, Huan Tan served as a郎官. He submitted memorials on governance, emphasizing the importance of wise advisors, harmony between ruler and ministers, and adapting policies to circumstances.

He is fond of drinking and drinking, and is good at archery, playing chess, five grids, six gambling, playing ball, and playing with money. He also likes to drive hawks and dogs, and race horses and fight cocks. At first, he served as the Minister of Huangmen, and was promoted to the official positions of Shizhong, Huben Zhonglangjiang, Yueqi, Infantry Colonel, and Zhijinwu. In the first year of Emperor Shun Yonghe's reign, Liang Ji was appointed Yin of Henan. During his tenure, he was brutal and cruel and did many illegal things. His father, Liang Shang, had a close friend, Lu Fang, the commander of Luoyang, who discussed many of Liang Ji's shortcomings with Liang, and Liang Shang blamed Liang Ji for this. Liang Ji had a grudge, so he sent someone to assassinate Lu Fang on the road. He was afraid that Liang Shang would find out, so he put the suspicion of assassinating Lu Fang on Lu Fang's enemies. When Liang Shang died and was not buried, Emperor Shun appointed Liang Ji as the general and Liang Ji's younger brother, Shizhong Liang Buyi, as the Yin of Henan. Although Liang Ji refused to take responsibility, he was even more extravagant and cruel. Soon, Emperor Chong of the Han Dynasty died again, and Liang Ji welcomed Emperor Zhi. After the death of Emperor Zhi, Liang Ji ushered in Emperor Huan and framed Li Gu and former Taiwei Du Qiao. Everyone in the country sighed and felt in danger. This incident was recorded in "The Biography of Li Gu". In the first year of the founding of the Han Dynasty, Emperor Huan of the Han Dynasty granted 13,000 households in Liangji food towns, and increased the number of people recommended by the General's Palace for outstanding candidates and the number of talented people. source: Liu Chang, a student from Guiyang, was a famous Confucian at that time and had always been close friends with Yuan Zhu. Liang Ji insulted him by calling him to fill the vacancy of a minor official like Ling Shi. At that time, Hao Xie and Hu Wu, both from Taiyuan, loved to express their honest opinions and profound insights. They are all friendly with Yuan Zhu. Originally, Hao Xie and others jointly submitted a letter to the Sangong Mansion, recommending noble and virtuous people in the world, but not to the general. Liang Ji now recalled this incident and was very angry; he also suspected that Hao Xie and others were Yuan Zhu's accomplices. So he ordered the officials in Zhongdu to issue official documents to capture those who wrote letters to the Sangong Mansion recommending virtuous people, and kill them all. He also killed Hu Wu's family, killing more than 60 people in total. When Hao Xie escaped before, he knew that he would not avoid disaster, so he used a car to pull the coffin to Liang Ji's house to submit a letter. After the letter was delivered, he committed suicide by taking poison. In this way, his family was saved. After Liang Ji was executed, the imperial court issued an edict to pay homage to Yuan Zhu and others. All the cruel and vicious things Liang Ji did were similar to this situation. Liang Buyi loved scriptures and treated virtuous corporals. Liang Ji was secretly jealous of him, so he told Emperor Huan through the Zhongchang Shi that he should be transferred to Guangluxun. He also hinted that the ministers jointly recommended Liang Yin, Liang Ji's son, to be the Yin of Henan. Liang Yin, also known as Hu Gou, was only sixteen years old at this time. He was ugly and could not wear official clothes or hats. Everyone who saw him on the road laughed at him. Liang Busu felt ashamed that he was estranged from his brothers, so he resigned and went home, closing the door with his younger brother Liang Meng and not participating in foreign affairs. Liang Ji didn't want Liang Buyu to interact with guests, so he secretly sent someone in disguise to wait in front of his door and take note of anyone coming and going. Ma Rong, the governor of Nanjun, and Tian Ming, the governor of Jiangxia, visited Liang Buyi when they first took office. Liang Ji hinted to the state and county officials to find other things to frame them, and sentenced them all to shaved heads and whippings, and sent them to Shuofang. Ma Rong attempted suicide and Tian Ming died on the road. In the second year of Yongxing reign of Emperor Huan of the Han Dynasty, Liang Ma, son of Liang Buyi, was granted the title of Marquis of Yingyin, and Liang Tao, son of Liang Yin, was granted the title of Marquis of Chengfu. In total, Liang Ji's family has seven people who have been granted the title of marquis, three queens, six nobles, two generals, seven women and daughters who have settled in the city and become "kings", and three people who have married princesses. The remaining fifty-seven people hold official positions such as Qing, General, Yin, and Xiao. Liang Ji had been in power for more than 20 years, and his power was extremely powerful. He exerted his despotic power inside and outside the court. All officials looked sideways and did not dare to disobey his orders. The emperor had no choice but to respect him and did not dare to handle all government affairs personally. Emperor Huan of the Han Dynasty was already dissatisfied with Liang Ji's arrogance.
target: Liang Ji's power grew unchecked, with all court matters decided by him. He killed officials who opposed him, including Wu Shu and Hou Meng. A young doctor named Yuan Zhu wrote to the emperor criticizing Liang Ji's power, but Liang Ji had him beaten to death. Liang Ji also killed many others, including Hao Xie and Hu Wu's families. Liang Buyi, who loved scriptures and treated others well, was estranged by Liang Ji and resigned. Liang Ji's family included seven marquises, three queens, six nobles, two generals, and many other officials. Liang Ji held power for over 20 years, dominating the court. Emperor Huan, angered by Liang Ji's arrogance, plotted with eunuchs to kill him. In the first year of Yanxi, after a series of events, Emperor Huan ordered the arrest of Liang Ji. Liang Ji and Sun Shou committed suicide.

source: At that time, Deng Meng's brother-in-law Bing Zun served as Yilang. Liang Ji was afraid that Bing Zun would prevent Xuan from letting his daughter change her surname, so he met an assassin in Yancheng who assassinated Bing Zun and also wanted to kill Xuan. The Xuan family lived in Yanxi, and were neighbors to Yuan She, a regular servant of the Central Government. Liang Ji sent assassins to the Yuan family's house, hoping to enter the Xuan family from there. When Yuan She found out, he beat drums to gather the people and told Xuan the situation. Xuan immediately ran to Emperor Huan to report. Emperor Huan was furious and discussed with Shan Chao, Ju Yuan, Tang Heng, Zuo Xuanguan, Xu Huang and others to kill Liang Ji. This incident is recorded in "Eunuch Biography". Liang Ji suspected Shan Chao and others, so he sent Zhang Yun from Zhonghuangmen to stay in the palace to prevent accidents. Ju Yuan ordered the officials to arrest Zhang Yun, saying that he had entered the palace without permission and had evil intentions. Emperor Huan therefore came to the front hall, called all the ministers in, and announced the matter. The minister, Yin Xun, was sent to hold the talisman, and officials below Shangshu Cheng and Shangshu Lang were sent to guard various official offices in the palace with weapons. Gather all the talismans and send them to the palace. Huangmen ordered Ju Yuan to lead the knights, Huben, Yu Lin, Duhou swordsmen and halberds from the left and right stables, totaling more than a thousand people, together with Sili captain Zhang Biao, to surround the Liangji mansion. He sent Guangluxun Yuan Xu to collect the seal and ribbon of General Liangji with a talisman, and conferred him the title of Marquis of Bijingdu Township. Only Yin Xun, Yuan Xu and Tingwei Handan Yi were in the court. At that time, because the incident suddenly broke out in the palace, the messengers rushed back and forth to report the incident. The ministers were at a loss and the government and the people were in great commotion. It took several days to settle down, and the people all applauded and celebrated. Liang Ji's property was confiscated and sold by the court, totaling more than three billion yuan, which was used to replenish the national treasury and reduce half of the world's taxes. Liang Ji's gardens were demolished and given to poor people for farming and grazing.

source: ◆Biography of Fan Hong, named Mi Qing, a native of Huyang, Nanyang County, and the uncle of Shizu. His ancestor, Zhou Zhongshanfu, was granted the title of Fan, and because of this, he became a prominent surname in the village. His father, Fan Zhong, whose courtesy name was Junyun, was good at farming and breeding goods. Fan Zhong was kind-hearted and law-abiding. He lived together for three generations, and his descendants respected him day and night, always like a public servant. In his business operation, he threw away nothing, taught children, slaves, and slaves, and everyone found his own suitability. Therefore, he was able to work together, and his financial profits doubled every year, so he opened more than 300 hectares of land. The cottages they built all had high halls and pavilions, and were filled with ponds and canals. There are also fish and livestock in the pond, and everything you ask for will be given. He once wanted to make utensils, so he first planted Ziqi lacquer, which was ridiculed by people at that time. However, over time, it was put to good use, and people who had ridiculed him in the past borrowed it from him. With a huge capital of tens of thousands, he provided relief to support the clan and enga the village. Fan Zhong, his grandson and his brothers, fought over property. Fan Zhong felt ashamed and settled their grievances with two hectares of land. The county praised him and recommended him as the third elder. He died at the age of eighty. The people who borrowed money from him accumulated millions in debt, and Fan Chong ordered the deeds to be burned. The debtors were very ashamed when they heard about it and tried to repay their debts, but the sons obeyed their father's orders and refused to accept. Fan Hong rarely has ambitions. In the last years of Wang Mang's reign, rebels rose up. Liu Boxheng and his clan brother Liu Ci both led their troops to attack Huyang, but failed to capture it. Liu Ci's sister was Fan Hong's wife, so Huyang arrested Fan Hong's wife and ordered her to tell Bo Sheng, but Fan Hong stayed behind and refused to return. The military commander of Huyang wanted to kill his wife, and the chief officials said the following: Fan Zhong and his son lived in the countryside with courtesy, justice, and kindness. Although they are guilty, we will talk about it later. Just when the Han soldiers arrived, the Yang army was frightened and anxious and did not dare to kill Fan's wife, so they were able to escape from danger. When Gengshi was appointed, he wanted to make Fan Hong his general, but Fan Hong kowtowed and declined, saying: Scholars don't understand military affairs. Unexpectedly, he was exempted from returning and built a camp with relatives of the clan to defend himself. More than a thousand people, old and weak, followed him. At that time, the Red Eyebrow bandits plundered Tangzi Township and killed many people. They also wanted to attack Fan Hong's camp. Fan Hong sent people to bring cattle, wine, rice and grain to the Red Eyebrows. The red eyebrow elders first heard about Fan Hong's benevolence and said: "Fan Jun has always been kind, and now he treats us so favorably, why attack him."
target: The biographies of Fan Hong and Yin Shi, two figures from the early Eastern Han dynasty. Fan Hong, a native of Huyang, Nanyang, was the uncle of Emperor Guangwu (Shizu). His ancestor was granted the title of Fan. His father, Fan Zhong, was a kind, law-abiding farmer and businessman who expanded the family's wealth to over 300 hectares of land, building grand estates with ponds and canals. He provided relief to his clan and village, and once settled a property dispute among his grandsons by giving them two hectares of land. Upon his death at eighty, his son Fan Hong burned the deeds of debtors, refusing repayment. During Wang Mang's reign, rebels attacked Huyang, and Fan Hong's wife was captured, but she was spared due to the family's reputation for kindness. Fan Hong declined a generalship under Gengshi, instead building a defensive camp that sheltered over a thousand people. When Red Eyebrow bandits threatened, he sent them gifts, and they spared him due to his benevolence.

target: Yin Shi, a native of Xinye, Nanyang, was the brother of Empress Guanglie. His ancestor was Guan Zhong, whose descendant changed his surname to Yin. During Liu Bo's uprising, Yin Shi abandoned his studies in Chang'an to join him, leading over a thousand followers. He became a captain and later a general under Gengshi, conquering five counties. Under Emperor Guangwu, he was made a Cavalry Captain and Marquis of Yin Township. He humbly declined additional titles, stating the world was newly settled. He served as a captain and later returned home for his mother's funeral.

Before the matter was completed, Wang Mang took charge of the emperor's affairs, so Qiao Xuan threw away the embroidered messenger's car, changed his name, ran back home privately, and hid himself. Later, Gongsun Shu claimed that he had a false name in Shu and hired him many times, but he refused to go. Gongsun Shu then sent an envoy to summon him with gifts; if Qiao Xuan refused to go, he would be given poison. The prefect himself sent the seal to Qiao Xuan's home, saying: "You are already famous for your high integrity, and the court intends to use you. You should not resign, or you will bring disaster." Qiao Xuan looked up to the sky and sighed: "For a great sage like Tang Yao, Xu You was ashamed to be his minister. For someone as virtuous as King Wu of Zhou, Boyi would rather starve to death than eat his corn." Who is Gongsun Shu and who am I? Keep your ambitions high, live a good life, and die without regrets! For receiving poison. Qiao Xuan's son Qiao Wangying kowtowed in tears and said to the eunuch: "There is a big enemy in the east now. The army is attacking. The country is spending a lot of money, there are a lot of military supplies, and the country's treasury is insufficient. I am willing to spend tens of millions of my family's money to atone for my father's death." The prefect made a request for him, and Gongsun Shu agreed. Qiao Xuan therefore hid in the fields until Gongsun Shu's death. At this time, wars continued for many years, and no one could talk about his studies. Qiao Xuan alone taught his disciples to study the classics diligently. He died in the eleventh year of Jianwu. The next year, when the world was at peace, Qiao Xuan's younger brother went to the capital to report Qiao Xuan's deeds to the emperor. Guangwu praised Qiao Xuan's deeds, ordered the county to sacrifice him in a prison, and ordered the locality to return Qiao Xuan's family money.
target: During Wang Mang's usurpation, Qiao Xuan abandoned his post and hid. Gongsun Shu tried to recruit him with threats of poison, but Qiao Xuan refused, citing historical examples of integrity. His son offered money to spare his life, and Qiao Xuan hid until Gongsun Shu's death. He died in the eleventh year of Jianwu, and Guangwu later honored him.

source: At that time, there was a Jian named Fei Yi, who refused to accept Gongsun Shu's fake post, so he painted his body with paint to act as a ghost, pretended to be crazy and escaped, and lived in the Tibetan mountains for more than ten years. After Gongsun Shu was eliminated, he became the prefect of Hepu. King Qiao Ying was good at explaining the Book of Changes and used it to teach Xianzong, and he was appointed as the guard order of Beigong. ◆The biography of Li Ye, whose courtesy name is Juyou, was born in Zitong, Guanghan. When he was young, he was ambitious and upright, admiring himself and not following the popular customs. He studied "Lu Shi" with Dr. Xu Huang as his teacher. In the first year of the Yuan Dynasty, he cited the Ming Sutra and was awarded the title of Lang. When Wang Mang came to power on behalf of the emperor, Li Ye resigned due to illness and refused to be appointed by the state and county. The prefect Liu Xian forced him to come out. Li Ye had no choice but to go to Liu Xian when he was ill. Liu Xian got angry and came out to teach him a lesson: A wise man does not avoid disaster. This is like a sword and crossbow shooting into a busy city. The less fortunate will die first. After hearing your reputation, I wanted to ask you to work with me to manage the county government. You don't know how to praise me, and you are just claiming that you are ill. Is this right? He was ordered to go to prison to recuperate and wanted to kill him. A guest said to Liu Xian: Zhao Jianzi killed Dou Mingdu, and Confucius refused to cross the river. I have never heard of people who seek virtuous people being threatened with jail time! Liu Xiancai released Li Ye and promoted him as Founder. Wang Mang appointed Li Ye as a bartender, but he refused to leave due to illness, so he hid in the valley and lost his name until Wang Mang's death. Gongsun Shu set up a false name. He often heard people say that Li Ye was talented, so he recruited him and wanted to use him as a doctor. Li Ye insisted that he could not afford to be ill. A few years later, Gongsun Shu thought he had lost face because he did not summon Li Ye, so he sent Dahong Yinrong to threaten Li Ye with poison and an edict: if he obeyed the order, he would give the Duke the throne; if he did not, he would give poison. Yin Rong persuaded Li Yedao: Today the world is falling apart, no one knows who is right and who is wrong. Why try the unpredictable abyss with your small body? The imperial court admires your reputation and morality, and has kept your official position and position vacant for seven years now. It has cherished you all the time and will not forget you. Isn't it good to serve your close friends at the top and consider your children and grandchildren at the bottom? If you don't go there for a few years now, if you are suspected of being hostile, disaster may befall you immediately. This is not an option. Li Ye had no choice but to sigh and said: "You can't enter a country that is in danger, and you can't live in a country that is in chaos." Doing evil deeds personally is not allowed by righteousness. When a gentleman sees danger and gives orders, how can he be lured with heavy bait from a high position? Seeing that Li Yezhi couldn't give in, Yin Rong said again: "You should call your wife, children and children to discuss it." Li Ye said: It took me a long time to make up my mind. Why did I ask my wife? He drank poison and died.
target: Li Ye, from Guanghan, was ambitious and upright, studying the "Lu Shi." He refused to serve under Wang Mang, feigning illness. Forced by Prefect Liu Xian, he was imprisoned but released after a guest intervened. He later hid in the valley. Gongsun Shu tried to recruit him with threats of poison, but Li Ye refused, stating that a gentleman should not enter a chaotic state. He drank poison and died. Gongsun Shu, ashamed, held a funeral. After Shu was pacified, Guangwu honored Li Ye. Others like Wang Hao and Wang Jia also refused to serve Gongsun Shu, choosing death over submission.

source: Those who commit adultery and adultery commit suicide. After Guangwu heard about it, he recruited them, but they all happened to die of illness at home. ◆The biography of Liu Mao, whose courtesy name is Ziwei, was born in Jinyang, Taiyuan. Lost his father when he was young. A person lives with his mother. His family was poor and he relied on his labor income to support his mother. His filial piety was praised by the villagers. When he grows up, he can study the Book of Rites and teach hundreds of students. During the reign of Emperor Ai, he promoted filial piety and integrity and was promoted to five former princes of the country. However, his mother died and he was dismissed. When the mourning period expires, he will be appointed Juyang Order. When Wang Mang usurped the throne of the Han Dynasty, Liu Mao abandoned his official position and hid in Hongnong Mountain to teach his students. In the second year of Jianwu, he came back from Hongnong Mountain and served as a subordinate of the county.
target: Liu Mao, from Taiyuan, was known for filial piety. He studied the "Book of Rites" and taught students. He abandoned his post during Wang Mang's usurpation and hid in Hongnong Mountain.

source: During the reign of Emperor Ai, he promoted filial piety and integrity and was promoted to five former princes of the country. However, his mother died and he was dismissed. At this time, more than 200,000 people from Chimei came to attack the county and killed the chief officials and government officials. Liu Mao carried the prefect Sun Fu on his back, climbed the wall and hid in a hollow, and narrowly escaped death. That night, the two people fled to Yu County. They hide during the day and come out to find food at night. In this way, it took more than a hundred days before the red-browed thief left and was able to return to the county.
target: During a Red Eyebrow attack, he carried the prefect Sun Fu to safety, hiding and foraging for food for over a hundred days. Sun Fu praised his integrity, and Liu Mao was appointed Yilang. He later died in office.

source: We should praise and promote righteous people. The imperial edict immediately conscripted Liu Mao as Yilang and promoted him to Zong Zhengcheng. Later, he was awarded the title of Shizhong and died in office. In Yanping, hundreds of people from Xianbei invaded Yuyang. The eunuch Zhang Xian led his officials to chase them out of the fortress. Looking at the fireworks of the prison camp in the distance, they followed closely. Yan Shuo, who was carrying soldiers and horses, was worried about an ambush and tried hard to persuade him not to pursue him, but Zhang Xian, the prefect, refused to listen to him. Zhang Xian still forced his way forward, but Yan Shui had no choice but to advance forward to fight. Sure enough, the Xianbei soldiers who were ambushing him suddenly attacked and Yan Shui was wounded ten times and died on the battlefield. Zhang Xian drew his sword and chased the scattered soldiers, but was unable to stop them. The enemy captured Zhang Xian and shot him. Chief Wei Fu and meritorious officer Xu Xian quickly went to rescue Zhang Xian. Zhang Xian fell under his horse. Wei Fu covered Zhang Xian with his body, and the enemy captured them all. The imperial court took pity on Yan Shu and other righteous martyrs, issued an edict to praise them, and gave them great rewards. Each of his sons was appointed a doctor. In the second year of Yongchu, the big thief Bi Hao and others entered the territory of Pingyuan, and the county magistrate Liu Xiong led his officials to chase them by boat. When he arrived at the Yanci River, he fought with the thieves. Liu Xiong was defeated and captured, and the thieves stabbed him with a spear. At this time, the assistant of the minor official came forward to kowtow and beg for mercy, and was willing to die in Liu Xiong's place. Bi Hao and others let Liu Xiong go to stab Suo Fu. The spear penetrated his heart and back, killing him immediately.
target: Other accounts describe Yan Shuo, who died fighting Xianbei invaders, and Suo Fu, who died saving a magistrate from thieves.

source: When he arrived at the Yanci River, he fought with the thieves. Liu Xiong was defeated and captured, and the thieves stabbed him with a spear.
