He became an official in the state. In the second year of Jianwu, the cavalry captain Gongli Shu led his troops to pacify Beizhou and arrived in Taiyuan. He visited handsome people and asked them for their plans. Gongli garrison met Wen Xu and thought he was a genius. He recommended Wen Xu to the emperor, so the imperial court recruited him to serve as a censor. He was promoted to captain of Wuling, but he resigned due to illness. In the sixth year, Wen Xu was granted the title of Visitor and promoted to the Colonel of the Qiang Protector. Wen Xu went to Xiangwu to inspect his subordinates and inspect the criminal administration, but he was arrested by Gou Yu, the general of Nang Guixiao. Gou Yu said to Wen Xu: If you cooperate with me, the world can win. Wen Xu said: "If you accept the heavy responsibility of the country, you can only put your life on the line. For the sake of righteousness, you must not be afraid of death and betray the kindness of the court." Gou Yu and others persuaded him again and again. Wen Xu, who was already strong, was furious and scolded Gou Yu and others: "How dare the ugly prisoners threaten the Han generals!" He killed a few people with his sword.
target: Wen Xu, from Taiyuan, was recommended as a talent and became a censor. He was captured by Gou Yu, who tried to persuade him to join a rebellion. Wen Xu refused, scolding the rebels and killing several before falling on his sword.

source: He killed a few people with his sword. There were many thieves and they were vying to kill Wen Xu. Gou Yu stopped them and said, "This is the day for the death of a righteous man. You can give him a sword." Wen Xu took the sword, put his beard in his mouth, looked around at the people around him and said, "I have been forced to kill by thieves, so don't let your beard be stained by dirt again." He fell on his sword and died. Wen Xu was in charge of registering Han Zun, and Wang Zhong was responsible for collecting the corpse and burying it. Guangwu felt sorry for him when he heard about it, and ordered Wang Zhong to send the funeral to Luoyang. He gave Wen Xu a cemetery next to the city, sent him a thousand dendrobiums and five hundred pieces of silk, and appointed his three sons as doctors. The eldest son, Wenshou, was appointed Houxiang of Zouping after his mourning period expired. In his dream, Wen Xu told him: I have been a guest away for a long time and miss my hometown. Wen Shou abandoned his official position and wrote a letter asking to go home and bury his father. The emperor approved his request and sent his father's coffin back to the old cemetery in his hometown. ◆Peng Xiu's biography, Peng Xiu's courtesy name is Ziyang, and he was from Piling, Kuaiji.
target: Guangwu honored him with a grand funeral and appointed his sons as doctors. Peng Xiu, from Kuaiji, defended his father from robbers at age fifteen, gaining fame.

source: When his mother died, he grieved excessively. His father's soul did not return and he died of grief. ◆Lu Yu was passed down, with the courtesy name Zhi Chu, from Wuxian County, Kuaiji. It has been the common surname in the county for generations. His grandfather, Lu Hong, whose courtesy name was Zichun, was a minister in Jianwu. He was a handsome man who liked to wear Yue cloth. Guangwu also liked this kind of Yue cloth when he saw it. From then on, he often ordered Kuaiji County to offer Yue cloth. His father died one after another when he was young, and he became an official in the county. At this time, the people were hungry, so the prefect Yin Xing sent gruel to the people in Duting one after another. All the hungry people were called together one after another and their names were asked one by one.
target: As an official, he saved a chief clerk from execution by reasoning with the prefect. He later died shielding the prefect from thieves' arrows.

source: Zai Chao forgave Zhong Liyi's punishment and pardoned the jailer's sins. Later, he was engaged in state recruitment. At this time, several hundred people including the thief Zhang Zilin made a rebellion, and the county reported to the state, asking Peng Xiu to be appointed magistrate of Wu County. Peng Xiu and the prefect went to beg the thieves. When the thieves saw the prefect and Peng Xiu's chariots and horses, they fought to shoot, and the arrows flew like rain. Peng Xiu used his body to cover the eunuch and was shot to death by a stray arrow, but the eunuch was saved. The thieves heard about Peng Xiu's favor on weekdays and killed the man who shot Peng Xiu with a crossbow. Some of the other thieves surrendered and some fled. He said: We surrendered for Lord Peng, not for the sake of the prefect. ◆Solu Fangzhuan, Solu Fang's courtesy name is Junyang, and he is from Dongjun. He taught more than a thousand students using "Shang Shu". He first served as a county magistrate. During the Gengshi period, envoys inspected the prefectures and states. If the prefect committed a crime, he should be beheaded. Suo Lufang stepped forward and said: The reason why the world now resents Wang Mang and returns to the imperial Han Dynasty is the reason why the Holy Government is merciful.
target: Suo Lufang, from Dongjun, taught the "Shang Shu" and served as a county magistrate. During the Gengshi period, he offered to die in place of a prefect condemned by an envoy, who pardoned them.

source: When the prefect was executed, he did not dare to say anything, but he was afraid that the whole world would be frightened and suspicious. Oh, it is better to use someone who has merit than someone who has made mistakes. I am willing to take the life of the prefect with my body. So he stepped forward and killed him. The messenger thought that he had sacrificed his life for justice, so he pardoned him. It became famous because of it. In the sixth year of Jianwu's reign, he was appointed the Luoyang Order and was known for his shrewdness and ability. He resigned due to illness and went home. He advised the officials and received many loyal suggestions. Later, he resigned due to illness. In the last years of Jianwu, when he could no longer be recruited, Guangwu sent someone to carry him to the capital in a sedan chair. He was summoned at Yuntai, Nangong, and given two thousand dendrobiums of grain, he was sent home and his son was consecrated as the prince's concubine.
target: He later became Luoyang Order, known for his ability. In his old age, Guangwu summoned him to the capital and honored him.

source: In the last years of Jianwu, when he could no longer be recruited, Guangwu sent someone to carry him to the capital in a sedan chair. Die at home. ◆Zhou Jiachuan, courtesy name Huiwen, was from Ancheng, Runan. My great-great-great-grandfather Zhou Yan was a county general Cao Cao during the reign of Emperor Xuan. The eunuch wanted to kill someone unjustly, but Zhou Yan refused to listen to his advice, so he killed the prisoner and deposed Zhou Yan at the same time. The prisoner's family stood guard at the palace gate, crying out for injustice and ordering a reexamination. Zhou Yan met the prefect and said, "I hope you will write the documents carefully, with my name written on them. The prince only said that you were ill at that time." When he came out of the prefect's office, he said to the governor: "When you are questioned, just blame me, Zhou Yan." If you say something to Fu Jun, I, Zhou Yan, will use my swords in my hands. The envoy then arrested Zhou Yan and imprisoned him. He was tortured many times and refused to tell the truth. According to the crime, he should be thrown into the Jamshi room, so he sighed and said: I am a descendant of King Ping and the great-great-grandson of Zhenggong. How can I go to see the late king without cutting off the sword? He went on a hunger strike and died. Zhou Yan had five sons, all of whom were governors and prefects. Zhou Jia became an official and became the governor of the county. In the last years of Wang Mang, a group of thieves entered Ruyang City. Zhou Jia followed the prefect He Chang to attack the thieves. He Chang was hit by a stray arrow. The county soldiers fled one after another. The thieves surrounded him for dozens of miles and fought with swords. Zhou Jia supported He Chang and defended He Chang with his own body. Because he scolded the thieves and said: You are all slaves of others. Being thieves is already treason. Is there anyone who kills his own superiors?
target: Zhou Jia, from Runan, followed a prefect into battle against thieves. When the prefect was wounded, Zhou Jia shielded him and scolded the thieves, who released them. He later refused to marry a princess and died as prefect of Lingling.

source: The thieves looked at each other and said, "This is a righteous man!" He returned his carriage and horses and sent him away. Later, the prefect Kou Xun promoted Zhou Jia to the title of Xiaolian and the minister of minister. Guangwu summoned him and asked him about Zhou Jia's death. Zhou Jia replied: The governor is injured and his life is in the hands of thieves. I am too stupid and coward to die. The emperor said: This is the elder. The imperial edict ordered Zhou Jia to marry the princess, but Zhou Jia said that he was seriously ill and did not dare to marry the princess. He was promoted to the prefect of Lingling and served for seven years before passing away. Lingling praised his legacy, and officials and people built a shrine in his honor. Zhou Jia's uncle and brother Zhou Chang, named Bochi, was kind-hearted and served as Yin of Henan. In the second year of Yongchu, there was a severe drought in the summer, and there was no rain after long prayers. Zhou Chang collected and buried the bones of more than 10,000 people who died in Luoyang, and a sweet rain fell at the right time, and this year he had a good harvest. The position reaches Guang Luxun. ◆The biography of Shishi, whose courtesy name is Juqing, was born in Jinxiang, Shanyang, and his last name was Si. When he was young, he entered the Imperial Academy and became a student, and became friends with Zhang Shao of Runan. Zhang Shao was named Yuan Bo. The two took leave and returned home. Shi Shi said to Uncle Yuan: "I will come back in two years' time and come to your house to pay homage to Lord Zunlingtang and see your son." So the two agreed on a date together. Later, when the day came, Zhang Yuanbo told his mother all the details of the incident, and asked his mother to prepare wine and dinner to wait for Fan Shi's arrival. His mother said: After two years apart, why do you take the words spoken thousands of miles away so seriously? Answer: Fan Juqing is a very faithful person and will definitely not break the contract. Mother said: In this case, I will prepare wine and food for you. On that day, Fan Juqing really arrived, went to the hall to worship, and parted happily. Shi Fan was appointed as the meritorious official of the county. Later, Zhang Yuanbo fell seriously ill, and fellow county residents Zhi Junzhang and Yin Zizheng visited him day and night. When Uncle Yuan was dying, he sighed: I regret not seeing my dead friend! Yin Zizheng said: "Jun Zhang and I are wholeheartedly recruiting you. We are not dead friends. Where can you find a dead friend?" Yuan Bo said: You two are my living friends, but Fan Juqing of Shanyang is my dead friend. Soon, he passed away. Shi Fan suddenly dreamed of Uncle Yuan's black crown hanging with tassels on his clothes and he shouted: "Ju Qing, I have died on a certain day. I should be buried on time and return to the underworld forever." You have not forgotten my words. Can you be there for the burial? Paradigm suddenly woke up, lamented and cried, reported to the prefect, and asked to be allowed to go to the funeral. Although the prefect didn't believe it in his heart, he believed that Shi Shi's feelings were valuable, so he agreed to attend the funeral. Paradigm dressed in his friend's mourning clothes and rode horseback on the day of burial. Before the paradigm arrived, Yuan Bo's mourning had already begun. He arrived at Xiengjing and was about to lower the coffin. At this time, the coffin could not be lifted and refused to enter.
target: Shi Shi, from Shanyang, was known for his faithfulness. He promised to visit his friend Zhang Shao after two years and kept his word. When Zhang Shao died, Shi Shi dreamed of him and traveled to attend his funeral, where the coffin moved only after his arrival. He later cared for another friend's family after his death. As governor of Jingzhou, he recognized a poor friend working as a laborer and offered him a position, but the friend refused. Shi Shi died as prefect of Lujiang.

source: Shifan ordered the county to replace Kong Song. Kong Song thought that he was hired first and the date of employment had not expired, so he refused to go. When Kong Song was in Ali, he acted righteously and strictly, and all the children in the street obeyed his teachings. So the government conscripted him. On the way to the capital, they stayed in the pavilion. Thieves stole his horse. Soon after they learned that it was Kong Song's horse, they scolded each other: Kong Zhongshan is a good man, how can he invade it? So the horse was returned to Kong Song. Kong Song was appointed as the governor of Nanhai. Shi Fan was later promoted to the prefect of Lujiang and became famous. He died in office. ◆Li Shanchuan, the second grandson of Li Shan, was born in Yuyang, Nanyang. He was originally a servant of Li Yuan from the same county. An epidemic was prevalent in Jianwu, and Li Yuan's family members died of illness one after another. Only an orphan, Li Xu, was born. In just a few dozen days, the family had tens of thousands of dollars in wealth. The slaves discussed privately and wanted to kill Li Xu too, so that everyone could divide the property. Li Shan pitied Li Shi, but was unable to stop him, so he secretly carried Li Xu and ran away, hiding in the Shanyang Xiaqiu world, feeding him himself, feeding him food and water, and his milk also produced milk, so as to avoid the heat and cold, and prepare for hardships. Although Li Xu was in his arms, Li Shan treated him like an elder brother. If something happened, he would kneel down and ask for instructions before reporting. The villagers were moved by his deeds and followed him in doing good deeds.
target: Li Shan, from Nanyang, saved an orphaned infant, Li Xu, from murderous slaves by fleeing and raising him. He treated Li Xu with respect and later returned to reclaim the family property, punishing the slaves.

source: When Li Xu was ten years old, Li Shan took him back to the county to reorganize his old business. He complained to the chief minister about the slaves, and he rounded them up and killed them all. At this time, Zhong Liyi Ren Xia Qiu ordered him to write a letter recommending Li Shan's deeds. Guangwu issued an edict to grant Li Shan and Li Xu both sacrifices for the prince. Li Shan was recruited by the government during the reign of Emperor Xianzong. Because he could manage difficult places, he was promoted to the governor of Rinan. On his way to his post in the capital, he passed by Xuyuyang and passed Li Yuan's tomb. A mile away, he took off his court clothes and started weeding with a hoe.
target: Guangwu honored them. Li Shan later became governor of Rinan, visiting Li Yuan's tomb with great reverence.

source: When he was young, he was a Zhusheng with a weird and unruly temperament. He often reads "Laozi" and seems to be a scholar. He is also like a madman. He likes to wear his hair disheveled and wear red raw silk hair. He often sits on the wooden bed in Zaobei. He has been like this for many years, leaving traces of his knees, ankles, and toes on the bed. He doesn't like to talk, but he likes to shout loudly. What the guests wanted to do from him was often hidden. There were disciples named Yan Yuan, Zigong, Ji Lu and Ran You.

source: For poor families in the countryside, the dead are helped to bury, and the widows and widowers are helped to marry. Emperor Xian moved the capital to Xijing, and Liu Yi was appointed as the chief minister. At this time, thieves were everywhere and the roads were blocked, making it very difficult to reach the post. Liu Yi left at night and hid during the day before arriving in Chang'an. The imperial edict commended his loyalty and diligence, and he was specially appointed as Yiyi Lang and promoted to Chenliu Grand Administrator. Liu Yi lost all his treasures, leaving only his carriage and horses, and rode back eastward. After leaving the customs for hundreds of miles, I saw a scholar-official died of illness on the roadside with no one to bury him, so he traded a horse for a coffin and took off his clothes for burial. He met his old friends who were hungry on the road, and couldn't bear to abandon them, so he killed the ox driving them to help them.
target: His mother's cooking helped identify her presence. He was pardoned and died of old age.

source: Favorite Lu Kang, the prequel has been seen. ◆Biography of Dai Feng, named Pingzhong, from Gang County, Jibei Province. At the age of fifteen, he went to Taixue and became his teacher, Lord Shen of the East China Sea. When Lord Shen passed away, Dai Feng sent Lord Shen to mourn in the East China Sea, passing through Dai Feng's own house. source: ◆Biography of Wang Chong, Wang Chong, courtesy name Zhongren, was from Shangyu, Kuaiji. His ancestors moved here from Yuancheng, Wei County. Later he went to the capital to study at Taixue, where he was taught by Ban Biao, a Fufeng native. He is well-read and does not stick to chapters. His family was poor and had no books, so he often went to Luoyang bookstore to read the books for sale, and he could memorize them after reading them once. So he understood the theories of various schools of thought. Later, he returned to his hometown and lived in seclusion to teach. He served as a meritorious official in the prefecture and county, but because he repeatedly advised the superiors, he left due to disagreements. Wang Chong likes to make comments, which may sound weird at first, but if you think about it carefully, they are reasonable and well-founded. He thought that those Confucian scholars with little knowledge clung to the chapters and sentences in the books and lost the essence and true meaning of the books. So I closed my door and thought deeply, and declined those social gatherings of congratulations and condolences. There were knives and pens placed on the door, windows and walls of his home. He wrote 85 chapters of "Lunheng", totaling more than 200,000 words, explaining the similarities and differences of objects and correcting people's doubts about certain things at that time.
target: Wang Chong, courtesy name Zhongren, was from Shangyu, Kuaiji, though his ancestors had moved from Yuancheng, Wei County. His father died when he was young, and he was praised for his filial piety. He studied at Taixue in the capital under Ban Biao of Fufeng. Despite his family's poverty and lack of books, he frequently visited Luoyang bookstores, memorizing texts after a single reading, which allowed him to master various schools of thought. He later returned home to teach and served as a meritorious official, but left due to disagreements with his superiors after repeatedly offering advice. Wang Chong criticized Confucian scholars for clinging to textual details while losing deeper meanings. He secluded himself, placing writing tools throughout his home, and composed 85 chapters of "Lunheng" (over 200,000 words) to explain phenomena and correct contemporary misconceptions.

The book denounces the shortcomings of the time and discusses customs and sentiments, from which the political fashion of the time can be seen. Here are five of them: 1. "Guizhong Pian" The emperor respects God the most, and God loves people the most. Now that human ministers are entrusted by the king to govern the people whom God loves, how can they not allow them to be raised and relieved safely and smoothly? Therefore, when a gentleman is in a position, he should think about how to benefit others, and those who are above should think about how to introduce wise people. Therefore, those who are in the upper position should not be resentful when they are below, and those who are in the front and behind will not be disobedient. This is what the Book of Books says about heaven's work being replaced by human power. The king established large and small official systems based on the arrangement of the stars in the sky. Therefore, the emperor did not dare to appoint officials casually due to partiality, and loyal ministers did not dare to accept official positions with an open mind. Stealing other people's money is still called a robber, let alone stealing from a heavenly official for personal gain!
target: Governor Dong Qin recruited him, but he resigned. His friend Xie Yiwu recommended him to the court, and Emperor Suzong issued an edict for his service, but illness prevented him from traveling. Near age seventy, with failing memory, he wrote sixteen chapters of "The Book of Cultivation of Nature" on self-discipline and spiritual preservation. He died at home during the Yongyuan period. Wang Fu, courtesy name Xin, was from Linjing, Anding. Studious and ambitious, he befriended Ma Rong, Dou Zhang, Zhang Heng, and Cui Yuan. Because he was born to a secondary wife, his village looked down on him. During the reigns of Emperors He and An, when powerful families recommended each other for office, Wang Fu's uprightness prevented him from becoming an official. Distressed, he secluded himself and wrote over thirty books criticizing contemporary politics, calling his work "The Theory of Qianfu" to remain anonymous. His writings denounced societal ills. He argued that officials should govern justly, as heaven loves the people, and that stealing official positions for personal gain was worse than robbery.

He will not be blamed at that time, and his life will be preserved forever. In this way, one can rise above the sky and be beyond the universe. Are you still envious of entering the imperial family? The flying snake abandons its scales and armor, and the divine dragon loses its head and horns. A great person can change, a noble person can transcend vulgarity. Riding on the clouds without a saddle or bridle, riding the wind with no satisfaction. The hanging dew becomes a tent curtain, and the Zhang Xiao becomes a scarf. Hangzhou serves as dinner, and Nine Suns replace candles. The stars are as bright as pearls, and the morning glow is as smooth as jade. Liuhe allows me to roam as much as I want. People and things can be left behind, so why be cramped. Although the road is flat, there are only a few people there. There is no right or wrong in anything you want, and there is nothing wrong with what you want. It has been a circuitous and complex process since ancient times. No matter what I do, the most important thing is still with me. Put your worries in heaven and bury them in the earth. The rebellion was dispersed in the Five Classics, and Heaven abandoned the Wind and Ya. Baijia is too messy, please use a fire. The ambition to fight is in the mountains, and the heart is in the sea. The vitality becomes a boat, and the breeze can be the rudder. Ao Xiang is in Taiqing, Zongyi is in Rongye. The minister ordered Xun to be surprised when he heard Zhong Changtong's name, so he appointed him as minister. Later he participated in the military affairs of Prime Minister Cao Cao. Whenever he talks about ancient and modern times and the customs and practices of that time, he often sighs with anger. Because the treatise is called "Chang Yan", it has a total of thirty-four chapters and more than 100,000 words. In the year when Emperor Xian abdicated, Zhong Changtong died at the age of forty-one.
target: He valued personal freedom over official service, describing an ideal life of leisure with fertile land, comfortable housing, family, friends, entertainment, and philosophical contemplation. He wrote poems expressing his desire to transcend worldly concerns. Minister Xun Yu appointed him, and he later served under Prime Minister Cao Cao. He wrote "Chang Yan," consisting of 34 chapters and over 100,000 words, expressing his critical views on contemporary society. He died at age forty-one during the year Emperor Xian abdicated.

source: Wang Chang was a prince, a native of Handan, Zhao State. He was originally a fortune-teller and fortune-teller, and he had some knowledge of astronomy and calculus. He often thought that Hebei had the aura of the Son of Heaven. At this time, Liu Lin, the son of King Mu of Zhao, loved magic and practiced chivalry between Zhao and Wei. He had many connections with powerful and lawless people, and Wang Chang was friendly with him. At first, when Wang Mang usurped the throne, there was a man in Chang'an who claimed to be Liu Ziyu, the son of Emperor Cheng, and Wang Mang killed him. Wang Lang relied on this clue and falsely claimed that he was the true son of the emperor, saying: My mother was a singer who became the emperor. One time when she was going down to the palace, she suddenly collapsed. When Ziyu was twelve years old, a doctor named Li Manqing took him to Shu. When he was seventeen, he arrived in Danyang. When he was twenty, he returned to Chang'an. He traveled between Zhongshan and Yanzhao, waiting for the arrival of the right time. Liu Lin and others were even more confused, so they conspired with Li Yu, Zhang Shen and others to plan to support Wang Lang. It happened that people said that Red Eyebrow was about to cross the Yellow River, so Liu Lin and others declared that Red Eyebrow was coming, and asked Liu Ziyu to see the reaction of the people, and many people believed it. In December of the first year of Gengshi, Liu Lin and others led hundreds of chariots and riders, entered Handan City early in the morning, stopped at the palace, and made Wang Lang the emperor. Liu Lin was the Prime Minister, Li Yu was the Grand Sima, and Zhang Shen was the General. Send generals to capture Youzhou and Jizhou respectively. Send the proclamation to the prefectures and counties and say: "I order the governors of each prefecture and the prefect of the prefecture: I am Liu Ziyu, the son of Emperor Xiaocheng." In the past, I was harmed by the Zhao family. After Wang Mang usurped the Han Dynasty, he killed the fake Ziyu. Fortunately, someone who knew the destiny protected me, and I was able to escape from the riverside and disappear between Zhao and Wei. Wang Mang's theft of the throne offended Heaven, and Heaven blessed us with the Han Dynasty, so we sent Zhai Yi, the governor of Dongjun, and Liu Xin, the Marquis of Yanxiang, to support the attack and go between the Hu people and the Han people.
target: Wang Chang, a prince from Handan in Zhao State, was originally a fortune-teller with knowledge of astronomy. He believed Hebei had the aura of a Son of Heaven. Liu Lin, son of King Mu of Zhao, was a chivalrous man with connections to powerful figures, and Wang Chang befriended him. After Wang Mang usurped the throne and killed a man claiming to be Liu Ziyu, son of Emperor Cheng, Wang Lang falsely claimed to be the true son. He fabricated a story about his mother, a singer who became the emperor's consort, and his escape with a doctor. Liu Lin and others, including Li Yu and Zhang Shen, conspired to support Wang Lang. In December of the first year of Gengshi, they entered Handan, made Wang Lang emperor, and appointed Liu Lin as Prime Minister, Li Yu as Grand Sima, and Zhang Shen as General. They sent proclamations to prefectures, declaring Wang Lang as Liu Ziyu and calling for support. Wang Lang's claims gained traction, and much of northern China submitted to him.

source: ◆Ban Biao's biography, Ban Biao, courtesy name Shupi, was born in Anling, Fufeng. His grandfather, Ban Kuang, served as a captain of the Yue Cavalry School when he became emperor. His father, Ban Zhi, served as the prefect of Guangping during the reign of Emperor Ai. Ban Biao has a serious personality and likes traditional culture. When he was in his twenties, Gengshi was defeated and fled, and there was chaos near the capital. At that time, Wei Xiao led everyone to revolt in Tianshui, and Ban Biao followed him to seek refuge. Once, Wei Xiao asked Ban Biao: "In the past, the Zhou Dynasty was destroyed, the Warring States Period was full of disputes, and the world was torn apart. It took several generations to stabilize." Will the combination of verticality and horizontality appear again today, or will it be a destiny for a certain person? Please give me your opinion, sir. Ban Biao replied: The decline and prosperity of the Zhou Dynasty was different from that of the Han Dynasty. In the past, the Zhou Dynasty was divided into five categories: Duke, Marquis, Uncle, Son, and Male. The princes controlled their own territories and governed their own affairs, just like a big tree, with weak roots and luxuriant branches and leaves. Therefore, later, when there were vertical and horizontal alliances, it was the situation that prompted it. The Han Dynasty inherited the system of the Qin Dynasty and changed the feudal system into a system of prefectures and counties. The monarch had autocratic authority and his subordinates did not have the power to control the country for a hundred years. When Emperor Cheng arrived, he used the power of his relatives to reign. Emperor Ai and Emperor Ping reigned for a short time. The three emperors had no children, so Wang Mang usurped the throne and stole the title of the country. The danger comes from above, and the harm is not as bad as below. Therefore, after Wang Mang actually usurped the throne, everyone in the world stretched their necks and sighed. For more than ten years, there have been disturbances at home and abroad, and actions have been taken by people near and far, each under the banner of the Liu family, and they have responded in unison. Nowadays, the states and counties ruled by heroes and heroes do not have the traditional capital of the Seven Kingdoms, but the common people miss the kindness of the Han Dynasty with one voice. The development trend can be imagined. Wei Xiaodao: Sir, your analysis of the situation between the Zhou Dynasty and the Han Dynasty is correct; as for saying that the Han family will definitely revive because the stupid people are accustomed to the Liu surname, it is not necessarily true. In the past, when the Qin Dynasty lost the world, it was like a deer running away. Liu Bang chased the deer and caught it. Who knew there was a Han Dynasty at that time? On the one hand, Ban Biao hated Wei Xiao's arrogance, and on the other hand, he lamented the difficult situation, so he wrote an article "On the King's Mandate", believing that Han De succeeded Tang Yao, as evidenced by the efficacious king's talisman, and that the king ascended the throne, not by deception. He wanted to use this to impress Wei Xiao, but Wei Xiao never realized it, so he avoided Hexi. Dou Rong, the general of Hexi Province, used him as an official, treated him with great respect, and treated him as a mentor and friend. Ban Biao made suggestions for Dou Rong, served the Han Dynasty, and led the Xihe area to resist Wei Xiao. Later, Dou Rong was ordered to return to the capital. Emperor Guangwu asked: Who was your adviser on the memorial you submitted? Dou Rong replied: It was all done by my colleague Ban Biao. The emperor had always heard that Ban Biao was very talented, so he summoned Ban Biao, promoted him to be the Secretary Maocai, and asked him to be the Order of Xuzhou. However, he was unable to take the post due to illness.
target: Ban Biao, courtesy name Shupi, was born in Anling, Fufeng. His grandfather Ban Kuang served as a captain of the Yue Cavalry School, and his father Ban Zhi was prefect of Guangping. Ban Biao had a serious personality and valued traditional culture. In his twenties, during the chaos following Gengshi's defeat, he followed Wei Xiao to Tianshui. When Wei Xiao asked whether the Warring States period's vertical and horizontal alliances would recur or if a single ruler would unify the realm, Ban Biao explained that the Zhou Dynasty's feudal system led to weak central control and allowed such alliances, while the Han Dynasty's prefecture and county system centralized power. He argued that the Han's decline stemmed from above, not below, and that after Wang Mang's usurpation, people longed for the Han, leading to widespread uprisings under the Liu family banner. Wei Xiao disagreed, citing the Qin collapse as an unpredictable event. Ban Biao, disturbed by Wei Xiao's arrogance, wrote "On the King's Mandate" to argue that Han virtue succeeded Tang Yao, but Wei Xiao remained unmoved, so Ban Biao fled to Hexi. There, Dou Rong employed him as an official, treating him with great respect. Ban Biao advised Dou Rong to serve the Han and resist Wei Xiao. When Dou Rong returned to the capital, Emperor Guangwu learned of Ban Biao's role and summoned him, promoting him to Secretary Maocai and appointing him as Order of Xuzhou, though illness prevented him from taking the post. Ban Biao later served under the Three Dukes.

source: Later, he went several times in response to Sangong's orders. Ban Biao was both talented and good at writing, so he concentrated on historical records. During the reign of Emperor Wu, Sima Qian wrote the "Historical Records". Since the Taichu period, there has been no writing. Later, some good people connected the deeds at that time, but the writing style is vulgar and is not worthy of being a follow-up to the "Historical Records". Ban Biao then continued to collect the historical relics of the previous dynasty, and also read some anecdotes from the side, and wrote dozens of later biographies, commenting on the gains and losses with reference to the previous history. The summary of the article reads: During the Tang and Yu dynasties, according to the records of "The Book of Songs" and "The Book of Books", each dynasty had historians to manage classic works. When it came to the vassal states, each country had its own history. Therefore, "Mencius" said that the history of Chu State is called "Mu Shou Chu", the history of Jin State is called "Cheng", and the history of Lu State is called "Spring and Autumn". Their records of history are all the same. In the era of Duke Dinggong and Duke Ai of Lu, Zuo Qiuming, a gentleman of the state of Lu, collected the history of that time and wrote thirty chapters of "The Biography of the Zuo Family", and based on various materials, he wrote twenty-one chapters of "Guoyu". There is also a book that records the deeds of emperors, princes, princes, princes and officials from the time of the Yellow Emperor to the Spring and Autumn Period, called "Shiben", with a total of fifteen chapters. After the Spring and Autumn Period, there were disputes among the seven kingdoms and the Qin State annexed the princes. Thirty-three chapters of "Warring States Policy" were published. The rise of the Han Dynasty brought peace to the world. Lu Jia, a senior official in Taizhong, recorded the situation at that time and wrote nine chapters of Chu-Han Spring and Autumn Annals. In the era of Emperor Xiaowu, Taishi ordered Sima Qian to collect "Zuo Shi" and "Guoyu", and delete "Shiben" and "Warring States Policy". According to the current affairs of the Chu and Han states, starting from the Yellow Emperor and going down to the second year of Taishi, he wrote a total of 130 chronicles, family biographies, books, and lists. Ten of them are missing. Sima Qian recorded that from the founding of the Han Dynasty to the last time of Emperor Wu, this is his contribution. As for the collection of scriptures and biographies, materials scattered among hundreds of schools of thought are found in many rough and schematic parts, which are not as true and detailed as the original ones. It is known for being widely read and widely published, and its discussion is superficial but not solid. When talking about academics, he praised Huangdi and Laozi and despised the Five Classics; when writing about goods and culture, he despised benevolence and righteousness and was ashamed of poverty; when writing about knight-errants, he despised those who were chaste and heroic and praised those who made meritorious deeds in the world. This is a serious problem, and it harms the righteousness, so it is the reason for being punished by corruption.
target: Ban Biao was talented in writing and focused on historical records. After Sima Qian's "Historical Records," no comprehensive history existed for the period after Taichu. Ban Biao collected historical materials and wrote dozens of later biographies, critiquing their merits and flaws. He noted that various states had their own histories, such as "Mu Shou Chu," "Cheng," and "Spring and Autumn." He praised Sima Qian's narrative skill but criticized his bias toward Huang-Lao thought, neglect of the Five Classics, and superficial discussions. Ban Biao emphasized the need for strict factual verification and stylistic consistency in history writing.

In the 30th year of Jianwu's reign, Ban Biao died in his official position at the age of 52. He wrote a total of nine Fu, treatises, books, notes and memorials.

In the 16th year of Yongping, Dou Gu, the captain of Fengdong, attacked the Xiongnu. He appointed Ban Chao as a fake Sima and asked him to lead an army to attack Yiwu. They fought in Puleihai and returned with many enemy heads beheaded. Dou Gu thought Ban Chao was very talented and sent him to follow Guo Xun on an envoy to the Western Regions. When Ban Chao arrived in Shanshan, King Guang of Shanshan received him respectfully and politely, but then suddenly became cold. Ban Chao said to his subordinates: Have you ever felt that King Guang of Shanshan's respect for us has diminished? This must be because the Huns envoys came, and King Shanshan was hesitant and didn't know why.
target: A fortune-teller predicted he would become a marquis. Emperor Xianzong appointed him Lantai Lingshi, but he was later dismissed. In the 16th year of Yongping, Ban Chao served as a fake Sima under Dou Gu, attacking the Xiongnu at Puleihai. Dou Gu then sent him as an envoy to the Western Regions. In Shanshan, Ban Chao deduced that the Huns had arrived when King Guang's hospitality waned.

source: It has only been a few days since the Huns envoy came, but King Guang of Shanshan has canceled the salute. If he captures us and gives them to the Huns, our bones will be fed to jackals forever. What do you think we should do? All the subordinates said: We are now in a critical situation, and we must obey Sima's orders whether we live or die. Ban Chao said: If you don't get into the tiger's cave, you won't be able to catch the little tiger. The best strategy now is to attack the Huns with fire when it is dark at night. They don't know how many of us there are, so they will be greatly frightened, and we can wipe them all out. After destroying the Huns, King Shanshan will be frightened out of his wits. We are done and things are done. The subordinates said: We should discuss this with the managers. Ban Chao said angrily: "Whether it is good or bad depends on today." If you are a vulgar civil servant, if you hear our plan, you will definitely leak the secret out of fear. He died unappreciated and was not a heroic and brave man. Everyone said: OK! At the first watch, Ban Chao led his subordinates to the camp of the Huns envoys. At this time, a strong wind was blowing. Ban Chao asked ten people to hold drums and hide behind the Xiongnu envoy's station, and made an agreement: When you see the fire attack, all of you will beat the drums and shout loudly. The rest of the people were armed with bows and arrows and ambush on both sides of the door of the Huns envoy's residence. Banchao set fire to the wind, beating drums and making noises in front and back, causing the Huns to panic and panic. Ban Chao killed three people with his own hands, and his subordinates killed the Xiongnu envoy, and also killed more than 30 of the Xiongnu envoy's followers, and chopped off their heads. The remaining more than a hundred people were burned to death.
target: He interrogated a servant, confirmed his suspicion, and gathered his 36 men. At night, he led a fire attack on the Hun camp, killing the envoy and over 30 followers, with 100 burned to death.

source: Only then did Guo Xun become happy. Ban Chao then called King Guang of Shanshan and showed him the head of the Huns envoy. The whole country of Shanshan was shocked. Ban Chao made the matter public and comforted him. So King Shanshan sent his son to the Han Dynasty as a hostage. Ban Chao came back and reported the incident to Dou Gu. Dou Gu was overjoyed and reported Ban Chao's achievements to the emperor in detail, and asked to send another envoy to the Western Regions. Emperor Ming of the Han Dynasty praised Ban Chao's integrity and ordered Dou Gu: Why don't you choose an official like Ban Chao, but choose someone else? Now Ban Chao is appointed as Army Sima and asked to complete his unfinished work. Ban Chao was once again ordered to go on an envoy to the Western Regions. Dou Gu wanted to give more soldiers to Ban Chao, but Ban Chao said: I only want to give me the original thirty more soldiers.
target: King Guang, impressed, sent his son as a hostage. Ban Chao reported to Dou Gu, who recommended him to Emperor Ming. Appointed Army Sima, Ban Chao refused extra troops, retaining only his original 36 men.

source: If Gumo and Wensu surrender, Qiuci will be defeated without any attack. I hope that my memorial will be approved and submitted to the competent authorities for reference. Even if there is extreme danger, if I die for my country, what is there to regret? I am a small official in the class, and I have received special support from the emperor's spirit. I selfishly hope that I will not die soon and can see the peace of the Western Regions with my own eyes. Your Majesty will hold the Cup of Ten Thousand Years high, recommend my merits to the ancestral temple, and announce the great joy to the world. After the memorial was sent, the emperor knew that he could succeed and discussed giving Ban Chao troops. Xu Qian, a native of Pingling, had always been like-minded friends with Ban Chao, and wrote to the emperor willing to do his best to help Ban Chao. In the fifth year of the founding of the People's Republic of China, the imperial court appointed Xu Qian as the fake Sima and allocated 1,000 prisoners and volunteers whose sentences were commuted to Ban Chao. In the past, Shadong thought that if the Han Dynasty did not send troops, it would have to surrender to Qiuci. However, Fan Chen, the captain of Shule, rebelled against the Han Dynasty. Just when Xu Qian led his troops, Ban Chao and Xu Qian joined forces to attack Fan Chen. They defeated Fan Chen, beheaded more than a thousand heads, and captured many prisoners. Ban Chao had defeated Fan Chen and wanted to attack Kucha. Because Wusun has a strong army, we should rely on his strength. So he wrote to the emperor and said: Wusun is a big country with one hundred thousand soldiers who use bows and arrows. Therefore, Emperor Wu married Princess Xijun, the daughter of King Fei of Jiangdu, to King Wusun. By the time of Emperor Xiaoxuan, he finally got its help and defeated the Xiongnu. Now you can send envoys to appease Wusun and work together with him. The emperor adopted Ban Chao's opinion. In the eighth year of the founding of the People's Republic of China, Ban Chao was appointed commander-in-chief of the generals and soldiers, and Xu Qian was appointed commander-in-chief of the army. In addition, Wei Hou Li Yi was sent to escort Wusun's envoys, and officials from Kunmi to Kunmi were all given brocade and silk. As soon as Li Yi arrived at Yucheng, he encountered Qiuci attacking Shule. He was afraid and did not dare to advance. So he wrote a letter to the emperor, stating that it was impossible to pacify the Western Regions. He also tried his best to slander Ban Chao, saying that Ban Chao embraced his beloved wife, held his young son in his arms, and enjoyed peace and happiness abroad without thinking about domestic affairs. When Ban Chao heard this, he sighed and said: "I have not participated in it but have been slandered by the Three Supreme Beings. I'm afraid someone will doubt me now." So he left his wife. The emperor knew that Ban Chao was loyal, so he scolded Li Yi severely and said: Even if Ban Chao embraces his beloved wife and carries his young son in his arms, how can more than a thousand soldiers who miss their hometown be of the same mind as Ban Chao?
target: In Yutian, Ban Chao killed a wizard who demanded his horse, shocking King Guangde into submitting. In Shule, he captured the usurper Douti, installed King Zhong, and released Douti to show prestige. After Emperor Ming's death, Ban Chao faced isolation but held Shule with minimal forces. Recalled by Emperor Suzong, he was persuaded by the people to stay, defeating rebels and stabilizing Shule. In the third year of Jianchu, he led 10,000 troops to capture Gumo, then petitioned for reinforcements to conquer Qiuci, proposing to use local forces and resources. The emperor approved, sending Xu Qian with 1,000 men. Ban Chao defeated Fan Chen, and later, despite slander from Li Yi, he remained loyal, leaving his wife to prove his commitment.

source: Ban Chao said: Why are you so ignorant? It is precisely because Li Yi slandered me that I am sending him back to his country now. I have a clear conscience, why should I be afraid of what others will say? Keeping him in order to vent your personal anger is not considered a loyal minister. The next year, the imperial court sent four people including Ji Si and Gong to lead an army of 800 people to Banchao's camp. Banchao then launched Shule and Yu Sheng's troops to attack Shadong. Shadong secretly sent someone to Shule Wang Zhong to bribe him with huge profits. King Zhong of Shule rebelled against Banchao and followed Shadong's instructions to protect Wuji City in the west. Ban Chao appointed Shule's prime minister, Cheng Da, as King of Shule, and mobilized all the troops who had not rebelled to attack King Zhong of Shule. Half a year later, Kang Ju sent elite troops to rescue Wang Zhong of Shule, but Ban Chao could not attack. At this time, Yuezhi had just married Kang Ju and they were friendly to each other. Ban Chao sent an envoy to bring more brocade and silk to King Yuezhi, and enlightened Xiao to King Kangju. King Kangju then stopped his troops, arrested Wang Zhong of Shule, and sent him back to Shule. Wu Jicheng surrendered to Ban Chao. In the next three years, King Zhong of Shule lobbied King Kang Ju to borrow troops from him and returned to Sizhong. He also secretly conspired with Qiuci and sent envoys to pretend to surrender to Banchao. Ban Chao learned of their plot and pretended to accept surrender. King Zhong of Shule was overjoyed and immediately led his light cavalry to Banchao to feign surrender. Ban Chao secretly ambush the soldiers, set up tents, arranged banquets and banquets, and waited for the arrival of Shule Wang Zhong. King Zhong of Shule came. While drinking, Ban Chao ordered his soldiers to tie up King Zhong of Shule and kill him. So he took advantage of the victory and attacked his army, killing more than 700 people, and the southern road was opened.
target: Ban Chao conquered Shadong, killed the treacherous King Zhong, and opened the southern route. In a major battle, he feigned retreat, then attacked Shadong at dawn, killing 5,000 and securing surrender. Yuezhi attacked but were repelled due to supply issues.

source: Ban Chao knew that two groups of enemy troops had set off, so he secretly ordered his troops to rush to the Shadong military camp when the rooster crows. The enemy was frightened and fled in a hurry. Banchao's army pursued the enemy, killed more than 5,000 enemy soldiers, and seized a large amount of property and horses. Sha Dong surrendered. Kucha and other countries also retreated and dispersed. From then on, Ban Chao became famous in the Western Regions. In the past, the Yuezhi helped the Han Dynasty attack the Cheshi Kingdom and made great contributions. This year, he contributed pearls, talismans, and lions to the Han Dynasty, and asked the Han Dynasty to marry him as a princess. Ban Chao rejected the Yuezhi's request and sent back their envoy. From then on, the Yuezhi resented the Han Dynasty. In the second year of Yongyuan, Yuezhi sent his deputy king Xie with 70,000 troops to attack Banchao. Ban Chao had few soldiers and horses, and the sergeants were frightened. Sergeant Ban Chao Xiaoyu said: Although there are many Yueshi soldiers, they have to travel thousands of miles and cross the green mountains to invade, and transportation is extremely inconvenient. What is there to worry about? As long as the food is stored well and held tight, the enemy will surrender due to hunger. The enemy will be defeated in just a few dozen days. Xie, the deputy king of the Yuezhi, led his army to attack Ban Chao, but could not win; he also looted and looted, but gained nothing. Ban Chao estimated that the enemy troops would run out of food and would definitely ask for help from Qiuci. So hundreds of troops were sent to intercept on the east road. Sure enough, Xie, the deputy king of Yuezhi, sent cavalry to bribe Qiuci with gold, silver, pearls and jade. Ban Chao's ambush troops stepped out to intercept and kill all the enemies, and sent someone to show the deputy king Xie the head of the Yuezhi envoy. Xie was shocked and immediately sent an envoy to Ban Chao to apologize, asking only for him to be allowed to go back alive. Ban Chao then released Yuezhi Deputy Wang Xie and asked him to go back. The Yueshi were greatly shaken from then on and paid tribute to the Han Dynasty every year. In the third year of Yongyuan, Qiuci, Gumo, and Wensu all surrendered. The imperial court appointed Ban Chao as the county protector, Xu Qian as the long history, Bai Ba as the king of Qiuci, and sent Sima Yao Guang to escort him. Ban Chao and Yao Guang jointly coerced Qiuci to depose the original king Yuliduo and establish Baiba as king, and sent Yao Guang to return to the capital with Yuliduo. Banchao was stationed in Tagancheng, Kucha, and Xu Gan was stationed in Shule. Only Yanqi, Weixu, and Yuli in the Western Regions had killed Chen Mu, the guard of the Han Dynasty, but had second thoughts and did not dare to surrender. The rest of the countries in the Western Regions were pacified. In the autumn of the sixth year of Yongyuan, Banchao mobilized a total of 70,000 troops from eight countries including Qiuci and Shanshan, and 1,400 officials and officials to attack Yanqi.
target: By the third year of Yongyuan, Qiuci, Gumo, and Wensu submitted. Ban Chao became Protector General, stationed in Tagancheng. In the sixth year, he led 70,000 troops to attack Yanqi, capturing and executing King Guang and others, pacifying over 50 states. He was granted the title Marquis of Dingyuan. Aged and homesick, Ban Chao petitioned to return, citing his long service. His sister Ban Zhao also pleaded.

source: I am stupid and do not understand justice, and I have violated a taboo. The memorial was sent up, and the emperor was moved by her words and recalled Ban Chao. Ban Chao lived in the Western Regions for thirty-one years. In August of the 14th year of Yongyuan, he returned to Luoyang and was appointed as the captain of Shesheng. Ban Chao had a disease in his chest and ribs. After returning home, his condition worsened. The emperor sent Zhonghuangmen to check on him and gave him medicine. He died in September of this year at the age of seventy-one. The imperial court took pity on him and sent envoys to express condolences and offer him generous rewards. Ban Chao's son Ban Xiong inherited his title. Previously, when Ban Chao was summoned back, the imperial court appointed Wuji Colonel Ren Shang as the Protector. When handing over the work, Ren Shang said to Ban Chao: "The prince has been in a foreign country for more than thirty years, and I am ashamed to succeed you. I have great responsibilities and short wits. You should be able to teach me."
target: In the 14th year of Yongyuan, he returned to Luoyang, dying at 71. His son Ban Xiong inherited his title. Ban Chao's advice to successor Ren Shang—to be lenient—was ignored, leading to rebellion.

source: Ban Shi could not hold back his anger. In the fifth year of Yongjian's reign, he drew his sword and killed the princess. Emperor Shun was furious and had Ban Shi cut in half, and all his people were killed. Ban Chao's youngest son is named Ban Yong. ◆Ban Yongzhuan, Ban Yong, courtesy name Yi Liao. When he was young, he had the general demeanor of his father, Ban Chao. In the first year of Yongchu, the Western Regions rebelled against the Han Dynasty, and the imperial court sent Ban Yong to serve as an army commander. Ban Yong and his brother Ban Xiong both sent troops from Dunhuang to welcome the return of the Duhu and the armored soldiers from the Western Regions. So he dismissed the governor. Later, there were no officials from the Han Dynasty in the Western Regions for more than ten years. In the sixth year of the Yuan Dynasty, Shi Suoban, the governor of Dunhuang Cao Zong, led more than a thousand people to garrison in Yiwu. The former king of Cheshi and the king of Shanshan both surrendered here to Suoban. A few months later, Bei Shanyu and the rear of the chariot division attacked Soban, drove away the former king, and occupied the road to the north.
target: Ban Yong, Ban Chao's son, served as an army commander. In the first year of Yongchu, he helped withdraw Han forces from the Western Regions. Later, he advised against a costly campaign, recommending a modest garrison in Dunhuang. His strategy was adopted, stabilizing the region.

source: So the imperial court listened to Ban Yong's advice and restored the Dunhuang County camp to 300 troops, and appointed the deputy captain of the Western Regions to live in Dunhuang. Although the Western Region was under control again, it was still unable to get out of the garrison area. Later, the Xiongnu and the charioteers invaded the border areas many times, and Hexi suffered great harm. In the summer of the second year of Yanguang, the imperial court sent Ban Yong to be the long history of the Western Regions and led 500 soldiers to station in Liuzhong. In the first month of the second year, Ban Yong arrived in Loulan. Because Shanshan had surrendered to the Han Dynasty, the imperial court specially added three ribbons to Ban Yong as a reward. But Baiying, the king of Qiuci, was still hesitant. Ban Yong used the grace and power of the Han Dynasty to enlighten him, so Baiying led Gumo and Wensu and tied himself up to surrender to Ban Yong. Ban Yong then mobilized more than 10,000 of his infantry and cavalry to go to King Qian of Che Division, drove away King Yili of the Xiongnu from Yihe Valley, and captured more than 5,000 people in the front, so the front was opened again. After returning, he still stayed in Liuzhong, defending and farming at the same time. In the autumn of the fourth year, Ban Yong mobilized 6,000 cavalry from Dunhuang, Zhangye, and Jiuquan and the front troops from Shanshan, Shule, and Che divisions to attack the king's army in the rear, and defeated them severely.
target: In the second year of Yanguang, he led 500 soldiers to Liuzhong, securing Shanshan and Qiuci's submission. He defeated the Xiongnu and pacified Cheshi. In Yongjian's first year, he attacked Yanqi but was imprisoned for missing a rendezvous, later dying at home.

source: Ban Yong walked from the south road, Zhang Lang walked from the north road, and agreed to meet at Yanqi on a date. However, Zhang Lang was guilty first and wanted to make atonement, so he rushed to Jue Liguan first. Sima was sent to lead troops to attack the front station and captured more than 2,000 enemy people. Yuan Meng was afraid of beheading, so he sent an envoy to ask for surrender. Zhang Lang went directly to Yanqi and surrendered. Yuan Meng actually refused to be tied up in person, and only sent his son to the court to pay tribute. Zhang Lang was pardoned from the death penalty. Because Ban Yong did not arrive as scheduled, he was convicted and imprisoned. He was pardoned soon after, and later died at home. ◆In the biography of Liang Jin, Liang Jin was named Bowei and was a native of Yiju in the north. His father, Liang Xi, served successively as governor of the state. In the first year of Yongyuan, Dou Xian, the general of chariots and cavalry, went to conquer the Xiongnu. Liang Xi was granted the title of Army Sima, and he was asked to bring gold and silk as an envoy to Bei Chanyu to promote the country's might and virtue. More than ten thousand people joined him. Later, because he violated Dou Xian's will, he was exiled to Wuwei, and the prefect of Wuwei ordered to kill him. After the Dou family was destroyed, Emperor He knew that Liang Xi had been unjustly killed by Dou Xian, so he summoned him as a doctor. Liang Jin was courageous and generous in his fame. At first, he was the Sima of Deng Hong, the chariot and cavalry general. He was promoted again and became the deputy captain of the Western Regions in the first year of Yanping. When Liang Jin went to Hexi, he encountered the rebellion of various countries in the Western Regions. He attacked the capital and protected Shang Yu in Shule. Ren Shang wrote a letter asking for help, and the court summoned Commander Liang Jin to lead five thousand Qiang and Hu cavalry from the four counties of Hexi to run to the rescue. However, Liang Jin did not arrive and Ren Shang had already rescued the siege. Just when Ren Shang was called back, the imperial court appointed Duan Xi, the Cavalry Commander, as the Protector, and Zhao Bo, the chief historian of the Western Regions, as the Cavalry Commander. Duan and Zhao guarded Qiancheng. Qiancheng was very small, and Liang Jin thought it was not very strong, so he cunningly persuaded Bai Ba, the king of Qiuci, to come in and protect the city together. Bai Ba agreed. The officials tried to dissuade him, but Bai Ba refused to listen. After Liang Jin entered the city, he sent generals to greet Duan Xi and Zhao Bo, with a total of eight or nine thousand sergeants. The officials of Qiuci all rebelled against their king, and they rebelled with tens of thousands of soldiers from Wensu and Gumo, and together they surrounded the city.
target: Liang Jin, a brave officer, served as Deputy Captain of the Western Regions. During a rebellion, he defended Qiuci with King Baiba, defeating tens of thousands of attackers. After the Western Regions were abandoned, he fought Qiang rebels, stabilizing Hexi. He later campaigned against the Xiongnu, accepting Chanyu's surrender. Appointed General Who Conquers the Liao, he died of illness while suppressing Qiang rebels.

source: ◆The legend of Shentu Gang is that Shentu Gang was named Juqing and was a native of Maoling, Fufeng County. The seventh generation ancestor Shen Tujia was the prime minister during the reign of Emperor Wen. Shentu was upright and upright, and often envied the conduct of Chief Shi Yu and Ji An. He became an official of the county meritorious service. During the reign of Emperor Ping, Wang Mang was in dictatorship, and there were many suspicions in the court. Wang Mang isolated the Feng clan of Emperor Ping's grandmother from the mother Wei clan, and was not allowed to go to Beijing to interact and serve as an official. Shentu Gang always resented this.
target: Shentu Gang, a native of Maoling, was an upright man who resented Wang Mang's isolation of Emperor Ping's maternal relatives.

source: Later, when he was praised as a virtuous and upright man, he wrote a countermeasure, saying: If I hear that the government is wrong, the gods of heaven and earth will be angry, and the treacherous and evil will cause trouble, so the yin and yang are wrong. This is why God condemns and warns the emperor, hoping to teach the unjust monarch to suddenly wake up and make those ministers with evil intentions fear and correct themselves. Nowadays, the imperial court does not examine merits or compare virtues, but instead accepts false slander or praise. It has issued several edicts and set up strict laws to suppress slander and prohibit discussion. Those who commit serious crimes may even be cut in half. This dampens the friendship of loyal ministers and dampens the spirit of loyal and upright people. It is contrary to the purpose of establishing banners to offer good words, hanging bells and drums for daring to give advice, opening up channels for words from all directions, and clearly observing the four directions so that the feelings of subordinates can be conveyed to superiors.
target: When recommended as a virtuous and upright man, he submitted a countermeasure criticizing the court for suppressing dissent and separating close relatives, arguing this violated the principles of good governance.

source: I heard that when King Cheng was young, the Duke of Zhou acted as regent. He listened to the opinions of others, treated the virtuous and corporal, shared rights and interests equally, spread favor widely, regardless of old or new, treated everyone with kindness, love and closeness, acted in accordance with heaven and earth, and did not violate the rules. However, if you are close, Duke Zhao is unhappy, and if you are far, there are rumors about Cai, Shang, and the four kingdoms.
target: He cited the examples of the Duke of Zhou and Huo Guang, warning that those with great power are often unsafe.

source: Your Majesty is young now, only nine years old. Since he came to the throne, his close relatives have been separated, his relatives are separated from each other, and his kindness is not as good as that of his uncle's family. Moreover, although the Han Dynasty system employed heroes and virtuous men, it was still necessary to use in-laws. In this way, kinship and distance were intertwined, and gaps could be closed. This was a method used to install ancestral temples and restructure the country. Now the Feng and Wei clans are innocent and have been deposed for a long time without being hired, or they are far away in remote and remote areas and are not as good as the common people. This is not the intention of loving, loyal and filial servants to the emperor.
target: He urged the emperor to welcome his grandmother and recall the Feng and Wei clans.

source: When the prophecy does not arrive, it is of course empty words, but once it arrives, it is too late, so the words of advice are true and I hope they will be accepted. May you think over and over again about my criticism. Wei Xiao refused to accept it, and finally rebelled against Han and followed Gongsun Shu. In the seventh year of Jianwu, there was an edict to conquer Shen Tugang. Just after Shentu returned, he wrote to Kaixiao again: I heard that people who insist on their own way are isolated, and people who refuse to accept advice are easy to get blocked. Isolated and blocked politics are the harbinger of national destruction. Although he has the qualifications of a wise sage, he still has to submit to the opinions of the public, so that he can be thoughtful and have no unintended plans, and his actions are appropriate and without wrongdoing. The sage does not regard his own unique opinion as wisdom, but regards all things as his heart. Those who obey others will prosper, and those who go against others will perish. This is a truth common to both ancient and modern times. The general was recommended by the village as a commoner. When he started the army, he had no predetermined plan. After he mobilized the army, he had no foresight. Nowadays, political and religious relations in the East are getting closer and closer, and the people are safe. However, when troops are sent to Xizhou, everyone is worried, turbulent and afraid, and dare not speak out. The masses are doubtful and worried. Not only does it lack the spirit of excellence and enterprising spirit, but its disasters are everywhere. When things are poor, accidents will happen. When things are urgent, plans are easy to form. It is caused by the situation. There is no one who can have a country and a family by deviating from morality and violating human feelings, in ancient and modern times. Generals have always been famous for their loyalty and filial piety, which is why scholar-bureaucrats come from thousands of miles away to admire and share their virtues. Now if you decide to act by chance, what else is left of loyalty, filial piety, virtue and justice? God bless you with prosperity, and people who help you are trustworthy. If there is no help from God, the common people will suffer misfortunes, destroy their lifelong virtues, ruin the integrity of monarchs and ministers, tarnish the kindness of father and son, and destroy the courage of all sages, so we must be cautious! Wei Xiao didn't accept it. When Shentu first arrived in Luoyang, he was appointed as the imperial censor, and then moved to the ministerial order. Guangwu once wanted to travel, but Shentu just thought that Longshu had not been pacified yet, so it was not suitable to have a leisurely meal. When his opinion was not accepted, he put his head on the wheel, and Guangwu stopped the tour. At that time, many officials at home and abroad were mostly elected by the emperor himself. They were subject to strict legal supervision. Their work was too hard, and the ministers and close ministers were even whipped and dragged forward. No ministers dared to speak honestly. Shen Tugang tried his best to dissuade him, and said many times that the crown prince should enter the East Palace and appoint virtuous guardians to achieve his virtue, but Guangwu refused to accept it. Because he repeatedly remonstrated against the will, a few years later, he was released as the Pingyin Order. Later, he was recalled to worship as Taizhong doctor. He resigned from his official position due to illness and died at home. ◆Bao Yongzhuan Bao Yong, courtesy name Junchang, was a native of Tunliu, Shangdang County. His father, Bao Xuan, was the captain of Sili School at the time of Emperor Ai and was killed by Wang Mang. When Bao Yong was young, he was ambitious and studied Ouyang's "Shang Shu". He was very filial to his stepmother. His wife once scolded the dog in front of his stepmother, so Bao Yong divorced his wife immediately.
target: Wang Mang had him dismissed from office. After Wang Mang usurped the throne, Shentu Gang fled. Later, when Wei Xiao considered betraying Han, Shentu Gang advised him to remain loyal to Emperor Guangwu, but Wei Xiao refused. In the seventh year of Jianwu, Shentu Gang was summoned. He again wrote to Wei Xiao, warning that isolation and refusal of advice lead to ruin, but Wei Xiao did not accept. Shentu Gang was appointed imperial censor and then ministerial order. He once stopped Emperor Guangwu from traveling by placing his head on the wheel. He repeatedly advised against the emperor's harsh treatment of officials and urged the appointment of virtuous guardians for the crown prince, but was not heeded. He was eventually released as the Pingyin Order, later recalled as Taizhong doctor, and died at home after resigning due to illness. Bao Yong, a native of Tunliu, was the son of Bao Xuan, who was killed by Wang Mang. He was filial, once divorcing his wife for scolding a dog in front of his stepmother.

source: Later, he was recalled to worship as Taizhong doctor. He resigned from his official position due to illness and died at home. ◆Bao Yongzhuan Bao Yong, courtesy name Junchang, was a native of Tunliu, Shangdang County. His father, Bao Xuan, was the captain of Sili School at the time of Emperor Ai and was killed by Wang Mang. When Bao Yong was young, he was ambitious and studied Ouyang's "Shang Shu". He was very filial to his stepmother. His wife once scolded the dog in front of his stepmother, so Bao Yong divorced his wife immediately. At first he was a county meritorious official. Wang Mang thought that Bao Xuan would not join him and wanted to kill his descendants. Duwei Luping followed Wang Mang's wishes and formulated a plan to kill Bao Yong. The prefect Gou Jian protected him, called him an official, and allowed him to live in the mansion permanently. Therefore, Bao Yong repeatedly stated the strategy of reviving the Han Dynasty and cutting off the treason for Gou Jian. Gou Jian repeatedly warned Bao Yong: If the ruler reveals the secret, the whole family will be killed. Bao Yong was grateful for his persuasion. After Gou Jian passed away, Bao Yong returned to Fufeng Luping to attend his funeral, so Bao Yong's younger brother Bao Sheng was put on trial. When the new governor Zhao Xing arrived, he sighed after hearing these things: I accepted the grant from the Han Dynasty and could not establish a festival. Bao Xuan was killed, how could I frame his son? The county magistrate was ordered to release Bao Sheng and restore Bao Yong to his position of meritorious service. At that time, there was a person pretending to be Shizhong living in Chuanshe, and Zhao Xing wanted to pay him a visit. Bao Yong suspected that he was lying and stopped Zhao Xing, but Zhao Xing refused to listen. Zhao Xing drove there, and Bao Yong drew his sword and cut the horse in the chest before the carriage stopped. A few days later, Wang Mang issued an edict to search for those who pretended to be servants, and Bao Yong became famous. It is inappropriate to recommend him as a scholar. In the second year of Gengshi's reign, Bao Yong was recruited, and then moved to the post of Shangshu Pushe, acting as the general's military affairs. He commanded the troops with Fu Jie, and assembled the Hedong, Bingzhou, and Shuo tribes, and authorized him to appoint partial generals and exercise military law. Bao Yong went to Hedong, led an army to attack Qingdu, and defeated him. He was granted the title of Marquis of Zhongyang.
target: Wang Mang sought to kill Bao Yong, but the prefect Gou Jian protected him. Bao Yong advised Gou Jian on reviving the Han. After Gou Jian's death, Bao Yong's brother was arrested, but the new prefect Zhao Xing released him. Bao Yong later exposed an impostor. During Gengshi's reign, he became a general and defeated Qingdu. After Gengshi's death, he submitted to Guangwu, dismissing his troops out of shame for serving Gengshi.

But the other commanders, Peng Feng, Yu Xiu, and Pi Chang, each with more than a thousand men, claimed to be "generals" and refused to surrender. Soon, the thorns in Confucius's palace were cleared for no reason, from the lecture hall to the inner gate. After the officials and the people were injured, Bao Yong relaxed the law to control the movement of people. He issued notices only to punish the violent ones, and calmed and appeased the people who threatened them, so the people settled down. When his mother passed away, he resigned and distributed all his property to his disciples. In the 11th year of Jianwu's reign, he was appointed as Sili Xiaowei. The emperor's uncle, King Liu Liang of Zhao, was a respected relative. target: He persuaded the governor of Huai County to surrender. As governor of Lu County, he killed the rebel generals Peng Feng and others. He later served as Yangzhou Mu, relaxing laws to pacify the people. As Sili Xiaowei, he impeached the emperor's uncle, King Liu Liang of Zhao, for disrespect, causing the court to be in awe. He wept at Gengshi's tomb, which initially displeased the emperor but was defended by a minister. He was later demoted for speaking out and then served as Yanzhou Mu until his death. The historian commented that Bao Yong's loyalty to his old master allowed him to serve a new one, and that upright words are difficult for people to understand.

source: Zheng Jing said: I am already satisfied. Back then, I went with you to search for Yu and Shun in Cangwu. Now I have returned to my hometown to live in seclusion and travel from Chisongzi. target: He then wrote to Wang Mang, urging him to return the throne to the Liu family, citing heavenly warnings. Wang Mang imprisoned him, but he was released. Later, he served under General Fu Jun, advising him to stop looting tombs and mistreating corpses, which the general did. Zhi Yun resigned, ashamed of gaining office through military merit. He avenged his friend Dong Zizhang by killing his enemy and then turned himself in, but the magistrate refused to imprison him. He later served as a meritorious officer under Prefect Ouyang She. At a feast, he publicly denounced another official, Yao Yan, as corrupt, causing the prefect shame. After a period of conflict, Zhi Yun left the prefect's service. He later became a marquis and gatekeeper, once refusing to let Emperor Guangwu enter the city at night. He remonstrated with the emperor about hunting and later advised the crown prince after Empress Guo was deposed. He served as governor of Changsha, where he praised a filial son, and later as magistrate of Mang County before retiring to teach. He wrote eight books and died of illness.

source: ◆Huangfu Song's biography, Huangfu Song's character is Yizhen, he was the son of the brother of Huangfu Gui, the general who conquered Liao Dynasty. Father Huangfu Festival, Yanmen Prefecture. When Huangfu Song was young, he had ambitions of literary and martial arts. He was good at "Poems" and "Books", and learned to bow, sword and ride horses. He began to be promoted as Xiaolian and Maocai. Taiwei Chen Fan and General Dou Wu were summoned one after another, but neither of them went. During the reign of Emperor Ling, he was promoted to Yilang by a public chariot and promoted to the governor of the North. In the past, Julu Zhangjiao claimed to be a great teacher. He believed in the teachings of Huangdi and Laozi, adopted disciples, knelt down and stated his faults, and used talisman water to recite mantras to cure diseases. The patients were cured, and the people believed in him. Therefore, Zhang Jiao sent eight of his disciples to all directions to educate the people of the world by doing good deeds and deceiving and confusing them. Over the past ten years, hundreds of thousands of believers have contacted counties and counties, and no one from the eight prefectures of Qing, Xu, You, Ji, Jing, Yang, Yan, and He did not respond. So thirty-six squares were set up. Fang is equal to the title of general. There are more than 10,000 people in Dafang and six or seven thousand in Xiaofang. Each party has a general. Rumors were spread that: Cang Tian is dead, Huang Tian should be established, and the age of Jiazi will bring good luck to the world. Written in white clay on temple gates in the capital and on state and county government offices, they are all marked with the character Jiazi. In the first year of Zhongping, Dafang Ma Yuanyi and others first collected tens of thousands of people from Jing and Yang, and gathered at Ye regularly to set off. Ma Yuanyi visited the capital many times, using Zhongchang Shifeng and Xu Feng as internal agents, and agreed to start an uprising both inside and outside the capital on March 5. Before the rebellion broke out, Zhang Jiao's disciple Jinan Tang Zhou wrote a letter to report, so he drove Ma Yuanyi to Luoyang. Emperor Ling used Zhou Zhang to issue orders to the three princes and officials, and ordered Zhou Bin to take the three government officials with him. He asked the palace guards and the people if they believed in Zhang Jiao, killed more than a thousand people, tracked down Jizhou, and arrested Zhang Jiao and others. Zhang Jiao and others knew that the matter had been exposed, so they notified all parties day and night and started revolts at the same time. They all wore yellow scarves as a symbol. At that time, they were called "yellow scarves" and also "moth thieves".
target: Huangfu Song, styled Yizhen, was a nephew of the general Huangfu Gui. His father served as the Prefect of Yanmen. From a young age, Huangfu Song was learned in the *Classic of Poetry* and *Book of Documents*, and skilled in archery, swordsmanship, and horsemanship. He was recommended as a Xiaolian and Maocai, but declined summons from Grand Commandant Chen Fan and General Dou Wu. During Emperor Ling's reign, he was appointed Yilang and later Governor of Beidi. When Zhang Jiao founded the Way of Great Peace, claiming to cure illness through faith and talismanic water, he amassed hundreds of thousands of followers across eight provinces over a decade. He organized them into thirty-six "squares," each led by a general, and spread the prophecy: "The Azure Heaven is dead; the Yellow Heaven shall rise. In the year of Jiazi, the world will be blessed." In the first year of Zhongping (184 AD), his disciple Tang Zhou betrayed the planned uprising, leading to the execution of Ma Yuanyi and a crackdown in Luoyang. Zhang Jiao then launched a nationwide rebellion, with followers wearing yellow scarves—hence called the "Yellow Turbans"—burning government offices and terrorizing provinces.
