source: The imperial court ordered the prefectures and counties to repair offensive and defensive positions, select and prepare ordnance, and set up captains at Hangu, Dagu, Guangcheng, Yique, Longyuan, Xuanmen, Mengjin, and Xiaopingjin passes. Call the ministers to a meeting. Huangfu Song believed that the ban on the party should be lifted, and he gave Zhongzang money and Xiyuan stable horses to the sergeants. Emperor Ling adopted his opinion. So he recruited the best soldiers from all over the world. Generals were widely selected, and Huangfu Song was appointed as the left Zhonglang general. He held the talisman, and together with the right Zhonglang general Zhu Ai, they sent out five schools, Sanhe knights and recruited brave warriors, totaling more than 40,000 people. Huangfu Song and Zhu Ai unified their armies and joined forces to attack the Yingchuan Yellow Turbans. Zhu Ji had previously fought against the thief Bo Cai and was defeated, so Huangfu Song marched to defend Changshe. Bocai led a large army to besiege the city, but Huangfu Song had few soldiers. The army became frightened, so he summoned the military officers and said: "There is a strange change in the army, not because there are more soldiers than there are fewer soldiers." Nowadays, thieves have camped on grass and are prone to catching fire due to the wind. If you set fire to it at night, you must be frightened and dispersed. I will send troops to attack and surround it on all sides. Tian Dan and Jimo will use the fire ox to attack Yan and win. That night, there was a strong wind, so Huangfu Song ordered his sergeants to tie up ropes and climb up the city. He sent elite and brave men to go out on the small road, lit fires and shouted, and the city raised torches in response. Huangfu Song beat drums and rushed to the enemy's position. The thieves fled in panic. At this time, Emperor Ling sent Cao Cao, the cavalry captain, to arrive with his troops. Huangfu Song, Cao Cao and Zhu Ji joined forces to fight again. They defeated the rebel army, beheaded tens of thousands of people, and made Huangfu Song the Marquis of Duxiang. Huangfu Song and Zhu Ji took advantage of their victory to attack Runan and Chen Guohuangjin, pursued Bo Cai in Yangdi, attacked Peng Tuo in Xihua, and defeated them all. The remaining thieves either surrendered or fled, and the three counties were pacified. They also attacked Dongjun Huangjin Buji in Cangting, captured Buji alive, and beheaded more than 7,000 people. At that time, Lu Zhi, the general of Bei Zhonglang, and Dong Zhuo, the general of Dong Zhonglang, attacked Zhang Jiao, but they all failed, so they ordered Huangfu Song to lead troops to attack Zhang Jiao. Huangfu Song fought against Zhang Jiao's younger brother Zhang Liang in Guangzong. Zhang Liang's troops were elite and brave, but Huangfu Song could not defeat him. The next day, Huangfu Song closed the camp and allowed the soldiers to rest and observe the changes in the enemy's army. Knowing that the thieves and sergeants had become lax, they quietly gathered their troops at night, waited until the rooster crow, launched a charge, and fought until dark. They defeated the enemy army, beheaded Zhang Liang, and won the 30,000-level leader. About 50,000 people went to the Yellow River and drowned. They burned more than 30,000 vehicles and equipment, captured all the enemy's wives, children, and arrested many. Zhang Jiao died of illness first, so he opened his coffin, killed his body, and reported it to the capital. Huangfu Song, together with Feng Yi and Guo Dian, the governors of Julu, attacked Zhang Jiao's younger brother Zhang Bao in Xiaquyang and killed him. More than 100,000 people were captured, and their corpses were piled up and sealed with earth to build a palace in the south of the city. Huangfu Song was appointed General of Zuo Chaoqi and Jizhou Mu, and was granted the title of Marquis of Huaili. He served in Huaili and Meiyang counties, totaling 8,000 households. Because the Yellow Turbans had been pacified, the year was changed to Zhongping. Huangfu Song petitioned to reduce one year's land rent in Jizhou to help the hungry people. Emperor Ling agreed.
target: The court appointed Huangfu Song as Left General of the Central Army, alongside Zhu Jun, to suppress the rebellion. After an initial defeat, Huangfu Song used a fire attack at Changshe, exploiting a strong wind to burn the enemy camp and rout Bo Cai's forces. Reinforced by Cao Cao, they defeated the rebels, beheading tens of thousands. Huangfu Song was made Marquis of Duxiang. They then pacified Runan and Chen, capturing Bo Cai and Peng Tuo. At Cangting, they captured Bu Ji, killing over 7,000. Huangfu Song was then ordered to attack Zhang Jiao. After initial setbacks against Zhang Liang at Guangzong, he feigned rest, then launched a surprise dawn assault, killing Zhang Liang and 30,000 rebels, with 50,000 drowning in the Yellow River. Zhang Jiao had died of illness, so Huangfu Song beheaded his corpse. He then killed Zhang Bao at Xiaquyang, capturing over 100,000. He was appointed General of the Left Chariot and Cavalry and Governor of Jizhou, with 8,000 households. He petitioned to reduce Jizhou's land rent, earning popular praise.

He loved justice more than wealth, and the villagers admired him very much. At that time, Zhou Gui of the same county summoned the government, and when he set out on his journey, he borrowed a million dollars from the county treasury to pay for clothing. As a result, his mother lost her inheritance and became furious and scolded him. Zhu Jun said: A small loss will lead to a big benefit. It is inevitable to be poor first and then rich. Yangdu Shang, the magistrate of Shangyu County, met Zhu Jun and thought he was not an ordinary person. He introduced him to Wei Yi, the prefect, and he took up some positions in the county. At this time, a group of thieves broke out in Jiaozhi tribe, but Mu Shou was too weak to stop them. He also handed over the rebels Liang Long and more than 10,000 people, who rebelled with Kong Zhi, the prefect of Nanhai, and conquered the counties. In the first year of Guanghe, he appointed Zhu Jun as the governor of Jiaochengzhi. He ordered Zhu Jun to recruit 5,000 soldiers in the county plus the ones he had dispatched. They marched in two directions and arrived at the state border. He stopped advancing. He first sent envoys to the county to observe the strength of the thieves and publicize the power of the court to shake their hearts. Then he joined forces with the soldiers of the seven counties to force the thieves. He killed Liang Long and tens of thousands of people surrendered. They were all pacified within a month. Zhu Jun was granted the title of Marquis of Tingting in the capital for his meritorious service, with 1,500 households, 50 jins of gold, and conscription as an admonishment official. When the Yellow Turban bandits arose, many ministers recommended Zhu Jun as a talented man. Huangfu Song went up to report on the situation of pacifying the thieves, and attributed the credit to Zhu Jun. Therefore, the Jin Dynasty granted Zhu Jun the title of Marquis of Xixiang, and promoted him to the rank of Lang General in the town of thieves.
target: When the Jiaozhi rebellion erupted, Zhu Jun was appointed Governor of Jiaozhi. He recruited 5,000 troops, pacified the rebels, killed Liang Long, and secured surrender. He was made a Marquis and later served as an admonishment official. During the Yellow Turban rebellion, Zhu Jun was appointed Right General of the Central Army, alongside Huangfu Song. They suppressed rebels in Yingchuan, Runan, and Chen. Huangfu Song credited Zhu Jun, who was made Marquis of Xixiang. Zhu Jun then besieged Nanyang Yellow Turban leader Zhao Hong at Wancheng for months. Despite advice to replace him, the court persisted.

source: Zhu Jun's crusade against the Yingchuan bandits has been successful. He has led his troops to the south. The plan has been made. Changing generals before the battle is taboo for military strategists. Zhu Jun should be given some time to win. Therefore, Emperor Ling did not recruit Zhu Jun. Zhu Jun therefore attacked Zhao Hong severely and finally killed him. The remaining thief commander Han Zhong took Wan again to resist Zhu Jun. The Jie soldiers were few and invincible, so they set up a siege and fortified the city. They raised earthen hills to serve as the inner city and beat drums to attack the southwestern side of the city. The thieves attacked with all their strength. Zhu Jun himself led five thousand elite troops, assaulted the northeast of the city, and climbed into the city. Han Zhong had no choice but to withdraw from the small town and asked to surrender in fear. Sima Zhang Chao, Xu Chu and Qin Jie all wanted to accept Han Zhong's surrender. Zhu Jun said: The military has the same physical appearance but different potential. In the past, during the reign of Qin Xiang, the people had no fixed masters, so they rewarded those who came to join him to encourage those who had not yet returned. Now that the country is unified, only the Yellow Turbans can cause chaos. Accepting surrender cannot encourage good people, and only crusade can punish evildoers. Accepting surrender now will further encourage the idea of ​​​​causing chaos. If it is advantageous to the thieves, they will go to war. If it is not advantageous, they will beg for surrender. It is not a good idea to indulge the enemy and encourage the rebellion. Due to the hasty attack, they were unable to win consecutive battles. Zhu Gan climbed up Tushan Mountain to look around, then turned around and said to Zhang Chao: I understand! The thieves' outer perimeter was strong, but the inner camp was pressed hard. They could neither surrender nor escape, so they fought to the death. It’s not enough for ten thousand people to unite, let alone one hundred thousand! The harm of a strong attack is too great. It is better to remove the siege and gather the troops into the city. When Han Zhong saw that the siege had been lifted, he would definitely come out on his own. When he came out, his thoughts would disperse. This is an easy way to break through. After the siege was lifted, Han Zhong came out to ask for a battle, and Zhu Jun attacked and won a great victory. And they took advantage of the victory and pursued for dozens of miles, beheading more than 10,000 people. Han Zhong and others surrendered. But because Qin Jie hated Han Zhong and killed him, the remaining thieves were frightened and uneasy, so they still stationed themselves in Wanzhong with Sun Xia as their commander. Zhu Jun rushed to attack, but Sun Xia escaped and chased him to Jingshan Mountain in western Hubei. He defeated him again and beheaded more than ten thousand people before the thieves were disbanded. In the spring of the next year, the imperial court sent an envoy to appoint Zhu Jun as the Right Cavalry General on the Emperor's Day. He returned to the capital in triumph and was appointed Guanglu Doctor. He resigned from the official position due to the death of his mother, and later came out from home to serve as an official. He was appointed as a master craftsman, and transferred to the Shaofu and Tai servants.
target: Zhu Jun killed Zhao Hong, then faced Han Zhong. Feigning weakness, he attacked the city's northeast, forcing Han Zhong to retreat. When Han Zhong sought surrender, Zhu Jun refused, arguing it would encourage rebellion. He lifted the siege, allowing Han Zhong to scatter, then defeated him, beheading over 10,000. After Han Zhong was killed by Prefect Qin Jie, Zhu Jun defeated Sun Xia, ending the rebellion. Zhu Jun was appointed General of the Right Chariot and Cavalry, then served as Guanglu Doctor. After his mother's death, he returned to office as Master of Works, then Shaofu and Grand Servant.

source: Although Dong Zhuo hated Zhu Jun for opposing him, he wanted to take advantage of his fame, so he asked him to be promoted to Taiwen as his deputy. The imperial envoy offered him an official position, but Zhu Junci refused to accept it. He said: If the country's capital moves westward, it will definitely disappoint the hopes of the people of the world and become a disaster for Shandong. I don't see how it is right. The messenger asked: I called you to worship, but you refused. I didn't ask you about moving the capital, but you talked about moving the capital. What's the reason? Zhu Jun said: I am not qualified to be the deputy prime minister; moving the capital is not a top priority. It is appropriate for me to resign those who are incompetent and say that those are not the urgent matters of the day. The envoy said: I have never heard of the capital relocation, and the state has not announced it. How did you know about it? Zhu Jun said: Prime Minister Dong Zhuo told me everything, so I know! After Dong Zhuo's death, Tao Qian and others recommended Zhu Jun as Grand Marshal, but Li Jue and Guo Si summoned him to court. Zhu Jun accepted, becoming Grand Commandant and Minister of Works.

source: Huangfu Guizhuan, whose courtesy name was Weiming, was from that county in Anding County. His grandfather Huangfuleng was a general of Liao Dynasty. source: Then he recommended Huangfu Gui to the position of planner. Later, Qiang soldiers gathered in large numbers to attack, burn, and plunder Longxi, and the court thought it was a disaster. Huangfu went to the imperial court and asked to serve the country, saying: In recent years, I have stated many times the measures to deal with the Western Qiang. The Qiang Rong had not yet moved, so I expected him to rebel. As soon as Ma Xian sent troops, I knew he would be defeated. These words said by chance are supported by facts everywhere. I often think that Ma Xian and others have been holding troops for four years without success. The cost of suspending the army is calculated in tens of billions. This money comes from the common people and falls into the pockets of traitors. Therefore, the common people in the rivers and lakes gathered together as thieves, there was famine in Qingzhou and Xuzhou, and the old and the weak were scattered. It turns out that the Qiang Rong rebelled, not when the world was at peace, because the border generals failed to appease and govern them. They should be in peace, but they invade them. In order to obtain small benefits, they end up causing great harm. In order to prove that they won the battle, they often falsely reported the number of beheadings, and they kept it secret when they lost the battle. The soldiers worked hard, were full of resentment, and were forced by the treacherous officials. They could not advance quickly to gain fame and retreat, and could not retreat to have enough food and clothing to survive. They starved to death in the ditch and left their corpses scattered everywhere. They saw the king's division send troops in vain, but did not see the king's division come back. Weeping and weeping for God's sorrow, fearing that something might happen. Therefore, the period of peace is very short, and once chaos breaks out, it lasts for many years. This is what I sigh with clapping my hands and tapping my heart. I hope to give me the strength of the two battalions of Ma Xian and Zhao Chong and the land of the two counties of Anding and Longxi. I will lead five thousand soldiers to sit down and eat. If there is an unexpected Qiang Rong incident, I will be responsible for the head and tail of Zhao Chong, the captain of the Qiang school. The situation of the land and valleys is familiar to me; the military situation is convenient and I have rectified it. You don't have to worry about using a square-inch seal to issue documents, and a foot of silk as a reward. High can eliminate worries, and low can accept surrender. If it is said that I am young and have a low official rank, I cannot be used. Those generals who defeated the army are not high in official rank and young in age. How can I say this? I am so sincere that I will risk my life to tell my story. The emperor did not use him at that time. During the reign of Emperor Chong and Emperor Zhi, the Empress Dowager Liang was in power, and Huangfu Gui was praised as virtuous and upright. Huangfu Gui countermeasures asked: If you want to be filial to the emperor, if you are in power and establish court discipline, the country will soon be at peace.

He requested command of troops from two battalions and two counties to lead 5,000 soldiers against the Qiang, but the emperor did not use him at that time. During the reigns of Emperors Chong and Zhi, when Empress Dowager Liang held power, Huangfu Gui was praised as virtuous and upright.

source: The memories of the Qiang rebellion in the past are still fresh in my mind, and I am really worried about this. Therefore, I went beyond my duties and submitted a letter to fulfill my only patriotic intention. In winter, all the Qiang people gathered together and were ready to move, and the court felt worried. Sangong promoted Huangfu Gui to the rank of Zhonglang General, held the emperor's talisman to supervise the Guanxi soldiers, conquered Lingwu and others, defeated them, and beheaded eight hundred people. There were more than 100,000 Qiang people who envied Huangfu Gui's prestige and persuaded each other to surrender. The next year, Huangfu Gui took the opportunity to mobilize his cavalry to jointly attack Longyou. However, the roads were blocked and an epidemic broke out in the army. Three or four out of ten people died of the disease. Huangfu Gui personally entered the nunnery to express condolences to the soldiers. The three armies were grateful and happy. Because the Eastern Qiang sent envoys to beg for surrender, Liangzhou was no longer blocked. At that time, Sun Gen, the governor of Anding, was very serious about bribery and corruption. Li Xi, the captain of the country, and Zhang Xun, the governor's censor, killed and surrendered the Qiang. Guo Hong, the governor of Liangzhou, and Zhao Xi, the governor of Hanyang, were both old and weak and could not hold their posts. However, they relied on powerful relatives and did not abide by the laws of the country. Huangfu Gui arrived at the state border and reported their crimes one by one. Some were removed from their official positions and some were sentenced to death. After hearing this, the Qiang people quickly surrendered. More than 100,000 people including Dianchang and Xongtian, the great tycoons of the Shen family, surrendered to Huangfu Gui. Huangfu Gui was born a few years ago and held the Emperor's Talisman as a general. He led the people to perform meritorious service and returned to supervise the countryside. He had no personal favors. On the contrary, he reported many bad people and bad deeds. He also hated eunuchs deeply and refused to associate with them. As a result, people inside and outside the court complained about him, and they all falsely accused Huangfu Gui of bribing the Qiang people and causing them to surrender. The emperor issued edicts one after another. Huangfu Gui was afraid that he would be killed, so he complained to Shangshu: In the autumn of the fourth year, Rong Chou made a fool of himself to cause chaos. From Xizhou to Jingyang, the old capital was frightened and the imperial court looked westward. The imperial edict of the Ming Dynasty did not consider me a fool and ordered me to urgently lead the army on the road. Thanks to the emperor's power, the country's fortunes were greatly boosted. Qiang and Rong, large and small, kowtowed and submitted. I immediately sent a letter to the military camp and the county guard to inquire how many they had killed and how many they had surrendered. This saved the cost, which was more than 100 million. I think this is the duty of a loyal minister, and I dare not say that I have any merit. He also believes that any self-report of minor achievements in a few words is shameful. But compared with the loss of generals and troops of the predecessors, the common people are almost free from guilt and regret.
target: After Liang Ji was killed, the court summoned Huangfu Gui five times but he did not respond. He was later appointed as the prefect of Taishan to deal with bandit Sun Wuji, and he successfully pacified all the bandits. However, Huangfu Gui reported the crimes of corrupt officials, including the governor of Anding and others, leading to their removal or execution. Huangfu Gui defended himself, explaining that his actions saved over 100 million in costs and that his expenditures were documented. Despite his merits, eunuchs Xu Huang and Zuo Xiang demanded bribes from him, and when he refused, they framed him. He was sentenced to hard labor but was released after an amnesty.

Shan Bingzou asked Changle Shangshu Zheng Sa, who was always cunning and extremely ruthless, to be sent to Beisi Prison. Chen Fan said to Dou Wu: These guys should be killed immediately, why bother interrogating them! Dou Wu did not listen to his opinions and ordered Shan Bing, Yin Xun, and Shi Yushi Zhu Wangjin to interrogate Zheng Sa in a chaotic manner. Sa's confession implicated Cao Jie and Wang Fu. Yin Xun and Shan Bing petitioned to arrest Cao Jie and others, and asked Liu Yu to report to the Empress Dowager. At this time, Dou Wu went out to stay and returned to his mansion. The person in charge of Zhongshu first reported him to Zhu Wangyu, the official historian of Changle. Zhu Wangyu stole Dou Wu's memorial and read it, and cursed: Of course the eunuchs who indulge in illegal acts can be killed.
target: Dou Wu, along with Grand Tutor Chen Fan, planned to eliminate the eunuchs. Chen Fan urged immediate action, citing a solar eclipse as an omen. Dou Wu proposed the plan to the Empress Dowager, but she hesitated, citing tradition. After executing some eunuchs, Dou Wu's plan to kill others like Cao Jie stalled. When an astrological omen appeared, Dou Wu and Chen Fan prepared to act. They appointed allies to key posts and arrested a eunuch, whose confession implicated Cao Jie and Wang Fu. However, a eunuch stole the memorial and alerted his colleagues. They falsely accused Dou Wu of treason to the young emperor, seized the Empress Dowager, and issued an edict for Dou Wu's arrest. Dou Wu refused to submit, rallied troops, but his soldiers were persuaded to defect by the imperial edict. Pursued, Dou Wu and his nephew committed suicide.

source: The camp was usually afraid of subduing the eunuchs, so Dou Wu's army returned to Wang Fu. From morning to lunch, Dou Wu's troops had almost surrendered. Dou Wu and Dou Shao fled and were pursued and surrounded by Wang Fu's army. They both committed suicide and showed their heads to Luoyang Duting. Their clansmen, guests, and in-laws were all captured and killed. Liu Yu and Feng Shu all annihilated their clans. Moved Dou Wu's family to Rinan and moved the Queen Mother to Yuntai. At this time, the vicious eunuch succeeded, and the upright people were discouraged and dared not say anything. Dou Wu's official Hu Teng from Guiyang, who learned from Dou Wu when he was young, collected and buried Dou Wu's body alone, so he was imprisoned and was not allowed to be an official. Dou Wu's grandson Dou Fu, who was only two years old at the time, was not harmed because he escaped. Later he was discovered, and Cao Jie and others arrested him urgently. Hu Teng and Ling Shi Nanyang and Zhang Chang helped Dou Fu escape to Lingling, pretending to be dead. Hu Teng considered him his son and got a wife for him.
target: Their clans were exterminated, and the Queen Mother was moved. Dou Wu's grandson, Dou Fu, was saved by a former student, Hu Teng, who hid him and later helped him establish a family.

source: Hu Teng's courtesy name is Zisheng. At first, Emperor Huan went on a tour of Nanyang and used Hu Teng as his escort. The ministers, nobles, and relatives have tens of thousands of entourages, and there is no end to the demand for money and labor. Hu Teng wrote a letter saying: The emperor has no inside or outside. The place where he goes is the capital. I asked Bi Si, the governor of Jingzhou, to serve as the school captain, and I myself served as the official of Tongdu. The emperor complied. From then on, the followers did not dare to ask for anything without authorization, and Hu Teng became famous for this. After the party ban was lifted, the official became minister. ◆He Jinzhuan, He Jinzhuan, courtesy name Suigao, was from Wan County, Nanyang. The half-brother and daughter were selected as nobles in the palace. Emperor Ling liked her and appointed He Jin as the doctor. He was promoted to the general of the doctor in Huben and became the prefect of Yingchuan. In the third year of Guanghe's reign, the nobleman was appointed as the queen. He was recruited to the capital and served as a servant. He was appointed as a master craftsman and Henan Yin. In the first year of Zhongping, the Yellow Turban thief Zhang Jiao and others rose up, appointed He Jin as the general, and led the five battalions of Yulin on the left and right to station in the capital pavilion to repair equipment and defend the capital. Zhang Jiao's faction, Ma Yuanyi, conspired to raise troops in Luoyang. He Jin discovered his treacherous plot and was granted the title of Marquis Shen for his merits. In the fourth year, thousands of Xingyang thieves rioted, attacked and burned the county, and killed the county magistrate of Zhongmou. He Jin's younger brother Henan Yin Hemiao was ordered to fight. He Miao defeated the thieves, quelled the riot and returned to the capital. The imperial edict sent an envoy to Chenggao to welcome him, and appointed He Miao as a chariot and cavalry general and the Marquis of Jiyang.
target: He Jin, from Nanyang, rose to power after his half-sister became Empress to Emperor Ling. He was made a general to suppress the Yellow Turban rebellion and later a marquis. He and his brother He Miao defeated a rebellion of thieves.

source: After the ceremony, Emperor Ling, wearing armor and horse, called the "Supreme General" and circled the formation three times before returning. He Jin was ordered to lead the entire army to watch. At this time, eight captains of Xiyuan were set up, with Xiaohuangmen Jianshuo as the upper military captain, Huben Zhonglang Yuan Shao as the middle military captain, Tunqi Commander Bao Hong as the lower military captain, Yilang Cao Cao as the dian military captain, Zhao Rong as the assistant military captain, Chunyu Qiong as the assistant military captain, and the left and right captains. Emperor Ling believed that Jian Shuo was strong and capable of military strategy. He trusted him especially and appointed him as a marshal, supervising and supervising the commanders and subordinates below the school captain. Even the generals were also under his leadership. Although Jian Shuo was in charge of military power in the imperial court, he was still a little afraid of being jealous of He Jin, so he talked to Emperor Ling with his ministers and asked him to send He Jin to the west to attack Bian Zhang and Han Sui. Emperor Ling listened to them and rewarded He Jin with hundreds of military chariots, tigers, sharp axes and axes. He Jin secretly knew this was a conspiracy. So he submitted a petition to send Yuan Zhaodong to attack Xu and Yanzhou soldiers. He wanted to wait for Yuan Shao to return before sending troops to delay time. At first, Queen He gave birth to Prince Bian, and Wang Gui gave birth to Prince Xie. The ministers asked for a crown prince, but Emperor Ling thought that he was too frivolous and unworthy to be a king. However, the queen was favored by Emperor Ling, and He Jin held great power, so he hesitated to decide. In the sixth year, Emperor Ling was seriously ill and asked Jian Shuo to assist Liu Xie. Jian Shuo had received the imperial edict and had always looked down upon and envied brothers He Jin and He Miao. When Emperor Ling passed away, Jian Shuo was in the palace and wanted to kill He Jin first and establish Xie as emperor. When He Jin came in from outside, Jian Shuo Sima Pan Yin and He Jin had known each other for a long time, and they welcomed He Jin with his eyes. He Jin was frightened and rode back to the camp from a shortcut, leading his troops to the Baijun Mansion, so he refused to go in because of illness. Jian Shuo's plot did not come true, and Prince Bian became emperor. The Empress Dowager He came to the court to attend to the affairs of state, while He Jin and the Grand Tutor Yuan Kai assisted in the administration and also took charge of the affairs of the Secretariat. He Jin had known for a long time that eunuchs were hated by everyone in the world, and he hated Jian Shuo for plotting to harm him and for taking over the power of the court, so he secretly arranged to kill the eunuchs. Yuan Shao also had a plan for a long time, and asked He Jin's relative Zhang Jin to persuade He Jin: Huangmen Changshi has been in power for a long time, and he has committed adultery with the Empress Dowager Changle. The general should select virtuous talents to rectify the world and eliminate harm to the country.
target: Emperor Ling established a new army with eight colonels, entrusting the eunuch Jian Shuo with overall command. Jian Shuo, fearing He Jin, plotted to send him away. When Emperor Ling died, Jian Shuo planned to kill He Jin and install Prince Xie as emperor, but He Jin was warned and avoided the trap. He Jin then made Prince Bian emperor, with the Empress Dowager as regent. He Jin, hating the eunuchs and Jian Shuo's plot, planned to eliminate them with Yuan Shao's support. However, the Empress Dowager refused, and He Jin's relatives, bribed by eunuchs, also opposed him.

source: He Jinxin was in charge of important tasks and was usually afraid of them. Although he was famous outside, he could not make a decision in his heart, so things could not be settled for a long time. Why did Yuan Shao and others plan to summon more powerful generals and a large number of heroes from all over the world, so that they could lead their troops to the capital to threaten the Queen Mother. He Jin agreed. Chen Lin, the chief bookkeeper, advised him: "The Book of Changes" states that if the deer is released, it cannot be caught. As the saying goes: Hunting sparrows while blindfolded. If you can't deceive small things with success, how much more can you use deceit to obtain important national affairs. Now the general has the imperial power, controls the military power, the dragon and the tiger step, whether it is high or low, it is all in your heart. This is like burning the hair on a stove. What's the difficulty? It conforms to the Tao, goes against the scriptures, and is obeyed by heaven and man. Instead, abandon the weapon and look for foreign aid. When the soldiers gather together, the stronger becomes the hero. This is what is called fighting and turning the tables on others. If you give the handle to others, the success will never be achieved, and the vain efforts will become the steps for chaos and evil. He Jin refused to listen. He summoned former general Dong Zhuo from the west to garrison in Shanglinyuan in Guanzhong, and sent Wang Kuang of Taishan to mobilize the strong crossbowmen of his county. He summoned Qiao Mao, the prefect of Dongjun, to garrison in Chenggao. He sent Ding Yuan, the commander of Wu Meng, to burn Mengjin. The fire lit up the city red, and they all said they wanted to kill the eunuchs.
target: He Jin hesitated, and Yuan Shao suggested summoning provincial generals like Dong Zhuo to threaten the court. Despite advice against this, He Jin agreed.

source: Zhonghuangmen threw He Jin's head to the minister and said: "He Jin has rebelled and has been killed." He Jin's subordinate generals Wu Kuang and Zhang Zhang were He Jin's cronies. They heard that He Jin had been killed outside and wanted to lead troops into the palace. The palace was closed and no one was allowed to enter. Yuan Shu and Wu Kuang worked together to cut and attack, while Zhonghuang Gate defended the pavilion with weapons. At sunset, Yuan Shu set fire to the Nine Dragon Gate of Nangong and the East and West Palaces, and wanted to threaten Zhang Rang and others to come out. Zhang Rang and others went in and told the Queen Mother that the general had rebelled, burned the palace, and attacked the Shangshu Gate, so he kidnapped the Queen Mother, the Emperor, and King Chenliu, and also robbed the palace officials and their families, and took the North Palace via Fudao. Shangshu Lu Zhi held a sword under the window of the pavilion, raised his head and scolded Duan Wanggui. Duan Wanggui was afraid and released the Queen Mother. The Queen Mother jumped from the pavilion and escaped without being robbed. Yuan Shao and his uncle Yuan Wei falsely claimed that the emperor ordered Fan Ling and Xu Xiang to be killed. He Miao and Yuan Shao then led troops to station under Zhuque Tower, arrested Zhao Zhong and others and killed them. Wu Kuang waited for a long time and complained that He Miao was not of the same mind as He Jin. He also suspected that he was conspiring with the eunuchs, so he ordered the army to say: The one who killed the general was the chariot. Can you avenge the general? He Jin was kind and kind to his subordinates, and all the soldiers cried and said: I am willing to die in repayment! Wu Kuang led his troops and Dong Zhuo's younger brother, Fengche Duwei Dong, attacked and killed He Miao and dumped his body in the garden. Yuan Shao closed the North Palace Gate and ordered his soldiers to capture the eunuchs. No matter how big or small, kill them all. Some were mistakenly thought to be killed by eunuchs, while others exposed themselves and were spared from being killed. More than two thousand people died. Yuan Shaoyin marched into the palace, and some people from the upper gates attacked the palace. Zhang Rang, Duan Wanggui and others could not escape the siege, so they kidnapped the emperor and dozens of King Chen Liu and fled to Xiaopingjin. The ministers all came out from Pingtang, and no one ran with them. Only Lu Zhi, the minister, rode on horseback on the river at night. Wang Yun sent Minggong from central Henan to follow Lu Zhi. Mingong arrived and killed several people with his sword, while the rest jumped into the river and died. The next day, the ministers and officials welcomed the emperor back to the palace, appointed Min Gong as the doctor, and granted the title of Marquis of Ting. Dong Zhuo then deposed Emperor Ling, forced the Queen Mother to be killed, and killed Lord Wuyang. The He family died, and the Han Dynasty also fell into chaos. The historian commented: Dou Wu and He Jin, as uncles, held the power of assisting the government. Inside the palace, they relied on the power of the Queen Mother to listen to the government, and outside they had favorable conditions for heroes to ride on the wind. Finally, they were defeated by the eunuchs, died in power, and were lamented by the world. Is it possible that they lacked intelligence but had more power?
target: The eunuchs, fearing for their lives, tricked their way back into the palace. When He Jin went to the palace to urge the Empress Dowager to act, the eunuchs ambushed and killed him. His subordinates then attacked the palace. Yuan Shao and others massacred the eunuchs, killing over two thousand. During the chaos, the eunuchs kidnapped the emperor and his brother, but were eventually killed. Dong Zhuo then deposed the emperor, killed the Empress Dowager, and the He family was destroyed, plunging the Han dynasty into chaos. The historian comments that both Dou Wu and He Jin, despite their power and favorable positions, were defeated by eunuchs due to a lack of wisdom and excessive reliance on power.

source: ◆Dou Rong's Biography: Dou Rong's courtesy name was Duke of Zhou, and he was a native of Pingling County, Fufeng County. Dou Guangguo, the seventh generation ancestor, was the younger brother of Queen Xiaowen and was named Zhang Wuhou. His great-great-grandfather moved from Changshan with two thousand stones as an official during the reign of Emperor Xuan. Dou Rong has been an orphan since he was a child. During the reign of Wang Mang, he was the Sima of Wang Jun, the strong crossbow general. He attacked Zhaiyi in the east and Huaili. He was named Jianwu Nan for his military merits. The younger sister is the younger wife of the great Sikong Wangyi. He lived in Chang'an, visited noble families, made friends with local heroes, and was famous for his chivalry and righteousness. However, he served his mother and elder brother and raised his weak younger brother, practicing benevolence and righteousness. In the last years of Wang Mang, bandits broke out in Qingzhou and Xuzhou. Wang Kuang, the Grand Master, asked Dou Rong to help the army and join him in the eastern expedition. When the Han army rose, Dou Rong was defeated by Wang Yi at Kunyangxia and returned to Chang'an. When the Han army commander entered the pass, Wang Yi recommended Dou Rong as General Bo Shui, rewarded him with a thousand catties of gold, and led his troops to Xinfeng. When Wang Mang was defeated, Dou Rong led his army and surrendered to Zhao Meng, the commander-in-chief of Gengshi. Zhao Meng regarded Dou Rong as a school captain and thought highly of him. He recommended Dou Rong to be the prefect of Julu. When Dou Rong saw the new establishment and the chaos in the east, he didn't want to leave the country. He remembered that his great-great-grandfather was the governor of Zhangye, his grandfather was the captain of the Qiang Guard, and his younger brother was the governor of Wuwei. They had been in Hexi for several generations and knew the local customs, so he said to his brothers alone: The safety of the world is still unknown. Hexi is rich and fertile, and the Yellow River is very strong. Zhangye's vassal state has thousands of elite soldiers and cavalry. In the event of an emergency, it will be enough to defend itself by eliminating the crossing of the Yellow River. This is a good place for us to leave to our descendants. The brothers all agreed. Dou Rong asked to see Zhao Meng that day, resigned as Julu governor, and asked to go to Hexi. Zhao Meng told Gengshi, and he became the captain of Zhangye's vassal state. Dou Rong was so happy that he took his family to the northwest.
target: Dou Rong, courtesy name Duke of Zhou, was from Pingling County, Fufeng. His seventh-generation ancestor Dou Guangguo was the younger brother of Queen Xiaowen. Orphaned young, he served as Sima under Wang Jun during Wang Mang's reign, earning the title Jianwu Nan for military merit. He was known for chivalry and filial piety, caring for his mother, elder brother, and younger sibling. During the chaos at the end of Wang Mang's rule, Dou Rong initially served under Wang Yi but later surrendered to Gengshi's general Zhao Meng. Seeking stability, he requested and received the position of Captain of Zhangye's Vassal State, moving his family to Hexi.

source: The brothers all agreed. Dou Rong asked to see Zhao Meng that day, resigned as Julu governor, and asked to go to Hexi. Zhao Meng told Gengshi, and he became the captain of Zhangye's vassal state. Dou Rong was so happy that he took his family to the northwest. When he arrived in Zhangye, he made friends with local heroes and lived in harmony with the ethnic minorities. He was very popular with the people from all over the world, and Hexi quickly surrendered to him. At this time, Liang Tong, the prefect of Jiuquan, Shejun, the prefect of Jincheng, Shi Bao, the captain of Zhangye, Zhu Zeng, the captain of Jiuquan, Xin Xu, the captain of Dunhuang, and all the heroes of the prefectures and counties, Dou Rong treated them kindly. When Gengshi failed, Dou Rong and Liang Tong discussed the situation and said: "Today there is chaos in the world, I don't know what the outcome will be." Hexi is in a dangerous position between Qiang and Hu. Without concerted efforts, we cannot defend ourselves. The power is generally great, and there is no leader. One person should be elected as a general to ensure the security of the five counties and observe changes in the current situation. After deliberation, it was decided that Dou Rong should be the general of the five counties in Hexi.
target: There, he befriended local heroes, harmonized with ethnic minorities, and gained widespread support. After Gengshi's fall, Dou Rong was elected General of the Five Counties in Hexi, overseeing a peaceful and prosperous region with tolerant governance and strong defenses against Qiang and Hu invasions.

source: He repaired his troops and horses, practiced archery, and sounded the beacon fire alarm at the border. When Qiang and barbarians invaded the border fortress, Dou Rong often led his troops to rescue the troops together with the counties. He always arrived as scheduled and often defeated the invaders. Later, the Huns also learned their lesson and rarely invaded again. The Qiang and Hu who were attached to the fortress were frightened by their relatives, and the homeless people who suffered from starvation in Anding, Beidi, Shangjun and other places came back in an endless stream. When Dou Rong and others heard that Guangwu had ascended the throne, they wanted to go east to Luoyang, because the river and the west were far apart and could not be reached by themselves. At this time, Wei Xiao first took the title of Jianwu, Dou Rong and others accepted Zhengshuo, and Wei Xiao all pretended to be his general's seal and ribbon. Kuai Xiao looked obedient to others but harbored dissatisfaction inside. He sent the debater Yong Lian to lobby Hexi and said: Gengshi became emperor and soon fell into ruin. This is the result of a surname that cannot be revived. Now if you identify a master and establish a relationship of dependence with him, once you are controlled by him, the power in your hands will be lost. If you encounter danger in the future, you will regret it. Now the heroes are competing, and the outcome is undecided. They should each occupy their territory and join forces with Long and Shu. If you are high, you can become the king of a country like the Six Kingdoms, and if you are low, you can be a captain of the South China Sea like Zhao Tuo. Dou Rong summoned the heroes and prefects to discuss the matter together. The brave and wise among them all said: The Han Dynasty inherited the lineage of Yao and cultivated it for a long time. Now the emperor's surname is found in the Hetu Chifu Fu Book. Since the ancient Taoist scholars Gu Ziyun and Xia Heliang have revealed that the Han Dynasty will receive the talisman again, it has been said a long time ago, so Liu Zijun changed his name to Liu Xiu in the hope that the talisman will be fulfilled. In Wang Mang's last years, the Taoist priest Ximen Junhui said that Liu Xiu should be the emperor, so he prepared to establish Liu Zijun. After the incident was discovered, Liu Zijun was killed. The people watching said: Liu Xiu is really your master. This was exposed not long ago and is common to all wise people. Let’s not talk about destiny, but let’s comment on human affairs: there are countless people who are now emperors, and Luoyang has the largest land, the strongest armored soldiers, and the clearest orders. Observing fortune and personnel, he is probably incompetent for the position of emperor. The prefects of various counties each had guests, some of whom were in favor and some who were against it. Dou Rong made a detailed comparative analysis and decided to go eastward.
target: When Guangwu ascended the throne, Dou Rong considered allegiance but was courted by Wei Xiao, who urged independence. After consulting with local leaders, Dou Rong decided to support Guangwu, citing prophecies and the strength of Luoyang. He sent an envoy with gifts, and Guangwu responded by appointing him General of the Five Counties and later Liangzhou Mu. Dou Rong rebuffed Wei Xiao's attempts at alliance, writing letters to persuade him to submit, but Wei Xiao refused. Dou Rong then prepared for military action against Wei Xiao. Dou Rong joined Guangwu's campaign against Wei Xiao, leading troops from five counties. After Wei Xiao's defeat, Dou Rong was enfeoffed as Marquis of Anfeng. Despite his high rank, he remained humble and repeatedly sought to resign, but Guangwu refused. His family became powerful, with multiple marriages to royalty, but later fell from grace due to misconduct.

source: When he was more than a year old, he received Dou Rong's seal and ribbon from the imperial guard, and was given cattle and bottles of wine. Dou Rong had been in Suwei for more than ten years. He was getting old, and his descendants were indulgent and lawless. Dou Mu and others interacted with some frivolous people, and they were entrusted to the county to interfere with political affairs. Because he was enfeoffed in Anfeng and wanted all his in-laws to occupy the original Liu'an kingdom, he asked the Queen Mother of Yin to order Liu Xu, the Marquis of Liu'an, to divorce his wife and marry his daughter to Liu Xu. In the fifth year, Liu Xu was abandoned and his wife's family wrote a letter to report the situation. The emperor was furious and dismissed Dou Mu and others from their official positions. All the ministers in Dou took their families back to their hometowns in the countryside. Only Dou Rong stayed in the capital. Dou Mu and others went west to Hangu Pass, and there was an imperial edict to recover them all. When Dou Rong died at the age of seventy-eight, he was given the posthumous title of Marquis of Dai. He sent a lot of money to help with the funeral.
target: Dou Rong died at seventy-eight, posthumously honored as Marquis of Dai. His descendants continued, though some faced imprisonment and loss of titles.

source: When Dou Rong died at the age of seventy-eight, he was given the posthumous title of Marquis of Dai. He sent a lot of money to help with the funeral. The emperor thought that Dou Mu could not cultivate himself and had a lot of wealth, so he often ordered Ye to guard his family alone. The audience reported that Dou Mu and his son had complained several times since they lost power, and the emperor ordered him to take his family back to the original county. Only Dou Xun, the son-in-law of Princess Biyang, was able to stay in the capital. Dou Mu was arrested and brought to justice by the county for bribing minor officials. Both Dou Mu and his son Dou Xuan died in Pingling Prison, and Dou Xun also died in Luoyang Prison. A long time later, the imperial edict was issued to bring back Mrs. Dou Jia and a young grandson to their residence in Luoyang. In the fourteenth year, Dou Rong, Dou Xun's younger brother, was granted the title of Marquis of Anfeng, with a settlement of 2,000 households, and was succeeded by Dou Rong's descendants. At the beginning of Emperor He's reign, he was the Shaofu. When Dou Xunzi, General Dou Xian was killed, he was spared from the country. Dou Jia died and was succeeded by his son Dou Wanquan. After Wanquan died, his son Huizong succeeded him. Dou Wu, a disciple of Dou Wanquan, has a unique legend. The historian commented: Dou Rong began to be known as a heroic hero, standing tall in the dust, and then emerged from the prince's position during the break, and finally won the title of minister. This is really a man who has a tendency to achieve merit. When his title is high and perfect, he can put aside his power and favors, fearing as if he has no choice. How smart is this! I once savored this man's demeanor in detail. Although his talents in the latitude and longitude of the country are not enough to talk about, the etiquette of advancing and retreating is worth talking about.
target: The historian comments that Dou Rong rose from obscurity to high office through merit, wisely yielding power when at his peak. While not a great strategist, his conduct in advancing and retreating was exemplary.

source: Liu Qing, the Xiaowang of Qinghe, whose mother was a noblewoman of the Song Dynasty. Guiren, the eighth grandson of Song Chang, was born in Pingling County, Fufeng County. His father, Song Yang, was praised by the village for his respectfulness and filial piety, and he should not be drafted by the state or county. Song Yang's aunt is the maternal grandmother of Empress Ma of Mingde. After Ma heard that Song Yang's two daughters were both talented and beautiful, she took them to teach them a lesson. At the end of Yongping, both daughters were selected into the prince's palace, and the prince liked them very much. When Suzong came to the throne, they were all nobles. In the third year of the founding of the People's Republic of China, the great nobleman Liu Qing was born. In the second year, he was established as the crown prince, and Song Yang was recruited as Yilang. He was highly praised and rewarded. The empress dowager liked her because she was a good person, dedicated to Changle Palace, and did the cooking work herself. After the death of the Empress Dowager, Empress Dou was favored by Su Zong. Because both noble sisters were favored by the emperor, and Liu Qing was the prince, he was jealous of them and conspired with her mother Biyang Zhu to frame the Song family. Outside, let her brothers collect her faults, even small ones; inside, let her attendants spy on her gains and losses. Later, I intercepted a letter from the nobleman at Yeting Gate, saying: I want some raw dodder when I am sick, and I want my family to look for it. Therefore, he slandered her and said that she wanted to do magic tricks to pray for ghosts and gods to bring disaster on Queen Dou. She used dodder as a means of victory. She was slandered and framed day and night. The noble mother and son gradually became alienated from the emperor. Liu Qing came to live in Chenglu Temple. A few months later, Queen Dou hinted that Ye Ting had ordered a noble man to survive and framed the noble man. Please test it and implement it. In the seventh year, the emperor deposed the crown prince Liu Qing and established the crown prince Liu Zhao. Liu Zhao is the son of Liang Guiren. So he issued an edict saying: The Crown Prince has a confusing and unpredictable nature, which started when he was a child and has become more obvious now. I'm afraid he inherited his mother's vicious style and cannot worship in the ancestral temple or be the master of the world. Killing relatives for the sake of justice, let alone surrendering? Now Prince Liu Qing is deposed as King Qinghe. Crown Prince Liu Zhao was raised by the Queen and was educated by his mother when he was a child, which induced him to have a good character and he was expected to become a great person. Most concubines have a loving mother as their mother and have a lifetime of kindness. How can it be compared with the righteousness of a direct descendant?
target: The lives and fates of Emperor Zhang's eight sons, focusing on the lineages of several kings. Liu Qing, King Xiao of Qinghe, was born to Noble Consort Song. His mother and aunt were favored by Emperor Zhang but were framed by Empress Dou after the death of Empress Dowager Ma, leading to their forced suicide. Liu Qing was deposed as crown prince in favor of his half-brother Liu Zhao (Emperor He). Despite this, Liu Qing maintained a close and respectful relationship with Emperor He, who treated him with great favor and trust. Liu Qing was known for his filial piety, caution, and grief over his mother's unjust death, often making private sacrifices.

source: Liu Qing began to hear that Er'e was beautiful, so he rewarded his nanny to get Er'e for him. Later, I was very happy, and other concubines could not compare with me. After the two sisters died, they were buried in the capital. Liu Qing was king for twenty-five years before he went to seal the country. In the same year, he fell seriously ill and said to Song Yan and others: "The Qinghe River is low and wet and the soil is thin. I would like to request that I be buried next to the nobles' tomb after my death." The court has shown great favor, and a shrine should be built so that the concubine, mother and son can eat together, so that the soul can be sheltered, and there will be no regrets after death. So he wrote to the Queen Mother and said: My land is low and humid, and I want to ask the nobles to follow Fan Zhuo after I die. Even if I die, I will not be immortal! Now while your mouth can still speak and your eyes can still see, be brave enough to ask. Every breath of life, I hope to be pitied. He died at the age of twenty-nine. The imperial court sent Sikong Chijie and Zongzheng to attend the condolence ceremony, and also sent Changle Yezhe Pushe and Zhongyezhe to help take care of the funeral. They also gave dragons Jiuqi and tigers to support hundreds of people, and the etiquette was the same as that of King Lehaigong. The Queen Mother sent Ye Tingcheng to send Zuo Ji to mourn, and she was buried with the king in Guangqiu. Zimin King Huwei succeeded to the throne. In the first year of Yongchu, the Empress Dowager granted Song Yan the title of Marquis of Shengxiang, divided Qinghe into two kingdoms, and granted Liu Qing's youngest son Chang Bao the title of King of Guangchuan. Song Jun was worried about the safety of the army and refused to return, so he discussed with the generals: Now that the soldiers who are far away are ill and unable to fight, how about using expedient measures to accept the surrender? All the generals fell on the ground and did not dare to agree. Song Jun said: When loyal ministers leave the country, they can find ways to stabilize the country and make decisions by themselves. So under the false imperial edict, Ma Yuan's subordinate Sima Lv Zhong was sent to guard Yuanling, and Lv Zhong was ordered to enter the enemy camp with the imperial edict and express the favor of the court, so he ordered his troops to follow behind. The barbarians were afraid, so they all killed their commanders and surrendered. Then they entered the bandit camp, dispersed their people, sent them back to their headquarters, and appointed senior officials for them before returning. Song Jun had not yet arrived at the court and had committed the crime of imposition himself. Emperor Guangwu commended him for his meritorious service, welcomed him and gave him gold and silk, and ordered his family members to visit his grave. In the future, whenever there were objections from all directions, he visited him many times. Song Jun was promoted to Shangcai Ling.
target: Song Jun, courtesy name Shuxiang, from Nanyang, became a doctor at fifteen via his father's appointment. Proficient in classics, he served as Chen Yang's assistant, establishing schools and banning improper sacrifices. He led 3,000 troops to rescue General Liu Shang but arrived after his death. With General Ma Yuan, he faced disease and blockades, so he forged an imperial edict to accept barbarian surrender, dispersing their forces. Emperor Guangwu pardoned his unauthorized action, rewarding him. As Shangcai magistrate, he refused to enforce strict funeral bans, prioritizing justice. As Jiujiang governor, he attributed tiger attacks to corrupt officials, removing traps and promoting virtue, causing tigers to leave. He ended a marriage sacrifice custom in Junqiu County. Promoted to prime minister of East China Sea, he was later dismissed but recalled due to public demand. As minister, he defended his principles against imperial anger, earning praise for his integrity. As Hanoi governor, he was beloved by the people. He retired due to illness, receiving honors. He advocated lenient governance, blaming harsh laws for social ills, and died in 76 CE.

He also wrote to Deng Zhongkuang to persuade him, but most of his articles were not recorded, so Deng Zhongkuang and Liu Gong surrendered. Liu Gong, courtesy name Meng Gong, was from Chang'an. He was good at argumentation. Fufeng, Ma Yuan and Ban Biao both thought highly of him. Su Jing did not take credit for his work, but devoted himself to Taoism. He wrote "Records of Teachings" and other articles that have been passed down to the world. He died at home when he was seventy years old.
target: While in Nanyang, Su Jing wrote to Liu Gong, Liu Xin’s nephew, who served as an adviser to the bandit Deng Zhongkuang. He urged Liu Gong to abandon rebellion, citing historical examples like Zhiguo and Chen Ping, who wisely avoided harm. He argued that the Han dynasty, despite Wang Mang’s usurpation, was revived by Guangwu, and that celestial signs—such as irregular movements of Taibai and Yinghuo—foretold doom for rebels like Dong Xian and Peng Chong. He warned against following false prophecies and urged surrender, comparing Liu Gong’s potential choice to the virtuous actions of Duke Zhou’s uncle Kang and King Jibei Liu Zhi. Su Jing also wrote to Deng Zhongkuang, who eventually surrendered with Liu Gong. Su Jing died at home at age seventy, leaving writings like *Records of Teachings*.

He died at home when he was seventy years old. ◆Biography of Yang Hou Yang Hou was named Zhonghuan and was a native of Xindu, Guanghan County. Grandfather Yang Chunqing was good at prophecy and was a general under Gongsun Shu. When the Han soldiers defeated Shu, Yang Chunqing committed suicide. Before his death, he told his son Yang Tong: "In my collection, there are secret records passed down by my ancestors for the use of the Han family. You should study them carefully." Yang Tong was grateful for his father's last words. After three years of mourning, Cijia followed Jianwei Zhouxun to learn the methods of his ancestors. He also learned the "He Luo Shu" and the astronomical push technique from Zheng Boshan, a native of the same county. When Jian Chuzhong was appointed as the magistrate of Pengcheng County, a severe drought hit the state. Yang Tong implemented the technique of yin and yang to eliminate depression, and the county boundaries were covered with rain. The prefect Zong Zhan asked Yang Tong to pray for rain for the county, and the rain also fell. From then on, whenever there was a disaster or disaster in the imperial court, he would often visit him for help. Yang Tong wrote two volumes of "Family Law Chapter Name" and "Nei Prophecy" to explain it. He reached the rank of Guanglu Dafu and was the third elder of the country. He died at the age of ninety. Yang Tong gave birth to a son, Yang Hou. Yang Hou's mother and her ex-wife's son, Yang Bo, were not on good terms. Yang Hou was nine years old. She wanted them to reconcile, so she used the excuse of being sick to not talk or eat. When the mother knew his intentions, she changed her original attitude and became more kind to her ex-wife and son. Yang Bo later became a doctor in Guanglu. Yang Hou studied Yang Tong's studies since he was a child, and he thought energetically. At the beginning of the year, in the third year of Emperor An's reign, Taibai entered Beidou and Luoyang was flooded. At that time, Yang Tong was the servant, and Yang Hou followed him in the capital. The imperial court asked Tong about this, and Yang Tong excused himself by saying that he was old and hard of hearing, and his son Yang Hou was well versed in books, so he knew what he meant. Empress Dowager Deng sent Zhong Changshi to ask Yang Hou about her wishes. Yang Hou replied: Many of the princes are in the capital. Changes may occur. They should be sent back to their home countries as soon as possible. The Queen Mother obeyed, and Taibai Star disappeared soon.
target: Yang Hou, courtesy name Zhonghuan, was from Guanghan. His grandfather Yang Chunqing, skilled in prophecy, served Gongsun Shu but committed suicide after Han’s victory, instructing his son Yang Tong to study secret records. Yang Tong learned prophecy and astronomy, served as a magistrate, and prayed for rain during droughts. He wrote two volumes on prophecy and died at ninety. Yang Hou, his son, studied these arts. In Emperor An’s third year, when Taibai entered Beidou and Luoyang flooded, Yang Hou advised sending princes back to their states; the queen mother complied, and the omens ceased.

source: Dong Zhuo, courtesy name Zhongying, was from Lintao, Longxi. He has a rough and scheming temperament. When he was young, he traveled among the Qiang and tried his best to make friends with the leaders. Later, when he returned home to farm, some of the leaders came to join him. Dong Zhuo slaughtered cattle for them and had banquets with them. The leaders thanked him for his kindness and collected the remaining heads of various livestock as gifts to him after returning. From then on, he became famous for his bravery and chivalry. The soldiers and horses who were appointed as state guards once patrolled and guarded under the fortress. Dong Zhuo has extraordinary physical strength. He wears two bow boxes and shoots them left and right. The Qiang and Hu people are afraid of him. In the last years of Emperor Huan's reign, as a son of a good family in six counties, he was appointed Yulin Lang, and followed Zhang Huan, the general of Zhonglang, as a military commander. Together they went to attack the rebellious Qiang people in Hanyang. After defeating them, he was named Langzhong and was rewarded with nine thousand bundles of silk. Dong Zhuo said: I am the one who records the merits, and the soldiers are the ones who make the merits. So they were all distributed to the soldiers, leaving nothing behind. He was gradually promoted to the rank of captain of Wuji School in the Western Regions, but was dismissed for some reasons. Later he became the governor of Bingzhou and the governor of Hedong. In the first year of Zhongping, he was appointed as Shu Zhonglang General. With integrity, he went to Xiaquyang to attack Zhangjiao on behalf of Lu Zhi. He was defeated and punished. That winter, the Ling Qiang and Paohan Heguan bandits in the north rebelled, so they jointly supported Beigong Boyu and Li Wenhou, the Hu people who had surrendered to Huangzhong, as generals, and killed the Qiang captain Ling Zheng. Boyu and others kidnapped Bian Zhang and Han Sui, who came to Jincheng, and made them specialize in military administration. Together they killed Jincheng prefect Chen Yi, attacked and burned the prefectures and counties. In the spring of the next year, he led tens of thousands of cavalry to invade the Third Auxiliary and approached the royal cemetery, under the pretext of killing the eunuchs. The imperial court issued an edict appointing Dong Zhuo as Zhonglang General and serving as the deputy of Zuo Chaoqi General Huangfu Song to conquer them. Huangfu Song was dismissed and recalled due to ineffectiveness, while Bian Zhang, Han Sui and others became more powerful. The imperial court also appointed Sikong Zhang Wen as the general of chariots and cavalry. During the holiday, Yuan Pang, the commander of Jinwu, was appointed as his deputy.
target: Dong Zhuo, a man of rough and scheming temperament from Lintao, Longxi, rose to prominence through his interactions with Qiang leaders, distributing rewards to soldiers and gaining a reputation for bravery. He served as a military commander under Zhang Huan, defeating rebellious Qiang forces, and was later appointed to various posts, including Governor of Bingzhou and Hedong. During the Zhongping era, he was tasked with suppressing rebellions, including those led by Bian Zhang and Han Sui, but faced defeats. Despite setbacks, he managed to preserve his army and was granted the title of Marquis of Lianxiang.

source: The soldiers have been close to each other for a long time. They cherish my kindness in raising them and are willing to do their best for me. Please take them with you to serve on the frontier. So he stationed troops in Hedong to observe changes in the situation. When Emperor Ling died, General He Jin and Sili Colonel Yuan Shao planned to kill the eunuchs, but the Queen Mother did not agree, so they privately summoned Dong Zhuo to lead troops into the court to intimidate the Queen Mother. After Dong Zhuo was summoned, he set out on the road that day. He also wrote a letter saying: Zhang Rang, the minister of the Central Committee, and others stole the favor and caused chaos in the world. I have heard that raising the soup to stop it from boiling is not as good as drawing fuel from the bottom of the cauldron; although it hurts to break a malignant sore, it is worse than having it invade the inside. In the past, I went to martingale to raise troops in Jinyang to drive away the evildoers around the monarch. Now I am going to Luoyang with drums to arrest Zhang Rang and others in order to eliminate the evil and filth. He Jin was defeated and died before Dong Zhuo arrived. Huben Zhonglang general Yuan Shu burned down the Nangong Palace to attack the eunuchs. Duan Gui, the general servant, and others kidnapped the young emperor and King Chenliu and fled to Xiaopingjin at night. Dong Zhuo saw the fire from a distance and led his troops forward quickly. He arrived at the west of the city before dawn. He heard that the young emperor was in Beimang, so he went to greet him. When the young emperor saw Dong Zhuo coming with his troops and horses, he was frightened and cried. Dong Zhuo talked to him, but he couldn't answer; he talked to King Chenliu and found out the cause of the trouble. Dong Zhuo believed that King Chenliu was wise and was born to the Empress Dowager Dong. Dong Zhuo believed that he was of the same clan as the Empress Dowager and had plans to dethrone the emperor. When Dong Zhuo entered Beijing, he had only three infantry and cavalrymen. He felt that he had few troops and was afraid that he would not be subdued by people near and far. For about four or five days, he secretly separated his troops from the city at night and camped nearby. After dawn, he returned to the city with great fanfare, making people think that the army from the west had arrived again, and no one in Luoyang knew it. Soon the troops previously led by He Jin and his brother He Miao all surrendered to Dong Zhuo. Dong Zhuo asked Lu Bu to kill Zhijin Wu Dingyuan and annex his tribe. Dong Zhuo's army greatly increased.
target: After Emperor Ling's death, Dong Zhuo was summoned to the capital by He Jin and Yuan Shao to intimidate the Empress Dowager. He entered Luoyang with a small force but cleverly expanded his army by integrating defectors, including troops from He Jin and He Miao. He deposed the young emperor, established Emperor Xian, and assumed the role of Prime Minister, wielding immense power.

source: Everyone present was shocked. Said: During the period of mourning for the late emperor, the emperor did not have the mentality of a son, and did not behave like a monarch. Now he is deposed as King Hongnong. So he established King Chenliu and created Emperor Xian. He also pointed out that the Queen Mother persecuted the Queen Mother Yongle, causing her to die of depression. She violated the etiquette of mother-in-law and daughter-in-law, and had no filial qualities. She moved her to Yong'an Palace, where she was subsequently murdered and died.
target: His rule was marked by brutality, including the massacre of civilians, looting, and the destruction of the economy through coinage reforms. He also moved the capital to Chang'an, forcing millions to relocate, causing widespread death and destruction.

source: Xun Shuang, a scholar without an official position, was appointed as Sikong. Chen Ji, Han Rong and others who were implicated by the party all became ministers. At first, Dong Zhuo took Niu Fu as his son-in-law, and he was always very close to him, so he sent him to lead troops to station in Shaanxi. Niu Fu assigned his lieutenants Li Cui, Guo Si, and Zhang Ji to lead tens of thousands of infantry and cavalry to defeat Henan Yin Zhujun in Zhongmou. Lü Bu sent Li Su to Shaanxi with Shao Ming of the imperial court to attack Niu Fu and others. Niu Fu and others fought with Li Su. Li Su was defeated and fled to Hongnong. Lü Bu killed him. Later, there was an unexplained panic in Niu Fu's camp. Niu Fu was afraid, so he took the gold, silver and jewelry and escaped over the city wall. His followers, greedy for his property, beheaded Niu Fu and sent his head to Chang'an. Li Cui, Guo Si and others hated the people of Bingzhou because Wang Yun and Lu Bu had killed Dong Zhuo, so they killed hundreds of men and women in Bingzhou in their army. After Niu Fu died, everyone was at a loss and planned to disperse.
target: He was eventually assassinated in a plot by Wang Yun and Lü Bu in 192 AD. His death was followed by chaos, as his former subordinates Li Jue and Guo Si seized control of Chang'an, leading to further violence and famine. The capital was devastated, with widespread cannibalism and depopulation.

source: Wang Yun had no choice but to come down and was killed a few days later. Li Ji and others buried Dong Zhuo in the county, collected the ashes of Dong's cremated body, and wrapped them in a coffin for burial. On the day of the burial, there was heavy wind and rain. Lightning struck Dong Zhuo's tomb. The rainwater flowed into the tomb and floated the coffin. Kuizhi was promoted to the general of chariots and cavalry, opened the government office, and became the commander of the Sili school. The imperial guard became the rear general, the third marriage was the right general, the retired general was the Zhendong general, and they were all granted the title of marquis. Kuizhi, Shudan, and Huizhou jointly took charge of the government. Zhang Wei left the capital and stationed himself at Di. He appointed Mai Chi as Zuofeng Yiyin and granted him the title of Marquis.
target: The aftermath saw continued infighting among Dong Zhuo's former allies and the rise of Cao Cao, who eventually took control of the imperial court. The text concludes with a critical assessment of Dong Zhuo as a ruthless and destructive figure whose actions plunged the empire into turmoil, leading to the collapse of central authority and widespread suffering.

source: ◆The biography of Yu Xu, whose courtesy name was Shengqing, was from Wuping in the state of Chen. My grandfather, Yu Jing, was a county prison officer. He handled cases impartially, was generous, and respected himself and others. Every winter month, the case is reported, and I often shed tears over it. He once said: In the East China Sea, a gate was built at the Duke's height, and the horses and chariots were made high, thinking that some of their descendants would become high officials. And his son Dingguo finally became prime minister. I have been in prison for sixty years. Although I am not as good as Yu Gong, maybe it is about the same. My descendants may not become Jiuqing. Therefore, Yu Xu was given the title "Qing". Yu Xu was twelve years old and could read Shangshu. Is an orphan. Take care of your grandmother. The county elected him as his grandson, and the prime minister admired him very much and wanted him to be an official. Yu Xu declined and said: "Grandma is ninety years old. Without me, there is no one to take care of her." The Prime Minister didn't ask him to go. After his grandmother passed away and the period of mourning expired, he was recruited into Taiwei Li's Mansion and was awarded the title of doctor.
target: Yu Xu, from Wuping in Chen, was known for his integrity. His grandfather, a prison officer, handled cases with compassion. Yu Xu was orphaned young and cared for his grandmother, refusing an official post until after her death. He later served as a doctor.

source: Abandoning Liangzhou is not a strategy. Li said: I didn't expect that. It’s not like you said that it almost failed in national affairs. So, what’s a good strategy? Yu Xu said: There is a commotion in Liangzhou today, and people are uneasy. I am worried that something unexpected will happen. The nine ministers of the four prefectures should be ordered to recommend several people from their respective states, and all the eldest sons of the Mu Shou Ling should be given official positions. On the surface, it is to reward their merits, but in fact, it is to monitor them and prevent them from causing trouble. Li thought he was right, and even extended the four prefectures to follow Yu Xu's plan. So he recruited the heroes of the two states as vassals, and appointed the sons of the shepherds and guardians as ministers to comfort them. The Deng Zhi brothers were dissatisfied because Yu Xu opposed Deng Zhi's opinions. He wanted to use the official law to frame Yu Xu.
target: When General Deng Zhi proposed abandoning Liangzhou due to Qiang rebellions, Yu Xu argued against it, stating it would expose the imperial tombs and that Liangzhou's people were a vital defense. He suggested controlling local leaders by giving their sons official posts to prevent rebellion.

source: Now, the thieves are in full swing and it is difficult to compete. Soldiers never tire of deceit. I hope you can give me more soldiers and horses so that I won't be in trouble. She was summoned to the Jiade Palace and received many rewards. Qiang then led thousands of people to stop Yu Xu between Chencang and Xiaogu. Yu Xu immediately stopped his troops and refused to advance. He threatened to send a letter to invite troops and wait for reinforcements to arrive before advancing. The Qiang knew about it and divided their troops to rob other counties. Because the Qiang soldiers were scattered, Yu Xu marched day and night, doubling his advance for more than a hundred miles.
target: Deng Zhi, resentful of Yu Xu's opposition, sent him to govern Chaoge, a bandit-ridden area. Yu Xu used deception, recruiting former bandits to ambush others and marking thieves' clothes with silk threads, leading to their dispersal. Promoted to Wudu's prefect, he again used deception against the Qiang, increasing his campfires to feign strength and marching rapidly. He then used a strategy of weak arrows to lure the Qiang into range of his strong crossbows, defeating them.

When they arrived at the county, there were less than 3,000 soldiers and more than 10,000 Qiang soldiers. They besieged Chiting for dozens of days. source: In the memorial, Zhang Fang complained in tears before the emperor, and Yu Xu was convicted and sent to Zuo School to do hard labor. Zhang Fang insisted on killing him. source: Stupid people are not enough to be punished. The emperor took Yu Xu's advice and gave him a spanking. Therefore, Yu Xu said to all the ministers: "A villain has a grudge. What kinship do you have with those corrupt officials, and what hatred do you have against the haters? I was so ashamed after hearing this. Yu Xu said again: "Shang Shulang is an important position, the ladder of officialdom. Now some people have seven or eight people in a county, and some have no people in a state.
