He was reprimanded nine times and punished three times, but his upright character remained unyielding until old age. At the beginning of Yongyuan Dynasty, he was promoted to Shangshu Ling and dismissed due to official business. The imperial court missed his loyalty and recruited him again, but he happened to die. On his deathbed, he said to Zi Yugong: I serve the court with integrity and selflessness, and I have no regrets in everything I do. What I regret is that as a Chao Ge, I killed hundreds of thieves for a long time. How could I not be unjust? Since then, there has not been a single person in the family for more than 20 years. This is because I have been punished by God!
target: He remained upright despite nine reprimands and three punishments, dying as Shangshu Ling. On his deathbed, he regretted killing many bandits at Chaoge, believing it brought divine punishment.

id: 后汉书/列传/虞傅盖臧列传::group-007
article_path: 后汉书/列传/虞傅盖臧列传
source: Yu Gong was a talented person, and his official position was supreme as the Party Governor. ◆The biography of Fu Xie, whose courtesy name is Nanrong, was from Lingzhou County, Beidi County. This character started at a young age, and I admired Nan Rong when he read the Book of Songs: Bai Wanggui's defilement can still be polished off, but what he said cannot be done. As for the three repetitions, I asked myself to be cautious in my words and deeds, so I changed "Youqi" to Nanrong. He is eight feet long and has a burly appearance. When he was young, he learned from Taiwei Liu Kuan and was promoted as filial and honest twice. Hearing that the commander-in-chief who promoted him as Xiaolian died, he abandoned his official post to mourn. Later, he was appointed as Sima of the Guard Army, and together with Zuo Zhonglang's general Huangfu Song, he attacked Zhang Jiao. Fu Xie was usually the most evil eunuch. Before leaving, he said to Shangshu: I heard that the disasters of the country are not external, but all happen internally. Therefore, when Yu Shun succeeded to the throne, he first eliminated the four evil spirits, and then appointed the sixteen prime ministers to show that if the evil people did not go away, the good people would have no way to come in. Now Zhang Jiao started from Zhao and Wei, and the Yellow Turbans caused chaos in the six states. They all happened in the interior, and then the chaos spread all over the world. I was ordered to lead the troops to attack them. When I first arrived in Yingchuan, I was invincible. Although the Yellow Turbans were powerful, they were not a cause for concern for the imperial court. What worries me is that water management does not start from the source, causing the downstream flow to become wider and wider. The emperor is benevolent and tolerant, but he is merciless in punishing bad people. Therefore, the eunuchs exercise great power, and loyal ministers cannot have any influence. Zhang Jiao was truly eliminated and the Yellow Turbans surrendered, which made me even more worried. Why? Because evil people and upright people cannot be together, just as ice cubes and charcoal cannot be placed together in the same container. All these illustrate the seriousness of rumors and rumors. If we don't examine the truth of the matter in detail, the incident of loyal ministers committing suicide like Bai Qi can also be seen today. The emperor should think about Yu Shun's resolute treatment of the four villains, and quickly punish those bad guys who framed the traitors. In this way, the good people will come to the emperor's side, and the traitors will be eliminated. I have heard that loyal ministers serve their monarch as filial sons serve their parents. How can a son not serve his father wholeheartedly? If I am executed by Yu Fuyue for this, it will be a blessing to the country if the emperor can accept a few words from me! The eunuch Zhao Zhong was extremely angry after reading the book. When Zhang Jiao was defeated, Fu Xie deserved to be knighted because of his many merits. Zhao Zhong framed him. Emperor Ling still remembered Fu Xie's words, so he was able to avoid the crime and finally appointed him as the captain of Anding. Dismissed due to illness. Later he was awarded the title of Yilang. When the Xiqiang rebelled, Bian Zhang and Han Sui made trouble in Longyou, asking for money and people from the people endlessly. Situ Cui Lie believed that Liangzhou should be abandoned. The imperial edict met with hundreds of officials to discuss, but Cui Lie insisted on his opinion.
target: Fu Xie, from Lingzhou, was known for his caution in speech and action. He served as Sima under Huangfu Song against Zhang Jiao's Yellow Turbans. Before the campaign, he warned the emperor that the real threat was internal, from eunuchs like Zhao Zhong, and that evil and good cannot coexist. Despite his merits, Zhao Zhong framed him, but the emperor spared him. Later, when Situ Cui Lie proposed abandoning Liangzhou during a Xiqiang rebellion, Fu Xie vehemently opposed him, arguing that Liangzhou was the empire's shield and that abandoning it would empower the barbarians. The emperor agreed. Fu Xie refused to curry favor with the powerful eunuch Zhao Zhong, even when offered a marquisate. As Hanyang's governor, he pacified the Qiang. He warned Governor Geng Bi against attacking Han Sui with untrained troops, predicting disaster.

id: 后汉书/列传/虞傅盖臧列传::group-008
article_path: 后汉书/列传/虞傅盖臧列传
source: When the thieves learn that our army is lax, they must think that our army is cowardly, and they will surely fall apart due to their internal struggle for power. Then lead the trained troops to defeat the disintegrating thieves, and then sit back and wait for victory to come. Now if you don't seek to be foolproof and take a path that is bound to fail, I won't do it for you. Geng Bi refused to listen. When the troops arrived at Didao, there were indeed rebels. They killed Cheng Qiu first and then Geng Bi. The thieves then surrounded Hanyang. There were few soldiers in the city and no food, but Fu Xie still held on. At this time, thousands of Hu cavalry from the north followed the bandits to attack Hanyang County. They all cherished Fu Xie's kindness for a long time. They kowtowed outside the city and asked to send Fu Xie back to his hometown. His son Fu Gan was only thirteen years old and lived in an official residence from his father. Knowing that his father had an upright temperament and awe-inspiring righteousness, I was afraid that he would not bend his will and avoid death. He advised his father: "The country is in chaos, which makes it difficult for you to be in the court." Now that the world has rebelled, your troops are not strong enough to defend themselves. The Qiang and Hu people in the countryside have received your kindness in the past. They want you to abandon the county and return to your hometown. I hope you will agree to them.
target: Geng Bi ignored him and was killed. When Hanyang was besieged, Fu Xie refused to abandon the city despite his son's pleas and the offer of safe passage from grateful Hu cavalry.

id: 后汉书/列传/虞傅盖臧列传::group-009
article_path: 后汉书/列传/虞傅盖臧列传
source: Now the imperial court is no worse than Shang Zhou, how can I surpass Boyi in virtue? Chaos in the world cannot nourish Haoran's righteousness. I usually receive a salary from the state, but when there is a war, I want to run away again! Where can I go? Must die here. You have talent, give it a try! Encourage it! Chief Registrar Yang Hui is my Cheng Ying, you can trust him. Fu Gan choked up and could no longer speak, and everyone around him was in tears. Huang Yan, the governor of Jiuquan, the first envoy of the kingdom, advised Fu Xie: "The situation of success or failure is already clear as the palm of my hand." The first to raise an army was to achieve the great deeds of an overlord, and to the bottom was the meritorious deeds of Yi Yin and Lu Shang. The world is no longer the world of the Han Dynasty. Does Mr. Fu mean to be our teacher? Fu Xie pressed his sword and cursed Huang Yan: "You were once a minister holding the emperor's talisman, but you spoke for a thief?" He commanded the troops to march from left to right and died in battle. His posthumous title is Zhuangjiehou. Fu Qian was well-known and had reached the rank of Governor of Fufeng. ◆In the biography of Gai Xun, Gai Xun was named Yuan Gu and was a native of Guangzhi County, Dunhuang County. From generation to generation, the family is worth two thousand stones. He was initially elected as Xiaolian and appointed as the chief historian of Hanyang. At this time, the prefect of Wuwei relied on powerful officials, was corrupt, violent, and had no scruples, and was engaged in Wudu Su Zhenghe's investigation of his crimes. Liangzhou Governor Liang Hu was afraid of his noble relatives and wanted to kill Su Zhenghe to avoid the guilt of Wuwei Prefect, so he asked Gai Xun for advice. Gai Xun usually had a grudge against Su Zhenghe, and some people advised Gai Xun to take revenge on him. Gai Xun said: No. It is unfaithful to kill a good person because of something; it is unkind to take advantage of others when they are in danger to attack them. So he admonished Liang Hu and said: "I originally wanted to eat the eagle and the kite because I wanted to get the bird of prey. Now that I have the bird of prey and I cook and kill it, what's the use?" Liang Hu accepted his words. Su Zhenghe was happy that he was saved from being killed and ran to Gai Xun to thank him. Gai Xun refused to receive him and said, "I am offering advice for Liang Shijun, not for Su Zhenghe." He still hates Su Zhenghe as before. In the first year of Zhongping, the Qiang Hu and Bian Zhang from the north invaded Longyou, and the governor Zuo Chang cut off tens of millions due to the opportunity of the war. Gai Xun strongly remonstrated, but Zuo Chang became angry, so he ordered Gai Xun to station in Ayang to resist the bandit's elite troops, hoping to use military force to incriminate him. Gai Xun had many military exploits. Bian Zhang and others attacked Jincheng and killed the governor Chen Yi. Gai Xun persuaded Zuo Chang to rescue him.
target: He chose to die in battle, cursing a defecting official. His posthumous title was Zhuangjiehou. Gai Xun, from Dunhuang, was a Xiaolian and Hanyang's chief historian. He refused to take revenge on an enemy, Su Zhenghe, when the governor wanted to kill him to cover for a corrupt prefect, arguing it was wrong to kill a good man. He later remonstrated with Governor Zuo Chang for embezzling funds, but Zuo Chang sent him to a dangerous post. Gai Xun survived and later rescued Zuo Chang from a siege by Bian Zhang.

id: 后汉书/列传/虞傅盖臧列传::group-010

source: Now I want to write more "The Classic of Filial Piety" so that every household can learn it. This may help people know etiquette and justice. Gai Xun remonstrated: In the past, when the Grand Duke was granted the title of Qi, Cui Zhu killed Duke Zhuang of Qi, Bo Qin was granted the title of Lu, and Qing's father attacked and killed Duke Min of Lu. Are there still a shortage of scholars in these two countries? Don't rush to find a solution to the problem now. Song Xiao refused to listen to him and went to the court to implement it. As expected, Gai Xun's words were not followed, so he was criticized by the imperial edict and summoned for being guilty of being conceited.
target: He criticized Governor Song Xiao's plan to teach the *Classic of Filial Piety* to pacify the border, calling it impractical.

source: Gai Xun gathered more than a hundred defeated soldiers to form Yuli's formation. The elite Qiang cavalry attacked from both sides, and many soldiers died. Gai Xun was injured in three places, but he stood firm, pointed at the wooden sign and said: "Kill me here." In the sentence, I planted Qiang Dianwu. I had received Gai Xun's kindness on weekdays, so I stopped everyone with weapons and said: Gai Changshi is a wise man. Killing him is called deceiving the sky. Gai Xun raised his head and cursed: "You are a rebel, what do you know?" Come and kill me! The soldiers looked at me and I looked at you, shocked. Dian Wu jumped off his horse and asked Gai Xun to mount his horse. Gai Xun refused and was captured by the bandit soldiers.
target: During a battle against Qiang rebels, he was wounded but refused to flee, cursing his captors. The Qiang, respecting his courage, released him.

id: 后汉书/列传/虞傅盖臧列传::group-012

source: Dian Wu jumped off his horse and asked Gai Xun to mount his horse. Gai Xun refused and was captured by the bandit soldiers. Qiang Rong admired Gai Xun's righteousness. He was brave enough to conquer the three armies and did not dare to harm him, so he was sent back to Hanyang. Later, the governor Yang Yong recommended Gai Xun to concurrently serve as the prefect of Hanyang. At that time, there was a famine and people were cannibalizing. Gai Xun allocated food to relieve the famine. He first took out his own food to set an example and saved more than a thousand hungry people.
target: As a famine relief official, he used his own grain to save over a thousand people.

id: 后汉书/列传/虞傅盖臧列传::group-013
article_path: 后汉书/列传/虞傅盖臧列传
source: At that time, Gai Xun, Zong Zheng, Liu Yu, and Assistant Military Colonel Yuan Shao were in charge of the emperor's security forces. Gai Xun said to Liu Yu and Yuan Shao: I have seen the emperor many times. The emperor is very smart, but he is just deceived by the left and right. If everyone worked together to kill the eunuchs, recruit and select handsome talents, revive the Han Dynasty, and retire with great success, wouldn't it be a great thing? Liu Yu and Yuan Shao had also discussed this matter on weekdays, so they contacted each other. Before they could take action, Sili Colonel Zhang Wen recommended Gai Xun to serve as Jing Zhaoyin. Emperor Ling still wanted to receive him. Jian Shuo and others were afraid of Gai Xun, so they all persuaded the emperor to approve Zhang Wen's memorial, so Gai Xun was appointed as Jing Zhaoyin. At that time, Chang'an ordered Yang Dang, whose father was a regular servant. Relying on his father's power, he engaged in corruption and misbehavior. Gai Xun found out that Yang Dang had embezzled more than tens of millions. The noble relatives all interceded for him, but Gai Xun refused to listen. He reported all the facts to the emperor, and involved Yang Dang's father. He ordered strict execution, and Gai Xun was powerful in the capital. At that time, Xiaohuangmen Jingzhao was highly regarded as the Shang Pharmacy Supervisor and was favored by the crown prince. Because of Jian Shuo's request, the crown prince asked Gai Xun to promote Gao Xun's highly respected son Gao Jin as Xiaolian, but Gai Xun refused. Some people say: The Crown Prince is the deputy lord and the heir to the throne, Gao Wang is the Crown Prince's favorite, and Jian Shuo is the Emperor's favorite, but you are unwilling to do this good thing. As the saying goes, "Three grudges make a house." Three grudges gather together. Aren't you afraid? Gai Xun said: "Electing worthy people to be filial and honest is to serve the country. If you are not a worthy person, even if you don't elect them, you will not regret it even if you die!" Although Gai Xun was a local official and had military and state secrets, Emperor Ling often issued edicts to ask him. He received many rewards and trusted him very much. No other minister in the court could compare with him. After the death of Emperor Ling, Dong Zhuo deposed the young emperor and killed the Queen Mother He. Gai Xun wrote to Dong Zhuo: In the past, Yi Yin banished Taijia and welcomed Taijia back to the throne three years later. Huo Guang welcomed Liu Zhi, the king of Changyi, and deposed Liu Zhi because of his promiscuity and established Emperor Xuan. Congratulations. The mourners have entered your house. Isn't it worth being careful? Dong Zhuo accepted the letter and was mentally afraid of him. Gaixun was appointed as Yilang. At this time, General Huangfu Song of the Left had 30,000 elite troops stationed in Fufeng. Gai Xun secretly planned with him to prepare for a crusade against Dong Zhuo. When Huangfu Song was also recruited, Gai Xun believed that his troops were too weak to act independently, so he returned to the capital with Huangfu Song. There was no one among the officials from Gongqing on down who did not bow to Dong Zhuo. Only Gai Xun bowed his head and resisted Dong Zhuo. Those who saw him turned pale with fright.
target: Summoned by Emperor Ling, he blamed eunuchs for the world's chaos. He planned with Liu Yu and Yuan Shao to kill the eunuchs, but was made Jing Zhaoyin instead. There, he prosecuted a corrupt official despite pleas from nobles. After Emperor Ling's death, he wrote to Dong Zhuo, criticizing his deposition of the young emperor. He openly defied Dong Zhuo in court, refusing to bow. He died of illness at 51, refusing Dong Zhuo's funeral gifts.

id: 后汉书/列传/虞傅盖臧列传::group-014
article_path: 后汉书/列传/虞傅盖臧列传
source: Zang Min led Chen Wei, the governor of Danyang, to defeat Xu Zhao. Xu Zhao still gathered his troops to harm the people. Zang Min and others sent troops to conquer and fought for three years before finally pacifying Xu Zhao, capturing Xu Zhao and his son, and killing thousands of people. Zang Min was promoted to be the envoy to the Xiongnu Zhonglang General. In the fifteenth year of Zang Hong's year, because of his father's contribution to the country, he was appointed Dong Zilang, who was famous in the Imperial Academy. His physical appearance is different from ordinary people. He was promoted to be filial and honest, and he was appointed as a complement to Lang Qiuchang. At the end of Zhongping Dynasty, he resigned and returned home. The prefect Zhang Chao asked him to be a meritorious official. At this time, Dong Zhuo killed the emperor and wanted to seize the Han Dynasty. Zang Hong said that Zhang Chao said: The prefect has been favored by the imperial court for generations, and his brothers have all served as high counties. Now the royal family is in danger, and thieves and ministers are watching. This is really the time for those who are loyal to the country to serve. Now that the county is still intact and the people are prosperous, if the war drums sound, we can gather 20,000 people and lead them to kill the national traitors and hold high the flag of righteousness for the world. Wouldn't it be great? Zhang Chao agreed with his opinion and went to Chenliu with Zang Hongxi to discuss with his brother Zhang Miao. Zhang Miao first said to Zhang Chao: I heard that you are a prefect and leave government affairs to Zang Hong. What kind of person is Zang Hong? Zhang Chao said: Zang Hong is a strange man in the country. He is more talented and resourceful than me. Zhang Miao immediately talked to Zang Hong and greatly appreciated him. He sent Zang Hong to see Liu Dai, the governor of Yanzhou, and Kong Danyou, the governor of Yuzhou, and they both became close friends with each other. Zhang Miao originally had an agreement. When Zhang Chao arrived, he made the decision, so he held a meeting with the herdsmen in Suanzao. They set up a altar and prepared to make an alliance, but they gave in to each other. No one dared to go first, and everyone recommended Zang Hong. Zang Hong then raised his clothes to the altar, expressed his blood and made an alliance, saying: The Han Dynasty was unlucky, and the rules and regulations of the court were in chaos. The traitor Dong Zhuo took the opportunity to cause harm, and the disaster fell on the emperor and poisoned the people. The most terrifying thing is that the Han Dynasty fell and the country was ruined. Liu Dai, the governor of Yanzhou, Kong Qianyou, the governor of Yuzhou, Zhang Miao, the governor of Chenliu, Qiao Mao, the governor of Dongjun, Zhang Chao, the governor of Guangling, etc., gathered volunteers to fight against the national calamity. All those who are in our alliance will work together to fulfill the loyalty of our ministers and kill their heads as they please without any second thought. If he violates the oath, he will die and die without any descendants. The emperor, the queen, the earth, the ancestors and the gods all learn from each other. Zang Hong's poems were so passionate that everyone who listened to them got excited. From then on, each army hesitated, and no one dared to go first, resulting in insufficient military supplies and the disintegration of the soldiers.
target: Zang Hong, from Guangling, was made a Dong Zilang due to his father's military merits. After Dong Zhuo killed the emperor, Zang Hong urged Prefect Zhang Chao to raise an army. He helped organize an alliance at Suanzao, where he gave a passionate oath, calling for the destruction of Dong Zhuo. The alliance, however, failed to act decisively.

id: 后汉书/列传/虞傅盖臧列传::group-015
article_path: 后汉书/列传/虞傅盖臧列传
source: His tribe was disbanded and Jiao He also died of illness. Zang Hong gathered together to comfort the scattered tribes, and the people were at peace. In the second year of his reign, Yuan Shao was afraid of his incompetence and appointed him as the prefect of Dongjun, with his capital in Dongwuyang. At this time, Cao Cao surrounded Zhang Chao in Yongqiu, and the situation was very dangerous. Zhang Chao said to the soldiers: Zang Hong is the only one who will come to save me today. Some people say: Yuan Shao and Cao Cao are getting along well, and Zang Hong is Yuan Shao's man. I'm afraid Zang Hong will not come far away, and he will bring disaster instead of good fortune. Zhang Chao said: Ziyuan is a righteous man in the world and will never deviate from his original aspirations. He may be held hostage by force, but there is nothing we can do! Zang Hong began to hear that Zhang Chao was surrounded, cried barefoot, and prepared his troops to rescue Zhang Chao. Thinking that his troops were too weak, he asked Yuan Shao for troops, but Yuan Shao refused. Zhang Chao's defense was breached and Zhang Chao's entire clan was killed. Zang Hong resented Yuan Shao and severed ties with him. Yuan Shao sent troops to surround Zang Hong, but could not capture it after many years. Yuan Shao sent Zang Hong to write a letter to Zang Hong from Chen Lin, a county resident, explaining the blessings and misfortunes to Zang Hong, and blaming each other with personal kindness and national justice. Zang Hong replied: Missing each other after farewell often occurs when we are asleep.
target: Later, Zang Hong served Yuan Shao as Qingzhou's governor, pacifying the region. When Cao Cao besieged Zhang Chao, Zang Hong begged Yuan Shao for troops to rescue him, but Yuan Shao refused. Zhang Chao was killed. Enraged, Zang Hong broke with Yuan Shao, who then besieged him. Despite a letter from Chen Lin urging surrender, Zang Hong refused, accusing Yuan Shao of betraying allies and killing loyal men.

id: 后汉书/列传/虞傅盖臧列传::group-016
article_path: 后汉书/列传/虞傅盖臧列传
source: You say that my body and reputation will be destroyed, and I will also laugh at you that your life and death will be unknown. We are the same but we are different, we work hard, what else is there to say? Yuan Shao read Zang Hong's reply and knew that he had no intention of surrender, so he increased his troops and attacked quickly. There was no food in the city, and there were no reinforcements outside. Zang Hong himself was probably going to die, so he called the officials and said: "Yuan Shao is unethical and has evil intentions. He also does not rescue my general Zang Hong. I have no choice but to die out of righteousness." I think you were fine and suffered this disaster in vain. You can lead your wives and children out of the city before the city is broken. The generals all cried and said: "You and the Yuan family have no quarrel before. For the sake of the general, we are in such danger. How can we bear to leave you?" At first, they dug up mice and boiled tendons to eat, but then they had nothing to eat. The chief clerk brought out three buckets of rice from the kitchen and asked him to cook some porridge for Zang Hong. Zang Hong said, "How can I eat alone?" Let it be cooked into porridge, and be eaten by all the soldiers. He also killed his beloved concubine and gave it to the generals to eat. The soldiers and generals were in tears and could not raise their heads. Seventy or eighty men and women died together, and no one betrayed them. The city was broken and Zang Hong was captured alive. Yuan Shaosheng opened the curtains, and all the generals in the assembly met with Zang Hong.
target: He stated he would rather die for righteousness. During the siege, he shared his last food with his soldiers and even killed his concubine to feed them.

id: 后汉书/列传/虞傅盖臧列传::group-017

source: I saw with my own eyes that the general called Zhang Chenliu his brother, so my prince Zhang Chao should also call him his brother. target: The city fell, and Zang Hong was captured. He defiantly cursed Yuan Shao for his treachery and was executed. His subordinate Chen Rong also chose to die with him.

id: 后汉书/列传/袁绍刘表列传上::group-000
article_path: 后汉书/列传/袁绍刘表列传上
source: ◆Yuan Shao Zhuan, Yuan Shao, courtesy name Benchu, was born in Ruyang, Runan, and was the grandson of Situ Yuan Tang. Yuan Shao's father, Yuan Cheng, had served as a lieutenant general with five senses. He was physically strong and liked to make friends. From the time of the great general Liang Ji, he was always friends with him. Yuan Shao served as a Langguan when he was young, and was later appointed as the Chief of Puyang. When his mother died, he resigned from the official position. After serving three years of funeral service, Yuan Shao recalled and lamented that he had lost his father since childhood and had to attend the funeral service for his father.
target: Yuan Shao, courtesy name Benchu, was from Ruyang, Runan, and the grandson of Situ Yuan Tang. His father Yuan Cheng served as a lieutenant general. Yuan Shao began his career as a Langguan and later became Chief of Puyang. After his mother's death, he resigned to observe mourning, and later also mourned his father.

id: 后汉书/列传/袁绍刘表列传上::group-001
article_path: 后汉书/列传/袁绍刘表列传上
source: After serving three years of funeral service, Yuan Shao recalled and lamented that he had lost his father since childhood and had to attend the funeral service for his father. After the mourning period expired, he moved to Luoyang. Yuan Shao was elegant, beautiful, kind to others, and focused on reputation. Yuan Shao's ancestors had served as three ministers for generations, and the guests came to join him. In addition, Yuan Shao lowered his status to befriend him, so all the scholars rushed to join him. Regardless of whether the scholars who came were high or low, Yuan Shaoyu and others were equal in etiquette. Various vehicles of visiting guests crowded the streets and alleys. The courtiers around the emperor were disgusted with him. Zhongchang Shi Zaozhong said in the ban: Yuan Benchu ​​does things to enhance his reputation and value, and likes to raise people who are not afraid of death. I don't know what this kid wants to do! After hearing this, Yuan Shao's uncle Taifu Yuan Wei called Yuan Shao and reprimanded him with the words of Zhong Zhong, but Yuan Shao never changed. Later, Yuan Shao was summoned by General He Jin as a subordinate officer and served as Shi Yushi and Huben Zhonglang General. In the fifth year of Zhongping, the imperial court began to set up eight Xiyuan captains and appointed Yuan Shao as the assistant military captain. When Emperor Ling died, Yuan Shao persuaded He Jin to recruit Dong Zhuo and other troops and coerced the Queen Mother to kill all the eunuchs. He Jin transferred Yuan Shao to serve as the captain of the Sili school. The incident has been recorded in "The Biography of He Jin". When Dong Zhuo led his army to the capital, Bao Xin, the cavalry captain from Taishan, persuaded Yuan Shao: If Dong Zhuo controls a powerful army, he will have the intention of rebelling. If we don't deal with it early, we will definitely be controlled by Dong Zhuo. When Dong Zhuo had just arrived and the soldiers were tired, they attacked Dong Zhuo and captured him. Yuan Shao was afraid of Dong Zhuo and did not dare to send troops. Soon, Dong Zhuo discussed deposing the emperor and establishing a new emperor. He said to Yuan Shao: The monarch who rules the world should find a wise person. Every time I think of Emperor Ling, it makes me angry. Marquis Dong seems to be okay, and he should be made emperor now. Yuan Shao said: "The emperor is young now and has done nothing wrong to spread the news to the world. If you ignore etiquette and follow your own desires, abolish your legitimate heir and establish your concubine as emperor, I am afraid that everyone will not think it is appropriate." Dong Zhuo put his sword in his hand and scolded Yuan Shao angrily, saying: How dare you talk like this! Don’t I have the final say in everything in the world? I want to do this, who dares to disobey! Yuan Shao replied wittily: This is a national matter. Please go outside to discuss it with the Taifu. Dong Zhuo also said: There are not enough descendants of the Liu family to keep. Yuan Shao was furious and said: "You are the only one who is tyrannical in the world, Dong Gong!" He laid out his sword, bowed to the end, and walked out. He hung the talisman on the upper door and fled to Jizhou. Dong Zhuo offered a reward for Yuan Shao's capture.
target: He then moved to Luoyang, where his elegant demeanor and generosity attracted many scholars, leading to resentment from court eunuchs. His uncle Yuan Wei reprimanded him, but Yuan Shao did not change his ways. Yuan Shao served under General He Jin as a subordinate officer and later as Colonel of the Eight Xiuyuan. After Emperor Ling's death, he advised He Jin to eliminate the eunuchs, but He Jin was killed. When Dong Zhuo arrived, Yuan Shao opposed his plan to depose the young emperor. After a heated argument, Yuan Shao fled to Jizhou. Dong Zhuo initially offered a reward for his capture but later pardoned him and appointed him Governor of Bohai and Marquis of Yunxiang.

id: 后汉书/列传/袁绍刘表列传上::group-002
article_path: 后汉书/列传/袁绍刘表列传上
source: It is better to pardon Yuan Shao and make him a county guard. Yuan Shao will be happy to see that he is exempted from guilt, and there will be no disaster. Dong Zhuo thought it was reasonable, so he sent someone to grant Yuan Shao the position of governor of Bohai and named him Marquis of Yunxiang. In name, Yuan Shao also served as Sili Xiaowei. In the first year of Chuping, Yuan Shao finally raised troops in Bohai. He and his cousin General Yuan Shu, Jizhou Mu Han Fu, Yuzhou Governor Kong Dian, Yanzhou Governor Liu Dai, Chenliu Governor Zhang Miao, Guangling Governor The governor Zhang Chao, the governor of Hanoi Wang Kuang, the governor of Shanyang Yuan Qian, the governor of Dongjun Qiao Mao, the prime minister of Jibei Bao Xin and others raised troops at the same time, with tens of thousands of troops each, under the banner of crusade against Dong Zhuo. Yuan Shao and Wang Kuang were stationed in Hanoi, Kong Dian was stationed in Yingchuan, Han Fu was stationed in Ye County, and other armies were stationed in Suanzao, and they agreed to form an alliance, nominally recommending Yuan Shao as the leader of the alliance. Yuan Shao claimed to be a general of chariots and cavalry, and was the commander of the Sili school. When Dong Zhuo learned that Yuan Shao had raised troops in Shandong, he killed Yuan Shao's uncle Yuan Wei and all the Yuan clan in the capital. Dong Zhuo then sent Da Honglu Han Rong, Shaofu Yin Xun, Zhi Jin Wu Hu Muban, General Wu Xun, the great craftsman, and Yue Qi Xiaowei Wang Quan to advise Yuan Shao and other armies. Yuan Shao assigned Wang Kuang to kill Hu Muban, Wang Quan, Wu Xun and others. Yuan Shu also hunted and killed Yin Xun, but Han Rong was spared because of his high moral character and prestige.
target: In the first year of Chuping, Yuan Shao raised troops in Bohai, joining forces with Yuan Shu, Han Fu, and others to crusade against Dong Zhuo. They formed an alliance with Yuan Shao as leader. Dong Zhuo killed Yuan Shao's uncle and clan members in the capital. Yuan Shao then took control of Jizhou from Han Fu through a combination of military pressure and persuasion, becoming its governor. He appointed Ju Shou as his advisor and expanded his territory.

id: 后汉书/列传/袁绍刘表列传上::group-003
article_path: 后汉书/列传/袁绍刘表列传上
source: Gongsun Zan's 30,000 troops formed a square formation, and another 10,000 cavalry were assigned as assault troops to guard both sides of the infantry. The force was very strong. Yuan Shaoxian ordered Qu Yi to lead 800 elite soldiers and 1,000 archers who could shoot hard bows as the vanguard. Gongsun Zan saw that Qu Yi's army was small and looked down upon him, so he let his cavalry rush towards him. Qu Yi's soldiers lay down under their shields and launched an attack at the same time. Gongsun Zan's army was defeated, and he killed Yan Gang, the Jizhou governor appointed by Gongsun Zan, and captured more than a thousand enemy heads. Qu Yi pursued Gongsun Zan to the boundary bridge, and Gongsun Zan gathered his troops and turned back to fight again. Qu Yi defeated Gongsun Zan again, and then chased Gongsun Zan's camp and captured the flag gate of the military camp. All the remaining troops of Gongsun Zan fled. Yuan Shao was more than ten miles behind. When he heard that Gongsun Zan had been defeated, he took off his saddle and let the horse rest. He was only defended by dozens of archers who could shoot hard bows and more than a hundred guards with halberds. Gongsun Zan's more than 2,000 scattered cavalry suddenly arrived and surrounded Yuan Shao several times, shooting arrows like rain. Tian Feng supported Yuan Shao and asked him to retreat into an empty wall. Yuan Shao took off his helmet and threw it to the ground, saying: "A real man should go forward and die in battle, why do you run into the wall and wrap your face instead?"
target: Yuan Shao defeated Gongsun Zan in battle, killing Yan Gang and pursuing him to the boundary bridge. Despite a near-capture by Gongsun Zan's cavalry, Yuan Shao's forces prevailed.

id: 后汉书/列传/袁绍刘表列传上::group-004
article_path: 后汉书/列传/袁绍刘表列传上
source: On the first day of March, Yuan Shao gathered his guests and subordinates at Boluojin. When they learned that the soldiers of Wei County had rebelled and that they, together with the Black Mountain bandit Kou Yudu and tens of thousands of others, captured Ye City and killed the county guard, all the guests who lived in Ye County were worried and frightened. Some stood up and cried. However, Yuan Shao's face did not change, as if nothing had happened, and he did not lose his usual demeanor. There was a thief named Tao Sheng, who called himself "General Pinghan" and rebelled against other thieves alone. He led his troops over the city wall from the west and entered the city, sealed off the county government, loaded the baggage into the car, and used the car to personally escort Yuan Shao's family and the families of other officials who lived in Jizhou City to Cuiqiu. After Yuan Shao returned, he stationed himself at Cuiqiu and appointed Tao Sheng as the general of Jianyi Zhonglang. In June, Yuan Shao then sent troops into the entrance of Cangyan Valley in Luchang Mountain, Chaoge, to attack Yu Du. After a five-day siege, Yu Du was defeated and more than 10,000 Yu Du and his followers were killed. Then Yuan Shao went north along Luchang Mountain to attack Zuo Zhuozhangba and other thieves, and wiped them all out. He also attacked Liu Shi, Qing Niujiao, Huang Long, Zuo Xiao, Guo Daxian, Li Damu, Yu Digen and others, killing tens of thousands again and destroying all their fortresses. Then he fought with Zhang Yan, the Black Mountain bandit, the fourth battalion of the Xiongnu Tu various tribes, and Wuhuan of Yanmen in Changshan. Zhang Yan had tens of thousands of elite soldiers and thousands of cavalry. The two sides fought continuously for more than ten days. Although Zhang Yan's army suffered many casualties, Yuan Shao's army was also exhausted, so they retreated. Qu Yi relied on his military exploits, pride and indulgence, and disobedience to the law. Yuan Shao summoned him, killed him, and merged his troops.
target: He later suppressed rebellions in Wei County and defeated the Black Mountain bandits, killing tens of thousands. Yuan Shao also killed his general Qu Yi for insubordination.

id: 后汉书/列传/袁绍刘表列传上::group-005
article_path: 后汉书/列传/袁绍刘表列传上
source: Qu Yi relied on his military exploits, pride and indulgence, and disobedience to the law. Yuan Shao summoned him, killed him, and merged his troops. In the second year of Xingping, the emperor appointed Yuan Shao as the right general. In the winter of this year, the emperor was pursued by Li Ji and others in Caoyang. Jushou persuaded Yuan Shao: "The general has served as the prime minister of the court for generations, and has assisted the country with loyalty throughout the ages." Now the emperor is wandering around and the ancestral temple is destroyed, but if you look at the states and counties, although they appear to be volunteers on the outside, they are actually thinking about each other in their hearts, and they have no worries about the country and the interests of the people. Moreover, the city of Jizhou was generally pacified, the army was strong, and the scholars returned, went west to meet the emperor, used Ye County as the imperial palace, held the emperor hostage and ordered the princes, raised troops and horses to attack those who did not worship the royal court, who could resist? Yuan Shao was ready to follow Ju Shou's plan. The wise men Guo Tu and Chunyu Qiong said: The royal family of the Han Dynasty declined for a long time. Isn’t it too difficult to revitalize the royal family now?
target: When Emperor Xian was in danger, Ju Shou advised Yuan Shao to welcome the emperor, but Yuan Shao hesitated due to advice from Guo Tu and Chunyu Qiong. He eventually declined.

id: 后汉书/列传/袁绍刘表列传上::group-006
article_path: 后汉书/列传/袁绍刘表列传上
source: The wise men Guo Tu and Chunyu Qiong said: The royal family of the Han Dynasty declined for a long time. Isn’t it too difficult to revitalize the royal family now? Besides, heroes rise up at the same time, occupy states and counties separately, and unite to gather followers, often tens of thousands of them. This is just like the Qin Dynasty who lost the throne and the person who got it first became the emperor. Now that the emperor has been brought in, he has to write to the emperor at every turn. If you obey, you will have too little power. If you don't obey, you will be disobeying the emperor's order. This is not a good approach. Jushu said: It is morally reasonable and the timing is appropriate to bring the emperor in now. If you don't decide early, someone else will be there to greet you first. Don't lose the opportunity to make a contingency, and don't be too quick to succeed. I hope you will consider it. The emperor's ascension was not in line with Yuan Shao's wishes, so Yuan Shao did not accept it. Yuan Shao had three sons: Shei Tan, whose courtesy name was Xiansi, Yuan Xi, whose courtesy name was Xian Yong, and Yuan Shang, whose courtesy name was Xianfu. Yuan Tan is older and wiser, while Yuan Shang is younger but more beautiful. Sai Niu's step-wife type overwhelms Zhi Cheng and dotes on her. She prefers Tong Yao and praises him many times in front of Zhi Cheng. Sai Niu is also amazed by Zhi Cheng's appearance and wants him to succeed him. So Yuan Shao adopted Yuan Tan as his brother's descendant and sent him to be the governor of Qingzhou.
target: Yuan Shao had three sons: Yuan Tan, Yuan Xi, and Yuan Shang. He favored Yuan Shang due to his wife's influence, adopting Yuan Tan as his brother's heir and sending him to Qingzhou, against Ju Shou's warnings.

id: 后汉书/列传/袁绍刘表列传上::group-007
article_path: 后汉书/列传/袁绍刘表列传上
source: However, he adopted the strategies of these people and used them as his masterminds, turning his brothers and sisters into enemies, causing swordsmen to fight against each other, and the disasters caused became more and more serious. Although I want to take off my armor and throw away my spear, the matter cannot end. I am indeed worried that your majesty’s radiance, which is as bright as the sun and the moon, may not shine in some places; your majesty’s ears may hear the clear observations from all directions, but there may be situations where you cannot hear them. I request your majesty to send the memorial to the ministers, ask all the wise ministers about the situation, and let the three ministers and nine ministers discuss the crimes committed by the ministers. If it were regarded as a crime for ministers to change their authority, then Duke Huan of Qi and Duke Wen of Jin should be sentenced to death; if it was regarded as virtuous that everyone did not attack the bandits, then there would be no need to write the derogatory word "regicide" on the shield. Although I am an ordinary person, I am determined to maintain integrity. If you can make your ministers express their sincerity and be worthy of the late emperor, then even if they lower their heads to use the torture knife or lift their clothes to use the soup pot, they will be willing to do so. Your Majesty, please pay attention to the meaning of equality in "Corpse Dove", avoid flattery remarks, and do not make your ministers resentful. So the imperial court appointed Yuan Shao as Taiwei and granted him the title of Marquis of Ye. At that time, Cao Cao himself served as the general. Yuan Shao felt ashamed of being under Cao Cao and deliberately wrote a letter of resignation to the emperor and refused to accept it. Cao Cao was very scared and gave up the position of general to Yuan Shao. In the second year of Jian'an, the emperor sent the great craftsman Kong Rong to hold the emperor's talisman to grant Yuan Shao the position of general. He also gave him bows and arrows, talismans, axes and irons, and a hundred tigers and swords. He was asked to take charge of the four states of Jizhou, Qingzhou, Youzhou and Bingzhou. Yuan Shao accepted the appointment. Every time Yuan Shao received an imperial edict, he was always worried that it would be detrimental to him, so he wanted the emperor to move closer to him. He sent people to tell Cao Cao that Xu County was low-lying and humid, and Luoyang was incomplete and ruined. The capital should be moved to Zhencheng to be close to a complete and abundant area.
target: In the first year of Jian'an, Cao Cao welcomed the emperor to Xu County and blamed Yuan Shao for not aiding the emperor. Yuan Shao responded with a lengthy letter defending his actions, citing his loyalty and efforts against Dong Zhuo and others. The court appointed him Taiwei and Marquis of Ye, but he refused until Cao Cao yielded the position of General. Later, he was granted command of four provinces.

id: 后汉书/列传/袁绍刘表列传上::group-008
article_path: 后汉书/列传/袁绍刘表列传上
source: Yuan Shao did not adopt it. In the spring of the fourth year, Yuan Shao attacked Gongsun Zan and pacified the Youzhou area. The incident is recorded in "The Biography of Gongsun Zan". Since Yuan Shao annexed the territory of four states and had hundreds of thousands of troops, his pride became strong, and the tribute to the emperor was sparse and simple. Geng Bao, the chief registrar, secretly wrote to Yuan Shao, saying: The Red Virtue of the Han Dynasty is about to decline. The Yuan family is the descendant of Yu Shun and Huang De, and they should comply with the will of God and the wishes of the people. Yuan Shao showed Geng Bao's petition to his staff. Everyone believed that Geng Bao was deceitful and should be beheaded. Yuan Shao knew that everyone disagreed, so he had no choice but to kill Geng Bao to cover up his feelings.
target: Yuan Shao attacked Gongsun Zan again, pacifying Youzhou. With control of four provinces and hundreds of thousands of troops, he grew arrogant.

id: 后汉书/列传/袁绍刘表列传上::group-009
article_path: 后汉书/列传/袁绍刘表列传上
source: Guo Tu and others took this opportunity to speak ill of Jushou: Jushou's authority inside and outside his supervision shocked the three armies. If he gradually becomes stronger, how can he be controlled? If the ministers have the same power as the monarch, the country will perish. This is taboo in the book "Yellow Stone". Besides, those who command external armies should not be involved in internal affairs. Yuan Shao then divided Jusuke's authority into three governors, and asked Jusuke, Guo Tu, and Chunyu Qiong to each be in charge of an army, but he did not have time to do so. In the fifth year, Liu Bei, the general of the left, killed Chezhou, the governor of Xuzhou, and occupied Peixian County to betray Cao Cao. Cao Cao was afraid and personally led his troops to attack Liu Bei. Tian Feng said to Yuan Shao: The one who competes with you for the world is Cao Cao. Cao Cao is going to Shubian to attack Liu Bei. The fighting between the two sides cannot end soon. Now mobilize all the troops to attack Cao Cao's rear, and they can be pacified as soon as they leave. The army is dispatched according to the opportunity, and the time is created. Yuan Shao refused because his son was ill, and Tian Feng's plan was not implemented. Tian Feng raised his crutch and knocked on the ground and said: Well, the big deal is over! It’s so hard to catch such an opportunity, but it’s a pity that the opportunity was lost because the child was sick! Yuan Shao was very angry after hearing this and alienated Tian Feng from then on. Cao Cao was afraid that Yuan Shao would cross the Yellow River, so he stepped up his attack on Liu Bei and finally defeated Liu Bei. Liu Bei defected to Yuan Shao, and Yuan Shao then marched to attack Xu County.
target: He planned to attack Xu County, ignoring Ju Shou's advice to rest and farm. Instead, he followed Guo Tu and Shen Pei's counsel to attack immediately. Tian Feng's warnings led to his imprisonment. In the fifth year of Jian'an, Yuan Shao marched south after Liu Bei's defection. He issued a proclamation condemning Cao Cao's crimes.

id: 后汉书/列传/袁绍刘表列传上::group-010
article_path: 后汉书/列传/袁绍刘表列传上
source: Yuan Shao sent Liu Bei and Wen Chou to challenge, and Cao Cao defeated Yuan Jun and killed Wen Chou. They fought again, and Cao Cao captured two of Yuan Shao's generals alive. Yuan Shao's army was greatly shocked. Cao Cao returned to Guandu to garrison, and Yuan Shao advanced to occupy Yangwu. Ju Shou also advised Yuan Shao: Although the northern army has more people, it is not as strong and decisive as the southern army; the southern army has less food and its reserves are not as good as the northern army. The Southern Army wanted a quick victory, while the Northern Army had the advantage of advancing slowly. It is best to use a slow and long-lasting method to delay time. Yuan Shao didn't listen. Yuan Shao connected the camps and gradually advanced, slowly approaching Guandu. The two sides fought. As a result, Cao's army was defeated and retreated to the camp to hold on. Yuan Shao built a tall watchtower and piled it into a mountain of earth, and fired arrows at Cao Cao's camp. The soldiers in the camp walked with shields on their heads. So Cao Cao used a stone chariot to fire stones and destroyed all Yuan Shao's watchtowers. The soldiers in the army called them "Thunderbolt Chariots". Yuan Shao dug tunnels to attack Cao Cao. Cao Cao immediately dug a long trench in the camp to stop Yuan Shao, and sent a surprise attack on Yuan's army's grain truck, burning all the grain. The two sides fought for more than a hundred days, and the people south of the Yellow River were exhausted. Many people betrayed Cao Cao and joined Yuan Shao. Yuan Shao sent Chunyu Qiong and others to lead more than 10,000 soldiers north to meet the troops transporting grain. Jushu persuaded Yuan Shao to send Jiang Qi to lead another army as foreign aid to cut off Cao Cao's looting. Yuan Shao disagreed. Xu You offered advice and said: Cao Cao has few soldiers and all his troops are used to resist our army. The remaining defense force in Xu County must be empty and weak. If another lightly-armed force is sent to attack day and night and capture Xu County, Cao Cao will naturally be captured. Even if Cao Cao's army is not defeated, they can be forced to run from both ends and they will definitely defeat Cao Cao. Yuan Shao couldn't accept it. It happened that someone in Xu You's family broke the law and was imprisoned. Xu You felt frustrated, so he defected to Cao Cao and suggested that Cao Cao sneak attack Chunyu Qiong and others. Chunyu Qiong and others were staying overnight at the Bird's Nest, which was forty miles away from Yuan Shao's troops. Cao Cao personally led five thousand infantry and cavalry to attack Chunyu Qiong and others overnight and wiped them out. Yuan Shao first learned that Cao Cao was attacking Chunyu Qiong, and said to his eldest son Yuan Tan: Even if Cao Cao defeats Chun Yuqiong and I capture Cao Cao's military camp, he will definitely have nowhere to return. So he sent Gao Lan, Zhang He and others to attack Cao Cao's camp, but they couldn't capture it. When the second general heard that Chunyu Qiong and others were defeated, he defected to Cao Cao. At this time, Yuan Shao's army panicked and was completely defeated. Yuan Shao, Yuan Tan and others, wearing turbans and riding horses, crossed the Yellow River with 800 cavalry, arrived at Liyang on the north bank, and entered the military camp of their general Jiang Yiqu.
target: His forces initially succeeded but were defeated at Guandu after Xu You defected and revealed the location of Yuan Shao's grain supplies at Wuchao. Cao Cao attacked and destroyed the supplies, leading to Yuan Shao's defeat. Yuan Shao fled with 800 cavalry, while many of his troops were killed or surrendered. Ju Shou was captured and executed after attempting to return to Yuan Shao.

id: 后汉书/列传/袁绍刘表列传上::group-011
article_path: 后汉书/列传/袁绍刘表列传上
source: So he pardoned Ju and treated him favorably. Soon Jushu tried to return to the Yuan family, and Cao Cao killed him. Yuan Shao appears to be generous, elegant and considerate, and does not show sorrow or joy on his face. However, he is proud and arrogant by nature and cannot listen to correct opinions, which leads to failure. When Yuan Shao's army returned, someone said to Tian Feng: You will definitely be used in important ways. Tian Feng said: Mr. Yuan is generous on the surface but jealous in his heart. He does not believe in my loyalty, and I have offended him many times by telling the truth. If he wins, he will definitely forgive me when he is happy; if he loses the battle, he will be resentful and jealous in his heart. If I had been victorious, I would have been saved. Now that I have been defeated, I have no hope of surviving. After Yuan Shao came back, he said: I didn't adopt Tian Feng's advice, and he really laughed at me. So Tian Feng was killed. Guan Du was defeated and Shen Pei's two sons were captured alive by Cao Cao. Meng Dai had a conflict with Shenpei, so he told Yuan Shao through Jiang Qi: Shenpei has monopolized power in office, has a large clan, strong military strength, and his two sons are in the south. He must want to rebel. Guo Tu and Xin Ping also thought so. Yuan Shao then appointed Meng Dai as the supervisor of the army to guard Ye County instead of Shen Pei. The guard Feng Ji and his colleagues tried to find out whether they were in harmony with each other. Yuan Shao asked Feng Ji about the incident. Feng Ji replied: "Shen Pei is strong and straightforward by nature. Every time he says something or does something, he admires the integrity of the ancients. He will not do anything unjust because his two sons are in the south. Don't doubt him." Yuan Shao said: Don't you hate him? Feng Ji said: In the past, the disputes were personal matters, but now we are talking about national affairs. Yuan Shao said: That's so right. So the judge was not dismissed. Since then, the relationship between Shen Pei and Feng Ji has become more harmonious. Many cities in Jizhou rebelled against Yuan Shao, and Yuan Shao was busy attacking and pacifying these cities. Yuan Shao became ill after his defeat. In the summer of the seventh year of Jian'an, Yuan Shao died. Yuan Shao had not had time to determine his successor. Fengji and Shenpei had always disgusted Yuan Tan because of their pride and luxury. Xin Ping and Guo Tu were both close to Yuan Tan and had conflicts with Shenpei and Fengji. Everyone thinks that Yuan Tan is older and wants to establish Yuan Tan. Shen Pei and others were afraid that Xin Ping and others would harm them after Yuan Tan came to the throne, so they pretended to be sent by Yuan Shao and supported Yuan Shang as their successor.
target: Yuan Shao appeared generous but was proud and unable to accept advice, leading to his downfall. After his defeat, he killed Tian Feng. He fell ill and died in the seventh year of Jian'an. His succession was disputed: Shen Pei and Feng Ji supported Yuan Shang, while others favored Yuan Tan, leading to internal conflict.

id: 后汉书/列传/袁绍刘表列传下::group-000
article_path: 后汉书/列传/袁绍刘表列传下
source: Liu Biao, courtesy name Jingsheng, was born in Gaoping, Shanyang, and was a descendant of King Lu Gong. Liu Biao was more than eight feet tall, with a gentle appearance and a burly build. Together with Zhang Jian and others from the same county, he was slandered and discussed as "Ba Gu". The emperor issued an edict to arrest the party members and punish them, but Liu Biao escaped without being caught. After the party ban was lifted, Liu Biao was summoned by General He Jin as an assistant. In the first year of Chuping, Sun Jian, the governor of Changsha, killed Wang Xu, the governor of Jingzhou, and issued an edict appointing Liu Biao as the governor of Jingzhou. At that time, there were many bandits of the same clan in the south of the Yangtze River, and Yuan Shu's troops were stationed in Luyang to block the road. Liu Biao could not reach Jingzhou, so he rode into Yicheng alone and invited Kuai Yue from Nanjun and Cai Mao from Xiangyang to discuss countermeasures. Liu Biao said to Kuai Yue: Although there are many thieves in the same clan, no one will join them. If Yuan Jie takes advantage of them, disaster will inevitably come. I want to recruit troops, but I'm worried that I can't combine them. What strategy should I use? Kuai Yue replied: When governing peace, benevolence and righteousness should be the first priority; when governing war, the first priority should be to use contingency strategies. The army does not have a large number of people, the important thing is to get the right talents. Yuan Shu was proud and had no strategy, and most of the thieves gathered from his own clan were greedy and cruel. Among them are people who I usually support. If I send someone to tell them the benefits, they will definitely lead their troops over. You kill the cruel ones among them and appoint the talented ones among them. Once your prestige and kindness are established, people will come to you carrying their children in swaddling clothes. The soldiers gathered and the people surrendered. Jiangling was captured in the south and Xiangyang was defended in the north. The eight counties under Jingzhou's jurisdiction could be pacified with a single proclamation. Even if Yuan Gongli arrives, there is nothing he can do. Liu Biao said: Yes. So he asked Kuai Yue to send people to lure the leaders of thieves from his own tribe. Fifteen people came, killed them all and captured their tribes by surprise. Only when the Jiangxia thieves Zhang Hu and Chen Li gathered their troops to occupy Xiangyang City, and Liu Biao sent Kuai Yue and Pang Ji to inform them, did they surrender. Everything south of the Yangtze River was pacified. Many prefects and county magistrates heard about Liu Biao's reputation, and many of them took off their seals and ribbons and left. Liu Hu then organized his troops in the fortress area to observe changes in the current situation.
target: Liu Biao, courtesy name Jingsheng, was a descendant of King Lu Gong from Gaoping, Shanyang. Over eight feet tall with a gentle appearance and burly build, he was implicated in the "Ba Gu" party affair and escaped arrest. After the party ban was lifted, he served as an assistant to General He Jin. In the first year of Chuping, he was appointed Governor of Jingzhou following Sun Jian's murder of Governor Wang Xu. Unable to reach Jingzhou due to bandits and Yuan Shu's troops blocking the road, Liu Biao rode alone to Yicheng and consulted Kuai Yue and Cai Mao. Following Kuai Yue's advice, he lured and killed fifteen clan bandit leaders, then pacified their tribes. The Jiangxia thieves Zhang Hu and Chen Li surrendered after negotiations, and the region south of the Yangtze River was subdued. Liu Biao organized troops to observe the situation.

id: 后汉书/列传/袁绍刘表列传下::group-001
article_path: 后汉书/列传/袁绍刘表列传下
source: Liu Biao said: Yes. So he asked Kuai Yue to send people to lure the leaders of thieves from his own tribe. Fifteen people came, killed them all and captured their tribes by surprise. Only when the Jiangxia thieves Zhang Hu and Chen Li gathered their troops to occupy Xiangyang City, and Liu Biao sent Kuai Yue and Pang Ji to inform them, did they surrender. Everything south of the Yangtze River was pacified. Many prefects and county magistrates heard about Liu Biao's reputation, and many of them took off their seals and ribbons and left. Liu Hu then organized his troops in the fortress area to observe changes in the current situation. There was a gap between Yuan Shu and his cousin Yuan Shao, and Yuan Shao was friends with Liu Biao, so Yuan Shu and Sun Jian jointly attacked Liu Biao from the north and south. Liu Biao was defeated, and Sun Jian then surrounded Xiangyang. Just as Liu Biao's general Huang Zu came to rescue him, Sun Jian was shot by a stray arrow and died, and the rest of the people retreated. When Li Cui and others entered Chang'an, in winter, Liu Biao sent envoys to pay tribute to the emperor. Li Ji appointed Liu Biao as the General of Zhennan and the Shepherd of Jingzhou, and made him a Marquis of Wu, holding the Emperor's Talisman as his aid. In the first year of Jian'an, the hussar general Zhang Ji fled from Guanzhong to Nanyang, attacked Lucheng along the way, and was shot to death by a flying arrow. Officials and subordinates from Jingzhou came to celebrate. Liu Biao said: Zhang Ji came because he was in embarrassment, and the master did not treat him politely, which resulted in a fight. It was not my idea to send him away. I accept condolences but not congratulations. He sent people to receive Zhang Ji's troops. The soldiers were very happy and surrendered to Liu Biao. In the third year, Zhang Xian, the governor of Changsha, led Lingling and Guiyang counties to betray Liu Biao. Liu Biao sent troops to besiege him, defeated Zhang Xian and pacified these areas. In this way, the area that Liu Biao expanded was very wide. It connected with Wuling in the south and Han in the north. It was thousands of miles in radius and had more than 100,000 armored warriors. At first, the people in Jingzhou were prone to harassment. In addition, there was shock and fear in all directions, and bandits were rampant, so there was turmoil everywhere. Liu Biao summoned and persuaded well, and used force and appeasement in a coordinated manner. Among the thieves, the cunning and cunning old thief even helped him, and he leveled everything within ten thousand miles. Everyone, young and old, was convinced by him. Thousands of scholars and literati from Guanxi, Yanzhou, and Yuzhou came to seek refuge. Liu Biao gave comfort and relief, and these people were fully supported. So Liu Biao established a school and extensively visited people with Confucianism. People like Qi Muhe, Song Zhong and others wrote chapters and sentences of the "Five Classics", which is called Houding. Liu Biao cared for the people, supported the scholars, and calmly defended Jingzhou.
target: Yuan Shu and Sun Jian attacked Liu Biao, but Sun Jian was killed by a stray arrow during the siege of Xiangyang. Liu Biao sent tribute to Emperor Xian and was appointed General of Zhennan, Shepherd of Jingzhou, and Marquis of Wu. When Zhang Ji attacked Lucheng and was killed, Liu Biao accepted condolences and recruited Zhang Ji's troops. He suppressed rebellions by Zhang Xian and others, expanding his territory to connect with Wuling in the south and Han in the north, commanding over 100,000 armored warriors. Liu Biao pacified bandits, supported scholars, established schools, and commissioned commentaries on the Five Classics.

source: If you want to make a difference, raising troops when they are tired is a feasible way; if you don't want to do this, you must choose appropriate measures. How can you have an army of 100,000, sit back and watch the success or failure of others, refuse to rescue others when they ask for help, and refuse to submit to wise people when you see them! In this way, the resentment of both parties will be concentrated on you, and I'm afraid it will be impossible for you to obtain neutrality. Cao Cao is good at using troops, and most of the wise and outstanding people defect to Cao Cao. This situation will definitely defeat Yuan Shao, and then mobilize his troops to attack the Yangtze River and Han River area. I am afraid that the general will not be able to resist. The best way at the moment is to surrender the entire Jingzhou to Cao Cao. Cao Cao must value the grateful general. You can enjoy the status of fortune and wealth for a long time and pass it on to future generations. This is an extremely perfect strategy. Kuai Yue also tried to persuade Liu Biao. But Liu Biao was hesitant and sent Han Song to Cao Cao to see what was going on. Liu Biao said to Han Song: Now I don't know who can pacify the world, but Cao Cao supports the emperor to make Xu County his capital. You can go and see the truth for me. Han Song replied: In my opinion, with Cao Gong's wisdom, he will definitely be able to realize his wish to unify the world. If the general wants to submit to Cao Cao, he can send me. If he is undecided, I go to the capital and the emperor offers me an official position. If my refusal is not accepted, then I will become the emperor's minister and the general's former subordinate. When you are with the Emperor, you will be loyal to the Emperor, and I will no longer devote myself to you. I hope you reconsider. Liu Biao thought that he was afraid of sending an envoy and forced him to go. After arriving in Xu County, the emperor appointed Han Song as his minister and prefect of Lingling. After returning, Han Song strongly praised the kindness of the emperor and Cao Cao, and persuaded Liu Biao to send his son to serve. Liu Biao was furious, thinking that Han Song had double-minded intentions, so he displayed his troops, insulted Han Song, and prepared to kill him. Han Song's expression remained unchanged as he slowly recounted what he had said before leaving. Liu Biao's wife Cai knew Han Song's virtues and dissuaded Liu Biao. Liu Biao was still furious, so he tortured and killed Han Song's entourage. Liu Biao learned that Han Song had no other intention but to imprison him. In the sixth year, Liu Bei came from Yuan Shao and defected to Jingzhou. Liu Biao treated Liu Bei favorably and made friends with him, but he could not use him. In the thirteenth year, Cao Cao personally led an army to conquer Liu Biao but did not reach Jingzhou. In August, Liu Biao died of malignant sores on his back. Liu Biao had been in Jingzhou for nearly twenty years, and his family had no extra savings.
target: During Cao Cao and Yuan Shao's conflict at Guandu, Liu Biao remained neutral despite advice from Han Song and Kuai Yue to submit to Cao Cao. He sent Han Song to observe Cao Cao, but after Han Song praised Cao Cao and urged submission, Liu Biao imprisoned him. Liu Bei defected to Jingzhou in the sixth year of Jian'an, but Liu Biao did not utilize him. In the thirteenth year, Cao Cao marched south, and Liu Biao died of illness in August after nearly twenty years in Jingzhou.
