source: Zhuge Liang said: "Don't you see that Shen Sheng is in danger at home and Chong'er is safe when he lives abroad?" Liu Qi realized in his heart and secretly planned a way out. It happened that Huang Zu, the governor of Jiangxia under Liu Biao, was killed by Sun Quan, so Liu Qi asked to take over the position. When Liu Biao was seriously ill, Liu Qi came back to visit him. Because Liu Qi was kind and filial by nature, Zhang Yun and others were afraid that they would have a father-son relationship after seeing Liu Biao. Liu Biao once again wanted to let him succeed, so he said to Liu Qi: The general has ordered you to govern Jiangxia. This responsibility is of great importance. If you leave your subordinates and come here without permission, you will definitely be scolded. It is not filial piety to ruin your father's interest and aggravate his illness. So he blocked the door and prevented him from seeing Liu Biao. Liu Qi left in tears, and many people sighed after hearing this. In this way, Liu Cong succeeded to the throne. Liu Cong awarded Liu Qi the seal of the feudal lords. Liu Qi became angry and threw the seal to the ground, preparing to take advantage of the funeral to make trouble. Just as Cao Cao's army arrived in Xinye, Liu Qi fled to the south of the Yangtze River. Kuai Yue, Han Song and Dong Cao's Fu Xun persuaded Liu Cong to surrender to Cao Cao. Liu Cong said: Now that I have the entire territory of Chu State with you, I can preserve the career of the late emperor and use it to observe the situation in the world. Why not? Fu Xun said: There are important principles for rebellion and surrender, and there are certain situations between strong and weak. It is rebellious to fight against the emperor as a minister; to rely on the newly created Chu land to resist the central power will be dangerous; to antagonize Cao Gong for Liu Bei's sake is not worth it. These three aspects are all shortcomings, and if you want to use them to resist the king's army, this is the road to inevitable destruction. How does the general compare with Liu Bei? Liu Cong said: I am not as good as him. Fu Xun said: If Liu Bei's ability is not enough to resist Duke Cao, then even if he owns the entire Chu land, he cannot protect himself. If Liu Bei is strong enough to resist Duke Cao, then Liu Bei will not be under your control. I hope the general won't doubt it. When Cao Cao's army reached Xiangyang, Liu Cong asked for the surrender of the entire Jingzhou, and Liu Bei rushed to Xiakou. Cao Cao appointed Liu Cong as the governor of Qingzhou and made him a marquis. Fifteen people including Kuai Yue were granted the title of marquis. Then Cao Cao released Han Song from prison. Because of his high reputation, he treated him with special courtesy and asked him to list the talents in Jingzhou. All those he recommended were promoted and appointed. Appoint Han Song as Da Honglu and treat him as a friend. Kuai Yue was appointed Guang Luxun, and Liu Xian was appointed Shangshu Ling. At first, Liu Biao made friends with Yuan Shao, but Deng Yi tried to dissuade him from doing so, but Liu Biao refused to listen. Deng Yi resigned on the pretext of illness and did not serve as an official while Liu Biao was alive. Cao Cao appointed him as a servant. Many others have become high-ranking officials. Cao Cao was later defeated in Chibi, and Liu Bei wrote a letter recommending Liu Qi to be the historian of Jing. He died the following year.
target: Liu Biao favored his son Liu Qi initially but later favored Liu Cong due to his wife Cai's influence. Liu Qi, feeling unsafe, sought advice from Zhuge Liang and requested to govern Jiangxia. When Liu Biao fell ill, Liu Qi was prevented from visiting him, and Liu Cong succeeded. Liu Cong surrendered Jingzhou to Cao Cao, who appointed him Governor of Qingzhou and granted marquisates to others. Cao Cao later released Han Song and appointed him Da Honglu. Liu Biao's alliance with Yuan Shao was criticized by Deng Yi, who resigned. Cao Cao was defeated at Chibi, and Liu Bei recommended Liu Qi as Jingzhou's historian; Liu Qi died the following year. The text concludes that Liu Biao's indecision and favoritism led to his downfall.

source: Xiqiang originally came from Sanmiao, another branch of the Jiang surname. The Western Qiang Kingdom is close to Nanyue. When Shun exiled four stubborn people, he exiled them to Sanwei, which is the Qiang area southwest of Heguan. This area is wrapped around the Cizhi River and stretches for thousands of miles to the head of Cizhi River. The gift branch is the analysis branch mentioned in "Yu Gong". This area borders the barbarians outside the borders of Shu and Han to the south, and borders Shanshan, Cheshi and other countries to the northwest. The Xiqiang people do not have fixed residences. They migrate with water and grass. Grains are rarely grown on this land, and they mainly rely on livestock raising. The custom of Xiqiang is that clans are not fixed. Some clans use the father's name and the mother's surname as the title of their tribe. After the twelfth generation, clans intermarry with each other. After the father dies, he marries his stepmother, and after his elder brother dies, he marries his widower. Therefore, there are no widowers or widows in the Xiqiang country, and the population reproduces quickly. Xiqiang does not have a king or ministers, and no one is its leader. If the power is strong, they will separate into races and become chiefs. If the power is weak, they will become subordinate tribes of others. They plundered and invaded each other, ruling the roost with violence. Kill for life, there is no other prohibition. The soldiers of Xiqiang are good at fighting in the valleys, but not on the plains; they cannot fight for a long time, but they dare to charge into battle; they regard death in battle as auspicious, while death from illness is considered unlucky.
target: The Xiqiang people, originally from Sanmiao, a branch of the Jiang surname, lived in a region near Nanyue, stretching from the Cizhi River to the borders of Shu and Han in the south and Shanshan and Cheshi in the northwest. They were nomadic, migrating with water and grass, relying primarily on livestock rather than grain. Their society lacked fixed clans, with tribes named after paternal or maternal lines. After twelve generations, intermarriage occurred, and customs included marrying stepmothers after a father's death and widows after an elder brother's death, leading to rapid population growth. They had no central ruler; power determined leadership, with violence and plunder common. Their soldiers excelled in valley combat but not on plains, valued death in battle over illness, and endured harsh conditions.

source: Xiqiang does not have a king or ministers, and no one is its leader. If the power is strong, they will separate into races and become chiefs. If the power is weak, they will become subordinate tribes of others. They plundered and invaded each other, ruling the roost with violence. Kill for life, there is no other prohibition. The soldiers of Xiqiang are good at fighting in the valleys, but not on the plains; they cannot fight for a long time, but they dare to charge into battle; they regard death in battle as auspicious, while death from illness is considered unlucky. The Xiqiang people can endure cold and hardship just like animals. Even when women give birth to children, they do not hide from the wind and snow. The Xiqiang people are strong and brave in fighting for the land, and they have accepted the energy of the metal element in the five elements and the west. If the emperor's government is clear and clear, the barbarians will surrender; if the emperor loses virtue and education, the barbarians will invade and cause chaos. In the past, Taikang, the king of the Xia Dynasty, lost the world and all the barbarians rebelled. When the later prime minister came to the throne, he conquered the Yiyi. Seven years later, the Yiyi came to submit. After Houxie, the title of nobility was added to Ruyi, and Ruyi obeyed the Xia Dynasty from then on. When Hou Jie was in turmoil, the Yi people came to live in the Linqi area. After the rise of Chengtang, he conquered the Yiyi and made them retreat. When the Yin Dynasty weakened in the middle period, all barbarians rebelled. When Wuding arrived, he conquered Xirong and Guifang, and it took three years to conquer them. So the poem says: Since the time of Di Qiang, no one has dared not to come to pay homage to the Emperor. When Wu Yi was brutal and cruel, and the dog soldiers invaded the border, Zhou Gugong Yi's father crossed Liangshan and took refuge at the foot of Qishan Mountain. At the time of his son Ji Li, he conquered the Xiluo Guirong. During the reign of Taiding, Ji Li attacked the Rong tribe in Yanjing, and the Rong tribe defeated Zhou's army. Two years later, when Zhou's troops defeated Yu Wu's Rong tribe, Taiding appointed Ji Li as priest. From then on, Ji Li attacked the Rong tribe of Shihu and Yitu, and won both of them. When King Wen was appointed as the Western Bodhisattva, there were Kun barbarians to the west of the Zhou Dynasty, and there were dangers to the north from the Ming dynasties. So King Wen repulsed the Rong and Di and garrisoned troops there, and all of the Rong and Di surrendered. King Wen then commanded the Xirong and conquered the countries that had betrayed the Yin and Shang dynasties to serve King Zhou. When King Wu attacked Shang, the Qiang people and Zhang Ren led their troops to meet in Muye. At the time of King Mu, the Rongdi did not pay tribute to the Zhou Dynasty. King Mu then marched westward against the Quanrong, captured the five kings of the Quanrong, and obtained four white deer and four white wolves. King Mu then moved the Rong people to Taiyuan. During the reign of King Yi, the Zhou Dynasty was weak and the Rong people from the outlying areas did not come to worship. The emperor ordered Duke Guo to lead a division of six armies to attack the Rong people in Taiyuan as far as Yuquan and obtained a thousand horses. King Li was cruel, and the Rong and Di invaded and plundered. He even entered Quanqiu and killed Qin Zhong's family. The emperor ordered to conquer the Rong people, but they could not win.
target: Historically, the Xiqiang's relationship with Chinese dynasties fluctuated. During the Xia Dynasty, Taikang's loss of control led to barbarian rebellion, but later rulers like Houxiang and Houxie subdued them. Under the Yin Dynasty, Wuding conquered Xirong and Guifang, but Wu Yi's brutality provoked Dog Soldier invasions. The Zhou Dynasty saw King Wen and King Wu command Xirong, while King Mu campaigned against Quanrong. As Zhou weakened, Rong tribes invaded, leading to conflicts with Qin and Jin. During the Spring and Autumn period, Rong groups like Yiqu and Dali grew powerful, building cities and claiming kingship. Qin gradually absorbed them, with King Zhao of Qin destroying Yiqu in the 4th century BCE.

source: He also sent translators many times to inform the situation, and allowed the Qiang and Yi people outside the frontier to serve as the officials' eyes and ears, so that the prefectures and counties could be on guard and on guard. It is time to restore the previous system to demonstrate deterrence and prevention. Guangwu adopted Ban Biao's advice and immediately appointed Niu Han as the Colonel Protecting Qiang, holding the Emperor's Talisman as before. When Niu Han died, he was relieved of the post of Colonel Protecting Qiang. Ten years later, the chiefs of Xianling colluded with the Qiang people of other tribes and invaded Jincheng and Longxi again. The imperial court sent Zhonglang Lai She and others to attack the invading Qiang people, and defeated the Qiang people. The incident has been recorded in the "Biography of Lai She". In the summer of the eleventh year, Xian Lingzhong invaded Lintao again. Ma Yuan, the prefect of Longxi, defeated Xian Lingzhong and made them surrender. Later, all the Qiang people surrendered, and the imperial court moved the Qiang people to Tianshui, Longxi, and Fufeng counties. The next year, the Shenlang Qiang in Wudu rebelled, and Ma Yuan defeated the Shenlang Qiang and made them surrender. The incident has been recorded in "The Biography of Ma Yuan". From Shaodang to Dianliang, they lived in the Dayun Valley north of the Yellow River for generations. The tribe was small and the people were poor. However, Xianling and Beinan were powerful and wealthy, and invaded Yunnan Liang many times. Dian Liang and his son had been bullied and slighted for a long time, and they were very angry. Moreover, they usually had kindness and loyalty in the tribe, so Dian Liang joined the affiliated tribes and other mixed tribes, marched from Dayu Valley, and suddenly attacked Xianling and Bei'an. They defeated Xianling and Bei'an. They killed 3,000 people, plundered property and livestock, and seized the central area of ​​Dayu Valley as their residence. From then on, they became powerful. Dian Liang's son Dian Wu succeeded to the throne. In the first year of the Zhongyuan Dynasty, the Shenlang Qiang in Wudu rebelled, killing and plundering officials and people. The prefect fought with the Shenlang Qiang, but failed to win. The Longxi prefect Liu Xu sent Li Bao, an officer from Xindu and the supervisor of the army, to lead five thousand people to Wudu and fight against the Qiang. They killed the Qiang leader and killed and captured more than a thousand Qiang people. At this time, Wudu's army also defeated the Qiang people, killing more than a thousand people, and the rest of the Qiang people surrendered. At that time, Dianwu's subordinate tribes became powerful and often dominated the Qiang tribes. Anyone who wanted to invade the border, Dianwu taught them strategies and became their big leader. In the autumn of the second year, Shaodang Qiang Dianwu and his younger brother Dian'an led 5,000 infantry and cavalry to invade the Longxi border fortress. Liu Xu sent troops to attack Dianwu in Paohan, but could not win. They fought again in Yunjie and were defeated by the Qiang. More than 500 people were killed. At this time, the Qiang people of various tribes who guarded the fortress followed and invaded the border one after another. The imperial court sent envoy Zhang Hong to lead the troops from various counties to attack the Qiang people. They fought at Yunwu and Tanggu, but were defeated. Zhang Hong and Longxi Chief Shi Tiansa both died. Tianshui's army was defeated by Lao Jiezhong at Baishi, and more than a thousand people died.
target: Under the Han Dynasty, the Xiqiang faced expulsion and relocation. Emperor Wu expanded borders, building fortresses and separating Qiang from Xiongnu. In 42 BCE, Xianling Qiang allied with Xiongnu, attacking Lingju and Paohan, but were suppressed by General Li Xi. Later, Zhao Chongguo defeated them in 60 BCE. During Wang Mang's reign, Qiang lands were seized, but after his fall, they rebelled. In 25 CE, Guangwu restored the Qiang Protectorate, but conflicts persisted. Ma Yuan defeated Qiang rebellions in 35 CE, moving them to Tianshui and Longxi. By 58 CE, Dianwu's rebellion was crushed, and Qiang were resettled in Sanfu. The Qiang continued to resist Han rule. In 77 CE, Miwu led a revolt, defeating Han forces. Fu Yu, the Qiang Protector, was killed in 87 CE. Zhang Yu retaliated by poisoning Qiang leaders, but Miwu's son Mitang continued raids. Deng Xun and later officials used bribery to divide the Qiang, but conflicts resumed. In 107 CE, the Qiang rebellion under Dianling and others devastated border regions, costing billions and causing massive displacement. Ren Shang and Deng Zun campaigned against them, but corruption and mismanagement plagued efforts. By 118 CE, the Qiang were largely subdued, though sporadic revolts occurred.

source: In the third year of Emperor Ling's Jianning reign, Shaodang Qiang sent envoys to pay tribute. In the first year of Zhongping, the Qiang Xianlingzhong who surrendered in the north took advantage of the Yellow Turban chaos, so they rebelled with Huangzhong Qiang, Yicong Hubeigong Boyu and others and invaded Longyou. The incident is recorded in "The Biography of Dong Zhuo". In the first year of Xingnuo, the Qiang people who surrendered under Feng Xiang rebelled and invaded various counties. Guo Bang and Fan Chou defeated them and killed thousands of Qiang people. Since Yuan Ren, his descendants have divided into a total of 150 tribes. Among them, nine tribes are located west of the head of the Cizhi River and north of the border between Shu and Han. Their population numbers are not recorded in previous history books. Only Shenlang Qiang is in Wudu and has thousands of men capable of fighting. There are fifty-two tribes that are weak and have few people and cannot be independent. They are scattered into subordinate tribes. Some of them have completely declined and have no descendants, and some have moved away. Among its eighty-nine tribes, only Zhong Qiang is the most powerful, with more than 100,000 people capable of fighting. Other tribes range in size from tens of thousands to thousands. They plunder and invade each other, and their strength and decline are ever-changing. During the reign of Emperor Shun, the total number of Qiang people capable of fighting was approximately 200,000. The Faqiang, Tangyan and other tribes were very far away and had no contact with them. The names of the tribes of Li Niu and Baima Qiang in Shu and Han cannot be known or recorded. In the thirteenth year of Jianwu's reign, Lou Deng, leader of the Baima Qiang outside the Great Wall of Guanghan, and others led more than 5,000 Qiang households of his tribe to surrender to the imperial court. Guangwu granted Lou Deng the title of Lord Commander of Guiyi. In the fifth and sixth year of Emperor He's reign, Zaotou and others, a fat Yi Qiang leader outside the borders of Shu County, led more than 500,000 people of the same tribe to surrender to the imperial court. Emperor He appointed Zaotou as the chief of the city and gave him a seal. By the first year of Yongchu reign of Emperor An, 17,280 people from six tribes including Longqiao and other Qiang tribes outside the borders of Shushu had surrendered to the imperial court. The next year, 36,900 people from eight tribes including the Qiang Bo Shen outside the borders of Shu County surrendered the entire area to the imperial court. In winter, 2,400 Qiang people from the Shenlang tribe outside the Guanghan border came to submit to the imperial court. In the second year of Emperor Huan's establishment of peace, more than a thousand Baima Qiang invaded the Guanghan vassal state and killed county officials. The Yizhou governor led the Banchu barbarians to defeat the invading Baima Qiang. The Yuezhi Hu in Huangzhong was originally another branch of the Da Yuezhi. Was it retreating in the past? Leg area resides. King Yuezhi was killed by Bao Shuandun, and the remaining tribes dispersed and crossed Congling to the west. Among them, the weak ones went south into the mountains, lived among the Qiang tribes, and intermarried with the Qiang people.
target: In later years, the Qiang faced further suppression. Ma Xian defeated them in 141 CE, but his death in battle in 144 CE led to renewed chaos. Zhao Chong and others campaigned, but the Qiang declined by the 2nd century CE. During the Han dynasty's decline, Qiang allied with Yellow Turban rebels in 184 CE. By the 3rd century CE, the Qiang had fragmented into 150 tribes, with the Zhong Qiang being the most powerful, fielding over 100,000 warriors. The Yuezhi Hu, a related group, intermarried with Qiang and lived in Huangzhong.

King Yuezhi was killed by Bao Shuandun, and the remaining tribes dispersed and crossed Congling to the west. Among them, the weak ones went south into the mountains, lived among the Qiang tribes, and intermarried with the Qiang people. When Husband General Huo Qubing defeated the Xiongnu, captured the Xihe area, and opened up Huangzhong, the Yuezhi came to surrender and lived mixed with the Han people. Although they relied on the imperial court, they hesitated to wait and see. They followed the Han army to fight, and their fighting intensity also changed with the strength of the Han army's situation. Their clothing, food, and language are roughly the same as those of the Qiang people, and they also use their father's name and mother's surname as tribal titles. There are seven large tribes, and the total number of those who can fight is more than 9,000, distributed in Huangzhong and Lingju. There are still hundreds of households in Zhangye, called Yiconghu. In the first year of Zhongping, they rebelled with Beigong Boyu and others, killing Ling Zheng, the captain of the Qiang Protector, and Chen Yi, the prefect of Jincheng, and then invaded Longyou to cause chaos. On Japan: The Qiang and Rong have been causing harm for a long time since the third generation. During the Han Dynasty, they were quite weak compared to the Xiongnu, but after the Guangwu Zhongxing, their harm to the border gradually became serious. The imperial court made mistakes in appeasing, governing and harmonizing the Qiang and Rong, and the army generals also violated their promises and trustworthiness. Some of the Qiang people who surrendered to the imperial court fell into poverty and embarrassment in the hands of the powerful, and some were forced to work as slaves and do manual labor. Sometimes when the border reconnaissance is peaceful, they will be angry and try to cause chaos; once drums and drums and military revolution suddenly arise, they will hang their quivers and panic like birds. Therefore, during the Yongchu period, the various tribes of the Qiang people protruded like a swarm of bees. So they resolved their hatreds, made alliances and swore an oath, attracted powerful people from the mountains, and then greeted each other and gathered together, holding up trees as weapons and carrying firewood as shields. The military chariots and war horses raised dust and ran rampant in the Sanfu area; they usurped the name of the emperor and wreaked havoc in the north.
target: The text concludes that the Qiang's persistent harm stemmed from Han mismanagement, including broken promises and exploitation. The Yongchu period saw widespread rebellion, with Qiang plundering Sanfu and cutting off Longxi. Despite costly campaigns by generals like Deng Lu and Ren Shang, the Han failed to achieve lasting peace. The author criticizes the policy of relocating Qiang into Han territory, which exacerbated conflicts. Ultimately, the Qiang were suppressed by Duan Yi, but the Han dynasty's decline followed. The narrative emphasizes the cyclical nature of Qiang-Han relations, marked by rebellion, suppression, and eventual fragmentation.

source: Preface to the biographies of Yimin. "The Book of Changes" says: The meaning of Dun Gua is very great! He also said: Don't serve princes and nobles, keep your noble reputation. Therefore, Emperor Yao took heaven as the law and could not make Chao Fu and Xu You accept his throne; King Wu of Zhou was a perfect man, and in the end he could only fulfill the innocent reputation of Boyi and Shuqi, the two sons of Lord Guzhu, for not eating Zhou Su. Since then, the trend of seclusion has become more popular. Most people's deeds are roughly the same, but their motivations for seclusion are very different. Some live in seclusion to satisfy their ambitions; some avoid the entanglements of big men to perfect their moral character; some seek a quiet environment to suppress impatience; some avoid dangerous disputes to seek temporary safety; some are cynical to establish their integrity; some despise wealth and honor to preserve their innocence. However, seeing that they are willing to work in the fields and fish in the rivers and seas, must they be so interested in fish, birds, forests and grass? But everyone has different personalities. Therefore, even though Liu Xiahui suffered humiliation and was dismissed three times, he still refused to leave Qi. Lu Zhonglian would rather jump into the sea and die than respect Qin as emperor. Even his status as the king of a thousand-year-old country could not tempt him. If they were put in another position, they wouldn't act the same way. Their stubbornness does have the appearance of seeking fame and fame, but they are like cicadas shed in the dust, jumping out of this filthy environment, far behind those who sharpen their heads to pursue fame and fortune. Xunzi said it well: If you have high ambitions, you will look down on wealth; if you are moral, you will look down on princes. The middle path of the Han Dynasty declined and Wang Mang usurped the throne. People with lofty ideals had strong indignation.
target: The preface explains that seclusion has been a respected tradition since ancient times, as seen in figures like Chao Fu and Xu You, who refused Yao’s throne, and Boyi and Shuqi, who rejected Zhou’s rule. The motivations for seclusion vary: some seek to fulfill ambitions, perfect moral character, suppress impatience, avoid danger, establish integrity, or preserve innocence. While some criticize such acts as seeking fame, the preface argues that true hermits transcend worldly pursuits, as Xunzi noted: high ambitions despise wealth, and strong morals disdain princes.

source: The middle path of the Han Dynasty declined and Wang Mang usurped the throne. People with lofty ideals had strong indignation. At that time, I don’t know how many people threw away their black gauze hats and left their official positions. Yang Xiong said: The swan geese flew so high that the hunter’s arrow missed. It is a metaphor for those who have traveled far away. Emperor Guangwu came to the throne and sat sideways waiting for the wise men. He was hungry and thirsty. He sent people to recruit people from Qiuyuan with banners, silk and push carts. There was an endless stream of messengers on the rugged mountain roads. For example, Xue Fang, Feng Meng and others invited him but refused to come out. Yan Guang, Zhou Dang, Wang Ba and others came out but refused to take their seats. At that time, all conditions were in place, and people with lofty ideals were also thinking about the sage emperor. Isn't this a great opportunity to promote the free people and make the people of the world surrender? Emperor Suzong also paid courtesy to Zheng Jun and hired Gao Feng to complete their honor. Since then, the emperor's virtue has gradually declined, and villains have taken over. The hermits are wary and feel that it is shameful to stand with those ministers. They even walk away, losing the way of neutrality. Now record those who lived in seclusion, and those who returned to seclusion one after another after coming out, are listed in this article. Xiang Changchuan, whose courtesy name is Ziping, was born in Chaoge, Hanoi. He lives in seclusion and does not serve as an official. He has a moderate personality and is proficient in Laozi and the Book of Changes. He was poor and had no resources for food. If a good person gave him some food, he would accept part of it and return the rest. Wang Mang's chief minister, Wang Yi, summoned him, but it took several years for him to arrive. He wanted to recommend him to Wang Mang, but Xiang Chang resolutely refused. Hidden at home. After reading the "Book of Changes" to the two hexagrams "Loss" and "Benefit", I sighed deeply and said: I already know that wealth is worse than poverty, and nobleness is worse than lowliness, but I don't know how death is worse than life. During the Jianwu period, after his son and girl got married, he severed ties with his family and said, "Just think of me as dead." So he acted randomly and traveled to the famous Five Mountains with his friend Beihai Qinqing, but in the end he didn't know where he ended up. Feng Meng's biography, Feng Meng's courtesy name is Zikang, and he was born in Duchang, Beihai. His family was poor and he worked as a pavilion chief in the county. At that time, the county captain passed by the pavilion, and Peng Meng was waiting to greet him. He dropped his wooden shield and sighed, "How can a man serve as a servant for others?" So he went to Chang'an to study and became proficient in the Spring and Autumn Classic. At this time, Wang Mang killed his son Yu. Pengmeng said to his friends: The three cardinal principles are severed!
target: During Wang Mang’s usurpation, many abandoned office, and under Emperor Guangwu, hermits like Yan Guang and Zhou Dang were recruited but often refused to serve. The text records those who lived in seclusion or withdrew after serving. Xiang Changchuan, a hermit from Hanoi, refused Wang Mang’s summons, studied the *Book of Changes*, and after his children married, he severed ties with his family and disappeared into the Five Mountains. Feng Meng, from Beihai, left his post as a pavilion chief, studied the *Spring and Autumn Annals*, and fled to Liaodong after Wang Mang killed his son. He later refused Guangwu’s summons, claiming old age and disorientation, and died in seclusion. Zhou Dang, a wealthy man from Taiyuan, studied in Chang’an, fought a duel over an old insult, and later refused to serve Wang Mang. Under Guangwu, he was summoned but declined, and the emperor defended his choice, granting him silk. Zhou Dang wrote books and died in Mianchi.

source: Boyi and Shuqi did not eat millet from the Zhou Dynasty, and the Zhou party in Taiyuan did not receive my salary, but they also had their own ambitions. Give forty pieces of silk. Zhou Dang lived in seclusion in Mianchi, wrote the first and second chapters of the book, and died. The people of the city considered him a worthy person and built a temple to commemorate him. At first, Zhou Dang, Tan Xianbosheng and Yanmen Yinmo, both of the same county, kept their integrity and refused to serve as officials for Wang Mang. During the Jianwu period, he could not be summoned. Wang Ba's biography, Wang Ba's courtesy name is Ru Zhong, and he was born in Guangwu, Taiyuan. There are clear festivals in childhood. When Wang Mang usurped the throne, he gave up his crown and belt and broke off all relations with the officials. During the Jianwu period, he was called to the minister's office and paid homage to him by name, but not as a minister. Someone asked him why. Ba said: The emperor has dissatisfaction with his subjects, and the princes have dissatisfaction with others. Situ Houba gave way to Wang Ba. Yan Yang ruined the king's domineering ways: Wang Ruzhong, a secular party in Taiyuan, had this kind of trend. So it was stopped. Returned home due to illness. Live in seclusion and keep your ambitions, with a thatched hut. After failing to call for several times, he died. Yan Guangzhuan, Yan Guang, courtesy name Ziling, also known as Zun, was born in Yuyao, Kuaiji. He became famous at a young age and traveled and studied with Emperor Guangwu. When Guangwu became emperor, Yan Guang changed his name and lived in seclusion. The emperor missed his talent, so he sent someone with the image to find it.
target: Wang Ba, also from Taiyuan, abandoned his official post during Wang Mang’s reign and refused to serve Guangwu, citing the emperor’s lack of respect for his subjects. Yan Guang, a childhood friend of Guangwu, changed his name and fished in seclusion. The emperor found him, but Yan Guang refused to serve, famously putting his feet on Guangwu’s belly while sleeping.

source: So he got in the car and left with a sigh. Another time, the emperor invited Yan Guang in and talked with him about the past. The two talked to each other for several days. The emperor calmly said to Yan Guang: How am I better than before? Answer: You are a little fatter than before. So they slept together, Yan Guang put his feet on Guangwu's belly. The next day, Taishi reported that there was a guest star in the sky invading the throne of the emperor, and the situation was urgent. The emperor smiled and said: I am sleeping with my old friend Yan Ziling! Emperor Guangwu worshiped Yan Guang as an admonishment official, but Yan Guang refused to do so, so he farmed in Fuchun Mountain. Later generations called the place where Yan Guang fished Yan Linglai. In the seventeenth year of Jianwu's reign, he sent someone to invite Yan Guang, but he still refused to come out. Yan Guang lived to the age of eighty and died at home. The biography of Jing Dan, named Dachun, was born in Fufeng. When he was young, he studied in Taixue. He was proficient in the Five Classics and was good at talking about it. Therefore, people in the capital said this: The Five Classics are rich in content and spring.
target: He later farmed in Fuchun Mountain and died at home. Jing Dan, a scholar from Fufeng, was known for his pride and refused invitations from princes. When tricked into a banquet by a relative of the empress, he criticized the host’s meager food and left, living in seclusion thereafter.

source: Later, Liang Hong entered Taixue to study. Because his family was poor, he was very frugal. He has read a lot of books and is very proficient, but he doesn't like writing articles. After studying, he herded pigs in Shanglin Garden. Once, a fire accidentally broke out and burned down someone else's house. Liang Hong found the burned house, learned about the damage, and used pigs as compensation. The owner of that house is still too few. Liang Hong said: I have no other property and am willing to use my own labor as compensation. The master agreed. So I worked very hard in the morning and evening. The neighbor old man saw that Liang Hong was not an ordinary person, so he blamed the owner of the house and called Liang Hong an elder. From then on, the owner respected Liang Hong and returned all his pigs.
target: Liang Hong, from Fufeng, studied in Taixue, worked as a pig herder, and compensated a neighbor for a fire by labor.

source: When Liang Hong heard about it, he went to pay the betrothal gift. The woman requires cloth clothes, hemp shoes, thread baskets, textiles and other tools as dowry. When you get married, you dress up and enter the house. After seven days, Liang Hong stopped talking to his wife. The wife knelt in front of the bed and said: I heard that you have high moral character and are very strict in choosing your partners. You have not agreed to several women, and I have also chosen several people. Now that I have been chosen by you, please tell me clearly if I have made any mistakes so that I can correct them. Liang Hong said: I want to find someone who is dressed simply and live in seclusion in the mountains together. Now that you are wearing nice clothes and applying makeup, are you the person I want? The wife said: I tested you on purpose. I still have clothes for seclusion. So he changed his hair into a bun, put on cloth clothes, dressed himself up for work, and stepped forward. Liang Hong said happily: "This is really Liang Hong's wife!" You can spend a lifetime with me! So he named her De Yao and named her Meng Guang. Not long after, the wife said: I often hear that you want to live in seclusion to avoid danger. Why are you silent now? Do you want to bow to power? Liang Hong said: You are right. So they went into Baling Mountain together and started farming and weaving. On weekdays, he spends his time reading poetry and playing the piano. I often envy the elegant people of my predecessors and write hymns for the twenty-four sages after Shangshan Sihao. One day, I went out along the east gate and passed the capital, and wrote a song called "Song of Five Ains": Climbing Beimang Mountain, I saw that the imperial capital was very gorgeous, the palaces towered into the clouds, and the hard work of life was infinite and endless.
target: He married Meng Guang, who dressed simply and shared his life of seclusion. They fled to Baling Mountain, then to Wu, where Liang Hong worked as a rice pounder.

source: My heart is sad and unhappy, and my stomach is full of knots and worries. The crowd kept shouting, and it was hard to find a place to hide. So when I arrived in Wu, I found a wealthy man named Gao Botong who lived under the eaves and pounded rice for others. When he comes home every day, his wife cooks for him. She dare not raise her eyes to look at her husband, but often raises the plate to her eyebrows. Botong felt strange when he saw it, so he said: "This hired man can make his wife respect him so much. He is definitely not an ordinary person." So he was allowed to live at home. Liang Hong wrote more than ten articles behind closed doors. Later, he fell ill and felt very sleepy, so he told his master: "In the past, Yanling Jizi buried his son between Yingbo and did not go to the countryside. After I die, please don't let my son carry the coffin back."
target: His wife served him with respect, raising the tray to her eyebrows. Liang Hong died in Wu and was buried near the martyr Yaoli.

source: Liang Hong wrote more than ten articles behind closed doors. Later, he fell ill and felt very sleepy, so he told his master: "In the past, Yanling Jizi buried his son between Yingbo and did not go to the countryside. After I die, please don't let my son carry the coffin back." After Liang Hong died, Bo Tong and others buried him next to Yaoli's grave in the state of Wu. They all said: Yaoli was a martyr, and Liang Boluan was very noble, which allowed them to get close. After the burial, the wife returned to Fufeng. At first, Liang Hong's friend Gao Hui from Jingzhao liked to read "Laozi" when he was young and lived in seclusion in Huayin Mountain. When Liang Hong traveled east, he thought of Gao Hui and wrote a poem: Birds are chirping looking for friends, and I also think of Gao Hui, hoping he can come here. The two never met again. Gao Hui was also a proud man and had never been an official in his life. Gao Fengzhuan, Gao Feng, courtesy name Wentong, was born in Nanyang Ye. When he was young, he was a student, and his family was engaged in farming. However, Gao Feng specialized in reading and never rested day and night. My wife once went to work in the fields and dried the wheat in the courtyard, calling Gao Feng to protect the chickens. At this time, it was raining heavily, but Gao Feng was holding a bamboo pole and chanting scriptures. Unconsciously, the rainwater flowed into the wheat.
target: Gao Feng, a scholar from Nanyang, was so absorbed in reading that he let rain ruin his wheat.

source: Later he became a famous Confucian and taught his disciples in the Western Tang Mountains. Neighbors who were fighting over property were fighting with weapons. Gao Feng went to try to persuade him. As a last resort, he took off his turban, knelt, and resolutely requested: "Why have you forgotten all about benevolence, righteousness, and humiliation?" The combatants were moved and put down their weapons to apologize to him. Gao Feng was old, but he persisted in his ambitions tirelessly, and his reputation spread far and wide. The eunuch continued to summon him, but Gao Feng was afraid that he would not be able to avoid it. He claimed that he was from the Wu family and should not be an official. He also pretended to have a lawsuit with his widowed sister-in-law over property, so he did not go out to serve as an official. He fished invisibly and died at home. Tai Tong's biography, Tai Tong's courtesy name is Xiaowei, and he was born in Ye, Wei County. He lives in seclusion in Wu'an Mountain, digging caves as his residence and collecting medicine as his occupation. During the early years of Jian's reign, he was not summoned by the state. When the governor arrived at Ye, he sent an official to visit Tai Tong. Tong Zaibing went to express his thanks. The governor took the meeting gift and asked Tong: "It's very hard for Xiaowei to live like this. What should I do?" Tong said: Fortunately, I was able to save my life and maintain my peace. Isn't it like having an envoy read out the imperial edict in the morning and working hard at night? Isn't it not painful? So he left, secluded himself, and never disappeared. According to the biography of Han Kang, Han Kang's courtesy name was Boxiu, also known as Tianxiu, and he was a native of Baling, Jingzhao. The family background is very famous. He often went to famous mountains to collect medicinal herbs and sold them in Chang'an market. The price was always the same for more than thirty years. At that time, a girl asked Han Kang to buy medicine, but Kang insisted that the original price should remain unchanged. The girl lost her temper and said: Are you Han Boxiu? Aren't they sold at two prices? Han Kang sighed and said: "I originally wanted to keep my name from others, but now the little girl knows my name, why are I selling medicine?" So he fled to Baling Mountain. The doctor invited Han Kang several times on his bus, but Han Kang never came. Emperor Huan prepared a black silk curtain as a gift and used a carriage to hire him. The envoy went to Han Kang's home with the emperor's edict, but Han Kang had no choice but to agree. But instead of taking an An chariot, he took a diesel chariot and set off early in the morning before the messenger set off. When they arrived at the pavilion, the pavilion chief knew that Han Zhengjun would pass by, so he sent someone to repair the road and bridge with a cow. Suddenly, he saw Han Kang arriving in a chariot and wearing a scarf. Thinking that he was an old man farming, he asked someone to take the cow away. Han Kang untied the cow in front of the car and gave it to him. Soon after, the official arrived and found that the old man who had the cow taken away was Zheng Jun. The envoy wanted to tell the emperor to kill the pavilion chief. Han Kang said, "I gave him this cow myself. What's the crime of the pavilion chief?" The messenger gave up. Han Kang fled halfway, and later died of a long life without any illness. Jiao Shen's biography, whose courtesy name is Zhongyan, was born in Maoling, Fufeng. When I was young, I loved the learning of Huangdi and Laozi. I lived in seclusion in the valley, built a house in a cave, and admired the skills of pine and Qiao Daoyin.
target: He mediated disputes and refused official summons, pretending to have a lawsuit to avoid service. Tai Tong, from Wei County, lived in a cave, collected herbs, and refused summons, stating his life was peaceful compared to officials’ toil. Han Kang, from Jingzhao, sold herbs at a fixed price for thirty years. When a girl recognized him, he fled to Baling Mountain and refused Emperor Huan’s summons, escaping halfway. Jiao Shen, from Fufeng, studied Huang-Lao, lived in a cave, and refused to marry. He predicted his death and later was seen in Dunhuang, rumored to be immortal. Dai Liang, from Runan, imitated his mother’s braying for fun, and after her death, he ate meat while mourning, arguing that rituals should not suppress genuine emotion. He refused office and fled to Jiangxia, marrying off his five daughters with simple dowries.

source: He is a great Confucian in Kansai who is eager to learn and not stick to any particular school. He is well versed in both internal and external classics. Disciples came from far away, including Chen Liu, Fan Ran and hundreds of others. The true nature of Dharma is quiet and has few desires, and is not interested in hearing about human affairs. The prefect asked to see him, and Fa Zhen arrived with a scarf. The prefect said: In the past, although Duke Ai of Lu was not a virtuous man, Zhongni still served as his minister. The prefect is weak, and I would like to ask you to serve as a meritorious officer and praise this dynasty. How about it? Fazhen said: Because the Ming Dynasty treated me with such courtesy, I dare not stay with the guests. If you want to use me as an official, I will be north of Beishan and south of Nanshan. The prefect felt strange and did not dare to say anything more. When setting up a government office and promoting virtuous people, the Dharma and the truth are not enough. Tongjun Tian Ruo recommends Fa Zhen Dao: A scholar of Fa Zhen, proficient in poetry, calligraphy, etiquette, and music, with all the knowledge and classics, goes out of the deep mountains, entertains himself peacefully, and is happy to forget his worries. He will follow Lao Tzu's high footsteps and will not be succumbed to Xuan Xunxun's etiquette. I wish that the Holy Dynasty would add the post of Sangong, and I would definitely be able to sing the song "Qing Temple" and attract the phoenix. It happened that Emperor Shun was on a hunting tour in the west, and Tian Ruo recommended him. Emperor Xu wanted to invite him, so he called him four times. Fazhen said: Since I can't escape from this world, how can I drink the water that Xuyou washes my ears with? So he lived in seclusion. My friend Guo Zhengcheng said: Fazhen's name can be heard, but his body is rare. If he runs away from his name but his name follows me, he avoids his name but his name follows me. He can be regarded as a master of all generations. So they published a book praising him and called him Mr. Xuande. He died at the age of eighty-nine, five years after his death. The biography of Hanyin Laofu, Hanyin Laofu, I don’t know who he is. During the Yanxi period of Emperor Huan, the emperor was lucky enough to visit the mausoleum, pass by Yunmeng, and visit the Mianshui River. The common people all went to see it, and there was an old man who continued to farm alone. Zhang Wen, the minister of Nanyang, felt strange and sent someone to ask: "People are coming to watch, but my father keeps plowing alone. Why?"
target: Fa Zhen, a great Confucian from Fufeng, refused a prefect’s offer of office, saying he would rather be north of Beishan or south of Nanshan. He was recommended to Emperor Shun but declined, living in seclusion and earning the title Mr. Xuande. The Hanyin Old Man, during Emperor Huan’s visit, continued plowing and criticized the emperor for indulging in leisure while the people suffered.

source: So they hugged each other and cried. The old father walked past in a hurry, leaning on his staff and sighing: Oh, why is the second doctor crying so sadly? The dragon does not hide its scales, the phoenix does not hide its feathers, the snare is hung high, no matter where it goes, what is the use of crying? The two wanted to talk to him, but left without knowing where they ended up. The biography of Pang Gong, Pang Gong, was from Xiangyang, Nanjun. They live in the south of Xian Mountain and have never been to the city. The husband and wife treat each other as if they were guests. Liu Biao, the governor of Jingzhou, invited him several times but could not give in, so he went to visit him. He said to him: If you can protect yourself, how can you protect the world? Pang Gong laughed and said: "The swan makes its nest in the high forest, and only has a place to rest at night; the stork makes its nest in the abyss, and only finds its home at night. People's choices and actions are also human nests." For the time being, everyone has his own place to stay, the world is not protected. So he plowed the soil on the ridges while his wife weeded the fields. Liu Biao pointed out and asked: "Master works in the fields and refuses to receive official salary. What will he leave to his descendants in the future?" Pang Gong said: "Everyone in the world leaves danger to their descendants, but now I leave peace to our descendants. Although the legacy is different, it can't be regarded as no legacy." Liu Biao sighed and left. Later, Pang Gong and his wife went to Lumen Mountain, but they never came back because they were collecting medicinal herbs.
target: The Chenliu Old Man, during the party insurrection, told weeping officials that crying was useless, as the world’s traps were everywhere. Pang Gong, from Xiangyang, refused Liu Biao’s summons, saying he left peace to his descendants, not danger. He and his wife later retreated to Lumen Mountain.

source: Deng Yu, courtesy name Zhonghua, was a native of Xinye County, Nanyang County. At the age of thirteen, he was able to recite poems and studied under a teacher in Chang'an. At that time, Guangwu was also traveling to the capital to study. Although Deng Yu was young, when he saw Guangwu, he knew that he was not an ordinary person, so he got close to him. Return home after a few years. When the Han army rose up and Gengshi came to the throne, many heroes recommended Deng Yu, but Deng Yu refused to comply. Guangwu said: Even so, what do you want to do? Deng Yu said: I hope that Duke Ming's majesty will spread throughout the world, and I will be able to do my best for Duke Ming and go down in history. Guangwu laughed and left him to sleep and chat. Deng Yujin said: Although Guanxi was the capital of Gengshi, there is no stability in Shandong now. The likes of Red Eyebrow and Qingdu are often robbed by tens of thousands, and people in Sanfu area often gather in groups under the guise of names. Gengshi did not defeat them, and they did not listen to the command and ruling. The generals were all mediocre people who wanted to get rich, compete for power, and be happy sooner or later. They were not loyal, wise, foresighted, and really wanted to respect the Lord and appease the people. The four parties are falling apart and the situation is clearly visible. Although Ming Gong has established a meritorious service in assisting the royal family, he may not be able to achieve great success. For the current plan, it is better to recruit heroes from all over the world, make sure to please the people, build the great cause of the great ancestor, and save the lives of the people. It is enough to pacify the world with public virtue and talent. Emperor Guangwu was so pleased that he ordered everyone around him to call Deng Yu General Deng. Let him stay in the tent and discuss strategic plans together. When Wang Lang raised his army, Guangwu went from Ji to Xindu and sent Deng Yu to recruit "quick troops" from various counties. He got thousands of people and ordered him to personally lead them to attack Leyang County. Deng Yu said: Now there is chaos in the sea, and people miss Ming Jun like a baby longing for its loving mother. In ancient times, it was the strength of virtue, not the size of the land, that made great achievements and conquered the world. Guangwu is happy.
target: Deng Yu, courtesy name Zhonghua, was from Xinye County, Nanyang. At thirteen, he could recite poems and studied in Chang'an, where he befriended Guangwu, recognizing his extraordinary nature. After returning home, he refused offers from other heroes when the Han army rose. He told Guangwu he wished to serve him and achieve lasting fame. Guangwu kept him close, and Deng Yu advised that while Gengshi held Guanxi, instability in Shandong and bandit groups like the Red Eyebrows threatened order. He urged Guangwu to recruit heroes, win over the people, and build a great cause. Guangwu appointed him General Deng and consulted him on strategies.

source: Let him stay in the tent and discuss strategic plans together. When Wang Lang raised his army, Guangwu went from Ji to Xindu and sent Deng Yu to recruit "quick troops" from various counties. He got thousands of people and ordered him to personally lead them to attack Leyang County. Deng Yu said: Now there is chaos in the sea, and people miss Ming Jun like a baby longing for its loving mother. In ancient times, it was the strength of virtue, not the size of the land, that made great achievements and conquered the world. Guangwu is happy. When appointing generals at that time, they often visited Deng Yu. The talents recommended by Deng Yu were all worthy of their positions. Guangwu believed that Deng Yu knew people. He was sent to lead another cavalry team with Gai Yan and others to attack the bronze horses in Qingyang. Gai Yan and others arrived first, but lost the battle and retreated to protect the city. They were trapped by the thieves. Deng Yu advanced to fight with the thieves, defeated the thieves and captured their general alive. From Guangwu chasing the thieves to Puyang, they won consecutive battles and Beizhou was generally pacified. When Chimei entered the pass in the west, Gengshi sent Duke Kuang of Dingguo, Chengdan of Xiangyi, General Liu Jun of Anti-Wei and other generals to guard Hedong and Hongnong counties respectively to resist. The Red Eyebrow tribe gathered in large numbers, and Wang Kuang and others could not resist it. Guangwu expected that the Red Eyebrow Army would break through Chang'an and wanted to take advantage of the opportunity to annex Guanzhong. However, he was busy with Shandong and did not know who to entrust with the Western Expedition. Since Deng Yu had the demeanor of a general, he gave him the strategy of Western Expedition. He worshiped Deng Yu as the former general and divided his 20,000 elite troops equally. He sent him to the west and ordered Deng Yu to select the generals and subordinates who could join him in the western expedition. So Han Xin was appointed as the military advisor, Li Wen, Li Chun, and Cheng Liu were used as sacrificial wines, Feng Yiyin was appointed as General Jinu, Fan Chong was appointed General Xiaoqi, Zong Xin was appointed General Chariot, Deng Xun was appointed General Jianwei, Geng Jinjin was appointed General Red Eyebrow, and Zuo Yu was appointed General Advisor, and they led the army westward. In the first month of the first year of Jianwu, Deng Yu entered Hedong County from Jiguan. The captain of Hedong County guarded the pass and refused to open it. Deng Yu attacked for ten days and broke through the pass, seizing more than a thousand vehicles with baggage. He entered Anyi and was unable to capture it for several months. Gengshi General Fan Shen led tens of thousands of people and crossed Dayang to attack Deng Yu. Deng Yu sent his generals to attack south of Jie County, defeated Fan Shen's army and beheaded Fan Shen.
target: Deng Yu recruited troops for Guangwu, defeating enemies like the bronze horses in Qingyang. When the Red Eyebrows threatened, Guangwu entrusted Deng Yu with the Western Expedition, appointing him Former General with 20,000 elite troops. In the first year of Jianwu, Deng Yu entered Hedong, defeating Gengshi generals and pacifying the region. Guangwu ascended the throne and made Deng Yu Chief Minister, praising his loyalty and achievements. At twenty-four, Deng Yu crossed into Xiayang, defeating more enemies as the Red Eyebrows entered Chang'an. His disciplined troops attracted many followers, and he became famous in Guanxi.

source: At this time, Sanfu's armies were defeated one after another. The Red Eyebrow Army brutally plundered wherever they passed, and the people did not know where they were going. I heard that Deng Yu always took advantage of victory and his troops were well-disciplined, so they all came to welcome Deng Yu's army with their young and old. Thousands of people returned every day, and the crowd was said to be millions. Wherever Deng Yu went, he often stopped to pay his respects and express his condolences. Fathers and children, with their white hair hanging in buns, crowded under his car. They were all grateful and happy, so Deng Yu became famous in Guanxi. The emperor praised him and wrote several letters praising him. All the generals and heroes advised Deng Yu to attack Chang'an directly. Deng Yu said: Otherwise, although we have many troops now, there are few who can fight. There will be no savings to rely on in the front, and there will be no resources for transfer behind. The Red Eyebrow Army had just captured Chang'an, with abundant wealth and unstoppable morale. However, thieves live in groups and have no plan for the whole day. Although there is a lot of wealth, there are many changes, how can they hold on? The three counties of Shangjun, Beidi, and Anding are vast, sparsely populated, and plentiful in grain, rice, and livestock. We are temporarily reorganizing the army in the north, providing food and nourishing the soldiers, so as to observe the weaknesses of the Red Eyebrow Army, and then try to attack them! So he led his army north to Yuyi County. Wherever Deng Yu went, he defeated the Red Eyebrow Army's various camps and defenses, and all counties and counties opened their doors and surrendered.
target: Deng Yu advised against directly attacking Chang'an, citing the Red Eyebrows' strength and advocating a strategy of gathering resources in the north to observe their weaknesses. He led his army north, defeating Red Eyebrow camps and gaining surrenders. However, internal conflicts among his generals led to setbacks. In the second year of Jianwu, Deng Yu was made Marquis of Liang.

source: Deng Yu led his troops to fight with Yan Cen in Lantian, but failed, so he went to Yunyang. Liu Jia, the king of Hanzhong, surrendered to Deng Yu. Liu Jiaxian Li Bao was arrogant and rude, so Deng Yu killed him. Li Bao's younger brother gathered Li Bao's troops to attack Deng Yu and killed the general Geng Jinjin. Since Feng Yiyin rebelled against Deng Yu, Deng Yu's prestige was damaged. At this time, the Red Eyebrow Army returned to Chang'an again. Deng Yu fought with it and was defeated. When they arrived at Gaoling, the soldiers were hungry and ate jujube vegetables to survive. The emperor then summoned Deng Yu back and issued an edict: "Chimei is short of food, so he will naturally come eastward. I only need to break the horse's staff and whip him to defeat him." The generals are not something to worry about, so don't rush into the army rashly. Deng Yu felt ashamed that he had not accomplished anything since he had been appointed. He sent hungry soldiers to fight several times, but was often unfavorable. In the spring of the third year, he attacked Chimei with Deng Hong, the chariot and cavalry general, but was defeated by Chimei. All his troops died and dispersed. He returned to Yiyang alone with twenty-four cavalry, and returned the seal to Da Situ and Liang Hou as apology. The imperial edict was returned to Hou Yinshou. After a few months, I paid homage to the right general.
target: He fought the Red Eyebrows but faced defeats, and Guangwu recalled him, advising caution. Deng Yu, ashamed, continued fighting but was ultimately defeated in the third year, returning to Yiyang with few men and resigning his posts. He was later reinstated as Right General and achieved victories against Yan Cen.

source: After a few months, I paid homage to the right general. Since Yancen was defeated in Dongyang, he cooperated with Qin Feng. In the spring of the fourth year, they invaded the Shunyang area again. He sent Deng Yu to protect General Deng Ye of the Fu Han Dynasty and General Yu Kuang of the Fu Han Dynasty, and defeated Yan Cen against Deng. He pursued them to Wudang and defeated Yan Cen again. Cen fled to Hanzhong, and the rest of the party surrendered. In the 13th year of Jianwu's reign, the world was peaceful, and all the meritorious officials increased their households. They appointed Deng Yu as the Marquis of Gaomi and received the taxes from the four counties of Gaomi, Chang'an, Yi'an, and Chunyu. The emperor considered Deng Yu's meritorious service and made Deng Yu's younger brother Deng Kuan the prince of the Ming Dynasty. Later, the titles of left and right generals were revoked, and they were granted special access to the court to see the emperor. Deng Yu was civilized at heart, honest, honest and considerate in his behavior, and he served his mother very filially. The world has been peaceful, and people often want to distance themselves from fame and power. He had thirteen children, and each of them mastered a skill. By regulating family rules and educating children and grandchildren, you can become a model for future generations. All expenses are derived from fiefdom taxes, and no private property is repaired or private gain is sought. Therefore the emperor respects him more. In the first year of the Zhongyuan Dynasty, he acted as Situ again. From the emperor's tour of Shandong, he went to Mount Tai to build an altar to worship heaven. When Xianzong came to the throne, because Deng Yu was the late emperor, he was worshiped as Taifu. When he came to court, he was ordered to stand facing east and treated like a guest, and he was very respected and favored. In the first year of Yongping, Deng Yu died at the age of fifty-seven. Later, although the power of the city was lost, the troops dispersed in Yiyang, and Situ's seal and ribbon were handed over, the marquis still died in his years, glorious and haggard, but his subordinates were always the same. He was promoted to an official, and he returned to the court in frustration. Guangwu never doubted him, so that future generations would not see any flaws or barriers in the beauty of the monarch and his ministers. Isn't this the most perfect act of a benevolent gentleman? Kou Xun, courtesy name Ziyi, was from Changping County, Shanggu County, and his surname has been prominent for generations. Kou Xun was initially a meritorious officer of the county, and the prefect Geng Kuang thought highly of him. When Wang Mang failed, Gengshi ascended the throne and sent envoys to declare to the various counties that those who surrendered first would have their titles restored. Kou Xun followed Geng Kuang to greet the envoy at the border. Geng Kuang presented the seal and ribbon. The envoy accepted it and had no intention of returning it all night. Kou Xun brought weapons to see the envoy. Please return the seal and ribbon. The messenger refused to give it and said: I am the messenger of the King of Heaven. Does the master want to coerce me? Now that the world has been settled, the country's credibility has not been declared, so the king can establish a talisman to carry out missions to all directions. Everyone in the county and country stretches their necks and tilts their ears, watching for the wind and returning to their fate. Now that you first arrived in Shanggu, you destroyed Daxin, discouraged the whole county's desire to return to Hue, and created a gap for centrifugal betrayal. How will you command other counties? Moreover, Lord Geng was in Shanggu and had been trusted by the officials and the people for a long time. Now if he is replaced, if he is succeeded by a virtuous man, Geng will be uneasy, and if he is an unworthy person, he will be reborn in chaos. In order to make your plans better, there is no better way to restore Geng Kuang's position as governor to bring peace to the people. The envoy did not agree, and Kou Xun angrily scolded the people around him to summon Geng Kuang according to the envoy's order. When Geng Kuang arrived, Kou Xun gave the seal and ribbon to Geng Kuang. The envoy had no choice but to reinstate Geng Kuang in accordance with the emperor's will. Geng Kuang returned from his post. When Wang Lang raised his troops, he sent generals to attack Shanggu and urgently ordered Geng Kuang to send troops. Kou Xun and his disciple Yu Minye jointly said to Geng Kuang: Handan has suddenly risen, and it is difficult to trust and return.
target: Kou Xun, courtesy name Ziyi, was from Changping, Shanggu, from a prominent family. He served as a county officer under Prefect Geng Kuang. When Wang Lang rose, Kou Xun advised Geng Kuang to ally with Guangwu, citing his virtue. He attacked Handan's envoys and joined Guangwu, who made him a partial general. source: Now I heard that Grand Sima Liu Gong was the half-brother of Liu Boxheng. Deng Yu said: In the past, Emperor Gaozu appointed Xiao He to Guanzhong, and he no longer had to worry about looking west, so he was able to plan Shandong carefully and achieve great success. Today, Hanoi is adjacent to the Yellow River. It is very stable and has a well-established household registration. It is connected to Dang in the north and close to Luoyang in the south. When Zhu Tuna heard that Guangwu was heading north and Hanoi was isolated, he sent his general Su Mao and deputy general Jia Qiang to lead more than 30,000 troops across the Gong River to attack Wen. target: Kou Xun fortified Hanoi, supplying Guangwu's army with arrows, horses, and grain. When Zhu Tuna attacked Wen, Kou Xun led a swift defense, defeating Su Mao and Jia Qiang with reinforcements. source: The emperor said: The world has not yet been peaceful, how can two tigers fight privately? Today I reconcile for you. If they hear that His Majesty is heading south, the thieves will surely surrender in fear. I am willing to lead the elite as a pioneer. The people gathered in the street and said, "I hope to borrow Kou Jun from your majesty for another year." target: Kou Xun governed Runan, building schools and teaching the Spring and Autumn Annals. He pacified Yingchuan again when bandits rose, and the people begged for his continued service. He advised Guangwu against personally attacking Gaoping, but when the campaign stalled, he persuaded Gao Jun to surrender by executing his advisor. Kou Xun was known for his virtue, generosity, and learning, and was considered prime minister material.

The imperial edict granted him the service of Guanglu Dafu. After completing his service, he was worshiped as the Captain of Fengche and promoted to Dasi Nong. A few months later, he replaced Bao Yu as Taiwei. When Deng Biao was in power, he was very clean and set an example for all officials. After serving as an official for four years, he resigned due to illness. In the first year of Yuanhe, he was dismissed from office, given 300,000 yuan as a gift, and lived with a salary of 2,000 dan for the rest of his life. He also ordered Taichang to send the sacrificial meat from the ancestral temple in all seasons. The Cheng Cunwen of Yinpai County in Henan often sent sheep wine and other items on the first day of the eighth month. Emperor He ascended the throne, appointed Deng Biao as Taifu, recorded the ministerial affairs, and granted him the title of Marquis of Guannei. source: Hu Guang was lonely and poor when he was young and did housework by himself. When he grew up, he followed his elders and joined the county as a casual official. Fazhen, the son of the prefect Faxiong, came from home to visit his father. The truth of the law is quite knowledgeable. Faxiong ordered Fazhen to help him select talents when he was due to take the year-end exam. Faxiong then held a meeting with all the officials, and Fazhen himself observed from the window, so he pointed Hu Guang to warn Faxiong and inspected his filial piety and integrity. After arriving in the capital, he was tested by Zhang Zhi. Emperor An regarded Hu Guang as the best in the world. In the tenth month, he was promoted to Shangshulang and was promoted to Shangshu Pushe five times. Emperor Shun wanted to make a queen, but among the nobles there were four favored ones. He didn't know who to make, so he decided to draw lots and ask God to choose the queen. Hu Guang, together with Shangshu Guo Qian and Shi Chang, went to the court to remonstrate: I saw the imperial edict privately and thought that establishing a queen was a major event. I was humble and refused to make my own decision. I wanted to use the method of drawing lots to ask God to resolve the doubts. There are no ancestral allusions recorded in ancient books. Relying on gods and witches may not necessarily find wise men, but even if you meet such people, you are not choosing people based on virtue. Human appearance comes from nature, so there must be different appearances in heaven. We should refer to good families and choose virtuous people. If they have the same virtues, they should look at their age. If they are equal in age, they should look at their appearance. They should consider the classics and judge from the saints. Government orders are like sweating. Once they come out, they cannot be taken back. Once the edict was issued, it was seen everywhere. The minister's duty is to collect lost things, and he is deeply concerned about the responsibility, so he is anxious and ventures to state his opinions. The emperor obeyed and appointed Liang Guiren, a woman from a good family, as his queen. At that time, Zuo Xiong, the official secretary of the Ministry of Finance, proposed to reform the system of examination and examination. The age limit should be above forty years old. Confucian scholars should be tested for classics and literary officials should be tested for zhangzou. Hu Guang also wrote a letter to Chang and Qian to refute: I have heard that the kings consider it a virtue to read and take photos at the same time. Is it true for the ministers to show loyalty to them?
target: He advised Emperor Shun against drawing lots to choose a queen, advocating for selecting based on virtue, age, and appearance. He opposed Zuo Xiong's proposal to set a minimum age of 40 for officials, arguing for flexibility based on talent.

source: Chen Liu was close to the county, and now the prefect is in vacancy. Hu Guang has profound talents and is able to get rid of troubles. He is willing to participate in the election to correct the decadent customs, make people practice good and encourage them. Hu Guang stayed in power for ten years and became the prefect of Jiyin. He was dismissed for making false promises in appointing officials. He also became the prefect of Runan and went to worship Da Sinong. In the first year of Han'an, he was promoted to Situ. After the death of Emperor Zhi, he took Li Gu's place as Taiwei and recorded the affairs of the minister. Because of his decision, he established Emperor Huan and was granted the title of Marquis of Yuyang Anle Township. Abdicated due to illness. He paid homage to Sikong and returned home. Soon after, he summoned Taichang to pay homage to Taichang and was promoted to Taiwei. He was dismissed due to the solar eclipse. Return to Tai Chang and pay homage to the Taiwei. In the second year of Yanxi, General Liang Ji was killed. Hu Guang, Situ Han Jinyin, and Sikong Sunlang committed the crime of not guarding the palace. They were all reduced to one level of death, seized the title, and were dismissed as commoners. Later, he paid homage to Taizhong Dafu and Taichang. In the ninth year, he worshiped Situ again. Emperor Ling came to the throne, and together with Taifu Chen Fan, he recorded the affairs of the ministers and restored the title of his homeland. Requested to retire due to illness. When Chen Fan was killed, he took over as Taifu, and the general record remained the same. At this time, he was already eighty years old, but his mental strength was strong. The stepmother is in the hall, greeting her morning and evening, and there are only a few sticks by her side, and she does not say anything about her age. After the mother's death, she was mourned and treated with courtesy. He has a gentle and discreet personality, and is often polite and courteous. Master the practice of affairs and understand the rules of the court clearly. Although there is no tendency to be upright, it often has the benefit of making up for the shortcomings. Therefore, the proverb of the capital says: Ignore everything and ask Bo Shi, there is only Hu Gong among the mediocre people in the world. When he and Li Feng decided to make a plan, the discussion was not complete, and he married Ding Su, the official of the Central Committee. Therefore, he was ridiculed by the people at the time. Hu Guang had been in Gongtai for more than 30 years, serving six emperors with excellent courtesy and appointments. Each time he abdicated his position, resigned from illness, and was dismissed and returned to the fields. Within a year, he was promoted again. He served as Sikong once, Situ twice, Lieutenant Commander three times, and Tufu again.
target: He served as Chenliu prefect, Jiyin prefect, Runan prefect, and Da Sinong. In Han'an's 1st year, he became Situ, then Taiwei, establishing Emperor Huan and becoming Marquis of Yuyang Anle Township. He served multiple terms, including as Sikong and Taiwei, but was dismissed after Liang Ji's death. He later served under Emperor Ling as Taifu. Known for his gentle and discreet nature, he mastered court rules and was praised in the capital: "Ignore everything and ask Bo Shi, there is only Hu Gong among the mediocre." He served six emperors for over 30 years, holding high offices repeatedly. He died at 82 in Xiping's 1st year, receiving grand honors.

source: ◆Zheng Taichuan, also named Gongye, was born in Kaifeng, Henan. The great-grandson of Sinong Zheng Zhong. He was talented when he was young. In the last years of Emperor Ling's reign, Mrs. Zheng knew that the world would be in chaos, so she secretly made friends with heroes. His family was very wealthy, with 400 hectares of land, but he often had no food to eat. He was very famous, and everyone in Shandong knew about him. At the beginning, he was promoted to Xiaolian, and he was recruited from the three government offices and buses, but he was not accepted. After the general He Jin assisted in the administration, he recruited famous people and appointed Zheng Gongye as the Minister of the Secretariat and promoted to the Censor. He Jin was preparing to kill the eunuchs and wanted to recruit Dong Zhuo, the governor of Bingzhou, as his assistant. Zheng Gongye said to He Jin: Dong Zhuo is violent, cruel, unloyal, and very ambitious. If you lend him the government affairs and grant him important tasks, you will be able to fulfill your evil desires and endanger the court. With your important position as a pro-German, you have the authority to guide the emperor and preside over state affairs. Chengyi is arbitrary and punishes the guilty, so he really shouldn't use Dong Zhuo's power as a back-up. And things change over time, and lessons are never far away. Why enter Chen's top priority? He Jin couldn't use it, so he abandoned his official position and left. He said to Xun You, a native of Yingchuan: Mr. He is not easy to help. He Jin was soon killed, and Dong Zhuo indeed rebelled. Zheng Gongye and others, together with his servant Wu Qiong and Dong Zhuo's chief historian He, jointly talked about Dong Zhuo and appointed Yuan Shao as the prefect of Bohai to carry out Shandong's plan. When the rebels arose, Dong Zhuo convened a discussion with the ministers and sent out a large army to attack the rebels. All the officials did not dare to violate Dong Zhuo's will. Zheng Gongye was worried that if Dong Zhuo had more soldiers, he would become more arrogant and vicious and difficult to control. He said: "Ruling a country depends on virtue, not on having many soldiers."
target: **Zheng Taichuan (Zheng Gongye)** was born in Kaifeng, Henan, as the great-grandson of Sinong Zheng Zhong. Talented from youth, his mother foresaw chaos in the final years of Emperor Ling's reign and secretly befriended heroes. Despite owning 400 hectares of land, he often lacked food. He was renowned throughout Shandong. Initially recommended for office, he declined multiple appointments. When General He Jin recruited him as Minister of the Secretariat and Censor, Zheng warned against recruiting Dong Zhuo, predicting his violent ambition would endanger the court. He Jin ignored this advice, so Zheng resigned. After He Jin was killed and Dong Zhuo rebelled, Zheng conspired with others to oppose Dong Zhuo. When Dong Zhuo wanted to attack the rebels, Zheng argued that governing depends on virtue, not military might. Fearing Dong Zhuo's anger, he fabricated a flattering analysis listing ten reasons why Dong Zhuo would defeat the rebels. Dong Zhuo appointed him general, but others warned of Zheng's cunning, so Dong Zhuo revoked the command. Zheng later plotted to kill Dong Zhuo, but the plan leaked. He escaped to Yuan Shu, who appointed him Governor of Yangzhou, but he died en route at age forty-one.

source: He, He and Xun You jointly planned to kill Dong Zhuo. When the incident was leaked out and the others were arrested, Zheng Gongye escaped from Wuguan and returned east to Yuan Shu. Yuan Shu made a memorial to appoint him as the governor of Yangzhou. He did not take office and died on the road at the age of forty-one. ◆Biography of Kong Rong, Kong Rong was a native of Lu and the 20th grandson of Confucius. Kong Ba, the seventh generation ancestor, was the disciple of Emperor Yuan of the Han Dynasty and served as an official. His father, Kong Zhou, was the captain of Taishan. Kong Rong had special talents when he was a child. At the age of ten, he went to the capital with his father. At that time, Henan Yin and Li Ying kept themselves simple and strict, and did not receive scholar-bureaucrats and guests casually. They were not allowed to inform anyone who was not a contemporary celebrity or a family with whom they had known each other for generations. Kong Rong wanted to see what kind of person Li Ying was, so he went to Li Ying's house and knocked on the door. The person who answered the door said, "I am a descendant of Li Juntong's family." The gatekeeper told Li Ying that Li Ying asked Kong Rong to meet him. Question: Did Grandfather Gao Ming ever have any friendship with me? Kong Rong said: Yes. The ancestor Confucius and your ancestor Li Laojun have the same virtues and synonyms, and they have a mentor-friend relationship. Then, I, Kong Rong, and you have been friends for generations. Everyone sitting here was impressed by it. Taizhong doctor Chen Wei arrived later, and those present told Chen Wei this.
target: **Kong Rong**, a descendant of Confucius, showed exceptional intelligence as a child. At ten, he cleverly gained an audience with Li Ying by claiming family friendship through Confucius and Laozi. When Chen Wei dismissed him, Kong retorted sharply. At thirteen, his father's death caused such grief he needed support to stand. At sixteen, he sheltered the fugitive Zhang Jian, leading to his brother's execution when the family competed to take blame. Kong Rong became famous and was recruited as an official.
