source: It is better to treat him with courtesy and let everyone in the world know that the general has a broad mind. He Jin thought it was right, and after being appointed as a general, he conquered Kong Rong, promoted him to a high rank, and became the imperial censor. Because he was at odds with Zhongcheng Zhao She, he returned home due to illness. Later he was conscripted as Sikong Peng and awarded the title of Military Marquis. After three days in office, he was promoted to General of Tiger and Lieutenant Commander. When Dong Zhuo deposed the Young Emperor and established the Xian Emperor, Kong Rong often corrected his mistakes when answering questions. Therefore, he violated Dong Zhuo's wishes and was transferred to Yilang. At that time, the Yellow Turbans invaded several states, and Beihai was the place where thieves attacked the most. Dong Zhuo then signaled the three governments to jointly appoint Kong Rong as the Prime Minister of Beihai. Kong Rong went to the county, summoned the soldiers and people, raised troops and taught martial arts. He not only issued proclamations, but also wrote letters himself, communicating with the prefectures and counties, and planning together. The thief Zhang Rao and other 200,000 people returned from Jizhou. Kong Rong faced him and was defeated by Zhang Rao. So he gathered scattered soldiers to defend Zhuxu County. Then he slowly gathered more than 40,000 officials and people, men and women who had been misled by the Yellow Turban, and built cities and schools, praised Confucianism, and recommended virtuous people such as Zheng Xuan, Peng Chu, and Bing Yuan. Zhen Ziran, a county native, was famous in Linxiaocun. He died young. Kong Rong regretted not seeing him. Ordered to distribute food to the county society. Even if the others have only a small amount of good deeds, they will not be treated with courtesy. County residents who had no descendants and travelers from all over the country who died were buried in coffins. At this time, the Yellow Turbans invaded again. Kong Rong then went to Duchang County and was surrounded by the thief Guan Hai. Kong Rong was in great danger and sent Donglai Taishi Ci to ask for help from Pingyuan Prime Minister Liu Bei. Liu Bei said in surprise: Kong Beihai actually knew that there was another Liu Bei in the world. Three thousand soldiers were immediately sent to rescue him, but the thief escaped because he was scattered. At that time, Yuan Shao and Cao Cao were very powerful, and Kong Rong did not rely on anyone. Zuo Chengzu was rich in strategy and advised Kong Rong to join forces with Cao Cao and Yuan Shao. Kong Rong knew that Yuan Shao and Cao Cao were ultimately trying to usurp the Han Dynasty, and he didn't want to get involved with them, so he killed Zuo Chengzu in a rage. Kong Rong himself thought that he had a noble spirit and was determined to quell the country's crisis, but he failed because of his limited talents and empty ideas. After six years in the county, Liu Bei recommended him to concurrently serve as the governor of Qingzhou. In the first year of Jian'an, he was attacked by Yuan Tan. From spring to summer, there were only a few hundred soldiers left. Arrows came like rain, and the city was already in close combat.
target: He criticized corrupt eunuch relatives, offended He Jin, and later opposed Dong Zhuo's deposition of the Young Emperor. Dong Zhuo sent him to troubled Beihai as punishment. There, Kong Rong built cities, schools, promoted Confucianism, and recommended worthy men. When surrounded by Yellow Turban rebels, Liu Bei rescued him, amazed that Kong Rong knew of him. Kong Rong refused to ally with Yuan Shao or Cao Cao, knowing they would usurp the Han. After six years, Liu Bei recommended him as Qingzhou governor. Yuan Tan attacked; though outnumbered, Kong Rong remained calm, reading and laughing until the city fell.

source: Kong Rong replied: Your Majesty is kind and considerate of the times. He mourns the souls of the two kings and issues pity edicts, examines and reviews the previous laws and regulations, and corrects the etiquette system. I look at history and it turns out that in the past, King Huai of Liang, King Linjiang Min, King Qi Ai, and King Huai of Linhuai all died without descendants. Their brothers, namely Emperor Jing, Emperor Wu, Emperor Zhao, and Emperor Ming, never heard that the previous dynasty performed sacrifices for them. If it's temporary, don't include it in the legend. I am not sensible and think that they all died at a young age. The emperor grieved and gave them posthumous titles through the coming-of-age ceremony. This should be done according to your wishes. After the sacrifice, don't do it again in the future. As for the one-year period, it is not in line with etiquette and violates the legal system established by the late emperor. This is inappropriate. Earlier, Cao Cao attacked Yecheng and massacred the residents of Yecheng. Many of the women and girls of Yuan Shao's family were taken captive. Cao Cao's son Cao Pi secretly married Yuan Xi's wife Zhen. Kong Rong wrote to Cao Cao, saying: King Wu defeated Zhou and rewarded Daji to Duke Zhou. Cao Cao didn't understand, and later asked Kong Rong where this scripture came from. Kong Rong replied: "Based on the current situation, I think it will be certain." Later, when Cao Cao attacked Wuhuan, Kong Rong laughed at him and said: "The general went on an expedition and was depressed overseas. In the past, Su was careful not to pay tribute to Mu Kuya, and Ding Ling stole Su Wu's cattle and sheep. We can attack him together!" At that time, there was famine and war, and Cao Cao petitioned for a ban on alcohol. Kong Rong wrote to Cao Cao many times, arguing that he should not ban alcohol, and his words were too insulting. Having seen Cao Cao's treacherousness and deceit gradually revealed, he couldn't bear it, so he spoke in extreme ways and often offended Cao Cao. He also once submitted a memorial that the ancient capital system should be followed, and no feudal princes should be allowed within a thousand miles. Cao Cao doubted what he said gradually and became even more afraid of him. However, because Kong Rong was famous all over the world, he pretended to be tolerant on the surface, but secretly he was jealous of his correct opinions and was afraid of hindering his great cause.
target: He fled, but his wife was captured. Later serving Emperor Xian, Kong Rong often made court decisions. He opposed corporal punishment, argued against publicizing Liu Biao's treason, and criticized Cao Cao's massacre of Yecheng and his son's marriage to Yuan Xi's wife. He mocked Cao Cao's campaigns and opposed his alcohol ban. Cao Cao, though outwardly tolerant, grew jealous. Eventually, Cao Cao had Kong Rong executed for treason at fifty-six.

source: Therefore, Confucius established his dynasty in an upright manner, and no one made any mistakes that would cause trouble to his lord. Yan Pingzhong was in the dynasty, and Tian Chengzi did not dare to kill the lord of Qi and steal his country. As for Kong Wenju's noble aspirations and frank feelings, they can definitely inspire loyalty and resist the treacherous heart. Therefore, when Cao Cao was alive, he did not dare to usurp the Han Dynasty, but it was Cao Pi who succeeded the Han Dynasty after his death. Strict qi and righteousness are nothing more than overturning and destroying. Is it possible to live a life of humiliation and compromise? Strict and neat, bright and white, Kong Rong's quality can be compared with that of white jade and autumn frost! ◆Xun Yu's biography, Xun Yu's courtesy name Wenruo, was born in Yingyin, Yingchuan, and was the grandson of Xun Shu, the magistrate of Langling County. His father, Xun Nu, served as Prime Minister of Jinan. Xun Yu was afraid of eunuchs, so he married Xun Yu's daughter to Tang Heng, the official minister of the imperial court. Xun Yu was saved from being ridiculed because he was famous for his talent at a young age. He Yong from Nanyang claimed to be able to understand people. When he saw Xun Yu, he thought he was extraordinary and said: "This is the talent of the emperor's assistant." In the sixth year of Zhongping, he was recommended as Xiaolian and appointed as the magistrate of Kangfu County. When Dong Zhuo rebelled, he abandoned his official position and returned to his hometown. Han Rong from the same county took more than a thousand members of his clan to escape the chaos in the western mountains of Mi County. Xun Yu said to his elders: Yingchuan is a place where war must pass. When the world changes, it is often the place where troops are needed. Although Mi County is somewhat safe, it is not enough to withstand a major disaster. You should leave here as soon as possible. Most of the fellow countrymen are nostalgic for their homeland and are unwilling to leave. When Han Fu, a fellow herdsman from Jizhou, sent cavalry to pick them up, Xun Yu led his clan to follow Han Fu. Most of the people he left behind were later killed and robbed by Dong Zhuo's general Li Jue. By the time Xun Yu arrived in Jizhou, Yuan Shao had already usurped Han Fu's position. Yuan Shao treated Xun Yu like a distinguished guest. Xun Yu was a well-informed person. Seeing the chaos in the Han Dynasty, he always wanted to correct things. At that time, Cao Cao was in Dongjun. Xun Yu heard that Cao Cao was talented and strategist, but he estimated that Yuan Shao would not be able to achieve great things in the end. In the second year of Chuping, he left Yuan Shao and went to Cao Cao. Cao Cao was overjoyed after talking to him and said: "This is my Zhang Liang." He was appointed Fenwu Sima when he was twenty-nine years old. The next year, he was appointed Sima of Zhendong. In the first year of Xingping, Cao Cao attacked Tao Qian in the east and sent Xun Yu to guard Zhen City to take charge of the affairs left behind. He caught up with Zhang Miao and Chen Gong and took Yanzhou to rebel against Cao Cao, and secretly welcomed Lu Bu. After Lu Bu arrived, all cities responded. Zhang Miao sent someone to deceive Xun Yu and said: General Lu came to help Cao Shijun defeat Tao Qian, so we should quickly supply him with military supplies. Xun Yu knew that Zhang Miao had changed, so he deployed troops to fortify Zhang Miao's plan. Therefore, Zhang Miao's plan could not succeed.
target: **Xun Yu**, grandson of Magistrate Xun Shu, was recognized as extraordinary by He Yong. Recommended as Xiaolian, he abandoned office when Dong Zhuo rebelled. He warned his clan to flee Yingchuan, predicting war; those who stayed were later killed. He joined Yuan Shao but, seeing the Han's chaos, left for Cao Cao, who called him "my Zhang Liang." When Zhang Miao and Chen Gong rebelled, Xun Yu defended Zhen City, outsmarting their deception and personally meeting Guo Gong to prevent his alliance with rebels. He secured three cities for Cao Cao's return. Xun Yu advised Cao Cao to stabilize Yanzhou before attacking Xuzhou, leading to Lu Bu's defeat. He urged Cao Cao to welcome Emperor Xian to Xuchang, arguing this would bring legitimacy. Xun Yu recommended talented men like Xun You, Zhong Yao, and Guo Jia. He predicted Yuan Shao's defeat despite his strength, correctly assessing his generals' weaknesses. During the Guandu stalemate, when Cao Cao wanted to retreat, Xun Yu insisted on holding position, leading to Yuan Shao's defeat. He advised against attacking Liu Biao before pacifying Yuan Shao's remnants. When Cao Cao wanted to restore the ancient Jiuzhou system, Xun Yu warned it would cause panic, and Cao Cao abandoned the plan. Cao Cao praised Xun Yu's strategies as turning defeat into victory. When Dong Zhao proposed making Cao Cao Duke of Jin, Xun Yu opposed it, saying Cao Cao should remain loyal to Han. Cao Cao grew resentful. During a southern campaign, Cao Cao kept Xun Yu at his camp, then sent him an empty food box. Xun Yu took poison and died at fifty. The next year, Cao Cao declared himself Duke of Wei.

source: ◆Zheng Xingzhuan, Zheng Xing, courtesy name Shaogan, was born in Kaifeng, Henan. He studied "Gongyang Chunqiu" when he was young, and "Zuo Shi Zhuan" in his later years. He accumulated knowledge, thought deeply, and understood the gist of the book. All his classmates regarded Zheng as their teacher. During the Tianfeng period, he led his students to teach Liu Xin the meaning of "Zuo Shi Zhuan". Liu Xin praised Zheng Xing's talent and asked Zheng Xing to write regulations, chapters, exegesis, and correct "Santong Li". He is eight feet long, has a tall and majestic appearance, wears loose clothes and wears a large belt, and travels around the country. I once walked between Chen and Liang, and when it rained, I folded a corner of the towel and put it up. At that time, people also learned to deliberately fold a corner of the towel, which was called Lin Zongjin. Most people admired it like this. Someone asked Fan Pang of Runan: What kind of person is Guo Linzong? Fan Pang said: Living in seclusion like Jie Zitui does not violate the mother's will; serving as an official is like Liu Xiahui, who is loyal and not pretentious. The emperor cannot treat him as a minister, and the princes cannot treat him as a friend. Others, I don't know. Later, his mother died and he had a reputation of being extremely filial. Although Guo Linzong was good at identifying and criticizing people, he did not make passionate and profound discussions, so the eunuch dictatorship could not harm him. The party disaster arose, and most of the famous people suffered from it. Only Guo Linzong and Runan Yuan Hong were spared. So he taught behind closed doors and had thousands of students. In the first year of Jianning, Taifu Chen Fan and General Dou Wu were killed by eunuchs. Guo Linzong cried in the wild and was extremely sad. Because he sighed and said: When people die, the country is also in danger.  The crow landed on that person's house. In the spring of the next year, he died at home at the age of forty-two. More than a thousand people from all over the world came to pay their respects to the funeral. The comrades then carved a stone and erected a stele together, and Cai Yong wrote the inscription. When it was completed, he said to Lu Zhi of Zhuojun: I have written many inscriptions! Everyone felt a little ashamed, but Guo Youdao was the only one who didn't feel ashamed.
target: Guo Taichuan, also known as Lin Zong, was born into a poor family in Jiexiu, Taiyuan. After his father's early death, he refused his mother's suggestion to work in the county, instead studying under Chenggao Qu Boyan. He became well-versed in many books, eloquent, and renowned for his loud voice. While traveling in Luoyang, he befriended Li Ying of Henan, gaining fame in the capital. Returning home, he crossed the river alone with Li Ying, impressing onlookers. Despite recruitment offers from officials like Situ Huang Qiong, he declined, citing his observations of heaven and society. He was known for his tall, majestic appearance and his habit of folding a corner of his towel, which others imitated as "Lin Zongjin." Fan Pang praised him as a man who could not be treated as a subject or friend. After his mother's death, he was known for extreme filial piety. During the party disaster, he avoided harm by refraining from passionate discussions, teaching behind closed doors with thousands of students. In the first year of Jianning, he mourned the deaths of Chen Fan and Dou Wu, predicting the country's danger. He died at home at forty-two, with over a thousand mourners. Cai Yong wrote his epitaph, feeling no shame in doing so.

source: Guo Linzong bowed to him and said, "You are so wise!" Because he persuaded him to study, he finally became a moral person. He left without even looking at it. Guo Linzong saw him and asked what he meant. Meng Min replied: The steamer is broken, what's the use of it? Guo Linzong believed that Meng Min was not an ordinary person and advised him to study abroad. After ten years of becoming famous, he was recruited by all three princes, but none of them went. Guo Linzong saw him, promoted him, and persuaded him to study as an official because all students were doing odd jobs. Later, when he was able to lecture on knowledge, he thought that he was from a humble background and often sat in the lower seat. Students and doctors asked him questions, so in the school, he was regarded as the most respected person in the lower seat. Later, when the imperial court called for him, he didn't answer the call. People called him "Zhengjun". Song Guo, courtesy name Zhongyi, was born in Fufeng. He has a strong personality and likes to avenge others and cause suffering for the county. Guo Linzong then taught him the right way of life and threatened him with disaster and failure. Song Guo was moved by him and repented, kowtowed and admitted his mistake. Therefore, correct your evil ways and discipline yourself. Later, he became famous for his uprightness. He was recruited by the government and served as a censor and governor of Bingzhou. Wherever he went, he taught widely. Jia Shu, whose courtesy name is Zihou, is a fellow villager of Guo Linzong. Although he comes from a family that has been officials for generations, his character is sinister and the village is troubled by him. Guo Linzong's mother passed away, Jia Shu went to express condolences, and later Julu Sun Weizhi also arrived. Sun Weizhi thought that Guo Linzong was a virtuous man but accepted the condolences of a wicked man. He felt strange and left without entering the house. Guo Linzong caught up with Sun Weizhi and said: Jia Zihou is indeed a bad person, but he has changed his mind and changed his mind. Zhongni does not refuse to visit home, so I allow him to come in. Jia Shu listened, changed her ways, encouraged herself, and eventually became a good person. When there were people in distress in the village, Jia Shu often tried her best to rescue them, and was praised by the governor. Shi Shubin, Chen Liuren. He was famous when he was young. Guo Linzong told people when he met: "The wall is high but the foundation is low. Even if you gain something, you will definitely lose it." Later, he really lost his reputation because of his flattery. Huang Yun, courtesy name Ziai, was born in Jiyang. Famous for his outstanding talents. Guo Linzong met him and said: You have extraordinary talents and can become a great weapon. However, I'm afraid that if you don't stick to the truth, you may lose what you gain. Later, Situ Yuan Wei wanted to propose to his niece. When he saw Huang Yun, he sighed and said, "I am so satisfied with my son-in-law." When Huang Yun heard about it, he dismissed his wife Xiahou.
target: Guo Linzong was skilled in identifying and rewarding scholars. He advised Zuo Yuan, a disgraced county student, to reform, citing historical examples. Zuo Yuan later attempted revenge but left out of shame. He recognized Mao Rong's filial piety, persuading him to study and become virtuous. He advised Meng Min, who ignored a broken steamer, to study abroad, leading to his fame. He promoted Yucheng from a servant to a respected scholar. He reformed Song Guo, a vengeful man, into an upright official. He accepted Jia Shu, a sinister man, after his mother's death, leading to Jia's transformation. He predicted Shi Shubin's loss of reputation due to flattery. He warned Huang Yun about losing gains without truth, which came true when Huang dismissed his wife. He noted Xie Zhen and Bian Rang's talents but lack of Taoism, leading to their downfalls. He correctly predicted Wang Rou and Wang Ze's career paths. He also discovered talents among commoners, such as Zhang Xiaozhong and Fan Tezu.

source: ◆The biography of Xu Shao, named Zijiang, was from Pingyu County, Runan County. When he was young, he established a reputation, was morally responsible, liked to talk about people, and was appreciated by many people. For example, Fan Zizhao and He Yangshi were all famous at that time. He began to serve as a meritorious officer in the county, and the prefect Xu Chu respected him very much. When I heard that my son was going to be an official, there was no one in the government who would not change his conduct and be careful about his words and deeds. Yuan Shao, a member of the same county, was a noble knight. He left the Puyang Order and returned home with a large number of carriages and horses. He was very luxurious. When he was about to enter the county, he sent away the guests and others and said, "Can Xu Zijian see my carriage and horse attire like this?" So I just took a car back home. Xu Shao once went to Yingchuan, and the people who traveled with him were some moral and knowledgeable elders. He did not visit Chen Chen alone. Chen Fan's wife died and she returned to her hometown for burial. Everyone in the village went to attend the funeral, but Xu Shao did not go. Someone asked him why, and Xu Shao said: Taiqiu's Taoism is too broad, and it is hard to be thorough in wideness; Zhongju has a severe temperament, and he cannot be thorough in Jun. So I won't go. Most of his comments on people are like this. When Cao Cao didn't want to make a name for himself, he once made generous gifts and humbly asked Xu Shao to talk to him. Xu Shao looked down on him and refused to speak, so Cao Cao found an opportunity to threaten Xu Shao. Xu Shao had no choice but to say, "You are a traitor in a time of peace and a hero in a time of trouble." Cao Cao left very happily. Xu Shao's uncle Xu Jing, Xu Jing's son Xu Xun, and Xu Xiang were all ministers of the Three Dukes. Because Xu Xiang flattered the eunuchs, he went to Taisi to grant him the title of Marquis. He sent people to invite Xu Shao many times. Xu Shao thought that Xu Xiang had no virtue and behaved abominably, so he never visited him. Li Kui, a native of the same county as Xu Shao, was upright and had noble ambitions. Xu Shao began to be friendly with him, but later they had conflicts and discord with his brother Xu Jing. Public opinion at that time was dissatisfied with him. At first, Xu Shao and Xu Jing were both well-known and liked to comment on township party figures. They changed the topic every month, so there was a custom of commenting on the first day of the month in Runan. When Sikong Yang Biao summoned Xu Shao, he promoted him as upright, upright, and honest, but he failed to respond. Someone advised Xu Shao to become an official. He replied: "Now that the villain has succeeded, the royal family will be in chaos. I want to go to Huaihai to escape to save the children and the elderly." So we went south to Guangling. Tao Qian, the governor of Xuzhou, treated each other with courtesy and was extremely considerate. Xu Shao felt uneasy and told his disciples: "Tao Gongzu has a good reputation on the surface, but he is not true in his heart." Although it is very kind to me, this situation cannot last long, so it is better to leave. So he went to Qu'a to join Liu Yao, the governor of Yangzhou. Later, Tao Qian indeed captured the guests who were staying with him. After Sun Ce pacified Wu, Xu Shao and Liu Yaonan fled Yuzhang and died there at the age of forty-six. Xu Shao's brother Xu Qian was also famous. People in Runan said Pingyu had two dragons.
target: Xu Shao, from Runan, was known for moral responsibility and commenting on people. He influenced Yuan Shao to reduce his luxury. He avoided visiting Chen Chen and Chen Fan, citing their flaws. He famously called Cao Cao a "traitor in peace, hero in trouble." He refused to visit his uncle Xu Xiang due to his flattery of eunuchs. He and his brother Xu Jing held monthly critiques in Runan. He declined official posts, fleeing to Guangling and later to Qu'a to join Liu Yao. He died in Yuzhang at forty-six. His brother Xu Qian was also famous, known as the "two dragons of Pingyu.".

source: ◆The biography of Guo Gong, named Zhongsun, was born in Yangzhai, Yingchuan. The family has been officials for generations. His father, Guo Hong, studied "Xiao Du Lv" and the prefect Kou Xun used Guo Hong to make judgments on Cao Cao. He stayed in prison for thirty years and his methods were fair. In all cases judged by Guo Hong, there is no resentment when he retreats. The county will compare Hong to Donghai Yugong. Guo Hong died at the age of ninety-five. Guo Gong inherited his father's business when he was young and taught hundreds of disciples. Later he became a county official and was called into the government. During the Yongping period, Dou Gu, the captain of Fengche, sent troops to fight against the Huns, and Qin Peng, the captain of cavalry, served as deputy commander. Qin Peng was stationed elsewhere and often killed people according to the law. Dou Gu reported that Qin Peng had exclusive power and requested that he be killed. Xianzong then cited officials and ministers to assess Qin Peng's crime. Because Guo Gong understood the law, he was summoned to the court to participate in the review. Everyone who discussed it agreed with what Dou Gu said, but Guo Gong said alone: ​​According to the law, Peng should be beheaded. The emperor said: When the army goes out for battle, the captain is unified under the governor. Since Peng has no axe, can he have the power to kill people? Guo Gong replied: "Unifying under the governor is a matter of trilogy." Today's special general Peng Zhuan is a little different from this. Military affairs are as urgent as human breathing, and the commander is not allowed to be notified in advance. Moreover, under the system of the Han Dynasty, Zhuoge was the same as Wu, and he was not considered guilty legally. The emperor listened to Guo Gong's opinion. There are also brothers who commit murder together, and it is hard to pin the blame on whom. The emperor believed that the elder brother should not discipline his younger brother, so he reported that the elder brother should be sentenced severely and the younger brother should be commuted to death. The imperial edict was read out by Sun Zhang, who made a mistake and was punished twice. The minister reported that Sun Zhang had falsely conveyed the imperial edict and should be cut in half for his crime. The emperor called Guo Gong to ask again, and Guo Gong replied: Sun Zhang should be fined. The emperor said: Sun Zhang falsely issued an imperial edict to kill people, how can he say that he was only fined? Guo Gong said: In law, there is a distinction between intentional homicide and manslaughter. Sun Zhang's mistake in conveying the order is considered manslaughter, and manslaughter is lighter in terms of regulations. The emperor said: Sun Zhang lives in the same county as the prisoner, so I suspect he did it on purpose. Guo Gong said: The road is as flat as a hammer, and as straight as an arrow. A gentleman will not cheat and deceive. The king regards heaven as the law, and punishment should not be compromised. The emperor said: OK. He was awarded the title of Tingweizheng, but was later dismissed for breaking the law. Later, he was promoted three times, and in the third year of Yuanhe, he was promoted to Tingwei.
target: The biography of Guo Gong, styled Zhongsun, was from Yangzhai, Yingchuan, in a family of officials for generations. His father, Guo Hong, studied "Xiao Du Lv" and served as a judge for Prefect Kou Xun, handling cases for Cao Cao. Guo Hong worked in prison for thirty years with fair methods, and those he judged felt no resentment, earning comparisons to Donghai Yugong. He died at ninety-five. Guo Gong inherited his father's work, teaching hundreds of disciples, then became a county official. During the Yongping period, he was summoned to court to review a case involving Dou Gu and Qin Peng. While others agreed with Dou Gu, Guo Gong argued that Qin Peng should be beheaded according to law, citing military urgency and Han system precedents. The emperor accepted his view. In another case of brothers committing murder, the emperor initially ruled the elder brother be severely sentenced, but Guo Gong advised leniency for a clerk, Sun Zhang, who mistakenly conveyed an imperial edict, distinguishing between intentional homicide and manslaughter. The emperor agreed. Guo Gong became Tingweizheng but was later dismissed for breaking the law. Promoted three times, he became Tingwei in the third year of Yuanhe.

source: Guo Gong said: The road is as flat as a hammer, and as straight as an arrow. A gentleman will not cheat and deceive. The king regards heaven as the law, and punishment should not be compromised. The emperor said: OK. He was awarded the title of Tingweizheng, but was later dismissed for breaking the law. Later, he was promoted three times, and in the third year of Yuanhe, he was promoted to Tingwei. Guo Gong's family has been in charge of law for generations, and their affairs are in Kuanping. When he was a magistrate, he decided on prisons and sentences, and mostly acted on the principle of mercy. Therefore, he reported to the emperor the forty-one things that meant severe punishment could be mitigated, and everything was implemented according to the law. In the first year of Zhanghe, the prisoners in the world were pardoned before Bingzi in April, and their death penalty was reduced to one level, without being flogged, and they were sent to Jincheng. However, the article did not mention those who escaped unnoticed. Guo Gong went to Fengshi and said: The reason why the holy grace reduces the death penalty and makes the border guards more important is that human life is the most important thing. There are probably tens of thousands of people on death row today, and since the pardon, many criminals have been arrested. Even if the edict does not involve them, they should all be punished with serious crimes. Thinking of God's kindness, all those who were convicted of capital crimes were reborn, but those who were arrested after escaping did not benefit from the kindness. I think that those who have committed capital crimes before and are imprisoned after the pardon may not be flogged to Jincheng, so as to save lives and benefit the frontier. Suzong thought it was very good and immediately issued an edict to pardon him. Guo Gong reported on the legal system, and many people saved their lives.
target: He advocated mercy in sentencing, reporting forty-one cases for mitigation, all implemented. In the first year of Zhanghe, he successfully petitioned to extend a pardon to escaped criminals, saving many lives.

source: Suzong thought it was very good and immediately issued an edict to pardon him. Guo Gong reported on the legal system, and many people saved their lives. In the sixth year of Yongyuan, he died in the official government. The middle son, Guo Rizhi, also understood the law. His official position was the prefect of Nanyang, and he was famous in politics. ◆Chen Chong's biography, Chen Chong's courtesy name is Zhaogong, and he was a member of the Pei Kingdom. My great-grandfather, Chen Xian, served as Minister of Law and Order during the reigns of Emperor Cheng and Emperor Ai. During the reign of Emperor Ping, Wang Mang assisted the government and made many changes to the Han Dynasty system, which made Chen Xian dissatisfied. When Wang Mang killed He Wu, Bao Xuan and others who were not attached to him because of Lu Kuan's affairs, Chen Xian sighed: "The Book of Changes" says: "A gentleman acts when the opportunity arises. If I don't wait until the end of the day, I can pass away!" Immediately asked to resign and left. When Wang Mang usurped the throne, he summoned Chen Xian to serve as the chief bandit officer, but Chen refused to take up the post on the grounds of illness. At this time, the three sons Shen, Feng, and Qin were all in official positions, so they were all dismissed from their positions. The father and son returned to their hometown together, staying behind closed doors. They still held sacrifices in the twelfth lunar month according to the custom of the Han family. When people asked him why, Chen Xian said: Do my ancestors know about Wang's wax sacrifice? Later, Wang Mang summoned Chen Xian and said that he was seriously ill, so he collected all the laws and regulations at home and hid them in the walls. Chen Xian had a kind and tolerant character, and often warned his descendants: When negotiating for others, you should rely on lightness. Even if you have the benefit of a hundred gold, never compare yourself with others. In the early years of Jianwu's reign, Chen Qinzi and Chen Gong served as the left prisoner of the Tingwei and died early. Chen Gong gave birth to Chen Chong, who learned about the family business. When he was young, Chong served as a state and county official and was called to Situ Baoyu's mansion. At this time, the three houses were very friendly, and it was considered noble to refuse to do anything. Chen Chongchang disagreed and worked hard alone, explaining contemporary politics to Bao Yu several times. Bao Yu was convinced of his ability to favor, so he resigned from Cao Cao and took charge of the world's lawsuits. His judgment was fair and did not fail to satisfy everyone's wishes. At that time, Situ's lawsuits were delayed for decades. The matters were complicated and easy to judge, and bad officials had to rely on them to make a difference. Chen Chong wrote seven volumes of "Resignation and Litigation Bi" for Bao Yu. The rules for dealing with the case were all in accordance with the categories of things. Bao Yu played this, and later the government took it as an example. After being promoted three times, in the early years of Emperor Suzong's reign, he became minister.
target: He died in the sixth year of Yongyuan. His son, Guo Rizhi, also understood law and served as Nanyang prefect. Chen Chong, styled Zhaogong, was from Pei Kingdom. His great-grandfather, Chen Xian, served as Minister of Law under Emperors Cheng and Ai but resigned during Wang Mang's usurpation, hiding legal texts in walls. Chen Chong learned family law, served as a county official, and later worked for Situ Bao Yu, writing seven volumes of "Resignation and Litigation Bi" to handle lawsuits fairly. Promoted three times, he became minister under Emperor Suzong. He advocated leniency, arguing against harsh punishments in a memorial, and the emperor adopted his views, abolishing cruel punishments and fixing over fifty legal items. Chen Chong also debated the timing of executions, supporting winter executions based on classical texts, and the emperor accepted his reasoning. He served as prefect of Taishan and Guanghan, where he appointed good officials, reduced lawsuits, and investigated mysterious cries, burying unburied bones to stop them. He refused to flatter Dou Xian, later becoming Tingwei in the sixth year of Yongyuan.

source: Kind and reserved personality. Later, he became a judge. He discussed difficult cases many times and often presented memorials in person. Every time he attached a sutra, he asked for forgiveness. The emperor often listened to him and saved many prisoners. Only at this time did the number of cases with profound stories decrease a lot. Chen Chong also cleaned up the laws and regulations, and eliminated them out of "Fu Xing". He also said: I have heard that there are three hundred rites and three thousand majestic rituals, so in the "Fu Xing", the decapitation of the great punishment is two hundred, and the five punishments and the like are three thousand. Where etiquette goes, punishment takes away. If etiquette is violated, punishment will follow. They are both exterior and interior. Today's law decrees six hundred and ten death sentences, one thousand six hundred and ninety-eight punishments, and two thousand six hundred and eighty-one atonements. It comes from the one thousand nine hundred and eighty-nine in "Fu Xing", of which four hundred and ten are great punishments, one thousand five hundred for one's punishment, and seventy-nine atonements. "Spring and Autumn Period Baoqian Tu" says: The king will practice his method every three hundred years. In the three hundred and two years since the rise of the Han Dynasty, the constitution has been slightly increased and the regulations are unlimited. There are three schools of law, and their explanations are different. It is necessary to order Sangong and Tingweiping to make decrees that should be consistent with the law, so that the general punishment can be 200, and the punishment and atonement can be 2800, and the total number can be 3000, and all the remaining orders should be deleted, corresponding to the etiquette, so as to change the hearing and hearing of thousands of people, so as to obtain the reputation of not using punishment measures, which can be passed down to endless generations. There was no time to implement it, so the jailer was ordered to socialize with the prisoners to compensate for the crime. The imperial court issued an edict to exempt him from punishment and worship him as minister. Promoted to Dahonglu. Chen Chong experienced two counties and three ministers, and his deeds were famous at that time. In the 16th year, he served as Sikong on behalf of Xu Fang. Although Chen Chong specializes in law, he is also a master of classics. He made a report to Wen Cui and was named Prime Minister. He died after reigning for three years.
target: He cleaned up laws, proposing to reduce death sentences to 200 and total punishments to 3,000, but this was not implemented. He served as Sikong and died after three years.

source: ◆Preface to the biographies of ruthless officials. The Han Dynasty inherited the turbulent and uneasy era of the Warring States Period, which affected many people, including those who were arrogant and cunning. Those who use the big to swallow up the small, cross the country and the city, and those who are strong and unruly become the kings and hegemons in the countryside. The prefectures and counties govern vast areas and have many household registrations. Therefore, officials can act arbitrarily and arbitrarily, and the traitors should be killed first and then punished. Show off his staunch spirit and achieve his unyielding power. He stood up to others and used his own opinions to reveal his unpredictable wisdom. As for the intricacies of the text, the indiscriminate accusations, and the infuriating of people, they are countless. Some pits were even filled with corpses, bleeding for miles. So Wang Wenshu has the reputation of a tiger-crowned official, and Yan Yannian has the reputation of being a butcher. Is this false? However, those among them who suppressed the strong and suppressed the ministers to the point of breaking their minds and ignoring them can be considered very heroic. Since the ZTE, the laws have gradually become stricter, and fewer officials and common people break the law than in previous lives. But eunuchs and relatives harm the world. They even ordered Yang Qiu to dig up Wang Fu's body and Zhang Jian to dissect Cao Jie's tomb. Such and such, although it vents public anger and is pleasing to everyone, it can also be said to be too cruel. Zhang Jian is a well-known figure, so he is included in the "Party Man Chapter". ◆Dong Xuan, courtesy name Shaoping, was a native of Yuxian County, Chenliu County. At first he was recruited by Situ Houba and recommended as a person with excellent performance. He was gradually promoted to the state minister of Beihai County.
target: The Han Dynasty inherited the turbulent Warring States period, fostering arrogant and cunning individuals who used power to dominate regions. Officials acted arbitrarily, killing traitors before reporting, displaying staunch spirit and unyielding power. Countless injustices occurred, with corpses filling pits and blood flowing for miles. Figures like Wang Wenshu and Yan Yannian gained reputations as tiger-crowned officials and butchers. After the Zhongxing period, laws tightened, but eunuchs and relatives harmed the world, leading to excessive acts like Yang Qiu digging up Wang Fu's body and Zhang Jian dissecting Cao Jie's tomb, which vented public anger but were deemed too cruel. Dong Xuan, from Chenliu, was recommended as a person of excellent performance and became state minister of Beihai.

At first he was recruited by Situ Houba and recommended as a person with excellent performance. He was gradually promoted to the state minister of Beihai County. When he arrived, he appointed Gongsun Dan as the chief minister of the five sense organs. source: Yao Qi, whose courtesy name is Ci Kuang, was born in Jiaxian County, Yingchuan County. He is eight feet two inches long, has a very strange appearance, is solemn and majestic. His father, Yao Meng, was the governor of Guiyang. After his death, Yao spent three years in mourning for him, and everyone in the village praised him. Guangwu raided Yingchuan. Hearing that Yao Qi was very ambitious, he summoned the thief Cao Yu to follow him and attack Ji. At that time Wang Lang sent a message to Ji, and Ji Zhong raised troops to respond to Wang Lang. Guangwu's chariots drove out, and the people gathered to watch. The roads were crowded with noise and chariots could not pass. Yaoqi rode on horseback and raised his halberd, glaring angrily and shouting "guards" to the left and right, and the spectators retreated one after another. When they arrived at the city gate, the gate was closed, so they broke through the city gate and left. When he arrived at Xindu, he took Zhao Qi as his assistant general. He, Fu Kuan and Lu Yan all belonged to Deng Yu. After attacking a nearby county, he also sent out soldiers. Deng Yu thought that Yao Qi was capable, so he paid homage to the partial generals alone and awarded him 2,000 soldiers, including several hundred soldiers each to Fu Kuan and Lu Yan. After returning, he reported the situation to Guangwu, who was very complimentary. He sent Yaoqi to attack Zhending Songzi and captured the counties of Leyang, Gaohe and Fei. Following Deng Yu, he attacked Wang Lang's generals Erhong and Liu Feng under a huge deer. Yaoqi took the lead and captured the enemy's formation. He killed more than fifty people with his own hands and was wounded in the forehead. He tied the wound with a turban and fought again, thus defeating the enemy. After Wang Lang was killed, he worshiped Yao Qi as General Huya. So he took the opportunity and said to Guangwu: "In the land of Hebei, which borders the border fortress, people practice military warfare and are known as elite and brave people." Now that the reform has failed, the unification of the Han Dynasty is in crisis, and there is no way to return to the country. The Ming Dynasty took control of the mountains and rivers of Hebei, supported the elite people, and obeyed the hearts of thousands of people who longed for the Han Dynasty. Who in the world would dare not to obey? Guangwu smiled and said: Do you want to call the police like before? At that time, hundreds of thousands of bronze horses entered Qingyang and Boping. Yaoqi and his generals attacked them. The battle was unfavorable. Yaoqi fought against the water even more, killing many enemies. It happened that Guangwu's reinforcements arrived, so they defeated the enemy and chased them to Guantao, where all the bronze horses surrendered. Following Ji Qing Du and Chi Mei Yu She Dog, the bandits attacked Yao Qi's baggage. Yao Qi fought back, killing dozens of people with his own hands and being wounded in three places on his body. However, he continued to fight hard, defeated the enemy and drove them away. Guangwu ascended the throne and was granted the title of Marquis of Ancheng, with a settlement of 5,000 households. At that time, Tanxiang and Wulou thieves entered Fanyang, Neihuang, and the Wei capital several times, and Gengshi general Zhuo Jing was planning to lead a rebellion in Yecheng. The emperor appointed Yaoqi as the prefect of Wei County to perform the affairs of the general. Yao Qi sent county soldiers to attack Zhuo Jing, defeated him, and beheaded more than 600 people.
target: **Yao Qi** (courtesy name Ci Kuang) was born in Jiaxian County, Yingchuan. Standing eight feet two inches tall with a striking appearance, he was known for solemnity and majesty. After his father Yao Meng, Governor of Guiyang, died, Yao Qi observed three years of mourning, earning village praise. When Guangwu raided Yingchuan, he recruited Yao Qi to attack Ji. During Wang Lang's rebellion, Yao Qi cleared crowded roads by brandishing his halberd and shouting, broke through a closed city gate, and later served under Deng Yu. Deng Yu recognized Yao Qi's capability, making him a partial general with 2,000 soldiers. Yao Qi captured several counties, fought bravely against Wang Lang's forces—killing over fifty enemies despite a forehead wound—and was appointed General Huya after Wang Lang's death. He advised Guangwu to consolidate Hebei's elite forces, and Guangwu smiled at his boldness. Yao Qi fought the Bronze Horse rebels, killing many despite initial setbacks, and later defeated bandits attacking his baggage, sustaining three wounds. After Guangwu ascended the throne, Yao Qi became Marquis of Ancheng with 5,000 households. As Prefect of Wei County, he suppressed Zhuo Jing's rebellion, beheading over 600, and pacified the region. When Li Lu plotted rebellion, Yao Qi showed mercy to Li Xiong, leading Li Lu to suicide from shame. Yao Qi served as Taizhong大夫 and Weiwei, known for integrity and remonstrating with the emperor, once stopping Guangwu from careless travel. He died in the tenth year of Jianwu, receiving posthumous honors as Marquis Zhong.

source: In the tenth year of Jianwu's death, the emperor came in person to present the deceased with clothes, as well as the seals and ribbons of Weiwei and Anchenghou, and was given the posthumous title of Zhonghou. Zi Yaodan succeeded to the throne. He also granted the title of Marquis of Jianping to his brother Yaotong. Later, Yao Dan was granted the title of Marquis of Ge Ling. Yao Dan passed away, and his son Yao Shu succeeded him. Yaoshu passed away and was succeeded by his son Yaoyu. Yao Yu passed away and was succeeded by his son Yao Cai Si. Wang Ba, whose courtesy name was Yuan Bo, was from Yingyang, Yingchuan. He has been fond of the legal system for generations. His father was a county magistrate, and Ba himself was a jailer when he was young. He often lamented that he was not happy with his official position. His father felt strange and sent him west to Chang'an to study. When the Han soldiers rose up and Guangwu passed through Yingyang, Wang Ba led his guests to meet him and said: "The general is raising righteous soldiers. I don't know what I think. I am greedy for the general's power and virtue, and I am willing to join the army." Guangwu said: I dream of wise men to achieve success together, how can it be different! So Cong Guangwu defeated Wang Xun and Wang Yi in Kunyang, and then rested in the countryside. When Guangwu became the captain of Sili school and passed through Yingyang, Wang Ba asked his father for instructions, hoping to follow Guangwu. His father said: I am old and not qualified for military service. You go and do your best! Wang Ba and Guangwu went to Luoyang. When Guangwu became the Grand Sima, he took Wang Ba as his meritorious officer and ordered him to cross Hebei. The guests followed Wang Ba's dozens of people and gradually left. Guangwu said to Wang Ba: All the people who followed me in Yingchuan have left, but you are left alone. effort! The strong wind knows the strong grass. When Wang Lang raised his troops, Guangwu was at Ji. Wang Lang sent a letter offering a reward for Guangwu's capture. Guangwu ordered Wang Ba to go to the city to recruit people and prepare to attack Wang Lang. The people in the city laughed and raised their hands to tease and ridicule. The king was ashamed and cowardly and returned. Guangwu immediately galloped south to Xiaquyang. It was rumored that Wang Lang's soldiers were behind him, and everyone who followed him was afraid. When we arrived at the Hutuo River, the reconnaissance officials came back and reported that the river was filled with ice and could not be crossed without a boat. The officials were greatly frightened when they heard this. Guangwu ordered Wang Ba to go and have a look. Wang Ba probably frightened everyone and wanted to cross the river, but was blocked by the water. When he came back, he falsely claimed that the ice was strong and could be crossed. The officials and their families were all happy.
target: **Wang Ba** (courtesy name Yuan Bo) was from Yingyang, Yingchuan. His family valued legal traditions, and he worked as a jailer before studying in Chang'an. When Guangwu passed through Yingyang, Wang Ba joined his army, fighting at Kunyang. Despite others leaving, Wang Ba remained loyal; Guangwu praised him, saying "The strong wind knows the strong grass." During Wang Lang's rebellion, Wang Ba falsely claimed the Hutuo River was frozen to calm frightened troops, and the ice miraculously formed, allowing crossing. He became a military commander and Marquis of Guan Nei, later capturing Wang Lang's seal. Known for comforting soldiers, he was made a partial general after Guangwu's ascension. In the fourth year of Jianwu, Wang Ba employed strategic patience against Su Mao, closing his camp and refusing battle until the enemy tired, then launching a surprise attack that routed them. He served as General Against Captives, fought Xiongnu forces at Gaoliu, and became Prefect of Shanggu. For over twenty years, he managed border defenses, built roads and barriers, and advocated peace with the Xiongnu. He died in the second year of Yongping, having been granted Marquis of Huailing. **Ji Zun** (younger brother's grandson) was from Yingyang, Yingchuan. Though wealthy, he was respectful and frugal.

source: At first, Zhang Man offered sacrifices to heaven and earth, saying that he should be the king. When he was caught, he sighed: The prophecy was wrong to me! So he, his wife, and his children were beheaded. Ji Zun led his troops south to attack Deng Feng's brother, Du Yan, and finally defeated him. At this time, Zhang Feng, the governor of Zhuo County, caught the envoy and raised his troops to rebel. He claimed to be the supreme general and joined forces with Peng Chong. In the fourth year of Jianwu, Ji Zun, Zhu You, Jianwei General Geng Yan, and Xiaoqi General Liu happy jointly attacked Zhang Feng. Ji Zun's soldiers arrived first and attacked Zhang Feng in a hurry. Zhang Feng's hero Cao Meng captured Zhang Feng and surrendered. At first, Zhang Feng was fond of alchemy. A Taoist priest said that Zhang Feng was regarded as the emperor. He wrapped a stone in a colorful bag and tied it to Zhang Feng's elbow, saying that there was a jade seal in the stone. Zhang Feng believed it and rebelled. After being caught and beheaded, he also said: There is a jade seal on his elbow. Ji Zun broke his stone vertebrae, and Zhang Feng realized that he had been deceived by the Taoist priest. He looked up to the sky and sighed: "I will die without regrets!" All the generals were led back, and Ji Zun was ordered to stay in Liangxiang to resist Peng Chong. Therefore, he sent the guard Fu Xuan to attack Peng Chong's general Li Hao and Yu Lu, and defeated his army, beheading more than a thousand people. They resisted each other for more than a year and were defeated several times. Many of Peng Chong's followers surrendered. When Peng Chong died, Ji Zun marched to pacify his territory. In the spring of the sixth year of Jianwu, he ordered Ji Zun and Jianwei General Geng Yan, Huya General Gai Yan, Han Zhong General Wang Chang, Capture General Ma Wu, Xiaoqi General Liu Xin, Wuwei General Liu Shang and others to attack Gongsun Shu from Tianshui. The army stopped in Chang'an, and Guangwu's chariots also arrived, but Kaixiao did not want the Han soldiers to go to Long, so he excused himself. Guangwu summoned the generals to discuss. They all say: You can temporarily delay the period of the sun and the moon of Wei Xiao, and add titles to his generals to promote their dispersion and disintegration. Ji Zun said: Kui Xiao has been plotting for a long time. If he stands still and procrastinates for a while now, it will prompt him to deepen his deception and make Gongsun Shu increase his security, so it is better to march directly. Guangwu obeyed and sent Ji Zun as the vanguard. Kaixiao sent his general Wang Yuan to stay at Longdi, and Ji Zun attacked, defeated Wang Yuan's army, and pursued him to Xinguan. When the generals arrived, they fought with Kai Xiao but failed, so they retreated to Long. Guangwu ordered Ji Zun to garrison troops in Qi, ordered Geng Yan to garrison troops in Qi, ordered General Feng Yi to garrison troops in the city, and ordered Grand Sima Wu Han and others to return to Chang'an. Since then, Ji Zun has defeated Kuai Xiao several times. See "Feng Yi Zhuan" for details. In the autumn of the eighth year of Jianwu, he went up to Long from Guangwu. When Kuai Xiao was destroyed, Guang Wu returned eastward and passed through Qian. He went to the Ji Zun military camp, comforted and fed the soldiers, and performed Huangmen martial arts, which stopped late at night.
target: After killing a bullying government official, he joined Guangwu. As a military commander, he executed Guangwu's own son for breaking the law, earning Guangwu's respect. He became a partial general and Marquis of Yingyang. Ji Zun fought bravely despite arrow wounds, defeated Zhang Man by cutting his food supply, and captured him alive. He attacked Zhang Feng, whose rebellion stemmed from a Taoist priest's deception about a jade seal. Ji Zun resisted Peng Chong for over a year, and after Peng's death, pacified his territory. In the sixth year of Jianwu, he argued for direct attack against Kui Xiao, serving as vanguard. He remained steadfast when others retreated, dying in the army in the ninth year of Jianwu. Ji Zun was known for self-denial, giving rewards to soldiers, owning no private property, and wearing plain clothes. Guangwu mourned deeply, personally attending his funeral. Posthumously named Marquis Cheng, Ji Zun was praised for his purity, loyalty, and Confucian conduct—selecting talents by Confucian standards, reciting poetry, and establishing a Confucian temple. He had no children, so his title was abolished.

source: ◆The biography of Chen Fan, whose courtesy name is Zhongju, was born in Pingyu, Runan. My grandfather served as the governor of Hedong. When Chen Fan was fifteen years old, he lived in a room with nothing to do, and it was very dirty inside and outside. His father's friend Xue Qin, who was from the same county, came to see him and said to Chen Fan: "Child, why don't you clean up to welcome the guests?" Chen Fan said: When a real man is alive, he should sweep away the rubbish in the world. How can he only care about his own room? Xue Qin knew that he had the ambition to clarify the world and admired him very much. At first, he served as an official in the county and was elected as Xiaolian and awarded the title of doctor. Because his mother passed away, he resigned from office and lived in mourning. When the mourning period expired, the governor Zhou Jing called him to serve as a chariot, but because he had different opinions on his advice, he abandoned the talisman and left. Later, the government recruited Fang Zheng, but he didn't go. Taiwei Li Gu recommended him and promoted him to Yilang, and then he was promoted to the prefect of Le'an. At this time, Li Ying was appointed as the governor of Qingzhou, and he was famous for his strict governance. After hearing the news, everyone in the subordinate city asked to leave. Chen Fan stayed alone because of his clean and honest performance. Zhou Chu, a county man, kept himself clean and cared for himself. He was invited by the county guards before and after him, but he refused to go. Only Chen Fan can recruit him. Chen Fan called him by his name instead of his name and respected him very much. A bed was specially built for him. After Zhou Chu left, the bed was hung up. The common man Zhao Xuan buried his relatives without closing the tomb passage, and lived in it for more than 20 years. The towns and cities praised his filial piety, and the states and counties treated him with courtesy several times. The county recommended him to Chen Fan and asked about his wife and children. They found out that Zhao Xuan's five children were all born during his mourning period.
target: Chen Fan, courtesy name Zhongju, was born in Pingyu, Runan. His grandfather served as Governor of Hedong. At fifteen, he lived in a dirty room. When his father's friend Xue Qin asked why he didn't clean it, Chen Fan replied that a real man should sweep away the world's rubbish, not just his own room. Xue Qin admired his ambition. Chen Fan began as a county official, was elected Xiaolian, and became a doctor. After his mother's death, he resigned to mourn. When the mourning period ended, Governor Zhou Jing summoned him, but Chen Fan left due to differing opinions. He later refused government recruitment. Taiwei Li Gu recommended him, and he became Prefect of Le'an. He remained in office while others fled from strict Governor Li Ying. Chen Fan recruited the reclusive Zhou Chu, treating him with great respect. He exposed Zhao Xuan's false filial piety—Zhao had lived in a tomb for over twenty years but fathered five children there—and punished him for deceiving the world.

source: Chen Fan then said angrily: "Sages make rituals, and moral people must abide by them, and unworthy people should also strive to do so." And the number of sacrifices does not need to be too many, as too much would be disrespectful. You are sleeping in the tomb, raising your children in the tomb, deceiving the world, stealing your reputation, confusing the people, and insulting the ghosts and gods. How is this unreasonable! So his crime was punished. General Liang Ji was a powerful man in the world. At that time, he sent a letter to Chen Fan, asking Chen Fan to handle private matters. The messenger was not allowed to see him, so he lied and asked to see Chen Fan. Chen Fan got angry and beat the messenger to death, and was sentenced to military service for his crime. After a slight promotion, he was appointed as minister. At this time, mountain bandits in Lingling and Guiyang were in harm's way, and the minister considered sending troops to fight. The emperor also ordered the prefectures and counties to select filial piety, integrity, and maocai as appropriate. Chen Fan went to the Supreme Court to argue and refute, saying: In the past, when Emperor Gaozu established a great cause, the people in the country were relieved, and the officials raised the people as if they were their own sons. Now the common people in the two counties are all the sons of the emperor. Isn't the cause of the harm to the sons caused by the corruption and cruelty of the local officials?
target: When General Liang Ji sent a messenger requesting private favors, Chen Fan beat the messenger to death and was sentenced to military service. He later became a minister. When mountain bandits threatened Lingling and Guiyang, Chen Fan argued against sending troops, stating that corrupt officials caused the unrest and that replacing them with virtuous men would resolve the problem without military action.

source: Because he offended the people around the emperor, he was released as the governor of Yuzhang. Chen Fan had a serious and upright temperament and did not receive guests. The scholars and the people also respected his aristocracy. He was recruited to serve as minister, and no one who saw him off walked out of the outer city gate. When he was promoted to Dahonglu, he met Li Yun, the magistrate of Baima County, who spoke bluntly and remonstrated. Emperor Huan was furious and Li Yun should be executed. Chen Fan wrote a letter to save Li Yun, but he was dismissed and returned home. He was appointed Yilang again, and a few days later, he was promoted to Guangluxun.
target: He also criticized the expedient recommendation of talents. Because he offended the emperor's associates, he was sent to be Governor of Yuzhang. Chen Fan was promoted to Dahonglu. When Emperor Huan wanted to execute Li Yun for blunt remonstrance, Chen Fan wrote to save him and was dismissed. He was later reinstated as Guangluxun.

source: Prisons are used to prohibit violations of laws and disciplines, and officials must manage them competently. If law enforcement is unfair and officials are unpopular, the country's politics will be harmed. Everyone in the world said that prisons were created because of public dissatisfaction, and titles were obtained because of bribery. If it wasn't smelly and dirty, where would the flies come from? You should investigate the gains and losses, choose the loyal and do the good, and issue an edict to hand over matters such as selecting talents to the minister and the three public officials, so that rewards and punishments should be in charge. Isn't this something to be thankful for? Emperor Huan adopted many of his opinions and released 500 maids. He only granted Huang Jun the title of Marquis of Guannei and Deng Wanshi the title of Marquis of Nanxiang. In the sixth year of Yanxi's reign, Emperor Huan came to Guangcheng Garden to hunt. Chen Fan advised him: I heard that the emperor only went to the garden to hunt in mid-autumn when he was offering sacrifices to heaven and earth. In accordance with the season, practicing weapons and shooting animals is helpful for sacrifices and is used to express filial piety.
target: He advised Emperor Huan against excessive titles and rewards, particularly for Deng Zun and Huang Jun, warning that improper enfeoffments caused cosmic disorder, crop failure, and poverty.

source: Emperor Huan read his memorial and became even more angry. Not adopted at all. Many people in the court hated him. As a result, the eunuch hated Chen Fan even more. He selected talents to send memorials, but the eunuch immediately rebuked him in the name of the emperor and sent them back. Many officials under him, including the long history and below, were often punished on pretexts, because Chen Fan was a famous official in his generation and they did not dare to harm him. Liu Wangzhi, whose courtesy name was Wenli, was from Gaotang, and Chengjin, whose courtesy name was Youping, was from Shaanxi County. They are all famous for their Confucian skills. They dare to speak outright when they are in office, and they often criticize some bad things. At that time, they all died in prison.
target: He noted that thousands of palace maids impoverished the country and urged their release. Emperor Huan adopted some advice, releasing five hundred maids and limiting titles.

Therefore, Gao Tao taught Shun that he should not wander around without instruction, and Zhou Gong taught Cheng Wang that he should not wander around in the fields. Yu, Shun and King Cheng should take this as a warning, let alone those whose virtues are not as good as those of their two masters! When the world is at peace, we need to exercise moderation, not to mention the current difficulties of "San Kong". The fields are empty, the court is empty, and the warehouses are empty. These are the so-called "three empties". In addition, the war continues and the people are scattered in all directions. This is when you are sad and haggard and can't sleep at night. How can you show off your power and be fascinated by the scene of galloping horses and horses? Moreover, it is rainy in early autumn, which is the time for the people to start sowing. Instead, they are required to drive birds and animals and do the hard work of opening roads. This is not the compassionate heart of a wise and sage king. Qi Jinggong wanted to go to Langyi to watch the sea. Yanzi told Qi Jinggong that the people did not like to listen to the sound of flags and horses, shaking their heads and frowning, so Jinggong did not go. King Mu of Zhou wanted to travel around the world and do whatever he wanted, and there were traces of his rutted horses everywhere. He sacrificed his father to read him the poem "Praying for Moves" to stop his thinking. I really hate the harm caused by amusement! The memorial was sent, but Emperor Huan did not accept it. Since Chen Fan became Guang Luxun, he and Huang Wan, a general with five senses, were in charge of the election of officials and did not favor the powerful. Therefore, he was framed and accused by the children of the wealthy family, and he was dismissed from office and returned home. Soon, he was recruited as a servant of Shangshu and transferred to Taizhong doctor. In the eighth year of Yanxi's reign, Yang Bing was replaced as Taiwei. Chen Fan declined and said: "Without mistakes or loss, I am not as good as Taichang Hu Guang in following the old classics; I am not as good as Yilang Wangchang in distinguishing the seven political principles of sun, moon, metal, wood, water, fire and earth and explaining the five classics." I am smart, open-minded, and versatile in both civil and military affairs. I am not as good as the consumptive prisoner Li Ying. Emperor Huan didn't allow it. Su Kang, Guan Ba ​​and others were appointed again. They excluded and framed the loyal ministers and collaborated with each other. Da Si Nong Liu, Ting Wei Feng Nui, and Henan Yin Li Ying were all punished for violating the emperor's will. Chen Fan took advantage of the court meeting to resolutely appeal to Li Ying and others, asking the emperor to pardon them and promote their titles.
target: Chen Fan advised against Emperor Huan's hunting at Guangcheng Garden, citing the "Three Empties"—empty fields, court, and warehouses—and ongoing wars. The emperor ignored him. As Guangluxun, Chen Fan and Huang Wan conducted elections without favoring the powerful, leading to false accusations and his dismissal. He was soon recalled as a servant and later became Taiwei, though he declined, citing his inferiority to Hu Guang, Wang Chang, and Li Ying. Chen Fan defended Li Ying and others punished for violating the emperor's will, weeping as he pleaded. He argued for leniency toward officials who executed eunuch associates despite pardons, comparing them to loyal ministers of old.

Chen Fan therefore wrote a letter to strongly dissuade him, saying: I heard that a wise king trusts his ministers, but a king who has subjugated his country is unwilling to listen to the straight words of his ministers.
target: Emperor Huan grew angrier and ignored him. The eunuchs hated Chen Fan, but because of his reputation, they dared not harm him directly. When Li Ying was imprisoned for party affiliation, Chen Fan wrote a strong remonstrance, comparing the persecution to Qin's book burning.

source: If you say the wrong thing, it will cause chaos in all directions. How much more to punish the innocent in prison and kill the innocent in the street! Once upon a time when Xia Yu was patrolling Cangwu and saw people killing people on the street, he got out of the car and cried, "Thousands of people are guilty, but only one person is guilty!" So Xia Yu prospered quickly. In addition, Qingzhou and Xuzhou were suffering from hot and drought conditions, and the grains were not harvested. The people had to leave their homes, and even coarse grains were not enough to eat. However, the palace is full of palace ladies, and all the national wealth is spent on them. The relatives have private families, are greedy for money and accept bribes. This is what Confucius said: Salary has nothing to do with the official position, and government orders come from the officials. Once upon a time, at the end of the Spring and Autumn Period, the virtues of the Zhou Dynasty declined, and no disasters were seen for decades. This was because God had abandoned it. God still misses the Han Dynasty, so he added some variation to inspire the emperor. The key to eradicating demons and evil is that you strengthen your self-cultivation. I am in the position of the Three Lords, and I am worried that I have a heavy responsibility. I dare not accept my salary for free, greedy for life, and sit back and watch the rise and fall of the Han Dynasty. If my suggestion is adopted, even if you kill me and leave my body with my body, I will not feel any hatred. Emperor Huan was dissatisfied with what Chen Fan said. He dismissed Chen Fan on the pretext that the talents he selected were inappropriate.
target: He warned that punishing the innocent would cause chaos and noted that droughts and famines plagued the land while the palace hoarded wealth. Emperor Huan dismissed Chen Fan for allegedly selecting inappropriate talents.

source: Emperor Huan was dissatisfied with what Chen Fan said. He dismissed Chen Fan on the pretext that the talents he selected were inappropriate. In the first year of Yongkang, Emperor Huan died, and Empress Dou took charge of the government. She issued an edict saying: The people are born to establish a king to manage them. There must also be virtuous assistant ministers to consolidate the great cause of the Wang family. The former Taifu Chen Fan was loyal, upright and magnanimous. Now Chen Fan was appointed as Taifu and managed the affairs of the minister. At that time, there had just been a national mourning, and the heir to the throne had not yet been determined. The ministers were afraid of offending the powerful ministers in the court, so they pretended to be ill and refused to go to court. Chen Fan wrote a letter to reproach them, saying: The ancients paid great attention to moral integrity and served the deceased monarch as if he were still alive. Now that the emperor's heir has not been decided, and political affairs are becoming increasingly urgent, why do you, gentlemen, abandon the sufferings of the country and lie down at home to rest? We are already lacking in righteousness, so how can we talk about benevolence? All the ministers were frightened and went to the court to do their work. After Emperor Ling ascended the throne, Empress Dowager Dou once again issued an edict to commend Chen Fan: to reward meritorious deeds to encourage good deeds, to praise righteousness and righteousness to encourage customs, and there is no virtue that cannot be repaid, as "Daya" chants. Grand Tutor Chen Fan assisted the late emperor and served as a capital official for many years. He was both loyal and filial. His moral conduct was the best in his dynasty. He was outspoken in his loyalty and advice and continued to do so even when he was old. Now Chen Fan is granted the title of Marquis of Gaoxiang, with a settlement of 300 households. Chen Fan declined and said: "The messenger came to my home and awarded me the seal of the Marquis of Gaoyang Township. I was really scared and didn't know what to do."
target: After Emperor Huan's death, Empress Dowager Dou appointed Chen Fan as Grand Tutor. When ministers feigned illness during the succession crisis, Chen Fan reproached them, and they returned to court. Emperor Ling granted Chen Fan the title of Marquis of Gaoxiang with three hundred households, but Chen Fan declined ten times.

source: Now the public opinion in the capital is boiling and the streets are noisy. It is said that Hou Lan, Cao Jie, Gongcheng Xin, Wang Fu, Zheng Sa and others, together with Mrs. Zhao Rao and other female officials in the palace, are disturbing the world and following their promotions. Anyone who opposes them will be punished. Now the ministers of the Manchu Dynasty are like driftwood in the river, floating here and there, coveting wealth and position, and fearing death. When you started your regency not long ago, you obeyed God's will and implemented punishments. Su Kang and Guan Ba ​​were both punished and executed. At that time, the sky and the earth were clear and bright, and people and ghosts were happy. Why did you indulge your attendants just a few months later? There is no greater evil or treachery than them. If they are not executed immediately, something will happen? It harms the country and the harm is unpredictable. I hope to show my memorial to the people around you and let the bad guys in the world know that I hate them. Empress Dowager Dou did not adopt it, and everyone in the court was shocked when they heard about it. Chen Fan discussed with Dou Wu and wrote in "The Biography of Dou Wu". When the incident was revealed, Cao Jie and others forged the Queen Mother's order to kill Dou Wu and others. Chen Fan, who was in his seventies at the time, heard about the rebellion. He led more than eighty officials and students and rushed into the Chengming Gate with swords drawn. He raised his arms and shouted: "The general is loyal to the country, but the eunuchs are rebelling. How can you say that the Dou family does not abide by the principles of being a minister?" Wang Fu came out of the palace at that time and happened to hear what he said, so he rebuked Chen Fan and said: The late emperor has just passed away and the tomb has not been built yet. What credit does Dou Wu have, while three brothers, father and son, are granted the title of marquis? In addition, he took away many palace maids, drank and had fun, and collected hundreds of millions of wealth in one month. If the minister is like this, is this the way of being a minister? You are the pillar of the country, you bend the law for your own interests and form cliques. How can you catch the thieves? So he ordered Chen Fan to be arrested. Chen Fan drew his sword and yelled at Wang Fu loudly. Wang Fu's soldiers did not dare to approach him. So more troops surrounded Chen Fan and others dozens of times, captured Chen Fan, and imprisoned him in Beisi Prison, which was run by eunuchs. The eunuch's knights kicked and stepped on Chen Fan, scolding Chen Fan: "Old man, can you still cut our staff and deprive us of extra income?" He was killed on the same day and his family members were exiled to Bijing. The clan, disciples, and old subordinates were all dismissed from their posts and imprisoned. Chen Fan's friend Zhu Zhen, who was from Chenliu, was the magistrate of Yuzhi County at the time. When he heard the news, he abandoned his official position and mourned Chen Fan, and his body was collected and buried. He hid Chen Fan's son Chen Yi in Ganling. After the incident was discovered, Zhu Zhen was arrested and imprisoned, and his whole family was imprisoned. Zhu Zhen was severely tortured, but he would rather die than tell Chen Yi's whereabouts. Chen Yi was able to escape. Later, the Yellow Turbans launched an uprising, and the court pardoned the party members, so Chen Yi was found. Later, Chen Yi became the prime minister of Lu.
target: Chen Fan and General Dou Wu planned to eliminate the eunuchs. Chen Fan warned the Empress Dowager about eunuch corruption, but she ignored him. When the plot was exposed, Cao Jie forged orders to kill Dou Wu. The seventy-year-old Chen Fan led over eighty officials and students into the palace, shouting against the eunuch rebellion. He was arrested, kicked and stepped on by eunuch soldiers, and killed that same day. His family was exiled, and his clan and disciples were imprisoned. His friend Zhu Zhen collected and buried his body, hiding Chen Fan's son Chen Yi. Zhu Zhen endured torture without revealing the son's location. Chen Yi later became Prime Minister of Lu.

source: Chen Yi was able to escape. Later, the Yellow Turbans launched an uprising, and the court pardoned the party members, so Chen Yi was found. Later, Chen Yi became the prime minister of Lu. Zhu Zhen, courtesy name Bohou, first served as a prefecture official. He wrote a letter to expose Shan Kuang, the prefect of Jiyin, for embezzlement, and implicated Shan Kuang's brother Zhongchang, the chariot and cavalry general Shan Chao. Emperor Huan ordered Shan Kuang to be arrested and handed over to Tingwei for interrogation. He reprimanded Shan Chao, and Shan Chao went to prison to plead guilty. There is a proverb in Sanfu: A chariot is like a chicken, a horse is like a dog, and evil is like the wind. The historian commented: During the reign of Emperor Huan and Emperor Ling, people like Chen Fan were able to establish a good reputation for their morals, speak out and comment on the dull reality, run through hardships and obstacles, and compete with the eunuchs in the same dynasty, which resulted in serious disasters.
target: The historian commented that during Emperors Huan and Ling's reigns, Chen Fan established a reputation for moral integrity, speaking out against corruption and competing with eunuchs despite great danger.

source: When it came time to meet Emperor Huan and Queen Mother Dou, he thought it was a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to advise Dou Wu. How solemn are the deeds of Yi Yin and Taigong in assisting the king that they pursue! Although the matter did not succeed, their faith was enough to support the people. The Han Dynasty was in chaos, but it did not perish. For more than a hundred years, it was the power of Chen Fan and others. ◆Biography of Wang Yun, also known as Wang Yun, Zi Shi, a native of Qi County, Taiyuan County.
target: Though his plans failed, his faith sustained the people, and the Han dynasty survived over a hundred years due to his efforts.
