Sima Xian, son of King Kang of Pengcheng, succeeded, then returned to his clan, and Sima Xian's son Sima Jun became heir.

source: Sima Lue then sent Sima Cao of the left to lead Cui Kuang and others to attack Wang Di. When the battle was about to begin, Cui Kuang quietly retreated and ran away. Cao Xu's army had no backup and was defeated. Cao Xu died on the battlefield. Sima Lue pardoned Cui Kuang's sins and sent his general Han Song to supervise Cui Kuang again to attack Wang Di. Wang Di surrendered. Soon after he came to the throne and opened a mansion, he was appointed as a regular servant of Sanqi. When Yongjia died in the third year, he was given posthumously to Shizhong and Taiwei. His son Sima Ju succeeded him. He died without a son and was succeeded by Sima Xian, the son of King Kang of Pengcheng. Later, Sima Xian returned to his clan and established Sima Xian's son Sima Jun as his heir. Sima Teng, the king of Wu'ai in Xincai, was named Yuanmai. When he was young, he was worshiped as a servant and served as a servant. He was granted the title of Shu Yinggong. He successively served as the prefect of Nanyang and Wei counties and was competent in his official position. He was recruited as Zongzheng, moved to Taichang, and transferred to Chijie, general of Ningbei, governor of Bingzhou's military affairs, and governor of Bingzhou. Emperor Hui attacked Sima Ying, king of Chengdu, and the six armies were defeated. Sima Teng and Anbei general Wang Jun killed Sima Ying's Youzhou governor He Yan and led a crowd to attack Sima Ying. Sima Ying sent Beizhonglang general Wang Bin to fight. Wang Jun led the Xianbei cavalry to attack Wang Bin, with Sima Teng as backup, and defeated the enemy. Sima Ying was frightened and took the emperor hostage back to Luoyang, where she promoted Sima Teng to General Anbei. In the early years of Yongjia, he was moved to the post of General of Chariots and Cavalry, Commander-in-Chief of Yecheng, and all military guards to guard Ye. Because of his meritorious service in welcoming the emperor, he was renamed King Xincai. At first, Sima Teng set out from Bingzhou and was stationed in Zhending. When it snowed heavily, the snow was several feet deep on the ground, and the snow melted and did not accumulate in front of the camp gate. Sima Teng felt strange and dug up the land. He got a jade horse, about a foot high, and dedicated the jade horse to him. Later, Ji Sang and others from Gongshi Fan and Pingyang people formed a group of bandits and raised troops in He County, Qinghe. More than a thousand people followed them to attack Dunqiu. On the pretext of burying Sima Ying, the king of Chengdu, he carried Sima Ying's memorial tablet in a car and attacked Ye with Zhang Hong's former general Li Feng and other generals. Sima Teng said: I have been in Chazhou for seven years, and Hu was unable to win when he besieged the city. That little thief Ji Sang is not worth worrying about. When Li Feng and others arrived, Sima Teng could not hold on and fled with Qingqi, but was killed by Li Feng. Sima Teng had four sons: Sima Yu, Sima Jiao, Sima Shao, and Sima Que.
target: Sima Teng, King of Xincai, served as Prefect of Nanyang and Wei, competent in office. He was recruited as Zongzheng, moved to Taichang, then served as General Ningbei and Governor of Bingzhou. When Emperor Hui attacked Sima Ying, Sima Teng and Wang Jun defeated Sima Ying's forces. Sima Ying fled with the emperor to Luoyang. Sima Teng was promoted to General Anbei, later General of Chariots and Cavalry. He was renamed King Xincai. When Ji Sang and others rebelled, Sima Teng dismissed them as insignificant but was killed by Li Feng. Sima Teng had four sons: Sima Yu, Sima Jiao, Sima Shao, and Sima Que. Sima Teng was frugal and stingy, not giving relief to people, leading to disaster.

source: That little thief Ji Sang is not worth worrying about. When Li Feng and others arrived, Sima Teng could not hold on and fled with Qingqi, but was killed by Li Feng. Sima Teng had four sons: Sima Yu, Sima Jiao, Sima Shao, and Sima Que. Si Juan was brave and powerful. When Sima Teng was killed, Si Ju chased Kuifeng, and Li Feng jumped into the river and died. On this day, Sima Yu, Sima Jiao, Sizhi Kui, Cui Ken, the governor of Chuchen, Shi Xianyuan, the chief of cavalry, and Cai Ke, a lieutenant in charge, were killed by Li Feng's remnant party. As for those famous and wealthy people who had drifted and moved to Ye, they were all dead. At the beginning, although Yezhong's inventory was empty, Sima Teng's capital expenditure was very rich. Sima Teng was frugal and stingy by nature, and did not give relief favors to people. When things were urgent, he gave the soldiers about a few liters of rice and a few feet of silk each. Therefore, the soldiers and the people did not contribute to him, which led to disaster. When Gou Xi rescued Ye, Ji Sang returned to Pingyang. It was midsummer and the corpses were rotten and unrecognizable. The bones of Sima Teng and his three sons were not recovered. The concubine Sima Que succeeded him. Sima Que, the king of Zhuang, whose courtesy name was Si'an, served successively as General Dongzhonglang, Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in Yuzhou, and guarded Xuchang. In the last years of Yongjia, he was killed by Shi Le. He had no sons, so at first Sima Tao, the son of King Sima Hun of Zhangwu, was asked to worship Sima Que, and later Sima Bi, the son of Sima Ku, the mighty king of Runan, was asked to be Sima Que's descendant. He died in the first year of Taixing without a son, so Sima Bi's younger brother Sima Miao succeeded Sima Que, and his official position was promoted to Shizhong. After his death, he was succeeded by his son Sima Huang, who became the Minister of Sanqi. Huan Wen deposed King Wuling, deposed Sima Huang as a commoner, and moved to Hengyang. Emperor Xiaowu established Sima Huang's younger brother Sima Chong as his heir, Sima Miao, who was killed by his slaves, and his son Sima Hui as his heir. Song accepted the abdication and the feudal state was cancelled. Nanyang King Sima Mo's character Yuan Biao was eager to learn when he was young. He was famous in the clan along with Emperor Yuan and Fan Yang King Sima You. At first he was named Pingchang Gong. In the last years of Emperor Hui's reign, many officials were worshiped as servants and servants, and gradually he was appointed as the crown prince's concubine and the official's official attendant. Sima Ying, king of Chengdu, ran to Chang'an, and Yue, king of Donghai, appointed Sima Mo as Beizhonglang general to guard Ye. In the early years of Yongxing, Shi Ai, Lou Quan, Hao Chang and others who had served under King Sima Ying of Chengdu attacked Ye, and Sima Mo's men planned and responded.
target: His bones were not recovered. Sima Que succeeded him, served as General Dongzhonglang, guarded Xuchang, and was killed by Shi Le. He had no sons, so Sima Tao, son of Sima Hun, was asked to worship Sima Que, later Sima Bi, son of Sima Ku, succeeded. Sima Bi died without sons, succeeded by his brother Sima Miao. After his death, his son Sima Huang succeeded, but Huan Wen deposed him. Emperor Xiaowu established Sima Chong as heir. Song accepted abdication and the feudal state was cancelled. Sima Mo, King of Nanyang, was eager to learn young, famous with Emperor Yuan and Sima You. He was initially named Pingchang Gong. He served as Crown Prince's Concubine and Official Attendant.

source: Sima Ying, king of Chengdu, ran to Chang'an, and Yue, king of Donghai, appointed Sima Mo as Beizhonglang general to guard Ye. In the early years of Yongxing, Shi Ai, Lou Quan, Hao Chang and others who had served under King Sima Ying of Chengdu attacked Ye, and Sima Mo's men planned and responded. Ding Shao, the prefect of Guangping, led his people to rescue Sima Mo. Sima Yan, the king of Fanyang, sent Kuiye governor Baodong to rescue him. Gong Yingxing and others fled separately. He was moved to the post of General Zhendong and guarded Xuchang. He was promoted to the title of King of Nanyang.
target: Sima Yue appointed him Beizhonglang General to guard Ye. He was promoted to King of Nanyang.

source: He was moved to the post of General Zhendong and guarded Xuchang. He was promoted to the title of King of Nanyang. In the early years of Yongjia, he was transferred to General Zhengxi, Kaifu, and Commander-in-Chief of Qin Yong and Liang Yi Zhu, replacing Wang Yong of Hejian to guard Guanzhong. Sima Mo was grateful for Ding Shao's kindness and ordered his countrymen to erect a monument for Gong Shao during his lifetime. At that time, there was a famine in Guanzhong, the people were eating each other, and there were diseases and plagues, and thieves openly committed evil. Sima Mo couldn't control his power, so he cast bronze human bells and tripods into cooking utensils in exchange for food. The commentators rejected this approach. Sima Yue, King of the East China Sea, summoned Sima Mo as Sikong and sent Fu Zhi, the supervisor of Zhongshu, to replace Sima Mo. Sima Mo's adviser Chun Yuding persuaded Sima Mo: Guanzhong is the land of abundance and the overlord's territory.
target: During famine in Guanzhong, Sima Mo cast bronze vessels into cooking utensils for food, criticized by commentators. Sima Yue summoned him as Sikong, but Sima Mo refused, persuaded by Chun Yuding.

source: Sima Cheng moved to cross the Yellow River on his own, and Wang Jun asked Sima Ji to serve as the governor of Jizhou to support his troops. Sima Yan entered Jizhou to mobilize his troops, then crossed the Yellow River south and defeated Liu Qiao and others. When Sima Ji, the king of Hejian, heard that Liu Qiao was defeated, he killed Zhang Fang and sent his head to Sima Yue. Sima Yue and Sima Jin went west to meet the emperor, while Sima Ke fled. So he escorted the emperor back to the capital and worshiped Sima Ji as Situ. In the third year of Yongxing's reign, he fell seriously ill and died at the age of thirty-seven. He had no son, so he adopted Sima Mo's son Sima Li Jisi. Sima Li followed Sima Mo to his own kingdom and was killed in Chang'an. Sima Sui, King Hui of Jinan, also known as Zibo, was the son of Wei Honglu, Sima Xun, the younger brother of Emperor Xuan. He was appointed as the Marquis of Guannei in Wei, was promoted to the Marquis of Qianchang Ting, and successively served as Dianjunlang. In the second year of Jingyuan, he was granted the title of Rural Marquis of Wucheng, the governor of Yecheng and the general of Beizhonglang. The fifth-class title was established, and he was named Zhu Abo, and gradually moved to the title of champion general. Emperor Wu accepted the abdication and named him King of Jinan. He died in the second year of Taishi. He has two sons: Sima Dan and Sima Ji. Sima Dan succeeded him and was renamed King of Zhongshan in the third year of Xianning. He died that year without any sons, and Sima Ji succeeded him. When the day was prosperous, Sima Ying appointed Sima Ji as General Jianwei. He, Hu Ju and others led the army to resist Wang Chuang, but fell into the battle formation and died. Without a son, the feudal state was cancelled. Later, Sima Sui's great-grandson Sima Xun, named Wei Chang, was more than ten years old. At the end of Emperor Min's reign, Chang'an fell, and Liu Yao's general Linghu Ni adopted Sima Xun as his son. When he reaches adulthood, he will be familiar with archery, horseback riding, and can shoot the bow left and right. In the sixth year of Xianhe, he came back from Guanyou and claimed to be the great-great-grandson of Sima Xun of Great Changqiu, the great-grandson of the champion general Sima Sui, King Hui of Jinan, and the son of Sima Can, the prefect of Lueyang. He therefore paid homage to Pu She, who was famous for his bravery.
target: Sima Sui, King Hui of Jinan, was son of Sima Xun, younger brother of Emperor Xuan. He was Marquis of Guannei in Wei, promoted to Marquis of Qianchang Ting, served as Dianjunlang. In the second year of Jingyuan, he was granted title of Rural Marquis of Wucheng, Governor of Yecheng and General Beizhonglang. He was named Zhu Abo, moved to Champion General. Emperor Wu made him King of Jinan. He died in the second year of Taishi. He had two sons: Sima Dan and Sima Ji. Sima Dan succeeded, renamed King of Zhongshan, died without sons, Sima Ji succeeded. Sima Ji served as General Jianwei, fought against Wang Chuang, died in battle. Without sons, the feudal state was cancelled. Later, Sima Sui's great-grandson Sima Xun, named Wei Chang, was adopted by Liu Yao's general Linghu Ni. He returned from Guanyou in the sixth year of Xianhe, claimed to be Sima Xun's descendant, paid homage to Pu She.

source: He successively served as the minister of the Huangmen of Sanqi, the regular servant of the Sanqi, secretary and supervisor, general of Annan, Chijie, and governor of all military affairs in Miannan, and moved to general Anbei and governor of all military affairs in Qingzhou. Sima Lue threatened Cheng Mu, the governor of Qingzhou, but Cheng Mu avoided him, and Sima Lue took charge of Qingzhou himself. In the early years of Yongxing, he ordered Liu Gen to raise troops in Donglai, deceive and confuse the people, and tens of thousands of people followed him. He attacked Sima Lue in Linzi, but Sima Lue could not resist and went to Liaocheng to defend.
target: He served as Governor of Liangzhou, attacked Chang'an, captured Hecheng. Guanzhong responded to him.

source: So Guanzhong all responded to Sima Xun by killing Ji Long's prefect commander. Sima Xun had few soldiers and could not stabilize himself, so he retreated to Liangzhou. During the Yonghe period, Zhang Ju occupied Longsu and sent an envoy to summon Sima Xun, who then entered Chang'an. At first, Du Hong, a native of Jingzhao, was superior to Zhang Ju because he was a wealthy man. Zhang Ju humiliated Du Hong because of his bravery. Du Hong knew that Sima Xun was afraid that Zhang Ju would strengthen his army, so he persuaded Sima Xun: If Zhang Ju is not killed, Guanzhong will not be owned by the country. Sima Xun then pretended to invite Zhang Ju and killed him on the spot. Zhang Ju's younger brother ran to Chiyang and gathered his troops to attack Sima Xun. After repeated defeats, he sued for peace and returned to Liangzhou. Later, Huan Wen attacked Guanzhong and ordered Sima Xun to send troops to Ziwu Road, but he was defeated by Fu Xiong; he withdrew his troops and stationed himself at Nuwa Fort. Soon he was promoted to the general who conquered the captives, supervising the military affairs in Guanzhong, and also the captain of the Xirong school. He was given the title of Marquis of Tongjiting. He was tyrannical and cruel in politics. As for the wealthy families under his jurisdiction and the state, if his words did not agree with him, he would kill them on their seats, or shoot them themselves with bows.
target: During the Yonghe period, he entered Chang'an, killed Zhang Ju, but was defeated by Fu Xiong. He was promoted to General Conquering the Captives, Marquis of Tongjiting. He was tyrannical, killing wealthy families who disagreed with him.

source: Later, Huan Wen attacked Guanzhong and ordered Sima Xun to send troops to Ziwu Road, but he was defeated by Fu Xiong; he withdrew his troops and stationed himself at Nuwa Fort. Soon he was promoted to the general who conquered the captives, supervising the military affairs in Guanzhong, and also the captain of the Xirong school. He was given the title of Marquis of Tongjiting. He was tyrannical and cruel in politics. As for the wealthy families under his jurisdiction and the state, if his words did not agree with him, he would kill them on their seats, or shoot them themselves with bows. The West is worried about his cruelty. In the state, he often wanted to occupy the Shu territory and had the intention of separatizing the Baifeng Dynasty. After Huan Wen heard about it, he devoted himself to appeasement and care and made his son Sima Kang the governor of Hanzhong. Sima Xun's rebellious plan was completed, but he did not take action because he was afraid of Zhou Fu, the governor of Yizhou. When Zhou Fu died, he gathered his troops into the sword pavilion. Liangzhou Biejia Yongduan and Xirong Sima Kaicui earnestly advised him, but they were both killed by Sima Xun. He claimed to be the shepherd of the two states of Liangyi and the king of Chengdu. Huan Wen sent Zhuzhuang to attack Sima Xun. Sima Xun's army was defeated and he was captured by Saizhuang. He and his son Long Wang, Chang Shisu, Sima Jintong and others were escorted to Danzhou Nahuo. They were all killed and their heads were sent to the capital. Sima Xun, the king of Qiao Gang, whose courtesy name was Zi Ti, was the son of Sima Jin, the younger brother of Emperor Xuan, Wei Zhonglang. He was appointed Marquis of Wei Guannei and was granted the title of Marquis of Yangting of Chengcheng. He participated in the military affairs and was worshiped as General Qingche and Zuojian Yulin. The fifth-class title was established and the title was changed to Jingyang Nan. Emperor Wu accepted the concession and named him King Qiao, granting him a fief of 4,400 households. He died in the second year of Taishi. He has two sons: Sima Sui and Sima Cheng. King Ding Sima succeeded him. After his death, his son Sima Sui succeeded him. He died in Shile. Emperor Yuan asked Sima to succeed him and his successor Sima Xun. King Min Sima Cheng was named Jingcai. He was loyal, ambitious and virtuous when he was young. At the invitation of the imperial court, he was promoted to General of Guangwei and Protector of Anyi to guard An'ding. He returned to Luoyang with Emperor Hui and became a guerrilla general. During the Yongjia period, the world gradually became chaotic, and they secretly attached themselves to Shan Jian, the general who conquered the south. When Shan Jian died, he entered Wuchang. When Emperor Yuan began to guard Yangzhou, Sima Cheng returned to Jiankang and took up the post of military counselor and wine worshiper. Emperor Min summoned him as General Longxiang, but he refused to take up the post. Emperor Yuan became the King of Jin, and according to the decree, he changed the title of Sima Cheng to King Qiao. In the early years of Taixing, he was appointed as the captain of the Tunqi School, and was appointed as the general of the auxiliary state and the general of the left army. Sima Cheng was frugal as an official and did not take concubines. Soon after, he was appointed as a regular servant of Sanqi, and his positions of auxiliary to the country and left army remained. Wang Dun was disloyal to the king, and the memorial was arrogant. The emperor summoned Sima Cheng at night, showed him Wang Dun's watch, and said, "Wang Dun has gained a high position in power in recent years, and there is no limit to what he wants. What should we do with him?"
target: He planned to occupy Shu territory. Huan Wen sent troops to attack him, Sima Xun was captured and killed. Sima Xun, King of Qiao Gang, was son of Sima Jin, younger brother of Emperor Xuan. He was Marquis of Wei Guannei, granted title of Marquis of Yangting of Chengcheng, served as General Qingche and Zuojian Yulin. He was named Jingyang Nan. Emperor Wu made him King Qiao with 4,400 households. He died in the second year of Taishi. He had two sons: Sima Sui and Sima Cheng. Sima Sui succeeded, died in Shile. Emperor Yuan asked Sima to succeed him. Sima Cheng, King Min, was loyal and virtuous young. He served as General Guangwei and Protector of Anyi. He returned to Luoyang with Emperor Hui, became Guerrilla General. During Yongjia period, he secretly attached himself to Shan Jian. When Shan Jian died, he entered Wuchang. When Emperor Yuan guarded Yangzhou, Sima Cheng returned to Jiankang, served as Military Counselor and Wine Worshiper. Emperor Yuan changed his title to King Qiao. He served as Captain of Tunqi School, General of the Auxiliary State and Left Army. He was frugal, did not take concubines. When Wang Dun was disloyal, the emperor summoned Sima Cheng at night, showed him Wang Dun's memorial. Sima Cheng advised early action.

source: Therefore, Taigong was granted the title of Qi, and Boqin lived in Lu. This was a beautiful system of the ancient kings and a moral principle that has prevailed in ancient and modern times. Our Jin Dynasty established its foundation, and all countries faced each other, so they appointed King Wu of Langye to guard and rule the Eastern Xia; Wencheng of Runan was in charge of Huaixu; King Fufeng and King Liang successively guarded Guanyou; and when Shuying came, he set up an official office in Bingzhou. Although the number of public clans today is no better than in the past, how can the old charter be abandoned? Sima Cheng, the regular servant of Sanqi, General Zuo, and King Qiao, is chaste, honest and upright, loyal and respectful in his heart. As a barrier to the left and right, his respect is even more obvious. Now Sima Cheng is appointed to supervise the military affairs of Xiangzhou, General Nan Zhonglang, and the governor of Xiangzhou. At first, Liu Wei thought that Wang Dun was too powerful and would eventually be difficult to control, so he persuaded the emperor to send his confidants to guard the place. Therefore, Sima Cheng was first appointed to Xiangzhou, and then Liu Wei, Dai Ruosi and others were appointed as state pastors. Sima Cheng traveled to Wuchang and went to see Wang Dun unarmed. Wang Dun held a banquet for him and wanted to observe Sima Cheng's intention. He said to Sima Cheng: Although the king is an elegant and talented man, I am afraid he is not a general. Sima Cheng said: I don’t necessarily know, can’t the lead knife cut it in one go? Sima Cheng said this because Wang Dun wanted to test his true feelings. As expected, Wang Dun said to Qian Feng: He doesn't know how to speak boldly even if he is afraid. What can a person like this who doesn't understand martial arts do? Let Sima Cheng go to his post. At that time, the land in Hunan was desolate and the public and private affairs were poor. Sima Cheng was frugal in person, rode a reed cart, and comforted him wholeheartedly, which earned him a good reputation. Wang Dun was afraid that he would become a disaster for himself, so he pretended to be a Northern Expedition and requisitioned all the ships in Sima Cheng's territory. Sima Cheng knew about his treacherous plan and gave half of it to him. Wang Dun soon began to create turmoil, and sent Huan Zhao, who joined the army, to persuade Sima Cheng. On the grounds that Liu Wei was a favorite and was now going on a crusade, Sima Cheng was appointed military commander and went on the road according to the military schedule. Sima Cheng sighed and said: I'm probably going to die! The land is desolate and sparsely populated, and the forces are alone and without reinforcements. Going into danger for the king is loyalty; dying for the king is righteousness. With loyalty and righteousness, what more can you ask for? So he wanted to advocate righteous deeds, but everyone was confused.
target: The emperor appointed him to guard Xiangzhou. Sima Cheng traveled to Wuchang, saw Wang Dun unarmed. Wang Dun tested him but let him go to his post. Sima Cheng was frugal, rode a reed cart, comforted people, earned good reputation. Wang Dun feared him, requisitioned his ships. When Wang Dun rebelled, Sima Cheng raised righteous deeds, but the city fell after more than a hundred days. Wei Yi sent him to Jingzhou, where Wang Yu killed him on the way at fifty-nine. After Wang Dun was pacified, Sima Cheng was posthumously awarded General of Chariots and Cavalry. His son Wuji succeeded him.

source: Ganzhuo's army was stationed at Gankou. Hearing that King Qiao's army had been defeated, the army stopped advancing. Wei Yi and others were fighting fiercely day by day. Wang Dun also sent the notes he had obtained from people in Taiwan Province and ordered Wei Yi to shoot them to Sima Cheng. Everyone in the city felt sad and regretful when they learned that the imperial court could no longer defend it. Liu Yi died in battle, and the stalemate lasted for more than a hundred days, and the city fell. Wei Yi sent Sima Cheng to Jingzhou in a carriage. The governor Wang Yu killed him on the way according to Wang Dun's wishes. He was fifty-nine years old at the time. Wang Dun was pacified, and Xia Shao posthumously awarded Sima Cheng the title of General of Chariots and Cavalry. His son Wuji succeeded him. Lie Wang Wuji was named Gongshou. When Sima Cheng was in trouble, he escaped because of his young age. During the Xianhe period, he was promoted to the rank of Sanqi Shilang, and gradually moved to Tunqi Xiaowei, Zhongshu, and Huangmen Shilang. Chu Pei, the governor of Jiangzhou, was going to the border town. Wuji, Dan Yang, Yin Huanjing and others paid him a farewell farewell at Banqiao. At that time, Wang Yu's son Danyang Cheng Qizhi was present. Wuji was determined to take revenge and drew his sword to kill Qizhi himself. Chu Pei and Huan Jing ordered the guards to protect Qizhi before he was spared. The imperial censor Zhongcheng Che recorded a report saying that Wuji wanted to kill someone on his own initiative and handed it over to Tingwei for punishment. Emperor Cheng issued an edict saying: Wang Dun caused a rebellion, and King Min was in trouble. Let's explore the origin of the matter. What is the fault of this king? However, the public and private legal system has also been decided. The king should focus on governing the country. How can he deduce the root cause and mess up the court laws. Those in charge should state the law, and from now on, those who violate it will be punished. So he was allowed to be treated as atonement. In the early years of the founding of the Yuan Dynasty, he moved to the position of regular attendant of Sanqi, then to the position of censor Zhongcheng. He left the capital to serve as the general of the auxiliary state, the prime minister of Changsha, and also the prime minister of Jiangxia. Soon he was transferred to the post of prefect of Nanjun and Hedong counties, and the position of general remained the same. He followed Dandan in the expedition against Shu, and because of his meritorious service, his youngest son Mo Qing was given the title of Duke Guangzhi, and was given the title of former general. Cheng Mian died in the sixth year and was given posthumously to General Wei. He has two sons: Sima Tian and Sima Qing. Sima Tian succeeded. King Jing Sima Tian was named Yuan Yu. When he was young, he became an official of Sanqi Shilang, and gradually rose to the rank of Sanqi Changshi, Huangmenlang, and Yushi Zhongcheng. At that time, Duke Haixi was deposed and Emperor Jian Wen ascended the throne. The martial law had not yet been lifted. Grand Sima Xun gathered in the middle hall and blew the police horn. Sima Tian presented an impeachment report but Zhou was disrespectful and asked to convict him.
target: Sima Wuji, King Lie, escaped when young during Sima Cheng's trouble. He served as Sanqi Shilang, moved to Tunqi Xiaowei and Zhongshu. He tried to kill Wang Yu's son Qizhi for revenge but was stopped. The emperor pardoned him. He served as Sanqi Changshi and Censor Zhongcheng, then General of the Auxiliary State and Prime Minister of Changsha. He followed Dandan in expedition against Shu, given title of Duke Guangzhi. He died in the sixth year of Cheng Mian, posthumously awarded General Wei. He had two sons: Sima Tian and Sima Qing. Sima Tian succeeded him. Sima Tian, King Jing, served as Sanqi Shilang, Sanqi Changshi, Huangmenlang, and Yushi Zhongcheng. When Duke Haixi was deposed, Sima Tian impeached Grand Sima Xun for disrespect. The emperor sighed at his courage.

source: Sima Tian succeeded. King Jing Sima Tian was named Yuan Yu. When he was young, he became an official of Sanqi Shilang, and gradually rose to the rank of Sanqi Changshi, Huangmenlang, and Yushi Zhongcheng. At that time, Duke Haixi was deposed and Emperor Jian Wen ascended the throne. The martial law had not yet been lifted. Grand Sima Xun gathered in the middle hall and blew the police horn. Sima Tian presented an impeachment report but Zhou was disrespectful and asked to convict him. Dan Wen looked at the memorial and sighed: "Young people from Japan dare to impeach me. It's really awe-inspiring." Sima Tian was loyal, upright and talented, and the officials in the court were afraid of him. He was moved to the post of General of the Right Guard, Si Yong, Grand Zhongzheng of the four states of Qin and Liang, paid homage to Shangshu, transferred to the post of Shizhong, and concurrently served as General of the Left Guard. He was appointed as the domestic history of Wu, and concurrently served as the Prince Zhanshi. Sima Tian had a high reputation and talent in the clan. During the reign of Emperor Xiaowu, he relied heavily on him and appointed him as the military governor of Yan, Qing, Ji, You, Jinling in Yangzhou, and the north and south counties of Xuzhou. He was also the general of Zhenbei, the governor of Yanqing and Jiejie. When he died in the fifteenth year of Taiyuan, he was given posthumously as a general of chariots and cavalry. He has four sons: Shangzhi, Huizhi, Yunzhi and Xiuzhi.
target: Sima Tian was loyal, upright, talented, feared by officials. He served as General of the Right Guard, Shangshu, Shizhong, and General of the Left Guard. He was appointed Domestic History of Wu and Prince Zhanshi. Emperor Xiaowu relied on him heavily, appointed him Military Governor of several states and General of Zhenbei. He died in the fifteenth year of Taiyuan, posthumously awarded General of Chariots and Cavalry. He had four sons: Shangzhi, Huizhi, Yunzhi, and Xiuzhi. Shangzhi succeeded him.

source: Sima Tian had a high reputation and talent in the clan. During the reign of Emperor Xiaowu, he relied heavily on him and appointed him as the military governor of Yan, Qing, Ji, You, Jinling in Yangzhou, and the north and south counties of Xuzhou. He was also the general of Zhenbei, the governor of Yanqing and Jiejie. When he died in the fifteenth year of Taiyuan, he was given posthumously as a general of chariots and cavalry. He has four sons: Shangzhi, Huizhi, Yunzhi and Xiuzhi. Shang's heir. Zhongwang Shangzhi's courtesy name was Bodao. He initially became a secretary-general and then moved to the rank of Sanqi-shilang. Sima Tian guarded Jingkou and served as General Zhenwei and Prime Minister Guangling. He resigned when his father died. After the mourning was over, he was appointed as a hussar to consult and join the army. Within the clan, there have been outstanding figures from generation to generation. When Wang Guobao was executed, Sanqi Changshi Liu Zhenzhi, Pengcheng Neishi Liu Juanzi, and Xuzhou Biejia Xu Fang were all arrested according to their accomplices and will be sentenced to death. Shang Zhi said to King Daozi of Kuaiji: The punishment should not be too extensive, Zhenzhi and others should be let go. Daozi obeyed him because all of Shang's brothers were serving in the court and relied on him whenever something happened. Wang Gong, the governor of Yanzhou, was jealous of Shang's growing power. He and Yu Kai, the governor of Yuzhou, raised troops to attack Shangzhi and went south to join forces with Yin Zhongkan, the governor of Jingzhou, Huanxuan, the Duke of Nanjun, and others. Daozi ordered the former general Wang Shi and the right general Xie Yan to attack Wang Gong, and Shangzhi to resist Yu Kai. Yun Zhi fought with Yu Kai's son Yu Hong in Dangli. Yu Hong was defeated and fled, killing Yu Kai's general Duan Fang. Yu Kai fled to Huan Xuan alone on horseback. Daozi appointed Shang Zhi as General Jianwei, Governor of Yuzhou, and Jiajie, all in accordance with Yu Kai's original positions, and soon he was promoted to General Former; he was allowed to be appointed as the domestic history of Wu; he was appointed as Hushi Sima and Danyang Yin; he was appointed as the prefect of Xiangcheng. Each is in charge of troops and horses, and his power surpasses others in the court. Later general Yuan Xian came to power and also relied on him as a back-up. Yuan Xian favored Zhang Fashun, and there was no difference between sitting up and sitting down during banquets. Shang Zhi entered the court and said to Yuan Xian with a serious face: Zhang Fashun is just an errand boy. If he has any outstanding talents, he will be promoted quickly. In today's holy world, this shouldn't be the case. Yuan Xian remained silent. Shang Zhi added: Although there are many people in the clan, there are few people who can correct and advise. The emperor still accepts the opinions of the people in the grassland. What's more, I have a close blood relationship with the chief. I have been favored for several generations. How can I sit back and watch the gains and losses without speaking out. So he scolded Bo Shu and ordered him to retreat. Everyone in the room was surprised. Shang Zhi talked and laughed freely, but Yuan Xian held a deep grudge. Later, Xiangfu issued a talisman and ordered two thousand warriors to be dispatched. He refused and said: Western Fan is connected to a remote area, where enemy invaders appear and disappear, but the number of troops is only a few thousand, which is not enough to defend it, and there are no more people to send out. Yuan Xian was particularly angry. It happened to be that he was about to attack Huan Xuan, so he did not cause any harm. When Yuan Xian attacked the west in the name of Feng Zhao, he ordered Shang Zhi to be the vanguard, and Shang Zhi's son Wen Zhong was appointed as General Ningyuan and announced the internal history of the city. When Danxuan arrived at Gushu, he sent Feng Gai and others to attack Liyang, cut off Dongpu and burned Shangzhi's ships.
target: Sima Shangzhi, King Zhong, served as Secretary-General and Sanqi Shilang. He guarded Jingkou as General Zhenwei and Prime Minister Guangling. After his father's death, he served as Hussar Consultant. Within the clan, outstanding figures appeared generation after generation. Hugh zigzag season preview. He was appointed to an important position in the Qing Dynasty. So he returned to the city and took his nephews to join Murong Chao. Hearing about the rise of the rebel army, he returned to the capital. The general, King Wuling, issued an order: "The former General Longxiang is a man of talent, integrity and careful review, and has accomplished his feats." In the Battle of Liyan, it all depends on being quick and resourceful. When he was exhausted, he risked his life and ran away, but he also gathered righteous people and embarked on the rugged and dangerous journey. Since it is in line with the behavior of being close to sages, he should be given the important task of governing Shaanxi. He can be allowed to supervise the military affairs of the six states of Jing, Liang, Ning, Qin and Yong, and concurrently serve as the captain of the Southern Barbarians, the governor of Jingzhou, and the governor of Jingzhou. source: The imperial court replaced him with Wei Yongzhi, the governor of Yuzhou, and summoned Xiuzhi back to the capital. Because his son Wensi made trouble, Shangshu apologized and said: Wensi cannot do good, so he remains guilty, worried, scared, shocked, confused, regretful and ashamed. I failed to manage the family well and failed to revive my authority and teachings, causing my sons and nephews to break the law and let down the sage's court. I was so frightened and ashamed that I had no shame in living like this. I asked to be relieved of my post and return to the court with my guilt. The emperor forbids it. Later, because of resentment about Wen Si, he colluded with Lu Zongzhi, the governor of Yongzhou, and planned to kill the people in power together.
target: He served as General of the Empress and Internal Secretary of Kuaiji. He was demoted for violating the ban. When Lu Xun rebelled, he was appointed military commander. source: I am indeed ignorant, but I have heard about it from a gentleman. With Ping Xi’s perfect virtue, wouldn’t there be no ministers who would devote themselves to him? source: Where did Wang Xiang and Zheng Chong ever Lithos Wang Xiang, whose courtesy name was Xiuzheng, was born in Linyi, Langye, and was a descendant of Wang Ji, an admonishing official of the Han Dynasty. His grandfather, Wang Ren, was the governor of Qingzhou. His father, Wang Rong, was recruited by the government, but he refused to become an official. Wang Xiang is very filial by nature. His mother died when he was young, and his stepmother Zhu was not loving and spoke ill of him many times, thus losing his father's love. Wang Xiang is often asked to clean the cattle pen, and Wang Xiang is more respectful and cautious. When his parents were ill, he couldn't take off his clothes, so he had to taste the medicine himself first. His stepmother once wanted to eat live fish. It was freezing cold at that time. Wang Xiang took off his clothes and was about to break the ice to catch fish. The ice suddenly cracked on its own and two carps jumped out. He took the fish home. Stepmother wants to eat roasted oriole again. Dozens more orioles flew into his tent and took them to his stepmother. The villagers were amazed and thought it was caused by the influence of filial piety. There was a red sand fruit tree bearing fruit, and his stepmother ordered him to guard it. Whenever there was wind or rain, Wang Xiang would hug the tree and cry. His filial piety reaches such an extent. During the war at the end of the Han Dynasty, he supported his mother and took his younger brother Wang Lan to escape to Lujiang. They lived in seclusion for more than 20 years and refused to accept appointments from prefectures and counties. When her mother passed away, she became ill due to grief and could only stand with a cane. Lu Qian, the governor of Xuzhou, asked him to be his guest. Wang Xiang, who was nearly sixty years old, resolutely refused to accept the offer.
target: Wang Xiang, courtesy name Xiuzheng, was from Linyi, Langye, a descendant of Han official Wang Ji. His grandfather Wang Ren served as Qingzhou governor, while his father Wang Rong refused government service. Wang Xiang was exceptionally filial. After his mother died young, his stepmother Zhu treated him poorly and spoke ill of him, causing his father to lose affection for him. Despite being ordered to clean cattle pens, Wang Xiang remained respectful. When his parents fell ill, he personally tasted their medicine. During freezing weather, his stepmother desired live fish; Wang Xiang removed his clothes to break ice, and two carps leaped out spontaneously. When she wanted roasted oriole, dozens flew into his tent. Villagers attributed these events to his filial piety. During late Han warfare, he supported his mother and younger brother Wang Lan while hiding in Lujiang for over twenty years, refusing official appointments. After his mother's death, he became ill from grief. At nearly sixty, he initially refused Governor Lu Qian's invitation but eventually accepted after Wang Lan's persuasion. He defeated bandits, brought peace to the state, and was praised in song.

source: At that time, there were robbers and thieves everywhere. Wang Xiang led and encouraged the soldiers to defeat the enemy many times. The state is peaceful and peaceful, and political decrees and enlightenment are passed unimpeded. People at that time sang: Haiyi's happiness really depends on Wang Xiang. The fact that the feudal country is not poor is due to others. Wang Xiang was recommended as a scholar, appointed as Wen Ling, and promoted to Da Sinong many times. Gaogui Xianggong ascended the throne, participated in the planning and made meritorious services, and was named Guannei Marquis. His official title was Guang Luxun, and he was transferred to Sili Xiaowei. Following his attack on his mother Qiu Jian, he increased his residence by 400 households, was promoted to Taichang, and was granted the title of Marquis of Wansui Ting. The emperor came to the Imperial Academy and ordered Wang Xiang to be the third elder. Wang Xiang faces south, leaning on several tables and holding a walking stick, and considers himself a teacher. The emperor asked for advice from the north, and Wang Xiang taught him the key points of political education for emperors and ministers of the Ming Dynasty. Everyone who heard this was inspired. When the noble countryman was killed, the ministers of the court held a mourning ceremony. Wang Xiang cried and said, "The old minister has no face to see others." His nose burst into tears and everyone looked ashamed. Soon after, he was promoted to Sikong, and was transferred to Taiwei, and then to Shizhong. He was awarded the fifth-class title and was named Suiling Marquis, with a settlement of 1,600 households.
target: Wang Xiang held various official positions including Wen Ling, Da Sinong, and was named Guannei Marquis. He served as Sili Xiaowei, Taichang, and Marquis of Wansui Ting. The emperor appointed him as third elder at the Imperial Academy, where he taught political education. He was promoted to Sikong, Taiwei, and Shizhong, eventually becoming Suiling Marquis with 1,600 households.

source: He was awarded the fifth-class title and was named Suiling Marquis, with a settlement of 1,600 households. When Emperor Wen became the king of Jin, Wang Xiang and Xun Pin went to see him. Xunjie said to Wang Xiang: "The Prime Minister respects his position. He Hou has already respected him, so he should kneel down and worship him now." Wang Xiang said: The prime minister is indeed noble, but he is the prime minister of Wei. We are the three princes of the Wei State. The difference between the prince and the king is only one level, and the ranks are the same. How can the three princes of the emperor be bowed to others easily? It damages the prestige of the Wei Dynasty and the reputation of the King of Jin. A gentleman treats others with courtesy, so I will not bow down. After entering, Xunjie knelt down and worshiped, while Wang Xiang performed a long salute alone. Emperor Wen said: Today I know the reason why you are appreciated! When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, he granted Wang Xiang the title of Taibao, promoted him to the title of Duke, and granted him the powers of seven additional officials. Not long after Emperor Wu came to the throne, he humbly sought out honest opinions. Wang Xiang, He Zeng, Zheng Chong and other senior ministers wished to see him again, so the emperor sent Ren Kai, an aide-de-camp, to inquire about the gains and losses and the primary measures for political enlightenment. Wang Xiang requested to retire many times on the grounds of old age and frailty, but the emperor refused. The censor, Zhongcheng Hou Shiguang, requested that Wang Xiang be removed from his official position on the grounds that Wang Xiang had been ill for a long time and could not attend court. The emperor issued an edict saying: The Taibao is an experienced official with high qualifications and high virtues, and I rely on him to govern. I have not complied with his wishes despite humility and concessions many times before and after. This is not something that officials can discuss. So the memorial of Bao Huangguang was withheld. Xingmang firmly requested to resign and issued an edict to allow Duke Suiling to return to his residence. His official position was the same as that of Baofu. He was above the three divisions and his salary was the same as before. The edict said: People in ancient times retired and no longer served princes. Now, although he is staying in the capital as the Duke of the country, he should not be made to suffer any more hardships due to court invitations. Give him a cane for several cases, so you don't have to go to court. Ask him for advice on important matters. He was given a chariot and four horses, a house, one million dollars, five hundred pieces of silk, beds and mats, six housekeepers named Suiling Gong's housekeepers, and twenty officers and cavalrymen. Wang Zhao, Wang Xiang's son, the Cavalry Commander, was appointed to serve as a minister, so that he would always have time to pay respects to Wang Xiang. Because Taibao was of high moral character and did not have a house at home, he temporarily stayed in the house until the house given to him was completed before moving out.
target: When Emperor Wen became King of Jin, Wang Xiang refused to kneel, stating that as a Wei official, he would not bow to others. Emperor Wu appointed him Taibao and promoted him to Duke. Despite repeated retirement requests due to age, the emperor refused, granting him privileges including exemption from court attendance. Upon critical illness, Wang Xiang instructed his descendants on simple burial, forbidding elaborate ceremonies and expensive items. He died in the fourth year of Taishi at age eighty-five. His sons included Wang Zhao, Wang Xia, Wang Fu, Wang Lie, and Wang Fen.

source: Wang Yan, nicknamed Shizhi, was appointed as the Central Guard. Wang Chen, whose courtesy name was Shiwei, was appointed as the son of the state to offer wine. At first, Lu Qian had a sword. Wang Lan's descendants had many talented people from generation to generation and prospered in Jiangzuo. There is another biography in this book about Wang Cai's son Wang Dao. Zheng Chong, courtesy name Wenhe, was born in Kaifeng, Rongyang. He was born in a poor and humble background, and established moral integrity beyond ordinary people. He was quiet and had few desires. He loved to ponder the classics and history, and he had extensive research on Confucianism and hundreds of schools of thought.
target: Zheng Chong, courtesy name Wenhe, was from Kaifeng, Rongyang. Born poor, he established moral integrity, was quiet with few desires, and extensively studied Confucian classics.

source: Zheng Chong, courtesy name Wenhe, was born in Kaifeng, Rongyang. He was born in a poor and humble background, and established moral integrity beyond ordinary people. He was quiet and had few desires. He loved to ponder the classics and history, and he had extensive research on Confucianism and hundreds of schools of thought. He has good looks and good reputation, must follow etiquette in his actions, be sincere and self-responsible, and does not seek the reputation of his hometown people. Therefore, the state and county did not discover his talent for a long time. When Emperor Wen of Wei was the crown prince, he searched for and promoted lowly talents, appointed Zheng Chong as the literary minister, and was promoted to Shangshulang many times. He also went to Beijing to replace Chenliu as the prefect. Zheng Chong regards elegance as his virtue. He does not have the reputation of being talented or magnanimous in his position. He only needs food and clothing and does not seek wealth. The world values ​​him for this. General Cao Shuang recommended him to serve as a lieutenant, and then he was promoted to a regular attendant of Sanqi and Guang Luxun. In the third year of Jiaping's reign, he was appointed Sikong. When the Duke of Gaogui was giving lectures on Shangshu, Zheng Chong took the scriptures and taught them in person, and was rewarded together with his attendant Zheng Xiaotong. Soon he was transferred to Situ. Chang Daoxiang came to the throne and appointed him as Taibao, ranking above the three divisions, and named him Shouguang Hou. Although Zheng Chong's official rank is the same as that of prime minister, he does not interfere in world affairs. At that time, Emperor Wen assisted the government and after pacifying the Shu Kingdom, he ordered Jia Chong, Yang Hu and others to formulate etiquette and legal regulations respectively. They all asked Zheng Chong first and then implemented them. When Emperor Wei announced his abdication, he sent Zheng Chong to present the policy letter. source: Wang Chen, courtesy name Chudao, was born in Jinyang, Taiyuan. His grandfather, Wang Rou, was a lieutenant general of the Huns in the Han Dynasty. Now that the decree is promulgated, it means that there will be rewards and encouragement. I am afraid that some honest and self-restrained people will be afraid of the rewards and will not speak up; those who are greedy for money will make random reports for the sake of profit. If the solicitation is not timely and unrealistic rewards are not given, then those who learn about the matter from afar do not know the details of the matter, see in vain that the promises are not fulfilled, and will say that the reward is empty but not implemented.
