He left the capital to serve as the governor of Hanoi, but because the county prince could not be appointed as the governor, he was transferred to General Dong Zhonglang to guard Xuchang. When Prince Minhuai was imprisoned in Xuchang, Wang Jun followed Empress Jia's will and killed the prince together with Sun Lu of Huangmen. He was promoted to general of Ningbei and governor of Qingzhou. Soon he was appointed as General Ningshuo, Chijie, and Commander-in-Chief of Youzhou's military affairs. At that time, the court was in chaos and thieves were emerging. For his own safety, Wang Jun made friends with Yi Di and married one of his daughters to Xianbei Wu Wuchen and the other to Su Shuyan.
target: He served as Prince Consort and later held various military and civil posts. During the chaos of the court, he allied with Yi Di, marrying his daughters to Xianbei leaders for safety.

source: When Prince Minhuai was imprisoned in Xuchang, Wang Jun followed Empress Jia's will and killed the prince together with Sun Lu of Huangmen. He was promoted to general of Ningbei and governor of Qingzhou. Soon he was appointed as General Ningshuo, Chijie, and Commander-in-Chief of Youzhou's military affairs. At that time, the court was in chaos and thieves were emerging. For his own safety, Wang Jun made friends with Yi Di and married one of his daughters to Xianbei Wu Wuchen and the other to Su Shuyan. After King Sima Lun of Zhao usurped the throne, the three kings raised troops to protest. Wang Jun led the troops to wait and see, preventing the message from being passed on, so that the people in his territory could not join the rebel army. King Sima Ying of Chengdu wanted to attack Wang Jun but had no time. King Zhao Sima Lun was executed, and Wang Junjin was named General Anbei. When Sima Yi, king of Hejian, and Sima Ying, king of Chengdu, attacked Luoyang and killed Sima Yi, king of Changsha, Wang Jun felt indignant. Sima Ying petitioned Youzhou Governor Shi Kan to serve as You Sima, replaced Shi Kan with You Sima He Yan, and secretly ordered He Yan to kill Wang Jun and annex Wang Jun's army. Heyan and Wuwan Shanyu Shendeng planned this matter, so they agreed with Wang Jun to go to the clear spring in the south of Jicheng to play. There are two roads going west in Jicheng, one for He Yan and one for Wang Jun. He Yan prepared to take the opportunity to strike when he met Wang Jun with the honor guard. It was raining heavily and all the weapons were wet, so they returned without being able to realize their plan. Shan Yu therefore plotted with his fellow tribesmen and said: He Yan planned to kill Wang Jun, but when he was about to succeed, it rained and the plan failed to come true. This is God's help to Wang Jun. Going against God's will is unlucky, and I cannot be complicit with He Yan for a long time. So he told Wang Jun his plan. Wang Jun secretly ordered the army to impose martial law, and He Chanyu surrounded He Yan. He Yan took the white banner and went to Wang Jun's place to surrender, so He Yan was killed and Wang Jun occupied Youzhou himself. He built equipment on a large scale, summoned Wuchen, and led a total of 20,000 Hu and Jin people to march against Sima Ying. With Chief Qi Hong as the vanguard, he encountered Sima Ying's general Shi Chao in Pingji and defeated Shi Chao. Wang Jun took advantage of the victory and captured Yecheng. The soldiers looted and looted brutally, and many people died. The Xianbei people plundered women wantonly. Wang Jun ordered the beheading of women who dared to hide them, so eight thousand people were thrown into the Yishui River.
target: After King Sima Lun of Zhao usurped the throne, Wang Jun led troops to wait and see. He later killed He Yan, who plotted against him, and occupied Youzhou. He built equipment and led 20,000 Hu and Jin troops against Sima Ying, defeating his general and capturing Yecheng, where his soldiers looted brutally. Wang Jun's power grew, and he was promoted to General Hussar and Commander-in-Chief of Hebei. During the Yongjia period, he fought Shi Le and Liu Kun, but his harsh rule led to defections. He planned to become emperor based on prophecies, killing those who advised against it. Shi Le pretended to surrender, and Wang Jun, trusting him, was captured and killed. Wang Jun had no sons, and his title passed to his nephew Daosu.

source: In the second year of Taiyuan, an edict was issued to promote the destruction of the country and succeed Jueshi, and made Wang Shen's nephew Daosu the Duke of Boling. After his death, he was succeeded by his son Chongzhi. In the eleventh year of Yixi's reign, he was renamed Dongguan County Duke. Song accepted the abdication and the feudal state was cancelled. Xunjie, courtesy name Jingqian, was from Yingchuan and was the sixth son of Wei Taiwei Xun You. When he was young, he was appreciated by his brother-in-law Chen Qun. He was extremely filial by nature, and was famous at an early age, with extensive knowledge and thoughtful thinking. Wei Shi was appointed Zhonglang because of his father's meritorious service. Emperor Xuan assisted in the government affairs and was surprised to see Xun Hao and said, "He is really Xun Lingjun's son." He was promoted to the rank of Sanqi Shilang, and then promoted to the rank of Shizhong. He taught classics to the young emperor of Wei. He was worshiped as a cavalry captain and given the title of Marquis of Guannei. He criticized Zhong Huizhi for not being consistent in the Book of Changes, and he discussed with Sima Jun, the king of Fufeng, about who should be the leader in benevolence and filial piety, which was praised by the world. At that time, Cao Shuang had sole power. He Yan and others wanted to harm Taichang Fu Gu, but Xun Hao rescued him and saved him from danger. When Gao Guixiang Gong came to the throne, Xunjie said to Emperor Jing: Now that the emperor has ascended the throne, the way to obtain the monarchy is unusual. We should quickly send people to various places to declare benevolence and observe the trends in the outside world. His mothers Qiu Jian and Wen Qin were indeed dissatisfied and sent troops to rebel. Xunjie participated in the expedition against Ceqiu Jian and others and made meritorious service. He was promoted to the title of Marquis of Wansuiting and was granted the title of 400 households.
target: Xunjie, courtesy name Jingqian, was from Yingchuan and the sixth son of Wei Taiwei Xun You. Known for filial piety and extensive knowledge, he served as Zhonglang and later Sanqi Shilang. He taught the young emperor of Wei and was granted the title of Marquis of Guannei. He rescued Fu Gu from Cao Shuang's harm and advised Emperor Jing to declare benevolence after Gao Guixiang Gong's ascension. He participated in suppressing rebellions and was promoted to Marquis of Wansuiting. Under Emperor Wen, he became Shangshu and later Sikong.

source: Xunjie's nephew Chen Tai died. Xunjie replaced Chen Tai as a servant and was also in charge of the staff. He resigned four times and then took office. Xun Hao succeeded Chen Tai and became more respectful and prudent, comprehensively assessed reputation and reality, and clarified customs. During the reign of Xianxi, he was promoted to Sikong and became a rural marquis. Xunjie was over sixty years old. He was filial and devoted. He resigned from his post because of his mother's funeral. He was so sad that he almost lost his mind. He was praised throughout the country. Emperor Wen ordered that Sikong should be given a funeral ceremonial entourage in accordance with the precedent of the Han Dynasty Fu Guang's funeral for his mother. After Shu was pacified, five levels of nobility were established, and Xun Zhuan was ordered to formulate etiquette. Xun Yun Shangshu asked Yang Hu, Ren Kai, Yu Jun, Ying Zhen, and Kong Hao to jointly delete the old regulations and compile the Jin etiquette. In the early years of Xianxi's reign, he was granted the title of Marquis of Linhuai.
target: He was filial, resigning for his mother's funeral, and was praised nationwide. He formulated Jin etiquette and was promoted to Duke of Linhuai.

source: Soon after, another edict was issued saying: "Shi Zhong, Taiwei Xun Pin, is gentle, respectful, loyal and fair, has pure conduct, is knowledgeable about ancient affairs and is knowledgeable, and is not slacking off despite his advanced age." Let him act as the Crown Prince and Tutor, and his official positions of Shizhong and Taiwei will remain. At that time, because the elegant songs in "Zhengde" and "Dayu" did not match, Xunhao was ordered to settle the music. Before the matter was over, he died in the tenth year of Taishi. The emperor mourned for him, the crown prince attended the funeral in person, and the emperor and empress presented items for the funeral furnace. The etiquette level exceeded the norm. The edict said: "Servants, Taiwei, Princes and Tutors, Linhuai Gong Xun Chan, have pure conduct and follow morality, are honest and fair in government, hold various internal and external official positions, have outstanding achievements, teach the prince, and promote good and beautiful ways. They can be said to be people with perfect behavior, beginning and ending." I am very sad that he passed away unfortunately. Give him a coffin, a court dress, and a set of clothes. Mi Hao Kang. He also issued an edict saying: The Taiwei did not care about his own home, he did not live in a gorgeous house, and his frugal ambitions became even more famous after his death. Give his family two million dollars and let them build a house. In the early years of Xianning, an edict was issued to rank the meritorious officials and to offer sacrifices in the ancestral temple. The official in charge asked Xun Hao and other twelve people to inscribe their achievements on Taichang's wrapping and offer them as sacrifices in the ancestral temple. Xun Pin understood the "Three Rites" and the court etiquette, but he had no upright moral integrity and only catered to Xun Xu and Jia Chong. At the beginning, when the crown prince was about to marry a concubine, Xunjie said that Jia Chong's daughter Zunrong had good moral character and could stand for election, so she was ridiculed by people at the time. Xun Zhuan had no sons, so his grandnephew Xun Hui succeeded him. In the early years of the Jin Dynasty's southern crossing to An'an, Xunxu, the great-great-grandson of Xunjie's brother, became a descendant of Xunjie and was granted the title of Duke of Linhuai.
target: He served as Crown Prince Tutor and Taiwei, settling music before dying in the tenth year of Taishi. The emperor mourned him greatly. Xunjie understood the "Three Rites" but lacked upright moral integrity, catering to Xun Xu and Jia Chong. He had no sons, and his title passed to his grandnephew Xun Hui.

source: In the early years of the Jin Dynasty's southern crossing to An'an, Xunxu, the great-great-grandson of Xunjie's brother, became a descendant of Xunjie and was granted the title of Duke of Linhuai. When Xun Xu died and there was no successor, Emperor Xiaowu granted Xun Xu's son Xun Heng the title of successor to Xun Zhuan. Xun Heng died and was succeeded by his son Xun Longfu. Song accepted the abdication and the feudal state was cancelled. Xun Xu, whose courtesy name was Gongzeng, was from Yingyin, Yingchuan. He was the great-grandson of Xun Shuang, Sikong of the Han Dynasty. His grandfather Xun Lai was appointed as the captain of Shesheng. My father suffered from swelling and died early. Xun Xu stayed at his uncle's house. He is smart and early in life and can write articles in his teens.
target: Xun Xu, courtesy name Gongzeng, was from Yingyin, Yingchuan, and the great-grandson of Han Sikong Xun Shuang. Orphaned young, he was raised by his uncle. He was intelligent and wrote articles in his teens.

source: He was promoted to Tingweizheng, participated in the military affairs of Emperor Wen's general, and was given the title of Marquis of Guannei. He was transferred to work as a lieutenant and also as a recorder. When Duke Gaogui wanted to launch a coup, the general sent Sun You and others to guard the gates of Khotan. Anyang Hou Sima Qian, the younger brother of Emperor Wen, heard that he was in trouble and wanted to enter the city. Sun You said to Sima Qian: Those who have not entered can enter through Dongye Gate. Sima Qian arrived. Emperor Wen thought he was late. Sima Qian told him the reason. Emperor Wen wanted to destroy Sun You's family. Xun Xu Jin remonstrated and said: Sun You should be punished for not accepting the Marquis of Anyang. However, things have seriousness, and punishment cannot be decided based on happiness and anger. Now that Cheng Chou's punishment was limited to himself, but Sun You's entire family was killed, I'm afraid the righteous people will discuss it privately. So Sun You was exempted from civilian status. At that time, the official cavalry sent a request to enter the Shu Kingdom as an assassin. Gou Xu said to Emperor Wen: Duke Ming rules the world by justice, and he should rely on justice to defeat disobedience. If you rely on assassins to eliminate enemies, you will not be the so-called model of the world. Relying on virtue to make distant people surrender. Emperor Wen thought it was right. When Zhong Hui rebelled, the details had not yet been discovered, and outsiders came to report first. Emperor Wen had always been kind to Zhong Hui and did not believe that he would rebel. Xun Xu said: Although Zhong Hui was favored, he was not necessarily loyal by nature, so he had to take precautions. Emperor Wen immediately went out to guard Chang'an. Guo Yi, the chief secretary, and Wang Shen, who joined the army, persuaded Emperor Wen to repel Xun Xu because he was Zhong Hui's nephew and uncle. He grew up in his uncle's family when he was young. Emperor Wen did not accept it, but asked Xun Xu to accompany him and treated him as before. Before this, Xun Xu stated that in order to conquer Shu, Wei Xuan should be appointed as the supervisor of the army. When the war broke out in Shu, it was all up to Wei Xuan to maintain it. After the Zhonghui rebellion was put down, he returned to Luoyang and took charge of important departments together with Pei Xiu and Yang Rong. At that time, an envoy was sent to visit the State of Wu, and the literati at that time were asked to write documents to Sun Hao. Emperor Wen chose the document written by Xun Xu. Sun Hao replied that he agreed to the marriage, and Emperor Wen said to Xun Xu: The documents you wrote before made Wu Guo want to submit, which is better than a hundred thousand troops. Emperor Wen ascended the throne of Jin and appointed Xunxu as his minister. He was granted the title of Anyangzi and was granted a settlement of 1,000 households. Emperor Wu accepted the abdication and was granted the title of Duke of Jibei County. Xun Xu resolutely refused and became a marquis because of Yang Hu's modesty. The official worship was Zhongshu Supervisor, and he was added as a servant. He was also in charge of writings and jointly formulated laws and regulations with Jia Chong. Jia Chong was about to guard Guanyou, and Xun Xu said to Feng Shou: "If you buy a public servant, you will be sent far away, and we will lose our power." The prince's marriage has not yet been decided. If Maichong's daughter is made the concubine, Jia Chong will not be able to leave without having to persuade her to stay.
target: He served under Cao Shuang and later became Zhongshu Tongshilang. After Cao Shuang's death, he alone attended the funeral, earning respect. He served as Anyang Order and later Tingweizheng, participating in Emperor Wen's military affairs. He advised against assassins and warned of Zhong Hui's rebellion. He wrote documents to Sun Hao of Wu, which were praised as better than a hundred thousand troops. After Emperor Wu's abdication, he was granted the title of Duke of Jibei County but refused, becoming a marquis. He served as Zhongshu Supervisor and jointly formulated laws with Jia Chong. He helped secure Jia Chong's daughter as crown prince's concubine, drawing criticism.

source: Xun Xu and Feng You both said when the emperor was free that Maichong's daughter would have unparalleled beauty. If she married into the East Palace, she would be able to assist the prince and have the virtues of the concubine in "Guan Ju". So they got married. At that time, he was very disgusted by honest people and was ridiculed as flattery. After a long time, he was promoted to Doctor Guanglu. After taking charge of rituals and music, he also revised the music rhythm, which became popular in the world. At first, Gou Xu heard the cow bell from Merchant Zhao on the road. Memorized the sound.
target: He revised music rhythms and compiled classics. He opposed the attack on Wu but was overruled.

source: After Xun Xu came back, he praised the prince's character highly, but He Jiao said that the prince was the same as before, so the world respected He Wei and looked down on Xun Xu. The emperor was about to abolish the imperial concubine, but Xun Xu, Feng Shou and others advised him, so the imperial concubine was not abolished. The discussion at the time believed that Gou Xu was the same type of person as Sun Zi and Liu Fang because he overthrew the country and endangered current affairs. However, Xun Xu had a meticulous temperament. Whenever there was an edict or important event, although it had been announced, he never mentioned it, not wanting others to know that he knew about it in advance.
target: He advised against sending princes to feudal states and discussed reducing officials. He praised the prince's character, leading to respect for He Jiao and disdain for him.

source: He sent a regular servant to Zhou Hui to announce the decree, and Xun Xu was ordered to govern. Xun Xu managed confidential affairs for a long time. He was talented and could guess the monarch's hidden thoughts and did not offend the monarch's disobedience. Therefore, he could always preserve his status and salary. When Taikang died in the tenth year of his life, Xia Shao gave Situ a posthumous gift of a noble coffin, a set of court clothes, five hundred thousand money, and one hundred pieces of cloth. He sent a censor and censor to guard the funeral, and the title of Mi was established. Xun Xu had ten sons, the most prominent of whom were Xun Ji, Xun Fan and Xun Zu.
target: He died in the tenth year of Taikang, with ten sons, including Xun Ji, Xun Fan, and Xun Zu. Xun Xu's descendants continued his legacy, with Xun Sui and Xun He crossing the river eastward during the chaos.

source: Feng Squid, courtesy name Shaozhou, was born in Anping. His grandfather, Feng Fu, was the school captain of Wei Sili. His father, Feng Yuan, was the prefect of Ji County. Feng You read a lot of classics and history books when he was young, and he was smart and eloquent. He successively served as the prefect of Wei County, transferred to the infantry school captain, and was transferred to Yueqi. He was highly regarded by Emperor Wu and was soon promoted to General Zuowei. He was able to please the emperor obediently and favored him greatly. Both Jia Chong and Xun Xu were friendly to him. Jia Chong's daughter became the dowager, and Feng Shou helped in this matter. When Concubine Jia was about to be deposed, Feng Shou and Xun Xu tried their best to save her, so she was not deposed. During the battle against Wu, Feng You, who was also the prefect of Runan, led the county soldiers to follow Wang Jun into Moling.
target: Feng You, courtesy name Shaozhou, was from Anping. He read extensively and was eloquent. He served as prefect of Wei County and later General Zuowei, favored by Emperor Wu. He befriended Jia Chong and Xun Xu, helping Jia Chong's daughter become dowager.

source: He was able to please the emperor obediently and favored him greatly. Both Jia Chong and Xun Xu were friendly to him. Jia Chong's daughter became the dowager, and Feng Shou helped in this matter. When Concubine Jia was about to be deposed, Feng Shou and Xun Xu tried their best to save her, so she was not deposed. During the battle against Wu, Feng You, who was also the prefect of Runan, led the county soldiers to follow Wang Jun into Moling. He was promoted to censor Zhongcheng and transferred to Shizhong. After the emperor recovered from a serious illness, Feng You and Xun Xu's desire to see each other inside and outside the court rested on Qi King Sima You. Sima You had always looked down on Xun Xu. Because the prince was stupid, Xun Xu was afraid that Sima You would succeed to the throne, which would be harmful to him, so he asked Feng Shou to tell the emperor: If your majesty has not recovered from his illness some time ago, the prince may be deposed. King Cha is the one whom the people turn to and whom the ministers look up to. Even if he is of high moral character and wants to give way, can he be spared? He should be sent back to the feudal state to stabilize the country. The emperor accepted his words. When Sima You died, there was sadness and resentment inside and outside the court. At first, the emperor's brotherly love was very deep. After adopting the heresies of Feng Shou and Gou Xu, he began to worry about what would happen after his death in order to stabilize the status of the crown prince. After hearing the news of Sima You's death, my grief was particularly deep. Feng Shou stood nearby and said, "The King of Qi has lived up to his reputation, and now he dies. This is the blessing of the Jin Dynasty." Why should Your Majesty be overly sad! The emperor no longer cried. At first, he planned to attack Wu. Feng You, Maichong and Xun Xu jointly tried their best to persuade him that it would not work. After Wu was put down, Feng You felt ashamed and fearful, and hated Zhang Hua as his enemy. After Zhang Hua came out to guard the capital, his prestige was remarkable, and the court's discussion believed that he should be appointed Shangshu Ling. Feng You calmly served the emperor, discussed the history of Jin and Wei, and took advantage of the situation to persuade the emperor, saying that he could not entrust Zhang Hua with important tasks. The emperor did not say anything and no longer appointed him. The details of the incident are recorded in the book "Zhang Hua Biography". In the seventh year of Taikang's reign, Feng You fell ill and issued an edict to appoint him as a regular servant of Sanqi. He was given 200,000 yuan and a set of bed tents. Died soon. He has two sons: Feng Bo and Feng Xiong.
target: He opposed the attack on Wu but later followed Wang Jun into Moling. He advised the emperor to send Qi King Sima You to his feudal state, leading to Sima You's death. He hated Zhang Hua and prevented his promotion. He died in the seventh year of Taikang, leaving two sons, Feng Bo and Feng Xiong. The historian comments that Wang Chen's disloyalty and Wang Jun's violence brought disaster, while Xunjie and Xun Xu, despite their talents, contributed to court strife. Feng You's flattery led to Sima You's death and Jia's rise, causing endless civil unrest.

source: Empress Xia Yuan Jing Yu, Yu Zhang Jun Ming, Empress Mu Yu became Gong Du Empress Concubine Zhang, Queen Kang Xian, Queen Mu Zhanghe, Queen Aijing The deposed emperor, Empress Xiaoyu, Jian Wenxuan, the Empress Dowager Zheng, Jian Wenshun, the king Empress Xiaowuwen Li Empress Dowager Xiaowu Dingwang Empress Ande Chen Empress Dowager Anxi Wang Empress Gongsi Chu Empress Queen Yuan Jingyu's name was Meng Mu, a native of Jiyang Waihuang. His father's name is Yu Yu, and his deeds can be found in "The Biography of Foreign Relatives". When Emperor Yuan was King Langxie, he married the queen as his concubine and had no sons. He died in the sixth year of Yongjia at the age of thirty-five. When Emperor Yuan became the king of Jin, he gave her the title of queen. Officials reported that the queen should build another temple. Emperor Yuan ordered: "The ancestral temple has not yet been completed, and it is inconvenient to build another one. The house above the mausoleum can be renovated and used as a temple." In the third year of Taixing, the second book says: The emperor lamented the former Langxie Princess Yu: I respectfully obeyed the orders of God, and therefore ascended the throne of God. I mourn the past of the concubine, her good name has not been promoted, there are no etiquette and regulations to govern the country, and the education in the harem is not enough, so I feel sad. The gift of the title Dingmi is an old code of the former kings. Today, envoy Chijie and Taiwei Wan Sheng were sent to present a posthumous jade seal to the Queen and use Tailao as a sacrifice. If the Queen's soul has a spirit, she should be honored. So he was offered sacrifices to the Imperial Ancestral Temple and buried in Jianping Mausoleum. During the Taining period, Emperor Ming commemorated his mother's kindness in raising her and gave Yuzhang's wife Wang as the queen of Qiuyang County. His aunt Sanqi often served as the wife of Sima Han, the king of Xinye, as the queen of Pingyang Township. The Xun family of Yuzhang Jun was a palace member of Emperor Yuan. After being favored at first, she gave birth to Emperor Ming and King Langxie Sima Sui, so she was hated by Empress Yu. Because of his low status and constant resentment, he was condemned by Emperor Yuan and gradually became alienated and neglected. When Emperor Ming came to the throne, he was granted the title of Jianxuanzhou and built another residence. In the first year of Zuo Zhen's reign, Dandao welcomed her back to the palace and provided her with grand and generous supplies. When Emperor Cheng came to the throne, he treated her with the same respect as the Queen Mother. He died in the first year of Xiankang. Shao Shu said: I suffered misfortune when I was young, but it was Jian Sairi who taught me lovingly and worked hard to raise me.
target: A detailed account of the empresses, consorts, and dowagers of the Jin Dynasty, chronicling their lives, titles, deaths, and roles in court politics. Empress Xia Yuan Jing Yu, who died young before her husband became emperor, and was later posthumously honored. Her rival, Concubine Zhang, bore Emperor Ming but was hated by Empress Yu and neglected by Emperor Yuan; she was later honored by her son. Empress Ming Mu Yu, known for her virtue, served as regent for her young son, Emperor Cheng, during a rebellion, and died in distress. Empress Cheng Gong Du, from a virtuous family, died young without children, and her funeral was kept simple by imperial decree. The text then covers Empress Kang Xian Chu, who served as regent for Emperor Mu, and later for Emperor Ai and Duke Haixi, including her role in the deposition of the latter. Empress Mu Zhang He, from a notable family, was captured during Huan Xuan's usurpation and later returned to the capital. Empress Ai Jing, originally a concubine, died childless. The deposed Emperor's Empress Xiao Yu was demoted after her husband's deposition. Empress Dowager Jian Wen Xuan Zheng, a widow who remarried Emperor Yuan, was posthumously honored by her son, Emperor Jian Wen, and later by Emperor Xiao Wu, despite debates over her proper sacrificial status.

source: In the past, when Empress Jing passed away, Prince Xiao had already passed away, so she still had to mourn. This is a clear precedent that I should follow. Queen Mingmu did not force him to change his mind, so she appointed King Langxie as King of Kuaiji and posthumously named the Queen as Princess of Kuaiji. Emperor Jian Wen ascended the throne and would have time to add titles in the future. When he was about to die, he named the prince Daozi the king of Langxie, led the country of Kuaiji, and offered sacrifices to the concubine. In the 19th year of Taiyuan, Emperor Xiaowu issued an edict saying: Concubine Kuaiji is the mother of virtue and virtue, with a harmonious sound of virtue, full of sage wisdom, and illumination of the Jin Dynasty. The late emperor gave the wise and kind-hearted concubine Kuaiji an additional honorary title. The court's opinions were inconsistent, and the Tao was suspected of being distorted. I stated that I would follow the late Emperor's ambition and always warned him in my heart. Today, in accordance with the "Spring and Autumn Annals", the Han Dynasty and the past practices of Emperor Xiaohuai, the concubine is given the title of Empress Dowager Jian Wenxuan. So a temple was built on the west side of Taimiao Road, and the mausoleum was called Jiaping. At that time, in order to cater to the emperor's will, the officials believed that Empress Dowager Zheng should be sacrificed to Emperor Yuan. The emperor asked Xu Miao about this, and Xu Miao said: I think the meaning of "Spring and Autumn" is that a mother becomes noble because of her son. Duke Yin of Lu respected Duke Huan's mother and built a separate palace for Zhongzi instead of sharing it with Hui Temple. Moreover, in the past, Empress Dowager Zheng was not the wife of the late emperor, so how could the descendants establish a first wife for their ancestors? Respect has reached the extreme. Because of the ministers, she can be called the Queen Mother, and the ceremony of the mausoleum and temple is complete. If they are buried together and sacrificed, it is not allowed by the righteousness and etiquette. Complied with him. Queen Jian Wenshun's name is Jian Ji, a native of Jinyang, Taiyuan. His father Wang Xia's deeds can be found in "Biography of Foreign Relatives". Because the queen came from a distinguished family, she was originally the princess of Kuaiji. She gave birth to a son, Daosheng, who was established as the prince. In the fourth year of Yonghe, both mother and son lost the emperor's favor and were both imprisoned and deposed. The queen died of depression. In the second year of Xian'an, Emperor Xiaowu ascended the throne and was given the additional honorary title of Queen Shun. They were buried together in Gaoping Mausoleum. They were posthumously presented to the Queen's father Wang Xia Tejin and Dr. Guanglu, and were granted the title of Sanqi Changshi. Empress Dowager Li Xiaowuwen was named Lingrong and came from a humble background. At first Emperor Jian Wen was the king of Kuaiji and had three sons, all of whom died in infancy. Since Daosheng was deposed and King Xian died prematurely, all the concubines have not been pregnant for nearly ten years. The emperor ordered the soothsayer Hu Qian to divine for this purpose. Hu Qian said: There is a woman in the back room who will be able to give birth to two rich boys, one of whom will eventually prosper and advance to the imperial family. At that time, Xu Guisheng gave birth to Princess Xin'an, who was favored because of her good virtues.
target: Empress Jian Wen Shun Wang, who lost favor and was deposed with her son, was posthumously restored. Empress Dowager Xiao Wu Wen Li, of humble origin, was chosen by a physiognomist and bore Emperor Xiao Wu and others, eventually being honored as empress dowager. Empress Xiao Wu Ding Wang, chosen for her beauty and virtue, was jealous and died young. Empress Dowager An De Chen, a concubine who bore two emperors, was posthumously honored. Empress An Xi Wang, married as crown princess, died childless. Empress Gong Si Chu, demoted after her husband's abdication, died later.

source: In the past, Emperor Gaozong was in mourning and left the affairs of state to the elders; King Cheng was young and ignorant, so he entrusted state affairs to his superiors. It is indeed not an ancient system for the Queen Mother to listen to government affairs in court. Empresses Mingmu and Kangxian came to the court successively. On cloudy and rainy days, the bullock carts are driven out and the carts without curtains are put into the warehouse. Someone asked why, and the answer was: carts without curtains are suitable for storage. When a court official visited him, even though his name was announced, the visitor's carriage and horses would be parked outside the door, and he might not be seen for a whole day. I was able to visit him sometimes and socialize with others. He was very respectful and humble, and there were no mistakes at first. Before and after my concubine died and was buried, the coffin was always left unnailed in an empty room at the back. I opened it every few days to look at it, maybe did some obscene things, and waited until the body rotted before burying it. King Zhao Sima Lun assisted in the government affairs and appointed Sima Qian as General Wei. Emperor Hui was deposed and re-established. Sima Qian wrote poems and was appointed Taibao. When King Sima Tong of Qi pacified King Sima Lun of Zhao, the members of the royal family and the officials in the court all comforted Sima Tong with cow wine. Only Sima Qian had a hundred coins in his pocket. When he saw Sima Tong take it out, he said: King Zhao rebelled and rebelled. It is your credit for your righteous deeds. Now I use a hundred coins to congratulate you. Even so, it is difficult for you to take advantage of the general trend, so you must be cautious. After Sima Jian assisted in the government affairs, Sima Qian went to visit him, and Sima Tong came out to greet him. After Sima Qian entered the house, he squatted on Sima Gang's bed and refused to let Sima Tong sit down. He said to him: "Don't imitate women." This word means Sima Lun. When Sima Tong was killed, Sima Qian cried very sadly and said to the people around him: "The clan is gradually declining, and only this son is the best. If you kill him, you will be in danger from now on!" Sima Yue, King of the East China Sea, acted righteously and arrived in Luoyang to visit Sima Qian, but Sima Qian stayed behind closed doors. Sima Yue's car stayed for a long time before Sima Qian sent someone to see the guest off, while he peeped through the crack in the door. At that time, no one could fathom his intentions. Some said he was ill, while others thought he was doing something cryptic. Yongjia died in the fifth year of his reign at the age of eighty.
target: His salary and goods were left to rot in the open air. He was known for eccentric behavior, such as keeping his concubines' coffins unsealed in empty rooms and opening them to look at them periodically. During the rebellion of King Zhao Sima Lun, Sima Qian was appointed as General Wei and later Taibao. When Sima Tong of Qi pacified Sima Lun, Sima Qian congratulated him with a hundred coins. He died in the fifth year of Yongjia at age eighty.

source: At that time, no one could fathom his intentions. Some said he was ill, while others thought he was doing something cryptic. Yongjia died in the fifth year of his reign at the age of eighty. It happened that Liu Cong invaded Luoyang and had no time to give him the nickname "Mi". He has two sons. The eldest son, Sima Guang, died young. The second son, Sima Yong, was named the Duke of Ande County in the Taixi year and served as a regular attendant. They are both good people. In trouble, the whole family will be exterminated. Sima Dian, the king of Langye Wu, was given the title Zijiang in the early years of his reign and was named Nan'antinghou. He was talented and famous very early. He initially served as General Ningshuo and guarded Yecheng. He had a reputation for being good at appeasing people and making them obey. Gradually he was moved to serve as a regular servant of Sanqi. In the Jin Dynasty, he was granted the title of Marquis of Shuwu Township. He was appointed as the Right General, supervised the military affairs of Yanzhou, and was the governor of Yanzhou. The fifth-class title was established and he was named Nanpi Bo. He was transferred to the post of General Zhenglu, Jiajie. Emperor Wu ascended the throne and granted him the title of Prince of Dongguan County, granting him a fief of 10,600 households. When the second ministers were first established, a special edict was issued to let the kings choose their own commanders. Sima Dian asked for permission, but the emperor refused. After entering the imperial court, he served as Shangshu Youpushe and Fujun General. He was appointed as General Zhenshu, Jiajie, and Commander-in-Chief of Xuzhou's military affairs. He replaced Wei Cui to guard Xiapi. Sima Dian defended the enemy well, and the soldiers were willing to die to serve him. The people of Wu were afraid of him. He was granted the title of Kaifu Yitong and the Third Division, and was granted the title of King Langxie, using Dongguan to expand his feudal kingdom. In the battle of Pingding County, Sun Hao led tens of thousands of troops from Tusheng. Sun Hao sent a letter and seal to Sima Dian to ask for surrender. Shaoshu says: Sima Bodu, King of Langxie, led the troops under his command to occupy Tuzhong one after another, making it impossible for the enemy to save each other. He also sent the fallen evil minister Liu Hong and others to march towards the Yangtze River. The enemy was shocked and frightened, and sent an envoy to present the fake seal and ribbon. Sima Dian then sent Chief Shi Wangheng to lead his troops to cross the Yangtze River, break through the enemy's border defenses, capture Lan Bian, the governor, beheaded and surrendered 50,000 to 60,000 people, and condemned Jiang Dan, Yu Sai and others to surrender and plead guilty. Sima Dian's meritorious service was outstanding, and his two sons were granted the title of Marquis of Ting, each with a title of 3,000 households and 6,000 pieces of silk.
target: Sima Dian, King of Langye Wu, was talented and famous from an early age. He served as General Ningshuo guarding Yecheng and later as General Zhenshu guarding Xiapi, where he defended well against the Wu people. During the pacification of Wu, Sun Hao surrendered to Sima Dian, who sent troops across the Yangtze River, capturing enemy officials and securing the surrender of 50,000 to 60,000 people.

source: He also sent the fallen evil minister Liu Hong and others to march towards the Yangtze River. The enemy was shocked and frightened, and sent an envoy to present the fake seal and ribbon. Sima Dian then sent Chief Shi Wangheng to lead his troops to cross the Yangtze River, break through the enemy's border defenses, capture Lan Bian, the governor, beheaded and surrendered 50,000 to 60,000 people, and condemned Jiang Dan, Yu Sai and others to surrender and plead guilty. Sima Dian's meritorious service was outstanding, and his two sons were granted the title of Marquis of Ting, each with a title of 3,000 households and 6,000 pieces of silk. Soon, he also supervised all the military affairs in Qingzhou and added the clothing of the servants. He was promoted to General, Kaifu Yitong and the Third Division. Sima Dian not only had a distinguished status because he was a relative of the emperor, but also contributed to the pacification of Wu. He restrained himself from being respectful and indulgent, and did not appear to be complacent about his achievements. His staff did their best, and the people were inspired and attached to him. When he was seriously ill, he was given bed tents, clothes, money, silk, rice and other items, and his servants were sent to greet him. Taikang died in the fourth year of his reign at the age of fifty-seven. On his deathbed, he petitioned to be buried next to his mother's mausoleum and to divide his kingdom among his four sons. The emperor agreed. His son, Prince Gong, Sima Su, succeeded to the throne. He also named his second son, Mo Shan, King of Juni, Sima Yao as King of Dong'an, and Sima Huai as King of Huailing.
target: His two sons were made marquises. He died in the fourth year of Taikang at age fifty-seven. His descendants included Sima Rui, who later became Emperor Yuan, and several others who successively held the title of King of Langye.

source: After the deposed emperor ascended the throne, King Kuaiji acted as the minister of sacrifice for the Langye Kingdom. Emperor Jianwen ascended the throne, and King Langxie had no successor. When the emperor was dying, he named his youngest son Daozi King Langxie. Daozi later became King of Kuaiji, and Emperor Gong was appointed King of Langxie. After Emperor Gong ascended the throne, Langye Kingdom was abolished. Sima Dan, the king of Wulingzhuang, was named Sihong. At first he served as a servant, and later he was granted the title of Duke of Dongwu, with a fief of 5,200 households. Transferred to the post of former general and central protector. He is jealous and harmful by nature and has no filial and friendly character. His younger brother Sima Yao, king of Dong'an, had a good reputation and was loved by his parents. Sima Dan hated him as an enemy, so he spoke ill of Sima Yao to Sima Liang, king of Runan. Sima Liang had always had conflicts with Sima Yao, so he petitioned to abolish him and move him. King Zhao Sima Lun rebelled and appointed Sima Dan as the leading general. Sima Dan has always been friendly with Guo Chu in Hanoi and Sima Chu's younger brother. When the wine was in full swing, He Ye and others talked about the grievances of Tui Gan. Sima Dan was a drunkard by nature, so he killed both of them and gave their heads to Sima Lun. He stopped drinking and went on a violent rampage.
target: Sima Dan, King of Wulingzhuang, was jealous and harmful by nature with no filial character. He hated his brother Sima Yao and spoke ill of him to Sima Liang. During Sima Lun's rebellion, Sima Dan served as leading general. He killed two men while drunk and gave their heads to Sima Lun.

source: When the wine was in full swing, He Ye and others talked about the grievances of Tui Gan. Sima Dan was a drunkard by nature, so he killed both of them and gave their heads to Sima Lun. He stopped drinking and went on a violent rampage. Sima Dan's wife, Su Di, was the queen's sister-in-law. At first, relying on his family status, he was rude to Sima Dan's mother. King Sima Tong of Qi was assisting in government affairs. Sima Dan's mother, Princess Zhuge, complained that Sima Dan was unfilial and begged to be let back. Therefore, Sima Dan, his wife and children moved to Liaosai. His son Sima Xi, who was five years old, refused to go with him, saying: "We should ask to come back for our father, and we should not move together."
target: His mother complained of his unfilial behavior, and he was moved to Liaosai with his family. He was later killed by Shi Le in the late Yongjia period.

source: The official title was Guanglu Dafu, Shangshu, Prince Taifu, and was renamed King Wuling. In the last years of Yongjia, he was killed by Shi Le, and his son Sima Zhe, King of Ai, succeeded him. Sima Zhe, whose courtesy name was Jinglin, was a regular servant of Sanqi. He was also killed by Shi Le. He had no son, so Emperor Yuan later appointed his prince Sima Xi as King of Wuling to offer sacrifices to Sima Dan. Sima Yao, King of Dong'an, had the courtesy name Si Xuan. At first, he was the Duke of Dong'an, and he successively served as the minister of Huangmen of Sanqi, and then moved to the position of regular servant of Sanqi. A person with a beautiful beard, resolute temperament, authority, erudition, filial piety in serving relatives, and exhaustive etiquette in mourning. When Yang Jun was executed, Sima Yao stationed troops in Yunlong and commanded all the troops. Because of his meritorious service, he was worshiped as the General of the Right Guard and the Colonel of Shesheng. He was granted the title of Prince of the County in the Jin Dynasty and was granted the title of 20,000 households. He was also appointed as the Shizhong and the General of the Dian Army. He also served as the General of the Right Guard.
target: Sima Yao, King of Dong'an, was resolute, authoritative, and learned, with filial piety in serving relatives. He was granted 20,000 households and held various positions.

source: On this day, more than three hundred people were punished and rewarded, and the orders were all issued from Sima Yao. The father of Shuyi captain Wen Fang, Sai Leng, was killed by Danwudeng's grandfather, Zhu Jiang Dan. Danwu Xun was worried that Sai Tan was a nuisance to his uncle's family, so Zaotian killed Wen because he was not guilty. Sima Yao's brother Sima Dan repeatedly accused Sima Liang of being accused by King Sima Liang of Runan, but Sima Liang refused to listen. At this time, because Sima Yao was arbitrary in punishments and rewards, Sima Dan took the opportunity to speak ill of Sima Yao. Sima Liang was deceived by Sizhui's rhetoric, so he dismissed Yao Sheng from his official position and returned to his mansion as a public servant. He was convicted of rebellious remarks and moved to Daifang. In the early years of Yongkang, Sima Yao was recruited and his title was restored. His official title was Zong Zhengqing, and he was moved to the post of Shangshu and Zuopushe. When Emperor Hui was attacking Sima Ying, the king of Chengdu, Sima Yao was holding a funeral for his mother in Ye, and he persuaded Sima Ying to lay down his weapons and surrender. When the emperor's army was defeated, Sima Ying resented Sima Yao and killed him. Later, Sima Hun, the Marquis of Changleting, son of Sima Jin, the king of Langxie, was appointed king of Shu'an to offer sacrifices to Sima Yao. He died soon after and the feudal state was lifted.
target: He was arbitrary in punishments and rewards, leading to his dismissal and exile to Daifang. He was later restored but killed by Sima Ying after the emperor's army was defeated.

source: He died without a son. During the reign of Emperor An, he appointed Sima Yun, the grandson of King Wulingwei, as King of Huailing to offer sacrifices to King Yuan. He died without a son, Yilin! Wang Sima Bao's son Anzhi succeeded him. Song accepted the abdication and the feudal state was cancelled. Sima Jing, the Marquis of Huiting in the Qing Dynasty, was given the title Zizuo as a prince in the late Wei Dynasty. When he died at the age of twenty-four, he was given posthumously as Captain Shesheng, and was succeeded by Emperor Wen's son Sima Ji, courtesy name Taixuan. In the first year of Taishi, he was granted the title of King of Yan and granted 6,663 towns. Sima Ji went to the feudal state. In the early years of Xianning, he was recruited as an infantry captain. He used Yuyang County to expand his feudal state and add clothes to his servants. The official paid homage to the governor of Qingzhou and the general of Zhenshu. During the holidays, he used 10,337 households in Beiping, Shanggu and Guangmi counties to increase the number of Yan Kingdom to 20,000. He died without a son, so King Sima Jian of Qi asked his son Sima Ji to succeed him. Later, Sima Tong failed and the feudal state was cancelled. Sima Jun, the King of Wu in Fufeng, was given the courtesy name Zizang. He was clever when he was young, and when he was five or six years old, he could write memorials and recite scriptures, and people who saw him were amazed.
target: Sima Jun, King of Fufeng Wu, was clever from childhood, able to write memorials and recite scriptures at age five or six.

source: Later, Sima Tong failed and the feudal state was cancelled. Sima Jun, the King of Wu in Fufeng, was given the courtesy name Zizang. He was clever when he was young, and when he was five or six years old, he could write memorials and recite scriptures, and people who saw him were amazed. When he grows up, he will be quiet, upright and upright, and he will have the best reputation in the clan. In the middle of Wei Jingchu's reign, he was named Pingyang Tinghou. King Cao Fang of Qi came to the throne. Sima Jun was eight years old and became a regular attendant of Sanqi. Soon he was transferred to the rank of captain of infantry and garrison cavalry, but his position of permanent attendant remained the same. He was promoted to the title of Marquis of Xiang, and served as General Pingnan, Jiajie, and Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in Huaibei. He was renamed Pingshouhou and transferred to General Anshu. In the early years of Xianxi's reign, he was granted the title of Dongmouhou and transferred to General Andong to guard Xuchang. After Emperor Wu ascended the throne, the Jin Dynasty granted him the title of King of Ruyin, granting him a fief of 10,000 households and commanding the military affairs of Yuzhou. General Ding Feng of the State of Wu invaded Shaopi, and Sima Jun led the army to resist and repel the enemy. He was moved to the post of envoy Chijie and governor of Yangzhou's military affairs, and guarded Shouchun in place of Shi Bao. Soon he was in charge of Yuzhou and returned to guard Xuchang. He was moved to the post of General of Zhenxi, Envoy Chijie, Commander-in-Chief of Yongliang and other state military affairs. He replaced Sima Liang, King of Runan, to guard Guanzhong. He was also awarded the attire of Gunmian Shizhong. Sima Jun was good at appeasing the rulers and had majesty and kindness. He advised and supervised agriculture and mulberry planting, and shared labor with the soldiers. He, his staff, assistants, generals and soldiers were limited to farming ten acres, and they all reported to the table. Shaoshu's orders spread to all states and counties, allowing people to engage in farming. In the early years of Xianning, Shu Jigeng and others of the Qiang tribe rebelled. Sima Jun sent many people to attack them and killed more than 3,000 people.
target: He was quiet, upright, and had the best reputation in the clan. He served as General of Zhenxi, guarding Guanzhong, and was skilled at appeasing rulers. He promoted agriculture and shared labor with soldiers. He suppressed Qiang rebellions and received surrenders from various tribes.

source: In the first year of the Han Dynasty, Sima Jun entered the dynasty and changed his title to King Fufeng. He used people whose households were within the boundaries of the feudal state to increase the number of households in his feudal town and gave it to Yu Bao and Guan. In the early years of Taikang, Jin was granted the title of General of Hussars, and the positions of Kaifu, Chijie, and Governor remained. Sima Jun had a filial character. His mother, Concubine Fu, followed his brother Sima Liang in the official position. Sima Jun often cried and missed her. If he heard that his mother was sick, he would worry about not being able to eat. Sometimes he would put down his official position to visit her and pay her respects. He was eager to learn when he was young, and was able to write books and treatises. He discussed the sequence of benevolence and filial piety with Xun Zhi, and his articles were commendable. When Sima You, King of Qi, left the capital to go to his own kingdom, Sima Jun came forward to persuade the emperor sincerely, but because the emperor refused, he fell ill and died. As a posthumous gift to the Grand Sima, he was given the title of Shizhong and Fake Huangtie. When people in the west heard that he was dead, people all over the road cried for him, and the people erected monuments for him. When the elders saw the monument, they all bowed down. This is the love he left behind.
target: He was filial to his mother and eager to learn, writing treatises on benevolence and filial piety. When he died, people wept for him and erected monuments.

source: Posthumously awarded the title of General of Hussars. He had no sons, so his elder brother's son Sima Shao was his heir. Yongjia died in Shile in the last years of his life. Liang Xiaowang Sima Xu was named Zihui. He practiced Qingjing, was respectful and prudent, and had no other talents. As a young master, he was named Pingletinghou. When the fifth-class title was established, he was renamed Kaipingzi. Emperor Wu ascended the throne and named him King of Liang, granting him 5,358 households. When he left the enfeoffed country, he was moved to the position of Beizhonglang General and supervised the defense of Yecheng. At that time, the kings selected their own officials and subordinates, and Sima Shu selected Zhang Fan, the chief official of Ruyin, as the middle official.
target: Sima Xu, King of Liang, practiced quietness and was respectful and prudent. He served as General of Zhengxi guarding Guanzhong and later as Grand Administrator and Situ.

source: In modern times, there is Taiwei Chen Zhun, a man with a foreign surname. Because his brother Chen Huiyou had betrayed King Sima Lun and had an old grudge, he was able to claim to be ill and not join the puppet court. What's more, Sima Xu is Sima Lun's biological brother, but he can't leave? Zhao Dun's advice to the court was not heeded, and he fled but did not go far. He was not immune from the guilt. What's more, Sima Xu could not resign his official position and face the north to serve the false monarch. He should be derogated and criticized according to the previous discussion to promote the integrity of ministers and clarify the principles of serving the king. So the court followed Cai Ke's argument. Sima Xu's former subordinates continued to pursue complaints, so he changed his nickname. Sima Xu had no sons, so he was succeeded by Sima Xi, the son of Sima Dan, King of Wuling, who was also King Huai. The official worshiped the general Zhenglu, and both died in Shile with Sima Dan. During the reign of Emperor Yuan, Sima Kui, the son of Sima Su, King of Xiyang, was the descendant of Sima Xu. He died early and became the Shang King. At this time, Dan Moqiao, the son of King Tan, returned from the mutual pressure and succeeded to the throne. He was also King Sheng, and his official position was to serve as a regular attendant. He died without a son. The imperial edict ordered Sima Lian, the son of King Wulingwei, to succeed Si Qusu, who successively served as the prime minister's servant. He and his father Dan Quzhong were deposed and moved to Xin'an. After his death, the feudal state was restored during the Taiyuan period, and his son Sima Su succeeded to the throne.
target: During Sima Lun's usurpation, he served as prime minister. After his death, there was debate over his posthumous name, with some criticizing him for failing to take a stand during crises. He had no sons, and his title passed through various relatives.

source: Huanxuan usurped the throne, and Kong Pu, the minister of the feudal state, fled to Shouyang. He returned in the early years of Yixi and gradually moved to the post of General Zuowei and Taichang Qing. Liu Yu crusades against Yao Xun, please! Rei joins the army as a consultant. He is killed by the plastic pass, and the feudal state is cancelled. Emperor Wen had nine sons, including Emperor Wenming, Wang You of Qi Xian, Wang Zhao of Chengyang Ai, Wang Dingguo of Liaohui, and Guangde of Guanghan. Wang Jian of Anping, Ji of Yan, Prince Yongzuo, and Yanzuo of Leping didn't know who their mothers were. There is another legend about King Yan's successor Qing Huitingbao. Yong Zuo died early and did not pass on. The king of Qi Xian, Sima You, was named Dayou. Be wise at a young age. When he grows up, he will be calm, kind and fair, be close to wise people, like charity, like classic books, be able to write articles, be good at letters, and be imitated by the world. His talent and reputation were greater than those of Emperor Wu, and Emperor Xuan often valued him. Emperor Jing had no sons, so he made Sima You his heir. He followed Wang Jun in his campaign and was named the Marquis of Changle Pavilion. When Emperor Jing died, Sima You was only ten years old. His sorrow moved the people around him and he was praised and praised. Inherited the title of Wuyang Hou. After serving Jing Xian Yang in another mansion, he became famous for his filial piety when serving the queen.
target: Sima You, King of Qi Xian, was wise from youth, calm, kind, and fond of classical books. He was made heir to Emperor Jing and inherited the title of Wuyang Hou. Under Emperor Wu, he was made King of Qi and managed military affairs. He was known for his filial piety and moral conduct. He advised on agricultural policies and government administration.

source: We must be considerate in all kinds of matters, and we must be kind in fundamental matters. When you see destruction, you should be alert to danger; when you see stability, you should think of survival. The eldest son presides over morality, I ventured to tell the gatekeeper. The world thinks that the proverbs are well written. In the second year of Xianning, he replaced Mai as Sikong, but his positions of Shizhong and Taifu remained the same. At first, Sima You was especially favored by Emperor Wen. Every time he saw Sima You, he patted the bed and called him by his nickname, saying "This is the seat of Taofu". There were many times when he was almost made the prince. When the emperor was ill, he was worried that Sima You would be uneasy and cried as Emperor Wu recounted the story of King Huainan and King Chensi of Wei in the Han Dynasty. Before he died, he took Sima You's hand and entrusted him to Emperor Wu.
target: He was especially favored by Emperor Wen, who nearly made him crown prince. However, due to the machinations of Xun Xu and Feng Shou, Emperor Wu sent him to his feudal state.

source: Jingdu died in the sixth year of Taishi, and his fifth son Sima Xian succeeded him. After his death, his sixth son Sima Zhi was made King of East China Sea and the descendant of King Ai. After his death, in the early years of Xianning, he named his thirteenth son Sima Ya the King of Qinghe and became the descendant of Sima Zhao. King Hui of Liaodong Dingguo died at the age of three. In the early years of Xianning, the title of Mi was added, and King Sima You of Qi made his eldest son Sima Rui the heir.
target: Sima You became ill from resentment and died at age thirty-six while traveling. His son Sima Tong succeeded him.

source: Wei Shu, courtesy name Yangyuan, was born in Renchengfan. His father died when he was young and he was adopted by his maternal grandfather's Ning family. When Mr. Ning built a house, the person who looked at the feng shui of the house said: "A noble nephew will be born." Because her grandson Wei was young and smart, my grandmother thought that he had followed the Feng Shui master's words. Wei Shu said: I should prove the auspiciousness of this house for my grandfather's family. It took a long time before I moved to another place. He is eight feet two inches tall, has a beautiful body and a majestic appearance, and can drink more than a stone of wine. However, he is slow and simple, and is not valued by the villagers. Wei Heng, the official uncle of the hall, was well-known in the world but didn't know him well. He asked him to guard the water-powered rice pounding facility. He often sighed and said: "Wei Shu can be the head of a hundred households, so I will be satisfied!"
target: Wei Shu, courtesy name Yangyuan, was born in Renchengfan. Orphaned young, he was raised by his maternal grandfather’s Ning family. A feng shui master predicted a noble nephew would be born, and Wei Shu’s intelligence led his grandmother to believe he fulfilled this prophecy. Tall and majestic, he was slow and simple, not valued by villagers. His uncle Wei Heng underestimated him, but Wei Shu remained unbothered.

source: Don't pay attention to ordinary people's moral integrity, don't do things that are reserved and arrogant, and always want to be tolerant in order to respect people. Never reveal the shortcomings of others. By nature, he likes to ride horses and shoot arrows. He wears reed clothes and goes into the mountains and rivers to fish and hunt. Only Wang Yi of Taiyuan said to Wei Shu: You will eventually become prime minister, but now you cannot protect your wife and children from hunger and cold. I should help you make a living. He often offered relief to Wei Shu for his shortcomings, but Wei Shu accepted it without refusing. Wei Shu once went to Yewang. The wife of the owner of the house was giving birth to a baby at night. After a while, he heard the sound of carriages and horses. The people in the carriages asked each other: "Is it a boy or a girl?" Answered: Boy, write it down, died by a sharp weapon at the age of fifteen. Asked again: Who is sleeping in the room? He replied: Wei Gong Wei Shu. Fifteen years later, he went to the house owner again and asked where his son was. He was told that he died because he was injured by an ax while cutting mulberry branches.
target: He enjoyed riding, archery, and hunting. Wang Yi of Taiyuan predicted he would become prime minister and supported him. Wei Shu once witnessed a prophecy about a boy who died at fifteen from an ax wound, which later came true.

source: Wei Shu said: If I go to the exam and fail, the responsibility lies with me. How can I take the honor of not going to the exam and stealing the false name of Gao Jie as my own glory? So he studied his own homework and studied a "Sutra" for a hundred days, so he answered the policy questions and passed the exam. He was granted the title of Chief of Mianchi, moved to the post of Jun Yi Ling, and entered the court as Shangshu Lang. At that time, Lang officials were selected and eliminated, and those who were incompetent were dismissed.
target: At forty, he studied for a hundred days, passed exams, and became Chief of Mianchi. He later served as Shangshu Lang, where he voluntarily resigned when incompetent officials were dismissed.

source: Those among his colleagues who had never spoken highly felt ashamed, while those who discussed the matter praised Wei Shu. After gradually moving to the post of general Zhong Yu, Zhong Yu often shot arrows with his subordinates, and Wei Shu often planned for him. Later, when he encountered a shortage of friends, he asked Wei Shu to make up the number. Zhong Yu didn't know Wei Shu was good at archery at first. Wei Shu's shooting posture was elegant and he never failed to hit the mark. Everyone in the audience was amazed. No one could compare with him. Zhong Yu sighed and apologized: I didn't give full play to your talent. With such a good archery skill, shouldn't it be limited to archery? He was transferred to the position of Prime Minister and joined the army, and was named Ju Yangzi. Regarding the trivial affairs of the government and court, Wei Shu's governance has never been seen to be good or bad; as for major issues related to the country's failure and prosperity, no one can make a decision, and Wei Shu plans it slowly, often beyond the consensus of the public. Emperor Wen valued him deeply. After every court meeting, he would see him off and say: "Wei Shu has a handsome appearance and is the leader of everyone." He was moved to the post of governor of Yiyang and Rongyang counties and gained a good reputation. He was conscripted into the imperial court and served as a regular attendant on the cavalry. Shan Tao advised him many times. Although the emperor understood it, he could not change it.
