source: Shan Tao wrote memorials for the screening and selection, each with its own title, which was called "Monkey Announcement" at the time. Shan Tao was an official in the government and held an important position. In his later years, he encountered the dictatorship of the Hou Party and did not want to appoint Yang. Shan Tao advised him many times. Although the emperor understood it, he could not change it. Later, due to old age and serious illness, Shangshu resigned and said: I am nearly eighty years old and I am trying to save my life every day. If I had a little energy, how could I not contribute in this era of sage? Forced by old age, he no longer holds office. Now the world is resting and recuperating, and the world is yearning for enlightenment to make them peaceful, and the people will naturally return to the right path. As long as you encourage them by advocating customs and education, there is nothing else for your Majesty to do. I am deaf, blind, and unable to encourage myself. Lord, minister, father and son, there is no need to hide, so I state my thoughts and beg to obey my request. So he took off his official uniform and handed over his seal and ribbon. The edict said: There are many things in the world, and Chengli has just been pacified and Pepsi has been founded. We should work together to promote education. You don't remember the past and asked to retire due to a minor illness. Is this what I expected? Shantao petitioned to retire, but the edict did not allow it. Shangshu ordered Qian Tuo to report: Shan Tao has been out of office for a long time due to a minor illness. The emperor repeatedly attacked, but still refused to obey. I think this is a lack of moral integrity and violates the principle of serving justice wholeheartedly. If you are really seriously ill, you should not be in a high position. Shan Tao can be removed from his official position. Xia Shao wrote to Man Dui: Shan Tao's virtue has always been valued by the imperial court, and he often made concessions deeply and sincerely. Therefore, there were successive edicts to change his mind and assist the court. The person in charge did not understand the purpose of Shaoshu, but instead slandered me deeply, damaging the culture of respecting sages and worsening my reputation for being unvirtuous. How can I set an example to far and near! Shan Tao had no choice but to take up the post of director again. In the early years of Taikang, he was promoted to Youpuse and became a Guanglu doctor, but his positions of serving in the palace and in charge of the election remained the same.
target: He resigned due to old age and illness, but was repeatedly called back to service. He was promoted to Youpuse and Guanglu doctor, but continued to decline due to health.

source: If you don't take back your refusal, I can't sleep peacefully. Shantao went to the table again and firmly declined, refusing to allow it. After Wu was pacified, the emperor issued an edict to stop military service to show peace in the world. All prefectures and counties withdrew their troops. One hundred military officials were appointed in large counties and fifty in small counties. The emperor once gave a martial arts lecture at the Xuanwu Field. Shan Tao was ill at the time, so he sent a letter to Shao to let him follow him in a sedan chair. So he discussed the use of troops with Lu Qin and believed that the armaments of prefectures and counties should not be withdrawn. His remarks were very accurate.
target: After Wu was pacified, he advised against withdrawing military forces, a warning that proved prescient during later chaos.

source: Later, when he was appointed Situ, Liangzhan resolutely declined. The edict said: You have high moral character and high prestige, and you are a famous elder in the court. Therefore, you were granted the high position of prime minister, but you gave in too much and repeated it many times. It is really sad. You should always serve the government and assist me. Shan Tao went on to say: I have served this dynasty for more than thirty years, but in the end I failed to make the slightest contribution to the advancement of education. His Majesty favored me infinitely and granted me the position of the Third Division. I have heard that a person with poor moral character and a high official but little ability to shoulder heavy responsibilities is in danger of ruining state affairs due to his incompetence and bringing disaster to his family. May your Majesty grant me generations of grace, and beg me to retire and return to my hometown. The edict said: I rely on your merits in assisting the government, stabilizing the royal family, and supporting the emperor. The position of Situ is actually in charge of national education, so I respectfully grant it to you to meet everyone's expectations. How can you suppress and degrade yourself by giving in? After ordering him no longer to submit memorials, he sent someone to add a seal and ribbon to Shan Tao's bed. Shan Tao said: How can a dying person defile the government? Riding home sick. He died in the fourth year of Taikang at the age of seventy-nine. Xia Shao gave him a noble coffin, a set of court robes, a set of clothes, 500,000 yuan in money, and a hundred bolts of cloth for funeral purposes. He was forced to serve as a Situ through a policy letter, and was given a purple ribbon with a honey seal to serve as Diao Chan.
target: He was appointed Situ but refused, eventually dying at seventy-nine. He was given posthumous honors and his family was provided for by the emperor.

source: The emperor built houses for it. At first, Shantao was a commoner and his family was poor. He said to his wife Han Di: "Bear the hunger and cold. I will be the third father-in-law in the future. I wonder if you can be the father-in-law's wife!" After becoming prosperous and wealthy, he was loyal, prudent and frugal. Although his title was like that of a prince, he did not take concubines. Salaries and rewards were distributed to relatives and friends.
target: Shantao was known for his frugality and loyalty, never taking concubines despite his high status. He distributed his salary to relatives and friends.

source: Salaries and rewards were distributed to relatives and friends. At first, Yuan Yi, a native of Chen County, served as a minister. He corrupted and bribed officials to gain fame. He also gave Shan Tao a hundred catties of silk. Shan Tao did not want to be different from others at that time, so he accepted the silk and kept it in the attic. Later, Yuan Yi's affairs were exposed and he was put into a carriage and handed over to Tingwei. Anyone who accepted a bribe would be held accountable. Shan Tao took out the silk and gave it to the officials. After years of dust accumulation, the seal was not opened.
target: He once accepted silk from a corrupt official but kept it sealed, later returning it when the official's crimes were exposed.

source: Shan Tao took out the silk and gave it to the officials. After years of dust accumulation, the seal was not opened. Shan Tao drank until he was drunk until he was drunk. The emperor wanted to test him, so he prepared eight measures of wine for him to drink, and secretly added more wine for him. Shan Tao drank to his limit and stopped drinking. He has five sons: Shan Gai, Shan Chun, Shan Yun, Shan Mo, and Shan Jian. Shan Gai, whose courtesy name was Bolun, inherited his father's title. He became governor of Bingzhou and crown prince Zuo Li, and was posthumously awarded the title of Captain of Changshui. Shan Gai's son Shan Zhang was named Yanzu and served as a lieutenant in the Yi Army. The second son returned to Shanshi and served as a official official and a regular attendant on Sanqi. Shan Chun, whose courtesy name was Zixuan, was not an official, while Shan Yun, whose courtesy name was Shuzhen, was appointed as the captain of Fengche. Both of them had a hunchback and were short in stature, but they were extremely intelligent.
target: He had five sons: Shan Gai, Shan Chun, Shan Yun, Shan Mo, and Shan Jian. Shan Gai inherited his title and served as governor of Bingzhou. Shan Jian, known for his gentle temperament, became a prominent official, serving as minister and governor of various regions.

source: When Wang Rong was fifteen years old, he followed his father Wang Hun in Langshe. Wang Rong was twenty years younger than Ruan Ji, and Ruan Ji befriended him. Every time Ruan Ji went to Wang Hun's place, he would leave after a while to see Wang Rong, and it would take him a long time to come out. Ruan Ji said to Wang Hun: Junchong is clean and noble, and cannot be compared with you. It is better to talk to A Rong than to talk to you. When Wang Hun died in Liangzhou, officials from his old friendship offered him millions of dollars, but Wang Rong refused to accept them, and his reputation spread far and wide. He is short in stature, straightforward and does not value dignity. He is good at asking questions and talking clearly, and he can get the essentials of talking clearly. The virtuous ministers of the court once visited Luo for a banquet on the last day of Shangsi. Someone asked Wang Ji, "What did you say during your trip yesterday?" Wang Ji said: Zhang Hua is good at talking about "Historical Records" and "Moshu"; Pei Dun talks about the past words and deeds, which is eloquent; Wang Rong talks about the ovary and Ji Zha, which is transcendent and mysterious. This is how Wang Rong was appreciated by people of insight. Wang Rong once drank with Yi Xun. At that time, the tomb of Tong Cong, the governor of the imperial court, was present. Ruan Ji did not pour wine for Liu Chang because he had little wine. Liu Chang did not show regret.
target: Wang Rong, courtesy name Junchong, was from Linyi. He was known for his intelligence and calmness from a young age, once standing unafraid during a tiger's roar. He was friends with Ruan Ji and others, and was known for his insight.

source: Zhong Hui was attacking Shu and said goodbye to Wang Rong when passing by. What was his plan? Wang Rong said: There is a saying in Taoism: If you do something without taking credit, it is not difficult to make merit, but it is difficult to keep it. When the Zhonghui failed, those who discussed it thought it was an insightful statement. Inheriting his father's title, he was requisitioned as Prime Minister, and served successively as Huang Menlang of the Ministry of Civil Affairs, Changshi of Sanqi, Governor of Hedong, and Governor of Jingzhou. He committed the crime of sending people to repair the garden and house, so he should be removed from the official position. Shaoshu ordered that he be punished as atonement. He was appointed governor of Yuzhou, added as general Jianwei, and accepted the imperial edict to attack Wu.
target: He served in various official roles, including governor of Jingzhou and Yuzhou, and was involved in the conquest of Wu.

source: Later he was promoted to Guang Luxun and Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, but resigned due to his mother's death. Born in Lu, he was extremely filial and did not adhere to etiquette. He would drink wine, eat meat, or watch people playing chess. However, he looked haggard and could only stand up with a wooden stick. Pei Dun went to express condolences and said to people: If grief hurts the body, Junchong will inevitably be criticized for mourning and destroying one's nature.
target: He was known for his filial piety, though he did not strictly adhere to rituals.

source: He likes to make money by nature, and he collects gardens and water-powered mills from all over the world. He accumulates money and material and is greedy, often holding chips and calculating day and night, but never feels that it is enough. He is also stingy and does not care about his own health. People all over the world say that he is seriously ill and blind. His daughter married Pei Dun and borrowed tens of thousands of dollars from Wang Rong, but has not paid it back for a long time. When his daughter came home later, Wang Rong looked unhappy. His daughter hurriedly paid back the money, and then Wang Rong smiled. When his nephew was about to get married, Wang Rong gave him a piece of clothing and asked for it back after the wedding was over. I have good plums at home and often sell them. I am afraid that others will get the seeds and break the cores. Therefore he is laughed at in the world. Later, he followed the emperor in the Northern Expedition. The royal army was defeated in Dangyin. Wang Rong went to Ye again and returned to Luoyang with the emperor. When the emperor moved westward, Wang Rong rushed to Jia. In times of crisis, he fought in person, talked and laughed freely, and never looked afraid. He often invites relatives, friends and guests to have fun all day long. In the second year of Yongxing, he died in Jiaxian County at the age of seventy-two. Mi was named Yuan.
target: He was criticized for his greed and stinginess, often calculating his wealth day and night. He died at seventy-two, posthumously named Yuan.

source: After Sun Xiu succeeded, all the officials in the court who had a grudge against him were killed, but Wang Rong and Wang Yan benefited from Sun Xiu. His son Wang Wan has a good reputation. He was young and obese. Wang Rong made him eat chaff and he became even more obese. Died at the age of nineteen. There was a concubine named Wang Xing, and Wang Rong looked down upon him. Let the son of his cousin Wang Qing, the prefect of Yangping, succeed him. Wang Yan, whose courtesy name is Yifu, has a clear and beautiful expression, tranquility and elegance. When I was a child, I visited Shan Tao. Shan Tao sighed for a long time. Wang Yan left. Shan Tao looked at him and said: What an old woman, she gave birth to such a son!
target: Wang Yan, courtesy name Yifu, was known for his clear expression and elegance. He was a leading figure in the Qingtan movement, advocating the philosophy of nothingness. He held high positions but was criticized for his lack of integrity and self-preservation.

source: He appointed his younger brother Wang Cheng as the governor of Jingzhou, and his younger brother Wang Dun as the governor of Qingzhou. He said to Wang Cheng and Wang Dun: Jingzhou has the dangers of Jianghan and Qingzhou has the dangers of the sea. You two are outside and I stay here, which is enough to be regarded as a cunning rabbit's three burrows. People of knowledge despised Wang Yan. Shi Le and Wang Mi invaded the capital, and appointed Wang Yan as the commander-in-chief to conquer the military, hold the knot, and fake yellow locks to meet the enemy. Wang Yan sent former general Xuan Wu, left guard general Gong Ji and others to meet the enemy, beat them back and seize their baggage. After being promoted to Taiwei, the position of Shangshu Ling remains the same. He was granted the title Marquis of Wuling, but refused to accept the title. At that time, Luoyang was in crisis, and most people wanted to move the capital to seek refuge, but Wang Yan was the only one who sold his chariots and oxen to calm everyone's minds. When Sima Yue was crusading against Gou Xi, Wang Yan served as the Taifu Army Chief as a Taiwei. When Sima Yue died, everyone elected Wang Yan as marshal. Wang Yan was too frightened to take responsibility because bandits were rising everywhere. He declined and said: When I was young, I had no desire to be an official. With the selection and replacement of officials, I reached the official position I have today. How can we use people without talents to fill today's affairs? Soon the whole army was defeated by Shi Le. Shi Le called the prince to meet him and asked Wang Yan about the old events of Jin. Wang Yan explained the reason for his failure and said that the plan was not his.
target: During the chaos of the Jin dynasty, he advised his brothers to take up posts in strategic regions, a plan known as the "cunning rabbit's three burrows." He was captured by Shi Le and killed after refusing to take responsibility for the dynasty's fall. He was fifty-six at his death.

source: So I dare not not say it. The king's tomb then sent people to return the land, and people praised him. Wang Dun valued Guo Shu's uprightness and rewarded him generously. He visited Guo Shu's home several times. The above table appointed him as the governor of Liangzhou. Death from illness. Yueguang's courtesy name was Yanfu, a native of Qingyang, Nanyang. His father, Le Fang, took part in the military affairs of Xia Guixuan, the general who conquered the West. Le Guang was eight years old at the time. Xia Houxuan once saw Le Guang on the road, so he called him over to talk to him. When he came back, he said to Le Fang: If you see Le Guang looking cheerful and clear, you will become a famous person. Although your family is poor, if you can let him concentrate on his studies, your family will definitely be revitalized. Le Fang died early, and Le Guang lost his father and became poor. He lived in Shanyang, worked hard and studied hard, and no one knew about him. Indifferent temperament, far-sighted, little desire, and aloof from the world. He is especially good at talking. He often uses simple words to explain the truth and convince people. He stays silent about things he doesn't understand.
target: Le Guang, courtesy name Yanfu, was known for his calm and far-sighted nature. He was skilled in conversation and used simple words to explain profound truths.

source: This is how Le Guang is praised by knowledgeable people. After leaving the court, he was appointed as the magistrate of Yuancheng, promoted to the title of minister of Zhongshu, transferred to the title of prince's concubine, and gradually promoted to minister of ministers and Henan Yin. Yue Guang is good at talking but not good at writing. He will resign from Henan Yin and ask Pan Yue to make a statement. Pan Yue said: You should tell me what you mean. Le Guang said 200 sentences about his aspirations. Pan Yue then wrote famous articles according to the sequence. People at that time said: If Le Guang did not rely on Pan Yue's pen, and Pan Yue did not follow Le Guang's wishes, he would not be able to accomplish anything good. There once was a guest who had not come for a long time. Le Guang asked the reason and replied: When I was here before, I was given wine, and I was about to drink it. When he saw a snake in the cup, he was disgusted and became ill after drinking it.
target: He served as Henan Yin and was known for his ability to resolve disputes. He once cured a guest's illness by explaining the illusion of a snake in a cup.

source: Critics believe that although Yang Qiao has a superhuman demeanor, he lacks charm and Yue Guang is just a good expositor. At that time, Wang Cheng, Hu Wufuzhi and others also regarded laissez-faire as understanding, and some even went naked. After hearing this, Le Guang smiled and said: There is something joyful about famous religions, why bother like this! He cherishes talents and behaves in a manner consistent with etiquette and law, all in this type of situation. At a time when the world is unstable and the court's laws are in chaos, I insist on being neutral and honest. At that time, it was difficult for people to know his heart.
target: He was praised for his integrity and adherence to ritual, even during times of chaos.

source: Sima Yi still had doubts, and Le Guang eventually died of worry. When Xun Fan heard that Yue Guang had not been able to escape the disaster, he shed tears for him. He has three sons: Le Kai, Le Zhao and Le Chen. Le Kai, whose courtesy name was Hongxu, was appointed as the commander-in-chief of the King of Qi, and participated in the Hussar Army. Yue Zhao, whose courtesy name was Hongmao, was appointed as Taifu Shuhaiwangju.
target: He died of worry after being slandered. He had three sons: Le Kai, Le Zhao, and Le Chen.

source: If you can't see him now, you can call him to the front of the palace and send your attendants to express condolences, so as to inspect the four vassal states. This is also convenient in form. The emperor agreed to Wang Hun's memorial. He also issued an edict and ordered Wang Hun to record the affairs of the minister. Wang Hun had always been famous in the positions he held, but when he became the prime minister in the palace, his reputation gradually declined. Yuan Kang died in the seventh year of his reign at the age of seventy-five, and his name was Yuan. The eldest son Wang Shang died early, and the second son Wang Ji succeeded him. Wang Ji, courtesy name Wuzi. When he was young, he had superhuman talents, was handsome and bold, and his spirit was beyond compare. He likes to bow and arrow and ride horses. His bravery is unmatched. He is good at "Yi", "Zhuang" and "Lao". His writing is beautiful and his skills are superhuman. He is famous in the world, and he is as famous as his brother-in-law He Wei and Pei Kai. Married Princess Changshan. At the age of twenty, he was called away from home to serve as Zhongshu Lang and resigned in mourning for his mother. He was appointed as a general of valiant cavalry, and was gradually promoted to the rank of servant. He was in the same official rank as the servants Kong Xun, Wang Xun and Yang Ji, and became a hero of his time.
target: Wang Ji, courtesy name Wuzi, was Wang Hun's son. He was exceptionally talented, skilled in archery and the "Yi," "Zhuang," and "Lao" texts, and married Princess Changshan. He served as Zhongshu Lang and later as a servant, known for his eloquence and favored by Emperor Wu.

source: Every time the servants come to see him, they always discuss the gains and losses of people and various things. Wang Nai was good at talking, eloquent, and sarcastic. No courtier could surpass him, and the emperor valued him more closely. Although he was promoted quickly, those who commented did not think it was because of Weng's son-in-law. They all said that he was achieved through talent. However, although he looks magnanimous and elegant on the outside, he is very jealous and harsh on the inside and likes to hurt others with words, so people around him despise him. Because of his father, Wang Jun was often excluded, and the discussions at that time ridiculed him. King Sima You of Qi was about to go to the vassal state. After Wang Ji stated his request, he repeatedly asked the princess to enter the palace with Princess Changguang, Zhen De's wife, and kowtowed and cried, begging the emperor to keep Sima You. The emperor angrily said to his attendant Wang Rong: "Brothers have the closest relationship. Now sending the King of Qi is naturally a matter for my family." And Zhen De and Wang Ji sent women one after another to cry to death! Due to his disobedience to the imperial edict, he was demoted to the post of Prince of the State to offer wine, but his position as a regular attendant remained unchanged.
target: However, he was inwardly jealous and harsh with words. He opposed sending Prince Sima You away, crying with the princess, which angered the emperor and led to demotion.

source: The emperor angrily said to his attendant Wang Rong: "Brothers have the closest relationship. Now sending the King of Qi is naturally a matter for my family." And Zhen De and Wang Ji sent women one after another to cry to death! Due to his disobedience to the imperial edict, he was demoted to the post of Prince of the State to offer wine, but his position as a regular attendant remained unchanged. A few years later, he entered the palace and served as a servant. At that time, Wang Hun was a servant, and his boss sometimes handled things improperly. Wang Ji was strict by nature and punished him according to law. Wang Jiping had always been at odds with his cousin Wang You. Wang You's party members believed that Wang Liao did not care about his father too much, so they encouraged different opinions. He took up the post of Henan Yin, but before he took office, he was found guilty of whipping an auxiliary official in the palace and was dismissed from office. Wang Youzheng was appointed. Shan Shan was dismissed from the court, so Wang Ji moved his family to the foot of Beimang Mountain. Wang Ji was extravagant by nature and was very particular about food and clothing. At that time, the land price in Luojing was very high. Wang Ji bought the land and used it as a riding and shooting track. He put the money together to pave the track. People at the time called it "Jingou". Because Wang Kai was the emperor's uncle, he was extravagant and luxurious. He had a cow named "Eight Hundred Miles Pier", and the horns of the cow's hooves were often decorated.
target: As Henan Yin, he was dismissed for whipping an official. He was extravagant, paving a riding track with money and betting a prized cow with Wang Kai, cutting it up after winning.

source: The emperor once visited Wang Ji's residence and served him a sumptuous meal, all of which was served in glassware. Steamed gizzards tasted very good. When the emperor asked why, he replied: Steamed with human milk. The emperor looked very unhappy and left before finishing his meal. Wang Ji knew the temperament of horses very well. He once rode a horse that was covered with dry mud. There was water in front of it, but the horse refused to cross. Wang Zha said: This must be because he is reluctant to give up the clay.
target: He once served human-milk-steamed food to the emperor, who left displeased. He understood horses, once recognizing a horse's reluctance to cross mud.

source: The emperor remained silent. The emperor once played chess with Wang Ji, and Sun Hao was beside him. The emperor said to Zhubi: Why do you like to skin people? Sun Hao said: If you see someone who is rude to the king, skin him. Wang Ji put his feet under the chessboard, so Sun Hao ridiculed Wang Ji. Soon he was made a civilian and served as a servant. At the age of forty-six, he died before Wang Yun, and was posthumously awarded the title of General of Hussars. When it was about to be buried, all the wise men of that time came. Sun Chu respected Wang Ji very much. He came late and cried very sadly. All the guests shed tears. After crying, he said to the coffin: You often like me to bray like a donkey, so I will bray for you. I learned that the shape is similar and the voice is lifelike, and the guests all laughed. Yaochu looked back at them and said: You didn't die, but Wang Zha died! At the beginning, Wang Ji married a princess. The princess was blind and very jealous. However, she never had children. She had two sons by his concubine. The king, named Seixuan, inherited the title of Yuyun and paid homage to Shizhong. The second son, Wang Lou, whose courtesy name was Jianxuan, succeeded the princess and was given the title of Qian Dancai. Wang Zha has two younger brothers, Wang Tuo, whose courtesy name is Su, and Wang, who has a short stem. They are both good at talking, intelligent and literary, and both have held high and noble positions. Wang Jun, courtesy name Shizhi, was from Hongnong Lake. Someone in the family has been a prefect. Wang Jun was well-read in ancient books and had a handsome appearance. He did not pay attention to reputation and conduct, and was not praised by the villagers. Later, I changed my moral integrity, became open-minded and had great ambitions.
target: He died at forty-six, posthumously named General of Hussars. At his funeral, Sun Chu brayed like a donkey in tribute, making guests laugh. He married a blind, jealous princess and had two sons by a concubine. Wang Jun, courtesy name Shizhi, was from Hongnong Lake. He was well-read and handsome, initially lacking reputation but later changed his ways.

source: Even if Lord Yan trusts Le Yi and Han Zu trusts Xiao He, they cannot exceed your trust in me. The kindness I received was so great that it would take my life to repay it, but I acted inappropriately due to my stubbornness and negligence. Your Majesty is very gracious and only blames me. I am terrified and ashamed. I hope your Majesty understands my absolute loyalty. Wang Hun wrote to Zhou Jun, saying that Wang Jun's army had obtained Wu's treasure. Wang Jun went to the table again and said: Following the "Edict of Renxu", I sent a letter from General Anton to Qie Qi, the governor of Qiangye, saying that the army under my command had received the physical object of chasing the pedal, and that General Li Gao of Yamen had set fire to Sun Bi's puppet palace. He wrote an official document and submitted it to the minister, listing all the circumstances. I also heard that Wang Hun wrote a document to file a false accusation against me. I am dull and honest by nature, and I do it with a clear conscience, just hoping to live up to the gods.
target: He built a house with a wide gate, saying it would accommodate halberds and flags.

source: Later, I changed my moral integrity, became open-minded and had great ambitions. Once a house was built, dozens of steps were left in front of the door. Someone asked him why he left too much space. Wang Jun said: I want to allow halberds and flags to be accommodated in front of the door. Everyone laughed at him, and Wang Jun said: "Chen Sheng once said, how can the sparrow know the ambition of the swan?" The state and county recruited him to work in Hedong. Those who were dishonest among the officials all left on their own after hearing the news. Xu Miao, a native of the state of Yan, the governor, had a daughter, Shu Xian, who was talented and unmarried. Xu Miao gathered his subordinate officials in a grand ceremony and asked his daughter to watch them in their buns. The daughter pointed at Wang Jun and told her mother, so Xu Miao married her daughter to him. Later, when he participated in the Southern Military Campaign, Yang Hu understood and treated him favorably.
target: He married Xu Miao's daughter after she saw him at a gathering. Yang Hu recognized his talent and helped him.

source: He was transferred to the position of charioteer and knight, and knowledgeable people said that Yang Hu could recommend talented people. He was appointed as the governor of Bajun. Bajun is adjacent to the border with Wu State. The soldiers are hard at work and most of the boys are not supported. Wang Jun then made the regulations strict and the corvee loose. Those who gave birth were allowed to rest and exempted from the corvee. Thousands of people survived in this way. He was transferred to the post of governor of Guanghan and implemented benevolent and benevolent policies, and the people relied on him. Wang Jun dreamed of three knives hanging on the beam in his bedroom at night, and then another knife was added. Wang Jun woke up with a start, hating this dream in his heart. Li Yi, the chief registrar, paid two obeisances to congratulate him and said: "The three knives are the characters for state. One more sword has been added. I'm afraid you are going to Yizhou?" When the thief Zhang Hong killed Huangfu Yan, the governor of Yizhou, he transferred Wang Jun to be the governor of Yizhou. Wang Jun planned to kill Zhang Hong and others, and was named a Marquis of Guannei for their meritorious services. To appease different customs and treat others with dignity and trust, most of the foreigners from outside the country came to submit and surrender. He was conscripted and appointed as a right-guard general, and appointed as a minister of agriculture.
target: As Governor of Bajun, he eased corvée for newborns, saving thousands. As Governor of Guanghan, he was benevolent. He dreamed of knives, interpreted as a sign he would govern Yizhou, and became its governor, pacifying rebels.

source: Jia Chong and Xun Xu stated their advice and advised that Wu should not be attacked. Only Zhang Hua persisted in persuading war. In addition to Du Yu's request, the emperor issued a letter from Shao, assigning orders to all parties to control the festival. Wang Jun then took command of the army. Previously, those who had preserved their fertility in Bajun were able to serve as corvees to provide for the army. Their parents warned them: "Prefect Wang has given birth to you, you must work hard and don't be reluctant to die!" In the first month of the first year of Taikang, Wang Jun sent troops from Chengdu and led the Badong Supervisory Army and Guangwu General Tang Bin to attack Danyang of Wu State, captured Nahuo, and captured Danyang Supervisor Shengji. The Wu people used iron locks to cut off the Yangtze River in dangerous and critical places, and made iron cones more than ten feet long, which were secretly placed in the river to block ships head-on. Before attacking Wu, Yang Hu captured Wu spies and fully understood the situation. source: Liu Song, courtesy name Ziya, was born in Guangling and was a descendant of Liu Xu, King Li of Guangling in the Han Dynasty. It has been a prestigious family for generations. This is enough to consolidate the domestic and foreign vassals and maintain the rule of the world. King Wu was the holy master, and King Cheng was his virtuous successor. However, the reason why King Wu did not rely on King Cheng's virtuousness to establish a feudal kingdom was because he considered the long-term spread of the country's great cause.
target: Liu Song submitted a lengthy memorial discussing various state affairs, including the establishment of feudal states, the importance of enfeoffing princes to create stable foundations, and the dangers of relying solely on county systems.

source: The sage emperor speculates on the shortcomings of the past and the present, weighs the principles of importance, tolerates the small mistakes of the princes, and stabilizes the great stability. This is enough to consolidate the domestic and foreign vassals and maintain the rule of the world. King Wu was the holy master, and King Cheng was his virtuous successor. However, the reason why King Wu did not rely on King Cheng's virtuousness to establish a feudal kingdom was because he considered the long-term spread of the country's great cause. Moreover, those who are good at talking about today's national affairs must use what happened in ancient times as verification. There are incomplete historical records of events before Tang and Yu, so it is difficult to know the details at that time. In the third generation, the benevolence of the saints and the relatives who established emperors were entrusted to them according to the fifth-level titles, so that they could establish the country and inherit the family, which was used to protect the royal family and ensure the long-term destiny of the country. The short time was five to six hundred years, and the long time was nearly a thousand years. In the Qin Dynasty, the princes were dismissed and prefectures and counties were established. The emperor, princes and younger brothers were not given any land, so they were isolated and without help, and they perished in two generations. After the Han Dynasty inherited the Zhou Dynasty and the Qin Dynasty, the princes, prefectures and counties were mixed and established, and each of them lasted for more than 200 years.
target: He argued that enfeoffment would ensure long-term stability, drawing comparisons between the Zhou Dynasty's long duration due to feudal systems and the Qin Dynasty's rapid collapse after abolishing them.

source: By doing this, the benefits to people all over the world will be incalculable. There are so many things about government affairs, and world affairs have not yet been managed well. It is difficult to list them all in the memorial. The key to outlining them is three points. If you want political peace, peace lies in reducing labor, and reducing labor lies in governing without horses. To make the warehouses full, we need to develop agriculture, and to benefit agriculture, we need to keep food prices down. To be in government lies in affirming one's faith, and in affirming one's faith lies in selecting worthy persons, and in selecting worthy persons it is necessary to serve as an official for a long time.
target: Liu Song also discussed the need for proper official evaluation, reducing labor burdens, developing agriculture, and maintaining grain prices.

source: The supervisory department investigates the culprits according to the law, the prison officials investigate the facts according to the crime, and the law enforcement officials strictly abide by the law according to the lawsuit. Although the laws are the same, there are some small differences between the supervisory department and the prison officials in the implementation process. Prison officers focus on facts, law officials focus on words, and supervisory departments want to list major mistakes and ignore minor mistakes. Why? Trivial mistakes and absurd shortcomings are commonplace for everyone, and if they are investigated in accordance with the law, there will be no one in the government and the public who does not make mistakes. This leads to the reason why the so-called governance actually makes the situation more chaotic.
target: He criticized current governance for focusing on minor faults while ignoring major crimes, comparing this to leaving dangerous beasts on the road while strictly prohibiting mice.

source: I hope your Majesty will pay more attention to my remarks. He also discussed his views on corporal punishment, which can be found in "Criminal Law Chronicles". The imperial edict replied: "I have received Chen's memorial to establish the feudal state system. It should abide by the ancient regulations, use punishments in accordance with the law, and restore corporal punishment. It also talks about the battle of soldiers in the six states, the methods of serving as officials, etc. From all the articles in the memorial, I know that you are serving the country loyally." Please report everything in the future if anything happens. In the early years of Yuankang, Liu Yuan followed Sima Yun, the king of Huainan, to enter the court. When Yang Jun was about to be executed, Liu Song was stationed in the guard palace. That night, an edict was issued to appoint Liu Song as the Minister of the Three Lords. He also wrote a letter to discuss matters related to laws and regulations, and was praised by current commentaries. Much later, he was transferred to the Ministry of Civil Affairs and set up a nine-class system. He wanted to make officials less likely to change their positions so that they could test their talents and have clear rewards and punishments. At that time, Jia Guo was specialized in government affairs, and officials wanted to be promoted quickly, so this system could not be implemented in the end. King Sima Lun of Zhao killed Zhang Hua and cried bitterly. When he heard that Zhang Hua's son had escaped, he said happily: Mr. Mao, you still have descendants! When Sima Lun's party member Zhang Lin heard about this, he was furious, but he was afraid that Sheng Feng was an upright person and could not assassinate him. Sun Xiu and others praised Sima Lun's achievements and believed that Jiuxi should be added, and the officials did not dare to raise objections. Only Xing Zuo said: In the past, nine tins were added to the droppings and nine tins were added to the cushions. They were only used temporarily and cannot be implemented as regular rituals. Now that the ancestral temple is safe, even if the queen is deposed and the traitorous ministers who are in power are executed, in the past Zhou Bo killed Zhu Lu and honored Xiaowen, and Huo Guang abolished Changyi and honored Xiaowen, but they did not give Jiuxi his life. It is not the system of the previous emperors to violate the old regulations and follow the system of the moment. Please don’t implement Jiuxi’s suggestion. Zhang Bing was very angry about this and believed that Liu Song was a member of Zhang Hua's party and was going to kill him. Sun Xiu said: Killing Zhang Hua and Pei Ban has already hurt people's popularity, so we can't kill Liu Song again. Zhang Lin gave up. Then he appointed Luluo as the official Guanglu, and set up a horse parade in front of his official office. Soon after he died of illness, the emperor sent someone to offer condolences and offered him 200,000 yuan and a court dress. Liu Chen, the assistant minister of Zhongshu, reported that Liu Tan was the junior at that time and should be given as a gift to open the mansion. Sun Xiuping always hated him and did not allow him. Song had no children, and his son Liu Yong, who raised his younger brother Liu He, died early, and Xingli, the son of Liu Yong's younger brother Xingyi, was his legitimate grandson and inherited the title. In the first year of Yongkang, an edict was issued to Liu Song for his meritorious service in taking charge of Pepsi when he killed Jia Mi. He was posthumously granted the title of Marquis of Liangzo County. Liu Biao, Liu Song's younger brother, who lived in the 1,500 households in the city, was given the courtesy name Zhongya to participate in the Andong military.
target: He advocated for simpler governance, long-term official appointments, and proper assessment of achievements. The imperial edict replied acknowledging his loyal service and requesting continued reports. In the early Yuankang period, Liu Song followed Sima Yun into court. When Yang Jun was executed, Liu Song guarded the palace and was appointed Minister of the Three Lords. He later transferred to the Ministry of Civil Affairs, establishing a nine-class system to reduce official turnover, but Jia Guo's specialized government prevented implementation. When Sima Lun killed Zhang Hua, Liu Song wept bitterly and rejoiced upon learning Zhang Hua's son had escaped. When Sun Xiu and others praised Sima Lun's achievements and proposed adding Jiuxi, Liu Song opposed it, citing historical precedents. Zhang Lin was furious but spared Liu Song due to Sun Xiu's advice. Liu Song soon died of illness, receiving imperial condolences and gifts.

source: At first, Liu Song married his daughter to Chen Jiao from Linhuai. Chen Jiao was originally a descendant of the Liu family and was a close relative of Liu Song. She was adopted by his aunt's family and changed her surname to Chen. Zhongzheng Liu You advised him on this matter. Liu Song said: After Shun, the surnames of Yao Yu, Chen Tian and others were originally from the same family, but intermarriage was inevitable for generations. The same thing applies to my family now, intermarriage is allowed. Liu Youzheng is thinking of writing a memorial. Stopped by sketch and therefore not impeached. Liu Song asked Ming Fa, Chen Fu and Ji Zang, and said: "Who among the villagers is the most aggrieved?" Both of them said: Liu You feels wronged. He changed his temper and scolded them. Jiantang argued: Liu You was wrong to offend the Ming Dynasty because of his private discussion, but the public opinion of the villagers said that he was wronged. Liu You was successively recruited into the positions of Duke Fu, Shangshu Lang, and Huangsha Yushi. Li Chong, courtesy name Maozeng, was born in Zhongwu, Jiangxia. His father, Li Jing, was the governor of Qinzhou and the Marquis of Dutingding. Kui Zhong was studious and talented since childhood. He became an orphan in his early years and lived with his younger brothers. He was known for his friendship.
target: Li Chong, courtesy name Maozeng, was born in Zhongwu, Jiangxia. His father, Li Jing, was governor of Qinzhou. Li Chong was studious and talented, becoming orphaned early and living with his younger brothers, known for his friendship.

source: His father, Li Jing, was the governor of Qinzhou and the Marquis of Dutingding. Kui Zhong was studious and talented since childhood. He became an orphan in his early years and lived with his younger brothers. He was known for his friendship. When he was twenty years old, he was appointed as the leader of the country. He was too humble to give in and refused to take office. Later, in the literature of King Sisu, Shangshu stated that Jiupin said: The previous emperors established systems and changed them at any time. The reason for change is to make them suitable for the national conditions. The nine-grade system was first implemented during the period of chaos. It was a system in the army and was not a long-term method of governing the country.
target: He discussed the nine-grade system, arguing it was a temporary military measure, not a long-term governance method. He advocated for simpler systems with fewer grades and long-term official positions. He opposed limiting slaves and property, arguing that without restoring the well-field system, such restrictions were impractical.

source: However, Huo Yuan was determined and lived in seclusion in the mountains, practicing Confucianism and Taoism, which is commendable for his virtue and justice. If it is not suppressed, it will disappoint the wishes of the people of Youzhou and harm the education of honesty and kindness. According to the imperial edict, Huo Yuan should be promoted to the second rank. The imperial edict was issued and he followed Liu Chen's advice. Li Chong and Li Yi were both ministers. At that time, Wang Rong was appointed minister. Li Chong was praised for his integrity and uprightness. Li Yi Botong was wise and talented. Although they had different moral integrity, they both held important positions. Wang Rong treated them as close friends and each benefited from their own strengths. Li Yi's courtesy name is Maoyan, and his deeds are not recorded in history books. At that time, internal officials had more power and external officials had less power. In addition, there were many official ranks. Li Duan discussed this disadvantage and found it in "Hundred Officials". Another Shangshu said: Although all those who escape favor in the mountains and forests are against the current world and have different origins, the reason why the late king praised them is to praise their noble sentiments. In the past, the late emperor was worried about the disadvantages of luxurious customs and wanted to return to simplicity, so he consulted the officials at court and searched for reclusive people. In the second year of Xianning, Huang Fumi of Anding was conscripted as the concubine of the crown prince. In the fourth year, Zhu Chong of Nan'an was conferred as the doctor. In the first year of Taikang, Zhu Chong was conscripted as the concubine of the crown prince. Although they all claimed to be ill and did not take office, both the government and the public expressed their joy and sincere submission. Now Your Majesty is carrying forward the purpose of honoring the late emperor and respecting the virtuous. I visited Zhu Chong's hometown. I said that although he was very old, he still had great ambitions. He studied Confucianism and Taoism carefully, and his virtues were renewed as he grew older. His morals were pure, and everyone in the place was taught by him. He was indeed a virtuous man who lived in seclusion in the mountains, and he could serve as an example to keep the customs honest. I think we should declare divine grace and give him a gift of recognition before he dies. The government was in chaos at the time and ultimately failed to obey. Li Chong served as the Protector of the Expeditions and the Prefect of Pingyang. He respected moral education, built schools, commended those who were loyal, and promoted talents. He was honest, frugal and without desires. He set an example for his subordinates. During his three years in office, he impeached and removed officials from four counties.
target: He recommended promoting reclusive talents like Huo Yuan, emphasizing the importance of selecting virtuous people regardless of background. Li Chong served as Protector of Expeditions and Prefect of Pingyang, respecting moral education and promoting talents.

source: The government was in chaos at the time and ultimately failed to obey. Li Chong served as the Protector of the Expeditions and the Prefect of Pingyang. He respected moral education, built schools, commended those who were loyal, and promoted talents. He was honest, frugal and without desires. He set an example for his subordinates. During his three years in office, he impeached and removed officials from four counties. After the death of his younger brother Li Yi, he resigned from his official post. In the early years of Yongkang, King Sima Lun of Zhao appointed Li Chong as Prime Minister Zuo Sima. He died of illness at the age of forty-eight due to worry. The family is poor, the house is small, and there is no place to collect the coffin. In the afternoon, the funeral is held at the Dianke Office.
target: After his brother's death, he resigned. He died of illness at age forty-eight, leaving his family poor with no place for his coffin.

source: His son's name was Li Shi, who had a good reputation. He reached the rank of servant and died in the early years of Xianhe. Shi Chen said: Ziya served as an official in the court when he was young. He devoted his loyalty and efforts to serving the country. He extensively discussed the establishment of feudal states, which was in line with the times. He discussed the names of punishments in detail, and everything he discussed was suitable for the political system. Although the words are not gorgeous and graceful, they must be reasonable. Compared with the people of the Xijing era, he was not far away from Maiyi; compared with the people of Shu State, he surpassed Lang Chan. During the period of Yuankang, the rebellious ministers and thieves were busy with the affairs of the court. The whole court was shocked and everyone was in peace. At this time, Liu Song was still loyal and unyielding. He cried bitterly for Zhang Gong's innocence and refused to make extravagances to the king of Zhao. Even the upright and famous officials in ancient times could not do this. As for private discussion, I have an unfair view on Liu You. It is the same as hating someone but being able to praise his merits, and recommending people without avoiding enemies!
target: The historical commentary praised Liu Song for his loyalty, extensive discussions on feudal states, and refusal to compromise with the king of Zhao.

source: Li emphasized the principle of reform based on public opinion, refuted the system of land property, and his words were appropriate to the matter, all of which have merit. How can it be false that he is determined to preside over the selection of officials, pays attention to recommending secluded sages, and treats Jun Chong as his confidant! Praising: Liu Song was strong and upright, and his moral integrity was evident in his words. He does have this virtue by working hard up and down. Li Chong is honest, upright and selfless. Recommend the virtuous and promote the reclusive, and good words and deeds will be reflected in him. These two sages are the cornerstone of the country.
target: Li Chong was commended for his integrity, uprightness, and recommendation of virtuous recluses. Both were considered cornerstones of the country.

source: Zheng Miao, courtesy name Uncle Lin, was a native of Kaifeng, Xingyang. The great ancestor Zheng Zhong was the chief agricultural officer during the Han Dynasty. His father, Zheng Tai, was the governor of Yangzhou during the Han Dynasty and had a good reputation. Zheng Miao lost his father when he was young, and he was insightful and able to identify talents very early. Xun You saw him and said, "Zheng Gongye seems to be still alive." Zheng Miao fled to Jiangdong with his uncle Zheng Hun. At that time, Hua Xin was the governor of Yuzhang, and Zheng Hun went to join him. Hua Xin had always been friendly with Zheng Tai and raised Zheng Miao as his own son.
target: Zheng Miao, a native of Kaifeng, lost his father young and was raised by his uncle Zheng Hun.

source: At that time, Wei Xie, a native of Jiyin, was appointed as the prime minister of the country and was very famous. Ren Lan, who was in the same county as Zheng Yu, made friends with him. Zheng Miao believed that Wei Xi was a traitor who would eventually cause disaster, and advised Ren Lan to stay away from him. When Wei Xi was defeated, everyone who discussed it praised Zheng Mao. When Emperor Wu of Wei first made his sons princes, he carefully selected their retainers and friends. Zheng Miao and Xu Qian both served as Marquis of Linzi, and later became Sili Gongcao.
target: Known for his insight, he warned Ren Lan to avoid Wei Xie, who later caused disaster.

source: Guanqiu Jian made a rebellion, and Emperor Jing personally conquered it. Hundreds of officials gathered in the city to offer sacrifices to him as a road god to see him off. Zheng Miao was ill and could not arrive. Emperor Jing said to Wang Su, the leader of the army: It's just a pity that I didn't see Yinmao. Wang Su told Zheng Miao, and Zheng Miao personally drove the car to chase Emperor Jing and caught up with him not far away. Emperor Jing smiled and said: I knew you would definitely come like Hou Sheng. So he and Zheng Miao rode in the car together and asked him: What strategy should I use first? Zheng Miao replied: Li Qiujian and I were both ministers in the past, so I knew him very well. This person likes strategies but does not know the truth. Since his past achievements in Youzhou, his ambitions and desires are unlimited. Wen Qin is brave but has no plans. Now the king's army was surprised, and the Jiang and Huai soldiers were energetic but unable to hold on. We dug deep ditches and built high fortresses to dampen their enthusiasm. This is what Yafuqu is best at. Emperor Jing agreed. Changing appointments is too common. Gaogui Jinggong asked the ministers to discuss the establishment of Mingtang Piyong, carefully selected doctors, and promoted Liu Yi, Liu Shi, Cheng Xian, and Yu Jun. They all later reached the high positions of three ministers and assistant ministers. When Changdao Xianggong became the monarch, because he participated in the discussion and support, he was granted the title of Marquis of Ancheng Township and a thousand households in the city. In the early years of Jingyuan, he became seriously ill and lost his sight. He requested to retire many times but was not approved. Dr. Ren Guanglu. When the fifth level of nobility was established, he was granted the title of Mi Lingbo. Emperor Wu ascended the throne and became a marquis. Although he had been ill for more than ten years, he was highly recommended by wise men at that time. During the Taishi period, the edict stated: "Guanglu Milinghou Yuan is a pure man, with a quiet and peaceful demeanor when he retires, and a pure and flawless moral integrity when he enters. He should ascend to the position of the Three Dukes to make up for the vacancies of the Duke." Zheng Miao was appointed Sikong. Emperor Wu walked to the front of the palace and sent the Fifth Palace Commander Guo Tan to Zheng Yuan's house to announce the decree. Zheng Miao repeatedly refused and sent his son back to the official seal, going back and forth more than ten times. He said to Guotan: Wei appointed Xu Jingshan as Sikong. I was the minister at that time, and I accepted Shao as an imperial edict.
target: He served as an official under Emperor Wu of Wei, recommended talents like Xu Yun, and governed with education and law, earning the people's love. During Guanqiu Jian's rebellion, he advised Emperor Jing to use defensive tactics. He declined high positions multiple times, eventually becoming Sikong, and died at eighty-five. His son Zheng Mo served as Tingwei, known for integrity and opening granaries during famine, and was posthumously honored.

source: He died in the second year of Yongjia, and was posthumously named Doctor Jin Ziguanglu, with the title of Yuan. Zheng Qiu's younger brother Zheng Yu served as minister in the last years of Yongjia. Li Yin, whose courtesy name was Xuanbo, was from Xiangping, Liaodong. Grandfather Li Min was the governor of Hanoi during the Han Dynasty. He resigned and returned to his hometown. Gongsun Du, the governor of Liaodong, wanted to force him to become an official. He drifted into the sea in a small boat and disappeared without a trace. His son Li Xin has been looking for him for many years, crossing the sea and outside the Great Wall, but has never found him. He wants to mourn, but doubts that he is still alive, so he feels like he is mourning and does not want to get married.
target: Li Yin, from Liaodong, was famed for filial piety, mourning his lost grandfather and father.

source: Emperor Wu refused to listen and sent his servants to announce the decree. He refused to go to the throne and issued a thick edict to urge him. Li Yin had no choice but to come out to deal with political affairs. When Taikang passed away in the third year of his life, Emperor Wu issued an edict to send censors to monitor the funeral procession and mourn him, and the title of Mi was established. The crown prince asked Wang Zan, the prince of the family, to write a condolence article. The writing style and content were very beautiful. Emperor Wu later remembered Li Yin's noble integrity and told Shao: The late Situ Li Yin, Taichang Peng Guan, was loyal, noble and frugal. After his death, his family had no money left. He rewarded Li Yin's family with two million yuan and one thousand dendrobiums of grain, while Peng Guan's family was given half of it. Three sons: Li Gu, Li Zhenchang, and Li Xiu. Li Gu, whose courtesy name was Wanji, served as a Sanqi Lang. He died before Li Yin, and his son Li Zhi inherited the title. Li Zhi, whose courtesy name was Yandao, served successively as Minister of Sanqi, General Jianwei, and Grand Administrator of Yangping. Chief Li Zhen arrives at Taipuqing. Li Xiu was appointed as Huangmen's minister and his concubine.
target: He served as a fair official, enforcing laws strictly, and was appointed Situ. Despite poverty, he refused gifts, and after his death, his family had no savings. His son Li Gu died early, and his grandson Li Zhi inherited the title.

source: Li Xiu was appointed as Huangmen's minister and his concubine. Lu Qin, named Ziruo, was from Fanyang Zhuo. His grandfather Lu Zhi was a minister during the Han Dynasty. His father, Lu Yu, served as Sikong during the Wei Dynasty. Confucianism has been prominent for generations. Lu Qin was indifferent and far-sighted, specializing in classics and history. He was promoted as a filial and honest man. However, if he did not leave, Cao Shuang, the general of Wei, recruited him as a subordinate official.
target: Lu Qin, from Fanyang, was a Confucian scholar who served as a local official, focusing on fair governance and not managing property.

source: Emperor Wu accepted the concession and appointed Lu Qin as the commander-in-chief of all the military forces in Mianbei, General Pingnan, and Jiejie. He also gave Zhuifeng Tao a sleeping chariot each, two horses for the second son-in-law, riding equipment, knives, mirrors and armor for the imperial men, horses, etc., as well as 300,000 yuan in money. Lu Qin was generous and fierce in the military town, and the border areas were safe and sound. He was summoned to serve as a servant of the minister, a servant, a captain of the chariot, and the leader of the official department. Because he was poor, he was given a hundred pieces of silk. Lu Qin is a talented person and enjoys the reputation of being honest and fair. Xianning died in the fourth year. The edict said: Lu Qin followed the right path and was honest and upright. Excellent in both civil and military affairs, he is famous in China. Keep secrets in hand and be fair in dealing with matters. Work diligently both internally and externally, and do your best. I am devastated by his tragic passing. As a posthumous gift to General Wei and the three divisions of Kaifu Yitong, he was given a coffin, a set of court clothes, a piece of regular clothes, 50 pieces of cloth, and 300,000 yuan in money. Mi Hao Yuan. Because Lu Qin was loyal and noble, and did not run any property. After his death, his family had no real estate, so he was given a special reward of 500,000 yuan to build a house.
target: He was appointed General Pingnan, securing borders, and died in Xianning. His family was so poor that the emperor granted funds for a house. His son Lu Fu declined high offices due to disability.

source: Sima Ying returned to Chang'an. Before she arrived, she heard that Sima Ji had killed Zhang Fang and asked Sima Yue for peace. Sima Ying lived in Huayin. Lu Zhi arrived in Chang'an, entered the palace to apologize, and immediately went to Wuguan to meet Sima Ying. He fled to Nanyang, but was driven back to Hebei by Liu Tao. When Sima Ying died, the officials and his family fled, and only Lu Zhi personally attended the funeral. People at that time praised him. Sima Yue appointed Lu Zhi as a military counselor and offered wine, and was promoted to Weiwei. In the last years of Yongjia, he was appointed minister. Luoyang fell, and Lu Zhi led his wife and children to the north to join Liu Kun, the governor of Bingzhou. When he arrived in Yangyi, he was captured by Liu Can and killed in Pingyang together with his second sons Lu Mi and Lu Jiu. The eldest son Lu Chen. Lu Chen, whose courtesy name is Ziliang, has a clear mind, quick wit and insights. He likes "Lao" and "Zhuang" and is good at writing articles. He married Princess Rongyang, the daughter of Emperor Wu, and served as Prince Consort, but the princess died before the marriage was consummated. Later, he was promoted to scholar in the state and conscripted into Taiwei. When Luoyang fell, he followed Lu Zhi to the north and attached himself to Liu Kun. He and Lu Zhi were captured by Liu Can.
target: Lu Zhi, Lu Qin's nephew, served as a strategist for Sima Ying, advising against rebellion and later escorting the emperor to Luoyang. He was captured and killed by Liu Can. His son Lu Chen, a talented writer, was captured by Shi Jilong and died in Xiangguo, leaving works like "Sacrifice" and commentaries.

source: He has six sons: Hua Du, Hua Cen, Hua Wei, Hua Jian, Hua Dan and Hua Jian. Hua Hao, whose courtesy name is Changjun, has a quick mind. Father-in-law Lu Yu presided over the election and did not mention in-laws, so Hua Yu was not allowed to be an official at the age of thirty-five, and was appointed Zhongshu Tongshilang very late. In the early years of Taishi's reign, he was promoted to redong servant servant. He was treated politely by Genduo when he was young, and served successively as Huangmen Shilang, Sanqi Changshi, Qianjun General, Shizhong, Nanzhonglang General, and Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in Hebei. When his father was seriously ill, he returned home and died of illness. According to the old rule, one must return to one's post after the burial, but Jianxiang refused to return, violating the emperor's will. At first, there were three guests in the district, so Hua Hao was sent to the county magistrate Yuan Yi to register his name, and the three guests were all used as slaves. When Yuan Yi was convicted of bribery, the verdict document was confusing and absurd. It no longer stated that slaves were used as guests, but directly said that three slaves were sent to Jiyu, and Yuan Yi was also the son-in-law of the Lu family. Furthermore, Zhongshu Jian Baoxi once asked Hua Fu to marry his daughter on behalf of his son. Because he did not agree, he held a grudge, so he secretly reported to the emperor that there were too many people who had given bribes and they could not all be punished. The closest person should be punished, so he suggested that Hua Yu would be suitable. Because Hua Mi had violated the imperial edict, Hua Yu was dismissed from his official position and deprived of his title and fief during Hua Yu's mourning period. Dahonglu He Zunqi reported that Hua Huan should be exempted from being an ordinary citizen and should no longer inherit the title. He requested that Hua Zhou's legitimate grandson Jie should be his heir. Relevant departments reported that: Hua Yu's original identity and title were revoked for committing crimes. This is only a temporary provision. If he is a legitimate son, it will be written in the name book and he will not be allowed to have any heirs. This is more severe than the punishment. When princes break the law, they should be dealt with fairly according to the Eight Disciplines, and their penalties should be reduced or reduced. The inheritance by a legitimate son does not constitute the crime of lifelong abolition. To abrogate the title is too much. According to the law, he should be allowed to succeed.
target: Hua Biao, from Gaotang, served as Taichang Qing, retiring due to illness. His son Hua Yu was dismissed for violating mourning rules but later restored. Hua Heng, Hua Yu's son, served as Taichang, establishing ritual systems after wars, and died in poverty with only books.

source: He died before completing the Ten Codes. The secretary supervisor He Shaoshang asked Hua Wei's son Hua Che to be his assistant and asked him to complete the work. He died before completing the work. Later, secretary-supervisor Miao Zheng proposed to appoint Hua Chang, Hua Wei's youngest son, as his assistant author. He finally completed the Ten Codes and wrote biographies of the Wei and Jin Dynasties. He and his author Zhang Zai were both historians. During the Yongjia Rebellion, the classics were lost, but more than thirty volumes of Hua Wei's books are still preserved. Hua Wo has three sons: Hua Yi, Hua Che, and Hua Chang. Hua Yi succeeded him and became an official in the internal history of Changle. Hua Chang has a quick mind and his articles are worth thousands of words. Encountering war, he took refuge in Jingzhou and was killed by thieves at the age of forty. Shi Jian, courtesy name Lin Bo, was a native of Yanci, Leling. He was born into a poor family, has noble aspirations and is fair in dealing with things. When he was an official in the Wei Dynasty, he served successively as Shangshu Lang, Shi Yushi, Shangshu Zuocheng, and Yushi Zhongcheng. He corrected many current affairs and personnel, and the emperor was afraid of him. He served as governor of Bingzhou, Jiajie, and Zhonglang general who protected the Huns. Emperor Wu accepted Emperor Wei's abdication and granted Shi Jian the title of Tang Yangzi. He was summoned to serve as Sili Xiaowei, and was changed to Shangshu. At that time, Qin and Liang were defeated by foreigners, and Shi Jian was sent to supervise the military affairs of Longyou. He was dismissed from his post for falsely reporting military exploits.
