During the Taishi period, he served as Yin of Henan. Du Yu believed that the capital was the starting point for royal enlightenment. From near to far, all policies and measures should be prophesied in general. Feng Shao formulated the regulations for dismissal and promotion, which roughly states: I heard that in ancient politics, people followed nature and pursued integrity with their own purity. Then there was the way of honesty and obedience; the spirit influenced the soul and communicated, and then the world's principles were achieved. The simple atmosphere gradually dissipated, virtues were revealed and vices were revealed, official positions were established, titles and salaries were awarded, and six canons were announced for detailed inspection of officials.
target: He codified laws, emphasizing simplicity and clarity to prevent violations. As Henan Yin, he advocated for straightforward official assessments, arguing that overly detailed regulations bred hypocrisy.

source: The reason for the recommendation is also based on hearsay. It is not recommended to be promoted after six years, and it is not in line with the original intention of the ancient three-year assessment. Nowadays, when there is an annual assessment, those who accumulate excellent ratings will be promoted, and those who accumulate poor ratings will be dismissed. With the heart of a scholar and a gentleman, there will be no upright officials who are dismissed six times in six years, and officials with poor performance who are promoted six times in six years. The Supervisor will also impeach at any time. If officials at both the upper and lower levels blatantly tolerate mistakes, it means that public opinion is completely corrupted, and it has nothing to do with the assessment for dismissal and promotion. Shi Jian, the captain of the Sili school, impeached Du Yu because of his original resentment, and Du Yu was dismissed from office. At that time, the enemy invaded Longyou and appointed Du Yu as the military commander of Anxi, giving him 300 soldiers and 100 mounts. When he arrived in Chang'an, he was appointed as the governor of Tongye, and concurrently as the captain of the Eastern Qiang army, the general of Qingche, and the official of Jiajie. When the enemy was strong, Shi Jian was the general of Anxi and sent Du Yu to attack the enemy.
target: He was dismissed after a conflict with Shi Jian but later served as a military commander, correctly predicting the enemy’s actions.

source: Because Du Yu married a princess, within the scope of the eight arguments to reduce the punishment, he was treated as a marquis atonement. Later, the situation in Longyou finally turned out as Du Yu expected. At that time, the imperial court believed that Du Yu was good at planning. When the Xiongnu commander-in-chief launched a fierce rebellion, he went from the west of Chazhou to Hedong and Pingyang. He ordered Si Yu to set up a strategy in the palace as a Sanhou, and soon he was appointed as the Minister of Zhi. Zhu Ling then submitted a report to establish Yutian, a stable border, and other important matters of governing the country. He also asked the producers to arrange new tools, build Changping warehouse to regulate grain prices, regulate grain prices, approve salt trafficking, formulate tax regulations, and made more than 50 suggestions that would benefit the country internally and aid the frontier fortresses externally, all of which were adopted.
target: He proposed numerous reforms, including new tools, granaries, and tax regulations. He built a bridge at Fupingjin despite skepticism, and crafted a water clock.

source: Du Yu creatively built it and reported it to the emperor. The emperor was very happy and praised it. In the autumn of the fourth year of Xianning, heavy rains continued and locusts were infested. Du Yu wrote a book about important matters for promoting agriculture, which were recorded in "Shi Huo Zhi". During Du Yu's seven years in the court, he made countless reforms in various government affairs. He was praised both inside and outside the court, calling him "Du Wuku" and saying that there was no success that he did not participate in. At that time, the emperor secretly had a plan to destroy the state of Wu, but most of the discussions in the court were contrary to this. Only Du Yu, Yang Hu, and Zhang Hua were in agreement with the emperor. When Yang Hu fell ill, he recommended Du Yu to replace him, so he used his original official position as a leave to replace General Ping Cambodia and also conquered the Southern Army Division. After Yang Hu's death, he paid homage to the general of Zhennan and the commander-in-chief of all the military forces in Jingzhou, and gave him a chariot and a second son-in-law. After Du Yu took office, he repaired mail weapons, showed force, selected elites, attacked Wu Xiling and governor Zhang Zheng, defeated the enemy army, and increased the number of food households by 365 households due to his meritorious service. Zhang Zheng was a famous general in the Wu Kingdom. He occupied a key position. He was ashamed of his unpreparedness and failed, and did not tell Sun Hao the truth about the casualties. Du Huan wanted to alienate the Wu border generals, so he sent a petition to return the captured Wu soldiers to Sun Hao.
target: Appointed to replace Yang Hu in Jingzhou, he repaired weapons, trained troops, and defeated Wu general Zhang Zheng, then alienated Wu by returning captives. He urged immediate conquest of Wu, countering objections about summer rains by citing overwhelming momentum. His forces captured Jiangling and other cities, leading to Wu’s surrender.

source: Du Yukaiyang traveled more than a thousand miles from Xiashui to Baling, eliminating water dangers in the Yangtze River internally and communicating with Linggui's water transport externally. The South eulogized him and said: There will be no rebellion in the future generations due to Duong, who can understand the wisdom, fame and bravery. There was nothing Du Yu knew about the public affairs that he would not do without doing it. Everything that is built and formulated must be inspected from beginning to end, and there are very few mistakes. Some people ridiculed him for his meticulousness, but Du Yu said: Yu Ji's achievement was to save the world, and I did the same thing. Du Yu valued leaving a name for future generations. He often said that "high banks can become canyons, and deep valleys can become mountains and mausoleums." He carved two stone tablets to record his achievements. One stone sank under the Wanshan Mountains, and the other stood on the Xian Mountain. He said: "Who knows that they will not become mountains and mausoleums and deep valleys in the future!"
target: He was enfeoffed as a marquis. After the war, he focused on education, irrigation, and stabilizing the region, earning the people’s trust. He carved stone tablets to record his achievements, predicting geological changes.

source: The saints in the Middle Ages were buried together, probably because they were not buried separately, but because they were alive to show their enlightenment. From then on, gentlemen were buried together or separately. They could not know life, so how could they know death? When I was working as a Tailang, I once passed by Xingshan in Mi County on official business. There was a tomb on the mountain. When I asked the farmer, he said it was Dr. Zheng's memorial to Zhong, or it was the tomb of Zichan, so he led his entourage to pay homage and watch. The tomb is built on the top of a mountain, with a wide view on all sides. It connects the middle of the north and south of the mountain and is tilted to the northeast, facing Xinzheng City, which shows that we have not forgotten our roots.
target: Though not a horseman or archer, he led effectively and was known for his humility and dedication to the *Zuo Zhuan*, which he annotated extensively.

source: Sun Xiu asked to date Du Xi, but Du Xi rejected him. Although Sun Xiu was resentful, she was afraid of his high reputation and did not dare to harm him. Emperor Hui was restored to power and promoted Du Xi to the rank of official official and prefect of Chengyang. However, he did not accept the offer and promoted him to Zuocheng, the minister of finance. When he died at the age of forty-eight, he was given as a posthumous gift a regular attendant on horseback. His son Du Yi succeeded him, see "Biography of Foreign Relatives".
target: He died at sixty-three while traveling, leaving instructions for a simple burial. His son Du Xi served as a crown prince’s tutor, known for his integrity, and survived political turmoil.

source: His son Du Yi succeeded him, see "Biography of Foreign Relatives". Shi Chen said: During the Taishi period, people and gods gave gifts, and Yang Gong proposed a strategy to pacify the Wu Kingdom. This shows the heart of heaven and earth. In the past, the Qi State had Qianfu, and the Yan people worshiped ghosts at the north gate; the Zhao State had Li Mu, and the King of Qin stopped the momentum of annexing eastward. Repay evil with kindness and eliminate old grudges.
target: The chroniclers praised Yang Hu’s strategic vision and Du Yu’s multifaceted talents, noting their contributions to unifying the realm.

source: Emperor Xuan's name was Yi, whose courtesy name was Zhongda. He was from Xiaojingli, Wen County, Henan, and his surname was Sima. His ancestors were descendants of Chongli, the son of Emperor Gaoyang, namely Xia Guan Zhurong. After experiencing the Tang, Yu, Xia and Shang dynasties, he inherited this official position. During the reign of King Xuan of Zhou Dynasty, the person who served as Sima of the Xia Dynasty was a man named Cheng Baixiu's father. Because he conquered and pacified Xu Fang as a world official, he was given the family name of Sima. Therefore, Longmo became their last name. During the Chu and Han Dynasties, Sima Yan was a general who joined the army of the princes in conquering the Se country. After the fall of the Qin State, it was established as: Mudou, and the king's capital was established in Chi. He designated the land as a county, and his descendants lived here permanently. From Sima, the eighth generation descendant, Sima Gou, the general of the Western Conquest, named Shuping. Sima Gou Sheng invited Tong Taishou to cultivate the land, named Gong Ji. Dandan was born in Yuanbei, Dankentan, the prefect of Yuanbei, with the courtesy name Wuken. When Siya was born and fled, Siken fell to Yin, whose name was Jiangong. Emperor Xuan was Si Yaduo's second son. Emperor Xuan had extraordinary integrity when he was young. He was smart, bold and had lofty ambitions. He was erudite and devoted to Confucianism. At the end of the Han Dynasty, the world was in chaos, and Emperor Xuan often lamented and worried about the world. Nanyang Prefect Dangyu, who was from the same county and was known for being good at identifying talents, met Emperor Xuan, who was underage at the time. He thought Emperor Xuan was an unusually talented person. Cui Yanyu, a native of Qinghe who served as minister, was a friend of Emperor Xuan's brother Sima Lang. He once said to Sima Lang: Your brother is smart, wise and honest, and his decisive ability is outstanding. He is not comparable to ordinary people.
target: Emperor Xuan, named Sima Yi with the courtesy name Zhongda, was from Wen County, Henan. His ancestors traced back to Chongli, a descendant of Emperor Gaoyang, who served as Xia Guan Zhurong. During the Zhou Dynasty, a descendant named Cheng Baixiu's father was granted the surname Sima for pacifying Xu Fang. In the Chu-Han period, Sima Yan was a general. By the eighth generation, Sima Gou emerged, and Emperor Xuan was the second son of Si Yaduo. From a young age, Emperor Xuan displayed extraordinary integrity, intelligence, and lofty ambitions, being erudite in Confucianism. During the late Han Dynasty's chaos, he lamented the state of the world. Nanyang Prefect Dangyu recognized his talent early on, and Cui Yanyu praised his wisdom and decisiveness.

source: At the end of the Han Dynasty, the world was in chaos, and Emperor Xuan often lamented and worried about the world. Nanyang Prefect Dangyu, who was from the same county and was known for being good at identifying talents, met Emperor Xuan, who was underage at the time. He thought Emperor Xuan was an unusually talented person. Cui Yanyu, a native of Qinghe who served as minister, was a friend of Emperor Xuan's brother Sima Lang. He once said to Sima Lang: Your brother is smart, wise and honest, and his decisive ability is outstanding. He is not comparable to ordinary people. Six years after the founding of the Imperial Household, the county recommended candidates for the imperial office. At that time, Yan Gen Zaoxuan invited Sikong to serve. After hearing about Emperor Xuan's reputation, he recruited him. Emperor Xuan understood that Yi's fortune was declining, and he was unwilling to lose his integrity and succumb to Tadang, so he declined on the grounds that he had wind paralysis and was unable to eat and live normally. Wei Genzuo sent a secret agent at night to spy on the situation, but Emperor Xuan lay motionless on the bed. When Emperor Wu of Wei was appointed prime minister, he summoned Emperor Xuan to be a literary advisor and ordered the people sent there: If he makes excuses again, he will be imprisoned. Emperor Xuan was afraid and took office. From then on, Emperor Wu of Wei ordered Emperor Xuan to accompany the prince at all times. He was promoted to the position of Huangmen Shilang, then Yilang, Prime Minister Shu Cao's family, and soon he was transferred to the chief secretary.
target: In the sixth year of the founding, he was recommended for office but initially declined due to illness, fearing the declining fortunes of the Han. When Emperor Wu of Wei (Cao Cao) summoned him as a literary advisor, he was threatened with imprisonment and reluctantly took the post. He served as Huangmen Shilang, Yilang, and Prime Minister Shu Cao's family, eventually becoming chief secretary.

source: From then on, Emperor Wu of Wei ordered Emperor Xuan to accompany the prince at all times. He was promoted to the position of Huangmen Shilang, then Yilang, Prime Minister Shu Cao's family, and soon he was transferred to the chief secretary. Emperor Xuan followed Cao Cao to attack Zhang Lu and advised Emperor Wu of Wei: Liu Bei captured Liu Zhang through deception and force. The Shu people sent troops to fight for Jiangling before they surrendered. This opportunity cannot be missed. Now if we go to Hanzhong to display our troops and show off our power, Yizhou will panic and seize the opportunity to march and attack the city, which will inevitably lead to collapse. With this momentum, it is easy to establish achievements. A saint cannot go against heaven's timing, nor can he lose his opportunity. Emperor Wu of Wei said: People are suffering from lack of satisfaction. They have captured Longxi and still want to capture Shu! In the end, he did not listen to Emperor Xuan's opinion. Soon Emperor Xuan followed Cao Cao to conquer Sun Quan and defeated Sun Quan's army. After the army triumphantly returned, Sun Quan sent an envoy to beg for surrender, presented a memorial to him, and stated that this was his destiny. Emperor Wu of Wei said: This boy wants to roast me on the fire! Emperor Xuan replied: The fate of the Han Dynasty is coming to an end, and the prime minister owns nine-tenths of the world, and serves the emperor accordingly. Sun Quan became a minister, which was the common wish of heaven and man. The reason why the Yu, Xia, Yin, and Zhou dynasties refused to give in and refuse was precisely because they feared God and knew God's will. After the establishment of the Wei Kingdom, Emperor Xuan was promoted to the crown prince and concubine. Whenever he participates in major decisions, he always has a good plan and wins the trust and respect of the prince. He is known as the four friends with Chen Qun, Wu Zhi and Zhu Shuo. Emperor Xuan was promoted to Army Sima and told Emperor Wu of Wei: In ancient times, Jizi discussed the strategy of governing the country and proposed that food is the first priority for the people. At present, there are about 200,000 people in the country who are not engaged in agricultural production. This is not a long-term solution for running the country. Although the war has not subsided, we should still cultivate the land and defend at the same time. Emperor Wu of Wei adopted this opinion and devoted himself to farming to accumulate grain. The country's property was rich and sufficient. Emperor Xuan also issued a memorial stating that Hu Xiu, the governor of Jingzhou, was cruel to the people, and Fu Fang, the governor of Nanxiang, was arrogant and extravagant, and neither of them should be appointed officials to serve as border guards. Emperor Wu of Wei did not investigate or deal with them. When Shu general Guan Yu besieged Cao Ren in Fan, Yu Jin and other seven armies were completely wiped out. Hu Xiu and Fu Fang surrendered to Guan Yu, making Cao Ren's siege even more critical. At this time, Emperor Han made Xuchang his capital. Emperor Wu of Wei thought that Xuchang was too close to the enemy and wanted to move to the north of the Yellow River. Emperor Xuan advised: "The defeat of Yu Jin and other troops by the water was not due to a blunder in combat and defense. The relocation did not harm the overall situation of the country. Moving the capital rashly not only showed our weakness to the enemy, but also caused extreme unrest among the soldiers and civilians in the Huaihe and Mianshui areas." Sun Quan and Liu Bei were close on the outside but distant on the inside. Guan Yu's victory was exactly what Sun Quan did not want.
target: Emperor Xuan accompanied Cao Cao on campaigns, advising against missing opportunities to attack Shu after capturing Hanzhong, but Cao Cao refused. He later followed Cao Cao to defeat Sun Quan. After Sun Quan's surrender, Emperor Xuan argued that the Han dynasty's fate was ending and Cao Cao should accept heaven's will. In the Wei Kingdom, he became crown prince and concubine, trusted by the prince, and was known as one of the four friends with Chen Qun, Wu Zhi, and Zhu Shuo. As Army Sima, he advocated for agricultural cultivation to support the military, which Cao Cao adopted, enriching the state. He also criticized corrupt officials Hu Xiu and Fu Fang, but Cao Cao ignored him; they later surrendered to Guan Yu, worsening Cao Ren's siege. Emperor Xuan advised against moving the capital, suggesting instead to ally with Sun Quan against Guan Yu, which led to Guan Yu's death. He also opposed relocating people from Jingzhou, allowing exiles to return home.

source: Guan Yu had just been defeated, and all kinds of evildoers hid and fled to watch. Now ordering those good people to migrate will not only hurt their feelings, but will also make those who have fled dare not return to their hometowns. Emperor Wu of Wei followed this opinion. After that, the exiles all returned to their hometowns to engage in their own professions. When Emperor Wu of Wei died in Luoyang, the government and the public were frightened. Emperor Xuan presided over the funeral and kept order inside and outside the court. Then he personally carried the coffin back to Ye. After Emperor Wen of Wei came to the throne, he granted Emperor Xuan the title of Marquis of Hejin Ting, and then the title of Prime Minister Chang Shi. At the same time, Sun Quan led his troops to march westward. The imperial court considered that Fan and Xiangyang did not have enough food reserves to defend themselves against the enemy. At that time, Cao Ren was guarding Xiangyang, hoping to recall Cao Ren to Wandi. Emperor Xuan said: Sun Quan recently defeated Guan Yu. This is the time when he wants to take the initiative to make friends, so he must not dare to invade. 襄阳是水陆交通的要道，抵御敌人的要害之地，不能放弃。 最终没听从。 So Cao Ren burned and abandoned the two cities. As expected, Sun Quan did not invade. Emperor Wei Wen regretted it very much. After accepting the abdication of the Han Dynasty, Emperor Xuan was appointed Shangshu. Soon, he was appointed as military governor and censor Zhongcheng, and was granted the title of Marquis of Anguo Township. In the second year of Jianchi's reign, he was dismissed from the post of military governor and promoted to Shizhong and Shangshu Youpushe. In the fifth year, the emperor visited the south and reviewed the army at the border of Wu. Emperor Xuan stayed to guard Xidan, and renamed it Xuesu Castle. He was granted the title of Fujun and Jiajie, commanding five thousand soldiers, and was given the title of Shizhong and Lu Shangshushi. Emperor Xuan firmly refused. The Emperor said: Because of many trivial matters, I work day and night without a moment of peace and rest. This is not an honor, it is just to share my worries. In the sixth year, the emperor mobilized a large naval army to conquer the state of Wu, and ordered Emperor Xuan to stay behind to appease the people internally and provide military supplies externally. Before setting off, he issued an edict saying: I am deeply worried about the rear affairs, so I entrust it to you. Although Cao Shen had military exploits, Xiao He was more important. Wouldn't it be great if I don't have to worry about anything? The emperor returned to Luoyang from Guangling and ordered Emperor Xuan: "I am in the east, you should be in charge of the affairs in the west; I am in the west, you should be in charge of the affairs in the east." So Emperor Xuan stayed to guard Xuchang. The emperor was seriously ill, and Emperor Xuan, Cao Zhen, Chen Qun and others paid homage to the emperor in the South Hall of Chonghua Hall, and together they accepted his deathbed orders to assist the government. The prince was ordered to say: If there is a estrangement between the three adults, do not be suspicious. After Emperor Ming ascended the throne, he changed the title of Emperor Xuan to Wuyang Marquis. Sun Quan besieged Jiangxia and sent generals Zhuge Jin and Zhang Ba to attack Xiangyang. Emperor Xuan led all armies to attack Sun Quan and drove back the Wu army. He marched in pursuit, defeated Zhuge Jin, killed Zhang Ba, and killed more than a thousand enemy soldiers in total. Emperor Xuan was promoted to General of Hussars.
target: After Cao Cao's death, Emperor Xuan managed the funeral and escorted the coffin to Ye. Under Emperor Wen of Wei (Cao Pi), he was made Marquis of Hejin Ting and Prime Minister Chang Shi. When Sun Quan attacked, he advised against recalling Cao Ren from Xiangyang, but was ignored; Cao Ren burned the city, and Sun Quan did not invade, causing regret. After the Han abdication, Emperor Xuan served as Shangshu, then military governor and censor Zhongcheng, later becoming Shizhong and Shangshu Youpushe. He guarded Xuchang and was granted titles, though he refused honors. During campaigns against Wu, he stayed behind to manage affairs. On his deathbed, Emperor Wen entrusted him, Cao Zhen, and Chen Qun with assisting the government. Under Emperor Ming, Emperor Xuan became Wuyang Marquis. He repelled Sun Quan's forces, killing Zhang Ba. He was promoted to General of Hussars and garrisoned in Wan.

source: So Emperor Xuan stayed to guard Xuchang. The emperor was seriously ill, and Emperor Xuan, Cao Zhen, Chen Qun and others paid homage to the emperor in the South Hall of Chonghua Hall, and together they accepted his deathbed orders to assist the government. The prince was ordered to say: If there is a estrangement between the three adults, do not be suspicious. After Emperor Ming ascended the throne, he changed the title of Emperor Xuan to Wuyang Marquis. Sun Quan besieged Jiangxia and sent generals Zhuge Jin and Zhang Ba to attack Xiangyang. Emperor Xuan led all armies to attack Sun Quan and drove back the Wu army. He marched in pursuit, defeated Zhuge Jin, killed Zhang Ba, and killed more than a thousand enemy soldiers in total. Emperor Xuan was promoted to General of Hussars. In June of the first year of Taihe, the emperor ordered Emperor Xuan to garrison in Wandi and add the military governor of Jingzhou and Yuzhou to the army. When Shu general Meng Da surrendered, the Wei Dynasty treated him very well. Emperor Xuan believed that Mengda's words and deeds were cunning and untrustworthy, and his repeated remonstrances were not accepted, so he appointed Mengda as the prefect of Xincheng, granted him the title of marquis, and gave him the title of holiday. Mengda then joined Wu An and Shu to plot the Central Plains. Zhuge Liang, the prime minister of Shu, disliked his capriciousness and worried that he would be a disaster. Meng Da had a conflict with Shen Yi, the prefect of Wei Xing. Zhuge Liang wanted him to raise an army and start an uprising, so he sent Guo Mo to pretend to surrender and go to Shen Yi's aid to reveal Meng Da's plot. Yuda knew that his plan had been leaked, so he prepared to raise his troops to cause chaos. Emperor Xuan was afraid that Mengda was about to send troops, so he wrote to him: "General, I have abandoned Liu Bei in the past and relied on the country. The country has entrusted you with the important task of guarding the border and entrusting you with the important task of conquering the Kingdom of Shu. It can be said that this heart is as bright and aboveboard as the sun." No matter whether they are stupid or smart, there is no one in Shu who does not hate the general with gnashing of teeth. Zhuge Liang wants to defeat us, but he has no choice.
target: When Shu general Meng Da rebelled, Emperor Xuan suspected his cunning and, despite warnings, marched swiftly, capturing and executing Meng Da in sixteen days. He then dealt with Shen Yi, who had forged edicts, and exiled Meng Da's followers. He advised leniency for surrendered border counties and proposed attacking Wu via Xiakou and Shuguan. He was promoted to general and joined Cao Zhen against Shu, but heavy rain forced a retreat.

source: He sent general Niu Jin to lure the Shu army with light cavalry. As soon as the two armies engaged, Zhuge Kui retreated and pursued him to Kongshan. He condemned Jiangtai and stationed troops at Lu Su, occupying the two mountains in the north and south, and cut off the water sources to create a circle of encirclement. Emperor Xuan attacked and broke through his encirclement. Zhuge Liang escaped at night, pursued and defeated him, captured and killed more than 10,000 people. The emperor sent people to comfort the army and increase the number of fiefs. At that time, military advisor Du Xi and military governor Xue Ti both said that when the wheat was ripe next year, the tomb robbers would definitely attack. There was no food in Luxi and it should be transported in advance in winter. Emperor Xuan said: Zhuge Liang came out of Qishan again, attacked Chenhe, was defeated and returned. Even if he comes again in the future, he will not attack the city. He will definitely hope to fight in the field, and it will definitely be in Longshu, not in the west. Zhuge Liang is often helpless due to lack of food. He will definitely accumulate food after returning. According to my speculation, he will not take action until three years have passed. So Shangzou moved the farmers from Jizhou to Shangbang and strengthened the supervision and management of Jingzhao, Tianshui and Nan'an. In the first year of the year, the Chengguo Canal was dug, a submerged pressure was built, thousands of hectares of land were irrigated, and the national treasury was enriched. In the second year, Zhuge Liang led more than 100,000 troops out of Xiegu and stationed troops in the plain south of the Wei River in Yongdi. The emperor was very worried and sent Qin Lang, the guard of Shu, to lead 20,000 infantry and cavalry to accept the command of Emperor Xuan. The generals wanted to fight in Weibei, but Emperor Xuan said: "The people are gathering in Mengnan. This is a battleground." So he led his army across the water and made a camp with his back to the water. Then he said to the generals: If Zhuge Liang is a brave man, he should start from martial arts and march eastward along the mountain. If you go west to Wuzhangyuan, then all armies and horses will be safe. As expected, Zhuge Liang went to the plain and prepared to cross the Wei River north. Emperor Xuan sent General Zhou Dang to lure the Shu army in Yangsu. For several days, Zhuge Liang remained silent. Emperor Xuan said: Zhuge Liang wanted to seize the plains instead of going to Yangsui. We can know his intentions. He sent general Hu Zun and Yongzhou governor Guo Huai to jointly guard Yang Sui, and met Zhuge Liang at Jishi. When the battle began near the plain, Zhuge Liang was unable to advance and returned to Wuzhangyuan. When a comet crashed into Zhuge Liang's camp, Emperor Xuan knew that Zhuge Liang would definitely fail, so he sent a surprise force to contain Zhuge Liang's rear, killing more than 500 people, capturing more than 1,000 alive, and more than 600 surrendered. At that time, the imperial court believed that Zhuge Liang was a distant enemy living in the south of the Yangtze River and was conducive to a quick victory. Emperor Xuan was often ordered to be cautious and wait for his changes. Zhuge Liang challenged Emperor Xuan many times, but Emperor Xuan refused to fight, so Zhuge Liang gave Emperor Yi women's clothes. Emperor Xuan was furious and petitioned for a decisive battle. The emperor disagreed and sent an upright minister, Wei Wei Xinpi, holding a talisman as a military advisor to stop Emperor Xuan.
target: When Zhuge Liang invaded, Emperor Xuan was sent west to command forces. He marched to Yumi, forcing Zhuge Liang to flee. He defeated Shu forces at Kongshan, capturing thousands. He predicted Zhuge Liang would not attack for three years due to food shortages, so he moved farmers and dug canals to enrich the state. In the second year, Zhuge Liang led 100,000 troops to Wuzhangyuan. Emperor Xuan avoided battle, despite Zhuge Liang sending women's clothes to provoke him. He petitioned for a decisive battle but was stopped by Xinpi. Zhuge Liang died, and Emperor Xuan pursued, confirming his death. He later learned Zhuge Liang ate little and handled all affairs, predicting his early death. He defeated Shu general Ma Dai and accepted surrenders from Di kings.

source: Emperor Xuan wanted to take advantage of the opportunity to march, but the edict did not allow it. In the third year, Emperor Xuan was promoted to Taiwei and increased the number of fiefs. The Shu general Ma Dai invaded, and Emperor Xuan sent his general Sheng Jin to repel them and killed more than a thousand people. Fu Shuang and Qiang Duan, the Di kings of Wudu, led more than 6,000 men to surrender. During the famine in Hedong, Emperor Xuan transported five million grains of dendrobium from Chang'an to the capital. In the fourth year, Emperor Xuan obtained a white deer and dedicated it to the emperor. The emperor said: In the past, Qi Gongdan assisted Liting and offered white pheasants. Now you are managing Shaanxi and you are offering a white deer. Isn’t this a combination of loyalty, harmony, and unity for thousands of years to govern the country and make it auspicious for thousands of years? When Gongsun Wenyi, the governor of Liaodong, rebelled, he summoned Emperor Xuan to the capital. The Emperor said: Originally it was not worth bothering you, but this matter must be won, so I have to bother you. What do you think he has planned? He replied: It is the best policy to abandon the city and leave in advance. Occupy the distant water and resist the army, this is the middle strategy. If you sit on the ground to guard Secuo, you will definitely be captured. The emperor asked: What good plan will there be? The answer is: A person who is discerning can think deeply about the enemy and ourselves and give up beforehand. It is not what he can do. Now that he is going deep into the country alone, his expedition will definitely not last long. He will definitely occupy the Liao River and hold on to it. This is the middle or lower strategy. The Emperor said: How long does it take to go back and forth? He replied: One hundred days to go, one hundred days to return, one hundred days to attack, and sixty days to rest. One year is enough. At that time, palaces were being built on a large scale, and the army was fighting, and the people were starving and dying. Emperor Xuan was preparing to use troops, so he advised him: "In the past, Zhou Gong built Luoyi, and Xiao He built Weiyang Palace. Now the palace is not complete. This is my responsibility." However, from the north of the Yellow River, the people are poor and distressed, and they are working hard both inside and outside. The forces cannot be developed at the same time, and construction should be temporarily stopped to relieve temporary emergencies.
target: When Gongsun Wenyi rebelled in Liaodong, Emperor Xuan predicted he would hold the Liao River and estimated a year for the campaign. He advised halting palace construction to relieve the people.

source: However, from the north of the Yellow River, the people are poor and distressed, and they are working hard both inside and outside. target: He refused further honors. He died at seventy-three, buried simply as per his wishes. Posthumously honored as Emperor Xuan of Jin, his temple name was Gaozu. He was described as jealous but generous, suspicious and manipulative. Cao Cao warned about his ambition, but Cao Pi protected him. He massacred after victories and usurped Wei power. His cruelty was noted, and Emperor Ming of Jin lamented the dynasty's foundation. His strategies were praised but his loyalty questioned, as he betrayed trust and killed rivals, leading to later ridicule.

target: Yu Liang and others fought Su Jun at Cihu, suffering defeat. The following year, Su Jun crossed the Hengjiang River, attacked the capital, and burned Qingxizha. Many officials were killed, and Yu Liang fled to Xunyang. Su Jun forced the emperor to move to Stone City, causing great suffering. Empress Dowager Yu died during this turmoil.

source: On the 25th, Tao Kan asked the governor Yang Qian to attack Su Jun who was defending Stone City. Wen Qiao and Yu Liang formed a formation at Baishi, and Li Yang, the prefect of Jingling, resisted the bandits' southward division. Su Jun led his light cavalry into battle, fell off his horse and was beheaded, causing his troops to disperse. The bandits appointed Su Jun's younger brother Su Yi as their leader. Zhang Lian, the former governor of Jiaozhou, occupied Shixing and rebelled, attacking Guangzhou. Zhennan Sima Zeng Xie and others defeated him. In October, Li Xiong's general Zhang Long invaded Fuling, and the prefect Zhao Bi was killed by the thieves. On December 21, Shi Le defeated Liu Yao in Luoyang and captured him alive. This year, Shi Le's general Shi Jilong attacked the Di leader Pu Hong in Longshan, and Pu Hong surrendered. In the first month of the fourth year of Xianhe's reign, the emperor was in Shitucheng. The bandit general Kuangshu surrendered to Xianyuan City, and all the officials rushed there. Attendant Zhong Ya and right guard general Liu Chao planned to leave the city for the emperor, but were killed by thieves. On the 25th, the champion general Zhao Yin sent Gan Miao to Liyang to conquer Zu Yue and defeated Zu Yue. Zu Yue defected to Shi Le, and his general Tian Teng surrendered with his troops. There was a great famine in the city, and a bushel of rice was worth ten thousand yuan. In February, it rained heavily. On the 13th, various armies attacked Shitou. Li Yang and Su Yi fought at Muqiepu, and Li Yang was defeated. Shi Tenghan, the commander of Jianwei, led his elite troops to attack, and Su Yi and others were defeated. Teng Han escorted the emperor to Wen Qiao's ship. The officials kowtowed and cried bitterly to apologize. Sima, the king of Yiyang, was guilty and was executed. On the 14th, a general amnesty was given to the whole world. After the war, the palace was reduced to ashes, so Jianpingyuan was used as the palace.
target: The rebellion was eventually suppressed. Various armies attacked Shitou, and Su Jun was beheaded after falling from his horse. His brother Su Yi became the new rebel leader but was later captured. The palace was reduced to ashes, and Jianpingyuan was used as the imperial residence. Liu Yao was captured alive by Shi Le. The empire continued facing challenges including Shi Jilong's attacks, Li Xiong's invasions, and natural disasters like floods and comets.

Although Emperor Cheng's majestic and mighty weapons were not as good as those of previous emperors, his virtues of respect and frugality were enough to track the heroes of previous generations. Emperor Kang, whose name was Sima Yue and whose courtesy name was Shitong, was the younger brother of Emperor Cheng. In the first year of Xianhe, he was granted the title of King of Wu, and in the second year of his reign, he was posthumously named King of Langxie; Jiuwei was appointed as a regular servant of Sanqi, plus a general of Hussar; in the fifth year of Xiankang, he was promoted to Shizhong and Situ. In the Jiawu period, Emperor Kang ascended the throne and ruled the world. Fangwu generals and local county governors stationed in various places are not allowed to leave their posts without authorization and come to attend the funeral. At the end of the year, Sima Pi, the son of Emperor Cheng, was named the King of Langxie, and Ma Mayi was named the King of the East China Sea. target: He showed concern for frugality, once stopping construction of a shooting hall due to cost. Emperor Kang, named Sima Yue (courtesy name Shitong), was Emperor Cheng's younger brother. He was initially made King of Wu, then King of Langxie, and served as Situ before being named successor. He ascended the throne after Emperor Cheng's death, entrusting Yu Bing and He Chong with government affairs. His reign saw continued conflicts with Shi Jilong and Li Shou, as well as military campaigns by various generals. Emperor Kang died at age twenty-three and was buried in Chongping Mausoleum.

source: Emperor Wu's name was Yan and his courtesy name was Anshi. He was the eldest son of Emperor Wen of Jin Dynasty. He is tolerant and kind, deep and magnanimous. During the Jiaping period of Wei Dynasty, he was granted the title of Tinghou of Beiping, and successively served as the commander of the army, the commander of the army, the general of the base, the general of the cavalry, the general of the cavalry, and the title of the protector of the army and the holiday. He went to Wuyang in the east to welcome Changdao Xianggong to the throne, moved to Zhongfujun, and was granted the title of Xinchang Xianghou in Jin Dynasty. When the Jin State was established, he was established as the heir apparent and granted the title of General of Fujun, Kaifu, and Deputy Second Prime Minister. At the beginning, because Emperor Jing was the heir of Emperor Xuan and died early without any heirs, Emperor Wen regarded Emperor Wu's younger brother Sima You as a heir of Emperor Jing. He took special care of him, thinking that he would be the prime minister and should pass on his great legacy to Sima You after his death. Chang said: This is King Jing's world, and I will not get involved. When it was time to decide on the crown prince, Emperor Wen wanted to appoint Sima You. He Zeng and others persisted in their dissent and said: The Zhongfu Army is smart and martial, with extraordinary talents. The hair is on the floor and the arms are above the knees. This is not the appearance of a minister! It’s been settled ever since. In May of the second year of Emperor Xianxi of Wei Yuan Dynasty, he was established as the crown prince of Jin Dynasty. Orders were given to relax punishments, pardon sinners, appease the people, reduce corvee service, and observe three days of mourning in the country.
target: Emperor Wu, named Sima Yan with the courtesy name Anshi, was the eldest son of Emperor Wen of Jin. He was known for his tolerance, kindness, and magnanimity. During the Jiaping period of Wei, he was granted the title of Tinghou of Beiping and held various military positions. He welcomed Changdao Xianggong to the throne in Wuyang, became Zhongfujun, and was granted the title of Xinchang Xianghou in Jin. When the Jin state was established, he was made heir apparent and given the title of General of Fujun. Emperor Wen initially intended to pass the legacy to Sima You, but after opposition from He Zeng and others, Sima Yan was established as crown prince in May of the second year of Xianxi. Upon Emperor Wen's death in August, he inherited the titles of Prime Minister and King of Jin, implementing policies to relax punishments, pardon sinners, and reduce corvée.

target: He issued an edict of general amnesty, changed the reign name, and granted various titles and rewards. He honored his ancestors with posthumous titles and established many kings and dukes. Throughout his reign, he conducted inspections, established institutions, and responded to natural disasters with relief efforts.

target: In his later years, Emperor Wu became neglectful of political affairs, indulging in banquets and favoring the queen's family, leading to the rise of relatives and nobles in power. He failed to depose the incapable crown prince, leading to chaos after his death. Despite his initial successes, his reign ended with turmoil, as the Western Jin dynasty eventually collapsed due to his lack of foresight and poor decisions. Historians note that while he had a good beginning, his later years were marked by decline and disaster.

source: Emperor Jianwen's name was Yu, with the courtesy name Daowan, and he was the youngest son of Emperor Yuan. He was very smart when he was young and was loved by Emperor Yuan. target: Emperor Jianwen, named Sima Yu with the courtesy name Daowan, was the youngest son of Emperor Yuan. He was exceptionally intelligent as a child and beloved by his father. The diviner Guo Pu predicted he would revitalize the Jin Dynasty. Sima Yu grew to be pure-hearted with few desires, particularly skilled in discussing metaphysical matters. He was granted the title of King of Langxie in the first year of Yongchang, and later became King of Kuaiji.

source: Emperor Jian Wen was only seven years old at the time. He cried blood when he cried to offer sacrifices to his biological mother, and insisted on wearing mourning clothes. source: In eight years, he was promoted to Situ, but Sima Yu firmly refused. At this time, some officials adhered to Huan Wen's will and petitioned to kill Sima Xi, the king of Wuling, but the emperor refused. Huan Wen insisted again and again, and the emperor personally issued an edict in reply: If the Jin Dynasty lasts for a long time, Ming Gong should implement the previous edict. If the great fortune of the Jin Dynasty is over, then please let me make way for the sages. Huan Wen looked at it and was so frightened that he broke into a cold sweat, his face changed, and he stopped talking.
target: After the deposed emperor was removed, the Empress Dowager issued an edict declaring Sima Yu the rightful heir to the throne. In the eleventh month of the first year of Xian'an, he ascended as emperor. Huan Wen, who had previously deposed the former emperor, maintained significant power. When Huan Wen insisted on executing Sima Xi, the King of Wuling, Emperor Jianwen personally issued an edict refusing, stating that if the Jin Dynasty was destined to continue, Huan Wen should follow his previous edict, but if the dynasty's fortune was exhausted, he would make way for worthier men. Huan Wen was so frightened by this response that he broke into a cold sweat and abandoned the matter. Emperor Jianwen was known for his graceful demeanor and disregard for material circumstances. He could remain calm even when Huan Wen deliberately created chaotic situations to test him.
