target: Emperor Xiaowu, named Sima Yao with the courtesy name Changming, was Emperor Jianwen's third son. He was initially made King of Kuaiji, then Crown Prince, and ascended the throne upon his father's death. His reign saw significant events including the death of Huan Wen, after which the Empress Dowager briefly returned to court. The famous Battle of Fei River occurred during his reign, where Jin forces defeated Fu Jian's massive army, capturing tens of thousands of enemy soldiers.

source: On the first day of March, there is a solar eclipse. In June, there were floods in Jingzhou and Xuzhou. In November, King Tuoba Wang Gui of Wei attacked Murong Chui's son Murong Bao in Shui Valley and defeated him. In the first month of the 21st year of Taiyuan, the Qingshu Palace was built. In March, Murong Chui captured Pingcheng. In April, the new Yong'an Palace was built. On the 14th, there was hail. Murong was dying, and his son Murong Bao succeeded him to the throne. On May 15th, Wang Cai Gong Xie Yan was appointed as Shangshu Zuopushe. Flood. In June, Lu Guang usurped the throne and became the emperor. On September 20, the emperor died in Qingshu Palace at the age of thirty-five. Buried in Longping Mausoleum. Emperor Xiaowu was known for his intelligence and enlightenment when he was young. When Emperor Jian Wen died, he was only ten years old. He did not attend the funeral in the evening, but came to give advice. He replied: "Weep when you are sad. What is the rule?" Xie An once lamented that Emperor Xiaowu was as good at affairs as the previous emperor. After the authority was established, some people were magnanimous and soon indulged in wine and sex, drinking almost all night long. When the comet appeared at the end of the year, the emperor was very disgusted in his heart. He raised a glass of wine in Hualin Garden and prayed: Comet, I advise you to drink a glass of wine. Since ancient times, where has the emperor lived for ten thousand years? The Taibai Star appears in the daytime year after year, and earthquakes, floods and droughts occur one after another. Days of sobriety are rare. And since there are no upright people around him, he cannot change in the end. At that time, Zhang Guiren was favored and she was nearly thirty years old. The emperor teased her and said: "You should be abandoned according to your age." Zhang Guiren was secretly angry. At night, the emperor got drunk and died suddenly.
target: Emperor Xiaowu was known for his intelligence and enlightenment in youth. After establishing his authority, however, he became indulgent in wine and sensual pleasures, often drinking through entire nights. He showed little concern for celestial omens, once toasting a comet and declaring that no emperor had ever lived ten thousand years. His reign was marked by natural disasters including earthquakes, floods, and droughts. He died suddenly at age thirty-five after drunkenly teasing his favored consort Zhang Guiren about her age, which led to her killing him in anger. He was buried in Longping Mausoleum.

source: Zhang Guiren was secretly angry. At night, the emperor got drunk and died suddenly. At that time, Sima Daozi was fatuous and confused, and Sima Yuan showed his power and did not even pursue the criminals. At the beginning, Emperor Jian Wen saw the text predicting good and bad luck and said: The national destiny of the Jin Dynasty failed in the hands of Changming. When Emperor Xiaowu was still a fetus, Empress Dowager Li dreamed that the man of God said to her: If you give birth to a boy, the character will be "Changming". When he was born, it was bright in the east, so he took the word "Changming" as his character. Emperor Jian Wen later understood and burst into tears. When the Qingshu Palace was built, knowledgeable people believed that the sound of "Qingshu" was the sound of "Chu", which meant a sign of sadness and sadness. Soon after the emperor died, the fortune of the Jin Dynasty collapsed. Shi Chen said: The historical books in the past said: "How can a king rise without being deposed? If he is as outstanding as a god, he will inherit the throne with glory, cross the thick clouds with high head, and cross the river with leaps." Shaokang only had one brigade of troops, so he won the throne of the Xia king; Chengtang only had seventy lands, but he revitalized the emperor's great cause; he was able to manage the rivers and seas after they broke out, and he was able to remedy the chaos in the sky; things are different from this, so the reasons are also different. Emperor Jian Wen was in a difficult time because of his innocuous nature. Government orders were issued by the Huan family, and people of his own clan had no power. After Taizong's death, Ningkang inherited the great cause. God was moved by his loyalty, and the treacherous officials perished on their own. So in the west, we surpassed Jianxiu and crossed Lingshan Mountain, and in the north, we crossed the Yellow River and reached the clear Luoshui River. The warriors of Jing and Wu became powerful, famous virtuous ministers appeared one after another, and the virtuous elders were still there. Xie An can lead elegant and popular people, Wang Biaozhi can regulate discipline, Huan Chong works hard all day long, and Xie Xuan is good at military affairs.
target: The historical commentary notes that Emperor Jianwen governed during difficult times with Huan family controlling government orders. After Emperor Xiaowu's ascension, treacherous officials perished naturally, and capable ministers like Xie An, Wang Biaozhi, Huan Chong, and Xie Xuan emerged. However, the decline of the Jin Dynasty was ultimately attributed to human failings rather than divine will.

source: Emperor Jing's famous teacher, named Ziyuan, was the eldest son of Emperor Xuan. Elegant and charming, calm and perseverant, with far-reaching strategies. When he was young, he had a good reputation and was as famous as Xia Houxuan and He Yan. He Yan often said: Sima Ziyuan is the one who can achieve great things in the world. During the early years of Wei Jingchu, he served as a regular servant of Sanqi and was promoted to the rank of Central Protector for many times. Formulate methods for selecting talents, promote people without exceeding their merits, and officials have no selfish feelings. When Queen Xuanmu passed away, Emperor Jing was famous for his extreme filial piety in mourning. When Emperor Xuan was about to kill Cao Shuang, he planned carefully and secretly with Emperor Jing alone. Emperor Wen didn't know what was going on and only told him the night before he was about to take action. Afterwards, someone was sent to spy on him. Emperor Jing fell asleep as usual, but Emperor Wen could not sleep peacefully. In the early morning, the troops gathered at Simamen. Emperor Jing was calm both inside and outside, and the arrangements were very strict. Emperor Xuan said: This son is really good after all. At the beginning, Emperor Jing secretly took in three thousand scholars who were not afraid of death and scattered them among the people. When they arrived, they gathered them together in one morning. No one knew where these people came from. After the incident subsided, because of his meritorious service, he was granted the title of Marquis of Changping Township, with a population of 1,000 households, and was later granted the title of General of Wei. When Emperor Xuan died, people who discussed politics said: Yi Yin is dead, and Yi Zhi will inherit the business. The emperor appointed Emperor Jing as the general of the Fu army to assist in government affairs. In the spring and first month of the fourth year of Wei Jiaping's reign, he was promoted to general and granted the title of Shizhong. He held the title of Commander-in-Chief, commanded all the Chinese and foreign armies, and recorded affairs of the Shangshu. Order the officials to recommend talents, clarify the hierarchy between the young and the elderly, sympathize with the poor and lonely, and clean up those who have been abandoned. Zhuge Dan, Mu Qiujian, Wang Chang, Chen Tai, and Hu Zun were appointed governors of the four directions; Wang Ji, Zhou Tai, Deng Ai, and Shi Bao were in charge of the prefectures and counties; Lu Yu and Li Feng were in charge of elections; Fu Gu and Yu Song participated in making plans; Zhong Hui, Xia Houxuan, Wang Su, Chen Ben, Meng Kang, Tan Feng, and Zhang Ji participated in the court meetings. They were admired by all the people and respected inside and outside the court. Occasionally, there were people who asked for changes in the system. Emperor Jing said: "As if you don't know anything, you obey the laws of God and do it. This is what the poet praises." The rules and regulations of three generations of ancestors should be observed; unless there is a war, they cannot be changed at will. In the summer and May of the fifth year, Zhuge Ke, the Taifu of Wu State, besieged Xincheng. The court was worried that he would divide his troops to invade Huaisi and planned to guard various waterway ports. Emperor Jing said: Zhuge Ke had recently gained power in Wu State, and wanted to seek temporary benefits. He gathered his troops in Hefei, hoping that he would succeed by luck and had no energy to cause trouble in Qingxu.
target: Emperor Jing, named Ziyuan, was the eldest son of Emperor Xuan. He was elegant, calm, and strategic, renowned from youth alongside Xia Houxuan and He Yan. He Yan once said he would achieve great things. Serving as a regular servant of Sanqi in the early Wei Jingchu period, he was promoted to Central Protector, where he formulated talent selection methods without bias. After Queen Xuanmu's death, he showed extreme filial piety. When Emperor Xuan planned to kill Cao Shuang, he secretly strategized with Emperor Jing alone, keeping Emperor Wen unaware until the night before action. A spy found Emperor Jing sleeping calmly, while Emperor Wen could not rest. At dawn, troops gathered at Simamen, and Emperor Jing's calm arrangements impressed Emperor Xuan, who praised him. He had secretly gathered three thousand fearless scholars, who assembled unnoticed. After the incident, he was made Marquis of Changping Township with 1,000 households and later General of Wei. Upon Emperor Xuan's death, he became General of the Fu army to assist in governance. In the fourth year of Wei Jiaping, he was promoted to general and Shizhong, commanding all armies and recording affairs of the Shangshu. He ordered officials to recommend talents, clarify hierarchies, and aid the poor. He appointed governors like Zhuge Dan and Mu Qiujian, and officials like Wang Ji and Deng Ai, earning admiration. When asked about system changes, he advocated following ancestral laws unless war necessitated change. In the fifth year, Wu's Zhuge Ke besieged Xincheng.

source: The rules and regulations of three generations of ancestors should be observed; unless there is a war, they cannot be changed at will. In the summer and May of the fifth year, Zhuge Ke, the Taifu of Wu State, besieged Xincheng. The court was worried that he would divide his troops to invade Huaisi and planned to guard various waterway ports. Emperor Jing said: Zhuge Ke had recently gained power in Wu State, and wanted to seek temporary benefits. He gathered his troops in Hefei, hoping that he would succeed by luck and had no energy to cause trouble in Qingxu. Besides, there is not one waterway port. If there are more guards, more troops will be needed. If there are fewer guards, it will not be enough to defend against the enemy. Zhuge Ke indeed concentrated his troops in Hefei, just as Emperor Jing had speculated. Emperor Jing sent General Guanqiu Jian, the general of Zhendong, Sai Zhen, the governor of Nuosu, and others to resist the enemy. Dan Qiu Jian and Sai Zhen requested to go out to fight. Emperor Jing said: Zhuge Ke went all out to penetrate our side and put the army in danger. Their sharp edge was difficult to withstand. Besides, the new city is small and strong, making it difficult for enemy troops to attack. So he ordered the generals to build high forts to defend. After several months of stalemate, Zhuge Ke's siege force was exhausted, and more than half of his troops were killed or injured. Emperor Jing ordered Governor Wen Lian to lead his elite troops to Heyu to intercept the enemy's retreat, and Wu Danjun led the generals as his successors. Jiang prisoner fled out of fear. Sai Xun went up to attack and defeated the enemy army, killing more than 10,000 enemies. In the spring and first month of the first year of the fifth year, the emperor and Zhongshu Ling Li Feng, the Queen's father Guanglu doctor Zhang Ji, Huangmen Supervisor Su Shuo, Yongning Department Ling Leqian, red servant Liu Zhili and others planned to use Taichang Xing Lou Sai to replace Emperor Jing to assist the government. Emperor Jing secretly knew about this and sent Wang Xian, his minister, to greet Kuifeng in his car. Kuifeng was forced to follow Wang Dong to see Ji Tong, who listed his sins. Kuifeng knew that disaster was coming, so he insulted him wantonly. Emperor Jing was angry and sent warriors to beat him to death with sword-tipped darts. The arrest of Xia Houxuan, Zhang Ji and others reduced the number of three clans. In March, he politely advised the emperor to depose Queen Zhang. The emperor then issued an edict saying: The treacherous official Li Feng and others are accustomed to listening to slander, using evil and evil, and secretly plotting evil. The general inspector worshiped the laws of heaven and put them under the criminal law. Zhou Bo surrendered to the Lu family, and Huo Guang captured Shangxuan's achievements, which are difficult to surpass. 9,000 additional households were added to the general's food estates, adding to the previous total of 40,000 households. Emperor Jing declined and refused to accept. The emperor felt deeply unsafe because Xia Houxuan and Zhang Ji were executed. Liangcha was also worried about causing disaster and secretly planned to depose and re-establish the emperor, so he secretly advised the Empress Dowager Wei Yongning in a polite way. In Jiaxu, the ninth month of autumn, the Empress Dowager issued an order: The emperor was too old to manage the complicated government affairs himself. He indulged in favors from the inner palace, indulged in lewdness, approached actors and actresses every day, indulged their ugly behavior, welcomed the concubine's family to stay in the inner palace, destroyed the morality between people, and disturbed the moral integrity of men and women. He was coerced by a group of villains and was about to endanger the country, so he could not continue to worship the ancestral temple. Emperor Jing convened a gathering of ministers for discussion, and said with tears: "The Queen Mother's order is this, what should we do with the royal family?" The ministers all said: Yi Yin exiled Taijia to bring peace to Yin, Huo Guang deposed the king of Changyi to bring peace to Mo, weighed the priorities, stabilized the country, and brought peace to the world.
target: Emperor Jing predicted he would concentrate forces in Hefei, not trouble Qingxu, and advised against excessive guards. He sent General Guanqiu Jian and others to resist, ordering high forts for defense. After months, Zhuge Ke's forces were exhausted, and Emperor Jing's counterattack killed over 10,000 enemies. In the first year of the fifth year, Li Feng, Zhang Ji, and others plotted to replace Emperor Jing. He secretly knew, forced Li Feng to confess, and had him beaten to death. Xia Houxuan and Zhang Ji were arrested, and their three clans were reduced. He advised deposing Queen Zhang, and the emperor added 9,000 households to his estate, totaling 40,000, but he declined. After Xia Houxuan's execution, the emperor felt unsafe. Emperor Jing, fearing disaster, secretly advised the Empress Dowager to depose the emperor. In autumn, the Empress Dowager issued an order citing the emperor's misconduct. Emperor Jing convened ministers, who supported deposition. He deposed the emperor as King of Qi, killing his associates. He proposed King Pengcheng as successor, but the Empress Dowager chose Cao Mao, Duke of Gaogui Township. Emperor Jing reluctantly agreed, but worried when the new emperor showed laziness. He advised the emperor on proper conduct. The emperor later issued an edict praising Emperor Jing's virtues and granting him the title of Prime Minister, adding 9,000 households, totaling 40,000, with honors like wearing swords in court. Emperor Jing resigned from the prime ministership and advised the emperor to study and be simple. The emperor accepted.

source: Zhongni said: I am not a person who knows things from birth, but a person who loves ancient things and diligently explores them. All the monarchs of the five generations since Huang Xuan have followed these principles. Zhuan Xu received education from Lu Yuan, and Gao Xin asked Bai Zhao. When King Cheng of Zhou came, he was assisted by Zhou Gongdan and Lu Wang, so he could distinguish the main themes of the chapters and sentences in the scriptures, and he was content with the right path and was happy with his career. Like this, then the way of the king is revealed above, and the common people obey below. The prosperous age when criminal law was put aside actually came from this. We should follow the spirit of the ancestors who were not ashamed to ask questions, so that lectures and poems can be heard frequently, and the words of the classics can be stated around them every day. At that time, the emperor loved luxury and extravagance, and Emperor Jing advised him: "When you first get involved in government affairs, you should advocate simplicity." The emperor respectfully accepted it. In November, white clouds fill the sky. In the first month of the spring of the second year, a comet appeared in the dividing line between Wu and Chu and disappeared in the northwest sky. Qiu Jian, the mother of the general Zhendong, and Wen Qin, the governor of Yangzhou, rebelled. Under the pretense of the Queen Mother's order, they sent a message to the county, set up an altar outside the west gate to swear an oath, and each sent four sons to serve as hostages in the state of Wu to ask for help. In February, Mu Qiujian and Wenqin led 60,000 troops to cross the Huaihe River and march westward. Emperor Jing gathered his ministers to plan the conquest. Most of the discussions in the court believed that generals could be dispatched to send troops. Wang Su, Shangshu Fu Gu, and Zhongshu Shilang Zhong Hui persuaded Emperor Jing to go out in person. In Wuwu, Emperor Jing led more than 100,000 Chinese infantry and cavalry to conquer. Traveling day and night, he summoned armies from all three parties and gathered in the countryside of Chen Xu in large numbers. Jiashen was stationed at Chuqiao, and his mother Qiujian's generals Shi Zhao and Li Xu surrendered one after another. Guanqiu Jian and Wen Qin moved their troops to Xiangcheng, and Emperor Jing sent Wang Ji, the governor of Jingzhou, to march and occupy Nandun to force Guanqiu Jian. Emperor Jing built high barriers and waited for Shumian's army to gather. The generals asked to march to attack Xiangcheng. Emperor Jing said: You only know one, but not the other. The soldiers south of the Huaihe River had no intention of rebellion. Moreover, Ceqiu Jian and Wen Qin wanted to follow the path of the political advisors and learn from the theories of Zhang Yi and Su Qin, thinking that the distant and near would definitely respond. However, when the rebellion was launched, the people north of the Huaihe River did not comply, and Shi Zhao and Li Xu collapsed one after another. Internally disobedient, externally betrayed, knowing that they must fail, the trapped beasts want a duel, and a quick fight is more to their liking. Although the enemy will definitely be defeated, it will also hurt many people. Besides, Mu Qiujian and others deceived the soldiers and were very cunning and fickle. If we stay with them for a while, the deception will naturally be exposed, and we can win without a fight. So Governor Zhuge Dan was sent to lead the Yuzhou armies to march from Anfeng to Shouchun. General Hu Zundu, the General of the East Conquest, led the Qing and Xu armies to send troops between Qiao and Song Dynasties to cut off the rebels' retreat.
target: In the second year, Mu Qiujian and Wen Qin rebelled, crossing the Huaihe River with 60,000 troops. Emperor Jing led over 100,000 troops to conquer, using strategy to avoid direct conflict. He sent generals to cut off retreat, and the rebels were defeated. Wen Qin fled, and Mu Qiujian was killed. Emperor Jing, suffering from an eye tumor, endured pain during the campaign, hiding it from his troops. He died in Xuchang at age 48. His funeral followed Huo Guang's precedent, and he was posthumously named Duke Wu, later Emperor Jing.

source: Order the ministers to discuss the funeral arrangements. Relevant officials discussed that Emperor Jing's loyalty had stabilized the country and his achievements had saved the world, so Huo Guang's precedent should be followed. The title of Grand Sima was added in front of the General, and fifty thousand households were added to the city, and Mi was given the title of Duke Wu. Emperor Wen expressed his resignation and said: My late father did not dare to accept the courtesy of Prime Minister Xiang Guo Jiu Ming, and my late brother did not dare to accept the high position of Xiang Guo, all because Taizu once served as prime minister. Now that the title of Mi is the same as that of Emperor Wu and Emperor Wen, it must be frightening. In the past, Xiao He, Zhang Liang, and Huo Guang all contributed to saving the situation and assisting the monarch. Xiao He's nickname was Wen Zhong, Zhang Liang's nickname was Wencheng, and Huo Guang's nickname was Xuancheng. If you must use Wenwu as your nickname, please follow the precedents of Xiao He and others when adding gifts. The emperor agreed to the edict and named Mi Zhongwu. After the establishment of Jin State. The additional honorary title is King Jing. Emperor Wu accepted the concession and was honored as Emperor Jing, the mountain mausoleum was called Junping, and the ancestral temple was called Shizong. Emperor Wen, whose name is Zishang, is the half-brother of Emperor Jing. In the second year of Wei Jingchu's reign, he was granted the title of Xincheng Rural Marquis. In the early years of Zhengshi, he was appointed as the lieutenant general of Diannong in Luoyang. It was the late period of Emperor Wei Ming's extravagant style. Emperor Wen exempted him from harsh and cumbersome conditions and did not take up farming time. The people were very happy. He was transferred to serve as a regular attendant of Sanqi.
target: Emperor Wen, named Zishang, was Emperor Jing's half-brother. He served as a lieutenant general in Luoyang, exempting harsh taxes and pleasing the people.

source: He was transferred to serve as a regular attendant of Sanqi. When the general Cao Shuang was conquering Shu, he appointed Emperor Wen as the general to conquer Shu. As Xia Houxuan's deputy, he sent troops to Luo Valley and stationed himself in Xingshi. Shu general Wang Lin attacked Emperor Wen's camp at night, but Emperor Wen lay motionless. Wang Lin retreated, and Emperor Wen said to Xia Houxuan: Fei Zhang occupied a dangerous position to resist and hold on. We can't fight if we advance, and we can't attack by force. We should return to the army as soon as possible and think about it later. Cao Shuang and others led their troops to retreat, and as expected, Fei Zhang led his troops to pursue them straight to the Three Ridges. After a battle and many obstacles, the Wei army was able to pass. So he returned to the court and paid homage to Yilang. When Cao Shuang was executed, he led the people to defend the second palace. Due to his meritorious service, he gained an additional 1,000 households. When Shu general Jiang Wei invaded Longxi, General Guo Huai sent troops from Chang'an to defend against the enemy. Emperor Wen was promoted to the general of Anxi and held a festival, and he stationed troops in Guanzhong to control the military affairs. Guo Huai attacked Jiang Wei's deputy general Ju'an in Qudi, and the outcome was indecisive for a long time. Emperor Wen then marched to occupy the Great Wall and ran south to Luo Valley to confuse the enemy. Jiang Wei was frightened and withdrew his troops to defend Nan Yin. Jushi's army cut off support and led everyone to surrender. Emperor Wen was transferred to General Anshu and Chijie to guard Xuchang. When the army attacked Wang Jun, Emperor Wen supervised the affairs of the armies in Huaibei and led the army to join forces in Xiangdi. Three hundred households were added to the city, and they were temporarily granted gold seals and purple ribbons. Soon he was promoted to governor, and he led Hu Zun, the general who conquered the east, and Zhuge Dan, the general who Zhendong, to attack the state of Wu and fought at Shuguan. The two armies fought and were defeated, and they were convicted and lost the marquis. Jiang Wei, the general of Shu, invaded Longxi again and threatened to attack Didao.
target: During Cao Shuang's campaign against Shu, he advised retreat, which proved correct. After Cao Shuang's execution, he gained 1,000 households. He defended against Shu's Jiang Wei, using strategy to force his retreat. He later led campaigns against Wu, but was defeated and lost his marquis title. He again faced Jiang Wei, predicting his tactics and defeating him. He suppressed a rebellion in Xinping, regaining his title.

source: Emperor Wen was sent to temporarily serve as General of the Expedition to the West and stationed in Chang'an. Chen Tai, the governor of Yongzhou, planned to occupy Didao before the enemy came. Emperor Wen said: Jiang Wei attacked the Qiang, took their hostages, gathered grain and grass to build a munitions depot, and then diverted the march to Zaojie. It was precisely because he wanted to settle the affairs of the Qiang tribe outside the wall and use it as future capital. If we really want to attack Didao. How can you publicize the exposure and let outsiders know? Now that he is threatening to send troops, he is planning to take action. As expected, Jiang Wei burned the military camp and retreated. Just when the Qiang and Hu tribes in Xinping rebelled, Emperor Wen defeated them and showed off his troops in Lingzhou. The enemies in the north were shocked and frightened, and the rebels surrendered. Because of his meritorious service, he was again granted the title of Xincheng Rural Marquis. When Gaogui Township was established as the king, because Saitong participated in the formulation of the strategy, he was granted the title of Gaodu Marquis and was granted the title of two additional households in the city. When Tan Qiujian and Wen Qin rebelled, the army marched eastward. Emperor Wen served as the leader of the army and stayed behind to guard Luoyang. When Emperor Jing became seriously ill, Emperor Wen went to visit him from Kyoto and was appointed General of the Guard. After Emperor Jing died, the emperor ordered Emperor Wen to guard Xuchang, and Shangshu Su led the Sixth Army back to the capital. Saitong adopted the strategy of attacking the bell box and led his army back. When he arrived in Luoyang, he was promoted to the rank of general, and was added to the rank of attendant. He was in charge of all the Chinese and foreign armies, recorded the affairs of the ministers, assisted in the affairs of the court, and went to the palace wearing swords and shoes. Emperor Wen resolutely refused to accept it. In the first month of spring of the first year of Ju Ling's reign, he was granted the title of Grand Governor, and there was no need to give his name when performing duties. In the sixth month of summer, he was granted the title of Duke of Gaodu, with a circumference of seven hundred miles, plus nine tins, an ax and cymbals, and the title of Grand Governor. He wore a sword and wore shoes to go to the palace. And he firmly refused to accept it. In autumn and August, Geng Shen added fake yellow iron and enfeoffed three more counties. At the end of the fifth month in the summer of the second year, Zhuge Dan, the general of Zhendong, killed Luan Ji, the governor of Yangzhou, and caused trouble in the south. He sent his son Zhuge Liang to Wu as a hostage to ask for reinforcements. The deliberation people requested that he be defeated quickly. Sai Tong said: Because Jiang Xi saw Dan Dan Jian's weak army and was quickly destroyed, he must have colluded with Wu State, which made him increase his troops and move slowly.
target: When Gaogui Township became king, he was made Gaodu Marquis. During Mu Qiujian's rebellion, he stayed in Luoyang. After Emperor Jing's death, he became General of the Guard, then general and Shizhong, commanding all armies. He refused high honors but was eventually made Duke of Gaodu with nine tins. In the second year, Zhuge Dan rebelled, seeking Wu aid. Emperor Wen led 500,000 troops, using strategy to besiege Shouchun. He defeated Wu reinforcements, and after a long siege, Zhuge Dan was killed. He was made Duke of Jin with nine tins, but resigned nine times.

source: Return to the army and gather your troops to command the world. There will be no one who is disobedient in the distance and no one who is not in order nearby. Let the virtues of the Wei Dynasty shine in the Jin Dynasty; the Ming Gong's greatest achievements surpass those of Qi Huan and Jin Wen. Facing the sea to express gratitude to Wen Bo, and climbing Jishan Mountain to salute Xu You, isn't it a grand event? It's very fair. Who can compare with me, so why should I be humble? Only then did Emperor Wen accept the emperor's gift. In November, Deng Ai led more than 10,000 people from Yinping to Jiangyou, where he defeated Shu general Zhuge Zhan in Mianzhu, killed Zhuge Zhan, and had his head revealed to the public. Marching into Luoxian County, Liu Chan surrendered. The emperor ordered the Duke of Jin to take charge of everything as the prime minister, so Emperor Wen sent a decree to remove himself from the titles of Shizhong, Grand Governor, and Lu Shangshu. Please appoint Deng Ai as Taiwei and Zhong Hui as Situ. Zhong Hui conspired to rebel, so he secretly sent people to speak ill of Deng Ai. In the first month of spring of the first year of Xianxi, a chariot was sent to arrest Deng Ai. In Yichou, Emperor Wen and the Emperor marched westward and were stationed in Chang'an. At that time, all the princes were in Yecheng. They ordered Zhonglang to be the military officer of Shantao March and guard in Ye. He sent the guard Jia Chongzhijie to supervise the troops and guard Hanzhong. Zhong Hui then rebelled in Shu. The supervisor Wei Gan and the right general Hu Lie attacked Zhong Hui and killed him. At the beginning, when Zhong Hui was attacking Shu, Shao Ti, a subordinate of Xicao, told Emperor Wen: Zhong Hui is difficult to trust and cannot be ordered to send troops. Emperor Wen smiled and said: "We are in control of conquering Shu, but everyone says no, only Zhong Hui agrees with me." After the reduction of Shu, the soldiers in the Central Plains missed their homeland. The people left behind in Shu were still shocked and fearful. Even if they had the intention to rebel, they were powerless. The result was just as Emperor Wen had predicted. In Bingchen, Emperor Wen returned from Chang'an. On Jimao in the third month, Emperor Wen was promoted to the title of king, and the fiefdoms were added together with the previous twenty counties. At the end of the fifth month of summer, the emperor ascended to the throne of Wuyang Xuanwenhou as King Xuan of Jin, and Wuyang Zhongwuhou became King of Jinjing.
target: He later planned to attack Shu, building warships and training troops. In the fourth year, he attacked Shu, sending Deng Ai and Zhong Hui. Deng Ai defeated Shu, and Liu Chan surrendered. Zhong Hui rebelled but was killed. Emperor Wen was made King of Jin, with twenty counties.

source: On Bingwu, the emperor appointed Sima Yan, the Marquis of Xinchang Township, Fujun, as the crown prince of the Jin Dynasty. On the first day of the second spring of the second year, Quji County presented a spirit turtle to the Prime Minister's Mansion. In the fourth month of summer, Sun Hao sent Ji Zhi to hire him and give him local specialties. In May, the emperor ordered Emperor Wen's crown to be decorated with twelve stars, established the emperor's banner, and established the etiquette of the police when entering and exiting. He rode a gold-rooted chariot, drove six horses, spared five o'clock auxiliary chariots, set up Yunhan for machetes, eight hundred for music and dance, and four columns for orchestra chimes. His status was higher than that of King Yan. The princess is regarded as the queen, the prince is regarded as the prince, and the titles of the prince, queen, and grandson are all the same as the emperor's etiquette. Emperor Wen of the People's Republic of China petitioned Emperor Wen to request exemption from the cumbersome and detailed rules of the imperial palace and the regulations that were inconvenient to implement. The Jin State established the official positions of Yushi Dafu, Shi Zhong, Chang Shi, Shangshu, Zhong Lingjun, and General Wei. In the eighth month of autumn and Xinmao, Emperor Wen died in the main hall at the age of fifty-five. In September Guiyou, he was buried in Chongyang Mausoleum and was named King Wen. Emperor Wu accepted the abdication and added the title of Emperor Wen, and the temple was called Taizu.
target: He established five-class titles and sent envoys to Wu. He died at age 55, posthumously named King Wen, later Emperor Wen.

source: Dan Qiu Jian and Sai Zhen requested to go out to fight. Emperor Jing said: Zhuge Ke went all out to penetrate our side and put the army in danger. Their sharp edge was difficult to withstand. Besides, the new city is small and strong, making it difficult for enemy troops to attack. So he ordered the generals to build high forts to defend. After several months of stalemate, Zhuge Ke's siege force was exhausted, and more than half of his troops were killed or injured.
target: His achievements included pacifying rebellions, conquering Shu, and stabilizing the realm, though he was criticized for regicide.

source: Emperor Mu's name was Sima Dan, whose courtesy name was Pengzi. He was the son of Emperor Kang. In September of the second year of Jianyuan, Bingshen was established as the crown prince. On Wuxu Day, Emperor Kangdi passed away. On the day of Jihai, the prince became emperor and was only two years old at the time. He granted amnesty to the whole world and honored the queen as the empress dowager. On Renyin day, the Empress Dowager came to serve as regent.
target: Emperor Mu, named Sima Dan, became emperor at age two after his father Emperor Kang's death. His mother, the Empress Dowager, served as regent.

source: Shi Jilong then sent his generals Shi Ning, Ma Qiu and others to attack Liangzhou and stationed in Quliu. Zhang Chonghua sent General Niu Xuan to resist them and retreated to Fanhan. In the Xinyou month of June, a general amnesty will be granted to the whole world. In the seventh month of autumn, Fan Wen captured Rinan again and killed the guard Liu Xiong. Wei Wen established Fan Bi as emperor. On Wuwu in August, Zhang Chonghua's general Xie Ai attacked Ma Qiu and defeated them. September, earthquake. In the tenth month of winter, Yichou, Zhang Chonghua, the governor of Liangzhou, was temporarily appointed as the commander-in-chief of Longyou Guanzhong, the military commander of Longyou, and the general. In December, Xiao Jingwen, the Zhenwei Guardsman, killed General Yang Qian, who conquered the captives, attacked Fucheng, and captured it. Then he captured Brazil and connected with Hanzhong. In the summer and April of the fourth year, Fan Wen violated Jiude and killed many people. In May, there was a flood. In autumn and August, Huan Wen, the general who entered Anxi, was appointed as the General of the Expedition to the West, Kaifu Yitong and the Third Division were granted the title of Linhe County Duke; Xie Shang, the general of Xizhonglang, was appointed as the General of Anxi. In September Bingshen, Murong Huang died, and his son Mu Rongjun succeeded to the pseudo-throne. At the end of October in winter, there was an earthquake. Shi Jilong sent his general Fu Jian to attack Jingling. In December, Huang Tao from Yuzhang, who was proclaimed Emperor Xiaoshen, gathered thousands of people and attacked Linchuan. The prefect Yu Tiao conquered and destroyed them. On the first day of the first lunar month of the fifth year of the Xinsi lunar month, a general amnesty was granted to the whole world. Gengyin day, earthquake. Shi Jilong became emperor in Yecheng. In February, Chu Pei, the general of the Northern Expedition, asked his general Wang Gong to expedition north, and captured Shi Jilong's general and led a heavy support. In April of summer, Yizhou governor Zhou Fu and Longxiang general Zhu Tao attacked Fan Bi and captured him, and Yizhou was pacified. He made Zhou Fu the Duke of the city. He was temporarily appointed as General Murong Jun, Mu of Youping Erzhou, Da Chanyu, and King of Yan.
target: During his reign, there were numerous military campaigns, rebellions, and natural disasters. Key events included Huan Wen's successful attack on Shu, the rebellion of Fan Wen, and the deaths of various generals and officials. The state of Zhao under Shi Jilong and later his sons experienced internal turmoil, while Murong Huang and his son Murong Jun established the state of Yan. There were also conflicts with Fu Jian, who later proclaimed himself emperor of Qin. The text records a series of battles, surrenders, and changes in leadership across various regions, including Liangzhou and Yizhou. Emperor Mu died at age nineteen and was buried in Yongping Mausoleum.

source: In the first month of the spring of the fourth year, Qiu Chigong Yang Jun passed away, and his son Yang Shi inherited the title. On Bingxu day, Murong Jun died, and his son Mu Rongwei succeeded to the throne. In February, Fenghuang appeared in Fengcheng with nine little phoenixes. In the seventh month of autumn, due to frequent wars and corvee labor, the palace meals were reduced. On the first day of Xin Chou in August, there is a solar eclipse, which is a total eclipse. In October in winter, the star Tengu sets in the southwest. In November, Taiwei Huan Wen was granted the title of Duke of Nanjun, his younger brother Huan Chong was granted the title of Duke of Fengcheng County, and his son Huan Ji was granted the title of Duke of Linhe. The phoenix appeared in Fengcheng again, followed by many birds. In the fifth year of spring and the first month of the year, there was a general amnesty, and five dendrobiums of rice were given to each of the widowers, widowers, and lonely people who had no means of living. General Beizhong Lang, Commander-in-Chief Xu Yanqing, the military commanders of the five prefectures of Hebei You, and Xi Tan, the governor of Xu Yan and the second prefecture, passed away. In February, Fan Wang, the general of the town army, was appointed as the commander-in-chief of Xu Yanqing, the military commander of the five states of Hebei You, the general of Anbei, and the governor of Xu Yan's two states. General Pingnan, governor of Guangzhou, and Marquis of Yangxia Tenghan passed away. In April in summer, there are floods. Taiwei Huanwen guarded Wancheng and sent his younger brother Huanhuo to lead troops to attack Xuchang. Fenghuang appeared in Mianbei. In May of Dingsi, Emperor Mu died in Xianyang Hall at the age of nineteen. He was buried in Yongping Mausoleum, with the temple name Xiaozong. Emperor Ai's name was Sima Pi, whose courtesy name was Qianling, and he was the eldest son of Emperor Cheng. In the eighth year of Xiankang's reign, he was granted the title of King Langxie. In the first year of Yonghe's reign, he was appointed as a regular servant of the scattered cavalry. In the twelfth year, he was awarded the title of general of the Chinese army. In the third year of Shengping, he was promoted to the general of hussar cavalry. In May of the fifth year of Shengping, Emperor Mu passed away. The Empress Dowager ordered: Emperor Mu suddenly fell ill and could not be cured, and there was no successor. King Sima Pi of Langxie was an orthodox and virtuous descendant of the Zhongxing royal family.
target: Emperor Ai, named Sima Pi, succeeded Emperor Mu. He was the eldest son of Emperor Cheng. The Empress Dowager declared him the rightful heir due to Emperor Mu's lack of an heir. His reign was marked by continued conflicts with Murong Wei's forces, who captured Luoyang, and the ongoing influence of Huan Wen. Emperor Ai was known for his interest in immortality, consuming elixirs that poisoned him and rendered him unable to govern, leading the Empress Dowager to resume regency. He died at age twenty-five and was buried in Anping Mausoleum.

source: On Renshen day, the imperial court sent someone to summon Huan Wen to become prime minister, but Huan Wen did not agree. On Dingmao in the seventh month of autumn, another imperial edict was issued to recruit Huan Wen to the court. In August, Huan Wen arrived at Zheqi and built a city to live there. Fu Jian's troops invaded Henan, and Murong Wei invaded Luoyang. In September, the champion general Chen You left Chang Shi Shen Jin to guard Luoyang and fled to the new city with his troops. In the spring of the third year of the first lunar month, Queen Wang passed away. At the end of February Yi, he appointed the right general Huan Huo to supervise the military affairs of Yicheng in Yangzhou in Jingzhou and Jingzhao in Yongzhou, and to lead the Nanman school captains and the governor of Jingzhou; Huan Chong was appointed to supervise the military affairs of the six counties of Jiangxia Suijun in Jiangzhou, Jingzhou and Yingchuan in Xincai, Xiyang, Runan, as well as the general Nanzhong Lang and the governor of Jiangzhou, and to lead the Nanman school captains, and all were awarded festivals. On Bingshen day, the emperor died in Xitang, when he was twenty-five years old. Buried in Anping Mausoleum. The deposed emperor's name was Sima Yi, whose courtesy name was Yanling. He was the half-brother of Emperor Ai. In the eighth year of Xiankang's reign, he was granted the title of King of East China Sea. In the eighth year of Yonghe, he was awarded the rank of regular servant of casual cavalry, and soon he was awarded the title of general of Zhenjun; in the fourth year of Shengping, he was awarded the title of general of chariot and cavalry. Five years later, he was granted the title of King Langxie. In the early years of Longhe, he was transferred to the third division of Shizhong, General of Hussar, and Kaifu Yitong. In February Bingshen of the third year of Xingning, Emperor Ai died without a son. On Dingyou Day, the Empress Dowager issued an edict saying: The emperor is unexpectedly ill and incurable, disasters occur frequently, and the Ai family feels very sad. Sima Yi, King of Langxie, has perfect moral character and is a relative with both ability and political integrity. He should inherit the throne, respect his ancestors and inherit the imperial line. Please prepare quickly to ascend the throne so that people and gods can be at peace. So all the officials went to Langxie Mansion to welcome King Langxie. On that day, the emperor ascended the throne and granted amnesty to the whole world.
target: The Deposed Emperor, Sima Yi, was the half-brother of Emperor Ai. He ascended the throne after Emperor Ai's death without an heir, as decreed by the Empress Dowager. His reign saw further wars with Murong Wei and Fu Jian. Huan Wen, seeking to increase his power after a failed military campaign, deposed the emperor. Huan Wen spread rumors about the emperor's impotence and illicit affairs to justify the deposition. The emperor was deposed as the King of Donghai and later granted the title of Duke of Haixi County. He was moved to Wu County, where he lived in fear, avoiding political involvement and indulging in pleasure to preserve his life. He died at age forty-five.

source: In November, the demon thief Lu Ju sent his disciple Xu Long to the gate of Haixi County Duke early in the morning. He said that there was a secret edict from the Queen Mother to welcome Haixi County Duke back to restore the throne. The emperor initially wanted to obey Xu Long, but gave up after listening to the centralized and unified advice. Xu Long said: "The big thing is about to succeed, why do you still listen to women?" The emperor said: I committed such a crime, but fortunately I was forgiven. How dare I act rashly! And if the Queen Mother has an edict, she should send her confidants. Why should it be you? You must be causing trouble. He shouted to his attendants to tie him up, and Xu Long fled in panic.
target: The text concludes with a historical commentary praising Emperor Mu's stable early reign, Emperor Ai's generosity, and the deposed emperor's wisdom in refusing a plot to restore him to the throne.

source: Emperor Yuan, whose name was Rui and whose courtesy name was Jingwen, was the great-grandson of Sima Yi, Emperor Xuan, and the son of Sima Jin, Prince Yagong of Lang. He was born in Luoyang in the second year of Xianning. When he was born, there was a strange divine light, which illuminated the whole room. The manuscript on which he was placed looked like freshly cut grass. When he grows up, he will have white hair on the left side of his forehead, a high bridge of nose, protruding brows, and bright eyes. At the age of fifteen, he succeeded to the throne as King Langya. A young man has a good reputation. During the reign of Emperor Hui, the royal family was troubled. Emperor Yuan often maintained a thrifty and conciliatory attitude, thus avoiding disaster. He is usually calm, smart and thoughtful, and does not show his talents easily, so he has not been recognized by people at the time. Only the servant Ji Shao thought that he was an extraordinary person. He once told people: King Lang Yawang's hair and bones are different from ordinary people, so he is not a minister. In the second year of Yuankang, he was appointed as a regular attendant of Yuanwai Sanqi. Promoted to General Zuo, he participated in the crusade against Sima Ying, king of Chengdu. The king's division failed in the Battle of Dangyin, and Emperor Yuan's uncle, Sima Yao, king of Dong'an, was killed by Sima Ying.
target: Emperor Yuan, named Sima Rui, was born in Luoyang in 276 CE with auspicious signs. He succeeded as King of Langya at fifteen and maintained a cautious, thrifty demeanor during the political turmoil of Emperor Hui's reign, avoiding disaster. Initially unrecognized for his talents, only servant Ji Shao perceived his extraordinary nature. He held various military posts, including General of the Left and General of the Auxiliary State, and participated in campaigns against Sima Ying.

source: After a while, dark clouds covered the sky and thunderstorms broke out. The patrols relaxed and they were able to escape secretly. Previously, Sima Ying ordered all the passes to prevent nobles from passing through. When Emperor Yuan arrived in Heyang, he was blocked by officials at the ferry. Attendant Song Dian came from behind, hit Emperor Yuan's horse with a whip and said with a smile: Chief of the House! The government prohibits noble people from passing through. Are you also being detained? The officials then let Emperor Yuan pass. Arriving in Luoyang, he welcomed the concubine back to the feudal country. When Sima Yue, King of the East China Sea, gathered troops in Xiapi and prepared to march westward, he gave Emperor Yuan the title of General of the Auxiliary State. Soon he added General Pingdong and the military supervisors in Xuzhou to guard Xiapi. Soon he was promoted to General Anton and Commander-in-Chief of Yangzhou's military affairs. Sima Yue went west to meet the emperor, leaving Emperor Yuan to stay in the east. In the early years of Yongjia, Wang Dao's strategy was adopted and he began to guard Jianye, with Gu Rong as the military commander and He Xun as the counselor. Wang Dun, Wang Dao, Zhou Qiye, and Diao Xie were all loyal ministers who respected famous people and inspected the people's sentiments. All the scholars and people in Jiangdong were sincerely convinced.
target: After a failed battle, he narrowly escaped capture during a thunderstorm. Following Sima Yue's westward march, Emperor Yuan adopted Wang Dao's strategy and established his base in Jianye, winning the loyalty of Jiangdong's elite through respectful governance.

source: When Sima Yue, King of the East China Sea, gathered troops in Xiapi and prepared to march westward, he gave Emperor Yuan the title of General of the Auxiliary State. Soon he added General Pingdong and the military supervisors in Xuzhou to guard Xiapi. Soon he was promoted to General Anton and Commander-in-Chief of Yangzhou's military affairs. Sima Yue went west to meet the emperor, leaving Emperor Yuan to stay in the east. In the early years of Yongjia, Wang Dao's strategy was adopted and he began to guard Jianye, with Gu Rong as the military commander and He Xun as the counselor. Wang Dun, Wang Dao, Zhou Qiye, and Diao Xie were all loyal ministers who respected famous people and inspected the people's sentiments. All the scholars and people in Jiangdong were sincerely convinced. When the concubine died in the feudal country, she went to the funeral. After the burial, she returned to Jianye and added 20,000 households to Xuancheng County's fiefdom, and added the titles of General Zhendong and Kaifu Yitong. Under the instruction of Sima Yue, he attacked Zhou Fu, the general who conquered the east, and drove Zhou Fu away. When Emperor Huai was kidnapped and taken to Pingyang, Sikong Xunfan and others issued a proclamation to the world, recommending Emperor Yuan as the leader of the alliance. Hua Yi, the governor of Jiangzhou, refused to obey. Xun Fan sent Zhou Guang, the internal historian of Yuzhang, and Wei Zhan, the former governor of Jiangzhou, to attack and capture him. After Emperor Min ascended the throne, he was given the post of Prime Minister Zuo. More than a year later, he ascended the throne as prime minister and governor, overseeing all domestic and foreign military affairs. He sent various generals to pacify Jiangdong respectively, beheaded the rebel general Sun Bi in Xuancheng, pacified Du in Xiangzhou, and implemented amnesty in Jingyang and Yangzhou according to the emperor's decree. When the western capital of Chang'an fell, Emperor Yuan went on an expedition. He personally wore armor and sent messages to all directions, recruiting soldiers and horses from all over the world, and marched on an appointment date. At this time, a jade album was discovered in Lin'an, and a white jade divine seal engraved with a unicorn was found in Jiangning. The text engraved on the seal was "Longevity for Ten Thousand Years". The sun appeared with two haloes. Everyone thought this was a sign that the country would be rejuvenated. On February 28, the first year of Emperor Jianwu's reign in the Yuan Dynasty, Pingdong General Song Zhe came to Jiankang and read out an imperial edict from Emperor Min, saying: Facing difficult times, the royal family's political order has declined.
target: After Emperor Huai was captured, Emperor Yuan was recommended as alliance leader and later appointed Prime Minister Zuo. He pacified Jiangdong, defeating rebels like Sun Bi and Du Zeng. When Chang'an fell, he mobilized troops and received auspicious signs, including a jade seal reading "Longevity for Ten Thousand Years." In 318 CE, Emperor Min's edict authorized him to govern, and after mourning, he accepted the title of King of Jin. He ascended the throne on the ninth day of the third month, implementing a general amnesty and establishing a bureaucracy in Jiankang. He rejected auspicious omens, stating his focus on self-blame for state failures.

source: He named his son Ma Fei of Xuancheng Company as King of Lang Ya. On June 15, Sikong, the governor of Bingzhou, Liu Kun, the Marquis of Guangwu, the governor of Youzhou, King Zuoxian, and Duke Duan of Bohai, Pi Shidan, were escorted by Colonel Wu Wan, General Zhenbei Liu Han, Chanyu, Duke Duan Chen of Guangning, and the family members of Duke Duan of Liaoxi. One hundred and eighty people, including the governor of Jizhou, Zhu Azi Shaoxu, the governor of Qingzhou and the Marquis of Guangrao, Cao Yi, the governor of Yanzhou and the Marquis of Dingxiang, Liu Yan, the captain of Dongyi School, Cui Ao, and the governor of Xianbei, Murong Chen, wrote a letter to persuade the Yuan Emperor to ascend the throne. Emperor Yuan wrote a letter to reply to the generals, encourage and comfort them, and the article is in "The Biography of Liu Kun". Shi Le's general Shi Jilong besieged Qiaocheng, but was repulsed by Pingxi general Zu Ti. On the 18th, Emperor Yuan sent a message to the world: The traitor Shi Le carried out a large-scale robbery in the Heshuo area. After years of crusade, he was frightened and fled far away. However, he also sent his evil party Shi Jilong to lead a group of dogs and sheep to cross the Henan River to invade and poison the people wantonly. General Zu Ti of Pingxi led a crusade and was immediately defeated. Now we dispatch nine armies, including General Chariot and Cavalry, King Lang Ya and King Sima Cai, with 30,000 elite soldiers, marching by land and water to attack the thief's lair and accept the sacrifice of Zu Ti. Anyone who can kill Shi Jilong's head will be rewarded with three thousand bolts of silk, fifty catties of gold, the title of county lord, and the food of two thousand households. If the thieves can cut off Shi Jilong's head and send it to him, the reward will be the same as before. In July, Zhu Song, the minister of Sanqi, and Gu Qiu, the minister, died. Emperor Yuan was very sad and planned to hold a mourning ceremony for them. Someone asked him to report that according to the old system, ministers were not included in the mourning ceremony. Emperor Yuan said: The decline of the country has caused bad social atmosphere, and we must mourn for them specially.
target: Emperor Yuan's reign faced challenges from Shi Le's invasions, repelled by General Zu Ti. He issued proclamations offering rewards for Shi Jilong's head. He mourned ministers Zhu Song and Gu Qiu despite protocol, emphasizing the need for special rites during national decline. In 319 CE, after Emperor Min's death, he assumed the imperial title, issuing edicts on governance, frugality, and moral conduct.

source: The Shang Dynasty encountered nine chaos, Yao suppressed the Eight Sounds, and the auspicious occasion of Emperor Ming's appointment appeared on this day. The operation can be roughly carried out in the palm of the hand, and a banner of obedience to the sky is erected on the riverside. The remaining ashes are rekindled, and the power is like the fire on the grassland after autumn. He took off his mourning clothes and went to the battlefield, killed the evil-doers, and offered sacrifices to the late emperor.
target: He banned extravagant gifts and promoted merit-based evaluations. Natural disasters like droughts and earthquakes prompted personal prayers and relief efforts.

source: Those virtuous and famous sages in Wu who were not commended or hired were listed on the list. A famine occurred in the three counties of Jiangdong, and envoys were sent to relieve the victims. Zhou Fu, the internal historian of Pengcheng, killed Zhou Mozao, the internal historian of Pei. On the twenty-sixth day of the first lunar month in the spring of the second year, the Chongyang Mausoleum collapsed. Emperor Yuan wore white clothes and cried for three days. He asked the champion general Liang Kan, the governor Chang Magui and others to repair the mausoleum. He sent people to Pingyang to meet the coffin of Emperor Huaimin, but was blocked and returned. In February, Xu Gong, the prefect of Taishan, beheaded the rebellious minister Zhou Fu, and his head was passed to the capital. In April of Xia, Longxiang general Chen Chuan occupied Junyi and rebelled, surrendering to Shile. Xu Gong, the governor of Taishan, rebelled in his own county, claiming to be the governor of Yanzhou, and invaded Jidai. Chen An, the governor of Qinzhou, rebelled and surrendered to Liu Yao. On May 13th, the Tomb of the Sun collapsed, and Emperor Yuan wore white clothes and cried for three days. A locust plague occurred in Xuyang and other counties in Jiangxi. A great famine occurred in Wu County. Pingbei general Zu Ti fought with Shi Le's general Shi Jilong in Junyi, and Zu Ti was defeated.
target: He dealt with rebellions, including those by Zhou Fu and Xu Gong, and faced military defeats against Shi Le's forces.

source: Liang Shuo, the governor of Xinchang, rebelled. A heavy fog broke out in the capital, black air covered the sky, and the sun and moon lost light. Shi Le captured Xiangcheng and Chengfu, then surrounded Qiao, defeated Zu Yue's other troops, and Zu Yue retreated to Shouchun. In November, Situ Xun was appointed as Taiwei. Jiyou, Taiwei Xunzu died. Situ was dismissed and his duties were merged with the prime minister. On the tenth day of the leap month, Emperor Yuan died in the inner hall at the age of forty-seven. He was buried in Jianping Mausoleum, with the temple name Zhongzong. Emperor Yuan's character was simple, frugal and calm, able to tolerate outspokenness and treat others with humility. When he began to guard Jiangdong, he often neglected his political affairs due to drinking. Director Wang earnestly warned him. Emperor Yuan asked Director Wang to pour a glass of wine, then picked up the cup and poured the wine away. From then on, he stopped drinking. Someone asked a minister to hang up a red curtain in the wide room of Taiji Hall. Emperor Yuan said: Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty collected the black book bags with letters from the officials to make a curtain. So they made curtains with green cloth in winter and green gauze in summer. A nobleman was granted a title in the palace, and someone asked him to buy a bird hairpin to make a headdress for the nobleman. Emperor Yuan thought the cost was too high and refused to allow it. The beloved Mrs. Zheng is plainly dressed and has no literary talent. Wang Na, the younger brother of Emperor Yuan's aunt, built a house for his mother that was too luxurious. Emperor Yuan dissuaded him with tears. However, the Jin Dynasty was in chaos and the emperor went into exile. The destiny of the Jin Dynasty was still in the Jin Dynasty, and the ministers were harmonious. The king's division was dispatched many times, but could not reach the Yangtze River Basin. The area under control was small and could only protect Wu and Chu. Finally, the powerful officials committed the crime, suffered the humiliation, and died of sorrow and anger.
target: In 322 CE, Wang Dun rebelled, capturing Stone City and defeating imperial forces. Emperor Yuan offered to abdicate, but Wang Dun assumed dictatorial powers, killing officials like Dai Ruosi and Zhou Qiye. Emperor Yuan died in the inner hall at age forty-seven, buried in Jianping Mausoleum with the temple name Zhongzong. He was known for simplicity and frugality, once pouring away wine after Wang Dao's admonition and using plain curtains instead of expensive ones. He refused costly gifts for his concubine and discouraged excessive construction. However, his reign was plagued by weak military control and internal strife, leading to his death from sorrow and anger.

source: The beloved Mrs. Zheng is plainly dressed and has no literary talent. Wang Na, the younger brother of Emperor Yuan's aunt, built a house for his mother that was too luxurious. The destiny of the Jin Dynasty was still in the Jin Dynasty, and the ministers were harmonious. The king's division was dispatched many times, but could not reach the Yangtze River Basin. Humility and frugality are sufficient virtues, but valor and talent are not enough. During the time of Qin Shihuang, a fortune-teller said: Five hundred years later, Jinling will have the spirit of the emperor. Therefore, Qin Shihuang traveled east to suppress the emperor's spirit, changed Jinling into Moling, and dug up the northern mountain of Jinling to eliminate its earthly spirit. When Sun Quan proclaimed himself emperor, he believed that he had fulfilled the prophecy of the Qin Dynasty. Sun Sheng believed that it was only 437 years from Qin Shihuang to Sun Quan, less than 500 years. It was 526 years until Emperor Yuan crossed the river, and the spirit of the emperor should be here. In the early years of Xianning, the Taishe tree was blown down by the wind, and green air came out of the society. The fortune teller believed that there was a good omen for the emperor in Dongguan, so he moved the King of Dongguan to the title of Langwang Yawang. This was Emperor Yuan's grandfather, Langwang Yawu King Sima Qianyou. In the battle to destroy Wu, Wang Jun actually arrived in Jianye first, but when Sun Hao surrendered, he gave the jade seal to Sima Qinyou's military camp, which was far away from Jianye. God's will and human affairs are in line with the auspicious omen of ZTE. During the Tai'an period of Emperor Hui, there was a nursery rhyme that said: Five horses floated across the river, and one horse turned into a dragon.
target: Historical accounts note prophecies of imperial destiny in Jinling, fulfilled when Emperor Yuan crossed the Yangtze River 526 years after Qin Shihuang. A nursery rhyme about five horses crossing the river symbolized the southern migration of kings, with Emperor Yuan becoming the dragon.

source: However, Xiahou, the concubine of King Sima Jin of King Yagong of Lang, actually had an affair with a minor official named Niu and gave birth to Emperor Yuan. Some people say that this is the talisman of "Niu succeeds Ma". Shi Chen said: With the land of Weiyang as its territory and the torrent of the Yangtze River as its support, there are often wars in the Chu River basin and Fangcheng is often a battlefield, so we have to sincerely trust the generals to lead the army. With tens of thousands of warships and a military force that is twice that of the royal family, those who are in such a position and have no intention of usurping the country are people like Duke Zhou.
target: Rumors suggested his birth resulted from an affair, fulfilling the "ox succeeds the horse" prophecy.

source: Emperor An's name was Dezong and his courtesy name was Dezong. He was the eldest son of Emperor Xiaowu. In August of the twelfth year of Taiyuan, Xin Si was established as the crown prince. In September of the 21st year of Gengshen, Emperor Xiaowu passed away. Xin You, the crown prince becomes the emperor and offers amnesty to the whole world. In Guihai, Situ and Prince Daozi of Kuaiji were appointed as Taifus to act as agents of the government. In Jiashen, the tenth month of winter, Emperor Xiaowu was buried in Longping Mausoleum. It's snowing heavily. On the first day of the first lunar month of the first year of Long'an, the emperor was crowned, his reign title was changed, and a first-class official rank was added to the civil and military officials. Taifu and King Daozi of Kuaiji returned to power. Appoint Shangshu Zuopushe Wang Xie as Shangshu Ling, and the leading general Wang Guobao as Shangshu Zuopushe. In February, Lu Guang's general Wu Gu called himself the Great Governor and the Great Chanyu, and his country was named Nanliang. In Jinchang, he attacked Lu Guang's general Dou Gou and defeated his army. In the third month of Jiayin, the Empress Dowager Li was honored as the Empress Dowager. On Wuwu day, Wang was made queen. Lu Guang's son Lu Zuan was defeated by Qifu Qiangui. Lu Guang's subordinate Duan Ye, the prefect of Jiankang, named himself Liangzhou Mu. Murong Shi Ji defeated the Wei army. In the fourth month of the summer, Jiaxu, Wang Gong, the governor of Yanzhou, and Yu Kai, the governor of Yuzhou, raised troops in the name of attacking Shangshu Zuopushe Wang Guobao and Jianwei general Wang Xu. Jiashen killed the national treasure and Wang Xulai to please Wang Gong, and Wang Gong stopped his troops. Wuzi, amnesty to the world. In May, former Situ Chief Shi Wangchang rebelled in Wu County, but Wang Gong conquered him and put him down. Murong Shi's general Murong Xiang ascended the throne as the pseudo-emperor in Zhongshan, and Murong Bao fled to Huanglong.
target: Emperor An, named Dezong, was the eldest son of Emperor Xiaowu. He was established as crown prince in 387 and ascended the throne in 396 after his father's death, granting amnesty to the empire. He appointed Prince Daozi of Kuaiji as regent. During his reign, numerous rebellions and military conflicts occurred across the realm. Various warlords declared themselves rulers, including Wu Gu who founded Southern Liang, and Duan Ye who proclaimed himself Liangzhou Mu. Wang Gong and Yu Kai raised troops against officials Wang Guobao and Wang Xu, leading to their executions to appease the rebels.

source: In May, former Situ Chief Shi Wangchang rebelled in Wu County, but Wang Gong conquered him and put him down. Murong Shi's general Murong Xiang ascended the throne as the pseudo-emperor in Zhongshan, and Murong Bao fled to Huanglong. In the eighth month of autumn, Lu Guang was attacked by his servant She Yang Gui and his Sanqi Changshi Guo Mo. Lu Guang's son Lu Zuan defeated them. In September, Murong Shi's general Murong Lin beheaded Murong Xiang in Zhongshan, and then ascended the throne as the pseudo-emperor. In October of winter, Murong Lin was defeated by the Wei army. In the spring and March of the second year, the dragon boat caught fire twice. In the fifth month of summer, Lan Khan killed Murong Shi and proclaimed himself the general and the king of Changli. In the seventh month of autumn, Murong Bao's son Murong Sheng beheaded Lan Khan and assumed the title of King of Changle, taking over the throne of emperor. Wang Gong, the governor of Yanzhou, Yu Kai, the governor of Yuzhou, Yin Zhongkan, the governor of Jingzhou, Huan Xuan, the governor of Guangzhou, and Yang Quanqi, the Nanman captain, rebelled. In August, Wang Yu, the governor of Jiangzhou, fled and arrived. In Bingzi, Ning Shuo's general Deng Qifang fought with Murong De's general Murong Fa in Guancheng, and Wang's division was defeated. In Bingxu, Murong Sheng usurped the throne in Huanglong and called himself emperor. Huan Xuan defeated Wang Shi in Baishi. On Xinmao in the ninth month, Huang Tie, the Taifu and Prince Daozi of Kuaiji, was added. He sent the conquest general Yuan Xian, the eldest son of King Kuaiji, the former general Wang Shi, and the right general Xie Yan to attack Huan Xuan and others. Jihai defeated Yu Kai at Niuzhu. On Bingwu, King Daozi of Kuaiji stationed troops in the middle hall, and Yuan Xian guarded the stone. In Jiyou, the former general Wang died defending the northern suburbs, and the right general Xie Yan guarded Xuanyang Gate. Liu Laozhi, the general of the auxiliary state, was stationed in Xinting and sent his son Jingxuan to defeat Wang Gong. Wang Gong fled to Changtang Lake in Qu'a. The lake captain arrested him and sent him to the capital, where he was beheaded. So he sent Taichang Yin Maoxiao to inform Zhongkan and Huanxuan, and Huanxuan waited in Xunyang. In October of winter, there were reports of the appearance of righteous beasts in Xinye. Bingzi, amnesty to the world. In Renwu, Zhongkan and others formed an alliance in Xunyang and elected Huan Xuan as the leader of the alliance. In November, King Dewen of Langxie was appointed as the general of Wei and the third division of Kaifu Yitong, and the leading general Wang Ya was appointed as Shangshu Zuopushe. In the twelfth month of the lunar month, Ji Chou, King Tuoba Gui of Wei ascended the throne and was named Tianxing.
target: The following years saw continued turmoil. Murong Xiang and Murong Lin successively claimed imperial titles. Wang Gong, Yu Kai, Yin Zhongkan, Huan Xuan, and Yang Quanqi rebelled. Huan Xuan defeated imperial forces at Baishi. The court sent Yuan Xian, Wang Shi, and Xie Yan to attack Huan Xuan and others. Liu Laozhi's son defeated Wang Gong, who was captured and beheaded. Huan Xuan became alliance leader. Tuoba Gui of Wei ascended the throne as Tianxing.

source: Fanhuda of Linyi captured Rinan and Jiuzhen, and then invaded Jiaotou. The prefect Du Yuan defeated him in a crusade. Duan Ye calls himself King of Liang. Qiu Chi Gong Yang Sheng sent an envoy to express his willingness to offer local products to the vassal. On March 9th, he honored his biological mother, Mrs. Chen, as the Empress Dowager De. At the end of April in Xia, he was granted the title of Shangshu Ling Wang to die as General of the Guard, and Yuan Xian, the prince of Kuaiji, was appointed as the governor of Yangzhou. In the sixth month of Wuzi, King Dewen of Langxie was appointed Situ. Ji Jiade captured Qingzhou and killed General Long Xiang Pi Jianhun, so he assumed the throne of emperor in Guanggu. In the eighth month of autumn, Bald-haired Wugu died, and his younger brother Lilugu succeeded to the pseudo-throne. In the tenth month of winter, Yao Xing captured Luoyang and captured Xin Gongjing, the governor of Henan. In the 11th month of Jiayin, the demon thief Sun En captured Kuaiji. Wang Ning, the internal historian, was killed. Huanqian, the internal historian of Wu, Sima Chong, the king of Xincai, the prefect of Linhai, and Wei Yin, the prefect of Yixing, all abandoned their offices and fled. Xie Miao, the prefect of Chengyuan, and Sima Yi, the prefect of Chengtai, were all killed. General Wei Xie Yan and General Liu Laozhi were sent to attack him and beat him away.
target: Sun En, a demon thief, captured Kuaiji, killing several officials. The court sent Xie Yan and Liu Laozhi to repel him.

source: Ding Si sent King Rouzhi of Qi, who was also serving as a minister, to use Yu banners to inform Jing and Jiang states. In Ding Mao, Huan Xuan defeated Wang Shi in Gushu, and King Qiao Shangzhi and King Qi Rouzhi died together. Wu Yinzhi, the right general, was appointed as the commander-in-chief and handed over to the military affairs of the two states of Guangzhou and the governor of Guangzhou. In March, Liu Laozhi betrayed and surrendered to Huan Xuan. At Xinwei, the king's army was defeated in Xinting. General Hussar, Prince Yuanxian of Kuaiji, Wang Yanzhang of Shuhai, champion general Mao Tai, and guerrilla general Mao Sui were killed together. In Renshen, Huanxuan appointed himself as a servant, prime minister, and recorded the affairs of the minister. He appointed Huan Qian as the minister's servant, and moved the Taifu and King Daozi of Kuaiji to Ancheng. Huanxuan soon called himself Taiwei, Yangzhou Mu, and Prime Minister of political affairs, and made Langxie Wang Dewen the Grand Prime Minister. Gui Liang, the corrupt prefect, attacked Zhu Mo and killed him. That month, Tu'elu died alone, and his younger brother Tu'an succeeded to the throne. In the tenth month of winter, Liu Gui, the governor of Jizhou, rebelled and fled to Jichashan. In the 12th month of Gengshen, King Dao of Kuaiji was killed by Danxuan. Special amnesty will be given to criminals in Guangling and Pengcheng who have committed crimes of treason and below. In the spring and February of the second year of Xinchou, Jianwei general Liu Yu defeated Xu Daofu in Shuyang. In Yimao, Huan Xuan called himself a general. Ding Si, Sun Wu, the governor of Jizhou, was killed by Huan Xuan. On the first day of the fourth lunar month in summer, there is a solar eclipse. source: Since Emperor An had not been buried yet, there was no court meeting. Make Chu the queen. In the Sino-Japanese War, Liu Yu was summoned to return to the court. After a while, the soldiers entered over the wall and killed Emperor Gong in the inner room. He was thirty-six years old. Mi was named Emperor Gong and was buried in Chongping Mausoleum. When the emperor was young, he was cruel and impetuous. Later, when he was a feudal country, he once let those who were good at archery shoot horses as a game. Soon someone said: "Ma is the surname of the country, but it would be unlucky to kill the horse yourself." Emperor Gong also woke up and regretted what he had done. From then on, he believed deeply in Buddhism. He cast tens of thousands of coins together and made a bronze statue one foot six feet high. He went to Waguan Temple to welcome him in person and followed him on foot for more than ten miles. Emperor An was an idiot, and Emperor Gong often served him, taking care of his daily life and food. He was famous for his courtesy, and people at that time praised him.
target: Emperor Gong, named Dewen, was Emperor An's half-brother. He had been enfeoffed as King of Langxie and held various positions including General of the Central Army and Grand Sima. After Huan Xuan's defeat, he returned to his former position. In 419, following Emperor An's death, Liu Yu issued a false edict proclaiming Emperor Gong's succession. In 420, following Liu Yu's instructions, Fu Liang persuaded Emperor Gong to abdicate. The emperor willingly complied, stating the Jin family had long lost the empire. He wrote the abdication edict on red paper. Liu Yu made him King of Lingling. In 422, Liu Yu sent soldiers who killed Emperor Gong in his inner chamber at age thirty-six. As a youth, Emperor Gong had been cruel and impetuous, once shooting horses for sport until someone noted that "Ma" (horse) was the imperial surname, making such killing unlucky. He then regretted his actions and became a devout Buddhist, casting a bronze statue and personally escorting it to Waguan Temple. He was known for his courtesy in serving his brother Emperor An, caring for his daily needs.

source: Emperor Hui Ji, Emperor Xiaohui's name is Zhong, and his courtesy name is Zhengdu. He is the second son of Emperor Wu. However, as time passed, the new year has entered, and the new era has changed, but the old rituals are still the same. The second year of Yongxi is now changed to the first year of Yongping. target: Emperor Hui Ji, named Zhong and styled Zhengdu, was the second son of Emperor Wu. In the first year of Yongxing, Sima Ying became crown prince, but was later deposed. Emperor Hui was kidnapped to Chang’an by Zhang Fang. Sima Yong controlled the government. In the second year, Sima Yue marched west to rescue the emperor. After battles, Emperor Hui returned to Luoyang. In the first year of Guangxi, Sima Yong killed Zhang Fang. Sima Yue’s forces escorted Emperor Hui back. Emperor Hui died in Xianyang Hall at age 48, possibly poisoned by Sima Yue.

source: In the past, Ma Xi observed the phenomena and laws of nature with the purpose of understanding the virtues of Heaven and comprehending the true feelings between Heaven and Earth. Therefore, the three emperors were diligent and diligent, and the sun, moon and five stars followed their orbits. Huangdi first studied the "River Map" and began to understand good and bad luck, good and evil, so his "Star Biography" is still preserved. In the Tang and Yu eras, it was the Xi family and the He family who inherited his rules, and in the Youxia era, it was Kunwu who inherited the previous rules. However, it has been a long time and the literature and classics have not been handed down. As for Wu Xian of the Yin Shang Dynasty and Shi Yi of the Zhou Dynasty, the historians of the vassal states, such as Zi Shen of Lu, Bu Yan of Jin, Bi Zao of Zheng, Zi Wei of Song, Gan De of Qi, Tang Mei of Chu, Yin Gao of Zhao, and Shi Shenfu of Wei, all were in charge of astronomical signs, and each discussed the fulfillment of the images. Until the time of Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty and Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, Sima Tan and his son successively served as Taishi Ling and wrote the "Book of Heavenly Officials" to clarify the laws between heaven and man. After that, Liu Xiang, the lieutenant of the Central Base, expanded the records of disaster laws in "Hong Fan" and compiled "Huang Ji Lun" to refer to past events. When Ban Gu wrote the "Book of Han", Ma Xu wrote "Tianwen", Cai Yong, Qiao Zhou and others also wrote their own records. In ancient times, there were three relevant theories proposed. One advocated the Gaitian theory, the other advocated the Xuanye theory, and the other advocated the Huntian theory. During the reign of Emperor Ling of the Han Dynasty, Cai Yong wrote a letter to Shuofang, saying in the book: Xuan Ye's theory has no basis for learning. Calculating the positions of the five planets is so precise and subtle that it is a method that has been passed down forever and remains unchanged. The government retained this instrument but did not have the original Huntian Shuo, and the previous records were incomplete. The book "Zhou Bi" mentioned by Cai Yong is the theory of Gaitian. It originated from the Zhou Tian Calendar created by the Pao Xi clan. It was passed down to the Duke of Zhou from the Yin Shang Dynasty and recorded by the people of the Zhou Dynasty, so it is called "Zhou Bi".
target: This allowed sages to review the past, predict the future, and align human affairs with natural laws. The *Book of Changes* states that Heaven reveals signs of good and bad luck through celestial phenomena, which sages imitate. Similarly, the *Shangshu* emphasizes that Heaven's wisdom is reflected in the people's understanding. The quality of governance is linked to the harmony of people's sentiments and celestial movements. Huangdi studied the "River Map" to understand good and bad luck, and his "Star Biography" survives. Later rulers appointed officials to oversee astronomy and geography, but many ancient texts were lost over time. During the Yin Shang and Zhou dynasties, various historians and astronomers, such as Wu Xian, Shi Yi, and others from different states, were responsible for interpreting celestial signs. Their theories, particularly those of Wu Xian, Gan De, and Shi Shenfu, were highly regarded. Despite Qin Shihuang's book burning, astronomical texts were preserved. During the Han Dynasty, Sima Tan and his son wrote the "Book of Heavenly Officials," and later scholars like Liu Xiang, Ban Gu, Ma Xu, Cai Yong, and Qiao Zhou expanded on these records. The text then introduces three ancient cosmological theories: the Gaitian (hemispherical sky) theory, the Xuanye (infinite void) theory, and the Huntian (celestial sphere) theory. Cai Yong favored the Huntian theory, which was used in the armillary sphere observatory. The Gaitian theory, described in the "Zhou Bi," posits a round sky like an umbrella and a square earth like a chessboard, with the sun and moon moving in relation to the celestial body. The Xuanye theory, promoted by Ximeng, suggests the sky is a boundless void with stars floating freely, their movements governed by atmospheric forces.

During the reign of Emperor Cheng of Xiankang, Yu Xi of Kuaiji wrote "An Tian Lun" based on Xuan Ye's theory, arguing that: The sky is very high and endless, and the earth is very deep and unfathomable. The sky is knotted and high above, and has the shape of constant stability; the earth is solid and real, and has a static and unchanging body below.
