Its surrounding edges are connected to the edges of the four seas and float on the vitality. It's like an upside-down basin placed on top of running water. The reason it doesn't sink is because the gas fills it. The sun moves around the north, sets in the west, and rises in the east, without entering or leaving the earth. target: The text then discusses various proponents and critics of these theories. Yu Xi of Kuaiji wrote "An Tian Lun" based on Xuanye theory, arguing that the sky is infinitely high and the earth unfathomably deep. Ge Hong criticized this view, questioning the existence of stars if they are not attached to the sky. Yu Xi's grandfather, Yushu, proposed that the celestial body is like an egg, with the earth floating on vitality. Yao Xin's "Xintian Lun" compared the sky's shape to a human chin, explaining seasonal temperature changes based on the pole's height. The text notes that these theorists were not dedicated astronomers. Wang Zhongren refuted the Huntian theory, arguing that the sky cannot move through water underground. He claimed that the sun's setting is an illusion of distance, like a torch disappearing on a distant plain. Ge Hong defended the Huntian theory, comparing the celestial body to an egg with the earth as the yolk, and explaining the sun's entry and exit from water using hexagrams from the *Book of Changes*.

target: The debate continues with Huan Junshan's observations supporting the Huntian theory. source: Human beings contain the spiritual energy between yin and yang of heaven and earth, and have emotions of sadness, joy, joy and anger. "Biography" says: For one day, if one restrains oneself and returns to ritual, the world will return to benevolence. Since the beginning of the world, the Sui people have drilled wood to make fire. Their ambitions have been modesty and frugality. Their feelings do not care about jade and silk. Xuanyuan and Zhuanxu obeyed the gods, and Yao and Yushun of Tang Dynasty investigated the archaeological system. It not only left an example of setting up hundreds of officials and formulated unchangeable laws and regulations; it also had 300 rules on etiquette and 3,000 kinds of rituals, all of which were used to promote and spread the will of God and adjust and standardize human behavior. At the end of the Zhou Dynasty, the world's social customs changed, the king's rule declined, things went against the traditions of a beautiful country, and even the way of running a family in etiquette was lost. Chang Jianzi asked Taishu about the etiquette of yielding and dealing with others, and he replied: "That can only be called a ceremony but not a true etiquette." The truth that is a matter of course has been ignored ever since. In the eleventh year of Duke Ai, Confucius returned to Lu from Wei, studied the models of the three generations, and wrote down the lessons of hundreds of kings. At that time, there was no wise king, so his ideas could not be implemented. If sentiment is allowed to develop, benevolence will inevitably be thrown aside; if heresy is allowed to cause trouble, the style of Confucianism may be excluded. Therefore, Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty abolished the two-year mourning system, and Emperor Guangwu combined the suburban sacrifices into one.
target: The evolution of ritual and ceremonial systems in ancient China, emphasizing their role in maintaining social order and moral conduct. Humans possess spiritual energy and emotions, and sages established rituals to control arrogance, worship heaven and earth, and define social hierarchies, thereby ensuring good governance. The text references the concept that self-restraint and a return to ritual can lead to universal benevolence. Historically, early practices were simple, with modest ambitions and frugal customs. Over time, rulers like Xuanyuan, Zhuanxu, Yao, and Shun developed systems, which were perfected during the Zhou dynasty with detailed regulations and rituals. However, by the end of the Zhou, social customs declined, and the king's rule weakened, leading to a loss of proper etiquette. Confucius later studied ancient models but could not implement his ideas due to a lack of a wise ruler. The text then discusses the Han dynasty's efforts to revive rituals, noting that Emperor Wen abolished the two-year mourning period, and Emperor Guangwu combined suburban sacrifices.

Comets, or "broom stars," signify sweeping away the old and ushering in the new, often bringing war and floods. Specific comets like the "Red You Flag" or "Heavenly Spear" portend rebellion, military defeat, or the death of a ruler. Guest stars like the "Old Man Star" or "Zhou Bo Star" indicate famine or prosperity. Meteors, as "angels," foretell events based on their size, speed, and direction; their fall marks war or the death of a general. Atmospheric qi, such as the "Emperor's Qi" (red inside, yellow outside) or the "Qi of a Fierce General" (like a dragon or beast), signal the rise of a king or a military leader. Cloud formations, like "formation clouds" or "hook clouds," predict war, and their colors (white for mourning, red for war, etc.) determine the nature of the event.

target: The text provides numerous historical examples of these portents. For continuous cold, it cites heavy snow, unseasonable frost, and hail, linking them to harsh punishments, framing of loyal officials, and unjust killings. Examples include frost damaging grains in the third year of Jiahe of Wu Sun Quan, and heavy snow in the fourth year of Chiwu. For continuous wind, it records strong winds overturning houses and breaking trees, linking them to ignorant and arbitrary rule, as during the reign of King Zhengshi of Wei Qi. target: The text also records instances of fish falling on arsenal roofs, interpreted as a sign of war, and locust plagues, linked to the lord's greed and harshness. Pig disasters, such as wild boars entering military camps, are seen as portents of failure and emptiness. Black and yellow mists are recorded as signs of impending doom or usurpation. Landslides and ground collapses are interpreted as signs of the emperor's way collapsing and the people losing favor. The appearance of dragons in wells is considered a bad omen, indicating that the ruler's virtue is at odds with fate. Finally, the text records numerous human anomalies, such as women turning into men, the dead coming back to life, and births of monstrous children, all interpreted as signs of social and political disorder, with subordinates overtaking superiors.

source: The expression of spirituality, for some reason, turns to chanting; the expression of emotion, for some reason, involves the hands and feet. What arises from the heart is called Tao, and what is reflected in images is called Yong. It is also influential to use this principle to look at the heaven and earth. All animals dance together, not to mention humans. They praise peace and mourn for chaos. In this case, the use of music can spread the sound. Shennong made the harp and Fuxi made the harp, and then made the bell and the chime to express the soul and temperament, and to imitate the achievements of all things. From this point of view, its origin is very old. The Yin Shang Dynasty had no discipline and left behind a very bad atmosphere. After the rise of obscene music, elegant music was lost and scattered. Works such as "Five Heroes" and "Six Stems" have declined. Confucius said: People can promote Tao, but Tao cannot promote people. Starting from the Zhou Dynasty, there were two "Southern", and "Guofeng" was compatible with six generations. In the past, the Yellow Emperor wrote "Yunmen", Yao wrote "Xianchi", Shun wrote "Da Shao", Yu wrote "Da Xia", Yin wrote "Da Xi", and Zhou wrote "Ren Wu". It is said that they inherited the etiquette of the virtuous kings of the previous generation and formulated the etiquette of bowing and behaving. The accumulation of gentleness is included, and the elegance is expressed on the outside. "Shang Shu" said that Kui was ordered to take charge of music and teach the noble children, which is what "Zhou Guan" said about playing Da Lu and singing Huang Zhong. When God's gift came down, people looked respectful and solemn, inheriting the glory of the Zhou Dynasty and promoting elegant music. The eldest son Fang Deng and Princess Hanzhen of Yichang were born. In May of the third year of Taiqing, he was ordered to commit suicide and was buried in Waguan Temple, Jiangling. Shi Chen said: The empress supported the royal customs morally, and the customs spread throughout the world. This was probably derived from the meaning of "Ge Tan" and "Guan Ju". As for Mu Guifei, her beautiful glory has long been displayed. She gave birth to a prince and encouraged the Sixth Palace with her own virtue. It is wonderful. The ancestor's concubine Xu had no virtue and brought about her own destruction. That's right.
target: She died in the seventh year of her life at age forty-two. A condolence poem praised her virtues. She was posthumously titled Mu. After Taizong ascended, she was honored as Empress Dowager Mu. Her father was a governor. Emperor Gaozu's doctor, Zhao Yao, originally surnamed Hu, was from Hejikung Yao. King Zha Shi'an took her as a concubine. After Dong Guang's defeat, she was brought into the palace by Donghun Hou. After Jianchenyuan was pacified, Zhidan accepted her as a palace maid. source: Pei Ziye, whose courtesy name was Jiyuan, was a native of Wenxi, Hedong, and the eighth-generation grandson of Pei Kang, Prince Zuo of the Jin Dynasty. His elder brother Pei Li and his younger brothers Pei Kai and Pei Chuo were all famous and were called the Four Peis. Great-grandfather Pei Songzhi was a Taizhong doctor in the Song Dynasty. His grandfather Pei Si was a foreign soldier of Nan Zhonglang and joined the army. My father Zhaoming is a regular attendant of Tongzhi Sanqi. His mother died after Ziye was born. He was raised by his grandmother. When he was nine years old, his grandmother passed away. He burst into tears and his family was surprised. When he was young, he was studious and good at writing articles. He started his career and entered the court as Zuo Changshi of the Wuling Kingdom of Qi. He joined the army as the King of Jiangxia on the right and resigned due to his father's death. His behavior during the period of mourning was completely in line with etiquette. Every time he went to the tomb, the grass withered for him when he was crying, and a white rabbit crouched beside him. In the early years of Tianjian, Shangshu Pushe Fan Yun praised his conduct and was about to report it to the emperor. However, due to Fan Yun's death, the matter was not completed. Ren Fang, a Le'an native, had a good reputation and was admired by his descendants. Anyone who studied under him would be recommended by Ren Fang. Ziye is Ren Fang's cousin, but he doesn't go to see him, and Ren Fang resents him. After a long time, in addition to being granted the title of King Ancheng of the Right Army to join the army, he was immediately moved to the post of concurrently serving as Wei Zheng. At that time, criminal judgment documents were jointly signed by officials from the three parties. Once when Ziye was absent, his colleagues signed his name. The memorial was not approved, and Ziye was implicated and was dismissed. Someone advised him to explain the facts to Yusi, and he would be clear of fault.
target: Pei Ziye, courtesy name Jiyuan, was from Wenxi, Hedong, and a descendant of Jin Dynasty royalty. He was raised by his grandmother after his mother died at his birth, and showed deep filial piety when she passed when he was nine. Known for his studiousness and literary skill, he began his official career as Zuo Changshi of the Wuling Kingdom of Qi. His mourning period for his father was so exemplary that withered grass and a white rabbit appeared at his father's tomb. Fan Yun praised his conduct but died before reporting it to the emperor. Ren Fang, a famous scholar, resented Ziye for not visiting him, despite being a cousin. Ziye later served as a military advisor but was dismissed when a document was signed in his absence without his knowledge. He refused to litigate to clear his name, accepting the dismissal without resentment.

source: After a long time, in addition to being granted the title of King Ancheng of the Right Army to join the army, he was immediately moved to the post of concurrently serving as Wei Zheng. At that time, criminal judgment documents were jointly signed by officials from the three parties. Once when Ziye was absent, his colleagues signed his name. The memorial was not approved, and Ziye was implicated and was dismissed. Someone advised him to explain the facts to Yusi, and he would be clear of fault. Ziye smiled and replied: "Although I feel ashamed that I don't have Liu Ji's conduct, I can't get a job by litigating." He has been deposed for a long time since then and has no hatred at all. In the second year, Xiao Jing, Marquis of Wu Ping, was appointed as the governor of Southern Yanzhou. He was introduced to serve as the champion. After Xiao Jing was transferred, he was dismissed. At that time, Zhongshu Fan Zhen had no contact with Ziye, but he praised him when he heard that he had good character and industry achievements. Fan Zhenqian was appointed as the doctor of Guozi, and he immediately recommended Ziye, saying: I heard that Pei Ziye, the former secretary of the Champion Mansion, joined the army in Hedong. He was forty years old and had a few words. He was endowed with superhuman conduct when he was young. When he grew up, he developed excellent moral integrity. He followed etiquette during mourning. Grief was almost life-threatening. After the mourning period was over, he still had no food. He was in a lower position, with a humble body and a low reputation, but his temperament was not greedy and he did not deceive his spouse. Therefore, knowledgeable people respected him and people in his hometown admired him. Moreover, his family knowledge has been passed down from generation to generation, he has studied Confucianism and history, read a lot of books, and devoted himself to research and writing in his daily life and actions. He is the author of twenty volumes of "Song Lue", which runs through the beginning and end, writing the history of a dynasty and writing articles and records, which are worth watching.
target: Fan Zhen later recommended Ziye, praising his moral integrity, filial piety, and scholarly achievements, including his twenty-volume "Song Lue." Despite some officials objecting to his qualifications, Ziye was appointed as Minister Bibu Lang and later as a county magistrate, where he resolved disputes through reasoning, eliminating lawsuits. He completed his great-grandfather's unfinished history, earning praise from Shen Yue and others.

source: At first, Pei Ziye's great-grandfather Pei Song was ordered to continue the "History of the Song Dynasty" compiled by He Chengtian during the Song and Yuan Dynasties. He died before completing it. Ziye often wanted to complete his father's work. By the end of the Yongming Dynasty of Qi Dynasty, the "Book of Song" written by Shen Yue had been published, and Ziye edited and edited the history of the Song Dynasty into twenty volumes of "Song Lue". His narrative comments were full of sublime points. Shen Yue read them and praised them, saying: I can't keep up with him. Xiao Chen from Lanling, Fu Gu from Beidi, and Dantu from Dayi all praised him and valued him. As a result, the Minister of Civil Affairs, Daedian, recommended him to Shandan and appointed him as a writer, responsible for compiling national history and daily life notes. Immediately, he was concurrently appointed Zhongshu Tongshi Shiren, and soon he was appointed Tongzhi Zhengyuanlang, and his duties as author and Shiren remained as before. He was also ordered to be in charge of Zhongshu's imperial edicts. During the period of the Han Dynasty, there were Baiti and Hua Kingdoms outside the Great Wall in the northwest, and they sent envoys from the Minshan Road to pay tribute. These two countries have never had envoys to meet with each other in the past dynasties, and they do not know the national conditions. Ziye said: In the Han Dynasty, Marquis Yingyin beheaded Hu Bai, a general named General. Fu Qian's "Notes" says: The title is blank, and the name is nonsense. Also in the Han Dynasty, Marquis Dingyuan attacked prisoners, and Ba Hua followed him. It must be his descendants who are here now. People at that time admired his broad knowledge. The imperial order still asked him to compile the "Picture of Envoys from Fang Kingdom", which extensively described the grand occasion of attracting people from outside the Great Wall. From remote areas to overseas, there were a total of twenty countries. Ziye and Liu Xian from Peiguo, Liu Zhilin from Nanyang, Yin Yun from Chenjun, Ruan Xiaoxu from Chenliu, Gu Xie from Wujun, and Wei Leng from Jingzhao were all well-read and deeply appreciated and loved each other. Liu Hao respected Ziye even more. At that time, Xiao Kan, the Marquis of Wuping, and Zhang Zuan, a native of Fanyang, asked Ziye to judge whenever they discussed ancient books and had any disputes. In the seventh year of the ordinary year, Wang Shi went north to conquer Wei and ordered Ziye to draft an edict against Wei. Ziye immediately wrote it after receiving the edict. Because of the heavy weight of the matter, Gaozu summoned Xu Mian, Prince Zhanshi Zhoushe, Hongluqing Liu Zhilin, and Zhongshu Minister Zhu Yi to gather in Shouguang Hall to read the article. Everyone present was amazed. Emperor Gaozu looked at Ziye and said: Although his appearance is weak, his writing is heroic. Immediately, he was ordered to draft an edict to Wei Xiangyuan. After accepting the edict that night, Ziye thought that it could be submitted tomorrow, so he did not start writing. However, at five o'clock, Shaoshu urged him to hand in the article at Kai Zhaimen. Wang Shu wrote calmly, and it was completed at dawn. After the performance, the stage manager was very complimentary. Naturally, he was asked to draft all kinds of talismans. Ziye's articles were elegant and quick to write, and he did not advocate gorgeous words and sentences. His style mostly imitated the ancients, which was different from today's style. Some people slandered him at the time, but they all respected him later.
target: He was then appointed as a historian and editor, known for his broad knowledge, such as identifying the origins of envoys from the Baiti and Hua kingdoms. He compiled the "Picture of Envoys from Fang Kingdom" and was admired by contemporaries like Liu Xian and Liu Zhilin. In the seventh year of the ordinary year, he drafted an edict against Wei quickly, impressing Emperor Gaozu with his heroic writing. Ziye's style imitated the ancients, and he wrote quickly, saying he wrote with his heart.

source: In the first year of Datong, he was transferred to Hongluqing, and then concurrently served as the infantry captain. Ziye served in the palace for more than ten years. He was quiet, clean and self-respecting. He never made any demands. Since his mother's family and father's family were poor, he gave all his salary to them. There was no residence, so we borrowed two acres of official land and built several thatched houses. His wife and children often suffered from hunger and cold, but he only focused on teaching. His children and nephews respected him as they served their father. In his later years, he believed deeply in Buddhism, strictly abided by religious rules, and only ate vegetarian food throughout his life. In the second year of Zhongdatong, he died in office at the age of sixty-two. First, Ziye himself estimated that his death date would not be past the Gengxu year. In the year of Zao, he reflected on himself and asked to retire. He said to his colleague Liu Zhiheng: I am going to pass away. We must be frugal and moderate in dispatching and funeral arrangements. Emperor Gaozu mourned and shed tears for him. The edict said: Pei Ziye, Qing Honglu, the captain of the infantry academy, the intellectual scholar, and the general secretary of Zhongshu, has sufficient knowledge of literature and history, is honest and self-respecting, and has worked hard for many years. Sudden loss makes people sad and missed. He can be given as a posthumous gift to the regular attendants of Sanqi, 50,000 yuan for the funeral, and 50 pieces of cloth, and he will be buried in the near future. The nickname is Sadako. When Ziye was young, he compiled two volumes each of "Collection of Mourning Clothes" and "Continued Biography of the Pei Family", and more than forty volumes of excerpts of events in the Later Han Dynasty. Shaoling also compiled twenty volumes of "Biography of Gan Seng", two volumes of "Hundred Officials and Nine Ranks", one volume of "Fu Yi Mi Fa", one volume of "Pictures of Fang Guo Envoy", and twenty volumes of collected works, all of which have been circulated in the world.
target: He served in the palace for over a decade, living frugally, giving his salary to poor relatives, and supporting his family on borrowed land. He was a devout Buddhist vegetarian in his later years. He died at sixty-two, and the emperor mourned him, granting posthumous honors and a burial. His works include "Collection of Mourning Clothes," "Continued Biography of the Pei Family," and others.

source: He also wanted to compile "Qi Liang Chun Qiu" and had started drafting it, but he died before it could be completed. His son Pei Jian was promoted to Tongzhilang. Gu Xie, whose courtesy name is Zhengli, is from Wu County, Wu County. The seventh-generation grandson of Gu He, Sikong of the Jin Dynasty. Gu Xie lost his father when he was young and was raised with his mother in his grandfather's house. My maternal grandfather Zhang Yong, Youguanglu of the Song Dynasty, once took his nephew and grandson to visit Huqiu Mountain. Gu Xie was only a few years old. Zhang Yong stroked him and said, "What do you want to play?" Gu Xie replied: My son just wants to live in seclusion in the mountains and forests. Zhang Yong sighed and said: The prosperity of the Gu family depends on this son. When he grew up, he was studious and was praised for his ability to concentrate. There are many wise and knowledgeable people in the Zhang family, and his brother-in-law, Zhang Sui, respects him even more. He began to serve as an official in Yangzhou, engaged in history, and was also a doctor of Taixue. As a scholar, Minister Shen Yue saw the policy essay he wrote and praised him: "Since the Eastern Jin Dynasty, there has been no such work." He was moved to the position of Zuo Changshi of the Ancheng Kingdom, and concurrently the court official. When the Taiwei King of Linchuan heard of his name, he called him to be the secretary, so he served Xifeng Hou Zhengde to study. Zhengde was appointed governor of Brazil and Zitong counties, and Gu Xie was appointed magistrate of Andu county. Before arriving at the county, his mother died.
target: Gu Xie, courtesy name Zhengli, from Wu County, lost his father young and was raised by his grandfather. As a child, he expressed a desire for seclusion, impressing his maternal grandfather. He was studious and praised for his concentration. He began his career as a historian in Yangzhou and later as a Taixue doctor. Minister Shen Yue praised his policy essay as unmatched since the Eastern Jin. He served in various roles, including as a magistrate and military advisor.

source: The minister's knowledge is not as good as that of Shao Shao and Yi Zuo. Although he does not know how to judge others, if he remains silent, he is afraid of making mistakes that will bury his talents. That is to say, he was summoned and appointed as the minister of Tongzhi Sanqi, and concurrently as Zhongshu Tongshi Shiren. He was moved to the infantry school captain, guarded by Honglu Qing, and became the regular servant of Sanqi outside. The positions of Qing and Shiren remained the same. He died in the eighth year of his reign at the age of seventy-three. Emperor Gaozu mourned and remembered him, and wrote a letter from Shao: "I was a member of the imperial family, a regular servant of Sanqi, a minister of Honglu, and a general secretary of Zhongshu. I was honest and self-respected. I never faded even when I was old. I stayed in the palace for a long time and was praised by people both inside and outside for my good deeds." Passed away suddenly, sadly missed. Can't stop. He has no close relatives, which makes people even more sad. After getting dressed and putting the coffin in, he immediately sent the coffin back to his hometown, built a cemetery coffin and paid for it, and tried his best to get everything done. You can posthumously give him a casual knight as a permanent attendant, so that he can express his condolences. Mi's nickname is Wen Zi. When Gu Xie was young, he was upright, upright and ambitious. When he first took office as Tingweizheng, his clothes were thin in winter. Ji Fadu, the minister of the temple, said to people: I would like to give the short coat I am wearing to Shou Lang. I am afraid that Shou Lang will not be able to accept the food and clothing given by others. I didn't dare to give him the short coat. When he took office, his fellow officials all decorated their houses. Gu Xie stayed in the official office for sixteen years, providing food and clothing and did not change the previous situation. The disciple came to see Gu Xie for something. Knowing that he was honest, he did not dare to give him a generous gift. He only gave him 2,000 yuan. Gu Xie became angry. He was beaten twenty times with a rod. From then on, anyone who came to him for trouble would never give him a gift. Since the death of his parents, he has been a vegetarian all his life. When he was young, he was engaged to his uncle's daughter. Before they got married, Gu Xie's mother died and he did not marry her after the mourning period expired. When she was more than sixty years old, the girl did not remarry. Gu Xie married her because of her affection. Although he got married in his later years, he had no children. Gu Xie is well-read and knows more about writing, animals, and plants. He compiled five volumes of "Yi Xing Yuan" and ten volumes of "Suo Yu", both of which have been circulated in the world. Xu Zhai, courtesy name Shixiu, was from Tan, Donghai.
target: At sixty, he was recommended for his conduct and knowledge, though he remained indifferent to fame. He was appointed as a minister and died at seventy-three. The emperor mourned him, noting his honesty and lack of close relatives. Gu Xie was known for his integrity, refusing gifts and living frugally. He married his uncle's daughter in his sixties, having no children. He was well-read and compiled works like "Yi Xing Yuan" and "Suo Yu.". Xu Zhai, courtesy name Shixiu, from Donghai, was studious and known for his innovative writing.

source: Xu Zhai, courtesy name Shixiu, was from Tan, Donghai. My grandfather Pingdao was the prefect of Hailing in the Song Dynasty. His father surpassed him. In the early years of Tianjian, he often served as an official on horseback. Xu Gan was young and eager to learn. When he grew up, he read books on classics and history. The writing is so new and varied, and doesn't stick to the old style. He started as a doctor of Taixue and moved to Sima Zuowei. At this time, King Gang of Jin'an went out to garrison the stone. Emperor Gaozu said to Zhou She: I am looking for a person for me who is good at literature and has good character. I want him to associate with Jin'an and accompany him. Zhou She said: My cousin Xu Go is humble in appearance and may not be able to wear more clothes, but he is capable of doing this job. Emperor Gaozu said: If Wang Can had talent, there would be no need to pick on his appearance.
target: He served as a Taixue doctor and was recommended by Zhou She to accompany Prince Jin'an, despite his plain appearance. He held various posts, including as a magistrate and military advisor.

source: The king was granted the title of crown prince, and Xu Xie was transferred to the family order and also in charge of the records. Soon he led the army. Xu Zhi's style was different from the tradition, and everyone in the palace imitated him, and the title of "gong style" came from Qian. When Emperor Gaozu heard about this, he was furious and summoned Xu Gou to scold him. When he saw him, he was very responsive and polite, and Emperor Gaozu's anger disappeared. So I asked him about the meaning of the Five Classics, then about the history of the past dynasties and the miscellany of hundreds of schools of thought, and finally about Buddhism. Xu Zhong made many comments and responses, and Gao Zu was even more amazed, and he became more and more close to him, and his favor increased day by day. Zhu Yi, the leader of the army, was unhappy and said to those close to him: "Xu Sou is coming in and out of the two palaces and is gradually threatening me. He must be transferred elsewhere as soon as possible." So he took the opportunity to report to Emperor Gaozu: Xu Gan is old and loves mountains and rivers. He wants to go to a county so that he can rest in peace. Emperor Gaozu thought that Xu Cai wanted to do this, so he summoned Xu Gao and said, "Xin'an has great mountains and rivers. Ren Fang and others have governed this place before. I am doing nothing to govern this county." After three years of Zhongdatong, he became the prefect of Xin'an. After arriving in the county, he managed affairs fairly and quietly, taught the people etiquette and righteousness, and encouraged and supervised farmers and mulberry trees. Within a year, the customs changed. After his term of office expired, he returned to the court and was appointed as the concubine and general Rongzhao. At this time, Duke Lincheng married his wife Wang, who was the niece of Concubine Taizong. Since the Jin and Song dynasties, on the third day of the first marriage, the bride pays homage to her parents-in-law, and all the guests watch. This is according to the records of "Spring and Autumn". Ding Chou and his wife Jiang arrived. On Wuyin day, Duke Zhuang sent the officials and wives to meet each other and used coins. Wuyin was Ding Chou's second time, so according to this record, the ceremony officials said that the rule should remain the same. Taizong asked Xu Gao, and Xu Gao said: "Etiquette" records that the bride paid homage to her parents-in-law at dawn. "Miscellaneous Notes" also said that when the bride paid homage to her parents-in-law, her brothers and sisters were all standing in the hall. It was precisely because the bride was from a foreign sect and had not yet been examined and ordered, so she stopped attending court to observe her seven virtues. The father-in-law received the foreign guests, the mother-in-law led the female guests, and a grand ceremony was prepared. In modern times, brides have a kinship relationship with their parents-in-law and do not look at each other. The wife is the niece of the concubine and has an alien marriage. The etiquette of visiting her should be omitted. Taizong listened to his advice. Later, he was awarded the title of Prince Zuowei. In the third year of Taiqing, Hou Jing captured Taicheng and sent Taizong to live in Yongfu Province. The thieves rushed in and raised their troops to the palace. The palace guards fled and no one was willing to stay. Xu Zhai stood alone and solemnly without moving, and slowly said to Hou Jing: "The Duke of Hou is supposed to bow before you, how can you do this?" Hou Jing was impressed by his fierceness.
target: His writing style, known as "gong style," was imitated in the palace, initially angering Emperor Gaozu but later earning his favor. Zhu Yi, feeling threatened, had Xu Zhai appointed as prefect of Xin'an, where he governed fairly and improved customs. He later served as a general and advisor on marriage rituals, advising the emperor on proper etiquette. During Hou Jing's rebellion, Xu Zhai stood firm, impressing Hou Jing with his fierceness.

source: Hou Jing was impressed by his fierceness. Hou Jing then paid homage to him, and from then on he was often afraid of Xu Gao. Taizong succeeded to the throne and was awarded the title of General Zuowei, but Xu Gao refused to accept the title. Later, Taizong was imprisoned, and Xu Zhai could not go to court. He died of a gas disease at the age of seventy-eight. The eldest son, Xu Ling, is the most famous. Bao Quan, whose courtesy name is Runyue, is from Donghai. His father, Bao Ji, was consulted by the king of eastern Hunan to join the army. Bao Quan was well-read in historical and biographical books and was good at writing both rhymed and non-rhymed articles. He served Emperor Yuan when he was young and was promoted and appointed very early. After Emperor Yuan inherited the throne, Lei moved to Xinzhou as governor. In the third year of Taiqing, Emperor Yuan ordered Bao Quan to go to Xiangzhou to conquer Xiao Yu, the king of Hedong. Bao Quan went to Changsha and deployed neighboring cities to force Xiao Yu. Xiao Yu led his troops to attack Bao Quan. Bao Quan held on to the fence, but Xiao Yu could not conquer it. Bao Quan took advantage of his fatigue to attack again, and Xiao Yu was defeated. Bao Quan captured many of his soldiers and surrounded the city, but could not capture it for a long time. The emperor Shizu denounced Bao Quan's crimes and sent Pingnan General Wang Sengbian to replace Bao Quan as governor. When the monk argued with the army, Bao Quan was very surprised and said to the people around him: "With Wang Jingling's help in my strategy, I can pacify the bandits without any effort." Monk Bian entered the room, sat with his back to Bao Quan, and said, "Bao Lang is guilty, and I have ordered you to be imprisoned. Please don't have any hope based on the feelings of an old friend." So he showed Bao Quan the edict and locked him under the bed. Bao Quan said: "I am willing to plead guilty for delaying the attack of the king's army, but I am afraid that people in the future will think more of Quan's confusion." So Seng Bian petitioned to forgive Bao Quan for his delay in using the army. Shizu soon resumed his position and ordered him, Seng Bian and others to lead a fleet of boats from Yingzhou in the east to attack King Shaoling. After pacifying Yingzhou, Emperor Yuan appointed his eldest son Fang Zhu as governor and Bao Quan as chief historian to handle the affairs of the prefecture. Hou Jingmi sent generals Song Zixian and Ren Yue to attack Yingzhou with fine cavalry. Fang Zhuyu Bao Quan did not consider military affairs, but only gambled and drunkenly enjoyed himself. When thieves and cavalry arrived, the people rushed to report. Fang Zhuyu Bao Quan was playing games and did not believe it. He said: "Xu Wensheng's army is guarding Shumian, how can the thieves come?" Then many people were informed, so the city gates were closed. The thieves set fire to the city. No one dared to resist. The thieves' cavalry were able to enter the city and the city fell. The arrests of Fang Zhu and Bao Quan were sent to Hou Jing's office. Later, Hou Jing attacked Wang Sengbian in Baling, but failed to capture him. He returned after failure, so he killed Bao Quan in Jiangxia and sunk his body in Huanghuji.
target: He died at seventy-eight after refusing a general title. His eldest son, Xu Ling, was famous. Bao Quan, courtesy name Runyue, from Donghai, was well-read and skilled in writing. He served Emperor Yuan and was appointed governor of Xinzhou. He defeated Xiao Yu but was later accused of delaying the king's army and imprisoned by Wang Sengbian. He was forgiven and later served as chief historian in Yingzhou. The city fell due to neglect by Fang Zhu and Bao Quan, who were captured by Hou Jing. Bao Quan was killed in Jiangxia.

source: When Bao Quan went to serve as the governor of Nanchao, his friend dreamed that Bao Quan had offended Shizu and told Bao Quan when he woke up. Within ten days, Bao Quan was indeed arrested. Soon, he dreamed of Bao Quan walking on the water wearing a red official uniform, and told Bao Quan: "Don't worry, you will be exempted from guilt soon." He told the dream to Bao Quan. Bao Quan kept a secret record of the matter and was appointed again soon, and he fulfilled what was said in the dream. Bao Quan knew "Ritual" best and compiled forty volumes of "Xinyi", which was circulated in the world. Yao Cha, the official secretary of the Chen Dynasty, said: Ruan Xiaoxu often said: Zhongni discusses four subjects, starting with virtue and ending with literature. Most virtuous people advocate simplicity, while most literary people do not abide by the rules. Therefore, Wei Wan and Shi Fen have nothing to spread, and Qu Yuan and Jia Yi have no reputation for virtue. Like following Ziyou and Zixia, imitating Yan Hui and Ziqian, virtue and literature coexist, which can be seen in Pei Jiyuan.
target: He had prophetic dreams about his fate. He was an expert on "Ritual" and compiled forty volumes of "Xinyi.". Yao Cha noted that Ruan Xiaoxu observed that virtue and literature rarely coexist, but Pei Ziye exemplified both, combining the qualities of Ziyou, Zixia, Yan Hui, and Ziqian.

source: Yuan Ang, whose courtesy name was Qianli, was from Yangxia, Chen County. His grandfather, Yuan Xun, was a general who conquered captives and a prefect of Wu County in the Song Dynasty. His father, Yuan Hao, was a champion general and the governor of Yongzhou. In the early years of Taishi, he raised troops to support Prince Xun of Jin'an, but was defeated and killed. When Yuan Ang was five years old, his wet nurse hid him in Lushan Mountain. He left the mountain only when he was pardoned and moved to Jin'an. During the Yuanhui period, he was allowed to return to his hometown when he was fifteen years old. At the beginning, Yuan Pinqi was defeated and his head was sent to the capital and hidden in the arsenal. It was only now sent back. Yuan Ang cried and vomited blood and came back to life. His brother Yuan Yuzeng raised and educated him. Yuan Ang put on mourning clothes and built a house in the cemetery to live. Later, he and Yuan Tuan went to visit his uncle, Situ Yuan Can. Yuan Can said to Yuan Tuan: "He can behave like this because he is young and alone, so he knows that his title and title have their own place." In the early years of the Qi Dynasty, Wang Xing, the first champion of Ancheng, joined the army and moved to the post of chief warden, prince Sheren, and Wang Jianzhen, the military official's meritorious official. After the Wei army retreated, Wang Mao returned to Yingzhou and served as the chief minister of the auxiliary state and the governor of Xiangyang. When Emperor Gaozu raised a righteous army, Wang Mao consulted privately with Zhang Hongce and persuaded Emperor Gaozu to welcome Emperor He, but Emperor Gaozu did not agree to do so. These words are recorded in "Gaozu Ji". Emperor Gaozu sent the Yong army to advance, often sending Wang Mao as the vanguard. The army was temporarily stationed in Yingcheng. Wang Mao attacked and pacified Jiahu, defeated Guangzijin, Wu Ziyang and others, beheaded and cut off the ears of tens of thousands of people, and returned to Hanchuan to report his victory. After Ying and Lu were pacified, he followed the emperor's troops and became the vanguard of the army. The army was stationed in Moling. Shuhunhou sent General Wang Zhenguo to assemble the army at Zhuque Gate. The number of soldiers was said to be 200,000, and they crossed the sea to fight. Wang Mao, Cao Jingzong and others went to attack together and defeated the enemy. The army was allowed to pursue the fleeing enemies, and the corpses of the enemy soldiers were piled up to the height of the fence. Those who died by jumping into the Huai River were incalculable. Chase them all the way to Xuanyang Gate. After Jiankang City was pacified, Wang Mao was appointed as the general guarding the army, and was soon promoted to the rank of Shizhong and leading general.
target: When Emperor Gaozu raised a righteous army, Wang Mao consulted with Zhang Hongce about welcoming Emperor He, but Gaozu disagreed. Wang Mao served as vanguard, pacifying Jiahu and defeating Guangzijin and Wu Ziyang, beheading tens of thousands. After Jiankang City was pacified, he became general guarding the army, then Shizhong and leading general.

The thieves set fire to Shenhu Gate. Wang Mao led his army to Dongye Gate to respond to the rescue. The thieves fired arrows at them. Wang Mao whipped his horse and advanced, while the thieves fled back. Wang Mao believed that he had failed to control the traitors, so he petitioned to be relieved of his duties, but the emperor's generous Shao Ling did not agree. He was also given the title of general of the town army, and was granted the title of Duke of Wangcai County, with a settlement of 2,300 households. In the first year of the Han Dynasty, Chen Bozhi, the governor of Jiangzhou, rebelled. Wang Mao was appointed as envoy Chijie, regular servant of Sanqi, governor of Jiangzhou's military affairs, general in the southern expedition, and governor of Jiangzhou. He was given a set of drums and drums and went to conquer Chen Bozhi in the south. Bozhi defected to Wei. At that time, Jiujiang had just suffered from military turmoil, and the people wanted to return to farming. Wang Mao focused on farming to reduce civil service, so the people were content with agricultural production. In the fourth year, Wei invaded Mozhong again. Wang Mao was ordered by Emperor Shao to march westward, and Wei retreated. In the sixth year, he was promoted to the right servant of Shangshu, and he still served as a regular attendant. However, he refused to resign and took up the post, so he was appointed as a minister in charge and a general in charge of the Central Guards, leading Prince Zhan to serve. In the seventh year, he was appointed as a general of chariots and cavalry, and he was still appointed as Prince Zhan Shi. In the eighth year, he took his title as Kaifu Yitong Sansi and Danyang Yin, and continued to write poems.
target: He was granted the title of Duke of Wangcai County with 2,300 households. In the first year of the Han Dynasty, he conquered the rebellious Chen Bozhi. He later served as right servant of Shangshu, general of chariots and cavalry, and Kaifu Yitong Sansi. He died at sixty, receiving posthumous honors and the title Zhonglie.

source: The joy has reached its extreme, how can there be no sorrow? He soon fell ill and died within a few days. His son Zhen Zhou succeeded him. Because he did not observe etiquette during the funeral, he was reported to the government and transferred to Yue. Later, the emperor ordered him to stay in Lu Ye's post. He secretly colluded with soldiers from the Renwei Prefecture to join the army and Du Jing, planning to attack the prefecture city. Gai Xian, the governor, conquered them. Silang surrendered from Wei and was killed together with Zhenxiu. Cao Jingzong's courtesy name is Zizhen, a new savage. His father's name was Xinzhi, and he was a military general in the Song Dynasty. His official positions were general of conquering captives and governor of Xuzhou. When he was young, Cao Jingzong was good at horseback archery and loved hunting. He often went with dozens of teenagers to chase wild deer in the grassy swamps. Whenever many riders drove the wild deer, the wild deer mixed with people and horses. Cao Jingzong would shoot the deer in the crowd. People were afraid of hitting the horse's leg, but the wild deer was shot down with the sound of the bow string. Cao Jingzong took this as fun. When he was just twenty years old, Cao Xinzhi sent Cao Jingzong out of the state to handle affairs in Xinye. He was alone and had only a few followers. On the way, he was unexpectedly surrounded by hundreds of barbarians. Cao Jingzong brought more than a hundred arrows and galloped around to shoot arrows in all directions. Every time he fired an arrow, he killed a barbarian. The barbarians fled in all directions, so he gained fame for his courage and courage. He loved reading history books. Every time he read "Rang Ju" and "The Biography of Le Yi", he put down the book and exclaimed: A man should be such a person!
target: Cao Jingzong, courtesy name Zizhen, was a new savage. His father Cao Xinzhi was a military general in the Song Dynasty. Young Cao Jingzong excelled at horseback archery and hunting. At twenty, while traveling alone with few followers, he was surrounded by hundreds of barbarians but fought them off with arrows, gaining fame for courage. He loved reading history books, particularly admiring Rang Ju and Le Yi.

source: He loved reading history books. Every time he read "Rang Ju" and "The Biography of Le Yi", he put down the book and exclaimed: A man should be such a person! He was recruited to serve as an official in Xicao, but he did not accept the appointment. During the reign of Emperor Yuanhui of the Song Dynasty, he left the state with his father and went to the capital to Jiankang. He served as Feng Chao, Yuan Wai Lang, and was transferred to Shangshu Zuo Minlang. Soon after his father passed away, he left his job and returned to his hometown. After the mourning period expired, the governor Xiao Chiaxu appointed him as a champion soldier to join the army and concurrently as the prefect of Tianshui. In the early years of the founding of the Southern Qi Dynasty, the barbarians gathered in crowds to riot. Cao Jingzong marched east and west, capturing thieves and defeating the enemy many times during the battle. Xiao Qiang, the king of Poyang in the Qi Dynasty, served as the governor of Yongzhou, and he was also used as a conscript soldier to join the army. He also served as the prefect of Feng Yi, supervising the military affairs in Xiannan, and was appointed as the captain of the garrison and cavalry school. When he was young, he had a close friendship with fellow countryman Zhang Daomen. Zhang Daomen was the youngest son of Zhang Jing'er, the Southern Qi cavalry general, and served as the prefect of Wuling. Zhang Jing'er was killed, and Zhang Daomen was also implicated and executed in the county. His relatives and old officials did not dare to come to collect the body. Cao Jingzong sent people and ships from Xiangyang to Wuling to collect Zhang Daomen's body and bring it back for burial. The people in the village thought that Cao Jingzong was loyal. In the second year of Jianwu reign of Emperor Ming of the Southern Qi Dynasty, Tuoba Hong, the leader of the Northern Wei Dynasty, attacked Zheyang, and Cao Jingzong was appointed as a partial general. Every time he attacked a strong enemy and captured the enemy's formation, he always killed someone and captured him. Because of his meritorious service, he was awarded the rank of guerrilla general. In the fourth year, Taiwei Chen Xianda led the troops north to besiege Maquan. Cao Jingzong accompanied the army and led 2,000 soldiers to set up an ambush and defeated the 40,000 reinforcements led by Tuoba Ying of the Northern Wei Dynasty. After conquering the horse circle, Chen Xianda rewarded Cao Jingzong for his merits and ranked him last. Cao Jingzong retreated without any complaints. The leader of the Northern Wei Dynasty led an army to attack again. Chen Xianda escaped at night. Cao Jingzong guided him into the mountain road, so Chen Xianda and his son were able to escape safely. In the fifth year, Xiao Yan, Emperor Wu of Liang Dynasty, became the governor of Yongzhou. Cao Jingzong became deeply friends with him and invited him to his home many times.
target: During the Southern Qi Dynasty, Cao Jingzong served as prefect of Tianshui and fought against barbarian uprisings. He showed loyalty by retrieving the body of his friend Zhang Daomen after Zhang's father was killed. In the Jianwu years, he fought against Northern Wei invasions, defeating Tuoba Ying's 40,000 reinforcements with 2,000 ambush soldiers. He became close friends with Xiao Yan (Emperor Wu of Liang) when Xiao served as governor of Yongzhou.

source: At that time, the world was in turmoil, and Emperor Wu of Liang also wanted to pay attention to Cao Jingzong. In the early years of the Yongyuan reign of Donghun Hou of the Southern Qi Dynasty, Emperor Wu of Liang asked Cao Jingzong to be appointed as the champion general and the prefect of Jingling. When Emperor Wu of Liang raised his troops to the east, Cao Jingzong gathered his troops and sent his confidant Du Sichong to persuade Emperor Wu of Liang to first welcome Xiao Wei, King of Nankang, to ascend the throne in Xiangyang, and then send troops. This was a sound strategy. Emperor Wu of Liang did not adopt this opinion, and the matter was recorded in "Gaozu Ji". Emperor Wu of Liang led his troops to Jingling and sent Cao Jingzong and champion general Wang Mao across the Yangtze River to besiege Yingcheng. From February to July, the Yingcheng defenders surrendered. He also led the troops as the vanguard to advance to Nanzhou, and led the horse infantry to advance towards Jiankang. On the way, the army was stationed in Jiangning. Donghun Hou's general Li Jushi led a heavy army and was stationed in Xinting. On this day, a thousand elite cavalry were selected to temporarily station in Jiangning. Cao Jingzong's troops had just arrived and the fortress had not yet been built. Moreover, the troops had been marching for a long time, and their weapons and armor were damaged and leaked. Seeing the situation of Cao Jingzong's troops, Li Jushi underestimated the enemy's carelessness, so he took advantage of the situation and beat the drums and shouted to attack Cao Jingzong. Cao Jingzong put on his armor and mounted his horse to fight. As soon as they engaged, Li Jingzong abandoned his armor and fled. Cao Jingzong captured all Li Jingshi's soldiers and horses, and took advantage of the victory to chase the enemy with drums. They advanced to Zaoying Bridge and built a fortress. Cao Jingzong, Wang Mao and Lu Sengzhen divided their forces to attack together, and defeated Wang Guozhen at Dahang.
target: When Emperor Wu raised troops, Cao Jingzong gathered his forces and served as vanguard, besieging Yingcheng for months until surrender. He advanced toward Jiankang, defeating Li Jushi at Jiangning despite his troops' worn equipment.

source: The sergeants in Cao Jingzong's army were all fierce and cunning scoundrels, and the residents on both sides of the imperial street were all from wealthy families. The sergeants robbed property and plundered their children, and Cao Jingzong could not stop them. When Emperor Wu of Liang entered the new city and solemnly declared military discipline, the plundering incidents subsided slightly. Cao Jingzong and other military commanders besieged the six gates. After the city was broken, he was appointed as a regular servant of the scattered cavalry and a general of the right guard. He was granted the title of Marquis of Xiangxi County and was granted the title of 1,600 households. So he moved to Chijie, the governor of Ying, the military commander of the two states, the general of Zuo, and the governor of Ying state. In the first year of Tianjian, Emperor Gaozu of Liang Dynasty, he was promoted to General Pingxi and changed to Marquis of Jingling County. Cao Jingzong was in Yingzhou, buying and selling goods to accumulate money, and built residences in the south of the city. He opened streets from the east of the Changdi to the north of Xiakou, several miles long from east to west, and the people were extremely disgusted by the brutality of his troops. In October of the second year of Tianjian, the Northern Wei Dynasty invaded Sizhou and surrounded Cai Daogong, the governor. At that time, the offensive of the Northern Wei Dynasty was becoming more and more serious day by day. People in the city had to carry door panels on their backs to guard against arrows to collect water. However, Cao Jingzong sat at home and watched without sending troops to rescue. He only went out to hunt in a show of force. After Sizhou City was captured, Cao Jingzong was impeached by the Japanese imperial censor Zhongcheng. Because Cao Jingzong was a hero, Emperor Wu suppressed the matter and did not sanction it. Instead, he recalled Cao Jingzong to serve as a guard. After Cao Jingzong arrived in Beijing, he was appointed as a regular servant of Sanqi and a general of right guard. In the fifth year, Tuoba Ying of the Northern Wei Dynasty invaded Zhongli and besieged Chang Yizhi, the governor of Xuzhou. Emperor Wu issued an edict and ordered Cao Jingzong to lead the army to rescue Chang Yizhi. Wei Rui, the governor of Yuzhou, also participated in this military operation and was controlled by Cao Jingzong. The imperial edict ordered Cao Jingzong to station himself at Daoren Island and wait for all the armies to gather before marching together. Cao Jingzong repeatedly requested that his troops be allowed to occupy the end of Shaoyang Island first, but Emperor Wu refused. Cao Jingzong planned to win this battle alone, so he defied the imperial edict and marched forward. A sudden storm blew up, and many soldiers fell into the water and drowned. He had no choice but to return to defend the previous station. After Emperor Gaozu learned about the news, he said: This is the condition for being able to defeat the thief. Cao Jingzong cannot move forward. It turns out to be God's arrangement! If Cao Jingzong went alone and the fortress could not be built in time, he would definitely suffer an embarrassing defeat. Now we can wait for all the armies to advance at the same time, so that we can achieve a complete victory. When Wei Rui arrived, he and Cao Jingzong advanced to station troops in Shaoyangzhou and built a fortress more than a hundred steps away from Wei City.
target: After the city fell, he was made Marquis of Xiangxi County with 1,600 households. In the Tianjian years, he was promoted to General Pingxi and Marquis of Jingling County. During the Northern Wei invasion of Sizhou, he was impeached for not sending timely rescue but was protected by Emperor Wu. In the fifth year, when Tuoba Ying invaded Zhongli, Cao Jingzong led rescue forces. Despite imperial orders to wait, he attempted to advance alone but was turned back by storms.

source: Yang Dayan, the general of Wei, built a city on the north bank facing the bridge to make the road for transporting grain smooth. Whenever herdsmen from the south came across the bank to gather livestock, they were all captured by Yang Dayan. Cao Jingzong then recruited more than a thousand brave soldiers and crossed the river to build a fortress a few miles south of Yang Dayan City. Cao Jingzong personally built and rammed it. Yang Dayan led his troops to attack, and Cao Jingzong fought and defeated him, so he was able to build a fortress. Cao Jingzong sent general Zhao Cao to guard the new base, so he called this military base Zhao Cao City. From then on, herders could graze their cattle here at will. Yang Dayan sent troops to plunder from time to time, but was often captured by Zhao Cao. Prior to this, Emperor Wu had ordered Cao Jingzong and others to build tall warships in advance, so that the tall buildings on the ship would be as high as the bridge, in order to implement the fire attack plan. Order Cao Jingzong and Wei Rui to attack an enemy bridge each, Wei Rui to attack the Wei army's south bridge, and Cao Jingzong to attack the north bridge. In March of the sixth year, the spring water rose, and the water in the Huaihe River surged six or seven feet high. Wei Rui sent generals Feng Daogen, Li Wenzhao, Pei Sui, Wei Ji and others under his command to land on warships, attack the Northern Wei garrison on the shore and annihilate them all. Cao Jingzong took the opportunity to order all the troops to beat drums and shout together. In the chaos, they boarded the Wei army's camp. The sound of killing shook the world. Yang Dayan burned the camp on the west bank, and Tuoba Ying abandoned the city on the east bank and fled. The various camps of the Wei army collapsed one after another, and they all abandoned their weapons and armor and jumped into the river to drown. The Huai River was blocked and could not flow. Cao Jingzong ordered the army commander Ma Guang to follow Yang Dayan to the shore of Xuisui River. During the more than 40 miles of the road, the corpses of the fallen enemies were piled on top of each other. Chang Yizhi sent troops to pursue Tuobaying to Luokou, but Tuobaying fled into Liangcheng alone. Along the Huaihe River for more than a hundred miles, there were piles of dead bodies everywhere, more than 50,000 Wei soldiers were captured alive, and the food and equipment of the Wei army were seized, which were piled up like mountains, including countless cattle, horses, donkeys, and mules. Cao Jingzong then collected more than 10,000 prisoners alive and thousands of horses, and sent people to escort them to the capital to offer victory. Emperor Gaozu issued an edict and ordered Cao Jingzong to return to his own army. Cao Jingzong's troops lined up in victory and returned to the court. They were granted an additional 400 households. Together with the previous grants, the total was 2,000 households. They were promoted to Dukes.
target: He eventually joined Wei Rui at Shaoyangzhou, building fortresses near Wei positions. In the sixth year, during spring floods, they launched a coordinated attack, burning Wei camps and causing massive casualties. Over 50,000 Wei soldiers were captured alive, with countless supplies seized. Cao Jingzong was promoted to Duke with 2,000 households.

source: The imperial edict ordered the officials to be worshiped as ministers and leading generals, and an agitating band was given to them. Cao Jingzong was a self-reliant man who relied on his merits and success. Every time he wrote a letter, he would not ask others if there were words he could not write, but would write them according to his own imagination. Even when dealing with high-ranking officials, he was never polite and modest; only Wei Rui was older than him and was a famous figure in the same state. Cao Jingzong showed great respect to him and attended the imperial banquet with him. Cao Jingzong was also polite and humble, and Emperor Wu praised him for it. Cao Jingzong was a womanizer. He had hundreds of singing prostitutes, wives and concubines at home, all of whom were dressed in extremely luxurious brocade.
target: Cao Jingzong was self-reliant and proud, showing respect only to Wei Rui. He was a womanizer with hundreds of concubines, impatient and restless, fond of drinking and hunting. He died at fifty-two while traveling to assume the governorship of Jiangzhou.

source: In the seventh year, Cao Jingzong was transferred to Shizhong, General of Zhongwei, and Governor of Jiangzhou. He died on the road when he went to take office at the age of fifty-two. The emperor issued an edict granting him funeral money of 200,000 yuan and 300 bolts of cloth. He was also given the posthumous title of General Zhengbei, Yongzhou Governor, and Kaifu Yitong. His posthumous title was Zhuang. Cao Jiao, Cao Jingzong's son, succeeded his father's title. Liu Qingyuan was named Wenhe and was born in Hedong Jie. Uncle Yuan Jing was a Taiwei of the Song Dynasty. Qingyuan was appointed from home as the chief administrator of Yingzhou. In the early years of Qi, he was appointed as Shangshu Duguanlang, Da Sima Zhongbing joined the army, General Jianwu, and Prefect of Wei Xing. The county suffered a flood and the residents were washed away by drifting water. The lower-level officials requested that the people be moved to the city to offer sacrifices. Qingyuan said: How can the city predict the rainfall from the sky? I heard that the rivers will only rise for three days, so there is nothing to worry about. He merely orders the earth to be pounded to make it solid. Soon the flood passed and the people admired him. He went to Beijing and served as the captain of Changshui School, and also served as Pingbei Green Affairs Joining the Army and Xiangyang Order. Emperor Gaozu went to Yongzhou and asked Du Zang, a native of Jingzhao, about finding an official who could serve as the head of the state. Du Zan recommended Qingyuan. Emperor Gaozu said: Wen He and I already know him, but I am asking about other people whom I don't know well. So he was recruited to work as a historian. At this time, Qi Zheng was in a lot of trouble. Qingyuan said to those close to him: If the world is going to be in chaos, heroes will definitely rise. The person who protects the people and establishes hegemony is probably our monarch, right? Therefore, he tried his best to assist Gaozu loyally. When Gaozu's rebellion rose, Qingyuan often strategized and became the mastermind. In the first year of the Zhongxing Dynasty, Xi Tai selected him as Huang Menlang and was promoted to champion general and a long history of the Eastern Campaign. He followed the army eastward and took the lead in fighting. When Emperor Gaozu was walking among the forts and saw the neat buildings where he stayed in Qingyuan, he often sighed and said: If everyone is like him, what do I have to worry about? After the city of Jiankang was pacified, he went to Beijing and served as a minister, leading the general of the front army and the prefect of Huailing and Qichang counties. There was a fire in the city at night, and the palace was panicked. At that time, Gaozu was living in the palace, collected all the keys, and asked everyone where Liu Shizhong was. When Qingyuan came, he handed all the keys to him. This is how he was trusted by Emperor Gaozu. After the establishment of Gaozu's Bafu, he was appointed as Taiwei and Zhonglang. Emperor Gaozu accepted the abdication and ascended the throne. He was promoted to the rank of regular attendant of Sanqi, general of right guard, general of conquering captives, and the title of Marquis of Chong'an, with a land of 1,000 households.
target: Liu Qingyuan, named Wenhe, was born in Hedong Jie. He served as chief administrator of Yingzhou and prefect of Wei Xing, where he handled a flood wisely. Emperor Gaozu recruited him as a historian, and Qingyuan became a loyal strategist during Gaozu's rebellion. After Jiankang was pacified, he served as minister and was deeply trusted by Gaozu, who entrusted him with palace keys during a fire. After Gaozu ascended the throne, Qingyuan became Marquis of Chong'an with 1,000 households. He served as governor of Yongzhou, where Emperor Gaozu praised him for eliminating western concerns.

source: Emperor Gaozu held a banquet in the new pavilion to see him off, and said to him: "You have returned home in fine clothes, and I no longer have the worries of looking westward." In the seventh year, he was recruited as a general to protect the army and led the prince's concubine. He did not take up any post, but was promoted to the rank of regular servant of Tongzhi Sanqi, general of Youwei, and general of Xiaoqi of the right. When he arrived in Kyoto, it was when Wei Su asked for surrender in advance of the city. He was ordered by the emperor to provide assistance, so he guarded Huaiyin with integrity. The Wei army retreated. In the eighth year, he returned to Kyoto and was promoted to Sanqi Changshi, Prince Zhanshi, and Yongzhou Dazhongzheng. In ten years, he was promoted to the rank of servant and general, and was given support and a set of drums and instruments. In the twelfth year, he was promoted to general Anbei, captain of Ningman, and governor of Yongzhou. Qingyuan served in Honshu again. He further improved his integrity and the hearts of scholars and common people all attached to him. He died in the spring of the next year at the age of fifty-seven. The imperial edict stated: "Remembering those who were loyal until the end of their lives is a legal system that existed during the time of the previous kings; it is a common practice for emperors to ceremoniously treat their subordinates with courteous treatment in all dynasties." Envoy Chijie, the commander-in-chief of the four prefectures of Yong, Liang, Southern Qin, and Northern Qin, as well as the military forces of Jingling in Yingzhou and Suijun in Sizhou, general Anbei, captain of Ningman, governor of Yongzhou, and Liu Qingyuan, the founder of Yundu County, are profound and knowledgeable, and their thoughts are smooth and elegant. From the earliest days of creation, he has participated in and followed the planning and management of national affairs; as far back as the peace of the world, he has worked hard in forbidden travel. Now that I have returned to rule Xifan, I was just about to carry forward my political ideas, but suddenly passed away, which makes me extremely sad. An honorable appointment should be added to him in recognition of his great merits. He can be posthumously granted the titles of Shizhong, General of the Central Army, and the Third Division of Kaifu Yitong. The rituals of Drum Music and Marquis are the same as those originally conferred. The nickname is Zhonghui. Two hundred thousand coins and two hundred pieces of cloth were given for the funeral. After the body of the deceased was transported back to Kyoto, Gao Zu came out of the palace to mourn. His son Liu Jin succeeded him. At the beginning, Qingyuan's cousin, General Wei Shilong, once said to Qingyuan: I once dreamed that the Taiwei gave me a mattress, and my status was second only to that of Taisi. Later, I happened to dream of giving my mattress to you. It seems that you will definitely honor your ancestors. By this time, Qingyuan had inherited the honor held by Shilong. Yao Cha, Chen's official minister, said: Wang Mao and Cao Jingzong: Although Liu Qingyuan has been a military leader for generations, they have not shown outstanding integrity. When the Liang Dynasty rose, they relied on the last light of the sun and the moon to realize their personal ambitions. Pei left relics in Fang, Shao and other places, and recorded their achievements on bells and tripods. How great! In the past, Emperor Guangwu of the Han Dynasty protected and cared for meritorious officials, but only awarded official positions such as court invitations and special promotions. Kou, Deng, Geng, and Mai could not fully display their talents. However, Wang Mao and others were able to take turns serving as local governors, and their official positions were finally generals. The relationship between the monarch and his ministers was better than that of the previous generation.
target: He later returned to Kyoto and served in various high positions. He died at fifty-seven while serving as governor of Yongzhou again, receiving posthumous honors and the title Zhonghui. Yao Cha commented that Wang Mao, Cao Jingzong, and Liu Qingyuan, though military leaders, achieved great success during the Liang Dynasty's rise, with their accomplishments recorded on bells and tripods. Unlike Emperor Guangwu of Han who limited his officials, these men were able to serve as local governors and reach high military positions, demonstrating superior monarch-minister relations.

source: Liu Ji, whose alias is Huixu, is from Pengcheng. His father, Liu Sisi, became prominent in the Song Dynasty because he was a younger brother of Emperor Gaozu of the Song Dynasty, reaching the rank of Jin Ziguanglu. Liu Jilian had a very good reputation and had served as an upright official very early on. After Emperor Qi Gao accepted the abdication and ascended the throne of the emperor, he killed all the close relatives of the Song Dynasty. When he was about to kill Liu Jilian and others, Ji Lian was saved from death because the Grand Prime Minister Chu Yuan had always been very good with Zhilian. With his firm plea, Ji Lian was saved. During the Jianyuan period, Liu Ji was re-elected as Minister Zuocheng. In the early years of the Yongming Dynasty, Liu Weilian served as the internal history of Jiangxia County, and was promoted many times to the internal history of Pingnan Changsha County, the champion chief historian, the prefect of Guangling County, and was in charge of the affairs of the prefecture. Later, he was called to serve as the minister of Huangmen, and was transferred to the prince's concubine. During the Jianwu period, Liu Jilian served as the long history of Xiao Yaoxin in Pingxi and the prefect of Lu Su.
target: Liu Ji, also known as Huixu, was from Pengcheng. His father, Liu Sisi, rose to prominence in the Song Dynasty as a younger brother of Emperor Gaozu, reaching the rank of Jin Ziguanglu. Liu Ji had a strong reputation and served as an upright official early on. After Emperor Qi Gao ascended the throne, he killed many Song relatives, but Liu Ji was spared due to the intervention of Grand Prime Minister Chu Yuan. During the Jianyuan period, Liu Ji became Minister Zuocheng. In the Yongming era, he held various posts, including internal history of Jiangxia and Guangling counties. Later, he served as Huangmen minister and prince's concubine. During the Jianwu period, he was long history of Xiao Yaoxin and prefect of Lu Su.

source: Liu Erlian's nephew, Ji Xing Artificial Hehe, was consulted by Luwei to join the army. Wanghe was handsome, talented and eloquent, and Luwei valued him very much. Wang Hui was so arrogant that he even argued with Xiao Yaoxin to insult Liu Jilian in front of everyone. Liu Jilian was very unhappy about this. He secretly reported to Emperor Ming that Xiao Yaoxin had abnormal signs. Emperor Ming accepted his opinion and appointed Xiao Yaoxin as the governor of Yongzhou. Emperor Ming was deeply grateful to Ji Lian. Four years later, he appointed Liu Jilian as an auxiliary general and the governor of Yizhou, and ordered him to guard the upper reaches of Xiao Yaoxin.
