In March of the eighth year, Wu Jin, the governor of Jingzhou in the Wei State, led an army of 70,000 to invade and move away. They drove and forced the barbarians, and the barbarians crossed the desert river one after another to seek refuge with the Liang Dynasty. Some people argued that the barbarians had repeatedly become a scourge on the border and they could take this opportunity to get rid of them. Xiao Jing said: They are desperate and come to join us. It is not good to kill them. Moreover, when the Wei people came to invade our country, the barbarians often had conflicts with them. If all the barbarians were killed, then there would be no obstacle for the Wei army, and sending them away would not be a long-term solution. So he opened the gates of Fancheng and accepted the surrendered barbarians.
target: In the eighth year, when Wei's governor Wu Jin invaded, Xiao Jing accepted surrendered barbarians, defeating the enemy and burying the dead.

source: Xiao Jing therefore ordered Sima Zhu Siyuan, Ningman chief minister Cao Yizong, and Zhongbing soldier Meng Huijun to attack Yuanzhi in Jinggou. They won a complete victory and captured Yuanzhi's chief minister Du Jing alive. More than 10,000 of the enemy were killed, and the Han River was covered with floating corpses. Xiao Jing sent his soldiers to join the army, Cui Ji led the soldiers, fished out the corpses and buried them. When Xiao Jing first arrived in Yongzhou, he was exempted from the formalities and uniforms required to welcome him, so as not to disturb the officials and people of the state. After he took office, he built barracks and cities and fortresses, issued repeated warnings to strengthen border defenses, tried cases and lawsuits, and encouraged the people to farm and grow mulberry trees.
target: He built barracks, strengthened defenses, and encouraged farming, resulting in a peaceful and theft-free territory.

source: After he took office, he built barracks and cities and fortresses, issued repeated warnings to strengthen border defenses, tried cases and lawsuits, and encouraged the people to farm and grow mulberry trees. For a time, all counties and counties in the state changed their policies and encouraged themselves. The territory of Yongzhou became quiet and tidy. The land and water along the desert river totaled more than a thousand miles, and theft no longer happened. In the eleventh year, Xiao Jing was called up to serve as General Youwei and concurrently as stone garrison military officer. In the twelfth year, he was again appointed as envoy Chijie, supervising the military affairs of the five states of southern Yanzhou, northern Yanzhou, northern Xuzhou, Qingzhou, and Jizhou, general Xinwei, and governor of southern Yanzhou. In the thirteenth year, Xiao Jing was summoned as the leading general, on duty in the palace province, in charge of the profit and loss affairs of ten states, and received an increase of 50,000 yuan in salary every month. Xiao Jing has always been very personable and good at rhetoric. When he was in the court, he was watched and admired by everyone. Although he and Gaozu were cousins ​​in terms of kinship, Gaozu treated him with great courtesy. When encountering military affairs and national affairs, he would discuss decisions with him.
target: He was later recalled to court and served in various roles, including General Youwei. In the thirteenth year, he was summoned as leading general, receiving a salary increase. Xiao Jing was personable and well-spoken, and Gaozu treated him with great courtesy, consulting him on military and state affairs.

source: In the seventeenth year, Xiao Hong, the Taiwei and the governor of Yangzhou, the king of Linchuan, was dismissed for breaking the law. The emperor's Shaoshu said: Yangzhou must be managed and suitable people must be selected. The talents of Wu Huhou and Xiao Jing, the leading general of the army, are qualified for this position. General An You can be used to supervise Yangzhou and set up the assistant history. If the position of minister is still maintained, his residence will be used as the official residence. Xiao Jing's distant relative lived in Yangzhou. He declined the appointment so sincerely that he burst into tears, but Gaozu refused to allow his resignation. When Xiao Jing took office in Yongzhou, he was particularly famous for his clear-cut decisions, and his instructions were very strict. There was an old woman in the countryside. After she complained, she received instructions from Xiao Jing. When she returned to the county, the county officials did not send them out immediately. The old woman said: Xiao Jianzhou's talisman will burn your hands like fire. How dare you keep it! Xiao Jing was so awed by people. In the eighteenth year, Xiao Jing repeatedly petitioned the emperor to be relieved of his duties, but Gaozu did not agree. In the second year, Xiao Jing served as envoy Chijie, regular attendant of Sanqi, military commander of Yingzhou, Sizhou and Huozhou, general of Anxi, and governor of Yingzhou. Before setting off, Emperor Gaozu came to Xingjian Garden to bid farewell to Xiao Jing, for which he burst into tears. Gaozu returned to the palace and ordered Xiao Jing to preach a piece of music. Xiao Jing was known for his ability during his tenure. The counties of Chabao, Deng and Tongduo bordered the Wei State, and there were many thieves. After Xiao Jing conveyed the notice to the Wei State, the Wei State immediately burned the earthen forts defended by the thieves to protect the border and prevent any further invasion of the two counties. Four years later, Xiao Liang died in Jian maggot at the age of forty-seven.
target: He declined a promotion to Yangzhou governor but was eventually appointed. His strictness was legendary; an old woman noted his talismans were like fire. He died at age forty-seven, posthumously titled Shizhong. Xiao Chang, Xiao Jing's second brother, served in various roles, including governor of Hengzhou, but was dismissed for crimes.

source: In the thirteenth year, Xiao Chang was appointed as the Minister of Sanqi, and soon he took the original official position and concurrently served as Zongzhengqing. In the same year, Xiao Chang became the chief historian of An You. He was repeatedly moved to serve as the prince's concubine, Tongzhi Sanqi's regular attendant, and also served as Zong Zhengqing. Xiao Chang is also very understanding and understanding, but he likes to drink by nature, and after drinking, he often makes mistakes. When he was in office in the state department, he would often go in and out of other people's homes whenever he was drunk, and sometimes go to the wilderness alone. He also had no limits in using torture and killing. He killed someone when he was drunk, and then went to find that person again when he sobered up. Just like that, he didn't regret it. Finally impeached by relevant officials, Luchang was summoned to stay in the capital. He was very unhappy, so he drank all day long, became very weak, and suffered from heart disease. In Gentijianzhai, Luken stabbed himself with a knife, but his entourage quickly rescued him, but he did not die. In the seventeenth year, Xiao Chang died at the age of thirty-nine. His son's name is Xiao Boyan. Xiao Ang, whose courtesy name is Ziming, is Xiao Jing's third younger brother. In the early years of Tianjian, he was transferred to Situ Youchangshi many times, served as general of light vehicles, and supervised southern Yanzhou. At the beginning, when his brother Lu Liang was appointed as the governor of Yinchaye for the second time, his merits and favors were still in people's hearts. When Xiao Ang came to replace him, people compared him to Feng.
target: He was understanding but prone to drinking and making mistakes, often killing people while drunk without remorse. He died at age thirty-nine. Xiao Ang, the third brother, served as governor of Southern Yanzhou and Guangzhou, among other roles. He died at age fifty-three, posthumously titled Gong.

source: He served as the governor of Jiangzhou. In the first year of Datong, Xiao Ang passed away at the age of fifty-three. Mi shouted Gong. Xiao Yu, also known as Zizhen, is Xiao Jing's fourth younger brother. In the early years of Tianjian, he was awarded the title of Secretary Lang, and was moved to the position of Prince Sheren, Xima, Zhongshu Sheren, and Zhongshu Shilang many times. He often asked for self-examination, and Emperor Gaozu appointed him as the governor of Jinzhi County, Yongjia County, and Xiangyang County, but he refused to take office.
target: Xiao Yu, the fourth brother, served as Secretary Lang and other positions but frequently refused appointments.

source: He volunteered to go to the border states and counties. Emperor Gaozu thought that he was frivolous, unstable and lacked prestige, so he suppressed him and refused to allow him to go. Later he was appointed as the Minister of Huangmen. Xiao Yu wrote to the emperor and said: The statement I submitted at the beginning of summer was not approved. Looking back on the past, shame and fear, really makes me tremble in my heart. I heard that it rains heavily in the summer and is cold in the winter, and the villains still complain. Who can forget whether they are proud or frustrated in politics, whether they are favored or humiliated? With the help of past connections, I was able to join the ranks of royal relatives and gain attention; the opportunities for repaying my gratitude were already mixed, and I was facing a fate of poverty and frustration.
target: He wrote a memorial expressing shame and fear, requesting dismissal. Emperor Gaozu replied, criticizing his refusals and dismissing him.

source: Since you have submitted a request for dismissal, let's do what you requested. Xiao Yu was dismissed from his official position as a result. From then on, he paid homage to guests and never went to the court to see the emperor again. He was no longer notified to attend any national celebrations or funerals. In ordinary five years, Xiao Yu broke the law because he minted coins in his own home. The relevant officials reported the copy to the imperial officer. He was spared death and moved to Linhai County. As soon as he reached Shangyu, he was chased by the emperor's order, asking him to go back and receive the Bodhisattva's warning. After Xiao Yu arrived in the capital, he followed the requirements of etiquette very respectfully and carefully, changed his will, followed the rules, and fasted very carefully and cleanly. Emperor Gaozu admired him very much and appointed him as General Zhaoyuan and Prefect of Jinling County.
target: Later, Xiao Yu was exiled for minting coins but was recalled. He became a model of propriety and was appointed Prefect of Jinling County, where he implemented beneficial policies.

source: After Xiao Yu took office, he encouraged himself with his fame and achievements, eliminated too many excessive taxes and miscellaneous taxes, affirmed the legal charter, strictly controlled the cunning officials, and implemented a policy of good care for the people. As a result, within ten days, great changes took place in Jinling County. Soon, Xiao Yu fell seriously ill and passed away. The people in the county, whether they were walking or sitting, cried loudly after hearing the news. The streets and alleys were abuzz with noise, and more than 400 people gathered in the courtyard of the county to pay homage. There was a woman named Xia in the farmhouse by the field, who was over a hundred years old. When she heard the news of Xiao Yu's death, she came to the county government with her great-grandson in her arms and cried sadly, unable to control herself. It can be seen that the influence of Xiao Yu's favorable policies is so great. The people built temples and erected steles for Xiao Yu one after another to commemorate his merits. They went to the capital to ask for a favor for Xiao Yu. When the emperor came to Shao, he posthumously appointed Xiao Yu as the governor of Xiangzhou. Mi Hao Gong. Shi Chen said: "Zhidan owns the world, and rewards and appointments are generally given. Those relatives and related people are all appointed and treated with courtesy." Lu Liang's talent, insight and judgment can be beneficial to the government and assist in current affairs. He is probably a person with good grace and dignity in the You clan.
target: He died after a severe illness, mourned by the people, who built temples and steles for him. He was posthumously appointed governor of Xiangzhou, titled Gong. The historian comments that Xiao Jing's talent and judgment benefited the government, making him a person of grace and dignity in the You clan.

source: Liu Jun, whose courtesy name was Xiaobiao, was from Pingyuan. His father, Liu Ge, was the internal historian of Shixing in the Song Dynasty. When Liu Jun was just one year old, his mother took him back to his hometown. In the early years of Song Taishi, Qingzhou fell to the Wei people. When Liu Jun was eight years old, he was kidnapped and taken to Zhongshan. Liu Shi, a wealthy man in Zhongshan, sympathized with Liu Jun's plight and redeemed Liu Jun with five pieces of silk and taught him to write and read. The people of Wei heard that Liu Jun had relatives in Jiangnan, so they moved him to Sangqian. Liu Jun was eager to learn, his family was poor, and he lived in other people's homes, but he set his own study schedule. He often lit a torch made of hemp straw and read all night. Sometimes he fell asleep and the torch burned his hair. When he woke up, he resumed reading and stayed up all night. During the next year of Qi Yong, Liu Jun was able to return to Qi from Sangqian. He thought that his knowledge was not extensive, so he went to look for other books that he had never seen. When he heard that there was such a book in the capital, he would rush to ask for it to be borrowed. Cui Weizu of Qinghe called him a "book slut". At that time, Xiao Ziliang, the real fallen minister, was recruiting scholars, and Xingjun asked for a position in Xiao Ziliang's kingdom through others. Xu Xiaosi, the Minister of Civil Affairs, devalued him and refused to agree. He was only appointed as the minister of Nanhai King, but he refused to take up the post. By the time of Emperor Ming, Xiao Yaoxin was appointed governor of Yuzhou and appointed Liu Jun as the prisoner of the government. He was treated very generously. Xiao Yaoxin passed away soon, and Liu Jun was not allowed to raise his tune for a long time. In the early years of Tianjian, Liu Jun was called to the Western Province and served as the secretary of the school with He Zong, a bachelor. Liu Jun's brother Liu Longqing was serving as governor at the time. Su asked for leave to visit him. He was impeached by the official for transporting prohibited items without permission and was dismissed from office. He liked learning. When he was transferred to the governor's office, he was promoted to join the army as a product of Cao. He was provided with some books and asked him to copy them into a book by category and named it "Lei Yuan". Before the book was compiled, Liu Jun left because of illness. He built a house there and lived there because he visited Ziyan Mountain in Dongyang. Liu Jun wrote "Mountain Qi Zhi", and the writing is beautiful. Emperor Gaozu recruited literary people, and those with high talents were often recommended for promotion, often without qualifications. Liu Jun acted according to his own temperament and could not follow the ups and downs of others. Emperor Gaozu disliked him very much, so he did not use him. Liu Jun then wrote "Discrimination of Fate" to express his feelings. The article said:
target: Liu Jun, courtesy name Xiaobiao, was from Pingyuan. His father was Liu Ge. At age one, his mother took him home. During Song Taishi, Qingzhou fell to the Wei, and at eight, Liu Jun was kidnapped to Zhongshan. A wealthy man, Liu Shi, redeemed him and taught him. The Wei moved him to Sangqian. He was an eager learner, often reading by torchlight all night, sometimes burning his hair. During Qi Yongming, he returned to Qi. He sought out rare books, and Cui Weizu called him a "book slut." He sought a position under Xiao Ziliang but was devalued by Xu Xiaosi. He served under Xiao Yaoxin, who treated him generously. After Xiao Yaoxin's death, Liu Jun was long without promotion. In early Tianjian, he served as a secretary. He was dismissed for transporting prohibited items. He was later given books to compile "Lei Yuan," but left due to illness. He wrote "Mountain Qi Zhi." Emperor Gaozu disliked him for not following others, so he was not used. Liu Jun then wrote "Discrimination of Fate" to express his feelings.

source: Liu Jun acted according to his own temperament and could not follow the ups and downs of others. Emperor Gaozu disliked him very much, so he did not use him. Liu Jun then wrote "Discrimination of Fate" to express his feelings. The article said: The emperor once talked about Guan Ren with many famous sages, and lamented that there were talented people in charge but their official positions were not high. A friend was in the court at that time and heard this discussion, so he told me when he came back. I believe that the embarrassment and enlightenment of a scholar's situation are all determined by fate, so I respectfully describe the outline of destiny and my own ambitions. In my opinion, the governor is a talent sent from heaven, magnificent and outstanding, with outstanding talents and excellent character. He is really a hero in the country, and he is not just an ordinary divination and blessing. But his official position is only that of Shaofu Cheng, and he is forty-eight years old. How few people God has given him to govern! However, talented people do not have prominent official positions, while gluttonous, cruel and greedy people are in prominent official positions. This phenomenon has often made people sigh since ancient times, how can it be just Gong Ming? Therefore, no one can understand the difference between human nature and endowment, a lifetime of embarrassment and enlightenment, setbacks, failures, and successes. When talking about this issue, Wang Zhongren covered up its root cause, and Sima Zichang expressed his doubts. As for the poor and humble people who wear humble clothes and live in thatched huts, they must say that their destiny is controlled by God, and good and bad fortunes depend on luck. For wealthy and wealthy families, it is said that misfortunes and misfortunes do not distinguish between families, but are only caused by people's virtues. There was a lot of talk and arguments, and various opinions emerged one after another. Li Xiaoyuan talked about the foundation of fate but did not explain its changes. Guo Zixuan talked about the changes of fate but did not clarify its origin. Let me try to talk about this issue: The Great Way gives birth to all things, so it is called Tao; if it is born without any master, it is called nature. Nature means that all things grow, but they don’t know why they grow; all things get their own place, but they don’t know why they get their own places. He stirs up the world and creates all things, but he does not regard it as his own strength or his own achievements. There is no intention to nurture it while alive, and death is not caused by killing. Falling into the abyss and becoming a fish and dragon is not a punishment from God; rising to the sky and becoming a bird is not a favor from God. This Tao is boundless and broad, and all things change with it; but it is also deep and pure, and it never changes once it is created. Once it is created, it will not change. This is called destiny. Fate refers to the fate sent down from heaven. Destiny is determined in the dark and will never change. Ghosts and gods cannot predict it, and sages cannot examine it. The force that knocks down the mountains cannot be resisted, nor can the sincerity that causes the sun to return cannot be affected. If destiny comes quickly, it cannot be delayed for a moment, and if it comes slowly, it cannot be missed in advance. The most virtuous sages cannot transcend the destiny, and the wise people cannot escape the constraints of destiny.
target: The article "Discrimination of Fate" argues that a scholar's situation is determined by fate. It laments that talented people like Guan Ren have low positions. It states that the difference between human nature and endowment, and a lifetime of setbacks, cannot be understood. It discusses the concepts of Tao and nature, stating that destiny is determined in the dark and never changes. It lists sages like Jin Wengong and Confucius who could not escape fate. It mentions modern examples like Liu Shan and Liu Fa, who were talented but died in obscurity. It argues that nobility, longevity, and wealth are produced naturally, not by talent. It lists five areas of confusion regarding fate, including the belief that honor and disgrace are determined by people, that success comes from martial power, that good and evil are always rewarded, and that a country's success depends on its ruler. It concludes that a gentleman follows the right path, obeys heaven, and secures his own destiny, understanding that fate is beyond human control.

source: They understand that they are helpless in the face of fate, and understand that rise and fall, honor and disgrace do not depend on human wisdom and strength. Therefore, when blessings pass away, one does not look for them; when disasters come, one does not resist them; when one survives, one does not feel particularly happy; when one faces death, one does not feel sad. Living in a Yaotai mansion will not make him happy; living in an earthen house and a humble household will not make him worried. When you are in wealth, you will not be complacent or arrogant. You will not be restless and pursue what you want. If this is the case, how can there be articles like "A Tragedy Man Is Not Encountered" by Ma Qian of the Taishi Company and Dong Zhongshu, the Prime Minister of Jiangdu! After Liu Jun's "Distinction of Fate" was written, Liu Bo of Zhongshan wrote to refute Liu Jun. He wrote twice in total, and Liu Jun defended and analyzed each one one by one, and gave Liu Bo a reply. It happened that Liu Ma passed away, and he did not see Liu Jun's subsequent reply to the letter. Liu Jun then wrote a letter to reply to Liu Ma, who had passed away, describing the incident and his own feelings, saying: Liu Ma has already raised such an inquiry. It was a matter of a brother's death in my family, but he failed to reply to him in time. Soon, Mr. Liu Bo said goodbye to us forever and became a foreign object. His other remarks were hidden and never came out. Someone got these remarks from his home and showed them to me. Not all of his good words could be said, but the man had passed away. The handwriting of the article was still new, but the grass on the tomb had grown lush. I was sad for this, and I didn’t know who the tears were flowing to. Although life is short, like a horse passing by, time flies like an arrow, like water waves passing by, and lightning flashing. His character is like autumn chrysanthemums and spring orchids, and his good reputation will never fade away. So I wrote down the general story of this incident to repay Liu Zhou's kindness. If what Mo Zhai said about Du Bo knowing after his death is correct, and what Ye Yi discussed in the announcement room about ghosts and gods has come true, then I hope the trees in your cemetery can be like the trees on the tomb, pointing to the capital to express your longing for your motherland; I hope you can be like the springs in the mountains, which can flow in response to the sound of music. I can only hang the sword on the tomb like Yanling Jizi to repay my friends. What a pity I feel! Liu Jun's paper is not published because it is too long. Liu Jun once wrote "Automatic Preface", which roughly stated: I compare myself with Feng Jingtong. He and I have three aspects in common and four aspects that are different.
target: After Liu Jun's "Distinction of Fate" was written, Liu Bo of Zhongshan wrote to refute him. Liu Jun replied, but Liu Bo died before seeing the reply. Liu Jun wrote a letter to the deceased Liu Bo, expressing his sorrow. Liu Jun's paper was not published due to its length. Liu Jun wrote an "Automatic Preface" comparing himself to Feng Jingtong, listing three similarities and four differences.

source: Although Feng Jingtong was burned like Zhi Cao Hui Cao and died silently, he was admired by famous sages, and the aftertaste of his style exuded a rich fragrance that spread for a longer time. His reputation will be greater; my life is indifferent, my reputation is unknown, and no one in the world understands me. Once I leave this world, I will be like dead autumn grass, no one cares about me. This is the fourth different aspect. So I tried my best to write a narrative and leave it to those who care about me. Liu Jun lived in Shuyang, and many Wu and Hui people studied under him. Two years later, Liu Jun died at the age of sixty. His disciples gave him the nickname Mr. Xuanjing. Liu Bo, courtesy name Mingxin, was born in Weichang, Zhongshan. His grandfather Liu Yu, six generations ago, was posthumously awarded the title of Hussar General during the Jin Dynasty. Liu Bo was good at writing articles since he was a child. When he grew up, he became knowledgeable. At the beginning of the Qi Dynasty, he took up an official position and was invited to join the army. In the early years of the year, Xingtuo was worshiped as the military supervisor and joined the army in the imperial palace of Cong Wangji. He was ordered by Moling. He died during the period of dispatch. Xie Jiqing was from Yangxia, Chen County. His great-grandfather Xie Lingyun was the internal historian of Linchuan during the Song Dynasty; his father Xie Chaozong was the Huangmenlang at that time. All were famous in previous generations. Yao Jiqing was alert, intelligent and eloquent since he was a child. People called him a child prodigy at that time. Later, Xie Chaozong was demoted to Yuezhou for being convicted. When passing through Xintingzhu, Xie Jiqing couldn't bear to say goodbye to his father, so he threw himself into the river. The people around him hurriedly rescued him and saved him from drowning in the river. When it came time to mourn for his father, he mutilated his body with grief, exceeding the requirements of etiquette. After the mourning period expired, he was called to be the son of the country. Prince Wenhui of Qi personally presided over the examination. He said to Wang Jian, the prince of the country, who was offering wine, "Xie Jiqing's original specialty is to be proficient in metaphysics, and now he can be tested on the classics and meanings." Wang Jian asked the questions according to Prince Wenhui's wishes. Xie Jiqing answered the questions correctly and spoke fluently. Prince Wenhui praised Xie Jiqing greatly. Wang Jian said to people: Xie Chaozong has a successor. When Xie Jiqing grew up, he was very studious. He read extensively and had literary talent.
target: He lived in Shuyang, where many studied under him. He died at sixty, and his disciples gave him the posthumous name Mr. Xuanjing. Liu Bo, courtesy name Mingxin, was from Zhongshan. He was good at writing articles and knowledgeable. He held various official positions and died during a dispatch. Xie Jiqing was from Yangxia. His great-grandfather was Xie Lingyun. He was a child prodigy. He once threw himself into a river when his father was demoted. He was studious and had literary talent.

source: Xie Jiqing moved to the position of Sanqi Shilang, Zhongshu Lang, Guozi Doctor, Shangshu Zuocheng. Xie Jiqing understood the old affairs and routines in detail. Xu Mian, the servant, often asked him every time he encountered a problem. However, Xie Jiqing was open-minded by nature and did not stick to trivial matters. He would do things that suited his heart and was not bound by court laws. He once participated in a banquet at Le Youyuan and came back without getting drunk. He stopped the car at a roadside restaurant on his way home, raised the curtains, and sat in the car to have a drink with three attendants and grooms in front of the car. The onlookers at that time were like a wall. Xie Jiqing took it calmly as if nothing had happened. Later, Xie Jiqing was punished by a supervisor because he was wrapped up in the imperial office, wore shorts at night, and his disciples drank and shouted in the pavilion. He was found guilty and removed from his official position.
target: He held various official positions, including Censor. He was open-minded and not bound by court laws. He was once dismissed for misconduct.

source: Soon, Xie Jiqing was appointed as the crown prince and led the order, and was moved to the post of Zhenwei Nanping Wang Changshi. In the sixth year of Ordinary Years, the emperor issued an edict to send the leading general Xichang Hou Xiao Yuanzao to lead various troops in the Northern Expedition. Xie Jiqing petitioned to accompany the army in the Northern Expedition, and was promoted to Army Division Commander Shi and Jiaweirong General. The Northern Expeditionary Army was defeated in Guoyang, and Xie Jiqing was convicted and removed from his official position.
target: He later petitioned to accompany the Northern Expedition but was dismissed after the army was defeated.

source: Xie Jiqing has not yet waited for the imperial court to appoint him according to his seniority. He died of illness. He has a collection of essays spread throughout the world. Liu Xie, courtesy name Yanhe, was born in Ju, Dongguan. His grandfather Liu Lingzhen was the younger brother of Sikong Liu Zhouzhu. His father served as a captain of the Yue Cavalry School. Liu Xie lost his father in his early years. He was determined, fond of learning, and from a poor family. He did not get married, but relied on the monk Sengyou and lived with the monks. After more than ten years, he became proficient in the Buddhist Tripitaka. He divided the categories and arranged the collections.
target: He lived in seclusion, often drinking with friends. He died of illness. He had a collection of essays. Liu Xie, courtesy name Yanhe, was from Ju. He lost his father early, did not marry, and lived with a monk, becoming proficient in Buddhist scriptures.

source: The scriptures currently collected in Dinglin Temple were compiled by Liu Xie. In the early years of Tianjian, Liu Xiechu became an official and was invited by the court. Xiao Hong, the king of Linchuan in the Chinese army, chose him as a concurrent secretary. He also moved to the chariot and cavalry warehouse to join the army. Liu Xie came to Beijing to serve as Tai Mo Ling, and he had a clean and honest government record. He was also awarded the title of Renwei Nankang Wang Jishi, and also the general secretary of the Cambodian palace. At that time, the sacrifices offered to the Seven Temples had switched to fruits and vegetables, but cattle, sheep, and hogs were still used as sacrifices in the suburbs to worship heaven and earth and to worship the gods of agriculture and shrines. Liu Xie then went to the table and suggested that the rituals of offering sacrifices to heaven and earth in the suburbs should be changed in the same way as those of offering sacrifices to the seven temples, and that the sacrifices should also use fruits and vegetables. The emperor issued an edict and handed it over to the minister for deliberation, and finally decided to follow Liu Xie's report. Liu Xie was moved to the post of captain of the infantry school, but his concurrent post remained unchanged. Prince Zhaoming liked literary people. He admired Liu Xie and had close contacts with Liu Xie. At first, Liu Xie wrote fifty chapters in "The Literary Mind and the Carving of Dragons", discussing ancient and modern literary styles, which he compiled and arranged in order.
target: He became an official in early Tianjian. He suggested changing suburban sacrifices to fruits and vegetables, which was adopted. Prince Zhaoming admired him.

source: Liu Xie was moved to the post of captain of the infantry school, but his concurrent post remained unchanged. Prince Zhaoming liked literary people. He admired Liu Xie and had close contacts with Liu Xie. At first, Liu Xie wrote fifty chapters in "The Literary Mind and the Carving of Dragons", discussing ancient and modern literary styles, which he compiled and arranged in order. The preface to "Wen Xin Diao Long" says: Wenxin refers to the intention of writing an article. In the past, Juanzi wrote "Qin Xin" and Wang Tzu wrote "Qiao Xin". Because the meaning of "heart" expressed is honest and perfect, they used it as the title of their books. Since ancient times, writing articles has relied on carving and decoration. I am afraid it is based on the example of Ding Xi, so everyone calls writing articles Diaolong. Throughout the ages, the world has been filled with mediocre and sage people, and those who stand out only rely on their intelligence and strategy. Time will pass quickly, and human intelligence cannot last forever. If you want to pass down your reputation and career, you can only rely on writing. The human form symbolizes heaven and earth, and inherits nature from the five elements. The ears and eyes are like the sun and moon, and the voice is like wind and thunder. Human beings are beyond all things and can be regarded as the most supernatural. However, the human body is more fragile than grass and trees, but reputation can be stronger than gold and stone and last forever. Therefore, when a gentleman lives in the world, he wants to establish meritorious deeds and write books. This is not because he likes to argue, but because he has no choice but to build reputation! I was already in my thirties, and one night I dreamed that I was following Confucius southward with a red lacquer sacrificial vessel in my hand. When I woke up in the morning, I felt very happy. Great saints are rare to see, and now he condescended to appear in the dream of a nobody like me! Since the beginning of mankind, there has never been a saint like Confucius.
target: He wrote "The Literary Mind and the Carving of Dragons" in fifty chapters. The preface explains his motivation, stating that a gentleman wants to establish merit and write books. He dreamed of following Confucius.

source: There are already many people who have studied modern times and theses. For example, Emperor Wen of Wei Cao Pi's "Dian Lun", Chen Si Wang Cao Zhi's "Books with Yang De Zu", Ying Chang's "Lun on Wen Zhi", Lu Ji's "Wen Fu", Zhi Zhong Qia's "Wen Liu Bie Lun", and Li Hongfan's "Han Lin Lun". Each of them touches only one aspect of the article and rarely allows analysis from all angles. Some of them praise and criticize the talents of the time, some criticize the articles of previous sages, some generally point out the elegance and vulgarity of the article's intention, and some make a rough summary of the article's content. Emperor Wen of Wei's "Dian Lun" is detailed but incomplete; Chen Si Wang's "Yu Yang De Zu Shu" is quite clear but rambling; Ying Jian's "Wen Zhi Lun" has literary talent but is rough; Lu Ji's "Wen Fu" is cleverly conceived but trivial and messy; Zhi Zhongqia's "Wen Liu Bie Lun" is concise but impractical; Li Hongfan's "Han Lin Lun" is shallow and out of focus. There are also people like Huan Junshan, Liu Gongqian, Ying Jifu, Lu Shilong, etc., who have generally discussed the purpose of the article, and sometimes have better opinions. However, they have not been able to trace the roots from the branches and leaves of the trees, trace the waves of the water back to the source, and have not inherited the teachings of the sages of the previous generations. Therefore, they are not helpful in developing the ideas of future generations. The writing of "Wen Xin Diao Long" is based on the right path, imitating the saints, relying on the classics, referring to Wei Shu, and exploring changes from "Chu Ci". The key points of the article can be considered exhausted. As for discussing rhymed and unrhymed passages, we should distinguish them by style, deduce the origin of style, describe the evolution of style, explain the names of various styles, reveal the meaning of the names, select articles of various styles to comment on, explain the writing principles, and summarize the characteristics of various styles. The first part of this book has already clarified the outline. As for analyzing emotions and literary talents, comprehensively analyzing the context of the article, inferring "Shensi" and "Physical Nature", considering "Character" and "Dingshi", embracing "Additional Meetings" and "Tongbian", observing "Lythm" and "Lianzi", The rise and fall of the article is discussed in the "Chronology", the praise and criticism are discussed in the "Talent", the melancholy is expressed in the "Zhiyin", the emotion is expressed in the "Chengqi", and the feelings are expressed in the "Preface" to control each article. The details of the next chapter are also revealed. Arrange the content and determine the title. There are fifty chapters in total, which exactly matches the number of "Dayan" in "Yi". Among them, there are only forty-nine articles that discuss the function of articles.
target: He argues that articles are branches of classics. He criticizes previous literary critics like Cao Pi and Lu Ji for being incomplete or trivial. His book discusses rhymed and unrhymed passages, analyzes emotions and literary talents, and covers various aspects of writing. He sought evaluation from Shen Yue, who valued the book.

Shen Yue built a new study in his suburban residence, and Shen Yue ordered someone skilled in calligraphy to inscribe this poem on the wall of the study.

source: Then Liu Yao was appointed as the Minister of Zhongshu. Soon after, Liu Yao was appointed as King Shu of Pingxi Xiang to consult and join the army, and his concurrent posts of serving as a minister and author remained unchanged. He was also moved to the post of Minister Zuocheng. In the second year of Datong, Liu Yao died during his tenure at the age of fifty. Liu Yao paid attention to self-cultivation, was honest and frugal, and had no hobbies. By nature, he does not boast or comment on the merits of others. After seeing the Buddhist scriptures and teachings, he always practices compassion and can endure humiliation. In the seventeenth year of Tianjian, after his mother passed away, Liu Yao stopped eating fishy mutton for a long time and followed the precepts to eat only vegetables. When Liu Yao was dying, he left his last words. During the funeral, he would put on the monk's robes, load the coffin in an open car without a cover, transport it home and bury it in the ancestral cemetery. A random piece of land should be enough to accommodate the coffin. There should be no funeral feast. Liu Xing's sons all followed the instructions one by one. Liu Yao wrote many books from childhood to adulthood. He wrote five volumes of "Ya Ya", one volume of "Chu Ci Cao Mu Shu", two volumes of "Biography of Gao Shi", 30 volumes of "New and Old Records of the East Palace", and five volumes of "Ancient and Modern Four Books", all of which have been handed down to the world. Xie Zheng, courtesy name Xuandu, was from Yangxia, Chen County. His great-great-grandfather Xie Jingren was the minister Zuopushe in the Song Dynasty.

source: Xie Zheng was smart since he was a child, and he was considered to have excellent talents. He often said to his relatives: This child is not an ordinary person. What is worrying is his life span; if God gives him a long life, I will have no regrets. When Xie Zheng grew up, he was very handsome, fond of learning, and good at writing articles. Xie Zheng was initially appointed as Facao, King of Chisheng of Anxi, and then moved to the post of Sangong Ercaolang of the Ministry of Jin of Shangshu, the Prince of Yuzhang, and a member of Zhongshushe. He also moved to Pingbei to consult and join the army, and concurrently served as minister of Hongshan. His position remained unchanged. At that time, Mengjian, the king of Zhongshan in Wei, returned to the north, and he went to Wushanyao to pay his last respects. Emperor Gaozu asked his ministers to compose thirty rhymes of poetry at the banquet, and the poem was limited to three seconds to be completed. Xie Zheng finished the poem in a second. The diction was beautiful and Gao Dan read it again and again. Xie Zheng also wrote Linru Houyuan's "Release Essay", which was also appreciated by contemporary people.
target: He held various official positions. He once finished a poem in one second at a banquet, which Emperor Gaozu admired.

source: In the first year of Zhongdatong, Tangtang left his job to mourn the death of his father, and then his mother passed away. The emperor issued an edict and ordered Xie Zheng to resume his duties as General Zhenwei during the mourning period and return to Beijing to temporarily take charge of his original duties. After the mourning period expired, he was awarded the title of Minister Zuocheng. In the third year of Zhongdatong, Prince Zhaoming passed away, and Emperor Gaozu appointed Dong Wang as the crown prince. When the edict was about to be issued, Emperor Gaozu just summoned Shangshu Zuopushe He Jingrong, Xuanhui general Kong Shudi and Xie Man to discuss with them. At that time, Yaotang was still young and his position was not high, but he was appointed and favored very generously. In the fourth year, Xie Luan was promoted to Zhongshulang due to his meritorious service, while the positions of Hongluqing and Sheren remained unchanged. In the sixth year of Zhongdatong, Xie Zheng went to Beijing and served as Beizhonglangsui Tonggongshi and Chenluqie prefect. Xie Zheng died during his tenure at the age of thirty-seven. Xie Zheng's friend Langye Wangshuan collected his manuscripts and compiled them into twenty volumes.
target: He was appointed to discuss the appointment of a new crown prince. He died at thirty-seven. His friend Wang Shuan compiled his manuscripts.

source: Zang Yan, courtesy name Yanwei, was born in Ju, Dongguan. His great-grandfather Zang Tao was posthumously granted the title of Dr. Zuo Guanglu during the Song Dynasty. His grandfather Zang Ning was appointed Minister Youcheng during the Qi Dynasty. His father, Zang Leng, served in the army and joined the army. Zang Yan had a filial character when he was young. He became famous for his grief-stricken body during the mourning for his father. He lost his father and his family was poor, but he was diligent and studious and never put down his books. Initially, he was appointed as the Minister of King Ancheng, and then as the Permanent Minister. Zang Yan's uncle Zang Weizhen was appointed as the prefect of Jiangxia and took Zang Yan with him to take office. Zang Yan wrote "Tuenyou Fu" during the trip. Ren Fang admired it very much when he saw the "Tuenyou Fu". Zang Yan also wrote "Seven Calculations", and the diction is also very rich and gorgeous. Zang Yan was upright and upright by nature, and did not follow the rules. He had never paid a visit to Xu Mian in this world. Xu Mian wanted to get to know him, but Zang Yan still refused to pay him a visit.

He could read "The Classic of Filial Piety" and "The Analects of Confucius" by the age of seven. When he grew up, he was very talented and liked to write articles. His five-character poems were good at imitating Xie Kangle's style. Futing's father's friend Le'an Renfang admired him deeply and thought he was a genius. When Gaozu's rebel army came to the capital, Fu Ting rushed to Xinlin to meet the rebel army and pay homage to Gaozu. Gaozu was very happy to see him, called him "Yan Zi", and promoted him to join the army as Zheng Shuxing. Fu Ting was only eighteen years old at this time. In the early years of Tianjian, Fu Ting was awarded the title of military officer in the Chinese army. Fu Ting's residence was in Chaogou, and he lectured on "The Analects of Confucius" in his residence. Officials from all over the dynasty came to listen to him. Fu Ting moved to Jian Kangzheng, but was soon removed from office due to impeachment. After a long time, Fu Ting went to Beijing again and served as Shangshu Yi Caolang. He moved to Xizhonglang's Ji office and joined the army. He successively served as the order of Jinling and Wukang. After being relieved of his duties as county magistrate, he returned to the capital, built a house in the eastern suburbs, and stopped serving as an official. Fu Ting had a great reputation when he was young, and he got along well with people at that time. Most of the powerful ministers in important positions and idle officials without real power in the court had contacts with Fu Ting, so Fu Ting could not remain in retirement for a long time. At that time, Pushe Xu Mian asked for leave to go home because of illness. Fu Ting wrote to Xu Mian to gauge Xu Mian's thoughts. The letter said:

source: He successively served as the magistrate of Yongkang, Qiantang, and Wukang, but had no outstanding performance in managing county affairs, and was often impeached. After a long time, Yu Zhongrong was dismissed and granted the title of Prince Ancheng's Zhongji Office, and he was about to leave the capital to follow the royal palace.
