Wang Ji and Xie Jiqing were not in harmony with everyone at that time, so the three of them socialized together, drank as much as they wanted, and no longer paid attention to ethics. After a long time, Yu Zhongrong was appointed as a consultant to join the army and left the capital to serve as the magistrate of Yi County. When the turmoil broke out during the Taiqing period, Yu Zhongrong lived in Kuaiji and died of illness at the age of seventy-four. Yu Zhongrong copied thirty volumes of books by various scholars, twenty volumes of geography books of various schools, three volumes of Biography of Women, and twenty volumes of collected works. These books are all circulated in the world.
target: He was appointed as a crown prince through his uncle's request. He was knowledgeable but impulsive and liked to drink. He was friends with Wang Ji and Xie Jiqing. He died at seventy-four. He copied many books and wrote several works.

source: Yu Zhongrong only had similar personalities and good friendships with Wang Ji, Xie Jiqing and others. Wang Ji and Xie Jiqing were not in harmony with everyone at that time, so the three of them socialized together, drank as much as they wanted, and no longer paid attention to ethics. After a long time, Yu Zhongrong was appointed as a consultant to join the army and left the capital to serve as the magistrate of Yi County. When the turmoil broke out during the Taiqing period, Yu Zhongrong lived in Kuaiji and died of illness at the age of seventy-four. Yu Zhongrong copied thirty volumes of books by various scholars, twenty volumes of geography books of various schools, three volumes of Biography of Women, and twenty volumes of collected works. These books are all circulated in the world. Lu Yungong, named Zilong, was from Wujun. His grandfather Lu Xian lived in Renzhou. His father, Lu Wan, had a long history with Ren Ningyuan. When Lu Yungong was five years old, he could recite "The Analects of Confucius" and "Mao Shi". When he was nine years old, he could read "Han Shu" and memorize everything. His grandfather Lu Bian and Pei Guo Liu Xian asked him about ten things in the "Book of Han", and he could answer them one by one without making any mistakes. Liu Xian was full of praise and thought he was different from ordinary people. When he grew up, Lu Yungong was studious and talented.
target: Lu Yungong, courtesy name Zilong, was from Wujun. He could recite classics at a young age. He was studious and talented.

source: When he grew up, Lu Yungong was studious and talented. He was elected as a scholar in the state. Lu Yun Gongjigong was transferred to the throne of Xuanhui, King of Wuling, and King of Pingxi, Xiangshu, to join the army. Lu Yungong originally wrote the "Taibo Temple Stele". Zhang Zuan, the governor of Wuxing, left his post and returned to the capital. On the way, he read the inscription written by Lu Yungong and said with emotion: This man is simply the contemporary Cai Bojie. After Zhang Zuan arrived in the capital, he was in charge of the selection of officials. He recommended Lu Yungong to Emperor Gaozu. Emperor Gaozu then called Lu Yungong to serve as the minister of Yi Cao Lang. He was soon appointed to this position and was assigned to Shouguang Province. He also used his original official position to know how to serve as a minister.
target: He wrote the "Taibo Temple Stele," which Zhang Zuan praised. He was called to serve by Emperor Gaozu.

source: Lu Yungong was good at playing Go. He once accompanied Gaozu at night. The crown he was wearing caught the light of a candle. Gaozu smiled and said to him: The candle burned the mink tail on your hat. Gaozu was about to appoint Lu Yungong as his minister, and his crown would be decorated with a mink tail, so Gaozu used these words to joke with Lu Yungong. At that time, a new bream boat was built in Tianyuanchi. The boat was wide and short. Gaozu often took this boat to ride on the waves in his spare time. Among the courtiers, he only brought Taichang Liu Zhilin, Guozi to Gai, and Youwei Zhu Yi. Lu Yungong was young at that time and his position was not high, but he was also among the courtiers who accompanied Gaozu on the boat. Emperor Gaozu's favor and favor towards him reached such an extent.
target: He was good at Go. Emperor Gaozu favored him greatly.

source: Emperor Gaozu's favor and favor towards him reached such an extent. In the first year of Taiqing, Lu Yungong passed away at the age of thirty-seven. Emperor Gaozu was deeply saddened by his death and wrote an edict in his own hand, saying: I serve as the minister of Huangmen and as Duke Lu Yungong. He is a rising star with beautiful demeanor and broad knowledge. His sudden death is deeply saddening. A date should be set to mourn him. He donated 50,000 yuan and 40 pieces of cloth to help his family with funeral arrangements. Zhang Zan was the governor of Xiangzhou at the time. He wrote to Lu Yungong's uncle Lu Xiang and his elder brother Lu Yanzi, saying: Messengers from the capital have come to know that your virtuous brother's son and virtuous brother, Huangmen Shilang, has unfortunately passed away. This is not only the loss of an outstanding talent in your family, but everyone who knew him feels the same sadness, and the sorrow and regret cannot stop.
target: He died at thirty-seven. Emperor Gaozu mourned him. Zhang Zan wrote a letter expressing his sorrow.

source: Suddenly encountered this sad and heartbreaking thing, what else can I say! Writing a letter increases the sadness and pain, making the words incoherent. Lu Yungong's cousin Lu Caizi was also famous for his talent. He successively served as Zhongshulang, Xuancheng Wangyou, and Prince's concubine. Ting Weiqing died before Lu Yungong. Lu Caizi and Lu Yungong both have collections of essays, which are also circulated in the world. Ren Xiaogong, whose courtesy name is Xiaogong, was born in Linhuai. His great-grandfather was a farmer and the governor of Southern Yuzhou during the Song Dynasty. Ren Xiaogong lost his father when he was young. He served his mother very filially and became famous for this. Ren Xiaogong was dedicated and diligent in his studies. His family was poor and he often asked people to borrow books when he had no books to act in. Every time he read it, he could recite it without missing anything. Ren Cuoyu's maternal grandfather, Qiu Ta, had a relationship with Emperor Gaozu. Hearing that Ren Xiaogong was talented and learned, he summoned him to the Western Province to compile history books.
target: Ren Xiaogong, courtesy name Xiaogong, was from Linhuai. He was filial and studious. He was summoned to compile history books.

source: Ren Cuoyu's maternal grandfather, Qiu Ta, had a relationship with Emperor Gaozu. Hearing that Ren Xiaogong was talented and learned, he summoned him to the Western Province to compile history books. Ren Xiaogong was first appointed to the imperial court, and was promoted to Shouguang Province as the Minister of Si Wen. Soon he was also appointed as Zhongshu General Shiren. Emperor Gaozu issued an edict and ordered Ren Xiaogong to write the "Inscription under the Temple of Jianling Temple". Ren Xiaogong also presented the "Preface" to the collected works of Emperor Gaozu written by himself. The words were rich and gorgeous. From the time of the Han Dynasty, Ren Xiaogong was in charge of the court's documents full-time. Ren Xiaogong wrote articles quickly, and he could write them immediately after receiving the imperial edict. It seemed that he didn't spend much time on it. He wrote good articles and presented them to memorials. Emperor Gaozu always praised his well-written articles and gave him gold and silk many times. When he was young, Ren Xiaogong read scriptures with Master Xiao Siyun and was well versed in Buddhist teachings. When he was sent away, Ren Xiaogong only ate vegetables, followed the precepts, and believed in Buddhism very sincerely. However, Ren Xiaogong liked to show off his achievements by nature, and often relied on his talents to put himself above others. He often showed contempt for famous figures at that time, and the world looked down upon him because of this. In the second year of Taiqing, Hou Jing invaded the capital, and Ren Xiaogong started recruiting sergeants. He led the recruited soldiers to be affiliated with Xiao Zhengde and stationed on the south bank of the Yangtze River.
target: He wrote quickly and was praised by Emperor Gaozu. He was well-versed in Buddhism. He was arrogant and looked down on others. During Hou Jing's invasion, he led soldiers but was killed when the rebels attacked.

source: Yan Xie, courtesy name Zihe, was from Linyi, Langxie. His ancestor Yan Han, seven generations ago, served as Shizhong, Guozi Jijiu, and Jinghou of Xiping during the Jin Dynasty. His father is far-sighted, knowledgeable, ambitious and ethical. In the past, when Emperor Qi He was guarding Jingzhou, he appointed Yan Jianyuan to join the army for the green affairs. When Emperor Qi He ascended the throne in Jiangling, he appointed Yan Jianyuan to serve as the official secretary and censor, and soon became the Zhongcheng. After Emperor Gaozu accepted Qi's abdication, Yan Jianyuan went on a hunger strike and died in anger for several days. When Emperor Gaozu heard the news, he said: I am following the destiny of heaven and obeying the will of man. What does it have to do with the scholar-bureaucrats in the world? And Yan Jianyuan actually did such a thing! Yan Xie lost his father when he was young and was raised by his uncle's family. He has been praised for his magnanimity since childhood. Yan Xie has extensively dabbled in group calligraphy and is good at writing cursive script and official script. When Yan Xie first became an official, he took up the post of permanent attendant of the Xiangdong Kingdom, and also served as the official secretary of the government. Shizu came out of the capital to guard Jingzhou, and Yan Xie was transferred to the office of actual professors and records. At that time, Gu Xie of Wu County also served in the palace. He and Yan Xie had the same names, and their talents and learning were comparable. They were called "Er Xie" in the palace. Yan Xie's uncle, Chen Jun Xie Chen, passed away. Yan Xie mourned his uncle with the same etiquette as he would an uncle because of his kindness to his uncle. People who talked about this matter valued Yan Xie's friendship more. Yan Xie also felt that his father at home died for his righteousness, so he did not pursue prominent positions and often refused calls from the court, only serving in the feudal prince's palace. In the fifth year of Datong, Yan Xie passed away at the age of forty-two. Shizu lamented his death and wrote "Nostalgic Poems" to mourn him. One of the chapters says: With great magnanimity and elegant demeanor, he is truly a talent in name and in reality! Although they have been promoted, they have not yet been promoted, resulting in talented people still staying in positions with low salaries. Five chapters of "Biography of Jinxian" and two volumes of "Disasters of the Sun and Moon" written by Yan Xie were burned down due to fire. Yan Xie had two sons: Yan Zhiyi and Yan Zitui, both of whom became famous very early.
target: Yan Xie, courtesy name Zihe, was from Linyi. He lost his father young. He was magnanimous and good at calligraphy. He served in the Xiangdong Kingdom. He and Gu Xie were called "Er Xie." He mourned his uncle with proper etiquette. He did not pursue prominent positions. He died at forty-two. His works were burned in a fire. His sons, Yan Zhiyi and Yan Zitui, became famous early.

source: "Yi" says: A gentleman escapes from the world and does not feel bored. He is independent and does not know fear. Confucius called Chang Ju and Jie Dun hermits. Some hermits in ancient times were ashamed to hear about the Zen Dynasty, considered it noble to give up the throne, regarded the Wancheng throne as a disgrace, and went to death without any regrets. This kind of person despises life and values ​​morality. He is rare in the world and appears occasionally. He is a superior hermit. Some work as prison gates to support themselves, and work as officials under the pillars to support themselves. They live a simple life to realize their ambitions, and their status is low but they don't show any shame. He was a so-called great hermit who hid in the city and court, and his status was lower than that of the superior hermits. Some exposed their bodies, pretended to be crazy, blinded their eyes, made their voices hoarse, renounced the world, abandoned rituals and music to return to the right path, and suppressed the need to talk about filial piety, love, and family affection. This kind of person protects himself, avoids harm, masters the way of escaping from the world, and his status is lower than that of the great hermit. However, these people have not forgotten the key to keeping silent, staying on the right path in seclusion, and finally getting good results. How can they and those who join in troubled times, compete for wealth and cater to the world, say the same thing? "Mencius" says: For people nowadays, regarding juelu, getting it is like gaining life, losing it is like losing life. "Huainanzi said: People use still water as mirrors, not running water." To be able to inspire righteousness, wash away filth, curb corruption and bend the law, and stop the pursuit of power and profit, I am afraid only a hermit can do it! Since ancient times, there has been no emperor who did not respect the conduct of hermits. Even Tang Yao couldn't make Chaofu and Xu You obey each other, and King Wu of Zhou couldn't make Boyi and Shuqi abandon their integrity and become ministers. Mo Gaozu was arrogant but respectful to Qili Ji and Xia Huang Gong. Mo Guang Wu Emperor governed the world according to the law but was submissive to Yan Guang and Zhou Dang. Since then, this has been the case for generations. During the Liang Dynasty, the country prospered and inherited the moral education and governance of the previous generation. All the hermits whose morals were worthy of imitation and whose knowledge could serve as role models were included in the "Chushi Pian".
target: The highest are those who value morality above life itself, despising wealth and power, and willing to face death without regret—rare figures who occasionally appear. The second tier includes "great hermits" who hide within cities or courts, living simply to fulfill their ambitions without shame despite low status. The third tier consists of those who feign madness, blind themselves, or abandon rituals to protect themselves and escape worldly entanglements. All these hermits, however, master the art of silence and seclusion, ultimately achieving good outcomes, unlike those who chase wealth and cater to the world. The text quotes Mencius and Huainanzi to emphasize that hermits alone can inspire righteousness and curb corruption. Historically, no emperor has failed to respect hermits. Even Tang Yao could not compel Chaofu and Xu You to obey, nor could King Wu of Zhou force Boyi and Shuqi to serve. Emperors like Gaozu of Han and Guangwu of Han showed deference to hermits such as Qili Ji and Yan Guang. During the Liang Dynasty, hermits with exemplary morals were recorded in the "Chushi Pian.".

source: All other etiquette had been completed, and when the wedding ceremony was about to take place, He Dian cried to He Shangzhi again and again, begging to be allowed to stick to his original wishes, so that the wedding was suspended. He Dian has a dignified and comely appearance, is well-read, and is good at talking and discussing. The He Dian family was originally a wealthy family, with many in-laws serving as high-ranking officials. Although He Dian did not enter the city or enter the government, he only wore household clothes, without hairpins or belts, and traveled among the people. Sometimes he drove a chariot and wore straw sandals. At that time, people called this point "Tongyin". He Dian's brother He Qiu also lived in seclusion in Huqiu Mountain in Wu County. After He Qiu's death, He Dian only ate vegetarian food and did not drink alcohol during the period of mourning for his brother. After the three-year mourning period was over, He Dian's waist circumference had been reduced by half.
target: The text then details the lives of several notable hermits. He Dian, from a wealthy family, refused marriage and office after his father’s execution, living simply among the people.

source: There is Bian Zhongzhen's tomb in the garden. He planted flowers on the side of the tomb. Every time he drank, he must first sprinkle the wine on the ground to pay homage to Bian Zhongzhen. At first, when Chu Yuan and Wang Jian were prime ministers, He Point said to people: I wrote "Qishu Praise", which said: "Chu Yuan is from a noble family, and Wang Jian is also a talented person in the country. Who can care about the country without relying on these close relatives and old ministers?" When Wang Jian heard this, he originally wanted to visit Hedian, but later he realized that he could not see Hedian, so he gave up the plan.
target: He rejected multiple imperial summons, fled from nobles who sought him, and gave away stolen clothes to a thief.

source: He Dian is very discerning in identifying talents, and he has identified and recommended many people. When Wu Xingqiu Chi was still a child, he admired him very much; when Ji Yang Jiangyan was still in a low status, Bao Shu praised him. Later, both of them showed their talents as He Dian said. When He Dian grew old, he married the daughter of Kong Si of Lu, who was also a hermit. Although He Dian was married, he did not meet his wife and built another house to accommodate her. No one understood his intention to do this.
target: He was known for his discerning judgment of talent and his unconventional marriage, where he did not meet his wife.

source: Since Hedian's virtue is higher than that of Yuan Yaoqing, he can be allocated to Yuanxia Valley based on old feelings just like Wei Taizu did to Yuan Yaoqing. In the third year of Tianjian, he died at the age of sixty-eight. Emperor Gaozu Xia Shao said: He Dian, the newly appointed servant, lived in seclusion from the world and placed his affection in Hengbi. His ambitions remained unchanged throughout his life. He died suddenly. I feel so sad and sad. You can give He Dian a coffin made of first-class wood, send 20,000 yuan, and fifty pieces of cloth to his family for the funeral. All the things needed for the funeral will be provided by the internal prison. He also ordered Yuzhe's younger brother Yuhuang to say: "Brother Zhengjun Baoyan, my virtuous brother, has lived in seclusion since he was weak, and his conduct has remained unchanged until his twilight years."
target: Emperor Gaozu, an old friend, repeatedly invited him to court, offering gifts and honors, but He Dian remained reclusive until his death at sixty-eight.

source: He Yin, whose courtesy name was Wang Ji, was He Dian's younger brother. When he was eight years old, he mourned his parents and, like adults, his body was damaged by grief. As an adult, he loved learning. He became a disciple of Peiguo Liu Shan and studied "Yi", "Book of Rites" and "Mao Shi"; he also went to Dinglin Temple in Zhongshan to study Buddhist scriptures. He learned all these things proficiently. However, he was casual and informal. No one understood him at that time. Only Zhou Yong of Runan deeply valued him and thought he was a genius.
target: He Yin, He Dian’s younger brother, was a scholar who studied Confucian and Buddhist texts.

source: In the early years of Jianwu, he had built a house in the suburbs, which he called a hill. He often lived in the house with his Shilin friends. When he arrived, He Yin sold his house and wanted to live in seclusion in Dongshan. Before he started to prepare for the affair, He Yin heard that Xie Quan would not return to the capital after being dismissed from the post of governor of Wuxing County. He was worried that Xie Li would live in seclusion in Dongshan, so he resigned and left the capital without waiting for a reply from the court.
target: He served in minor official posts but later resigned to live in seclusion, building a house in the mountains.

source: Now I have sent a special person to wait for news from you. I am eagerly looking forward to your reply. I hope you can comfort my earnest expectations. He Yin refused to take up a post in the palace. Emperor Gaozu ascended the throne and issued an edict to appoint He Yin as the Tejin and Youguanglu officials. Emperor Gaozu personally wrote an order to He Yin saying: I am experiencing good luck, the people are happy to support me, and I have ascended to the throne. It's just that I am ignorant and not proficient in governing the country.
target: He refused high-ranking positions, even when Emperor Gaozu personally wrote to him, citing his age and health.

source: After crossing the Yangtze River in the south, people of the He family were buried in Wuxi Mountain for generations, starting from Sikong Hechong of Jin Dynasty. Several generations of He Yin's family did not live long. Only his grandfather He Shangzhi lived to be seventy-two years old. When He Yin reached the age of seventy-two, he left Qinwang Mountain and moved to Wu. He composed a poem "Farewell to the Mountain" with very sad and sad words. After arriving, He Yin lectured on Confucian classics at the West Temple in Xuqiu, and the students all studied with him. The eastern governors passed by Wu on their way to and from Wu, and they all came to the temple to listen to He Yin's lectures. He Yin often forbids killing. A man from Yu was chasing a deer. The deer kept running towards He Yin and lay motionless beside him. There is also a strange bird, shaped like a crane and red, which gathers in the lecture hall. It is tame and friendly to people, just like a domestic fowl.
target: He taught students, forbade killing, and was known for miraculous events, such as a deer seeking refuge with him and a strange bird appearing in his lecture hall.

source: Those who commented on the incident said that nearly two hundred years had passed since the death of Master Yuan before virtuous people like Zhang Xiaoxiu and Liu Huifei appeared on Kuangshan Mountain. Letters from Shizu, King Wuling and others continued to Liu Zhanying. Died at the age of fifty-nine. Fan Yuanyan, courtesy name Bogui, was born in Qiantang Dynasty, Wu County. His grandfather Fan Yuezhi was recruited as a doctor of Taixue, but he did not take up the post.
target: He died at eighty-six, leaving extensive annotations on the "Book of Changes" and "Book of Rites.".

source: Ruan Xiaoxu, courtesy name Shizong, was born in Chenliuwei family. His father, Yanzhi, served as a lieutenant in the Song Dynasty and worked as a lieutenant. When Ruan Xiaoxu was seven years old, Ruan Xiaoxu adopted his uncle Ruan Yinzhi as his heir. Ruan Yinzhi's mother, the Zhou family, passed away and left more than one million yuan in property. Ruan Xiaoxu should inherit all the property, but Ruan Xiaoxu refused to accept it at all. He gave all the inheritance to Ruan Yinzhi's sister, the mother of King Yan of Langxie. Everyone who heard the news was amazed. Ruan Xiaoxu has been very filial since he was a child. He is calm and quiet by nature. Even if he plays games with children, he often digs ponds and builds mountains as entertainment. At the age of thirteen, he was proficient in all the Five Classics. After the crowning ceremony at the age of fifteen, Ruan Xiaoxu went to see his father Ruan Yanzhi. Ruan Yanzhi told Ruan Xiaoxu: After the crowning ceremony, your status becomes more important. This is the beginning of becoming an adult and participating in personnel affairs. You should always think of yourself and encourage yourself to protect yourself. Ruan Xiaoxu replied: I am willing to follow Chi Songzi's footsteps to Yinghai and imitate Xu You's behavior to hide in the deep valley, hoping to save my short life and avoid the burden of the world. From then on, Ruan Xiaoxu avoided staying in a room alone. Except for visiting his parents, he did not give birth. No one at home saw him, so his relatives and friends called him "householder". Ruan Xiaoxu's cousin Wang Yan was in a prominent position and visited Ruan Xiaoxu's home many times. Ruan Xiaoxu estimated that Wang Yan would be defeated, so he often hid himself and avoided seeing Wang Yan.
target: Ruan Xiaoxu, from a wealthy family, refused inheritance and lived in poverty, avoiding even his prominent cousin Wang Yan.

source: Practicing benevolence depends entirely on yourself, what does it have to do with the world! Do you think I am not the same type of person as the sages of the past? Later, Ruan Xiaoxu listened to a lecture in Zhongshan. His mother Wang suddenly fell ill, and Ruan Xiaoxu's brother wanted to call him back. Ruan Xiaoxu's mother said: "Cunxu has a secret nature, and he will definitely come back by himself." As expected, Ruan Xiaoxu was so frightened by Zhongshan that he rushed home. The neighbors were amazed at what he had done. Ruan Xiaoxu's mother must make medicine with fresh ginseng. It was said that Zhongshan produced ginseng, so Ruan Xiaoxu personally went over the mountains and deep valleys to search for it, but could not find it after many days. Suddenly he saw a deer walking forward, and the doctor seemed to sense it, so he followed the deer forward. When he reached a place, the deer suddenly disappeared. Ruan Xiaoxu caught up and found the ginseng grass he wanted. His mother mixed the medicine with ginseng and took it, and the disease was cured. At that time, people lamented about this, thinking that it was because Ruan Xiaoxu's filial piety moved the gods.
target: He was known for his filial piety, once finding ginseng for his mother by following a deer. He refused official summons, stating that seclusion depends on personal choice, not the state of the world.

source: Ji Zhidao continued to arrange the hexagrams, and finally "Zhu Hexagram" appeared. Zhang Youdao sighed and said: This image says that there is no disadvantage in fat escape. The hexagram corresponds to your virtue, and your heart and actions are consistent. Ruan Xiaoxu said: Although the "Ei Gua" was obtained, the upper nine Yang Yao did not appear. The way to live in seclusion is to secede from the world like Xu You. Zao Buxu then wrote the "Biography of Gao Yin", starting from Yan and Huang to the biography of the hermit in the last years of Zuo Jian, and rated these people as third grade, with a total of several volumes. Ruan Xiaoxu also wrote "Gao Yin Zhuan Lun" and said: The highest foundation of Tao lies in advocating inaction; the actions of the saints are to save the evils of the times. To remedy current problems, we must take action. Relying on action to achieve results violates the foundation of Tao. Since the foundation of Tao is advocating inaction, taking action is not the highest criterion of Tao. However, if we do not take action, the world will not be stable; if we do not implement the fundamentals of Tao, Tao will eventually decline. Confucius and Ji Dan wanted to insist on taking action, so they temporarily concealed the foundation of Tao; Lao Dan and Zhuang Zhou should conceal their actions as long as they promoted the foundation of Tao. Actions can be concealed, which is why Lao and Zhuang felt free and at ease; fundamentals can be concealed, so Confucius felt powerless in busying with worldly affairs. If a scholar cannot grasp one aspect, he will lack wise insights; if he can understand both aspects, he will have a unique ability to examine and discern. In this way, when the saint has enlightened the world, he will turn around to expand the influence of his actions; before the wise man is in a position of being respected, he should promote the foundation of Tao. The truth is that actions should remedy the current ills, and those who are not saints cannot undertake this task; principles should be used to explain principles, and wise men can know and show them to the world. If you can understand the relationship between roots and actions, and understand the principle of ups and downs, then you can understand most of the thoughts of Confucius and Zhuang Zhou.
target: He wrote a "Biography of Gao Yin" and a treatise on the balance between action and inaction, arguing that saints act to remedy ills while wise men promote the foundation of Tao. He died at fifty-eight.

source: Tao Hongjing, courtesy name Tongming, was born in Moling, Danyang. It turned out that Tao Hongjing's mother dreamed that a green dragon came out of her arms, and at the same time she saw two gods coming to her place holding incense burners. Soon after, Tao's mother became pregnant and gave birth to Tao Hongjing. Tao Hongjing has a unique talent since he was a child. When he was ten years old, he got the Biography of Immortals written by Ge Hong, and he studied it day and night, and then he came up with the idea of ​​​​preserving health and longevity.
target: Tao Hongjing, a polymath, resigned from office at thirty-six to live in Maoshan, where he studied alchemy and the Talisman Sutra.

source: In the early years of Yongyuan, Tao Hongjing built another three-story building. Tao Hongjing lived on the top floor, his disciples lived on the middle floor, and guests stayed on the lower floor when they came. Tao Hongjing cut off contact with the rest of the world from then on, and had only one servant boy at home to serve him. Tao Hongjing especially loved the sound of wind in the pine forest. Every time he heard the sound of the wind blowing in the pine forest, he felt happy. Tao Hongjing sometimes played alone by the springs and rocks. People who saw him from a distance thought he was an immortal. Tao Hongjing was fond of writing by nature, and he advocated strange things in his writings. He cherishes time, and will cherish it even more as he grows older. He is especially proficient in yin and yang and the five elements, wind angle astrology, mountain geography, surrounding products, and medical materia medica. Tao Hongjing wrote the "Almanac of the Emperors" and once created the Huntian phenomenon. Tao Hongjing said that the Huntian phenomenon was not only used by historians, but was also necessary for Bi Dao.
target: He built a three-story house, cutting off contact with the world, and was known for his love of pine wind and his expertise in yin-yang, astrology, and medicine.

source: After the rebel army against Donghun Hou pacified Jiankang, Tao Hongjing heard that the Hua Dynasty was being discussed, so he quoted the prophecy, and after several deductions, it became the character "Liang", so Tao Hongjing ordered his disciples to submit the deduction results to the court. Emperor Gaozu had long been friends with Tao Hongjing. After he ascended the throne, his favor and courtesy to Tao Hongjing became even more generous and considerate. He and Tao Hongjing exchanged letters continuously and sent envoys to visit Tao Hongjing one after another. In the fourth year of Tianjian, Tao Hongjing moved to Jijinshujian. Tao Hongjing is good at the health-preserving technique of bigu guidance. Although he is over eighty years old, he still maintains a healthy appearance. Tao Hongjing deeply admired Zhang Liang's character and said that Zhang Liang was a Japanese man. Among the ancient sages, no one could compare with him.
target: He predicted the rise of the Liang dynasty through prophecies and maintained a close friendship with Emperor Gaozu, who frequently sent envoys. He died at eighty-one, leaving instructions for a modest burial.

source: He only made a living by collecting firewood, but he was still content and did not change his purpose. In the fourth year of Tianjian, Liang launched a large-scale northern expedition, so he recruited strong men. Liu Yun, the prefect of Wuxing, ordered Shen Yi to serve as a laborer. Lu Ren, the governor of Yangzhou, wrote a letter to blame Liu Zang. Liu Zang was very ashamed and sent Shen Zhan a rich gift and asked Shen Wei to go home. Shen Hao died in his home that year. Shen Wei has written dozens of articles. Liu Huifei, courtesy name Wenxuan, was born in Pengcheng. He has been knowledgeable and able to write articles since he was a child. Liu Huifei first became an official and served as King Xuanxu, Facao Xing, and joined the army. Liu Huifei once passed through Xunyang on his way back to the capital and went to Kuangshan to visit. He went to visit Zhang Xiaoxiu, a minister. The two had similar interests and were very compatible. Liu Huifei then came up with the idea of ​​​​living in Kuangshan for the rest of his life. So he stopped being an official and lived in Shulin Temple by himself. He also built a garden in the north of the mountain and named it Lijiu Garden. At that time, people called Liu Huifei Mr. Li Guo. Liu Huifei was particularly proficient in Buddhist classics. He was proficient in seal script and official script. On Kuangshan Mountain, he hand-copied more than 2,000 volumes of Buddhist scriptures, of which more than 100 volumes were often recited. Liu Huifei recited Buddhist scriptures day and night, tirelessly, and people near and far admired him. Taizong came to Liao Dynasty and gave Liu Tomufei a few sticks. Those who commented on the incident said that nearly two hundred years had passed since the death of Master Yuan before virtuous people like Zhang Xiaoxiu and Liu Huifei appeared on Kuangshan Mountain. Letters from Shizu, King Wuling and others continued to Liu Zhanying. Died at the age of fifty-nine. Fan Yuanyan, courtesy name Bogui, was born in Qiantang Dynasty, Wu County.
target: Other hermits include Zhuge Gu, a teacher who refused office and lived in poverty; Shen Yi, who remained content despite extreme hardship; Liu Huifei, who copied Buddhist scriptures in Kuangshan; Fan Yuanyan, who hid his kindness to thieves; Liu Xu, who fled his own wedding; and Liu Xian, who wrote a treatise on death and burial, advocating simplicity. Yu Shen, a scholar of vast knowledge, lived frugally, forgave a thief, and refused official posts, dying at seventy-eight. Zhang Xiaoxiu and Yu Chengxian also lived in seclusion, the latter known for his lectures on Laozi.

source: The county government recruited Yu Chengxian as a meritorious officer, but Yu Chengxian refused to take office. He and the monk Wang Sengzhen went to Hengyue to visit. In his later years, Yu Chengxian returned to his hometown because of his brother's illness and lived in Tutai Mountain. King Zhonglie of Poyang was in the state at that time. He admired Yu Chengxian's elegant character and invited Yu Chengxian to have fun with him. King Zhonglie of Poyang also ordered Yu Cheng to preach "Laozi" first. Famous monks from near and far gathered together to raise various questions and heresies. Yu Chengxian answered them one by one calmly and calmly. Everyone who attended the meeting heard truths they had never heard of before. King Zhonglie of Poyang admired and respected Yu Chengxian even more and made him the governor of the state. When King Xiangshu heard the news, he also appointed Yu Chengxian to join the army in the name of his own palace, but Yu Chengxian did not even go to the post. In the third year of Zhongdatong, Liu Huifei from Lushan came to Jingzhou. Yu Chengxian had a friendship with Liu Huifei, so he went to visit Liu Huifei. Scholars from Jingshan and Shanxi took this opportunity to ask Yu Cheng to speak about "Laozi" first. The King of Eastern Hunan came to listen to the lecture in person and discussed it with Yu Chengxian for a whole day. He was deeply impressed by him. King Xiangshu also invited Yu Chengxian to the palace and stayed there for more than a month before Yu Chengxian returned to the mountains. When he returned to the mountain, King Xiangshu personally held a farewell banquet for him and wrote poems as gifts. People who lived in seclusion felt that this was an honor. This year, Yu Chengxian died at the age of sixty. Yao Chaqiu, the Minister of the Ministry of Official Affairs of Chen, said: Most of the people in the world who speak ill of virgins accuse them of simply stealing empty names without any merits suitable for world use. They are really people who do not deserve their names. With Zhuge Can's knowledge and Ruan Xiaoxu's family background, how could they have any difficulty in seeking official positions?
target: The text concludes with a reflection by Yao Chaqiu, who defends hermits against accusations of stealing empty names, noting that figures like Zhuge Can and Ruan Xiaoxu could have easily sought office but chose seclusion by nature.

source: "Yi" said: "Kang has regrets". The meaning of the word "Kang" means that he only knows how to advance in officialdom, but does not know how to retire; he only knows how to survive, but does not know how to die. I am afraid that only a saint can understand the principles of advance and retreat and survive without losing track of the right path! "The Biography" says: If you are content, you will not be humiliated; if you know how to stop, you will not be in danger. According to this, if you don’t know how to advance or retreat, if you don’t understand the principle of knowing where to stop and be content, you will be humiliated, embarrassed, and in a dangerous situation, and you will soon be in a dangerous situation. The advancement of the ancients was to help people govern the world, and the retreat of the ancients was to promote the right path and encourage folk customs. However, people's advancement in officialdom is glorious and easy, so it is the goal that ignorant people strive to pursue; people's retirement requires adhering to integrity and persisting in hardships and dangers, so it is something that mediocre people are afraid of. Although it is common for people to see and hear cases of people who seek to advance in officialdom encounter disaster or defeat, people who live in seclusion are rarely seen in previous history books. Moji retired from the emperor after his success, and was lying in his sick home, practicing the method of immortality. This is better than wandering around after he succeeded in Luanqi and Jianlong. Later, Zheng Guangde, Shuguang, Shushou and others retired according to the court's etiquette and left their jobs to live in their homes, which is also worthy of praise. Yu Kun's "Wei Lue Zhizuo Zhuan" compared Tian and Xu with Guan and Hu. In fact, their principles of conduct were originally different. Xie Lingyun's "Jin Shu Zhizu Zhuan" first comments on those Jin Dynasty literati who escaped from the turmoil. They probably did not belong to the Zhizu type of people; only Ruan Sikuang liked to escape from the world, abandoning glory and wealth, which was considered to be far away from the embarrassing and dangerous situation of humiliation. "Song Book." In "The Legend of Zhizu" there are biographies of Cha Ao and Wang Miao, both of whom are similar characters to the previous ones. During the Revolution, Zhou Suyou, also named Wangbi, refused to be an official, insisted on integrity, traveled in the mountains and forests, cultivated his ambition, did not feel sad and sorrowful in poverty, and did not pursue wealth and glory greedily. He was a noble person among Confucian scholars. After Liang took over the world, the way of villains declined, and wise men and officials invited each other to gather in the court to measure their own strength and stick to their ambitions of retirement. Those who have not been heard of in the contemporary era. Occasionally, some people retired due to old age, and some had little ambition and weak desires. The history of the country recorded the deeds of these people and compiled it into the "Zhizu Zhuan".
target: The principles of advance and retreat in officialdom, noting that those who only know how to advance but not retreat will face humiliation and danger. It contrasts the glorious and easy pursuit of advancement, which ignorant people strive for, with the difficult and principled act of retirement, which mediocre people fear. The text mentions historical figures like Moji, who retired after success, and Zheng Guangde, Shuguang, and Shushou, who retired according to court etiquette. It also references Xie Lingyun's "Jin Shu Zhizu Zhuan," which comments on Jin Dynasty literati who escaped turmoil, and notes that Ruan Sikuang was considered to have avoided humiliation by abandoning glory. The "Zhizu Zhuan" includes biographies of Cha Ao and Wang Miao, and during the Revolution, Zhou Suyou was a noble Confucian who refused office and cultivated his ambition in the mountains.

The history of the country recorded the deeds of these people and compiled it into the "Zhizu Zhuan". Gu Xian's courtesy name was Shisi, and he was a native of Wu County, Wu County. His grandfather Gu Qianzhi was the general of the town army and the governor of Xiangzhou during the Song Dynasty. Before he reached the age of twenty, Gu Xianzhi was appointed by the state as a councilor, promoted scholars, and accumulated merits and was promoted to Prince Sheren, Shangshu Bibu Lang, and Fujun Chief. During the Yuan Dynasty, Gu Xianzhi was appointed as the Jiankang Order. At that time, someone was stealing cattle, and the stolen cattle were recognized by the owner of the cattle. The person who stole the cattle also said that the cattle were his own. The verbal evidence on both sides was similar. No one of the previous county magistrates could decide this case. After Gu Xianzhi arrived, he reviewed the case materials and then said to both parties: "No need to say more, I have thought of a solution." So Gu Xianzhi ordered his people to untie the rope from which the cow was tied and let the cow go wherever it wanted. The cow went straight back to its original owner's house, and the thief confessed his crime. Gu Saizhu exposed the evildoers hidden in the dark. He was so smart and decisive in many such things that people at the time called him a god. As for dealing with the private requests of dignitaries and dignitaries in the imperial court, he never flattered or obeyed. He never tolerated the corruption and cruelty of his officials, and he judged them all fairly and in accordance with the law.
target: The text then provides a detailed biography of Gu Xianzhi. He was a native of Wu County, served in various official posts, and was known for his intelligence and decisive judgment, such as solving a cattle theft case by letting the cow lead him to its owner.

source: When Emperor Gao of Qi ascended the throne, Gu Xianzhi was dismissed and appointed as the internal history of Hengyang. Before Gu Xianzhi took office, there had been plagues in Hengyang for several years, and more than half of the people died of the disease. The price of coffins was extremely expensive, so the people all wrapped the dead in reeds and dumped them on the roadside. As soon as Gu Xianzhi took office, he notified the counties under his jurisdiction to find the relatives of the dead and ordered them to bury the dead. For those dead people who had no relatives, Gu Xianzhi took out his salary and ordered the chief clerk of the government to organize the burial. According to the local folk custom in Hengyang, when people in the mountains are sick, they often say that the disaster was caused by their ancestors, so they dig graves, open coffins, and wash the bones of the dead with water. This is called "removing evil spirits". Gu Xianzhi used principles to educate the people, explaining to them the difference between the living and the dead, and pointed out that diseases were not caused by the dead, and the local customs were therefore changed. At that time, the governor Wang Huan had just taken office, and there was only one county in Hengyang where no one came to the governor's office to complain. So Wang Huan sighed and said: Gu Hengyang's education has reached a very good level. Suppose all nine counties of this state are like this. So what else is wrong with me? Gu Xianzhi returned to Beijing and served as Taiwei and Zhonglang. He also left the capital and served as the chief historian of Shuzhong and engaged in the affairs of Kuaiji County. Lu Wendu, a native of Shanyin, was favored by Emperor Wu of Qi, so he built a mansion in Yuyao and acted freely and unscrupulously in the area. When Gu Xianzhi took office in Kuaiji County, he immediately went to court to demolish Lu Wendu's mansion. Lu Wendu later went back to his hometown to bury his mother. Officials from counties and counties rushed to express their condolences, but Gu Xianzhi refused to associate with him. Lu Wendu deeply hated Gu Xianzhi in his heart, but in the end he could not slander Gu Xianzhi. Gu Xianzhi moved to Nanzhonglang and was appointed as the chief historian of Baling King. He also added General Wei to conduct affairs in southern Henan and southern Yanzhou. At that time, King Situ Jingling established a military camp at the junction of Xuancheng, Lincheng and Dingling counties, demarcating Baili Mountain and marsh, and prohibiting people from entering to collect firewood. Gu Xianzhi resolutely stated that this could not be done, and his words were sincere and straightforward. King Jingling answered him: If it weren't for you, I wouldn't be able to hear such sincere and kind words.
target: He was honest, frugal, and fair, earning the nickname "Gu Jiankang" for his purity. As an official, he improved local customs, such as ending the practice of "removing evil spirits" in Hengyang and demolishing the mansion of the favored Lu Wendu. He also successfully petitioned King Jingling to lift a ban on collecting firewood.

source: In the second year of the Zhongxing Dynasty, the rebel army who attacked Qidong Hunhou pacified Jiankang. Emperor Gaozu was appointed as the shepherd of Yangzhou, and Gu Xianzhi was recruited to serve as a historian. By the time Gu Xianzhi arrived in the capital, Gaozu had accepted Qi's concession and ascended the throne. Gu Xianzhi's condition gradually became serious due to a stroke, so he firmly requested to return to his hometown of Wuxian. In the second year of Tianjian, the imperial court sent people to Gu Xian's home to confer him the title of Taizhong doctor. Although Gu Xianzhi served as county magistrate many times, he did not even have any savings. When he returned to his hometown, his family was destitute, so he was inevitably suffering from hunger and cold. In the eighth year of Tianjian, Gu Xianzhi died at home at the age of seventy-four. When he was dying, Gu Xianzhi wrote in advance instructions on the funeral arrangements and warned his son:
target: Gu Xianzhi died at home at age seventy-four, leaving instructions for a simple funeral, emphasizing frugality and sincerity over elaborate rituals.

source: Wang Jian followed Tao Jizhi's advice. Tao Jizhi also asked Wang Jian to erect a monument for Chu Yuan. After the stele was erected, Tao Jizhi protected the stele well from beginning to end and maintained the ethics of an official. People at that time praised Tao Jizhi for this kind of virtue. Tao Ji moved directly to the Taiwei Ji office and joined the army. He also came to Beijing to serve as Champion Sima and Dongguan Prefect. During his tenure, Dongguan County was known as peaceful and stable. Tao Jizhi returned to Beijing and was appointed as the minister of Sanqi, leading the left guard Sima, and was transferred to Zhenxi to consult and join the army. Emperor Wu of Qi died, and Emperor Ming of Qi became prime minister. He punished dissenters, but Tao Jizhi refused to flatter him. Emperor Ming of Qi was very afraid of him, so he asked him to leave the capital and serve as the chief minister of the auxiliary state and the prefect of Beihai. The subordinate officials of the DPRK held posts in border towns, and it was rare for scholars to be appointed as officials. Someone advised Tao Ji to come to Emperor Qi Ming to apologize. After Emperor Ming of Qi met with Tao Jizhi, he left him in the capital and appointed him as a hussar to consult with the army and to serve as minister Zuo Cheng. Then he was moved to the post of governor of Jian'an. Tao Jizhi advocated tranquility in his administration, and the people felt comfortable. Tao Jizhi returned to Beijing and served as the Vice Minister of Zhongshu, and then moved to the post of guerrilla general and court lieutenant.
target: The text also includes biographies of Tao Jizhi and Xiao Wangsu. Tao Jizhi was known for his intelligence from a young age, refusing to take money from his grandfather. He served in various posts, refused to flatter Emperor Ming of Qi, and eventually resigned to return home.

source: Tao Jizhi returned to Beijing and served as the Vice Minister of Zhongshu, and then moved to the post of guerrilla general and court lieutenant. When Liang Wangtai Mansion was established, Tao Jizhi moved to serve as the Minister of Huangmen. Tao Jizhi often said that when an official reached a position with a salary of two thousand dan, all his life's wishes were fulfilled. He no longer pursued glory and wealth in the world, so he resigned and returned to his hometown on the grounds of illness. In the early years of Tianjian, the imperial court sent people to his home to confer him the title of Taizhong doctor. Emperor Gaozu said: Liang ruled the world, but he could not see this person. In the tenth year of Tianjian, Tao Jizhi died at home at the age of seventy-five. Tao Jizhi had always lived a poor life, no one could compare with him, and he had been living in seclusion for more than ten years. When he died, his family was destitute and his descendants had no money to bury him. Everyone who heard about the incident felt sad for his integrity. Xiao Wangsu was born in Lanling. His grandfather Xiao Sihua was posthumously awarded the title of General Zhengxi and Kaifu Yitong Sansi in the Song Dynasty. His father, Xiao Huiming, served as the prefect of Wuxing. His grandfather and father both had great reputations. Xiao Wangsu lost his father very early and his family was poor. He was adopted by his uncle Xiao Huixiu.
target: He died in poverty at age seventy-five. Xiao Wangsu was adopted by his uncle, served in official posts, and was known for his quiet, humble, and scholarly nature.

source: Xiao Shisu had a quiet and humble temperament, a pure heart, and a fondness for learning. He could talk about the mysteries of Lao and Zhuang, and he never talked about wealth and wealth, and his joy and anger were indistinguishable. Regardless of whether he was living without an official or holding an official position, he acted according to his own temperament, was open-minded and frank, never arrogant, and showed his simple and simple nature. Scholars therefore respected him. When he took office in Jingkou, he came up with the idea of ​​settling down in Jingkou for the rest of his life, so he built a house in Sheshan. At this time, the imperial court recruited him as the minister of Zhongshu, so he refused to be an official and took up the post. He returned to his residence in Sheshan and lived alone without being concerned about worldly affairs. If he was not a relative, he would not be able to reach the gate of his residence. Xiao Wangsu's wife was the daughter of Taiwei Wang Jian. Xiao Wangsu had separated from her a long time ago and had no children. In the eighth year of Tianjian, Xiao Shisu passed away. His relatives and friends inspected his deeds and conferred upon him the title of Mr. Zhenwen. Shi Chen said: Gu Xianzhi and Tao Jizhi were people who retired to prolong their lives, but Xiao Shisu lacked enthusiasm for being an official. Compared with those who miss their salary, indulge in favors, and work hard in the world, there is indeed a big difference.
target: He built a house in Sheshan and lived in seclusion, refusing to engage with worldly affairs. He died at an unknown age. The text concludes that Gu Xianzhi and Tao Jizhi were people who retired to prolong their lives, while Xiao Wangsu lacked enthusiasm for officialdom, distinguishing them from those who greedily pursue wealth and power.

source: Xiao Zong, the king of Yuzhang, whose courtesy name was Shiqian, was the second son of Emperor Gaozu. In the third year of Tianjian's reign, he was granted the title of Prince of Yuzhang County and was granted a residence of 2,000 households. In the fifth year of Tianjian, he left the capital as envoy Chijie, commander-in-chief of all military affairs in South Xuzhou, general Renwei, and governor of South Xuzhou. Soon he was promoted to the title of Beizhonglang General. In the tenth year of Tianjian's reign, he was transferred to the governorship of Yingsi, Huo Sanzhou Zhujun, General Yunhui, and Yingzhou governor. In the 13th year of Tianjian, he was promoted to General Anyou and led the stone garrison army. In the fifteenth year of Tianjian, he was moved to the post of General Xizhonglang and General of the Guard Army, and then moved to General Anqian and Danyang Yin. In the 16th year of Tianjian's reign, he was appointed as Beizhong Langjiang and South Xuzhou Governor. In the second year of ordinary life, he entered the court as Shizhong and Zhenyou General, and his subordinates began to set up assistant historians. At first, his mother Wu Shuyuan was the concubine of the Marquis of Shuhun of Qi. She was favored by Emperor Gaozu and gave birth to Xiao Zong seven months later. Therefore, many people in the palace suspected that she was not Gaozu's biological son. When Wu Shuyuan's favor faded and she became dissatisfied, people in the palace reported their suspicions to Xiao Zong, so Xiao Zong kept the affair in mind. When he grew up, he was talented and knowledgeable, and was good at writing articles. Gaozu used etiquette to discipline his children, and his sons did not see him often. Therefore, Xiao Zong often complained that Gaozu did not understand him.
target: Xiao Zong, Prince of Yuzhang, was Emperor Gaozu's second son. He held various military and civil posts, including governor of South Xuzhou and Yingzhou. His mother, Wu Shuyuan, was a former concubine of the Marquis of Shuhun of Qi, and Xiao Zong was born seven months after Gaozu married her, leading to suspicions he was not Gaozu's biological son. Xiao Zong grew up talented but resentful, believing Gaozu did not understand him.

source: However, he still couldn't convince himself that he was the son of Houhun Hou of Qi Dong. He heard the saying that if the blood of a living person is dripped on the bones of a dead person, and the blood seeps in, it means that there is a father-son relationship. Xiao Zong secretly dug up Qi Shuhunhou's grave, took out the bones, and dripped blood from his own arm on the bones for testing. At the same time, he killed one of his own sons and took his bones for blood testing. The results could be verified. From then on, Xiao Zong often harbored thoughts of rebellion.
target: He performed a blood-dripping test on the bones of the Marquis of Shuhun and his own son, confirming his paternity, which fueled his rebellious intentions.

source: Xiao Zong heard that Xiao Shiyin, King of Qi Jian'an, was in Wei, so he sent people to Wei to get acquainted with Xiao Baoyin, called Xiao Shiyin his uncle, and promised to lead his territory to submit to Wei. At the time when Emperor Gaozu was launching his Northern Expedition, in the sixth year of Pengcheng, Wei general Yuan Faseng surrendered to Emperor Gaozu in Pengcheng. Emperor Gaozu ordered General Xiao Zong to lead the army and defend Pengcheng City to confront Wei general Anfeng and Wang Yuanyanming. Later, Emperor Gaozu thought that the continuous war had lasted for a long time and was worried about chaos, so he ordered Xiao Zong to withdraw his troops. Xiao Zong was afraid that he would never have a chance to see Xiao Shiyin after returning to the south, so he and Fu Qi fled to Yuan Yanming at night and surrendered to Wei. Wei appointed him as Shizhong, Taiwei, Gaoping Gong, and Danyang King. Xiao Zong changed his name to Xiao Zuan, with the courtesy name Dewen, in memory of the deposed Emperor Shuhunhou of Qi Dynasty. He also wore mourning clothes for him according to the etiquette of treating his father. So some ministers petitioned Emperor Gaozu to remove his title and fiefdom, expel him from his name, and change his surname to Ni. Soon, Shao Ming restored his name and made his son Xiao Zhi the Marquis of Yongxin, granting him a land of thousands of households. In the second year of Datong, Xiao Baoyin occupied Chang'an in Wei and rebelled against Wei. Xiao Zong fled north from Luoyang and was about to flee to Chang'an. He was caught by Jin officials and Wei people killed him. He was forty-nine years old when he died. At first, when Xiao Zong was frustrated, he wrote "Listening to the Ringing of the Bell" and "Sad Poems on Falling Leaves" to express his thoughts and feelings.
target: He eventually surrendered to Wei, changed his name to Xiao Zuan in memory of the deposed Emperor Shuhun, and was killed by Wei at age 49. His poems, "Listening to the Ringing of the Bell" and "Sad Poems on Falling Leaves," expressed his sorrow and frustration.

source: The leaves fall and fly, sometimes flying horizontally and never to return. Lamenting the fallen leaves, how sad are the fallen leaves? Life is like the fallen leaves, falling and withering cannot last forever. Lamenting the fallen leaves, when will the fallen leaves return? They were all born from the same foundation in the past, but now they are no longer related to each other. No one who read his poems at that time did not feel sad. King Lan Ji of Wuling, courtesy name Shixun, was the eighth son of Emperor Gaozu. He has been diligent and studious since he was a child, and is very talented in literature. He does not like to be frivolous and extravagant when writing articles, but pays attention to profound and touching things.
target: Xiao Ji, King of Wuling, was Gaozu's eighth son. He was diligent and talented in literature.

source: The imperial court also called him as envoy Chijie, general Xuanhui, commander-in-chief of the military affairs of Yangnan and Xuzhou, and governor of Yangzhou. Soon after, he was awarded the titles of Chijie, Commander-in-Chief of Yiliang and other thirteen states' military affairs, General of Anxi, and Governor of Yisu, and he was also given the title of Advocate. In the eleventh year of Datong, the imperial court awarded him the titles of Changshi of Sanqi, General of the Expedition to the West, and the third division of Kaifu Yitong. In the past, during the Tianjian period, lightning struck the Sun Gate, and the traces of the lightning strike formed the character "Shaozong Liang Weiwang". The interpreter believed that King Wu referred to King Wuling, so people inside and outside the court turned to him. During the Taiqian period, Hou Jing rebelled and did not send troops to reinforce the capital. After the death of Emperor Gaozu, he proclaimed himself emperor in Shu. He changed his reign name to Tianzheng. Lizi's son Yuanzhao was the crown prince, Yuanzheng was the king of Xiyang, Yuanman was the king of Jingling, Yuanpu was the king of Nanqiao, and Yuansu was the king of Yidu. Xiao Jie, Marquis of Yongfeng, the prefect of Brazil and Zitong counties, was appointed as the general of the expedition to the west, the governor of Yizhou, and the title of King of Qin County. Sima Wang Seng Lue and Zhi Bing joined the army Xu Tong repeatedly warned him. Xiao Ji thought they had second thoughts about him and killed them.
target: He held several official positions, including governor of Jiangzhou and Yangzhou. During the Taiqing period, Hou Jing rebelled, and Xiao Ji did not send troops to reinforce the capital. After Gaozu's death, he proclaimed himself emperor in Shu with the reign name Tianzheng.

source: Shidan knew that Jiaoqi would definitely be defeated, so he refused to agree to him. In Bingxu, Fu Sheng, Xu Zichu and others from Basu killed Xiao Ji's lord Gongsun Huang of Xiaokou City and surrendered to the imperial army. Wang Lin, Song Peng, Ren Yue, Xie Dayen and others took the opportunity to attack Hou Shu and captured three of his fortresses, so more than ten cities on both sides of the Taiwan Strait surrendered. General Fan Meng captured Xiao Ji and his third son Yuanyuan and killed them both at Kip Kou. Xiao Ji was forty-six years old when he died. A petitioner petitioned him to expunge his family name, and Shizu agreed to do so, giving him the surname Taotie. At the beginning, when Xiao Ji was about to usurp and proclaim himself emperor, more than one strange and strange thing happened. The strangest one was that flowers grew out of the brackets surrounding the pillars of the Cypress Palace in the palace. It had forty-six stems, thin and cute, and looked like a lotus. A knowledgeable person said: It is not a good thing to have flowers growing on Wang Dun's ceremonial guard. Xiao's reign name is Tianzheng, which is the same as Xiao Dong's. People say that Tianzheng's Tianzi is Erren, and Zhengzi is Yizhi.
target: He killed advisors who warned him, and his rule was marked by omens, such as flowers growing from palace pillars.

Hou Jing supported Xiao Zhengde as emperor, changed the year to the first year of Zhengping, and Hou Jing became prime minister.
target: He led an army downriver to attack Hou Jing but was defeated by Western Wei forces.
