target: He was captured and killed at age 46. His reign name Tianzheng was considered unlucky, and he was posthumously given the surname Taotie.

source: A knowledgeable person said: It is not a good thing to have flowers growing on Wang Dun's ceremonial guard. Xiao's reign name is Tianzheng, which is the same as Xiao Dong's. People say that Tianzheng's Tianzi is Erren, and Zhengzi is Yizhi. Xiao Dong and Xiao Ji pretended to be emperors, but each only lasted a year before being eliminated. King Xiao Zhengde of Linhe, also known as Gonghe, was the third son of King Jinghui of Linchuan. When he was young, he was rough, evil, and disrespectful of etiquette. At first, when Gaozu had no sons, he adopted him as his son. When Gaozu ascended the throne, Xiao Zhengde hoped to make himself the prince. Later, Gaozu established Prince Zhaoming and named Xiao Zhengde the Marquis of Xifeng, with a settlement of 500 households. From then on, Xiao Zhengde became dissatisfied. He often harbored ulterior motives and coveted the throne of the emperor, hoping that disaster would happen by chance. In ordinary six years, he appointed Huangmen Shilang as Qingche General and appointed an assistant historian. Soon, he fled to Wei, and a minister asked Gaozu to remove the officials he had granted. In ordinary seven years, Xiao Zhengde escaped from Wei again. Emperor Gaozu did not blame him, restored his title, and then appointed him as the general to conquer the captives. In the fourth year of Zhongdatong, Xiao Zhengde was appointed General Xinwu and Grand Administrator of Wu County. Later, the imperial court recruited him as a servant, a general of the Fu army, and appointed him as an assistant historian. He was also named the king of Linhe County, with a settlement of 2,000 households, and he was also made a general of the left guard. But he became increasingly violent and recruited desperadoes.
target: Xiao Zhengde, Prince of Linhe, was the third son of Prince Jinghui of Linchuan. He was adopted by Gaozu but became dissatisfied when he was not made crown prince. He fled to Wei but later returned.

source: I hope you will obey the wishes of the people of the world and understand my sincerity. Xiao Zhengde was very happy after reading Hou Jing's letter and said: Hou Jing's meaning coincides with mine. This is God's support for me. Then he agreed to Hou Jing's request. When Hou Jing arrived at the river, Xiao Zhengde secretly brought an empty boat, pretending to load it with reeds, but actually using it to carry Hou Jing across the river. The imperial court did not know Xiao Zhengde's conspiracy and sent him to guard Zhuquehang. When Hou Jing arrived at Zhuquehang, Xiao Zhengde led his army to attack the capital together with Hou Jing. Hou Jing supported Xiao Zhengde as emperor, changed the year to the first year of Zhengping, and Hou Jing became prime minister. After the capture of Taicheng, Hou Jing restored the Taiqing era title and demoted Xiao Zhengde to Grand Sima. Xiao Zhengde had a complaint. When Hou Jing found out about it, he was worried that he would rebel, so he falsely conveyed the imperial edict and killed him. The great-grandson of Xiao Yu, King of Hedong, was the second son of Prince Zhaoming. In ordinary two years, he was named the Duke of Zhijiang County. In the third year of Zhongdatong, Emperor Gaozu changed his title to the king of Hedong County, with a settlement of 2,000 households. And appointed him as General Ningyuan and Shitou garrison. Later, he was transferred out of the capital to serve as the prefect of Langxie and Pengcheng counties. Later, he was transferred back to the capital and served as Shizhong and Qingche General, and was appointed as an assistant historian. Later, he was transferred to Nanzhong Langjiang and Xiangzhou Governor. Soon, Hou Jing invaded the capital, and Xiao Yu led the army to come for reinforcements. When the army arrived at Qingcao Lake, Taicheng had fallen. An order was issued to withdraw the troops and turn back. Luo Yu led the army back to Xiangzhou to defend it. At that time, Shizu led his army and was stationed there. Zhang Zuan, the newly appointed governor of Yongzhou, reported secretly to Shizu: "Kou Yu is recruiting troops to start a rebellion in Hedong and gathering food and grass in Yueyang. These are all illegal things. They plan to attack Jiangling." Shidan was very frightened after hearing this, so he walked back to Jiangling by a small road, and sent Zhou Hong to consult with Xiao Yu's naxiang to supervise Xiao Yu's grain and army. Xiao Yu said: We are all governors, why do we suddenly want to be subordinate to others? Shizu sent people there three times, but Xiao Yu refused to obey Shizu. Shi Dan was furious and sent his son Lu Chabi to conquer him, but his friends were defeated and killed by Lu Yu.
target: He conspired with Hou Jing, who supported him as emperor with the reign name Zhengping. After Hou Jing captured Taicheng, he demoted Xiao Zhengde and later killed him out of fear of rebellion. Xiao Yu, Prince of Hedong, was the second son of Prince Zhaoming. He held various posts, including governor of Xiangzhou. When Hou Jing invaded the capital, Xiao Yu led reinforcements but arrived after Taicheng fell. He returned to Xiangzhou to defend it. Shizu, suspicious of Xiao Yu's intentions, sent forces to attack him. Xiao Yu was besieged in Changsha for a long time but eventually captured and beheaded.

source: Xiao Yu was brave and courageous when he was young. He was able to appease the soldiers and was very popular among the soldiers. After being besieged for a long time, although the inside and outside were cut off, the defense was still very strong. Later, Shizu sent the leading general Wang Tanluan to attack Ludeng instead of Baose. Wang only avoided building earth mountains and stayed close to the city. He attacked hard day and night. Arrows and stones were like rain, and more than half of the soldiers in the city were killed or injured. Xiao Yu was very embarrassed and anxious, so he secretly equipped a large ship and prepared to break out. Just as Xiao Yu's general Murong Hua was leading Wang Shidao into the city, Lu Deng looked around and saw that all the people close to him were scattered, so he was captured. Xiao Yu said to his guard: "Don't kill me. I want to meet Shizu. I want to rebuke this thief who slandered others. I will die without regret." The person in charge of guarding him said: I was ordered not to allow it. So he beheaded him and sent his head to Jingzhen. Shizu sent his head back and buried him. At first, when Xiao Yu was about to fail, he secretly looked at his face in the mirror, but his head was not visible. He also saw a tall man lying on the house, with his hands on the ground looking down at his navel. He also saw a white dog as big as a donkey, running out of the city and gone somewhere. Xiao Yu hated this phenomenon, and soon the city was captured. Shi Chen said: Xiao Zong and Xiao Zhengde were both rebellious and wanted to do as they pleased, so it was right for them to bring about their own destruction. During the Taiqing period, Hou Jing rebelled and invaded the capital. Xiao Ji took advantage of the rich resources of Yong and Shu, but did not lead his army to rescue the court in danger, which showed his integrity. When the rebel Hou Jing was killed, he began to raise troops, and his troops were unknown, which caused a disaster. Alas! He was punished like Guan Shu and Cai Shu, the ministers who caused chaos in the Western Zhou Dynasty. The disaster was brought about by himself.
target: Before his fall, he experienced ominous visions, including his head disappearing in a mirror and a large white dog fleeing the city. The historical commentary concludes that Xiao Zong and Xiao Zhengde's rebellions led to their own destruction, while Xiao Ji's failure to aid the capital during Hou Jing's rebellion and his subsequent uprising brought disaster upon himself.

source: Hou Jing, whose courtesy name was Wanjing, was from Shuofang. Some people say he was from Yanmen. When he was young, he behaved wildly and his fellow villagers were afraid of him. When he reached adulthood, he was vigorous and strong, and was good at horseback riding and archery. Therefore, he was selected as a garrison in Beizhen and gradually made meritorious service in the army. In the first year of Wei Xiaochang, Xianyu Xiuli, a soldier from Huaishuo town, rebelled in Dingzhou and captured the county. At the same time, Tujin Luozhou, a soldier from Rouxuan town, led his party to invade Youzhou and Jizhou. They joined forces with Xianyu Xiuli, totaling more than 100,000 people. Later, Xianyu Xiuli was killed by Yuan Hongye, and his men were scattered. Ge Rong, the general of Huaishuo Town, took the opportunity to gather Xianyu Xiuli's scattered soldiers, attacked and killed Tujinluozhou, and annexed all Tujinluozhou's troops. People called him "Ge Thief". In the fourth year of Xiaochang, Emperor Wei Ming died, and Empress Dowager Hu came to rule. Tianzhu General Er Zhurong raised troops from Jinyang and entered Luoyang, killing Empress Hu and Hu's relatives. Hou Jing initially brought his army to see Er Zhurong. Er Zhurong thought that Hou Jing had a genius and immediately appointed him as a general to lead the troops. When they were dispatched, Ge Rong's bandits marched south to Luoyang. Er Zhurong went to conquer it in person. He ordered Hou Jing to be the vanguard and led his army to Hanoi to attack Ge Rong. He defeated Jiang's army and captured Ge Rong alive. Because of his great achievements, Hou Jing was promoted to the governor of Dingzhou, Daxingtai, and was granted the title of Duke of Puyang. Hou Jing became famous from then on.
target: Hou Jing, courtesy name Wanjing, was from Shuofang, possibly Yanmen. Wild in youth, he became a strong, skilled horseman and archer, serving as a garrison in Beizhen. During Wei Xiaochang's first year, Xianyu Xiuli rebelled in Dingzhou, joined by Tujin Luozhou, amassing over 100,000 troops. After Xianyu Xiuli was killed, Ge Rong gathered his forces, killed Tujin Luozhou, and became known as "Ge Thief." In the fourth year, Emperor Wei Ming died, and Empress Dowager Hu ruled. Er Zhurong raised troops, killed her, and appointed Hou Jing as a general. Hou Jing served as vanguard against Ge Rong, capturing him alive, earning promotion to governor of Dingzhou and Duke of Puyang.

source: Hou Jing became famous from then on. Soon, Emperor Shenwu of Qi became the prime minister of Wei. He led his army into Luoyang and killed the Zhu family. Hou Jing led his army to surrender to Gao Huan and was appointed by Emperor Shenwu. Hou Jing was cruel and tyrannical, and controlled the army strictly. However, all the treasures he plundered from the enemy were distributed to the soldiers, so the soldiers were happy to serve him and often won battles. General Hou Jing holds military power, which is equal to that of Emperor Shenwu. Wei appointed him as Situ and Nandaoxingtai, with an army of 100,000, and he controlled Henan alone.
target: Hou Jing later surrendered to Gao Huan, becoming Emperor Shenwu of Qi. He was cruel but shared plunder with soldiers, ensuring loyalty.

source: The areas east of Hangu Pass and west of Xiaqiu are all willing to submit to the Holy Dynasty so that the people can recuperate and live. To this end, they work together and swear to the death without any second thoughts. As for Qing and Xu Shuzhou, they only need to write a letter and send an emissary to deliver the order, without having to worry about the planning and operation of the Holy Dynasty. The estrangement and hatred between me and the Gao family has already formed. When the Prime Minister was seriously ill, he sent a letter to recruit him. The south of the Yellow River is the area under my jurisdiction. It is not difficult to convert the Holy Dynasty to the same country. All the officials admire me and obey my call. If the Qi and Song areas are pacified, we can slowly try to capture Yan and Fang. I hope that your majesty will open the sky net and rule the world. I hope you can understand my sincere feelings and show me kindness. When Ding He arrived, Gaozu summoned the ministers to discuss the matter in the court hall. The minister, Pushe Xieju, and all the officials said that it was not appropriate to recruit Hou Jing. Gaozu did not follow the opinions and decided to accept Hou Jing's surrender. When Emperor Shenwu died, his son Gao Cheng succeeded him and became Emperor Wenxiang. Emperor Gaozu then issued an edict to make Hou Jing the King of Henan, a general, an envoy to hold the festival, supervise the military affairs in the north and south of Henan, and the Daxingtai. Qi Wenxiang sent General Murong Shaozong to surround Hou Jing in Changshe. Hou Jing asked the Western Wei Dynasty for help. The Western Wei Dynasty sent Wuxu Wang Douqing and others to lead troops to rescue him, and Murong Shaozong retreated. Hou Jing asked Sizhou Governor Yangyaren for help. Yangyaren sent Chief Shi Denghong to lead troops to Rushui. Upon seeing this, the Yuanqing army fled at night. So he occupied Xuanhu and Xiangcheng, and asked Emperor Gaozu to send governors to guard them. Gaozu Shao ordered Yang Yaren to be the governor of Yuzhou and Sizhou and move his troops to guard Xuanhu; he ordered Yang Sijian, the prefect of Xiyang, to be the governor of Yinzhou and guard Xiangcheng. Marshal Wei Gang died, and Yiliang took his parents and surrendered to the Chu Dynasty. Emperor Wenxiang of Qi was worried that Hou Jing's alliance with the West and South would become a disaster for himself, so he wrote to Hou Jing:
target: He held military power equal to Emperor Shenwu, controlling Henan with 100,000 troops. When Emperor Shenwu fell ill, he warned his son Gao Cheng of Hou Jing's cunning. Hou Jing, fearing for his life, surrendered to Liang's Emperor Gaozu in Taiqing's first year, citing Gao Cheng's threats. Emperor Gaozu accepted, making Hou Jing King of Henan. Qi's Murong Shaozong besieged Hou Jing, who sought Western Wei aid, forcing a retreat. Hou Jing then occupied Xuanhu and Xiangcheng.

source: If you treat your parents like this, it's even less important to treat your wife and children. If there is any benefit to killing my wife and children, it is impossible for you to stop. Killing them will do me no harm, it is just killing in vain. The life and death of my wife's family is entirely up to you, and it has nothing to do with me. What Zundao said is not false, but he was imprisoned. I am afraid that the details are not enough, so I restate it and express my diligent thoughts again. I hope you will make good plans and reply to me in time to tell me your thoughts. Your father and I used to work together like brothers. Later, a treacherous villain who loved to slander us alienated us and turned us into enemies. When I stroked the bow string and held the arrow in my hand, I felt sad. When I cut off the silk and wrote a reply to you, I was so excited that I didn't know how to express it. In December, Hou Jing led his army to besiege Qiaocheng, but failed to capture it, so he withdrew his troops to attack Chengfu and captured it. Hou Jing also sent his Xingtai Zuocheng Wang Wei and Zuo Minlangzhong Wangze to Gaozu to offer advice, advocating that a descendant of the Yuan family should be selected as the lord of Wei and help him ascend the throne through the Northern Expedition. Emperor Gaozu agreed to the plan. An imperial edict was sent to send Prince Sheren Yuan Zhen to be the King of Xianyang, and wait for him to cross the river. After crossing the river, he was allowed to ascend the throne and proclaim himself emperor, and he was provided with an imperial chariot. Emperor Wenxiang of Qi sent Murong Shaozong to pursue Hou Jing, but Hou Jing retreated into Guoyang. At this time, Hou Jingshang had thousands of horses, tens of thousands of soldiers, and more than 10,000 vehicles, and he and Murong Shaozong were in a stalemate in the north of Woyang. Hou Jing ran out of food, and his soldiers were all from Jiangbei and were unwilling to cross south. His general Bao Xian and others led their men to surrender to Murong Shaozong. When Hou Jing saw that his army was in disarray, he crossed the Huaihe River from Xia Shi with a few of his friends, and gradually gathered scattered troops. He got 800 horses and infantry, and fled to Shouchun. Wei An of Jianzhou accepted him. In Shouchun, Hou Jing sent someone to petition Emperor Gaozu to demote his official position. Emperor Gaozu treated him favorably, but Xia Shao did not agree to his request for demotion and still appointed him as the shepherd of Yuzhou without changing his original official position.
target: Qi's Emperor Wenxiang wrote to Hou Jing, urging his return with promises of rank and family safety. Hou Jing replied, justifying his actions and rejecting the offer. In December, Hou Jing besieged Qiaocheng, failed, but captured Chengfu. He proposed selecting a Yuan descendant as Wei's lord for a Northern Expedition; Emperor Gaozu agreed. Qi's Murong Shaozong pursued Hou Jing to Woyang, where Hou Jing's army disintegrated due to starvation. He fled to Shouchun with 800 horses, where Emperor Gaozu treated him favorably, appointing him shepherd of Yuzhou.

source: When Hou Jing saw that his army was in disarray, he crossed the Huaihe River from Xia Shi with a few of his friends, and gradually gathered scattered troops. He got 800 horses and infantry, and fled to Shouchun. Wei An of Jianzhou accepted him. In Shouchun, Hou Jing sent someone to petition Emperor Gaozu to demote his official position. Emperor Gaozu treated him favorably, but Xia Shao did not agree to his request for demotion and still appointed him as the shepherd of Yuzhou without changing his original official position. After Hou Jing occupied Shouchun, he became rebellious. All the residents of Shouchun's city were recruited as sergeants, and he stopped collecting taxes and land rent without authorization. All the children of the people were assigned to the soldiers in the army. He also requested the emperor to provide tens of thousands of pieces of brocade to make military uniforms. Zhu Yi, the leader of the army, believed that the imperial brocade office was only used by the imperial court to award meritorious deeds nearby, and could not be used as military uniforms for border towns, so he asked for permission to provide him with green cloth. Hou Jing got the cloth and used it all to make robes, so he admired the color cyan. He also thought that the weapons supplied by Xingtai were not of high quality, and asked for the blacksmiths from Dongye to be rebuilt. Gaozu ordered that all be given to him. After Hou Jing's defeat in Wuyang, he repeatedly requested funds from the imperial court, but the imperial court was generous and never refused. Previously, the governor of Yuzhou, Zhenyang Marquis Xiao Yuanming, led all the troops to besiege Pengcheng. He was defeated and fell to Wei. During the period, he sent people back to Liang to state the Wei people's request to restore old friendship. In February of the second year, Emperor Gaozu discussed peace with Wei again. Hou Jing was very frightened when he found out, and hurriedly sent someone to send a seal to Gaozu to try his best to dissuade him. Gaozu did not listen to Hou Jing's dissuasion. Later, Hou Jingshang's memorial was arrogant and his words were arrogant. Xiao Fan, the king of Poyang, was guarding Hefei. He and Yang Yaren, the governor of Sizhou, repeatedly reported that Hou Jing had the intention to rebel. The leader Zhu Yi said: Hou Jing only has hundreds of rebels, how can he rebel. They suppressed their official seals and did not report to Emperor Gaozu, but instead increased the rewards to Hou Jing, so Hou Jing's conspiracy to rebel became more and more exposed. Hou Jing also knew that Linhe King Xiao Zhengde had grudges and complaints against the court, so he secretly sent people to make friends with him and collude with him. Xiao Zhengde agreed to be Hou Jing's internal adviser. In August, Hou Jing sent troops to rebel, attacked Ma Tou and Muzha, and captured the prefect Liu Shenmao, the garrison leader Cao Zhu and others.
target: In Shouchun, Hou Jing rebelled, conscripting residents and stopping taxes. He requested brocade for uniforms but received green cloth, which he used. After a defeat, he sought funds from the court, which were granted. In the second year, Emperor Gaozu discussed peace with Wei, alarming Hou Jing, who sent arrogant memorials opposing it. Poyang King Xiao Fan and others reported Hou Jing's rebellion intentions, but official Zhu Yi dismissed them. Hou Jing secretly allied with Linhe King Xiao Zhengde. In August, Hou Jing rebelled, attacking Ma Tou and Muzha. Emperor Gaozu ordered multiple governors to counter him.

source: They suppressed their official seals and did not report to Emperor Gaozu, but instead increased the rewards to Hou Jing, so Hou Jing's conspiracy to rebel became more and more exposed. Hou Jing also knew that Linhe King Xiao Zhengde had grudges and complaints against the court, so he secretly sent people to make friends with him and collude with him. Xiao Zhengde agreed to be Hou Jing's internal adviser. In August, Hou Jing sent troops to rebel, attacked Ma Tou and Muzha, and captured the prefect Liu Shenmao, the garrison leader Cao Zhu and others. Emperor Gaozu then ordered the governor of Hezhou, Poyang King Xiao Fan, to be the governor of the South Road, the governor of North Xuzhou, Fengshan Hou Xiao Zhengbiao, to be the governor of the north, Sizhou governor Liu Zhongli to be the governor of the west, and Pei Zhigao, the regular servant of Tongzhi Sanqi, to be the governor of Shudao. In October, Hou Jing left one of his troops, Wang Haogui, to guard Shouchun City, while he led his army to pretend to attack Hefei, but actually went to sneak attack Qiaozhou, and Qiaozhou assisted Dong Shao in opening the city and surrendering. The governor, Fengcheng Hou Xiaotai, was captured. Emperor Gaozu learned of this and sent Wang Zhi, the prince's family commander, to lead three thousand troops to defend along the river. Hou Jing attacked Liyang. Zhuang Tie, the prefect of Liyang, sent his brother Zhuang Jun to lead hundreds of people to attack Hou Jing's camp at night. They were unsuccessful. Zhuang Jun died in the battle and Zhuang Tie surrendered. Xiao Zhengde first dispatched dozens of large ships, pretending to be carrying Diwei, but actually carrying Hou Jing across the river. Hou Jing arrived at Jingkou and was about to cross the river. He was worried about Wang Zhi's obstruction. Soon, Wang Zhi retreated without any reason. Hou Jing still didn't believe it when he heard that he secretly sent someone to spy. He said to the sent person: If Wang Zhi really retreats, you can break the branches of the river as a signal. The man who went to spy came back as he said. Hou Jing was overjoyed and said, "My mission was successful." Just crossing the river from Caishi, there were hundreds of horses and thousands of soldiers, but the people in the capital did not notice it. Hou Jing immediately divided his troops to attack Gushu, captured Wencheng Hou Kukong, the prefect of Jinhu, and then arrived at Cisu.
target: In October, Hou Jing feigned an attack on Hefei but took Qiaozhou, capturing Fengcheng Hou Xiaotai. He crossed the Yangtze from Caishi with hundreds of horses and thousands of soldiers, unnoticed. He divided troops to attack Gushu, then reached Cisu. Defenders fled, and Hou Jing advanced to the palace city, burning gates. After failed assaults, he built a barrier, cutting off supplies.

source: In November, Hou Jing established Xiao Zhengde as emperor. Xiao Zhengde assumed the pseudo-throne in Yixian Hall and changed his reign name to Zhengping. At the beginning, there were words like "正平" in nursery rhymes, so the era name was established to fit in with it. Hou Jing proclaimed himself Prime Minister and General Tianzhu, and Xiao Zhengde married his daughter to him. Hou Jing attacked Dongfu City again, built a hundred-foot-high tower cart, and completely collapsed the city battlements, and Cambodian City was captured.
target: He established Xiao Zhengde as emperor in November, naming himself Prime Minister. Hou Jing attacked Dongfu City, capturing it and killing over 2,000 officials.

source: Hou Jing then sent Lu Genshan's sons Xiao Jianli and Yi to guard Dongfu City with Lu Huilue. Hou Jing also built an earth mountain on the east and west side of the palace city to monitor the city. He also built two earth mountains inside the city to deal with the earth mountains outside the city. He ordered everyone below the prince to carry the earth mountain on their backs. At the beginning, Hou Jingjun arrived at the city, expecting to capture the capital in one fell swoop. The order was very strict and the people were not allowed to be invaded. After the siege failed, the people were scattered and depressed. He was also afraid that reinforcements would arrive and his army would collapse, so he allowed the soldiers to kill and plunder. The roads were blocked with corpses. Some wealthy families were arbitrarily robbed and extorted, and their children, wives, and concubines were all taken into the military camps. When it came time to build a mountain of earth, no matter how high or low they were, they would work day and night. The sergeants would beat them with wooden sticks, and the weak ones would be killed to fill up the mountain. The sound of wailing shook the heaven and the earth.
target: He built earth mountains to monitor the city, forcing labor, with weak killed to fill them.

source: Hou Jing gradually ran out of food. At this time, a handful of rice was worth hundreds of thousands of dollars, and five or six out of ten people resorted to cannibalism to satisfy their hunger. At first, when the reinforcements arrived on the north bank, the people supported the old and young to wait for the king's army. Unexpectedly, these armies had just crossed the Huai River, and they robbed and plundered. Originally, some people in the thief party wanted to leave the thief army anyway, but after hearing this situation, they gave up the idea of ​​surrendering.
target: Reinforcements arrived, but Hou Jing defeated them. Food ran out, leading to cannibalism.

source: I can't see him again. Although Gaozu's actions were restricted, he was still very resentful in his heart and often condemned and denied what Hou Jing heard about. Hou Jing was deeply in awe of Gaozu and did not dare to force him. Hou Jing sent soldiers to be on duty in the palace province. Emperor Gaozu asked Zhou Shizhen, the supervisor of the production bureau: "Who sent them?" He replied: It’s the Prime Minister. Gao Dan pretended to be confused and said, "What Prime Minister?" He replied: "It's Prime Minister Hou." Emperor Gaozu said angrily: "It's the man named Hou Jing." Why call him prime minister! From then on, Emperor Gaozu had many needs, but many of them were unsatisfactory. Even the food was cut off. Emperor Gaozu then became ill and died of anger. After the death of Emperor Gaozu, Hou Jingmi did not mourn, and the coffin was temporarily parked in Zhaoyang Hall. None of the civil and military officials inside and outside knew about the incident. More than twenty days later, the coffin was carried to the front hall of Taiji to welcome the crown prince as emperor. Hou Jing then pretended to issue an edict to pardon the Northerners who had been slaves. Trying to bribe these people for his use. He also sent Yi Tong to Lailiang and led his troops to attack Xuancheng. Yang Hua, the internal historian in Xuancheng, was beheaded by Yang Liang. Hou Jing sent his general Li Xianming to attack Yang Hua, and Yang Hua led the county to surrender. Hou Jing sent Yi, Song Zixian and others to lead the army eastward and stationed in Qiantang. The new city garrison leader Dai Sengyi seized the county to resist him. This month, Hou Jing sent the Chinese army Hou Zijian into the Wu army, arrested Yu Ziyue and Zhang Dahei, and returned to the capital to kill them. At that time, Lincheng Gong Xiao Dalian, the governor of Dongyangzhou, was guarding the state, and Zhang Sheng, the prefect of Wuxing, was guarding the county. From Nanling onwards, they were all guarding each other. The only areas where Hou Jing's order could be implemented were west of Wu County and north of Nanling. In June, Hou Jing appointed Guo Yuanjian as Shangshu Pushe, Beidao Xingtai, and general of all military forces in the north of the Yangtze River to guard the New Qin Dynasty. County residents Lu Ji, Dai Wenju and others raised more than 10,000 troops and killed Su Shanyu, the governor sent by Hou Jing. They elected the former Huainan governor Wencheng Hou Xiaoning as the leader of the alliance to resist Hou Jing. After Song Zixian learned about it, he led his army to attack them, and Lu Ji and others abandoned the city and fled.
target: Hou Jing sought peace, demanding four Yangtze-right states and hostages. An alliance was made, but Hou Jing broke it, attacking again. The palace city fell; Hou Jing plundered, captured officials, and burned corpses. He falsely issued edicts, demoted Xiao Zhengde, and appointed his own governors. Emperor Gaozu died in May, reportedly from anger after Hou Jing's actions. Hou Jing hid the death for over twenty days before proclaiming the crown prince emperor.

source: Hou Jing was furious when he heard about this, so he sent Baekje's envoys to Xiaozhuangyan Temple and locked them up, preventing them from entering or leaving. In the first month of the first year of Dabao, Hou Jing pretended to have Shao's orders and added forty swordsmen to himself without permission. He also appointed himself a front and rear Yu Bao advocate, and also appointed himself a left and right chief minister and four ministers. The former Jiangdu ordered Zu Hao to raise troops in Guangling, killed Dong Shao, the governor sent by Hou Jing, and elected Xiao Meng, the former prince's native, as the governor. He also contacted the Wei people as backup and used fast riding to publish proclamations to places far and near to denounce Hou Jing. When Hou Jing heard the news, he was very frightened. On the same day, he led Hou Zijian and others to send troops from Saidan, and all the land, water and rain troops were mobilized. Hou Jing refused to defend the city, but Hou Jing attacked the city and captured it. Hou Jing split Zu Hao's chariot to show the public, and killed everyone in the city, old and young.
target: Hou Jing continued campaigns, killing Xiao Zhengde and appointing puppet kings. He faced rebellions, including Zu Hao's in Guangling, which he crushed, killing all residents.

source: What's more, it's a wonderful strategy, a brilliant plan, profound and difficult to predict. The Prime Minister has great merits and deeds, and his achievements are unparalleled in the stars. How can he continue to use the usual name unchanged? The Prime Minister should be granted the titles of General of the Universe and Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in Liuhe, while all other positions remain unchanged. source: Liu Xun, courtesy name Wentong, was born in Jie County, Hedong. His father Shilong was Sikong in the Qi Dynasty. When Liu Xun was seventeen years old, Emperor Wu of Qi was still a member of the Central Army, so he was appointed to join the army and transferred to the position of chief registrar. The poem goes: After you are crowned among the others at the banquet, I am the only one who really thinks about meritorious deeds. I once chatted with Gaozu again, and Gaozu said: Xu Yuanyu disobeyed orders in Cennan, and the "Book of Zhou" is not related to the crime. I have pardoned his disciples, how about it? Liu Xun replied: "The punishment will not be imposed on his descendants, and the rewards will be extended to future generations. Today I see the Holy Dynasty again." At that time people called it wisdom. Soon he was transferred to the right servant of Shangshu. In the fourth year of Tianjian, a large-scale Northern Expedition was launched. Liang Hong, the king of Linchuan, supervised the army, with Liu Xun as his deputy. After the army returned, they still served as servants. Due to a long illness, he was transferred to the post of Dr. Jin Ziguanglu, with additional Sanqi regular attendants and twenty close followers. Before becoming an official, he served as envoy Chijie, General Annan, and governor of Xiangzhou. He died in office in October of the sixth year at the age of forty-six. Emperor Gaozu wore plain clothes and expressed his condolences. He was given as a gift to Shizhong and the general of the Fu army, and was given a piece of propaganda, with the posthumous title Mu. Not long ago I heard that all the ministers in the capital were so frightened that they dared not even speak out; now, fortunately, we are far away from the court and are temporarily safe. The imperial court ordered us to attack Yongzhou, but it was just a way for both sides to kill each other. Didn't you see Xiao Lingjun's fate? source: My cousin Du Youwen was the governor of Liangzhou and asked Wei Rui to go with him. Great-grandfather Wei Gui moved south to Xiangyang in the early Taiyuan years of Emperor Guiwu's reign in the east, where he served as the minister of the local cavalry and scattered cavalry. His grandfather, Wei Gongxun, served as the prefect of Yiyang in Song Dynasty. His father, Wei Yizheng, passed away at an early age. Wei Ai lost his father when he was young. He served his mother very filially and became famous for this. Wei Aiqing was an upright and upright man who did not want to socialize and was dedicated to learning. source: Zhang Huishao, courtesy name Deji, was from Yiyang. He had military talent in his youth. He was appointed as a soldier in the army and joined the army as general Ningshuo and military leader. The righteous army was temporarily stationed in Han Dynasty, and Emperor Gaozu sent Zhu Siyuan, the leader of the Hui Shao Yu army, to patrol the Yangtze River to block the grain transportation channel between Ying and Lu cities. Shen Nandang, the navy chief of Yingcheng, led ten light warships to challenge Hui Shao, but was defeated by Hui Shao. Shen Nandang was beheaded and all his weapons were seized. The righteous army stopped at Xinlin and Zhuque, and Hui Shao made many military exploits. After Jiankang City was captured by the righteous army, Hui Shao moved to serve as the general of the auxiliary state and the front army, the commander of Zhihe and Zuoxi. After Liang Gaozu ascended the throne, he granted Huishao the title of Marquis of Shiyang County, with a settlement of 500 households. Hui Shao was again promoted to General of Xiaoqi, and the masters of Zhihe and Xizhan remained the same. At that time, the remnant party of Donghun Hou, consisting of hundreds of people, secretly sneaked into Nanyemen and Beiyemen, set fire to Shenhumen, and killed the guard Zhang Hongce. Hui Shao led his men to rush to fight and beheaded them to the tenth level. Only then did the rest of the party escape. Due to his meritorious service, Hui Shao increased his residence by 200 households, and was moved to the position of the crown prince's right guard.

source: Everyone was looking for the monk everywhere, but no one knew where the monk was. After his parents died, Teng Tanggong did not eat or drink for about ten days. He cried so sadly that he vomited blood, fainted and then woke up. Teng Tanggong did not wear cotton-padded clothes during the mid-winter season and only ate vegetables throughout his life. Every time on the anniversary of the death of my parents, I can't bear the longing, and I cry heartbroken day and night. There were two winter trees outside Teng Tangong's house. Suddenly a divine light appeared from the trees. Soon the image of the Buddha and the guards of honor on both sides appeared. Their appearance was clear. They walked into Teng Tangong's house from the gate. Everyone in the Teng family, big and small, bowed and worshiped the Buddha. It took a long time for the Buddha's image to disappear. Monks and people from far and near preached and performed things. The prefect Wang Sengqian recommended Teng Tanggong to be a meritorious officer, but Teng Tanggong firmly refused to take up the post. Wang Jian followed Wang Sengqian in the county at that time, and he called Teng Tanggong Teng Zengzi. In the first year of Tianjian, Lu Lian was ordered to serve as an envoy to visit various places to understand the customs and conditions of the people. He reported Teng Tangong's filial piety and his response to the gods and Buddhas. Teng Tangong had three sons, all of whom were virtuous and accomplished. At that time, there was also Xu Puji, a native of Linxiang, Changsha. He was in mourning and the coffin had not yet been buried. A fire broke out in his neighbor's house and the fire spread to his house. Xu Puji howled and cried bitterly and leaned on the coffin, trying to cover the fire with his body. Neighbors went to rescue him, but he was roasted until he passed out. It took many days for him to wake up. There was a girl in Wanling, Xuancheng, who was sleeping in the same bed with her mother. Her mother was caught by a tiger. The girl screamed and grabbed the tiger, and all the tiger hairs were caught by her. After running for more than ten miles, the tiger dropped the girl's mother. The girl carried her mother home, and her mother was still alive. It took an hour before she died. The prefect Xiao Chen presented gifts to her family to help with the funeral and reported the situation to the emperor. Shen Chongsu, whose courtesy name is Si Zheng, was born in Wukang, Wuxing. Shen Chongsu's father, Shen Huaiming, served as the governor of Yanzhou during the Song Dynasty. When Shen Chongsu was six years old, his father died. During the funeral, the ceremony of crying and dancing exceeded the usual ceremony. When he reached adulthood, he would work as a copywriter to support his mother. In the early years of Qi Jianwu's reign, Shen Chongsu was recruited from his home to serve in court.
target: Xu Puji, from Linxiang, protected his mother's coffin from a fire, suffering severe burns. A girl from Wanling fought a tiger to save her mother, carrying her home before she died. Shen Chongsu, from Wuxing, mourned his mother with extreme grief, lying on her grave in all weather. Despite an imperial edict promoting him, he refused the position and died from grief at age thirty-nine.

source: He should be asked immediately to remove his mourning clothes and be promoted to the post of prince's horse washer. The door panel is decorated with banners to encourage this custom. target: Xunjiang, from Yingyin, mourned his father and brother with such intensity that he lost his hair and eyesight. He was promoted by imperial decree but died at twenty-one from grief.

source: The prefectures and counties reported this situation to the court, and Gaozu Xiashao sent Zhongshushe to remove his mourning clothes and promoted him to the Zuo Changshi of the Yuzhang Kingdom. Not only is your father's order irresistible, but it will also make you famous in future generations. It's not just your reputation that will be made famous! Xunjiang then accepted the official position. In the end, he died at home due to grief and physical damage. He died at the age of twenty-one. Yu Qianlou's courtesy name is Zizhen, a new savage. Yu Yi, the father of Yu Qian Lou, was recruited as the chief secretary of Situ. He refused to take office, so he was famous.
target: Yu Qianlou, from Xinye, tasted his father's excrement to check his health and prayed to die in his father's place. He served as an honest official, refusing treasures, and died at forty-six.

source: Ji Feo's courtesy name is Yanxiao, and he is a native of Feng Yilianshao. His family has lived in Xiangyang for generations. Ji Feo was very filial when he was young. When he was eleven years old, his biological mother passed away. During the mourning period, Ji Feol was in a state of poverty, almost destroying his life due to grief. His relatives were surprised by his filial piety. In the early years of Tianjian, Ji Min's father served as the original township magistrate of Wuxing. He was framed by treacherous officials and was arrested and handed over to Tingwei for interrogation. Ji Feo was fifteen years old at the time. He stood on the thoroughfare and cried, begging the ministers to avenge his father's justice. The passers-by who saw this scene shed tears for him. Ji Fol's father is theoretically innocent, but he is ashamed of being interrogated by officials, so he bears the guilt out of thin air and will be sentenced to death if convicted. Ji Fol then rushed outside the court to beat the Dengwen drum set up for people to redress their grievances, and asked to die in his father's place.
target: Ji Feo, from Xiangyang, begged to die for his father, who was falsely accused. At fifteen, he beat the Dengwen drum and faced torture without flinching.

source: Ji Fei rejected Wang Zhi's request. When Ji Fol was seventeen years old, he was called up to be the chief registrar of the state. He was released from prison in Wannian County and served as county magistrate for one year. His education moved the people and benevolence and righteousness prevailed. Ji Feo returned to Ying from Yong, and Liu Chen, the governor of Xiangzhou, summoned Ji Feo to take charge of the book. Later, Pei Jian, a fellow countryman of Ji Ce, Danyang Yin Cheng Zang Dun, Yangzhou Zhongzheng Zhang Ping and others jointly recommended Ji Fe, thinking that he was filial, sincere and sincere, and he was proficient in "Yi" and "Laozi". The emperor ordered Taichang to be commended and recommended. At first, Ji Fol suffered from heart palpitations because his father was falsely accused of guilt, and later died of heart palpitations. Zhen Tian, ​​courtesy name Yanyue, was born in Wuji, Zhongshan, and had lived in Jiangling for generations. Zhen Tian's grandfather, Zhen Qinzhi, was appointed Chang Ningling. His father selected him and Renzhou engaged in it. Zhen Tian's father passed away when he was only a few years old. He was as sad and painful as an adult. target: His father was pardoned, but Ji Feo later died from heart palpitations. Zhen Tian, from Jiangling, mourned his father from childhood, with birds responding to his cries. He was commended by the emperor and appointed to a military post.

source: Zhen Tian's filial piety is particularly outstanding, and her reputation is well-known in her hometown. This has many benefits for the honest and honest folk customs. The magistrate presented the dispatches just as I saw them with my own eyes. His whole family should be commended and he should be given a title. Zhen Tian was appointed an official and went to Annan to join the army. Han Huaiming, a member of the Shangdang Party, lived in Jingzhou. When he was ten years old, Han Huaiming's mother suffered from tuberculosis, and each attack was often dangerous. Han Huaiming was kowtowing and praying under the starry sky at night. It was very cold at that time. He suddenly smelled the fragrance. Someone in the air said to him: Little child, your mother will recover permanently in a while, and you don’t have to worry about it anymore. Before dawn, his mother's illness had recovered. The fellow villagers were surprised by this. When Han Huaiming was fifteen years old, his father passed away. He was extremely sad during the funeral, almost to the point of destroying his life. He piled dirt on his back and made a grave, and did not accept any gifts or help from others.
target: Han Huaiming, from Jingzhou, prayed for his mother's recovery and heard a divine voice. He mourned his father excessively and served his mother with devotion.

source: Han Huaiming secretly asked others why Liu Qiu was sad and alone. Liu Qiu's family replied: Today is the death anniversary of my grandfather's death. Liu Qiu's mother had also died at that time. When Han Huaiming heard about this, he stopped studying that day and went home to support his mother. Liu Qiu sighed and said: Han Sheng no longer has the regret of not being able to support his parents like Qiu Wuzi. Han Huaiming's family was poor, so he often tried his best to provide his mother with delicious food, and often laughed at his mother's side to make her happy. He would not leave his mother's side all day long. When his mother was ninety-one years old, she passed away. Han Huaiming was deprived of water and food for ten days, howling and crying incessantly. A pair of white doves built a nest on the thatched cottage where he was mourning. They laid eggs and raised small birds. They were very close to people, just like poultry. The white doves did not leave until the mourning period of Han Huaiming was over.
target: White doves nested at his mourning hut. He refused official posts and died at home.

source: After Liu Tanjing's father died, he served his mother with utmost sincerity and filial piety. He cooked the rice and porridge himself and did not leave the chores to others. When his mother was sick, he took care of her day and night without taking any clothes off. After his mother died, he went without food or water for nearly ten days. His mother's coffin was temporarily buried at Yaowang Temple. The weather was cold at that time. Liu Tanjing, wearing single clothes, built a thatched cottage at the place where the coffin was buried to observe the mourning. He cried continuously day and night, and his grief moved everyone on the way. Within a year, Liu Tanjing himself passed away.
target: Liu Tanjing, from Pengcheng, mourned his father with vomiting blood and later served his mother with care, dying within a year of her death.

source: He Jiongtang's uncle He Changyu said to him: "Why do you want to live in seclusion? You should not behave like this again." Moreover, every gentleman has his own way of becoming an official and retiring from office. When Yu Yan was nineteen years old, he became an official for the first time and held the owner's book. He was recommended as a scholar, and was successively promoted to the royal palace to join the army, Shangshu Bing, and the second caolang of the Treasury. He left the capital and served as Yongkang Ling, and was famous for his harmonious handling of affairs. He returned to Beijing and served as the internal record office of Renwei Nankang King, and moved to the post of official secretary and censor. Because his father was ill, He Jiong stayed naked for more than ten days without combing or washing his hair. He was busy serving his father. In two or three nights, his appearance suddenly changed a lot. After his father passed away, He Jiong howled and cried constantly, sitting and lying on the ground, and sleeping with his head on the earth. As a result, his waist and kidneys were weak and his feet were swollen. Eventually, his body was destroyed by excessive grief and he died. Yu Shami, a native of Yingyin. The sixth generation grandson of Jin Si Kong Yubing. His father, Yu Peiyu, served as the official governor of the state and the internal history of Changsha. During the reign of Emperor Shengming of the Song Dynasty, he was executed for being convicted of Yu Shami's affair. Yu Shami had just been born at that time. When Yu novice was five years old, his biological mother made him a minor's dress, but he often refused to wear it. When his mother asked him why he refused to wear it, he answered with tears: Our family has suffered a tragic disaster, what's the use of sending things away! After growing up, he wore civilian clothes and ate a vegetarian diet throughout his life. Yu Shami was recruited from his family to serve as the Zuo Changshi of the Linchuan Kingdom, and moved to the Central Army Tian Caoxing to join the army. When his aunt passed away and fell ill, Yu novice stayed by her side morning and evening, undressed, and sometimes needed acupuncture treatment, so Yu novice would test it on his own body first. After his aunt's death, he had no food or drink for many days. Until the period of mourning is over, he does not take off his mourning clothes and does not leave the gate of the mourning hut. He howls and cries day and night, and the neighbors cannot bear to hear his cry. My aunt's tomb was built in the new forest, and then there were more than a hundred unplanted pine trees growing beside the tomb. Yu Yong, the official minister of the capital of Yushami tribe, reported Yushami's filial piety and recommended him to the subject of pure filial piety. Emperor Gaozu summoned Yushami, commended him for his filial piety, and appointed him as the replacement magistrate of She County.
target: He Jiong, from Lujiang, served his ill father without rest, changing appearance drastically. He died from grief after his father's death. Yu Shami, from Yingyin, refused fine clothes due to family tragedy. He served his aunt with devotion, and pine trees grew at her tomb. He was commended for filial piety and died in office.

source: He served as the Great Wall Order and died. Jiang Yu, whose courtesy name is Hanjie, was born in Kaocheng, Jiyang. His father, Jiang Bei, served as doctor Guanglu. Jiang Bian had a filial nature since he was a child. When he was thirteen years old, his father suffered from an eye disease. Jiang Biao served his sick father for nearly a year without taking off his clothes. He dreamed of a monk at night who said: People suffering from eye diseases will definitely be cured by drinking Eye Wisdom Water. Jiang Pu woke up and told the story, but no one could explain the meaning of "Hui Yan Shui". Jiang Pu's third uncle Liao Zheng had a good relationship with Master Zhizhe of Caotang Temple, so he went to consult Master Zhizhe. Master Wise said: "The Infinite Life Sutra" says: The wise eye sees the truth and can cross to the other side. Jiang Hao followed the inspiration of the wise master and dedicated a house in Niutun, Tongxia County, as a temple, asking God to give him a good name. The imperial edict replied: A loyal minister and a filial son are responsive everywhere. Yan Han of the Jin Dynasty finally saw the medicine sent from the underworld. I met a wise man recently and learned that your second son had a dream because of his sincerity, saying that he wanted to drink the water of wisdom. Wisdom Eye is the name of one of the five eyes. If you want to build a temple, you can use Wisdom Eye as the name of the temple. When they built the temple, they discovered an old well with clear water, which was different from ordinary spring water.
target: Jiang Yu, from Kaocheng, served his blind father, dreaming of "Wisdom Eye Water." He built a temple where an old well appeared, curing his father's eyes.

source: People at that time thought this was an expression of filial piety. The King of Nankang was the governor of Southern Xuzhou, and he summoned Pi to be the chief official. Dou Mian is quiet by nature, likes the mystical words of "Laozi" and "Zhuangzi", is especially proficient in the essence of Buddhism, and is not willing to enter an official career. After his father passed away, Jiang Huai built a thatched cottage next to his father's tomb, howling and crying all day long. More than a month later, Jiang Pu also passed away. Liu Ji, courtesy name Shiju, was from Pingyuan. His grandfather Liu Chengmin was the governor of Jizhou during the Song Dynasty. His father, Liu Wenwei, was a member of the imperial family during the Qi Dynasty. When Liu Ji was nine years old, he could recite "Zuo Shi Zhuan" and his relatives were surprised by his talent. When he was fourteen years old, his father died. Liu Ji had a natural sense of filial piety and cried until he vomited blood every time. The family was poor, so Liu Ji and his younger brothers Liu Yao and Liu Di encouraged each other and devoted themselves to study. After growing up, Liu Ji has been involved in a wide range of subjects and is knowledgeable and talented. During the Tianjian period, Liu Ji was recruited from his home to serve at the court's invitation. He was gradually promoted to Xuanhui and joined the army in Jin'an Palace. He also went to Beijing and served as Minister of Host and Guest. Within a year, he was appointed as the Order of Haiyan. Liu Ji served as magistrate of two counties. During his tenure, he was known for his harmonious handling of affairs. When he returned to the capital, he was appointed as Jian Kangzheng, but he did not like the position. He was soon dismissed because of illness. Soon he was awarded the Jiankang Order, but he did not accept the appointment. Liu Ji's mother, Mingshi, fell ill. Liu Ji was already fifty years old at that time. He served his mother untiedly for seventy days and recited the "Avalokiteśvara Sutra" ten thousand times. At night, he had a dream due to emotion. In his dream, he saw a monk saying to him: My wife's life span has been exhausted. With your sincerity and sincerity, I will extend your wife's life for you. Liu Ji's mother passed away more than sixty years later. Liu Ji built a thatched hut next to his mother's grave to mourn. His grief exceeded common courtesy. There is often a pair of white cranes flying docilely beside the thatched cottage. Ruan Xiaoxu, a virgin, wrote to him to comfort and enlighten him. But Liu Ji still missed his deceased mother endlessly, and died before the mourning was over. He died at the age of fifty-two.
target: He mourned his father excessively and died. Liu Ji, from Pingyuan, mourned his father with vomiting blood and served his mother, reciting sutras. White cranes appeared at his mourning hut. He died before mourning ended at fifty-two.

Liu Ji is the author of eight volumes of "Explanation of Common Sayings" and ten volumes of collected works. The deeds of his younger brother Liu Yao are in "The Biography of Literature", and the deeds of Liu Di are in "The Biography of Chu Shi". Chu Xiu was a native of Qiantang, Wu County. His father, Chu Zhongdu, was proficient in "The Book of Changes" and his knowledge was the most profound at that time. During the Tianjian period, Chu Zhongdu successively served as a doctor of "Five Classics". Chu Xiu inherited his father's studies since he was a child. He was also proficient in "The Classic of Filial Piety" and "The Analects of Confucius". He was good at writing letters and articles. Chu Xiu initially served as the minister of the Xiangshu Kingdom, and gradually moved to the Qingche Xiangdong Prefecture to join the army, and also served as an assistant to the emperor. King Wuling was appointed as the governor of Laoye, and he was recommended! He was succeeded by Xuanhui and joined the army, and was limited to the internal record office. Chou Kai was a very filial man by nature. When his father died, he grieved beyond the ordinary limits, which damaged his body and suffered from Qi reversal. When his mother died, he couldn't eat or drink for twenty-three days, falling into unconsciousness and waking up again and again. He often howled and cried so hard that he vomited blood and eventually died from excessive physical weakness. Xie Lin, whose courtesy name is Xiru, was born in Yangxia, Chen County. He is the eighth generation grandson of Jin Taifu Xie An. Xie Lin's father, Xie Jing, was appointed Beizhonglang to consult and join the army. When Xie Lin was five years old, whenever her parents had not eaten yet, her wet nurse would ask Xie Lin to eat first. Xie Lin said, "I don't feel hungry yet." Even if he is forced to do so, he still refuses to eat. When his uncle Ruan Xiaoxu heard about this, he praised him and said: "If you leave your children at home, you are like Zengzi, and if you serve the king, you are like Lin Sheng."
target: Chu Xiu, from Qiantang, mourned his parents with extreme grief, fasting for twenty-three days and dying from weakness. Xie Lin, from Yangxia, refused food before his parents ate. The text concludes by comparing these individuals to ancient filial exemplars like Zeng Shen, noting that some, like Liu Tanjing, He Jiong, Jiang Yu, and Xie Lin, died from grief, similar to Ruqiu and Wu.

source: Wei Can, whose courtesy name is Changxi, is the grandson of Wei Rui, the cavalry general, and the son of Wei Gan, the governor of Northern Xuzhou. Wei Can has the demeanor of his father, loves to learn, is willful, eight feet tall, and tall. He first became an official and served as the king of Jin'an in Yunhui and joined the army. Soon he acted as Fa Cao and moved to join the army as a foreign soldier and concurrently as a Chinese soldier. At that time, Ying! Yu Zhongrong and Wu Jun Zhang Shu were both well-known figures in the past. They were colleagues with Wei Can and had become close friends with each other. The king of Jin'an moved to be the governor of Yongzhou, and Wei Can also followed the palace and was transferred to the record office, but his position as a military soldier remained unchanged. King Jin'an was established as the crown prince, and Wei Can was moved to the rank of infantry captain. He entered the court and served as the leader of the East Palace. He resigned when his father died. Soon he was reinstated as General Zhaoyuan. The army was appointed as the leader. After the mourning period expired, he inherited the title of Marquis of Yongchang County and was appointed as a consultant to the king of Anxi and Xiangdong. He was repeatedly promoted to the prince's servant, led by Zuowei, and his position as leader remained unchanged. Because Wei Can had an old friendship with the crown prince, he was often appointed to positions close to him. Although his position changed many times, he often stayed in the palace and served as a guard, which was quite prestigious. Moreover, Wei Can had an unruly and arrogant personality, so the celebrities at the time felt deeply unfair. The right guard general Zhu Yi once said to Wei Can in a stern voice during a banquet: How can you put on the face of a leader and face others! In the 11th year of Datong in Central China, Wei Can was moved to serve as a regular servant of Tongzhi Sanqi. Before he took office, he left the capital to serve as the governor, supervising the military affairs of Hengzhou, general Anyuan, and governor of Hengzhou. The Crown Prince came out of the palace and was farewelling the boy. He took Wei Can's hand and said, "You and I won't be apart for a long time." In the first year of Taiqing, not long after Wei Can arrived in Hengzhou, he petitioned to be dismissed. In the second year, the imperial court recruited Wei Can as a regular attendant of Sanqi. Wei Can returned to the capital and walked to Luling. When he heard about Hou Jing's rebellion, he selected 5,000 elite soldiers and 100 horses from his subordinates, and rushed to the capital day and night to rescue him. When they arrived in Yuzhang, a messenger reported: The rebels have arrived at Hengjiang. Wei Can immediately went to the internal historian Liu Xiaoyi to discuss countermeasures. Liu Xiaoyi said: If this is really the case, there should be another order. How can one send an envoy credulously and act in panic? Maybe this is not the case. At that time, Liu Xiaoyi was giving a banquet to entertain Wei Can. Wei Can became angry, threw the cup on the ground and said: The rebels have crossed the river and are about to invade the capital. All water and land routes have been cut off. Where will there be messengers to return the favor? If the order is not issued, can you feel at ease? How can I, Wei Can, think about drinking now? After saying that, he immediately rode out and deployed his troops to prepare for departure. Just as Xiao Daxin, the governor of Dangyang in Jiangzhou, sent an envoy to invite Wei Can, Wei Can rode to see Xiao Daxin and said: Among the vassal towns in the upper reaches of the Yangtze River, only Jiang maggot is the closest to the capital. Considering the situation of His Highness, it is really necessary to go to the rescue first; but the position in the middle reaches is important, and your task of garrisoning Jiangzhou is important. Others also need your support to rescue the capital. Wei Guo cannot be left unattended.
target: Wei Can, grandson of General Wei Rui and son of Governor Wei Gan, was a tall and learned man who served in various official positions under Prince Jin'an. He became close friends with Yu Zhongrong and Zhang Shu. As the prince rose to crown prince, Wei Can held several palace guard roles, though his arrogant nature caused resentment among peers. General Zhu Yi once rebuked him for his haughty demeanor. In 545, Wei Can became governor of Hengzhou, but resigned shortly after. Recalled in 546, he learned of Hou Jing's rebellion while traveling and rushed to the capital with 5,000 elite troops. After consulting with officials Liu Xiaoyi and Xiao Daxin, he coordinated with his cousin Liu Zhongli and General Pei Zhigao, eventually securing command for Liu. During battle at Qingtang, Wei Can ignored advice to hold position, ordered an attack, and was overwhelmed by Hou Jing's forces.

source: Liu Shuyin was too timid and afraid to lead his troops forward, so Zheng Yi was defeated. The rebels took advantage of the victory and rushed into the military camp. People around Wei Can pulled him away, but he remained motionless and loudly ordered his children to fight desperately. Almost all the soldiers were killed, and Wei Can was also killed. He was fifty-four years old at the time. Wei Can's son Wei Ni and Wei Can's three younger brothers Wei Zhu, Wei Jing, Wei Gou, and cousin Wei Ang were all killed in the battle. Hundreds of his relatives died in the battle.
target: He and his sons, brothers, and cousin were killed at age 54. The emperor mourned him deeply and posthumously promoted him.

source: Wei Zang, the eldest son of Wei Can, was given the courtesy name Junli. Wei Zang once served as the Third Duke of Shangshu, the prince washed horses, and the palace leader. When Hou Jing was besieging the capital, he led his troops to garrison Xihua Gate. After the fall of Beijing, he fled to Jiangzhou, gathered his old troops, and guarded Yuzhang. He was later killed by his subordinates. Jiangzi, whose name is Yuanzhen, was born in Kaocheng, Jiyang. He is the seventh generation descendant of Jiang Tong, a regular servant of Sanqi during the Jin Dynasty. His father, Jiang Facheng, was appointed to the imperial court during the Tianjian period. When Jiangzi was young, he loved to study, was ambitious and moral, but because his family was poor and his parents did not provide enough support, he became a vegetarian all his life. He first took up an official position as the minister of the kingdom and was invited by the court. He petitioned to go to the secret pavilion to read. Emperor Gaozu agreed and ordered Jiang Ziyi to be on duty in Hualin Province. Jiang Ziyi's uncle, Youwei General Sai Yu, was a powerful figure in the dynasty. Whenever he went home on vacation, his house would be crowded with guests, but Jiang Ziyi never came to visit him. His conduct was so noble. Later, Jiang Ziyi gradually moved to the post of Minister Caolang, and went to Beijing to serve as the magistrate of Suichang and Qu'a counties, all of which achieved good political performances. Jiang Ziyi was appointed as the Minister of Tongzhi Sanqi. He left Beijing and served as General Rongzhao and Colonel Nanjin. Jiang Ziyi's younger brother Jiang Zisi once served as Shangshu Jinbulang. In the early years of his reign, he moved to Youcheng. Both brothers have strong personalities. Jiang Wangpan, as You Cheng, presented the seal to the court and spoke freely about the court's gains and losses. Gaozu appreciated it very much and ordered the minister to carefully examine it and choose the good ones for implementation. Zuo Minlang Shen Jiong and Shaofu Cheng Gu Qi once scolded them sternly because of improper performance. Jiang Zisi quickly stepped forward to answer for Shen Jiong and Gu Qi. His words were very fierce and forthright. Gaozu angrily called for people to tie him up. Jiang Zisi fell on the ground and refused to be bound. Gaozu's anger subsided and he asked people to let him go. However, he was still convicted and dismissed. Hou Jing rebelled, captured Liyang, and was about to cross the Hengjiang River. Jiang Ziyi led more than a thousand naval troops to intercept Hou Jing downstream. His deputy general Dong Taosheng, who lived in the north of the Yangtze River, fled with his accomplices. So as soon as Jiang Zi retreated to Nanzhou, he gathered the remaining troops and hurried to the capital on foot from the alley. The rebels soon arrived in the capital. Jiang Ziyi reported to Taizong: The rebels' encirclement has not been closed yet. We can try to break out. If we wait for them to build all the fortresses, then we will have no use. Jiang Ziyi requested that he and his brothers Jiang Zisi and Jiang Ziwu lead more than a hundred soldiers to open the Chengming Gate and challenge the rebels. The rebels agreed. Jiang Zi took the lead and rushed into the enemy camp alone with his sword. The rebels attacked him, and the people behind him did not dare to rush in. Seeing that the situation was critical, Jiang Zisi and Jiang Ziwu followed them and rushed into the enemy camp. All three of them were killed.
target: Jiangzi, a seventh-generation descendant of Jiang Tong, was a studious and principled man from a poor family. He served as a county magistrate with distinction before becoming a court official. His brother Jiang Zisi served as Youcheng and once boldly defended colleagues Shen Jiong and Gu Qi during a court dispute, angering Emperor Gaozu but eventually being pardoned. During Hou Jing's rebellion, Jiangzi led naval forces to intercept the rebels but was betrayed by his deputy. He retreated to Nanzhou and then to the capital, where he proposed a breakout. He and his brothers Jiang Zisi and Jiang Ziwu charged into enemy lines alone and were killed. The emperor posthumously honored them with high titles. Jiangzi also authored works like "Huang Tu" and "Guang Jiupin.".

source: Jiang Ziyi once continued to write "Huang Tu" and "Guang Jiupin", as well as dozens of poems, poems, rhymes and prose, all of which have been circulated in the world. Zhang Sheng, named Sishan, was the son of Zhang Ji, the general of Zhenbei. When Zhang Sheng was young, he behaved upright and elegantly, had ambition and integrity, and was able to talk about mysteries. When his father was governing Qingzhou, he was killed by the local people. Zhang Zhu was so sad about the disaster at home that he ate vegetarian food and wore common clothes all his life, without holding a knife in his hand. The state promoted him as a scholar. Zhang Sheng first became an official and served as Secretary Lang. He was repeatedly promoted to Prince Sheren, Xima, Situ Zuoxi, and Zhongshu Lang. He left the capital and served as the internal history of Yongyang. After returning to the capital, he was appointed as the Sima of Xuancheng King of the Chinese Army and the regular attendant of Sanqi.
target: Zhang Sheng, son of General Zhang Ji, was a virtuous and scholarly man who became a vegetarian after his father's murder. He held various official posts, including governor of Wuxing.

source: The traitor Liu Shenmao from Xingtai captured Yixing. He sent envoys to persuade Zhang Sheng, saying: If you surrender early, you will still be made the county guard, and you will be given official rewards. Zhang Sheng ordered the envoy to be beheaded, and then sent the army leader Wang Xiong and others to lead his troops to meet Shen Mao at Yudu and defeated him. Shen Mao fled. Hou Jing heard that Shenmao had been defeated, so he sent his central army officer Hou Zijian to lead 20,000 elite troops to help Shenmao attack Zhang Sheng. Zhang Sheng sent his army leader Fan Zhilang to the west of the county to resist, but was defeated by Shenmao and then retreated. The rebel cavalry took advantage of the victory and burned the camp fence, and the defenders inside the fence collapsed. Zhang Sheng took off his military uniform and sat in the hall. The rebels threatened him with a knife, but he still refused to give in. So the rebels tied him up and sent him to Hou Jing. Hou Jing killed him in the capital market, and more than ten of his disciples were killed together with him. Zhang Sheng was sixty-two years old when he died. After Hou Jing's rebellion was settled, Shizu posthumously awarded him the titles of Shizhong, Zhongwei General, and Kaifu Yitong. He was given the nickname Zhongzhenzi. Shen Jun, courtesy name Shuyuan, was born in Wukang, Wuxing. His grandfather Shen Xian was a regular servant of Sanqi during the Qi Dynasty. There is a biography of Shen Xian in the history of Qi.
target: During Hou Jing's siege of the capital, he sent troops to help. After the city fell, he organized resistance in Wuxing, defeating rebel Liu Shenmao. When Hou Jing sent reinforcements, Zhang Sheng's forces were overwhelmed. He refused to surrender, was captured, and executed at age 62. He was posthumously honored as Zhongzhenzi.

source: After Hou Jing's rebellion was settled, Shizu posthumously awarded him the titles of Shizhong, Zhongwei General, and Kaifu Yitong. He was given the nickname Zhongzhenzi. Shen Jun, courtesy name Shuyuan, was born in Wukang, Wuxing. His grandfather Shen Xian was a regular servant of Sanqi during the Qi Dynasty. There is a biography of Shen Xian in the history of Qi. Shen Jun was erudite and talented when he was young. He served successively as the magistrate of Shanyin, Wu, and Jiankang counties, and had a reputation for being able to handle affairs. He went to Beijing and served as Zhongshu Lang and Shangshu Zuocheng. When Hou Jing besieged the capital, he moved to the post of censor Zhongcheng. At that time, reinforcements from all walks of life arrived near the capital, and Hou Jing petitioned to conclude an alliance, and the emperor agreed. After the covenant was made, Qiang learned that a plague had broken out in the city, so he had treacherous intentions and delayed leaving. Several days later, the Crown Prince ordered Shen Jun to go to Hou Jing's military camp. Hou Jing said: The weather is getting hotter. It's not the time to march. How can I leave with 100,000 troops?
target: Shen Jun, a learned official from Wukang, served as magistrate of several counties and later as censor.

source: When you say these words, do you want to threaten the court? Hou Jing put the knife across his knees and scolded Shen Jun with his eyes wide open. Shen Jun sternly condemned Hou Jing and said: You are a minister of the imperial court, but you launched a mutiny and besieged the capital. The wise monarch has given grace to forgive your sins, and we have also concluded a covenant together. Now that the blood of the covenant has not been dried, you will regret it. I am already sixty years old, and I am the envoy of the Emperor. I am determined to live or die by my fate. Am I afraid of the blade of a traitor like you? After saying that, he went out without looking back. Hou Jing said: This man is truly Sizhi who is loyal to the country! Yet I still harbor a grudge against him. After breaking through Zhang Sheng's camp, Hou Jing searched for Shen Jun and killed him. Liu Jingli is the grandson of Liu Qingyuan, the third minister of Kaifu Yitong. His father Liu Jin was appointed Prince Zhan Shi. Liu Jingli and his elder brother Liu Zhongli were famous for their loyalty and bravery when they were young. Liu Jingli was recruited from his family to serve as Zuo Lang, and gradually he was promoted to the governor of Fufeng. When Hou Jing was crossing the river, Liu Jingli led 3,000 cavalry and infantry to rescue him. When he arrived near the capital, he defended Qingxidai and fought with Hou Jing many times. He often took the lead in charging into the city and gained far-reaching prestige. After the palace city was captured, both Liu Jingli and Liu Zhongli went to see Hou Jing. Hou Jing sent Liu Zhongli to govern the upper reaches of the river, leaving Liu Jingli as a hostage and appointing him as a guard. Hou Jing held a banquet for Liu Zhongli in Houzhu to see him off. Liu Jingli secretly said to Liu Zhongli: Hou Jing came to the banquet today. I hugged him tightly, so you pulled out your sword and killed him. I will die without regrets. Liu Zhongli thought his words were very heroic and agreed to his request. After drinking for a few rounds, Liu Jingli signaled Liu Zhongli with his eyes. Liu Zhongli saw that the surroundings were heavily guarded and did not dare to take action, so his plan failed. Later, when Hou Jing was conquering King Xi of Jin Dynasty, Liu Jingli and Nankang King Xiao Huili discussed sending troops to attack the city where Hou Jing was guarding. They had agreed on a date to prepare for the uprising. Jian'an Marquis Xiao Bi knew about it and reported them, so Liu Jingli was killed. Shi Chen said: Morality is more important than life, which is the admonition left by the ancient books. This is also the character valued by the sages. Therefore, King Gen said, life is what I want to get, and justice is also what I want to get. If I cannot get both at the same time, I would rather sacrifice my life for righteousness. People like Ji Cricket sacrificed their lives for their country and returned home even if they died. Their heroic spirit and unyielding integrity shine through the ages. People should know that there were loyal ministers in the Liang Dynasty!
target: During Hou Jing's siege, he negotiated with the rebel leader, boldly condemning his treachery. Hou Jing admired his loyalty but later killed him after breaking through Zhang Sheng's camp. Liu Jingli, grandson of Liu Qingyuan, was known for bravery. He defended Qingxidai during Hou Jing's invasion, leading charges. After the palace fell, he plotted with his brother Liu Zhongli to assassinate Hou Jing at a banquet, but the plan failed due to heavy guards. Later, he conspired with Prince Xiao Huili to attack Hou Jing's stronghold but was betrayed and killed. The historian concludes that these men exemplified the principle of sacrificing life for righteousness, proving that the Liang Dynasty had loyal ministers.

source: In the past, the history books of Sima Qian and Ban Gu both compiled the "Biography of Sima Xiangru". Sima Xiangru did not participate in the major affairs of the Han Dynasty, so his articles are particularly famous for his biography. Ban Gu also wrote the "Biography of Jia Zou Meilu", also because they could write articles and spread them to the world. Fan Ye's "Book of Houmo" contains the "Biography of Wenyuan". The deeds of the people included in the biography have been recorded in great detail. Formulating rituals and music, governing the country, understanding the past and present, recording good and bad deeds are all impossible without writing. Therefore, no one who is a king and governs the world does not respect and value the function of articles; scholars among the Jin gentry also value and value the function of articles. This situation has not changed since ancient times. Emperor Gaozu was both intelligent and virtuous, well aware of affairs, and had a vast empire. He went to Shao to seek liberal Confucian scholars and accepted talents with special knowledge. As a result, the ritual and music system flourished, and talents of all kinds gathered in the capital, glowing with dazzling brilliance. Whenever Emperor Gaozu visited a place, he often ordered his officials to compose poems and essays. Those who wrote good poems and essays would be rewarded with gold and silk. Those who went to the palace to present poems and eulogies would sometimes be favored by being received. Those literati with official titles, such as Shen Yue, Jiang Yan, Ren Fang, etc., were all called excellent at the time because of their literary talent. As for people like Pengcheng Daohang, Wu Xingqiuchi, Shuhai Wang Sengru, Wujun Zhang Shu and others, some of them were honored by the Wende Hall of Zhidai Shao, and some enjoyed the favor of the Shouguang Hall where the monarchs and ministers feasted. These are all outstanding and outstanding talents in the future. Shen Yue, Jiang Yan, Ren Fang, Wang Sengru and Zhang Sui are separately described according to their merits and achievements. The collection was limited to the Taiqing period, and the deeds of talented and knowledgeable figures such as Dao Hang were collected into "Wenxue Biography".
target: The historical tradition of compiling biographies of literary figures, beginning with Sima Qian and Ban Gu, who included Sima Xiangru's biography due to his literary fame, and Fan Ye's "Book of Houmo," which detailed the deeds of literary scholars. It emphasizes the importance of writing in governance, ritual, and recording history, noting that rulers and scholars have always valued literary works. Emperor Gaozu of Liang promoted literature by rewarding poets and scholars, leading to a flourishing of talent in the capital. Notable literary figures like Shen Yue, Jiang Yan, and Ren Fang were celebrated for their skills, while others like Pengcheng Daohang and Wu Xingqiuchi gained favor at court.

source: If you think the current poetry is correct, then the ancient poetry does not meet the requirements; if the sages of the past are worthy of praise, then the current style of poetry should be abandoned. I cannot agree with the idea that everyone has their own interests and should coexist. From time to time, there are people who imitate the poems and essays of Xie Chenle and Yuan Bianlin, which is also very confusing. Why? Xie Kangle's writing is outstanding and superb, all out of nature, but informality often appears, which is his dregs; Pei Hongshan is a talented writer of history, but he has no beauty in his words.
target: The text then provides biographies of several scholars. Daohang, a native of Pengcheng, was intelligent from childhood, excelling in writing and calligraphy.

source: Whenever Emperor Gaozu visited a place, he often ordered his officials to compose poems and essays. Those who wrote good poems and essays would be rewarded with gold and silk. Those who went to the palace to present poems and eulogies would sometimes be favored by being received. Those literati with official titles, such as Shen Yue, Jiang Yan, Ren Fang, etc., were all called excellent at the time because of their literary talent. As for people like Pengcheng Daohang, Wu Xingqiuchi, Shuhai Wang Sengru, Wujun Zhang Shu and others, some of them were honored by the Wende Hall of Zhidai Shao, and some enjoyed the favor of the Shouguang Hall where the monarchs and ministers feasted. These are all outstanding and outstanding talents in the future. Shen Yue, Jiang Yan, Ren Fang, Wang Sengru and Zhang Sui are separately described according to their merits and achievements. The collection was limited to the Taiqing period, and the deeds of talented and knowledgeable figures such as Dao Hang were collected into "Wenxue Biography". To Hang, named Mao, was a native of Wuyuan, Pengcheng. His great-grandfather came to Yanzhi and served as a general in the Song Dynasty. When his father arrived in Jie, he was appointed Minister of the Fifth Army of Qi Dynasty.
