target: He served in various official roles under Emperor Gaozu, who admired his talent. Daohang was known for his humility and friendships with contemporaries like Ren Fang and Fan Yun. He died at thirty, leaving over a hundred poems.

source: Soon, he went to Hang to take charge of the secretary of the East Palace and the Youcewen of Sanqi Province with the post of washing horses. In the third year of Tianjian, Emperor Gaozu ordered Shao to select Shangshulang who was honest, capable or talented and knowledgeable during his tenure and promoted him to the rank of Minister. When he arrived at Han, he was appointed as the Minister of Cao in the palace. Daohang and his cousins ​​Daogai and Daoqia were both known as talented men. At that time, they all took turns holding positions in the palace, which was considered an honor by contemporary people. In the fourth year of Tianjian, he moved to Hang and was appointed Prince Zhongsheren. He was a man who did not boast of his own merits or talk about the merits of others. Le'an Renfang and Nanxiang Fan Yun both had a good friendship with him. In this year, he was moved to Danyang Yincheng. Because he was ill and unable to take office, he was moved to Beizhonglang to consult and join the army. In the fifth year of Tianjian, Daohang died during his tenure at the age of thirty. Zhidan was deeply saddened by his death and issued an edict granting him twenty thousand dollars and thirty pieces of cloth to his family. Daohang wrote more than 100 poems and poems. Qiu Chi, courtesy name Xifan, was from Wucheng, Wuxing. His father, Qiu Lingju, was famous for his talent. He became an official in Qi Dynasty and was promoted to Taizhong doctor.
target: Qiu Chi, from Wuxing, began writing at eight and was recognized for his talent. He held several official positions, including prefect of Yongjia, and was known for his literary contributions, such as writing letters that persuaded Chen Bozhi to surrender. He died at forty-five, with his works widely circulated.

source: After returning to school, Qiu Chi was worshiped as Zhongshu Lang and moved to Situ to work as Zhongshu Lang. In the seventh year of Tianjian, Qiu Chi died during his tenure at the age of forty-five. The poems and poems written by Qiu Chi have been spread all over the world. Liu Bao, courtesy name Xiaochang, was born in Pengcheng. His grandfather Liu Kuang was Sikong during the Song Dynasty. His father, Liu Zhi, was the concubine of the crown prince at that time. When Liu Bao was four years old, his father passed away. When he was six or seven years old, Liu Bao would often cry when he saw his uncles. At that time, Liu Bao's uncle Liu Chan and uncle Liu Hui were already in high status. Liu Bao's mother thought that Liu Bao was crying out of fear and was very angry about this. Liu Bao replied: I lost my father very early and did not remember his face. I heard that my uncle and uncle had very similar faces to my father, so I felt sad when I saw them and had no other meaning.
target: Liu Bao, from Pengcheng, lost his father early and showed filial piety by managing family burials alone at sixteen.

source: As he spoke, he sobbed again, and his mother became even more sad. At first, Liu Bao's parents and two brothers died one after another, and they were all buried temporarily. When Liu Bao was sixteen, their coffins were moved to the cemetery. The planning and arrangements for the reburial were all done by Liu Bao alone, without the help of his uncles and uncles. It didn't take long for everything to be done. Liu Hui often praised him and admired his ability. Liu Bao has been eager to learn since he was a child and can write articles. When he first became an official, Cao Xing joined the army, but he did not take office. In the early years of Tianjian, because he was the younger brother of the Princess of Linchuan, he was promoted from the war chief to the military meritorious officer of the Linchuan King. He also accumulated merit and was moved to the post of minister of Shangshu Kubu, Danyang Yin Cheng, Prince Taifu Cheng, minister of Shangshu Palace, and Nanxuzhou Zhizhong. He was dismissed because of official business. After meeting for a long time, Liu Bao appointed the prince to wash horses, be in charge of the secretary, and serve as a lecturer in Shouguang Palace. After Emperor Gaozu came to the throne, he selected young scholars with literary talents. Liu Bao, his cousins ​​Liu Xiaochuo, Liu Ru, Dao Gai from the same county, Dao Gai's younger brother Luo Qia, Dao Gai's cousin Dao Hang, Wu Jun Lu Chui, and Zhang Shu were all appreciated for their literary talents and often participated in the banquets of the monarchs and ministers. Although their official positions were different, the rewards they received were the same.
target: He was learned and held various posts, including lecturer in Shouguang Palace. He was part of a group of young scholars favored by Emperor Gaozu for their literary talents.

source: After Emperor Gaozu came to the throne, he selected young scholars with literary talents. Liu Bao, his cousins ​​Liu Xiaochuo, Liu Ru, Dao Gai from the same county, Dao Gai's younger brother Luo Qia, Dao Gai's cousin Dao Hang, Wu Jun Lu Chui, and Zhang Shu were all appreciated for their literary talents and often participated in the banquets of the monarchs and ministers. Although their official positions were different, the rewards they received were the same. In the tenth year of Tianjian, Liu Bao passed away at the age of thirty. When Liu Bao was about to die, he called his friends Nanyang and Liu Zhisheng to entrust him with the funeral arrangements and requested that the funeral affairs must be frugal. Liu Bao had a reputation for being capable when he was an official, and he was gentle by nature. But he is upright in dealing with things, interacts with people, criticizes his friends' shortcomings and mistakes in person, praises their friends' strengths and virtues behind their backs, is frank in his feelings, and does not hide his privacy. His friends all praise him for this. Yuan Jun, courtesy name Xiaogao, was born in Yangxia, Chen County. He was the eighth generation descendant of Wei Langzhong's order, Yuan Huanzhi. Yuan Jun lost his father at an early age, but he devoted himself to studying. His family was poor and had no books. He often borrowed books from others to read, and he had to copy the borrowed books. He set a pace for himself, copying fifty pages every day. If the number of pages did not reach the specified number, he would not rest.
target: Liu Bao died at thirty, known for his upright character and frugal funeral requests. Yuan Jun, from Chen County, was orphaned young and studied diligently, copying books daily.

source: Wang Qian was appointed governor of Yingzhou and made Cao the capital of the army. Gaozu was very fond of poetry. At that time, there was an endless stream of people submitting poems and essays to Gaozu in Nanque. Among them, the authors of poems and essays with gorgeous diction and appreciable words were sometimes rewarded or promoted. In the sixth year of Tianjian, Yuan Locust imitated Dangbi and wrote "Guan Zhen" and dedicated it to Taizu. Emperor Gaozu commended him and gave him five pieces of silk. In addition to being appointed as a member of the Sanqi Shilang, Yuan Jun was appointed as a bachelor of the province. He copied twenty volumes each of "Historical Records" and "Moshu". Following Emperor Gaozu's order, he and Lu Jue each wrote "Xinque Ming", but because the words were too long, they could not be included in the text. Yu Yuling's courtesy name was Zijie. He was the younger brother of Qian Lou, who was often served by Sanqi. When Yu Yuling was seven years old, he could discuss subtle principles with others. As an adult, he was sharp-witted, knowledgeable and talented. Xiao Zilong, the Sui King of Qi, was appointed as the governor of Jingzhou. He called Yu Yuling to be the chief bookkeeper and ordered him to copy and compile books together with Xie Tiao, Zong Yang and others. Xiao Zilong was replaced in his post and returned to the capital. He also ordered Yu Yuling to be the master of farewell. Xiao Zilong was killed by Emperor Ming soon after. Xiao Zilong's old staff and former officials avoided him out of fear. No one dared to deal with the funeral affairs. Only Yu Yuling and Zong Yang stayed to handle the funeral for Xiao Zilong.
target: He served in official roles and wrote "Guan Zhen," earning praise and silk from Emperor Gaozu. He also copied historical texts and composed "Xinque Ming" with Lu Jue. Yu Yuling, from a scholarly family, was sharp-witted and served as a bookkeeper for Xiao Zilong. After Xiao Zilong's death, Yu Yuling alone handled his funeral, showing loyalty.

source: He also accumulated merit and was promoted to the position of Minister of Huangmen of Zhongshu. His positions of Shiren and Zhongzheng remained unchanged. Yu Yuling later left the capital and served as the chief historian of Jin'an King Xuanyi and the prefect of Guangling. He was responsible for the affairs of the prefecture and state, but was dismissed due to official business. He was appointed as Tongzhilang, and soon he was awarded the title of Hongluqing, and also led the Dazhongzheng of Jingzhou. Yu Yuling died during his tenure at the age of forty-eight. Yu Yuling has ten volumes of collected works. Yu Yuling's younger brother Yu Jianwu. Yu Jian's name is Zi Shen. He was able to compose poems when he was eight years old, and his elder brother Yu Yuling was particularly friendly to him. Yu Jianwu first served as a permanent servant of the Kingdom of Jin'an, and then moved to the palace of King Xuanhui of Jin'an to join the army. From then on, every time the King of Jin'an moved the town, Yu Jianwu also followed the palace. He successively served as the prince's lieutenant, Yunhui joined the army, and also joined the army as a secretary. In the third year of Zhongdatong, the king of Jin'an became the crown prince, and Yu Jianwu also served as the general secretary of the East Palace. In addition, he was appointed as the official recorder of King Xiangshu of Anxi and joined the army. Soon he took charge of the Dazhongzheng of Jingzhou with his own official position. After his meritorious service, he was moved to the post of Zhonglu Shi and consulted to join the army. The prince led the army to make more orders, and the prince became a concubine. At the beginning, when Taizong was in the vassal state, he liked literary scholars very much. At that time, Yu Jianwuyu Shu Hai Xu Gao, Wujun Lu Dai, Pengcheng Liu Zun, Liu Xiaoyi, and Liu Xiaoyi's younger brother Liu Xiaowei were all appreciated and invited. When Taizong became the crown prince, he also established the Wende Province and established bachelors. Yu Xin, son of Yu Jianwu, Xu Ling, son of Xu Go, Zhang Changgong of Wujun, Fu Hong of Beidi, Bao Zhi of Donghai and others were all outstanding talents who served as bachelors. When Qi Yong asked next year, scribes Wang Rong, Xie Tiao, Shen Yue and others began to use the four tones changes in their articles, and new changes appeared when writing articles. By the time of Qi Yong, more emphasis was placed on the neatness of the rhyme, and more emphasis was placed on the beauty and beauty, and the requirements for the four tones in the articles were higher than before. At that time, the prince wrote to King Xiangdong about this trend and said: We people don't have the hobby of traveling. We only know how to write books on wooden boards. We like to write articles and recite short poems from time to time. Although it is a mediocre voice, I cannot stop writing. Although I feel ashamed when I feel itchy, I cannot avoid relapse into my old ways. Recently, I have seen that the articles circulating in the capital are particularly weak and weak. The literati are vying to imitate the style of flashy and unrealistic, and are vying to imitate weak and weak works.
target: He held various posts, including prefect of Guangling, and died at forty-eight, leaving ten volumes of works. His brother Yu Jianwu began writing at eight and served under the Prince of Jin'an, later becoming a scholar in Wende Province. He was part of a literary circle that included his son Yu Xin and Xu Ling. The text includes a letter from the prince criticizing contemporary literary trends for being weak and imitative, advocating a return to classical styles like those of Yang Xiong and Sima Xiangru.

source: His grandfather Liu Bolong was famous for his filial piety during the funeral for his father. Emperor Wu of the Song Dynasty ordered the crown prince and other kings to go to his home to express condolences. Liu Bolong's official position was promoted to the rank of minister of government. Liu Zhao's father, Liu Biao, was in charge of the Imperial Records of Jin'an during the Qi Dynasty. Liu Zhao was smart and alert since he was a child. He could understand the meaning of "Lao Han" and "Zhuangzi" at the age of seven. When he grew up, he studied more diligently and was good at writing articles. His cousin Jiang Yan appreciated him and praised him very early. In the early years of Tianjian, Liu Zhaochu became an official and was invited by the court. After his meritorious service, he was promoted to the north and joined the army. He successively served as the Prince of Yuzhang, Xuanhui, and the Prince of Linchuan, Zhongjun. At first, Liu Zhao's uncle Liu Wei collected the "Books of Jin" from various schools to annotate Qian Shi's "Ji Ji", a total of forty volumes. By the time of the Han Dynasty, Liu Zhao also collected the differences in the "Books of Hou Mo" from various schools to annotate Fan Ye's "Book of Hou Mo". People at that time called the Japanese annotations extensive and comprehensive. Liu Zhao moved to the post of Tongzhilang and left the capital to serve as Liu Ling. He died during his tenure. Liu Zhao wrote 180 volumes of "Collected Comments on Houmo", 10 volumes of "Biography of Young Children", and 10 volumes of Collected Works. Liu Sui, the son of Liu Zhao, was well-spoken and fond of learning, and was proficient in the "Three Rites".
target: Liu Zhao, from Pingyuan, was intelligent and studied "Laozi" and "Zhuangzi" early. He annotated Fan Ye's "Book of Houmo" and wrote 180 volumes of commentary, along with other works.

source: Liu Sui, the son of Liu Zhao, was well-spoken and fond of learning, and was proficient in the "Three Rites". During the Datong period, Liu Juan was appointed minister of the Shangshu Temple, but soon resigned and no longer served as an official. Liu Sui's younger brother, Liu Sui, also known as Handu, has been famous since he was a child. He once served as the royal secretary of Xiangdong in Anxi. At that time, there were many literary people gathered in the Xifu, among whom Liu Sui was at the top. Liu Sui was dismissed and granted the title of Tongzhilang. Soon he moved to Zhennan and was appointed as the official recorder of the affairs of the King of Eastern Hunan Province. He also came with the government and died in Jiangzhou. He Xun, courtesy name Zhongyan, was born in Tan County, Donghai. His great-grandfather He Chengtian was the censor Zhongcheng during the Song Dynasty.
target: He died in office. His sons Liu Sui and Liu Su were also learned, with Liu Su serving as a secretary.

source: His great-grandfather He Chengtian was the censor Zhongcheng during the Song Dynasty. Grandfather He Yi was appointed Yuanwailang. His father, He Xun, served as a lieutenant in the Qi Dynasty and joined the army. He Xun could compose poems at the age of eight, and was elected as a scholar by the state at the age of 20. Fan Yun of Nanxiang saw the strategies written by He Xun and greatly appreciated them, so he and He Xun formed a lifelong friendship. From then on, Fan Yun praised every article and poem written by He Xun after seeing it. Fan Yun said to those close to him: Looking at the poems and essays of these literati recently, the simple ones are like Confucian scholars preaching scriptures, and the extravagant ones are a bit immoral. The ability to contain the aura of heaven and earth and include the principles of modern and ancient times can only be seen in He Sheng's poems. Shen Yue also liked He Xun's poems. He once said to He Xun: Every time I read your poems, I repeat them many times a day, and I still can't get enough of them. He Xun was praised by celebrities to such an extent. During the Tianjian period, He Xun took up an official position at home and was invited by the court to move to the Zhongwei Jian'an Wangshui Cao Xing to join the army and also serve as the recorder's office. King Jian'an loved literary scholars and entertained and feasted with them every day. King Jian'an moved to Jiangzhou, and He Xun was still the secretary in charge. He Xun returned to the capital and served as King Cheng of Anxi to join the military affairs and serve as Minister of the Ministry of Water. He resigned because of his mother's mourning. When the mourning period expired, He Xun was dismissed and granted the title of Renwei Luling Prince Ji. He then followed the royal family to Jiangzhou, where he died not long after. Wang Sengru of the East China Sea collected He Xun's poems and essays into eight volumes. At the beginning, both He Xun's poems and Liu Xiaochuo's poems were valued by the world, and the world called them "He Liu". Shizu wrote an article commenting on He Xun, saying: Shen Yue is the one who has many poems but shows his talent; Xie Tiao and He Xun are the ones who show his talent with few poems. At that time, there was Yu Qian in Kuaiji, who was good at writing five-character poems. His reputation was equal to that of He Xun, and his official position was that of the minister of the kingdom. Later, there were Kong Wenggui from Kuaiji and Jiangbi from Jiyang, both of whom served as the secretary of the Grand Sima Mansion of Nanping King. Kong Wenggui was also good at poetry. Jiang Bi was erudite and talented in reasoning. He also wrote annotations for the Analects and the Classic of Filial Piety.
target: He Xun, from Donghai, began writing at eight and was praised by Fan Yun and Shen Yue for his poetry. He served under King Jian'an and died in Jiangzhou, with his poems collected by Wang Sengru. He Xun was compared to Shen Yue and Xie Tiao, and his works were valued alongside Liu Xiaochuo's.

source: Later, there were Kong Wenggui from Kuaiji and Jiangbi from Jiyang, both of whom served as the secretary of the Grand Sima Mansion of Nanping King. Kong Wenggui was also good at poetry. Jiang Bi was erudite and talented in reasoning. He also wrote annotations for the Analects and the Classic of Filial Piety. Both men have collected works. Zhong Rong, whose courtesy name was Zhongwei, was from Changshe, Yingchuan. He was the seventh generation descendant of Zhong Bi, a minister of Jin Dynasty. His father, Zhong Chu, served in the Zhongjun Army during the Qi Dynasty.
target: Zhong Rong, from Yingchuan, was learned in the "Book of Changes" and served in various roles. He wrote a letter criticizing the misuse of official titles during the Yongyuan period, advocating for merit-based appointments.

source: It was not until Li Ling of the Mo Dynasty that he created the name of five-character poetry. The era of ancient poems is so long ago that it is difficult to clearly examine their author and writing time. However, judging from its content and style, it should be a work of Modai, not a work of the weekend decline period. Since Wang Bao, Yang Xiong, Mei Cheng, Sima Xiangru and others, they have all competed in the creation of poems and poems, each showing his or her own talents, but poetry recitation has never been heard of. From Li Ling and Li Duwei to Ban Jieyu, in nearly a hundred years, although there were women among them, there was only one person. The trend of poetry writing suddenly stopped. In the two hundred years of the Later Han Dynasty, there were only Ban Gu's "Ode to History" poems, which were simple and without literary talent. During the Jian'an period, Cao Cao and his son loved literature; Cao Zhi's brothers, with their prolific works, were actually pillars of the literary world; Liu Zhen and Wang Can grew in power around them. There are also nearly a hundred people who follow them voluntarily. The grand occasion of abundant talents can be regarded as appearing in this era. After the Rebellion, the literary world gradually declined until the Jin Dynasty. During the Taikang period, Zhang Zai, Zhang Xie, Zhang Hua, Lu Ji, Lu Yun, Pan Yue, Pan Ni, and Zuo Si all rose up, revived the literary world, followed Cao and his son, and inherited the lingering charm of the Jian'an period. Qian was also the period of the resurgence of five-character poetry. In the Yongjia era, the theories of Huang and Lao were valued and the style of metaphysical poetry was advocated. The poetry works of this period focused on metaphysical reasoning rather than content and literary talent, making them boring to read. As for when the Jin Dynasty moved south, the aftermath of this trend still spread. The works of Sun Chuo, Xu Xun, Huan Wei, Yu You and others were all simple and flat, like "On Moral Theory", and the Jian'an style was completely lost.
target: He later wrote "Poetry Criticism," a review of five-character poetry from ancient times to his era, discussing its evolution and key figures like Cao Zhi, Lu Ji, and Xie Lingyun. He died in office.

source: Soon, Zhong Rong died during his tenure. Zhong Yan's courtesy name was Changyue, and he was promoted to the government to join the army and Jiankangping. He is the author of ten volumes of "Biography of Good Officials". Zhongyu, whose courtesy name was Ji Wang, was appointed as the county magistrate of Yongjia County. In the fifteenth year of Tianjian, Emperor Gaozu ordered his bachelor to compile "Qilue", and Zhong Yu also participated in the compilation. Both brothers have anthologies. Zhou Xingsi, also known as Si Zuan, was a native of Xiang County, Chen County. He was a descendant of Zhou Kan, the prince of Mo. His great-great-grandfather Zhou Ning served as a member of the army in Zhengxi Prefecture and the governor of Yidu during the Jin Dynasty. Zhou Xingsi lived in Gushe for generations. When he was thirteen years old, he went to the capital to study. He spent more than ten years in total, and eventually read extensively and became proficient in historical books and was good at writing articles. Zhou Xingsi once traveled from Gushu and stayed in a hotel. Someone said to him at night: Your talents and learning surpass those of contemporary people. You were first appreciated by noble ministers and finally appreciated by the British Lord.
target: His brothers Zhong Yan and Zhong Yu also held official posts and wrote works. Zhou Xingsi, from Chen County, was a prolific writer who served Emperor Gaozu, composing inscriptions and poems. He was highly valued by Gaozu and Ren Fang, and died at an unknown age, leaving over 100 volumes of works.

source: In the fourteenth year of Tianjian, Zhou Xingsi was dismissed and granted the title of Linchuan County Magistrate. In the 17th year of Tianjian, he was appointed to Shizhong and headed to the Western Province. Zuo Wei led Zhou She to write annotations for the poems written by Emperor Gaozu, and Zhou She asked Zhou Xingsi to help him. In ordinary two years, Zhou Xingsi passed away. He wrote more than 100 volumes of "Records of the Emperor", "Records of the Emperor's Virtues", "Notes on Daily Life", and "Professional Etiquette", and has ten volumes of collected works. Wu Jun, whose courtesy name is Shuxiang, was born in Guzhang, Wuxing. His family has been poor for generations, but Wu Jun is eager to learn and has outstanding talents. Shen Yue once saw Wu Jun's articles, appreciated them very much, and praised them greatly. In the early years of Tianjian, Liu Pan was appointed as the prefect of Wuxing, and he called Wu Jun to take over the post of chief registrar. He asked Wu Jun to compose poems with him every day. Wu Jun's writing style is elegant and refined, with the temperament of the ancients. Some people like his style and imitate him, which is called Wu Jun style. Xiao Wei, the king of Jian'an, was appointed as the governor of Yangzhou and promoted Wu Jun to serve as a clerk in the record office and to be in charge of clerical matters. King Jian'an moved to be the governor of Jiangzhou, and Wu Jun was appointed as the Minister of State and concurrently as the governor of the city. After Wu Jun returned to the capital, he was dismissed and granted the title of "Feng Chao". Prior to this, Wu Jun petitioned to compile "Qi Chunqiu", which he later submitted to Gaozu. Gaozu believed that the book he wrote was not consistent with reality, so he sent Liu Zhilin, a member of the Zhongshushe, to question Wu Jun about several records in the book. Wu Jun was confused and unable to answer correctly. Gaozu ordered the book to be handed over to the Shangshu Province for burning, and Wu Jun was dismissed from his post.
target: Wu Jun, from Wuxing, was a talented writer whose style was imitated as "Wu Jun style." He served under King Jian'an and wrote "Qi Chunqiu," which was criticized for inaccuracies and burned.

source: Prior to this, Wu Jun petitioned to compile "Qi Chunqiu", which he later submitted to Gaozu. Gaozu believed that the book he wrote was not consistent with reality, so he sent Liu Zhilin, a member of the Zhongshushe, to question Wu Jun about several records in the book. Wu Jun was confused and unable to answer correctly. Gaozu ordered the book to be handed over to the Shangshu Province for burning, and Wu Jun was dismissed from his post. Not long after, Emperor Gaozu issued an order to summon Wu Jun and sent him to write the "General History", which began with the Three Emperors and ended with the Qi Dynasty. Wu Jun drafted this chronicle and the family was completed, but only the biographies were not completed. In the first year of ordinary life, Xian Jun died at the age of fifty-two. Fan Ye wrote ninety volumes of Hou Mo Shu, thirty volumes of Qi Chun Qiu, ten volumes of Temple Records, sixteen volumes of Twelve States, five volumes of Biography of the Sages of Qian and Tang Dynasties, five volumes of Su Wen Shi, and twenty volumes of collected works. Before this, there were Gao Shuang in Guangling, Jiang Hong in Jiyang, and Yu Qian in Kuaiji, all of whom were good at writing articles. During the Yongming period of Qi Dynasty, Gao Shuang presented poems to General Wang Jian of the Wei Army, which was appreciated by Wang Jian. When Wang Jian took charge of Danyang Yin, he recommended Gao Shuang as Xiaolian of the county. In the early years of Tianjian, Gao Shuang successively served as the Linchuan King of the Chinese Army and joined the army. He came out of Beijing and served as the magistrate of Jinling. He was imprisoned in Yezhong because of his guilt. He wrote "Ode on Wok Fish" to express his feelings. The text of the poem was very exquisite. Later, he was pardoned and Gao Shuang was released. He died soon after.
target: He later worked on a "General History" but died before completing it, leaving numerous works. Other writers like Gao Shuang, Jiang Hong, and Yu Qian were also noted for their literary skills, with Gao Shuang's "Ode on Wok Fish" being particularly praised.

source: Zang Dun, whose courtesy name was Xuanqing, was from Ju, Dongguan. His great-great-grandfather Zang Tao was the doctor Zuo Guanglu during the Song Dynasty. His grandfather Zang Tanzhi was appointed Minister of Zuo Min. His father, Zang Weizhen, was extensively involved in literature and history and was very talented. He was highly appreciated by his cousin Runan Zhou Yi when he was young. At the end of the Song Dynasty, Zang Weizhen was recruited from his family to serve as the leader of the army and serve Emperor Wu of Qi. After entering the Qi Dynasty, he successively served as Taiwei Jijiu, Shangshu Zhugulang, Jian'an Luling Second Prince's Palace Recorder, Former Military Cao Shi, Tongzhilang, Nanxuzhou Zhongzheng, Danyang Yincheng. Emperor Gaozu pacified the capital, established the royal palace, and selected Zang Weizhen to serve as a hussar in the prison and join the army. In the early years of Tianjian, Zang Weizhen was appointed as the Houjun Consultation Zhonglang and Nan Xuzhou Biejia. He also went to Beijing as Huangmenlang, and later moved to the right army Ancheng Wang Changshi and Shaofu Qing. He came to Beijing to serve as the prefect of Xin'an and was known for his ability in handling affairs. After returning to the capital, he served as the crown prince's concubine, Sinong Qing, and Taiwei Chief of History. Zang Weizhen mourned her biological mother and built a thatched cottage next to the cemetery for three years. After the mourning period expired, he was appointed Tingweiqing. Zang Weizhen left the capital and served as Changshi of King Ancheng and Grand Administrator of Jiangxia. He died in office. Zang Dun studied the "Five Classics" from the concubine Langye Zhuge Gu since he was a child, and he was proficient in analyzing chapters, sentences and explaining the meaning of the classics. Zhuge Can's students often numbered from dozens to hundreds. Zang Dun got along with them every day, but never got close to them. Zhuge Zhang admired him and sighed: This person is a great weapon to shoulder important responsibilities and a great talent to assist the emperor! Zang Dun first became an official and served as Fu Junxing to join the army, and later moved to Shangshu Binglang. He had a handsome demeanor, beautiful appearance, and elegant manners. Whenever he came to pay homage to him, Gaozu was very happy to see him. Zang Dun entered Beijing and served as Zhongshu General Secretary Shiren, and was later appointed as An Youlushi to join the army, but Shiren's position remained unchanged. Zang Dun had a filial nature. One day, while he was on duty with his father in Tingwei, his mother Liu was at home and suddenly fell ill and died in the middle of the night. That night, Zang Dun suffered a sudden severe pain in the middle finger of his left hand and could not sleep. When dawn came, someone at home reported the news of his mother's death. The spiritual connection between him and his relatives had reached such an extent. Zang Dun mourned for his mother before his father died. Zang Dun stayed in mourning for five years without leaving his thatched cottage. He was so haggard and skinny that no one in his family could recognize him. Wang Duan, a fellow countryman, reported the situation to the court. Emperor Gaozu praised him very much and sent people to comfort him many times.
target: Zang Dun, courtesy name Xuanqing, was from Ju, Dongguan. His lineage included notable ancestors: great-great-grandfather Zang Tao served as doctor Zuo Guanglu during the Song Dynasty; grandfather Zang Tanzhi was Minister of Zuo Min; and father Zang Weizhen, a talented scholar versed in literature and history, held various official posts under Emperor Wu of Qi and later under Emperor Gaozu of Liang, including Taiwei Jijiu, Shangshu Zhugulang, and prefect of Xin'an. Zang Weizhen mourned his mother for three years in a thatched hut by her grave and died as Grand Administrator of Jiangxia. Zang Dun studied the "Five Classics" under Zhuge Gu, excelling in textual analysis. Zhuge admired him as a future great leader. Zang Dun began his career as Fu Junxing to join the army, later becoming Shangshu Binglang. He was known for his handsome appearance and elegant manners, which pleased Emperor Gaozu. He served as Zhongshu General Secretary Shiren and An Youlushi. His filial piety was evident when he felt a sudden pain in his finger the night his mother died, leading him to mourn for five years in a thatched hut, becoming emaciated. Emperor Gaozu praised and comforted him.

source: Zang Dun entered Beijing and served as Zhongshu General Secretary Shiren, and was later appointed as An Youlushi to join the army, but Shiren's position remained unchanged. Zang Dun had a filial nature. One day, while he was on duty with his father in Tingwei, his mother Liu was at home and suddenly fell ill and died in the middle of the night. That night, Zang Dun suffered a sudden severe pain in the middle finger of his left hand and could not sleep. When dawn came, someone at home reported the news of his mother's death. The spiritual connection between him and his relatives had reached such an extent. Zang Dun mourned for his mother before his father died. Zang Dun stayed in mourning for five years without leaving his thatched cottage. He was so haggard and skinny that no one in his family could recognize him. Wang Duan, a fellow countryman, reported the situation to the court. Emperor Gaozu praised him very much and sent people to comfort him many times. After the mourning period expired, Zang Dun was appointed Yin Cheng of Danyang, transferred to Zhongshu Lang, and also served as Zhongshu Sheren, and later moved to Shangshu Zuocheng, Shu Zhonglang, Wuling Wang Changshi, conducted state affairs in the prefecture, and served as the governor of Kuaiji County. After returning to Beijing, he was appointed as Shaofu Qing, led the infantry school captain, and moved to Yushi Zhongcheng. Zang Dun has a strong and fair character and is very competent in the Yushi Mansion. In February of the fifth year of Zhongdatong, Emperor Gaozu came to Tongtai Temple to lecture on Buddhist scriptures and held a conference for the four tribes of monks, bhikshunis, Upasakas and Upasikas. Tens of thousands of people attended the meeting. During the meeting, the tame elephant presented by South Vietnam suddenly ran wild in the crowd. The emperor's chariots, horses, honor guards and people in the public gathering were frightened and fled. Only Zang Dun and Sanqi Lang Pei Zhili remained motionless and calm. Emperor Gaozu admired them very much. Soon the emperor issued an edict and appointed Xian Dun as a regular servant of the Sanqi. Before Xian Dun was appointed, Gaozu issued another Shao order saying: The post of commanding the six armies cannot be given to people without talent. Zang Dun, the censor Zhongcheng and the newly appointed Sanqi Changshi, is ambitious, loyal and prudent, knows people well and is cautious and thoughtful. He holds official positions fairly and fairly, and handles government affairs diligently and respectfully. He will definitely be able to handle military affairs well. He can also lead the army, and his position as a regular servant remains unchanged. In the second year of Datong, Zang Dun was moved to the position of leader. The leader is in charge of the military power of the country and is responsible for many affairs. Zang Dun was smart, agile, well-informed, courageous, and good at handling complex government affairs, so all matters within his scope of responsibility were handled in an orderly manner.
target: After mourning, Zang Dun held positions including Yin Cheng of Danyang, Zhongshu Lang, Shangshu Zuocheng, and governor of Kuaiji County. He became Yushi Zhongcheng, known for his strong and fair character. In 536, during a Buddhist lecture at Tongtai Temple, a tame elephant ran wild, but Zang Dun remained calm, earning the emperor's admiration. He was appointed Sanqi Changshi and later leader of the army, handling military affairs with intelligence and courage. He died in 543 at age 66, posthumously honored as Attendant.

source: In the seventh year of Datong, Zang Dun recovered from his illness and became the leading general again. In the ninth year of Datong, Zang Dun died at the age of sixty-six. On the day of his death, the emperor issued an edict to mourn for him. Zang Dun was posthumously given the title of Attendant, and his position as leader remained unchanged. The imperial court gave Shuyuan a secret weapon, a set of court clothes, and a set of funeral clothes? Coins and cloth were given in certain quantities. Mi cup. Zang Dun's eldest son Zang Changbo, named Meng Hong, served as the internal history of Guiyang. The second son Zang Zhongbo was appointed Qu'aling. Zang Dun's younger brother is Zang Jue. Zang Jue, also known as Xianqing, was also known for his talent and magnanimity. When he first took up his official position, he served as Xizhonglang and joined the army, serving as the chief guest of the Shangshu. Later, he entered Beijing and served as the general secretary of the Zhongshu, and was promoted to Zhengyuanlang and Hongluqing. His position as the general secretary of the Zhongshu remained unchanged. He was moved to the position of Minister Youcheng. Before he could take office, he left the capital to serve as the prefect of Jin'an. Jin'an County is located near the mountains and the sea, where escaped criminals often gather. Although the former county governor recruited sergeants to carry out raids, the thieves' intrusion could not be stopped. As soon as Zang Jue took office, he preached enlightenment, and the criminals dragged their sons and daughters and their families out of their hiding places to join them. The local people resumed their normal business, the roads were smooth, and merchants and travelers continued to come and go. However, Zang Jue believed in severe punishments and strict laws in handling political affairs and was unwilling to be lenient. Officials and people would be punished with rods for even the slightest mistake. The people called him "Zang Hu".
target: Zang Dun's brother, Zang Jue, also talented, served as prefect of Jin'an, where he quelled crime through enlightenment but was known for harsh punishments, earning the nickname "Zang Hu." He died in office at 48. Emperor Gaozu valued his judgment, often entrusting him with difficult cases.

source: When Zang Jue took office successively, the emperor ordered that all important matters in the official office and matters that the imperial censor Tingwei could not decide were handed over to him. The pressure analysis and judgment should be accurate, thorough and reasonable. After Kuan Hao passed away, someone beat the Dengwen drum to complain, requesting that the case be handed over to Yue Jue, the upright Sheren. Emperor Gaozu said: Zang Jue has passed away, so there is no one to entrust with this matter. Zang Jue was understood and appreciated by Emperor Gaozu to this extent. Xian Jue's son Zang Cao was appointed Sangong Lang of Shangshu. Fu Qi, named Jingping, was from Lingzhou in the north. His great-great-grandfather Fu Hongren was Taichang during the Song Dynasty. Grandfather Fu Yan served as the Shanyin magistrate in the Qi Dynasty. He had the ability to manage political affairs and was promoted from the county magistrate to the governor of Yizhou. Fu Xie's father, Fu Hui, was a member of the Shanyin and Jiankang orders during the Tianjian period. He was also famous for his talents and served as an official for consultation. Fu Qi started out as a student of the Imperial Academy of Ming Dynasty. He first became an official and served as Zuo Changshi, King of Nankang. Later, he moved to join the army and served as minister of Jinbulang. He resigned due to the death of his mother, and he did all the etiquette of mourning with all his heart.
target: Fu Qi, courtesy name Jingping, from Lingzhou, had ancestors like Fu Hongren (Taichang) and father Fu Hui (Shanyin magistrate). Fu Qi started as a student, served as Zuo Changshi, and later as Jinbulang.

source: His great-great-grandfather Fu Hongren was Taichang during the Song Dynasty. Grandfather Fu Yan served as the Shanyin magistrate in the Qi Dynasty. He had the ability to manage political affairs and was promoted from the county magistrate to the governor of Yizhou. Fu Xie's father, Fu Hui, was a member of the Shanyin and Jiankang orders during the Tianjian period. He was also famous for his talents and served as an official for consultation. Fu Qi started out as a student of the Imperial Academy of Ming Dynasty. He first became an official and served as Zuo Changshi, King of Nankang. Later, he moved to join the army and served as minister of Jinbulang. He resigned due to the death of his mother, and he did all the etiquette of mourning with all his heart. After the mourning period expired, he did not serve for a long time due to illness. During the Han Dynasty, the imperial court rebuilt the altar in the northern suburbs and began to appoint Fu Qi to supervise the construction. After the project was completed, the imperial court appointed him as the new order. Some people in Shixin County fought with each other and died. The family members of the deceased went to the county to file a complaint. The county guard arrested their enemy and tortured him in every possible way. The man still refused to plead guilty. The county guard transferred the case to Shixin County for trial. Fu Qi immediately ordered the handcuffs to be removed and asked the criminal gently, and the man immediately pleaded guilty. According to the law, the criminal should be sentenced to pay for his crime with his life. It happened to be the winter solstice, so Fu Qi let the criminal go home for reunion and let him return to prison after the winter solstice. The county official refused to release him and argued with Fu Qi: "This was done in ancient times, but it cannot be practiced now." Fu Qi said: If he is not trustworthy, I, the county magistrate, should be punished. You, the supervisor, don't worry. The criminal returned as scheduled.
target: He resigned to mourn his mother. He supervised the northern suburbs altar construction and became Shixin county magistrate, where he released a criminal on the winter solstice, who returned as promised, earning the prefect's praise.

source: Fu Qi said: If he is not trustworthy, I, the county magistrate, should be punished. You, the supervisor, don't worry. The criminal returned as scheduled. The prefect was amazed by this incident and immediately reported it in detail. Later, when Fu Qili established a new county, all the people, young and old, left the country to say goodbye. The sound of crying could be heard dozens of miles away. Fu Qi arrived in the capital and was appointed Tingweizheng. He entered the court and served as Zhongshu General Secretary and Shiren. He also moved to the Ningyuan Yueyang Prince's Office to join the army, but his position as Shiren remained unchanged. Fu Qi left the capital to serve as Jiankang Order, but was dismissed due to official duties. Soon after, he was appointed as a secretary. After repeated promotions, he was promoted to the Anxi Zhongji Office. He consulted in Zhennan to join the army, but his position as a concurrent secretary remained unchanged. Fu Qi has a handsome appearance, a smart manner, a wide range of interests, and fluent answers. During the Datong period, the imperial court made peace with the State of Wei. Envoys from the State of Wei came twice a year, and the emperor often sent Fu Qi to receive them. In the first year of the Taiqing Dynasty, he was promoted to the rank of Imperial Servant and Minister of Agriculture, but his position remained unchanged. He has served in the imperial palace for more than ten years and participated in the planning of state secrets and worked diligently, which is comparable to Zhu Yi. In the winter of this year, Xiao Yuanming, Marquis of Zhenyang, the governor of Yuzhou, led his troops to attack Pengcheng. After the failure, he was trapped in the Wei state. In the second year of Taiqing, Xiao Yuanming sent an envoy back to Liang to convey the intention of the Wei people to resume friendly relations with Liang. The emperor ordered Yousi and close ministers to discuss the decision. Zuowei General Zhu Yi said: Gao Cheng's intention this time is to continue to maintain the previous friendly relations between the two countries; by doing so, our border will be free from foreign enemies and the people can live in peace. It will be beneficial to things if we agree to make peace. Everyone who participated in the discussion believed that Zhu Yi's opinion was correct. Only Fu Qi said: Gao Cheng just won the battle and his power is not weak. Why must he ask for peace? Wei must have set up a plan to alienate Marquis Zhenyang, and deliberately asked Marquis Zhenyang to send an envoy to make Hou Jing suspect that the emperor would exchange himself for Marquis Zhenyang. Hou Jing felt uneasy and must plot a rebellion. If we agree to Gao Cheng's request for peace now, we will fall into his treacherous scheme. Besides, our army failed in Pengcheng last year and Wuyan was recently defeated. We reconciled with Gao Cheng as soon as he expressed his intention. This further shows the weakness of the country's strength. If you follow my opinion, you cannot agree to Gao Cheng's request for peace this time. Zhu Yi and others insisted on their opinions, and Gaozu followed Zhu Yi and others' opinions.
target: He served as Tingweizheng, Zhongshu General Secretary, and Jiankang Order. During the Datong period, he received Wei envoys. In 547, he opposed peace with Wei, warning it would alienate Hou Jing and cause rebellion, but Emperor Gaozu followed Zhu Yi's advice. Hou Jing rebelled in 548, and Fu Qi's predictions proved correct.

source: After the alliance was signed, the civil and military ministers in the city were very happy, hoping that the capital would be able to relieve the siege. Only Fu Qi said to everyone: The rebels launched an army to rebel and asked for peace without achieving their goals. This foreigner has a human heart like a beast. He must not be trusted. This time he signed a covenant and he will eventually be deceived. Everyone complained and blamed him. When Hou Jing broke the covenant, no one could not express his admiration for Fu Qi. Not long after, the emperor issued an edict that because of Fu Qi's hard work, he should be granted the title of Marquis of Nanfeng County, with a settlement of 500 households, but Fu Qi firmly refused to accept it. After the fall of Miyagi, Fu Qi escaped from the siege despite being ill and later died at home. Yao Cha, the Minister of the Ministry of Civil Affairs of Chen, said: Those who preside over affairs must plan carefully first, so they will not make mistakes in anything they do. What Kuo said is so true. Fu Qi saw through the Qi family's conspiracy to pretend to sue for peace, and it can be said that he was good at planning. If Fu Qi's ideas had been adopted at that time, the chaos in the Taiqing period would not have happened in the first place.
target: He refused a marquis title and died at home after Miyagi fell. Yao Cha praised Fu Qi's foresight, noting that if his advice had been heeded, the Taiqing chaos might have been avoided.

source: Wang Sengbian, also known as Juncai, was the son of Youwei General Wang Shennian. During the Tianjian period, Wang Sengbian came to join his father. He was recruited from his family and served as the Zuo Changshi of the Xiangdong Kingdom. King Xiangshu was appointed Danyang Yin, and Wang Sengbian was transferred to Fu Xing to join the army. King Shu of Hunan was appointed as the prefect of Kuaiji, and Wang Sengbian also served as a soldier in the military. King Xiangshu was appointed governor of Jingzhou, and Wang Sengbian was still appointed as a soldier in the army and held a confidential position.
target: Wang Sengbian, son of General Wang Shennian, began his military career during the Tianjian period, serving under various princes in positions such as Zuo Changshi and military advisor.

source: Soon he moved to oversee Anlu County, and returned to the palace not long after. Soon he was appointed governor of Xincai, still holding the post of Sima, and his title of general remained unchanged. King Shu of Xiang was appointed as the prefect of Jingzhou. Wang Sengbian consulted for General Zhenyi's office and joined the military. He was given food for a thousand people. He replaced Liu Zhongli as the prefect of Jingling and changed his title to General Xiongxin. When Hou Jing rebelled, the king of eastern Hunan ordered Wang Sengbian to go on holiday. The governor sent 10,000 naval troops to aid the capital with food supplies. When Monk Wang arrived at the capital, the palace was captured and the emperor was humiliated. Wang Sengbian, Liu Zhongli brothers, Tang Bochao and others first surrendered to Hou Jing, and then entered the palace to see the emperor. Hou Jing confiscated all their weapons and food, and deeply comforted them. Not long after, Hou Jing sent Wang Sengbian back to Jingling. Wang Sengbian then doubled his travels, traveling day and night, and went west to join Shizu. Shizu followed the emperor's will and appointed Wang Sengbian as the leading general. There was a rift between the governor of Jingzhou, King Xiangdong, and the governor of Xiangzhou, King Hedong. They were suspicious of each other, and the army could not be commanded in a unified manner. The emperor ordered Wang Sengbian and Bao Quan to lead the army to attack them, allocate enough military rations, and set a date for departure. At that time, Wang Sengbian planned to wait for all of Jingling's men to gather before moving forward together because not all of Jingling's men had arrived. Wang Sengbian said to Bao Quan: You and I accepted the order to march southward, but the army formation is so uneven. What are your plans? Bao Quan said: Since we have accepted the imperial court's war plan and led our brave soldiers to kill the enemy, the situation is like pouring hot water on snow, so why should we worry more?
target: He quelled a rebellion in Wuning County and held several governorships, including Wuning, Guangping, and Anlu. When Hou Jing rebelled, Wang Sengbian led 10,000 naval troops to aid the capital, but the palace was captured. He briefly surrendered to Hou Jing before rejoining Shizu (Emperor Yuan of Liang). Ordered to attack the governor of Xiangzhou, Wang Sengbian delayed departure due to insufficient troops, angering Shizu, who struck him with a sword and imprisoned him. He was later pardoned to defend against King Yueyang's attack, successfully defeating him and replacing Bao Quan to pacify Xiangzhou.

source: After returning, Wang Sengbian was appointed as the leading general. Hou Jing led his army to invade west along the Liao Dynasty by boat, and the army was stationed in Xia Shou. Wang Sengbian was appointed as the governor, and led Chun Yuliang, the governor of Bazhou, Du Gong, the governor of Dingzhou, Wang Lin, the governor of Yizhou, Pei Zhiheng, the governor of Chenzhou and others to rush to Xiyang, and the army was stationed in Baling. Hearing that Yingzhou had been captured, Sengbian defended Baling City. Shizu then ordered Xu Sihui, the governor of Luozhou, and Du Dian, the governor of Wuzhou, to join Sengbian in Baling. After Hou Jing also captured Jiangxi, the number of soldiers increased and their morale was very strong, and they were about to attack Xingye. So he sent Iuguan Yi and Ding He to lead 5,000 soldiers to guard the Red Star. General Song Zixian led 10,000 horses as the vanguard to go straight to Baling. Jiangxi Liang led all the rebels to follow the vanguard by land and water. So the soldiers garrisoned along Liao asked to surrender when they heard the news. The rebels extended the patrol soldiers as far as Yinji. Wang Sengbian transported all the rice and grain from Liaozhu ashore and sank all public and private ships into the water.
target: Wang Sengbian then defended Baling against Hou Jing's invasion, employing strategies like sinking ships and stockpiling supplies. Despite fierce assaults, including fire attacks and siege equipment, the rebels were repelled.

source: The rebels repeatedly attacked and were defeated. The rebel leader Yu Dian was captured by Lu Yunsu again. He burned down the camp and escaped at night, leading his army back to Xia Shou. The ancestors discussed meritorious deeds and rewarded him, and ordered Wang Sengbian to be the general of the East Conquest, the third division of Kaifu Yitong, the governor of Jiangzhou, and the title of Duke of Changning County. So Shizu ordered Wang Sengbian to immediately lead all the troops in Baling and go down the river to conquer Hou Jingliang. The army was stationed in Yingcheng and sent infantry to attack Lushan. Zhi Huaren, the chief defender of Lushan City, was a cavalry officer under Hou Jing. He led his followers to fight with all their strength, but was still severely defeated by Wang Sengbian's army, so Zhi Huaren surrendered. Wang Sengbian then led various troops to cross the river to attack Ying, and immediately entered Ying's outer city. Song Zixian gathered all his men and horses to defend the inner city, but Wang Sengbian attacked the city but failed to capture it. Song Zixian sent his subordinate Tong Xihu to lead 3,000 troops to open the city gate and go out to fight. Wang Sengbian defeated the rebels who left the city, captured Di Xihu alive, and killed more than a thousand people. Sai Zixian led his army to retreat and defend, relying on the natural dangers to defend around Liao. Wang Mengbiao led his troops to attack repeatedly but failed to conquer it. Hou Jing heard the news that Lushan had been captured and that the outer city of Ying, an important town, had been lost, so he led the remaining troops to return to Jianye day and night. Song Zixian and others were in a difficult situation and had nothing to do, so they asked Wang Sengbian to hand over Yingcheng and let him lead his troops back to Hou Jing.
target: Rewarded as General of the East Conquest and Duke of Changning, he led forces to capture Lushan and Yingcheng, defeating Song Zixian and capturing him alive. He advanced to Jiushui, and after learning of the emperor's death, urged Shizu to take the throne. Marching toward Jianye, he allied with Chen Baxian at Baimaozhou, swearing an oath to destroy Hou Jing. Their combined forces defeated the rebels at Stone City, and Hou Jing fled. Wang Sengbian captured rebel leaders and restored order, earning the title of General of the Town Guard and Situ.

source: The rebels and puppet officials, Fan Xirong and Lu Huilue, still occupied Huancheng. When Wang Sengbian and his troops arrived, Fan Xirong and others took Jiangzhou Governor Lincheng Gong hostage and fled the city. Shizu gave Wang Sengbian additional official positions such as Shizhong, Shangshu Ling, and General of the Eastern Conquest, and also gave him the Department of Advocacy. Then he ordered Wang Sengbian to temporarily garrison Jiangzhou until all the troops were concentrated and he got the opportunity before attacking. Soon, Shizu ordered people from all walks of life in Jiangzhou to launch a massive attack. Wang Sengbian then announced the bad news of the emperor's death and reported the bad news to Shizu in Jiangling. So he led more than a hundred generals to jointly write a letter to Shizu, urging Shizu to take the throne as emperor. When he was about to march against Hou Jing, he wrote again to persuade him to advance. Although Shizu did not listen, he received a graceful reply from Shizu. The incident was recorded in the "Benji" of Emperor Shizu Xiaoyuan. Wang Sengbian then set out from Jiangzhou and aimed directly at Jianye. He first ordered Hou Tian, ​​the governor of Nanyanzhou, to lead his elite soldiers in a light fast boat to attack Nanling, Quetou and other garrison posts. Wherever they went, they immediately captured them. Prior to this, Chen Baxian led 50,000 men and set out from Nanjiang, sending 5,000 men as the vanguard and had already arrived at Fankou. Chen Baxian had outstanding talents and was good at strategy. His reputation surpassed that of Wang Sengbian, and Wang Sengbian respected him. After Chen Baxian arrived at Fankou, he met Wang Sengbian at Baimaozhou. The two went to the altar and swore an oath of alliance. Chen Baxian wrote an alliance article saying:
target: Later, Wang Sengbian suppressed the rebellion of Lu Na in Xiangzhou, using cautious tactics to surround and defeat him. He then guarded against Qi invasions, defeating their forces at Dongguan. After his mother's death, he received honors and a eulogy from the emperor.

source: Turn around the army that was preparing to return to the division and continue to advance towards Liyang. The people who were originally agreed to be hostages also wanted to come to that place. The Qi army will not cross the river, which is clearly stated in the alliance letter. This is exactly the arrangement made by the Shengming Emperor of Dacha who is particularly tolerant to us. King Shangdang, who is extremely virtuous and talented, has promised not to lose his credibility in order to obtain the original. If Duke Wen of Jin does not do such a stupid thing, Qi will not do it in the end. I'm just waiting to see you again, not far away. My hometown is very close, and the scene evokes emotions, which makes people even more sad. Wang Sengbian sent an envoy to send the hostages to Ye. When the Marquis of Zhenyang crossed the Liao Dynasty, he asked for 3,000 guards to be brought with him. Wang Sengbian was worried that they might instigate a rebellion, so he was only willing to accept 1,000 stragglers. He also sent a dragon boat with the emperor's luan chariot to meet him. On the day when Marquis Zhenyang crossed the river, Wang only took a boat and stopped in the center of Liao Dynasty, not daring to dock. Later he met Marquis Zhenyang at Jiangningpu. Marquis Zhenyang ascended the throne of the pseudo-emperor, so he appointed Wang Sengbian as the Grand Sima, leading the Crown Prince, Tutor, and Yangzhou Mu. The other titles remained unchanged. Su Xixian was then the governor of Sikong and South Xuzhou. He hated Wang Shifeng's capriciousness, so he discussed with the generals to send 100,000 troops from Jingkou to attack Jiankang by land and water. So the navy arrived first. Wang Sengbian often lived in Stone City. One day when he was dealing with political affairs, soldiers had climbed over the wall in the north of the city to attack. Someone came on horseback from the south gate to report that an army was coming to attack. Wang Sengbian and his son Wang Fu hurriedly ran out of the government office, followed by dozens of close friends. All the troops sent by Chen Baxian had arrived, and Wang Sengbian had no choice but to defend the south gate tower and beg Ling Baxian for mercy. Chen Baxian ordered the South Gate Tower to be set on fire. Wang Sengbiancai and Wang Zhi went downstairs and were captured. Su Ling first said: What crime do I have? Do you want to join Qi Jun to attack me? He also said: Why are you so defenseless? Monk Wang argued: If I hand over the north gate to you, how can I be considered unprepared? That night Chen Baxian killed Wang Sengbian. Wang Sengbian's eldest son, Wang Chan, was promoted to the rank of Attendant at the beginning of his reign. At first, after Wang Sengbian pacified Jianye, he sent Chen Baxian to guard Jingkou, but he did not take any precautions against him. Wang Jie repeatedly made suggestions on the affairs, but Wang Sengbian did not listen, and eventually fell into trouble. When the Western Wei Dynasty invaded Jiangling, Shizu sent Wang Jie to supervise all military affairs in the city. After Jingcheng was captured, Wang Jie followed Wang Lin to Qi State and served as the governor of Jingling County. Qi sent Wang Lin to guard Shouchun and planned to invade Jiangzuo. After Chen pacified Huainan, he captured Wang Lin and killed him. Wang Hao heard the news of Wang Lin's death, so he went to the south of the county city, climbed to the top of a mountain and cried bitterly, and died of extreme sorrow. Wang Hao's younger brother, Wang Ban, had ambition and integrity since he was a child, and often followed Shizu. When Jingcheng was captured, Wang Ban was captured by the Western Wei Dynasty.
target: When Western Wei attacked Jiangling, Wang Sengbian was summoned but failed to arrive before the capital fell. He supported Emperor Jing and negotiated with Qi to accept Xiao Yuanming as emperor, sending hostages and meeting him at Jiangningpu. This led to conflict with Chen Baxian, who attacked Jiankang. Wang Sengbian, caught off guard, was captured and killed by Chen Baxian. His sons met various fates: Wang Chan died early, Wang Jie fled to Qi, Wang Hao died of grief, and Wang Ban was captured by Western Wei. The historian notes that despite his merits, Wang Sengbian's decision to install a puppet emperor under Qi coercion led to his downfall.

source: Fu Manrong, courtesy name Gongyi, was born in Anqiu, Pingchang. His great-grandfather Fu Tao was a scholar in the Jin Dynasty. His father Fu Yinzhi was the chief secretary of Sikong during the Song Dynasty. Fu Manrong lost his father very early, and he lived in the South China Sea with his mother and brother. Fu Manrong has been attentive and studious since he was a child, and he is proficient in "Laozi" and "Book of Changes". He is bold and free and likes to exaggerate. He once said: He Yan has questions about nine things in "Yi". From my perspective, He Yan does not study at all, so I know that Uncle He Ping has shortcomings.
target: Fu Manrong, from Anqiu, lost his father early and lived with his mother and brother in the South China Sea. He was studious, proficient in Laozi and the Book of Changes, and bold in speech.

source: His father, He Xin, was invited to the court by Qi Shi. He Tongzhi has been interested in "Three Rites" since he was a child. He takes his heart as his teacher, studies independently, works hard to improve, and never lets go of the book. He read three hundred chapters of "Li" and read them all with proficiency, and the sentences could be spoken smoothly. Taiwei Wang Jian was the master of Confucianism at that time, and he also respected He Tongzhi very much. He Tong first became an official in Yangzhou, and then became a bachelor of Zongming Hall. He was promoted repeatedly, and later he served as Situ Chaqi, a member of the military, and Shangshu Temple Minister. During the Jianwu period of Qi Dynasty, he served as the Zhenbei Ji Office, joined the army, served as an assistant to the crown prince, and led the Zhongzheng of Danyang City.
target: He gathered students to teach and held various official positions, including Piaoqi Canjun and Nanhai Prefect. During the Qi Dynasty, he served as Tongzhi Sanqi Changshi and later as Zhongshu Lang.

source: Cui He wrote twenty-two volumes of "Collection of Mao's Poems", forty volumes of "Collection of Zhouli", forty-seven volumes of "Sanli Yi Zong", twenty-two volumes of "Zuo Shi Jing Chuan Yi", ten volumes of "Zuo Shi Regulations", and ten volumes of "Gongyanggu Liang Wen Ju Yi". Kong Qian came in from Shanyin in Kuaiji. When he was young, Wang Yu worshiped He Yin as his teacher. He was proficient in the Five Classics, especially the Three Rites, Xiaozhi and the Analects of Confucius. He expounded and taught these scriptures dozens of times and had hundreds of students. Renxi successively served as an assistant teacher of Guozi, a doctor of "Five Classics" three times, and moved to the post of Shangshu Temple Minister. He left Beijing and served as magistrate of two counties. Kong Qian was a Confucian scholar who only knew the classics and was not good at governing the people. He had no political achievements during his tenure as county magistrate. When turmoil broke out during the Liqian period, Kong Yu died at home. Kong Chuxuan, the son of Kong Qian, focused on studying Confucianism, and his official position was promoted to Doctor of Taixue.
target: He was known for lecturing on scriptures at home, attracting dozens or hundreds of students.

source: Fu Manrong moved to Situ to join the army. When Yuan Can was appointed Danyang Yin, he requested that Fu Manrong be appointed as Jiangning Order. Fu Manrong entered the capital and was awarded the title of Shangshu Waibinglang. At the end of the Ming Dynasty, he served as the governor of the auxiliary state and the governor of Nanhai. In the early years of the Qi Dynasty, he served as the minister of Tongzhi Sanqi. In the early years of the Yongming Dynasty, he led the crown prince's orders and served the crown prince. General Wei Wang Jian and Fu Manrong were very friendly and had a deep friendship. Wang Jian ordered Fu Manrong to co-write the "Mourning Clothing Yi" with Sima Xian of Hanoi and Wujun Lu Cheng. After writing the "Mourning Clothing Yi", Wang Jian wanted to review the rituals and music with Fu Manrong. Coinciding with Wang Jian's death, Fu Manrong was promoted to Minister of the Secretariat, Grand Sima, and joined the army. He also left the capital to serve as the prefect of Wuchang. During the Jianwu period, Fu Manrong entered Beijing and was awarded the title of Zhongsan doctor. At that time, Emperor Ming did not attach great importance to Confucianism, and Fu Manrong's residence was beside Waguan Temple. Fu Manrong set up a high seat in the hall of his home. When guests came, he would climb on the high seat and lecture on the scriptures to them. There were often dozens or hundreds of students gathered to listen to the lectures. Liang Guotai Mansion was established. Because Fu Manrong was a great Confucian scholar with a high reputation, Emperor Gaozu summoned him to worship him as Sima and as the prefect of Linhai. In the first year of Tianjian, Fu Manrong died during his tenure at the age of eighty-two. Fu Manrong is the author of "Annotation of Zhouyi", "Annotation of Mao's Poems", "Annotation of Mourning Clothes", "Laoziyi", "Zhuangziyi" and "On Semantics".
target: In the Liang Dynasty, he was appointed as Sima and Linhai Prefect, dying at eighty-two. He authored annotations on the Zhouyi, Mao's Poems, and other works.

source: The deeds of Fu Manrong's son Fu Qu are in "The Biography of Good Officials". He Tong, whose courtesy name was Shiwei, was from Sa County, Lujiang. He was the sixth-generation grandson of He Pang, the governor of Yuzhou. His grandfather He Shaozhi was a member of the imperial court during the Song Dynasty. His father, He Xin, was invited to the court by Qi Shi. He Tongzhi has been interested in "Three Rites" since he was a child. He takes his heart as his teacher, studies independently, works hard to improve, and never lets go of the book. He read three hundred chapters of "Li" and read them all with proficiency, and the sentences could be spoken smoothly. Taiwei Wang Jian was the master of Confucianism at that time, and he also respected He Tongzhi very much. He Tong first became an official in Yangzhou, and then became a bachelor of Zongming Hall. He was promoted repeatedly, and later he served as Situ Chaqi, a member of the military, and Shangshu Temple Minister.
target: He Tongzhi, from Lujiang, was deeply interested in the Three Rites from childhood, studying independently and mastering three hundred chapters of the Li. Respected by Taiwei Wang Jian, he held various posts, including Shangshu Temple Minister and Infantry Colonel. During the Yongyuan period, despite war, he continued lecturing.

source: In the early years of ZTE, He Tongzhi was worshiped as a general of heroic cavalry. After Emperor Gaozu ascended the throne, he respected Confucianism and appointed He Tongzhi as Minister Zuocheng. At that time, various systems were in the process of being created. He Tongzhi relied on "Li" to determine his views, which was of great help in formulating the system. In the second year of Tianjian, He Tongzhi died during his tenure at the age of fifty-five. Emperor Gaozu mourned his death and planned to grant him a title and an official position. According to the previous regulations, there was no precedent for conferring official positions on Zuocheng after his death. However, Emperor Gaozu specifically issued an edict to confer the post of Minister of Huangmen to He Tong. Confucian scholars felt honored by this favor. He Tongzhi wrote about one hundred articles in "Li Yi".
target: After Emperor Gaozu's ascension, he became Zuocheng, aiding in system creation. He died at fifty-five, posthumously honored as Huangmen Shilang. He wrote about one hundred articles on Li Yi.

source: He Tongzhi's sons were named He Chaoyin and He Chaohui. Fan Zhen, courtesy name Zizhen, was born in Wuyin, Nanxiang. He is the sixth generation grandson of Fan Wang, the general of Jin'an North. His grandfather Fan Xuzhi served as Zhongshu Lang. His father, Fan Meng, died young. Fan Zhen lost his father when he was very young. His family was poor and he served his mother with filial piety and respect. When Fan Zhen was less than 20 years old, he heard that Liu Shan of Pei State had gathered students to discuss the meaning of the classics, so he went to study with Liu Shan as his teacher. Fan Zhen has outstanding talents, is different from ordinary people, and studies diligently. Liu Shan thinks he is a genius and crowns him personally. Fan Zhen studied under Liu Shan for many years. Every time he went home, he often wore straw sandals and common clothes and walked back and forth. Liu Shan's family had many princes and nobles who rode in carriages and horses. Fan Zhen was under Liu Shan's family and did not feel ashamed at all because of his poverty. When Fan Zhen grew older, he became proficient in classics, especially the "Three Rites". Fan Zhensheng has a straightforward nature and likes to make honest and extraordinary remarks, so the scholars and friends who associate with him often feel unhappy. Fan Zhen only has a good relationship with his cousin Xiao Chen. Xiao Chen is known as an eloquent person, but he is often very impressed by Fan Zhen's concise and thoughtful diction.
target: Fan Zhen, from Nanxiang, lost his father young and served his mother filially. He studied under Liu Shan, excelling in the Three Rites. He served as an envoy to the Wei and was known for his straightforward nature.

source: After Fan Zhen personally welcomed Emperor Gaozu's army, he was determined to serve as a minister. Soon his ambition was not realized, and he often became unhappy, so he became close to Wang Liang in private to correct the current situation. Later, he was eventually moved to Guangzhou because of Wang Liang's incident, which was recorded in "The Biography of Wang Liang". At first, when he was still in the Qi Dynasty, Fan Zhen once accompanied Xiao Ziliang, the king of Jingling. Xiao Ziliang firmly believes in Buddhism, while Fan Zhen strongly claims that there is no Buddha. Xiao Ziliang asked Fan Zhen: If you don't believe in cause and effect, then how can there be wealth and poverty in the world? Fan Zhen replied: Life is like flowers on the same tree. They grow on the same branch and bloom on the same pedicle. They fall with the wind. Some flowers blow open the curtain and fall on the mat, while others meet the fence and fall next to the dirty soil pit. Your Majesty, you are the one who is on the mat; this is the case with me, your Majesty, who is lying next to the filthy pit. Although high and low have different paths, where does cause and effect ultimately end? Xiao Ziliang couldn't reason with him, and was deeply surprised by Jian Long's views. After returning, he discussed his own principles and wrote "Theory on the Destruction of Gods", saying:
target: He debated Buddhism with Xiao Ziliang, arguing against the existence of gods. His "Theory on the Destruction of Gods" sparked controversy.

source: Fan Zhen had been in the south for many years and was recalled to the capital. After returning to the capital, the imperial court appointed him Zhongshu Lang and Doctor Guozi. He died during his tenure. Fan Zhen has ten volumes of collected works. Fan Zhen's son Fan Xu, also known as Changcai. He inherited his father's knowledge and became a doctor of Taixue at the beginning of his career. Fan Xu was an eloquent person. During the Datong period, he served as host and guest, responsible for welcoming and answering envoys from the north. Fan Xu moved to Pingxi to consult with the king of Xiangdong and join the army, and served as an assistant to the king of Xuancheng. He left the capital and served as the internal history of Poyang and died in the county. Yan Zhi's courtesy name was Xiaoyuan, and he was a native of Zigui, Jianping. His grandfather Yan Qin was a regular attendant of Tongzhi Sanqi during the Song Dynasty. Yan Zhizhi has been proficient in Zhuangzi and Laozi since he was a child. He can talk about the metaphysical theories of Laozi and Zhuangzhuang, and has a very sophisticated understanding of "Mourning Clothes", "The Classic of Filial Piety" and "The Analects of Confucius". When he reached adulthood, he extensively studied "Li", "Book of Changes", "Mao Shi" and "Zuo Shi Chun Qiu" annotated by Zheng. He has a simple and filial temperament, is respectful and kind, and does not put his own merits above others. Yan Zhi's father died when he was young, so he only ate vegetables for twenty-three years. Later, he changed his habit of eating only vegetables because he contracted wind and cold. During the next year of Qi Yong, he first became an official and served as the minister of the Luling Kingdom. Moved to serve as the Right Changshi of the Guanghan Kingdom.
target: He held various posts, including Yidu Prefect and Jin'an Prefect, dying as Zhongshu Lang. His son Fan Xu inherited his knowledge. Yan Zhizhi, from Jianping, was proficient in Zhuangzi, Laozi, and the Three Rites. He served as Luling Kingdom Minister and Guanghan Kingdom Right Changshi, known for his righteousness in handling the Guanghan King's funeral.

source: Zha Ximo established his own point of view and combined the theories of Tantian and Gaitian. Cui Lingen went to Beijing to serve as the internal history of Changsha. When he returned to Beijing, he was awarded the title of Doctor of the State. There were many students who studied with him. He went to Beijing to serve as General Mingwei and Governor Guacong, and died during his tenure. Cui He wrote twenty-two volumes of "Collection of Mao's Poems", forty volumes of "Collection of Zhouli", forty-seven volumes of "Sanli Yi Zong", twenty-two volumes of "Zuo Shi Jing Chuan Yi", ten volumes of "Zuo Shi Regulations", and ten volumes of "Gongyanggu Liang Wen Ju Yi". Kong Qian came in from Shanyin in Kuaiji. When he was young, Wang Yu worshiped He Yin as his teacher. He was proficient in the Five Classics, especially the Three Rites, Xiaozhi and the Analects of Confucius. He expounded and taught these scriptures dozens of times and had hundreds of students. Renxi successively served as an assistant teacher of Guozi, a doctor of "Five Classics" three times, and moved to the post of Shangshu Temple Minister. He left Beijing and served as magistrate of two counties. Kong Qian was a Confucian scholar who only knew the classics and was not good at governing the people. He had no political achievements during his tenure as county magistrate. When turmoil broke out during the Liqian period, Kong Yu died at home. Kong Chuxuan, the son of Kong Qian, focused on studying Confucianism, and his official position was promoted to Doctor of Taixue.
target: He was appointed as a Five Classics doctor, lecturing to hundreds of students. He died at fifty-two, leaving his family in poverty. He authored 479 volumes of Annotations on Evil Etiquette.

source: Yan Zhizhi had many benevolent deeds like this. Yan Zhizhi wrote four hundred and seventy-nine volumes of "Annotations on Evil Etiquette". He Yuan's courtesy name was Delian, and he came from Shanyin in Kuaiji. His grandfather He Daoli was proficient in the "Three Rites" and served as Sangong Lang and Jiankang Ling in the Song Dynasty. He Tan inherited his family education from an early age. During the Qi Dynasty, Liu Xian of Pei State was the Prime Minister of Kuaiji. When he saw He Yu, he was very surprised by his talents and thought highly of him. Liu Xian once visited Zhang Rong of Wu County with He Chang. Liu Xian pointed to the brush and ink and said to Zhang Rong: This young man has a smart and agile mind and will become a master of Confucianism in the future. After Liu Xian returned to the capital, he recommended He Yuan as the son of the emperor. He Tuan was recommended as Ming Jing, Jijiu, and soon served as Guozi's assistant. He successively served as a doctor of Taixue and Taichang Cheng at the invitation of the imperial court. He resigned when his mother died. In the early years of Tianjian, he was appointed as Taichang Cheng. A minister recommended him to study Bin Li. Emperor Gaozu summoned him to lecture on the meaning of "Li". He was deeply surprised by his knowledge and issued an edict to go to court on the first and fifteenth day of every month and participate in lectures in Hualin Garden. In the fourth year of his reign, the Five Classics School had just been opened, and he was ordered to hold a doctorate in the Five Classics. He specially ordered Hechang to write the "Five Classics Meanings" for the crown prince.
target: He Chang, from Kuaiji, inherited family education in the Three Rites. Recommended by Liu Xian, he served as Taichang Cheng and Five Classics doctor, lecturing on the Li.

source: He also left the capital and served as Xinwu, the successor of Guiyang, Changshi, and the prefect of Xunyang. He was also appointed as the chief historian of Wuling King, and his post as governor remained unchanged. He died during his tenure. Shen Jun, courtesy name Shisong, was born in Wukang, Wuxing. The family has been a farmer for generations, until Yingkong. He loved learning, and he and his uncle Taishi Shuming chose Shen Jun as their teacher from the same clan. He studied under Shen Junmu for many years. He assigned himself tasks to study day and night. Sometimes he would doze off and hit himself with a wooden stick. He was so concentrated. After Shen Lin's death, Licai left the capital and traveled to various schools, so he became proficient in the Five Classics, especially the Three Rites.
target: He authored works on etiquette and the Five Classics, dying at fifty-nine. His son He Ge also became a renowned scholar, lecturing on the Three Rites.

source: Isn't it a clear proof that Ren Shibao's loving mother and son do not have to mourn? Zheng Xuan did not distinguish between the three types of loving mothers, and gave vague explanations. He quoted Ren Shibao's example of a kind mother who did not need to mourn to explain "the concubine who raised oneself." The etiquette fallacy that future generations will understand actually comes from Zheng Xuan's comment. It is said in the scriptures that "the son of a gentleman" refers to starting from the high-ranking officials, but it also clearly points out that the high-ranking officials are still within the scope of sending, and there should be no difference from the sending to the top. Therefore, the text says that "the son of a gentleman" refers to the son of a nobleman. If you call them aristocrats, then they are all inclusive. The scriptures of "Biao" and "Zhuan" complement each other, complement each other, and explain each other. It is known that the rules for strengthening the etiquette for loving mothers and changing from wearing gills to wearing Xiaogong mourning clothes are common to all officials and above. The regulations of the Song Dynasty do not violate the original intention of the "Li", and it is really doubtful to eliminate them.
