So Sima Yun and others requested that the relevant etiquette be changed in accordance with the order of Emperor Gaozu: if the son of the legitimate wife is raised by his father's concubine after the death of his mother, he should mourn for his adoptive mother for five months after his adoptive mother dies. Both the noble and the low should adopt the regulations and make it a permanent system. Sima Yun accumulated merit and moved to the palace to serve as a consultant, with the right to know the affairs of Zuo Cheng. Soon after, he was awarded the title of Shangshu Zuo Cheng. He came out of Beijing to serve as the internal history of Shixing and died during his tenure. Sima Yun's son Sima Shou inherited his father's studies and was proficient in the "Three Rites". During the Datong period, he served as minister of the ancestral hall of Shangshu and went to Beijing to serve as Qu'aling. Bian Hua, whose courtesy name is Zhaoqiu, was born in Jiyin Yuanju. He is the sixth generation descendant of Zhongzhen Gongtutong, the hussar general of Jin Dynasty. His father was a thrifty man who gave everything he wanted. Bian Hua lost his father when he was young. His family was poor, but he loved to study. When he was fourteen years old, Bian Hua was called to serve as a national scholar and he was proficient in "The Book of Changes". After becoming an adult, Bian Hua studied the Five Classics extensively. He studied together with Pingyuan Mingshanbin and Kuaiji He Qian, and they had a good friendship.
target: Sima Yun, from Hanoi, lost his father young but loved learning, excelling in the Three Rites. He served as Shangshu Temple Minister and debated mourning rites for loving mothers. He died as Shixing Neishi. His son Sima Shou inherited his studies. Bian Hua, from Jiyin, lost his father young but studied the Five Classics, especially the Book of Changes.

He was also appointed as the chief historian of Wuling King, and his post as governor remained unchanged. He died during his tenure. Shen Jun, courtesy name Shisong, was born in Wukang, Wuxing. He studied under Shen Junmu for many years. He assigned himself tasks to study day and night. Sometimes he would doze off and hit himself with a wooden stick. He was so concentrated. After Shen Lin's death, Licai left the capital and traveled to various schools, so he became proficient in the Five Classics, especially the Three Rites.
target: He served as a Five Classics doctor, known for his eloquence and musical expertise. He died as Wuling Prefect.

source: When he was fourteen years old, Bian Hua was called to serve as a national scholar and he was proficient in "The Book of Changes". After becoming an adult, Bian Hua studied the Five Classics extensively. He studied together with Pingyuan Mingshanbin and Kuaiji He Qian, and they had a good friendship. When he first became an official, he was appointed as the minister of the Yuzhang Kingdom of Qi. After his meritorious service, he was promoted to the imperial court and went to the west to join the army. In the early years of Tianjian, Bian Hua moved to Linchuan Wang Gongcao to join the army and served as an assistant to Guozi. He was transferred to Ancheng Wang Gongcao to join the army and was also a doctor of "Five Classics", gathering students to teach Confucian classics. Bian Hua covered a wide range of subjects, was knowledgeable, witty and eloquent. He explained scriptures and analyzed their meanings. He was the leading figure at that time. After the Jin Dynasty moved to Jiangzuo, music rhythm became a unique skill, and it was not until Bian Hua that he became proficient in music rhythm. Bian Long moved to the post of Minister Cao Lang, and left the capital to serve as Wu Ling. He died. Cui Lingen is from Wucheng, Qinghedong. He has been attentive and eager to learn since he was a child. He followed his teacher to learn all the Five Classics, and he was especially proficient in the Three Rites and the Three Legends. Cui Lingen first served as an official in the Northern Dynasties and served as Dr. Taichang. In the thirteenth year of Tianjian, he returned to Liang Dynasty.
target: Cui Lingen, from Qinghe, studied the Five Classics, especially the Three Rites and Three Commentaries. He served as Taichang Doctor in the Northern Dynasties before returning to Liang, where he lectured to hundreds. He authored numerous works on the classics.

source: Zha Ximo established his own point of view and combined the theories of Tantian and Gaitian. Cui Lingen went to Beijing to serve as the internal history of Changsha. When he returned to Beijing, he was awarded the title of Doctor of the State. There were many students who studied with him. He went to Beijing to serve as General Mingwei and Governor Guacong, and died during his tenure. Cui He wrote twenty-two volumes of "Collection of Mao's Poems", forty volumes of "Collection of Zhouli", forty-seven volumes of "Sanli Yi Zong", twenty-two volumes of "Zuo Shi Jing Chuan Yi", ten volumes of "Zuo Shi Regulations", and ten volumes of "Gongyanggu Liang Wen Ju Yi". Kong Qian came in from Shanyin in Kuaiji. When he was young, Wang Yu worshiped He Yin as his teacher. He was proficient in the Five Classics, especially the Three Rites, Xiaozhi and the Analects of Confucius. He expounded and taught these scriptures dozens of times and had hundreds of students. Renxi successively served as an assistant teacher of Guozi, a doctor of "Five Classics" three times, and moved to the post of Shangshu Temple Minister. He left Beijing and served as magistrate of two counties. Kong Qian was a Confucian scholar who only knew the classics and was not good at governing the people. He had no political achievements during his tenure as county magistrate. When turmoil broke out during the Liqian period, Kong Yu died at home. Kong Chuxuan, the son of Kong Qian, focused on studying Confucianism, and his official position was promoted to Doctor of Taixue. Kong Chuxuan, the son of brother Kong Ling, was also proficient in the "Three Rites" and had a great reputation, but he died young. Lu Guang, a native of Fanyang Zhuo, said he was a descendant of Lu Chen, a middle-ranking official in Zhi Sikong.
target: Kong Qian, from Kuaiji, studied under He Yin, excelling in the Five Classics. He served as a Five Classics doctor but was not skilled in governance. He died during the Liqian turmoil. Lu Guang, from Fanyang, was proficient in scriptures and served as a Five Classics doctor, known for his clear pronunciation. He died as Xunyang Prefect.

source: At that time, Confucian scholars from the north, including Cui Lingen, Sun Xiang, Jiang Xian and others, gathered students to teach Confucian classics, but their pronunciation was vulgar and clumsy; only Lu Guang spoke clearly and elegantly, unlike the northerners. Pushe Xu Mian was also proficient in Confucian classics, and he deeply appreciated Lu Guang. Soon after, Lu Guang was appointed as a regular attendant of Yuanwai Sanqi, but his position as a doctor remained unchanged. He also left the capital and served as Xinwu, the successor of Guiyang, Changshi, and the prefect of Xunyang. He was also appointed as the chief historian of Wuling King, and his post as governor remained unchanged. He died during his tenure. Shen Jun, courtesy name Shisong, was born in Wukang, Wuxing. The family has been a farmer for generations, until Yingkong. He loved learning, and he and his uncle Taishi Shuming chose Shen Jun as their teacher from the same clan. He studied under Shen Junmu for many years. He assigned himself tasks to study day and night. Sometimes he would doze off and hit himself with a wooden stick. He was so concentrated. After Shen Lin's death, Licai left the capital and traveled to various schools, so he became proficient in the Five Classics, especially the Three Rites.
target: Shen Jun, from Wuxing, studied the Five Classics, especially the Three Rites. Recommended as a Five Classics doctor, he lectured to hundreds. He died as Wukang Ling.

source: Shen Jun lectures in the school, and there are often hundreds of students attending his lectures. Shen Jun left the capital and served as Huarong Ling. After returning to the capital, he was awarded not only as a member of the Sanqi Shilang, but also as a doctor of "Five Classics". At that time, He Chen, a member of Zhongshushe, was ordered by the emperor to compile "Liang Guan", so he petitioned Shen Jun and Confucius Qubu to serve as bachelors in the Western Province to help him write "Liang Guan". After the book "Liang Guan" was completed, Shen Jun entered the court and served as Zhongshu General. Later he left the capital and served as Wukang Ling, and died during his tenure. Shen Jun's son, Shen Wen'a, inherited his father's studies, and was especially proficient in "The Biography of the Zuo Family". During the Taiqing period, Shen Wen'a was promoted from assistant teacher of Guozi to doctor of "Five Classics". Those who inherited Shen Jun's studies include Zhang Ji of Wujun and Confucius Yun of Kuaiji. Their official positions were promoted to doctor of the Five Classics and minister of the temple. Taishi Shuming was a native of Wucheng, Wuxing. He was a descendant of Wu Taishi Ci.
target: Taishi Shuming, from Wuxing, was proficient in Zhuangzi, Laozi, and the Book of Changes, lecturing to over five hundred. He died at seventy-three. Confucius Qu, from Kuaiji, lost his father young but became proficient in the Guwen Shangshu. He served as a lecturer and helped compile the Liang Guan. He died at fifty-one, authoring works on the Shangshu.

source: After the matter was completed, Gaozu ordered Jie Ziguai, right guard Zhu Yi, and Zuo Cheng He Chen to take turns every day in the Shilin Pavilion to practice scriptures, ask questions, and assess the scholars. Zhizi Qu accumulated merit and was promoted to Tongzhi Zhengyuanlang, but his position remained unchanged. In the first year of Zhongdatong, Confucius died during his tenure at the age of fifty-one. Confucius Qu wrote a total of 20 volumes of "Shang Shu Yi", 30 volumes of "Collected Comments on Shangshu", a 100-volume continuation of Zhu Yi's "Collected Comments on Zhouyi", and a 150-volume continuation of He Chengtian's "Ji Li Lun". Huang Kan, a native of Wu County, is the ninth generation descendant of Huang Xiang, the governor of Qingzhou. Huang Kan loved studying since he was a child. He worshiped He Chang as his teacher and devoted himself to learning from He Chang. As a result, he became proficient in Confucian classics, especially the Three Rites, the Classic of Filial Piety, and the Analects of Confucius. When he first became an official and served as an assistant to Guozi, he gave lectures on classics and meanings in the academy, and hundreds of students attended his lectures.
target: Huang Kan, from Wu County, studied under He Chang, excelling in the Three Rites. He lectured to hundreds and authored the Book of Rites. He died at fifty-eight.

source: After Huang Kan went to King Shaoling, he contracted a heart disease and died in Xia Shou in the eleventh year of Datong at the age of fifty-eight. The ten volumes of "On Meaning" and "Book of Rites" written by Huang Kan were valued by scholars at that time, and some scholars inherited his theories. Yao Cha, the Minister of Chen's Ministry of Civil Affairs, said: In the past, Shusun Tong lectured on Confucian classics on horseback during the war years, and Huan Rong lectured on Confucian classics during the turmoil and hunger.
target: Yao Cha noted that these scholars, despite varying fortunes, contributed to Confucian learning during the Liang Dynasty.

source: Hu Sengyou, whose name is Yuanguo, is a champion in Nanyang. He has been brave and decisive since he was a child, and has the ability to be a soldier. He served as an official in the State of Wei and reached the rank of Yinqing Guanglu. He returned to the capital in the second year of Datong and frequently applied for titles. Emperor Gaozu thought highly of him and awarded him the title of "Fake Festival", "Super Military General" and "Wende Commander", and sent him to guard Xiangcheng. Xiangcheng was captured, and Hu Sengyou fell to Wei again. In the first year of Zhongdatong, Chen Qingzhi sent Wang Yuanhao of Wei Beihai to Luoyang. Hu Sengku was able to return to the capital and was awarded the title of prefect of Nantianshui and Tianmen counties. He left good political achievements wherever he served as an official. Hu Sengku liked reading by nature, but he was not good at writing poems and compositions. However, every time at the court banquet, Hu Sengyou would try his best to compose poems. The poems were vulgar and often ridiculed by others. Hu Sengyou was happy as usual, thinking that his poems were indeed exquisite. Conceit and boasting are even more powerful. Hu Sengyou served Shizu in his later years and served as Zhenxi Lushi to join the army. When Hou Jing rebelled, the Western Jumans also rebelled. Shizu ordered Hu Sengcoff to attack the Western Jumans, and ordered Hu Senghu to kill all the barbarian chiefs and leaders. Hu Sengyou came to remonstrate and was imprisoned for violating Shizu's will. In the second year of Dashi, Hou Jing invaded Jingshan and surrounded Wang Sengbian in Baling. The emperor summoned Hu Sengyou from prison, awarded him the title of General Jiajie and Wumeng, and named him the Marquis of Xinshi County, and ordered him to rush to aid Wang Sengbian. When Hu Sengyou was about to set off, he said to his son: You can open two gates, one gate is to be turned into a red gate, and the other gate is to be turned into a white gate. Good luck will enter the house through the red door, and bad luck will enter the house through the white door. I will not go home unless I win. When Shizu heard Hu Sengyou's words, he felt that he was brave and commendable. Hu Sengku led his army to Yangpu and sent his general Ren Gou to lead 5,000 elite soldiers to guard the fort and wait for Hu Sengyou's army to fight from a distance. Hu Sengyou advanced westward by another road. Ren Yue thought that they were retreating because they were afraid of him, so he led his army to pursue them in a hurry. They caught up with Hu Sengku at Qiankou, Nan'an. Ren Yue called to Hu Sengyou and said: "Wu'er, why don't you surrender early?" Where to escape to? Hu Sengyou ignored his answer and secretly led his army to retreat. When they arrived at Chisha Pavilion, Lu Fahe and his army arrived. Hu Sengyou and Lu Fahe attacked Ren Yue together with the two armies, defeated Ren Yue's army, captured Ren Yue alive and sent him to Jiangling. Hou Jing led his army to escape after hearing the news that Ren Yue had been captured. Shizu appointed Hu Sengyou as a minister and general, and recruited him back to Jingzhou. In the second year of Chengsheng's reign, Hu Senyou was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry and Kaifu Yitong Third Division, while all other positions remained unchanged. When the enemies of the Western Wei Dynasty invaded, Hu Sengyou was appointed as the governor of the city to supervise all military affairs. The Wei army launched attacks from all sides, with many units attacking at the same time. Hu Sengyou personally braved the rock with arrows, supervised the battle day and night, rewarded the soldiers, and strictly rewarded and punished them. The soldiers were moved by him and were willing to fight to the death for him. Wherever Hu Sengyou went, Naxiang's enemies were destroyed, and no enemy dared to attack again. Soon Hu Sengyou was shot by a stray arrow and died at the age of sixty-three. When Shizu heard the news, he rushed to the east of the city to mourn.
target: The lives and military careers of several figures from the Liang Dynasty. Hu Sengyou, a brave champion from Nanyang, served Wei and later returned to Liang, where he was appointed to guard Xiangcheng. After its capture, he returned to Wei but eventually came back to Liang, serving as a prefect with good governance. Despite his poor poetry, he remained confident. He was imprisoned for remonstrating against killing barbarian chiefs but was later released to aid Wang Sengbian against Hou Jing. He defeated Ren Yue, captured him, and caused Hou Jing to flee. He died at 63 from a stray arrow while defending against Wei, leading to the city's fall.

source: Du Chong was Wang Sengbian's son-in-law and served as the prefect of Wuxing. He believed that Chen Baxian was not from a noble family, and his soldiers were disorganized. When handling military affairs, he did not take Chen Baxian into consideration at all. When managing the affairs of the county, he always dealt with Chen Baxian's fellow clan members according to law and discipline without mercy. Chen Baxian hated this and gritted his teeth. After Wang Sengbian was killed, Du Chong defended Wuxing to resist Chen Baxian, and sent his deputy Du Tai to the Great Wall to attack Chen Bei. Du Tai was defeated by Chen Hao. Chen Baxian then sent his general Zhou Wenyu to attack Du Chong. Du Chong ordered his cousin Du Beisou to fight, but was defeated by Zhou Wenyu. He then fled to Yixing, and Chen Baxian personally led an army to surround them. When Qi general Liu Damo and others attacked the capital, Chen Ba was frightened and returned to the capital to make peace with the Qi people. Du Chong surrendered after hearing that the Qi army had returned to the country, and was killed. Yin Zichun, whose courtesy name is Youwen, was born in Guzang, Wuwei. In the last years of Jin Yixi, Yin Zichun's great-grandfather Yin attacked and moved south with Song Gaozu to Nanping, where he settled down. Yin Zichun's father, Yin Zhibo, lived next to Gaozu, and the two had been very friendly since childhood. Yin Zhibo once entered Gaozu's bedroom and saw the strange brilliance of five colors in the room. He took Gaozu's hand and said: You will be very noble in the future, no longer a minister. The world is in turmoil, and the one who can calm the people is probably you! Emperor Gaozu said: I hope you won’t say too much. As a result, the friendship between the two became more and more profound. Whenever Gaozu needed something, he would get it from Yin Zhibo's place, just like getting it from a warehouse outside his home. After Emperor Gaozu ascended the throne, Yin Zhibo was promoted to governor of Liang and Qin states. Zichun, in the early years of Tianjian, Yin Zichun was recruited from his family to serve as General Xuanhui and Prefect of Xiyang. During ordinary years, Yin Zichun was promoted to General Mingwei and the governor of Nanliang Prefecture many times. He was also promoted to General Xinwei, governor of the military affairs of the three prefectures of Chitaigui, and governor of Liang and Qin Prefectures. In the second year of Taiqing, Yin Zichun conquered the rebellious barbarians and put down the rebellion. He was conscripted as the general of the left guard and moved to the rank of servant. At the time of Hou Jing's rebellion, Shizu ordered Yin Zichun to follow the leading general Wang Sengbian to Yingzhou to conquer King Shaoling and pacify Yingzhou. He also marched eastward with Xu Wensheng, the general of the left guard, to conquer Hou Jing. When they arrived at Beji, they met Hou Jing. Yin Zichun fought hard, often ranking first among the troops in military exploits, and defeated Hou Jing many times.
target: Xu Wensheng, from Pengcheng, led his father's troops to surrender to Liang and became a governor of Ningzhou, where he reformed corrupt barbarian customs. During Hou Jing's rebellion, he was sent eastward but hesitated to fight, influenced by his wife's return from Hou Jing. His army was defeated after Yingzhou's capture, and he fled to Jingzhou. He was imprisoned for corruption and resentment, dying in prison after a taunt from Ren Yue.

source: At the time when the king of Genbian District under Qinzhou rebelled, Si Huaiyi led his army to defeat Sanmi. In the fifth year of Taitong, Du Huaishi died at the place where he served. Du Ze is Du Huaishi's seventh son. He has been ambitious since he was a child and is known in his hometown for his courage and bravery. When he first became an official, he was appointed as a soldier in Lujiang Huqi Prefecture and joined the army. When Shizu was in charge of Jingzhou, Du Zhu still joined the army for the shogunate and later served as the governor of Qixing. In the second year of Taiqing, Du Tuan followed King Yueyang to invade Jingzhou. Because of his long-standing friendship with Du Ze, Shizu secretly invited Du Qi to join him. Du Tuan, his elder brother Du An, his younger brother You'an You'an, his elder brother's son Zhuan Xin and others returned to Shisu at night. Shizu conferred the title of Silk Witch as Chijie, General Xinwei, and the governor of Wuzhou. Soon he was promoted to General Xuanyi, leading the Zhenman Guards and the internal history of Wuling. He was granted the title of Marquis of Zhijiang County and was granted the title of a thousand households in the town. Shizu ordered Du Ze to follow Wang Sengbian and march eastward to conquer Hou Jing. When he led his army to Baling, he was met by Hou Jing who came to attack. Hou Jing attacked for ten days and ran away after failing to win. Du Xun was promoted to Shizhong and Zuowei General, his title was promoted to Duke, and he was granted an additional 500 households. Du Xun continued to follow Wang Sengbian in pursuit of Hou Jing until he reached Shitou, where he held a stalemate with the rebels at Jinling. When the two sides fought, Hou Jing personally led the elite soldiers, charging left and right. Du Juan rushed out from behind the ridge, intercepted and killed Hou Jing's army. Hou Jing was defeated and fled east to Jinling, while Du occupied Stone City. After Hou Jing's rebellion was put down, Du Yajia added Sanqi Changshi, Zhijie, supervised the military in Jiangzhou, and the governor of Jiangzhou, adding thousands of households to the city. This month, Qi general Guo Yuanjian attacked Qinzhou governor Yan Chaoyuan in Qin County. Wang Sengbian ordered Du Juan to rush to the rescue, and Chen Ba also led his army from Kamu to join Si Ouyanghe. They fought against Shilin in Yuanjian. Chen Baxian ordered a volley of powerful crossbows, and Yuan Jian's army retreated. Du Juan took the opportunity to attack and defeated Guo Yuanjian's army, killing more than 10,000 people and capturing more than a thousand alive. Jian gathered up the remaining soldiers and fled.
target: Du Chan, from Duling, was the seventh son of Du Huaibao. He joined Shizu and followed Wang Sengbian against Hou Jing, defeating him at Baling and Shitou. He later fought Qi general Guo Yuanjian and suppressed rebellions in Changsha and against King Wuling. He died of illness.

source: Du An then traveled day and night to attack Xiangyang City first. Before it was conquered, King Yueyang arrived, and Yueyang fled to rely on his brother Du Guo, who was the governor of Nanyang at the time. Yueyang soon sent troops to capture the city, and Du An and his brother Du Xie were killed together. Du Youan was the most filial by nature, generous to others, and extremely brave. During the reign of Zuo Zha, Du You'an and his brother Du Guan joined Shizu. Shizu granted him the title of General Yunhui, governor of West Jingzhou, and the title of Marquis of Huarong County, with a settlement of 1,000 households. Shizu ordered him to go to Changsha with Pingnan General Wang Sengbian to conquer Hedong Wang Yu and quell the rebellion. Shi Piao also ordered Du Youan to lead 10,000 elite troops to assist Zuowei General Xu Wensheng in marching eastward to conquer Hou Jing. When they arrived at Beji, they met Ren Yueyue, the general waiting for Jing, to fight against him. He fought with Ren Diao and was defeated. He killed the puppet official Yi Tongchi Luo Zitong, the Xiangzhou governor Zhao Weifang and others, and sent their heads to Jiangling. So he marched until he went there and held a stalemate with Hou Jing. In addition, he sent people to attack Wuchang and pull it out. Hou Jing crossed Liao from the upper reaches of Luzhou to attack Xu Wensheng and others. You'an and other troops attacked Hou Jing. Hou Jing was defeated and all the ships were captured. At that time, Hou Jing secretly sent troops to attack and capture Jianye, and captured Lu Zuozhan, the governor of Jianye, and others and brought them back. Xu Wensheng and the army were frightened and panicked. Xu Wensheng fled back from Hankou. All the troops were defeated. Du You'an surrendered to Hou Jing. Hou Jing killed Du You'an because of his erratic behavior. Du Gong is the son of Du Cen, Du Gong's second brother. He was very strong and brave when he was young, and was good at using soldiers. During the Taiqing period, he and his uncles joined Shizu. Shizu awarded him the title of Chijie, Zhongwu General, Yunzhou Governor, and the title of Marquis of Zhonglu County, with a settlement of 1,000 households. His uncle Du Youan followed Wang Zengluan to conquer the King of Return to Tomb and put down the rebellion. He followed Wang Sengbian down the river and arrived at Baling after Xu Wensheng's army. Hearing that Hou Jing had attacked and captured Yingzhou, he was heading up the river and marching westward. When he was about to reach Baling, Du Chong, Wang Sengbian and others defended Baling and waited for Hou Jing to attack. Hou Jing went to Baling and besieged it for dozens of days, but could not conquer it and then escaped. Du Chong moved to the post of Taifu Qing, General Anbei, supervising the military affairs of Dingzhou, and governor of Dingzhou. He was also granted the title of Tongzhi Sanqi Changshi, and added 500 households in the city. Du Fu continued to follow Wang Sengbian in pursuit of Hou Jing as far as Jiangxia, and besieged the city of Jiangxia. Hou Jing's general Song Zixian abandoned the city and fled. Du Chong pursued him to Yangpu and captured Song Zixian alive. In the third year of Dashi, various armies arrived at Gushu. Hou Jing's general Hou Zijian fought against him. Du Chong, Chen Baxian, Wang Lin and others led the elite soldiers to attack and defeated Hou Zijian, so the army arrived at Shitou.
target: His brothers Du An and Du Youan also served, with Du An killed attacking Xiangyang and Du Youan surrendering to and killed by Hou Jing. Du Chong, Du Chan's nephew, was a brave general who defeated Hou Jing's forces, captured Song Zixian, and later resisted Chen Baxian after Wang Sengbian's death, ultimately surrendering and being killed.

source: Yin Zichun, whose courtesy name is Youwen, was born in Guzang, Wuwei. In the last years of Jin Yixi, Yin Zichun's great-grandfather Yin attacked and moved south with Song Gaozu to Nanping, where he settled down. Yin Zichun's father, Yin Zhibo, lived next to Gaozu, and the two had been very friendly since childhood. Yin Zhibo once entered Gaozu's bedroom and saw the strange brilliance of five colors in the room. He took Gaozu's hand and said: You will be very noble in the future, no longer a minister. The world is in turmoil, and the one who can calm the people is probably you! Emperor Gaozu said: I hope you won’t say too much. As a result, the friendship between the two became more and more profound. Whenever Gaozu needed something, he would get it from Yin Zhibo's place, just like getting it from a warehouse outside his home. After Emperor Gaozu ascended the throne, Yin Zhibo was promoted to governor of Liang and Qin states. Zichun, in the early years of Tianjian, Yin Zichun was recruited from his family to serve as General Xuanhui and Prefect of Xiyang. During ordinary years, Yin Zichun was promoted to General Mingwei and the governor of Nanliang Prefecture many times. He was also promoted to General Xinwei, governor of the military affairs of the three prefectures of Chitaigui, and governor of Liang and Qin Prefectures. In the second year of Taiqing, Yin Zichun conquered the rebellious barbarians and put down the rebellion. He was conscripted as the general of the left guard and moved to the rank of servant. At the time of Hou Jing's rebellion, Shizu ordered Yin Zichun to follow the leading general Wang Sengbian to Yingzhou to conquer King Shaoling and pacify Yingzhou. He also marched eastward with Xu Wensheng, the general of the left guard, to conquer Hou Jing. When they arrived at Beji, they met Hou Jing. Yin Zichun fought hard, often ranking first among the troops in military exploits, and defeated Hou Jing many times. Just as Yingzhou was captured, the army retreated. In the second year of Dashi, Yin Zichun died in Jiangling. Sun Hao has been famous since he was a child. When he first became an official, he was invited by the court to serve as Shangshu Jinbulang. Yinhao later attached himself to Zhou. He wrote twenty volumes of "Qiong Lin". Shi Chen said: Hu Sengyou has long been famous for his military talents. He pulled down the enemy's flag and broke the enemy's formation, and made many military exploits. He even sacrificed his life to maintain his integrity and died in the king's affairs. Even among the loyal and martyrs in ancient times, there is no one who can surpass him. Xu Wensheng made great achievements initially, but was unable to maintain his existing reputation in the end. This is unjust. Du Xun understood the principle of change and the appropriate choice of direction. In addition, he was in charge of the army many times, frequently annihilated rebellions, and made outstanding achievements. In the end, he became the hero of the Liang Dynasty's resurgence. He was really moral!
target: Yin Zichun, from Guzang, served as a general and prefect, suppressing barbarian rebellions. He fought with Wang Sengbian and Xu Wensheng against Hou Jing, achieving many victories, but died in Jiangling after the army retreated. The text concludes with a commentary praising Hu Sengyou's loyalty, criticizing Xu Wensheng's failure, and lauding Du Chan's moral choices and achievements.

source: Queen Taizong gave birth to Prince Xiao Daqi, Prince of Nanjun, Xiao Dalian; Chen Shurong gave birth to Prince Xiao Daxin of Xunyang; Mrs. Zuo gave birth to Prince Xiao Dalin of Nanhai, and Prince Xiao Dachun of Anlu; Mrs. Xie gave birth to Duke Xiao Daya of Liuyang; Mrs. Zhang They gave birth to Xiao Dazhuang, the king of Xinxing; Xiao Dajun, the king of Xiyang, was born to Bao Zhaohua; Xiao Dawei, the king of Wuning, was born to Mrs. Fan; Xiao Daqiu, the king of Jianping, was born to Chu Xiuhua; Xiao Daxin, the king of Yi'an, was born to Mrs. Chen; Xiao Dazhi, the king of Suijian, was born to Mrs. Zhu. The deeds of the other sons are not recorded in this book. Xiao Daxin, king of Xunyang, was named Renshu. He has been smart and enlightened since childhood and is good at writing articles. In the fourth year of Zhongdatong, he was granted the title of Dangyang Gong because of his status as the emperor's grandson, and was granted a residence of 1,500 households. In the first year of Datong, he went to Beijing to serve as envoy Chijie, governor of Ying's southern and northern divisions, Dingxin's military forces of the five states, general of light vehicles, and governor of Yingzhou.
target: This historical text records the lineage and fates of the sons of Emperor Taizong and Shizu during a period of rebellion. Queen Taizong bore Prince Xiao Daqi and Xiao Dalian; other consorts and ladies bore numerous other princes, including Xiao Daxin, Xiao Dalin, Xiao Dachun, Xiao Daya, Xiao Dazhuang, Xiao Dajun, Xiao Dawei, Xiao Daqiu, Xiao Daxin, and Xiao Dazhi. The deeds of some sons are not recorded.

source: In the autumn of the second year of Dashi, Xiao Daxin was killed at the age of twenty-five. Xiao Dalin, king of Nanhai, was named Renxuan. In the second year of Datong, he was granted the title of Duke of Ningguo County, with a settlement of 1,500 households. Xiao Dalin has been smart and smart since he was a child. When he was eleven years old, his biological mother, Mrs. Zuo, passed away. He cried every day, which made him weak and thin, so he was famous for his filial piety. Later, Xiao Dalin entered Chinese studies, ranked first in the Ming Dynasty's archery examination, was awarded the title of Minister of Zhongshu, and was transferred to Minister of Huangmen. In the eleventh year of Datong, he was appointed as the chief and also as the minister.
target: Xiao Daxin, King of Xunyang, was intelligent and a skilled writer. Ennobled as a duke at age thirteen, he was appointed to military and gubernatorial posts. Despite his youth, his opinions were wise.

source: At that time, Poyang King Xiao Fan led his army to abandon Hefei and stationed at Zhakou, hoping to wait until all the reinforcements gathered before marching together. When Xiao Daxin heard the news, he sent someone to invite Xiao Fan to go up the river and march westward, and gave Xiao Fan the city to garrison. The food supplies were very generous, and the two of them worked together to put an end to the chaos. When Zhuang Tie occupied Yuzhang and rebelled, Xiao Daxin ordered his soldiers to join the army. Attract and recruit literary people, never tire of appreciating and receiving them, often discuss books, and then write articles. However, the injury was minor and it was called "uterine body" at that time. He wrote five volumes of "The Biography of Prince Zhaoming", thirty volumes of "The Biography of the Kings", twenty volumes of "Li Dayi", twenty volumes of "Laozi Yi", twenty volumes of "Zhuangzi Yi", one hundred volumes of "Changchun Yiji", and three hundred volumes of "Magic Treasure Lianbi". Shi Chen said: Taizong was smart and wise when he was young. His beautiful knowledge has been spread for a long time. His talents are beyond the past and present. Because the article was influenced by the frivolous and flashy writing style of the time, it was not appreciated by gentlemen. When Taizong cultivated his morality in the Eastern Dynasty and his reputation spread throughout the country, and when he succeeded to the throne, he truly possessed the virtues of a human king. Just when Taizong was governing the country like Emperors Wen and Jing, his fate was unlucky as shown in "Tuen" and "Pi". He was controlled by traitors and could not display his talents. source: The captured weapons were destroyed and made into bells, indicating that they would no longer be used. The common people were spared the pain of the turmoil of the Warring States Period, and everyone thought that they had met the wise emperor and gained a new life. If the Qin Dynasty had leniently suspended punishments, lightened taxes and levies, eliminated corvees, valued benevolence and righteousness, despised power, advocated loyalty, despised sycophancy, changed customs, and promoted enlightenment at home, then the Qin Dynasty would have had peace from generation to generation. The Qin Dynasty did not advocate the promotion of such social customs, but continued its old customs. Those who played with cleverness and power were promoted, and those who were honest, loyal, and upright were dismissed. The laws were harsh, the decrees were harsh, and there were many flatterers. The emperor listened to their sweet words and praises every day, and he was full of ambitions and fantasies. Wanting to show off his power overseas, he sent Meng Tian to lead troops to attack the Xiongnu in the north, expand the territory, and guard Beihe. He ordered the people to quickly transport grain and fodder to follow the army. He also sent the commander-in-chief Tu Sui to lead the soldiers of the building boats to attack Baiyue, and sent the censor Lu Shilu to dig the Ling Canal to transport grain, and went deeper into the country, and more people fled. The war lasted for a long time and the food supply was insufficient. The Yue people launched an attack and the Qin army was defeated. The Qin Dynasty then sent Wei Tuo to lead troops to garrison the territory of Yue. At that time, the Qin Dynasty's troubles were that the north was resentful of the Xiongnu and the south was enmity with the Yue people. The troops were stationed in useless places and could not retreat when they advanced. More than ten years passed like this, with the male serving as a soldier and the female transporting. They were miserable and hanged themselves on a tree by the roadside, looking at each other. When Qin Shihuang died, the world was in rebellion. Chen Sheng and Wu Guang captured Chen, Wu Chen and Zhang Er captured Zhao, Xiang Liang defeated Wu, Tian Dan captured Qi, Jing Ju went to Ying, Zhou Shi fell to Wei, Han Guang raised Yan, and the mountains were full of heroes, which is unforgettable. However, these people are not the descendants of princes, nor are they local governors. They have no power at all. They started in Yanxiang, holding the handles of spears and halberds. They followed the trend of the times, started troubles at the right time, gathered together by chance, attacked cities and plundered lands, and finally became kings. This was the result of the education at that time. The emperor of the Qin Dynasty was regarded as the Son of Heaven, rich in the world, and his lineage was exterminated and sacrifices were cut off. This was a disaster caused by military violence. Therefore, the fault of the Zhou Dynasty was that it was weak, and the fault of the Qin Dynasty was that it was strong. Both of them were unable to adapt to the times, which led to the disaster of national destruction. Now the Han court wants to appease the Nanyi, send Yelang to come to the court, surrender Qiang Fen and Lingzhou, and build cities there. It also wants to penetrate deeply into the Xiongnu and burn their dragon city. The discussants praise these plans. This is the selfish desire of ministers and is not a long-term strategy for governing the world. Now China doesn't even have a dog barking alarm, but it is implicated in foreign defenses, causing the country to wither and decline. This is not the way to nurture the people.
target: Yan An, from Linmiao, wrote a letter as the late Prime Minister Shi, criticizing the extravagance of the wealthy, who decorated their carriages, clothes, and palaces excessively, leading to social ills like greed, lawlessness, and moral decay. He argued that luxury without restraint causes dissatisfaction, drives people from their proper occupations, and fosters treachery and violence. Yan An proposed laws to curb extravagance, reduce envy, and promote harmony, which would lead to peace, reduced crime, and natural prosperity. He contrasted the Zhou Dynasty's long rule with its decline due to weak leadership, leading to the Warring States period and the rise of the Five Hegemons, who upheld the emperor's authority. The Qin Dynasty, under Emperor Qin Shi Huang, unified China but failed to reform its harsh laws and heavy taxes, instead expanding aggressively against the Xiongnu and Baiyue, causing widespread suffering and rebellion. Yan An warned the Han court against similar overreach, advocating for domestic stability over foreign conquests, and noted that the Zhou's weakness and Qin's strength both led to their downfalls due to inflexibility.

source: Once upon a time, when King Wu of Zhou was on his way to the middle of the Yellow River during his expedition against the Shang Dynasty, a white fish jumped into the boat that King Wu of Zhou was riding in. King Wu leaned over to pick it up and grilled it over a fire. Everyone said, "What auspiciousness!" Nowadays, when people offer sacrifices to heaven and earth in the countryside, they do not see the gods of heaven and earth, but they get strange beasts to sacrifice. This is the sky using it to show that they have enjoyed the sacrifice, and it is consistent with the auspiciousness of sincerity and sincerity. We should choose an auspicious time, change the year name, weave mats, put white cogon grass on them, float them on the Yangtze River and Huaihe River, and climb Mount Tai to seal them, so as to harmonize the light and make it recordable by historians. The six parrots flying back symbolize the rebellion of the princes; the white fish boarding the boat symbolizes the submission of the princes to King Wu. Signs of light and darkness confuse the birds in the sky, stir up the fish underwater, and so on. Now the white unicorn has a single horn on its head, indicating that it has the same origin; the branches of the strange tree are attached inside, indicating that it has no outward orientation. When this phenomenon comes to fruition, the surrounding ethnic minorities will probably untie their hair, abandon their left-front clothing, wear hats and belts, and wear Han clothes to accept the enlightenment of the Central Plains. These are just waiting for their arrival! The countermeasures were presented to Emperor Wu. Emperor Wu thought it was unusual, so he changed the reign name to Yuanshou. A few months later, famous kings from Yue and the Huns came to surrender to the Han Dynasty with their troops. At that time, people thought that Zhongjun's words were right. During the Yuanding period, Dr. Xu Yan was sent as an envoy to inspect the customs and education of the county. Xu Yan pretended to act under the orders of the imperial court and asked Jiaodong and Lu to cast iron and dry it with salt. After returning to Beijing, he reported what he had done and was transferred to Taichang Cheng. Zhang Tang, the imperial censor, impeached Xu Yan for acting under the pretense of imperial orders, which was a great harm to the country and should be executed according to the law. Xu Yan believed that according to the meaning of "Spring and Autumn", when officials go out of their borders and encounter matters that can stabilize the country and comfort the people, they can handle it arbitrarily. Zhang Tang could only judge Xu Yan's crime according to the law, but could not refute the meaning of "Spring and Autumn" he used to defend himself. Emperor Wu ordered Zhongjun to interrogate the case. Zhongjun interrogated Xu Yan and said: In ancient vassal states, the customs of different countries were different, and they could not communicate with each other within a hundred miles. There were often appointments and alliances between the court, and the situation of stability or danger would change in a breath. Therefore, there was talk of acting arbitrarily without asking for instructions and pretending to be ordered by the court. Now that the world is unified, the customs are the same within thousands of miles, so the "Spring and Autumn Annals" said There is nothing like a king.
target: Zhongjun, from Jinan, was a talented scholar who became Emperor Wu's envoy. He wrote a response to Emperor Wu's discovery of a white unicorn and a strange tree, interpreting them as auspicious signs of the Han dynasty's virtue and the submission of foreign peoples. He advised the emperor to perform sacrifices and change the reign name, which Emperor Wu did, renaming it Yuanshou. Later, Zhongjun interrogated Dr. Xu Yan for falsely claiming imperial orders to operate salt and iron in Jiaodong and Lu, exposing his deceit and securing his conviction. Emperor Wu praised Zhongjun's handling of the case. Zhongjun also volunteered to envoy to the Xiongnu and South Vietnam, famously requesting a "long tassel" to bind the King of South Vietnam. He successfully persuaded the king to submit to Han rule, but was killed by the South Vietnamese prime minister Lu Jia during a rebellion.

target: Jia Ganzhi, great-grandson of Jia Yi, advised Emperor Yuan against attacking Zhuli County (in modern Hainan), which had repeatedly rebelled since its establishment. He argued that the territory was not worth the cost, citing historical precedents like Yao, Shun, and the Zhou Dynasty, which did not forcibly conquer distant lands. He contrasted Emperor Wen's frugality and peace with Emperor Wu's costly expansions, which led to widespread suffering and rebellion. Emperor Yuan accepted his advice and abandoned Zhuli County. Later, Jia Ganzhi and Yang Xing, a favored official, conspired to recommend each other for high positions, but Shi Xian reported their scheme. They were tried for deceit and leaking palace secrets; Jia Ganzhi was executed, and Yang Xing was reduced to penal servitude.

target: He Wu, styled Jungong, was from Pixian County, Shu County. The Queen Mother apologized for him, but the Emperor couldn't bear to kill him because of the Queen Mother, so he demoted Wang Yi and appointed him as the captain of the Xihe vassal state, reducing the number of thousands of households. Later, Shao ordered to recommend Dachang. Wang Mang privately encouraged He Wu to ask for the recommendation, but He Wu did not dare to recommend him. A few months later, Emperor Ai died. The Queen Mother summoned Wang Mang to the palace that day, took back the seal and ribbon of Dong Xian, the Grand Sima, and ordered Yousi to recommend someone who could be the Grand Sima. Wang Mang turned out to be a Sima, but he resigned from his official post because he avoided Ding and Fu. People praised him as a virtuous man and he was also a close relative of the Queen Mother. All the officials from Bai Da Situ Kong Guang on down recommended Wang Mang. He Wu was a former general who had a good relationship with Gongsun Lu, the left general. The two planned alone, believing that when the two young emperors Xiaohui and Xiaozhao were in power, their relatives Lu, Huo and Shangguan controlled the power and almost endangered the country. Now that Xiaocheng and Xiaoai have no heirs for two consecutive generations, people should be selected to appoint close people to assist the young emperor. Ministers with different surnames should not be allowed to control the power. People who are close and distant are mixed together to facilitate the country's planning. Therefore, He Wu recommended Gongsun Lu to be the Great Sima, and Gongsun Lu also recommended He Wu. The Queen Mother finally appointed Wang Mang as Grand Sima on her own initiative. Wang Mang hinted that there was a petition to impeach He Wu and Gongsun Lu, who praised each other and recommended each other, and both of them were dismissed from office. After He Wu returned to the feudal country, Wang Mang's power gradually became stronger and he became the prime minister, secretly killing those who did not depend on him. In the third year of Yuanshi, Lu Kuan and other things happened. At that time, Grand Sikong Zhenfeng accepted Wang Mang's secret order and sent envoys to clean up and punish his comrades, which implicated many people Wang Mang wanted to kill, including Shangdang Bao Xuan, Nanyang Peng Wei, Du Gongzi, and hundreds of heroes from the county and country were convicted and died. He Wu was also framed. Dali was recruiting He Wu with a carriage, but He Wu committed suicide. Many people thought that He Wu was unjustly accused. Wang Mang wanted to satisfy the public opinion and made He Wu's son Gu Ji the successor as a marquis and Mi He Wu as a marquis. Wang Mang usurped the throne and was deposed, let alone a commoner. Wang Jia, whose courtesy name was Gongzhong, was from Huling. He passed the Ming Jing She Ce Jia Ke examination and became a doctor. He was convicted and dismissed because he did not stop people who should not enter when he was guarding the palace gate.
target: When Emperor Ai died, the Queen Mother appointed Wang Mang as Grand Sima. He Wu and Gongsun Lu, fearing relatives' control, recommended each other, but the Queen Mother chose Wang Mang. Wang Mang had them dismissed for mutual recommendation. As Wang Mang's power grew, He Wu was framed and committed suicide. Many thought him wronged, so Wang Mang made his son a marquis, but the title was later abolished. Wang Jia, styled Gongzhong, from Huling, passed examinations and became a doctor, but was dismissed for a gate duty error.

He was convicted and dismissed because he did not stop people who should not enter when he was guarding the palace gate. Guang Luxun appointed him as a subordinate official in Yuyong. He was promoted to Nanling County magistrate because of his integrity, and Changling County captain because of his integrity. During the Hongjia period, Wang Jia was summoned to the Propaganda Office to answer questions about the pros and cons of political affairs, and was promoted to the rank of Taizhong doctor. He left the capital and served as the governor of Jiujiang and Henan, and was very famous for his governance. He was recruited to Beijing as Da Honglu, transferred to Jing Zhaoyin, and promoted to the imperial censor. In the third year of Jianping's reign, he replaced Ping as prime minister, was granted the title of Xinfu Marquis, and was granted an additional 1,100 households in the city. Wang Jia was upright, resolute and prestigious, and the emperor respected him very much. Emperor Ai had just ascended the throne and wanted to rectify the political affairs of Emperor Cheng, but there were many changes. Wang Jiashang said: I heard that the merit of a wise king lies in acquiring talented people. Confucius said: Talents are rare, isn't it? Therefore, those who succeed the previous generation and establish themselves as princes only need to be as virtuous as their ancestors. Even if they cannot all be capable, the emperor can select ministers for them and appoint ministers to assist them. According to this feudal state, the scholars of all ages respected the scholars and valued the virtuous, and then the scholars and the people would submit to him. Therefore, the merits of education and rule were established. Nowadays, the status of the governor is more important than that of the ancient princes. In the past, it was difficult to recruit and select talented people. Talents were difficult to find. Some of the people who could be selected and promoted were selected from prisoners. In the past, Wei Shang was convicted and imprisoned. Emperor Wen was moved by Feng Tang's words and sent an envoy with a talisman to pardon his crime and appointed him as the prefect of Yunzhong. The Huns were afraid of him. Emperor Wu promoted Han Anguo from among those who had been sentenced to hard labor and appointed him as Liang's internal history, so that his flesh and blood could live in peace.
target: He later served as Nanling county magistrate and Changling county captain. During the Hongjia period, he was promoted to Taizhong doctor, then governor of Jiujiang and Henan, gaining fame. He became Da Honglu, Jing Zhaoyin, and imperial censor, then prime minister and Marquis of Xinfu. Wang Jia was upright and prestigious. He advised Emperor Ai to carefully select talents, forgive minor faults, and encourage officials, citing historical examples like Wei Shang and Han Anguo. He recommended Confucian scholars and talented officials, all of whom became famous.

source: Wang Jia then dressed up and went out. When he saw the envoy, he bowed twice and accepted the imperial edict. He took a soldier's car with the cover off and followed the envoy to pay homage to the imperial officer. The Tingwei took back the seal and ribbon of Wang Jia's prime minister Xinfuhou, bound Wang Jia and drove him to Duchuan Shao Prison in a car. The emperor was furious when he heard that Wang Jia was still alive and had met with the officials. He sent officials below the general level and five officials with two thousand stones to jointly deal with it. The jailer questioned Wang Jia, and Wang Jia replied: Those who investigate prison cases hope to get the facts. I have seen privately that Liang Xiang and others handled Prince Ping's case in the past. I don't think Liu Yun deserves to die. I just need to be cautious in matters involving ministers. The preparation of post horses to transport prisoners must not exceed the winter months. There is indeed no evidence that they watched Afu Liu Yun inside and outside. Fortunately, I was able to receive amnesty. Liang and others are gentle and kind officials. I selfishly cherish talented people for the country, and I am not partial to these three people. The jailer said: If that's the case, why do you think the charges are still fair? He must have failed the country and not be imprisoned without guilt. The jailer slightly offended Wang Jia. Wang Jia looked up to the sky and sighed: "I am lucky enough to serve as prime minister. I cannot promote the talented and reject the stupid. Therefore, I have failed the country and will die with more responsibility." The jailer asked the names of the virtuous and unworthy people, and Wang Jia said: The virtuous ones are Prime Minister Kong Guang and Sikong Hewu, and they cannot be promoted; the evil ones are Gao'an Marquis Dong Xian and his son, who are flattering and evil and disturb the court, but they cannot be removed. My crime deserves death, and I will die without any resentment. Wang Jia was detained in prison for more than 20 days. He refused to eat and vomited blood and died. The emperor's uncle, the Grand Sima Hussar General Ding Ming, always valued Wang Jia and sympathized with him. The emperor then dismissed Ding Ming and replaced him with Dong Xian. This incident is recorded in "The Biography of Dong Xian". Wang Jia was executed as prime minister for three years and his country was deprived of his title. After his death, the emperor read his reply and thought about his words. He replaced Wang Jia with Kong Guang as prime minister, and recruited He Wu as the imperial censor. In the fourth year of the Yuan Dynasty, an edict was issued to pursue the loyal ministers. Wang Chong, Wang Jia's son, was granted the title of Xinfu Marquis, and Wang Jia of Mi was granted the title of Zhonghou. Shidan's courtesy name was Zhonggong, and he was a native of Langye Dongwu. He studied the Book of Songs and took Kuang Heng as his teacher. Because of his filial piety and honesty, he became a man. In the last years of Emperor Yuan's reign, he became a doctor and was later dismissed. During the first year of the founding of the People's Republic of China, the prefecture recommended Maocai, who was also appointed as a doctor and appointed as the Taifu of King Shuping. Prime Minister Fang Jin and imperial censor Kong Guang recommended Shi Dan to be profound in discussion, honest and upright, and recruited him to Beijing to serve as Dr. Guanglu and Prime Minister Sizhi. A few months later, he became a doctor of Guanglu and served in Shizhong. From then on, he was appointed Shaofu, Guangluxun and Shizhong, and he was very respected. In the last years of Emperor Cheng's reign, he appointed King Dingtao as the Crown Prince and Shi Dan as the Crown Prince and Tutor. When Emperor Ai ascended the throne, Shi Dan was appointed General Zuo, and was given the title of Marquis of Guannei, a food town, and the office of Minister. He then replaced Wang Mang as the Grand Sima and was granted the title of Marquis of Gaole. More than a month later, he was promoted to Da Sikong.
target: When Dong Xian was favored, Wang Jia opposed granting him a title without proper discussion, warning against losing public trust. The emperor initially relented but later granted the title, reprimanding Wang Jia. Wang Jia continued to admonish, criticizing Dong Xian's extravagance and the emperor's favoritism, which harmed the state. He urged restraint, citing past examples like Emperor Xiaowen's frugality. The emperor grew displeased but doted on Dong Xian more. Wang Jia also recommended Liang Xiang and others, but the emperor, angered by Wang Jia's defense of them, had him questioned. Wang Jia was impeached for confusing the country and died in prison after refusing food. After his death, the emperor regretted it and later honored him. Shi Dan, styled Zhonggong, from Langye, studied the *Book of Songs* under Kuang Heng. He became a doctor, then Taifu of King Shuping. Recommended by Fang Jin and Kong Guang, he served as Dr. Guanglu and Prime Minister Sizhi, later becoming Shaofu, Guangluxun, and tutor to the crown prince. When Emperor Ai ascended, Shi Dan became Grand Sima and Marquis of Gaole, then Grand Sikong.

source: When Emperor Ai came to the throne, Emperor Cheng's mother was honored as the Empress Dowager, and Empress Cheng was honored as the Empress Dowager. The emperor's grandmother, Empress Dowager Fu, and mother, Empress Ding, both stayed in their residence in the feudal state and took the title of King Dingtao Gong. Dong Hongjin, Marquis of Gaochang, wrote in a memorial that King Zhuangxiang of Qin's mother was originally from the Xia family, and he was raised as a son by Mrs. Huayang. After he came to the throne, both of them were honored as Queen Mother. Queen Tao Gong should be made the Queen Mother. The matter was reported to Yousi. At that time, Shi Dan, as General Zuo, impeached Dong Hong together with the Grand Sima Wang Mang. Knowing clearly that the Queen Mother is the most noble title and the world has been unified, but using the example that led to the fall of Qin as a metaphor to deceive and mislead the Ming Dynasty is not what a minister should say, and it is very unethical. The emperor was new to the throne and was very humble. He accepted the words of Wang Mang and Shi Dan and exempted Dong Hong from being a commoner. Empress Dowager Fu was furious and forced the emperor to use his title. The emperor then honored King Ding Tao Gong as the Gong Emperor, the Empress Dowager Fu as the Gong Empress Dowager, and Empress Ding as the Gong Empress.
target: He advised the emperor to be cautious, citing disasters from hasty changes. He opposed honoring Empress Dowager Fu and Empress Ding with imperial titles, arguing it violated ritual propriety. This led to his disfavor.

source: A few months after Shi Dan was deposed, the emperor adopted Zhu Bo's suggestion and honored Empress Dowager Fu as the Empress Dowager, and Empress Ding as the Imperial Empress Dowager, with the same dignity as the Empress Dowager and the Empress Dowager. He also built an ancestral temple in the capital for the Communist Emperor, with the same etiquette as Emperor Xiaoyuan. Zhu Bo was promoted to prime minister, and he and the imperial censor Daxuan Tangxuan reported: Dong Hong, the former Marquis of Gaochang, first proposed the idea of ​​establishing a title, but was impeached by Shi Dan and exempted from being a commoner. At that time, there was a funeral in the world, and political affairs were entrusted to Shi Dan. Shi Dan did not carefully consider the principle of praising and promoting respect for relatives, but made random remarks, belittled the title, and damaged filial piety. There is no greater disloyalty than this. His majesty is saintly and kind, so he clearly established his honorary title. Dong Hong was also granted the title of Marquis of Gaochang because of his loyalty and filial piety. Shi Dan's crime of disobeying the emperor's order was obvious. Although he was pardoned, he should not enjoy the title or fief. I asked him to be exempted from being a commoner. The petition was approved. Shi Dan was dismissed and returned to his hometown for many years. When Emperor Ping came to the throne, Wang Mang, the Marquis of Xindu, reported to the Empress Dowager that he excavated the tombs of Empress Dowager Fu and Empress Dowager Ding, stripped them of their seals and ribbons, and buried them with common people's rites. Ding Tao destroyed the Gonghuang Temple.
target: After Zhu Bo's rise, Shi Dan was further demoted for opposing the honorary titles. When Emperor Ping came to power, Wang Mang restored Shi Dan, granting him the title of Marquis of Yiyang. He died shortly after, and his title ended with Wang Mang's fall.

source: Shi Dan was dismissed and returned to his hometown for many years. Ding Tao destroyed the Gonghuang Temple. Those who suggested this matter, such as Lingli, Duan You and others, were exiled to Hepu, and Dong Hong, the Marquis of Gaochang, was deposed as a commoner. He summoned Shi Dan to the public transport department and granted him the title of Marquis of Guannei, enjoying the original fiefdom. A few months later, the Empress Dowager Shao ordered the Great Situ and the Great Sikong to say: "Reward those who are virtuous and reward the ministers who have made the most contributions. This is the system of the sages and the unchanging rule of emperors of all dynasties." The former Empress Dowager Tao of Dingtao used her honorary title in vain, which was very contrary to justice. Hou Shidan of Guan Nei was loyal and upright to the country, regardless of adversity, adhered to loyalty and integrity, followed the laws of the Holy King, and clearly distinguished the system of superiority and inferiority. According to Si Tiao Chen's suggestion, the evil minister who was given the honorary title has been demoted or dismissed, but Shi Dan did not add rewards based on his merits. I am afraid that it violates Miao's principle of rewarding first and punishing later, and cannot promote virtue to repay his merits. Now, 2,100 households in Zhongxiang, Houqiu, are granted the title of Yiyang Marquis. More than a month later, Shi Dan passed away and Mi was named Jiehou. His son Shiye inherited the title, which was discontinued after Wang Mang's defeat. Praise said: He Wu's memorial, Wang Jia's admonishment, Shi Dan's ideas, and the examination of their misfortunes and blessings all came true in the future. When Wang Mang arose and everyone inside and outside was convinced, Dong Xian was favored as much as the emperor's relatives. He Wu and Wang Jia's ministers blocked the rivers with a piece of loess, thereby drowning themselves.
target: The commentary notes that He Wu, Wang Jia, and Shi Dan's warnings proved true. Wang Mang's rise and Dong Xian's favor led to He Wu and Wang Jia's downfalls, while Shi Dan faced alternating rewards and punishments. It reflects the difficulty of receiving titles in turbulent times.

source: Since the establishment of the Han Dynasty, sycophants and favored ministers who flattered the emperor and gained favor continued to appear. There were famous registered children in the Emperor Gaozu's dynasty, and there were Hong children in the Emperor Xiaohui's dynasty. These two people have no outstanding talents. They just blindly flatter and please the emperor and gain wealth and favor. They follow the emperor closely, go out and go in together, and have a very close relationship. Even the ministers use them to express themselves in front of the emperor. They had a great influence at that time because of their good words for themselves. Therefore, Emperor Hui's ministers and ministers all decorated their hats with delicate feathers, decorated their belts with sea shells, and applied makeup and powder. This custom was caused by the influence of people like boudoir and jiru. Both of them became rich and noble during their lifetime and moved to Anling. Later favorites included the scholar Deng Tong, the eunuch Zhao Tan, and Beigong Bozi during the reign of Emperor Wen; the scholar Han Yan and the eunuch Li Yannian during the reign of Emperor Wu; the eunuchs Hong Gong and Shi Xian during the Yuan Emperor; the scholars Zhang Fang and Chun Yuchang during the Cheng Emperor; and Dong Xian during the Emperor Ai's reign. Emperor Jing, Emperor Zhao, and Emperor Xuan all had no favorite ministers. If calculated broadly, during the reign of Emperor Jing, only Lang Zhongling Zhou Ren was a favored minister; during the reign of Emperor Zhao, the prince-in-law Duwei surprised Hou Jinshang and inherited the title of marquis from his father, the chariot general Jin Chan. Although the two of them were more favored than ordinary people, they were not particularly favored; Emperor Xuan, who had not yet become the emperor, studied poetry and books at the same table. When Emperor Xuan ascended the throne, Peng Zu was named Marquis of Yangdu by the emperor based on his friendship at that time. He often served as a guard when he went out and was known as the emperor's favorite. This man was relatively cautious and strict, and did not do anything harmful to others. In the end, he was poisoned by his concubine, and his feudal kingdom was abolished.
target: Since the Han Dynasty's founding, sycophants and favored ministers who gained imperial favor through flattery appeared regularly. During Emperor Gaozu's reign, there was Ji Ru; under Emperor Xiaohui, there was Hong Ru. Neither possessed outstanding talents, relying solely on flattery to gain wealth and favor. They accompanied the emperor closely, influencing even ministers who used them to communicate with the throne. Their impact was so great that Emperor Hui's officials adopted their customs, decorating hats with delicate feathers, belts with seashells, and applying makeup—a trend attributed to figures like Ji Ru and Hong Ru. Both became wealthy and noble in their lifetimes, later moving to Anling. Subsequent favored figures included Deng Tong, eunuch Zhao Tan, and Beigong Bozi under Emperor Wen; Han Yan and eunuch Li Yannian under Emperor Wu; eunuchs Hong Gong and Shi Xian under Emperor Yuan; Zhang Fang and Chun Yuchang under Emperor Cheng; and Dong Xian under Emperor Ai. Emperors Jing, Zhao, and Xuan had no notable favorites, though Zhou Ren under Emperor Jing, Jin Shang under Emperor Zhao, and Peng Zu under Emperor Xuan received some favor without causing harm.

source: Deng Tong, a native of Nan'an, Shu County, was known as Huangtoulang because he could hold a table, sail a boat and wear a yellow hat. The master boy once had a dream, in which he wanted to ascend to heaven, but could not. Suddenly a yellow-headed man pushed him hard, and he finally ascended to heaven. He turned around and saw that the man who pushed him had his jacket on under the leather belt on his buttocks, which was very unusual. After Emperor Wen woke up, he went to Jiantai and looked for the Huangtou man dressed in rowing clothes based on what he saw in his dream. He suddenly saw Deng Tong. His clothes were worn from behind, just like the man he saw in his dream. So he was summoned and asked his name. Deng Tong said his surname was Deng Mingtong. The pronunciations of Deng and Deng are similar. Emperor Wen was very happy and favored Deng Tong very much, saying that he was very happy. Deng Tong was very attentive and solemn in character and did not like to interact with outsiders. Even if the emperor rewarded him with a bathing vacation, he would not go out. Therefore, Emperor Wen rewarded Deng Tong with tens of thousands of dollars, more than a dozen times, and Deng Tong became a high official. Emperor Wen sometimes went to Deng Tong's house to play games in private, but Deng Tong had no other special acting talents and could not show them to the emperor. He was just cautious to please the emperor. The emperor once sent a fortune teller who was good at reading Deng Tong's fortune. The fortune teller said: "He will definitely die of poverty and hunger in the future." The emperor said: I am the one who can make Deng Tong rich. As the king of a country, how can I say that Deng Tong will be poor? So the emperor rewarded Deng Tong with the Tongshan Mountain in Yandao, Shu County, and asked him to mint coins for use. As a result, the coins minted by Deng Tong spread all over the world, and he became so rich. Emperor Wen once had abscesses on his body, and Deng often used his own mouth to suck the abscesses for the emperor. The emperor was unhappy and asked Deng Tong calmly: Who in the world do you think loves me the most and cares about me the most? Deng Tong said: There should be no one who can surpass the prince. The prince came in to greet the emperor, and the emperor asked the prince to suck the sore. Although the prince sucked it, he could see that he was very uncomfortable. Later, the prince heard that Deng Tong had been very active in sucking the emperor's sores. The prince was very ashamed, and the prince secretly hated Deng Tong in his heart. When Emperor Wen died and Emperor Jing came to the throne, Deng Tong was dismissed and returned home to live. Not long after returning home, someone reported that Deng Tong had gone out to the southwest to mint money, so Emperor Jing sent officials to investigate the matter. There was considerable evidence, so he was convicted and everything was confiscated. In addition, Deng Tong's family also owed tens of millions. The officials confiscated all the money given to Deng Tong by the eldest princess, and did not even leave him a hairpin to wear. So the eldest princess asked someone to lend him clothes and food. Deng Tong was penniless and ended up living in someone else's home and died. Zhao Tan was favored by his observation of stars and weather; Beigong Bozi treated others with the generosity and compassion of an elder, so the emperor got close to him, but neither of them could compare with Dian Tong. Han Yan, courtesy name Wangsun, is the grandson of Gonggaohou Qidang. When Emperor Wu was the king of Jiaodong, Han Yan and Emperor Wu studied poetry and calligraphy together. They were friendly to each other and had a friendly relationship. When Emperor Wu became the prince, Emperor Wu became closer to Han Yan. Han Yan is good at horseback riding and archery, and is smart and wise. After Emperor Wu became emperor, he wanted to attack the northern minorities. Since Han Yan had studied military affairs before, Emperor Wu favored him more and Han Yan became more noble. Han Yan later became a high official, and the rewards he received were comparable to Deng Tong. At first, Han Yan often slept and got up with Emperor Wu. Once, King Jiangdu came to see the emperor and went hunting with Emperor Wu in Shanglin Garden. Before the emperor's carriage set off, he sent Han Yan to take a auxiliary carriage and lead nearly a hundred knights to check out the wild beasts. At that time, King Jiangdu saw it from a distance and thought that the emperor had arrived. He avoided the people who followed Han Yan and knelt down by the roadside. Unexpectedly, Han Yan did not see him and rushed over. King Jiangdu was furious and cried to the empress dowager. He demanded that the title be returned to the emperor and that he also serve as a palace guard to compete with Han Yan. When the Queen Mother heard about this, she hated Han Yan ever since. Han Yan served the emperor and had no hindrance in entering and leaving the palace. When the news of adultery reached the ears of the Queen Mother, the Queen Mother was furious and sent someone to kill Han Yan. The emperor personally interceded for Han Yan, but the Queen Mother had already made up her mind and finally refused to change her mind, and Han Yan died. Han Yan's younger brother Han Shuo was also favored by Emperor Wu. He was named a Case Daohou for his military exploits. In the last years of Emperor Wu, he was killed by the ruthless prince during the witchcraft disaster. Han Shuo's son Han Zeng was later named Long Luohou and Da Sima Cavalry General. There is another biography of him.
target: Deng Tong, from Nan'an in Shu, was known as Huangtoulang for wearing a yellow hat while rowing. Emperor Wen once dreamed of ascending to heaven but was unable until a yellow-headed man pushed him upward. After waking, the emperor sought the man and found Deng Tong, whose clothing matched the dream. Delighted, the emperor favored him greatly, rewarding him with tens of thousands in cash and high office. Deng Tong was cautious and solemn, avoiding outsiders even during holidays. A fortune-teller predicted he would die poor and hungry, but the emperor, confident in his power, gave him Tongshan Mountain in Shu to mint coins, making Deng Tong immensely wealthy. When Emperor Wen developed abscesses, Deng Tong sucked them with his mouth. The emperor asked who loved him most, and Deng Tong replied the prince. The prince, uncomfortable with sucking the sores, later resented Deng Tong. After Emperor Wen's death, Emperor Jing dismissed Deng Tong. Accused of minting coins outside, Deng Tong was convicted, his property confiscated, and he died penniless in another's home. Zhao Tan gained favor through astrology, and Beigong Bozi through elder-like generosity, but neither matched Deng Tong. Han Yan, grandson of Gonggaohou Qidang, studied with Emperor Wu during his youth. After Emperor Wu became emperor, Han Yan's skills in horseback riding and archery, along with his intelligence, earned him favor comparable to Deng Tong. He often slept and rose with the emperor. Once, while hunting, King Jiangdu mistook Han Yan's entourage for the emperor and knelt, but Han Yan passed without noticing. The king complained to the empress dowager, who hated Han Yan thereafter. When adultery rumors reached her, she had Han Yan killed despite the emperor's pleas. Han Yan's brother, Han Shuo, also favored, was later killed during the witchcraft disaster.

source: Li Yannian is from Zhongshan. He and his parents and brothers are all music lovers. Li Yannian suffered corruption and was in charge of the emperor's dog; his sister was favored by the emperor and was named Mrs. Li. Her biography is in "Biography of Foreign Relatives". Li Yannian is good at singing, and he sings emerging tunes. At that time, Emperor Wu was building various temples to worship heaven and earth. When he wanted to create music, he asked Sima Xiangru and others to write poems to praise it. Li Yannian always adhered to Emperor Wu's orders and composed and sang these poems into new variations. Li Yannian's sister was adopted by Emperor Wu as his wife and gave birth to the King of Changyi. As a result, Li Yannian's worth doubled, from humble to noble. He became the captain of Xielu, wore a two thousand stone seal ribbon, and lived with the emperor. The favor he received was equal to that of Han Yan. As time went by, Li Yannian's younger brother Li Ji became promiscuous with the palace officials and became arrogant and domineering. After Mrs. Li's death, the two brothers could no longer be favored by Emperor Wu, so Emperor Wu killed the Li Yannian brothers and their clan. From then on, the favored ministers were basically relatives. Although Wei Qing and Huo Qubing were favored by the emperor, they were promoted based on their true military achievements and talents.
target: Li Yannian, from Zhongshan, was a musician who suffered corruption and managed the emperor's dogs. His sister, favored as Lady Li, gave birth to the King of Changyi. Li Yannian's musical talents earned him high rank, equal to Han Yan. After Lady Li's death, his brother Li Ji's promiscuity led to their execution. Thereafter, favored ministers were mostly relatives. Wei Qing and Huo Qubing, though favored, rose through genuine military merit.

source: As time went by, Li Yannian's younger brother Li Ji became promiscuous with the palace officials and became arrogant and domineering. After Mrs. Li's death, the two brothers could no longer be favored by Emperor Wu, so Emperor Wu killed the Li Yannian brothers and their clan. From then on, the favored ministers were basically relatives. Although Wei Qing and Huo Qubing were favored by the emperor, they were promoted based on their true military achievements and talents. Shi Xian, courtesy name Junfang, was from Jinan; Hong Gong was from Peidi. They both suffered corruption when they were young, and later served as officials in Zhonghuangmen and were elected as Zhongshangshu. During the reign of Emperor Xuan, Honggong served as the Secretary of the Central Committee. He was familiar with old laws and regulations, and was good at requesting and submitting reports. His talents were sufficient for his position. Hong Gong was appointed as Zhongshu Ling, and Shi Xian was appointed as Pu She. A few years after Emperor Yuan came to the throne, Hong Gong died and was replaced by Shi Xian as Zhongshu Ling. At that time, Emperor Yuan was ill and unable to take care of the government affairs personally. He was also passionate about music. Because Shi Xian had been in this position for a long time and had no outside connections in the palace, he was focused and trustworthy, so Emperor Yuan entrusted Shi Xian with all kinds of government affairs. All political affairs, big or small, were decided based on Shi Xian's words; Shi Xian's dignity and favor dominated the court, and all officials served Shi Xian respectfully. Shi Xian was clever and clever, and could understand the emperor's thoughts. He was extremely cunning, and often used various inexplicable reasons to secretly attack others. He would treat people with strict laws for the smallest things. During the early Yuan Dynasty, former general Xiao Wangzhi and Guanglu doctor Zhou Kan and Zongzheng Liu Gengsheng were all responsible for the work. Xiao Wangzhi took charge of the affairs of the Secretariat. He knew that Shi Xian was monopolizing power and was evil, so he stated his opinion: "The Secretariat is the foundation of all officials and the key to national power. Fair and transparent people should be allowed to hold this position." Emperor Wu traveled and feasted in the harem day and night, so he reused eunuchs, which was not in line with the old regulations. Eunuchs should not be allowed to serve as Zhongshu, in response to ancient etiquette, and people who are still serving their sentences should not be allowed to approach the emperor. Emperor Yuan did not adopt Xiao Wangzhi's suggestion, so Xiao Wangzhi made Shi Xian very angry. Later, Xiao Wangzhi and others were persecuted by Shi Xian. Xiao Wangzhi was forced to commit suicide and died. Zhou Kan and Liu Gengsheng were deposed and imprisoned and were no longer appointed. These contents can be found in "The Biography of Wang". Later, Taizhong doctor Zhang Meng, Wei Jun's prefect Jingfang, Yushi Zhongcheng Chen Xian, Dai Shaojia Gianzhi and others all secretly wrote memorials, often exposing Shi Xian's shortcomings when summoned by the emperor. Shi Xian sent people to inquire about him and convicted him. The house in Beijing and the house he bought for donation were abandoned on the market. Zhang Meng committed suicide in the bus station. Chen Xian was the one to answer the crime and had his hair shaved off and served the sentence of Cheng Dan. Later, Su Jian, the governor of Zheng District, obtained Shi Xian's private message and reported it to the emperor. Shi Xian later sentenced him to death for other reasons.
target: Shi Xian, from Jinan, and Hong Gong, from Pei, both suffered corruption and served as eunuchs. Under Emperor Xuan, Hong Gong became Zhongshu Ling, skilled in laws and reports. After Hong Gong's death, Shi Xian succeeded him under Emperor Yuan. When Emperor Yuan fell ill, he entrusted all government affairs to Shi Xian, who became all-powerful. Shi Xian was cunning, using strict laws to attack opponents. He persecuted Xiao Wangzhi, Zhou Kan, and Liu Gengsheng, leading to Xiao's suicide and the others' imprisonment. Later, Zhang Meng, Jing Fang, Chen Xian, and others who exposed Shi Xian's faults were convicted. Su Jian, who reported Shi Xian's private letters, was executed. Officials feared Shi Xian, who formed a clique with Lao Liang and Wulu Chongzong.
