Those who attached to them could obtain high-ranking officials. A folk song goes: Lao Liang and Shi Xian are all frequent visitors to the Wulu Chong family! How many official seals are in their hands! How long are the ribbons they wear! This folk song tells the story of their official position and great power. Shi Xian saw that General Zuo Feng Fengshi and his son were very prestigious as ministers, and Feng Fengshi's daughter was Zhaoyi in the emperor's inner palace, so he wanted to attach himself to him, so Shi Xian recommended Zhaoyi's brother Feng Kui to the emperor, saying that Feng Kui had a strict temperament and could serve in the palace. Therefore, the emperor summoned Feng Kui and wanted to appoint him as a minister. Feng Kui took the opportunity and asked to tell the emperor something secretly. When the emperor heard that Feng Kui said that Shi Xian had monopoly power, he was very angry and immediately dismissed Feng Kui from his position and became a Langguan. Later, when the position of the imperial censor became vacant, all the ministers recommended Feng Kui's brother, Da Honglu, Ye Wang, for his unparalleled character and talent. The emperor asked Shi Xian about this, and Shi Xian said: "No one among the nine ministers is more qualified for this position than Ye Wang."
target: A folk song mocked their power. Shi Xian tried to attach himself to Feng Fengshi but recommended Feng Kui, who then exposed Shi Xian's monopoly. The emperor dismissed Feng Kui. When the censor position opened, ministers recommended Feng Kui's brother, but Shi Xian blocked it. Shi Xian often feigned self-criticism to maintain trust. After Emperor Yuan's death, Emperor Cheng demoted Shi Xian, who died on the road. His followers were dismissed.

source: This is how Shi Xian deliberately played tricks to escape disaster and win the trust of the emperor. Emperor Yuan was ill in his later years. Prince Dingtao Gong was very favored by Emperor Yuan at that time, but Shi Xian supported the crown prince very actively and forcefully. After Emperor Yuan died and Emperor Cheng ascended the throne, he transferred Shi Xian to Changxin Palace as a servant with an official salary of two thousand dan. After Shi Xian lost his support and within a few months of losing power, the prime minister and censor listed Shi Xian's previous crimes to the emperor, and his accomplices Lao Liang and Chen Shun were dismissed from office. Shi Xian, his wife and son returned to their hometown. They were worried and unable to eat, and died on the road. Those who used to flatter Shi Xian and obtain official positions were all dismissed. Wulu Chongzong of the Shaofu was demoted to be the prefect of Xuantu, and Yijia, the censor Zhongcheng, was demoted to the captain of Yanmen. A new ballad circulated in Chang'an, saying: The geese migrate when the birds migrate, and the dodders migrate when the deer migrate, so we can go to the prison to be with Chen Shiwujia. Chun Yuchang, courtesy name Ziru, was a native of Yuancheng, Wei County. When he was a child, he served as a Huang Menglang because he was the son of the Empress Dowager's sister, but he was not promoted to an official position and was not favored. It happened that General Wang Feng fell ill, and Chun Yuchang served Wang Feng very seriously. He helped Wang Feng morning and night, and he became a nephew and uncle. Before Wang Feng died, he entrusted Chunyu Chang to the Queen Mother and the Emperor. The emperor commended Chun Yuchang for his loyalty and worshiped him as Lieutenant of Lieutenants and Zhucao. He later moved to Shuihengdu Weishizhong, and later to Weiwei Jiuqing. After some time, Feiyan was deeply favored by the emperor, who wanted to make her his queen. However, the queen mother saw that she was of low origin and opposed making Feiyan his queen. Chunyu Chang specially sent a message on behalf of the emperor to Shu Palace where the Queen Mother was. More than a year later, Tong Feiyan was made empress. The emperor was very excited about Chun Yuchang's efforts, so the emperor commended Chun Yuchang for his previous contributions. I conveyed Chunyu Chang's words to the ministers for discussion, and everyone agreed with Chun Yuchang's strategy. Chunyu Chang proposed a good strategy from the beginning, so the people were relieved from toil and gained peace. Therefore, Chunyu Chang was granted the title of Marquis of Guannei. Later, Chunyu Chang was granted the title of Marquis of Dingling. He was trusted and reused by the emperor. Chun Yuchang's wealth exceeded that of the ministers at that time. Chunyu Chang made friends with princes, herders, and guards outside. The rewards he received from the emperor and the money given to him by princes, herders, and guards to please him totaled tens of millions. He married many beautiful wives and concubines, Shen? In the face of sexual pleasure, they do not abide by the laws and regulations of the country and do whatever they want. At the beginning, Queen Xu committed a crime because she believed in witchcraft and was deposed as queen and thrown into Changding Palace. At that time, Queen Xu's sister Xu Wei was the wife of Long'e Sihou. Long'e Sihou was dead and was living as a widow at home. Chunyu Chang took the opportunity to have an affair with Xu Marry and married her as a side wife.
target: Chun Yuchang, from Yuancheng, served Wang Feng diligently, becoming his nephew. Before Wang Feng's death, he recommended Chun Yuchang to the empress dowager and emperor. Chun Yuchang helped make Feiyan empress, earning a marquis title. He became wealthy, marrying many concubines and having an affair with Xu Wei, sister of deposed Empress Xu. Empress Xu bribed Chun Yuchang to regain favor, but he deceived her. Wang Mang, fearing Chun Yuchang's rise, exposed his crimes to Wang Gen and the empress dowager. Chun Yuchang was dismissed and exiled, dying in prison. His family was exiled, and many officials lost their posts.

source: When Chunyu Chang was sent away for his crime, Hongyang Houli's eldest son Rong followed Chunyu Chang and asked for a ride. Chunyu Chang bribed Hongyang Houli with rare treasures through Hongyang Houli's son Rong, and Hongyang Houli in turn spoke for Chunyu Chang. The emperor saw the great change in Hongyang Houli's attitude and knew that there must be something fishy, ​​so he sent relevant departments to investigate the matter. Officials captured Rong, and Hongyang Houli forced Rong to commit suicide. The emperor became more suspicious that there must be serious treachery involved, so he ordered Chun Yu to be arrested and handed over to Shao Prison in Luoyang for investigation into the case. Chunyu Chang truthfully confessed that he was teasing Queen Xu of Changding Palace and wanted to re-establish Queen Zuo. Chunyu Chang rebelled and died in prison. Chunyuchang's wife and son were punished and exiled to Hepu. If his mother is sent back to her hometown. Hongyang Houli was also deported from Kyoto to the vassal states. Because Chun Yuchang lost power, dozens of generals, ministers, officials, and county guards related to him in the court were dismissed from office. Wang Mang then replaced Wang Gen as the Grand Sima. Not long after, Chun Yuchang's mother and her son Chun Yuchou were moved back to Chang'an. Later, Chun Yuchou committed a crime, and Wang Mang killed him and sent his family members home. At first, Chunyu Chang was close to the emperor because of his status as a relative, but he was not as favored as Fuping Hou Zhang Fang. Zhang Fang often went out and lived together with the emperor. He changed his clothes and went in and out together with the emperor. Dong Xian, courtesy name Shengqing, was born in Yunyang. His father's name was Gong, who served as censor, and Dong Xian served as the prince's minister. Emperor Ai succeeded to the throne, and Dong Xian was promoted from Prince Subordinate to Lang Guan. More than two years later, Dong Xian reported the time to His Highness. He was handsome and pleasant. When Emperor Ai saw him, he liked his appearance. He looked at him and asked: "Are you Dong Xian, the prince's servant?" So he was summoned to the palace to talk, and he was appointed Huang Menlang, and he began to be favored from then on. When asked, he learned that his father was Yunzhonghou, who should be promoted to Baling County Magistrate, and then to Guanglu Doctor. Dong Xian was favored for a day and served as the prince's consort, the captain's attendant. He would ride with him in the carriage when he went out, and would serve around him when he entered the court. He was rewarded tens of millions in total in ten days, and his noble status shocked the court. He often stood up and slept with Aizha. Once when he was sleeping during the day, his body pressed against Emperor Ai's sleeve. Emperor Ai remembered that Dong Xian was not awake yet. Emperor Ai did not want to wake Dong Zhi, so he cut off his sleeve and stood up. Such was the favor he received. Dong Xian is also very gentle in temperament, yet eccentric and dishonest. He is good at flattering and gaining favor to gain a foothold. Whenever he was given leave to take a bath, he refused to go out and often stayed with the emperor to take care of medicine. Because Dong Xian rarely came home, the emperor ordered Dong Xian to take his wife to live temporarily in the palace, sleeping in Dong Xian's resting place, just like the wives of officials living in official dormitories.
target: Dong Xian, from Yunyang, served as prince's minister under Emperor Ai. His handsome appearance won favor, and he became Huang Menlang. He rode with the emperor and slept with him. Once, when Dong Xian slept on Emperor Ai's sleeve, the emperor cut it off rather than wake him. Dong Xian's family received immense rewards, and he became Grand Sima at age twenty-two. After Emperor Ai's death, the empress dowager summoned Wang Mang, who impeached Dong Xian for failing to care for the emperor. Dong Xian and his wife committed suicide.

source: The Grand Sima seal should be taken back, dismissed from office and returned home. When Dong Xian and his wife both committed suicide, their family members panicked and buried them overnight. Wang Mang suspected that he had faked his death, so the deacon officials asked him to send the coffin and go to the prison to inspect it. Wang Mang also hinted that the great Situ Kong Guang had written a letter, saying that Dong Xian's character was cunning and flattering, and he was granted a title by virtue of his treachery. His father and son were good at government affairs, and his brothers were favored at the same time, and received many rewards. The father and son were arrogant and foolish. They did not receive the emperor's envoys with courtesy and did not thank them when receiving rewards. Their sins were obvious.
target: Their property was confiscated, and his family exiled. The text concludes that these favored ministers, lacking virtue, met bad ends, and their rise contributed to the Western Han's decline.

source: Fu Jiezi was from the North and was promoted to an official because he joined the army. It turns out that both Qiuci and Loulan had killed envoys of the Han Dynasty, which was recorded in "Biography of the Western Regions". During the Yuanfeng period, Fu Jiezi requested to be sent to Dayuan as an envoy of Junma, and took the emperor's Shao letter to condemn Loulan and Qiuci. When Fu Jiezi arrived in Loulan, he blamed the King of Loulan for encouraging the Huns to intercept and kill the Han Dynasty envoys. He said: The large army is about to arrive. If you don't encourage the Huns, why don't you report the Huns' envoys to other countries after passing through? King Loulan expressed his guilt and said: The Huns envoy has just passed by. He should have gone to Wusun and passed through Qiuci on the way. When Fu Jiezi arrived at Kucha, he blamed the King of Kucha again, and the King of Kucha also admitted his guilt. Fu Jiezi returned to Kucha from Dayuan. The Kucha people said that the Huns envoy was here after returning from Wusun. Fu Jiezi took the opportunity to lead his officers and soldiers to kill the Huns envoy. Fu Jiezi returned to the capital to report the situation, and the emperor issued an edict appointing him as Zhonglang and promoted him to Ping Yue Supervisor. Fu Jiezi said to the general Huo Guang: Loulan and Qiuci have been capricious many times but have not been condemned. They cannot be used to punish other countries. When I passed through Qiuci, their king was very close to others and could easily be attacked. I was willing to go and assassinate him, so as to establish my prestige and announce it to other countries. The general said: "Qiuci country is far away, so let's go to Loulan to test this method for now." So he told the emperor to send him there. Fu Jiezi and the soldiers brought gold and silver coins together, claiming that they were gifts to foreign countries.
target: Fu Jiezi, from the North, became an official through military service. During the Yuanfeng period, he was sent as an envoy to Dayuan and condemned the kings of Loulan and Qiuci for killing Han envoys. After returning, he proposed to General Huo Guang to assassinate the King of Loulan to establish Han prestige. Huo Guang agreed, and Fu Jiezi used gold and silk as bait to lure the king.

source: He immediately took out the gold coins and showed them to the translator. The translator came back and reported the situation to King Loulan. King Loulan was greedy for the property of the Han Dynasty, so he came to meet the envoy. Fu Jiezi sat drinking with him and showed him his belongings. After drinking, Fu Jiezi was drunk and said to King Loulan: The emperor sent me to report some things to the king privately. King Loulan got up and followed Fu Jiezi into the tent. The two were talking alone. Two strong men stabbed King Loulan from behind. The blades met in the chest. King Loulan died immediately. His nobles and left and right officials all fled. Fu Jiezi told them that King Loulan was guilty of the Han Dynasty, and the emperor sent me to kill him. The prince who had been left as a hostage in the Han Dynasty should be replaced as king.
target: During a private meeting, two soldiers stabbed the king to death. Fu Jiezi declared the king's guilt and installed a new ruler.

source: The emperor then issued an edict saying: King Angui of Loulan had acted as a spy for the Huns, secretly spying on the envoys of the Han Dynasty, and sent troops to kill and plunder three guards, including Ma Anle, Guanglu Dafuzhong, and Qi Menlang Suicheng, as well as envoys from Anxi and Dawan. Fu Jiezi, the supervisor of Pingle, went out as an envoy with the talisman and killed King Angui of Loulan. He hung his head on the north tower and repaid the resentful people with integrity without disturbing the troops and stirring up the crowd. Fu Jiezi was granted the title of Marquis of Yiyang and given to 700 households in the city. Among the soldiers who assassinated King Loulan, they all replaced their officials as ministers. After Fu Jiezi died, his son Fu Chang was guilty and could not inherit the title, and the feudal state was abolished. In the middle of the first year of the Yuan Dynasty, the descendants of the heroes were renewed, and Fu Chang, the great-grandson of Fu Jiezi, was granted the title of Marquis of Yiyang. It was only after Wang Mang's failure that the throne was cut off.
target: He was rewarded with the title of Marquis of Yiyang and 700 households. His title was later abolished due to his son's crime but restored under Wang Mang.

source: General Huo Guang hinted that Chang Hui would make his own decisions based on the situation. Chang Hui arrived at the Wusun Kingdom with 500 officers and soldiers. When he came back and passed by Kucha, he recruited 20,000 troops from the western country. He ordered his deputy to send 20,000 troops from Kucha to tie up the country. Wusun sent 7,000 troops to attack Kucha from three sides. Before the army could gather together, they sent someone to accuse King Qiuci of killing the envoys of the Han Dynasty in the past. King Qiuci apologized and said: This is the result of being harmed by the noble Gu Yi when I was the late king. I am not guilty. Chang Hui said: Even so, Gu Yi must be tied up, and I can let the king go. King Qiuci tied up Guyi and took him to Chang Hui. Chang Hui killed Guyi and went back. Later, Chang Hui replaced Su Wu as the vassal state. He was familiar with the situation in foreign countries and worked hard many times with meritorious deeds. In the middle of the year of Ganlu, the later general Zhao Chongguo passed away, and the emperor appointed Limulus Tomb as the right general, and the official position of the Dian vassal state remained as before. When Emperor Xuan died, Chang Hui served Emperor Yuan. He died three years later, and his nickname was Zhuang Genyao. The feudal state was passed down to the great-grandson, and was discontinued in the middle of Jianwu year. Zheng Ji is from Kuaiji. Because he served in the army and went on several missions to Yousu, he was named Lang. Dian Mu is a strong and persistent person and is familiar with foreign affairs. Since the fortress was connected to Youqiu and Kui Luxing was conquered, school captains were set up to work in Quli. At the time of Emperor Xuan, Zheng Ji worked in Quli as a minister and accumulated grain. He then mobilized armies from various countries to defeat the chariot division. He was promoted to Sima of the Guard and sent to guard the southern road west of Shanshan. In the middle of the year of Shenjue, internal turmoil broke out among the Xiongnu. The Xianxian Shan, the king of Chu, planned to surrender to the Han Dynasty and sent someone to contact Zheng Ji. Zheng Ji mobilized 50,000 people from Quli, Qiuci and other countries to meet King Yue Zhu. There were 12,000 people. Xiao Wang sent 12 people to follow Zheng Ji to Hequ. Many people fled. Zheng Ji chased these people and killed them, and then brought the remaining people to the capital. Emperor Mo granted King Ri Zhu the title of Marquis of Guide. After Zheng Ji defeated the chariot division, he surrendered and surrendered to the king. His reputation shocked the Western Regions, so he also took charge of the North Road to the west of the chariot division, so he was known as the Protector. The establishment of Duhu began with Zheng Ji. In order to commend him for his achievements, the emperor issued an edict saying: Zheng Ji, the captain of the cavalry in the Western Regions, appeased the foreign barbarians, declared his hope and credibility, welcomed the cousin of the Xiongnu Chanyu, King Ri Zhu, and his men, and attacked the Cheshi Douzi City, which was a remarkable achievement.
target: Chang Hui, from Taiyuan, was detained by the Xiongnu for over a decade while accompanying Su Wu. After Emperor Zhao's reign, he was sent to Wusun, where he coordinated a joint Han-Wusun attack on the Xiongnu, resulting in significant victories. He later executed a noble from Qiuci for killing a Han captain. Chang Hui succeeded Su Wu as a vassal state official and served under Emperors Xuan and Yuan, earning the posthumous title Zhuang Genyao. Zheng Ji, from Kuaiji, served as a military officer and became an expert in foreign affairs. He established agricultural colonies in Quli and defeated the Che division, earning the title of Protector of the Western Regions.

source: Emperor Mo granted King Ri Zhu the title of Marquis of Guide. After Zheng Ji defeated the chariot division, he surrendered and surrendered to the king. His reputation shocked the Western Regions, so he also took charge of the North Road to the west of the chariot division, so he was known as the Protector. The establishment of Duhu began with Zheng Ji. In order to commend him for his achievements, the emperor issued an edict saying: Zheng Ji, the captain of the cavalry in the Western Regions, appeased the foreign barbarians, declared his hope and credibility, welcomed the cousin of the Xiongnu Chanyu, King Ri Zhu, and his men, and attacked the Cheshi Douzi City, which was a remarkable achievement. Zheng Ji was granted the title of Marquis of Anyuan, and was granted food to 1,000 households in the city. Zheng Ji then established a shogunate in the center of various countries in the Western Regions, and the official office was in Wulei City to pacify the various countries, kill, conquer, appease and recruit them. The orders of the Han Dynasty were issued to the Western Regions, and construction was started by Zhang Qian and completed by Zheng Ji. These are recorded in the "Biography of the Western Regions". After Zheng Ji passed away, he was given the title of Marquis Mu. His son Zheng Guang inherited the title, but he died without a son and the feudal state was abolished.
target: He was granted the title of Marquis of Anyuan with 1,000 households. His son died without an heir, ending the title, but it was later restored to his great-grandson.

source: The orders of the Han Dynasty were issued to the Western Regions, and construction was started by Zhang Qian and completed by Zheng Ji. These are recorded in the "Biography of the Western Regions". After Zheng Ji passed away, he was given the title of Marquis Mu. His son Zheng Guang inherited the title, but he died without a son and the feudal state was abolished. In the middle of the first year of the Yuan Dynasty, among the meritorious officials who were not expelled due to crimes, Zheng Yong, the great-grandson of Zheng Ji, was granted the title of Marquis of Anyuan. Gan Yanshou, courtesy name Junkuang, was from Yuzhi in the north. When he was young, he was selected as Yu Lin because he was good at horseback riding and archery. His skills in throwing stones and jumping were unparalleled among his peers. He once jumped into Yu Lin's pavilion, so he was promoted to Lang. After testing his hand-fighting skills, he was appointed as a disciple. He relied on his strength and was favored. Soon he was transferred to the post of governor of Liaodong and was dismissed. The cavalry general Xu Jia recommended Gan Yanshou as a doctor and admonished the doctor. He went to the Western Regions as an envoy to protect the cavalry captain. Together with the deputy captain Chen Tang, he killed Zhizhi Shanyu and was named Yichenghou. After Gan Yanshou died, Mi was named Zhuanghou. The feudal state was passed down to his great-grandson. After Wang Mang failed, the feudal state was ended. Chen Tang, whose courtesy name is Zigong, is from Shanyang Xiaqiu. When he was young, he liked to read, he was knowledgeable and well-versed in affairs, and he could write good articles. The family was poor and relied on begging and borrowing money to make a living. He had no moral integrity and was not praised by the people in the state. Chen Tang went west to Chang'an to seek an official position, hoping to become an eunuch and serve as a prime minister. A few years later, Zhang Bo, the Marquis of Fuping, dated Chen Tang and admired his talent. In the second year of the Yuan Dynasty, Emperor Shao of the Yuan Dynasty ordered the princes to recommend talents, and Zhang Bo recommended Chen Tang. In order to wait for promotion, Chen Tang did not go to the funeral after his father's death. Sili impeached Chen Tang for not observing filial piety. Zhang Bo's election and recommendation were fraudulent and did not follow the actual situation. He was cut off from 200 households. When he died, he was given the title of Mihou. Chen Tang was imprisoned and sentenced.
target: Gan Yanshou, from Yuzhi, was a skilled horseman and archer. He served as an envoy to the Western Regions and, with Deputy Captain Chen Tang, killed Zhizhi Chanyu. He was named Marquis of Yicheng. His title passed to his great-grandson before ending under Wang Mang. Chen Tang, from Shanyang, was a learned but poor man who sought office in Chang'an. He was recommended by Zhang Bo but imprisoned for failing to attend his father's funeral. Later, as Deputy Captain of the Western Regions, he and Gan Yanshou led a campaign against Zhizhi Chanyu, who had killed Han envoys. They mobilized over 40,000 troops, besieged Zhizhi's city, and killed the chanyu.

source: Chen Tang was usually greedy, and most of the property he seized entered the Han Dynasty and was not handed over in accordance with the law. Captain Sili sent a letter to the officials on the road, arresting officers and soldiers to investigate the matter. Chen Tang then wrote a memorial and said: I, together with the officers and soldiers, killed the Zhizhi Chanyu. Fortunately, we were able to eliminate them. When the army returns victorious from thousands of miles away, there should be envoys on the road to welcome the reward. Now Si Li went against the grain and arrested the officers and soldiers for examination. This was to avenge Zhizhi Chanyu! The emperor immediately sent officers and soldiers and ordered the counties to prepare food and wine on the road to reward the passing troops. After returning to the capital, they commented on their merits. Shi Xian and Kuang Heng believed that Gan Yanshou and Chen Tang had used the emperor's orders to mobilize troops without permission, and were lucky to have not been executed. If they were granted titles and granted land, then the envoys who were ordered in the future would rush to take risks to gain luck, cause trouble among the barbarians, and bring disaster to the country. This cannot be done. Emperor Yuan praised the contribution of Gan Yanshou and Chen Tang in his heart, but it was difficult to go against the opinions of Kuang Heng and Shi Xian, and the matter was not decided for a long time.
target: Despite their success, they faced criticism for acting without orders. After a lengthy debate, Emperor Yuan granted them titles and rewards, though Chen Tang was later dismissed for misconduct. He was eventually exiled to Dunhuang but recalled before his death in Chang'an.

source: In the past, Bai Qi was the general of the Qin State. He captured the capital of Ying in the south and killed Tongkuo in the north. Because of a small mistake, he was killed by Du You. The people of Qin mourned for him and all of them shed tears. Now Chen Tang personally carries weapons and fights thousands of miles away with bloodshed. He sacrifices his military exploits to the ancestral temple and reports to heaven. All warriors admire his integrity. There is no great sin in committing a sin because of telling something. "Book of Zhou" says: If you keep in mind the merits of others and forget the faults of others, you will be fit to be a monarch. Besides, if dogs and horses work hard for people, they can still get shacks built for them in return, not to mention the meritorious officials of the country! Privately, I worry that your Majesty has ignored the sound of the military drums, failed to understand the meaning of the "Book of Zhou", and forgotten the kindness of building a shack, treated Chen Tang as a mediocre minister, and finally obeyed the officials' decision. Letting the people also have the resentment of the people of Qin is not a way to spur ministers who risk their lives. After the memorial was submitted, the emperor released Chen Tang, revoked his title and became an ordinary soldier. A few years later, Duan Huizong, the protector of the Western Regions, was surrounded by the Wusun army. People from the post station came on horseback to report, hoping to send troops from countries with towns in the Western Regions and Dunhuang troops to rescue them. Prime Minister Wang Shang, General Wang Feng and hundreds of officials discussed the matter for several days with no result. Wang Feng said: "Chen Tang is very good at planning and familiar with foreign situations. You can call him to ask."
target: Duan Huizong, from Tianshui, served as Protector of the Western Regions and was respected for his integrity. He killed a rebellious Wusun prince, Fanqiu, with a small force, earning the title of Marquis of Guannei. He died in Wusun at age 75, mourned by all nations.

source: Duan Huizong said: If you tell King Wusun in advance and let Fanqiu escape and hide, you will commit a serious crime. If I provided him with food and then handed it over to me, it would be a disservice to my family members, so I didn't inform him in advance. King Wusun and his men wept and withdrew their troops. Duan Huizong went back to report the situation. The ministers discussed that Duan Huizong should act according to the situation and use a small force to go deep into the Wusun Kingdom and kill Fanqiu. This demonstrated the country's prestige and should be rewarded heavily. The emperor gave Duan Huizong the title of Marquis of Guannei and one hundred catties of gold. At this time, Bei Yuanxu, the younger brother of King Wusun's father, led everyone to harm King Wusun. The Han Dynasty sent Duan Huizong there to work with Sun Jian, the protector, to appease him. The next year, Duan Huizong died of illness in Wusun Kingdom at the age of seventy-five. All countries in the city mourned him and built ancestral halls for him. Zan said: From the Yuanshou period, Zhang Qian began to communicate with the Western Regions. In the Dijie period, Zheng Ji established the title of Protector. Until the era of Wang Mang, there were 18 people in total. They were all elected for their bravery and strategy. However, those who had meritorious deeds among them are all recorded here. Lian Guo was praised for his kindness and trust, Guo Shun was famous for his honesty and fairness, Sun Jian was famous for his dignity in handling affairs, and the rest of them had nothing to praise. Chen Tang behaved unruly and did not restrain himself, and finally fell into hardship and embarrassment. The commentators pitied him, so they also listed him here.
target: The text concludes that from Zhang Qian's time to Wang Mang's era, 18 protectors served, with notable figures like Zheng Ji, Gan Yanshou, and Chen Tang. Chen Tang's unruliness led to his downfall, but his deeds are recorded for posterity.

source: Ancient Confucians studied extensively the articles in the "Six Arts". "Six Arts" is a classic of the Wang Sect. It was used by the sages to clarify the Tao, correct human relations, and achieve great governance for the world. Zhou Dao was in decline, bad at the time of Youli, and the conquests of ritual and music came from the princes. Confucius rose up after the decline for more than two hundred years. Because of his saintly virtue, he encountered the end of time, wise words were not used, and the road was impassable, so he sighed: The phoenix and the bird will not come, and the river will not flow out of the map. Let me forget it! King Wen is dead, doesn't this matter about the article? So he applied for a job among the princes to pay courtesy and do justice. He entered the Zhou Dynasty in the west and Chu in the south. He was frightened by Kuang and was short of food at Chen. He went to pay homage to more than seventy kings. When we all heard the music of "Shao", we didn't know the taste of meat in March. After returning from Wei to Lu, the music was revised, and "Ya" and "Song" each found their place. After exploring ancient and modern books, he praised: Yao was so great as a monarch! Only Heaven is the greatest, and Yao imitated it. How high his achievements are, and how beautiful his rituals and music are! He also said: Zhou pursues the second generation and his articles are prosperous. I agree with Zhou. Therefore, the entire review of "Books" begins with "Yao Dian", "Shao Wu" is used as the method for describing music, and "Zhou Nan" is used as the starting point for discussing "Poetry". Connected with the Zhou rites and following Lu's "Spring and Autumn", the actions of the twelve princes were listed, using the civil and military methods as the standard, and became a unified king's law until Huolin. In his later years, he liked "Yi". He read "Yi" so many times that the belt connecting the bamboo slips was broken several times, so he wrote a biography for it. They all use the events of modern saint kings to establish the teachings of the previous kings. Therefore, it is said: inheritance without innovation, integrity but love of the past; study personnel at the bottom, and reach destiny at the top. It is probably God who knows me! After the death of Confucius, the seventy disciples scattered among the princes. Those with higher positions became masters of ministers and ministers, while those with lower positions became mentors and friends of scholar-bureaucrats. Some of them retired from the world and became invisible.
target: The history and transmission of Confucian classics from ancient times through the Han dynasty. Ancient Confucians studied the "Six Arts," a classic of the Wang Sect used by sages to clarify the Tao, correct human relations, and achieve governance. During the decline of Zhou Dao, Confucius emerged after more than two hundred years. Due to his saintly virtue but encountering difficult times, he sighed about the phoenix not coming and the river not flowing out the map. He traveled among princes, entering Zhou in the west and Chu in the south, facing hardships like being frightened in Kuang and short of food in Chen. He revised music after returning from Wei to Lu, ensuring "Ya" and "Song" found their places. He explored ancient and modern books, praising Yao and Zhou, and reviewed the "Books," "Shao Wu," and "Zhou Nan." He connected Zhou rites with Lu's "Spring and Autumn," listing actions of twelve princes using civil and military methods as standards. In his later years, he liked "Yi," reading it so much that the bamboo slip bindings broke several times, and he wrote a biography for it. After Confucius's death, his seventy disciples scattered among princes, with some becoming masters and others mentors.

source: For example, Tian Zifang, Duan Qianmu, Wu Qi, Qin Hua Ya, etc. were all trained by Zixia's generation and became the king's teachers. At this time, only Wei Wenhou was eager to learn. source: Gongsun Hong was born in Xue County, Sichuan State. He worked as a jailer when he was young. Removed from office for committing a crime. Because his family was poor, he made a living by herding pigs on the beach. When he was in his forties, he began to study "Spring and Autumn" and miscellaneous treatises of various schools. When Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty first came to the throne, he recruited virtuous and literary people. At this time, Gongsun Hong was sixty years old and got a doctorate as a virtuous and literary person. He was sent as an envoy to the Huns and returned to the court to report, which was not in line with the emperor's wishes. Emperor Wu was very angry and thought he was incompetent, so Gongsun Hong wrote a letter claiming to be ill and was dismissed from office and returned to his hometown. In the fifth year of Yuanguang, Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty once again selected virtuous literary people, and Dong Weihui once again recommended Gong Zhucong.
target: Gongsun Hong, born in Xue County, Sichuan State, began his career as a jailer but was dismissed for a crime. Left impoverished, he herded pigs until his forties, when he started studying the "Spring and Autumn" and various philosophical texts. At sixty, he was recruited as a virtuous and literary person under Emperor Wu of Han, but his mission to the Huns displeased the emperor, leading to his dismissal. In the fifth year of Yuanguang, he was recommended again and, despite initial reluctance, presented a detailed policy response.

id: 汉书/传/公孙弘卜式儿宽传::group-001

source: Gongsun Hong once again wrote to Shu and said: Your Majesty has the position of the First Sage but not the reputation of the First Sage, and has the reputation of the First Sage but does not have the officials of the First Sage. Therefore, your Majesty is in the same situation as the First Sage, but the results of his governance are different. In the past, the officials were honest, so the people were loyal; now, the officials are greedy, so the people are vulgar. Bad politics will not be implemented, and hateful laws will not be obeyed. Appointing corrupt officials to implement bad governance and using abhorrent laws to govern vulgar people will make it impossible for the people to be educated, which is why different governance results will occur.
target: His essay emphasized governance through righteousness, trust, and eight principles: appointing by talent, avoiding useless discussions, reducing taxes, not harming agriculture, promoting the virtuous, rewarding merit, punishing crime appropriately, and rewarding virtue.

source: The above four articles are the fundamental principles and methods for governing the world. They should all be formulated and implemented and cannot be abandoned. If you master the key points, the world will be happy and peaceful. Although the criminal law is established, it will not be used because no one breaks the law. If you cannot master these methods, the emperor will be deceived and the officials will cause chaos. The gains and losses of these things are the basis for inheriting and continuing the achievements of our ancestors. I heard that there were floods in Yao's time and he sent Yu to control them. I didn't hear that there were floods when Yu was in charge of the world. As for the drought in the Shang Tang era, it was caused by the remnants of Xia Jie. Xia Jie and Shang Zhou implemented evil policies and were punished by heaven; Dayu and Shang Tang did good deeds and accumulated virtue, so they became kings of the world. From this point of view, God does not have personal preferences, likes and dislikes. If you comply with God's virtues, harmony will prosper. If you go against the grain, disasters will happen. Creation is the law of astronomy, geography, and human affairs. I am foolish and reckless, and I am not qualified to answer the emperor's policy questions. At that time, there were more than a hundred people who responded to the imperial edict. When Taichang reported the results of the edict, Gongsun Hong was ranked lower. After the strategy slip was presented to the emperor, the emperor selected Gongsun Hong's strategy as the first. Gongsun Hong was summoned to see him. The emperor saw that he was a talented person, so he appointed him as a doctor and waited for the Shao Jin Ma Alliance. Gongsun Hong once again wrote to Shu and said: Your Majesty has the position of the First Sage but not the reputation of the First Sage, and has the reputation of the First Sage but does not have the officials of the First Sage. Therefore, your Majesty is in the same situation as the First Sage, but the results of his governance are different.
target: He argued that harmony between heaven and earth arises from unified virtue, and that floods and droughts under Yu and Tang were due to prior misrule. His response was ranked first by the emperor, who appointed him as a doctor.

source: Whenever there was a political meeting in the court, Gongsun Hong would state his opinions and let the emperor make his own choice, rather than refute or argue face to face in the court. From this, the emperor saw that his behavior was cautious and honest, he left room for debate, he was familiar with documents, laws and official duties, and he decorated it with Confucianism, so he liked him very much and promoted him to Zuo Neishi within a year. When Gongsun Hong went to court, he did not argue in court if he thought something was wrong.
target: Gongsun Hong rose quickly, becoming Zuo Neishi within a year, known for cautious debate and Confucian decorum.

source: As one of the Three Lords, using a cloth quilt is indeed a pretense and deception, in order to gain fame and reputation. I heard that when Guan Zhong was the prime minister of Qi, he married three women with different surnames. His luxury was comparable to that of a monarch. Duke Huan of Qi relied on his assistance to dominate, but he was against an arrogant king. Yan Ying served as Qi Jinggong's prime minister. He did not eat two portions of meat and vegetables for one meal, and his concubines did not wear silk clothes. Qi State was also governed very well. He was looking down on the common people. Now I, Gongsun Hong, serve as the imperial censor. I use cloth quilts to eliminate the distinction between high and low officials from Jiuqing to the junior officials. It's exactly what Ji An said. Besides, without Ji An, how could your Majesty hear what I said? The emperor thought he could be polite and respected him more and more. During the Yuanshuo period, Gongsun Hong replaced Xue Ze as prime minister. In the original Han Dynasty, princes were generally appointed as prime ministers. Only Gongsun Hong did not have a title. The emperor issued an edict: "I admire the way of governing the country by the sages. I open the door wide and recruit wise men from all over." In ancient times, positions were arranged according to merit, and different palace positions were awarded based on talents. People with great merits received generous salaries, and people with high virtues received prestigious titles. Therefore, those with martial arts were promoted, and those with literary virtues were praised. We hereby order that 650 households in Pingjin Township, Gaocheng County, be granted to Prime Minister Gongsun Hong and be granted the title of Marquis of Pingjin.
target: He avoided court confrontations, often aligning with the emperor’s wishes, which drew accusations of hypocrisy from Ji An. Gongsun Hong defended himself, and the emperor favored him more. He served as imperial censor and later prime minister, receiving the title Marquis of Pingjin. Despite his high rank, he lived frugally, eating simple meals and using cloth quilts, spending his salary on guests and relatives.

id: 汉书/传/公孙弘卜式儿宽传::group-005
article_path: 汉书/传/公孙弘卜式儿宽传
source: This became the system thereafter. The promotion of officials to prime minister and the title of marquis began with Gongsun Hong. At that time, when the emperor was making great achievements, he repeatedly selected virtuous people. Gongsun Hong stood out because he was the first to take countermeasures. He was dressed in white cloth, and a few years later he was promoted to prime minister and was granted the title of marquis. For this reason, he built a guesthouse, opened the gates, invited wise men, and discussed matters with them. Gongsun Hong himself only ate a meat dish and brown rice for each meal. His relatives, friends and guests all relied on him to provide food and clothing. As a result, he spent all his salary and there was nothing left at home. But he has a jealous temperament, and is gentle on the outside but deep inside. Those who have had quarrels with Gongsun Hong, no matter near or far, although he is friendly to them on the surface, they will always seek revenge in the end. It was Gongsun Hong's idea to kill his father Yan and demote Dong Zhongshu to Jiaoxi. Later, the King of Huainan and the King of Hengshan rebelled, and when the court was severely investigating their accomplices, Gongsun Hong fell seriously ill. He felt that he had done nothing, so he was granted the title of marquis and held the position of prime minister. He should assist the wise emperor to calm down and pacify the country, so that people would follow the moral principles of a minister.
target: However, he was inwardly vengeful, contributing to the downfall of rivals like Dong Zhongshu. During the Huainan and Hengshan rebellions, he fell ill and offered to resign, but the emperor refused, granting him leave. He died in office at eighty.

source: He was appointed prime minister and granted the title of marquis, but he covered himself with quilts, ate brown rice, and used his salary to provide for old guests, so that he had nothing left. The food and clothing he enjoys are below the standards stipulated by the system. It can be said that they use themselves as an example to promote simple folk customs, which is completely different from those who hide their wealth but dress frugally on the surface to gain a false reputation. It is the law of the Holy King to guide by commending virtues and righteous deeds and encourage changes in secular folk customs. The direct descendants of Gongsun Hong were given the title of Marquis of Guannei, with a settlement of 300 households. Bu Shi, from Henan. The occupation is farming and animal husbandry. He had a younger brother. When he grew up, Bu Shi separated from his family and took over a hundred sheep. He gave all his farm, house and property to his younger brother. Bu Shi had been tending sheep in the mountains for more than ten years, and there were more than a thousand sheep, so he bought a farm and a house. But his younger brother went bankrupt, and Bu Shi immediately distributed the property to his younger brother. This happened many times. At that time, the Han Dynasty was resisting the invasion of the Huns, and Bu Shi wrote a letter willing to donate half of his family wealth to help the border affairs.
target: Bu Shi, a farmer and herder from Henan, donated half his wealth to support border campaigns against the Xiongnu, but Gongsun Hong advised against accepting, calling it irregular. Later, during a famine, Bu Shi gave 200,000 yuan to aid refugees, earning imperial recognition.

source: At first, Bu Shi was unwilling to become a husband. The emperor said, "I have sheep in Shanglin Garden, and I want you to graze them." After Bu Shi became a Langguan, he still wore commoners and straw sandals to herd sheep. After more than a year, the sheep became fat and multiplied. The emperor passed by the sheep herding field and praised him very much. Bu Shi said: Not only shepherding sheep, but also governing the people. Live on time, get rid of the bad ones immediately, and don't let them harm others. The emperor was surprised by his words and wanted him to try to govern the people. Renbu Shi was appointed as the Feng family order, and the Feng family was in great control; he was moved to the Gao order to be in charge of water transportation, and he was the best in the assessment. The emperor was honest and honest in his divination style, and he became the Tutor of the King of Qi, and then became the Prime Minister. When Lu Jia rebelled, Bu Shi wrote: I heard that the Lord was ashamed and I died.
target: He was appointed as a langzhong to herd sheep in Shanglin Garden, where he excelled. The emperor, impressed, made him a magistrate, then tutor to the King of Qi, and eventually prime minister. During the Lu Jia rebellion, Bu Shi offered to fight, but the emperor honored him instead. As imperial censor, he criticized salt and iron taxes, displeasing the emperor, and was demoted.

source: Kuan is a gentle man, honest and wise, capable of self-defense, good at writing, weak in martial arts, and unable to express himself verbally. At that time, he was appointed as a Tingwei, and the Tingwei government was full of officials of literature, history and law, but Zhe was among them as a Confucian scholar. He showed that he was not familiar with affairs and could not be a low-level official. He was appointed as a Congshi and went to Jidian to guard livestock for several years. Returning to the mansion, he submitted the livestock register. When the imperial officer encountered a problem, the memorial had been returned many times, and the officials did not know what to do. Ni Kuan explained to him how to write it, and the officials asked Ni Kuan to write the memorial. After the performance was completed, everyone who read it was convinced and told the official Zhang Tang. Zhang Tang was shocked and called Ni Kuan to talk. He appreciated his talent and appointed him as his assistant. Submit the memorial written by Ni Kuan and get immediate permission. The next day, Zhang Tang met with the emperor. Asked: The last memorial was beyond the reach of ordinary officials. Who wrote it? Zhang Tang said it was Ni Kuan. The emperor said: I have heard of him a long time ago. Zhang Tang yearned for learning from then on, and appointed Ni Kuan as an official to report cases. He used the meaning of ancient law to judge difficult cases, which was very popular. When he went to Zhangtang, he was appointed as the official censor, Ni Kuan was appointed as a subordinate official, and he was promoted to serve as the censor. Meet the emperor and talk about Confucian classics. The emperor was delighted and asked about another article in "Shang Shu". He was promoted to Zhongdafu and moved to Zuo Neishi. After being leniently appointed to the post of civil administration, he encouraged farming, reduced sentences and punishments, and managed prison litigation. He was courteous to his subordinates and devoted himself to winning the hearts of the people. He chose benevolent people, treated his subordinates favorably, and did not seek reputation. The officials and the people were extremely trustworthy and loved.
target: Ni Kuan, a scholar of "Shangshu," worked as a farmer while studying. He became a Tingwei official, known for his writing and legal expertise. Promoted by Zhang Tang, he served as Zuo Neishi, where he encouraged farming, reduced punishments, and built irrigation canals.

source: The emperor then ordered Ni Kuan, Sima Qian and others to jointly establish the Han Taichu Calendar. See "Lü Li Zhi" for details. At the beginning, Chu Da, the Prime Minister of Liang State, was proficient in the Five Classics and was a doctor. At that time, Ni Kuan was his disciple. When there was a vacancy for the imperial censor, Chu Da came to take up the post. Chu Da thought he was qualified to be the censor. When he arrived in Luoyang, he heard that Ni Kuan had taken office, and Chu laughed. When he arrived at the court and discussed with Ni Kuan in front of the emperor, Chu was not as good as Ni Kuan, so he stood back and said in admiration: Your Majesty really knows people. Ni Kuan was the imperial censor. Because he was satisfied with his position, he did not give any advice to the emperor for a long time, and his officials despised him. He reigned for nine years and died in office. Zan said: Gongsun Hong, Bu Shi and Ni Kuan all used Hongjian's wings to be trapped in the sparrows, traveling far between sheep and pigs. How could they have reached this point without luck? At that time, the Han Dynasty had been prosperous for more than sixty years. The country was stable and the treasury was abundant. However, the four sides were not convinced and there were many systems lacking.
target: When dismissed for poor tax collection, the people paid their debts, restoring his position. He advised on the Fengshan ceremonies, supporting the emperor’s plans, and helped establish the Taichu calendar. As imperial censor, he became complacent and died in office after nine years. The text concludes that Gongsun Hong, Bu Shi, and Ni Kwan rose from humble origins due to the Han dynasty’s prosperity under Emperor Wu, who recruited diverse talents.

source: At that time, the Han Dynasty had been prosperous for more than sixty years. The country was stable and the treasury was abundant. However, the four sides were not convinced and there were many systems lacking. The emperor had just started a great civil and military undertaking, but he could not find the talents he asked for, so he started to use a pulsar cart to welcome Mei Cheng, and sighed when he saw his master's father dying. The people were envious and yearned for it, and strange people and talents appeared at the same time. Bu Shiba was promoted from herding, Hongyang was promoted from the Jia people, Wei Qing was promoted from the slaves, and Jin Yuechan was promoted from the captives. These are the ancient version of building and selling cattle.
target: This era saw a flourishing of Confucians, loyalists, legalists, writers, and generals, achieving great deeds.
