source: Zhu Maichen and others raised ten questions, but Gongsun Hong could not refute any of them. So he apologized to the emperor and said: I am a vulgar person from Shandong. I don't understand how beneficial it is to establish Shuofang County. I hope to stop moving to Southwest Yi and Canghai County and focus on running Shuofang County. The emperor then agreed to his request. Ji An said: Gongsun Hong is ranked among the three nobles and has a lot of salary, but he uses cloth to make quilts. This is hypocrisy.
target: Later, under Emperor Xuan, similar talents emerged, but none matched the brilliance of Emperor Wu’s reign.

source: Feng Fengshi, courtesy name Ziming, was a native of Lu County, Shangdang County, and later moved to Duling. His ancestor Feng Ting was the governor of Shangdang County in South Korea. Qin attacked Shangdang and blocked the passage in the Taihang Mountains. South Korea could not defend it, so Feng Ting dedicated Shangdang City to Zhao and defended it. The State of Zhao granted Feng Ting the title of Lord of Huayang, and together with General Zhao Kuo of the State of Zhao, he resisted the State of Qin and died in battle in Changping. Since then, the Feng family has dispersed in various places, some staying in Lu County and some traveling to other places. Those in Zhao became official generals, and the sons of official generals became prime ministers of the country. After Qin destroyed the six kingdoms, Feng Ting's descendants Feng Wuze, Feng Quji, and Feng Jie all became Qin's generals. After the rise of the Han Dynasty, Feng Tang was very famous during the reign of Emperor Wen. He was the son of the Prime Minister of Dai. By the end of Emperor Wu's reign, Feng Fengshi was elected as a Langguan because he was a son of a good family. During the reign of Emperor Zhao, he was appointed as the Chang Palace of Wu'an County in accordance with the size and order of his achievements. When he was dismissed from office, he was already in his thirties. He only studied "Spring and Autumn", studied its subtle meanings, read the art of war, and knew its contents and examples. Former general Han Zeng reported to him and appointed him as the military commander. During this period, he accompanied the army to attack the Xiongnu. After the war, he became a Langguan again. Prior to this, the Han Dynasty sent envoys to the Western Regions several times, but most of them failed to fulfill their mission, some were corrupt, and some were made difficult and insulted by foreign countries. At this time, the Wusun Kingdom was very powerful and had the merit of attacking the Xiongnu. At the same time, the countries in the Western Regions had just reconciled with the Han Dynasty. The Han Dynasty was preparing to treat them well. If they wanted to take the opportunity to appease these countries, they selected people who could be sent as envoys to foreign countries. Former general Han Zeng recommended Feng Fengshi to escort guests from Dawan and other countries back home as an envoy. When they arrived at Yixiu City, Captain Song said that the Shache people, together with some other countries, had attacked and killed King Wannian of Shache appointed by the Han Dynasty, and also killed Xi Chongguo, the envoy of the Han Dynasty. At this time, the Xiongnu sent troops to attack Cheshi City again, but they went back because they failed to capture it. The Shache Kingdom sent envoys to threaten that the Northern Kingdoms had belonged to the Xiongnu. At that time, they attacked and plundered the Southern Kingdoms, and made a blood alliance with them to betray the Han Dynasty, cutting off all traffic from the Shanshan Kingdom to the west. The Protector Zheng Ji and the Colonel Sima Yi were both trapped among the countries on the North Road. Feng Fengshi discussed with his deputy Yan Lu and believed that if they did not attack quickly, the Shache Kingdom would become increasingly powerful, making the situation difficult to control and jeopardizing the entire Western Region. So he notified the kings by envoys and mobilized their armies. A total of 15,000 people from the north and south attacked the Shache Kingdom and captured its city. King Shache committed suicide and his head was sent to Chang'an. All the countries were pacified, and Feng Fengshi's reputation shocked the Western Regions. Feng Fengshi withdrew his troops and returned home, reporting the situation to the court. Emperor Xuan summoned Han Zeng and said: Congratulations to the general on the competent person he recommended. Feng Fengshi traveled west to the Kingdom of Dayuan. The Kingdom of Dawan heard that he had killed King Shache and respected him more than other envoys. After getting the famous horse Xianglong from Dayuan, he returned to Chang'an.
target: Feng Fengshi, courtesy name Ziming, was a native of Lu County in Shangdang, later moving to Duling. His ancestor Feng Ting, governor of Shangdang under South Korea, surrendered the city to Zhao during Qin's invasion and died at Changping. The Feng family dispersed; some became officials in Zhao, and after Qin's unification, descendants like Feng Wuze served as Qin generals. Under Han, Feng Tang gained fame under Emperor Wen. Feng Fengshi was elected as a Langguan under Emperor Wu, later serving as a military commander under General Han Zeng, accompanying campaigns against the Xiongnu. During Emperor Xuan's reign, Feng Fengshi was sent as an envoy to the Western Regions. At Yixiu City, he learned that the Shache Kingdom had killed Han-appointed King Wannian and envoy Xi Chongguo, while the Xiongnu attacked Cheshi. Shache threatened the southern kingdoms, cutting off traffic from Shanshan westward. Protector Zheng Ji and Colonel Sima Yi were trapped. Feng Fengshi, with deputy Yan Lu, mobilized 15,000 troops from northern and southern kingdoms, attacked Shache, and captured its city. King Shache committed suicide, and his head was sent to Chang'an. Feng Fengshi's reputation spread across the Western Regions. After returning, Emperor Xuan praised Han Zeng for his recommendation. Feng Fengshi later obtained a famous horse from Dayuan.

source: Feng Fengshi withdrew his troops and returned home, reporting the situation to the court. Emperor Xuan summoned Han Zeng and said: Congratulations to the general on the competent person he recommended. Feng Fengshi traveled west to the Kingdom of Dayuan. The Kingdom of Dawan heard that he had killed King Shache and respected him more than other envoys. After getting the famous horse Xianglong from Dayuan, he returned to Chang'an. The emperor was very happy and issued an order to discuss the matter of rewarding Feng Fengshi. The prime minister and the generals all said: The meaning of "Spring and Autumn" is that when an official is on a mission abroad, if he encounters something that is beneficial to the country, he can take matters into his own hands. Feng Fengshi's contribution is particularly significant, and he should be awarded a title and land. Xiao Wangzhi, the Shaofu, believed that Feng Feng was on an envoy mission and had his mission, but he pretended to be the emperor's order and went against the will and sent troops from various countries. Although he had merit, he should not be used as an example for future generations. If Feng Fengshi is to be rewarded, it will open the door for future envoys to use Feng Fengshi as an example to mobilize armies, claim credit and reward from thousands of miles away, and cause trouble for the country among the Yi and Di tribes. This is an unacceptable example, and Feng Fengshi should not be rewarded. The emperor thought Xiao Wangzhi's suggestion was good, and granted Feng Fengshi the titles of Doctor Guanglu and Captain Shuiheng.
target: The court debated rewards: the prime minister and generals favored a title, but Shaofu Xiao Wangzhi argued against it, citing the precedent of unauthorized military action. The emperor agreed, granting Feng Fengshi the titles of Doctor Guanglu and Captain Shuiheng.

source: War is a dangerous thing, and there will definitely be success or failure. I am afraid that the strategy is not agreed upon in advance, and it is not prudent to understand the enemy's situation, so I send General Fenwu. The Art of War says that when a general goes on an expedition, he must have a supporting general to show off his power and provide advice. What doubts does the general have? Care for the soldiers, gain military morale, and you will not regret your decision. You must be thorough in capturing the enemy. This is the responsibility of the general. As for the transportation costs, special officials are responsible for them, so the general does not have to worry. Wait until General Fenwu's troops arrive and attack the Qiang bandits together. In October, the army gathered in Longxi County. In November, attack together. The Qiang thieves were defeated and thousands of their heads were beheaded, while the rest fled across the border. When the outcome of the war was still undecided, the Han Dynasty recruited another 10,000 soldiers and appointed Han Anguo, the prefect of Dingxiang, as General Jianwei. Before setting off, I heard that the Qiang rebels had been defeated. The emperor said: The Qiang rebels were defeated and punished, and fled from the border. Those soldiers who had a truce should leave more field guards to defend key points. In February of the next year, Feng Fengshi returned to the capital and was appointed General Zuo, while Guang Luxun's position remained unchanged. After recording his meritorious service and conferring a title, the emperor issued an edict saying: The Qiang thieves were cruel and cunning, killing officials and common people, attacking Longxi County government offices, burning post houses, and cutting off roads and bridges, which greatly violated the law of heaven. The general of the left, Guang Luxun and Feng Fengshi, led an army to conquer the area, beheading more than 8,000 prisoners and seizing tens of thousands of cattle, horses and sheep. Feng Fengshi was given the title of Marquis of Guannei, a settlement of 500 households, and 60 kilograms of gold. More than thirty generals and lieutenants were rewarded. More than a year later, Feng Fengshi died of illness. He served as a military general for ten years. He was a veteran general who killed enemies and defended the country, and his reputation was second only to Tong Chongguo. General Fenwu was appointed Qianqiu, and his father was appointed to the palace. During Emperor Zhao's reign, he used the prime minister's campaign to capture and kill the rebellious left general Shangguan Jie, and granted him the title of Marquis. Emperor Xuan was appointed Taichang and died. Qianqiu inherited the title and was appointed Taichang. When he became emperor, Wang Shang, the Marquis of Lechang, replaced Feng Fengshi as the left general, while Ren Qianqiu was appointed the right general, and later the left general. Descendants inherited the title from generation to generation until the era of Wang Mang. Two years after Feng Fengshi's death, Gan Yanshou, the governor of the Western Regions, was named a prince because he killed the Zhizhi Chanyu. At that time, Prime Minister Kuang Heng also used Gan Yanshou's counterfeit edicts to cause trouble as an excuse. Based on Xiao Wangzhi's case, he believed that Gan Yanshou should not be made a marquis. However, the commentators all praised Gan Yanshou's achievements, and the emperor followed everyone's opinions and made him a marquis. At that time, Du Qin went to Shangshu and praised Feng Fengshi's previous contributions: In the past, King Yarkand killed the envoys of the Han Dynasty and formed an alliance with other countries to betray the Han Dynasty.
target: Under Emperor Yuan, Feng Fengshi became Jinwu and later Right General of the Dian Kingdom. In the second year of Yongguang, the Qiang rebelled in Longxi. Amid famine, Feng Fengshi volunteered to lead an army, proposing 40,000 troops for a swift campaign. The prime minister and others advocated for only 10,000, but Feng Fengshi warned that insufficient forces would embolden the Qiang and other tribes. He was granted 12,000 troops initially, later reinforced to 60,000 under General Fenwu Ren Qianqiu. After initial defeats, the combined forces defeated the Qiang in November, beheading thousands and driving the rest across the border. Feng Fengshi was appointed General Zuo and Marquis of Guannei with 500 households and gold. He died of illness over a year later, having served as a military general for ten years, with a reputation second only to Tong Chongguo. After Feng Fengshi's death, Gan Yanshou was made a marquis for killing the Zhizhi Chanyu. Du Qin later petitioned, arguing that Feng Fengshi's similar merits had been overlooked due to Xiao Wangzhi's precedent, creating inconsistency in rewards. The emperor declined to revisit the matter.

source: Feng Fengshi relieved the danger, risked his life in the battle, completed the mission with extraordinary achievements, and achieved a remarkable reputation. He was a model for generations of envoys, but he was suppressed and did not praise him. This is not the meaning of a sage monarch who eliminates doubts and encourages integrity. I hope it will be handed over to the relevant departments for discussion. The emperor believed that this was a matter of the late emperor's time, so he no longer accepted his opinion. Feng Fengshi had nine sons and four daughters. The eldest daughter Feng Yuan was elected to the palace as Emperor Yuan Zhaoyi and gave birth to Prince Xiao of Zhongshan. After the death of Emperor Yuan, Feng Yuan became the Queen Mother of Zhongshan and followed King Xiao of Zhongshan to the feudal state. Feng Fengshi's eldest son, Feng Tan, was recommended by Taichang as Xiaolian to be a Langguan, and he was appointed Tianshui Sima in order of merit. Feng Fengshi attacked Xiqiang. Feng Tan was a captain. He served in the army with his father and died of illness before he was promoted to an official. Feng Tan's younger brothers Feng Yewang, Feng Kui, Feng Li, and Feng Shen all became high officials. Feng Yewang, nicknamed Junqing, studied with a doctor and was proficient in the Book of Songs. When he was young, he was appointed as the crown prince's concubine because his father was an official. When he was eighteen years old, he wrote to the emperor hoping to be tried as the magistrate of Chang'an County. Emperor Xuan was surprised by his ambition and asked Prime Minister Wei Xiang, who thought it was unacceptable. Later, he was appointed Dangyang County Magistrate in order of merit, promoted to Liyang County Magistrate, and transferred to Xiayang County Magistrate. During the reign of Emperor Yuan, he was promoted to the prefect of Longxi County. Because of his outstanding political achievements, he entered the court and served as Zuo Fengyi. For more than a year, the magistrate of Chiyang County, who was not known to be corrupt, despised King Feng Ye as a young relative, and did not correct his misdeeds in governance. King Feng Ye deployed the postal supervisor Zhao Du from Touxu County to file a case for investigation and found out that the person in power was responsible for stealing ten gold coins from himself and arrested him. When he refused to obey the arrest, Zhao Duge killed him. Bing's family wrote a letter stating their grievances, and the matter was handed over to Tingwei. Zhao Du committed suicide in front of the officials to prove that he had nothing to do with King Feng Ye. People in the capital praised his prestige and promoted him to Dahonglu. A few years later, the imperial censor Li Yanshou died of illness, and many officials recommended King Feng Ye to succeed him.
target: Feng Fengshi had nine sons and four daughters. His eldest daughter Feng Yuan became Emperor Yuan's Zhaoyi and mother of Prince Xiao of Zhongshan. His sons—Feng Tan, Feng Yewang, Feng Kui, Feng Li, and Feng Shen—all held high offices. Feng Yewang, known for his character, was recommended for high posts but was passed over due to his sister's imperial favor, leading him to lament that their family was humbled by her status. He later served as prefect of several commanderies but was dismissed after being implicated in a political dispute.

source: At first, King Feng Ye inherited his father's title as Marquis of Guannei and was dismissed from his post and returned home. A few years later, he died at home of old age. His son Feng Zuo inherited the title, but his grandson was stripped of his title because of the case of being the Queen Mother of Zhongshan. Feng Kui's courtesy name is Zichan, and he is familiar with the Book of Changes. Taichang inspected those who were filial and honest and appointed them as Langguan, and supplemented those who were appointed as Ye. During the Jianzhao period, he was elected as Futu Xiaowei. Guang Luxun recommended him as a scholar in Yong and appointed him as the magistrate of Meiyang County. In order of merit, he was promoted to Sima of Changle Palace Guards, Captain of Qinghe County, and Prefect of Longxi County. His governance was honest and fair, and he died in his forties. When he was the captain, he had some ideas about regulating the embankment of the Yellow River. For details, see the book "Gou Xi Zhi". Feng Li, also known as Shengqing, was proficient in the Spring and Autumn Annals. Because of his father's relationship, he was appointed as Lang Guan, and then promoted to Cao Guan. During the Jingning period, because he was the uncle of the state, he was appointed as the captain of the vassal state of Wuyuan County. A few years later, he was promoted to the prefect of Wuyuan County, and then to the prefect of Xihe County and Shang County. Feng Li was fair and honest as an official, and his political performance was roughly the same as that of King Feng Ye. He was often wise, generous and kind to others, and liked to formulate rules and regulations. The officials and the people praised Feng Yewang and Feng Li for being the prefects before and after. They praised them by saying: Great Feng Jun and Xiao Feng Jun are brothers who serve as prefects. They are smart and wise and love the officials and the people. Their government is like Lu Weide's Hua Gou, Zhou Gong and Kang Shu are still two monarchs. Later he was promoted to the prefect of Donghai County. The local terrain was low and humid, and he suffered from rheumatism. When the emperor heard about the incident, he appointed Feng Li as the governor of Taiyuan. He served as the governor of five counties successively and made political achievements wherever he went. He died in office when he was old. Feng Shen, courtesy name Shuping, was proficient in Shangshu. When he was young, he served as Huang Menlang and worked as a palace guard for more than ten years. Feng Shen is a solemn and serious person, likes to modify his appearance and etiquette, behaves cautiously and honestly, and is very graceful. Feng Shen is Zhaoyi's younger brother. He is cautious and prepared. Because he is serious and awe-inspiring, he cannot be the emperor's close minister.
target: Feng Kui was known for his governance and died in his forties. Feng Li served as prefect of five commanderies, praised for his fairness. Feng Shen, cautious and dignified, was made Marquis of Yixiang but committed suicide under Emperor Ai after being framed for treason, along with seventeen family members. The Feng family then returned to their hometown. The historical commentary laments their tragic fate, comparing it to ancient figures like Boqi and Qu Yuan.

source: The ancestor of the Xiongnu was a descendant of the Xiahou family, named Chunwei. Before Yao, Yu and Shun of the Tang Dynasty, there were Shanrong, Yanyun, Xunzhou and other branches. They lived in the northern border of China and moved along with water, grass and livestock husbandry. Most of the livestock raised are horses, cattle, and sheep. The exotic livestock include camels, donkeys, mules, Yaosao, colts, and Yixi. They migrated in pursuit of water and grass. They did not have cities or agriculture for permanent residence, but they also had separate grazing lands. There are no written books, only words are used for restraint and management. When the men were young, they could ride sheep, draw bows and shoot mice, and learn archery. When they grew up, they could shoot foxes and rabbits, and mostly ate meat. Men in their prime are strong and can bend bows and shoot arrows, so they serve as armored cavalry. The living customs of the Huns were that when there was no war, they would graze and hunt birds and animals as a way of making a living; in case of emergency war, people would practice battle formations to attack and plunder others. This was the nature of the Huns. Their long weapons are bows and arrows, and their short weapons are swords and spears. When fighting, attack if things go well, retreat if things go wrong, and don't be ashamed to run away. If there is a profit, then etiquette and justice will be ignored. The Huns, from the king on down, all eat animal meat, wear animal hides, and wear felt fur. Strong young people eat rich food, and old people eat leftovers. Those who are strong are valued and those who are old and weak are looked down upon. When his father died, his son took his stepmother as his wife; when his brothers died, the surviving ones took their wives as wives.
target: The Xiongnu, whose ancestor Chunwei was a descendant of the Xia dynasty, were a nomadic people living in the northern border of China. They raised horses, cattle, sheep, and exotic livestock, migrating with water and grass without permanent cities or agriculture. They had no written language, relying on oral agreements. Men learned archery from youth, and in adulthood served as armored cavalry. Their customs prioritized the strong, who ate well while the elderly ate leftovers. Upon a father's death, a son married his stepmother; upon a brother's death, the surviving brother married the widow. They had no naming taboos or posthumous titles.

source: More than twenty years later, Rong Zhai went to Luoyi and attacked King Xiang of Zhou Dynasty. King Xiang fled to Panyi in Zheng State. At first, King Xiang of Zhou wanted to attack the State of Zheng, so he married Rong Zhai's daughter as his queen and joined forces with Rong Zhai to attack the State of Zheng. Soon after, Empress Zhai was deposed, and Empress Zhai was very resentful. King Xiang's stepmother was named Empress Hui, and she had a son named Zidai. Queen Hui wanted to make Zidai king. So Empress Hui, together with Empress Zhai and Ziying, responded internally and opened the city gate to welcome Rong Zhai. Rong Zhai therefore attacked the city, defeated and drove away King Xiang, and established Zidai as King of Zhou. At that time, some Rong Zhai were already living in Luhun, and Shu Bian arrived in Wei State, and the invasion became even more severe. King Xiang of Zhou had been wandering for four years, so he sent an envoy to Jin to ask for help. Duke Wen of Jin had just ascended the throne and wanted to establish hegemony, so he sent troops to attack Rong Zhai, killed Zidai, and welcomed King Zhou Xiang back to Luoyi. At this time, Qin and Jin were very powerful. Duke Wen of Jin attacked and expelled Rong Di. Rong Di lived between the Huan River and Luo River in the Xihe River, and they were called Chidi and Baidi. Duke Mu of Qin got Yu Yu, and the eight kingdoms of Xirong surrendered to Qin. Therefore, there are Rong tribes such as Mianzhu, Dengrong and Diyuan living in Longxi. To the north of Qishan, Liangshan, Jinghe and Qihe there are Rong tribes such as Yiqu, Dali, Wushi and Quyan. To the north of Jin there are Rong tribes such as Linhu and Loufan. To the north of Yan there are Donghu and Shanrong. They live scattered in the valley, each with its own leader. There are more than a hundred Rong tribes living together, but they cannot be unified. More than a hundred years later, the Duke of Jin sent Wei Jiang to negotiate peace with Rong Di, and Rong Di began to pay homage to the king of Jin. More than a hundred years later, Tsai Xiangzi led his troops across Juzhu Mountain, conquered and annexed the state of Dai, and approached Hu Xian. Later, Zhao Xiangzi, together with the Han and Wei families, destroyed Zhi, and the three families occupied the land of Jin. In this way, Zhao State occupied Daidi and the area north of Juzhu Mountain, while Wei State occupied Xihe and Shangjun, adjacent to the Rong people. Later, the Rong people in Yiqu built cities for self-defense, while the Qin State slowly encroached on the land of Yiqu. When King Hui arrived, he captured twenty-five cities in Yiqu. King Hui of Qin attacked the State of Wei, and the State of Wei dedicated all the areas of Xihe and Shangjun to the State of Qin. During the reign of King Zhao of Qin, King Yiqurong had an affair with Queen Mother Xuan and gave birth to two sons. Queen Mother Xuan deceived King Yiqurong and killed him in Ganquan, and then raised troops to attack and eliminate Yiqu. Therefore, the Qin State occupied Longxi, Beidi, and Shangjun, and built the Great Wall to resist the Hu people.
target: The text traces the history of interactions between the Xiongnu and various Chinese dynasties, beginning with the Zhou dynasty. The Zhou declined, and Rong and Di tribes frequently attacked. King Xuan of Zhou attacked the Xiongnu, but later King You was killed by Quan Rong. Qin and Jin became powerful, with Duke Mu of Qin conquering Xirong and Duke Wen of Jin expelling Rong Di. During the Warring States period, Qin, Zhao, and Yan built walls to resist the Xiongnu. Qin Shihuang sent Meng Tian to attack the Xiongnu, recovering land south of the Yellow River and building the Great Wall. After Meng Tian's death, the Xiongnu regained strength under Chanyu Touman.

source: King Shuhu became more arrogant and invaded westward. There is an uninhabited wasteland between the Xiongnu and Donghu, which is more than a thousand miles away. The Xiongnu and Donghu each live on one side and set up observation posts. Shuhu sent an envoy to Modu and said: The Huns cannot reach the deserted land guarded by the observation post on the border with us, and we want to occupy it. Mao Dun asked the ministers, and some ministers said: "This is abandoned land, give it to them." After hearing this, Mo Dun was furious and said: Land is the foundation of the country, how can you give it to others! Those who said they could give land to Shuhu were killed. Maodun mounted his horse and ordered his countrymen to kill anyone who retreated, so he went east to attack Donghu. At first Shu Hu looked down upon Mao Dun and took no precautions. When Mao Dun arrived with his troops, he completely defeated and eliminated King Donghu, captured the people of Ding Donghu, and plundered their livestock and products. After returning, he sent troops to the west to drive away the Yuezhi, and to the south he annexed Loufan and the Aries King of Henan. He also completely recovered the Xiongnu territory that Qin sent Meng Tian to invade. Using the original Henan fortress as the boundary with the Han Dynasty, he reached Chaona and Fushi, and then invaded Yan and Dai. At that time, Liu Han was fighting Xiang Yu, and the Central Plains was exhausted by the war, so Maodun was able to become strong and strong, with more than 300,000 warriors who could bend bows, ride and shoot. It was more than a thousand years from Chunwei to Touman. Sometimes the Xiongnu were large, sometimes small, and their residences were scattered and separated. They were so long ago that their lineage inheritance cannot be arranged one by one in order. However, when Maodun became the Chanyu, when the Huns were at their most powerful, all the ethnic minorities in the north were subject to his rule and became enemies of the Chinese ethnic groups in the south. It was only then that its lineage, surnames and official titles could be recorded. The Chanyu's surname was Lyuta, and their people called the king "Pengli Gutu Chanyu". The Huns called the sky "Plough Holder" and the son "Gu Tu". The name "Chanyu" means vast. This name means that the Chanyu is as big as the sky. The Xiongnu had left and right Xian kings, left and right Guli kings, left and right generals, left and right captains, left and right Danghu, and left and right Guduhous.
target: Touman's son, Maodun, trained his cavalry with a signaling arrow, killing his father and establishing himself as Chanyu. Maodun defeated the Donghu, drove away the Yuezhi, and annexed Loufan and the Aries King of Henan, becoming powerful with over 300,000 warriors. The Xiongnu's official structure included left and right kings, generals, and governors, with the Chanyu's surname being Luanti.

source: The Huns often raised troops to fight according to the waxing and waning of the moon. They attacked when the moon was full and retreated when the moon was waning. When they fought, whoever beheaded the enemy would be rewarded with a jug of wine, and the spoils captured would belong to him, and the captured people would be made slaves. Therefore, when they fight, everyone moves forward bravely for the sake of gain, and is good at luring the enemy into the encirclement and then annihilating them. Therefore, when they pursue interests, they fly together like birds; when they are in danger and collapse, they fall apart and disperse. Whoever transports the deceased back during the war will own all the property of the deceased. Later, Maodun Chanyu conquered the northern countries of Hunyu, Qushe, Dingling, Gekun, Xinhua and other countries. At that time, the Hun nobles and ministers all admired Mo Dun and thought he was wise and talented. At this time, the Han Dynasty had just settled down and moved King Han Xin to Daidi and established the capital in Mayi. The Huns laid siege to Mayi, and Han Xin surrendered to the Huns. After the Xiongnu got Han Xin, they led their troops southward across Juzhu Mountain, attacked Taiyuan, and reached the city of Jinyang. Emperor Gao of the Han Dynasty personally led his troops to fight against the Xiongnu.
target: They held annual meetings, had strict laws, and practiced burial with concubines. Maodun later conquered northern countries, and the Han dynasty, under Emperor Gao, made peace through marriage alliances and tribute.

source: During the reign of Emperor Xiaohui and Empress Dowager Lu, Maodun gradually became arrogant and even wrote a letter and sent an envoy to Empress Lu, saying: I am a lonely and helpless monarch. I was born in a humid swamp and grew up in a vast place where cattle and horses are grazed. I have been to the border many times, hoping to visit the Central Plains. Your Majesty, you are an independent king, but you are also lonely and helpless, living alone.
target: During the reign of Empress Dowager Lu, Maodun sent an insulting letter, but she responded diplomatically.

source: Our country has done nothing wrong and should be forgiven. I have two chariots and eight horses for you to ride on. When Mao Dun received a reply, he sent an envoy to apologize and said: "We have never heard of the etiquette of the Central Plains. Fortunately, Your Majesty forgives us." The Xiongnu offered horses, and the Han and the Huns made peace. After Emperor Xiaowen ascended the throne, the marriage was completed. In the summer of the third year, King Youxian of the Xiongnu entered the area south of the Yellow River to harass and invade, so Emperor Wen issued an edict saying: The Han Dynasty and the Xiongnu are brothers and do not invade each other's borders. The Han Dynasty sent a lot of silk, silk, food and other items to the Xiongnu. Now King Youxian has left his country and led his troops to invade our land south of the Yellow River. This is inconsistent with the previous boundaries. The people of King Youxian came and went into our Khotan fortress, hunting down our officials and soldiers, and driving away and violating our ethnic minorities who lived in Shangjun to protect the frontier fortress, so that they could not live in their original places. 匈奴人欺凌殴打我们边地的官吏，进行偷盗，非常傲慢无道，这不是和约所要求的样子。 He ordered the dispatch of 80,000 chariots and cavalry from the border areas to Gaonu, and sent Prime Minister Guan Ying to lead them to attack King Youxian. King Youxian was driven away and escaped from the frontier fortress. Emperor Wen went to Taiyuan to inspect. At this time, the King of Jibei rebelled, and Emperor Wen returned to the capital and stopped the prime minister's military operations against the Huns. The next year, the Chanyu sent a letter to the Han Dynasty saying: The great Chanyu of the Xiongnu established by heaven asked the emperor if he was safe and well. The emperor's previous words about the marriage were consistent with the meaning of the letter, and both parties were very happy.
target: Emperor Wen continued marriage alliances, though the Xiongnu frequently invaded. The Xiongnu Chanyu wrote to the Han, claiming to have conquered the Yuezhi and other states, and sought peace. The Han agreed, sending gifts. After Maodun's death, his son Laoshang Chanyu succeeded. A eunuch, Zhongxing, defected to the Xiongnu and taught them Chinese customs, advising against adopting Han ways. He argued that Xiongnu simplicity and mobility were strengths, while Han complexity led to internal strife.

source: When the Chanyu fled, the Xiongnu soldiers often mixed with the Han army and followed the Chanyu. The Chanyu was unable to meet his own troops for a long time. King Yougu Li thought that the Chanyu was dead, so he proclaimed himself the Chanyu. The true Chanyu later gathered his own tribe, and King Yougu Li removed the title of Chanyu and restored his original title. General Huo Qubing set out from Dai and crossed more than 2,000 miles north to fight with King Zuoxian. The Han army killed and captured more than 70,000 Huns, but King Zuoxian and his generals all escaped. General Hussar built an altar to worship heaven on Langjuxu Mountain and a place to worship on Guyan Mountain. He did not return to the army until he reached Hanhai. After that, the Xiongnu fled far away, and Monan no longer had the royal court of Shan Yu. The Han people crossed the Yellow River and went west from Shuofang to Lingju. They built canals and opened fields everywhere, and set up officials. There were fifty or sixty thousand officials and soldiers. They slowly encroached on the Xiongnu territory, and the land was connected to the north of the Xiongnu's old territory. At the beginning, generals Wei Qing and Huo Qubing of the Han Dynasty sent troops to besiege Shanyu, killing and capturing 89,000 Xiongnu people. Tens of thousands of Han soldiers died, and more than 100,000 Han army horses died. Although the Xiongnu were exhausted and fled far away, the Han army lacked horses and could not pursue them. Chanyu adopted the letter's suggestion and sent an envoy to say good things and ask for a marriage. The emperor handed the matter over to the ministers for discussion. Some of the ministers said that they should make peace with the Huns, while others said that they should be made vassals. Prime Minister Shi Renchang said: The Xiongnu were newly defeated and tired. They should be allowed to serve as foreign ministers and go to the frontier areas to pay homage to the Emperor of the Han Dynasty. The Han Dynasty sent Ren Chang as an envoy to Shan Yu Nahuo. After Shan Yu heard about Ren Chang's idea, he became furious and detained Ren Chang and refused to let him go back. Prior to this, the Han Dynasty also recruited and surrendered some Huns envoys, and the Chanyu always detained the Han Dynasty's envoys to compensate. The Han Dynasty was mobilizing troops and horses, but Huo Qu, the general of the Hussars, died of illness. Therefore, the Han Dynasty did not attack the Xiongnu in the north for a long time.
target: Under Emperor Wu, the Han attempted to ambush the Xiongnu at Mayi but failed, leading to open conflict. The Han sent multiple campaigns, with generals like Wei Qing and Huo Qubing achieving victories, killing tens of thousands of Xiongnu and capturing their kings. The Xiongnu suffered heavy losses and fled north. The Han also expanded into the Western Regions, isolating the Xiongnu from allies. Despite peace negotiations, the Xiongnu continued border raids. The Han detained Xiongnu envoys, and the Xiongnu retaliated.

source: Therefore, the Han Dynasty granted Chang Hui the title of Marquis of Changluo. The number of Xiongnu troops who lost their lives and injuries, as well as the livestock that died due to long-distance migration, are countless. As a result, the Xiongnu declined and were very resentful of Wusun. That winter, Shanyu personally led 10,000 cavalry to attack the Wusun Kingdom. He captured a few old and weak people and wanted to return to the army. At this time, there happened to be heavy snowfall, which was more than ten feet deep in one day. Many of the tribesmen and livestock froze to death, and less than one tenth of them came back alive. So Ding Lingguo took advantage of the Xiongnu's weakness to attack it from the north, Wuhuan State attacked it from Shubian, and Wusun State attacked it from the west. These three countries killed tens of thousands of Huns and robbed tens of thousands of horses, as well as many cattle and sheep. In addition, many people died of starvation, three-tenths of the Xiongnu people died, and five-tenths of the livestock died. The Xiongnu country declined greatly. Those subordinate countries of the Xiongnu rebelled and left one after another, attacking and harassing each other, and no one was able to govern them. Later, the Han Dynasty sent more than 3,000 cavalry, divided into three groups, to attack the Huns together, and captured and brought back thousands of people. In the end, the Xiongnu did not dare to retaliate against the Han Dynasty to compensate for the losses, but wanted to make peace with the Han Dynasty even more, and the borders of the Han Dynasty became peaceful and less troublesome from then on. Hu Yanqian Chanyu died in the seventeenth year of his reign, and his younger brother Zuoxian Wang succeeded him as Chanyu. This is Xulu Quanqu Chanyu.
target: Later, the Xiongnu faced internal strife and external attacks from Dingling, Wuhuan, and Wusun, leading to decline. The Han sent multiple expeditions, further weakening the Xiongnu. The Xiongnu Chanyu sought peace, but the Han demanded the prince as a hostage, which the Xiongnu refused. The Xiongnu continued to raid, but the Han's military campaigns and alliances with Wusun and other states devastated them. The Xiongnu suffered from famine, disease, and livestock losses, with many tribes rebelling or surrendering to the Han.
