source: A few months after Huhanxie Shanyu returned to the royal court, he stopped the war and asked everyone to return to their original places. He summoned his brother Hutuwusi, who was a commoner, and appointed him King Zuoguli. He also sent people to inform the nobles of Youxian, asking them to kill King Youxian. That winter, Dulongqi and King Youxian jointly supported the king Zhu Wanglian and set up the hall as Kenzhouliyu, and sent tens of thousands of troops to the east to attack Huhanxie Chanyu. Huhanxie Chanyu's army was defeated and fled. Tuqi Chanyu returned to the court of the Xiongnu, and appointed his eldest son Dutuwuxi as the king of Zuoguli, and his youngest son Gujiloutou as the king of rightguli, leaving them in the court of the Shanyu. In the autumn of the next year, Tuqi Chanyu appointed King Youaota, the elder brother of the Richu King Xianxian Shan, as the Wujie Captain, and asked them to lead 20,000 cavalry respectively and station them at Shubian to guard against Huhanxie Chanyu. At this time, the king of Hujie from the west came to plan with Weili, and together they slandered the Shanyu of Tu Qi and slandered King Youxian, saying that he wanted to establish himself as a Uprising Chanyu. So Tuqi Chanyu killed King Youxian and his son. Later, Tuqi Chanyu knew that King Youxian had been wronged, so he killed Weili in his own right. Therefore, King Hujie was very frightened, so he betrayed Tuqi Chanyu and ran away, and established himself as Hujie Chanyu. When King Youao Tartar heard about it, he established himself as the chayu chanyu. Wujiu Duwei also established himself as Wujii Chanyu. In this way, the Xiongnu had five chanyus. Tuqi Chanyu personally led his troops eastward to attack Cheli Chanyu, and sent Dulongqi to attack Wujii Chanyu.
target: After Huhanxie Chanyu returned to his court, he ended the war and appointed his brother Hutuwusi as King Zuoguli. He also ordered the killing of King Youxian. That winter, Dulongqi and King Youxian supported Zhu Wanglian as a rival chanyu and attacked Huhanxie, who was defeated and fled. Tuqi Chanyu then took control, appointing his sons as kings. The following autumn, Tuqi Chanyu stationed troops to guard against Huhanxie. Internal strife escalated when King Hujie slandered King Youxian, leading to his execution. This caused King Hujie to flee and declare himself Chanyu, followed by others, resulting in five rival chanyus.

source: Therefore, King Hujie was very frightened, so he betrayed Tuqi Chanyu and ran away, and established himself as Hujie Chanyu. When King Youao Tartar heard about it, he established himself as the chayu chanyu. Wujiu Duwei also established himself as Wujii Chanyu. In this way, the Xiongnu had five chanyus. Tuqi Chanyu personally led his troops eastward to attack Cheli Chanyu, and sent Dulongqi to attack Wujii Chanyu. Both Wujii Chanyu and Chesai Chanyu were defeated and fled to the northwest to join Hujie Chanyu's army, which totaled 40,000 people. King Wujie and King Hujie both removed their titles of Chanyu and worked together to assist Chanyu Cheli. When Tuqi Chanyu heard about it, he sent General Zuo and Duwei with 40,000 cavalry to station in the east to guard against Huhanxie Chanyu. King Xingzhouli himself led 40,000 cavalry to the west to attack Cheli Chanyu. Cheli Chanyu was defeated and fled to the northwest. Tuqi Chanyu led his army to the southwest and garrisoned at Mengdun. The next year, Huhanxie Chanyu sent his younger brother Yougu Li Wang and others to lead troops west to attack Tuqi Chanyu's army stationed in Hedun, killing and plundering more than 10,000 people. When Tu Qi Chanyu heard about it, he personally led 60,000 cavalry to attack Huhanxie Chanyu. They had traveled nearly a thousand miles, but they hadn't arrived yet! In the cricket area, they encountered Huhanxie Chanyu's nearly 40,000 troops. The two sides fought, and Tu Qi Shanyu was defeated and committed suicide. Tsang Longtong escaped with Tu Qi Chanyu's youngest son, Youguli Wang Guzhong Loutou, and surrendered. Cheli Chanyu went east and surrendered to Huhanxie Shanren. Hu Hanxie Shanyu's left-hand general Dan Quli and his father Hu Yingleigu Nie Wenzheng saw Bao Nui in such chaos, so they led tens of thousands of their troops to surrender to the south and surrendered to Forsythia. He also sealed Wu Li Zhou as the new city marquis and Gu Li Wen Chi as the Zhan Wu Fort. At this time, Kui Lu's son supported Zhou Jiedu as Chanyu. Huhanxie Chanyu sent people to hunt and kill them. So Huhanxie Chanyu returned to the court of the Xiongnu. However, there were only tens of thousands of people in his tribe. King Xiu Xun, cousin of Tu Qi Chanyu, led his five or six hundred cavalry to attack and kill Zuo Daqiequ, annexed his army, arrived at Youdi, and established himself as Runzhen Chanyu, living in the west of the Xiongnu. Later, Huhanxie Chanyu's brother Zuoxian King Hutuwusi also established himself as Chanyu, the Marquis of Zhizhigu, and lived in Baosusubu. Two years later, Runzhen Chanyu led his troops to attack Zhizhi Chanyu eastward. Zhizhi Chanyu faced off against Runzhen Chanyu, killed him, annexed his troops, and then attacked Huhanxie Chanyu. The army was defeated, and Zhizhi Chanyu made his capital in the royal court. When Huhanxie was defeated and Huhanxie Shanyu was defeated, King Zuoyi Zhizi made plans for King Lizheng Wuli, and persuaded him to surrender to Han and serve the emperor, so as to seek help from Huansu Nabuo, so that he could stabilize his body. Huhanxie Shanyu discussed with the ministers and asked them. The ministers all said: This cannot be done.
target: Tuqi Chanyu attacked Cheli Chanyu and Wujii Chanyu, both of whom fled to join Hujie Chanyu. Tuqi then sent forces east and west, but Huhanxie Chanyu attacked and killed over 10,000 of Tuqi's troops. Tuqi retaliated with 60,000 cavalry but was defeated and committed suicide. Huhanxie Chanyu's general Dan Quli surrendered to the Han Dynasty. Huhanxie returned to his court with only tens of thousands of followers. Runzhen Chanyu and Zhizhi Chanyu emerged, with Zhizhi killing Runzhen and attacking Huhanxie, who was defeated.

source: At this time, Kui Lu's son supported Zhou Jiedu as Chanyu. Huhanxie Chanyu sent people to hunt and kill them. So Huhanxie Chanyu returned to the court of the Xiongnu. However, there were only tens of thousands of people in his tribe. King Xiu Xun, cousin of Tu Qi Chanyu, led his five or six hundred cavalry to attack and kill Zuo Daqiequ, annexed his army, arrived at Youdi, and established himself as Runzhen Chanyu, living in the west of the Xiongnu. Later, Huhanxie Chanyu's brother Zuoxian King Hutuwusi also established himself as Chanyu, the Marquis of Zhizhigu, and lived in Baosusubu. Two years later, Runzhen Chanyu led his troops to attack Zhizhi Chanyu eastward. Zhizhi Chanyu faced off against Runzhen Chanyu, killed him, annexed his troops, and then attacked Huhanxie Chanyu. The army was defeated, and Zhizhi Chanyu made his capital in the royal court. When Huhanxie was defeated and Huhanxie Shanyu was defeated, King Zuoyi Zhizi made plans for King Lizheng Wuli, and persuaded him to surrender to Han and serve the emperor, so as to seek help from Huansu Nabuo, so that he could stabilize his body. Huhanxie Shanyu discussed with the ministers and asked them. The ministers all said: This cannot be done. The custom of our Huns has always been to advocate bravery and strength, and despise surrender and service to others. We build our own country by fighting others on war horses, so we have high prestige among many ethnic minorities. To die in battle is a heroic act. Now you brothers are competing for the throne. The winner is either the elder brother or the younger brother. Even if he dies in the battle, he still leaves a good reputation of majesty. Your descendants can still dominate the countries and be their kings. Even if the Han Dynasty is very powerful, it cannot annex the Xiongnu. How can we disrupt the system set by our ancestors, surrender to the Han Dynasty, tarnish the reputation of the first Chanyu, and be laughed at by all countries! Even if we did this and pacified the Xiongnu, how could we then dominate the various ethnic minorities and become their rulers? Zuo Yi Zhizi said: What you said is wrong. They were strong at that time and weak at this time, which cannot be said in the same way. Now when the Han Dynasty is prosperous, the countries in the Western Regions that built cities and settled in the country, such as Wusun, all surrendered to the Han Dynasty. Since the time of Qie Qianhou Chanyu, the Xiongnu territory has been invaded day by day, but we have been unable to recover. Although we are still trying to show off our strength here, we have never been quiet for a day. The current situation is: if we serve the Han Dynasty, we can survive safely, otherwise we will only perish. What better strategy can there be than this! Those Xiongnu ministers debated for a long time, and finally Huhanxie Chanyu followed the advice of King Zuoyi Zhizi, led his troops to go south, approached the Han Dynasty frontier, and sent his son Youxian King Zhuo Louqutang to the court to serve the Han emperor. And Zhizhi Shanyu also sent his son Ju Yuli, the right general, to serve the emperor of Han Dynasty.
target: King Zuoyi Zhizi advised Huhanxie to surrender to the Han Dynasty for stability. Despite opposition from ministers who valued Xiongnu martial traditions, Huhanxie agreed and led his people south, sending his son as a hostage. The Han emperor received Huhanxie with great honor, granting him titles, gifts, and troops for protection. Huhanxie requested to stay near the Han border for defense. The Han provided food and military support. Zhizhi Chanyu, meanwhile, moved west, attacking Wusun and other tribes, establishing his capital in Jiankun.

source: Zhizhi Shanyu considered that his own strength could not defeat the Xiongnu, so he went further west and approached Wusun. He wanted to unite with Wusun and sent an envoy to see Xiaokun Miwu and slaughter him. When Wujiutu saw that Huhanye Chanyu was receiving courtesy and help from the Han Dynasty, while Zhizhi Chanyu was on the run, he wanted to attack Zhizhi and cater to the Han Dynasty, so he killed Zhizhi's envoy, sent his head to the Han Dynasty's Western Region Protector, and dispatched eight thousand cavalry to attack Zhizhi. Chanyu Zhizhi saw that Wusun had many soldiers and his envoy failed to return, so he led his army to attack Wusun and defeated Wusun. Taking the opportunity to attack Wujie to the north, Wujie surrendered. He also sent his own troops to the west to conquer Jiankun and to the north to defeat Ding Ling, and annexed these three countries. Zhizhi Chanyu sent troops to attack Wusun many times and often won. Jiankun was seven thousand miles away from the king's court in the east and five thousand miles away from Cheshi in the south. The Zhi branch stayed there and established its capital there. Emperor Yuan had just ascended the throne, and Huhanxie Shanyu wrote to the Emperor of Han again, saying that the people of Baoqu were very poor and impoverished. Xing issued an edict ordering Yunzhong County and Wuyuan County to transport 20,000 hu of grain for packaging. Because his residence was far away from the road of the Han Dynasty, and he was very resentful of the Han Dynasty's support and help to Huhanxie Chanyu, Zhizhi Chanyu sent an envoy to Zhuimou to submit a letter, requesting to take back his son who had become a servant. Xuansu sent Zhuzao to send him back, but Shanyu Zhuzhi killed Gu Ji. The Han Dynasty did not know the news about Gu Ji. The Huns who came to surrender to the Han Dynasty reported that they had heard from the Huns in Ou Tuo that Gu Ji had been killed. Hu Hanxie Chanyu sent envoys to the court, and the Han Dynasty was always very anxious to send documents asking for news about Gu Ji. The next year, the Han Dynasty sent Han Chang, the captain of chariots and cavalry, and Zhang Meng, the Guanglu doctor, to escort Hu Hanxie Shanyu's son, who was serving as a servant, back to the Huns. They also inquired about Gu Ji and others, and announced a pardon for the Huns' sins, lest they worry that the Han Dynasty would attack them. Han Chang and Zhang Meng saw that the Xiongnu tribe was prosperous and that all the animals under the fortress had been hunted down. The Chan Yu was strong enough to defend himself and was no longer afraid of Zhizhi. Han and Zhang heard that many Xiongnu ministers advised the Shanyu to return to the north where they originally lived. They were worried that it would be difficult to govern the Xiongnu after they returned to the north. Han Chang and Zhang Meng made an alliance with the Shanyu, saying: From now on, the Han Dynasty and the Xiongnu are one family, and they are not allowed to deceive or attack each other from generation to generation.
target: Emperor Yuan succeeded and Huhanxie requested aid due to poverty. The Han sent grain. Zhizhi, resentful of Han support for Huhanxie, killed a Han envoy. The Han sent envoys to escort Huhanxie's son back and made an alliance with him, pledging mutual defense. However, Han officials criticized the alliance as unauthorized. Huhanxie eventually returned north, stabilizing his rule. Zhizhi, fearing Han retaliation, moved further west and allied with Kangju, but was later killed by Han forces. Huhanxie, relieved, requested to visit the Han court again.

source: Kangju also sent nobles with thousands of camels, donkeys, and horses to meet Zhizhi. Many of Zhizhi's tribe died of cold and starvation on the road, and finally only 3,000 people were left to reach Kangju. Later, the governor Gan Yanshou and the deputy governor Chen Tang sent troops to Kangju to kill Zhizhi Shanyu. These are recorded in the biographies of Gan Yanshou and Chen Tang. After Zhizhi Chanyu was killed, Huhanxie Chanyu was happy and scared, and wrote to the Emperor Xuan: I often hope to go to see His Majesty, but it is actually because Zhizhi Chanyu lives in the west, and I am worried that he will attack me with Mercer, so I cannot go to see the Emperor. Now that Wai Mu has been convicted and killed, I hope that I can be allowed to come to the court to pay my respects. In the first year of Jingning, Huhanxie Chanyu came to the Han Dynasty again. The Han Dynasty treated him with the same courtesy and rewards as before, and increased the rewards of clothes, brocade, silk, and thick silk and cotton, which were twice as much as in the Huanglong year. Chanyu himself said that he would like to be the son-in-law of the Han Dynasty to get closer to the Han Dynasty. Emperor Yuan of the Han Dynasty gave Shanyu Wang Qiangzi Zhaojun, a good woman who was a servant of the harem, as his wife. The Chanyu was very happy and wrote to the emperor, saying that he was willing to protect the Han Dynasty frontier from Shanggu west to Dunhuang and pass it on forever. He asked the emperor to withdraw the officials and soldiers guarding the border fortress so that the emperor's subjects could rest and recuperate. The emperor handed the matter over to the ministers for discussion, and the ministers in charge thought it was very convenient. Langzhong Linghou should be familiar with the affairs of the frontier fortress and thought that he could not agree to the Huns like this. Emperor Mo Yuan asked him why, and Hou Ying replied: Since the Zhou and Qin Dynasties, the Xiongnu have been very violent and unruly, invading the frontiers. After the establishment of the Han Dynasty, they suffered particularly serious consequences. I heard that our northern border fortress reaches all the way to Liaodong. Outside is the Yinshan Mountains, which is more than a thousand miles long from east to west, with lush vegetation and many animals. This place was originally the place where Maodun Shanyu relied on. He made bows and arrows here, trained his troops, and came in and out of Yinshan to harass us. Yinshan was the garden where they raised animals.
target: In the first year of Jingning, Huhanxie visited the Han court and received generous gifts. He requested to become a Han son-in-law, and Emperor Yuan gave him Wang Zhaojun as a wife. Huhanxie offered to defend the Han border from Shanggu to Dunhuang and asked for the withdrawal of Han border troops. The emperor consulted officials, and Hou Ying argued against withdrawal, citing ten reasons: the strategic value of the Yinshan Mountains, the Xiongnu's untrustworthy nature, the need to prevent internal crime and defections, and the risk of future emergencies. The emperor agreed and declined Huhanxie's request.

source: Shanyu thanked him and said: I don't understand the emperor's profound thoughts, but thanks to the emperor sending ministers to tell me, I am very grateful. At first, King Zuo Yi Zhizi made suggestions for Huhanxie Chanyu and asked him to submit to the Han Dynasty. Later, the Huns finally settled down because of this. Later, some people slandered Yi Zhizi for showing off his achievements and being often unhappy and dissatisfied. Hu Hanxie became suspicious of him. King Zuo Yi Zhizi was afraid of being killed, so he led more than a thousand of his men to surrender to the Han Dynasty. The Han Dynasty made him the Marquis of Dingguannei, with a settlement of 300 households, and allowed him to wear the seal and ribbon of the original king. During the Jingning period, Hu Hanxie Chanyu came to the Han Dynasty to pay homage to the Emperor of Han, and met King Zuoyi Zhizi. The Chanyu apologized and said: "My lord, you planned for me at the beginning. Your kindness and kindness have made us Xiongnu peaceful and peaceful to this day. These are all due to you, lord. How can I forget your kindness?" It was my fault that I lost the favor of the prince and made the prince leave and no longer want to stay in the Huns. These are all my fault. Now I want to talk to the emperor and ask you to return to the court of the Huns. Yi Zhizi said: Shanyu relied on the arrangement of heaven to surrender to the Han Dynasty, and the Huns were at peace. Shanyu is a blessing from the emperor. What credit can I have! Now that I have surrendered to the Han Dynasty, if I return to the Xiongnu, I will be half-hearted. I am willing to be your envoy and stay in the Han Dynasty. If you ask me to go back, I will not obey your order. The Chanyu made repeated requests, but in the end he could not change King Zuoyizhizi's mind, so he returned to the Huns. Wang Zhaojun's title was Ninghu Pi, and he gave birth to a son named Yitu Zhiyaoshi, who was established as King Youri Zhu. Hu Hanxie Shanyu reigned for twenty-eight years and died in the second year of Jianshi. At first, Huhanxie Chanyu doted on the two daughters of King Huyan, brother of Zuoyi Zhizi. The eldest daughter is Zhuanquban, and she gave birth to two sons. The eldest son is named Qiemoche, and the second son is named Nangzhiyasi. The second daughter of King Hu Xian was of the Dapi family, and she gave birth to four sons. The eldest son was called Diao Tao Mogao, and the second son was named Qie Mixu, both of whom were older than Qie Moche. The two younger sons were Xian and Le, both younger than Nangzhi Yasi. There were also more than ten other sons born to Pi. Zhuanquban's family was noble, and Moche was also favored by Shanyu. Hu Hanxie Shanyu was about to die of illness and wanted Qie Moche to succeed him. His mother, Zhuan Qupi, said: The Xiongnu have been in chaos for more than ten years, and this situation cannot be cut off like hair. Fortunately, with the help of the Han Dynasty, the Xiongnu was able to stabilize. The country has not been peaceful for a long time, and many people have been killed and injured in wars. Moreover, Mo Che was still young and the people failed to rally to him. If he were to take the throne, it would probably put the Xiongnu in danger again. Zuo Tiya and I are sisters, and we have the same sons. It would be better to have Tao Mogao carved as a chanyu.
target: King Zuoyi Zhizi, who had advised Huhanxie to submit to Han, later fell under suspicion and surrendered to Han. Huhanxie later apologized and asked him to return, but he refused. Huhanxie died after 28 years, succeeded by his son Diao Tao Mogao as Fuzhuanruo Qianchanyu, following the advice of his mother Zhuanquban to avoid instability. The new chanyu appointed his brothers as kings and continued relations with Han. Subsequent chanyus maintained ties, sending sons as hostages and visiting the Han court.

source: When Xiahou Fan arrived at the Xiongnu, he waited for an opportunity to give advice to Shanyu and said: I saw that the Xiongtan was connected to a steep mountain and entered the Han Dynasty. Facing Zhangye County, there were three captains of the Han Dynasty leading hundreds of soldiers stationed on the tomb. It was very cold and hard, and they had to work hard for a long time on duty. Chanyu, you should write to Emperor Mo to donate this land and give it directly to the border officials. This will save two captains and hundreds of soldiers guarding the Han Dynasty, in order to repay Emperor Mo's kindness to the Xiongnu. The reward from the Han Dynasty must be very generous. Shanyu asked: Is this an edict from the Emperor of the Han Dynasty, or is it a request from the envoy? Xiahou Fan said: This is the emperor's will, but I just came up with a good idea for your sake. The Chanyu said: Emperor Xiaoxuan and Emperor Xiaoyuan took pity on my father, Huhanxie Chanyu, and promised to return the area north of the Great Wall to the Xiongnu. The place they want is where King Wen Outuo lives. I don't know what grows there or what it looks like. Please let me send an envoy to find out.
target: During the reign of Wuzhuliu Chanyu, Han envoy Xiahou Fan requested land from the Xiongnu, but the chanyu refused, citing ancestral rights. The Han emperor punished Xiahou Fan.

source: The Xiongnu killed many people and drove away nearly a thousand women, old people, and children from Wuhuan. They left them in the left area and sent people to tell Wuhuan: "You can redeem your people with horses, animal skins, and cloth." Wuhuan sent more than 2,000 relatives of the robbed people to bring property and livestock to redeem the people. The Xiongnu accepted the property and detained the people. Wang Mang usurped the territory of the Han Dynasty. In the first year of the founding of the People's Republic of China, he sent the five mighty generals Wang Jun and six men, Zhen Fu, Wang Sa, Chen Rao, Bo Chang, and Ding Ye, with a lot of gold, silver, and cloth to give to Shan Yu to inform Shan Yu that Wang Mang had been ordered by heaven to replace the Han Dynasty, and to exchange for Shan Yu's original seal. The original seal text was Xiongnu Chanyuxi, but Wang Mang changed it to New Xiongnu Chanyuzhang. After the generals arrived at the Xiongnu, they represented the imperial court and awarded the Chanyu the seal and ribbon, and Xuan Shao ordered the Chanyu to hand over the original seal and ribbon.
target: Later, conflicts arose over Wusun raids and Wuhuan tax issues. Wang Mang, after usurping the Han throne, changed the Xiongnu seal and imposed new regulations, causing resentment. The Xiongnu resumed border raids.

source: So Wang Mang greatly increased the number of Xiongnu chanyu titles to fifteen, and sent 10,000 cavalry led by Zhonglang General Lin Bao and deputy captain Dai Jie to the border fortress of Yunzhong County with many pearls and treasures. He lured several sons of Huhanxie Shanyu by seduction, hoping to make them chanyus one by one. He sent an interpreter outside the border fortress to lure King Xian of Youli Khan, his sons Deng and Zhu, and three others. After arriving, he was forced to accept the title of Xiao Chanyu, and was rewarded with an An chariot and a drum chariot, one thousand catties of gold, one thousand pieces of miscellaneous silk, and ten halberds with flags. Wang Mang also granted Lin Bao the title of Duke Xuanwei and appointed him General Huya; he conferred the rank of Dai to Duke Yangwei and appointed him General Huben. When the Chanyu heard these things, he said angrily: "The Chanyu has been favored by Emperor Xuan of the Han Dynasty, but he cannot bear the responsibility to the Han Dynasty."
target: Wang Mang's military campaigns failed, leading to chaos. The Xiongnu chanyu died, and his successor Xian sought peace with Han but continued raiding. Wang Mang's attempts to control the Xiongnu through titles and gifts ultimately failed, and the border remained unstable.

source: The ruling minister of the Xiongnu, Hou Xubutang, the right bone capital, was the son-in-law of Wang Zhaojun's daughter Yimo Juciyun. Yun often hoped to make peace with China, and usually had a good relationship with Xian. When she saw that Xian was appointed by Wang Mang, she went beyond her father's will and made Xian the king of Wureruo Qiandan. After Wulei Chanyu Xian ascended the throne, he made his younger brother Yu the king of Zuoguli.
target: After Wang Mang's death, the Han Dynasty restored relations with the Xiongnu, but the chanyu remained arrogant. The historian concludes that peace treaties and military campaigns both had limitations, and the Xiongnu's nature made lasting peace difficult.

source: Kuang Heng, courtesy name Zhigui, was born in Haicheng County, Cambodia. His grandfather had been farming for generations, and when he came to Kuangheng, he liked to study. Because his family was poor, Kuangheng worked as a hired worker to pay for his expenses. Kuang Heng's energy exceeded ordinary people. Many Confucian scholars praised him and said: Don't talk about "Poetry", Kuang Heng will come; Kuang Heng comes to talk about "Poetry", making people happy and laughing. Kuang Heng was awarded the title of "Jia Ke", but because he failed to pass the "Jia Ke" regulations, he was only appointed as Taichang's storyteller, and later he was appointed as "Pingyuan County Literature". Many scholars wrote letters recommending that Kuang Heng was proficient in classics and was unparalleled in the world. He should be appointed as a literary scholar and go to the capital as an official. The younger generation were willing to follow Kuang Heng to study in Pingyuan County. Kuang Heng should not be an official far away from the capital. The emperor handed this matter over to Prince Taifu Xiao Wangzhi and Shaofu Liang Qiuhe for questioning. Kuang Heng answered with the righteousness of the Book of Songs, which was very profound and brilliant. Xiao Wangzhang reported that Kuang Heng was proficient in classics and his lectures were passed down from a teacher's perspective, which can be viewed. Emperor Xuan did not make much use of Confucian scholars, so he sent Kuang Heng back to his original place. However, after the crown prince saw Kuang Heng's correct question, he secretly appreciated him. When Emperor Xuan died and Emperor Yuan ascended the throne, a relative of Leling Marquis Shi Gao was appointed as the Great Sima Cavalry General and concurrently as Minister, with former general Xiao Wangzhi as his deputy. Xiao Wangzhi was a famous Confucian and the emperor's mentor. The emperor valued him and made great contributions in recommending talents. Shi Gao, on the other hand, had no interest in political affairs and only had a reputation, which created a gap between him and Xiao Wangzhi.
target: Kuang Heng, courtesy name Zhigui, was born in Haicheng County. His family had farmed for generations, and despite poverty, he loved studying and worked as a hired laborer to fund his education. His energy exceeded ordinary people, and many Confucian scholars praised him. He was awarded the title of "Jia Ke" but failed to pass its regulations, so he was appointed as Taichang's storyteller and later as Pingyuan County Literature. Scholars recommended him as unparalleled in classical studies, but Emperor Xuan did not favor Confucian scholars and sent him back. However, the crown prince secretly appreciated him. When Emperor Yuan ascended the throne, Shi Gao appointed Kuang Heng as historian of Cao and recommended him to the emperor, who made him a doctor. During disasters like solar eclipses and earthquakes, Kuang Heng submitted a memorial stating that different times required different governance.

source: Nowadays, there is famine every year in Guandong, and the people are poor and impoverished. In some places, people are eating each other. This is because the taxes are too high, the people pay too much, and the officials are incompetent in arranging the people. Your Majesty feared God's warning, cherished and mercied the people, and was very frugal. He reduced the number of guards in Ganquan and Jianzhang Palaces, stopped Zhuya County, stopped using force, and promoted civil rule. He will inherit the prosperity of Yao and Shun and avoid the decline of Yin and Zhou Dynasties. After everyone saw the edict to abolish Zhuya County, everyone was happy. Everyone thought that they were about to see a peaceful and prosperous age. Therefore, Your Majesty should immediately reduce the expenses of the palace and royal family, eliminate the extravagant and gorgeous decorations, revise the rules and regulations, rectify the internal and external affairs of the court, pay more attention to the loyal and upright ministers, alienate the smooth-talking and sycophantic people, prohibit Zheng and Wei Promote the etiquette and music of "Ya" and "Song", recommend people with outstanding talents, open up channels for speaking out, appoint kind and virtuous people, remove cruel and mean officials, commend noble and innocent people, and read "Six The general idea of "Art" is to clearly understand the essentials of governing the country in the past, understand the way of natural change, and promote the atmosphere of harmonious coexistence, so as to promote the supreme benevolent government, correct the corrupt customs, change the desires of the people, and let the world Everyone clearly knows the example set by the imperial court. Let the moral ethos be carried forward in the capital and the good reputation spread abroad. After that, education can be achieved and etiquette and humility can become a common practice. The emperor was very happy after hearing what he said, and promoted Kuang Heng to the rank of Guanglu Doctor and Prince Shaofu. At this time, the emperor liked Confucian scholarship and articles, and made many political changes during the reign of Emperor Xuan. Many people who discussed political affairs in Shangshu were summoned by the emperor, and everyone thought that what they said would be in line with the emperor's wishes. At the same time, because Fu Zhaoyi and his son King Dingtao were favored by the emperor, they surpassed the queen and crown prince.
target: He observed that amnesty did not reduce crime and argued that education should promote etiquette and humility. He criticized corrupt customs, greed, and luxury, urging the emperor to set an example through moral leadership. He cited classical texts to support his arguments and recommended reducing palace expenses, eliminating extravagance, promoting virtuous officials, and reforming education. The emperor was pleased and promoted him to Guanglu Doctor and Prince Shaofu.

source: At the same time, because Fu Zhaoyi and his son King Dingtao were favored by the emperor, they surpassed the queen and crown prince. Kuang Heng went to Shu again and said: I've heard that the key to a country's peace and security lies in examining one's own intentions. Generally speaking, the main task of an emperor who accepts the mandate of heaven is to establish a business and continue the power of the country. The main purpose of a monarch who inherits the system of the previous kings is to inherit and carry forward the virtues of the previous kings and praise the achievements of the previous kings. In the past, when King Cheng of Zhou inherited the throne, he wanted to trace the way of governing the country by King Wen and King Wu of Zhou, so as to cultivate his moral character. All his achievements and reputations were attributed to King Wen and King Wu of Zhou, and he did not dare to enjoy the fame alone. Therefore, God was satisfied with his achievements, and all the ghosts and gods protected him.
target: Kuang Heng frequently advised the emperor on proper conduct, emphasizing that governing a country begins with governing one's family.

source: It is not a needless addition of etiquette styles, but the inner feeling that there is a big difference between the two. Therefore, etiquette is used to express inner feelings and express them in actions. Whether the saint is active or quiet, playing or having fun, the things he comes into contact with, no matter how big or small, high or low, have their own order; things can each get their proper place, the world will be naturally governed, and the people will obey the teachings. People who should be close will be alienated, people who should be respected will be despised, and treacherous and obedient people will take advantage of the opportunity to disrupt the country.
target: He stressed the importance of distinguishing between the queen and concubines and establishing proper hierarchies.

source: The Sutra says: If you manage your family well, then the country will be stable. During the years when Kuang Heng was the Crown Prince and Young Fu, he wrote to the emperor many times to state what the emperor should do. When there were political matters in the court that needed to be discussed, Kuang Heng always answered based on the scriptures and his words were mostly in line with the laws and principles. The emperor thought that he could assume the duties of a public minister, so he appointed Kuang Heng as Guang Luxun and Yushi Dafu. In the third year of Jianzhao's reign, he succeeded Wei Xuancheng as prime minister, was granted the title of Marquis of Le'an, and enjoyed a settlement of 600 households. After Emperor Yuan died and Emperor Cheng ascended the throne, Shangshu Kuang Heng warned the emperor to be careful in choosing a spouse, and explained the rules of Confucian classics and etiquette, saying:
target: After Emperor Cheng ascended the throne, Kuang Heng warned about choosing a spouse according to Confucian etiquette. He later submitted a memorial to renovate suburban temples and cancel extravagant sacrifices.

source: At the beginning of the first month of this year, the emperor will receive congratulations from all officials in the main room, and arrange a banquet to entertain guests from all over the world. "Yi Zhuan" says that a gentleman starts with caution. I hope that your majesty will pay attention to the etiquette of your behavior so that the officials and people can look up to the glory of your noble virtues and establish the foundation for governing the country. In this way, the world will be very lucky! The emperor respected his advice. Soon after, Kuang Heng made a memorial to renovate the northern and southern suburban temples and cancel all kinds of extravagant and extravagant sacrifices. His memorial was recorded in "Jiao Sacrifice Chronicles". When Emperor Yuan was in power, Zhongshu ordered Shi Xian to take charge of court affairs. From the former prime minister Wei Xuancheng to Kuang Heng, everyone was afraid of Shi Xian and did not dare to go against his wishes. When Emperor Cheng first came to the throne, Kuang Heng and the imperial censor Zhen Tan jointly submitted an impeachment report to Shi Xian, investigating his old evil deeds one by one and tracking down his party members. At this time, Wang Zun, the lieutenant of the Sili School, submitted an impeachment report saying: Kuang Heng and Zhen Tan were serving as ministers, and they knew that Shi Xian and others were dictatorial, tyrannical, and a great harm to the country. However, Kuang Heng and Zhen Tan did not file an impeachment report in time to punish them. After impeaching Shi Xian and others, he did not state his crime of disloyalty to the emperor. Instead, he publicized the fault of the late emperor for appointing bad guys who subverted the country and the country. He committed an unethical and grave crime. The emperor issued an edict not to impeach Kuang Heng. But Kuang Heng still felt ashamed and frightened. Shangshu confessed, claimed that he was ill and asked to return to his hometown, and handed over the seal of Prime Minister Le'an Hou.
target: During Emperor Yuan's reign, Kuang Heng feared Zhongshu Ling Shi Xian and did not oppose him. When Emperor Cheng first ruled, Kuang Heng and Zhen Tan impeached Shi Xian, but were themselves impeached for not reporting Shi Xian's crimes earlier. The emperor did not punish Kuang Heng, but he felt ashamed and asked to resign. The emperor refused and encouraged him.

source: Concentrate, take your medicine, eat hard, and take care of your body. He was also rewarded with fine wine and raised beef cattle. Kuang Heng took charge of government affairs again. Because the emperor had just ascended the throne, he praised his ministers a lot, but most of the court officials were people like Wang Zun. Kuang Heng was very uneasy. Every time there were floods, droughts, or bad weather, he would write letters to resign and ask to give up his position. The emperor always comforted and encouraged Kuang Heng with edicts and did not allow Kuang Heng to abdicate in old age. Later, Kuang Heng's son Kuang Chang served as a captain of the Yue Cavalry School. He killed someone while drunk and was imprisoned. Yueqi officials and Kuang Chang's brother prepared to conspire to save Kuang Chang. After the incident was discovered, Kuang Heng took off his official hat and went to plead guilty with bare feet. The emperor sent envoy Shao Ling to restore Kuang Heng's official hat and shoes. However, a supervisor impeached Kuang Heng for monopolizing land theft, and Kuang Heng was implicated and was dismissed from office. At the beginning, Kuang Heng's fiefdom was in Le'an Township, Tong County, Linhuai County. The entire township had a total of 3,100 hectares of farmland, bounded by Fujian and Bai in the south. In the first year of the Chu Yuan Dynasty, the county map of Linhuai County mistakenly identified Min Bai as Pingling Bai. For more than ten years, the Kuangheng fiefdom in Linhuai County actually used the original Pingling Bai as the boundary of the fiefdom, which was 400 hectares more than the real Minbai as the fiefdom. In the first year of the founding of the People's Republic of China, the national boundaries were demarcated, the acres were re-counted, new books were made, the maps were re-drawn, and the matter was reported to the Prime Minister's Office.
target: Kuang Heng's son Kuang Chang killed someone while drunk and was imprisoned. Kuang Heng's brother conspired to rescue him, and when discovered, Kuang Heng pleaded guilty. The emperor restored his position, but Kuang Heng was later impeached for land theft. His fiefdom in Le'an Township had mistakenly used incorrect boundaries for over ten years, gaining 400 extra hectares. Kuang Heng did not correct this and collected rent from the additional land.

source: The principles of "Spring and Autumn" indicate that princes cannot monopolize land and must abide by the country's legal system. Kuang Heng had a high official position among the three public officials, assisting the state in government affairs, mastering the land acreage book of the fiefdom, and knowing the actual situation of demarcating the boundaries of the county and land. He should draw the boundaries correctly. However, after the local land recalculation and the redrawing of the fiefdom boundaries, Kuang Heng still violated the national regulations. According to the family's legal system, land was stolen and arbitrarily used to increase personal gain. His subordinate officials Lu Ci and Ming Ai flattered Kuang Heng's will, distorted the statistics of reported fiefdoms, reduced county boundaries indiscriminately, deceived superiors and subordinates, and annexed land to ministers without authorization, which was all illegal. So the emperor approved the two men's memorials and did not punish Kuang Heng. He was only removed from the post of prime minister and demoted to a commoner. Kuang Heng finally died at home. Kuang Heng's son Kuang Xian was also proficient in classics and righteousness, and once held the position of Jiu Qing.
target: He was impeached, and although the emperor did not punish him severely, he was removed from the post of prime minister and demoted to a commoner. He died at home. His son Kuang Xian was also proficient in classics and held the position of Jiu Qing.

source: Kuang Heng's son Kuang Xian was also proficient in classics and righteousness, and once held the position of Jiu Qing. His descendants produced many doctors of Confucian classics. Zhang Yu, whose courtesy name was Ziwen, was a native of Ruan County, Hanoi County. When his father arrived, he moved to Lianshao County. When Zhang Yu was a child, he often went to the market with his family and liked to watch those who performed divination and fortune telling. As time goes by, I am very good at identifying the good and bad meanings of yarrow and gossip, and I often tell what I mean from the sidelines. The fortune teller liked him very much and thought he was extraordinary in appearance, so he said to Zhang Yu's father: This child is very smart and he can learn scriptures. When Zhang Yu grew up, he went to Chang'an, the capital, to study. He learned the Book of Changes from Shi Yu, a native of Peijun, and the Analects of Confucius from Wang Yang, a native of Langxie, and Yongsheng, a native of Jiaodong. When he became proficient in these classics, he gathered his disciples to teach them, and was later recommended as a county literature scholar. During the Ganlu reign of Emperor Xuan of the Han Dynasty, various Confucian scholars recommended Zhang Yu, and the emperor ordered the prince and Taifu Xiao Wangzhi to be responsible for inspecting Zhang Yu's knowledge. Zhang Yu answered about the great meaning of "The Book of Changes" and "The Analects of Confucius". Xiao Wangzhi appreciated it very much and reported to the emperor that Zhang Yu was very proficient in Confucian classics and had learned the classics. He suggested that the emperor should try Zhang Yu as an official. However, this report was not approved, and Zhang Yu returned to his original official position. Much later, the emperor tried Zhang Yu as a doctor. In the first year of the Yuan Dynasty, the crown prince was established. At that time, Dr. Zheng Kuanzhong taught the prince "Shang Shu". He recommended that Zhang Yu was good at "The Analects of Confucius", so the emperor ordered Zhang Yu to teach the prince to learn "The Analects of Confucius". Therefore, Zhang Yu was promoted to doctor Guanglu.
target: Zhang Yu, courtesy name Ziwen, was born in Ruan County. As a child, he liked watching fortune tellers and became skilled at divination. He studied the Book of Changes and the Analects of Confucius in Chang'an, then gathered disciples to teach. During Emperor Xuan's reign, Xiao Wangzhi praised his knowledge, but the emperor did not approve his appointment. Later, he became a doctor and taught the prince the Analects of Confucius.

source: Therefore, Zhang Yu was promoted to doctor Guanglu. A few years later, he served as the internal history of Shuping County. Emperor Yuan died and Emperor Cheng ascended the throne. Zhang Yu and Zheng Kuanzhong were recruited to Chang'an. They were both given the title of Marquis of Guannei because they had been teachers of the prince. Zheng Kuanzhong had a settlement of 800 households, and Zhang Yu had a settlement of 600 households. Zhang Yu was appointed to the various officials as Guanglu Dafu, with an official rank of two thousand shi, and was assigned to Shizhong, and he was in charge of the secretarial affairs. When he was sent, Emperor Cheng of the Han Dynasty's uncle Yangpinghou Wang Feng was appointed as a general. He was called assistant to the government, but he was actually authoritarian. The emperor was very young, modest, fond of classics, and respected teachers. At that time, Zhang Yu and Wang Feng concurrently served as ministers, and he felt very uneasy. He petitioned to resign and return to his hometown several times due to illness, and wanted to avoid working with Wang Feng. The emperor replied: I ascended the throne at a young age and was very worried about making mistakes. You became my teacher because of your high moral character, so I entrusted the affairs of the country to you. What do you have to worry about, so that you repeatedly asked to resign? Are you forgetting our master-disciple relationship, or are you avoiding some rumors? I haven't heard any rumors about you. You should work with peace of mind, still be in charge of political affairs, show your tireless spirit, and don't go against my wishes. Then he rewarded Zhang Yu with a hundred catties of gold, beef cattle and fine wine, ordered the eunuchs to provide food for Zhang Yu, ordered the doctors to treat him, and often sent envoys to express condolences to him. Zhang Yu was deeply disturbed, so he began to go to court again. In the fourth year of Heping reign of Emperor Cheng of the Han Dynasty, Zhang Yu succeeded Wang Shang as prime minister and was granted the title of Marquis of Anchang. Zhang Yu served as prime minister for six years. In the first year of Emperor Hongjia's reign, he requested to resign on the pretext that he was old and sick. The emperor praised him repeatedly before allowing him to resign.
target: When Emperor Cheng ascended, Zhang Yu was appointed Guanglu Dafu and served as Shizhong. He felt uneasy serving alongside the authoritarian Wang Feng and repeatedly asked to resign, but the emperor refused and rewarded him generously. Zhang Yu eventually became prime minister and was granted the title of Marquis of Anchang. After six years, he resigned due to old age and illness.

source: Zhang Yu was a cautious and kind man, and his family was engaged in business and farming. Zhang Yu rose to prominence in the officialdom and bought 400 hectares of farmland in the Jingshui and Weihe river basins, both of which were fertile lands with convenient irrigation. There are also quite a lot of other belongings. Zhang Yu himself was proficient in and fond of music, and lived a relatively luxurious and luxurious life. After he resigned and returned home, he often went to the back hall to play silk, bamboo, wind, string and other musical instruments. Among Zhang Yu's students, the more accomplished ones were Peng Xuan from Huaiyang, who had an official rank of Da Sikong, and the other was Dai Chong, a Peijun native, who had an official rank of at least Jiuqing. Peng Xuan treats others with respect and humility, and pays attention to laws, while Dai Chong is harmonious, simple, smart and versatile. Their characters are different. Zhang Yu liked Dai Chong more in his heart, but stayed away from Peng Xuan. Every time Dai Chong visited Zhang Yu, he often asked the teacher to prepare a banquet with wine and share the fun of playing the harp with him.
target: Zhang Yu was cautious and kind, engaging in business and farming. He bought 400 hectares of fertile farmland and lived luxuriously, enjoying music. He treated his students differently: with Dai Chong, he shared wine and music in the back hall, while with Peng Xuan, he had simple meals in the main hall.

source: When Peng Xuan and Dai Chong learned that the teacher received them in different ways, they both thought it was suitable for their personalities. When Zhang Yu was old, he built a tomb and temple for himself. He liked the Fei Niu Pavilion in Pingling, which was close to Yanling, so he asked the emperor for the land. The emperor granted Zhang Yu permission to build a tomb and temple here, and Shao ordered the prefect of Pingling County to move the Fei Niu Pavilion to another place.
target: When old, he built a tomb at Fei Niu Pavilion in Pingling, which was a royal ancestral worship site.

source: Confucius once said to Zigong: You love his sheep and I love his rituals. The emperor should give Zhang Yu another place. Although Wang Gen was the emperor's uncle, the emperor did not respect him as much as Zhang Yu. Although Wang Gen spoke very sincerely, the emperor did not listen to his dissuasion and finally gave the Fei Niu Pavilion to Zhang Yu. Wang Gen was jealous of Zhang Yu's favor, so he wrote many times to slander Zhang Yu. But the emperor respected Zhang Yu even more and treated him favorably. Every time Zhang Yu fell ill, the emperor would ask about his daily life and even visit Zhang Yu in person. When the emperor arrived, Zhang Yu was grateful, kowtowed and thanked him, and took this opportunity to report to the emperor: I have four sons and one daughter, and I prefer my daughter, but she is married to Xiao Xian, the prefect of Zhangye. I miss her very much and hope she will be closer to me. The emperor immediately ordered Xiao Xian to be transferred to be the prefect of Hongnong. In addition, Zhang Yu's youngest son did not have an official title at that time. When the emperor visited him, he looked at his youngest son many times. After the emperor understood what he meant, he appointed his youngest son as Huang Menlang in front of his bed, giving him the title of "Huang Menlang". Although Zhang Yu has resigned, he still serves as the emperor's teacher as a special official. Whenever the country makes major decisions, the emperor must ask Zhang Yu. During the reigns of Emperor Cheng Yongshi and Yuanyan, there were many solar eclipses and earthquakes. Officials and people wrote letters saying that these were disasters, and ridiculed that they were caused by the Wang family's monopoly. The emperor was afraid that disasters would occur many times, and he was worried and uneasy. He did not express his clear position on the petitions from ministers and people, so he drove to Zhang Yu's mansion, dismissed the guards on the left and right, and then asked Zhang Yu about his views on food and earthquakes, and stated the opinions of the officials and people on the Wang family.
target: Despite Wang Gen's objections, the emperor granted his request. Wang Gen slandered him, but the emperor respected Zhang Yu even more. When the emperor visited him during illness, Zhang Yu requested that his daughter be closer, and the emperor transferred her husband. The emperor also appointed Zhang Yu's youngest son as Huang Menlang. Zhang Yu served as the emperor's teacher even after resigning, and the emperor consulted him on major decisions. During solar eclipses and earthquakes, when officials blamed the Wang family, Zhang Yu advised the emperor not to trust such claims, dispelling doubts about Wang. He died in the second year of Jianping and was given the title of Marquis of Jie.

source: Kong Guang, courtesy name Zixia, was the fourteenth generation grandson of Confucius. Confucius's son was given the given name Boyu, and his given name was Li; Kong Li's son was given the given name Zisi, and his given name was Ji; Kong Ji's son was given the given name Zishang, and his given name was Bo; Kong Bo's son was given the given name Zijia, and his given name was Qiu; Kong Qiu's son was given the given name Zizhen, and his given name was Ji; Kong Ji's son was given the given name Zigao, and his given name was Chuan. Kong Chuan's son was named Shun, and Kong Shun served as the prime minister of Wei. Kong Shun's son was named Yu. Kong Yu served as Chen She's doctor and died in Chen. Kong Yu's disciple Xiang was Dr. Xiaohui, the Taifu of Changsha. Zixiang's son was named Zhong, and Zhongzhong had two sons: Kong Wu and Kong Anguo. Kong Wu was born in Yannian. Yannian's son was named Ba, named Ciru. Kong Ba's son was Kong Guang. Anguo and Yannian both became doctors during the reign of Emperor Wu by studying "Shangshu". An Guoguan arrived at Linhuai Prefecture. Kong Ba also studied "Shangshu" and followed the Taifu Xiahou Sheng. He was awarded the title of doctor in the last years of Emperor Zhao. During the reign of Emperor Xuan, he served as Taizhong doctor. Because he was selected to teach the classics to the crown prince, he was promoted to Zhanshi and Gaomixiang. At this time, the ministers of the princes and kings were all above the county guards. Emperor Yuan came to the throne, recruited Kong Ba as his teacher, rewarded Kong Ba with the title of Marquis of Guannei, granted him eight hundred households in the city, and gave him the title of Chengjun. Kong Ba is humble and courteous in his treatment of others, and does not like power. He often says that his title is too high and he has no moral character to be qualified for the job! The emperor wanted Kong Ba to serve as prime minister. From the death of Gong Yu, the imperial censor, to the dismissal of Xue Guangde, the emperor always wanted to worship Kong Ba as prime minister. Kong Ba gave way again and again, and the emperor knew that he was sincerely humble, so he did not appoint him as prime minister. After that, the emperor respected Kong Ba even more and his rewards became more generous. After Kong Ba passed away, the emperor came to mourn twice in mourning clothes. He gave Shuyuan's secret utensils, money and silk, and gave them according to the etiquette of the princes, calling him Liejun. Kong Ba had four sons. The eldest son, Mingfu, inherited the title of Marquis of Guannei. The second son Kong Jie and the third son Kong happy both served as school captains and other officials. Kong Guang, the youngest son of Kong Ba, was particularly proficient in Confucian classics. He was elected as Yilang when he was less than twenty years old. Guang Luxun Kuang Heng recommended Kong Guang to be an admonishing doctor because of his good conduct. Because his discussion of political affairs was inconsistent with the emperor's wishes, he was demoted to the magistrate of Hong County. Kong Guang was dismissed in vain and went home to teach Confucian classics. When Emperor Cheng first came to the throne, Liao Guang was elected as a doctor. He was repeatedly asked to be responsible for redressing injustices, regulating customs, and providing relief to victims. Kong Guang successfully completed the mission every time he was ordered to go on an envoy, and Kong Guang's reputation spread throughout the government and the public.
target: Kong Guang, courtesy name Zixia, was the fourteenth generation grandson of Confucius. His father Kong Ba was a doctor and teacher to the crown prince. Kong Guang was proficient in classics and was elected as Yilang before age twenty. Kuang Heng recommended him as an admonishing doctor, but he was demoted for disagreeing with the emperor. He later became a doctor and successfully completed missions, gaining fame. He was promoted to Guanglu Dafu and served as Shangshu for over ten years, maintaining laws and revising systems.

source: A few years later, Kong Guang was promoted to the official position Guanglu Dafu, with a salary of 2,000 dan, a reward of 100 jin of gold, and the title of Shangshu. Later, he was promoted to Guang Luxun, still responsible for the affairs of the minister, and served as an official in charge of affairs as before. Kong Guang was in charge of the government affairs for more than ten years, maintaining laws and revising systems. When the emperor asked about political affairs, Kong Guang always answered with the answer he thought was right according to the classic laws, and did not want to be in conflict with the emperor's will. Just as sometimes the emperor did not obey, Kong Guang did not dare to forcefully remonstrate, so Kong Guang served as an official for a long time and was safe. Sometimes he wrote letters to express his opinions, and the memorials he had already written were always deleted and revised. He believed that writing letters to publicize the emperor's faults in order to gain a reputation for loyalty and uprightness was a major sin in officialdom. When Ziguang recommended others to become officials, he was also afraid that others would hear him. When it was my turn to have a holiday, I would go home to rest and talk to my brothers, wives and children about everyday things, but never mention the political affairs surrounding the imperial court.
target: He was cautious, never leaking court affairs, and avoided forcefully remonstrating. He recommended officials secretly and did not form factions.

source: I have seen privately that in national government affairs, the post of Minister has been constantly changing, and it is very difficult for someone without outstanding talents to be qualified. The servant of the minister is open, fair, diligent in his duties, and quick-witted when dealing with problems, so he can serve as the minister. Now solemnly write it down and seal it for memorial. Because of Kong Guang's recommendation, Chang became the prefect of Shuping. Chang's surname is Chenggong, and he is from Shuhai County. Kong Guang served as doctor for a month. Prime Minister Wang Jia was imprisoned and died. The censor doctor bought an extension and was dismissed. Kong Guang resumed his role as the imperial censor, and two months later he resumed his role as prime minister and was granted the title of Marquis of Boshan again.
target: He became imperial censor and later prime minister, granted the title of Marquis of Boshan.

source: According to the "Li", the emperor had records that not all brothers could enter the temple. In addition, the queen and Zhaoyi wanted to establish King Dingtao, so he selected King Dingtao as the crown prince. Kong Guang was demoted to Tingwei because his comments were not in line with the emperor's wishes. Kong Guang has been in charge of Shangshu affairs for a long time and formulated the legal system, which is known as fine and peaceful. At this time, Chunyu Chang, the Marquis of Dingling, committed a crime of treason and was killed. Chun Yuchang's concubine Naishi and the other six people all left Chunyu Chang before his crime was discovered, and some of them remarried. After Chunyu Chang's incident happened, Prime Minister Fang Jin and Grand Sikong Hewu discussed it and believed that according to the law, those who broke the law should be punished according to the law at the time of breaking the law, and there was a clear limit on time. When Chunyu Chang committed the crime of treason and immorality, it was his wife who had already committed the crime of implication, just as he had committed the crime. They left him only after committing a crime, and according to the law, they could not be exempted from guilt. Please make your decision. Kong Guang expressed his opinion that he had committed a crime of treason, and that the offender's parents, wife, children, and co-mother were involved. Relatives, regardless of age, should be beheaded and their bodies dumped on the streets as a warning to future criminals. The rule between husband and wife is that if there is affection for each other, they will be united; if there is no affection, they will separate. Chunyu Chang himself did not know that he was committing a crime of treason, so he abandoned Naishi and others. Some of them remarried, and the friendship between husband and wife was no longer true. If he still thought that they were Chun Yuchang's wives and killed them, it would be unfair in name, so he should not be implicated in the crime. The emperor wrote to Shao, confirming that Kong Guang's opinion was correct. In this year, the right general Lian Bao and the rear general Zhu Bo were also dismissed as commoners because of their close friendship with the criminal Dingling Marquis Chun Yuchang and Hongyang Marquis Wangli. Kong Guang was appointed as the left general and held the official position of the right general, and Zhijinwu Wang Xian was appointed as the right general and held the official position of the rear general. The post of general was revoked. A few months later, Prime Minister Fang Jin passed away. The emperor summoned Kong Guang, the general of the left, and prepared to worship him as prime minister. He had already carved the seal of Hou and written a policy letter to worship him as prime minister. At this time, the emperor suddenly died. On the night of the emperor's sudden death, before the funeral, he paid homage to the Prime Minister and the Marquis of Boshan. When Emperor Ai first came to the throne, he set an example and advocated frugality, which reduced a lot of expenses. The emperor was responsible for handling all court affairs. The court was shocked and looked forward to the arrival of peace and prosperity. The emperor praised and rewarded the ministers and granted Kong Guang an additional 1,000 households. At this time, Emperor Cheng's mother, the Empress Dowager, lived in Changle Palace by herself, while Emperor Cheng's grandmother, the Empress Dowager Dingtaofu, lived in the emperor's residence. The emperor issued an edict asking the prime minister, Da Sikong: Where should the Empress Dowager Dingtao live?
target: During the succession debate, Kong Guang argued for King Zhongshan based on blood relations, but the emperor chose King Dingtao. Kong Guang was demoted to Tingwei. Later, he argued that Chunyu Chang's concubines who left before his crime should not be implicated, and the emperor agreed. After Emperor Cheng's sudden death, Kong Guang was appointed prime minister. When Emperor Ai ruled, Kong Guang advised against Empress Dowager Fu living close to the emperor, but was overruled. He later opposed retaining the treacherous Fu Qian, but the emperor kept him. Kong Guang was eventually dismissed for failing to advise properly during disasters. After several prime ministers failed, the emperor recalled Kong Guang during a solar eclipse. Kong Guang explained that eclipses occurred when ministers became too powerful and advised the emperor to reform governance. The emperor reappointed him as prime minister.

source: Didn't the "Book of Songs" say: The flattering villain was rampant in deception and caused chaos in the country, so Fu Jia was removed from his official position and became a civilian, and was sent back to his original county. The next year, the official position of the three princes was evaluated, and Kong Guang was changed to the post of Grand Situ. Coinciding with the death of Emperor Ai, the Empress Dowager took Wang Mang, the new capital lord, as the Grand Sima and elected King Zhongshan as the emperor, namely Emperor Ping of the Han Dynasty. Emperor Ping was very young, so the Empress Dowager was in charge of the government, and the Empress Dowager entrusted political affairs to Wang Mang. During the reign of Emperor Ai, the Wang family was deposed. Therefore, the Queen Mother and Wang Mang were very resentful towards Ding, Fu and Dong Xian. Wang Mang believed that Kong Guang was the former prime minister, a famous Confucian, trusted and admired by the world, and the Queen Mother also respected him and always received him with courtesy. Whenever it was necessary to attack political opponents, Li Guang was always asked to help draft documents. According to the Queen Mother's orders, Kong Guang was asked to write the memorial. Anyone who has enmity against the Queen Mother, even if it is a small amount of hatred, will be retaliated and no one will be killed. Wang Mang's power became stronger day by day. Kong Guang was very frightened and worried. He didn't know what to do, so he wrote to the emperor to resign. Wang Mang then said to the Queen Mother: The emperor is very young and should be given a teacher. He appointed Kong Guang as the emperor's Taifu, with the official position of Fourth Assistant. He was responsible for providing food, clothing, carriages, horses and food. In the second year, he was promoted to Taishi, and Wang Mang served as Taifu. Kong Guang often complained of illness and did not dare to take the throne with Wang Mang in the court. The emperor ordered Wang Mang to go to court on the first and fifteenth day of each month and asked Wang Mang to command the city gate guards. Wang Mang also ordered his officials to submit a memorial praising Wang Mang's merits. Emperor Ping of the Han Dynasty gave Wang Mang the title of Prime Minister, ranking him above the princes and kings and commanding hundreds of officials.
target: Under Empress Dowager and Wang Mang's rule, Kong Guang was used to draft documents attacking political opponents. Fearing Wang Mang's growing power, Kong Guang tried to resign. Wang Mang appointed him as the emperor's Taifu, and later Taishi. Kong Guang often claimed illness to avoid attending court with Wang Mang.

source: The Queen Mother then issued an edict saying: Taishi Kong Guang is a descendant of a saint and the son of the late emperor's teacher. He is pure and upright in virtue, proficient in morality and academics, and serves as the fourth assistant to assist the emperor. Now I am old and sick. But highly respected ministers like Kong Guang are important ministers of the country and are still indispensable. "Book of Zhou." Zhao Gao said: "Never abandon mature people. If the country wants to prosper, it must respect and reuse teachers." He ordered Grand Master Kong Guang not to go to court, but to reward him with a meal every ten days. The Grand Master was given a longevity stick, and the Huangmen Order set up a place for the Grand Master to sit within the palace. The Grand Master could hold the staff when entering the palace, and was rewarded with seventeen kinds of food. Then he returned to the mansion to retire, while his subordinate officials continued to work as usual. Kong Guang served as the imperial censor and prime minister twice, and once as the chief situ, Taifu and Taishi. He experienced three generations of emperors and held the high position of auxiliary minister for a total of seventeen years. After becoming the minister, he stopped teaching activities, and later became the prime minister. Sometimes he would meet his disciples to discuss and raise difficult questions, and Kong Guang would often explain his principles to them. Many of Kong Guang's disciples were successful in their studies and became doctors and doctors. When they saw their teacher holding important positions, they all wanted his help. However, Kong Guang never recommended them, so some people complained about him. Kong Guang acted fairly, that's all. Kong Guang was seventy years old and died in the fifth year of Yuanshi. Wang Mang told the Queen Mother that he would give Jiu Qing's policy book to the Taishi Boshan Hou Yinshou, and give him a carriage, a coffin, money, and miscellaneous silk. The Shaofu set up the curtains, and sent the admonishing doctor to hold the talisman and the visitor to receive the guests to take charge of the funeral. The doctor was responsible for the funeral ceremony. The Queen Mother also sent visitors to come with talismans in hand to express their condolences. All the ministers and officials paid their condolences and paid their respects together. A funeral car and an auxiliary funeral car were used to carry the emperor's Habayashi guards and many Confucian scholars, a total of four hundred people. There were more than 10,000 funeral vehicles. Everywhere they went, passers-by burst into tears. The crying stopped after the motorcade finished. Five hundred soldiers were used to dig a hole and lower the coffin, and the tomb was raised, just like the funeral of General Wang Feng. He was given the title of Jian Liehou. At first, Kong Guang was granted the title of prime minister, and later he was granted additional titles, with a total of 11,000 households. When Kong Guang was seriously ill, he wrote a letter to return 7,000 households and the first house given by the emperor. Kong Guang's son Kong Fang inherited the title. After Wang Mang usurped the throne, he appointed Kong Yong, the son of Kong Guang's brother, as the Grand Sima and a marquis.
target: He served as imperial censor and prime minister twice, and as chief situ, Taifu, and Taishi, holding high positions for seventeen years. He died at age seventy in the fifth year of Yuanshi, receiving an elaborate funeral with thousands of mourners. His title was Jian Liehou. His descendants inherited his title, and Wang Mang later appointed his nephew as Grand Sima.

source: After Kong Fu died, his son Kong Fang succeeded to the throne. After Kong Fang died, his son Kong Mang succeeded to the throne. In the first year of the Yuan Dynasty, the emperor granted the descendants of Zhou Gong and Confucius the title of marquis, with 2,000 households each. Kong Mang was later granted the title of Marquis of Baocheng, and was later renamed Kong Jun to avoid Wang Mang's taboo. Ma Gong, courtesy name Youqing, was born in Qixian County, Shuhai. After studying Yan's "Spring and Autumn Annals", he was selected as a member of the Jia Division in response to the examination, and served as a minister. He was later promoted to the chief historian of Chu, and was dismissed soon after. Later he served as Prime Minister Shi Sizhi. Shi Dan recommended that Ma Gong was of high moral character and was promoted to Ting Weiping. He served successively as the governor of Qingzhou and the prefect of Runan and Jiujiang. He was qualified for official positions and received praise everywhere he went. Therefore, he was recruited by the emperor as Zhan Shi, Guang Luxun, and General You. He replaced Kong Guang as the chief disciple and was granted the title of Fudehou. After Kong Guang's death as Grand Master, Ma Gong succeeded Kong Guang as Grand Master and concurrently served as Situ. During the reign of Emperor Ai, Ma Gong discussed the issue of the title of the emperor's grandmother, the Empress Dowager Fu, with the prime minister and the imperial censor. During the Yuanshi period, Wang Mang moved the tomb of Empress Dowager Fu back to Dingtao, buried it according to common people's etiquette, and investigated the charges against those who had discussed the funeral. Because Ma Gong had a close friendship with Wang Mang, he was the only one who was not forced to investigate. Ma Gong felt ashamed and frightened, so he wrote a letter to the emperor to confess his guilt and asked to retire. Wang Mang issued an edict in the name of the Empress Dowager and gave Ma Gong a policy letter saying: Taishi and Grand Situ Fudehou wrote a letter saying: When I was serving as Guangluxun, I discussed the nickname of the mother of the late Dingtao Gongwang. It was said that a woman should be honored by her husband's title, and the nickname should be Empress Xiaoyuan Fu, and she should be called Weiling Shuyuan. I know that concubines cannot represent the king, and the lowly ones cannot be compared with the noble ones, but they cater to the will of the superiors, agree with them, go against the scriptures, and express heresy, causing the emperor to be confused and make mistakes. As a minister, if you are disloyal to your superior, you should be put to death. Fortunately, the emperor asked me to repent and changed my ways, and I was able to save my life. I have deeply reflected on myself. I served as the fourth minister in the court, enjoyed the treatment of the three princes when I came in and out, and was given the title of lord. I really have no face to enter the court again, no intention to hold an official position anymore, and I should no longer enjoy the food. I respectfully hand over the great seal of Grand Master and Grand Situ Fudehou to make way for the virtuous people. They all believe that the four auxiliary ministers are responsible for implementing the country's charter laws, and the three ministers shoulder the important task of assisting the monarch. Without outstanding moral character, they cannot hold this position. What you said in your letter shows that you are loyal and heartwarming, but just because you made the mistake before you repented, no one dared to protect you. I respect you very much and will not deprive you of your title and land, in order to promote the great righteousness of people since ancient times. You hand over the seal of Grand Master Situ to the envoy, and return home to take care of yourself in your old age. After Wang Mang usurped the throne, he appointed Ma Gong as the crown prince's counselor and died in office.
target: Ma Gong, courtesy name Youqing, studied Yan's Spring and Autumn Annals and served as a minister. He was promoted to Ting Weiping and served as governor of several provinces, gaining praise. He replaced Kong Guang as chief disciple and was granted the title of Fudehou. After Kong Guang's death, Ma Gong succeeded him as Grand Master and Situ. During the Yuanshi period, Wang Mang investigated those who discussed Empress Dowager Fu's funeral. Because Ma Gong was Wang Mang's friend, he was not investigated, but he felt ashamed and resigned. Wang Mang allowed him to return home. After Wang Mang usurped the throne, Ma Gong became the crown prince's counselor and died in office.

source: Wei Qing, courtesy name Zhongqing. His father, Zheng Ji, was from Pingyang, Hedong Province. He served as a county official and worked as an errand in the Pingyang Hou family. Pingyang Hou Cao Shou married Princess Yang Xinchang, the sister of Emperor Mowu. Zheng Ji had an affair with his master's servant Wei Wei and gave birth to Wei Qing. Wei Qing had an elder brother, Wei Changjun, and an elder sister, Wei Zifu. Wei Zifu was favored by Emperor Wu in Princess Pingyang's family, so Wei Qing assumed the surname Wei. Wei's eldest daughter is Junru, her second daughter is Shaoer, and her third daughter is Wei Zifu. Wei Zifu's younger brother Bu Guang took the surname Wei. Wei Qing was considered a member of Pingyang Hou's family and returned to his father's home when he was a child. His father made him herd sheep, and his aunt's sons treated him as a slave and were not counted among their brothers. Wei Qing once followed someone to the prisoner's room in Ganquan Palace. A prisoner who was being tortured came to him and said, "You are a noble person. If you become an official, you can become a marquis." Wei Qing smiled and said: "A son born from a slave would be very satisfied if he could not be beaten or scolded. How could there be such a good thing as becoming a prince?" When Wei Qing grew up, he became a knight of the Pingyang Hou family and followed Princess Pingyang. In the spring of the second year of Jianyuan, Wei Qing's sister Wei Zifu entered the palace and was favored by the emperor. Queen Chen is the daughter of the eldest princess. She has no son and is jealous of others. The eldest princess heard that Wei Zifu was favored and was pregnant. She was jealous of her and sent people to arrest Wei Qing. Wei Qing was working as an errand in Jianzhang Palace at that time and was not yet famous. The eldest princess caught Wei Qing, imprisoned him, and wanted to kill him. Wei Qing's friend Qi Lang Gongsun Ao and the warriors went to snatch him out, and Wei Qing avoided death. When the emperor heard about this, he summoned Wei Qing and asked him to be the eunuch of Jianzhang Palace and serve as a minister. When his half-brothers became prominent, the rewards amounted to thousands of gold in a few days. Jun Ru married Grand Servant Sun He as his wife.
target: Wei Qing, courtesy name Zhongqing, was the illegitimate son of Zheng Ji, a county official in Pingyang, and a servant named Wei. He assumed the surname Wei after his sister Wei Zifu gained favor with Emperor Wu. As a youth, Wei Qing herded sheep and was treated poorly by his relatives. A prisoner once prophesied he would become a marquis, but Wei Qing dismissed this, content to avoid beatings. He later became a knight for the Pingyang Hou family. Wei Zifu's entry into the palace and pregnancy provoked jealousy from Empress Chen and her mother, the Grand Princess, who imprisoned Wei Qing. His friend Gongsun Ao rescued him, and the emperor subsequently appointed Wei Qing as a eunuch and minister.

source: King Youxian of the Xiongnu faced Wei Qing and other troops, thinking that the Han army could not reach him, so he got drunk. Han soldiers arrived at night and surrounded King Youxian. King Youxian was frightened and fled overnight. He took only one of his concubines and hundreds of strong cavalry and fled northward through the Han army's encirclement. The Han Dynasty Qingqi Colonel Guo Cheng and others chased for hundreds of miles, but failed to catch up. They captured more than ten people under King Youxian, more than 15,000 men and women, and tens of millions of livestock. So Wei Qing led his army back. When the army arrived at the frontier, the emperor sent an envoy to hold the seal of the general, and appointed Wei Qing, the general of chariots and cavalry, as the general in the army. All the generals put their troops under the command of the general, and the general established his official title and returned. The Emperor said: General Wei Qing personally led his soldiers in the battle and achieved a great victory. He captured more than ten Xiongnu kings and granted 8,700 additional households in Wei Qing's food town. He also granted Wei Qing's sons Wei and his wife the title of Marquis of Yichun, Wei Busuo as the Marquis of Yin'an, and Wei Deng as the Marquis of Fagan. Wei Qing resolutely refused and said: I am fortunate to be able to serve in the army. Relying on His Majesty's divine power, our army's great victory is all due to the hard work of all the captains.
target: His rise brought wealth to his family. In 129 BC, Wei Qing led a cavalry attack on the Xiongnu, reaching Longcheng and killing hundreds. He was made Marquis of Guannei, while other generals faced punishment for failures.

source: The princess smiled and said: He grew up in my family and often followed me on horseback. What about him? The people on the left and right said: Now you are extremely noble. So the eldest princess told the queen what she wanted, and the queen told her truthfully. The emperor ordered Wei Qing to marry the eldest princess, and they were buried together after their death in a tomb built like Lushan Mountain. General Wei Qing attacked the Xiongnu seven times in total, killing and capturing more than 50,000 enemies. After fighting the Huns, they recovered the area south of Hetao and established Shuofang County. Additional rewards will be added, totaling 16,300 households; the three sons will be granted the title of marquis, each with 1,300 households, for a total of 20,200 households. Nine lieutenants and captains were appointed marquis, and fifteen specially dispatched generals. Li Guang, Zhang Qian, Gongsun He, Li Cai, Cao Xiang, Han Shuo, and Su Jian all had their own biographies. Li Xi, a native of Yuzhi, served Emperor Jing. Eight years after Emperor Wu took the throne, he was promoted to General Caiguan and stationed in the military district. Six years later, he was promoted to General and led his army to attack Baochao from Weisun. Three years later, he served as a general and accompanied the general to attack Xiuli, but he had no military exploits.
target: In subsequent campaigns, Wei Qing defeated the Xiongnu, capturing livestock and driving out kings. He was granted the title of Marquis of Changping with 3,800 households. The emperor praised his victories, which included pacifying the Henan area and building Shuofang City. Despite continued Xiongnu raids, Wei Qing's successes led to additional rewards.
