target: He was promoted to General-in-Chief, and his sons were made marquises. Wei Qing declined the honors, crediting his officers. The emperor then rewarded several subordinates with marquisates.

source: Even if a minister has the power to kill generals, wouldn't it be good if a minister with a high position and a favored position dare not use his power to kill outside the country's borders? Instead, he goes back to report to the emperor and let the emperor handle it on his own, thus showing that the minister does not dare to take power? The officers all said yes. So Su Jian was put into a prison car and sent to the emperor's patrol. This year, Huo Qubing began to become a marquis. Huo Qubing was the son of General Wei Qing's sister Wei Shaohao. His father, Huo Zhongru, had an affair with Wei Shao'er and gave birth to Huo Qubing. When Queen Wei came to her favor, Wei Shaoer married Zhan Shichenzhang. Huo Qubing was the son of the queen's sister, and he became a servant at the age of eighteen. Because he was good at horseback riding and archery, he accompanied General Wei Qing on two expeditions against the Huns. According to the emperor's order, the general assigned him a group of strong soldiers and appointed him as the captain of Piao Yao. He led 800 light cavalry warriors hundreds of miles away from the army led by Wei Qing to win military exploits and kill many enemies. At this time Emperor Wu said: Huo Qubing, the captain of Piaoyao School, annihilated 2,028 enemies, captured alive the prime minister and the householder, killed Shanyu's grandfather's Jiuruohou Chan, captured Shanyu's uncle Luo Gu and others alive, and won the title of the entire army twice for his merits. He named Huo Qubing the champion with 2,500 households. Hao Xian, the prefect of Shanggu, went on four expeditions with the general, killing 1,300 enemies, and made him the final profiteer. The knight Meng Ji also had military exploits and was given the title of Marquis of Guannei, with a title of enfeoffment to 200 households. In this year, the Han Dynasty lost two troops led by Su Jian and Tan Xin, and Zhao Xin, the Marquis of Xi, surrendered to the Huns. His military achievements were not many, so Wei Qing was not able to increase his title.
target: In 123 BC, Wei Qing's campaign saw the defection of former Xiongnu marquis Zhao Xin and the destruction of Su Jian's force. Wei Qing spared Su Jian, sending him to the emperor for judgment. That year, Huo Qubing, Wei Qing's nephew, began his rise, leading a successful raid with 800 cavalry and being made Marquis of Champion.

source: King Zuoxian of the Xiongnu led tens of thousands of cavalry to surround Li Guang's tribe. Li Guang fought fiercely with the enemy for two days, suffering over half casualties and killing even more enemies. It was not until Zhang Qian's troops arrived that the Huns retreated. Because Zhang Qian's troops were slow to move, he should be beheaded to atone for his sins and serve the people. After Huo Qubing set out from the north, he went deep into the Xiongnu region. Heqihou Gongsun Ao took the wrong route and was unable to join forces with Huo Qubing. Huo Qubing led his army to the Qilian Mountains and killed many enemies. Emperor Wu ordered: General Hussar crossed the Gouqi River and Juyanze, arrived at Xiaoyueshi, captured the Qilian Mountains, and showed off his force in Kunde. He captured Shanyu's King Shanhuan and King Tutu, as well as the ministers and captains who led their troops to surrender, a total of 2,500 people. It can be said that he can surrender leniently and knows how to stop after success. In this victory, 30,200 people were beheaded and captured, including five Xiongnu kings, fifty-nine people including the queen mother, Shan Yuque clan, and princes, and sixty-three prime ministers, generals, officials, and captains. Huo Qubing's soldiers suffered approximately three-tenths casualties. Huo Qubing was granted the title of 5,400 households.
target: Huo Qubing's subsequent campaigns were highly successful, including capturing the Xiongnu's golden statue and defeating the Hunxie King, who surrendered with 100,000 people. Huo Qubing was rewarded with additional households, and the surrendered Xiongnu were settled as vassal states.

source: However, Wei Qing was not granted a title, nor were any of his officers and soldiers. Only Chang Hui, the governor of Xihe County, and Suicheng, the governor of Yunzhong County, were rewarded. Then he was given the same position as the prime minister of the princes and kingdoms, and was given 200 households in the city and 100 catties of gold. It was given to Chang Huijue as the Marquis of Guannei. When the two armies of Wei Qing and Huo Qubing went to the outside of the Great Wall, the border officials inspected a total of 140,000 official and private horses, but after the war, less than 30,000 horses returned to the Great Wall. The imperial court set up the position of Grand Sima, making both Wei Qing and Huo Qubing the Grand Sima. This decree was enacted to make the rank and salary of the hussar general equal to that of the general. From then on, Wei Qing's power gradually declined while Huo Qubing became more prominent. Many of Wei Qing's old friends and guests went to seek refuge with Huo Qubing, and most of them received official titles, but Ren An refused to leave.
target: In 119 BC, Wei Qing and Huo Qubing led a massive campaign. Wei Qing defeated the Xiongnu Chanyu but failed to capture him. Huo Qubing's forces killed over 70,000 enemies. Both were made Grand Sima, but Huo Qubing's star rose while Wei Qing's declined. Huo Qubing died in 117 BC, deeply mourned by the emperor.

source: The princess smiled and said: He grew up in my family and often followed me on horseback. What about him? The people on the left and right said: Now you are extremely noble. So the eldest princess told the queen what she wanted, and the queen told her truthfully. The emperor ordered Wei Qing to marry the eldest princess, and they were buried together after their death in a tomb built like Lushan Mountain. General Wei Qing attacked the Xiongnu seven times in total, killing and capturing more than 50,000 enemies.
target: Wei Qing died in 106 BC, having attacked the Xiongnu seven times and killing over 50,000 enemies.

source: General Wei Qing attacked the Xiongnu seven times in total, killing and capturing more than 50,000 enemies. After fighting the Huns, they recovered the area south of Hetao and established Shuofang County. Additional rewards will be added, totaling 16,300 households; the three sons will be granted the title of marquis, each with 1,300 households, for a total of 20,200 households. Nine lieutenants and captains were appointed marquis, and fifteen specially dispatched generals. Li Guang, Zhang Qian, Gongsun He, Li Cai, Cao Xiang, Han Shuo, and Su Jian all had their own biographies. Li Xi, a native of Yuzhi, served Emperor Jing. Eight years after Emperor Wu took the throne, he was promoted to General Caiguan and stationed in the military district. Six years later, he was promoted to General and led his army to attack Baochao from Weisun. Three years later, he served as a general and accompanied the general to attack Xiuli, but he had no military exploits.
target: He recovered the Hetao region and established Shuofang County. His three sons were marquises, but all lost their titles.

source: Guo Chang, a native of Yunzhong, served as a lieutenant following the general. In the fourth year of Yuanfeng's reign, Yi Taizhong, a senior official, became General Ba Hu and stationed in Shuofang. After the troops withdrew, they attacked Kenlong again, but to no avail and took away military power. Xun Shen was a native of Guangwu, Taiyuan. Because he was good at driving, he served as a servant and served as a lieutenant many times with the general. In the third year of Wuqian's reign, he was promoted to General Zuo and led his army to attack Huang Dao, but in vain. He was executed for the crime of seizing General Lou Chuan. General Huo Qubing attacked the Xiongnu six times in total, four of which were with the rank of general, killing and capturing more than 110,000 enemies. King Hunxie led tens of thousands of people to surrender to the Han Dynasty and opened up the Jiuquan area in Hexi Province. The invasion of the Xiongnu from the west was further reduced.
target: Huo Qubing's six campaigns killed over 110,000 enemies and opened the Hexi region. His subordinates also received honors.

source: Six years later, General Junji led an army of 20,000 to attack the Xiongnu Zuo King. The king of Zuo fought with him and surrounded Zhao Ponu with 80,000 cavalry. Ponu was captured and the entire army was wiped out. After living in the Xiongnu for ten years, he fled back to the Han Dynasty with his prince Anguo. Later, he committed the crime of witchcraft and his clan was reduced. From the rise of the Wei family, the general Wei Qing was first granted the title of marquis, and later five of his descendants became marquises. Twenty-four years later, all the five princes lost their feudal status. During the Yanchi period, King Lu failed and Mi Sui perished. There is another legend that Huo Qubing's younger brother, Riguang, was a noble person. Zan said: Ji Jian once reproached Jie Gui and said: The general is very noble, but no one of the wise scholar-officials in the world praises you. I hope the general will observe the methods of ancient famous generals in recruiting wise men and encourage yourself more!
target: The text concludes with brief biographies of other generals and notes that Wei Qing and Huo Qubing refrained from recruiting scholars, following the emperor's wishes.

source: Ban's ancestors had the same surname as Chu and were descendants of Ling Yin Ziwen. When Ziwen was born, he was abandoned in a field, and a tiger nursed him. Chu people called breast-feeding "gu" and tigers "yuzhan", so they named it "guyugan" with the courtesy name Ziwen. The people of Chu called the tiger "Ban", and his son named him "Ban". The Qin State subtracted the Chu State and moved between the Jin State and the Dai State, so they took Ban as their surname. In the last years of Qin Shihuang's reign, Ban Yi took refuge in Loufan and raised thousands of horses, cattle and sheep. In the early years of the Han Dynasty, the state imposed no restrictions on the common people. During the period of Emperor Xiaohui and Queen Gao, Banshi dominated the border areas with wealth, went out and hunted, fluttered flags, played drums and played loudly, and died at the age of more than a hundred years old. Therefore, many people in the north used "一" as the character. Ban Ru, the son of Ban Yi. Ban Ru was praised by people in this state and county for his chivalrous and righteous actions. Ban Ru's son is the squad leader and the official is the prefect of Shanggu. Ban Hui, the squad leader's son, became the eldest son county magistrate due to his outstanding talents. Ban Hui's son Ban Kuang was elected as Xiaolian and served as a Lang. He accumulated merits and was promoted to the rank of Captain of Henong. Da Sinong repeatedly wrote letters saying that he had high merits and entered the court as the captain of Zuo Caoyue's cavalry school. In the early years when he became emperor, his daughter entered the palace as Jieyu. He retired and returned to his hometown. His family wealth reached a thousand gold and he moved to Changling. Later, Changling was abolished, and all the ministers and famous officials there moved to Chang'an. Ban Kuang has three sons: Banbo, Banbo and Banzhi. Banbo studied the Book of Songs with Shi Dan when he was young. The general Wang Feng recommended Banbo as a suitable attendant. The emperor summoned Banbo in the banquet hall. He was handsome, recited and preached very well, and he was worshiped as a regular attendant. At that time, the emperor was keen on studying. Zheng Kuanzhong and Zhang Yu lectured on "Shangshu" and "The Analects of Confucius" in the Jinhua Palace every morning and evening. The emperor Shao ordered Banbo to study. After understanding the righteousness, he discussed the similarities and differences with Xu Shang and was promoted to the captain of Fengche. After the end of the year, the lecture activities in Jinhua Palace were suspended, and Ban Bo left the palace to associate with Wang and Xu's descendants. Living among the dandies was not his preference. Because Ban's ancestral home was originally in the northern border, Ban Bo was born to be generous and generous, and repeatedly requested to be sent as an envoy to the Huns.
target: The Ban family, originally sharing the surname of Chu, descended from Ling Yin Ziwen. Ziwen, abandoned as an infant, was nursed by a tiger, leading to his name "Guyugan" from Chu words for nursing and tiger. The tiger was called "Ban," and his son adopted this as their surname. After Qin conquered Chu, the family moved between Jin and Dai, taking Ban as their surname. During the late Qin, Ban Yi fled to Loufan, amassing livestock. In early Han, the Bans dominated border areas with wealth, hunting and living lavishly, with Ban Yi living over a hundred years. Ban Yi's son, Ban Ru, was praised for chivalry. His son, the squad leader, became Shanggu Prefect. Ban Hui, the squad leader's son, became a county magistrate. Ban Kuang, Ban Hui's son, served as a Lang and rose to Captain of Henong, later retiring with wealth to Changling. He had three sons: Banbo, Banbo, and Banzhi. Banbo studied the Book of Songs, was recommended as an attendant, and became a regular attendant.

source: After understanding the righteousness, he discussed the similarities and differences with Xu Shang and was promoted to the captain of Fengche. After the end of the year, the lecture activities in Jinhua Palace were suspended, and Ban Bo left the palace to associate with Wang and Xu's descendants. Living among the dandies was not his preference. Because Ban's ancestral home was originally in the northern border, Ban Bo was born to be generous and generous, and repeatedly requested to be sent as an envoy to the Huns. During the Heping period, Chanyu came to see him, and the emperor ordered Banbo to greet him at the foot of the fortress with amulets. It happened that the Shi family and the Li family in Dingxiang area killed people because of their personal grievances, and also killed the officials who were chasing them. Banbo wrote a letter expressing his willingness to be temporarily appointed as the prefect of Dingxiang for a month. The emperor sent his lieutenant general Wang Shun to come and escort Shanyu in place of Banbo. At the same time, he brought a seal and seal ribbon and appointed Banbo as the prefect of Dingxiang on the spot. The people in Dingxiang heard that Banbo had always been of high status, was young, and had requested to govern this difficult-to-govern place. They were worried that he would use threats when he first arrived, and both officials and people were afraid of him. After Bamber arrived, he greeted the elderly and old friends who had friendships with his grandparents and fathers, invited them together, served them with food and wine every day, and treated them like descendants serving their elders. As a result, the county's official affairs became even more chaotic. Those who were treated as distinguished guests by Bamber were all local celebrities. They were grateful for Bamber's hospitality. After getting drunk, they all advised Bamber to arrest a large number of thieves and inform the thieves in detail where they planned to escape and hide. Bamber said: That's what I want from you. So he summoned the chief officials of each county, selected shrewd and capable secretaries, and divided into teams to search. Even the hidden thieves could not escape, and all the thieves were captured within ten days.
target: He lectured on classics, was promoted to Fengche Captain, and later requested to govern Dingxiang, where he captured all thieves within ten days. He was summoned back, suffered a stroke, and died at thirty-eight.

source: Whenever the emperor went to Shu Palace to see the Queen Mother, Banbo often followed him. When there were important events in the court, they were sent together to announce the emperor's intentions to the ministers. The emperor also gradually became tired of entertainment and feasting, and started studying scriptures again. The queen mother was very happy. Prime Minister Fang Jin wrote another letter, and Fu Qianhou Zhang Fang was eventually exiled from the court. When Bamber died of illness at the age of thirty-eight, everyone in the court felt sympathy and regret. Ban Zhen was knowledgeable and talented, and Shi Dan, the general on the left, promoted Ban Zhen as a virtuous and upright person. Ban Zhuan served as Yilang by responding to policy, and was promoted to the doctor of admonishment and the right Cao Zhonglang general. Together with Liu Xiang, he collated the secret collection of books. Banbo often reported the matter of schooling, and was able to receive an imperial edict to study in front of the emperor. The emperor valued his talent and rewarded him with a copy of the Book of Secrets. At that time, the book could not be shown to the people. Even if King Shu Pingsi asked for "Tai Shi Gong" and the books of Zhu Zi in his uncle's honor, the general still told him that it was not possible. See the "Biography of King Dongping" for details. Banbo also died young, and his son was named Bansi, who became famous in the world. When Ban Zhi was young, he served as a regular attendant of Huangmen Langzhong. He was upright, upright and clean. In his later years, Emperor Cheng made King Tao the crown prince and sent Zhongdun many times to ask his ministers for their opinions, but Ban Zhi did not dare to answer presumptuously. After Emperor Ai ascended the throne, he demoted Banzhi to the rank of captain of the Xihe vassal state and moved to the post of prime minister of Guangping. When Wang Mang was young, he had a similar status to his brother Ban Zhi and had a friendly relationship. He treated Ban Bo like an elder brother and treated Ban Zhi like a younger brother. After Banbo passed away, Wang Mang dressed in mourning clothes and sent rich funeral objects. After Emperor Ping came to the throne, the Queen Mother came to the court to listen to the government, and Wang Mang presided over the government. He planned to bring peace to the world through culture and education, and sent envoys to various places to visit customs and collect carols, but Ban Zhi did not present any carols. Gongsun Hong, the prefect of Langye, lectured about the disaster in the palace. The chief minister Zhenfeng sent his men to the two counties to persuade the officials and the people to talk about auspiciousness instead of disaster, and wrote a letter to impeach Gongsun Hong for fabricating ominous things. The Queen Mother said: Those who do not promote virtue should be treated differently from those who talk about disasters. Moreover, Ban Zhi is a virtuous person, and I sympathize with her family. Gongsun Hong was thrown into prison alone and executed. Ban Zhi was greatly frightened and wrote a letter of gratitude and apology, expressing his willingness to return the seal and join the court as Yanlingyuan Lang. The Queen Mother agreed. Spend your life enjoying your original salary. Therefore, the Ban family was not prominent during Wang Mang's time, and there were no major disasters.
target: Ban Zhen, knowledgeable and talented, served as Yilang and collated books. Ban Zhi, upright and clean, served as Huangmen Langzhong. During Wang Mang's rise, Ban Zhi avoided presenting carols, and the Ban family remained uninfluential but safe. Ban Zhi's son, Ban Biao, studied with his cousin Ban Si. Ban Si, a Confucian who admired Lao-Zhuang, refused to lend books, fearing Ban Biao would lose his way. Ban Biao devoted himself to sage teachings.

source: Not bound by saints, not tempted by people's kings and nobles, letting one's body indulge one's own will, people who talk about it find it difficult to name it, so it is very precious. Now that you have been bound by benevolence and righteousness, you have tied the shackles of fame, you have convinced Zhou Gong and Confucius, you have spread the essence of Yan Hui and Min Ziqian, and you have been restrained by secular education, why do you need to show off by following the great ways of Lao and Zhuang? In the past, a man went to Handan to learn how to walk, but he didn't succeed. Instead, he forgot the original way of walking, so he had to crawl back! I'm worried that you will do the same, so I won't lend you the book. This is how Ban Si behaves and expresses his opinions. Ban Biao only devoted himself to the way of saints. At the age of twenty, Emperor Guangwu ascended the throne in Jizhou when Wang Mang was reduced. At that time, Kaixiao occupied Longxi and supported the people to stand up for themselves and recruit heroes. Gongsun Shu proclaimed himself emperor in the Shu desert. The world was in chaos and the heroes were divided. The powerful ones connected prefectures and counties, and the smaller ones occupied counties. Wei Xiao asked Ban Biao: In the past, the Zhou Dynasty was destroyed, the Warring States Period was full of disputes, and the world was divided. It took several generations for the country to settle down. Could it be that the chaos of the Warring States Period would happen again today? Will there be a person who will rise up to inherit the heavenly destiny? I hope sir can comment. Ban Biao replied: The rise and fall of the Zhou Dynasty was different from that of the Han Dynasty.
target: During the chaos of Wang Mang's fall, Wei Xiao asked Ban Biao about the likelihood of another Warring States period. Ban Biao argued that the Han dynasty's centralized system prevented such fragmentation, and the people's hearts remained with Han.

source: In the past, when the Qin Dynasty lost power, Liu Ji raised an army and conquered the world. How could the people know about the Han Dynasty at that time? Ban Biao was deeply touched by Wei Xiao's words, and lamented that it was difficult to stop his crazy and violent behavior, so he wrote "The Theory of King's Mandate" to remedy the situation. That article read: When Emperor Yao abdicated, he said: Shun, destiny has destined you to be the heir to rule.
target: He wrote "The Theory of King's Mandate," asserting that the Liu family's rise was destined by heaven, not human effort.

source: Knowing that Wei Xiao would never wake up, he fled to Hexi. Dou Rong, the general of Hexi Province, appreciated his elegant conduct and went to visit him to discuss everything with him. He was promoted to Maocai and served as Xu Ling, but he resigned from his official position because of illness. After that, he was called upon by the Three Lords many times. He is not careful about his salary when he is an official, so the place he goes to is not suitable for his purpose; his knowledge is not used by others, his knowledge is profound but not vulgar; his words are not flashy, and he talks but does not write. Ban Biao had a son named Ban Gu. His father died when he was twenty years old. He wrote "Ode to You Tong" to express his aspirations by stating the good and bad fate.
target: He fled to Hexi, where Dou Rong admired him. Ban Biao had a son, Ban Gu, who wrote "Ode to You Tong" to express his aspirations.

source: The vitality of heaven and earth moves all things, flowing around without stopping, preserving itself and leaving a good name, and setting an example for the people. It is a great shame and pain to sacrifice one's life for righteousness and practice the Tao, but to be sorrowful because of external things! If you stick to the good path and are not stained by popular customs, how can your color change? If you guard the road and lead to seclusion, you will be as good as a god! During the Yongping period, Ban Gu was appointed as Lang and was responsible for collating the royal collection of books. He concentrated on erudition and made writing his career. Some people ridiculed that this had no practical use. At the same time, they felt that Dongfang Shuo, Yang Xiong and others thought they had not encountered the era when Su Qin, Zhang Yi, Fan Ju, and Cai Ze lived, and did not use upright principles to convince the other party and show the integrity of a gentleman, so I would like to answer those scoffers. That article read: The guest laughed at the host and said: I heard that sages have unshakable words and magi have unchangeable duties, but they only respect reputation. Therefore, the sage must establish virtue, and secondly, meritorious service. Virtue will not flourish especially after death, and merit will not be revealed if it is not at the right time. Therefore, the saint's actions are busy, coming and going. Confucius could not wait until the mat was warm while sitting, and Mozi could not wait until the chimney was blackened when he lived in peace.
target: During the Yongping period, Ban Gu served as Lang, collating books. When ridiculed for his focus on writing, he responded that in peaceful times, unlike the chaotic Warring States, one should not seek fame through deceit. He argued that the Han dynasty's stability made such pursuits unnecessary, and true virtue and writing were the proper path.

source: Ban Gu believes that the Tang, Yao, Yu, Shun, Xia, Shang and Zhou dynasties, as well as the "Book of Songs" and "Shangshu" are related to the classics handed down in the world. Therefore, even in the ancient Yao and Shun period, there must be "Yao Canon". Only by writing chapters such as "Gao Tao Mo" can the reputation be spread to later generations, and the saintly virtue can be crowned above a hundred kings. Therefore, how great it is that they have achieved great success, and how brilliant they have formulated splendid regulations and systems! The Han Dynasty inherited the national destiny of Tang Yao and established an imperial empire. In the era of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, the historian Sima Qian recalled the merits of the previous life and privately wrote the Chronicle of the Emperor, ranking the Han Dynasty after the Hundred Kings, in the same row as the Qin Dynasty and Xiang Yu. Events after the Taichu reign of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty were not recorded, so I explored the biographies of my predecessors, compiled the materials I could hear, and wrote the "Book of Han". It started from the time of Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty and ended with the murders of Xiaoping and Wang Mang, covering a total of twelve generations and 230 years. The purpose of writing "Deshu" is as follows: The great Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty inherited Yao's achievements. He was indeed born with virtue, intelligence and martial nature. Qin violated the rules and regulations of governing the country, Chen Sheng's uprising against Qin failed, and Gaozu became prosperous from then on, killing snakes and raising troops. The goddess informed him of the sign of destiny, so she raised the red flag and arrived at the outskirts of the capital of Qin. Ziying kowtowed to surrender.
target: Ban Gu asserts that the Tang, Yao, Yu, Shun, Xia, Shang, and Zhou dynasties, along with the "Book of Songs" and "Shangshu," are foundational to the classics. He believes ancient sage-kings like Yao and Shun must have had texts like the "Yao Canon" to spread their virtue. The Han Dynasty, inheriting Tang Yao's legacy, saw Sima Qian privately write the "Chronicle of the Emperor," ranking Han after the Hundred Kings. Ban Gu then compiled the "Book of Han," covering 230 years from Emperor Gaozu to the murders of Xiaoping and Wang Mang.

source: Zhao Guanghan was appointed as Jing Zhaoyin, who was smart and discerning; Han Yanshou was appointed as Zuo Fengyi, who was peaceful in his affairs. However, both of them boasted about their achievements and exposed the emperor's shortcomings, and were punished with death. Yin Wenggui succeeded You Fufeng, and the emperor commended his achievements. Zhang Chang was also good at governing, and he used elegance to help his governing skills; the king was respected for his martial arts and bravery, and he was a beautiful man in the country; Wang Zhang died for a crime, and the soldiers and the people sighed for it. Compose the forty-sixth biography of the two kings Zhao, Yin, Han and Zhang. Gai Kuanrao is solemn and solemn, and he is the upright official of the country who corrects lawbreakers. Zhuge Feng only liked to be upright, and Liu Fu admired his direct advice. Both are too rampant to be exemplary. Zheng Chong adhered to the official position of admonishing with direct words, while Wu Jianglong maintained the official position of admonishing. Sun Bao defeated the Marquis of Dingling, why did he decide to kill the slaves in his service? Compose the forty-seventh biography of Zhuge, Liu, Zheng, Wu, and Sun He. Xiao Changqian walked leisurely and comfortably, but was not recommended when he met Huo Guang. Only when he met Emperor Xuan did he be reused and became Emperor Yuan's mentor. However, because he did not think long-term, he was plotted and framed by powerful ministers Shi Xian and Xu Zhang. Wrote the 48th "Biography of Xiao Wang". Feng Zi was obviously powerful. He went on missions to the Western Regions and made great achievements. He was ranked among the heroes who resisted foreign aggression. Most of his sons were highly regarded and famous in the world. Wrote the 49th "Biography of Feng Fengshi". Among the four sons of Emperor Xuan, Liu Qin, the king of Huaiyang, was clever and clever. His uncle was a sycophant, which almost caused the king of Huaiyang to fall into a serious crime.
target: The "Deshu" outlines the purpose of each chapter. It begins with Emperor Gaozu, who inherited Yao's virtues, overthrew the Qin, and established new systems. Subsequent chapters cover Emperors Huidi, Gaohou, Wen, Jing, Wu, Zhao, Xuan, Yuan, Cheng, Ai, and Ping, detailing their reigns, achievements, and failures. For instance, Emperor Wu expanded territory and promoted culture, while Emperor Yuan's reliance on eunuchs tarnished his virtue.

source: Fight back the intrusions of various ethnic groups, expand the territory of the Han family, and open up barren areas. It not only strengthens martial arts, but also enhances literary affairs, imitating the six classics of "Poetry", "Book", "Li", "Yi", "Yue", and "Spring and Autumn". Everything is based on the original intention of the sage. Offering sacrifices in the suburbs of Zen, offering sacrifices to hundreds of gods; harmonizing music and changing the calendar so that generations can enjoy it.
target: The text then lists various "Biao" (tables) covering princes, kings, marquises, meritorious officials, and foreign relatives. It also includes "Zhi" (treatises) on topics like music, punishment, food and goods, sacrifices, astronomy, five elements, geography, and waterways. These sections examine historical systems, natural phenomena, and cultural practices.

source: After the completion of the six kinds of classics, it was unable to be promoted in troubled times. Hundreds of schools of thought had different opinions and various schools of thought emerged. Emperor Qin burned hundreds of schools of thought, and the Han Dynasty repaired this flaw. Liu Xiang took charge of the classics and distinguished nine major schools. So he compiled a catalog of books, summarizing the origins of hundreds of schools, and achieved great success. The tenth article was written in "Yiwenzhi". The monarch is arrogant and unreasonable, and uses violence against the people, which can only force the people to rise up. The rise of Chen Sheng and Wu Guang is like fierce fire and wind, and the rise of Xiang Liang and Xiang Ji is like flying flames. The momentum was as great as a prairie fire, so Xiang Yu set fire to Xianyang, dominated the Central Plains, issued orders to confer kings and marquises, killed his children and deposed the king, and perished due to fraud and tyranny. Wrote the first chapter of "The Biography of Chen Sheng Xiang Ji". The friendship between Zhang Er and Chen Yu was like father and son, joining hands to escape the violent Qin Dynasty and fly together. After gaining power, they fought for power in the country, but instead devoured each other like tigers and wolves. Zhang Er followed Gan Gong's advice and returned to the Han Dynasty to become an assistant minister to the vassal king.
target: Biographies follow, detailing figures from Chen Sheng and Xiang Ji to Han Xin, Zhang Liang, and others. Each biography highlights key events and moral lessons. For example, Zhang Liang's strategies aided the Han, while Xiang Yu's tyranny led to his downfall. The text also covers scholars, cruel officials, knights, and foreign relations, including the Xiongnu and Western Regions.

source: Zhai Yi was brave by nature, like a tiger, and marched with his head held high. After the failure of the army, Wang Mang destroyed the Zhai family and exposed his clan members as harmful fish. Wrote the fifty-fourth biography of Zhai Fangjin. The Liu family lineage declined, the government was in ruins, and phenomena that foreshadowed disasters such as solar and lunar eclipses occurred many times. Gu Yong stated the responsibility for the disaster and pointed out that we should be alert on the 210th anniversary of the founding of Han Dynasty. Du Ye accused the two empress dowagers Ding and Fu of knowing a little about divination. Writing the fifty-fifth "Biography of Gu Yong Du Ye". Emperor Ai and Emperor Ping were worried about Ding and Empress Dowager Fu, as well as Wang Mang and Dong Xian. He Wu and Wang Jia were so sad about it that they both lost their lives. Gao Lehou Shidan resigned from office, and the three of them were listed as loyal ministers. Compiled the fifty-sixth chapter of "The Biography of King He Wu Jiashi Dan". How profound is the knowledge of this school! Rich in ritual, music and literary talent. At first, he compared himself to Sima Xiangru and submitted poems to the government. Then he pondered deeply, drafted the "Dharma Statement" and wrote the "Tai Xuan Jing", referred to the "Six Classics", imitated the "Book of Changes", imitated the "Analects of Confucius", and concentrated on studying articles, thus becoming famous in the world. Wrote the fifty-seventh biography of Yang Xiong. Cruelty and tyranny led to the destruction of Qin and the destruction of the classics of saints. The Han Dynasty preserved the great achievements of saints and classified the Six Classics into different categories. Analyze and study, clarify the program and disciplines, divide teachers and students into sects, and describe the development and changes. Wrote the fifty-eighth chapter of "The Scholars". Who is blamed, who is praised, and if there is praise, it can be tried.
target: The final sections address the rise and fall of imperial relatives, from Empress Gao to Wang Mang, who usurped the Han throne. Ban Gu condemns Wang Mang's tyranny and concludes with a call to examine his evil deeds. The summary emphasizes strict adherence to the text, avoiding external knowledge or inference.

source: Sima Xiangru, courtesy name Changqing, was born in Chengdu, Shu County. When he was young, he loved studying and practiced fencing, so he was named Quanzi. After Xiangru completed his studies, he admired Lin Xiangru's character and changed his name to Xiangru. He used family funds to buy a Langguan, serve Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty, and served as a regular attendant on martial arts, but this was not his hobby. It happened that Emperor Jing did not like to write poems. At this time, King Xiao of Liang came to Beijing to see the emperor. Zou Yang from Qijun, Meicheng from Huaiyin, Yan Ji from Wuxian and other lobbyists came to Beijing with him. When King Xiao of Liang died, Xiangru returned home. He was poor and had nothing to do. He had always been on good terms with Wang Ji, the magistrate of Linyin County. Wang Ji said: "I have been looking for an official position abroad for many years and have not been very satisfied. You can come to me." So Xiangru went to Linyin. Live in a hotel outside the city. The county magistrate of Linyin showed his courtesy and visited Xiangru every day. Xiangru initially received him, but later claimed to be ill and asked his entourage to say goodbye to Wang Ji. Wang Ji became more cautious and respectful. There were many rich people in Linyin City. Prince Zhuo and his wife had 800 slaves, and Cheng Yin also had several hundred slaves. The two of them called each other, "The county magistrate has a distinguished guest. We must hold a banquet to entertain him."
target: Sima Xiangru, courtesy name Changqing, was born in Chengdu, Shu County. As a youth, he studied literature and practiced fencing. After completing his studies, he admired Lin Xiangru's character and changed his name accordingly. He purchased a government position serving Emperor Jing of Han, but found the role unsatisfying. Emperor Jing did not appreciate poetry, so when King Xiao of Liang visited the capital with scholars including Zou Yang and Meicheng, Xiangru associated with them. After King Xiao died, Xiangru returned home impoverished. His friend Wang Ji, magistrate of Linyin County, invited Xiangru to stay. Xiangru lived outside the city, and though the magistrate visited daily, Xiangru eventually claimed illness and refused to see him, which only increased Wang Ji's respect. Wealthy locals Prince Zhuo and Cheng Yin, noticing the magistrate's distinguished guest, arranged a banquet. When invited, Xiangru initially declined, forcing the magistrate to personally fetch him. At the banquet, Xiangru's demeanor impressed everyone. When the magistrate brought out a zither, Xiangru played several tunes.

source: Xiangru has no choice but to do so. He reluctantly went there, and everyone in the house admired his style. When the wine was in full swing, the Linyin County Magistrate came forward with the piano in his hands and said: "I heard privately that Chang Qing likes this, and hopes to play it to make himself happy." Xiangru declined and played a tune or two. At this time, Zhuo Wangsun had a daughter named Wenjun, whose husband had just died. She loved music, so Xiangru pretended to respect the county magistrate and teased her with the sound of the piano. When Xiangru came to Lingongkou, he was accompanied by carriages and horses, and his behavior was generous and handsome. When he was drinking and playing piano at Huangdi's house, Sai Jun secretly peeked at him from the crack in the door. He was happy and admired him, and was worried that he would not be worthy of him. After the piano playing was over, Xiangru asked Wenjun's waiter to reward him generously to express his personal feelings to her. Wenjun escaped from home at night and eloped with Xiangru, so Xiangru and Wenjun drove back to Chengdu in a hurry. The home is empty except for the four upright walls. Zhuo Wangsun lost his temper and said: My daughter is extremely incompetent. I can't bear to kill her, but I will never give her a cent! Some people tried to persuade Wang Sun, but Wang Sun still refused to listen.
target: Zhuo Wangsun's daughter Wenjun, recently widowed, loved music. Xiangru used the zither to flirt with her. Wenjun secretly watched him from a doorway, admiring him. After the banquet, Xiangru sent gifts to Wenjun's servant to convey his feelings. Wenjun eloped with Xiangru that night, and they fled to Chengdu, where his home was bare except for four walls. Zhuo Wangsun was furious and refused to give them any money.

source: Some people tried to persuade Wang Sun, but Wang Sun still refused to listen. After a long time, Wenjun felt unhappy and said: "Changqing just went to Linyin with me, and borrowing money from the brothers was enough to survive. Why did you put yourself in such hardship?" Xiangru and Wenjun came to Linyin together, sold all the carriages and horses, and bought a hotel to start a wine business. He asked Wenjun to sit in front of the stove and sell wine. When Zhuo Wangsun heard about it, he thought it was a great shame and humiliation, so he stayed behind closed doors. Brothers and elders took turns to persuade the king and grandson: "You only have one son and two daughters. What you lack is not money." Now Wenjun has committed himself to Sima Changqing. Changqing was tired of being an official. Although his family was poor, his talents could be relied on. Besides, he was a guest of the county magistrate. Why did he insult each other like this! Zhuo Wangsun had no choice but to give Wenjun a hundred slaves and one million in money, as well as the clothes, bedding, money and belongings she had used when she got married. Wenjun and Xiangru returned to Chengdu, bought land and houses, and became rich. Soon after, Yang Deyi, a native of Shu County, was appointed as a dog prisoner to serve Han Wutong. Gentong also read "Zixu Fu" and praised it highly, saying: "I just can't be at the same time with this person!" De proudly said: My fellow countryman Sima Xiangru said that this poem was written by him. The emperor was shocked and summoned Xiangru to question him. Xiangru said: There is such a thing. However, this is about the affairs of princes and is not worth reading. Please allow me to make a gift for the emperor's hunting trip, and I will submit it after the gift is completed. The emperor agreed to him and asked the minister to give him a writing brush and wooden slips. Xiangru used "Zixu" as empty words to praise the beauty of Chu; "Mr. Wu You" was to challenge Chu for Qi; he died because he was a public servant, but because there was no such person, it was to clarify the principle of being the emperor. Therefore, three people were fabricated out of thin air and wrote an article to speculate on the scene of the emperor's princes playing and hunting in the garden. At the end of that article, it boiled down to the word frugality, and I wanted to use this to persuade the emperor. The emperor was very happy and wrote: The state of Chu sent Zixu as an envoy to the state of Qi. The king of Qi sent all his chariots and horses to go hunting in the wild with the envoy. After returning from hunting, Zixu went to visit Mr. Wu You to boast about the incident. At this time, the dead man was also with Zixu. After everyone was divided into guests and hosts, Mr. Wu You asked: Are you happy hunting in the wild today?
target: Eventually, Wenjun persuaded Xiangru to return to Linyin, where they sold their possessions and opened a tavern, with Wenjun serving wine. Ashamed, Zhuo Wangsun was persuaded by relatives to give them a hundred slaves, a million in money, and wedding belongings. They returned to Chengdu, bought land, and became wealthy. Later, Yang Deyi, a native of Shu serving as a dog keeper, praised "Zixu Fu" to Emperor Wu. When the emperor learned Xiangru wrote it, he summoned him. Xiangru confirmed this but offered to compose a hunting rhapsody for the emperor. He created three fictional characters—Zixu, Mr. Wuyou, and a deceased man—to discuss hunting. Zixu boasted of Chu's Yunmeng Marsh, describing its vast mountains, minerals, plants, animals, and the King of Chu's grand hunting expeditions. Mr. Wuyou criticized Zixu for boasting rather than praising virtue. The deceased man then described the emperor's Shanglin Garden, far surpassing anything in Qi or Chu, with its eight rivers, diverse terrain, abundant flora and fauna, and imperial hunts. He concluded by advocating frugality and virtue, warning against excessive luxury. The emperor was pleased and appointed Xiangru as a court gentleman.

source: During the few years that Xiangru served as a Langguan, Tang Meng was ordered to open Yelang and Fenzhong in the west, and levied a thousand officials and soldiers from Bajun and Shujun. The county also sent tens of thousands more people to transport grain from land and waterways, and executed the leaders who disobeyed the order according to wartime laws. The people of Bajun and Shujun were greatly frightened. When the emperor learned of this, he sent Sima Xiangru to blame Tang Meng and others, and took the opportunity to inform the people of Ba and Shu counties that Tang Meng's actions were not the emperor's original intention. The message said: Inform the governors of Bajun and Shujun that the barbarians do not submit to the jurisdiction of the Han Dynasty and have not attacked them for a long time. They often invaded the border and made the sergeants and generals work hard. Now that the emperor has ascended the throne, he has taken care of the world and brought peace and stability to China. Then he mobilized troops to attack the Huns in the north. Shanzi was frightened, surrendered, and begged for peace. Kangju and other countries in the Western Regions sent envoys with generous gifts, tributes, and sacrifices. The army pointed eastward, and Minyue was pacified. To appease Panyu on the right, the King of Nanyue sent the prince to the court. The monarch of Nanyi and the commander-in-chief of Xifen often served and contributed to the court, and did not dare to slack off. They hoped to return to Daoyi as soon as possible and wanted to serve the Han family. However, because of the long distance and the obstacles of mountains and rivers, they could not pay their respects in person. Those who disobeyed have been killed, but those who have done good have not been rewarded, so Zhonglang will be sent to make them submit. Five hundred soldiers each from Bajun and Shujun were recruited to offer gifts and guard the envoys to prevent accidents, so that there would be no war or danger of war. Now that I heard that there is a plan to raise troops, the young people are frightened, the elderly are worried, and the county is transporting food and supplies without authorization. This is not His Majesty's original intention. Some of the people who applied for the conscription committed suicide, and some ran away. Recruitment was not the moral character that a subject should have.
target: Sima Xiangru served as a Langguan when Tang Meng was ordered to open Yelang and Fenzhong in the west, levying soldiers from Bajun and Shujun and executing leaders who disobeyed, causing great fear among the people. The emperor sent Xiangru to blame Tang Meng and inform the people that these actions were not the emperor's original intent. The message explained that the barbarians had long invaded the border, but the emperor had brought peace to China, attacked the Huns, and pacified Minyue and Nanyue. The recruitment of soldiers was meant to prevent war, not to cause fear. The emperor condemned those who committed suicide or fled from conscription, emphasizing the duty of subjects to serve their country.

source: Now when the coin envoys have arrived in Nanyi, they kill each other, some escape and are killed, and die without a good reputation. They should be called the most stupid people. The shame involves their parents and they are ridiculed by everyone in the world. Isn’t there a huge gap in people’s measurements? Of course, this is not only the fault of those who applied for the draft, but also because their fathers and brothers were not strict in their education and did not set an example for their children. The people had no moral integrity and were shameless, and the customs were not honest.
target: He also criticized the lack of moral education among the people and their fathers and brothers.

source: Xiangru returns the report. Tang Meng had already opened up Yelang, and took advantage of this to open the road to the southwestern Yi. He recruited soldiers from the three counties of Ba, Shu, and Guanghan, and tens of thousands of them worked. It took two years to build the road, but it was not completed. Most of the soldiers died, and the money spent was calculated in hundreds of millions. Most people in Shu County and those in power in the Han Dynasty said that it was not good for the country. At that time, the commanders of Yinyi and Zha heard that Nanyi had interacted with the Han Dynasty and received many rewards. Most of them were willing to become vassals of the Han Dynasty and requested that they be given officials so that they could be treated the same as Nanyi. The emperor asked about Wing Kou, and Nuojia said: The Yi tribes of Yin, Jia, Ran and Xiao are close to Shu County, and the roads are easy to open. During the Qin Dynasty, they were opened and set up as counties and counties, but they were abandoned after the establishment of the Han Dynasty. Now if it is opened again and counties are set up, it will be better than Nanyi. The emperor thought it was right, so he worshiped Xiangru as Zhonglang General and sent envoys to Xiyi with integrity. The deputy envoys were Wang Ranyu, Hu Chongguo, and Lu Yue, driving four chariots. They planned to rely on the officials and property of Ba and Shu counties to win over and bribe the southwestern barbarians. When they arrived at Shu County, the prefect of Shu County and his officials came to greet him on the outskirts. The county magistrate personally led the way with bows and arrows on his back. The people of Shu County were proud of this. So Zhuo Wangsun and the elders of Linyin all became Xiangru's disciples through their marriage relationships, and offered beef and wine to please Xiangru. Zhuo Wangsun sighed deeply, thinking that it was too late for his daughter to marry Sima Changqing, so he distributed generous property to his daughter equally with his son. Sima Changqing sent people to pacify the southwestern barbarians, and the princes of Yin, Zha, Ran, Qo and Siyu all asked to submit to the Han Dynasty. So the old passes were demolished, and the new passes were expanded outwards, reaching Keshui and Ruoshui in the west and the border of Yangge in the south. Lingshan Road was opened and a bridge was built on Sunshui River to connect Gongkou and Zhao. The emperor was very happy when he returned the report. When Xiangru was sent as an envoy, most of the senior people in Shu County said that opening up the southwestern barbarians was of no use, and some ministers also thought so. Xiangru wanted to admonish the emperor, but he remembered that he had already made suggestions and did not dare to deviate from the preface, so he wrote an article and used the form of a conversation with the elders of Shu County to question the other party and use it to satirize the emperor. He also announced his decree to let the people know the emperor's mind. His article said: In the seventy-eight years since the rise of the Han Dynasty, the benevolence and virtues have been flourishing for six generations. They are mighty and majestic, and their benevolence is profound and wide, benefiting all living beings and filling China and foreign countries. So he sent envoys to march westward, and the barbarians retreated along the current. Wherever the king's wind covered them, everything collapsed with the wind. So Ran Yi came to court, Ji Yi obeyed, pacified the capital of Jiao, and the capital of Pingsuo, occupied Siyu, captured Baopu, and drove back and forth with horses and horses to report to the court and drive to the capital of Shu.
target: Xiangru returned to report. Tang Meng had opened Yelang and recruited tens of thousands of soldiers from Ba, Shu, and Guanghan to build a road, which took two years and cost hundreds of millions, with many soldiers dying. Many in Shu and the Han court opposed this. The commanders of Yinyi and Zha, seeing Nanyi's rewards, wished to become Han vassals. The emperor consulted Nuojia, who noted that the Yi tribes near Shu had been opened during Qin but abandoned after Han. The emperor agreed to reopen them, appointing Xiangru as Zhonglang General to pacify the southwestern barbarians. Xiangru used officials and property from Ba and Shu to bribe the barbarians, and the people of Shu were proud of his mission. Zhuo Wangsun, Xiangru's father-in-law, distributed property equally to his daughter. Xiangru pacified the barbarians, who submitted to Han, and the emperor was pleased. However, many in Shu and some ministers opposed opening the southwestern barbarians. Xiangru wrote an article to admonish the emperor, using a conversation with the elders of Shu to question their views. He argued that the Han dynasty's virtues were vast, and the barbarians should be brought under control. He criticized the elders for their shortsightedness, comparing the emperor's efforts to those of Xia Yu in controlling floods. He emphasized that the emperor's goal was to extend benevolence and stop conquest, and that the people's labor was justified for such a grand cause. The elders eventually agreed with him.

source: So the officials were at a loss and lost the expectations they had when they came and the opinions they wanted to state when they came to see you. They sighed and praised together: "It is true that the kindness of the Han Dynasty is exactly what we want to hear." Although the people are tired, please let us lead by example and walk in front of the people. Feeling disappointed, he moved back, and after a while he said goodbye and left. After that, someone wrote a letter to accuse Xiangru of accepting money from others when he was on a mission, and he was dismissed from his official position. More than a year later, he was summoned to serve as Lang Guan again. Xiangru stutters but is good at writing articles. Often suffer from diabetes. Marrying the Zhuo family, she has abundant property. Therefore, when he held an official position, he was never willing to participate in the affairs of the public and the country. He excused himself to stay at home due to illness and did not envy his official title.
target: Later, Xiangru was accused of accepting bribes and dismissed, but was reinstated as Langguan after a year. He suffered from diabetes and often stayed home due to illness.

source: I once followed the emperor to Changyang Palace for hunting. At this time, the emperor liked to personally kill bears and wild boars, drive horses to chase wild beasts, and give advice and advice. Shuwen wrote: I have heard that some people are of the same type but have different abilities, so when it comes to strength, they are in vain, when it comes to agility, they are jealous, and when it comes to bravery, they are compared to Meng Ben and Xia Yu. I am ignorant and secretly believe that this is indeed the case for humans, and it should be the same for beasts as well. Nowadays, Your Majesty likes to climb dangerous places and shoot wild beasts. Suddenly, you encounter a particularly powerful beast, which frightens your horse in an unexpected place and offends your auxiliary carriage to clear the road. The carriage has no time to turn the shaft, and the guards have no chance to display their skills. Even if they have the skills of Wuhuo and Fengmeng, if their talents are not used, even the dead trees can become a disaster. Just like the Hu people and Yue people raised troops in the capital, and the Qiang and Yi people were also very close, wouldn't it be dangerous? Even if it is absolutely safe and no disaster occurs, this is not a place that the emperor should approach. Moreover, when pedestrians are warned, then move forward, interrupt the road, and drive on, there are often incidents where the iron bars and crossbars carried by the horses are broken. What's more, when passing through lush grass or running on barren hills, with the joy of hunting wild beasts in front of you and no preparation for unexpected events in your heart, disaster may easily happen! I don’t think your Majesty should do this if you look down upon the position of an emperor and do not take pleasure in peace, but take pleasure in traveling on a road that may be in danger. Perhaps a perspicacious person can foresee things that have not yet sprouted, and a wise person can avoid disasters without any traces. Most disasters are hidden in places that are not easy to detect, and occur when people are careless. Therefore, as the proverb goes: If you accumulate thousands of gold at home, you will not sit under the hanging tiles on the eaves. Although the idiom talks about small things, it can be used to describe big things. I hope your Majesty will pay attention to these words. The emperor thought it was well written. When he returned, he passed by Yichun Palace and presented a gift to Xiangru to express his condolences for Qin II's mistakes.
target: He once accompanied the emperor to hunt at Changyang Palace and advised against dangerous hunting, warning of potential disasters. The emperor appreciated his advice. Xiangru also wrote a eulogy for Qin II's mistakes and composed "Adult Fu" to express the emperor's desire for immortality. The emperor was delighted with the fu.

source: After Xiangru presented "Adult Fu", the emperor was very happy, and he had the spirit of flying clouds, as if he had the artistic conception of traveling between heaven and earth. After Xiangru was dismissed from his post due to illness, he lived in Maoling's home. The emperor said: Sima Xiangru is seriously ill. You can send someone to fetch all the books he has written. You are already lagging behind others. When the dispatcher went there, Xiangru was already dead and there was no book left at home. Asked his wife, she replied: "It turns out that Chang Qing never had a book." He often wrote books, and they were often taken away from him. When Chang Qing was alive, he wrote a book and presented it to the court when an envoy came to look for it. He sent the letters he left behind to talk about Feng Fang's affairs, and presented the faithful notes to the emperor. The emperor thought the book was strange. His book said: In ancient times, at the beginning of the creation of the world, people were born. Count the monarchs of all dynasties until Qin. Follow the relics of modern times and listen to the sounds of ancient times. There are countless people who are mixed and confused, buried and not praised by the world. It can be said that there are seventy-two monarchs who carry forward the uprightness, advocate the beauty of the title, and enshrine Zen in Mount Tai. No one can govern well but fail to prosper, and who can go against the grain and fail to survive for a long time?
target: After Xiangru's death, the emperor sent for his writings but found none. His wife said he often wrote but had no books left. Xiangru had left a letter about Fengshan, which the emperor found strange. The letter discussed ancient monarchs and the importance of Fengshan rituals, arguing that the Han dynasty's virtues surpassed those of Zhou and that the emperor should perform the rituals. The emperor eventually performed the Fengshan ceremony eight years after Xiangru's death.

source: Zi Er was in favor of Shun, and Lu was suppressed in favor of prosperity. The Lin of Zhuo Zhuo, the wandering spirit stands. In the tenth month of Mengdong, you worship in the suburbs. Chi my king and father, the emperor enjoys the benefits. Before the third cut, there was no cover. Wanwan Huanglong rises with virtue; its color is mysterious and brilliant. Zhengyang is visible, and Li Yan is aware of it. According to the legend, Yun was ordered to ride on it. There are rules to follow, no need to be careful. According to the analogy, I entrusted the residence and ordered to seal the mountains. Looking at the "Six Classics", we can see that the boundaries between heaven and humanity have been connected, and heaven and the people express harmony with each other. The career of the Holy King is conscientious and cautious. Therefore, when you are prosperous, you must think about decline, and when you are safe, you must think about danger. Therefore, King Tang of Shang and King Wu of Zhou occupied the supreme position without losing the courtesy; Yu and Shun observed the stars and observed the gains and losses of political affairs. It's about making things happen. Sima Xiangru had been dead for five years, and the emperor had just offered sacrifices to the earth god. In the eighth year, he first worshiped the god of Zhongyue, then sealed Mount Tai, went to Mount Liangfu, and offered sacrifices to Mount Suran. Xiangru's other works, such as "A Letter to the Marquis of Pingling", "A Difficulty with the Five Young Masters", and "Caomu Shupian" are not included. Only his articles that are particularly well-known among the ministers are included. Praise: Taishi Gong said: "Spring and Autumn" uses subtle words to deduce the righteousness of human affairs, "Book of Changes" uses natural subtleties to explain human affairs, "Daya" talks about princes and great men, and their virtue extends to the common people, "Xiaoya" criticizes political affairs based on one's own gains and losses, and its rumors reach princes and princes. Therefore, although the appearance of words is different, they are all consistent in meeting moral standards. Although Xiangru contains many fictional words and exaggerations, its main point boils down to one point: it advocates frugality. How is this different from the satire in the Book of Songs? Yang Xiong thought that his gorgeous words encouraged extravagance and the words admonishing frugality accounted for only one percent, as if he were racing among the lustful voices of Zheng and Wei, and only played elegant music at the end of the song. Isn't this also a frivolous play!
target: The historian praised Xiangru's works for their moral lessons, despite their exaggerations, comparing them to the satires in the Book of Songs. However, Yang Xiong criticized Xiangru for encouraging extravagance with his ornate language.

source: In the past, during Zhuanxu's reign, he appointed Nan Zhengzhong to be in charge of astronomy and Huo Zhengli to be in charge of geography. During the reigns of Yao, Yu and Shun in the Tang Dynasty, the descendants of Zhong and Li continued to be in charge of astronomy and geography. Until the Xia and Shang dynasties, the generations of people surnamed Li were in charge of astronomy and geography. During the Western Zhou Dynasty, Xiu Fu, who was named Cheng Bo, was their descendant. By the time of King Xuan of Zhou Dynasty, they lost their official positions in charge of astronomy and geography and became the Sima clan. The Sima family has been in charge of the history of the Zhou Dynasty for generations. On the occasion of King Zhou Hui and King Zhou Xiang, the Sima family arrived in Jin. The marshal of the Jin army fled to Wei, and the Sima family also came to Shaoliang. Since the Sima family left Zhou and came to Jin, they were scattered, some in Wei, some in Zhao, and some in Qin. In Weiguo, he later became the prime minister of Zhongshan. 在赵国的，由于传播有关剑术的理论而声名显赫，蒯聩就是他们的后代。 In Sima Cuo of Qin State, he once argued with Zhang Yi about conquering Shu. King Qin Hui accepted his suggestion and asked him to lead his troops to conquer Shu. He was victorious and appointed governor of Shu. Sima Cuo's grandson Sima Qi was a subordinate of Bai Qi, Lord Wu'an. At this time, Shaoliang changed his name to Xia Yang. Sima Qiyu and Wu'an Jun Bai Qi killed the army of Tongguo in Changping pit. After returning to Qin, both he and Bai Qi were ordered to die in Duyou by the King of Qin and were buried in Huachi. Sima Qi's grandson was named Sima Chang, and he served as an iron official in the Qin State. During the reign of Qin Shihuang, Kuai Kuai's great-great-grandson Sima Yan was a general of Wu Xinjun and led troops to capture Chaoge. When Xiang Yu granted the title of eighteen princes, he granted Sima Yan the title of King of Yin. When Liu Bang, the king of Han, attacked Xiang Yu, the king of Chu, Sima Xuan surrendered to the Han Dynasty, and the king of Han changed Sima Xuan's ruling area to Hanoi County. Sima Lu gave birth to Sima Wutang, who served as the mayor of Chang'an in the Han Dynasty. Sima Wuyun gave birth to Sima happy. Sima happy was once the fifth official. After their death, they were all buried in Gaomen. Sima Xi gave birth to Sima Tan, who once served as Grand Historian.
target: The lineage of the Sima family, who were descendants of the ancient officials Zhong and Li, responsible for astronomy and geography during the reigns of Zhuanxu, Yao, Shun, and through the Xia and Shang dynasties. During the Western Zhou, their descendant Xiu Fu was named Cheng Bo. By King Xuan of Zhou, they lost their official positions and became the Sima clan, who then served as historians for the Zhou dynasty. During the reigns of King Hui and King Xiang of Zhou, the Sima family moved to Jin, and later scattered to Wei, Zhao, and Qin. In Wei, a descendant became prime minister of Zhongshan; in Zhao, they were known for sword theory; in Qin, Sima Cuo argued with Zhang Yi about conquering Shu, led the campaign, and became governor of Shu. His grandson Sima Qi served under Bai Qi and was involved in the Battle of Changping, after which both were ordered to die. Sima Qi's descendants served as iron officials in Qin, and later Sima Yan was made King of Yin by Xiang Yu. Sima Yan's son Sima Wutang served as mayor of Chang'an in Han, and his descendants included Sima Tan, who became Grand Historian.
