Tai Shigong studied astronomy from the Tang Dynasty, "Book of Changes" from Yang Zhe, and Taoism from Huang Zi. Tai Shigong served as an official during the reign of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty from Jianyuan to Yuanfeng. He was worried that those who studied the various schools of thought in the pre-Qin Dynasty would fail to understand the original meaning of each school and blindly believe in some absurd statements. He discussed the main spiritual principles of the six schools of thought: "Yi Da Zhuan" says: People all over the world have the same direction, but their ideas are diverse, their goals are the same, but their paths are different. Yin-Yang, Confucianism, Mohism, Mingjia, Legalism, Moralism, these schools of thought all take governing the country as their top priority, but their theories are different, with or without provinces. I think that the Yin-Yang theory advocates auspiciousness and has many taboos, which often restricts people and creates a lot of fear. However, the order of the four seasons it arranges cannot be abandoned. Confucianism is broad but lacks essentials, and it takes a lot of effort but has little effect. Therefore, it is difficult to fully implement what it advocates. However, the etiquette between monarch, minister, father and son, and the distinction between husband and wife, elder and younger, which it stipulates cannot be changed. Mohism advocates frugality but it is difficult to follow it, so all the things Mohism advocates cannot be adopted. However, the Mohist ideas on strengthening the development of the industry and practicing economy cannot be discarded. Legalism's ideas are harsh and harsh and lack kindness. However, the fact that they uphold the status of emperor and ministers cannot be changed. Famous scholars are too rigid in their formality and easily lose their correct understanding of things. However, the dialectical relationship between name and reality cannot but be seriously considered. Taoism unites people's spirit and actions in line with the invisible Tao, making all things abundant and perfect. Their doctrine follows the order of Yin and Yang in the four seasons, absorbs the strengths of Confucianism and Mohism, and takes the essence of Ming and Dharma. It transfers with time and changes with things. In this way, there is nothing inappropriate in establishing routines and handling affairs. The purpose is concise and easy to grasp. Although they do not do many things, they are very effective.
target: Sima Tan studied astronomy, the Book of Changes, and Taoism, and served under Emperor Wu of Han. He worried that scholars misunderstood the six schools of thought—Yin-Yang, Confucianism, Mohism, Legalism, Mingjia, and Taoism—and discussed their principles. He noted that Yin-Yang had many taboos but its seasonal order was useful; Confucianism was broad but lacked essentials, though its rituals were important; Mohism was frugal but hard to follow, yet its emphasis on economy was valuable; Legalism was harsh but upheld the ruler-minister distinction; Mingjia was too formal but its name-reality dialectic was worth considering; and Taoism united spirit and action, absorbed strengths of other schools, and was concise and effective. He criticized Confucianism for tiring the ruler and praised Taoism for its simplicity and adaptability.

source: The dead cannot be reborn, and the body and spirit will not be reunited if they are separated, so the saints attach great importance to this issue. From this point of view, the spirit is the foundation of human survival, and the body is the tool for human survival. If you don't first stabilize your own spirit and body, then you say that I have a way to govern the world. What can I rely on? The official position of Taishi is in charge of astronomical work and does not care about civil affairs. He had a son named Sima Qian. Sima Qian was born in Longmen and lived a life of farming and herding at the southern foot of Longmen Mountain. At the age of ten, he was able to read ancient Chinese works. At the age of 20, he traveled south to the Yangtze River and Huaihe River. He climbed Mount Kuaiji, visited Yu's Cave, went to Mount Jiuyi, inspected Shun's deeds, and went boating on the Yuan and Xiang Rivers. He crossed the Wenshui River and the Sichuan River in the north, studied in the capitals of Qi and Lu, observed the teachings of Confucius, and learned the etiquette of local archery in Zoufeng. When he traveled to Fan, Xue, Pengcheng and other places, he encountered danger for a time, and returned to Chang'an after passing through the lands of Liang and Chu. So Sima Qian became a doctor and sent an envoy to the west to conquer the area south of Bashu under the order of the imperial court. After briefly setting up Qiong, Jia and Kunming, he returned to Chang'an to report his orders to the imperial court. In this year, the emperor began to hold the Han Dynasty's Zen ceremony, but Tai Shigong was left in Zhounan and could not participate in the ceremony. Therefore, he became ill and was about to die due to anger. His son Sima Qian happened to return from his mission at this time and met his father in Luoyang. Taishi Gong held Sima Qian's hand and said with tears: Our ancestor was the Taishi of the Zhou Dynasty. As early as the ancient times of Yu, Shun and Xia Yu, he had achieved great fame and was in charge of astronomical work. Later, it declined. Do you think it will be ruined by me? If you become Taishi, you can continue the work of our ancestors.
target: Sima Tan had a son, Sima Qian, who was born in Longmen, farmed and herded, and could read ancient texts at ten. At twenty, he traveled extensively, visiting historical sites and studying in Qi and Lu. He became a doctor and was sent on a mission to the southwest. Upon returning, he found his father ill in Luoyang. His father, unable to participate in the imperial Fengshan ceremony, urged Sima Qian to continue their ancestral work as historians, emphasizing the importance of recording history. Sima Qian promised to complete his father's plan. After his father's death, Sima Qian became Grand Historian and began compiling historical records.

source: What's more, as a historian, if I ignore the emperor's saintly merits and fail to record them, bury the achievements of meritorious ministers and wise officials without discussing them, and betray my father's instructions, it will be a great sin. What I write is just a record of historical stories, and a compilation and summary of historical materials passed down from generation to generation. It is not what people call a work. And you are wrong to compare it to "Spring and Autumn". So he discussed and compiled his book in order. In the tenth year of writing, he suffered the disaster of Li Ling and was imprisoned. In prison, he sighed: This is my sin! There is no use in being crippled. After thinking about it carefully, he said: The reason why the meaning of "Poetry" and "Book" is implicit is that the author used it to better express his deep thoughts. He finally began to record the history from the Yellow Emperor to the Emperor Wu Huolin. Its titles are:
target: He later suffered the Li Ling disaster, was imprisoned, and castrated. Despite this, he continued his work, writing the "Records of the Grand Historian" from the Yellow Emperor to Emperor Wu.

source: Supporting the righteous, generous and outstanding people, they did not let themselves lose the opportunity, and established their fame in the world, and wrote seventy biographies for them. The book has a total of 130 chapters and 526,500 words. This is the "Tai Shi Gong Shu". This "Preface" summarizes the purpose of the narrative, which is to pick up lost historical events to supplement the shortcomings of the six arts and become a family story. It harmonizes various interpretations of the Six Classics and organizes hundreds of miscellaneous theories. Hide the original in a famous mountain and leave the copy in the capital, waiting for future generations of saints and gentlemen to view it. The seventieth chapter of the biographies is Sima Qian's autobiography. However, ten articles are missing among the one hundred and thirty articles. There is a table of contents but no content.
target: The text includes a detailed table of contents for the 130 chapters, covering annals, tables, treatises, hereditary houses, and biographies.

source: King Wen of Zhou was imprisoned in Xianli and deduced "The Book of Changes"; Confucius was impoverished and wrote "Spring and Autumn"; Qu Yuan was exiled and wrote "Li Sao"; Zuo Qiuming was blind and wrote "Guoyu"; Sun Tzu was executed and wrote "The Art of War"; Lu Buwei was exiled to Shu, and his "Lü Lan" was passed down to later generations; Han Fei was imprisoned in Qin and wrote "Speaking of Difficulties" and "Huan Ang". There are 300 poems in "Poetry", most of which are works by sages expressing their anger. These people are all depressed because their ideals cannot be realized, so they discuss the past to place their hopes in the future. Just like Zuo Qiuming, who lost his eyesight, his grandson lost his legs and could no longer be used by the world for the rest of his life, so he retired and wrote books to express his inner resentment in the hope that the article would be passed down to future generations and his feelings could be expressed. In recent years, I have overestimated my ability and expressed my thoughts in superficial articles. I have collected old stories that have been lost all over the world, examined historical facts, studied the reasons for the success or failure of enterprises, and explored the reasons for the rise and fall of dynasties. There are a total of 130 articles. I also want to use them to reflect the relationship between nature and society, understand the changes from ancient times to the present, and form a theory. The first draft was not finished yet, just in time for this disaster. I regret that the book was not completed, and therefore suffered a capital punishment without any sign of resentment. I really completed the writing of this book, kept it in a famous mountain, and passed it on to like-minded people in Tongdu and Dayi. In this way, I can repay the debt of humiliation I suffered in the past. Even if I am killed, I will never regret it! However, these can only be told to knowledgeable people, and it is difficult to tell simple people. Moreover, it is difficult to gain a foothold in society with a bad reputation, and one's humble status is often slandered. I suffered this disaster because of my comments. I was ridiculed by the villagers and insulted my ancestors. How could I go to pay homage to my parents' graves? Even after EMI, the shame will still get deeper and deeper! Therefore, I felt restless all day long. I stayed at home and felt as if I had lost something. When I went outside, I didn't know where to go. Whenever I think of this shame, my clothes are soaked in cold sweat. I am just a servant in the palace, how can I live in seclusion in the mountains! So I had no choice but to go with the flow for the time being and live a muddle-headed life to express my inner depression. Now Shaoqing is teaching me to recommend wise men. I am afraid this is contrary to my personal thoughts! Now even if I want to decorate myself and use beautiful words to liberate myself, it is useless. The worldly people will not believe me. On the contrary, it will only bring shame. In short, right and wrong will only be decided on the day of death. This letter cannot express my thoughts in detail, but only briefly outlines my superficial opinions. After Sima Qian's death, his books gradually spread. During the reign of Emperor Xuan, Sima Qian's grandson Yang Pang, Marquis of Pingtong, was the first to state Sima Qian's works, and thus they were published.
target: Sima Qian wrote a letter to his friend Ren An, explaining his reasons for enduring humiliation rather than committing suicide. He emphasized the importance of completing his historical work, comparing himself to ancient figures like King Wen, Confucius, Qu Yuan, and others who wrote under duress. He argued that death could be heavier than a mountain or lighter than a feather, and that his duty was to finish his book to express his thoughts and preserve history. After his death, his works gradually spread, and his grandson Yang Pang helped publish them. The text concludes with a commentary praising Sima Qian as a talented historian but noting his deviations from orthodox views, such as favoring Huang-Lao over the Six Classics and promoting knights and wealth.

source: The queen of Emperor Xiaoyuan was the mother of Emperor Cheng. The Wang family has a total of ten princes and five chief ministers. Among the relatives, no one is more prosperous than their family. Queen Wang's relatives have their own biographies. Empress Xu of Emperor Xiaocheng was the daughter of Ping Enhou Xu Jia, the general of the Great Sima Chariot Cavalry. Emperor Yuan mourned the death of his mother and mourned the murder of the Huo family for a short period of time in her reign. He specially selected Xu Jia's daughter to be betrothed to the crown prince. When Mrs. Xu first entered the crown prince's palace, the emperor sent his ministers and close associates from Huangmen to serve him. When these people came back, they told how happy the crown prince was. Emperor Yuan was overjoyed and said to his left and right: "Please pour some wine to congratulate me!" Everyone on the left and right shouted long live. After meeting for a long time, Concubine Xu gave birth to a son who died in infancy. After Emperor Cheng ascended the throne, he appointed Concubine Xu as empress. Empress Xu gave birth to another daughter, who also died in infancy. At first, the queen's father, Xu Jia, had been appointed as a general in charge of carriage and cavalry to assist the government since the Yuan Dynasty. It had been eight or nine years. After Emperor Cheng ascended the throne, he named his uncle Wang Feng, Marquis of Yangping, the Great Sima General, alongside Xu Jia. Du Qin believed that according to the old rules, the queen's father's status should be more noble than the emperor's uncle, so he advised Wang Feng: "The chariot general's status is extremely noble. General, you should respect him and do not go against his wishes." Even small differences can lead to catastrophic hostility, so we must not be careless. At that time, the glory of General Wei was greater than that of Gaihou. In modern times, older people often talk about it and hope that the general will consider it carefully. Later, the emperor planned to appoint only Wang Feng, so he gave Xu Jiawen a letter saying: The general has a distinguished status and should not be burdened by his official position. He was rewarded with two hundred catties of gold and established in the court with a special promotion position. More than a year later, Xu Jia passed away and was given the title Gonghou. Queen Xu was intelligent by nature and good at writing official scripts. From the time she became the crown prince to the time she was appointed queen, she was often favored by the emperor. Women in the harem were rarely summoned by the emperor. The empress dowager and the emperor's uncles were worried that the emperor would have no heirs. At this time, disasters occurred repeatedly. Liu Xiang, Gu Yong and others all reported that the fault was in the harem. The emperor thought they were right. Therefore, the expenses for the Queen's Palace and Yeting were reduced.
target: The Wang family, relatives of Emperor Xiaoyuan's queen, produced ten princes and five chief ministers, making them the most prosperous among all imperial relatives. Empress Xu of Emperor Xiaocheng was the daughter of General Xu Jia. Emperor Yuan selected her for the crown prince after mourning his mother's death. She initially brought joy to the court, but her children died in infancy. After Emperor Cheng ascended, he appointed her empress and appointed his uncle Wang Feng alongside Xu Jia as co-regents. Du Qin advised Wang Feng to respect Xu Jia's superior status according to tradition. Eventually, the emperor appointed only Wang Feng and granted Xu Jia a special retirement with gold. Xu Jia died over a year later. Empress Xu was intelligent and skilled in calligraphy, enjoying the emperor's favor for many years while other concubines were rarely summoned. When disasters occurred repeatedly, officials Liu Xiang and Gu Yong blamed the harem, leading to reduced expenses for the queen's palace.

source: The empress dowager and the emperor's uncles were worried that the emperor would have no heirs. At this time, disasters occurred repeatedly. Liu Xiang, Gu Yong and others all reported that the fault was in the harem. The emperor thought they were right. Therefore, the expenses for the Queen's Palace and Yeting were reduced. The queen went to the court and said: I came from a poor family with a poor diet, and I was young, ignorant, and ignorant of the truth. I was fortunate enough to be able to leave a commoner's home and serve His Majesty in the harem. Thanks to your majesty's wrong love, I am in the position of queen that I should not have earned. However, I cannot keep myself clean and fulfill my duties. I have always violated laws and regulations and undermined the system. Even though I was sentenced to exile, it was not enough to justify my crime. So the edict was read out in the Changqiu period of Renyin: The queen should follow the etiquette and laws, dress her carriages and horses, take the property from the official office, make useful items, and reward her relatives and families, all in accordance with the old practices before Emperor Xiaoyuan. I secretly thought to myself that since I became the Queen, the rewards for my family have never exceeded the system. Every time I discuss the decision with Your Majesty, Your Majesty can verify everything. Nowadays, times are different, and the system will also change. Increases and decreases complement each other. As long as it does not exceed the customization of the Han family, it is difficult to achieve complete consistency in details. Can Emperor Xiaoyuan and Emperor Xiaoxuan do the same thing? Officials don't understand these principles. Once I get such an edict, I will make mistakes at every turn.
target: The empress petitioned the emperor, arguing that her rewards to her family had never exceeded proper limits, that changing times required adapting systems, and that officials were using vague edicts to restrict her unfairly.

source: Empress Xu reigned for a total of fourteen years before being deposed. She lived in Zhaotai Palace for more than a year and then moved to Changding Palace. Nine years later, Emperor Cheng took pity on the Xu family and issued an edict saying: It is said that benevolence does not forget those who are far away, and righteousness does not forget relatives. Xu Ye, the wife of Ping'an Ganghou, had previously committed a crime of treason and injustice. Fortunately, her family was pardoned and returned to their place of origin. I think that Marquis Ping'endai is the late emperor's grandfather. His soul has nowhere to live, and there is no one to keep vigil and offer sacrifices to him. I have always kept this incident in my heart and will never forget it.
target: She requested clarification on what property she could obtain and asked to maintain traditional practices for sacrifices and family rewards.

target: Emperor Cheng responded by citing numerous natural disasters and celestial omens—solar eclipses, white vapors, meteors, floods, earthquakes, and fires—as evidence that excessive yin energy from the harem was causing the royal family's lack of heirs. He urged the empress to practice frugality and virtue.

source: The way of a gentleman is to stick to the old system and not change easily. When someone from the state of Lu was in charge of the governor's office, Min Ziqian said, "It's enough to stick to the old ways. Why change it?" Probably just hate change. "Poetry" says: Although there are no old ministers, there are still old laws and regulations, but if you don't follow the old laws, the country is in danger. Emperor Xiaowen is an example for me to learn from. The empress dowager is the standard that the queen abides by. Even if the Queen Mother did not follow common sense in the past because she did not have her ambitions, and now she is being treated favorably by the Queen Mother, how can she go beyond the Queen Mother's system? The queen should devote herself to practicing virtue and not violate the system of the previous queens. She should work hard, abide by women's ethics, save money, and put humility and economy first. To be filial to the Empress Dowager, the courtesy of meeting the emperor on the first day of the new year and the first day of the morning must not be abolished. If we continue to do this, what kind of bad things will happen! Establish a good reputation and show off your good virtues, so as to calm the discussions of the people in the world, and let the law be spread in the harem so that the concubines can obey the law. Please think deeply and don't take these things lightly. At that time, it was General Wang Feng who was in charge of the government and had the greatest power. Later, there were food shortages for three consecutive years, and most of the people who came to remonstrate blamed Wang Feng. But Gu Yong and others thought it was Queen Xu's fault. Queen Xu knew in her heart that Wang Feng would not help her. After a while, Emperor Cheng's favor for the queen diminished, and many people in the harem were favored. The queen's sister, Ping'an Ganghou's wife, Xu Ye, and others used benign ways to curse Wang Mei, Wang Feng, and others in the harem who were pregnant. When the incident was revealed, the queen mother was furious and threw these people into prison for torture. Xu Ye and others were executed. Queen Xu was convicted and deposed. Empress Xu reigned for a total of fourteen years before being deposed. She lived in Zhaotai Palace for more than a year and then moved to Changding Palace. Nine years later, Emperor Cheng took pity on the Xu family and issued an edict saying: It is said that benevolence does not forget those who are far away, and righteousness does not forget relatives. Xu Ye, the wife of Ping'an Ganghou, had previously committed a crime of treason and injustice. Fortunately, her family was pardoned and returned to their place of origin. I think that Marquis Ping'endai is the late emperor's grandfather. His soul has nowhere to live, and there is no one to keep vigil and offer sacrifices to him. I have always kept this incident in my heart and will never forget it. He ordered Ping Enhou Xu Dan and Xu's relatives in Shanyang County to return to the capital. This year, Xu Feihou died. At first, Xu Feihou's sister Xu Biao was widowed and living alone. She had an affair with Chun Yuchang, the Marquis of Dingling, and she became his concubine. Chunyu Chang lied to her and said: I can report to the Queen Mother and re-establish Queen Xu as Queen Zuo. After Xu was abolished, he secretly bribed Chun Yuchang through Aunt Xu, and exchanged letters to thank each other many times. Chunyu Chang made rude remarks in a letter and was reported. Emperor Cheng sent his court official Kong Guang to give Xu Feihou poison with a talisman. She had no choice but to commit suicide and was buried to the west of the Yanling Road Stables. Emperor Xiaocheng's classmate was selected into the harem when Emperor Cheng just ascended the throne. He started as a young envoy, but soon became favored by Emperor Cheng. He was granted the title of Jiantun and lived in Zengchengshe. He gave birth twice in the outer house, giving birth to a boy, who died a few months later. When Emperor Cheng was playing in the harem, he once planned to ride in a chariot with Ban Shizuo. Ban Tuzai refused and said: "Looking at the pictures from ancient times, the wise monarchs are sitting next to famous ministers. Only the kings of the three generations of subjugation will have favored women. If your majesty rides in the chariot with me now, won't you be similar to those monarchs who have subjugated their countries?" Emperor Cheng thought what she said made sense, so he gave up. When the Queen Mother heard about this, she said happily: "In ancient times, there was Fan Ji, and now there is Ban Shidan." Ban Jiantan recited "The Book of Songs" and "Youyao", "Dexiang", "Female Master" and other articles. Every time you are summoned by Emperor Cheng or have a speech, you must act in accordance with ancient etiquette.
target: As Wang Feng dominated the government, three years of famine led critics to blame him, but Gu Yong continued faulting Empress Xu. The emperor's favor diminished, and the empress's sister Xu Ye was discovered cursing pregnant concubines and Wang Feng. The empress dowager had Xu Ye executed, and Empress Xu was deposed after fourteen years. Nine years later, Emperor Cheng showed mercy to the Xu family, allowing them to return to the capital. The deposed empress died after her sister's affair with Chunyu Chang led to a scheme to reinstate her. Chunyu Chang made inappropriate remarks in letters, and when reported, the emperor sent poison for her to commit suicide. Ban Jiantun entered the harem when Emperor Cheng ascended and soon gained favor. When the emperor wanted her to share his chariot, she refused, citing ancient examples of wise monarchs accompanying ministers rather than favored women. The empress dowager praised her comparison to Fan Ji of ancient times. Ban Jiantun studied classical texts and always followed ancient etiquette.

Since the Hongjia period, the number of concubines favored by Emperor Cheng gradually increased. Ban nephew offered his maid Li Pingjin to Emperor Cheng. Li Ping was favored and named Jieyu. Emperor Cheng said: In the past, Queen Wei also came from a humble background. He gave Li Ping the surname Wei, which is also the so-called Wei envoy. Later, the Zhao Feiyan sisters also rose from a humble position and transcended etiquette to a greater extent than before. Both Ban Jianzi and Queen Xu fell out of favor and were rarely summoned by Emperor Cheng. In the third year of Hongjia, Zhao Feiyan falsely accused Empress Xu and Ban Jianzi of behaving like women, cursed the harem, and even cursed the emperor. Queen Xu was offended and deposed. When interrogating Ban Jianzi, she replied: I heard that life and death are determined by destiny, wealth is in heaven, and being kind and upright has not been blessed, so what do you want to gain by doing these evil things? If the ghosts and gods are aware, they will not accept this kind of prayer that loses the courtesy of being a minister; if the ghosts and gods are ignorant, it is useless to pray to them, so I will not do this kind of thing. Emperor Cheng thought what she said was reasonable and felt pity for her, so he rewarded her with one hundred catties of gold. The Zhao sisters were arrogant and jealous, and Ban Jiandan was afraid that they would harm her over time, so he requested to serve the Queen Mother in Changxin Palace, and Emperor Cheng agreed. Ban Jiantun retired to the Cambodian palace and wrote a poem lamenting his fate. His words said: Inheriting the virtues of my ancestors, my character is upright and kind, and my humble body has allowed me to enter the palace. I live in the harem. Thanks to the great love of the Holy One, the bright light of the sun and moon shines on me. How prosperous the emperor's favor is. I am favored in Zengchengshe.
target: As the emperor's favor shifted to other concubines, she presented her maid Li Ping to the emperor, who became favored and was given the surname Wei. Later, the Zhao sisters rose to even greater prominence. When Zhao Feiyan falsely accused Empress Xu and Ban Jiantun of cursing the harem, Ban Jiantun defended herself by stating that if ghosts and gods were aware, they would not accept improper prayers, and if ignorant, prayers were useless. The emperor pitied her and rewarded her. Fearing the Zhao sisters' jealousy, she requested to serve the empress dowager in Changxin Palace, where she wrote poems lamenting her fate and describing her lonely life in the palace. After Emperor Cheng's death, she guarded his cemetery until her death.

source: Life is only once in this world, but it is fleeting like duckweed. Wealth, honor, and favor have been obtained, but how can the common people be so happy? It’s a pleasure to work hard, but if you are like this in this life, how can you seek happiness? Concubines usurp the legitimate throne all the time, "green clothes" and "white flowers" have existed since ancient times. After the death of Emperor Cheng, Ban Jianzi was sent to guard the cemetery, where she was buried after her death. Empress Zhao of Emperor Xiaocheng was originally a palace official in Chang'an. When she was first born, her parents didn't want to feed her, but after throwing her away for three days, she didn't die, so they took her home and raised her. When she grew up, she went to Princess Yang's house to learn singing and dancing, and was called Feiyan. Emperor Cheng once left the palace incognito and visited Princess Yang'a. The princess made people sing and dance for her. Emperor Cheng liked Zhao Feiyan very much when he saw her, so he invited her to the palace, where she was extremely favored. Feiyan had a younger sister who was also summoned to the palace. Both sisters were named disciples, and their status was higher than that of the entire harem. After Queen Xu was deposed, the emperor planned to appoint Zhao Tudan as the queen. The empress dowager thought she was of low origin and refused to agree. Chunyu, the son of the Queen Mother's sister, wrote poems and sent messages to and from him many times. Emperor Cheng understood the Queen Mother's thoughts and made Zhao Lin, the father of Zhao Nephew, the Marquis of Chengyang. More than a month later, Zhao Tudan was appointed queen. He also recalled Chunyu Chang's contribution to the construction of Changling, and was granted the title of Marquis of Dingling. After Zhao Feiyan was appointed queen, she was no longer so favored, but her sister was the most favored and was named Zhaoyi. Living in Zhaoyang House, the courtyard is decorated with red, the hall is painted with two layers of paint, the steps are made of copper, coated with a layer of gold, and the steps are made of white marble. The wall strips are often made of gold and decorated with blue field jade, pearls, and green feathers. The entire harem has never been so luxurious. The Zhao sisters have been doting on her for more than ten years, but they have never had children. In the last years of Emperor Cheng's reign, King Dingtao came to pay homage. King Dingtao's grandmother, the Queen Mother Fu, secretly bribed Queen Zhao and Zhao Zhaoyi, and King Dingtao was finally appointed as the crown prince. In the spring of the next year, Emperor Cheng died. Emperor Cheng was usually in good health and had no illnesses. At this time, King Liu Yan of Chu Si and King Liu Li of Liang came to see him. They had to leave early the next morning, so Emperor Cheng arranged a curtain and stayed in the White Tiger Palace. He also plans to make Kong Guang, the general of the left, prime minister, and the official seal and official announcement have been prepared. After a night of nothing, I woke up in the morning, put on my pantyhose, and tried to sit up, but my clothes suddenly fell off and I was speechless. At ten quarters of the day, Emperor Cheng died. The people believed that Zhao Zhaoyi was guilty, and the Empress Dowager issued an edict to the Grand Sima Wang Mang and the Prime Minister Da Sikong, saying: The emperor suddenly died, and people were talking about it and they didn't know what was going on.
target: Empress Zhao, originally a palace official in Chang'an, was abandoned at birth but survived. She learned singing and dancing at Princess Yang'a's house and was called Feiyan. Emperor Cheng visited incognito, became enamored with her, and brought her to the palace. Her sister also entered the palace, and both received unprecedented favor. After Empress Xu was deposed, the emperor wanted to make Zhao empress, but the empress dowager objected due to her low birth. Through Chunyu Chang's mediation, the emperor made Zhao's father a marquis, and Zhao became empress. Her sister became Zhaoyi and lived in unprecedented luxury. After more than a decade without children, they were bribed by King Dingtao's grandmother to support him as crown prince. Emperor Cheng died suddenly while in good health, and Zhao Zhaoyi was blamed. An investigation revealed that two other concubines had borne sons who were killed by Zhao Zhaoyi's orders. After Emperor Ai's death, Wang Mang reported to the empress dowager, who demoted and then deposed Empress Zhao, who committed suicide after sixteen years as empress.

source: Ji Bu, a native of Chu, was famous for his chivalry. Xiang Yu asked him to lead troops, which put the king of Han in difficulty several times. After Xiang Yu was wiped out, Emperor Gaozu spent a thousand taels of gold to purchase Ji Bu. Anyone who dared to harbor Ji Bu would be punished by the three tribes. Ji Bu hid in Zhou's house in Puyang. Zhou said: The Han Dynasty is anxious to find the general and will come to my house to look for him soon. If you can listen to me, I will dare to find a way for you; if you can't listen to me, I am willing to commit suicide first. Ji Bu agreed. So he treated Ji Bu as a criminal, shaved off his hair, tied his neck with an iron ring, put on the prisoner's coarse cloth, and put him in a funeral car. Together with dozens of his slaves, he went to the Zhu family's home in Ludi and wanted to sell them. Zhu Jiaxin knew that he was Ji Bu, so he bought it and placed it in a house in the countryside. He himself went to Luoyang to see Xia Houying, the Marquis of Ruyin, and asked, "What crime did Ji Bu commit?" Now, the emperor has just brought peace to the world, and if he rewards a person with a thousand pieces of gold for his personal grudge, doesn't it show that he is not broad-minded? Moreover, given Ji Bu's talents, the Han Dynasty captured him so quickly. Didn't this force him to flee north to the Huns and south to South Vietnam? To hate strong men and force them to go to the enemy's country is not the lesson of Wu Zixu who helped Wu destroy Chu and dug up the tomb of King Ping of Chu and whipped his corpse. At that time, some elders in the society praised Ji Bu for his ability to turn toughness into softness, and the Zhu family became famous all over the world because of this incident. Ji Bu was summoned by the emperor. Ji Bu expressed his gratitude and confessed his crime, and the emperor appointed him as a doctor. During the reign of Emperor Hui of the Han Dynasty, Jibu Guan rose to Zhonglang General. The Xiongnu Chanyu once wrote a letter to insult the Queen Mother Lu. The Queen Mother was very angry and summoned the generals to discuss countermeasures. General Fan Kuai said: I am willing to lead an army of 100,000 to sweep across the Xiongnu. The generals all obeyed Empress Lu's will and believed that Fan Kuai's statement was correct. Ji Bu said: Fan Kuai should be beheaded. In the past, Emperor Gao led more than 300,000 soldiers and was surrounded by the Xiongnu in Pingcheng. At that time, Fan Kuai was also surrounded and surrounded. How could Fan Sha be able to sweep away the Xiongnu with more than 100,000 men now? This is a lie to his face. Moreover, the Qin Dynasty's use of troops against the Xiongnu led to an uprising by Chen Sheng and others.
target: Ji Bu, a native of Chu, was known for his chivalry and served as a general under Xiang Yu, causing difficulties for Liu Bang, the King of Han. source: Uncle Tian was the prime minister of Lu. When he first took office, more than a hundred people reported to King Lu that he had taken away their property. King Lu immediately stopped him and asked him to rest in the garden. But Uncle Tian often sat outside his room to wrap himself in the open air, and never went into the house to rest. He said: "The king of Lu is wrapping his clothes in the open air, how can I wrap myself in the house alone?" For this reason, King Lu did not go out much for hunting. A few years later, Uncle Tian died in office. The State of Lu offered a hundred catties of gold as a sacrifice, but his youngest son Tian Ren refused to accept it, saying: Morally, the honor of his father cannot be harmed. Because Tian Ren was strong and brave, he became a household official of General Wei Qing. He followed Wei Qing to attack the Xiongnu several times. General Wei recommended him to Emperor Mowu, and he was appointed as a doctor. He was transferred to Erqianshi and served as prime minister for a long time. target: Uncle Tian, a native of Zhao, served as a doctor under King Zhang Ao. When Zhang Ao was implicated in a plot against the emperor, Uncle Tian followed him to Chang'an in prison garb. He died in office, and his son Tian Ren refused funeral gifts, later serving as a general under Wei Qing. Tian Ren was executed for allowing the crown prince to flee during a rebellion.

target: Liu Tong, Zhongshan Aiwang, was made King of Qinghe and later moved to Zhongshan but died young without heirs. Emperor Xiaoyuan had three sons: Empress Wang gave birth to Emperor Cheng, Fu Zhaoyi to Liu Kang of Dingtao, and Feng Zhaoyi to Liu Xing of Zhongshan. Liu Kang, favored by Emperor Yuan, was treated specially by Emperor Cheng. He died after nineteen years, succeeded by his son Liu Xin, who became Emperor Ai. Emperor Ai honored his father as Emperor Gong. Liu Xing, Zhongshan Xiaowang, was made king and later moved to Zhongshan. Emperor Cheng considered him as heir but chose Liu Xin instead. Liu Xing died after thirty years, succeeded by his son Liu Yan, who became Emperor Ping. Emperor Ping’s line ended under Wang Mang. The commentary notes that Emperor Xiaoyuan’s descendants spread widely but were cut off in his grandchildren’s generation, perhaps by fate. Liu Qin was intelligent but nearly fell into immorality due to Zhang Bo’s greed, echoing the *Book of Songs*’ warning about greedy people.

source: Zhang Shizhi, courtesy name Ji, was born in Duyang, Nanyang. Lives with his brother Zhang Zhong. He used his family wealth to buy a job as a knight and served Emperor Wen of Han. He had not been promoted for many years and had no reputation. Zhang Shizhi said: I feel uneasy about being a Langguan for a long time and depleting my brother's family property. I want to automatically request to be dismissed and go home. The lieutenant-general Yuan Ang knew that he was talented and could not bear to see him leave, so he asked Zhang Shizhi to be transferred to fill the vacant post. After Zhang Shizhi's audience was over, he took advantage of this opportunity to step forward and state things that would benefit the country and the people. Emperor Wen said: Be realistic. Don't talk too much about ancient things, but talk about what can be implemented in the present. So Zhang Shizhi talked about the affairs between Qin and Mo, and talked about the reasons for the demise of Qin Dynasty and the rise of Han Dynasty.
target: Zhang Shizhi, a native of Nanyang, served Emperor Wen of Han but remained unpromoted for years. He sought to resign, but Lieutenant-General Yuan Ang recognized his talent and arranged a transfer.

source: Emperor Wen said: Be realistic. Don't talk too much about ancient things, but talk about what can be implemented in the present. So Zhang Shizhi talked about the affairs between Qin and Mo, and talked about the reasons for the demise of Qin Dynasty and the rise of Han Dynasty. Emperor Wen praised Zhang Shizhi and promoted him to the rank of Servant. Zhang Shizhi traveled with the emperor and visited the tiger enclosure. The emperor asked Shang Lin about the registration of various animal books and asked more than a dozen questions. Shang Lin looked around but couldn't answer. The stingy man who was in charge of the tiger enclosure answered the emperor's questions on behalf of Lieutenant Shang Lin. He was very detailed and wanted to show that his answers were as fluent as the responses to the dance. Emperor Wen said: Shouldn't officials be like this? You can't go to Lieutenant Lin! So Zhang Shizhi was ordered to declare the stingy husband as the Shanglin Order. Zhang Shishang stepped forward and said: What kind of person does Your Majesty think Jianghou Zhou Bo is? The Emperor replied: A loyal elder.
target: During an audience, Emperor Wen advised him to focus on present matters rather than ancient ones. Zhang Shizhi discussed the fall of Qin and the rise of Han, earning promotion to Servant. While visiting a tiger enclosure, the emperor questioned officials about animal records. A lowly keeper answered fluently, impressing the emperor, who wanted to promote him.

source: Now that Your Majesty has promoted a stingy man to a higher level because of his eloquence and eloquence, I am worried that people in the world will follow the trend and rush to exaggerate instead of being practical. Moreover, the following imitates the response from above, which is faster than a shadow and echoes. Your Majesty, you can do whatever you want, so you must be cautious! Emperor Wen agreed and said: OK! So no more promotion of stingy men. The emperor got into the carriage and summoned Zhang Shizhi to accompany him. As the car moved forward slowly, the emperor asked about the shortcomings of the Qin Dynasty, and Zhang Shizhi answered truthfully. When they arrived at the palace, the emperor granted Zhang Shizhi the official carriage order. Soon, the prince and the King of Liang entered the court together in a car. They passed by Sima Gate without getting off the car. At that time, Zhang Shizhi chased after him and stopped the prince and the King of Liang from entering the palace gate. He then accused them of being disrespectful by not getting out of the car at Simamen and reported them to the police. When Empress Dowager Bo learned about this, Emperor Wen took off his hat and said, "I blame my lax teaching of my son." Empress Dowager Bo then sent an envoy to pardon the prince and King Liang, and then they were able to enter the palace. Emperor Wen believed that Zhang Shizhi was different from this incident and appointed him as a senior official. Soon, Zhang Shi's official position was Zhonglang General. He followed the emperor to Ba Ling. The emperor sat on the north side of his mausoleum and looked far away.
target: Zhang Shizhi cautioned against valuing eloquence over substance, citing Qin's decline due to such practices. The emperor agreed and halted the promotion. Later, Zhang Shizhi stopped the prince and King of Liang from entering the palace gate without dismounting, accusing them of disrespect. Empress Dowager Bo pardoned them, but Emperor Wen appointed Zhang Shizhi as a senior official. At Ba Ling, the emperor lamented the difficulty of securing his tomb, but Zhang Shizhi argued that greed, not materials, determines security.

source: Emperor Wen praised him for being right. After that, Zhang Shizhi was promoted to Tingwei. Soon, the emperor was on his way to menstruation? At the Wei Bridge, a man ran out from under the bridge, frightening the horse that the emperor was driving. So he ordered the knight to arrest the man and hand him over to the court captain for punishment. Zhang Shizhi interrogated the man. The man replied: I am a countryman from Chang'an County. When I came here, I heard about the martial law on Qingdao and hurriedly hid under the bridge. After a long time, I thought the emperor had passed by, so I came out from under the bridge. When I saw the emperor's carriage, horses and honor guard in front of me, I immediately turned around and ran away. Zhang Shizhi reported the punishment he deserved based on this, saying: This person violated the martial law order of the Qing Dynasty and should be fined. Emperor Wen was furious and said: "This man frightened my horse. Fortunately, my horse has a gentle temper. If it had been another horse, wouldn't it have injured me long ago?" But Tingwei only imposed a fine! Zhang Shizhi said: The law is obeyed by the emperor and the people of the world. Nowadays, the law stipulates in this way but the punishment must be increased. In this way, the law cannot win the trust of the people. Besides, at that time, the emperor could just have him killed on the spot. Now that it has been handed over to Tingwei, and Tingwei is the symbol of fairness in the world, once there is any deviation, the world will use the law arbitrarily, lightly or heavily. Where can the people put their hands and feet? I hope your Majesty will understand clearly. After a long time, the emperor said: Wei Ting was the one who did the right thing. After that, someone stole the jade ring in front of the shrine in Gaozu Temple and was arrested. Emperor Wen was furious and handed it over to Tingwei for punishment. Zhang Shizhi petitioned to be sentenced to be beheaded in accordance with the provisions of the law for stealing the ancestral temple's clothing and utensils. The emperor was furious and said: "That man did something wrong and actually stole the artifacts from the late emperor's ancestral temple!" The reason why I handed him over to your Tingwei for trial was because I wanted him to exterminate his clan, but you petitioned him in accordance with the ordinary legal provisions. This was not my original intention to respect my ancestors. Zhang Shizhi took off his hat and kowtowed and explained: According to the law, this sentence has reached the limit. Moreover, beheading and genocide are both capital crimes, but they are based on the degree of disobedience. Today, if someone steals the artifacts from the ancestral temple, his entire clan will be killed. Suppose a fool steals a handful of earth from Changling, how will your Majesty punish him? Later, Emperor Wen and Empress Dowager Bo discussed the matter and approved Tingwei's verdict. At that time, Lieutenant Tiaohou Zhou Yafu and Liang Xiangshan Duhou Wang Tianqi saw that Zhang Shizhi was fair in his comments, so they became close friends with him. Zhang Shizhi was praised by people all over the world. Later, Emperor Wen died and Emperor Jing came to the throne. Zhang Shizhi was afraid when he remembered that he had offended Emperor Jing, so he asked for leave due to illness.
target: Promoted to Tingwei, he handled cases with fairness. When a man startled the emperor's horse, Zhang Shizhi imposed a fine, not execution, insisting on legal consistency. In another case, he opposed executing a thief's entire clan for stealing from Gaozu Temple, arguing proportionality. Emperor Wen approved his verdict. After Emperor Jing's accession, Zhang Shizhi feared retribution for past offenses but was forgiven. He later died of illness.

source: At this time, Tangguo almost became the overlord. After that, Wang Qian happened to come to the throne. His mother was originally a singing artist. When Wang Qian came to the throne, he believed the slander of his favored minister Guo Kai and finally had Li Mu killed and replaced him with Yan Ju. Therefore, the army was defeated and the soldiers fled and were destroyed by Qin. Now I heard privately that Wei Shang was appointed as the prefect of Yunzhong. He used all the taxes from the military market to reward the soldiers. He also used his personal salary to kill cattle every five days and entertain guests, military officials and close subordinate officials. Therefore, the Xiongnu stayed far away and did not dare to approach the Yunzhong Fortress. The Huns once invaded, and Wei Shang led his troops to fight back, killing many enemy troops. Those soldiers were all sons of ordinary people. They came from Tianwen to join the army. How could they know military laws and regulations such as "Chi Ji" and "Wu Fu". They fought hard all day long, beheaded enemies, and captured prisoners. But when they reported their merits to the Yamen, as long as they did not comply with one sentence, the judges would invoke the law to punish them. Their rewards are not fulfilled but the laws of the justices are enforced. I think His Majesty's laws are too fastidious, the rewards are too light, and the punishments are too severe. Moreover, Wei Shang, the governor of Yunzhong County, was only six heads short of the number of enemy soldiers he reported killed. Your Majesty handed him over to the judicial officer for punishment, deprived him of his title and sentenced him to one year in prison. From this point of view, even if His Majesty gets Li Mu, it is impossible to reuse him. I was indeed stupid and violated a taboo, a capital crime! Emperor Wen was happy after hearing this. On the same day, he ordered Feng Tang to send an envoy to Chijie to pardon Wei Shang, and appointed him as the governor of Yunzhong County again. He also appointed Feng Tang as the chariot and cavalry captain, in charge of the lieutenants and chariot warriors of various counties and countries. Ten years later, Emperor Jing of Han came to the throne and asked Feng Tang to be the prime minister of Chu. After Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty came to the throne, he issued an imperial edict to recommend virtuous people and recommended Feng Tang. Feng Tang was over ninety years old at the time and could no longer hold an official position, so he made his son Feng Sui the official. Feng Sui, also known as Wang Sun, was also an outstanding talent. Wei Shang was from Huaili. Ji An, whose courtesy name is Changru, was born in Puyang. His ancestors were favored by Nao in ancient times. It is the tenth generation to reach the end of the chapter, and he has been appointed as a minister for generations. Ji An benefited from his father's position and was the prince Xima during the reign of Emperor Xiaojing. He was respected by others because of his seriousness in handling affairs. When Emperor Wu ascended the throne of God, he paid a visit to An. The Dongyue tribes were fighting among themselves, and the emperor sent Ji An to inspect. He did not go to Shuyue, but only came back to the border of Kuaiji County, and reported: "The Shuyue people attack each other. This is their custom, and it is not worth bothering the emperor's envoy."
target: Feng Tang, known for filial piety, served Emperor Wen. The emperor lamented not having generals like Lian Po and Li Mu to fight the Xiongnu. Feng Tang boldly claimed the emperor could not use them, citing harsh laws and unfair rewards. He used the example of Wei Shang, a capable governor punished for minor discrepancies in battle reports. Emperor Wen, initially angered, later pardoned Wei Shang and appointed Feng Tang as chariot and cavalry captain. Under Emperor Jing, Feng Tang became prime minister of Chu. Emperor Wu later recommended him, but he was too old to serve. Ji An, from Puyang, served Emperor Wu. He was known for his blunt advice and disdain for trivialities. Sent to inspect conflicts, he deemed them unworthy of imperial attention. During a famine, he distributed grain without authorization, earning the emperor's favor.

source: Because he had repeatedly expressed his strong advice to the emperor, he could not stay in the palace as an official for a long time, so he was transferred to the prefect of Shuhai County. Ji An studied the opinions of Huangdi and Laozi and managed the affairs of the government and the people. He likes to be quiet and inactive, so he chooses county magistrates and capable book historians and entrusts them with all affairs in the county. When he governs county affairs, he only controls and supervises major matters and does not pay attention to trivial details.
target: As a governor, he favored quiet governance, delegating tasks and achieving stability. In court, he criticized the emperor's hypocrisy and opposed Confucian scholars. He clashed with officials like Zhang Tang, accusing them of manipulating laws.

source: Ji An had already bid farewell to the emperor and visited the general Li Xi, saying: I have been abandoned to a foreign county and cannot participate in the discussion of important affairs of the court. But Zhang Tang, the imperial censor, was clever enough to reject criticism from others, and his tricks were able to cover up his mistakes. He was unwilling to speak for the people of the world according to the right way, and only catered to the Lord's wishes. The Lord slanders what His heart does not desire; He praises what He desires. He likes to cause trouble, play with laws and regulations, be cunning in the court to cater to the Lord's will, and intimidate cruel and greedy officials outside the court to maintain his dignity. You are in the rank of Jiuqing, why don't you give advice to the emperor as soon as possible? Both you and him will be killed. Li Xi was afraid of Zhang Tang and finally dared not speak. Ji An still handled the county affairs according to the past governance methods, and the affairs of Huaiyang County were clear and clear. Later, Zhang Tang was defeated as expected. The emperor heard what Ji An said to Li Xi and sentenced Li Xi. Ji An was ordered to have the same status and treatment as the prime minister of the princes and kingdoms during his tenure as the governor of Huaiyang. Ji An passed away ten years later. After Ji An's death, the emperor made his younger brother Ji Ren the official of Jiuqing because of Ji An, and his son Ji Yan became the prime minister of the vassal kingdoms.
target: Despite his integrity, he was demoted for minor offenses. Later appointed governor of Huaiyang, he warned General Li Xi against Zhang Tang's cunning. Ji An died after ten years, leaving a legacy of principled governance.

source: Zheng Jun died during the reign of Emperor Xiaowen. At that time, Zheng was proud of his chivalrous deeds and rescued Zhang Yu, the general of King Xiao of Liang, from the trouble, and his reputation spread throughout the Liang-Chu region. During the reign of Emperor Xiaojing, he sacrificed his life for the prince. During every five-day holiday, stagecoaches are often set up in the suburbs of Chang'an to invite or thank guests, working day and night until dawn, which is often not thoughtful. Zheng Zhuang liked the teachings of Huangdi and Laozi. He admired the elderly and virtuous people, fearing that they would not be satisfied with them. Although he was young and held a low official position, the close friends he made were all famous scholars from his grandfather's generation. Emperor Wu Liu Che ascended the throne, and Zheng Zhuang was successively promoted to lieutenant of Lu State, prefect of Jinan County, prime minister of Jiangdu State, and finally to Jiuqing as the right internal history. Because of his involvement in the dispute between Wu'an Hou Tianchi and Wei Qihou Dou Ying, he was demoted to Zhan Shi, and later promoted to Da Sinong. Zheng Zhuang, as a high official, warned the gatekeeper: When guests arrive, please come in immediately. No matter whether they are noble or cheap, do not wait at the door. He performs the courtesy of a host to his guests and treats his guests humbly with his noble status. Zheng Zhuang has a clean character and does not acquire any private property. He relies on his salary and rewards to provide for his elderly friends.
target: Zheng Zhuang, from Chen County, admired Huangdi and Laozi teachings. He treated guests humbly, regardless of status, and lived frugally, using his salary to support friends.

source: He performs the courtesy of a host to his guests and treats his guests humbly with his noble status. Zheng Zhuang has a clean character and does not acquire any private property. He relies on his salary and rewards to provide for his elderly friends. But the gift he gave to people was just a plate of food. Every time he goes to court, when the emperor is free, he always makes remarks without praising the wise people in the world. When recommending scholars, prime ministers, historians and other subordinate officials, he praised them with great enthusiasm and often mentioned that he thought they were more talented than himself. He never calls his subordinates by their first names, and talks to them as if he is afraid of hurting them. I heard the kind words spoken by others and recommended them to the emperor, but I was afraid that I would be too slow. Therefore, all the scholars in Jingshan Yishu praised Zhengzhuang in unison. Zheng Zhuang was sent to inspect the breach of the Yellow River, and he applied for a five-day leave to repair his luggage. The emperor said: I heard that Zheng Zhuang traveled thousands of miles without food. Now I am applying for leave to pack my luggage. Why? However, when Zheng Zhuang was discussing matters in the court, he often echoed and catered to the emperor's wishes and did not dare to clearly state whether his position was right or wrong.
target: He recommended scholars enthusiastically, often praising them as superior to himself. However, he avoided taking clear stances in court, echoing the emperor's wishes.

source: The emperor said: I heard that Zheng Zhuang traveled thousands of miles without food. Now I am applying for leave to pack my luggage. Why? However, when Zheng Zhuang was discussing matters in the court, he often echoed and catered to the emperor's wishes and did not dare to clearly state whether his position was right or wrong. The Han Dynasty conquered the Xiongnu and recruited the Yi tribes from all directions. The country spent a lot of money and became increasingly depleted of financial and material resources. When Zheng Zhuang was appointed as the chief minister, some of the people he recommended and the guests who were familiar with him were engaged in transportation for the chief minister, and they owed a lot of money. Sima An, the governor of Huaiyang County, exposed this incident, and Zheng Zhuang committed a crime. After Nasu atones for his crime, he was demoted to a commoner. Soon, he temporarily served as the chief historian in the Prime Minister's Mansion. He was also promoted to the post of prefect of Runan County. He died in office a few years later.
target: During the Xiongnu campaigns, his recommendations led to financial mismanagement, resulting in his demotion. He died as governor of Runan, leaving no property.

source: The two men resigned from office midway, and the guests became even more scattered. After Zheng died at that time, his family had no property left. Earlier, Zhai Gong, a native of the lower state, was appointed as a court captain, and the guests were crowded. After he lost his official position, a bird trap could be set up outside the door. Later, when the official resumed his duties, guests wanted to come, and Zhai Gong wrote in big characters on the door, saying: One life and one death, one can know the depth of friendship; one poor and one rich, one can know the human condition; one noble and one low, one can see the friendship.
target: The text reflects on the fickleness of human relationships, noting that guests flock to the powerful but abandon the fallen.

source: Zhang Cang, a native of Yangwu, Henan, was fond of writing, music and calendars. In the Qin Dynasty, he served as censor and was in charge of household registration albums all over the world. He fled back to his hometown because he broke the law. When Pei Gong was marching through Yangwu, Zhang Cang followed Pei Gong as a guest to attack Nanyang. When Zhang Cang was about to be executed, he took off his clothes and leaned on the chopping block of the torture instrument, revealing his tall figure and fat muscles as white as gourds. At that time, Wang Ling saw Zhang Cang and was very surprised by this beauty, so he told Pei Gong that he would not be punished by beheading if he was pardoned. So he entered Wuguan in the west and arrived in Xianyang. Pei Gong became the king of Han, entered Hanzhong, and returned to the army to pacify the Sanqin area. Chen Yu drove away Zhang Er, king of Changshan, and Zhang Er defected to the king of Han. The king of Han appointed Zhang Cang as the governor of Changshan County. Following Han Xin to attack Zhao, Zhang Cang captured Chen Yu. After the Zhao area was pacified, the King of Han appointed Zhang Cang as acting prime minister to guard against border bandits. Soon he was moved to the state of Zhao and became the prime minister of Zhao Wang Zhang Er. Zhang Er died, and Zhang Cang became his son Zhang Ao, the prime minister. Later, he was appointed as the Prime Minister of Daiguo. King Zang Tu of Yan rebelled, and Zhang Cang served as the Prime Minister and accompanied the army to attack Zang Lai. He was granted the title of Marquis of Beiping and was granted a settlement of 1,200 households. Zhang Cang changed his plan, and one month later, he made Liehou the leader for four years. At that time, Xiao He was appointed as the prime minister, and Zhang Cang had been the censor under the pillar since the Qin Dynasty. He was familiar with the world's atlas and household registration, and was good at calculating the calendar. Therefore, Zhang Cang was appointed to serve in the prime minister's mansion as a lieutenant, in charge of the books sent by the county.
target: Zhang Cang, from Yangwu, Henan, was a scholar of writing, music, and calendars. He served as a censor under the Qin Dynasty, managing household registries, but fled home after breaking the law. He later joined Pei Gong (Liu Bang) as a guest, and was spared execution after Wang Ling admired his physique. He followed Pei Gong to Xianyang, served as governor of Changshan, and helped capture Chen Yu. He became prime minister of Zhao and Dai, and was made Marquis of Beiping for suppressing a rebellion. As censor-in-chief, he used his expertise in calendars and registries to serve in the prime minister's office. He later became prime minister of Huainan and then censor-in-chief.

source: At the beginning, Ren Ao was dismissed, and Pingyang Marquis Cao Zhuo replaced Ren Ao as the imperial censor. After the death of Empress Gao, she and her ministers jointly annihilated the Lu family. Later, he was dismissed from office for violating the law and appointed Huainan Prime Minister Zhang Cang as the imperial censor. Zhang Cang, Jianghou Zhou Bo and others established Emperor Xiaowen as emperor. Four years later, they replaced Guan Ying as prime minister. The Han Dynasty had been established for more than 20 years, and the world had just been peaceful. All the officials were military officers. When Zhang Cang was appointed as the Prime Minister, the calendar was corrected. Since Emperor Gaozu arrived at Bashang in October, he continued to use the Qin calendar with October as the beginning of the year without any changes. Calculating the movement of the five elements, it is believed that Mo is in the realm of water virtue and advocates black, just like the Qin Dynasty.
target: He corrected the calendar, adopting the Qin system with October as the new year, and advocated for water virtue.

source: Calculating the movement of the five elements, it is believed that Mo is in the realm of water virtue and advocates black, just like the Qin Dynasty. Adjust the sound of the music, set the rhythm, and formulate laws and regulations. It is like a craftsman’s standard of measurement, which sets the rules for making utensils. Eventually he reached the position of prime minister. Therefore, those who talked about laws and regulations in the Han Dynasty took Zhang Cang as the standard. Zhang Cang likes books. He can read everything and knows everything, especially the music and calendar. Zhang Cang was grateful for Wang Ling, the Marquis of Anguo, for saving his life. After he became a nobleman, he served Wang Ling like a father. After Wang Ling's death, Zhang Cang became prime minister. During his vacation, he often visited Mrs. Ling and served her dinner before returning home. Zhang Cang had been prime minister for more than ten years. Gongsun Chen from Lu State wrote a letter stating the order of transmission of the Five Elements. He said that when Han ascended to virtue, it should coincide with the appearance of the Yellow Dragon, and the month at the beginning of the year should be changed and the color of sacrificial clothing should be changed. The matter was handed over to Zhang Cang. Zhang Cang thought it was wrong and canceled it. Later, Huanglong appeared in the Chengji period, so Emperor Wen summoned Gongsun Chen as a doctor, established Tu De and the calendar system, and changed the first year. Zhang Cang therefore devalued himself and claimed that he was old and sick. Zhang Cang recommended a middle-ranking official who committed treacherous things for profit. The emperor blamed Zhang Cang, and Zhang Cang was dismissed from office due to illness. Xiaojing died in the fifth year, and Mi was given the title Wenhou.
target: He served Wang Ling like a father after being saved by him. He was dismissed after opposing Gongsun Chen's proposal for Han's earth virtue, which was later confirmed by a yellow dragon sighting. He died around age 100, leaving writings on yin-yang and calendars.

When Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty raised an army in Peixian County, he defeated the governor and supervisor of the Sishui County, so the two brothers Zhou Ke and Zhou Chang went to Pei Gong as soldiers. Pei Gong took Zhou Chang as the flag bearer and Zhou Ke as the guest in the tent.
target: Zhou Chang, from Pei, served as a soldier under Pei Gong with his cousin Zhou Ke. Zhou Ke died defending Xingyang against Xiang Yu, and Zhou Chang became censor-in-chief. He was known for his bluntness, once calling Emperor Gaozu a tyrant.

source: When Prime Minister Zhao arrived in Beijing, he paid a visit to the Queen Mother. The Queen Mother scolded Zhou Chang and said, "Don't you know that I hate the Qi family?" He didn’t even send King Zhao here! After Zhou Chang was summoned to Beijing, Empress Gao sent envoys to summon King Zhao. As expected, King Zhao came to Beijing and was poisoned to death after arriving in Chang'an for more than a month. Zhou Chang refused to go to court due to illness. He died three years later and was given the title of Mourning Hou. It was passed down to the marquis to his son, and then to Sun Zhouyi, who violated the law and was removed from the marquis state. Emperor Jing also made Zhou Chang's grandson Zhou Zuoche the Marquis of Anyang. He was removed from the Marquis State due to his crimes. At the beginning, after Zhao Yao replaced Zhou Chang as the imperial censor, Emperor Gaozu died and served Emperor Hui until his death. In the first year of Gaohou, Gaohou resented Zhao Yao for proposing a strategy to protect King Zhao Ruyi, so he convicted Zhao Yao and asked Guang'ahou to appoint Ao as the censor. Ren Ao, a native of Peijun, worked as a jailer when he was young. Emperor Gaozu once escaped from the pursuit of officials. The officials captured Empress Lu and acted frivolously towards her. Ren Ao always valued Gaozu, so he was furious and injured the minor official who was guarding Empress Lu. When Emperor Gaozu started to raise troops, Ren Ao followed Zhidan as a guest and became the censor, and stayed in Fengdan for two years.
target: He opposed deposing the crown prince, earning gratitude from Empress Lü. He was appointed prime minister of Zhao to protect Prince Ruyi, despite his reluctance. After Gaozu's death, Empress Lü summoned and killed Ruyi; Zhou Chang died of illness three years later. His descendants lost the marquisate. Ren Ao, from Pei, was a jailer who protected Empress Lü from abuse. He followed Gaozu, became censor-in-chief, and was made Marquis of Guang'a. He was later dismissed. Shen Tujia, from Liang, rose from a crossbowman to censor-in-chief and then prime minister. He was upright, refusing private visits.

source: At that time, Deng Tong, the Taizhong doctor, was favored and received hundreds of millions of rewards. Emperor Wen often went to Deng Tong's house to drink in his spare time, and he was so favored. When Shen Tujia entered the dynasty in this temple, Deng usually stayed next to the emperor, showing signs of neglect and disrespect. After Shen Tujia finished the divination, he immediately said: Your Majesty loves his ministers and makes them rich and noble. As for court etiquette, it must not be lax! The emperor said: "Don't say anything. I will warn him privately." After retiring from the court, Shen Tujia sat in the Prime Minister's Mansion and personally wrote a message to summon Deng Tong to come to the manor. If he did not come, Deng Tong would be executed immediately.
target: He once ordered the execution of the favored courtier Deng Tong for disrespect, but Emperor Wen intervened.

source: Deng Tong was frightened and went to court to tell Zaoshang. The emperor said: Just go, I will send someone to call you out immediately. When Deng Tong arrived at the Prime Minister's Mansion, he took off his hat and went barefoot, kowtowed to apologize to Shen Tujia. Shen Tujia sat calmly as usual, without any courtesy to the guests, and scolded Zhen, saying: "The imperial court is the imperial court of Emperor Gao. It is the greatest disrespect for a minor minister to play in the palace and should be beheaded." Prime Minister Shi went to execute the beheading! Deng Tong kowtowed, and blood flowed from his head, but it still didn't stop. The emperor estimated that the prime minister had already punished Deng Tong, so he sent an envoy to recall Deng Tong with a talisman, thanked the prime minister, and said: "This man is my mocking minister, please let him go." Deng Tong went to the palace, cried to the emperor, and said: The prime minister almost killed me. Shen Tujia served as prime minister for five years, Emperor Wen died, and Emperor Jing ascended the throne. In the second year, Chao Cuo was in office and was highly appreciated by Zaoshang. He proposed to change many laws and regulations, and also proposed punishments to weaken the power of the princes. However, Prime Minister Shen Tujia demoted himself and his words were not accepted. He hated Chao Cuo very much. During Chao Cuo's tenure, it was inconvenient to enter and exit the east gate, so he opened another gate and entered and exited from the south. Entering and exiting from the south, pass through the open space outside the inner wall and within the outer wall of Taishanghuang Temple. Shen Tujia heard that Chao Cuo had passed through the ancestral temple wall and was preparing to petition Chao Cuo to be killed.
target: As prime minister, he clashed with Chao Cuo over legal changes. When Chao Cuo opened a gate through a temple wall, Shen Tujia sought his execution but was thwarted.
