However, I heard that about a thousand miles west of Kunming, there is Chengxiang Kingdom, named Dianyue. Some businessmen from Shu County who privately trade goods have been there. So the Han Dynasty began to communicate with the Dian Kingdom in search of the road to Daxia. At first, the Han Dynasty wanted to communicate with the southwestern barbarians, but stopped this work because it was too expensive.
target: The campaigns opened routes to the Western Regions, with Han establishing Jiuquan County and building fortresses. Envoys continued, but conflicts arose with small states like Loulan and Gushi, leading to Han military actions. The Han Dynasty's influence expanded, though some states remained distant.

source: At the beginning of the rise of the Han Dynasty, the bad governance of the Qin Dynasty was reversed, so that the people could recuperate and live, everything was simplified, and prohibitions and laws were greatly relaxed. The prime ministers Xiao He and Cao Shen became models for the world with their generous and quiet style of work. The people therefore compiled a "painting and a song" to praise them. Emperor Hui ruled without doing anything, Empress Lu lived in seclusion in the palace, but the world was peaceful, the people concentrated on agricultural production, and there was a scene of plenty of food and clothing. During the reigns of Emperors Wen and Jing, customs changed again. At that time, officials who were able to obey the law and obey the law, such as Wu Gong, the governor of Henan County, and Weng Weng, the governor of Shu County, were strict with themselves, set examples for others, acted honestly and justly, and could make the people obey and accept the influence without using coercion. During the reign of Emperor Wu, he resisted the barbarians from all directions externally and revised laws and regulations internally. As a result, the people were exhausted and internal strife and external troubles could not be prevented.
target: During the early Han Dynasty, the harsh policies of the Qin Dynasty were reversed, allowing the people to recover and live simply, with relaxed laws. Prime Ministers Xiao He and Cao Cao set an example with their generous and quiet governance, earning praise from the people. Emperor Hui ruled without intervention, and Empress Lu remained secluded, yet the realm was peaceful, with abundant food and clothing. Under Emperors Wen and Jing, customs improved, and officials like Wu Gong and Weng Weng governed with integrity, inspiring obedience without force. Emperor Wu's reign saw external conflicts and internal legal reforms, exhausting the people and causing unrest.

source: At that time, officials who were able to obey the law and obey the law, such as Wu Gong, the governor of Henan County, and Weng Weng, the governor of Shu County, were strict with themselves, set examples for others, acted honestly and justly, and could make the people obey and accept the influence without using coercion. During the reign of Emperor Wu, he resisted the barbarians from all directions externally and revised laws and regulations internally. As a result, the people were exhausted and internal strife and external troubles could not be prevented. At that time, there were very few people who were famous for their education and governance. Only Dong Zhongshu, the Prime Minister of Jiangdu, Gongsun Hong and Ni Kuan, the internal historian, whose political performances are worthy of a book. The three of them were all Confucian scholars, who were both proficient in the way of life and writing. They used Confucian thinking and methods to help themselves handle government affairs, and the emperor valued them very much. Dong Zhongshu resigned from office many times due to illness, while Gongsun Hong and Ni Kuan fulfilled their duties as officials. Emperor Zhao ascended the throne at a young age, and Huo Guang took charge of government affairs on his behalf. At this time, after years of war, domestic consumption was very high. Huo Guang followed this and abide by his duties without changing his previous practices. In the Shiyuan and Yuanfeng years, the Xiongnu surrendered, and the people's lives gradually became richer, so they began to recommend talents, care about the people's sufferings, abolished the wine tax, and discussed the benefits of salt and iron. When Emperor Xuan arrived, because he was an emperor who came from a humble background and started his family in an alley, he was well aware of the people's joys and sorrows. After Huo Guang's death, he began to personally handle various court affairs and worked hard to govern. He went to court every five days to listen to government affairs and reported to the court in order from the prime minister to the other officials. When officials such as governors, governors, and princes are conferred, they must be interviewed in person to understand their thoughts, and then their actions are examined to compare with their words. If the names are inconsistent with reality, the root cause must be found.
target: Few officials were noted for good governance, except Confucian scholars Dong Zhongshu, Gongsun Hong, and Ni Kuan, who used Confucian principles in administration and were valued by the emperor. Emperor Zhao ascended young, with Huo Guang as regent, who maintained stability after years of war. During the Shiyuan and Yuanfeng years, the Xiongnu surrendered, and the people grew prosperous, leading to talent recommendations, care for the people, and discussions on salt and iron taxes. Emperor Xuan, who rose from humble beginnings, understood the people's hardships. After Huo Guang's death, he personally managed court affairs, holding court every five days and interviewing officials to ensure their actions matched their words.

source: When officials such as governors, governors, and princes are conferred, they must be interviewed in person to understand their thoughts, and then their actions are examined to compare with their words. If the names are inconsistent with reality, the root cause must be found. Emperor Xuan once said: The reason why the people can rest assured in agricultural production and eliminate the bad mood of worry and resentment is because the politics are peaceful and the law can uphold justice. The only people who jointly guarantee this with me are those good county guards. He believes that county guards are the basis for managing officials and the people. Frequent changes will cause local unrest. When the people know that the selection of the prefect is very stable and cannot be deceived, they will obey his teachings. Therefore, if the county governor is effective in governance, he will always issue letters to encourage him personally, increase his salary and give him a large sum of money, or confer a title to a marquis in Guannei. When the official position is vacant, he will be appointed in turn by those who have been commended. For this reason, Xunliang officials emerged in endlessly in the Han Dynasty, which is known as the ZTE. People such as Zhao Guanghan, Han Yanshou, Yin Wenggui, Yan Yannian, and Zhang Chang were all competent and conscientious in their duties, but they were punished and some even committed capital crimes. Wang Cheng, Huang Ba, Zhu Yi, Gong Sui, Zheng Hong, Zhao Xinchen and others were prosperous when they were in office, but missed by the people after they left office. They were given honorary titles during their lifetimes, and were worshiped and remembered after their deaths. This kind of style may be the style of gentlemen who are benevolent and courteous. Wen Weng was from Shu County, Lujiang County. When he was young, he loved learning and was proficient in "Spring and Autumn". He was promoted to the imperial court as a county official. In the last years of Emperor Jing's reign, Weng Weng served as the prefect of Shu County. He was tolerant and caring for the people, and liked to use political enlightenment to influence and govern the people of Shu County. He saw that Shu County was located in a remote and remote border area and was affected by the backward customs of ethnic minorities, so he wanted to educate and inspire it in many aspects to make progress. So he selected more than ten people from the county officials who were enlightened, wise and talented, such as Uncle Zhang, to personally instruct and encourage them. , and sent them to the capital Chang'an, either to study Confucian classics with the doctors, or to learn laws and regulations from the officials; to reduce the expenses of the county and magistrates, buy the precious specialties of Shu, golden knives and cloth, and let the officials in charge of accounting books bring them with them when they report the situation to Beijing, and give them to the doctors. A few years later, when the students who had been sent out to study returned to school, Wen Weng appointed them to high-level positions in the county, and successively recommended them to the court through inspections and other channels, and some of them became county governors or governors. In addition, Wen Weng also established a school in Chengdu City, recruiting young children from counties outside Chengdu as students, exempting them from paying more taxes and corvee, and those with good academic performance supplemented the county officials, while those with poor academic performance served as filial piety, Litian and other township officials. They often select young students from schools and let them help handle government affairs in the county government's side houses. Whenever he went out to patrol various counties, Wen Weng always asked many students who were well versed in scriptures and of good conduct to go around with him to preach enlightenment policies and go in and out of county offices. When the county officials and people saw this situation, they were very envious. Within a few years, everyone was vying to become a student in the school, so that wealthy families paid for the education. From then on, enlightenment prevailed and the atmosphere in Shu County changed greatly. The number of people from Shu County studying in the capital is comparable to that of Qi, Lu and other places. When Emperor Wu arrived, he ordered counties and counties to set up schools and relevant management officials. This was started by Wen Weng. After Wen Wengshou returned to Shu County, the local officials and people built an ancestral hall for him, and offered sacrifices continuously during every year and festival. To this day, the people in the Bashu region like elegance and are influenced by Wen Weng's teachings. Wang Cheng, I don’t know which county he is from. He once served as the minister of mice and was very prestigious in governing the place. Emperor Xuan was the first to praise him. The Book of Shao issued in the third year of Dijie said: If you don't reward those who have merit and punish those who are guilty, then even the names of Yao and Shun of Tang Dynasty will not be able to educate the world. Now the Prime Minister Wang Cheng has never slackened his efforts to encourage the people, and has attracted more than 80,000 refugees. He has made special achievements in governing the place. Wang Cheng was given the title of Marquis of Guannei and a salary of two thousand stones.
target: He believed that stable county governors were key to peace, rewarding effective ones with promotions and titles. This led to a flourishing of virtuous officials, known as the ZTE era. Some, like Zhao Guanghan and Han Yanshou, were diligent but faced punishment, while others like Wang Cheng and Huang Ba were honored in life and remembered after death. Wen Weng, a native of Shu County, was known for his love of learning and governance. As prefect of Shu, he selected talented officials to study in Chang'an, reducing expenses and providing gifts to scholars. He established schools in Chengdu, exempting students from taxes and appointing them to official positions. His efforts transformed Shu's culture, making it comparable to Qi and Lu. Emperor Wu later ordered all counties to establish schools, following Wen Weng's example. After his death, the people built a temple for him, and his influence persists in the Bashu region. Wang Cheng, whose origins are unknown, served as a minister and attracted over 80,000 refugees, earning Emperor Xuan's praise and a marquis title.

source: Wang Cheng was given the title of Marquis of Guannei and a salary of two thousand stones. But before the time of requisition, Wang Cheng fell ill and died. Later, he asked the prime ministers and censors to inquire about the gains and losses of the county's chief accountants, prefects, and government officials. Some reported that the former prime minister Wang Cheng had made false reports and exaggerated his own achievements in order to defraud prominent officials. As a result, mediocre officials later also used all means to pursue false fame. Huang Ba, courtesy name Cigong, was a native of Yangxia County, Huaiyang County. His family was a wealthy gentry and moved to Yunling.
target: However, after his death, it was reported that he had exaggerated his achievements, leading to a trend of false fame among officials.

source: Huang Ba, courtesy name Cigong, was a native of Yangxia County, Huaiyang County. His family was a wealthy gentry and moved to Yunling. Huang Ba studied laws and regulations when he was young and liked to be an official. In the last years of Emperor Wu, he donated money as an imperial edict and was rewarded with an official position. Later, he donated grain to Shenli County to supplement Zuo Feng Yi's official salary of 200 shi. Because Huang Ba donated money to serve as an official, Zuo Fengyi despised him and refused to give him a high position, making him responsible for the county's money and grain access.
target: Huang Ba, from Yangxia County, studied law and became an official through donations. He was known for his integrity, gentle demeanor, and ability to unite people.

source: In general, the principle of governing the people is not to go too far. Huang Ba won the hearts of officials and the people with his lenient outside and bright inside. As a result, the county's household registration increased year by year, and the governance situation was ranked first in the world. The emperor conscripted him to try to serve as Jing Zhaoyin, with a salary of two thousand dan. Later, because he dispatched migrant workers to repair Chidao without reporting it to the court in advance, and dispatched knights to the north, which caused a situation where the army and horses could not be rationed, Huang Ba was impeached and affected the dispatch of the army, so he was demoted and demoted one after another. Later, an edict ordered him to return to Yingchuan County as the governor, but his salary had been reduced to 800 shi. In the past eight years, Anshun has become more and more popular in the county. During the dispatch, Phoenix Shenwu flew to various counties many times, especially in Yingchuan County. The emperor thought this was a good omen for Huang Ba's long-term rule, so he wrote a letter of Shao to praise him: Huang Ba, the prefect of Yingchuan County, actively announced the emperor's will to the people. The people yearned for it and joined the imperial court. There were more and more filial sons, elder brothers, chaste wives, and obedient grandchildren. People working in the fields were humble to each other. People walking on the road do not pick up other people's lost belongings, support and visit the widowed and elderly, support and help the poor, and the prison has not even had a serious prisoner for eight years. The officials and the people yearn for enlightenment, and they are familiar with each other. It can be said that he is a wise man.
target: As prefect of Yingchuan, he implemented policies to support the poor, promote agriculture, and reduce crime. His governance was so effective that the county's household registration increased, and he was praised by Emperor Xuan.

source: The filial and virtuous people of Yingchuan County, as well as the three elders in the township and palace, Li Tian, ​​etc. were all awarded titles and silk pieces according to their levels. A few months later, the imperial court recruited Huang Ba as the crown prince and tutor, and then transferred him to the imperial censor. In the third year of Wufeng's reign, Huang Ba replaced Bingji as prime minister, became a marquis, and owned 600 households. Huang Ba's ability was mainly to govern the people locally. When he became prime minister, he needed to coordinate and issue nationwide orders. His ability and demeanor were not as good as those of his predecessors such as Bingji, Wei Xiang, and Yu Dingguo. His political performance and reputation were also lower than when he governed the county.
target: However, as prime minister, his performance declined, and he was criticized for overstepping his duties.

source: It is your prime minister's duty to enlighten people and enlighten them, so that there will be no more unjust cases in prison and no more thieves in the local area. Officials at the general and ministerial levels are appointed by me. Shi Gao, Marquis of Leling in the imperial court, is my closest minister. I already know his talents well. Why would you go beyond your duties and recommend him? The minister asked the prime minister to make a statement. Huang Ba was so ashamed that he quickly took off his hat and apologized. After a few seconds, Huang Ba was exonerated. From then on, Huang Ba never dared to report to the emperor again. However, since the rise of the Han Dynasty, when it comes to managing local officials and people, Huang Ba still ranks first. Huang Ba served as prime minister for five years, and Ganlu died in three years. Mi was named Dinghou. After Huang Ba's death, Shi Gao, Marquis of Leling, was promoted to Grand Sima. Huang Ba's son, Sihou Huang Shang, inherited the title and was appointed Captain of Guan. When Huang Shang died, his son Zhonghou Huang Fu succeeded him, and his official rank was Weiwei Jiuqing. When Huang Fu died, his son Huang Zhong succeeded him as marquis. It was only when Wang Mang arrived that the Huang family ceased to have nobility.
target: Despite this, he is remembered as one of the best local officials in Han history. He died in office, and his descendants continued to serve as officials until Wang Mang's era.

source: Huang Ba went over to inquire about the woman's surname, and it turned out that she was the daughter of a shaman family in the countryside. Huang Ba married her and grew old with her. After Huang Ba became prime minister, he moved to Duling. Zhu Yi, whose courtesy name is Zhongqing, was born in Shu County, Lujiang County. When he was young, he served as a stingy man in charge of hearing lawsuits and collecting taxes in Tongxiang, Shu County. He was honest and fair in his work, did not impose harsh policies, and benefited the people with a benevolent heart. He never beat or bullied the villagers. He cared for the elderly, orphans and widowed mothers, and was very kind to them. Therefore, the officials and people in his area respected and loved him.
target: Zhu Yi, from Shu County, was known for his honesty and fairness as a minor official. He rose to become a minister of agriculture, living frugally and sharing his salary with his hometown elders.

source: Zhu Yi passed away in the first year of Shenjue. The emperor took pity on him, so he went down to Shao and praised him, saying: "The great minister, Zhu Yi, is honest, honest and public-minded. He does not make casual friends or accept bribes. He can be called an upright gentleman." I feel very sorry for this misfortune. One hundred catties of gold were specially given to the son of Zhu Yi for the purpose of offering sacrifices. When Zhu Yi was critically ill, he told his son: I was originally a minor official in Tongxiang. The local people loved me and I will be buried in Tongxiang after my death.
target: He died in 61 BC, and Emperor Xuan praised his integrity, granting gold for sacrifices. He was buried in Tongxiang, where the people built a temple for him.

source: Xiangguo Anle was transferred to Changle Palace Guard. Gong Sui went to see him and told him with tears: Since the king became emperor, he has become more and more proud and complacent every day. He no longer listens to the advice of others. Now he is still in mourning and observes filial piety. He drinks and hases with his relatives and officials every day. When he is not fighting tigers and leopards, he or she gathers in leather carts with nine streamers on them. They run around everywhere. What they do is contrary to the right path. In ancient times, the legal system was lenient, and ministers could retire when they saw that the king was dishonest, but now they cannot resign. They want to pretend to be crazy and resign to avoid disaster, but they are also afraid that others will find out, and if they die, they will be laughed at by the world. What should they do? You used to be the Emperor's Prime Minister, so you should speak out and advise! Liu He took the throne for seventeen days, but was finally deposed by his ministers due to his debauchery and confusion. The ministers from Changyi committed the crime of condoning the king's evil and immorality, and they were all executed. More than 200 people in total were executed. Only Gong Sui and Lieutenant Wang Yang, who had repeatedly admonished Liu He and fulfilled their certain duties, were reduced from the death penalty and sentenced to four years of hard labor in building the city. After Liu He was deposed, Emperor Xuan ascended the throne. A few years later, famine broke out in the counties near the Bohai Sea. The hungry people rose up in rebellion one after another, and the prefect could not subdue them. Emperor Xuan wanted to choose someone who could govern the Bohai Sea. The prime minister and the imperial censor recommended Gong Sui and considered him useful, so Emperor Xuan appointed him as the governor of the Bohai Sea.
target: Gong Sui, from Pingyang County, was a loyal advisor to King Liu He of Changyi, often admonishing him for his unruly behavior. After Liu He was deposed, Gong Sui was sentenced to hard labor but later appointed governor of Bohai County.

source: Gong Sui turned around and asked him what he was shouting for. He said: If the emperor asks you how you manage the Bohai Sea, you must not say anything more. You should only answer: It all depends on the power of the Holy Spirit. It is not that I have any ability! , Gong Sui accepted his opinion. Gong Sui arrived in front of Emperor Xuan. As expected, the emperor asked him about the management of the Bohai Sea, and he answered according to Wang Sheng's words. Emperor Xuan was pleased with his humility and courtesy, and said with a smile: "Where did you learn the words of a loyal elder?" Gong Sui took the opportunity to step forward and said, "I don't know what I should say. It was my advisor Cao Wangsheng who warned me." Because Gong Sui was old and could not take on the important responsibilities of a minister, Emperor Xuan appointed him as the Commander-in-Chief of Shuiheng, and proposed that King Cao be appointed Shuihengcheng to express his praise and respect for Gong Sui. Shuiheng Duwei was in charge of Shanglin Garden, responsible for the furnishings of the palaces and pavilions, and providing sacrifices for the ancestral temple. It was an official position that was close to the emperor. Gong Sui was highly regarded by Emperor Xuan and died in office. Zhao Xinchen, named Wengqing, was from Shouchun County, Jiujiang County. He was appointed as a Langguan as Ming Jingjia Ke, and left the capital to serve as the county magistrate of Guyang. Ranked first in the performance appraisal, he was transferred to Shangcai County Magistrate. He called his trusted ministers to love the people like his own sons, and was highly praised during his tenure as an official. Later, he was promoted to the prefect of Lingling County, but he returned due to illness. After recovering from the illness, he was recruited as an admonishing doctor and later transferred to the post of governor of Nanyang County. His governance was as good as when he was in Shangcai. Zhao Xinchen is diligent and resourceful, likes to provide welfare for the people, and is committed to making them rich. I personally work hard at farming, go to and from the fields, and stay in country houses. I rarely have any leisure time. He inspected water springs in the county, presided over the opening of ditches, and erected dozens of water gates and sluices, which increased the irrigated farmland, reaching a maximum of 30,000 hectares. The people benefited from water conservancy and irrigation, and the harvested grain was sufficient for storage. Zhao Xinchen also formulated water regulations for the people, and engraved these regulations on stone tablets and erected them at the boundaries of the fields to prevent competition. In addition, he also prohibited extravagance and waste during weddings and funerals, and was committed to promoting the trend of diligence and thrift. If the children of prefecture and county officials roam freely, and if the prefecture and county officials do not regard farming as their official duties, they will all be reprimanded and dismissed from office. In serious cases, they will be brought to justice to observe the good and evil. Through the above measures, education has been widely implemented in the county. Everyone in the county is engaged in agriculture. The people support county officials. The number of households in the county has also doubled, and the number of thieves and lawsuits has been reduced to a very small level.
target: He quelled a rebellion by offering amnesty to farmers and promoting agriculture, leading to prosperity. He died in office, highly regarded by Emperor Xuan. Zhao Xinchen, from Shouchun County, was a diligent official who improved agriculture through irrigation, opening ditches and building water gates. He prohibited extravagance and promoted thrift, leading to increased household numbers and reduced crime. He served as governor of Henan and later as a minister, advising against wasteful palace projects. He died in office, and a temple was built for him in Nanyang.

source: The next year, the emperor wanted to boast to the barbarians about the abundance of animals. In autumn, he ordered You Fufeng to recruit the people into Nanshan, starting from Baoxie in the west, Hongnong in the east, and Hanzhong in the south. He opened nets and set traps to catch bears, porcupines, tigers, leopards, and even foxes, dodders, and elk. They were loaded on carts and transported to the Changyang Shooting Bear Pavilion. They used nets as a siege, wrapped the animals in dough, and taught the barbarians to fight with their bare hands. They took away the ones they caught, and the emperor went to watch them in person. At this time, farmers cannot harvest crops. Yang Xiong followed him to Shexiong Pavilion, and when he came back, he presented "Ode to Chang Yang". Since it was written in pen and ink, he used Hanlin as his host and Zimo as his guest to satirize him. The words said: Zimo Keqing asked the master of Hanlin: I heard that the Holy Lord nourishes the people, is benevolent and nourishing, and does not act for himself. This year when hunting in Changyang, we first ordered the right to Fufeng, the left to Taihua and the right to Baoxie, cut down the banks for cruising, and arranged them around Nanshan. Thousands of horses were arranged in the forest, and tens of thousands of cavalry were distributed at the foot of the mountain. They led the troops to the paddocks and rewarded Rong, Di, and animals. Catching bears, catching porcupines, and piling up wooden guns as savings is something you only see in the world. Even so, it is very harassing to the farmers. More than thirty years old, very hardworking, but unable to achieve anything. I am afraid that people who don’t know better will think of it as an entertainment trip outside, but not as a dried bean sacrifice inside. Isn’t it for the people?
target: The emperor, seeking to impress barbarian envoys with the empire's abundance of animals, ordered a massive hunt in the Nanshan region. Nets and traps were set to capture bears, porcupines, tigers, leopards, foxes, and elk, which were transported to the Changyang Shooting Bear Pavilion. The animals were enclosed in nets, and the barbarians were taught to fight them bare-handed. The emperor personally watched, while farmers were unable to harvest their crops due to the disruption. Yang Xiong accompanied the emperor and later presented "Ode to Chang Yang," using a dialogue between Zimo Keqing and the master of Hanlin to satirize the hunt. Zimo criticized the hunt for harassing farmers and questioned the emperor's priorities, arguing that such displays of power were not the monarch's urgent duty. The master of Hanlin defended the hunt by recounting past military campaigns against the Qin and various barbarian tribes, framing the hunt as a necessary demonstration of strength to maintain peace and deter future invasions. He argued that the hunt was part of a broader strategy to uphold the emperor's legacy and ensure the prosperity of the people.

source: We have to wait for Fu Rui to come to the base of Liangfu Mountain to add to the majesty of Mount Tai. It will be more glorious than the past and continue in the future. Is it just a wanton tour, galloping in the japonica rice fields, wandering around the pear and chestnut forests, trampling on the grass and trees, showing off to everyone, and harvesting more deer and elk! Moreover, blind people cannot see things close at hand, but Li Lou can see corners thousands of miles away. You only regret that the Hu people got our beasts, and you don't know that we have got their princes. Before he finished speaking, Mo Jie left the table and paid homage to Jishou twice and said: "You know the general picture!" It's really not something I can compare to. Inspire Chaos today and it has become very clear! During the reign of Emperor Ai, Ding, Fu, and Dong Xian were in power, and some of their vassals were appointed officials up to two thousand shi. At that time, Di was drafting "Tai Xuan" to keep himself indifferent. Some people mocked the slut for using black and advocating white. La gave an explanation for this, which was called "Explanation of Mockery". The words said: The guest laughed at Yangzi and said: I heard that the scholars of the past world were guided by the following principles: before they were born, they would respect the king upwards, honor their parents below, distinguish people's honors, receive other people's titles, own other people's talismans, receive other people's salaries, wear blue and purple ribbons, and ride in the car of Zhu Dan. Now you are lucky enough to meet the Ming Dynasty, to be in the court where you don't have to worry about, and to be among the wise men. It has been a long time since you passed through the Golden Gate and went to the Jade Hall. His eyes are like stars, his tongue is like lightning, he moves vertically and horizontally, no one can resist the debating, but he wrote "Tai Xuan" with five thousand words, spread out among the branches and leaves, and only explained more than one hundred thousand words. The depth is as deep as the underworld, the height is as high as the sky, the big one contains the vitality, and the fine one is incomparable. However, he cannot be ranked as a minister, and he has only been promoted to serve in the Huangmen. Did you expect that Xuan can't be used to worship the color white? Why is being an official so reclusive? Yangzi smiled and replied: You just want my chariot and horses to be gorgeous, but you don't know that one mistake will make my family bleed! In the past, the Zhou Dynasty was weakened and the feudal princes were in dispute. They were divided into twelve, which were combined into six or seven. They were divided into four parts and became the Warring States Period. Scholars do not have a permanent monarch, and the country does not have fixed ministers. When they gain wealth from scholars, they become poor when they lose them. They fly with their wings and rest wherever they want. Therefore, some scholars use bags to pack themselves, and some cut through walls to escape. Therefore, Kuiyan gained fame due to his uncertainty, and Meng Ke was still a master of ten thousand chariots despite encountering difficulties. Now the Han Dynasty has the East China Sea on its left, Qusou on its right, Panyu in front, and Taotu in the back.
target: Yang Xiong also wrote "Explanation of Mockery" in response to critics who questioned his reclusive lifestyle and his work on "Tai Xuan." He defended his indifference to worldly success by contrasting the chaotic Warring States period, where scholars could rise and fall rapidly, with the stable Han Dynasty, where opportunities were limited. He argued that his focus on "Tai Xuan" was a deliberate choice to avoid the dangers of political ambition, comparing himself to historical figures who thrived or perished based on timing.

source: When Wang Mang usurped the throne, commentators used talismans to praise his merits and many people were knighted. Yang Xiong was still not knighted. He was gradually promoted to a doctor because of his age. He was so indifferent and snobbish. He really loved the ancient times and loved Taoism, and wanted to be famous for his articles in later generations. He believed that the greatest classic was "Yi", so he wrote "Tai Xuan"; In the "Exuns and Compilations", the best precepts are "Yu Zhen", so I wrote "Zhou Zhen"; the most profound poems are "Li Sao", so I contradict it and promote it; the most gorgeous words are Danru, so I wrote four poems: they all explore the origin and imitate it. His heart was inward and he did not seek anything from the outside. At that time, people despised him. Only Xingti and Liankui respected him, while Danai thought he was incomparable. During the reign of Wang Mang, both Liu Xin and Zhen Feng became princes. Since Wang Mang relied on the talisman to establish himself, after he came to the throne, he wanted to ban this practice in order to deify his past affairs. Zhen Feng's son Zhen Xun and Liu Xin's son Liu Fen also presented the talisman's fortune. Wang Mang killed Zhen Feng and his son, and exiled Liu Fen to the fourth generation. Anyone implicated in his confession was immediately dismissed without any need to report.
target: In "Resolving Difficulties," Yang Xiong addressed complaints that "Tai Xuan" was too obscure. He argued that profound truths are inherently difficult to communicate, comparing his work to the "Book of Changes" and classical texts that required deep understanding. He maintained that his writings were meant for discerning readers, not the masses, and that their value would be recognized over time. Yang Xiong's later years were marked by political turmoil during Wang Mang's usurpation. Despite being implicated in a scandal involving Liu Xin's son, he was spared due to his lack of involvement. He lived in poverty, indifferent to fame, and died at seventy-one.

source: After hearing this, Wang Mang said: Yang Xiong has never been involved in this matter, why is he in this case? They secretly inquired about the reason and found out that Liu Fen had learned to write strange characters from Yang Xiong, but Yang Xiong didn't know about it. Shao Shao will not pursue him. However, the capital master commented on this: Because of loneliness, he is in harmony with himself; because of tranquility, he is a talisman. Yang Xiong was dismissed from his post due to illness and was called a doctor again. His family has always been poor and he likes to drink. People rarely come to his home. At that time, troubled people brought wine and food to study with him. Julu Houba often lived with Yang Xiong and learned "Tai Xuan" and "Fa Yan". Liu Xin also saw it and said to Yang Xiong: You have made yourself suffer in vain! Nowadays, scholars with good fortune cannot understand "Yi", let alone "Xuan"? I'm afraid that future generations will use it to cover sauce pots. Yang Xiong smiled but didn't answer. He lived to be seventy-one years old and died in the fifth year of Tianfeng. Houba built a tomb for him and kept a mourning for him for three years. At that time, Grand Sikong Wangyi and Nayan Yanyou heard that Yang Xiong had died and said to Huan Tan: Can your book praising Yang Xiong be passed down to future generations? Huan Tan said: It will definitely spread. But you and Huan Tan can’t see it. Mortals despise the near and value the far. Seeing with their own eyes that Yang Ziyun's status and appearance are not impressive, they despise his books.
target: His works, particularly "Fayan," gained popularity after his death, though "Tai Xuan" remained less understood. Critics compared his writing of scriptures to unauthorized claims of kingship, but Huan Tan predicted his works would endure, noting that future generations would appreciate their depth.

source: Emperor Xiaowen had four sons: Empress Dou gave birth to Emperor Xiaojing and King Xiao of Liang Wang Wu, and Zhu Ji gave birth to Prince Xiao Shen and King Huai of Liang Yi. In the second year of Emperor Xiaowen's reign, Liang Xiaowang Liu Wu was crowned king on the same day as Taiyuan Wang Liu Shen and Liang Wang Liu Yi. Liu Wu was first granted the title of King of Dai. In the fourth year of Emperor Xiaowen, he was transferred to the title of King of Huaiyang. In the twelfth year of Emperor Xiaowen, Liu Wu was transferred to the Kingdom of Liang. From the initial appointment, he was the king for a total of eleven years. In the fourteenth year of King Xiao's reign, Liu Wu entered the court. In the 17th and 18th years, he entered the DPRK one after another and stayed in the capital. He returned to China in the second year. He entered the DPRK again in the twenty-first year. In the twenty-second year, Emperor Wen died. Entered the DPRK in the twenty-fourth year. Twenty-five years later, he entered the DPRK again. At that time, the emperor had not decided on the crown prince, so he casually said while having a banquet with Xiao Wang Liu Wu: I will pass the throne to you after my death. King Xiao resigned. Although King Xiao knew that what the emperor said was not true, he was very happy. The same is true for the Queen Mother. In the spring of this year, the seven kingdoms of Wu, Chu, Qi, and Tang rebelled. They first attacked Liang Guo Jibi and killed tens of thousands of people. Liang Wang Liu Wu stayed in Suiyang and sent Han Anguo, Zhang Yu and others as generals to fight against Wu and Chu. Wu and Chu were stopped by Liang Guo and did not dare to go westward. They faced off with Taiwei Zhou Yafu and others for three months. Wu, Chu and other countries were defeated, and the number of enemy troops killed by Liang and Han was approximately the same. In the second year, the Han Dynasty established a prince. The Liang Kingdom was the closest to the emperor, had military exploits, and was a big country with fertile territory. It stretched from Mount Tai in the north to Gaoyang in the west. It had more than 40 cities in total, most of which were large counties. Xiao Wang Liu Wu was the youngest son of the Queen Mother. The Queen Mother liked him very much and gave him countless rewards. King Xiao then built Shuyuan, with a radius of more than 300 miles, which was 70 miles wider than Suiyang City. He built a large palace in Dongyuan, built an air passage between the pavilions, and built a road more than 30 miles from the palace to the platform to leave the palace. Under the banner of the emperor's gift, he followed thousands of people on horseback and avoided pedestrians when he came in and out, just like the emperor. He also recruited heroes from all over, and Yang Sheng, Gongsun Gui, Zou Yang and other wanderers from Shandong came to him one after another.
target: Emperor Xiaowen had four sons. Empress Dou bore Emperor Xiaojing and Liu Wu, King Xiao of Liang, while Zhu Ji bore Liu Shen, Prince Xiao, and Liu Yi, King Huai of Liang. Liu Wu was initially made King of Dai, later transferred to Huaiyang, and finally to Liang in the twelfth year of Emperor Xiaowen’s reign, serving as king for eleven years. He frequently entered the court, and during one banquet, Emperor Xiaojing casually offered to pass the throne to him, which Liu Wu declined but was pleased by. In the spring of the twenty-fourth year, the seven kingdoms of Wu, Chu, Qi, and others rebelled, attacking Liang. Liu Wu defended Suiyang with generals Han Anguo and Zhang Yu, holding off Wu and Chu for three months until they were defeated. Liang’s military exploits and proximity to the emperor made it a large, fertile kingdom with over forty cities. Liu Wu, favored by the Queen Mother, built a grand garden and palace, amassed vast wealth, and recruited heroes like Yang Sheng, Gongsun Gui, and Zou Yang. He manufactured weapons and stored treasures exceeding the capital’s.

source: King Xiao also ordered hundreds of thousands of crossbows, bows and arrows to be made, and the money in the treasury was millions, and the jewels and jades were more than those in the capital. In October of the 29th year, King Xiao entered the court. Emperor Jing sent someone in a four-horse chariot to meet him outside the city. After arriving at court, King Xiao wrote to Emperor Jing and stayed. Because of the empress dowager, King Xiao was of the same generation as Emperor Jing when he went in, and rode with Emperor Jing when he went out, and went hunting in the mountains and forests together. The servants, ministers and eunuchs of the Liang Kingdom could enter and leave the Emperor's Palace with their name certificates, just like the eunuchs in the desert. In November, the emperor deposed Prince Li, and the Queen Mother wanted to let Prince Liang succeed him. The ministers and Yuan An and others remonstrated with Emperor Jing, and the Queen Mother's suggestion was shelved. King Xiao did not dare to discuss the succession with the Queen Mother anymore. The matter was a secret and unknown to the world, so King Xiao immediately left and returned to his country. In the summer, the emperor made King Micellar the crown prince. The King of Liang hated Yuan An and the ministers who made suggestions, so he conspired with Yang Sheng, Gongsun Gui and others, and secretly sent people to assassinate Yuan An and a dozen other ministers. As a result, the assassin failed. The emperor suspected that this matter was done by Liang Guo, and after further investigation, he found out that it was indeed sent by Liang Guo. So he sent a large team of people to Liang Guo to investigate the matter. Gongsun Gui and Yang Sheng were hunted down and hid in the palace of Queen Liang. The envoy sent two thousand stone officials to urge the king of Liang to surrender. Liang's Prime Minister Xuan Qiubao and Internal Secretary Han Anguo cried to persuade the King of Liang, and the King of Liang ordered Yang Sheng and Gongsun Gui to commit suicide and then hand them over. The emperor was angry with King Liang because of this. The King of Liang was in panic, so he sent Han Anguo to apologize to the Queen Mother through the eldest princess, and then he calmed down. After the emperor's anger subsided, King Xiao of Liang immediately submitted a letter to the court. When they arrived outside the city, the doctor Mao Lan advised King Xiao to enter the city in a carriage with a cloth curtain, taking only two knights with him, and first hid in the eldest princess's garden. When the Han Emperor's envoy came to pick up King Xiao, King Xiao had already entered the city, but his carriage and horses were outside the city, and others did not know where he had gone. The Queen Mother cried and said: The emperor has killed my son! The emperor was also very nervous. Soon King Xiao of Liang came to the palace to plead guilty. The Queen Mother and the Emperor were overjoyed to see him. After crying with each other, they reconciled as before. King Xiao's followers were also summoned into the city. However, Emperor Jing became more distant from Prince Xiao and stopped riding in the chariot with him. In the winter of the thirty-fifth year, King Xiao entered the court again and wrote a letter to stay, but the emperor refused. King Xiao felt unhappy after returning home. One day, King Xiao went hunting on Liangshan Mountain in the north. Someone offered a cow with legs growing out of its back. King Xiao didn't like it very much. On June 6, King Xiao fell ill with fever and died. King Xiao was very filial. Every time he heard that the Queen Mother was ill, he couldn't eat and often wanted to stay in Chang'an to accompany the Queen Mother.
target: In the twenty-ninth year, he entered the court and was honored by Emperor Jing, riding together and hunting. After the emperor deposed Prince Li, the Queen Mother wanted Liu Wu to succeed, but ministers like Yuan An dissuaded the emperor, and Liu Wu left. Later, Liu Wu conspired to assassinate Yuan An and others, but the plot failed. The emperor investigated, and Liu Wu’s men hid. After pressure, Liu Wu ordered them to commit suicide. The emperor grew distant, and Liu Wu, in panic, apologized through the eldest princess. He later hid in the princess’s garden, causing the Queen Mother to weep, but reconciled with the emperor. However, Emperor Jing stopped riding with him. In the thirty-fifth year, Liu Wu entered the court but was denied stay, becoming unhappy. He died of fever on June 6 after hunting and seeing a strange cow. He was filial, often wanting to stay with the Queen Mother when she was ill.

source: The Queen Mother also liked him very much. After hearing that King Xiao died, Queen Mother Dou cried very sadly, refused to eat or drink, and said: The emperor really killed my son! The emperor was sad and scared, and didn't know what to do. After discussing with the eldest princess, the emperor decided to divide the Liang Kingdom into five kingdoms, grant the title of king to each of King Xiao's five sons, and grant land and salary to King Xiao's five daughters. This matter was reported to the Queen Mother, who became happy and had a meal for the sake of the Emperor. Before the death of King Xiao, his property was in the tens of millions, which was countless. By the time of his death, there were more than 400,000 kilograms of gold hidden in the house, and other properties were also equivalent to that. On behalf of Xiao Wang Liu Canchu was granted the title of King of Taiyuan. In the fourth year of Emperor Xiaowen's reign, the original king Liu Wu was granted the title of King of Huaiyang. Liu Shen was renamed the acting king and continued to be in charge of Taiyuan, with Jinyang as the capital.
target: Her grief led the emperor to divide Liang into five kingdoms for Liu Wu’s sons and grant land to his daughters. Liu Wu’s wealth was immense, with over 400,000 kilograms of gold at death.

source: However, Liu Nian sent his father Ji to greet and see off Liu Ze, which continued year after year. A superior reported that Liu Nian was guilty of promiscuity, so Liu Nian was deposed as a commoner, moved to Fangling, and granted a hundred households a fief. Three years later, the state was abolished. In the second year of the first year of the Yuan Dynasty, the prince of Xindu sent a mission to support the extinct kingdom. He sent a report to the Empress Dowager and established his younger brother's son, Zhuxuan, as King Chensai to succeed King Xiao. After Wang Ling usurped the throne, the feudal state was abolished. Although Liang Huai Wang Yi was the youngest son of Emperor Wen. He likes "Shi Zhen" and "Shang Shu", and the chief inspector likes him differently from other sons. He entered the DPRK once every five years and entered the DPRK twice in total. Died due to falling from a horse and reigned for ten years. Since there were no successors, the country was abolished. In the second year, King Luan Xiao died and moved to Feng Kuang. The five sons of King Xiao of Liang were all named kings: the eldest son Liu Mai was the King of Liang Gong, the second son Liu Ming was the King of Ji, the third son Peng Li was the King of Ji Shu, the fourth son Liu Xuan was the King of Shanyang, and the fifth son Pi Yao was the King of Nadan Mu. They were all crowned kings on the same day in the sixth year of Emperor Xiaojing's reign. Liang Communist King Liu Mai died after reigning for seven years, and his son Ping Wang Liu Xiang succeeded to the throne. Liu Ming, the king of Jichuan, was granted the title of king from the title of Marquis of Yuanyi. When he was in power for seven years, he shot and killed one of his lieutenants. His superiors reported that he should be executed. Jihu could not bear to kill him, so he was deposed as a civilian and moved to Fangling County, thus deposing his kingdom. King Pengli of Jidong reigned for twenty-nine years. Peng Li has an arrogant temperament. He often goes out secretly at night to rob with dozens of his desperate youths, taking pleasure in killing people and grabbing money. As far as anyone knew, they killed more than a hundred people. The whole country knew about this, and the people did not dare to go out at night. The victim's children complained, and a minister petitioned the emperor to behead him. Emperor Wu couldn't bear it, so he deposed him as a commoner and moved him to Shangyong County. He abolished his feudal state and changed it to Dahe County. Liu Ding, the Ai King of Shanyang, died after reigning for nine years. Because he had no children, the feudal state was abolished. King Ji Yin'ai died without a son within a year of his reign, and the feudal kingdom was abolished. Prince Xiao and his concubine were all crowned kings, but they all died without heirs. The mother of Liang Ping Wang Liu Xiang was the Queen Mother Chen. The mother of King Gong of Liang was Queen Mother Li.
target: Liu Shen, King of Taiyuan, visited court three times before dying. His descendants ruled until Liu Nian was deposed for incest with his sister. Liu Yi, King Huai of Liang, died from a fall, leaving no heirs. Liu Wu’s five sons were all made kings on the same day. Liu Mai, King Gong of Liang, died after seven years. Liu Ming was deposed for murder. Peng Li, King of Jidong, was deposed for robbery and murder. Liu Ding, King Ai of Shanyang, died without heirs. Another son died without issue.

source: Prince Xiao and his concubine were all crowned kings, but they all died without heirs. The mother of Liang Ping Wang Liu Xiang was the Queen Mother Chen. target: Liu Xiang, King Ping of Liang, favored Queen Ren, who coveted a wine bottle left by Liu Wu. Queen Mother Li refused, but Liu Xiang took it. Conflicts arose, and Queen Mother Li’s adultery was exposed. After her death, Queen Ren failed to mourn.

She cried and shouted, but she still didn't see the Han envoy. Because Empress Dowager Li had committed adultery with the Chief Food Officer and Lang Guan Yin Ba, King Ping and Empress Ren sent people to dissuade Empress Dowager Li, and Empress Dowager Li gave up. Later Empress Dowager Li died of illness. When Empress Dowager Li was ill, Empress Ren did not visit her; when she died, Empress Ren did not go to mourn her either. During the Yuanshuo period, someone insulted the father of a rebel named Suiyang. The man went out to ride with the guests of Suiyang Prefect, and then he jumped on the train and killed the enemy, and then ran away.
target: During the Yuanshuo period, a fugitive revealed palace scandals. The emperor investigated, found Queen Ren guilty, and reduced Liang’s territory. Liu Xiang died after forty years. His descendants ruled until Liu Li, King Huang, committed adultery with his aunt and murdered officials. Despite multiple crimes, the emperor showed mercy, only reducing territory. Liu Li later committed suicide after being deposed. The kingdom was eventually abolished.

source: Emperor Xiaojing had fourteen sons. Queen Wang gave birth to Emperor Xiaowu. Li Ji was born to Liu Rong, the Min king of Linjiang, Liu De, the Xian king of Hejian, and Liu Yan, the Ai king of Linjiang. Cheng Ji gave birth to Liu Yu, king of the Communist Party of Lu, Liu Fei, king of Yi in Jiangdu, and Liu Duan, king of Jiaoxi. Buying a wife gave birth to King Zhao Jingsu, Liu Pengzu, and King Jing of Zhongshan, Liu Sheng. Tang Ji grew up and settled with King Liu Fa. Mrs. Wang was born as Prince Hui of Guangchuan, Liu Yue, Prince Kang of Micellar, Liu Ji, Prince Ai of Qinghe, Liu Cheng, and Prince Xian of Changshan, Liu Shun. He always started from reality and reached correct conclusions. If you get a good book among the people, you must make a good copy to the book owner, leave the original copy of the book, and give money and silk to widely recruit good books. In this way, people with moral knowledge from all over came from far and wide, some of whom had books collected by their ancestors, and most of them donated to King Xian, so the number of books obtained was as large as that of the Han Dynasty.
target: Emperor Xiaojing had fourteen sons by various consorts. Among them, Liu De, the King of Hejian, was a notable scholar who loved ancient texts. He diligently collected books from the people, offering generous compensation for rare copies, amassing a collection as vast as the imperial library.

source: Mrs. Wang was born as Prince Hui of Guangchuan, Liu Yue, Prince Kang of Micellar, Liu Ji, Prince Ai of Qinghe, Liu Cheng, and Prince Xian of Changshan, Liu Shun. Liu De, the king of Hejian, was granted the title of king in the second year of Emperor Jing's reign. He studied academically and loved ancient affairs. He always started from reality and reached correct conclusions. If you get a good book among the people, you must make a good copy to the book owner, leave the original copy of the book, and give money and silk to widely recruit good books. In this way, people with moral knowledge from all over came from far and wide, some of whom had books collected by their ancestors, and most of them donated to King Xian, so the number of books obtained was as large as that of the Han Dynasty. At the same time, Huainan King Liu An also loved books, and most of the books he recruited were useless. The books that King Xian obtained were all old ancient texts from before the Qin Dynasty, such as Zhou Guan, Shangshu, Rites, Book of Rites, Mencius, Laozi and other books. They were all written by seventy disciples of Confucius. King Xian studied and applied the Six Classics, and established doctors of Mao's Poetry and Zuo's Spring and Autumn Annals. Practice rituals and music, experience Confucian academics personally, and everything you learn must be based on Confucianism. Many scholars from Shandong followed him there. During the period of Emperor Wu, King Xian came to court, offered elegant music, and answered more than 30 questions from Sanyong Palace and imperial edicts. As far as the moral scholarship he talks about is concerned, it is reasonable and the language is concise and clear. King Xian died after reigning for twenty-six years.
target: Unlike King Huainan of An, whose books were often useless, Liu De’s collection consisted of pre-Qin classics like the *Zhou Guan*, *Shangshu*, *Rites*, *Mencius*, and *Laozi*, all attributed to Confucius’s seventy disciples. He established doctors for the *Mao Poetry* and *Zuo’s Spring and Autumn Annals*, practiced rituals and music, and adhered to Confucian teachings, attracting many scholars from Shandong. During Emperor Wu’s reign, he presented elegant music and answered over thirty questions from the court with clarity and reason.

source: When the officials dealt with Sui's affairs, he confessed to King Chen. Cho Yi faced her closest relative, secretly sad, fell ill and died, not daring to have any heirs. So I heard that Liu Ji had his eldest son Liu Xian, who was not favored by his mother, but his younger son Liu Qing was favored. Liu Ji often wanted to make him king, but it was not in the right order. Because of his mistakes, he finally had something to say. The emperor took pity on him and made Liu Xian the King of Micellar to accept the sacrifices of King Kang. He also made Liu Qing the King of Liu'an and the king of the former Hengshan Mountain. Wang Xian died after reigning for fifteen years, and he became King Ai. His son Dai Wangtongping succeeded him and died after reigning for twenty-four years.
target: After reigning for twenty-six years, he died, praised by officials for his uprightness, kindness, and frugality.

source: Liu Bo was granted the title of king for several months, but was abolished and the fiefdom was taken back. More than a month later, because the emperor was closest to the king, he issued an edict to Yousi, saying: King Xian of Changshan died early, and later he was at odds with his concubines. His concubines and concubines made false accusations and fought with each other. They fell into injustice and reduced the country. I have great sympathy for him.
target: His descendants ruled Hejian for generations, though later kings like Liu Yuan faced scandal and deposition for cruelty and misconduct, leading to the kingdom’s abolition and restoration under Emperor Cheng.

source: His son Liu Shang succeeded to the throne, but Wang Mang's line of succession was cut off. Linjiang Ai Wang Xing'er was granted the title of king in the second year of the Yuan Dynasty in Jicha. He died after reigning for three years without leaving any sons, and the title was abolished as a county. Linjiang Min King Liu Rong was the crown prince in the fourth year of Emperor Jing's reign. Four years later, he was deposed as the prince of Linjiang. Another three years passed. Because he occupied the open space of the temple to build a palace, the emperor conscripted Liu Rong. When Liu Ming set out, he worshiped his ancestors at the north gate of Jiangling. After getting on the car, the axle broke and the car broke down. The elders of Jiangling cried privately and said: Our king will not come back! After Liu Rong arrived in the capital, he went to the Lieutenant's Mansion for trial. Lieutenant Zhidu interrogated the king with a confession. The king was frightened and committed suicide. He was buried in Lantian, and tens of thousands of swallows placed earth on the grave. The people felt pity for his plight. Liu Rong was the oldest and had no sons, so his feudal state was abolished. The fiefdom was transferred to the Han Dynasty and became Nanjun. King Gong of Lu, Liu Yu, was granted the title of King of Huaiyang in the second year of Emperor Jing's reign. Wu Chu rebelled, and after being defeated, Liu Yu moved to Lu in the third year of Emperor Jing's reign. Liu Yu liked to build palaces, gardens, and raise dogs and horses. In his later years, he liked music but disliked literature. He was born with a stutter and had trouble speaking. King Liu Gong of Lu died after reigning for twenty-eight years. His son An Wang Liu Guang succeeded to the throne. He was initially fond of music, carriages and horses, but in his later years he was greedy and stingy for fear of insufficient wealth. He died after reigning for forty years. His son Xiao Wang Qingji succeeded him and died after reigning for thirty-seven years. His son Liu Jin, King of Qing, succeeded him and died after reigning for twenty-eight years. His son, King Wen Liu, succeeded him to the throne. He died after reigning for eighteen years without any sons, and the feudal state was abolished. In the third year of Emperor Ai's reign, he also made Liu Min, Marquis of Buxiang, the younger brother of King Wen Liu Sui, the son of King Qing, as king. It was cut off when Wang Mang died. Prince Gong initially liked to expand his palace and destroyed Confucius' old house to expand his palace. When he heard the sound of bells, chimes, harps and harps, he did not dare to destroy it any more, and he obtained ancient scriptures and scriptures in the walls of the old house. Liu Fei, the king of Yi in Jiangdu, was granted the title of King of Runan in the second year BC of Xiaojing. When Wu Chu rebelled, Liu Feigang was fifteen years old and talented. He wrote a letter asking for an attack on Wu. Emperor Jing gave Liu Fei the seal of general to attack Wu. The State of Wu was conquered, and the king moved to Jiangdu to govern the former State of Wu. He was awarded the emperor's flag for his military exploits. During the Yuanguang period, the Xiongnu invaded the Han border in large numbers. Liu Fei wrote a letter willing to attack the Xiongnu, but Emperor Jing did not agree. Liu Fei liked strength, expanded his palaces and buildings, attracted heroes from all over, and was very arrogant and extravagant.
target: Other sons of Emperor Xiaojing had varied fates. Liu Rong, the Min King of Linjiang, was once crown prince but was deposed and later committed suicide after being accused of building a palace on temple grounds. Liu Yu, the King of Lu, was known for building palaces and raising dogs and horses, but he had a stutter and disliked literature. His descendant, Liu Gong, destroyed Confucius’s old house to expand his palace but stopped upon hearing music, discovering ancient scriptures in the walls. Liu Fei, the King of Yi in Jiangdu, was a talented youth who fought against Wu during the rebellion, but later became arrogant and extravagant. His son, Liu Jian, was notoriously depraved, committing adultery, murder, and even plotting rebellion with weapons and seals. He was eventually forced to commit suicide, and his kingdom was abolished. Liu Duan, the King of Jiaoxi, was cruel and physically weak, often killing officials who tried to govern lawfully, leading to his kingdom’s reduction and eventual abolition.

source: After Yousi requested many times, his feudal state was reduced by more than half. Liu Duan was angry, so he stopped managing the capital. The treasury was ruined and leaked, all the property was rotten, and the losses amounted to tens of thousands of dollars, but they were never cleaned up or moved. Officials were ordered not to collect taxes. Liu Duan removed the guards, sealed the palace, and entered and exited through one door. He changed his name many times, pretended to be a civilian, and traveled to other countries. When Xiang Erqianshi arrived, he followed Han law to govern Jiaoxi. Liu Duan often tried to find out their crimes and sued them, and the innocent ones were killed with poison by fraud. Therefore, he deceives others to seek change, is strong enough to refuse other people's advice, and is resourceful enough to cover up his mistakes. Xiang Erqianshi followed the king to govern, but was brought to justice by Mo Mo. So Jiaoxi is a small country, but the two thousand stones killed are quite a lot. The King of Jiaoxi died in his forty-seventh year without a son. The feudal state was abolished and the land was transferred to the Han Dynasty and became Jiaoxi County. King Zhao Jingsu and Liu Pengzu were named King of Guangchuan in the second year of Emperor Jing's reign. King Liu Sui of Zhao rebelled and was defeated, so he moved the king to Zhao. Jie Dan is hypocritical, flattering, overly respectful to others, but cruel at heart, accustomed to using the law, and using sophistry to frame people.
target: Liu Pengzu, the King of Zhao, was deceitful and flattering, using sophistry to frame officials and amassing wealth through trade.

source: In the second year of Emperor Hongjia's reign, Yunke, the son of Lixianghou, the grandson of King Xian's younger brother, was named King of Yi in Guangde. After reigning for three years, he died without any children, and the country was isolated for fourteen years. Emperor Ai also appointed Guanghan, Yunke's younger brother, as King Guangping. Dead, no descendants. In the second year of Emperor Ping's reign, Liu Lun, the great-grandson of King Hui of Guangchuan, was appointed King Guangde, and he was adopted as Queen Jing. It was cut off when Wang Mang died. Liu Fa, the king of Changsha, whose mother Tang Ji was the former attendant of Cheng Ji. Emperor Jing summoned Cheng Ji to accompany him, but Cheng Ji was inconvenient and unwilling to go, so he asked his attendant Tang Er to disguise herself and go in at night. The emperor was drunk and didn't know it. He thought it was Cheng Ji and had sex with her, and Tang Er became pregnant. It was only after the emperor had a relationship with her that he realized she was not Cheng Ji. When a son was born, he was named Liu Fa. In the second year of Emperor Jing's reign, he was granted the title of king. Because her mother was born in a humble family and could not be favored, she went to govern a poor country with low-lying and humid land. He died after reigning for twenty-eight years. His son, King Dai Liu Yong, succeeded him and died after reigning for twenty-seven years. His son, King Qing, Yuxuan, succeeded him and died after reigning for seventeen years. His son assassinated King Jiande and succeeded him to the throne. During the reign of Emperor Xuan, he burned down ninety-six houses and killed two people due to hunting and arson. He also resented the internal history due to court affairs and instigated others to make false accusations. He was punished for abandoning the city. Eight counties were reduced and the lieutenant was dismissed. He died after reigning for thirty-four years. His son, King Yang, Liu Dan, succeeded him and died after reigning for two years. He has no son and has been in isolation for more than a year. In the third year of the Yuan Dynasty, Emperor Yuan appointed Liu Dan's younger brother Liu Zong as King Xiao, who reigned for five years until his death. His son, a native of Lu, succeeded him to the throne, but Wang Mang's reign was cut off. Liu Yue, King Hui of Guangchuan, was granted the title of king in the second year of Emperor Jing's reign and passed away in the thirteenth year of his reign. His son Liu Qi, King Miao, succeeded him and died after reigning for forty-four years. Once upon a time, Liu Qi had a favored minister, Chengju, who later committed a crime. Liu Qi wanted to kill Chengju.
target: He died after sixty years of rule, but his son Liu Dan was executed for promiscuity and murder. Liu Sheng, the King of Zhongshan, was a drunkard with over 120 children, but he famously wept before Emperor Wu, complaining of officials’ encroachments on princes’ rights. This led to Emperor Wu’s policy of dividing princes’ lands among their sons, weakening their power. Liu Fa, the King of Changsha, was born from a concubine’s deception and ruled a poor, humid kingdom. His descendants faced scandals, including a king who burned houses and killed people. Liu Yue, the King of Guangchuan, died early, and his son Liu Qi was accused of incest and false accusations, leading to his kingdom’s temporary abolition. Liu Qu, a later king, was a scholar who studied the *Yi* and *Analects*, but he became tyrannical, torturing and killing concubines under the influence of his queen, Zhaoxin. He was deposed and committed suicide.

source: His son Haiyang succeeded to the throne. During his fifteenth year of reign, he hung a painting of naked men and women having sex in the studio, and offered wine to his uncles and sisters to drink, making them look up at the paintings. Haiyang's sister was already a wife, and he allowed her to commit adultery with his favorite ministers. He also murdered three people in the family with his cousin Liu Tiao and others. In the fourth year of Ganlu's reign, he was convicted and abolished. He moved to Fangling and the feudal state was abolished. Fifteen years later, in the second year of the Yuanshi period of Emperor Ping, Liu Yu, the son of King Dai's brother Xiangdihou, was appointed King of Guangde, and he succeeded King Hui as his queen. He reigned for two years until his death. His son Liu Chi succeeded to the throne, but Wang Mang cut off the throne. King Kang Xingzhou of Jiaodong was granted the title of king in the second year of Zhongyuan in Jihu, and he died after reigning for twenty-eight years. When the King of Huainan rebelled, Xingyi heard about it secretly, secretly made chariots, bows and arrows, and prepared all the troops to guard against the rebellion. When the officials dealt with Sui's affairs, he confessed to King Chen. Cho Yi faced her closest relative, secretly sad, fell ill and died, not daring to have any heirs. So I heard that Liu Ji had his eldest son Liu Xian, who was not favored by his mother, but his younger son Liu Qing was favored. Liu Ji often wanted to make him king, but it was not in the right order. Because of his mistakes, he finally had something to say. The emperor took pity on him and made Liu Xian the King of Micellar to accept the sacrifices of King Kang. He also made Liu Qing the King of Liu'an and the king of the former Hengshan Mountain. Wang Xian died after reigning for fifteen years, and he became King Ai.
target: Other kings included Liu Shun of Changshan, who was arrogant but often forgiven by his father. His son Liu Bo was deposed for neglecting his father’s funeral, and the kingdom was divided among his brothers. Liu Ji of Jiaodong was cautious during the Huainan rebellion, but his sons were made kings of smaller states. The text concludes with a reflection on the dangers of luxury and power, noting that most princes became arrogant and immoral, except for the noble King Xian of Hejian.

source: Li Guang, a native of Shengqi, Longxi County. His ancestor Li Zhi was a general in the Qin Dynasty and once hunted down Prince Dan of Yan State. Li Guang's family has been learning archery for generations. In the fourteenth year of Emperor Xiaowen's reign, the Huns invaded Xiaoguan in large numbers. Li Guang joined the army to fight against the Huns as a son of a good family. Because he was good at archery, he killed and captured many enemies. He became a Langguan of the Han Dynasty and served as a riding attendant. Li Guang often went hunting with Emperor Wen and killed fierce beasts, so Emperor Wen said: It's a pity that you didn't get the chance; if you were in the era of Emperor Gao, it wouldn't be a problem to be granted the title of Marquis of Ten Thousand Households! Emperor Xiaojing ascended the throne, and Li Guang was appointed Cavalry General. When the seven kingdoms of Wu and Chu rebelled, Li Guang served as the commander of Xiaoqi. He followed Taiwei Zhou Yafu to attack Wu and Chu, and made outstanding achievements in Changyi City. Because the King of Liang privately awarded General Li Guang the seal, he did not receive the reward after returning to the court. He was transferred to the prefect of Shanggu and fought many battles with the Xiongnu. Sun Kunxie, the Duke of Dian, said to the emperor with tears in his eyes: "Li Guang's talent is unparalleled in the world." He relied on his own ability and fought against the enemy many times, fearing that he would be sacrificed.
target: Li Guang, a native of Longxi County, was a descendant of a Qin general and came from a family skilled in archery. He began his military career during Emperor Wen's reign, fighting the Xiongnu at Xiaoguan, where his archery skills earned him a position as a Langguan. Emperor Wen lamented that Li Guang's talents would have earned him a marquisate in the era of Emperor Gaozu. Under Emperor Jing, he served as a Cavalry General and fought in the campaign against the rebellious seven kingdoms of Wu and Chu, but was denied a reward due to accepting a seal from the King of Liang. He later served as the Prefect of Shanggu and other border commanderies, frequently battling the Xiongnu.

source: Sun Kunxie, the Duke of Dian, said to the emperor with tears in his eyes: "Li Guang's talent is unparalleled in the world." He relied on his own ability and fought against the enemy many times, fearing that he would be sacrificed. So he was transferred to the prefecture of Shangjun. The Huns invaded Shangjun, and the emperor sent noble men to follow Li Guang and lead his own troops to fight against the Huns. The noble man galloped with dozens of cavalry, met three Huns, and fought with them. The three Huns turned around and fired arrows, wounding the noble man and killing almost all the cavalry he had brought with him. The noble man ran to Li Guang. Li Guang said: This must be the Condor Shooter. Li Guang then led a hundred cavalry to chase the three men.
target: During a campaign in Shangjun, Li Guang, with only a hundred cavalry, encountered thousands of Xiongnu.

source: Now that we stop, the Xiongnu must think that we are decoys of the army and will not dare to attack us. Li Guang ordered: Forward! After entering about two miles away from the Huns' position, they stopped and ordered: "Everyone, dismount and unsaddle!" His cavalry said: There are many enemies and they are close. What if there is an emergency after unsaddled? Li Guang said: Those enemies thought that we would escape, and now they took off their saddles to show that they would not leave. They used this method to confirm their suspicions. So the Huns' cavalry finally did not dare to attack. A general on a white horse came out to guard his soldiers. Li Guang mounted his horse, galloped over with more than a dozen cavalry, and shot the Xiongnu general on a white horse to death. Then he returned to his cavalry, took off the saddle, and ordered the soldiers to let go of their horses and lie down. It was almost dusk on this beautiful day, and the Huns soldiers were always uncertain and did not dare to attack. In the middle of the night, the Huns also thought that the Han army had an ambush nearby and would attack them at night, so the Huns all retreated.
target: He cleverly halted his men and dismounted, convincing the enemy they were a decoy, which prevented an attack. After nightfall, the Xiongnu withdrew, suspecting an ambush.

source: A general on a white horse came out to guard his soldiers. Li Guang mounted his horse, galloped over with more than a dozen cavalry, and shot the Xiongnu general on a white horse to death. Then he returned to his cavalry, took off the saddle, and ordered the soldiers to let go of their horses and lie down. It was almost dusk on this beautiful day, and the Huns soldiers were always uncertain and did not dare to attack. In the middle of the night, the Huns also thought that the Han army had an ambush nearby and would attack them at night, so the Huns all retreated. Early the next morning, Li Guangcai returned to his main army. Later, he successively served as the prefect of Longxi, Beidi, Yanmen and Yunzhong. When Emperor Wu came to the throne, his ministers said that Li Guang was a famous general, so Li Guang was transferred to the Weiyang Palace Guards, while Cheng Bushi also served as the Changle Palace Guards at that time. In the past, Cheng Bushi and Li Guang both led the army as governors of border counties and stationed fields to guard the border. When he sent out troops to attack the Huns, Li Guang's army did not have strict organization, queues or formations. They stationed themselves near good water sources and grasslands, and stayed and stayed at their own convenience. They did not patrol or patrol at night to defend themselves. The military's documents and books were kept simple, but reconnaissance posts were also set up in the distance, so they did not encounter any danger. Cheng Bushi strictly required the establishment, formation and formation, and patrolled at night, and the officers processed military documents until dawn, and the troops were not allowed to do what they wanted. Cheng Bushi said: Li Guang's troops were very casual, but when the enemy suddenly attacked them, they were unable to parry them; and his soldiers were comfortable and happy, and they were all willing to die for him.
target: Li Guang later served as a palace guard under Emperor Wu, alongside Cheng Bushi. While Cheng Bushi's army was strictly disciplined, Li Guang's was more relaxed, yet his soldiers were loyal and willing to die for him. The Xiongnu feared Li Guang's strategies, and soldiers preferred serving under him.

source: Four years later, Li Guang was transferred from a guard to a general and attacked the Huns from Yanmen County. The Huns had more soldiers and defeated Li Guang's army and captured Li Guang alive. Shan Yu always heard that Li Guang was talented and issued an order: If Li Guang is captured, he must be delivered alive. The Huns cavalry captured Li Guang, who was injured at the time. They placed Li Guang between the two horses and used ropes to form a net bag for Li Guang to lie down. After walking for more than ten miles, Li Guang pretended to be dead and squinted at a Hun boy riding a good horse next to him. Li Guang suddenly jumped up, climbed on the Hun boy's horse, held the boy in his arms and rode south for dozens of miles, and gathered the remaining troops of him. Hundreds of Xiongnu cavalry chased him. As he ran, Li Guang picked up the bow and arrow of the Xiongnu boy and shot the chasing cavalry to death, thus escaping. So he returned to the Han capital, and the Han court handed Li Guang over to the judge. The judge ruled that Li Guang had lost many men and horses and was captured alive by the enemy. He should be beheaded and use money to atone and become a civilian.
target: Li Guang was captured by the Xiongnu in a later campaign but escaped by feigning death, stealing a horse, and shooting his pursuers.

source: Li Guang ordered the soldiers to draw their bows and not to release arrows. Li Guang personally used the big yellow crossbow to shoot at the enemy's lieutenants, killing several of them, and the Huns gradually relaxed. It happened to be dark, and the officers and soldiers were pale, but Li Guang looked as usual and commanded the army more energetically. The soldiers in the army admired his courage. The next day, they continued to fight hard, and Bowang Hou's army also arrived, and the Huns army finally relieved the siege. The Han army was tired and could not pursue him. At this time, Li Guang's army was almost wiped out and he had to withdraw his troops. According to the laws of the Han Dynasty, Bowang Hou delayed the scheduled date and was sentenced to death. He paid for his sins and was reduced to a commoner.
target: He was sentenced to death for his losses but redeemed himself with money, becoming a commoner.

source: Shouldn’t my life be granted a title of marquis? Wang Shuo said: General, think about it yourself, has there ever been any regret? Li Guang said: I was once the governor of Longxi. The Qiang people rebelled. I lured them to surrender. More than 800 people surrendered. I used deception to kill them on the same day. So far, my biggest regret is only this incident. Wang Shuo said: There is no greater sin than killing someone who has surrendered. This is why the general cannot be granted the title of marquis. Li Guang served as the governor of seven counties for more than 40 years. After receiving rewards, he immediately distributed them to his subordinates, and shared his food and drink with the soldiers.
target: He later served as the Right Governor of Beiping, where the Xiongnu avoided him for years.

source: Li Guang was tall, long-armed, and talented in archery. Even if his descendants and others learned archery from him, they could not catch up with him.
