Li Guang was arrogant and did not talk much to others. He lived with others and drew battle formations on the ground. He shot arrows wider and narrower than the area he shot. If he lost, he drank wine as a penalty. Specialized in archery as a game. When leading troops on the march, they encounter a shortage of food and water. When they see water, not all the soldiers drink the water. He does not go near the water. Not all the soldiers have food. He does not taste the food. He treats soldiers generously and carefully, so soldiers like to work for him. When he shoots an arrow and sees an enemy within a few dozen steps, he probably won't hit the target and will fall to the ground as soon as he shoots.
target: During a hunt, he famously shot an arrow into a stone, mistaking it for a tiger.

source: During the reign of Emperor Jing, Li Cai received a salary of two thousand stone levels for his accumulated merit. During the Yuanshuo period of Emperor Xiaowu, he served as General of Qingchao and followed the general to attack King Youxian. His meritorious service reached the standard of reward and he was named Marquis of Le'an. In the second year of Yuanshou, he replaced Gongsun Hong as prime minister. Li Cai's character was among the lowest, and his reputation was far below that of Li Guang. However, Li Guang did not receive a title or fief, and his official position did not exceed Jiuqing. Many of Li Guang's officers and soldiers were awarded the title of Marquis. Li Guang once chatted with Wang Shuo, a Wangqi master, and said: Ever since the Han Dynasty attacked the Huns, I have never been absent from them. However, the talents of each army commander and below are not average enough. However, there are dozens of people who have obtained marquises because of their military exploits in attacking the Huns. However, I did not fall behind others, but I did not have a small amount of merit to obtain a fief. What is the reason? Shouldn’t my life be granted a title of marquis? Wang Shuo said: General, think about it yourself, has there ever been any regret? Li Guang said: I was once the governor of Longxi. The Qiang people rebelled. I lured them to surrender. More than 800 people surrendered. I used deception to kill them on the same day. So far, my biggest regret is only this incident. Wang Shuo said: There is no greater sin than killing someone who has surrendered. This is why the general cannot be granted the title of marquis.
target: Despite his reputation, Li Guang never received a marquisate, a fact he lamented to Wang Shuo, who attributed it to Li Guang's past deception and killing of surrendered Qiang rebels.

source: At this time, Gongsun Ao had recently lost a marquis and was serving as lieutenant general. The general also wanted Gongsun Ao to fight against Shanyu with him, so he transferred former general Li Guang. Li Guang knew this situation at the time and resolutely refused to be transferred to the general. The general refused to listen and ordered the chief historian to send a document to Li Guang's shogunate, saying: Go to the military headquarters where you are and do as the document says. Li Guang set out without saying goodbye to the general. He went to the military headquarters in anger, led his soldiers and the right general to the place where they joined forces, and set off from the east road. He lost his way and fell behind the general.
target: In his final campaign, Li Guang served as a former general under Wei Qing. Ordered to take a circuitous eastern route, he lost his way and failed to join the main force.

source: In the second year after Li Guang's death, Li Cai became the prime minister. He should be punished by the judge for occupying the open space of Emperor Xiaojing's Yangling Mausoleum. The open space given to him at that time was only 20 acres, and Li Cai occupied three hectares. After selling the land, he received more than 400,000 yuan. He also occupied an acre of land outside the Shinto as a cemetery. He was sentenced to prison, so Li Cai also committed suicide. As a school captain, Li Gan followed the hussar general to attack King Zuoxian of the Huns. He fought hard and captured King Zuoxian's war drum and flag. He beheaded many of the enemies. He was awarded the title of Marquis of Dingguannei and enjoyed the title of 200 households. He succeeded Li Guang as the doctor's order. Soon, Li Gan resented the general Wei Qing for causing his father to die out of hatred, so he wounded the general, but the general concealed the incident. Not long after, Li Gan accompanied the emperor to Yongzhou Ganquan Palace for hunting. General Huo Qubing resented Li Gan for injuring Wei Qing and shot Li Gan to death. Huo Qubing was favored by the nobles at that time, but the emperor concealed the truth and said that a wild deer killed him. More than a year later, Huo Qubing died. Li Gan had a daughter who was the prince's maid and was favored. Li Gan's son Li Yu was also favored by the prince, but he was fond of wealth and had courage. He once drank with a nobleman in his attendants and insulted him, but the nobleman did not dare to say anything. Later, he told the emperor. The emperor summoned Li Yu and asked him to stab the tiger. He hung down to the tiger enclosure, but before he reached the ground, he ordered Li Yu to be pulled up. Li Yu cut the rope from the net and wanted to stab the tiger. The emperor thought he was brave, so he rescued him and stopped him from stabbing the tiger. Li Danghu had a posthumous son named Li Ling, who led an army to attack the Huns. He was defeated and surrendered to the Huns. Later, someone accused Li Yu of trying to follow Li Ling and was executed. Li Ling, whose courtesy name is Shaoqing, was appointed as the Jian Zhang Supervisor of the Imperial Palace when he was young. He is good at riding and shooting, loves and cares for others, and is humble to his subordinates. He has a good reputation. Emperor Wu felt that he had Li Guang's demeanor, so he asked him to lead 800 cavalry and penetrated more than 2,000 miles into the Huns' territory. He passed through the Juyan area and inspected the terrain. When the Huns were not seen, he returned. He worshiped the official Cavalry Captain and led 5,000 warriors to teach archery in Jiuquan and Zhangye areas to prevent the Huns from invading. A few years later, the Han Dynasty sent the general of the Second Division to attack Dawan, and sent Li Ling to lead five schools of troops to follow. When marching to the frontier fortress, he met the general of the Second Division returning. The emperor gave Li Ling a letter, and Li Ling left his officers and soldiers behind. He left Dunhuang with 500 light cavalry and went to Yanyan to welcome the return of the general of the second division, and then stationed at Zhangye. In the second year of Tianhan, the general of the Second Division led 30,000 cavalry to Jiuquan to attack King Youxian of the Xiongnu in the Tianshan Mountains.
target: After Wei Qing's interrogation, Li Guang, feeling humiliated and over sixty, committed suicide. His death caused widespread mourning. His son Li Gan later wounded Wei Qing in revenge and was killed by Huo Qubing, who claimed it was a deer attack. Li Guang's grandson Li Ling led a campaign against the Xiongnu with 5,000 infantry, fighting bravely but ultimately surrendering after running out of arrows and reinforcements. The emperor, misled by reports that Li Ling was training the Xiongnu, executed his family. Li Ling remained with the Xiongnu, marrying a Chanyu's daughter and dying there years later.

source: Su Wu, also known as Ziqing, was appointed as a Lang along with his brothers when he was young because his father Su Jian had made great contributions to the country. Su Wu was later gradually promoted to the supervisor of the Zhongzhong Stable. At that time, the Han Dynasty continued to attack the Xiongnu. Both sides sent envoys to secretly observe the situation of the other side. The Xiongnu successively detained more than ten batches of Han envoys, including Guo Ji and Lu Chongguo. When the Xiongnu envoys arrived, the Han Dynasty also detained them to compensate. In the first year of the Han Dynasty, Shanyu, the marquis of Tartar, had just ascended the throne and was afraid of the Han Dynasty's attack, so he said: The emperor of the Han Dynasty is my elder. Return all the detained Han Dynasty envoys such as Lu Chongguo and others. Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty praised him for his righteousness, so he sent Su Wu as a Zhonglang general to escort the Huns envoys who were detained in the Han Dynasty with the Han Dynasty talisman, and presented Shanyu with many properties to repay his kindness. Su Wu, his deputy envoy Han Zhonglang, Zhang Sheng, and Chang Hui, who temporarily served as the envoy's subordinates, recruited more than 100 soldiers and scouts to go to the Xiongnu.
target: Su Wu was sent as an envoy to the Xiongnu in 100 BCE. When a conspiracy involving his deputy Zhang Sheng was exposed, Su Wu attempted suicide to avoid disgrace.

source: You know that I will not surrender. If you want the two countries to attack each other, the Xiongnu's defeat will begin with killing me. Wei Lu knew that he could not threaten Su Wu to surrender in the end, so he reported the situation to Shan Yu. The Chanyu wanted Su Wu to surrender more and more, so he imprisoned him in Dajiaoxiang and cut off food and drink from him. It snowed heavily, so Su Wu lay down on the ground and ate snow balls and felt wool, so that many of them did not starve to death. The Xiongnu thought he was a man of God, so they moved him to an uninhabited place in the North Sea and let him herd rams. He was not allowed to come back until the rams gave birth to babies. They separated him from his subordinates Chang Hui and others and placed him in different places. After Su Wu was exiled to Beihai, the Huns did not provide him with food, so he had to dig grass seeds stored by wild rats to satisfy his hunger.
target: He survived and was imprisoned, surviving on snow and felt. Exiled to the North Sea to herd rams, he steadfastly refused to surrender, even when his former friend Li Ling tried to persuade him.

source: Wei Lu and I’s sins are higher than the sky! Then tears fell like rain, soaking his clothes, and he said goodbye to Su Wu and left. Li Ling was too shy to give Su Wu his belongings in person, so he sent his wife to send some cattle and sheep to Su Wu. Later, Li Ling went to Beihai and told Su Wu: The Xiongnu frontier post captured Han Chinese in Yunzhong alive, saying that everyone from the prefect to the common people were wearing white mourning clothes, and that the emperor was dead. When Su Wu heard the news, he faced the south and cried so hard that he vomited blood. He cried in mourning for Emperor Wu every morning and night. A few months later, Emperor Zhao ascended the throne. After a few years, the Xiongnu and the Han Dynasty reconciled. The Han Dynasty sought Su Wu and others, but the Huns falsely claimed that Su Wu was dead. Later, the Mo envoy came to the Xiongnu again. Chang Hui asked his guard to go with him to see the Mo envoy at night. He described what happened in detail. He also told the Han envoy to tell Shanyu that the Han emperor was hunting in Shanglin Garden and shot down a wild goose. There was a silk letter tied to his foot, saying that Su Wu was in a certain big swamp.
target: After nineteen years, the Han Dynasty learned he was alive through a clever ruse involving a wild goose with a message.

source: Chang Hui later rose to the rank of General You, and was granted the title of Marquis. There is a biography of him in the "Book of Han". Su Wu was detained by the Xiongnu for nineteen years. He was in the prime of life when he went on the mission, but when he returned, his beard and hair were all white. In the second year after Su Wu returned, Shangguan Jie's son Shangguan An conspired with Sang Hongyang, King Yan and Lord Gai to rebel. Su Wu's son Su Yuan conspired with Shangguan An and was killed for the crime.
target: Su Wu returned to Chang'an, honored for his loyalty, though his son was later executed for conspiracy.

source: All the rewards and gifts Su Wu received were given to his brothers and old friends, and no property was accumulated at home. The queen's father, Ping'enhou Xu Bo, Emperor Xuan's uncle, Changhou Wang Wuyou and Leluhou Wangwu, the chariot general Han Zeng, the prime minister Wei Xiang, and the imperial censor Bingji all respected Su Wu. Su Wu was old, and his son Su Yuan committed a crime and was killed. Emperor Xuan felt pity for him and asked his ministers: "Su Wu has been in the Huns for so long. Didn't he have any children?" Su Wu stated to Emperor Xuan through Marquis Ping'en: When I returned from the Huns, my Huns wife happened to give birth to a son named Su Tongguo. There happened to be news that I could redeem him with property through the messenger. Emperor Xuan agreed. Later, Su Tongguo came back with the envoy, and Emperor Xuan appointed him as Lang. He also appointed Su Wu's nephew as Youcao. Su Wu was in his eighties and died of illness in the second year of Emperor Xuan's reign.
target: He died in his eighties, and his portrait was later placed in the Qilin Pavilion among eleven notable ministers of Emperor Xuan's reign.

source: Although this is a small matter, it can also be said to be a big deal. However, the generals of the third generation of the Li family were taboo to Taoists. From Li Guang to Li Ling, the clan members were exterminated. How sad! Confucius said that a man with lofty ideals and benevolence should sacrifice his life to achieve benevolence, and do not seek to survive in order to harm benevolence. He can serve in all directions and do not disgrace the king's orders. These moral standards of life are all reflected in Su Wu.
target: The text praises Li Guang's integrity and Su Wu's unwavering loyalty, noting the tragic fate of the Li family and the exemplary virtue of Su Wu.

source: Du Zhou was born in Du Yan County, Nanyang County. When Yi Zong was the governor of Nanyang County, he regarded him as his right-hand assistant, and later recommended him to Zhang Tang as the official history of the court. He was sent to investigate the losses in border counties, and many people were convicted and executed. The affairs of the memorial were in line with the emperor's wishes, and he was trusted. He succeeded each other with the reduction of propaganda, and served as Zhongcheng for more than ten years. Du Zhou is taciturn and slow-tempered, but has a kind heart. Jiaxuan served as Zuo Neishi, and Du Zhou served as Tingwei. Most of his governance followed Zhang Tang's example and he was good at observing the emperor's intentions. If the emperor wants to exclude him, he will be framed; if the emperor wants to forgive him, he will be imprisoned for a long time, and he will secretly visit him to reveal his grievances. Someone among the disciples reproached Du Zhou and said: You judge cases for the emperor, do not follow the established laws, and handle cases exclusively according to the monarch's will. Is this what judicial officials should be like? Du Zhou said: How did the law come into being? In the past, whatever the monarch thought was correct was enacted into law, and later monarchs thought it was correct and wrote it down as decree. If it suits the situation at that time, it is correct. Why use the laws of the past? When Du Zhou served as a court lieutenant, the emperor assigned more cases. Two thousand officials were imprisoned, old and new, and no less than a hundred people were imprisoned. Cases from the county governor, prime minister and censor's office were all sent to the court, reaching more than a thousand cases a year. A big case involves hundreds of arrest witnesses, and a small case involves dozens; these people are thousands of miles away and hundreds of miles away. During the trial, the judge ordered these people to plead guilty according to the indictment. If they refused to plead guilty, they would be tortured to extract confessions and be convicted. At that time, when people heard the news that someone was going to be arrested, they ran away or hid. The case dragged on for a long time and went through several amnesties. It lasted for more than ten years and was still being prosecuted. Most of them were framed on charges of "injustice" or more. The prisons of various government offices in Tingwei and the capital housed 60,000 to 70,000 criminals, and the number of criminals added by ordinary officials was as high as 100,000. Du Zhou was deposed midway, and later served as Jinwu, hunting down thieves, arresting and interrogating the sons of Sang Hongyang and Queen Wei's brothers. He was harsh and vicious. The emperor believed that he did his best and had no selfish motives, so he was promoted to the imperial censor. Du Zhou initially served as a court official and had a horse. After he had been an official for a long time, he was promoted to the position of three princes. One of his two sons was the governor of Hanoi and the other was the governor of Henan. His family wealth accumulated to hundreds of millions. Everyone handles cases very violently, but only Shaozi Yannian is kind-hearted. Du Yannian, named Yougong, was also well versed in law.
target: Du Zhou, a native of Du Yan County in Nanyang, rose from being an assistant to Governor Yi Zong to an official historian under Zhang Tang. He gained the emperor's trust by convicting and executing many during investigations of border counties, serving as Zhongcheng for over a decade. Taciturn and slow-tempered but kind-hearted, Du Zhou succeeded Xuan as Tingwei, modeling his governance after Zhang Tang and adeptly reading the emperor's intentions. He would frame those the emperor wished to exclude and prolong imprisonment for those the emperor wished to forgive, secretly revealing their grievances. When criticized for not following established laws, Du Zhou argued that laws were created by monarchs and should adapt to current circumstances. As Tingwei, he handled over a thousand cases annually, with large cases involving hundreds of witnesses. Many fled or hid upon hearing of impending arrests, and cases could drag on for over a decade through multiple amnesties. Prisons held 60,000 to 70,000 criminals, with ordinary officials adding up to 100,000. Du Zhou was later deposed but returned as Jinwu, harshly pursuing thieves and interrogating Sang Hongyang's sons and Queen Wei's brothers. Promoted to imperial censor, his family wealth accumulated to hundreds of millions. His two sons served as governors, but only his youngest, Du Yannian, was kind-hearted.

source: At that time, when people heard the news that someone was going to be arrested, they ran away or hid. The case dragged on for a long time and went through several amnesties. It lasted for more than ten years and was still being prosecuted. Most of them were framed on charges of "injustice" or more. The prisons of various government offices in Tingwei and the capital housed 60,000 to 70,000 criminals, and the number of criminals added by ordinary officials was as high as 100,000. Du Zhou was deposed midway, and later served as Jinwu, hunting down thieves, arresting and interrogating the sons of Sang Hongyang and Queen Wei's brothers. He was harsh and vicious. The emperor believed that he did his best and had no selfish motives, so he was promoted to the imperial censor. Du Zhou initially served as a court official and had a horse. After he had been an official for a long time, he was promoted to the position of three princes. One of his two sons was the governor of Hanoi and the other was the governor of Henan. His family wealth accumulated to hundreds of millions. Everyone handles cases very violently, but only Shaozi Yannian is kind-hearted. Du Yannian, named Yougong, was also well versed in law. Emperor Zhao ascended the throne, and General Huo Guang took power. Because Du Yannian was the son of the Three Lords, he had the talent to serve as an official to supplement the army. In the fourth year of the First Yuan Dynasty, barbarians invaded Yizhou. As a school captain, Yannian led the Nanyang soldiers to attack the Yizhou rebellion, returned to the army, and served as an admonishment official. The left general Shangguan Jie and his son plotted rebellion with the Lord of Gai and the King of Yan. Yancang, the acting rice envoy, knew about the plot and reported it to Yang Chang, the chief agricultural officer. Yang Chang was frightened and moved away because of illness, and reported to Yannian. Yannian reported to the emperor, and Shangguan Jie and others were executed. Yannian was granted the title of Marquis of Jianping. Du Yannian was originally a subordinate of the general Huo Guang. He was the first to report the traitor. He had a reputation for loyalty and integrity, so he was promoted to the position of Imperial Servant Youcao to Shizhong. Huo Guang held strict punishments and extended his life with lenient punishments. When handling the case of King Yan, Sang Qian, the son of Sang Hongyang, the imperial censor, stayed at the home of his father's old subordinate Hou Shiwu when he escaped. After Sang Qian was arrested, he was executed. At the time of the amnesty, Hou Shiwu was released from prison. When Prince Tingwei and Shaofu Xu Ren tried the rebellion case, they both believed that Sang Qian was implicated in his father's rebellion, but Hou Shiwu only stayed with Sang Qian, not to hide the rebels, but to hide his followers, so Hou Shiwu was pardoned.
target: Du Yannian, well-versed in law, served under Emperor Zhao with General Huo Guang in power. He led Nanyang soldiers to suppress a rebellion in Yizhou and later reported the rebellion of Shangguan Jie and others, earning the title of Marquis of Jianping. As a subordinate of Huo Guang, Yannian advocated lenient punishments. When Hou Shiwu was implicated for harboring Sang Qian, Yannian argued against harsh penalties, balancing the court's harmony. He advised Huo Guang to promote frugality and tolerance, leading to the abolition of monopolies on wine, salt, and iron. During Emperor Zhao's illness, Yannian managed prescriptions.

source: In the last years of Emperor Zhao's life, he was ill and recruited famous doctors from all over the world. Du Yannian was in charge of prescriptions. When the emperor died, King Changyi ascended the throne and was deposed. The general Huo Guang and the chariot general Zhang Anshi discussed the establishment of the emperor with the ministers. At that time, Emperor Xuan was raised in Yeting, and he was named the emperor's great-grandson. He was friendly with Yannian's middle son Du Tuo. Yannian knew his great-grandson's virtue and persuaded Huo Guang and Anshi to establish him as emperor. When Emperor Xuan ascended the throne, he praised the ministers, extended his life, and made plans to install the ancestral temple. He added 2,300 households, making a total of 4,300 households with the initial enfeoffment of food. According to the imperial edict, the meritorious merits of the general Huo Guang surpassed the Taiwei Jianghou Zhou Bo, the chariot general An Shi and the prime minister Yang Chang surpassed the prime minister Chen Ping, the former general Han Zeng and the imperial censor Cai Ying surpassed Ying Yinhou Guanying in merit, the servant Du Yannian surpassed Zhu Xuhou Liu Zhang in merit, the later general Tachong Guo, the chief minister farmland Yannian, and the Shaofu Shi Le successfully surpassed Dianke Liu Jie, all of them were granted the title of marquis Yitu. Yannian is a peaceful person, good at handling various government affairs, and has been in charge of government affairs for a long time. The emperor trusts him, and he will accompany him when he leaves home. After Huo Guang's death, his son Huo Yu rebelled against the clan and was executed. The emperor regarded Du Yannian as an old member of the Huo family and wanted to avoid retirement. However, Prime Minister Wei Xiangzhuo Yannian had always been honorable and trustworthy, and many of the officials he appointed were illegal. Officials were sent to open a case for investigation, but it was found that many horses died, and the official servants lacked food and clothing. Yannian was implicated in breaking the law and dismissed from office, and two thousand households were cut off. A few months later, he was appointed as the governor of the north. Yannian was appointed as a border official by the former Jiuqing, but his performance in governing the county was not obvious. The emperor used a seal to reprimand Yannian. In Yannian, good officials were selected, the powerful were captured, and the county was peaceful. More than a year later, the emperor sent an audience to give Yannian a seal, twenty pounds of gold, and moved him to be the governor of Xihe. He was famous for his achievements in governance. During the Wufeng period, he was transferred to the imperial court as a censor. He lived in his father's official residence and did not dare to use his father's seat. He moved to another place to sit and lie down. At this time, the four barbarians were harmonious and the country was at peace. He served for three years and resigned due to old age and illness. The emperor treated him favorably and sent Dr. Guanglu to give him a hundred catties of gold and wine, as well as medicine. Du Yannian was seriously ill, and the emperor gave him a chariot and horses, and he was dismissed from office. Died a few months later. Mi was given the title Jinghou, and his son Du Xu succeeded him as Marquis. Du Xu served as a Langguan when he was young. In this year, he followed General Pulei to attack the Xiongnu as a school captain. He also served as an admonishing official in the court, and was transferred to the captain of Shanggu and the prefect of Yanmen.
target: After the emperor's death, he helped establish Emperor Xuan, gaining additional fiefs. Despite being an old member of the Huo family, Yannian was dismissed after Huo Guang's death due to legal violations but later reinstated as governor of Xihe, where he achieved peace. He served as censor during the Wufeng period but resigned due to old age and illness, dying a few months later. His son Du Xu succeeded him as marquis. Du Xu served as a Langguan, followed General Pulei against the Xiongnu, and later became Taichang.

source: When his father passed away in Yannian, he was in charge of funerals. Afterwards, he became Taichang and managed the counties where the tombs were located. Whenever the verdict was finalized in the winter months, he often went to drink and save food. All the subordinate officials praised him for his kindness. When Emperor Yuan first came to the throne, the price of grain was high and the people were scattered. During the Yongguang period, the Western Qiang rebelled, so Du Su sent a letter to donate money to the valley to support the army, worth millions. Du Xu had six younger brothers, five of whom reached senior officials. The younger brother Du Xiong successively held the official position of two thousand stones in five counties and was the governor of three states. He was famous for his ability. Only the middle brother Du Qin is the most famous without being an official. Du Qin, whose courtesy name was Wang Xia, was a young man who loved scriptures. His family was rich but he was blind, so he was not good at being an official.
target: He was known for his kindness, often drinking and saving food during winter verdicts. During Emperor Yuan's reign, he donated money and grain to support the army. Du Xu had six younger brothers, five of whom became senior officials. His brother Du Qin, though blind, was renowned for his knowledge and strategy. Du Qin advised General Wang Feng on establishing a system of nine concubines to ensure heirs and longevity, warning against lust and its consequences.

source: Wang Feng was unable to legislate his own laws and was just following the old system. It happened that Sima Junli, the sister of the Empress Dowager, had an affair with Du Qin's brother and son. When the matter was reported to the police, Du Qin was so frightened that he begged to leave his job. Later, there were solar eclipses and earthquakes, and orders were given to recommend virtuous and upright people who could speak out and give advice. Liangfang, the Marquis of Heyang, recommended Du Qin. Du Qin said to him: Your Majesty is afraid of destiny and disaster. He introduces officials and recommends outspoken people. He will seek God's will and observe the disappearance. The minister Du Qin is stupid and has shallow Confucian skills, and is not able to answer the emperor's questions. I heard that solar eclipses and earthquakes are signs that Yang is weak and Yin is strong.
target: He also addressed solar eclipses and earthquakes as signs of weak yang and strong yin, urging the emperor to restrain female favors and promote frugality.

source: The minister Du Qin is stupid and his words are not accepted. In the summer, the emperor summoned all the outspoken people to the White Tiger Palace to countermeasures. The emperor asked: What is the most precious way of heaven and earth? What is the king's method? What is the highest meaning in the Six Classics? What comes first in human behavior? What is the art of employing people? What is the urgent need to govern the country today? Each uses classic answers. Du Qin replied: "I have heard that belief in the way of heaven is precious, and righteousness is the most precious thing in the earth's way. If you don't believe in the righteousness, all things will not come into being."
target: His countermeasures at the White Tiger Palace emphasized filial piety, righteousness, and the importance of knowing and employing people.

source: The matter is in "The Biography of Empress Yuan". Wang Zhang was dead, and the people thought he had been wronged and ridiculed the court. Du Qin wanted to make amends for his mistake and advised Wang Feng: The matter of Wang Zhang breaking the law in Jingzhao was very confidential. Seeing that Wang Zhang always spoke for the people, the officials thought that he would not break the law and be dismissed from office. They suspected that the solar eclipse was related to Wang Feng and reported it to the emperor. If Wang Zhang has other inside information and commits a crime, he will be punished. If the matter is not revealed, no one will know about it in the capital, let alone in remote places. I am afraid that the world does not know that Wang Zhang is really guilty, but thinks that he committed a crime because of his words in the letter. In this way, the real reasons for the disputes and remonstrances are covered up, and the magnanimous and wise virtues of Ya are undermined. Du Qin thought that he should make a blunt remonstrance on Wang Zhang's matter, and summoned his subordinates to clarify his intentions, plus the incident of the solar eclipse reported before, so as to show his true intention to all parties and let everyone in the world know that the Lord is a sage and does not condemn people based on his words. In this way, rumors will be dispelled and doubts will be resolved. Wang Feng stated Du Qin's strategy to the emperor. That's what Du Qin did to help the United States. Du Qin Youyou did not become an official and died of his old age.
target: Du Qin later warned Wang Feng against excessive power, citing historical examples. After Wang Zhang's death, Du Qin advised Wang Feng to clarify the matter to dispel rumors. Du Qin never became an official and died of old age.

source: Xue Xuan, the Marquis of Gaoyang, was known as an unnurturing mother, and Zhang Yu, the Marquis of Anchang, was the leader of the traitors. They confuse the court and make the late emperor bear the name of domestic slander. We must not be careless. When Your Majesty first came to the throne, he had no time to be humble. He was alone and independent, with no support to rely on. The changes in power officials were like testing boiling water with his hands. We should show kindness with great righteousness as early as possible to comfort the hearts of the people. The minister privately saw that Zhu Bo was loyal, brave, and talented, which was rarely seen in modern times. He was actually a great and treasured minister of the country. He was called upon to serve Zhu Bo and placed him on his left and right to control the world. With this person in court, Your Majesty can sit back and relax. In the past, when Zhu Lu wanted to harm the Liu family, it was only because Zhou Bo and Chen Ping were still there, otherwise they would have been ridiculed by the treacherous ministers. Du Ye also said that a temple should be built in the capital for Prince Gong to show his filial piety. At that time, Dong Hong, the Marquis of Gaochang, also said that the emperor's mother should be respected and Queen Tao Ding should be honored as the emperor's empress dowager. Grand Sikong Shidan and others impeached Dong Hong for his wrongdoing in the government, so he was convicted and exempted from being a commoner. Du Ye wrote a letter to defend Dong Hong. What Du Ye said before and after was in line with his purpose and was carried out, and Zhu Bo was indeed promoted and reused. Du Ye was thus recruited and appointed as Taichang. After more than a year, he was demoted to captain of Shangdang. When the official reported that Du Ye's appointment as Taichang was false, Du Ye committed a crime and was dismissed from office, and returned to the feudal state. When Emperor Ai died and Wang Mang came to power, all those who had proposed temple titles were dismissed from office and moved to Hepu. Du Ye had been deposed before, so he treated him leniently, but due to fear, he fell ill and died. In his early years as emperor, Du Ye married the emperor's sister, Princess Yingyi, but the princess died without any children. Du Ye's family wrote a letter requesting that the coffin be returned to the capital to be buried with the princess, but the court did not allow it. Instead, Mi was given the title of Huanghou, and his descendants passed on to his grandson Juefeng. At first, Du Zhou moved to Maoling during the reign of Emperor Wu, and then moved to Duling in Yannian. The praise said: Zhang Tang and Du Zhou both started as Wen Mo Xiaoli, and advanced to San Gong, and were classified as cool officials. However, they all have virtuous sons, whose virtues and talents are better than those of their fathers. They have noble titles, inherit their father's generation, and serve as officials in the court. The two families are equally matched. It was not until the end of Han Dynasty that the title of Du family was discontinued. Looking at their fortune traces, no one can compare with them after the great heroes and scholars.
target: Du Ye, Du Qin's nephew, inherited the marquis title and served as Taichang. He criticized Prime Minister Zhai Fangjin for bias and corruption, and later defended Dong Hong's proposal to honor the emperor's mother. Du Ye was demoted to captain of Shangdang and eventually dismissed from office. When Wang Mang came to power, Du Ye, fearing punishment, fell ill and died. The Du family, starting with Du Zhou and Du Yannian, were known as harsh officials but produced virtuous sons. Their lineage continued until the end of the Han Dynasty, with no one surpassing them after the great heroes and scholars.

source: Yang Wangsun was from the time of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty. Learn the art of Huang Lao, make a fortune, pay attention to health preservation, and try to get everything that is beneficial to health. When he was critically ill and dying, he first ordered his son in his instructions: "When I die, I will be buried naked. Let me return to the way of nature. I must not change my wishes." After death, I put the body in a cloth bag and put it seven feet into the ground. After putting it down, I pulled the cloth bag off my feet so that my body was in direct contact with the soil. His son wanted to silently disobey, but found it difficult to disobey his father's orders; he wanted to obey his father's wishes, but he couldn't bear it, so he went to visit his father's friend Qi Hou. Qi Hou wrote a letter to Yang Wangsun saying: You are suffering from illness. I was eager to follow the emperor to Yong County to offer sacrifices, so I was unable to visit you at the house. I hope you can keep your spirits up, think less about problems, seek medical treatment, and take good care of yourself. I heard that you made an order to be buried naked after death. If the deceased is unconscious, forget it. If the deceased is conscious, you will kill the body underground and go to see the ancestors naked. I don’t think you should do this. Moreover, the "Book of Filial Piety" says that coffins, coffins, and quilts are provided for the deceased. This is also a system passed down by the saints. Why should you insist on your own opinions alone? I hope you will review my comments. Yang Wangsun wrote back and said: I heard that the ancient sage kings followed human feelings and did not suppress their relatives, so they planned funerals for people. Now they go beyond the etiquette regulations and practice rich burials. Therefore, I asked for a naked burial, intending to correct the social trend of rich burials. A grand burial is really not beneficial to the deceased, but secular people compete with each other and spend all their money to buy funeral objects, leaving these things to rot in the ground. Or it may be buried in the ground today and exhumed tomorrow. It is really no different from the corpse wilderness! Moreover, the so-called death is the end of life and the destination of all things. The destination can be reached, the dead can be transformed, and creation means that objects return to their origins. Returning the origin to the underworld, invisible and silent, is in line with reason and emotion. Decorating the appearance to attract attention, burying it in a luxurious manner and isolating the origin, making it impossible to reach the final destination and unable to change the deceased, are causing objects to lose their place. And I heard that the spirit belongs to heaven, and the body belongs to the earth. The spirit leaves the body and returns to its original state, so it is called a ghost. Ghost means returning.
target: Yang Wangsun, a man from Emperor Wu's reign, studied Huang-Lao teachings and focused on health preservation. When terminally ill, he ordered his son to bury him naked, directly in contact with soil, to return to nature. His son consulted their friend Qi Hou, who argued against this, citing filial piety traditions requiring coffins and burial clothes. Yang Wangsun responded that lavish burials were wasteful and harmful, preventing the dead from returning to their natural state. He argued that the spirit returns to heaven and the body to earth; elaborate burials only create mummies that cannot decompose properly. He insisted on naked burial, which was ultimately carried out.

source: Qihou read Yang Wangsun's reply and said: Well said. After Yang Wangsun died, he was finally buried naked. Hu Jian, courtesy name Zimeng, was from Hedong County. During the Tianhan period of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, he was appointed military official for trial. His family was poor and had no money to buy a carriage and horses. He often walked and lived with his officers, so he took the opportunity to comfort the officers, which was very popular. At that time, the censor of the Imperial Army committed a crime and cut through the wall of the Northern Army's fortress to build a small house for selling goods for profit. Hu Jian wanted to kill him, so he invited the officers and said, "I plan to kill someone with you. If I tell you to catch him, you will catch him; if I ask you to kill him, you will kill him." So it was scheduled to be the day to select soldiers and horses for the operation. On that day, the censor and the military guards were sitting in the corridor. Hu Jian and his officers walked quickly to the corridor to pay homage. When Hu Jian got up, he took advantage of the momentum and climbed onto the corridor, and the officers followed closely. Hu Jian pointed at the censor and said: "Catch him." The officer stepped forward and grabbed the censor and dragged him down the hall. Hu Jian said: Kill him! The officer hacked the censor to death. The guards and schools were all shocked and didn't know why. Hu Jian had already carried the written memorial in his arms, so he submitted the memorial and said: I have heard from military law that military force is established to command authority over the masses, and that evildoers are punished to prohibit evil.
target: Hu Jian served as a military official during Emperor Wu's Tianhan period. When a military censor illegally built a shop within the army fortress for profit, Hu Jian gathered his officers, seized and executed the censor on the spot. He submitted a memorial citing military law, arguing the censor's crime warranted death and that military officers could handle such matters without civilian court involvement. The emperor approved his actions, citing the principle that military and civil laws differ.

source: Why should you be suspicious? Hu Jian became famous from then on. Later, Hu Jian became the magistrate of Weicheng County and was famous for his achievements. When Emperor Zhao was young, the queen's father, the hussar general Shangguan An, was very close to Ding Wairen, the lover of Emperor Zhao's sister, Princess Gaichang. Foreigner Ding was arrogant and unruly. He resented his predecessor, Jing Zhao Yin Fanfu, so he sent an assassin to shoot him. The assassin was hiding in the building owner's villa, and the officials did not dare to catch him. Weicheng County Magistrate Hu Jian led officers and soldiers to surround the villa to arrest the assassin. When Gai Zhu heard about it, he and his fellow Ding, Hussar General Shangguan'an, and many slaves and soldiers came over. They ran and shot at the officials, who then fled in all directions. Lord Gai ordered his servants to impeach Weicheng County Magistrate Hu Jian, who sent a parade to injure Lord Gai's servants. Hu Jian wrote a letter pleading that he was not guilty. Lord Gai was very angry and sent a letter to falsely accuse Hu Jian of violating and insulting the eldest princess, and shot an arrow at the gate of Lord Gai's mansion. Hu Jian knew clearly that his subordinate officials had harmed the princess's domestic slave, but he avoided retribution and deliberately did not pursue the investigation. General Huo Guang suppressed their memorial. Later, when Huo Guang fell ill, Shangguan Jie took charge of government affairs and ordered the officials to arrest Hu Jian. Hu Jian was forced to commit suicide. Officials and people all said that he died unjustly, and his ancestral hall is still built in Weicheng. Zhu Yun, whose courtesy name was You, was a native of Lu and later moved to Pingling.
target: Hu Jian later became magistrate of Weicheng County. During Emperor Zhao's reign, he arrested an assassin hiding in a noble's villa, angering Princess Gaichang and General Shangguan An. After General Huo Guang fell ill, Hu Jian was forced to commit suicide, though people considered his death unjust.

source: Zhu Yun, whose courtesy name was You, was a native of Lu and later moved to Pingling. When he was young, he made friends with the agile and powerful knights, and used the knights to take revenge. He is more than eight feet tall, has a majestic appearance, and is famous for his courage. At the age of forty, he changed his moral integrity and studied "The Book of Changes" with Dr. Bai Ziyou, and also studied "The Analects of Confucius" with former general Xiao Wangzhi, and was able to pass on the "Book of Changes" and "The Analects of Confucius". He liked to be suave and free-spirited, and people in the society valued him for this. During the reign of Emperor Yuan of the Han Dynasty, Gong Yu, a native of Langye County, was appointed as the imperial censor. On behalf of Cheng Jia of Huayin County, he submitted a sealed memorial to the emperor, saying: The method of governance is to obtain talents. The censor is the deputy prime minister, ranking above the nine ministers, and must be selected.
target: Zhu Yun, originally a chivalrous man, later studied the Book of Changes and Analects. During Emperor Yuan's reign, he debated Wulu Chongzong on the Liangqiu interpretation of the Book of Changes, defeating him soundly. He became a doctor and later magistrate of several counties.

source: Zhu Yun went to court many times, saying that Prime Minister Wei Xuancheng was secure in his position and could not advance or retreat, while Chen Xian criticized Shi Xian many times. After a long time, the relevant officials tortured Zhu Yun, suspecting that he secretly instigated the officials to kill. When the officials met in court, Emperor Yuan asked Prime Minister Wei Xuancheng about Zhu Yun's achievements in government affairs. Wei Xuancheng said that Zhu Yun was tyrannical and had no good governance. Chen Xian was nearby at the time and heard what Wei Xuancheng said and told Zhu Yun. Weiyun wrote a letter to defend himself, and Chen Xian drafted a draft memorial for him, requesting the emperor's approval to hand over the matter to Yushi Zhongcheng. As a result, the emperor handed the matter over to the prime minister. Prime Minister Wei Xuancheng arranged for his subordinates to torture Zhu Yun and convicted Zhu Yun of murder. Zhu Yun fled to Chang'an and approached Chen Xian to discuss countermeasures. Prime Minister Wei Xuancheng found out all these things and reported to the emperor: Chen Xian, as a minister who stayed in the imperial palace and was in charge of laws and regulations, was fortunate enough to be able to see the emperor. However, he leaked what he heard and told Zhu Yun privately. He also drafted a draft of a memorial for Zhu Yun, hoping that the emperor would let him handle Zhu Yun's case. Later, he knew that Zhu Yun was a criminal who was on the run, but he colluded with him, so the officials could not catch Zhu Yun. The emperor then ordered Chen Xian and Zhu Yun to be imprisoned and sentenced to death as a punishment. Chen Xian and Zhu Yun were deposed and imprisoned until the death of Emperor Yuan. When he became emperor, Zhang Yu, the former Prime Minister and Marquis of Anchang, was given a special position and favored by him because he was the emperor's teacher. Zhu Yun wrote a letter asking for an audience. When the emperor summoned him, all the ministers and ministers were nearby. Zhu Yun said: Nowadays, the ministers of the imperial court cannot help the monarch and cannot bring benefits to the people. They are all people who occupy empty positions and receive white-collar salaries and do not take care of the affairs. They are what Confucius said, "short-sighted people cannot assist the king. They are afraid of losing their favor and fortune, so there is nothing they can't do." I hope that the emperor will give me Shang Fang's horse-killing sword to cut off the head of a sycophant minister as a warning to others. The emperor asked: Who is it? Zhu Yun replied: Zhang Yu, the Marquis of Anchang. Emperor Cheng was very angry and said: A junior minister who slanders his superiors and insults my teacher in the court will be punished by death! The imperial censor dragged Zhu Yun down to the palace. Zhu Yun clung to the railing in front of the palace and refused to move. As a result, the railing broke. Zhu Yun shouted: I can go underground and hang out with Guan Longpang and Bigan, I am already satisfied! I just don’t know what the future of the country will be like? The censor finally took Zhu Yun away. At this time, the left general Xin Qingji took off his hat, took off his seal and ribbon, kowtowed to His Highness and said: This minister has always been famous for his wild and upright character.
target: He criticized powerful officials including Shi Xian and Prime Minister Wei Xuancheng. After being convicted of murder, he fled and sought help from Chen Xian, who was also imprisoned. During Emperor Cheng's reign, Zhu Yun requested the emperor's sword to kill sycophantic minister Zhang Yu. The emperor was furious and ordered his execution, but Zhu Yun clung to a palace railing, breaking it. General Xin Qingji intervened, and Zhu Yun was spared. He retired, taught students, and died at home in his seventies, requesting simple burial.

source: Meifu, whose courtesy name is Zizhen, was born in Shouchun County, Jiujiang County. When he was young, he studied in Chang'an. He was proficient in Shangshu and Guliang Chunqiu. Later, he resigned and returned to Shouchun. He wrote many times through county envoys to discuss extraordinary matters. He also asked to borrow a roller carriage at the post station to go to the emperor's place to record the emperor's inquiries about urgent political matters one by one, and then answered them one by one, but they were always rejected. At this time, Emperor Cheng entrusted the political affairs to the general Wang Feng. Wang Feng was specialized in government affairs. However, Wang Zhang of Jingzhao Yin, who had always been loyal and upright, ridiculed Wang Feng and was killed by Wang Feng. As the Wang family's power gradually grew stronger, disasters occurred many times, and no one among the ministers dared to speak frankly. Mei Fu wrote again: I heard that Jizi pretended to protect himself during the Yin Dynasty, but presented the book "Hong Fan" to King Wu of Zhou Dynasty; Shusun Tong escaped and became invisible during the Qin Dynasty, and later returned to the Han Dynasty and formulated the etiquette system for Liu Bang.
target: Mei Fu studied in Chang'an, mastering the Book of Documents and Guliang's Spring and Autumn Annals.

source: Since the establishment of the Han Dynasty, the country has experienced three crises. The Lu family, the Huo family, and the Shangguan family are all the families of the emperor's mother and queen. When it comes to keeping close friends, safety is the top priority. They should be given a virtuous master to teach them the ways of loyalty and filial piety. Today is to give them respected positions and grant them great authority, making them proud and rebellious to the point of being exterminated by the Yi clan. This is a very important matter of losing their relatives. A wise man like Huo Guang cannot think carefully about his descendants, so the next generation of ordinary powerful officials is in danger. "Shangshu" says: Don't be like a big fire, which starts off as a mediocre fire. Those who have more power than the monarch later find it too late to prevent problems. Emperor Cheng refused to adopt it. Emperor Cheng had no heirs for a long time, so Mei Fu believed that a three-line circulation system should be established and Confucius' line should be designated as the descendants of the Yin and Shang Dynasties. He wrote again: I heard that I am not in my position and do not pursue political affairs. Politics is a job. It is a crime for someone with a low position to talk big words. If he commits a crime beyond his authority and harms the world by making alarmist remarks, even if he is executed and his body and head are separated, I am willing to do so.
target: He repeatedly submitted memorials criticizing the growing power of the Wang family and urging Emperor Cheng to recruit talented advisors. He warned that killing honest officials like Wang Zhang silenced criticism and endangered the state. He advocated establishing Confucius' descendants as heirs to the Shang dynasty's sacrifices.

source: When he became emperor, Mei Fu wrote another letter saying that the descendants of Confucius should be named to inherit Shangtang's sacrifices. In the first year of Suihe, he established the descendants of the two kings as kings of princes. He deduced and traced the traces of ancient written records and verified each other with "Zuo Zhuan", "Gu Liang Zhuan", "Shiben" and "Book of Rites", so he issued an edict to confer the descendants of Confucius as the Duke of Yin Shao. The words are in "Chronicles of Emperor Cheng". At this time, Mei Fu lived at home and often took reading and self-cultivation as his job. During the Yuanshi period, when Wang Mang was in power, Mei Fu abandoned his wife and children one morning and went to Jiujiang. It is now said that he became a god. After that, someone saw him in Kuaiji County. He changed his name and worked as a market servant in Wu County. Yunchang, named Youru, was born in Pingling.
target: His advice was largely ignored. During Wang Mang's reign, Mei Fu abandoned his family and disappeared, later seen working as a market servant in Wu County under a false name.

source: He worshiped Wu Zhang, a native of the same county, as his teacher. Wu Zhang studied "Shang Shu Jing" and became a doctor. Emperor Ping ascended the throne from the King of Zhongshan. He was young, and Wang Mang controlled the affairs of the state, with the white title of Anhan Gong. With Emperor Ping as the heir of the emperor, Emperor Ping could no longer take care of his relatives. His mother, maternal grandparents, and uncle's Wei family all stayed in Zhongshan Kingdom and could not go to the capital Chang'an. Wang Mang's eldest son, Wang Zi, blamed Wang Mang for isolating the Wei family and worried that Emperor Ping would be resentful when he grew up. Wang Yu and Wu Zhang conspired to smear blood on Wang Mang's door late at night, pretending to be a warning from ghosts and gods, in an attempt to frighten Wang Mang. Wu Zhang planned to take the opportunity to point out Wang Mang's fault in countermeasures. After the incident was discovered, Wang Mang killed his son Wang Yu and executed the Wei family. Everyone involved in the conspiracy was imprisoned and more than a hundred people were executed. Wu Zhang was cut in half and his body was quartered at Shushi Gate. At the beginning, Wu Zhang was a famous Confucian in the world. He was particularly famous as a professor of "Shangshu" and had more than a thousand disciples. Wang Mang regarded them as a group of evil people, and they were all condemned and imprisoned, and they were not allowed to be officials. As a result, Wu Zhang's disciples all accepted other people as their teachers and kept secret that they were Wu Zhang's disciples. Yun Chang was serving as Chief Situ at that time. He admitted that he was Wu Zhang's disciple. He collected Wu Zhang's body and returned home. He bought a coffin for burial and everyone in the capital praised him. Wang Shun, the general of chariot and cavalry, admired his ambition and integrity and compared him to Le Bu. He petitioned the emperor to approve Yun Chang's appointment as his subordinate, and later recommended him as Zhonglang's admonition to the doctor. After Wang Mang usurped the throne, Wang Shun was appointed as the Grand Master and recommended Yun Chang to be appointed as the assistant minister. Yun Chang said he was ill and was exempted from official duties. Tang Lin said that Yun Chang could be in charge of the county's political affairs, so Wang Mang promoted him to Dayin of Lu County. At the beginning of the revolution, the imperial court used an automobile to recruit Yunchang to serve as the imperial censor. He resigned due to illness and later died at home.
target: Yun Chang studied under Wu Zhang, a famous scholar of the Book of Documents. When Wu Zhang was executed for conspiring against Wang Mang, his disciples denied their connection. Yun Chang alone admitted being Wu Zhang's student, collected his body, and arranged proper burial. He later served as an official under Wang Mang but resigned due to illness and died at home.

source: At the beginning of the revolution, the imperial court used an automobile to recruit Yunchang to serve as the imperial censor. He resigned due to illness and later died at home. Zanri: In the past, Confucius said that if you can't meet a mediocre person and discuss the Tao with him, you should think about making progress and do nothing. Looking at Yang Wangsun's ambition, it is far better than Qin Shihuang's. The world's praise of Zhu Yunduo is exaggerated, so the Analects of Confucius says: There may be people who do not know the situation and just describe it casually. I, Confucius, do not do this. Hu Jian dared to make decisions when facing the enemy, and his bravery was evident externally. Kill the evildoers so that the army will not be lazy. Mei Fu's words are consistent with the Book of Songs.
target: The commentary praises Yang Wangsun's noble aspirations, Hu Jian's decisive bravery, and Mei Fu's principled words.

source: Mei Fu's words are consistent with the Book of Songs. Meifu finally followed her own preferences and preserved her temperament in Wuxian City. Yun Chang's integrity was revealed from the burial of Wu Zhang. He did benevolent and righteous deeds by himself, first as a great situ, and then as a general of chariots and cavalry. When there was trouble, he became an official, and when there was chaos, he lived in seclusion. His approach was very different from "Chu Ci".
target: Yun Chang's integrity was revealed through burying his teacher, and he wisely withdrew from service during troubled times.

source: So he worshiped Bi Qiang as Doctor Guanglu and Guardsman of Kenle. He was already eighty years old at that time. He was promoted to Zongzheng and died within a few months. Liu De, named Lu Shu, practiced Huang Lao's skills and had strategies. When he was young, he discussed political affairs many times and was summoned to Ganquan Palace. Emperor Wu called him Qianliju. In the early years of Emperor Zhao's reign, he became Zong Zhengcheng and participated in the execution of Liu Ze's imperial edict. Because his father was Ren Zongzheng, he was changed to Dahonglucheng, and then to Taizhong doctor, and later Zongzheng, and participated in the torture of Shangguan family and Gaizhu. Liu Dechang held the idea of ​​​​"Laozi" that he would always be content with his content. After his wife died, General Huo Guang wanted to marry his daughter to him, but Liu De did not dare to marry him for fear of being too prosperous. Tan, the grandson of Princess Gai, stopped Liu De to complain about the incident. Liu De repeatedly blamed the princess for her inappropriate behavior. The censor thought that Huo Guang resented Liu De for not accepting his daughter, and guessed that he wanted to impeach Liu De for slandering him and send him to prison, so that he could avoid being a commoner and live in seclusion in the mountains and fields. Huo Guang was very angry when he heard about it, and reported to the emperor to summon Liu De to guard the Qingzhou governor. More than a year later, he became Zongzheng again and participated in the establishment of Emperor Xuan. For supporting the establishment of the emperor, he was given the title of Marquis of Guannei. During the Dijie Festival, he was granted the title of Marquis of Yangcheng due to his close behavior.
target: He was eighty years old then. He was promoted to Zongzheng and died within months. Liu De, named Lu Shu, practiced Huang Lao's skills and had strategies. He discussed political affairs and was summoned to Ganquan Palace. In Emperor Zhao's early years, he became Zong Zhengcheng and participated in executing Liu Ze's imperial edict. He became Dahonglucheng, then Taizhong doctor, and later Zongzheng, participating in torturing the Shangguan family and Gaizhu. Liu De held the *Laozi* idea of contentment. After his wife died, Huo Guang wanted to marry his daughter to him, but Liu De refused, fearing prosperity. He repeatedly blamed Princess Gai for inappropriate behavior. The censor thought Huo Guang resented Liu De and wanted to impeach him. Liu De avoided being a commoner and lived in seclusion. Huo Guang was angry and summoned Liu De to guard Qingzhou. Over a year later, he became Zongzheng again and participated in establishing Emperor Xuan. He was given the title of Marquis of Guannei and later Marquis of Yangcheng.

source: What’s more, there is also the kinship between flesh and blood, plus the unrequited old kindness! I wanted to be as honest as possible, but I was afraid of going beyond my duty. However, thinking of the two unpaid kindnesses and the loyalty of my ministers, my foolishness aroused me and I retreated to the farmland. I died without any regrets. I heard that Shun appointed nine officials, and all the officials gave way to each other, and there was great harmony. If all the sages are in harmony in the court, then all things will be in harmony in the wilderness. Therefore, when the flute plays "Shao" nine times, the phoenix flies; when the bell rings and the chime is struck, all the beasts come and dance. There is no disharmony within the four seas. When Zhou Wen arrived, the foundation was opened in the western suburbs, and all the sages gathered. There was no one who did not respect harmony, advocated the custom of giving in, and eliminated disputes and lawsuits. When King Wen passed away, Duke Zhou missed him and praised King Wen's virtues. The "Poetry" said: The beautiful Qing Temple is solemn and harmonious, and famous officials and officials come to participate in the sacrifice; many scholars carry out King Wen's virtues. At this time, King Wu and Duke Zhou inherited the political affairs, the courtiers were in harmony at home, and all the countries were happy abroad, so they were able to win their favor and serve their ancestors. "Poetry" says: The guests come in harmony, and when they arrive, they pay homage and offer sacrifices. The princes are connected continuously, and the emperor is dignified and magnificent. It is said that peace comes from all directions. The princes are in harmony below, and heaven will retaliate above. Therefore, "Ode to the Zhou Dynasty" says, "Blessings will be many," and it also says, "Give me Lili." Lizi, the wheat, first fell from the sky. This is all achieved through the use of harmony and the blessing of God. Later, during the period of You and Li, the court was at odds with each other, and the poet said sadly and worriedly: People do not do good deeds, keep to themselves, and resent each other. When villains are in power, they obey evil opinions, and competing with each other is a traitor, and betrays the noble man. Therefore, the "Poetry" says: Competing with friends is a traitor, and slandering each other, how sad! If you plan something good, go against it; if you plan something bad, follow it! A gentleman sticks to justice alone and does not give in to public criticism. He works hard to do kingly things but is hated and framed. Therefore, the "Poetry" says: He acts diligently and dares not to tell himself about his hard work. He has no sin, but is framed by everyone! At this time, the moon is eclipsed and has no light. "Poetry" says: On the first day of the lunar month and at the end of the lunar month, there is an eclipse, how ugly it is! He also said: The moon is dim, the sun is dim, how sad are these people now? The changes in the sky appear above, the changes in the earth move below, the springs boil, and the valleys shift.

The *Poetry* said the beautiful Qing Temple is solemn and harmonious. At this time, King Wu and Duke周公 inherited the political affairs, and the courtiers were in harmony. source: The changes in the sky appear above, the changes in the earth move below, the springs boil, and the valleys shift. "Poetry" says: Hundreds of rivers are boiling, mountain tops are cracking, high banks have become low valleys, and deep valleys have become mountains. How can those who mourn now not be punished! The frost falls out of control and does not follow the season. "Poetry" says: There is a lot of frost in the first month, and my heart is sad; people's lies are too powerful! There are many people who say that they mistake right for wrong. These are all caused by disharmony, the transformation of virtuous and unfaithful people. From then on, the world was in chaos, usurpation and murder occurred. King Li fled to pig, and King You was killed. In the last years of King Ping, when Lu Ying just ascended the throne, Dr. Zhou broke away from his brother-in-law and ran away to Lu. However, the "Spring and Autumn" evaded taboos for him and did not say that he came to run. This was the beginning of sad disasters. From then on, the Yin family's ministers had exclusive power and unbridled power for generations. The princes betrayed the Zhou Dynasty and refused to worship, and the Zhou family was humble.

During the previous rebellion of Yingbu, Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty was very ill and did not want to see anyone. He lived in the inner palace and ordered the guards not to let the ministers in. No one, including ministers Jianghou and Guan Ying, dared to enter. After more than ten days, Fan Kuai opened the palace door and rushed in. The ministers followed him. The emperor was lying alone with a eunuch on his pillow. Fan Kuai and others saw the emperor weeping and said: Your Majesty led us to raise troops in Fengyi, Pei County to pacify the world. How majestic it was! Now that the world is at peace, how tired it is! Besides, Your Majesty is seriously ill and the ministers are shocked and frightened. Your Majesty will not summon us to discuss state affairs, but will you just say goodbye to a eunuch alone? Besides, didn’t Your Majesty see what happened to Zhao Gao? Gaozu stood up with a smile. Later, Lu Wan rebelled, and Mo Gaozu sent Fan Kuai to attack Yan as prime minister. At this time, Emperor Gaozu was very ill. Some people slandered Fan Kuai for colluding with the Lu family, saying that once the emperor died, Fan Kuai would use his troops to kill all Madam Qi, King Zhao Ruyi and others. Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty was very angry when he heard these words, so he sent Chen Ping to take Zhou Bo to lead the army instead of Fan Kuai, and beheaded Fan Kuai on the spot. Chen Ping was afraid of Empress Lu, so he arrested Fan Kuai and came to Chang'an. When they arrived in Chang'an, Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty had already passed away. Empress Lu released Fan Kuai and restored his title and estate to him. In the sixth year of Xiaohui, Fan Kuai died, and Mi was named Marquis of Wu. His son Fan Kuai succeeded him as Marquis. Fan's mother, Lu Xu, was also granted the title of Marquis of Linguang. During Queen Lu's period, she had monopolized power and the ministers were all afraid of her. After Empress Lu died, the ministers killed Lu Xu and others, and also killed Fan and his wife. The title of Wuyang Marquis was suspended for several months. After Emperor Xiaowen ascended the throne, he granted Fan Kuai's concubine Fan Shi the title of Marquis of Wuyang and restored his original title and fiefdom. After the death of Fan Shi, Mi was named Huanghou. His son Fan Tuoguang inherited the title. Six years later, the family members of Hou Wuyang wrote a letter saying: Huanghou Fan was sick and infertile, so his wife had an affair with his younger brother and gave birth to Fan Tuoguang. Fan Tuoguang was not actually the son of Huanghou. The emperor ordered that he be handed over to the officials and dismissed from the title. In the second year of the Yuan Dynasty, Emperor Ping inherited the severed title and granted Fan Zhang, the son of Fan Kuai's great-great-grandson, the title of Marquis of Wuyang, with a land of 1,000 households.

He followed Gaozu to attack Huling, surrendering Ping, the Sishui Supervisor, and receiving the ninth rank. He attacked Qin at Yangdong, captured Jiyang and Hufu, defeated Li You at Yongqiu, and received titles and silk. He attacked Zhang Han at Shu'a and Puyang, using chariots to defeat the Qin army, becoming Zhigui. He attacked Trip Ben at Kaifeng and Yang Xiong at Quyu, capturing 68 and surrendering 850, receiving a cabinet of official seals. He pursued Qin at Luoyang, becoming magistrate of Teng County. He fought at Lantian and Zhiyang to Bashang. Peigong became King of Han, granting him the title of Marquis of Zhaoping and making him a royal servant. He followed the king to Shuhan and pacified the Three Qin Dynasties. At Pengcheng, Xiang Yu defeated the Han army. Xiahou Ying rescued Emperor Xiaohui and Princess Lu Yuan, carrying them despite Gaozu's attempts to abandon them. He sent them to Fengdi. At Rongyang, he received Yiyang as a food city. He attacked Xiang Ji at Xiayi, pursuing to Chen, defeating Chu. At Lucheng, he added Zishi County. After the emperor's ascension, he attacked Zang Tu and captured Han Xin.

source: Seeing that the battle situation was not going well, the King of Han quickly retreated and met Emperor Xiaohui and Princess Lu Yuan. Xia Houying asked them to get in the chariot and go together. The King of Han was impatient, his horse was tired, and his enemies were chasing behind him, so he kicked the two children out of the car several times and abandoned them. Xia Houying always carried them and hugged them tightly. The King of Han was furious and tried to kill Xia Houying more than ten times, but finally escaped and sent Emperor Xiaohui and Princess Lu Yuan to Fengdi. After the King of Han arrived in Rongyang, he gathered the scattered soldiers, revitalized the army, and gave Yiyang to Xiahou Ying as a food city. Attacked Xiang Ji in Xiayi, pursued them all the way to Chen, and finally defeated Chu. When he arrived in Lucheng, he added Zishi County as a food town. After the King of Han proclaimed himself emperor, King Yan Zang Tu rebelled, and Xia Houying followed Emperor Gao to attack Zang Tu. The next year, he followed to Chen County and captured Han Xin, King of Chu. He was granted the title of Marquis of Ruyin, and the talisman was dissected as evidence and passed down from generation to generation. Following Emperor Gao, he attacked the state of Dai, went to Wuquan and Yunzhong, and added a thousand households to the settlements. He followed Emperor Gaozu to attack Han Xin's army Hu Qi near Jinyang and defeated the enemy. They pursued northward to Pingcheng, where they were surrounded by the Huns and could not communicate with them for seven days.
target: He was made Marquis of Ruyin with a talisman. He attacked Dai, going to Wuquan and Yunzhong, adding 1,000 households. He attacked Han Xin at Jinyang, defeating the enemy. Surrounded at Pingcheng for seven days, he advised slow retreat, escaping.

Therefore, the descendants of Teng Gong also changed their surname to Sun. Guan Ying was born as a businessman selling silk products in Suiyang County.

I am afraid that the Han army does not trust us. We would like to be assisted by people who are good at cavalry fighting around the King of Han. Although Guan Ying was young, he had experienced many battles, so he worshiped Guan Ying as the middle doctor, ordered Li Bi and Luo Jia to be the left and right captains, and led the Langzhong cavalry to attack the Chu cavalry with Cambodia in Rongyang, defeating the enemy.

source: When Ying Bu rebelled against the Han, Guan Ying went out with his chariot and cavalry generals first. He attacked Ying Bu's partial generals at Xiangdi, defeated the enemy, and beheaded the three deputy generals, Lou Fan and others. Then he marched and destroyed the army of Shangzhu State and Da Sima of Yingbu. He also defeated Ying Bu's general Fei Zhu. Guan Ying captured Zuo Sima alone. His soldiers killed ten young generals and pursued them to the upper reaches of the Huaihe River. The emperor increased his food estate by 2,500 households. After Yingbu was wiped out, the emperor returned to the court and decided to let Guan Ying use the five thousand households in Yingyin as a food town and take back the previously sealed food town. In total, he captured two generals with a salary of two thousand stone, led his troops to destroy the enemy sixteen times, occupied forty-six cities, pacified one traitor, two counties, and fifty-two counties. He captured two generals, one Zhuguo and Xiang each, and ten people with a salary of two thousand stone. Zhuo Ying defeated Ying Bu and returned to the army. Emperor Gao died and became a prince to assist Emperor Hui and Empress Lu. After Queen Lu died, Lu Lu and others wanted to rebel. King Ai of Qi heard the news and led his troops to march westward. Lu Lu and others used Guan Ying as their general to attack the Cha army. When Zhengying arrived at Mingchang, he and Jihuangdong waited for the plan, stationed troops in Rongyang, and persuaded the King of Qi to focus on the execution of the Lu family, and the Qi troops stopped advancing. After Jianghou and others punished the Lu, the King of Qi withdrew his troops and returned to the country. Guan Ying returned from Rongyang and joined ministers Jianghou and Chen Ping to support Emperor Wen. So Guan Ying was given three thousand households to live in, he was rewarded with a thousand catties of gold, and he was worshiped as a Taiwei. In the third year of Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty, Zhou Bo, the Marquis of Jiang, was dismissed as Prime Minister. Zhuo Ying became Prime Minister and no longer served as a Taiwei officer. This year the Huns invaded the north in a large scale, and the emperor ordered Guan Ying to lead a cavalry of 85,000 people to fight against the Huns.

source: I heard that Wu Zixu lost his title for being loyal, Bigan sacrificed himself for being benevolent, and the loyal ministers were loyal and expressed their opinions regardless of the sword or ax on their necks. I hope your majesty will feel relieved and appreciate the relationship between father and son a little. Don't worry about the prince's mistakes, withdraw your troops quickly, and don't let the prince live in exile for a long time. Your Majesty, I am very sincere. source: After reading the letter, Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty was moved and woke up. The prince fled eastward to Hu County and hid in a common people's house in Quanjiu. The family was poor and often sold shoes to support the prince. The prince had an old friend living in Hu County. Hearing that he was wealthy, he sent someone to call him, and he was discovered. The local officials brought people to round up the prince. The prince thought that he could not escape, so he went into the house, closed the door and hanged himself. Zhang Fuchang, a big man from Shanyang County, was a soldier. He kicked the door open. Shi Lishou, the magistrate of Xin'an County, hurriedly stepped forward to untie the prince and hug him. The owner of the house fought with the soldiers and died, and the two royal grandchildren were killed together. Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty was already sad about the death of the prince, but he still issued a Shao Shu saying: "The promised reward is to prove our faith." Li Shou was granted the title of Marquis of Han, and Zhang Fuchang was granted the title of Marquis of Ti. After a long time, most of the stories about witchcraft harming people were untrue.
target: The prince fled east to Hu County, hiding in a commoner's home. The family was poor, selling shoes to support him. When discovered by local officials, the prince hanged himself. His two grandsons were also killed. Emperor Wu, saddened, later learned the witchcraft accusations were mostly untrue.

source: Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty knew that the prince was just scared and ran away, and had no other intentions. In addition, Che Qianqiu once again appealed for the prince's grievances. Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty promoted Che Qianqiu to the rank of prime minister, and then executed Jiang Chong's entire family. Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty was saddened that the prince had died innocently, so he built the Palace of Thoughts and a Tower for Returning and Watching Thoughts upon Return in Hu County.

source: At the beginning, the prince had three sons and one daughter. The daughter was married to the son of Chengsi of Marquis Pingyu. When the prince failed, they were all killed at the same time.
