The two grandsons who fled with the prince were buried in Hu County with the prince. The prince had a grandson who survived, and he was the son of Emperor Shi and Mrs. Wang. When he was eighteen years old, he inherited the throne and became Emperor Mo Xiaoxuan. As soon as Emperor Xiaoxuan came to power, he issued an edict saying: The former crown prince is buried in Hu County. There is no Mi name and a temple to hold sacrifices throughout the year. It is necessary to decide on the Mi name, build a cemetery and arrange for the households to guard the tomb. Relevant officials petitioned and said: According to etiquette and law, if you become someone else's heir, you must be someone else's son. Therefore, your biological parents were demoted and condescended to enjoy no sacrifices. This was out of respect for their ancestors.
target: The prince had three sons and one daughter, all killed when he failed. Empress Wei and Shi Liangdi were buried south of Chang'an. One grandson survived and later became Emperor Xiaoxuan. Upon ascending, he issued edicts regarding proper burial and memorial arrangements for his father, the former crown prince, establishing cemeteries and households for worship.

source: Destiny is fickle, and a person's love for benevolence can make him smart and brilliant; if he does not pursue benevolence and righteousness, it will make a gentleman slack. If you wholeheartedly adhere to the virtues of being righteous and tolerant, you will be able to preserve the blessings given to you by the Emperor of Heaven forever; if you commit sins and behave badly, disaster will befall your kingdom and yourself. Alas! To protect the country and govern the people, can we not be cautious? You, the king, need to be vigilant! Liu Hong's mother, Mrs. Wang, was favored by Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty. Liu Hong was especially favored by Emperor Wu. Eight years after becoming king, he died without a son and the feudal state was abolished. The policy letter to Liu Dan, King of Yanla, said: Woohoo! Little Liu Dan, accept this black soil, build your country, seal it in the north, and serve as a barrier and auxiliary wing of the Han Dynasty for generations. Alas! The Xunhuan family mistreats the elderly, has a heart like an animal, and uses cunning and cunning to conquer hundreds of thousands of people on the border. I ordered the generals to go and punish them for the crimes they committed. The commanders of tens of thousands, the commanders of thousands, and the thirty-two military commanders all stopped their troops and rushed to surrender to us. Xunhuan migrated to other places, and my northern region was peaceful. You must be whole-hearted, do not create any grudges, do not do immoral things, and do not weaken border defenses. Soldiers who have not received training are not allowed to be called into battle. You, the king, need to be vigilant! When Liu Dan grew up, he came to the feudal state. He was an eloquent person, studied classics and various schools of thought extensively, and was fond of astrology, calendars, mathematics, advocating leisure travel, archery and hunting, etc., and attracted knights and warriors. When Prince Wei was defeated and King Huai of Qi died again, Liu Dan thought that he should be made the crown prince according to the ranking of his brothers, so he wrote a letter requesting to return to Beijing to stay in the palace. Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty was angry and imprisoned the envoy he sent to write the letter. Later, because of harboring fugitives, his fiefdom was cut off from Liangxiang, Anci, and Wen'an counties. From then on, Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty disliked Liu Dan, and later made his youngest son the prince.
target: King Huai of Qi, Liu Hong, died without son after eight years. King Liu Dan of Yanla was eloquent, studied classics, and attracted knights. After Prince Wei's defeat and Liu Hong's death, Liu Dan believed he should be crown prince. Emperor Wu became angry, imprisoned his envoy, and later cut off his fiefdom. Emperor Wu disliked Liu Dan and made his youngest son prince instead.

source: When Liu Dan grew up, he came to the feudal state. He was an eloquent person, studied classics and various schools of thought extensively, and was fond of astrology, calendars, mathematics, advocating leisure travel, archery and hunting, etc., and attracted knights and warriors. When Prince Wei was defeated and King Huai of Qi died again, Liu Dan thought that he should be made the crown prince according to the ranking of his brothers, so he wrote a letter requesting to return to Beijing to stay in the palace. Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty was angry and imprisoned the envoy he sent to write the letter. Later, because of harboring fugitives, his fiefdom was cut off from Liangxiang, Anci, and Wen'an counties. From then on, Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty disliked Liu Dan, and later made his youngest son the prince. When Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty died, the prince succeeded to the throne and was named Emperor Xiaozhao. He issued letters stamped with jade seals to various princes and kings. When Liu Dan received the letter, he refused to mourn. He said: The envelope containing the seal is small. I suspect there has been a change in the capital. He sent his cronies Shou Xichang, Sun Zongzhi, Wang Ru and others to Chang'an to inquire about the news in the name of asking about etiquette. Wang Ru went to see Jinwu Guo Guangyi and asked what kind of illness the emperor had when he died, who succeeded him and how old he was. Guo Guangyi said that at that time, he was waiting for the emperor's edict in Wuzha Palace. People in the palace were clamoring that the emperor had died. The generals supported the prince as emperor. The prince was about eight or nine years old and would not leave the palace during the funeral. Wang Ru and others came back and reported to King Yanla. King Yanla said: "The emperor abandoned his ministers and left without saying anything. The eldest princess of Gaiyi was not seen. It's very strange." Then he sent a senior official to Chang'an, the capital, to write a letter saying: I privately saw Emperor Xiaowu practicing the way of a sage. He was filial to his ancestors and loving to his relatives. He harmoniously united his subjects and billions of people. His benevolence united the heaven and earth. The sun and the moon shined brightly. Might permeated the world. Countries from far away offered treasures. Come to worship, add dozens of counties and counties, nearly double the territory, offer sacrifices to Mount Tai, worship Father Liang, travel around the world, and place treasures and foreign objects from far away in the Ancestral Temple. His benevolence is so majestic and grand. I request that temples be built for Emperor Xiaowu in every county. The memorial was submitted and reported back that the emperor had read it. At that time, the general Huo Guang was in charge of the government and rewarded King Yan with 30 million yuan and increased the number of 13,000 households in the fiefdom. Liu Dan said angrily: I should be the emperor, how can you reward me! So he formed a conspiracy with Liu Chang, the son of King Ai of Zhongshan, and Liu Ze, the grandson of King Xiao of Qi, and others in the clan. They lied that they had received an edict from Emperor Wu and could take charge of local administration, build military preparedness, and prepare for extraordinary incidents.
target: When Emperor Wu died and the prince succeeded as Emperor Xiaozhao, Liu Dan refused to mourn, suspecting changes in the capital. He sent inquiries and later requested temples be built for Emperor Wu. General Huo Guang rewarded him, but Liu Dan angrily claimed he should be emperor. He conspired with others, claiming the young emperor was not Emperor Wu's true son. The plot was discovered, and Liu Dan's co-conspirators were executed. Later, Liu Dan's sister and others conspired with him against Huo Guang. The fourteen-year-old Emperor Zhao trusted Huo Guang and distrusted Liu Dan. The conspiracy was exposed, and Liu Dan hanged himself after receiving an imperial seal condemning his actions.

source: You, the king, need to be careful! When Liu Xu grew up, he liked to advocate excellent entertainment and debauchery. He was very strong, could lift a tripod, and could fight bears, wild boars and other beasts with his bare hands. His behavior was inconsistent with the rules, so he was later unable to be made the crown prince of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty. When Emperor Zhao of the Han Dynasty first came to the throne, he granted Liu Xu an additional 13,000 households. When Liu Xu came to court in the Yuanfeng year, he granted another 10,000 households. He also rewarded 20 million yuan, 2,000 kilograms of gold, a special car for riding, a cart with four horses and a sword, and a sword. When Emperor Xuan ascended the throne, Liu Xu's four sons Liu Sheng, Liu Zeng, Liu Bao, and Liu Chang were all granted the title of marquis, and Liu Xu's youngest son Liu Hong was also appointed as King of Gaomi. The praises and rewards given were very generous. When Emperor Zhao was in power, Liu Xu saw that the emperor was young and had no sons, so he coveted the throne. Chu Di was also superstitious about ghosts, gods and witches, so Liu Xu took the witch Li Nuxu and asked her to invite the gods to the lower world to pray for disaster.
target: King Li of Guangling, Liu Xu, was strong and liked entertainment. He coveted the throne when Emperor Zhao was young and childless.

source: Liu Xu's left and right attendants all knelt down. Li Nuxu then said in the tone of Emperor Wu: I must make Liu Xu the emperor. Afterwards, Liu Xu rewarded Li Nuxu with a lot of money and asked her to go to Wushan to pray. While it was being built, Emperor Zhao of the Han Dynasty passed away. Liu Xu said: Li Nuxu is a witch who can really communicate with gods! In return, a cow is killed as a sacrifice. When King Changyi was conscripted into the capital and succeeded to the throne, Liu Xu asked witches to sacrifice to the gods in order to bring disaster. Later, when King Changyi was deposed, Liu Xu became even more superstitious about Li Nuxu and other witches, and rewarded them with money and materials many times. When Emperor Moxuan ascended the throne, Liu Xu asked: Why was the grandson of the former prince made emperor instead? Let Li Nuxu pray to God for curses again as before. In addition, Liu Xu's daughter was the younger brother-in-law of Chu King Liu Yanshou. They often exchanged gifts and exchanged private letters with each other. Later, Liu Yanshou was executed for treason, and his confession implicated Liu Xu. The emperor ordered Liu Xu not to be held accountable, and gave Liu Xu gold, weighing five thousand kilograms before and after, and many other utensils. When Liu Xu heard that the imperial court had appointed a prince, he said to Ji Concubine and others: I can never be made emperor. It also stops letting witches curse. Later, Liu Xu's son Nanlihou Liu Shi was deprived of his title for committing murder. He returned to Guangling and committed adultery with Liu Xu's concubine Zuo Xiu. After the incident, Liu Shi was thrown into prison and his head was beheaded in public.
target: He employed witches to pray for his ascension. When Emperor Zhao died and King Changyi succeeded, Liu Xu had witches curse him. After King Changyi was deposed and Emperor Xuan ascended, Liu Xu continued his schemes. His treason was discovered, and he hanged himself after a final banquet.

source: Initially, Liu Hong, the Ai King of Gaomi, was granted a title in the first year of Benshi because he was the youngest son of Liu Xu, King of Guangling. He died nine years after becoming queen. Liu Hong's son Liu Zhang, the king of Qing, succeeded him and died after reigning for thirty-three years. Liu Zhang's son, King Huai Liu Kuan, succeeded him and died after reigning for eleven years. Liu Kuan's son Liu Shen succeeded to the throne and ended the Wang Mang era. Liu Zhen, the Ai king of Changyi, was established in the fourth year of Tianhan Dynasty. He died in the eleventh year of his reign and was succeeded by his son Liu He. Thirteen years after the establishment of the Han Dynasty, Emperor Zhao of the Han Dynasty died without heirs. General Huo Guang summoned the mourning king Liu He to preside over the funeral.
target: King Ai of Changyi, Liu He, was summoned to preside over Emperor Zhao's funeral. He traveled hastily, causing horses to die.

source: When we got downstairs, we cried according to the etiquette. Changyi King Liu He accepted the emperor's seal and inherited the emperor's title. During his twenty-seventh day in office, he behaved lewdly. General Huo Guang discussed with the ministers, and then reported to Queen Xiaozhao, deposed Liu He, returned him to his hometown of Luyi, and gave him 2,000 households in Tangmuyi. All the property he had when he was king of Changyi was returned to him.
target: During his twenty-seven days as emperor, he behaved lewdly. General Huo Guang deposed him and returned him to his hometown.

source: After the death of Liu He, Marquis of Haihun, it was reported to the government that his son Liu Chongguo was the heir. When Liu Chongguo died, his brother Liu Fengqin was reported to the government. Liu Fengqin also died. This was God cutting off his heirs! Your Majesty was wise and kind, and was very kind to Liu He. Even Shun did the same to his subjects. Liu He's title should be terminated according to etiquette to comply with the will of the Emperor of Heaven. The request was handed over to the relevant officials for discussion. The result of the discussion was that they should not establish heirs for the sake of plastic fall, and abolish the feudal state. After Emperor Yuan ascended the throne, he also granted Xinghe's son Liu Fese the title of Marquis of Haihun. The succession was passed on to his grandson, and he is still a marquis. Praising: How sad the harm caused by the witchcraft case! But this is not Jiang Chong's fault alone. It is also God's will and cannot be caused by human power. In the sixth year of Jianyuan, the demon star Chiyou Banner appeared, and its tail grew to the horizon. After that, the imperial court ordered generals to go out to conquer Henan and establish Shuofang County. In the spring of that year, Prince Ru was born. From then on, during the thirty years of the war, the army killed and destroyed countless people. When the witchcraft case broke out, the capital Chang'an became a river of blood, with tens of thousands of corpses lying on the ground. The prince's family, father and son, were all destroyed.
target: Later, Emperor Xuan granted him the title of Marquis of Haihun. After his death, his title was terminated. The text concludes with a reflection on the witchcraft case's harm, noting it was not solely Jiang Chong's fault but also divine will, comparing the situation to the Qin dynasty's downfall and emphasizing that war, like fire, burns itself if not stopped.

source: King Li of Huainan, with a long name, was the youngest son of Emperor Gao of the Han Dynasty. His mother used to be the beauty of King Zhao Zhang Ao. In the eighth year of Emperor Gao's reign, Emperor Gao passed by the State of Zhao from Dongyuan. King Tong presented a beautiful woman to Emperor Gao. This was King Li's mother. She became pregnant after being favored. King Zhao did not dare to let her return to the palace, so he built an outer palace for her to live in. When the rebellion by Guangao and others was discovered and King Zhao was implicated, King Tong's mother, brothers and beauties were all arrested and imprisoned in Hanoi. King Li's mother was also imprisoned. She told the officials: I was once favored by the emperor and had a son. After hearing this, the officials told the emperor that the emperor was very angry with King Zhao and ignored King Li's mother. King Li's uncle Chang Jian told Empress Lu through Piyanghou. Empress Lu was jealous and refused to defend them, and Piyanghou did not fight for him. Queen Li's mother committed suicide out of resentment and anger after giving birth to Queen Li. The officials sent King Li to the emperor. The emperor regretted it very much and asked Queen Lu to raise King Li, and she was buried in the county where King Li's mother lived. In the eleventh year of the Han Dynasty, the king of Huainan, Yingbu, rebelled. The emperor personally led his troops to destroy Yingbu, so he made his son Liu Chang the king of Huainan. King Huainan lost his mother when he was young and often relied on Empress Lu. During the reigns of Emperor Xiaohui and Empress Lu, he was favored for this reason and had no trouble. However, he often resented Marquis Piyang in his heart, but he did not dare to show it. In the early days of Emperor Xiaowen's accession to the throne, he thought he was the closest person to the royal family and was proud and indulgent, breaking the law several times. The emperor forgave him. In the third year of Emperor Wen's reign, he behaved very arrogantly when he came to court. He followed the emperor to the royal gardens for hunting, rode in the same car with the emperor, and often called the emperor "big brother". King Li was powerful and could lift the cauldron, so he went to pay homage to Marquis Piyang. When Marquis Piyang came out to receive him, King Li took out the iron spine hidden in his sleeve and struck Marquis Piyang, and ordered his followers to chop off his head. Then he drove his horse to the emperor's palace, took off his shirt, exposed his arms, and apologized to the emperor, saying: "My mother should not have committed a crime and been imprisoned for visiting the king. Marquis Piyang had the ability to persuade Empress Lu to save her, but he did not try his best to save her. This is the first crime." King Zhao Ruyi and his mother were both innocent. Empress Lu murdered them, and Marquis Piyang did not try his best to dissuade them. This was the second crime. Empress Lu wanted to harm our Liu family by conferring the title of king on the Lu family. Marquis Piyang did not try to dissuade her. This is the third crime. I just killed bad guys for the people of the world and avenged my mother. I am willing to confess my sin to Your Majesty. Emperor Wen took pity on him because he was avenging his relatives and pardoned his sin. At that time, everyone from Queen Mother Bo to the Crown Prince and all the ministers were afraid of King Li. As a result, King Li returned to the feudal state and became more arrogant and indulgent. He did not obey the laws of the Han Dynasty. He had left and right guards and clear roads like the emperor when he came in and out. He made his own laws and showed disrespect when writing to the emperor several times.
target: King Li of Huainan, the youngest son of Emperor Gao of Han, was born to a former beauty of King Zhao Zhang Ao. His mother became pregnant after being favored by Emperor Gao during a visit to Zhao. When King Zhao was implicated in a rebellion, she was imprisoned and revealed her pregnancy, but Emperor Gao ignored her pleas. After giving birth to King Li, she committed suicide out of resentment. Emperor Gao regretted this and had Empress Lu raise the child. In the eleventh year of his reign, Emperor Gao made Liu Chang the King of Huainan after suppressing a rebellion. King Li grew up relying on Empress Lu and was favored during the reigns of Emperor Xiaohui and Empress Lu, but he resented Marquis Piyang for not saving his mother. After Emperor Xiaowen ascended, King Li became arrogant and broke laws repeatedly. In the third year of Emperor Wen's reign, he killed Marquis Piyang in revenge, claiming three crimes: failing to save his mother, not preventing Empress Lu's murder of King Zhao Ruyi, and not stopping Empress Lu from ennobling the Lu family. Emperor Wen pardoned him out of pity, but King Li grew more defiant, making his own laws and acting like an emperor. Emperor Wen's uncle Bo Zhao admonished King Li in a letter, listing eight dangerous behaviors: abandoning his state, disobeying orders, prioritizing his mother's grave over his father's, and more. He warned that disaster would follow if King Li did not reform. King Li was displeased and ignored the advice.

source: Thinking about the mistakes I had made, I was filled with fear. Now I am lying on the ground waiting for the Fa-rectification and dare not get up. The emperor will definitely be happy after hearing this. Your Majesty, if your brothers above are happy, your ministers below will live longer. If there is harmony between above and below, the world will be at peace. May your Majesty accept my suggestion and implement it immediately. If you hesitate and refuse to implement it, disaster will be like an arrow that has been shot out and cannot be taken back. King Li was very unhappy after receiving the remonstrance. In the sixth year, he sent Dan and other seventy men to conspire with Chai Qi, the prince of Chaiwu, the Marquis of Jipu, and sent forty military chariots back to the valley, and sent people to Minyue and Xiongnu. After the incident was discovered, the emperor wanted to punish him, so he sent someone to summon King Huainan to Beijing.
target: In the sixth year, he conspired with seventy men, including Chai Qi, to rebel, contacting Minyue and Xiongnu. The plot was discovered, and King Li was summoned to Chang'an.

source: Liu Chang did not want to accept the reward, but said contemptuously: "There is no hard work." Wang Zhi of Nanhai wrote a letter to the emperor asking for jade and silk, but Qu Ji burned the letter without reporting it to the emperor. Officials asked to summon Qu Ji to Chang'an, but Liu Chang refused to let Lin Ji come, saying that "Yin Ji was ill." The crime Liu Chang committed should be beheaded in the market, and we request that he be sentenced in accordance with the law. The emperor issued an edict saying: I cannot bear to punish King Li, so I should discuss it with the princes and the two thousand officials. After discussion, the princes, 2,000 officials and 43 officials and infants all agreed that the matter should be dealt with according to law. The emperor ordered: Then pardon Liu Chang's death penalty and dethrone him from the throne. The officials reported: I request Zaoshang to exile him to Qiongdi, Yandao County, Shu County, and order his children and their mother to live with them. The Yandao County magistrate can build a house for them, and provide firewood, vegetable salt, cooking utensils and mats for each meal. The emperor ordered: Supply Liu Chang with food, give him five kilograms of meat and two measures of wine. He ordered ten favored concubines of his past to live with him. So all the people who conspired with Liu Chang were killed. He dispatched Liu Chang and sent them heavy-loaded carriages and horses, and all the counties they passed through were equipped with carriages to transport them one by one.
target: After interrogation, officials reported his crimes: abandoning Han laws, appointing officials without authorization, harboring fugitives, and planning rebellion. They demanded his execution, but Emperor Wen commuted the sentence to exile in Shu County.

source: Yuan Ang said: The King of Huainan is already like this. There is no other way. Please be at ease, Your Majesty. The emperor asked: What should we do? He replied: Only by killing the prime minister and censor can we apologize to the world. The emperor immediately ordered the prime minister and censors to arrest those who did not deliver food and food to the king of Huainan from various counties and beheaded them on the street. So the King of Huainan was buried in Yongdi according to the treatment of the princes, and thirty families were arranged to guard his tomb. In the eighth year of Emperor Xiaowen's reign, the emperor took pity on King Huainan. He still had four sons, all seven or eight years old, so he named his sons Liu An the Marquis of Fuling, Liu Bo the Marquis of Anyang, Liu Ci the Marquis of Yangzhou, and Liu Liang the Marquis of Shucheng.
target: King Li refused food and died on the way. Emperor Wen mourned and executed the officials who failed to provide food. He later enfeoffed King Li's four sons as marquises.

source: The two brothers are incompatible! After hearing this, the emperor said: In the past, Yao and Shun exiled their own flesh and blood, and Zhou Gong killed Guan Shu and Cai Shu. The whole world called them saints, and they would not harm the national interests for selfish reasons. How can people in the world think that I am coveting the land of King Huainan? So King Chengyang was moved to the old land of Huainan to become king, and King Mi of Huainan was named King Li, and his cemetery was set up according to the etiquette of the princes. In the 16th year, the emperor took pity on King Huainan because he abolished Han law without authorization and behaved indulgently, which caused him to lose his feudal status and died at an early age. Therefore, he moved King Liu Xi of Huainan back to Chengyang as king, and established King Li's three sons as kings in his hometown of Huainan. They are: Fuling Hou Liu An as the King of Huainan, Anyang Hou Liu Bo as the King of Hengshan, and Yangzhou Hou Liu Ci as the King of Lujiang. Liu Liang, the Marquis of Shucheng, died young and had no descendants. In the third year of Xiaojing's reign, the seven kingdoms of Wu and Chu rebelled. Wu's envoys went to the King of Huainan, who wanted to send troops to meet the King of Wu. His prime minister said: If your Majesty must raise an army with King Wu, I would like to be a general. The king of Huainan then handed over the army to the prime minister.
target: In the sixteenth year, he made three of them kings in Huainan. During the Rebellion of the Seven States, King Huainan Liu An initially considered joining Wu but was restrained by his prime minister. Liu An, known for his literary pursuits, compiled the "Inner Books" and other works.

source: At that time, all the princes were allowed to ennoble their own children as marquises. King Huainan had two sons, one of whom was established as the prince, but Liu Jian's father was not allowed to be established as a marquis. So Liu Jian secretly made some friends and wanted to murder the prince and let his father be the prince instead. When the prince found out, he arrested and whipped Liu Jian many times. Liu Jian knew about the prince's plot to kill Lieutenant Mo, so he sent his friend Shouchun to write a solemn letter to the emperor, saying: Good medicine is bitter and good for the disease, and loyal advice is hard on the ears and good for action. Nowadays, Liu Jian, the grandson of King Huainan, is very talented, so Liu Qian, the son of King Huainan and Queen Tu and Tu, often frame him. Liu Jian's father was imprisoned many times despite being innocent. They wanted to kill him. Now that Liu Jianren is here, His Majesty can interrogate him personally, and he will know the plot of King Huainan. After receiving the memorial, the emperor handed over the matter to Tingwei and Henan Order. This happened in the sixth year of Yuanshuo.
target: He plotted rebellion after a comet appeared, believing the emperor had no heir. His daughter Liu Ling spied in Chang'an. The plot was exposed when his grandson Liu Jian informed on him. King Huainan committed suicide, and his kingdom was abolished as Jiujiang County.

source: The king of Huainan thought that it would be meaningless to just kill the prime minister and leave the history and lieutenant in the future, so he ordered the prime minister to go back. When he was hesitating, the prince thought that the crime they committed was just the murder of a Han Dynasty lieutenant, and all those involved in the murder were dead and there were no witnesses, so he said to the King of Huainan: All the useful officials among the officials have been arrested, and now there is no one who can help in the rebellion. If your Majesty raises troops at an inappropriate time, I'm afraid it won't be successful. It's better to let them arrest me. The King of Huainan became less and less willing to take action, so he agreed to the prince's request. The prince committed suicide but did not die. Wu Ban went to surrender and confessed to the rebellion against the King of Huainan. The officials of the Han Dynasty arrested the prince and the queen, surrounded the palace, took away all the guests of King Huainan, copied the utensils used in the rebellion, and reported them to the emperor. The emperor sent his ministers to investigate and investigate. Thousands of princes, erganshi, and heroes were implicated in King Huainan's rebellion. They were all punished according to the severity of their crimes. Hengshan Wang Xingmeng, the younger brother of Huainan Wang Xingxuan, should be arrested. Someone asked for the arrest of the King of Hengshan, and the emperor said: "The princes each have their own enfeoffments and govern the country, and they should not be implicated." Please discuss and discuss with the princes, kings and princes. Forty-three people including Diesi Qiandan and Liehou Rang all said: Liu An, the king of Jinnan, is treasonous and treasonous. The evidence of rebellion is conclusive and he should be questioned and executed. Liu Duan, King of Jiaoxi, said: Liu An is lawless, does not follow the right path, has ulterior motives, and is ready to disrupt the world, confuse the people, betray his ancestors, and confuse the public with his evil words. "Spring and Autumn" says: If the minister does not use the general, he will be executed. Liu An's crime did not just sprout, his rebellion was already a fact. In my opinion, after identifying the tools of his rebellion, he can be punished. Officials of the Huainan Kingdom with a salary of more than 200 shi and those with a salary equivalent to this, as well as favorites of the royal family, who have not rebelled but failed to assist the King of Huainan should be dismissed from their posts, and their titles can be reduced to civilians, and they will not be allowed to serve as officials again. The other people who were not officials each paid two catties and eighty taels of gold to atone for their death penalty, so that Liu An's crimes could be publicized, so that everyone in the world would understand the way of being a minister and would not dare to have bad intentions and rebel against the court. Prime Minister Gongsun Hong, Tingweitang and others reported their opinions to the kings, and the emperor sent Zongzheng to punish Liu An. Before Zong Zheng arrived, Liu An committed suicide. The queen, prince and other people involved in the rebellion were all executed. Huainan Kingdom was abolished and changed to Jiujiang County. Queen Chengshu of Hengshan King Liu Ci gave birth to three children: the eldest son Liu Shuang was the prince, the second daughter Liu Wucai, and the youngest son Liu Xiao. The beloved concubine Xu Lai gave birth to four children, and the beautiful concubine Jue Ji gave birth to two children.
target: King Hengshan Liu Ci, brother of King Huainan, also plotted rebellion. He feuded with his son, Prince Liu Shuang, and favored his younger son Liu Xiao. After Queen Chengshu died, Queen Xu Lai and concubine Jue Ji slandered the prince. The prince was whipped and later accused his father of rebellion. King Hengshan committed suicide when investigated. His kingdom was also abolished. The historian comments that both kings, despite being imperial relatives, perished due to their rebellious nature and the corrupting influence of their ministers, noting that people of Jingchu have historically been prone to insurrection.

source: In ancient times, when the emperor established a country, the princes established their families, and there were certain levels of hierarchy from officials to common people, so that the people could obey their superiors and subordinates would stop having any wrong ideas. Confucius said: When the world is at peace, the highest political power of the country will not be in the hands of the officials. All officials can obey the law and perform their duties, those who neglect their duties will be investigated and those who violate the law will be punished. Only in this way can everything go smoothly and everything is in order. With the decline of the Zhou royal family, the formulation of ritual and music conquests began to be made by the princes individually. After Duke Huan of Qi and Duke Wen of Jin, the officials had exclusive power and issued orders to important ministers in the court. When the situation evolved into the Warring States Period, the princes began to join forces with each other. They abandoned propriety and justice and fought with prestige and force. As a result, some princes from various countries, such as Lord Xinling of Wei, Lord Pingyuan of Zhao, Lord Mengchang of Qi, and Lord Chunshen of Chu, all relied on the authority of princes and nobles to compete to become knight-errants. Those who croaked, roosters, and dogs were all disrespectful and submitted to them. The Prime Minister Yu Qing did not hesitate to leave the country and the monarch to save his friend Wei Qi from danger; Wei Wuji, the Lord of Xinling, stole the military talisman, falsely conveyed the monarch's orders, hunted down the generals, and sent out a dedicated army to relieve the Pingyuan Lord of Zhao State from being besieged by the Qin soldiers. They are all famous for their emphasis on relations between princes. Those chivalrous people who hold hands and talk are all led by the "four heroes": Lord Xinling, Lord Pingyuan, Lord Mengchang and Lord Chunshen. As a result, the agreement to betray the imperial court and form secret alliances with best friends became a reality, and the culture of strictly observing official duties and respecting the monarch began to decline. After the rise of the Han Dynasty, bans and regulations were very loose, so the situation of deportation remained unchanged. Therefore, the Prime Minister sent thousands of chariots with rare entourage, and King Liu Bi of Wu and King Liu An of Huainan both invited thousands of guests. The subordinates of the foreign ministers Wei Qihou Dou Ying and Wu'an Hou Tianyi were wandering around in the capital to cause trouble. Meng and Guo Xie, who were civilians, wandered in the lanes and rampaged through the prefectures and counties, and their power overran the princes. Many ordinary people regard their fame and deeds as a kind of honor, yearning for and admiring them. Even though they were punished by the criminal law, they did not hesitate to kill themselves to become famous, just like Ji Lu and Qiu Mu, who died without regrets. Therefore, Zengzi said: If those in high positions do not act according to the rules, the people will have long since abandoned their moral principles. Without a sage king above him to instruct the good and evil in the world and formulate the country's etiquette, how can the people know the prohibitions and correct themselves! The ancient orthodox view is that the Five Hegemons are the sinners of the Three Kings; and the Six Kingdoms are the sinners of the Five Hegemons. From this point of view, these four tycoons should be the sinners of the Six Nations. What's more, people like Guo Xie, in their low status as civilians, stole the power of life and death. Their crimes are already intolerable in heaven and earth. However, on the other hand, they are gentle and friendly, helpful, humble and courteous, and they all have extraordinary charm.
target: In ancient times, the emperor established a country with a clear hierarchy from officials to common people, ensuring order and obedience. Confucius noted that when the world is at peace, political power does not rest with officials, who must obey the law and face punishment for neglect or violation. However, with the decline of the Zhou royal family, princes began to control rituals and military campaigns. After Duke Huan of Qi and Duke Wen of Jin, officials gained exclusive power, leading to the Warring States Period, where princes abandoned propriety for force. Figures like Lord Xinling, Lord Pingyuan, Lord Mengchang, and Lord Chunshen relied on noble authority to become knight-errants, attracting followers who valued personal bonds over official duties. This trend continued into the Han Dynasty, where bans were loose, and powerful figures like King Liu Bi of Wu and King Liu An of Huainan hosted thousands of guests. Commoners like Guo Xie gained influence, often resorting to violence and crime, yet were admired for their generosity and charm. Despite their crimes, they were seen as sinners against orthodox moral standards, and the emperor eventually ordered Guo Xie's execution for forming a secret faction and abusing power.

source: However, Jumeng's mother passed away, and thousands of funeral vehicles came from far away. When Ju Meng died, the family had little money left. There is also Wang Meng of Fuli, who is also famous among Jianghuai for his reputation as a heroic hero. At that time, Jinan's family and Zhou Fu of Chenjun were also famous for their heroes. Emperor Jing heard about them and sent people to kill them all. Later, the Bai family of Zhujia in Fajun, Han Wupi of Liang State, Xue Kuang of Yangdi, Hanru of Shaanxi, etc. also came back as famous heroes one after another. Guo Xie was a native of Zhi County, Hanoi County, and the grandson of Xu Fu, a good minister from Wen. Guo Xie's father was a chivalrous man and was killed during the reign of Emperor Xiaowen. Guo Xie was a calm and brave person, and did not like drinking. When he was young, he was vicious and violent. Whenever he was unhappy, he would use force to kill people. Many people were hurt by him. He was willing to sacrifice his life to avenge himself with blood. He also hid desperadoes and carried out robbery and theft. When he had nothing to do, he minted counterfeit money and dug graves. His misdeeds were countless. Thanks to God's blessing, he was often relieved in times of crisis, as if he had experienced amnesty. When Guo Xie grew up, he began to reflect on his mistakes, exercise self-discipline, respond to grudges with kindness, be willing to do good, and be pure of desire. However, his desire to be a knight became stronger and stronger. Although he has done some good deeds to save lives without seeking fame, his sinister nature is often shown between his eyebrows and remains the same as before.
target: Guo Xie, a native of Zhi County, was the grandson of a good minister. His father was a chivalrous man killed during Emperor Xiaowen's reign. Guo Xie was calm and brave but vicious in his youth, committing murder, robbery, and grave robbing. As he matured, he reflected on his mistakes, practiced self-discipline, and responded to grudges with kindness, though his sinister nature persisted.

source: When Guo Xie grew up, he began to reflect on his mistakes, exercise self-discipline, respond to grudges with kindness, be willing to do good, and be pure of desire. However, his desire to be a knight became stronger and stronger. Although he has done some good deeds to save lives without seeking fame, his sinister nature is often shown between his eyebrows and remains the same as before. Many young men admired his character and always took risks and hurt others for revenge, but Guo Xie himself had no way of knowing these things. Guo Xie's sister's son relied on Guo Xie's reputation and became very domineering. Once he drank with others and made someone drink all the wine in the palace. The person couldn't bear it, so he forced the person to drink. The man was furious, assassinated Guo Xie's sister's son and fled. Guo Xie's sister said: You dared to kill my son while Guo Xie was still alive, but the murderer escaped. So she abandoned the son's body on the roadside without burial, hoping to anger Guo Xie with humiliation. Guo Xie sent people to find out where the murderer was. He was desperate, so he came over and told Guo Xie the truth. Guo Xie said: You are right to kill him, it is my son who is shameful. So he let the murderer go, and Guo Xie placed the blame on his sister's son, collected his body and buried it. When everyone heard about this, they all respected Guo Xie's benevolence and righteousness, and more and more people followed him. One time when Guo Xie went out, everyone avoided him. Only one person sat there with his legs stretched out and looked at him. Guo Xie asked him his name, and his followers wanted to kill the man. Guo Xie said: Someone disrespected me in the alley because my moral character was questionable. What crime did he have? So he secretly told Wei Shi: "This man is someone I respect. Please don't use him when recruiting soldiers who are on duty." Whenever it was time to change the duty, he went there several times, but the officials in charge did not let him change the duty. He was very surprised and asked the reason. The official told him that it was Guo Xie who exempted him from duty. Only those who showed disrespect to Guo Xie bared their chests and apologized to Guo Xie. When the young people heard this, they all admired Guo Xie's character even more. Someone in Luoyang had an enemy, and more than ten famous people and wealthy people in the city intervened, but the enemy did not listen to his advice. Someone came to ask Guo Xie. Guo Xie went to his enemy's house at night to see him, and the enemy finally succumbed to him. Guo Xie said to the man: I heard that everyone in Luoyang was trying to mediate, but you didn't listen. Now I am fortunate to have listened to my Guo Xie's advice, but how can I, Guo Xie, compete for the power of local celebrities as a foreigner!
target: His sister's son was killed for forcing someone to drink, and Guo Xie, deeming the victim at fault, let the murderer go, earning respect. Another incident involved a man who disrespected Guo Xie; instead of retaliating, Guo Xie secretly exempted him from duty, leading to the man's apology and increased admiration for Guo Xie. In Luoyang, Guo Xie mediated a dispute where local celebrities failed, and he ensured the credit went to them. Despite his humble and frugal lifestyle, Guo Xie's influence grew, and he was eventually forced to move to Maoling due to imperial suspicion.

source: There was a man named Ji Shaoweng in Linjin who admired his name but had never seen Guo Xie, so he released him privately. The young man released Guo Xie, and Guo Xie went to Taiyuan. Wherever he went, he often told the host of the incident. The arrester followed the traces and found the young man, who was so anxious that he committed suicide, thus cutting off all witnesses. After a long time, Guo Xie was finally arrested and the crimes he committed were comprehensively investigated. However, his murders all occurred before the amnesty and it was difficult to pursue them. There was a Confucian scholar sitting with the envoy in Zhi County. Most of the people spoke well of Guo Xie, but the Confucian scholar said: Guo Xie specialized in violating public laws with treachery and robbery. How can we say he is a wise man? Upon hearing this, Guo Xie's family members assassinated the Confucian scholar and cut off his tongue. For this reason, the officials brought Guo Xie up for questioning. Guo Xie really did not know who the murderer was, and the murderer was not identified at the time. The officials reported that Guo Xie was not guilty.
target: After his move, conflicts arose, leading to murders and his eventual arrest. Although many crimes were pardoned, Guo Xie was executed for treason after a Confucian scholar was assassinated by his followers.

source: Gongsun Hong, the imperial censor, pointed out: As a commoner, Guo Xie formed a secret faction, abused his power, and killed people wantonly for trivial matters. Guo Xie himself did not know that this crime exceeded the crime of beheading that Guo Xie knew about. It should be punished as a crime of treason. So the emperor ordered Guo Xie's entire family to be executed. From then on, there were many knights from various places, but there were none worth mentioning. But Fan Zhongzi from Chang'an in Guanzhong, Wangsun Fang from Huaili, Gongzi Gao from Changling, Guo Wengzhong from Xihe, Lu Wengru from Taiyuan, Er Changqing from Linhuai, Chen Junru from Shuyang, etc., although they are knights, they all have the courtesy and humility of gentlemen. As for the Yao family in the North Road, the Du families in the West Road, Qiu Jing in the South Road, Young Master Tuo Yu in Shu Road, Zhao Diao in Nanyang and others, they are all bandits and are mixed among the common people, so why bother! Even people like the Zhu family would feel humiliated. Wan Zhang, courtesy name Zixia, was from Chang'an. Chang'an is a very prosperous place, and there are many heroic people in the streets. Wan Zhang lived in Liushi, west of the city, and was known as Wan Zixia in the west of the city. Later, he became Jing Zhaoyin's secret friend and followed Jing Zhaoyin to the palace. Among the servants, princes and nobles, they were all vying to bow to Wan Zhang, but no one went to talk to Jing Zhaoyin. Wan Zhang was very embarrassed and frightened. From then on, Jing Zhaoyin never asked Wan Zhang to accompany him again. Wan Zhang was very close to Zhongshu Ling Shi Xian, and they also took advantage of Shi Xian's power, so there was always a continuous flow of cars and horses in front of his house. In the early years of Emperor Cheng's reign, Shi Xian was dismissed from office because of the crime of taking advantage of power and moved back to his hometown. At that time, Shi Xian's family had a fortune of tens of millions. Before leaving, he left some bed mats and utensils worth several millions and wanted to give them to Wan Zhang, but Wan Zhang did not accept them. Some guests asked about the reason, and Wan Zhang sighed and said: I am a commoner wearing cloth, and I owe you the pity of Mr. Shi. Now that Mr. Shi has ruined his family and career, I cannot save him, but I still accept his property. Could it be that this misfortune of the Shi family, I, the Wan family, regard it as a blessing? After hearing this, everyone was convinced and praised his conduct. During the Heping period, Wang Zun became Jing Zhaoyin and began to capture the heroes. He killed Wan Zhang, Zhang Hui, the archer, Tong Jundu from the wine market, Jia Ziguang and others. They were all famous heroes in Chang'an City, and they were also those who loved private revenge and adopted assassins. Lou Hu, courtesy name Junqing, was from Qi State. His father was a doctor handed down from generation to generation. When Lou Hu was a child, he practiced medicine with his father in Chang'an and visited the homes of noble relatives. Lou Hu recited hundreds of thousands of medical classics, materia medica, and alchemy books. The elders loved and valued him, and they all said to him: With your talent, Lou Junqing, why don't you learn to be an official? From then on, Lou Hu said goodbye to his father and began to study the classics. He worked as a minor official in the capital for several years and gained a great reputation. At this time, the Wang family had just become prosperous, and the house was full of guests. The five brothers were competing for fame and fortune, and each of them had his own favorite people to treat the guests. It was difficult for the guests to have both sides. Only Lou Hu was accepted by them all at the same time, and gained the favor of each of them.
target: After Guo Xie, many knights emerged but none were notable. Figures like Fan Zhongzi, Wangsun Fang, and others were courteous and humble, while others like the Yao and Du families were bandits. Wan Zhang, a knight from Chang'an, became a secret friend of Jing Zhaoyin but was embarrassed by the attention he received. He later refused gifts from the disgraced Shi Xian, earning praise for his conduct. During the Heping period, Wang Zun captured and killed many heroes, including Wan Zhang. Lou Hu, from Qi State, initially practiced medicine but later studied classics and became a minor official. He gained fame by serving the five Wang brothers simultaneously, known for his eloquence and integrity. After his mother's death, thousands mourned.

source: He and Gu Yong were both honored guests of the Five Marquises, so there was a rumor in Chang'an City that Gu Ziyun's writings and Lou Junqing's words spoke of their respective talents that were valued by the world. When Lou Hu's mother died, two or three thousand mourners came, and people in the alleys sang: "Lou Junqing is busy organizing the funeral for the five princes." After a long time, Ping'ahou recommended Lou Hu as a talented man, appointed as an admonishing official, and sent out as an envoy to the county. Lou Hu was responsible for supervising the property lent by the government to the poor. He had a lot of coins and silks with him. He passed by Qi State and wrote a letter requesting that the graves of his ancestors be visited. This allowed him to meet his relatives and friends, and he gave some money and silks to each of them according to their closeness. In one day, he distributed gifts worth a hundred gold. After the envoy returned to the court, Lou Hu reported the situation of the envoy and the emperor was satisfied, so he was promoted to the prefect of Tianshui County.
target: Lou Hu later served as an envoy, distributing gifts to relatives, and was promoted to prefect of Tianshui.

source: Lou Hu was responsible for supervising the property lent by the government to the poor. He had a lot of coins and silks with him. He passed by Qi State and wrote a letter requesting that the graves of his ancestors be visited. This allowed him to meet his relatives and friends, and he gave some money and silks to each of them according to their closeness. In one day, he distributed gifts worth a hundred gold. After the envoy returned to the court, Lou Hu reported the situation of the envoy and the emperor was satisfied, so he was promoted to the prefect of Tianshui County. A few years later, Lou Hu was dismissed from office and lived in Chang'an City. At that time, the Marquis of Chengdu, Wang Shang, was appointed as the Great Sima Wei General. After going to court once, he wanted to visit Lou Hu. His boss, Bo Guan, persuaded him: General, as a supreme being, it is not appropriate for you to go in and out of lanes. Wang Shang didn't listen, so he went to Lou Hu's house. The building guard's residence was very small, and they could only stand under the car. They stopped for a long time. It was going to rain. The chief registrar said to the officials of Xicao: The general did not listen to the advice, and now he has to stand in the alley in the rain! After Wang Shang returned, he learned these words of the chief registrar and was very disgusted with him. He dismissed him from the post of chief registrar on the grounds of job transfer, and never let him serve as an official again in his life. Later, Lou Hu was recommended as the prefect of Guanghan County again. During the first year of the Yuan Dynasty, Wang Mang was appointed Duke of Anhan and specialized in government affairs. Wang Mang's eldest son Guang Guang and his wife's brother Dankuan conspired to smear Wang Cha's house door with blood in an attempt to threaten Wang Mang into handing over the power of government. After discovering this, Wang Mang was furious and killed Wang Yu, but Lu Kuan fled.
target: He was dismissed but later reinstated, and during Wang Mang's regency, he captured a fugitive, earning a marquisate. However, he was eventually dismissed again and lived in obscurity, though he maintained his principles by supporting an old friend, Lu Gong, for life.

source: Lou Hu and Lu Gong, Lou's wife and Lu Concubine were eating together. After Lou Hu was dismissed as an official, his wife was very tired of Lu Gong. When Lou Hu found out about this, he cried and blamed his wife, saying: Mr. Lu came to live in my house because of old feelings and because he was lonely and poor. Morally speaking, we should support him. So he served Lu Gong for life. After Lou Hu's death, his son inherited his title. Chen Zun, courtesy name Meng Gong, was born in Duling County. His grandfather's name was Chen Sui, also known as the eldest son. When Emperor Xuan of the Han Dynasty was a humble man, he was very close to him and often played chess with him. As a result, he owed gambling debts many times.
target: Chen Zun, from Duling County, was known for his indulgence and extravagance, contrasting with his friend Zhang Song's frugality. Despite his reckless behavior, Chen Zun was valued for his talent and became a magistrate.

His boss, Bo Guan, persuaded him: General, as a supreme being, it is not appropriate for you to go in and out of lanes. Wang Shang didn't listen, so he went to Lou Hu's house. After Wang Shang returned, he learned these words of the chief registrar and was very disgusted with him. He dismissed him from the post of chief registrar on the grounds of job transfer, and never let him serve as an official again in his life. Later, Lou Hu was recommended as the prefect of Guanghan County again. During the first year of the Yuan Dynasty, Wang Mang was appointed Duke of Anhan and specialized in government affairs. Wang Mang's eldest son Guang Guang and his wife's brother Dankuan conspired to smear Wang Cha's house door with blood in an attempt to threaten Wang Mang into handing over the power of government. After discovering this, Wang Mang was furious and killed Wang Yu, but Lu Kuan fled. Dankuan's father had always known Lujin, but Dankuan didn't tell him the real situation until he passed by Lujin in Luhuan County.
target: He was later dismissed for misconduct but continued to host lavish parties. During Wang Mang's reign, he served as governor of Henan County but was dismissed again.

source: When Wang Mang failed, both of them stayed in Chiyang, and Zhang Song was killed by bandits. When Emperor Gengshi arrived in Chang'an, the ministers recommended Chen Zun to be the Great Sima Protector of the Army, and he and Liu Sa, the Marquis of Guide, were sent as envoys to the Huns. The Shanyu of the Xiongnu forced Chen Zun to surrender to the Xiongnu. Chen Zun explained his interests to him and explained the merits. The Shanyu admired him very much. Let him return to the Han Dynasty. Just when Gengshi was defeated, Chen Zun had to stay in Shuofang. Later, he was defeated by the bandits. Chen Zun was killed by the bandits while he was drunk. Yuanshe, named Juxian. His grandfather migrated from Yangdi County to Maoling as a hero during the reign of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty. His father served as the prefect of Nanyang County during the reign of Emperor Moai. At that time, the world was rich, and the governors of major counties who died in office received more than tens of millions of money from others to help with funeral arrangements. If their families received all the money, they could use it to buy property. At that time, few people could mourn the deceased for three years. After Yuan She's father died, Yuan She not only returned the funeral money donated by the people of Nanyang County, but also lived in Yazhong Cottage and mourned his father for three years, so he became famous in the capital. As soon as the funeral ceremony was over, the envoys inviting him to serve as a council member for the county government arrived like a gust of wind, and scholar-bureaucrats who admired him also gathered from all directions. Because he was recommended by Situ Shidan and said that he had the ability to handle complex affairs, Yuan She became the magistrate of Gu County. He was only in his twenties at that time.
target: Chen Zun was known for his eloquence and charm, and his letters were treasured. He died in Shuofang after being captured by bandits. Yuan She, from Maoling, gained fame by returning funeral donations and mourning his father for three years. He became a magistrate but was dismissed after seeking revenge for his uncle's murder. Yuan She was known for his generosity and ability to mobilize people, often helping the poor and organizing funerals.

source: Only then did Duke Yin agree. So Yuan Si went to apologize as the heroes said, and Yin Gong let him go home with his clothes still on. At first, Yuan She was friends with Qi Taibo, a wealthy man from Xinfeng, but Taibo's half-brother Wang Yougong had always hated Yuan She. Wang Yougong was working as an official in the county government at this time, so he advised Yin Gong: You humiliated Yuan She just by being an acting county magistrate. Once the official county magistrate took office, you still drove your bicycle back to the county government to work as a government official. There were so many assassins among Yuan She's guests and friends that you didn't know who did the killings. I'm really worried about you. Yuan Sheng built tombs and houses, was extravagant and exceeded the legal system, and was guilty of obvious crimes. These emperors also knew about it.
target: However, he was also involved in violence, killing a man who slandered him. During Wang Mang's reign, Yuan She was appointed as an official but was eventually executed after ordering the assassination of a chief registrar.

source: Yuan She was angered by this and sent his guests to assassinate the chief registrar Yin Gong. Yuan She planned to escape, but Shen Tujian felt that he had been humiliated and held a grudge against Yuan She. He pretended to say: I want to jointly control the Sanfu area with Yuan Juxian. How could I change my mind just because a petty official died? The guests informed Yuan She of this and asked him to surrender to prison and apologize to Shen Tujian. Shen Tujian agreed to do this. So, the guests took dozens of cars to take Yuan Shep to prison. Shentu Jian sent troops to intercept Yuan Shen on the way and arrested Yuan Shen in the car. The escorting vehicles split up and fled quickly, so he immediately beheaded Yuan Shenwen and his head was hung in Chang'an City. Since the reign of Emperor Ai and Emperor Ping, there have been heroes everywhere in the county, but the number cannot be counted.
target: Since the reigns of Emperor Ai and Emperor Ping, many heroes emerged in various counties, but their numbers were too many to count.

source: Yuan Ang, Zisi. His father was a native of Chu. He once worked as a thief and later moved to Anling. During the period of Empress Lu, Yuan Ang once served as Lu Lu's retainer. When Emperor Wen of Han came to the throne, Yuan An's brother Yuan Sha recommended Yuan An to be a doctor. Jianghou Zhou Bo became the prime minister. After retiring from the court, he walked out quickly, feeling very contented. The emperor treated him with great courtesy and often saw him off with his eyes. Yuan Ang stepped forward and said, "What kind of person is the Prime Minister?" The emperor said: An important minister of the country. Yuan An said: Jianghou is what is usually called a hero, not an important minister of the country. The important ministers of the country are the master and the minister, and the master will die and the minister will perish. During the period of Empress Lu, Zhu Lu was in power and granted the title of king without authorization. Although the Liu family's world was not cut off, it was as weak and weak as a belt. At that time, Jianghou was serving as the Taiwei and had military power, so he could not help or save him. After Empress Lu died, the ministers worked together to punish Lu. The Taiwei controlled the army, which happened to make him successful. He was a hero in general, not an important official of the country.
target: Yuan Ang, also known as Zisi, was a native of Chu who later moved to Anling. He served as a retainer to Lü Lu during Empress Lü's reign and was recommended as a doctor by his brother Yuan Sha under Emperor Wen of Han. Yuan Ang famously criticized Prime Minister Zhou Bo, calling him a "hero" rather than an "important minister," arguing that Zhou Bo had failed to act against the Lü clan during their usurpation and only succeeded after Empress Lü's death. Despite Zhou Bo's initial anger, Yuan Ang later defended him when Zhou Bo was falsely accused of treason, leading to their friendship.

source: The emperor said: This situation occurred because your opinions were not adopted. Yuan An said: If the emperor wants to think about it himself, this matter has already passed, how can he regret it? Besides, you have three outstanding behaviors, which are not enough to ruin your reputation. The emperor said: What are the three things that make me superior to others? Yuan Ang said: When you were in the Kingdom of Dai, the Queen Mother was ill. For three years, you never closed your eyes, went to bed without undressing, and refused to give the medicine to the Queen Mother unless you tasted it yourself. As a commoner, it was difficult for Zeng Shen to do this, but now as a king, you have implemented it, and you are far ahead of Zeng Shen in terms of filial piety. Zhu Lu is in power, and the powerful ministers do their own thing. However, you took six post cars from Dai State to the capital city where misfortune and fortune are unpredictable. Even warriors like Meng Ben and Xia Yu cannot compare with you. When you arrive at the official residence of the King of Dai, you sit to the west to abdicate the throne of emperor three times, and to the south to abdicate the throne of emperor twice. Xu You surrendered only once, but you surrendered the world five times, more than Xu You surrendered four times. Besides, you exiled the King of Huainan because you wanted to put some hard work on his mind and make him correct his mistakes. Because the officials were careless in protecting him, he died of illness. The emperor was relieved at this time, and Yuan An became famous in the court. Yuan Ang often talks about great principles and is impassioned. Because the eunuch Tangtan had been favored by the emperor many times, he often secretly harmed Yuan An, which made Yuan An feel worried. Yuan An's nephew Yuan Zhong served as an attendant knight, guarding the emperor with talismans. Yuan Zhong advised Yuan Ang: "You have humiliated him in the court. If you say bad things about you in the future, the emperor will not believe him." When Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty went out, Zhao Tan accompanied him in the carriage. Yuan Ang bowed in front of the carriage and said: I heard that those who accompanied the emperor in the six-foot-tall carriage were all domestic heroes. Even if the Han Dynasty lacks talents, why do you only ride in the same carriage with people with broken bodies?
target: Yuan Ang advised Emperor Wen against indulging Liu Chang, the King of Huainan, whose arrogance led to rebellion. When the king died in exile, Yuan Ang consoled the grieving emperor by listing his three great virtues: filial piety during his mother's illness, courage in facing danger when coming to the capital, and humility in repeatedly declining the throne. Yuan Ang also clashed with the eunuch Zhao Tan, insisting he should not ride in the emperor's carriage, and prevented the emperor from reckless chariot racing.

source: The emperor then stopped. The emperor arrived at Shanglin Garden, accompanied by the queen and Mrs. Shen. They often sit on the same level of seats in the palace. When they were seated, Chief Lang arranged the seats, and Yuan Ang pulled Mrs. Shen's seat back a little. Mrs. Shen was angry and refused to sit down. The emperor was also angry and got up. Yuan An took the opportunity to step forward and persuade: I heard that if there is an order of superiority and inferiority, then there will be harmony between the superiors and inferiors. Now that His Majesty has confirmed the Queen, Mrs. Shen is just a concubine. How can the concubine and the Lord sit at the same table?
target: He corrected the seating order between the queen and Consort Shen, warning against favoritism by citing the tragic fate of "human pigs.".

source: When saying goodbye and setting off, Yuan Zhong said to Yuan An: King Wu has been arrogant for a long time, and there are many traitors in the country. If you want to expose and punish him now, those people will either write a letter to accuse you, or they will kill you with a sharp sword. The land in the south is low and humid. You drink wine every day and do nothing more than persuade the King of Wu not to rebel. If you can do this, you may be able to get away from trouble. Yuan Ang adopted Yuan Zhong's strategy, and the King of Wu treated him favorably. Yuan Ang took leave and went home. He met Prime Minister Shen Tujia on the road and got out of the car to worship him. The prime minister only expressed his gratitude to Yuan Ang from the car. When Yuan An returned home, he felt ashamed in front of his subordinates, so he went to the Prime Minister's residence to send a name card and asked to see the Prime Minister. It took a long time for Cheng to meet Yuan Ang. Yuan Ang knelt down and said, "I hope to receive you alone." The prime minister said: If what you are talking about is a public matter, go to the official office to discuss it with the official, and I will report your opinions. If it is a private matter, I will not accept private requests. Yuan Ang knelt down and persuaded him: "As the prime minister, you can weigh it yourself. How do you compare to Chen Ping and Jianghou?" The prime minister said: I can't compare. Yuan Ang said: Yes, you think you can't compare.
