This year, six financial and economic management systems were reaffirmed. Every time a management system is issued, laws and regulations must be set up to prevent it. Those who violate it may even be executed for the most serious crimes. Officials and civilians are punished for more crimes. He also levied a tax on all those who kept slaves and slaves, each slave had to pay 3,600 yuan. The people of the world became more resentful and thieves rose up. Nayan and Feng Chang advised him on the six management systems. Wang Mang was furious and removed Feng Chang from his official position. Set up law enforcement on the left and law enforcement on the right. Select capable officials, Hou Baren, to supervise the Sixth Lieutenant and the Sixth Team respectively. Their powers are like the governors of the Han Dynasty, and they will accompany one person from each county to handle relevant matters.
target: In the fourth year of his reign, Wang Mang granted titles and rewards to several officials, including Lu Ta and Xian Zhi, who received the rank of special advance and were treated with the same etiquette as the three princes. He also awarded them houses, money, and ceremonial items. In June, he formally enfeoffed princes at the Mingtang, claiming he had spent nearly nine years planning the land system and feudal hierarchy based on classical texts. However, Wang Mang was known for his empty rhetoric and stinginess, using the undetermined land plan as an excuse to delay actual implementation while granting symbolic titles to appease those who desired rank. Wang Mang reaffirmed six financial management systems, establishing harsh laws with punishments including execution for violations. He levied taxes on slave owners, requiring 3,600 yuan per slave, which caused widespread resentment and led to the rise of bandits. When officials like Nayan and Feng Chang advised against these policies, Wang Mang removed them from office. He appointed law enforcement officers with powers similar to Han dynasty governors to supervise the six systems.

source: Nayan and Feng Chang advised him on the six management systems. Wang Mang was furious and removed Feng Chang from his official position. Set up law enforcement on the left and law enforcement on the right. Select capable officials, Hou Baren, to supervise the Sixth Lieutenant and the Sixth Team respectively. Their powers are like the governors of the Han Dynasty, and they will accompany one person from each county to handle relevant matters. Guatianyi and others from Linhuai County acted as thieves and occupied Changzhouyuan, the capital of Kuaiji County. Lu Mu, a woman from Langxie County, also started to rebel. At first, Lu's mother's son was a county official and was unjustly killed by the county magistrate. Lu's mother used her family's property to buy wine, meat, and weapons. She secretly treated poor young men and gained more than a hundred people, then attacked Haiqu County, killed the county magistrate and went to worship her son's grave. Then she led her troops to the sea, and her team gradually grew, eventually totaling tens of thousands of people.
target: Rebellions erupted across the country, including Guatianyi's occupation of Changzhouyuan and Lu Mu's uprising in Langxie County, where a woman whose son was unjustly killed by a county magistrate gathered followers, attacked Haiqu County, and eventually commanded tens of thousands of troops.

source: Liu Xin in Jiangzhong became an enemy and avenged his grievances. He wanted to restore and inherit the cause of his ancestors and sent troops in the Four Years Congress. There is a big thief in the rivers and lakes. He calls himself King Fan and his surname is Liu. Tens of thousands of people have gathered in groups. They do not accept the order of pardon and want to shake Chang'an and Luoyang. In the eleventh year, there will be an attack. The Taibai Star shines brightly and the Sui Star enters Dongjing Su. His orders should be carried out. It also explains that the good and bad fortunes of Wang Mang's ministers have their own dates. It was compiled into more than 100,000 words. Li Yan asked his subordinates to copy the book, but the subordinates escaped and reported him. Wang Mang sent envoys to arrest Li Yan on the spot, handed him over to judicial officials for trial, and was executed. When thieves broke out in Sanfu District, they set up the official post of Captain of the Thief Catcher, and asked law enforcers to pursue the thieves in the suburbs of Chang'an. They set up alarm flags that sounded drums to attack the thieves, and envoys followed them to supervise.
target: Wang Mang's envoys reported that thieves dispersed but regrouped due to harsh prohibitions, heavy taxes, and the inability of people to make a living. Wang Mang dismissed officials who reported these truths and promoted those who flattered him.

source: The income from hard work is not enough to pay taxes. If you keep the door closed and stay safe, you will be implicated by your neighbors who secretly mint money and hide copper, and the traitors will use it to blackmail the people. The people had no choice but to turn into thieves. Wang Mang was furious and removed them from their official positions. Some of them followed his intention and said that the rebellious people were arrogant and cunning and should be punished. They also said that the fate of the people was like this and they would soon be eliminated. Wang Mang was happy and always promoted them. In August of this year, Wang Mang personally went to the southern suburbs to create a powerful force. Weidou was made of copper mixed with five-color stones. It was shaped like a Big Dipper and was two feet and five inches long. It was intended to be used to intimidate various peasant armies. The mighty battle was forged, and Siming was asked to carry it. When Wang Mang went out, it was in front of him, and when Wang Mang entered the palace, he put it next to him. On the day when Wei Dou was cast, the weather was extremely cold, and hundreds of officials and horses froze to death. On the first day of the first lunar month of the fifth year, a fire broke out at the south gate of the Northern Army camp. The Grand Sima Sima Yun Fei Xing was appointed as the shepherd of Jingzhou. Wang Mang met him and asked him about his plans after taking office. Fei Xing replied: Most of the people in Jingzhou and Yangzhou rely on the mountains, forests and lakes, and use fishing and woodcutting as their occupations. Some time ago, the country implemented the six-management system and levied taxes on mountains, forests, lakes and swamps, which harmed and deprived the people of their interests. Coupled with successive years of drought, the people were hungry and poor, so they became thieves. After I arrived at my post, I wanted to order the thieves to return home, loan them farm tools, cattle, seeds, and grain, and reduce or exempt them from taxes, hoping to disband and appease them. Wang Mang became angry and dismissed Fei Xing from his official position. Officials all over the country sought illegal profits one after another because they could not get their salaries. The property of the county chiefs and governors accumulated thousands of gold.
target: In August, he forged a copper weapon shaped like the Big Dipper to intimidate peasant armies, but during its casting, extreme cold killed many officials and horses. Fires broke out at the Northern Army camp, and when newly appointed officials like Fei Xing suggested lenient policies to address the root causes of rebellion, Wang Mang dismissed them. Officials across the country sought illegal profits due to unpaid salaries, amassing fortunes.

source: Wang Mang wrote a letter to Shao saying: After a thorough investigation of the Huns' invasion of the Central Plains in the second year of the founding of the People's Republic of China, all military officers and border officials who have made illegal profits and increased their property and made a fortune will have four-fifths of their family property confiscated to support the urgent needs of border defense. Government officials traveled all over the country in carriages, carefully examining corruption cases, mobilizing officers to report on their generals, and slaves to report on their masters. They hoped to use this method to suppress evil, but the evil became more and more serious. The emperor's grandson Gong Chonggong Wang Zong drew a portrait of himself, wearing the emperor's clothes and the emperor's crown, and engraved three seals: the first is "Wei Zhi Guan, Cun Ji Xia, Nanshan, Hidden by Thin Ice", the second is "Su Sheng Bao Ji", and the third is "De Feng Chang Tu". In addition, Wang Zong's uncle Lu Kuan's family was exiled to Hepu County, and he secretly contacted Wang Zong. After being discovered, Wang Zong committed suicide after investigation and verification. Wang Mang said: Wang Zong's kinship is that of the emperor's grandson, and his title is that of Grand Duke. He knew that Lu Kuan and others were rebels, so he tried to associate with them. He engraved three steel seals. The meaning of the seals is very sneaky, not satisfied, and coveting undue hope.
target: Wang Mang's grandson Wang Zong was discovered drawing himself in imperial regalia and engraving seals with rebellious inscriptions. After investigation, Wang Zong committed suicide, and his sister Wang Zhi also died after being implicated in murder and witchcraft.

source: He's moody like this. Appoint Zhidaohou Wangshe as the general of the guard. Wang She is the son of Quyanghou Wanggen. Wang Gen served as Chief Sima during the reign of Emperor Cheng and once recommended Wang Mang to succeed him. Wang Mang was grateful to him and thought that Quyang was not a good name, so he followed Wang Gen as Zhidao and let Wang She inherit his title. This year, the Red Eyebrow Army Li Zidu, Fan Chong and others gathered together due to famine, and started an uprising in Langxie County. They looted everywhere, with a total of ten thousand troops. Wang Mang sent envoys to mobilize local troops to attack them, but they could not win. In the spring of the sixth year, Wang Mang saw that there were many thieves, so he asked Taishi to calculate the outline of the calendar for 36,000 years. He changed the year name every six years and announced it to the whole country. The following report says: "Purple He Tu" says: Taiyi and Huangdi both became gods and ascended to heaven, playing fairy music on Qianshan Mountain in Kunlun Mountains. The wise emperors whose descendants have gained auspiciousness should play fairy music on Zhongnan Mountain in Qin. I wasn't smart enough to follow it consciously, and I didn't understand it until now. Then General Ningshi was called General Gengshi. It means obeying the destiny. Didn't the "Book of Changes" say it? It is said that renewal is excellent moral character. In the process of movement and change, new things are constantly produced, which is called Yi. I will enjoy this happiness! I want to use this method to dazzle the people and eliminate thieves. Everyone laughed at these practices.
target: The Red Eyebrow Army, led by Li Zidu and Fan Chong, began their uprising in Langxie County due to famine, gathering ten thousand troops. Wang Mang's attempts to suppress them failed. In the sixth year, Wang Mang calculated a 36,000-year calendar and changed the year name, claiming to follow divine instructions, but people laughed at these practices.

source: I will enjoy this happiness! I want to use this method to dazzle the people and eliminate thieves. Everyone laughed at these practices. For the first time, he presented "Xin Yue" to Mingtang and Ancestral Temple. Ministers began to wear buckskin hats. Someone heard the melody of the music and said: It is sad, serious and low, not the music to revitalize the country. At this time, the Kanto region suffered from drought and famine for several consecutive years, and the number of tribes such as Lizidu gradually increased. Gengshi general Lian Dan failed to win in Yizhou and was recalled. After the restoration, he sent Guo Xing, the Great Sima Protector, and Li Bi, the Yongbu Mu Li Bi, to attack the tribal leader Ruodou and others, and sent Taifu Xishu Shi Sun Xi to pacify the thieves in various places. At the same time, the Xiongnu invaded the border very severely. Wang Mang then recruited a large number of strong men from all over the country, as well as condemned criminals and domestic slaves of officials and civilians. He named them Zhutu Xiyong and used them as elite soldiers. All fees were collected from officials and civilians across the country, one-thirtieth of the estimated property was taken, and all silk and silk were transported to Chang'an. Officials from the ministerial level to the county officials wearing yellow seals were ordered to maintain military horses. The number of horses was determined according to each person's salary. He also extensively recruited specialized talents who had unique skills that could be used to attack the Xiongnu, and planned to hire them by upgrading their positions. There are tens of thousands of people who suggest things that are beneficial to the country: some say that you can cross rivers without boats and connect people and horses, and you can cross an army of millions; some say that you don’t need to carry a bucket of grain, but just take medicine, and the army will not be hungry; some say that you can fly, flying a thousand miles a day, to spy on the Huns. Wang Mang asked him to try it. The man made two wings from the feathers of a big bird, attached feathers to his head and body, and wrapped them with ring ties all over his body. After flying a few hundred steps, they fell off. Wang Mang knew that they could not be used, so he insisted on gaining the reputation of cherishing talents, so he appointed them all as commanders, rewarded them with chariots and horses, and waited for their departure.
target: The Kanto region suffered from drought and famine for consecutive years, causing rebel numbers to grow. Wang Mang recruited strong men, condemned criminals, and slaves to form elite troops, collecting one-thirtieth of property from officials and civilians to fund military campaigns. He also recruited specialists with unique skills to attack the Xiongnu, including a man who claimed to be able to fly but only managed a few hundred steps before falling. Wang Mang appointed them all as commanders despite knowing their claims were false.

source: Dong Zhong, the descendant of Fu Bo, was appointed as the Grand Sima. The Yiping County Company led the field report to the county. The county's estimate of the people's property was untrue, and Wang Mang levied it at one-thirtieth. Thinking that Tian Kuang was loyal and caring about the country, he promoted his title to earl and rewarded him with two million yuan. The general public cursed him. Many people in Qingzhou and Xuzhou abandoned their homes and fled. The old and weak died on the road, while the strong joined the ranks of thieves.
target: Wang Mang's policies led to widespread suffering. People abandoned their homes, the old and weak died on roadsides, and the strong joined thieves.

source: Wang Mang heard this and resented Han Bo. He asked Ju Guuba to stay in Xinfeng County where he was located, and changed his surname to Ju Mu, which meant that thanks to the birth of this person, Queen Mother Wen, this was the destiny that made him the overlord. Put Han Bo in jail, thinking that those words were not what he should say, and put him to death. In the second year, the year name was changed to Emperor of the Earth, which was based on the outline of the 36,000-year calendar. On the last day of the first lunar month of the first year of the Earth Emperor's reign, a nationwide amnesty was announced. The following report said: When the troops are marching, anyone who dares to run around and make noise and violate the law will be beheaded. Do not wait until the execution season. This order will be implemented until the end of the year. So in the spring and summer, people were killed in the city, and the people were terrified. When they met on the road, they only looked at each other and did not dare to talk. On Renshen Day in February, the sky was dark when the sun was at its peak. Wang Mang hated this phenomenon and reported below: Some time ago, there was darkness, the Yin energy invaded the Yang energy, and the black energy caused disasters. The people were all surprised. Wang Kuang, the general of Zhaoyu, sent his subordinates to pursue the person who reported the abnormal accident in order to cover up the emperor's ears and eyes. Therefore, he was condemned from heaven and should be punished by law to remedy such a catastrophe.
target: Officials like Han Bo tried to ridicule Wang Mang with absurd reports, but Wang Mang executed them. He changed the year name to Emperor of the Earth and issued harsh decrees allowing executions even in spring and summer, terrifying the people. When natural disasters occurred, Wang Mang blamed his officials rather than his own policies.

source: Wang Mang sent the Sangong officials to arrest and pursue their party members. Thousands of authority figures in various counties and counties were implicated, and they were all executed. Granted Wang Dan the title of auxiliary prince. Since Wang Mang's measures were out of season and the people were resentful, Wang Mang was still content with this situation. He continued to report: Since the formulation of such expedient laws, Chang'an has become the central city of the six major counties. The sound of alarm drums has become less frequent, the number of thieves has weakened, and the people have settled in the countryside. As a result, there has been a bumper harvest. This is the effect of adopting expedient measures.
target: The rebellion continued to spread, with various leaders emerging across the country. Wang Mang's attempts to suppress them through military force and harsh laws only worsened the situation. His officials grew increasingly fearful, and the people's suffering intensified.

source: Later, he promoted Wang Mang's replacement of the Han Dynasty, and Shentu Jian asked Prime Minister Liu Ci to kill Cui Fa to show the public. Shi Chen, Wang Yan, Wang Lin, Wang Wu and Zhao Hong also surrendered and were killed. At first, everyone in the troops who established their own names wanted to be granted the title of marquis. Shen Tujian had not only killed Wang Xian, but also threatened that the people in the Sanfu area were cunning and killed his monarch together. Therefore, the officials and civilians in the Sanfu area became frightened, and the counties under their jurisdiction gathered troops to separate themselves. Shen Tujian and others failed to capture it, so they sent flying horses to report to Gengshi Emperor. In February of the second year of Gengshi, Emperor Gengshi came to Chang'an and issued an edict announcing a general amnesty. As long as they were not Wang Mang's children, everyone else would be pardoned for their crimes, so the Wang family could be preserved. All the Sanfu areas were pacified, and Emperor Gengshi made his capital Chang'an and lived in Changle Palace. The treasury was intact, except for the Weiyang palace fire that attacked Wang Mang for three days. Once Wang Mang died, he settled down and returned to his original state. After the arrival of Emperor Gengshi, it took more than a year for the political education to be implemented throughout the country. In the summer of the next year, hundreds of thousands of people from the Red Eyebrow Army, Fan Chong and others entered Hangu Pass, supported Liu Penzi as emperor, and attacked Emperor Gengshi, who surrendered to them. The Red Eyebrow Army burned the palaces and streets of Chang'an and killed Emperor Gengshi. The people were starving to the point of cannibalism, and hundreds of thousands of people died. The city of Chang'an was in ruins, and no one walked in the city. All the ancestral temples and tombs of the ancestors of the Han Dynasty have been excavated, but only Du Ling and Ba Ling are still intact. In June, King Shizu ascended the throne, and then the state power was re-established and the country was at peace.
target: The Han dynasty eventually revived under Emperor Gengshi, who captured Chang'an and executed Wang Mang's supporters. The Red Eyebrow Army later overthrew Emperor Gengshi, causing further destruction, until Emperor Shizu restored order and peace to the realm.

source: Da'a, Youfu, Da Sikong, and Wei generals Guangyang Hou Zhenfeng were appointed as Gengshi generals and were granted the title of Guangxin Gong; Wang Xing from Jingzhao Yin was appointed as the Wei general and was granted the title of Xingong; General Qingche Cheng Wuhou Sun Jian was appointed as the founding general and was granted the title of Xingong; Wang Sheng from Jingzhao Yin was appointed as the former general and was granted the title of Chongxin Gong: these are the four generals. Others with the same name were awarded the title of Langguan. On this day, a total of several hundred people were awarded the official positions of minister, minister, and minister. It is responsible for realizing the right amount of rain at the right time, the light of cyan nourishing all things and the equal growth, and paying attention to the sun's shadow and sun rules.

source: At that time, King Wu of Zhou attacked King Zhou of Shang, destroyed the Shang Dynasty, and moved the Nine Tripods, which symbolized state power, from the Shang capital to Luoyi. Boyi and Shuqi believed that King Wu was unfaithful and unfilial, so they ate Zhou millet in shame and starved to death in Shouyang Mountain. Even the people of Zhou praised them for their noble moral character. Confucius thought the two of them were virtuous and praised them for not changing their ambitions and not allowing themselves to be humiliated. Mencius also said: Hearing Boyi's demeanor is enough to make greedy people honest and cowardly people to establish their ambitions; to inspire behavior before a hundred generations, everyone after a hundred generations will be deeply inspired. Who can do this if he is not a sage? After the rise of the Han Dynasty, there were Yuan Gong, Qili Ji, Xia Huang Gong and Mr. Jiao Li. When the Qin Dynasty ruled the world, these four people fled to the depths of Shangluo Mountain and waited for the world to be peaceful. Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty heard about it and summoned them, but they did not come. Later, Empress Lu adopted the strategy of leaving Zhang Liang behind, and asked the crown prince to bring silk fabrics, bow down and greet him with humility, and use a small car to welcome him to her side to assist her. After the four arrived, they followed the prince to see Gaozu. Gaozu respected them and treated them as honored guests. From this, the prince was taken seriously and his position was stabilized. This incident is recorded in detail in "The Biography of Liuhou". Later, there was Zheng Zizhen in the mouth of the valley, and there was a strict gentleman in Shu. They were able to cultivate themselves and respect themselves, not wearing what they shouldn't wear, and not eating what they shouldn't eat. When Emperor Cheng of the Han Dynasty was in power, his uncle and general Wang Feng recruited Zizhen with courtesy, but Zizhen did not accept the call and ended up not yielding. A gentleman was doing divination in the Chengdu market. He thought: Although divination is a humble profession, it can benefit everyone. If someone inquires about something evil or unfair, tell him the pros and cons according to the yarrow and the shell of a tortoise. The divination for a son is based on the principles of filial piety; the divination for a younger brother is based on the principle of obedience; the divination for a minister is based on the idea of ​​loyalty to the king. In this way, we can take advantage of the situation and guide different people towards the good side. More than half of the people obey my words. He only receives a few people every day. When he can earn a hundred yuan to survive, he closes the stall and teaches "Laozi" at home. He also read a lot of various books and became proficient in them all. According to the theories of Laozi and Zhuangzhou, he wrote more than 100,000 words of books. Yang Xiong studied with him when he was young, and later became an official in the capital and became famous. He repeatedly praised Yan Junping's conduct to the virtuous officials in the court. Li Qiang, a native of Duling, had always been very good with Yang Xiong. Later he became an official and became a shepherd in Yizhou. He happily said to Yang Xiong: Now I really want to get King Yan Zhou. Hexiong said: You have to treat him with courtesy. He is a person who can be seen and cannot be used by others. Li Qiang disagreed in his heart. After he took office in Shu, he met Junping with courtesy, but he still dared not bring up the matter of calling him as an official, so he sighed: "Yang Ziyun really understands people!" Yan Junping lived to be more than ninety years old, and he continued to work on divination and fortune-telling until his death. People in Shu loved and respected him, and they still praise him to this day. Later, Yang Xiong wrote a book about the people of the world, praising these two people in particular. He commented: There is a world: a gentleman is afraid that he will live his whole life without a name, so why not use the power of a famous minister to achieve his name? I believe that if a gentleman accumulates his own virtues, his reputation will be established. Liang, Qi, Chu, Zhao and other princes and kings are not without wealth and honor, but what do they use to achieve their reputation? Gu Zhengzi really persevered in his ambition and worked under the rocks, but his reputation spread throughout the capital. Is it because he was a public official?
target: King Wu of Zhou overthrew King Zhou of Shang, moving the Nine Tripods to Luoyi. Boyi and Shuqi, deeming King Wu unfaithful and unfilial, starved to death on Shouyang Mountain rather than eat Zhou grain, earning praise for their moral purity. Confucius lauded their unwavering resolve, and Mencius declared that hearing of Boyi’s conduct could reform the greedy and cowardly, inspiring generations. After the Han rose, four recluses—Yuan Gong, Qili Ji, Xia Huang Gong, and Mr. Jiaoli—fled to Shangluo Mountain during Qin rule. Emperor Gaozu summoned them in vain, but Empress Lu, following Zhang Liang’s strategy, had the crown prince humbly invite them with gifts. Their presence stabilized the prince’s position, as recorded in the *Biography of the Marquis of Liu*. Later, Zheng Zizhen of Gu Valley and Yan Junping of Shu cultivated self-respect, refusing improper attire or food. Zheng Zizhen declined recruitment by General Wang Feng. Yan Junping, a diviner in Chengdu, used his trade to guide people toward filial piety, obedience, and loyalty, earning a modest living before teaching Laozi. He authored over 100,000 words on Daoist philosophy. Yang Xiong, who studied under him, praised his conduct to officials, noting that Yan could be seen but not employed. Yan lived past ninety, revered by the people of Shu. Yang Xiong later wrote that a gentleman’s virtue establishes his reputation, contrasting the wealth of princes with the enduring fame of recluses like Zheng Zizhen and Yan Junping, whom he deemed national treasures.

source: For example, Wang Ji, Gong Yu, and Liang Gong all knew how to be courteous and courteous when going out to serve and when they retired. Wang Ji, courtesy name Ziyang, was born in Langxie, Gao and Yu. He was eager to learn when he was young and was proficient in classics. He first served as a county official. He was elected as a Lang due to his filial piety and integrity, filling the position of Lu Youcheng, and later he was appointed as the Yunyang County Magistrate. Ju Xianliang was appointed as the lieutenant of Changyi. The king of Changyi liked hunting and often drove horses galloping in the country. His behavior was uncontrolled. target: Wang Ji (Ziyang) of Langxie excelled in classics, serving as a county official and later as lieutenant of Changyi. source: Wang Ji then excused himself to feel unwell and returned to his hometown of Langye. When Wang Ji was young, he studied and lived in Chang'an City. Their food, clothing, housing, and transportation are all very particular and outstanding, but they do not have gold, silver, brocade, and other items. Every time we moved, all the car carried was a bag of spare clothes. They don't store excess belongings. When he left his official home, he also lived in common people's clothing and ate vegetarian food. People all over the world admired their honesty, but they were very surprised that they were so particular about food, clothing, carriages and horses. Therefore, it was said among the people that "Wang Yang could turn gold". Gongyu, courtesy name Shaoweng, was born in Langxie. target: Wang Ji taught the Five Classics and died en route to a summons from Emperor Yuan. Talented people were appointed, Only a tax equivalent to one-tenth of the people's income is collected. Apart from this, there are no other taxes or labor and border guards. A thousand miles away, the emperor determines a certain type and quantity based on their production, so that they can pay tribute on time.

From the senior officials of various states in the Spring and Autumn Period to the generals, ministers and ministers since the rise of Han Dynasty, how many people have missed their official positions, indulged in favors and favors, and have lost the moral integrity of the world! Therefore, those with high moral character are extremely rare. However, most people can only govern themselves but cannot govern others. Talents like Wang Ji and Gong Yu are far superior to Gong Sheng, Gong She and Bao Xuan. By adhering to the good path until death, Gong Sheng truly practiced the way of a saint. Consistent and intelligent, Xue Fang's words and deeds are close to those of a saint. Guo Qin and Jiang Yi avoided chaos and did not taint their integrity. When the emperor traveled, Hou and Sima, as the forerunners, had to give memorials first, and this was institutionalized from then on. Kuanrao was appointed as Sima Chu. He did not leave the palace gate, cut his single coat short so that it could leave the ground, wore a big hat, and carried a long sword. He personally visited the soldiers' houses, inspected their diet and daily life, personally comforted and asked the sick soldiers, gave them medicine, and treated them very kindly. When the shift was handed over at the end of the year, the emperor personally rewarded the retired soldiers. Thousands of soldiers kowtowed and asked to stay and serve for another year to repay the generous kindness.

source: Emperor Xuan commended him for his kindness, appointed him as Taizhong doctor, and asked him to inspect the customs of various places. He commended, recommended, demoted, and deposed many people, and completed the mission in line with the emperor's wishes. Therefore, he was promoted to the rank of Sili Xiaowei, and he was able to inspect and expose the mistakes of officials without hesitation. Small and big matters were reported to the public, and many people were impeached. The Tingwei dealt with them according to the law, and half of his opinions were adopted and half were not adopted. However, the ministers, nobles, and officials of the county and state who were envoys to Chang'an were all too afraid to violate the ban, and the capital was peaceful. When Ping Enhou Xu Bo moved into his new residence, all the prime ministers, censors, generals, and officials with a salary of two thousand dan went to congratulate him, but Kuan Rao did not go. Uncle Xu invited him, so he went up to the hall from the west steps and sat alone facing the east. Uncle Xu poured him wine himself and said: "You are late." Kuanrao said: Don't pour more wine for me. I'll go crazy if I drink too much. Prime Minister Wei Hou smiled and said: "You are a little crazy when you are awake. Why do you have to drink?" Everyone present looked at him with contempt. When the wine was in full swing, the music started playing. Tan Changqing, the young master of Changxin, got up and danced, performing a monkey and dog fight, and everyone present laughed. Kuangrao was unhappy, looked up at the roof and sighed, "How beautiful!" However, wealth is impermanent, and everything changes in a blink of an eye. When the owner changes, the building becomes like a hotel. I have seen it a lot. Only by being cautious can we maintain our long-term success. How could you not be vigilant? So he stood up and walked out quickly, impeaching Changxin Shaofu to perform the monkey dance as a minister, which was disrespectful. The emperor wanted to punish the young master, but Xu Bo apologized for him. After a long time, the emperor stopped pursuing the case. Kuan Rao is an upright person with high integrity and determination to serve the court. His family was poor, and his monthly salary was several thousand, half of which was used to pay for the officials and common people who investigated and reported the situation for him.
target: Emperor Xuan promoted him to Sili Xiaowei, where he fearlessly investigated officials, creating peace in the capital. At a celebration for Xu Bo's new residence, Kuanrao sat apart and warned about the impermanence of wealth. He later impeached a performer for disrespectful dancing. Despite his integrity and poverty—using half his salary to pay informants—his harshness and tendency to frame others created enemies. Wang Sheng advised him to be more cautious, but Kuanrao ignored this counsel.

source: At this time, the emperor was governing the country with criminal laws. The intruders who have been punished by castration are regarded as the Duke of Zhou summoning the public, and the law is regarded as the "Book of Poetry". It also quoted the "Han Shi Yi Zhuan" as saying: The five emperors regarded the world as the commonwealth, the three kings regarded the world as the family, passed on the world as the family to their descendants, and regarded the world as the commonwealth to pass on to the virtuous. Just like the movement of the four seasons, those who have accomplished something will leave, and those who are not the right person will no longer be in their place. After sending the seal to the emperor, the emperor thought that he had not repented after all, so he handed over his memorial to Zhong Erqianshi. At that time, Zhi Jinwu commented that Lenon's intention was to ask the emperor to abdicate, which was treason. Zheng Chang, the admonishing doctor, had pity on Gen Geng, was loyal, upright and concerned about state affairs. Because his discussion of state affairs was not in line with the emperor's wishes, he was slandered and slandered by the officials who were eloquent. So he wrote a letter to praise Gen Geng and said: I heard that there are ferocious beasts in the mountains, so tribulations are not picked; the country has loyal ministers, so treacherous people dare not rise up.
target: He submitted a memorial criticizing the emperor's reliance on eunuchs and suggesting that rulers should yield to the worthy. The emperor deemed this treasonous. Despite Zheng Chang's defense, Kuanrao was imprisoned and committed suicide.

source: The emperor refused to obey, so he handed over mercy to the jailer. Kuanrao drew his sword and committed suicide at the foot of the North Tower. People all pitied him. Zhuge Feng, whose courtesy name was Shaoji, was from Langxie. Because he was proficient in classics, he took charge of the county's literature and was famous for his independence, strength and integrity. Gong Yu was the imperial censor. He appointed Zhuge Feng as a subordinate official, and later recommended him to serve as the censor. Emperor Yuan promoted him to the position of Sili Xiaowei, and he was able to avoid any investigation or prosecution. People in the capital made up a sentence for him: Why haven't we seen each other for a long time? It's just because I met Zhuge. The emperor commended him for his integrity and awarded him the title of Doctor Guanglu. At that time, Xu Zhang, the servant, was honored and favored by virtue of his status as a relative. He was extravagant and did not abide by the law. One of his retainers committed an offense and was implicated in Xu Zhang. Zhuge Feng investigated Xu Zhang in accordance with the law and wanted to report his case. He happened to meet Xu Shizhong going out privately. Zhuge Feng stopped the car, raised the talisman in his hand and ordered Xu Zhang: "Come down!" Want to arrest him. Xu Zhang was embarrassed and drove away, with Zhuge Feng chasing him behind. Xu Shizhong was then able to enter the palace gate and beg for mercy from the emperor. Zhuge Feng also submitted a memorial, and at that time the emperor confiscated Zhuge Feng's talisman. Sili's cancellation of the Talisman Festival began with Zhuge Feng.
target: Zhuge Feng, from Langxie, became Sili Xiaowei under Emperor Yuan. He attempted to arrest the favored relative Xu Zhang but was thwarted when Xu fled to the palace. The emperor confiscated Zhuge's talisman, ending the Sili's traditional authority. Zhuge apologized in a memorial but continued criticizing corrupt officials.

source: The emperor did not allow it. After that, what he said was less and less accepted, and Zhuge Feng wrote again: I heard that Boqi was filial but was abandoned by his parents, Zixu was loyal but was killed by the king, Yin Gong was kind but was killed by his younger brother, Shuwu respected his elder brother but was killed by his elder brother. With the virtues of these four people and Qu Yuan's talents, he still couldn't let himself show off and was killed instead. Isn't that enough of a lesson? If I can give my life to stabilize the country and be killed to bring glory to the king, I am really willing to do it. I'm afraid that it will not be beneficial to the country, but will be squeezed out by some evil forces, allowing those who blindly speak ill of people behind their backs and frame others to succeed. The path of upright people will be blocked, loyal ministers will be cold-hearted, and wise people will be silenced. This is what I am afraid of. Zhuge Feng arrested and punished prisoners in spring and summer, and many people in power spoke ill of him. The emperor transferred Zhuge Feng to serve as the city gate captain. Zhuge Feng wrote a letter to accuse Guanglu Xun Zhou Kan and Guanglu doctor Zhang Meng. The emperor thought that Zhuge Feng was wrong, so he issued an edict to the censor: Zhuge Feng, the captain of the city gate school, once worked with Guanglu Xun Zhou Kan and Guanglu doctor Zhang Meng in the court. He praised the merits of Zhou Kan and Zhang Meng many times. Zhuge Feng, a former Sili school captain, did not follow the seasons or follow the rule of law, but specialized in harsh cruelty, thus gaining false prestige. I could not bear to hand him over to the jailer, so I asked him to serve as the city gate school captain. Instead of introspecting, he instead resented Zhou Kan and Zhang Meng, seeking revenge. His words of conviction had no evidence, he exposed crimes that were difficult to verify, and he relied solely on subjective wishes to slander and praise others, regardless of what he had said before. This was a serious act of not being trustworthy. I pity Zhuge Feng that he is old and cannot bear to impose punishment, so I order him to be removed from his official position and become a commoner. Zhuge Feng died at home.
target: He was transferred to city gate captain after arresting prisoners in spring and summer. When he accused former colleagues, the emperor removed him from office for untrustworthiness, and he died at home.

source: Liu Fu is a member of the royal family of Hejian Kingdom. He was promoted to Xiaolian and served as the county magistrate of Xiangbi. He wrote a memorial to discuss the gains and losses of national affairs, and was summoned by the emperor. The emperor appreciated his talents and promoted him to the position of admonishing doctor. Just in time when Emperor Cheng wanted to make Tang Jiandan his queen, he first issued an edict to confer the title of prince to Lin, the envoy's father.
target: Liu Fu, a royal family member, became an admonishing doctor under Emperor Cheng. He opposed making Tang Jiandan queen, arguing it defied divine will.

source: However, within ten days, he was arrested and imprisoned in a secret prison. If there are major crimes, they should be handed over to judicial officials for public trial, so that everyone can know his crimes and punish him together. Once upon a time, Confucius went to Jianzi to kill his doctor Mingdu. Confucius walked to the Yellow River and returned. Nowadays, God's will is not happy, disasters are coming frequently, and floods and droughts are coming one after another. It is the time to be generous, solicit opinions widely, and praise integrity to maximize the power of the people. However, he carried out tragic and sudden executions on ministers who dared to remonstrate, which shocked everyone and chilled the hearts of loyal and upright people. If Liu Fu did not commit a crime because he spoke out and dared to remonstrate, then no one in the world would know about the crime he committed if he did not publicly announce it. A minister who has the same surname as the emperor and is close to the emperor originally gained high status because he dared to tell the truth. From the perspective of dealing with relatives and protecting loyal people, he should not be secretly imprisoned in Yeting Prison.

source: The emperor then moved and imprisoned Liu Fu to the imperial prison under the control of the Shaofu, reduced the death penalty to one degree, and sentenced him to hard labor in the ancestral temple. He is always at home. Zheng Chong, also known as Ziyou, originally belonged to a wealthy family in Gaomi Kingdom and had been intermarrying with the Wang family for generations. My grandfather moved to Pingling because he had money. His father, Zheng Bin, was well versed in laws, served as a royal censor, and served Duke Gong. He was known for his fairness and uprightness. Zheng Chong served as the literary historian of the county when he was young, and later became a chariot attendant in the Prime Minister's Mansion. His younger brother Zheng Li and Gao Wuhou Fu Xi studied under the same teacher and were friendly to each other. When Fu happy became the Grand Sima, he recommended Zheng Chong, and Emperor Ai promoted him to the position of Minister of Public Affairs. He asked to see the emperor several times to remonstrate, and the emperor initially accepted his opinions. Every time he saw him dragging his rawhide shoes, the emperor smiled and said: I can hear Zheng Shangshu's footsteps. After a long time, the emperor wanted to knight Fu Shang, the cousin of his grandmother, the Empress Dowager Fu. Zheng Chongjin advised him: Emperor Xiaocheng made five of his uncles marquis. As a result, the sky turned red and yellow, the daytime became dim, and there was black energy in the sun. Now your grandmother's two cousins ​​have become marquises.
target: Zheng Chong served under Emperor Ai, known for his distinctive leather shoes. He opposed ennobling Fu Shang, the emperor's grandmother's cousin, citing precedents where such actions caused celestial disturbances. Despite the Empress Dowager's anger, Zheng persisted. He also criticized Dong Xian's excessive favor.

source: Zheng Chong also remonstrated with the emperor because Dong Xian was too favored by the nobles, and therefore committed a serious crime. source: Zhi Ji had many ears and eyes. After hearing about the incident, he closed the door and refused to interact with people outside. He dug through the wall behind the house to open a small door and only managed the garden with a hoe. He stated these situations himself through people who had close connections with Hou Wen. Hou Wen said: "Zhiji and I are fortunate to be from the same hometown. We usually don't even have a small quarrel. We just accepted the order of the prefect. My duty should be to punish you." If you can truly correct your mistakes, I will no longer pursue the past. If you don't change your mind and just change your appearance, it will only accelerate the arrival of disaster. Zhiji finally did not dare to break the law again, and Sun Bao did not punish others throughout the year. The next year, Zhiji fell ill and died. Sun Bao served as Jing Zhaoyin for three years, and people in the capital praised him. When Chunyu Chang fell, Sun Bao, Xiao Yu and others were implicated and were dismissed from office. Hou Wen also left his official position again and died at home. Zhiji's son Du Cang, also known as Jun Ao, was more famous among the knights than Ji Ji. When Emperor Ai came to the throne, he recruited Sun Shi as an admonishing official, and was later promoted to Sili. At first, Empress Dowager Fu and Empress Dowager Feng, the mother of Prince Xiao of Zhongshan, served Emperor Yuan together. There was a rift between the two. Empress Dowager Fu sent officials in charge to torture Empress Dowager Feng and forced her to commit suicide. People all thought she was wronged. Sun Bao submitted a memorial requesting for investigation. Empress Dowager Fu was furious and said: The emperor set up a secretary and sent an envoy to interrogate me. The fact of Feng's rebellion is very clear, and some people deliberately want to find fault with me. I want him to sit down together. The emperor then followed the Queen Mother Fu's order and put Sun Bao in prison. Shangshu Pushe Tang Lin argued the matter. The emperor believed that Tang Lin had formed a clique for personal gain and demoted him to the post of Dunhuang Yuzezhan Marquis. Grand Sima Fu happy and Guanglu Doctor Gong Sheng persisted in their efforts, and the emperor interceded on their behalf with the Queen Mother, and then Sun Bao was released and his official position was restored. Soon after, Zheng Chong was imprisoned. I am fortunate to be able to accept the mission and have the responsibility of prosecuting and reporting. I dare not avoid the power of the powerful and favored people to block the emperor's hearing and hearing so that the emperor does not know the true situation. Shangshu Lingchang falsely accused his servant of shooting Zheng Chong and put him in prison for investigation and investigation. Zheng Chong was tortured to death. As a result, he did not give a confession. Even passers-by on the road said that he was unjustly accused.
target: Sun Bao served as Yizhou governor, quelling rebellions by offering amnesty to non-leaders. He exposed corruption involving the emperor's uncle Wang Li. As Jing Zhaoyin, he was pressured to protect the knight Du Zhiji but managed to avoid confrontation. He was dismissed when Chunyu Chang fell from power. Recalled under Emperor Ai, he investigated Empress Dowager Feng's death, angering Empress Dowager Fu, who had him imprisoned. Released after appeals, he later defended Zheng Chong but was dismissed. Under Emperor Ping, he opposed praising Wang Mang's virtues, was dismissed again, and lived in retirement.

source: Sun Shi replied: I am already seventy years old and my mind is confused. My affection for supporting my mother has become weak. I only care about my wife, family and children, just as the memorial said. As a result, Sun Bao was dismissed from office and stayed at home for the rest of his life. During the Jianwu period, virtuous ministers were appointed, and Sun Bao's grandson and his wife were appointed county magistrates of various counties. Wu Jianglong, named Junfang, was from Lanling, Shuhai. Wang Yin, the cavalry general of the Grand Sima, was in charge of Shangshu affairs inside the court and commanded troops and horses outside the court. Following the old practice, he selected and set up a Zhonglang to participate in the discussion and decision-making. He petitioned Wu Jianglong to be appointed Zhonglang, and was later promoted to an admonishing doctor. In the last years of Emperor Cheng's reign, Wu Jianglong handed over a sealed memorial saying: In ancient times, princes were selected to serve as ministers in the imperial court in order to praise their merits. King Dingtao should be recruited and let him live in the mansion in Beijing in order to pacify the world. After that, the emperor finally appointed King Tao as the crown prince, and Wu Jianglong was promoted to Jizhou Mu and Yingchuan Prefect. After Emperor Ai came to the throne, Wu Jianglong was promoted to Jing Zhaoyin because of his excellent examination results, and was later promoted to Zhi Jinwu. At that time, Dong Xian, the servant, was being favored. The emperor sent Zhong Huangmen to take out the weapons from the arsenal. There were ten batches before and after, and they were sent to the homes of Dong Xian and the emperor's wet nurse Wang A. Wu Jianglong wrote in his memorial: The weapons contained in the arsenal are common to the whole world and are designed for national armament. The funds required for their repair and manufacture are all paid by Bai Dasinong.
target: Wu Jianglong advised Emperor Cheng to recruit the Prince of Dingtao as heir. Under Emperor Ai, he criticized giving weapons from the imperial arsenal to Dong Xian and the emperor's wet nurse. After Empress Dowager Fu's maid purchase dispute, he was demoted. Wang Mang later exiled him for his role in Empress Dowager Feng's case.

source: He Jing personally led the officials and soldiers to chase Lin Qing. After walking for dozens of miles, Lin Qing was desperate, so he asked his servant to put on his hat and short coat instead. He got into the car and asked the servant on horseback to follow him. He changed his clothes and ran forward from the road. Just as the sun was going down, He Jing caught up with him and tied up the servant wearing Lin Qing's hat. The man said, "I am not a servant, just his servant." He Bing knew that Lin Qing had escaped, so he said: The king was forced to have nowhere to hide, and he claimed to be a servant. Do you want to escape the death penalty? So he ordered his men to cut off his head and bring it back, hang it on a broken drum, and put it under the pavilion of the city. He wrote: The former servant Wang Linqing committed murder. He buried the murdered man in the house guarding the tomb, and asked his servants to chop up the drum in front of the government office. Officials and people were shocked and frightened. Lin Qing then ran for his life, and people started talking, thinking that he was really dead. Because Empress Dowager Qiong Cheng loved Lin Qing, Emperor Cheng shed tears when she heard about this incident, and told Emperor Ai about it. Emperor Ai inquired about the situation and thought that the matter was done well, so he promoted him to be the governor of Longxi. Later, He Bing was transferred to Yingchuan Prefecture, succeeding Yan Xiang from Lingyang. Yan Xiang originally became an official based on his filial piety. He regarded his subordinates as teachers and friends. When he made mistakes, he would blame himself behind closed doors and never spoke much. There was a riot in the county. Wang Mang sent people to recruit Yan Xiang. Several hundred officials gathered to prepare a farewell banquet for him. Yan Xiang fell on the ground and cried. The subordinates said: It is a good thing that you were called up today. It should not be like this. Yan Xiang said: I am a scholar who pities Yingchuan. I have nothing to worry about: I was recruited because of my weakness, and the court will inevitably choose a strong person to replace me. Once the replacement arrives, there will be people who are bedridden, so it will be sad. After Yan Xiang arrived, he was appointed as the envoy of beauty and customs. At this time, Zhong Yuan, a native of Yingchuan, served as Shangshu Ling and concurrently as Ting Wei, handling affairs with authority and making changes. His younger brother Zhong Wei was a subordinate of Yingchuan County and illegally hid a large amount of gold. He Bing served as the prefect and told Zhong Tingwei about the incident when he saw him. Zhong Tingwei took off his hat and asked for a reduced death penalty for his brother, hoping to accept the punishment of crotch clamps as soon as possible. He Bing said: The fault lies with your brother for violating the king's law, not with the prefect. Zhong Yuan was afraid and sent Pegasus to greet his brother. Yangdi's rangers Zhao Ji and Li Kuan supported many guests, used their strength to rob the neighbors, and even raped other people's wives and daughters. They took advantage of the officials' shortcomings and ran rampant in the county. When they heard that General He was coming, they all fled. As soon as He Bing took office, he sought out nearly ten officials who were brave and knowledgeable about the law. He sent civilian officials to review the cases of the three people and military attachés to arrest them. Each had their own arrangements. The order said: These three people did not fail the prefect, but violated the king's law, so they had to be punished.
target: He Bing, as Changling magistrate, killed the fugitive Wang Linqing, who had murdered a servant. Though Empress Dowager Qiong Cheng grieved, Emperor Ai promoted He Bing. As Yingchuan prefect, he arrested criminals Zhao Ji and Li Kuan, and drove out Zhong Wei, whose brother was a powerful official. He Bing governed with integrity, his family not living in the government office. On his deathbed, he requested a simple burial.

source: Suihong, courtesy name Meng, was from the state of Lu and Fan. He was young, fashionable and chivalrous, and liked cockfighting and horse racing. Later, his style changed drastically and he studied "Spring and Autumn" with Ying Gong. Because he was proficient in Confucian classics, he became a Yilang, and he reached the official position of Fuli Jieliang. In the first month of the third year of Emperor Zhao Yuanfeng's reign, there was a roar like thousands of people coming together from the south of Laiwu Mountain in Mount Tai. When the people went to look, they saw a big stone standing up by itself. It was one foot to five feet high, as thick as forty-eight people surrounded it, and it was eight feet deep into the ground. There were three other stones as the feet of the big stone. After the boulder stood on its own, thousands of white crows flew down and gathered around it. At the same time, the dead trees in the Changyi Shrine and Temple came to life again, and the big willow tree that had been broken and withered and lying on the ground in Shanglin Garden actually stood up on its own and regained its vitality. There were many insects eating the leaves of the tree, and the leftover leaves were shaped like these words: Gongsun Bing has been established. Suihong then deduced the main idea of ​​"Spring and Autumn" and believed that: Stones and willows are both negative objects, symbolizing the common people at the bottom, while Mount Tai is the head of the mountains, and it is the place where emperors worshiped heaven to repay their merits after the change of dynasties. Nowadays, big rocks stand on their own and dry willows come back to life. They are not made by human beings. Their creation shows that ordinary people will become emperors. The resurrection of dead trees in the temple symbolizes the revival of the previously deposed Gongsun clan.
target: Suihong, courtesy name Meng, was from the state of Lu. Initially fond of cockfighting and horse racing, he later transformed his character and studied the "Spring and Autumn" with Ying Gong. Through his mastery of Confucian classics, he became a Yilang and reached the position of Fuli Jieliang. In the first month of the third year of Emperor Zhao's Yuanfeng reign, a great roar was heard south of Laiwu Mountain in Mount Tai. A large stone stood up by itself, measuring one to five feet high, as thick as forty-eight arm spans, and eight feet deep into the ground, with three other stones serving as its feet. Thousands of white crows gathered around it. Simultaneously, dead trees in the Changyi Shrine revived, and a broken willow in Shanglin Garden stood up and regained life, with insects eating its leaves into shapes resembling the words "Gongsun Bing has been established." Suihong interpreted these events through the "Spring and Autumn," concluding that stones and willows symbolized common people, while Mount Tai represented the site of imperial ceremonies. He argued that these phenomena indicated commoners would become emperors and the deposed Gongsun clan would revive.

The king of Changyi was furious and said that Xia Housheng was deceiving the public with his evil words, so he tied him up and handed him over to the officials. The official reported the incident to the general Huo Guang, but Huo Guang did not punish Xiahou Sheng. At this time, Huo Guang and the cavalry general Zhang Anshizheng were discussing how to depose the king of Changyi. Huo Guang blamed Zhang Anshi for leaking the truth, but in fact An Shi did not leak it. So Xia Housheng was interrogated, and Xia Housheng replied: "The Biography of Hong Fan" says that if an emperor does not rule according to the rules, he will be punished by the constant evil. At this time, there will be a crusade against him by the subordinates. It is just because the taboo is so obvious, so it is only said that there are ministers plotting against the emperor. Huo Guang and An Shi were both shocked, and they valued Confucian scholars even more from then on. More than ten days later, Huo Guang and An Shi finally petitioned the Queen Mother to depose King Changyi and establish Emperor Xuan. Huo Guang believed that the ministers reported political affairs to the East Palace and the Queen Mother inspected government affairs, so they should understand the classics, so he asked Xia Housheng to teach the Queen Mother "Shangshu". After Xiahou's victory, he was appointed as the Shaofu of Changxin and was given the title of Marquis of Guannei. He participated in the planning of the abolition of the establishment and the major decision-making of the ancestral temple and the country. Later, he was added to the food fiefdom of a thousand households.
target: Xiahou Shichang, from Lu, was proficient in the Five Classics and taught Qi Shi and Shangshu. After Dong Zhongshu and Han Ying died, Emperor Wu valued him greatly. Shichang understood yin and yang, once predicting the exact date of a fire at Bailiang Terrace. He served as tutor to King Changyi and died of old age. His nephew Xiahou Sheng, courtesy name Changgong, was also a renowned Confucian scholar. Xiahou Sheng lost his father young but studied diligently, learning "Shang Shu" and "Hong Fan's Five Elements" from Shichang, and later studied under Jian Qing and Ouyang. He was sophisticated and learned from multiple teachers. When King Changyi succeeded Emperor Zhao, he frequently traveled. Xiahou Sheng once blocked the king's carriage to remonstrate, warning that prolonged overcast weather without rain indicated ministers plotting against the emperor. The king was furious and had him bound, but Huo Guang did not punish him. When Huo Guang and Zhang Anshi were discussing deposing the king, Xiahou Sheng explained his prediction came from the "Hong Fan" biography, which stated that when an emperor rules improperly, subordinates will rebel. Huo Guang and Anshi were impressed and valued Confucian scholars more thereafter. They eventually petitioned the Queen Mother to depose King Changyi and establish Emperor Xuan. Xiahou Sheng was appointed Shaofu of Changxin and given the title of Marquis of Guannei.

source: So the officials in charge asked the Temple of Emperor Wu to be revered as the Temple of Sejong, and perform music and dance performances of "Shengde", "Wenshi", and "Five Elements", and worship them for generations to come to highlight the virtues. The forty-nine counties that Emperor Wu visited also had temples, just like Gaozu and Taizong. Xia Housheng and Huang Ba have been imprisoned for a long time. Huang Ba wanted to learn Confucianism from Xia Housheng, but Xia Housheng rejected him on the grounds that he had been sentenced to death. Huang Ba said: If you hear the Tao in the morning, you will die in the evening. Xia Housheng thought he spoke very well, so he taught him Confucian classics. Another winter passed like this, but the lectures remained the same. In the summer of the fourth year of Emperor Xuan's reign, there was an earthquake or landslide in the forty-nine counties of Guandong on the same day. City walls and houses collapsed, and more than 6,000 people died. Emperor Xuan wore plain clothes and did not attend court in the main hall. He sent ministers to express condolences to officials and people, and gave the deceased money to pay for his coffin. Emperor Xuan issued an edict saying: The occurrence of disasters is a warning from heaven and earth to us. I inherited the achievements of my ancestors and placed myself above the people, but I did not let them live a good life. In the past, there was an earthquake in Beihai and Langye, which damaged the ancestral temple. I was also very afraid. All the learned men among the princes and the middle two thousand stones, if you can find a way to deal with the disaster and make up for my shortcomings, don't be afraid. So a general amnesty was granted to the whole country. Xia Housheng was pardoned and served as an admonition to the officials, and Huang Ba was appointed as the assassin of Yangzhou. Xia Housheng was a simple and upright man, approachable but not dignified. When meeting Emperor Xuan, he addressed Emperor Xuan as king, and addressed his colleagues by names in front of Emperor Xuan. These practices were not etiquette, but Emperor Xuan became closer and more trusting to him because of these practices. One time after Xiahou Sheng was received, he went out to tell others what Emperor Xuan had said. Emperor Xuan heard about it and blamed Xiahou Sheng. Xiahou Sheng replied: Your Majesty said it very well, so I will publicize it. Yao's words spread throughout the world and are still recited today. I thought these words could be spread, so they spread. The last time the court had something important to discuss, because Emperor Xuan had always known that Xia Housheng was very forthright, Emperor Xuan would say to Xia Housheng: Sir, please speak frankly, don't be afraid because of past events. Xia Housheng once again became the Shaofu of Changxin, and was promoted to Prince Taifu. He was ordered by Emperor Xuan to write "Shangshu" and "The Analects of Confucius" and was given a hundred pounds of gold. Xia Housheng died in office when he was ninety years old. He was given a cemetery and buried in Pingling. The Queen Mother gave him two million and wore mourning clothes for Xiahou Sheng for five days to repay his master's kindness. Confucian scholars were proud of it.
target: When Emperor Xuan wanted to honor Emperor Wu's achievements, Xiahou Sheng opposed, arguing that although Emperor Wu defeated barbarians and expanded territory, he killed many ministers, exhausted resources, and caused widespread suffering and cannibalism. The ministers impeached Xiahou Sheng for slandering the late emperor, and he was imprisoned. After an earthquake killed over six thousand people, Emperor Xuan issued a general amnesty, and Xiahou Sheng was pardoned and served as an admonition official. He was known for his forthrightness, addressing the emperor as "king" and calling colleagues by name in court. Emperor Xuan trusted him for this honesty. Xiahou Sheng died in office at ninety, and the Queen Mother mourned him for five days.

source: Xiahou Sheng's son Xiahou also served as Zuocao Taizhong's doctor, his grandson Xiahou Yao served as the official of Changxin Shaofu, Sinong, and Honglu, and his great grandson Xiahoufan served as county governor, prefectural pastor, and Changle Shaofu. Xiahou Shang, the son of Xiahou Sheng's half-brother, became Liang Neishi, and Xiahou Shang's son Dingguo became the prefect of Yuzhang. Xiahou Jian's son Qianqiu also served as the Shaofu and Prince Shaofu. Jingfang, whose courtesy name is Junming, was born in Dunqiu, Shujun County. He studied "The Book of Changes" and studied under Jiao Yanshou from Liang Dynasty. The word for longevity is Gan. Jiao Gan was born in a poor family, but because of his love of learning, he received courtesy from the King of Liang. The King of Liang provided him with the necessary expenses so that he could study with peace of mind. After completing his studies, Jiao Gan served as county historian and was selected to replace Xiaohuang County Magistrate. Because Jiao Gan could often know evil things in advance, the thieves did not dare to commit crimes. Jiao Gan also cared deeply about lower-level officials and ordinary people, so the atmosphere in Xiaohuang County was very good. As a result, his political performance scored very high in the examination, and according to regulations, he should be promoted to another official. However, the three elders of Xiaohuang County wrote a letter expressing their hope to keep Jiao Gan. As a result, the edict was issued to allow Xiaohuang County to keep Jiao Gan and increase his salary. Jiao Gan died in Xiaohuang County. Jiao Gan often said: The person who can get my way but die because of it must be Jingfang. Jiao Gan was the best at talking about disasters. He connected the sixty-four hexagrams with things to be done every day, and used meteorological changes such as wind, rain, cold and temperature as symptoms, each with its own calculation and fulfillment. Jingfang is particularly good at this. Jing Fang is good at the rhythm of bells and knows the rhythm of music. In the fourth year of the Yuan Dynasty, he promoted Xiaolian as a Langguan. During the Yongguang and Jianzhao years, the Xiqiang rebelled, and soon there was a solar eclipse. Then the sky was always dark with no sunlight, and the sky was full of fog with no bright color at all. Jingfang wrote several times, predicting that something was going to happen, whether it was a few months or a year, and what he said came true many times. Emperor Yuan was very happy about this, so he often called Jingfang to ask him. Jingfang replied: In ancient times, emperors selected talents based on merit, so all things were procreated and auspiciousness appeared. But in the declining world, talents were selected only based on praise, so merit was abandoned and disasters appeared. At this time, it is best to let all officials review their own performance, so that the disaster will subside.
target: Jingfang, courtesy name Junming, studied "The Book of Changes" under Jiao Yanshou. Jiao Gan, his teacher, was known for predicting evil events and governing Xiaohuang County well. Jingfang was particularly skilled in connecting hexagrams with daily events and using meteorological changes as symptoms. During Emperor Yuan's reign, he predicted events accurately and was frequently consulted. He warned about disasters and criticized the appointment of flattering officials like Shi Xian. Jingfang recommended implementing a system to inspect officials' performance, but faced opposition from powerful ministers. He was eventually appointed prefect of Wei County but feared being isolated from the emperor.
