source: Dou Ying, courtesy name Wangsun, was the son of Queen Xiaowen's cousin. Tracing back to his father, he has lived in Guanjin for generations and likes to entertain guests. During the reign of Emperor Xiaowen, Baoying was the prime minister of Wu State, but was dismissed due to illness. Emperor Xiaojing came to the throne and appointed Dou Ying as Zhan Shi. Emperor Xiaojing's younger brother, King Liang Xiao, was doted on by his mother, Queen Mother Dou. Once, when King Xiao of Liang entered the court, Emperor Xiaojing drank with his brothers. There was no crown prince at this time, and when everyone had finished drinking, Emperor Xiaojing said calmly: After my death, I will pass the throne to King Liang. Queen Mother Dou was very happy to hear this. At this time, Dou Ying brought a glass of wine to the emperor and said: The world belongs to Emperor Gaozu, and the throne should be passed down from father to son. This is a legal restriction of the Han Dynasty. How can the emperor pass it on to King Liang? The Queen Mother hated Bao Ying because of this, and Dou Ying also felt that Zhan Shi's official position was too young, so she resigned due to illness. The Empress Dowager then removed the name list that allowed Dou Ying to enter and leave the palace. During festivals, he was not allowed to enter the palace to see him. In the third year of Emperor Xiaojing's reign, Wu and Chu rebelled. At this time, the emperor investigated and found that neither the Liu clan nor the Dou family members were as wise as Dou Ying, so he recruited Dou Ying. After Dou Ying came to see him, he resolutely declined, saying that he was ill and could not take on this important task. The Queen Mother also felt ashamed. The emperor said: "Now the world is in crisis, how can Wang Sun refuse?" So he made Dou Ying a general and rewarded him with a thousand pieces of gold. At this time, Yuan An, Le Bu and other famous generals and wise men retired from their posts and stayed at home, so Dou Ying recommended them to Emperor Jing to recruit them. Dou Ying placed all the gold given to him by the emperor in the hallway. Whenever his military officials came to see him, he would ask them to use the gold according to their own expenses. He never took the gold given by the emperor to his private residence. Dou Ying sat in Rongyang and supervised the armies of Qi and Zhao. After the rebellion of the Seven Kingdoms was put down, Dou Ying was granted the title of Marquis of Wei. At this time, many tourists and guests rushed to join Wei Qihou's family. Whenever Emperor Xiaojing went to court to discuss important matters with his ministers, all the princes would not dare to treat him with courtesy like Tiaohou and Wei Qihou. In the fourth year of Emperor Xiaojing's reign, he established Prince Li and ordered Wei Qihou to be the prince's teacher. In the seventh year of Emperor Xiaojing's reign, Prince Li was deposed. Wei Qihou argued for Prince Li many times, but to no avail. Wei Qihou claimed that he was ill and stayed at the foot of Nanshan Mountain in Lantian for several months. People named Dou, many guests and debaters asked him to come out, but he was unwilling to come out. Liang Guoren Zhisui said to Bin Ying: The one who can make you rich is the emperor, and the one who can make you a confidant of the court is the Queen Mother. Now the general is the master of the prince. The prince has been deposed and cannot fight for it. He cannot fight hard and cannot die. He retires due to illness, embraces a beautiful singer, and lives in Nanshan, refusing to go to the capital to see him.
target: Dou Ying, courtesy name Wangsun, was the son of Queen Xiaowen's cousin. He lived in Guanjin and enjoyed entertaining guests. During Emperor Xiaowen's reign, he served as prime minister of Wu State but was dismissed due to illness. Under Emperor Xiaojing, he became Zhan Shi. When Emperor Xiaojing offered the throne to his brother King Liang Xiao, Dou Ying objected, citing Han law that the throne must pass from father to son. This angered Queen Mother Dou, leading to Dou Ying's resignation and exclusion from court. In the third year of Emperor Xiaojing's reign, during the Wu-Chu rebellion, Dou Ying was appointed general and granted gold, which he distributed to his officers. After suppressing the rebellion, he was made Marquis of Wei. He later served as the prince's teacher but argued for the deposed prince, leading to his retirement. Persuaded by Zhisui, he resumed his duties. Despite Queen Mother Dou's recommendations, Emperor Xiaojing refused to make Dou Ying prime minister, citing his pride and rashness.

source: Dou Ying thought what he said was right, so he resumed his duties and went to court to see the emperor as before. When Taohou was removed from his position midway, Empress Dowager Dou repeatedly recommended Wei Qihou to be the prime minister. Emperor Xiaojing said: Does the Queen Mother think that I am stingy by not letting Wei Qihou become prime minister? Wei Qihou was proud and complacent, and often acted rashly and casually. It was difficult for him to be the prime minister and shoulder important responsibilities. In the end, he was not appointed, but Wei Wan, Marquis of Jianling, was appointed as prime minister. Tian Fu was the half-brother of Emperor Xiaojing and Queen Wang, and was born in Changling. After Dou Ying became the general, he was in his prime. Tian Fu, then a minister and not yet a nobleman, went to and from Dou Ying's house, accompanying Yi Ying to drink, kneeling and rising, as if he were a junior member of the Dou family. In the later years of Emperor Xiaojing's life, Danxuan became more and more noble and fortunate, and became a middle-aged doctor. Tian Fu was very talented in literature and had studied some ancient books such as "Pan Yu". Queen Wang thought he was very talented. Emperor Xiaojing passed away and Emperor Wu Liu Che had just ascended the throne. Tian Fu was named Marquis of Wu'an as his uncle, and Tian Sheng, Tian Fu's younger brother, was named Marquis of Zhou Yang. Tian Fu had just gained power and was very humble to his retainers. He also introduced those who had not served as officials among his retainers and made them serve as officials, hoping to overwhelm the power of the generals and ministers in the court. Most of the emperor's efforts to calm the political situation at that time were planned by Tian Fu's guests. When the Prime Minister Wei Wan was dismissed due to illness, the Emperor discussed setting up the Prime Minister and the Taiwei. He persuaded Tian Fu to borrow the opportunity and said: "Wei Qihou has been a noble man for a long time, and all the talents in the world have always been loyal to him. General, you have just become more prosperous and cannot be compared with Wei Qihou." Even if the emperor intends to use the general as prime minister, the general must give up the position to Wei Qihou. When Wei Qihou becomes prime minister, the general will definitely become a Taiwei. The noble status of the Taiwei and the Prime Minister are the same. The general not only gets the Taiwei, but also has a good reputation of giving his position to the wise. Tian Fu secretly revealed his thoughts to the Queen Mother and asked the Queen Mother to hint to the emperor. So Dou Ying was made prime minister and Tian Fu was made Taiwei. I congratulated Dou Ying by taking advantage of his blessings, and advised him by the way: The nature of a prince is to like good and hate evil. Now good people praise the prince, so the prince can be the prime minister. But there are many evil people, and they will also slander the king. If the ruler can be tolerant to both good and bad people, then the ruler's position is expected to last for a long time; otherwise, he will be slandered and leave his job immediately. Dou Ying didn't listen to him. Dou Ying and Tian Fu both liked Confucianism, so they elected Zhao Wan as the imperial censor and Wang Zang as the doctor. Welcoming Lord Shen of Lu State to the capital and preparing to set up a Mingtang. Let the princes return to their respective fiefdoms, cancel the confinement, and uniform them according to ancient rituals to show peace.
target: Tian Fu, half-brother of Emperor Xiaojing and Queen Wang, rose in prominence after Emperor Wu's ascension, becoming Marquis of Wu'an. He initially humbled himself before Dou Ying but later gained power. Tian Fu recommended Dou Ying as prime minister while becoming Taiwei himself. Both favored Confucianism, promoting Zhao Wan and Wang Zang, and planned to establish a Mingtang. However, Queen Mother Dou, a Huang-Lao adherent, opposed them, leading to their dismissal. Tian Fu remained influential due to his ties to the Queen Mother, while Dou Ying's power waned. After Queen Mother Dou's death, Tian Fu became prime minister, growing arrogant.

source: So Zhao Wan, Wang Zang and others were dismissed and expelled, and Dou Ying was removed from the post of prime minister and Tian Fu from the post of Taiwei. In addition, Bai Zhi Hou Xuchang was appointed as the prime minister, and Wuqiang Hou Zhuang Qingzhai was appointed as the censor. From then on, Dou Ying and Tian Fu only lived at home as Hou. Although Tian Fu, the Marquis of Wu'an, did not hold an official position, he was still favored by the emperor because of his relationship with the Queen Mother. He discussed political affairs many times, and most of them were adopted and came into effect. Those officials and scholars who were in favor of others left Wei Qihou Dou Ying and joined Tian Fu. As a result, Marquis Wu'an became more and more arrogant day by day.
target: He built lavish residences, acquired fertile lands, and received countless treasures. Dou Ying, by contrast, became alienated and powerless, finding solace only in his friendship with Guan Fu.

source: I also want to appoint a few people! Once, he asked the emperor to allocate the official land of the examination room for him to expand his private residence. The emperor was furious and said to him: Why don't you take away my arsenal too? After this time, he restrained himself a little. Once, he invited guests to a banquet and asked his elder brother Gaihou to sit facing north, but he sat facing east. He believed that the prime minister of the Han Dynasty was noble and he could not wrong himself in private just because he was his elder brother. From then on, Tian Fu, the Marquis of Wu'an, became even more arrogant. The residences he built were extremely gorgeous and majestic, surpassing those of all nobles. His fields and manors are extremely fertile, and there is an endless stream of people he sends to counties to buy valuable artifacts on the road. There are bells, drums and music in the front hall, and there are hundreds of women in the back room. The treasures, dogs, horses, antiques and furnishings presented to him by the princes are countless. Contrary to Tian Fu, Wei Qihou Dou Ying became even more alienated, not reused, and had no power since the death of Queen Mother Dou. All the guests gradually retreated and even treated Dou Ying with arrogance. Only Guan Fu still treated him the same way. Dou Ying felt depressed every day, but he only had a particularly good relationship with Guan Fu. Guan Fu, courtesy name Zhongru, was born in Yingyin. His father was Zhang Meng, who had once been the servant of Guan Ying, the Marquis of Yingyin. He was very favored, so he promoted him to an official of two thousand shi, so he took the surname of Guan and changed his name to Guan Meng. When Wu and Chu were in power, Guan Ying, Marquis of Yingyin, was a general and was subordinate to Taiwei Zhou Yafu. He recommended Guan Meng to the Taiwei as a school lieutenant.
target: Guan Fu, courtesy name Zhongru, was born in Yingyin. His father, Zhang Meng, served Guan Ying and took the surname Guan. During the Wu-Chu rebellion, Guan Fu fought fiercely to avenge his father, earning fame despite severe injuries. He later served as a general but lost his position due to legal troubles.

source: In crowded situations, Guan Fu always praises and praises low-status juniors, so most people praise him. Guan Fu didn't like learning, but he liked chivalry and would always do what he promised. Those who associate with him are nothing more than heroes, knights, or cunning people. His family's assets are tens of millions, and the number of diners every day ranges from dozens to nearly a hundred. He built pits in his fields to store water for irrigation purposes. In order to monopolize the water conservancy fields, Guanfu's clan guests often fought for power and became rampant in the Yingchuan area. So the children in Yingchuan sang: If the Yingshui is clear, the Guan family will be at peace; if the Yingshui is dirty, the Guan family will be destroyed. Although Guan Fu's family was wealthy, they lost their power. As a result, the ministers, ministers, and those who had always been Guan Fu's guests gradually distanced themselves from him. When Dou Ying lost power, he also wanted to rely on Guan Fu to settle accounts with those who followed Yan's influence. Guan Fu also wanted to use Dou Ying's relationship to make friends with the princes and clan members to increase his social status. Therefore, the two of them respected each other and were as close as father and son. The two of them were very compatible and had no objections. They just regretted that it was too late for them to know each other.
target: Known for his uprightness and disdain for flattery, Guan Fu respected the poor and insulted the powerful. He associated with heroes and rogues, amassing wealth and a large following. His family's arrogance in Yingchuan led to a local song warning of their downfall. After losing power, Guan Fu bonded with Dou Ying, each seeking to bolster the other's status. Their friendship deepened, though Guan Fu's bluntness often caused conflict.

source: Let me inform Wei Qihou and ask him to prepare wine and food. Please come early tomorrow. Tian Fu then agreed. Guan Fu told Wei Qihou Baoying the details of his appointment with the prime minister. Dou Ying and his wife specially bought more meat and wine. They got up at night to clean, prepare wine and food, and were busy until dawn. At dawn, he asked his servants to wait in front of the house. But at noon, Prime Minister Tian Fu still didn't come. Dou Ying said to Guan Fu, "Has the Prime Minister forgotten?" Guanfu was very unhappy and said, "I don't mind asking him to keep his promise during the mourning period. He should come himself and should not forget." So Guan Fu drove his car and went to meet the prime minister in person. Prime Minister Tian Fu just agreed to Guan Fu the day before and had no intention of actually going to the banquet. When Guan Fu came, the prime minister was still lying down. So Guan Fu went in to see him and said, "General, I was fortunate enough to agree to visit Wei Qihou yesterday." Wei Qihou and his wife organized a banquet, but from early morning to now, they have not dared to eat anything! Wu Anhou pretended to be stunned and apologized to Guan Fu, saying: I was drunk yesterday and forgot what I said to you. So he ordered him to go, but he went very slowly, which made Guanfu even more angry. When the wine was almost done, Guan Fu started dancing, and after the dance invited the prime minister, but the prime minister didn't get up, so Guan Fu used words to offend the prime minister during the banquet. Dou Ying helped Guan Fu leave and apologized to the prime minister in person. Prime Minister Tian Fu drank wine until dark before leaving happily. Later, Prime Minister Tian Fu asked Dou Ying to give him the land in the south of the city to take advantage of his blessings. Dou Ying said very unhappy: Although I, an old man, have been abandoned by the court, and the general is noble, can I use my power to seize my land? Refuse to agree. When my husband heard about this, he cursed me for being lucky. Not wanting Dou and Tian to be at odds with each other, he made up some good words and said to the prime minister: Wei Qihou is old and is about to die. It's not difficult to endure it for a few more days. Let's wait. Soon, Tian Fu heard that Dou Ying and Guan Fu were actually angry and refused to give him the land. He also got angry and said, "The son of Wei Qihou once committed a serious crime of murder, and I saved him." I serve Wei Qihou, and I refuse to obey him on anything. Why is he reluctant to part with these few hectares of fields? Besides, what does this have to do with Guan Fu! I don't dare to ask for this land anymore. From then on, Tian Fu became very resentful towards Dou Ying and Guan Fu. In the spring of the fourth year of Yuanguang, the Prime Minister reported that Guan Fu's family was extremely arrogant in Yingchuan and the people suffered from it, and asked the emperor to investigate Guan Fu.
target: Tian Fu once agreed to visit Dou Ying with Guan Fu but forgot, causing Guan Fu to confront him. At a banquet, Guan Fu insulted Tian Fu, leading to a rift. Tian Fu later demanded land from Dou Ying, who refused, deepening their enmity. In the fourth year of Yuanguang, Tian Fu reported Guan Fu's family's arrogance, and Guan Fu retaliated by exposing Tian Fu's misdeeds. At a wedding feast for Tian Fu, Guan Fu insulted guests, leading to his arrest. Tian Fu accused him of disrespect, and Dou Ying tried to save him, arguing his drunken mistake was minor. In court, Tian Fu slandered Guan Fu as treasonous.

source: The memorial was submitted, but when checking the archives of the inner court, there was no sign of Emperor Jing's dying words. This edict was only kept in Baoying's home and was sealed by his family chief. So Dou Ying was impeached again, saying that he forged the emperor's edict and should be sentenced to the death penalty of beheading in public. In October of the fifth year of Yuanguang, Guan Fu and his family were all convicted. It took a long time for Dou Ying to hear the news. As soon as he heard this, he felt extremely sad and angry, and suffered a serious stroke. He didn't want to eat but wanted to die. Later, I heard from somewhere that the emperor had no intention of killing him, so he resumed his diet and healed his illness. The imperial court had decided not to execute Dou Ying, but at this time, rumors spread again, saying a lot of bad things about Dou Ying, deliberately letting the emperor hear it, so on December 30 of that year, Dou Ying was beheaded on the streets of Weicheng. In the spring of the sixth year of Yuanguang, Tian Fu fell ill and felt pain all over his body, as if someone was beating him. He kept shouting loudly, admitting his guilt and apologizing. The emperor invited a wizard who could see ghosts to diagnose his illness. The wizard said: Two ghosts, Wei Qihou and Guan Fu, were guarding Wu'anhou and whipped him with whips to kill him. Finally died. His son Tian Tian inherited his father's title. During the Yuan Shuo period, his title was revoked because of his crimes. Later, the rebellion of Huainan King Liu An was discovered.
target: The emperor asked ministers to judge, but opinions were divided. Queen Mother Dou pressured the emperor, leading to Guan Fu's execution and Dou Ying's imprisonment. Dou Ying was later executed for allegedly forging an imperial edict. Tian Fu died soon after, haunted by ghosts of Dou Ying and Guan Fu. His son's title was later revoked.

source: His son Tian Tian inherited his father's title. During the Yuan Shuo period, his title was revoked because of his crimes. Later, the rebellion of Huainan King Liu An was discovered. A few years ago, the King of Huainan, Liu An, came to Beijing to pay homage. At that time, Tian Fu was the Taiwei and went to Ba Shang to greet the King of Huainan. He said to Liu An: The emperor does not have a prince yet. Your Majesty, you are the wisest and the grandson of the great ancestor. Once the emperor dies, who else should inherit the throne instead of you, the King of Huainan! The King of Huainan was very happy after hearing this and gave Tian Ai many gold and silver items. Ever since the incident involving Dou Ying and Guan Fu happened, the emperor did not take Tian Fu's actions seriously and tolerated them just to hinder the Queen Mother. When the emperor heard about Tian Fu's collusion with King Huainan and the incident of accepting money from King Huainan, he said: If Marquis Wu'an is still there, it is time to exterminate the clan. Han Anguo, whose courtesy name is Changru, was born in Cheng'an County, Liang State, and later moved to Suiyang. He once studied "Han Feizi" and the doctrines of Zajia in Tiansheng's place in Zouxian County. Serve King Xiao of Liang and become a great official. When Wu Chu rebelled, King Xiao sent An Guo and Zhang Yu as generals to resist the Wu army in Shu territory. Because Zhang Yu fought hard and An Guo was mature and prudent, the Wu army could not cross Liang's defense line. After the Wu Chu rebellion was over, the reputations of Han Anguo and Zhang Yu became prominent in the Liang Kingdom.
target: Han Anguo, courtesy name Changru, was born in Cheng'an County, Liang State. He studied Han Feizi and served King Xiao of Liang during the Wu-Chu rebellion, helping repel the Wu army. After the rebellion, his reputation grew.

source: Because in governing the world, one cannot harm the public for private reasons. As the saying goes: Although I have a biological father, how do I know that he is not a tiger? Although he has a biological brother, how do you know that he will not turn into a wolf? Now the king is a prince, but he listened to the false words of an evil official, violated the monarch's prohibition, and distorted the strict law. Because of the Queen Mother, the Emperor cannot bear to use laws against you. The Queen Mother cried at night, hoping that the king would realize and change his ways, but the king still could not wake up. If the Queen Mother dies, who else can you cling to, Your Majesty? Before he finished speaking, King Xiao burst into tears and blamed himself to Han Anguo: "I will hand over Gongsun Gui and Yang Sheng immediately." On that day, Gongsun Gui and Yang Sheng committed suicide. The Han envoys returned to answer their orders, and Liang's troubles were completely resolved. This was all due to An Guo's contribution. So Emperor Jing and Empress Dowager Dou valued Han Anguo even more. After the death of King Xiao, King Gong came to the throne. Han Anguo lost his official position because of breaking the law and lived at home. After Liu Che, Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, ascended the throne, Tian Fu, Marquis of Wu'an, became the Taiwei, favored and trusted and held great power. Han Anguo gave five hundred gold to Tian Fu. Tian Fu mentioned Han Anguo to the Queen Mother. The emperor often heard about Anguo's talents, so he called him the captain of the North, and later he was promoted to Da Si Nong. Min Yue and Shu Yue attacked each other, so the emperor sent Han Anguo and Daxing Wang Hui to lead troops to Vietnam. Before reaching Yue, the Yue people killed their king and surrendered, and the Han court withdrew its troops. At that time, Tian Fu became the prime minister, and Han Anguo was the censor. The Xiongnu sent people to ask for peace, and the emperor asked the emperor to discuss it. Wang Zheng of Daxing was an artist and had served as an official in border counties many times. He was very familiar with the situation of the Xiongnu. He made a comment and said: Most of the time when the Han soldiers make peace with the Huns, the Huns break the treaty again within a few years.
target: When Emperor Jing was displeased with King Liang's extravagance, Han Anguo defended him to the eldest princess, easing tensions. He later became internal history of Liang, resolving conflicts by persuading King Xiao to surrender conspirators. After King Xiao's death, Han Anguo lost his position but regained favor under Emperor Wu through Tian Fu's patronage. He became a censor and advocated peace with the Xiongnu, opposing Wang Hui's war plans. Despite initial success, the Mayi ambush failed, and Wang Hui committed suicide. Han Anguo later served as a general but was demoted due to military setbacks.

source: Although he is greedy for money, he only recommends honest people who are more capable than himself. Recommend Yi Ya in Luang time? Wei Zhou and others were also famous people in the world, so the scholars praised and admired him very much. Even the emperor thought he was a talented person in governing the country. Han Anguo served as the imperial censor for five years, and the prime minister passed away. Longxuanli also acted as prime minister. When he was leading the way for the emperor, he fell from his car and became lame.
target: He died of illness, frustrated and unhappy. His colleague Husui, a virtuous official, also died before becoming prime minister.

source: Zan said: Dou Ying and Tian Fu both held important positions because of their relatives, while Guan Fu became famous at that time because he made up his mind and showed his performance. They are all in the ranks of ministers, and their great cause has been determined. However, Bao Ying was too ignorant of current affairs, Guan Fu was uneducated and not humble, and Tian Fu relied on his noble status to become arrogant and domineering. The evil qualities of each other collide with each other, and they will show up at the right moment. Although Jiufeng mediates between them sincerely, how can he save their decline? Based on Han Anguo's knowledge and understanding, when he was about to ascend to the throne, he suffered from illness and failed, and finally slowly died of worry. What happened to people is really destined, how sad! For example, Wang Hui first proposed the use of troops against the Xiongnu but suffered disasters as a result. Was the dispatch ordained by fate?
target: In summary, Dou Ying and Tian Fu rose through family ties, while Guan Fu gained fame through valor. Their conflicts, fueled by pride and arrogance, led to their downfalls. Han Anguo's wisdom and loyalty were overshadowed by fate, and Wang Hui's war advocacy ended in tragedy.

source: Zhai Fangjin, courtesy name Ziwei, was from Shangcai, Runan. His family has been humble and humble for generations. Fang Jin's father Zhai Gong was fond of learning and served as a county scholar. When Fang Jin was twelve or thirteen years old, his father died and he could no longer continue his studies. He worked as a minor historian in the prefect's mansion. He was considered slow and could not do good things, and was repeatedly scolded and insulted by the governor. Fang Jin was very sad, so he went to meet Cai's father in Runan and asked him what he was suitable for. Cai's father thought that his appearance was unusual and told him: You have the bone image of a feudal lord. You should use it according to the classics and study the knowledge of Confucian scholars. Fang Jin was tired of being a minor historian. After hearing what Cai's father said, he felt very happy, so he returned home saying he was ill, said goodbye to his stepmother, and wanted to go west to the capital to study scriptures. His mother felt pity for Fang Jin when he was young, so she came to Chang'an with him, knitted shoes for him to study, and taught him "Spring and Autumn" by a doctor. After more than ten years of accumulation and study, he became proficient in Confucian classics, and his number of disciples increased day by day, and all the Confucian scholars praised him. Take Shece Jiake as the man. Two or three years later, he was promoted to Mingjing and moved to Yilang. At this time, there was a mature and knowledgeable scholar Hu Chang from Qinghe, who was studying the same classics as Fang Jin. Hu Chang was a senior, but his reputation was not as good as Fang Jin's. He was jealous of Fang Jin's talent, and did not praise Fang Jin when discussing. After Fang Jin knew about it, he waited for Hu Chang to gather his students to give lectures, and sent students under his disciples to Hu Chang's place to ask for advice on difficult issues in the scriptures, and record Hu Chang's teachings accordingly. After such a long time, Hu Chang felt uneasy knowing that Fang Jin respected and humbled him. From then on, he was known as Fang Jin among the scholar-bureaucrats, and they became close friends. During the Heping period, Fang Jin became a doctor. A few years later, he was moved to Shuofang as governor. When serving as an official, he is not cumbersome and harsh, and his observations are carried out in an orderly manner, which is very prestigious. He reported to the imperial court many times and was moved to the position of Prime Minister Sizhi. He followed Emperor Cheng to Ganquan and drove on the Chi Road. Chen Qing, the captain of Sili School, impeached him, so Fang Jin had his carriage and horses confiscated. After arriving at Ganquan Palace, they gathered in the palace and talked with Chen Qing and Tingwei Fan Yanshou. At that time, Chen Qing was being impeached by a memorial. Chen Qing said himself: "What happened in the past should be punished as a crime. Now that the Minister has come with a memorial to impeach me, the verdict should be wrapped up here."
target: Zhai Fangjin, courtesy name Ziwei, was from Shangcai, Runan, born into a humble family. After his father died when he was twelve or thirteen, he worked as a minor historian but was often scolded. Seeking guidance, he consulted Cai's father in Runan, who noted his noble bone structure and advised him to study Confucian classics. Inspired, he feigned illness, left his job, and traveled to Chang'an with his stepmother, who supported him by knitting shoes. He studied the "Spring and Autumn Annals" under a doctor, and over a decade became proficient in Confucian classics, gaining many disciples and acclaim. He passed the imperial exams, became a doctor during the Heping period, and later served as governor of Shuofang, known for orderly governance. He was promoted to Prime Minister Sizhi. While accompanying Emperor Cheng to Ganquan, he violated road rules, leading to his carriage being confiscated by Sili Xiaowei Chen Qing. Later, Fangjin impeached Chen Qing for disrespect, resulting in Chen's dismissal. He also impeached Juanxun, another Sili Xiaowei, for arrogance and disrespect, leading to Juanxun's demotion. Within a year, Fangjin dismissed two high officials, instilling fear in the court. As Jingzhaoyin, he cracked down on powerful families, but at Hu Chang's advice, he moderated his strictness.

source: The emperor believed that he was qualified for the position of public minister and wanted to use him to govern the people. He transferred him to the position of Jing Zhaoyin. Fang Jin attacked the powerful and powerful, and everyone in the capital was afraid of him. At that time, Hu Chang was the governor of Qingzhou. When he heard about this, he wrote to Fang Jin: I heard privately that your decrees are very strict. With Jing Zhaoyin's talents, I am afraid that he will feel uncomfortable. Fang Jin knew in his heart what Hu Chang was referring to, and then relaxed his dignity a little. Fang Jin served as Jingzhaoyin for three years, and was promoted to imperial censor in the second year of Yongshi. A few months later, Prime Minister Xue Xuan happened to be exempted from being a civilian because of the riots caused by thieves in the vast desert and the three auxiliary officials of Zha during the funeral of the Empress Dowager. Fang Jin was also demoted to Zhijinwu because he was ordered to hold funerals when he was appointed Jingzhao Yin and disturbed the people. Twenty days later, the official position of prime minister became vacant. Most of the ministers recommended Fang Jin. The emperor also valued Fang Jin's talents, so he promoted Fang Jin to be prime minister and made him the Marquis of Gaoling, granting him a land of thousands of households. Fang Jin was already rich, but his stepmother was still alive. He paid attention to cultivating family conduct and worshiped his mother very piously and generously. When his stepmother passed away and was buried twenty-six days later, he took off his funeral clothes and started working. He believed that as the prime minister of the Han Dynasty, he did not dare to go beyond the country's system. As prime minister, he was impartial and honest, and did not ask the four counties and counties for personal matters. The law is strict and strict, and the ministers and ministers are reported to the nine ministers. The laws are strict and detailed and are deeply slandered. There are many people who conspire to frame him. People such as Chen Xian, Zhu Bo, Xiao Yu, Feng Xin, and Sun Hong all came from aristocratic families in the capital. Because of their talents, they served as ministers at a young age and were very famous at that time. However, Fang Jin came from behind because of his outstanding performance and was promoted to prime minister in more than ten years. Chen Xian and others were impeached according to the law, and they were all dismissed.
target: After three years, he became imperial censor, then prime minister and Marquis of Gaoling. He was impartial and strict, often impeaching ministers like Chen Xian and Feng Xin for corruption, leading to their dismissal. He also targeted Chunyu Chang's associates, removing over twenty officials. Despite his harshness, Emperor Cheng trusted him.

source: Fang Jin was rich in knowledge and talent, and he also knew the law and officials. He decorated the law with elegant writing and was called the Tongming Prime Minister. The emperor valued him very much. Fang Jin reported to the emperor everything that was not in line with his wishes and ordered him. He also explored the emperor's hidden will to consolidate his position. Previously, Dingling Marquis Chunyu Chang was a relative, but because he was good at strategy, he was listed as the Jiuqing. When he first took office, Fang Jin interacted with Chun Yuchang alone, praised and recommended him. When Chun Yuchang was executed for treason, all those who were friendly to Chun Yuchang were dismissed from their posts because of him. Because Fang Jin was a minister, the emperor always valued him and concealed the secrets for him. Fang Jin felt guilty and asked to resign and go home. The emperor replied: Dingling Marquis Chunyu Chang has already confessed his crime. Although you associate with him, doesn't it say so in the scriptures? If you know your mistakes in the morning, you will correct them in the evening. A gentleman praises him. What doubts do you have? Please stay focused and don't slack off. See your doctor and take medicine to take care of yourself. Fang Jin just got up to do things, and reported one by one to Chunyu's elders, Yin Sunbao of Jingzhao and Xiao Yu of Youfufeng. There were more than 20 people who had been dismissed from their posts as governors with more than 2,000 shi. Fang Jin was trusted by the emperor. Although Fang Jin studied "Gu Liang Zhuan", he loved "Zuo Shi Zhuan" and astronomical ephemeris. His "Zuo Shi Zhuan" was taught to the national teacher Liu Xin, and the ephemeris was taught to Chang'an Lingtian Zhongshu. Fang Jin valued Li Xun and appointed him as Yi Cao. Fang Jin had been prime minister for nine years. In the spring of the second year of Suihe, Mars entered the heart of the sky. Li Xun wrote in a memorial: You know the tactics of dealing with changes.
target: Fangjin studied "Guliang Zhuan" but favored "Zuo Shi Zhuan" and astronomy. After nine years as prime minister, Mars entered the heart constellation, and his subordinate Li Xun warned of impending disaster. Fangjin grew anxious. The emperor later criticized him for poor governance and tax policies, but spared him.

source: You must carefully consider careful strategies, eliminate the source of evil, worry about the country as much as you worry about your family, and devote yourself to stabilizing the people to assist me. Since I have repented, you should also reflect on yourself, eat hard and do your duty with all your heart. I will send the Minister to reward you with ten stones of good wine and an ox. Please consider it carefully. Fang Jin committed suicide that day. The emperor concealed the letter and sent Jiuqing to give Fang Jin the seal and ribbon of Prime Minister Gaolinghou. He also rewarded Fang Jin with a vehicle and a coffin. He set up offerings in the young mansion and wrapped the pillars and thresholds with white cloth.
target: Fangjin committed suicide that day. The emperor honored him with posthumous titles and gifts.

source: I want to raise an army now, will you follow me? Chen Feng was eighteen years old and full of courage, so he agreed to Zhai Yi. Zhai Yi then formed an alliance with Liu Yu, the captain of Shujun, Liu Xin, the Marquis of Yanxiang, and Liu Huang, the Marquis of Wuping, Liu Xin's younger brother. When Sun Qing, the king of Dongjun, was summoned to the capital because he had always been brave in strategy and knew the art of war, Zhai Yi forged a document and issued an order to arrest Wang Sun Qing in the name of a serious crime. Therefore, on the day of the examination in September, he killed the magistrate of Guan, commanded the magistrate's cavalry and infantry, recruited brave people in the county, and arranged generals. Liu Xin, Marquis of Yanxiang, was the son of Wang Yun of Dongping. Liu Yun was killed, and Liu Xin's brother Kaiming succeeded him as king. Kaiming died without a son, and Liu Kuang, Liu Xin's son, became king again. Therefore, Zhai Yi led the army to annex Ding Dongping and made Liu Xin the emperor. Zhai Yi proclaimed himself Great General Sima Zhutian, and appointed Su Long, the teacher of King Ping of Cambodia, as prime minister, and Lieutenant Gao Dan as imperial censor. He sent documents to various counties and counties, saying that Wang Mang had killed the filial emperor with poisonous wine, and pretended to adopt the title of emperor. Now that Liu Xin had ascended the throne, he ordered all counties to jointly carry out God's punishment for Wang Mang. The whole country was shocked. When Zhai Yi's army arrived in Shanyang, it numbered more than 100,000 people.
target: His son Zhai Xuan was a gentleman, while another son, Zhai Yi, became a governor. During Wang Mang's regency, Zhai Yi rebelled, declaring Liu Xin emperor and amassing over 100,000 troops. Wang Mang crushed the rebellion, executing Zhai Yi and his family, and desecrating Fangjin's grave. The rebellion's failure led to Wang Mang's usurpation. Historian Ban Biao noted Fangjin's rise from poverty to prominence, but lamented Zhai Yi's doomed uprising.

source: The year after Liu Ze became King Langxie, Empress Dowager Lu died of illness. Liu Ze then said: The emperor is young, Zhu Lu is in power, and the Liu clan is lonely and weak. So he led his troops and conspired with the King of Qi to march westward, intending to kill Zhu Lu. When he arrived in Liangdi, he heard that General Guan Ying of the Han Dynasty was stationed in Rongyang, so he withdrew his troops and stationed them in the western frontier of his country, and then rushed to Chang'an alone. At this time, Liu Heng, the king of Dai, also arrived in Chang'an, the capital of Dai. The generals and ministers and Liu Ze jointly supported the king of Dai as the emperor of the Han Dynasty, that is, Emperor Xiaowen. In the first year of Emperor Xiaowen's reign, Liu Ze was renamed King of Yan. The Langye area was still given to Qi. Liu Ze died after two years as King of Yan, and Mi paid tribute to him. His son Kang Wang Liu Jia succeeded to the throne and died in the ninth year. Dingguo, the son of King Kang, succeeded to the throne. Dingguo committed adultery with his father's concubine. She gave birth to a boy, took his sister-in-law as a concubine, and committed adultery with her three daughters. Dingguo planned to kill the Ying people, the magistrate of Feiru County. The Ying people and others reported to the court, and Dingguo sent envoys to kill the Ying people and silence them for violating other laws. During the Yuanshuo period, the brothers of the Ying people once again wrote to the court to report Dingguo's crimes in detail. Emperor Wu asked the ministers to discuss it, and they all said: Dingguo's behavior is like an animal, messing up human relations and violating the will of God, and he should be punished with death. The emperor approved this proposal. Dingguo then committed suicide. Forty-two years after the establishment of the feudal state, it was abolished. During the reign of Emperor Ai, in order to continue the vassal family that had cut off the feudal state, Liu Guisheng, Liu Ze's great-great-grandson's grandson from Wuzhong County, who had only a first-class title, was granted the title of Marquis of Yingling. During the Gengshi period, Liu Guisheng was killed by soldiers. King Wu Liu Bi was the son of Liu Zhong, brother of Emperor Gao. Emperor Gao made Liu Zhong the acting king. When the Xiongnu attacked Dai, Liu Zhong could not hold on, so he secretly abandoned the country and fled, returning to the capital Chang'an from Luoyang. The emperor could not bear to bring him to justice, so he deposed him from the throne and demoted him to the rank of Marquis of Heyang. His son Liu Bi was granted the title of Marquis of Pei. King Yingbu of Huainan rebelled, and Emperor Gaozu personally led troops to attack him. At this time, Liu Bi was twenty years old and followed Gaozu as a cavalry general to defeat Yingbu. After King Liu Mai of Jing was killed by Ting Bu, he had no descendants. Emperor Gaozu was worried that the people of Wu County and Kuaiji County were frivolous and fierce, and there were no powerful princes to control them. His son was still young, so he appointed Liu Bi as King of Wu in Pei, with jurisdiction over three counties and fifty-three cities. After receiving the seal, Emperor Gaozu summoned him and gave him a face, saying: You have the appearance of rebellion. I regretted that I should not have sealed him, but I could not take back my life, so I patted Liu Bi on the back and said: Fifty years after the founding of the Han Dynasty, there will be a rebellion in the southeast. Could it be you?
target: The histories of three Han dynasty princes: Liu Jia (King of Jing), Liu Ze (King of Yan), and Liu Bi (King of Wu). Liu Jia, a cousin of Emperor Gaozu, served as a general, leading campaigns against Chu forces, burning supplies, and later capturing Jiujiang. He was made King of Jing but was killed in battle against the rebel Yingbu. Liu Ze, a brother of Gaozu, was initially a marquis. Through a scheme by Tian Sheng, he was made King of Langye after persuading Empress Lu to enfeoff the Lü clan. After Empress Lu’s death, he joined others in supporting Emperor Xiaowen and was renamed King of Yan. His descendants included a son, Kang Wang, and a grandson, Dingguo, who committed adultery with his father’s concubine and sisters, leading to his suicide and the abolition of his state. Liu Bi, son of Liu Zhong, was made King of Wu after defeating Yingbu. He grew wealthy from copper and salt, and after his son was killed by the crown prince, he feigned illness and plotted rebellion. During Emperor Jing’s reign, Chao Cuo advocated reducing the princes’ territories, prompting Liu Bi to lead a rebellion of seven states (Wu, Chu, Zhao, Jiaoxi, Jiaodong, Jinan, and Zichuan) in 154 BCE. Liu Bi issued a call to arms, offering rewards for killing Han officials. Emperor Jing executed Chao Cuo to appease the rebels, but the rebellion continued. Zhou Yafu, a Han general, cut off Wu’s supply lines and defeated them. Liu Bi fled to Dongyue, where he was killed. The other rebel princes were also defeated or committed suicide. The text concludes that Liu Jia’s kingship was due to the unstable times, Liu Ze’s was based on a risky scheme, and Liu Bi’s rebellion stemmed from his wealth and personal grievance, leading to disaster.

target: Xiao He, from Peidi, began his career as a meticulous official under Pei Lord, supporting the future Emperor Gaozu (then a commoner and later a pavilion chief) in official matters. When Gaozu served in Xianyang, Xiao He contributed 500 yuan for his farewell, exceeding the 300 yuan given by others. As an official in Sishui County, he excelled in inspections, but declined a court recruitment to remain. When Gaozu rose as Duke of Pei, Xiao He became his prime minister and governor. Upon entering Xianyang, while others seized gold and silk, Xiao He collected Qin’s legal and administrative books, enabling Gaozu to understand the empire’s geography, households, and people’s grievances. As prime minister, he governed Ba and Shu, pacifying the people and supplying the army. In the second year of the Han Dynasty, Xiao He stayed in Guanzhong, governing Yueyang, establishing laws, temples, and counties, reporting to the emperor when possible.

And you are just following me with your own body, there are only three or two people, and dozens of people from Xiao He’s family are following me. The credit must not be forgotten! Although Cao Shen had the credit for strategically planning the country, this was only a temporary matter. The emperor had a stalemate with Chu for five years, losing troops and generals, and fleeing many times. However, Xiao He often sent troops from Guanzhong to supplement them. target: He recruited soldiers and supplied grain, earning the emperor’s trust. During the confrontation with Xiang Yu, the emperor’s frequent consolations led Bao Sheng to advise Xiao He to send his capable relatives to the army to allay suspicion, which he did, pleasing the emperor. When the emperor returned after pacifying the Taing Bu, the people stopped him on the road and wrote a letter saying that the prime minister had forcibly bought thousands of people's fields and houses at low prices. He gave Xiao He all the books written by the people and said: "You can apologize to the people yourself!" I hope that the people can farm and not harvest the stalks for animal food. The emperor was furious and said: Prime Minister accepted their bribe and asked for my Linyuan for them! So Xiao He was handed over to Tingwei and imprisoned with torture instruments. A few days later, Wang Weiwei served the emperor and asked: What serious crime has the Prime Minister committed that your Majesty detained him so roughly? The emperor's divination said: I heard that Li Si served as the prime minister for the Qin Emperor. Any good deeds should be attributed to the Lord, and any wrongdoing should be attributed to himself.
target: During Chen Xi and Han Xin’s rebellions, Xiao He helped Empress Lu kill Han Xin. The emperor granted him 5,000 households and a guard, but Zhao Ping warned this was due to suspicion, advising Xiao He to refuse the reward and fund the army. He complied, pleasing the emperor. When Yingbu rebelled, a retainer warned Xiao He’s popularity could lead to his extermination, urging him to damage his reputation by buying land cheaply. He did so, and the emperor was happy. Later, the emperor imprisoned Xiao He for requesting Linyuan for the people, but a courtier argued his loyalty, leading to his release. Xiao He served Emperor Hui, recommending Cao Shen as his successor. He died in the second year of Xiaohui’s reign, posthumously named Wen Zhonghou. His descendants inherited his title, with later emperors restoring it after extinctions.

Mourning Clothes". The Confucian scholars in the capital all praised him. At that time, General Huo Guang was in power. target: Xiao Wangzhi, courtesy name Changqian, was a scholar from Lanling who later moved to Duling.
