The inferior ones were given approval or dismissed from office and sent back to their hometown. Everything Xiao Wangzhi reported was approved. He was successively promoted to admonish the doctor and prime minister Sizhi. He was promoted three times within a year and became an official of two thousand stone level.
target: After Huo Guang's death, Xiao Wangzhi was appointed as Minister of Ceremonies of Daxing. He warned Emperor Xuan about the dangers of ministers holding too much power, citing historical precedents. Emperor Xuan appointed him as a visitor, and he quickly rose through the ranks to become an official of two thousand stone level. He was later appointed as the governor of Pingyuan but preferred to serve in the court. He was eventually recalled to manage the Shaofu and later became Zuo Fengyi.

source: I am fortunate enough to be ranked among the ministers, and it is my duty to assist the two governments. I dare not fail to do my best. Xiao Wangzhi and Li Qiang retorted: The late emperor was a sage, benevolent and virtuous man who served in the imperial court. He formulated charters and promulgated decrees as a permanent system and long-term consideration of the living difficulties of the people on the border. Therefore, the first article of "Jinbulingjia" said The border counties suffered from wars several times and suffered from hunger and cold. The people could not live to the end of their lives and would die young. The father and son were separated and ordered the people of the world to jointly provide for their expenses. It turned out to be preparations for the sudden outbreak of war. It is said that in the fourth year of Tianhan Dynasty, prisoners on death row were asked to pay 500,000 yuan to avoid the death penalty and have their sentences commuted to one level. Powerful officials, officials and the people begged, robbed, borrowed, and even acted as thieves to obtain money to atone for their crimes. From then on, treacherous and evil people were rampant, and many thieves appeared at the same time, attacking cities and killing county guards. These people spread all over the mountains and plains, and officials could not stop them. The state publicly ordered to send embroidered messengers to lead the army to attack them, killing more than half of them, and then they declined and disappeared. We believe that this is caused by letting the death row inmates redeem themselves, so it is inappropriate to do so. At this time, Prime Minister Wei Xiang and Yushi doctor Bingji also believed that the Xiqiang rebels would be defeated and the transshipment supply could basically meet the needs, so they did not implement Zhang Chang's suggestions. Xiao Wangzhi served as Zuo Fengyi for three years, and everyone in the capital praised him. Was promoted to Dahonglu. Prior to this, King Weng Guimi of Wusun submitted a document through Changluo Hou Changhui, willing to take his grandson Yuan Guimi of the Han Dynasty as his heir, hoping to marry the young princess again, become an in-law, join the Han Dynasty, and betray the Huns. The emperor issued an edict to the ministers to discuss the matter. Xiao Wangzhi believed that Wusun was a remote area, and it was not a long-term solution to believe their good words and enter into a marriage thousands of miles away. The emperor didn't listen. In the second year of Shenjue's reign, Changluo Houhui was sent as an envoy to escort the princess to be betrothed to Yuan Guimi. Before leaving the border, Weng Guimi died, and his nephew Kuang Wang broke the agreement and proclaimed himself king. Chang Hui wrote to the emperor from under the fortress, hoping to let the princess stay in Dunhuang County temporarily. Chang Hui went to Wusun and blamed them for breaking the promise, so he made Yuan Guimi king and came back to welcome the princess. The emperor issued an edict to the ministers for discussion, but Xiao Wangzhi thought it was impossible. Wusun, the head of the rat, can't stick to the promise, and the consequences have been seen. The former princess had been in Wusun for more than forty years, and the relationship between husband and wife was not deep, so the border was not stabilized. This was already a test of the matter. Now that the young princess has come back because Yuan Guimi cannot inherit the throne, she has indeed failed the Yi people in all directions. This is a great thing for the Han Dynasty. If the young princess does not stay, corvee service will arise, and the root of the matter lies in Zaojie. The emperor followed his advice and summoned the princess back to the court. Later, although Wusun was divided into two parallel countries and made Yuan Guimi the great king, the Han Dynasty no longer entered into marriage with him. In the third year of Shenjue's reign, Xiao Wangzhi replaced Bingji as the imperial censor. During the Wufeng period, the Huns were in chaos. Most commentators believed that the Huns had been causing harm for a long time, and they could take advantage of the civil strife to send troops to eliminate them.
target: During the Xiqiang rebellion, Xiao Wangzhi opposed Zhang Chang's proposal to allow criminals to atone for their sins by donating food, arguing it would lead to inequality and moral decay. His views were supported by Prime Minister Wei Xiang and Yushi doctor Bingji, and the proposal was not implemented. Xiao Wangzith served as Zuo Fengyi for three years and was promoted to Dahonglu. He advised against marrying a princess to Wusun, citing the unreliability of the alliance, and the emperor eventually recalled the princess. During the Wufeng period, he advised against attacking the Huns during their civil strife, advocating for a policy of benevolence and assistance instead.

source: In the past, the Chanyu admired our dynasty's teachings, was dedicated to doing good, and regarded himself as his younger brother. He sent envoys to ask for peace. People in the four seas were very happy, and all the Yi and Di tribes heard about it. The treaty was not carried out to the end, and Shanyu was unfortunately killed by the rebels. To attack him now is to take advantage of the civil strife of others and take pleasure in others' misfortune. They will definitely run away. If we do not fight with benevolence and righteousness, we may be in vain. Envoys should be sent to express condolences, help them when they are weak, and rescue them when they are in trouble. The barbarians from all over the world will admire the benevolence and righteousness of the Han Dynasty. If he can return to the throne due to this favor, he will definitely surrender to the Han Dynasty. This is a grand act of virtue. The emperor followed his advice and finally sent an army to escort Huhanxie Shanyu to stabilize his country. At that time, Geng Shouchang, the chief minister of Nongzhong, proposed the establishment of Changpingcang. The emperor thought it was very good, but Xiao Wangzhi opposed it. Prime Minister Bingji was old and respected by the emperor. Xiao Wangzhi reported again: Some people live in poverty, thieves appear constantly, and many officials with a rank of two thousand stone are incompetent and incompetent. If the three ministers are not chosen properly, the sun, moon and stars will lose their brilliance. The sun and moon will have no light in the first month of this year, and the responsibility lies with our ministers. The emperor thought that Xiao Wangzhi meant to look down on the prime minister, so he ordered the imperial guards Jianzhang Weiwei Jin Anshang, Guangluxun Yang Pan, and the imperial censor Zhongcheng Wang Zhong to question Xiao Wangzhi.
target: Xiao Wangzhi later became the imperial censor but fell out of favor with Emperor Xuan due to conflicts with the prime minister and accusations of arrogance and misconduct.

source: He entertained him with the etiquette of a guest, placed Shan Yu above the princes and kings, and addressed him as a minister without addressing him by name. When Emperor Xuan was ill in bed, he selected ministers who could take care of his affairs. He summoned his relatives Shi Gao, Marquis of Leling, Prince Tai Fu Xiao Wangzhi, and Shao Fu Zhou Kan to the palace. Shi Gao was appointed as the Chief Chariot Cavalry General, Xiao Wangzhi was appointed as the former General Guang Luxun, and Zhou Kan was appointed as the Guanglu Doctor. When Emperor Xuan died, the prince inherited the title of Emperor Xiaoyuan. Xiao Wangzhi and Zhou Kan were originally respected by the emperor as masters. After the emperor ascended the throne, he summoned them several times in his spare time to discuss how to deal with chaos and explain the things of being an emperor. Xiao Wangzhi recommended Liu Gengsheng, a Sanqi admonishment official in the royal family who was well versed in Confucian classics, to serve as Shizhong, and he and Jin Chang, the attendant, served as ministers to the emperor. The four people made plans together and used ancient systems to advise and guide the emperor. There were many things they hoped to support and correct. The emperor trusted them very much and adopted their opinions. At the beginning, Emperor Xuan did not believe in Confucianism but Legalism, and the eunuchs in Zhongshu were in power. Zhongshu Ling Honggong and Shi Xian had been managing the central secrets for a long time, and were familiar with the laws and regulations. They also acted as partners with the cavalry general Shi Gao. When discussing government affairs, they often adhered to the old rules alone and did not listen to the opinions of Xiao Wangzhi and others. Hong Gong and Shi Xian were often refuted because of their paranoid and narrow opinions.
target: He was demoted to Crown Prince Tutor. After Emperor Yuan ascended the throne, Xiao Wangzhi served as a trusted advisor but clashed with eunuchs Hong Gong and Shi Xian.

source: Zhongshu Ling was by his side and knew what I was talking about. When Xiao Wangzhi heard about this, he used it to question Hong Gong and Shi Xian. Shi Xian and Hong Gong were afraid that Xiao Wangzhi would file a complaint on his own and the emperor would hand over the case to other officials, so they would threaten Zheng Peng and Hua Long. During the reign of Emperor Xuan, Hualong was waiting for an imperial edict with Zhang Zijiao and others. He was not appointed because of his bad conduct and wanted to attach himself to Zhou Kan and others. Zhou Kan and others did not accept him, so he made friends with Zheng Peng. Hong Gong and Shi Xian ordered them to report Xiao Wangzhi and others' intention to depose General Chaoqiu and alienate the Xu and Shi families. They waited for Xiao Wangzhi to go on vacation and instruct Zheng Peng and Hua Long to report to them. This matter was handed over to Hong Gong to inquire about the situation, and Xiao Wangzhi responded: Most of the relatives who hold important positions are extravagant and extravagant. I am here to help the country, not to do bad things. Hong Gong and Shi Xian reported that Xiao Wangzhi, Zhou Kan, and Liu Gengsheng colluded with their cronies to recommend each other, repeatedly slandered ministers, attacked and alienated the emperor's relatives, and wanted to use their power to gain power.
target: He was falsely accused of conspiring to depose the general and alienate the emperor's relatives, leading to his imprisonment. He committed suicide by drinking poison, deeply saddening Emperor Yuan.

source: Xiao Wangzhi asked his disciple Zhu Yun about this. Zhu Yun was a man who loved fame and honor, so he advised Xiao Wangzhi to commit suicide. At that time, Xiao Wangzhi looked up to the sky and sighed and said: I once served as a general, and I am over sixty years old. Isn't it too despicable to go to prison at an old age and live an ignoble life? The factory called Zhu Yun and said: You, come and get the medicine. I would rather die than stay alive for a long time! Finally he committed suicide by drinking poisonous wine. The emperor was shocked when he heard about this. He clapped his hands and sighed and said: I suspected that he refused to go to jail before, but he really killed my good teacher! At that time, the eunuch had just served lunch when the emperor pushed away the food and cried for Xiao Wangzhi. His sorrow moved the attendants around him. Immediately summoned Shi Xian and others to question them for their poor planning. They all took off their hats to apologize, and it took a long time before they gave up. Xiao Wangzhi died guilty, and the relevant departments requested that his title and title be abolished. However, the emperor issued an edict to increase his favor, and his eldest son Xiao Ji succeeded him as Marquis of Guannei. The emperor could not forget Xiao Wangzhi's memory, and sent envoys to pay homage to Xiao Wangzhi's grave during every year and festival. This was the case throughout the Yuan Dynasty. Xiao Wangzhi had eight sons, among whom Xiao Yu, Xiao Xian and Xiao You became high officials. Xiao Yu was named Cijun. When he was young, he was appointed as the prince's concubine due to his father's kindness. Emperor Yuan ascended the throne and served as a Langguan. He was dismissed due to illness and later became a censor. General Wang Feng, because of Xiao Yu's father's reputation and his own outstanding talents, appointed him as a meritorious officer, promoted to Yezhi, and served as deputy captain on an envoy to the Huns. Later, when he became the magistrate of Maoling County, during an inspection, Xiao Yu ranked sixth. However, Guo Shun, the magistrate of Qixian County, ranked last and was scolded. Xiao Yu interceded with him. Fufeng got angry and said, "You came sixth in the exam and you got away. How can you intercede for your colleagues?" After the examination, he went out and summoned Maoling to Hou Cao to ask him to report on the situation during his tenure. Xiao Yu walked straight out of Hou Cao, and the clerk followed him and grabbed him. Xiao Yu held down his saber and said: Xiao Yu is Du Ling's man, why should he go to Hou Cao! He hurriedly walked out, wanting to abandon his official position and leave. The next morning, the emperor issued an edict to summon him and appointed him as Sili Xiaowei. Xiao Yu passed by the gate of Fufeng Mansion, and officials and hundreds of people gathered in front of the car to pay their respects. Later he was dismissed from office for violating the general's will. He also served as Zhonglang General on an envoy to the Huns.
target: Xiao Wangzhi had eight sons, including Xiao Yu, Xiao Xian, and Xiao You, who became high officials. Xiao Yu was known for his bravery and integrity, serving in various positions despite frequent dismissals. Xiao Xian and Xiao You also held significant posts, with the Xiao family producing six or seven officials of two thousand stone level. The historian praised Xiao Wangzhi as a leading Confucian scholar and capable minister, lamenting his tragic death at the hands of sycophants and eunuchs.

source: Create what I call the strategy of pacifying Qianli by sending a message. , Xu Gong thanked him repeatedly and prepared carriages and horses to send Kuai Tong away. Kuai Tong persuaded the military ministers with these words. The military officials used a hundred chariots and two hundred cavalry to greet Duke Xu. When Yan and Fang heard about this, more than thirty cities surrendered, just as expected by Kuai Tong's strategy. Later, the Han general Han Xin captured the King of Wei, conquered Tiao and Dai, made Yan surrender, and pacified the three kingdoms one after another, and then led his troops eastward to attack Qi. The army had not yet passed Pingyuan County. When I heard that Liu Bang, the king of Han, had sent Li Shiqi to persuade Qi to surrender, Han Xin wanted to stop the advance. Kuai Tong lobbied Han Xin and said: General, you were ordered by the King of Han to attack the State of Qi, and the King of Han sent a separate envoy who was also a spy to persuade the State of Qi to surrender. Is there an edict ordering you to stop attacking? Why not march? Moreover, Mr. Li, as a scholar, rode there and persuaded more than 70 cities of Qi to surrender with his sharp tongue. General, you led tens of thousands of troops to capture more than 50 cities of Zhao. Having been a general for several years is not as great as the contribution of a Confucian scholar. So Han Xin thought what he said made sense, adopted his suggestion, and finally crossed the Yellow River. The King of Qi had listened to Li Shiqi's persuasion, so he left him behind, drank and had fun together, and removed the defense against the Han Dynasty. Han Xin therefore attacked the Qi army in Lixia and came to Linmiao City. The King of Qi thought that Li Shiqi had deceived him, so he put him in boiling water and boiled him to death. As a result, he was defeated and fled. Han Xin finally pacified Qi and established himself as the acting king of Qi. At that time, the King of Han was under siege in Rongyang, so he sent Zhang Liang to make Han Xin the official King of Qi, comfort him, and make him firmly side with the King of Han. Xiang Yu also sent Wu She to persuade Han Xin to join forces with him. Kuai Tong knew that the change of the world situation depended on Han Xin, and wanted to persuade Han Xin to betray the Han Dynasty, so he first hinted at Han Xin in cryptic words: I once learned the art of physiognomy, and observing your face, I can only be made a marquis, and you will always be in danger; but looking at your back, it is very noble and difficult to tell. Han Xin asked: What do you mean? Kuai Tong then asked others to go away, and then said: When the world first rises up, heroes and heroes establish themselves as princes and kings, raise their arms and shout, and the people of the world gather like clouds and mist, are mixed and accumulated like fish scales, and rise up quickly like a strong wind. People often only worry about overthrowing the Qin Dynasty. Now Liu Bang and Xiang Yu are fighting, and countless people have been displaced. The King of Han led hundreds of thousands of troops to defend Gong and Luo. Taking advantage of the dangers of the mountains and rivers, he fought several battles in vain. He was defeated and fled without rescue. He was defeated in Rongyang, wounded in Chenggao, and fled to Wan and Ye. This is said to be a person whose wisdom and courage are in trouble.
target: Kuai Tong, a native of Fanyang, lobbied Xu Gong, the magistrate of Fanyang, during the Chu-Han conflict. He warned Xu Gong that his harsh rule had created many enemies, and with Qin laws no longer enforceable, he was in danger. Kuai Tong then proposed a plan to Wu Chen, Wu Xinjun: rather than attacking cities, he should welcome Xu Gong with honor to encourage other cities to surrender. Wu Chen followed this advice, and over thirty cities surrendered without battle. Later, Kuai Tong persuaded Han Xin to attack Qi despite Li Shiqi's diplomatic mission, arguing that military conquest would earn greater merit. Han Xin agreed, crossed the Yellow River, and defeated Qi, leading to Li Shiqi's execution. Kuai Tong later urged Han Xin to betray Liu Bang and create a tripartite balance of power, warning that Han Xin's achievements made him a threat to the Han king. Han Xin hesitated, citing Liu Bang's kindness, and declined. Kuai Tong, fearing retribution, feigned madness. After Han Xin's execution, Liu Bang summoned Kuai Tong, who defended himself by saying a dog barks at those not its master. Liu Bang pardoned him. Kuai Tong later served as a guest to Cao Shen, the prime minister of Qi, and recommended the reclusive scholars Shu Guo and Liang Shijun. He also wrote a book on lobbying strategies.

source: Cao Xiangguo said: I respectfully accept your order. Treat both of them as distinguished guests. Kuai Tong discussed the contingency techniques of lobbyists during the Warring States Period, also added his own comments, and wrote a book called "Juan Yong". At the beginning, Kuai Tong had a good relationship with Qiren An Qisheng. An Qisheng once made suggestions for Xiang Yu, but Xiang Yu could not adopt them. Xiang Yu wanted to give Kuai Tong and An Qisheng titles and fiefs, but these two were always unwilling to accept them. Wu Bei, a native of Chu. Some people say that his ancestor is a descendant of Wu Zixu. Wu Bei became famous for his talents and served as a lieutenant in Huainan Kingdom. At that time, the king of Huainan, Liu An, loved academics and was devoted to the virtuous. He recruited hundreds of handsome and learned people, and Wu was ranked first. After a long time, the king of Huainan conspired to rebel, and Wu was admonished privately many times. Later, the King of Huainan was sitting in Shu Palace and summoned Wu Bei to discuss matters with him. He called: General, please come forward. Wu was asked: Where did the king get the words of subjugation? Once upon a time, Wu Zixu advised the king of Wu, but the king did not accept it. Wu Zixu said: "Now I see elk roaming on the Gusu platform, and now I will also see thorns growing in the palace, and dew soaking the skirts of my clothes." So the King of Huainan was very angry and detained Wu Bei's parents and imprisoned them for three months. The king of Huainan summoned Wu Yuan again and said, "General, have you listened to me?" Wu Bei said: No! I will advise you, your Majesty. I heard that smart people are wise and can predict things before they appear, so the saints are foolproof when doing things. King Wen of Zhou's actions made him famous in later generations, and he was listed as the second king. Creation means that he should act in accordance with the heart of heaven. King Huainan asked: Is the Han Dynasty now stable or chaotic? Wu was said: The world is safe and sound. King Huainan said unhappily: "Why do you say that the world is stable?" Wu Bei replied: I have privately observed that the relationship between the emperor and his ministers, father and son, husband and wife, elder and younger are all orderly and reasonable. Everything the emperor does follows the way of the ancient sage kings. The customs are honest and the rules and regulations are perfect. Wealthy merchants traveled around the world carrying large amounts of goods in their vehicles. Roads were open to all directions and trade was very prosperous.
target: Wu Bei, a descendant of Wu Zixu, served as a lieutenant in Huainan under King Liu An. When the king plotted rebellion, Wu Bei repeatedly admonished him, arguing that the Han dynasty was stable and prosperous, with orderly governance, thriving trade, and subdued enemies. The king dismissed this, citing the Qin collapse as precedent. Wu Bei countered that Qin's tyranny had caused widespread suffering, while the Han emperor ruled with benevolence and had popular support. He warned that rebellion would fail, as the king's forces were weak and the times were peaceful. The king ignored him and proceeded with plans, but the conspiracy was discovered. Wu Bei surrendered and confessed, but was executed despite his earlier praise of Han, as Zhang Tang argued his initial role in planning the rebellion was unforgivable.

source: The emperor thought that Wu Ban always praised the beauty of the Han Dynasty and wanted not to kill him. Zhang Tangjin said: Wu Ban first planned a rebellion for the King of Huainan. His crime was so heinous that it cannot be pardoned. Wu Ban was finally killed. Jiang Chong, courtesy name Ciqian, was a native of Handan, Tongguo. Jiang Chong's real name was Jiang Qi. He had a younger sister who was good at playing the piano and dancing and married Prince Liu Dan. Jiang Qi was favored by King Zhao Jingsu and Liu Pengzu and became his first-class guest. After a long time, Prince Liu Dan suspected that Jiang Qi had told the king of his secrets, so he fell out with Jiang Qi and sent officials to hunt down Jiang Qi. When they didn't catch him, he arrested his father and brother, interrogated them, and beheaded them all in public. Jiang Qi then fled in hiding, entered Guanzhong in the west, changed his name to Jiang Chong, and went to the palace to report that the crown prince Liu Dan had committed adultery and incest with his half-sister and the concubines of King Zhao.
target: Jiang Chong, originally named Jiang Qi, fled to Chang'an after a feud with Prince Liu Dan of Zhao. He reported the prince's incest and adultery, leading to Liu Dan's deposition. Jiang Chong gained Emperor Wu's favor through his appearance and advice on foreign policy.

source: Jiang Chong had already come to Emperor Wu. Emperor Wu asked him about the political affairs of the country at that time and was very satisfied with him. Jiang Chong then voluntarily requested to be sent as an envoy to the Xiongnu. Emperor Wu sent a letter to Shao Shu asking about the strategy of the envoy. Jiang Chong replied: It is necessary to adapt to changes and adapt to circumstances, not to plan in advance. Emperor Wu appointed Jiang Chong as his visitor. After Jiang Chong came back from his mission to the Xiongnu, he was appointed as the envoy of Zhizhi Xiuyi, supervising the thieves in the Sanfu area and prohibiting the powerful and wealthy from excessive luxury and going beyond the system. Many of the noble relatives and the emperor's ministers were extravagant and violated the system. Jiang Chong reported and impeached them, and wrote a letter requesting that their carriages and horses be confiscated and put on standby in the Northern Army to prepare for the attack on the Huns.
target: He was appointed to supervise the capital, enforcing laws against luxury and arresting offenders. He detained the prince's envoy for using the imperial road, earning the emperor's praise.

source: As a result, Jiang Chong gained great credibility and became a powerful figure in the capital. Jiang Chong was promoted to Captain Shuiheng, and many of his family and friends received help from him. After a long time, he was dismissed from office because of his crime. It happened that Zhu Anshi of Yangling reported that Prime Minister Gongsun He's son and Grand Servant Gongsun Jingsheng had cursed the emperor with witchcraft, which implicated Princess Yangshi and the princesses of Zhuyi. Gongsun He and his son were killed as a result. See "The Biography of Gongsun He" for details. Later, Emperor Wu visited Ganquan Palace and fell ill. Jiang Chong saw that Emperor Wu was old and was afraid that he would be killed by the prince after his death, so he took the opportunity to cause trouble and wrote a letter saying that the emperor was ill because someone was practicing witchcraft. So Emperor Wu appointed Jiang Chong as an envoy to investigate and deal with those who practiced witchcraft. Jiang Chong directed the Hu wizards to dig in the ground everywhere, looking for puppets, and arresting those who engaged in witchcraft and night-time ritual curses. Let the Hu wizards observe the places contaminated by ghosts, mark them, dig out the puppets, arrest the people in the package, torture them, heat the iron, roast the interrogated person, and force him to confess.
target: Later, fearing the prince would harm him after the emperor's death, Jiang Chong fabricated a witchcraft scandal, accusing the prince of cursing the emperor.

source: At that time, Emperor Wu was already old and suspected that everyone around him was practicing witchcraft to curse him. No matter whether he was guilty of this crime or not, no one dared to file a lawsuit. Jiang Chong had already understood the emperor's thoughts and took the opportunity to say that there was a witchcraft spirit in the palace. He first investigated the wives in the harem who were not favored by the emperor, and then in turn got the queen's head. Finally, he dug out the witchcraft in the palace and obtained the Tongmu Ren. The prince was very frightened and could not explain to the emperor himself, so he arrested Jiang Chong and personally supervised and executed him.
target: He tortured confessions, killing tens of thousands. The prince, unable to defend himself, arrested and executed Jiang Chong. The prince's rebellion failed, and Emperor Wu later annihilated Jiang Chong's clan.

source: He scolded: You are a slave of the country! Isn't it enough to disturb your king and his son? Come to disturb our father and son again! The prince was finally defeated because of this. For details, see "The Biography of Prince Ru." Later, Emperor Wu found out that Jiang Chong was responsible, so he annihilated his three clans. Xifu Gong, whose courtesy name is Ziwei, is from Heyang County, Hanoi County. When he was young, he was a doctoral student, studied "Spring and Autumn", and read biographies and books of hundreds of schools of thought. His majestic appearance made everyone feel strange. When Emperor Ai first came to the throne, the queen's father, Fu Yan, the Marquis of Kongxiang, and Xifu Gong were from the same county. They had a good relationship. Therefore, through Fu Yan's introduction, Xifu Gong's circle of friends became wider and wider. Before this, Sun Chong of Chang'an was also known for his good lobbying skills. He was dismissed when he was the governor of Runan County. He made friends with Xi Fu Gong, and they both submitted letters at the same time and were recruited to obey the emperor's orders. At that time, Emperor Ai was ill and had just ascended the throne. Someone reported that the Queen Mother of King Xiao of Zhongshan had cursed the emperor with witchcraft. The Queen Mother and her brother Feng Shen, the Marquis of Yixiang, committed suicide, but their charges have not yet been found out.
target: Xifu Gong, a scholar from Heyang, gained fame through his friend Fu Yan, the queen's father. With Sun Chong, he fabricated a plot against King Shuping Liu Yun, accusing him of witchcraft. The king and his associates were executed, and Xifu Gong was made Marquis of Yiling. He became a close advisor to Emperor Ai, criticizing officials and proposing policies, including expanding irrigation canals.

source: Emperor Ai promoted Sun Chong to be the prefect of Nanyang County, Tan, the right master, to be the captain of Yingchuan County, and Song Hong and Xifu Gong were both appointed to the post of Zuo Cao, the official of Guanglu. At that time, Dong Xian, the servant, was very favored by the emperor. The emperor wanted to make him a marquis, so he issued an edict saying: Xifu Gong and Sun Chong reported the conspiracy through Dong Xian. Now Dong Xian is made Marquis of Gao'an, Sun Chong is Marquis of Fangyang, and Xifu Gong is Marquis of Yiling. Each of them has a thousand households. The right master was given the title of Marquis Tan Guannei and was given the title of food town. Prime Minister Wang Jiaxin suspected that King Shuping's case was untrue and wrote a letter to argue, not wanting to make Dong Xian and others marquises. For details, see "Biography of Wang Jia". Wang Jia insisted that Dong Xian was too noble, and that Sun Chong and Xi Fu Gong were both insidious, treacherous, and had flattering and evil talents. They would definitely endanger the country and should not be appointed. Wang Jia was convicted for this. Since Xifu Gong was close to the emperor, he went to see him many times to discuss political affairs, pointing out gains and losses without any evasion. People are afraid of being impeached by him and dare not face him when they meet him. Xifu wrote a letter and falsely accused the ministers one by one, saying: The current Prime Minister Wang Jia is strong and impatient and cannot be appointed. Jia Yan, the imperial censor, was cowardly and incompetent. General Gongsun Lu, the general of the left, and Bao Xuan, the captain of the Sili school, both had false reputations for being upright, but in fact they were dull and unfamiliar with political affairs. Officials below Cao Cao are mediocre and not worth mentioning. If suddenly a powerful crossbow besieges the city, and a sharp halberd is pointed at the palace, who will you and your majesty take to guard against it? If the mob howls in the east, the Huns drink their horses in the Wei River, the borders are in danger, and the world is in turmoil, no matter how brave the soldiers and sophisticated weapons are in the capital, no one can take the lead in facing the enemy. Military documents were passed quickly and gathered in the capital, and urgent messages were passed to the court one after another. The mediocre ministers and cowardly people would be distracted and at a loss.
target: He suggested a deceptive strategy to weaken the Xiongnu by forging letters, but General Gongsun Lu opposed it. Xifu Gong also urged military preparations based on astrological signs, but Prime Minister Wang Jia warned against flattery and deceit. The emperor initially supported Xifu Gong, but after a solar eclipse, Dong Xian undermined him. Xifu Gong was dismissed and later accused of cursing the emperor.

source: The emperor sent the imperial censor and the imperial eunuch to arrest Xifu Gong and imprison him in Luoyang prison with an imperial edict. Just as he was about to be tortured and interrogated, Xifu bowed to the sky and shouted, falling to the ground. The officials went to check and found that Xifu Gong had stopped shouting, blood flowed from his nose and ears, and he died soon after. More than 100 of his close party members and friends participated in the conspiracy and were implicated and arrested. Xifu Gong's mother, Sheng, was convicted of treason and unruly because she offered sacrifices to the Kitchen God and begged for disaster to be brought upon the emperor. She was beheaded in public display. Xifu Gong's wife, Chonghan, and her family were moved to Hepu County. On the contrary, it will cause trouble for our government. However, Wusun has united with us before, and today together with the Xiongnu, they have submitted to our court. From a moral point of view, they cannot refuse. But Kang Ju was arrogant and unruly, and actually refused to worship the envoys of the Han Dynasty. The Duhu sent officials to their country, and they competed to let our officials sit under the envoys from Wusun and other countries. After the king and the nobles had finished eating, they only let the officials of the Duhu eat, deliberately ignoring the Han envoys to show off to other countries. Inferring from these things, why did they send princes to serve the emperor? They just want to do business, and all the good things they say are lies. Dunhuang, the small counties of Jiuquan, and the eight southern countries were in great difficulty in providing food and drink for the envoys, horses, donkeys, and camels. About two thousand miles northwest from Kangju, there is the state of Yancai. There are more than 100,000 warriors who can shoot arrows.
target: During Emperor Xuan's reign, the Han Dynasty killed Zhizhi Chanyu. Under Emperor Cheng, King Kangju was arrogant, and the Protectorate recommended cutting ties, but the court maintained relations. Yancai, northwest of Kangju, had over 100,000 warriors and customs similar to Kangju.

source: There are 60,000 households, a population of 300,000, and an army of 60,000. There is one deputy king and one assistant king. source: In the Wusun Kingdom, Da Kunmi governed Chigu City and was sent to Chang'an for 8,900 miles. There are 120,000 households, a population of 630,000, and an army of 188,800 people. Later, Wusun Kunmo defeated Dayuezhi, and Dayuezhi moved westward and surrendered to Daxia. target: The Wusun Kingdom, governed by Da Kunmi from Chigu City, was located 8,900 miles from Chang'an. It had 120,000 households, a population of 630,000, and an army of 188,800. The kingdom had a structured government with officials including a prime minister, generals, marquises, and eunuchs. The land was grassy, rainy, and cold, with residents practicing nomadic herding like the Xiongnu. The country was rich in horses, with wealthy individuals owning up to 4,000-5,000. The people were strong-willed but greedy and unfaithful. Wusun originally submitted to the Xiongnu but later became powerful and resisted them. It bordered the Xiongnu, Kangju, Dawan, and various Chengguo Kingdoms. The region was originally inhabited by the Sai people, then conquered by the Dayuezhi, and later by Wusun Kunmo, who incorporated both Sai and Dayuezhi populations.

source: This incident is recorded in "The Biography of Zhang Qian". Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty came to the throne and ordered Zhang Qian to bring gold coins and treasures to Wusun. Kun Mo met Zhang Qian with the attitude of the Xiongnu Chanyu. Zhang Qian was very ashamed and angry, and said to Kun Mo: If you don't thank the emperor for giving you a gift, then return the gift to us. Kunmo stood up and thanked him, but in other respects he remained the same. At the beginning, Kunmo had more than a dozen sons. The middle son Dalu was very strong and good at leading troops. He led more than 10,000 cavalry and lived elsewhere. Dalu's brother was the prince, and the prince had a son named Cen Zuo. The prince died early. Before his death, he said to Kunmo: "Cen Zou must be the prince." Kunmo was sad and agreed. Dalu was very angry about this incident, so he captured all the other brothers, led his soldiers to rebel, and prepared to attack Cen Zuo. Kunmo gave Cen Zuo more than 10,000 cavalry and ordered him to station elsewhere. He also had more than 10,000 cavalry for self-defense. At this time, the country was divided into three parts, all under the control of Kunmo. After Zhang Qian handed over the gifts given to Kunmo by the Han Dynasty, he said to Kunmo: If Wusun can return to his hometown, the Han Dynasty will send the princess as Kunmo's wife. The two countries will become brotherly countries and resist the Xiongnu together. The Xiongnu will definitely be defeated. But Wusun was far away from the Han Dynasty, and the size of the Han Dynasty was unknown. Wusun himself was close to the Xiongnu and had obeyed the Xiongnu for a long time. None of the ministers were willing to move eastward. Kunmo is old, the country is divided, and power cannot be concentrated. So an envoy was sent to take Zhang Qian back to Chang'an, and at the same time, he offered dozens of horses as a thank you. The envoy saw that the Han Dynasty had a large population and rich products. After returning home, Wusun respected the Han Dynasty more and more. When the Xiongnu heard that Wusun had contact with the Han, they were very angry and wanted to attack Wusun. In addition, the envoys of the Han Dynasty passed south of Wusun to Dayuan and Yuezhi, and they were not stopped on the road. Wusun was very frightened, so he sent an envoy to offer horses to the Han Dynasty and offered to marry Princess Mo, and the two countries became brothers. The emperor asked the ministers for their opinions, and the court agreed. Decision: The bride price must be paid first, and then the princess must be sent away. Wusun gave a thousand horses as a betrothal gift. During the Yuanfeng period of the Han Dynasty, Xijun, the daughter of King Liu Jian of Jiangdu, was sent to marry Kunmo as a princess. The emperor gave her carriages, horses and royal utensils. He also equipped her with hundreds of officials, eunuchs, maids and servants, and gave her rich gifts. Wusun Kunmo took Mr. Bin as his right wife. The Xiongnu also sent women to marry Kunmo, and Kunmo took the Xiongnu girl as his left wife. After the princess arrived in Wusun, she built a palace to live in. She had gatherings with Kunmo several times a year, drank and ate, and rewarded the nobles around Kunmo with property, silk fabrics, etc. Kunmo was old and couldn't understand the language. The princess was very sad and composed a song by herself: My family married me to the far side of the sky, and asked King Yan of Wu to come to a foreign country far away.
target: Zhang Qian, sent by Emperor Wu of Han, attempted to persuade Wusun to return to their homeland and ally with Han against the Xiongnu. Kunmo initially treated Zhang Qian with Xiongnu-like arrogance but eventually showed respect. Wusun was divided among Kunmo's sons, with internal conflicts over succession. Despite Zhang Qian's efforts, Wusun was reluctant to move east due to distance and longstanding ties with the Xiongnu. However, after envoys saw Han's wealth, Wusun grew more respectful. The Xiongnu, angered by Wusun's contact with Han, threatened attack, leading Wusun to propose marriage to a Han princess. The Han agreed, and during the Yuanfeng period, Princess Xijun was sent to marry Kunmo. The Xiongnu also sent a bride, and Kunmo took both as wives. The princess, homesick and unable to communicate with the elderly Kunmo, composed a sorrowful song. Emperor Wu, pitying her, sent gifts regularly.

source: The dome is the room, the walls are the walls, the meat is the food, and the cheese is the pulp. Living in this land, I miss you and my heart hurts. I wish you could return to your hometown as a yellow swan. When the emperor heard about it, he felt pity for her and sent envoys every other year to deliver curtains, brocade and other items. Kunmo is old and wants his grandson Cen Zuo to marry the princess. The princess disagreed and wrote to the emperor explaining the matter. The emperor replied: Following the custom of Wusun country, Mo wants to join forces with Wusun to destroy the Xiongnu. Cen Zuo married the princess. Kun Mo died, and Cen Zou became king in his stead. Cen Zuo is an official title, and his name is Jun Xumi. Kunmo is the king's name, and his name is Liejiaomi. Later, the king was named Kunmi. Cen Zuo married the princess of Jiangdu and gave birth to a daughter named Shaofu. After the princess died, the Han Dynasty sent Jieyou, the granddaughter of King Liu Wu of Chu, to marry Cen Zou for the princess. Cen Zou's son Nimi by his Hun wife was still young. When Cen Zou was about to die, he passed the throne to his uncle Dalu's son Weng Guimi. He said: When Nimi grows up, he will return the throne to Nimi. Weng Guimi came to the throne and was named King Fei. He married Jieyou and gave birth to three sons and two daughters: the eldest son was named Yuan Guimi; the second son was named Wannian and was the king of Shache; the third son was named Dalue and was the general of Zuo; the eldest daughter was named Shi and was the wife of King Jiangbin of Qiuci; the younger daughter was named Suguang and was the wife of Ruohulinghou. During the reign of Emperor Zhao of the Han Dynasty, Princess Jieyou wrote to the emperor, saying that the Xiongnu sent cavalry to farm in Cheshi, and that the Cheshi and the Xiongnu united to invade Wusun, hoping that the emperor would rescue them. The Han Dynasty prepared soldiers and horses to attack the Xiongnu. When Emperor Zhao died and Emperor Xuan had just ascended the throne, Princess Jieyou and Kunmi both sent envoys to write, saying that the Xiongnu invaded and attacked Wusun in succession, captured Cheyan, Eshi and other places, and plundered all the local residents. He also sent an envoy to tell Wusun to send the princess to the Huns as soon as possible, hoping to destroy the relationship between Wusun and Han. Kunmi is willing to send half of the country's elite troops and prepare 50,000 cavalry to attack the Xiongnu with all his strength. I hope the emperor will send troops to rescue the princess and Kunmi as soon as possible. The Han Dynasty sent an army of 150,000 cavalry, led by five generals. This incident is recorded in "The Biography of the Huns". The Han Dynasty also sent Lieutenant Chang Hui as an envoy to protect the Wusun soldiers. Kunmi personally led a total of 50,000 knights under the Marquis of Ji to attack the Xiongnu from the west. When the Xiongnu arrived at the royal court of Yougu Li, they captured 40,000 people including Shanyu's father, sister-in-law, Juzi, Ming Wang, Ligu Duwei, Qian Chang, and cavalry generals, as well as more than 700,000 horses, cattle, sheep, donkeys, and camels. Wusun took these trophies away. When the Han army returned home, Emperor Xuan granted Chang Hui the title of Marquis of Changluo.
target: After Kunmo's death, his grandson Cen Zuo married the princess per Wusun custom, as Emperor Wu approved to maintain the alliance. Cen Zuo became king, and the princess bore a daughter. Upon her death, Princess Jieyou, granddaughter of a Han king, was sent to marry Cen Zuo. Cen Zuo's son by his Xiongnu wife was young, so the throne passed to his uncle's son, Weng Guimi, who married Jieyou and had three sons and two daughters. During Emperor Zhao's reign, Princess Jieyou sought Han aid against Xiongnu attacks. Emperor Xuan later sent a large force, including 150,000 Han cavalry and 50,000 Wusun troops, defeating the Xiongnu and capturing many people and livestock. Wusun took the spoils. Emperor Xuan rewarded Chang Hui, who had led the Wusun forces.

source: The Han Dynasty also sent Lieutenant Chang Hui as an envoy to protect the Wusun soldiers. Kunmi personally led a total of 50,000 knights under the Marquis of Ji to attack the Xiongnu from the west. When the Xiongnu arrived at the royal court of Yougu Li, they captured 40,000 people including Shanyu's father, sister-in-law, Juzi, Ming Wang, Ligu Duwei, Qian Chang, and cavalry generals, as well as more than 700,000 horses, cattle, sheep, donkeys, and camels. Wusun took these trophies away. When the Han army returned home, Emperor Xuan granted Chang Hui the title of Marquis of Changluo. This year is the third year of the original year. The Han Dynasty also sent Chang Hui with valuable belongings and silk fabrics to be given to the nobles of Wusun who had made military exploits. In the second year of Yuankang, Wusun Kunmi wrote to Emperor Xuan through Chang Hui, saying: I would like to make my grandson Yuan Guimi of the Han Dynasty the heir to the throne, and let him also marry a Han princess, form a double marriage, and sever ties with the Huns. I am willing to use a thousand horses and mules as a betrothal gift. Emperor Xuan ordered ministers to discuss the matter. Xiao Wangzhi, the great emperor, thought: Wusun is located very far away and there is no guarantee that it will not change. Don't agree to their request. Emperor Xuan admired Wusun's recent great achievements and found it difficult to sever the established marriage relationship, so he sent an envoy to Wusun to receive the betrothal gift first. Kunmi, the crown prince, the left and right generals, and the captain sent a delegation of more than 300 people to the Han Dynasty to welcome the young princess. Emperor Xuan took Princess Jieyou's niece and husband as the princess, and appointed more than a hundred officials, maids, etc. to live in Shanglin Garden and learn the Wusun language. Emperor Xuan personally came to Pingganguang, met with the Huns envoys and foreign princes, performed a jiaoduan drama, music, singing and dancing, and then sent the princess to the west to marry. The envoy Chang Luohou Guanglu, the doctor Chang Hui assisted, and four people were envoys to send the young princess to Dunhuang. Before leaving the frontier fortress, they heard that Wusun Kunmi Weng Guimi had died. According to the agreement made by Cen Zou during his lifetime, the Wusun nobles appointed Cen Zou's son Nimi as Kunmi, named Kuangwang. Chang Hui wrote to Emperor Xuan saying: He wanted to keep the young princess in Dunhuang temporarily. Chang Hui rushed to Wusun and blamed Yuan Guimi for not appointing Yuan Guimi as Kunmi, and then took the young princess back to Chang'an. The matter was discussed by the ministers, and Xiao Wangzhi said: "It is difficult to make a treaty with Wusun, who is headed by a rat." Princess Jieyou has been in Wusun for more than 40 years. The relationship between the two countries is not close and the border is not peaceful. This is proved by creation. Today, the young princess returned to Chang'an because Yuan Gui was not able to stand up. She did not feel sorry for Wusun, and it was also a blessing for the Han Dynasty. If the young princess does not stop going to Wusun, the corvee will flourish, and this is where the roots begin. Emperor Xuan accepted this opinion and took the young princess back to Chang'an. The mad king married Princess Jieyou again and gave birth to a son named Ou Mi. The mad king was at odds with the princess and was cruel and unpopular.
target: Wusun Kunmi proposed making his Han-descended grandson Yuan Guimi heir, with a double marriage to sever ties with the Xiongnu. Emperor Xuan agreed but faced opposition from officials like Xiao Wangzhi, who doubted Wusun's reliability. Despite this, the emperor proceeded, sending a young princess to Wusun. However, Weng Guimi died before her arrival, and the throne passed to Nimi, Cen Zuo's son. Chang Hui advised keeping the princess in Dunhuang, and after debate, Emperor Xuan recalled her. Princess Jieyou remained in Wusun for over 40 years, and the mad king, who succeeded, was cruel and unpopular.

source: The Han Dynasty sent Wei Si Ma Wei Heyi and deputy candidate Ren Chang to send a servant to Wusun. The princess told the Wusun people that the mad king was dissatisfied and said it would be easy to get rid of him. So, they planned to have someone kill the mad king with a sword at the cocktail party. The sword failed to cut accurately, and the mad king was injured, so he mounted his horse and fled. His son Tao Shenshou led his troops to surround Princess Wei Heyi, Ren Chang and Heyou in Chigu City. A few months later, Zheng Ji, the governor of the Western Regions, sent troops from nearby countries to rescue him and bundled up Shen Shou and fled. The Han court sent Zhang Zun, a lieutenant general, to bring medicine to the mad king to treat his injuries. He also gave the mad king twenty kilograms of gold and various silk fabrics. They also arrested Wei Heyi and Ren Chang, who were transported from Yuli to Chang'an in a prison car and beheaded. The chariot general Shi Zhangweng stayed in Chigu to investigate the murder of the mad king by Princess Jieyou, Wei Heyi and Ren Chang. The princess was dissatisfied, kowtowed to Zhang Weng, and refused to plead guilty. Zhang Weng threw the princess's hair and cursed. The princess wrote to Emperor Xuan, and Zhang Weng returned to Chang'an and was executed. Ji Du, the deputy envoy of the Han Dynasty, led others to treat and nurse the mad king's injuries. When he returned to Chang'an, the mad king led more than ten knights to see him off. Ji Du returned to Chang'an, knowing that the mad king was guilty and should be beheaded, but failed to get rid of the mad king and was castrated. When the mad king was injured, Wujiutu, the son of Fat King Weng Guimi's Huns wife, fled to the northern mountains with all the princes, threatening that the Huns soldiers from his grandmother's house were coming soon, so many people surrendered to him. Later, he attacked and killed the mad king and established himself as Kunmi.
target: A plot to kill him failed, leading to conflict. The Han intervened, executing those involved. Later, Wujiutu, a son of Weng Guimi, killed the mad king and declared himself Kunmi. The Han sent forces but ultimately negotiated, dividing Wusun into two Kunmi with separate households.

source: Later, the Wujiu Massacre failed to return all the people of the Xihous to their original owners. The Han Dynasty sent Changluohou Changhui to lead three schools to farm in Chigu, and divided the ruling areas within Wusun. Dakunmi had more than 60,000 households, and Xiaokunmi had more than 40,000 households. However, people's hearts were in favor of Xiaokunmi. Yuan Guimi and Juan Mi both died of illness. The princess wrote to Emperor Xuan, saying that she was homesick in old age and hoped to die in Han. Emperor Xuan took pity on her and sent someone to welcome her and her three grandchildren to Chang'an. This year is the third year of Ganlu, and the princess is nearly seventy years old. Emperor Xuan gave the princess fields, houses, slaves, etc., and she was well supported. The etiquette for meeting the emperor was the same as that for the emperor's own princess. Two years later, Princess Jieyou passed away, and her two grandchildren stayed in Chang'an to guard the tomb.
target: Princess Jieyou, now elderly, was allowed to return to Chang'an, where she died two years later.

source: The Xiongnu Chanyu was appointed Chen Liang, and eventually he was made the captain of Wuben. Three years later, the Chanyu died. His younger brother Wu abandoned the Chanyu and established him as the Chanyu in Xian. He also made peace with Wang Mang. Wang Mang sent an envoy to bring a lot of gold, treasure, silk and satin to Shan Yu, demanding that Chen Liang, Zhong Dai and others be handed over. Chanyu arrested a total of twenty-seven people, including Chen Liang, Zhong Dai, Han Xuan, and Ren Shang, as well as Zhiyin, who killed Dao Hu himself, and their wives. They were all put into prison carts and handed over to the Han envoys. After arriving in Chang'an, Wang Mang burned and killed all these people. Later, Wang Mang deceived Shanyu again, and the harmonious relationship between the Xiongnu and Han was severed. The Huns invaded Han's northern border and Han's rule in the Western Regions collapsed. The Yanqi Kingdom was close to the Xiongnu, and they rebelled against the desert first and killed Danqin, the governor. Wang Mang was unable to send troops to conquer. It was only in the third year of Tianfeng's reign that he sent General Wang Jun of the Five Powers, Li Chong, the Protector of the Western Regions, and Guo Qin, the captain of the Wuji School, to the Western Regions. All countries in the Western Regions welcomed him in the suburbs and supplied him with food. King Yanqi also pretended to surrender to the Han Dynasty, but secretly prepared his own troops. Wang Jun and others led more than 7,000 soldiers from Yarkand and Qiuci into several groups and entered Yanqi. Yanqi set up an ambush to intercept Wang Jun and others. National soldiers such as Zhumo, Xianken and Yuti secretly communicated with Nie Yi and jointly attacked Wang Zhui and others, killing all Wang Zhui's officers and soldiers. Only Wuji captain Guo Qin led another army to Yanqi later. Yanqi's soldiers had not returned from the battle, so Guo Qin killed all the old and weak in their city and retreated back to the chief's room. Wang Ling conferred the title of Ginsengzi. Kuise gathered up the remaining soldiers and retreated to Kucha. A few years later, Wang Mang died, and Li Chong fled to the Western Regions, which cut off contact with the Central Plains dynasty. There are fifty countries in total. There are 376 people in total who have been translated as chiefs, city chiefs, kings, jailers, officials, dalu, baichang, qianchang, captains, ququ, danghu, generals, ministers, marquises, and kings, all wearing seals and ribbons issued by the Han Dynasty. Kangju, Dayuezhi, Anxi, Shanbin, Wuyi and other countries are not among the fifty countries because they are far away from the desert. If these countries come to Chang'an and make contributions, the Han Dynasty will repay them with considerable wealth and will not rule over them. Zan said: During the reign of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, he tried to subdue the Xiongnu. However, the Xiongnu threatened the various countries in the Western Region and united with the Southern Qiang, posing a serious problem to the Han Dynasty. Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty established four counties in Hexi and opened the Yumen Pass to connect the Western Regions to cut off the right arm of the Xiongnu and isolate the connection with the Southern Qiang and Yuezhi.
target: The text also details various other kingdoms in the Western Regions, including Gumo, Wensu, Qiuci, and others, with their distances from Chang'an, populations, armies, and administrative structures. It describes the Han Dynasty's efforts to establish agricultural colonies, such as in Luntai, and the challenges of maintaining control over distant territories. Emperor Wu's later years saw a shift away from expansion, with a focus on domestic recovery and reduced military campaigns. The narrative covers conflicts with the Xiongnu, internal rebellions, and the eventual decline of Han influence in the region, culminating in the collapse of the Western Regions Protectorate during Wang Mang's reign. The summary concludes with a reflection on the costs and benefits of Han's Western Regions policy, noting that while the region offered exotic goods, it also drained resources and led to instability.

source: Gu Yong, named Ziyun, was from Chang'an. His father, Gu Ji, served as Sima of the Wei Dynasty. As an envoy, he sent Shanyu Zhizhi's servant back to his country, but was killed by Zhizhi. This incident was recorded in the "Chen Tang Biography". Gu Yong wrote a short history of Chang'an when he was young, and later studied the classics extensively. During the reign of Emperor Jianzhao, Fan Yanshou, the imperial censor, heard that he had outstanding talents and appointed him as his subordinate. Later, he recommended him as Taichang Cheng. He wrote many memorials to discuss political gains and losses. In the winter of the third year of Jianshi's reign, a solar eclipse and an earthquake occurred on the same day. The emperor ordered the selection of scholars who were upright, dared to speak out, and could try their best to persuade. Tai Chang Yangcheng Marquis Liu Qingji recommended Gu Yong to wait for the imperial edict.
