source: During the reign of Emperor Jianzhao, Fan Yanshou, the imperial censor, heard that he had outstanding talents and appointed him as his subordinate. Later, he recommended him as Taichang Cheng. He wrote many memorials to discuss political gains and losses. In the winter of the third year of Jianshi's reign, a solar eclipse and an earthquake occurred on the same day. The emperor ordered the selection of scholars who were upright, dared to speak out, and could try their best to persuade. Tai Chang Yangcheng Marquis Liu Qingji recommended Gu Yong to wait for the imperial edict. Gu Yong replied: Your Majesty has the purest moral character of the most sage. He is worried about the strange phenomena warned by heaven and earth. He organizes his own state affairs, inquires and adopts the suggestions of the ministers, and issues wise orders, asking the officials to recommend people who dare to speak out. He takes the time to summon them to explore the origins of the changes, to find the reasons for the heaven's punishment, so that we scholars can come to the court of the sage to accept the inquiry of the sage. I am not very talented and have little knowledge, and I am not familiar with political affairs. I have heard privately that when a sage emperor ascends the throne, he should correct his appearance, speech, sight, hearing, and thinking, establish the rules of imperial rule, and obey the will of the Emperor of Heaven. Only in this way can many auspicious signs appear in sequence below, and only when the sun and moon move in the sky can there be Laws; if the king is too indulged in the harem, content with pleasure and hunting, and loses the correction of the five things, and the rules of rule cannot be established, then the signs of disaster will come and the six abnormal phenomena of punishment will appear. All disasters and visions appear, each symbolizing a fault and warning the world according to its type. So on the first day of the twelfth lunar month, when the solar eclipse was in Wu Nu, and the earthquake was in Xiao Qiang, both happened on the same day. I repeatedly told Your Majesty that those mistakes are not too far away, and you should deeply look for the reasons in yourself. Is it God's will that His Majesty pays attention to women's sex, does not worry about political affairs, does not behave prudently, and repeatedly loses his integrity? Is it because she dotes on concubines too much, because women do not abide by women's ethics, because they want to possess the Holy One alone due to jealousy, and hinder the prosperity of their descendants?
target: The emperor ordered the selection of upright scholars who dared to speak out. Tai Chang Yangcheng Marquis Liu Qingji recommended Gu Yong to await the imperial edict. Gu Yong replied that the emperor, with his pure moral character, was worried about the strange phenomena and sought advice. He stated that when a sage emperor ascends the throne, he must correct his appearance, speech, sight, hearing, and thinking, and establish imperial rules to obey the will of the Emperor of Heaven. If the king indulges in the harem, pleasure, and hunting, disasters will appear. The solar eclipse and earthquake were signs of faults, and the emperor should look for reasons within himself, possibly due to excessive attention to women, lack of political concern, or improper behavior.

source: Is it because she dotes on concubines too much, because women do not abide by women's ethics, because they want to possess the Holy One alone due to jealousy, and hinder the prosperity of their descendants? The ancient kings abolished the five principles of justice and lost the moral relationship between husband and wife. If their wives and concubines were favored, they could fulfill their requests internally and abuse their power externally, to the point of overthrowing the country and confusing and disrupting the order of yin and yang. In the past, Guo Si was in power, and Zong Zhou lost his country because of it; Yan's wife was arrogant and pampered, so she became prosperous, so there was a solar eclipse.
target: Gu Yong cited historical examples: Guo Si caused Zong Zhou's downfall, and Yan's wife's arrogance led to a solar eclipse.

source: This is a sign of a vision. The scriptures say: The principle of imperial rule is to greatly establish the rule of justice. The Sutra says: If the rules of governance are not upright, this is called non-establishment. At this time, the movement of the sun and the moon will be chaotic. Your Majesty ascended the most noble throne and became the monarch of the world. He accepted the responsibilities of an emperor to rule all living beings. Peace and instability in the four directions are all under your control. If you really can pay attention to self-correction, strive to do things to the best of your ability, reduce the time for private banquets to worry about the affairs of the world, give up and stay away from over-indulged pleasures, stop advocating for the entertainment of outstanding artists, put an end to behaviors that are not enjoyed by ghosts and gods, carefully control the fun of hunting and hunting, have certain rules in your daily life, follow the etiquette and law, manage political affairs personally, devote yourself to practical actions without being tired, and do everything with peace of mind as natural as nature. The scriptures say: From now on, kings who inherit the ancestral inheritance should not indulge too much in banquets or indulge in hunting, but should only revise themselves respectfully. There is no such thing as a lord who can cultivate the righteousness himself while his ministers are treacherous. The relationship between husband and wife is the rule of law for the king and the key to the safety of the country. It is what a wise king should be most cautious about. In the past, Shun warned the two women to speak and behave in a correct manner to make his noble character even nobler; King Zhuang of Chu endured the pain and did not see Danji, thus achieving the feat of overlord; King You of Zhou was deceived by Bao Si, and Zhou's virtue declined and the country perished; Duke Huan of Lu was coerced by Qi's daughter Jiang, and the state of Ji was overthrown. If you can really regulate the affairs of the harem and clarify the order of superiority and inferiority, those with high status cannot monopolize the emperor's favor due to jealousy, so as to cut off the traces of arrogance and arrogance, and suppress the troubles such as Guo Si and Yan's wife. Those with low status can serve the monarch in order, and each can perform their duties. It can expand the continuation of future generations, quell the resentment of "White Flowers" and the like, and make them rich financially with relatives in the harem, and do not let them participate in political affairs. This can alienate people like the emperor's father who rely on favor to get official positions, weaken the power of the wife's party, and the world will be in chaos without the maintenance of the boudoir.
target: He emphasized that the relationship between husband and wife is crucial for national safety. He advised regulating the harem, clarifying superiority and inferiority, and preventing jealousy and arrogance. He urged the emperor to correct himself, reduce private banquets, stop excessive pleasures, and follow etiquette and law. He also stressed the importance of selecting virtuous officials, assessing their merits, and avoiding favoritism. He warned that disasters are warnings from heaven, and if ignored, punishments will increase.

source: In the past three years, disasters and visions have appeared in droves, both large and small. This is because the actions are not in line with the will of the Emperor of Heaven, and the Emperor of Heaven is not happy, which is very obvious. If you don't seek the reasons within yourself, you won't be able to make corrections. If you recommend scholars quickly and solicit opinions widely, but don't adopt their opinions, you are following a path that is not in line with God's will. If you don't take practical actions to thank you, the punishment from the Emperor of Heaven will be heavier. These five matters are the laws of the king's political affairs and are important matters for governing from the south. I hope your majesty will pay attention to them. The emperor was surprised when the countermeasures were advanced and summoned Gu Cheng specially. That summer, all the founders were ordered to come up with countermeasures. This incident was recorded in "The Biography of Du Qin". After Gu Yong finished answering, he continued: I was fortunate enough to be able to make a statement about the effectiveness of the disaster. The disaster was extreme, and the words were related to the sage you listened to. The memorial statement was given in front of him, but His Majesty rejected it and refused to adopt it, but instead gave in to the correct countermeasures. He did not face up to the unusual phenomena that were worthy of worry, asked for ordinary opinions that were not urgent, and abolished the wise words that were in line with God's will. He offered useless empty words, trying to obliterate the disaster and deceive the emperor, so the emperor became angry. The storms between armies and Ji came three times, uprooting and breaking the trees. This is the most holy test of the emperor and cannot be deceived. The emperor specifically asked Gu Yong, and Gu Yong replied: The solar eclipse and earthquake were caused by the exclusive favor of the queen's concubine. This incident is recorded in the "Five Elements Chronicles". At this time, the emperor had just ascended the throne. He was modest and courteous and entrusted the political affairs to the general Wang Feng. Most of the ministers blamed Wang Feng. Gu Yong knew that Wang Feng had just been trusted and took power, and secretly wanted to rely on Wang Feng, so he said: Now that all the barbarians have surrendered, they have all become your concubines. There is no need to worry about making porridge or food in the north, and there is no need to worry about Zhao Tuo or Lu Jia in the south. The borders on three sides are stable, and there is no warning of military revolution. The big princes only had salaries in several counties, and the officials of the imperial court controlled their power, preventing them from doing anything. There was no longer a situation where Wu, Chu, Yan, and Liang stood side by side.
target: The emperor was surprised by Gu Yong's countermeasures and summoned him. Gu Yong continued, stating that the solar eclipse and earthquake were caused by the exclusive favor of the queen's concubine. He knew that General Wang Feng had just gained power and secretly wanted to rely on him. He argued that the borders were stable, the princes had limited power, and officials were loyal, so the disasters could not be blamed on the uncles. He advised the emperor to understand the warnings, change past mistakes, eliminate biased favor, and ensure all concubines served in turn to secure descendants and end disasters.

source: Now that the general has unfortunately passed away prematurely, it should be your turn to rank in order of closeness and ability. On the day of the ceremony, the scholar-bureaucrats in the capital were disappointed. This is all because we people are stupid and have low talents, and we cannot reward and praise even one ten thousandth of it. Recently I heard that you lead the city gate soldiers with the special rank, which makes the general of chariots and cavalry in power in the court with grace and grace, while your dearest uncle is holding the keys to the city gate outside. I'm personally unhappy for you. You should resolutely demand to resign, state that your talents are not enough to strengthen the guards of the city gate, accept the name of Taibo's humility, keep the path of humility, close the door and sleep in peace, and be the leader of wise people. I hope you will consider this matter with knowledgeable people, and I have arranged it for you. Wang Tan was very moved by his letter, so he refused to accept the position of leading the city gate. From then on, Wang Tan and Wang Yin were at odds with each other. Gu Yong was working as a county official in a distant place. He was worried about being harmed by Wang Yin, so he claimed that he had been ill for three full months and was relieved of his duties. Wang Yinzhuo asked Gu Yong to be appointed as the commander of the camp. Gu Yong apologized many times and stated his case, so he was transferred to the post of Chang Shi. Because Wang Yin transcended his close relatives and assisted in political affairs as a cousin, his power and influence were lower than those of Wang Feng. Gu Yong then persuaded Wang Yin and said: "The general holds the position of general, enfeoffs the fertile land of the big city, bears the same responsibilities as Duke of Zhou and Duke of Zhao, and controls the secrets of the world. It can be called the ultimate wealth. If there is no second among ministers, the world's blame will come from all sides. What will you rely on to occupy this position?" You should work tirelessly day and night, with a strong character like Yi Yin, to uphold your duties and assist the emperor, punish evildoers without avoiding those who are close to you, believe in and love them, and promote virtuous people without avoiding those who are hostile and hostile, so as to show the greatest justice and establish credibility in all directions. Only by concentrating on implementing these three aspects can you be able to shoulder heavy responsibilities for a long time and enjoy deep favor for a long time. Taibai appeared in the west for sixty days. According to the law, it should reach the sky. Now it has expired and is still among the mulberry trees. Its body is weak and its movement is slow. Its shape is small and its light is weak. Yinghuojiao is strong, large and bright, and is located in Ojuku in retrograde motion. When Mars is retrograde, it is fixed; when Mars is in Osu, it is mutable. Does God's will mean that the general forgets the deep and hidden righteousness, is submissive, the deacon is not strong, does not widely appoint scholars, still has taboos about likes and dislikes, and the magnanimous character is not pure, and is the beginning of betrayal by the generals and ministers? Why did Venus and Mars mutate like this when you just inherited the title of Sima? God is the most holy and will not show visions out of thin air. I hope that the general will look at all this with awe and caution, think deeply about the reasons for the changes, and change the way to seek governance to comply with God's will.
target: Gu Yong was promoted to Doctor Guanglu. He wrote to thank Wang Feng, praising his support. Later, when Wang Feng died, Wang Yin succeeded him. Gu Yong advised Wang Tan to resign from leading the city gate soldiers, which Wang Tan did, causing a rift with Wang Yin. Gu Yong then advised Wang Yin to work diligently, punish evildoers, and promote virtuous people. He warned about celestial signs like Taibai and Yinghuo, urging Wang Yin to change his ways to comply with God's will.

source: When Wang Yin died, Wang Shang, the Marquis of Chengdu, took his place as the Great Sima Wei General, and Gu Yong was promoted to the governor of Liangzhou. After finishing the performance in the capital, it was time to go to the ministry. At that time, a black dragon appeared in Shulai. The emperor sent a minister to ask Gu Yong to hear what he had to say. Gu Yong replied: I heard that the people who rule the world and occupy the country are worried that the monarch's behavior will endanger the country, but the words of warning of danger cannot be heard by the monarch. If the words of warning of danger were heard by the monarch immediately, then the Shang and Zhou Dynasties would not change their surnames and rise alternately, and the three generations would not change their politics but use each other. The Xia and Shang Dynasties were about to perish, and everyone on the road knew it, but the monarch safely thought that no one could harm him like the sun in the sky. Therefore, his sins became more and more serious, but he himself did not know it, and his fate was overthrown, but he did not realize it. "Book of Changes" says: Only those who can consider danger can maintain stability, and only those who can think of destruction can exist. If your Majesty can really listen to opinions magnanimously and wisely, without killing people because of taboos, so that the humble ministers can state everything they hear in front of you without worrying about future troubles, and the path of speaking out will be opened, then many wise men from all over the world will travel thousands of miles and gather at the court like the spokes of a car on an axis to express their loyalty. This is the greatest wish of the ministers and the long-term blessing of the country. The Han family follows the first month of the lunar calendar. The first month of the lunar calendar is black, and the black dragon is a symbol of the same surname. The dragon belongs to Yang De, from small to large, so it is the auspicious sign of the king. I wonder if someone with the same surname has seen that Fuqing, who has no heir in this dynasty, has many dangerous gaps, and wants to take advantage of this to invade and cause chaos and raise troops? Or do you start your mind and hope that your successor will be cruel and unkind, like Luling and Changyi? I am too stupid to make a decision. In September of the first year of the year, the black dragon appeared, and on the last day of September, there was a solar eclipse.
target: When a black dragon appeared, Gu Yong explained it as a sign of the same surname, possibly indicating a threat from a relative or a cruel successor.

source: When it comes to Your Majesty, just by violating the laws of heaven and indulging selfish desires, belittling oneself and acting recklessly, in the prime of life, without the blessing of an heir, but with the worry of danger and death, and by accumulating and losing the way to be a king, there are already many things that are not in line with God's will. As the descendants of our ancestors, if we preserve the merits and deeds of our ancestors, wouldn’t we be living up to our ancestors? Now the key to the safety and good fortune of the Sheji Ancestral Temple lies with Your Majesty. Your Majesty is really willing to carry forward the virtues of sage. He is clearly and deeply awakened to fear the majesty and wrath of God. He is deeply wary of the signs of danger and danger. He must wash away his bad ambitions and interests, cheer up and devote himself to political affairs. He must return to the way of a king wholeheartedly. He must prevent villains from being personal guests and avoid unfair appointment of officials. , all preparations for private slaves in the Beigong to go out, restrain themselves and restore etiquette, and do not make the mistake of leaving the palace for banquets in order to avoid imminent disasters. Think deeply about the signs of the two solar eclipses, refrain from detracting from the favor of the prosperous Jiaofang and Yutang, do not listen to the invitations of the harem, abolish the illegal prison in Yeting, fill up the traps like cannons, and kill the treacherous and flattering ministers. And those who come to serve the emperor in evil ways, in order to satisfy the world's expectations, temporarily stop the work of the early mausoleum, stop all kinds of repair and renovation projects of the palace, reduce the number of soldiers and reduce taxes, completely stop using the people's power, condolences and provide relief to the poor, so as to stabilize the distant places, encourage and respect the loyal and upright people, banish the cruel and tyrannical people, and do not let the officials who eat for free stay for a long time. Occupy a generous salary, carry out the work in sequence, persevere without violating it, be diligent in the morning and evening, review many times without getting tired, correct all the old mistakes, show new virtues, and no longer take small evils to heart, then the grand vision will almost disappear, the destiny will be gone without virtue, virtue will be almost restored, and the Sheji Ancestral Temple will be almost preserved. I hope Your Majesty will be careful not to repeat the same mistakes and carefully examine my words. I am fortunate to be appointed as a border official. I do not understand the gains and losses of this dynasty. My fallacies violate taboos and deserve death. Emperor Cheng was generous by nature and fond of articles. He had no heirs for a long time, traveled incognito many times, and often got close to favored and unscrupulous ministers. Zhao and Li were able to monopolize favors from their humble status. This was a constant worry for the Empress Dowager and her uncles morning and night. The people closest to him could not say much, so they recommended Gu Yong and others to take advantage of the changes in the celestial phenomena to sincerely advise and persuade the emperor to accept their words.
target: He warned about the dangers of women and evil people in power, citing historical examples. He criticized the emperor for indulging in private pleasures, neglecting duties, and causing disasters. He urged the emperor to reform, reduce taxes, stop excessive construction, and care for the people. The emperor was moved but did not fully trust Gu Yong.

source: As long as you can reflect on the words of the foolish minister for a moment, realize the three disasters, be deeply worried about the great vision, make up your mind to implement good governance, abandon and forget the evil ambition, do not make the same mistakes again, cheer up and devote yourself to governance, and transmit the greatest sincerity to heaven, then the long-standing vision in the sky will be stopped, and the disaster and rebellion on the ground will be subdued, what else is there to worry about? Privately, I am worried that Your Majesty is not single-minded in his public ambitions, that he is very reserved in his private hobbies, and that he still loves all the villains and is unwilling to pursue them! The emperor was very moved by his words. Gu Yong was generally as clear and accessible as Du Qin and Du Ye about scriptures, but he was not as comprehensive as Liu Xiang, his son and Yang Xiong. He was the most proficient in Tianguan and "Jingshi Yi", so he was good at talking about disasters and phenomena. He recounted more than 40 things before and after, with slight repetitions, and specifically blamed the lord himself and the harem. Being protected by the Wang family, the Lord also knew that he was not very close and trusted him. Gu Yong was very competent in every position he held. He served as the governor of the North for more than a year. General Wang Shangguan of the Guard and Wang Gen, the Marquis of Quyang, became generals of hussars. They recommended Gu Yong and conscripted him into the capital to be the chief agricultural officer. More than a year later, Gu Yongsheng became ill. Two months later, a supervisor petitioned to remove Gu Yong from his position. As a precedent, when a minister fell ill, the emperor granted him a leave of absence, and Shan Shan was immediately dismissed from his post when he arrived in Gu Yong. A few months later, Gu Yong died at home. His real name was Gu Bing, but it is said that he changed his name to Gu Yong because of Fan Bing's rebellion. Du Ye, named Zixia, was originally from Fanyang, Wei County. After accumulating meritorious service, my grandfather and father were promoted to county governors. During the reign of Emperor Wu, they moved to Maoling. Du Ye lost his father when he was young, and his mother was Zhang Chang's daughter. When Du Ye was in his prime, he studied with Zhang Chang's son Zhang Ji and obtained books from his family collection. He became a man because of his filial piety and integrity. Du Ye was friendly with the chariot general Wang Yin.
target: Gu Yong served as governor of the North and later died at home. He was proficient in Tianguan and "Jingshi Yi," and his memorials focused on the lord and the harem. Du Ye, styled Zixia, was from Fanyang and studied with Zhang Ji. He was friendly with Wang Yin and advised him to cooperate with Wang Shang. Du Ye later served as governor of Liangzhou but was dismissed due to illness.

source: In the past, what poets criticized and "Spring and Autumn" ridiculed was this, and probably not in other ways. When looking at the past from the perspective of the future, one resents it and thinks it is wrong. When it comes to one's own behavior, one does not look at oneself in the mirror and thinks it is right. This is a mistake in strategy. The alienated and despicable minister only saw it from the side. I suspected that there were people like me in the palace. The changes in heaven are not empty. If you try your best to protect the monarchs of all ages like this, why don't you correct the political affairs in accordance with God's will! I heard that the pheasant behaved strangely, and Emperor Gaozong was deeply moved; a strong wind blew violently, and King Cheng was frightened. I hope that your majesty will be more careful and sincere, consider inheriting the prosperity of the early period of the country, and examine ancient laws in everything to satisfy the people's wishes. Then the people of Li will not be unhappy. When the gods in heaven withdraw their power and anger, there is no need to worry about whether blessings and blessings will come in return: Du Ye died of illness without being awarded an official title. Du Ye talks about people spreading rumors to prepare for divination, and Gu Yong talks about kings buying private fields, and the divination of comets, meteorites and lock springs being lost. These are all recorded in "Five Elements Chronicles". At first, Du Ye studied with Zhang Ji. Zhang Ji's son Zhang Song lost his father when he was young and studied with Du Ye. He was also famous at that time, especially good at writing. Du Ye's son, Du Lin, was a quiet and ancient man, and also had great talents. He was a minister in Jianwu and the highest in the palace, Sikong. His writing skills were better than those of Du Ye and Zhang Song, so people say that the study of writing began with Si Gong. Zan said: During the era of Emperor Xiaocheng, the political power was entrusted to the family of relatives, and the uncles controlled the political power. Their power was even greater than that of the Lie family and the Fu family during the period of Emperor Xiaoai. Therefore, Du Ye dared to accuse the Ding family and the Fu family, while Qin did not dare to talk about the Wang family. This was because the situation made them like that. Du Qin wanted to suppress and reduce Wang Feng's power, but Du Ye relied on Wang Yin and Wang Shang. The same was true. Gu Yong stated Sanqi's warning, which showed his loyalty. When he cited Shen Bo's story to flatter Wang Huang, alienated Ping Ahou and General Chaoqi, and stated the changes of Jinhuo to seek reconciliation, he can be called a person who lacks integrity but is more than capable of talking.
target: During Emperor Ai's reign, he criticized the influence of the Fu and Ding families, warning about solar eclipses and earthquakes as signs of imbalance. He urged the emperor to follow ancient laws and satisfy the people's wishes. Du Ye died without an official title. The commentary notes that during Emperor Xiaocheng's era, power was with relatives, while during Emperor Xiaoai's era, the Fu and Ding families held power. Du Ye dared to accuse the Ding and Fu families, but Gu Yong avoided criticizing the Wang family due to circumstances. Gu Yong's loyalty was shown in his warnings, but he also flattered Wang Feng and alienated others, lacking integrity but excelling in rhetoric.

source: In the past, the system of the kings, from the emperor, princes to slaves, their official titles, salary, life and death system had different levels. The small ones could not surpass the big ones, and the lowly ones could not surpass the noble ones. Therefore, the top and bottom were orderly and the people's hearts were stable. Therefore, different geographical conditions such as land, rivers, lakes, hills, fertile land, plains, and depressions were identified, and the people were taught planting and livestock raising techniques. In this way, the people's supplies for daily life and funerals, including grains, livestock, fish, turtles, birds, beasts, firewood, wood, instruments, and other materials were produced. Production must follow certain seasons, and consumption must be controlled. Before the first month of the lunar calendar, one cannot go into the mountains and forests to cut down trees. Before the first month of the lunar calendar, one cannot go to the rivers and lakes to fish. In addition to complying with seasonal production, they are also not allowed to cut down small trees in the mountains, cut young grass by the lake, catch young insects, fish, or beasts, or collect bird eggs. This is to adapt to the seasonal climate and allow various organisms to reproduce and thrive. In this way, you can give full play to the effects of nature and make all kinds of property reserves abundant. Then, according to the natural conditions of the area, the scholars, farmers, industry and merchants gave full play to their intelligence and physical strength, got up early and went to bed late, managed their own industries, and exchanged with each other: the results of their work met their respective needs. In this way, there is no additional requisition of civilian manpower and material resources, and there is sufficient property in areas near and far. Therefore, the "Book of Changes" says: The monarch uses decrees to determine the changes in nature, assists the heaven and earth to suit the needs of the world, teaches the people to engage in production, produces various kinds of property, uses it in various aspects, and makes various utensils so that the world can benefit. This is the greatness of the sage, and this is what it means. "Guanzi" said: In ancient times, scholars, farmers, workers, and merchants were not allowed to live together. Scholars discuss benevolence and righteousness with each other in the place where they study, craftsmen discuss skills with each other in the government office, businessmen discuss wealth and profit with each other in the market, and farmers discuss farming affairs with each other in the fields. They are engaged in one occupation from morning to night and do not change when things change. Therefore, even if their father and brother's teachings are not strict, they can teach their children well; their children can learn skills even if they do not work hard. They are content with where they live and are happy to pursue their own professions. Even if they see strange and gorgeous items, they will not accept them because they are not suitable for their customs. This is just like the customs of the Rong people and Di people in the northwest and the Wuyue people in the southeast cannot be integrated. In this case, people's desires are few and things are simple, and property is abundant without competition. So the rulers use morality to guide them and use rituals to unify them. Therefore, the common people have integrity and courtesy, value benevolence and righteousness, and despise wealth. This is the summary of why the Xia, Shang and Zhou dynasties were able to develop along the right path and govern the country without resorting to harsh politics. When the Zhou royal family declined and etiquette was destroyed, Duke Zhuang of Lu violated Zhou etiquette by carving on the rafters of his father Huan Gong's temple and dyeing the pillars red. Zang Wenzhong, a senior official in the State of Lu, violated the Zhou rites by carving mountain shapes on the tops of the columns and painting algae on the short columns on the beams. Shiqing Ji of Lu State played music and dance in the temple with eight hundred people. The three families of Meng Sun, Shu Sun and Ji Sun of Lu State actually sang the poem "Yong" to remove the sacrifices when worshiping their ancestors. This trend spread to ordinary scholars and civilians. Everyone deviated from the system of the Holy King and gave up their business. The number of people working in agriculture decreased, and the number of people doing business increased. There was a shortage of food and an abundance of luxury goods. This trend of decline developed after Duke Huan of Qi and Duke Wen of Jin, etiquette and righteousness were greatly destroyed, superiors and subordinates offended each other, the politics of various countries were very different, the ethos of the officials were different, the activities of pursuing profit could not be curbed, and there was no end to the behavior of destroying the hierarchy. As a result, merchants sold rare and exotic goods, craftsmen produced utensils with no practical value, and scholars engaged in crooked activities to obtain wealth in pursuit of the favor of the times.
target: The ancient system of kings established hierarchical distinctions from emperor to slave, with graded official titles, salaries, and life-and-death rites, ensuring that the lowly did not surpass the noble, thus stabilizing society. People were taught to cultivate land and raise livestock according to seasonal and geographical conditions, with strict rules against cutting trees or fishing before the first lunar month, and prohibitions on harvesting immature plants, animals, or eggs to allow natural reproduction and abundant reserves. Scholars, farmers, artisans, and merchants each specialized in their occupations, exchanging goods to meet needs without excessive taxation, as noted in the "Book of Changes" and "Guanzi," which emphasized that people content with their professions and customs would have few desires and ample property, guided by morality and ritual. The decline began when the Zhou royal family weakened and etiquette collapsed, exemplified by Duke Zhuang of Lu violating Zhou rites by carving and painting his father's temple, and other officials like Zang Wenzhong and the three Huan families of Lu exceeding their ranks in music and sacrifices. This spread to commoners, who abandoned farming for commerce, leading to food shortages and luxury excess. After the reigns of Duke Huan of Qi and Duke Wen of Jin, ritual and righteousness were destroyed, superiors and subordinates offended each other, and deceitful, treacherous, and murderous individuals gained wealth and status.

source: Etiquette and righteousness cannot restrain a gentleman, and punishment and killing cannot frighten the common people. The rich use silk to decorate their houses and walls, and their dogs and horses eat grain and meat with leftovers, while the poor cannot even wear coarse cloth and often eat beans and drink raw water. They are all common people with registered households, but their status is different due to different financial resources. Although some become slaves, they still have no resentment. Therefore, those who play political tricks and do evil can be rich all their lives; those who follow justice and stick to the right path are not immune to the threat of hunger and cold. This trend emerged from the upper echelons of society and stemmed from the destruction of the legal system. Therefore, these things are listed to record the changes in the world. In the past, when King Gou Jian of Yue was besieged on Kuaiji Mountain by Wu soldiers, he appointed Fan Li and Ji Ran to assist in state affairs.
target: The rich decorated homes with silk and fed dogs and horses grain, while the poor wore coarse cloth and ate beans, yet the poor did not resent their status. Those who followed justice faced hunger, while the wicked prospered, all stemming from the destruction of the legal system. In response, King Gou Jian of Yue, besieged on Kuaiji Mountain, appointed Fan Li and Ji Ran to govern.

source: In the past, when King Gou Jian of Yue was besieged on Kuaiji Mountain by Wu soldiers, he appointed Fan Li and Ji Ran to assist in state affairs. Ji Ran said: If you know how to fight, you will organize your defense; if you know when to use what, you will truly understand the value of things. If you understand the relationship between time changes and the supply and demand of goods, you can understand the market conditions of various goods. Therefore, when there is a drought, ships are purchased in advance to prepare for floods, and when there are floods, vehicles are purchased in advance to prepare for drought. This is in line with the laws of development and change of things. The State of Yue pursued the policy of Ji Ran, and after ten years of rule, the country became greatly wealthy. It rewarded the soldiers with large sums of money, and finally avenged the State of Wu and washed away the shame of being besieged in Kuaiji. Therefore, people who are good at making money must first be able to choose people, and secondly, they must be good at seizing opportunities. In his 19th year, Duke Zhu earned a thousand pieces of gold three times and distributed it twice to his poor friends and distant brothers. Later, when he got old and frail, he left it to his children and grandchildren to make the decision. The children and grandchildren could inherit the family business and develop it, and eventually the family would be rich. Therefore, when people in later generations talk about rich men, they all praise Duke Tao Zhu. After Zi Gan studied under Confucius and became an official, he returned to Wei and became an official. source: Among the fellow exiled prisoners, those who had a little extra money rushed to give it to the officials in charge, begging to be moved to a closer place and placed in Jiameng County. Mr. Bing started his career by smelting iron and his wealth reached tens of millions. But his family, from father to brother to descendants, all abide by a family rule: when you bend down, you must gain something, when you raise your head, you must gain something, and every move must be profitable. His family made loans and did business throughout the counties. Because of the influence of the Bing family, many people in Zou and Lu areas abandoned literature and went into business to make profits. The custom in Qi despises slaves, but Dao Xian likes to value slaves. source: Jia Yi, a native of Luoyang, was famous locally for his ability to recite poems and write articles when he was eighteen years old. Jia Yi remembered and mourned him, so he compared himself with Qu Yuan. His poem reads:
target: Jia Yi, a native of Luoyang, was renowned for his literary talents at eighteen. Governor Wu Gong of Henan summoned him after hearing of his abilities. Jealous officials slandered Jia Yi, leading to his demotion as Tutor to the Prince of Changsha. On his journey, he wrote a poem mourning Qu Yuan, comparing their fates. The poem lamented Qu Yuan's unjust exile and suicide, criticizing a world that values the worthless over the worthy. Jia Yi advised retreat and self-preservation, using metaphors of dragons and phoenixes to urge distancing from corruption. He argued that Qu Yuan should have sought a wise ruler rather than cling to Chu.

source: Is my life span long or short? Please tell me a period. The owl sighed, then raised its head and flapped its wings vigorously. Although it could not speak human language, it could answer with gestures and guess its mood based on its expression. It means: Thousands of species in the world cycle and change, and there is no end to them. They rotate, flow, and change. Sometimes they rotate and disappear, and sometimes they move and return. The transformation of form and energy is continuous and endless, just like the transformation of a cicada. There are so many profound and subtle things that cannot be described in words. It is simply beyond words. Misfortune contains the cause of blessing, and blessing contains the root of disaster. Misfortunes and blessings follow each other. Misfortunes often lead to blessings, and blessings hide disasters. Sadness and joy gather at the same door, good and bad luck come together in the same area. Thousands of years later, if he passed it on to the old mother and weak son, they would not be able to live in peace. This cannot be said to be benevolent. I heard that when the Holy Spirit wanted to speak, he first asked his ministers instead of speaking first. Therefore, the ministers can show their loyalty. I hope your Majesty will accept my words. Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty then adopted Jia Yi's strategy and appointed Liu Wu, King of Huaiyang, as King of Liang. The Liang Kingdom was bounded by Mount Tai in the north and Gaoyang in the west, with more than 40 large counties. He appointed Liu happy, King of Chengyang, as King of Huainan to appease his people. At that time, the four sons of Liu Chang, King Li of Huainan, were all made marquises. Jia Yi knew that the emperor must restore the titles of princes and kings, so he admonished him and said: "I am privately worried that your majesty will make several sons of King Li of Huainan king. This has not been carefully discussed with the ministers." The King of Huainan rebelled and started rebellion. Who in the world didn’t know about his crime? Fortunately, His Majesty was lenient and banished him. He committed suicide and died. Who in the world thinks that his death was undeserved? Today's use of the son of a sinner has just lived up to the condemnation of King Li by the people of the world! When King Li's son grew up, could he forget his father's hatred? Bai Gongsheng avenged his father, targeting his grandfather, uncle, and uncles. Bai Gongsheng launched a coup, not to seize power, but to vent his resentment. He stabbed his enemy in the chest with a sharp knife, intending to die together with his enemy. Although Huainan is a small place, Yingbu once used it to rebel against the Han Dynasty. It was really lucky for the Han Dynasty to exist. It would be unwise to let the enemy possess capital that could endanger the Han Dynasty. Although King Li's four sons were separated, they had the same idea of ​​avenging their father. Give them a lot of people and enable them to accumulate a lot of property. If they do not openly raise armies in the capital to avenge like Wu Zixu and Bai Gong, there will be assassinations like Zhuanzhu and Jingke. This is the so-called lending weapons to thieves and giving wings to tigers. I hope your Majesty will give it some thought!
target: He urged the emperor to respect ministers, using historical examples to show that honor fosters loyalty. He advised against humiliating officials, as it erodes their integrity. He used the case of Zhou Bo, falsely accused of treason, to argue for leniency. Emperor Wen heeded this, and thereafter, guilty ministers committed suicide rather than face execution. Jia Yi later proposed strengthening the kingdoms of Huaiyang and Liang to counter powerful princes like Huainan. He warned against granting titles to the sons of the rebellious King Li of Huainan, predicting they would seek revenge. Emperor Wen partially adopted his advice, appointing Liu Wu as King of Liang. After Jia Yi's death at thirty-three, his predictions came true: the Seven Kingdoms rebelled, but Liang's strength helped suppress them. Emperor Wu later executed some of King Li's sons for rebellion.

source: Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty remembered Jia Yi's words, so he divided Qi into six small kingdoms and made King Hui's six sons king respectively. He also transferred Huainan King Liu happy to Chengyang, divided Huainan into three small countries, and made King Li's six sons king respectively. In the next ten years, Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty died and Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty succeeded to the throne. In the third year of Emperor Jing's reign, Wu, Chu, Zhao and the four Qi kings jointly rebelled and marched westward to the Mojing city of Chang'an. Liang Xiao Wang Liu Wu defended Chang'an and finally defeated the Seven Kingdoms. By the time of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, the son of King Li of Huainan became king, and some of the two rebelled against him and were executed. Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty ascended the throne and appointed Jia Yi's two grandsons as prefects of the county. Among them, Maijia is the most studious and inherits a scholarly family background. Praise: Liu Xiangcheng Jia Yi talked about the significance of the Xia, Shang, Zhou and Qin dynasties in regulating chaos. His discussion was very beautiful. He was familiar with national regulations and systems. Even Yi Yin and Guan Zhong in ancient times could not surpass him. If his ideas had been implemented at that time, his achievements and enlightenment would have been significant. But it is really sad that he was framed by mediocrity. Looking back, we can see that Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty was quiet and inactive, and took action to change customs. The ideas stated by Jia Yi were slightly implemented.
target: The historian praised Jia Yi's insights on governance, comparing him to Yi Yin and Guan Zhong. Though his ideas were only partially implemented, his writings on statecraft were influential.

source: Emperor Gao ascended to the throne of emperor by virtue of his sage and might, and enfeoffed the fertile land to these people as princes and kings. The most were more than a hundred cities, and the least were thirty or forty counties. His kindness was extremely profound. But in the next ten years, nine rebellions occurred. Your Majesty's relationship with these people is not that he personally fought with them to make them willing to surrender, nor did he personally make them princes and kings. In this case, Emperor Gao couldn't get a year of peace, so I know that His Majesty couldn't get peace either. However, there is another excuse for being distant from them, so let me talk about those people with the same surname who are close to them.
target: His early death prevented him from reaching high office, but his legacy endured through his fifty-eight essays.

source: Zhao Chongguo, named Wengsun, was from Shangbang in Longxi. He later moved to Jincheng Lingju. He was just a knight at the beginning, but later he was a member of a good family in six counties and was good at horseback riding and archery and was promoted to a guard of the feather forest. He was calm and courageous, with profound strategies. When he was young, he liked the integrity of a general, so he went to study the art of war and became familiar with the affairs of the barbarians in all directions. During the reign of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, Zhao Chongguo followed the Second Division General as a fake Sima to attack the Xiongnu, and was heavily surrounded by the enemy. The Han army was without food for several days and suffered many casualties. Zhao Chongguo and more than 100 strong men broke through the siege and captured the enemy's formation. The general of the Second Division led the soldiers to follow him, and they were able to escape the siege. Zhao Chongguo suffered more than 20 injuries all over his body. General Ershi reported the situation to Emperor Wu, who ordered Zhao Chongguo to be summoned to the place where he was traveling. Emperor Wu personally received Zhao Chongguo and visited his injuries. He praised him, awarded him the title of Zhonglang, and promoted him to the post of General of Chariots and Cavalry. During the reign of Emperor Zhao, the Di people in Wudu County rebelled. Zhao Chongguo led troops to attack and quelled the rebellion as a general to protect the army. He was promoted to Zhonglang General and led his troops to garrison in Shanggu County. After returning, he was appointed as the captain of Shuiheng. Later, he went to attack the Xiongnu and captured King Xiqi. He was promoted to the post-general, and he still served as the captain of Shuiheng. Zhao Chongguo and General Huo Guang decided to support Emperor Xuan and were named Yingpinghou. During the Benshi period, he used the post of General Pulei to conquer the Xiongnu and killed hundreds of enemies. After returning the army, he was appointed as the Hou General and Shaofu. The Xiongnu mobilized more than 100,000 cavalry and went south to approach the Han Dynasty border fortress. They reached Mount Fuxi and prepared to invade and plunder. Tichu Qutang, who had escaped from the Xiongnu, surrendered to the Han Dynasty and told the story. The Han Dynasty sent Zhao Chongguo to lead 40,000 cavalry to garrison the nine counties on the border. After Shanyu heard what had happened, he led his troops and left. At this time, Guanglu doctor Yiqu Anguo was on an envoy to inspect various Qiang tribes. The chief Xianling expressed his hope to cross the river to the north bank of the Huangshui River at a certain time to find places where Han people did not cultivate their livestock. Anguo reported the dispatch to the emperor. Zhao Chongguo impeached Anguo for the crime of disrespect after being ordered to send an envoy. After that, the Qiang people violated Han law and crossed the Huangshui River as mentioned above, but the counties and counties could not stop them. In the third year of Yuankang, Xianling resolved his grudges with more than 200 Qiang chiefs, exchanged hostages and signed an oath of alliance. After the emperor learned about this, he consulted Zhao Chongguo. Zhao Chongguo replied: The reason why the Qiang tribe was easily suppressed is because each tribe has its own leader. They often attack each other and their forces cannot be unified. More than 30 years ago, when the Xiqiang people created the Han Dynasty, they resolved their enmities in advance and made an alliance to attack Lingju and compete with the Han Dynasty. It took five or six years to calm down. In the fifth year of Zhenghe, Xianling leader Feng Jian and others sent envoys to the Xiongnu, and the Xiongnu sent envoys to Xiaoyueshi. Rumors told the tribes that: General Ershi of the Han Dynasty led more than 100,000 people to surrender to the Xiongnu. The Qiang people had a hard time serving the Han Dynasty.
target: Zhao Chongguo, styled Wengsun, was from Shangbang in Longxi and later moved to Jincheng Lingju. He began as a knight, was promoted to a guard of the feather forest for his skill in horseback riding and archery, and was known for his calm courage and strategic depth. He studied military strategy and became familiar with barbarian affairs. Under Emperor Wu, he served as a fake Sima under the Second Division General against the Xiongnu, breaking through an enemy siege with over 100 strong men despite heavy casualties and over 20 wounds. Emperor Wu personally honored him, appointing him Zhonglang and later General of Chariots and Cavalry. Under Emperor Zhao, he quelled a Di rebellion in Wudu, was promoted to Zhonglang General, and later captured Xiongnu King Xiqi, becoming a post-general. He supported Emperor Xuan’s ascension with Huo Guang and was named Yingpinghou. During the Benshi period, he led a campaign against the Xiongnu, killing hundreds, and was appointed Hou General and Shaofu. When the Xiongnu mobilized over 100,000 cavalry near the border, Zhao Chongguo led 40,000 cavalry to garrison nine counties, causing the Shanyu to retreat. He later impeached Yiqu Anguo for disrespect after Anguo mishandled Qiang affairs. In the third year of Yuankang, Qiang chief Xianling formed alliances, and Zhao Chongguo warned of potential rebellion, citing past Qiang uprisings and Xiongnu collusion. He advised preparations, but Anguo’s subsequent actions—killing over 30 Qiang leaders and attacking their tribes—provoked a widespread Qiang revolt. Zhao Chongguo, over 70, was tasked with leading the campaign. He insisted on personal command, saying “seeing once is better than hearing a hundred times,” and Emperor Xuan agreed.

id: 汉书/传/赵充国辛庆忌传::group-001
article_path: 汉书/传/赵充国辛庆忌传
source: They also sent troops to attack their tribe and killed more than a thousand people. So all the Qiang tribes who originally submitted to the Han Dynasty, as well as the Guiyi Qiang Marquis Yang Yu and others, were afraid and angry. They lost trust and returned to the Han Dynasty. They coerced and kidnapped the weak tribes, betrayed and invaded the border fortresses, attacked the cities, and killed the officials. As the cavalry captain, Anguo led three thousand cavalry to assemble to defend against the Qiang people. When they arrived at Haodian, they were attacked by enemy soldiers and lost many vehicles, baggage and weapons. An Guo led his troops back and reported the situation after arriving at Ling's residence. This year is the spring of the first year of Shenjue. Zhao Chongguo was already over seventy years old at that time. The emperor thought he was old, so he sent Bingji, the imperial censor, to ask who could lead the army. Zhao Chongguo replied: There is no one more than the veteran. The emperor sent someone to ask again: "General, what do you think will happen to the Qiang enemy? How many people should be used?" Zhao Chongguo said: Seeing once is better than hearing a hundred times. The military situation is difficult to predict remotely. I hope to rush to Jincheng and formulate a battle plan before submitting it. However, the Qiang Rong are just a weak Yi tribe. They have betrayed the country against God's will and will soon perish. I hope your Majesty will leave this matter to the old ministers and don't worry. The emperor smiled and said: "Okay." Zhao Chongguo arrived at Jincheng and waited until the army gathered 10,000 cavalry to prepare to cross the Yellow River. However, he was afraid of being intercepted by the enemy, so he sent three schools of troops to cross the river at night. Dozens and hundreds of enemy cavalry came and entered and exited the edge of the military camp. Zhao Chongguo said: "Our troops and horses are tired and cannot gallop to chase." This is difficult for the enemy's brave cavalry to subdue, and I'm afraid this is a tactic used by the enemy to lure troops. Attack the enemy with the goal of total annihilation. The small benefits are not worth coveting. Zhao Chongguo sent an order to the army not to attack. The cavalry was sent to conduct reconnaissance in the surrounding areas, but no enemy was found. He led his troops upriver to Luodu at night, then summoned the Sima from each school and said to them: I already know that the Qiang people don't know how to use troops. If the enemy sends thousands of people to stand in the middle of nowhere, how can our troops get in? Zhao Chongguo often made it a priority to send scouts far away. He must be prepared for battle when marching and strengthen the forts when stationed. He must be cautious and prudent, love his soldiers, and plan in advance before fighting. So Zhao Chongguo went west to the Western Commandant's Mansion, and rewarded the sergeants every day, and the soldiers wanted to serve him. The enemy came to challenge him several times, but Zhao Chongguo could not hold on.
target: At Jincheng, Zhao Chongguo crossed the Yellow River cautiously, avoiding enemy traps. He prioritized reconnaissance, fortifications, and soldier welfare, refusing to engage in small skirmishes. His son Zhao Yin led reinforcements, but Zhao Chongguo advocated a strategy of kindness and power, recruiting Qiang tribes like Han and Kai to disrupt enemy plans. Emperor Xuan assembled 60,000 troops, but Zhao Chongguo opposed a proposed attack by Xin Wuxian, arguing it risked logistical failure and enemy ambush. He recommended a defensive approach, focusing on farming and waiting for the enemy to weaken. Despite imperial pressure, Zhao Chongguo submitted a memorial detailing a plan to withdraw cavalry and station 10,281 soldiers for farming, listing twelve benefits including cost savings, enemy attrition, and border security. Emperor Xuan eventually approved his strategy.

source: In the autumn of this year, Zhao Chongguo fell ill, and the emperor sent a letter saying: General after issuing the imperial edict: I heard that you are suffering from pain in your legs and feet, and the wind and cold are coming down. The general is old and sick, and I cannot hide the changes. I am very worried about this. Now Shao ordered General Po Qiang to arrive at the station. As the general's deputy, he quickly took advantage of the favorable weather and the vigor of the officers and soldiers to attack Xianling Qiang in December. If the condition is serious, you can stay at the station and only send Poqiang and Qiannu generals. By this time, more than 10,000 Qiang people had surrendered.
target: Zhao Chongguo’s campaign succeeded: over 10,000 Qiang surrendered, and by the following year, only about 4,000 enemies remained.

article_path: 汉书/传/赵充国辛庆忌传
source: At that time, Xin Tang had already accepted Fu Jie and issued an edict to change his position to Xin Linzhong. Later, Xin Linzhong was dismissed from office due to illness, and the Five Governments again recommended Xin Tang. Xin Tang often got drunk and cursed the Qiang people, so the Qiang people rebelled, and finally agreed to what Zhao Chongguo said. At first, Po Qiang general Xin Wuxian often chatted with Zhao Yin, the Zhonglang general in the army. Zhao Yin said: Chariot general Zhang Anshi was not in line with Emperor Xuan's wishes at the beginning, and Emperor Xuan wanted to kill him. My general believed that Zhang Anshi had served Emperor Xiaowu for decades with a book bag in his hand and a brush in his hair. He was recognized as loyal and prudent, so he should be preserved. Zhang Anshi was able to avoid death because of this. When Zhao Chongguo came back and discussed military affairs with the emperor, Xin Wuxian was dismissed from office and returned to his original post. Feeling deeply resentful, he wrote a letter to sue Zhao Yin for leaking what was said in the palace. Zhao Yin violated the ban and entered Sima Zhong, the shogunate of Zhao Chongguo, and disrupted the military regulations. He was sent to a judge for trial. He committed suicide. Zhao Chongguo asked for retirement and was given a four-horse carriage, sixty pounds of gold, and was relieved of his duties and returned home. Whenever there was a major discussion about Sebari, the imperial court often invited him to participate in military planning and asked him about plans and strategies. He died at the age of eighty-six, two years after Ganlu died, and was given the title Zhuanghou. The title was passed from his son to his grandson Zhao Qin, who married Princess Jingwu. The princess had no son, so she asked Zhao Qin's husband Xi to pretend that she was pregnant, but in fact she was someone else's son. Zhao Qin died, his son Zhao Cen succeeded to the throne, and Xi became the dowager. Zhao Cen's biological parents had no end to their demands for money, so they resentfully reported on each other. Zhao Cen was exempted from his title and fiefdom because he was not his biological son. During the first year of the Yuan Dynasty, the descendants of the heroes were reborn and Zhao Ji, the great-grandson of Zhao Chongguo, was granted the title of Yinghuhou. At the beginning, Zhao Chongguo painted his portrait in Weiyang Palace because his merits and virtues were comparable to Huo Guang's. When he became emperor, there was an alarm in Xiqiang. The emperor missed the generals and ministers, commemorated and praised Zhao Chongguo, so he summoned Yang Xiong, a man from Huangmen, to write a eulogy next to Zhao Chongguo's portrait: In the era of Emperor Xuan of the Han Dynasty who was wise and holy, there were Xianling in Rong and Di. Xian Ling was rampant and invaded the western frontier of the Han Dynasty.
target: He was praised for his foresight, though his son Zhao Yin committed suicide after a dispute. Zhao Chongguo retired with honors and died at 86. His portrait was placed in Weiyang Palace, and a eulogy by Yang Xiong celebrated his achievements. The text also covers Xin Wuxian and his son Xin Qingji, noting their military roles and eventual decline under Wang Mang. The commentary reflects on the martial traditions of western regions like Tianshui and Longxi, attributing the prevalence of generals there to proximity to Qiang and Hu peoples.

id: 汉书/传/赵尹韩张两王传::group-000
article_path: 汉书/传/赵尹韩张两王传
source: Zhao Guang, whose Chinese name is Zidu, was a native of Liwu County, Zhuo County. Liwu County was originally part of the Hejian Kingdom. When he was young, he worked as a county official and a state official. He was famous for his integrity, savvy, courtesy and corporal. He was elected as Maocai and made a leveling order to manage market prices. After assessment, he was appointed as the Yangdi Order. Because his performance in managing government affairs was particularly outstanding, he was promoted to the rank of Lieutenant of Jingfu, acting as Jing Zhaoyin. When Emperor Zhao died, Xinfeng Du Jian was appointed as Jingzhao and was responsible for the construction of Emperor Zhao's tomb. Du Jian has always been a hero, and his guests made illegal profits from it. When Guanghan heard about this, he tactfully warned him in advance. Du Jian refused to change, so the case was closed and punished. Many powerful people and eunuchs interceded on his behalf, but Guanghan finally did not listen. The clan and guests planned to kidnap Du Jian. Guanghan learned all of their plans and the name and residence of the mastermind. He sent officials to tell them: If they plot like this, the whole family will be destroyed. He ordered all the officials to execute Du Jian in the busy city, but no one dared to approach him. Everyone in the capital praised him. At that time, Liu He, the king of Changyi, was summoned to Beijing to ascend the throne. He behaved lewdly. General Huo Guang and his officials deposed the king of Changyi and established Emperor Xuan. Guanghan was given the title of Marquis of Guannei because he participated in the discussion and formulation of strategies. Guanghan moved to Yingchuan as governor. The Yuan and Chu tribes in the county were rampant and their guests broke the law and became thieves. None of the former officials of two thousand stone could capture and subdue them. A few months after Guanghan arrived, he killed the evildoers led by Yuan and Chu. The people in the county were shocked and frightened.
target: Zhao Guanghan, a native of Zhuo Commandery, began his career as a county and commandery official, known for his integrity and talent. He was elected as Maocai and served as a market price regulator before becoming the magistrate of Yangdi. His exceptional governance led to his promotion to Lieutenant of Jingfu and acting Jing Zhaoyin. After Emperor Zhao's death, he executed the corrupt Du Jian despite powerful intercessions, earning praise from the capital. He participated in deposing King Changyi and establishing Emperor Xuan, receiving the title of Marquis of Guannei. As Governor of Yingchuan, he suppressed the powerful Yuan and Chu clans and used innovative methods like the "snitch bucket" to break up local factions, restoring order. His reputation spread even to the Xiongnu.

id: 汉书/传/赵尹韩张两王传::group-001
article_path: 汉书/传/赵尹韩张两王传
source: After returning from the army, he still acted as Jing Zhaoyin, and was actually awarded Jing Zhaoyin a year later. As a Yin of the capital, Zhao Guanghan accepted scholars and looked good. He treated his subordinates with comfort and recommendation, and was diligent and diligent. When he succeeded, he declined the credit and attributed it to his subordinates, saying: "It was a certain officer who did it, and it is not what I can do with two thousand stones." Actions originate from a sincere heart. The officials who met him all confided their secrets without hiding anything. They were all willing to be used by him and would not escape even if they died. Guanghan clearly knows what their abilities are suitable for and whether they can try their best. If anyone among them betrays him, let him know first. If he refuses to change after being advised, he will be arrested. If he cannot escape, he will be charged according to his crime and immediately punished. Guanghan is a shrewd and capable man, and is naturally proficient in the ways of being an official. You can stay up all night to meet with officials and people. He is especially good at the art of hook distance, and can use this to find out the whole story. The method of hook distance is, if you want to know the price of a horse, first ask the price of the dog, then the price of the sheep, then the price of the cow, and then the price of the horse. Compare these prices with each other, and measure them by category, and you will be able to know whether the horse is worthy or not.
target: As Jing Zhaoyin, Guanghan was diligent and generous, attributing successes to his subordinates. He was skilled in the "hook distance" method of investigation, uncovering crimes with precision. He once prevented a kidnapping by negotiating with the kidnappers and later treated them with dignity before their execution. He also exposed private affairs with uncanny accuracy, such as knowing a pavilion chief's message before it was delivered.

id: 汉书/传/赵尹韩张两王传::group-002
article_path: 汉书/传/赵尹韩张两王传
source: The head of the pavilion kowtowed and was convinced that this was indeed the case. Guang Han then said: Go back and ask the director of the pavilion for me to ask him to do his job well and do his best. Jing Zhao will not forget his loyalty. He reveals private affairs like a god, and this is often the case. Guanghan petitioned to increase the salary of the traveling wardens in Chang'an to a hundred shi. From then on, the subordinate officials who received a salary of a hundred shi were more self-respecting and did not dare to arrest people arbitrarily in violation of the law.
target: He increased the salary of traveling wardens to prevent corruption, leading to a well-governed capital.

id: 汉书/传/赵尹韩张两王传::group-003
article_path: 汉书/传/赵尹韩张两王传
source: The official offices of Zuo Fengyi and You Fufeng were both located in Chang'an, and criminals often traveled to the boundaries of Jingzhao to commit crimes. Guang Han sighed and said: Those who disrupt my management are often Zuo Fengyi and You Fufeng. If I can control the second assistant at the same time, it will be easier to govern Chang'an. At the beginning, the general Huo Guang was in power, and Guanghan served Huo Guang. After Huo Guang died, Guanghan knew the emperor's intentions and sent the Chang'an officials to lead him personally. They went with him to the residence of Huo Guang's son, Bolu Marquis Huo Yu. They broke into the palace gate, searched and arrested those who secretly slaughtered animals and sold wine, smashed Lu Yue with his spine, and cut off the door bolt with an axe. Huo Guang's daughter was the queen at the time. When she heard about this incident, she cried to the emperor.
target: However, after General Huo Guang's death, Guanghan raided his son's residence, offending the queen and powerful relatives.

id: 汉书/传/赵尹韩张两王传::group-004
article_path: 汉书/传/赵尹韩张两王传
source: After Huo Guang died, Guanghan knew the emperor's intentions and sent the Chang'an officials to lead him personally. They went with him to the residence of Huo Guang's son, Bolu Marquis Huo Yu. They broke into the palace gate, searched and arrested those who secretly slaughtered animals and sold wine, smashed Lu Yue with his spine, and cut off the door bolt with an axe. Huo Guang's daughter was the queen at the time. When she heard about this incident, she cried to the emperor. The emperor applauded this matter in his heart, so he only summoned Guanghan for questioning. Guanghan offended his relatives and ministers. Guang Hanping likes to appoint the young descendants of the old officials and blindly promote their strong and sharp spirit. When they see something happen, they can't avoid it. Most of them have the intention of making a decisive decision with him, and no one can support him in the crisis situation. Guanghan eventually got into trouble because of this. At first, a retainer from Guanghan was selling wine secretly in the Chang'an market, but the prime minister's officials drove him away. The retainer suspected that the man Su Xian had reported the matter, so he told Guang Han. Guanghan sent Chang An Cheng to track down Su Xian, and Wei Shiyu therefore impeached Su Xian as a knight to station in Ba Shang, but he could not reach the station and lacked military supplies. Su Xian's father filed a complaint against Guang Han, and the matter was dealt with again by the department. Yu was sentenced to death and asked to arrest Guanghan.
target: He eventually fell from favor after a series of conflicts, including a false accusation against the prime minister's wife. Despite his integrity and popularity among the people, he was executed by waist-cutting.

id: 汉书/传/赵尹韩张两王传::group-005
article_path: 汉书/传/赵尹韩张两王传
source: Guanghan was finally cut in half. Although Guanghan was punished for breaking the law, he was an honest and upright person, restrained the powerful, and allowed the common people to take their own positions. The people still miss him and praise him. Yin Wenggui, named Zixiong, was originally from Pingyang, Hedong, and later moved to Duling. Weng Gui lost his father when he was young and lived with Ji's father. He works as a prison clerk and is familiar with the law. He loves fencing and no one can resist him. At this time, the general Huo Guang was in charge of the government. The Huo family lived in Pingyang. The slaves and guests of the family came to the market with swords and weapons to fight and cause chaos. The officials could not stop it. When Weng returned to work as a market official, no one dared to break the law and cause chaos.
target: Yin Wenggui, from Hedong, lost his father early and worked as a prison clerk. As a market official, he curbed the violence of Huo Guang's retainers.

source: Now send Zhang Fu to prison, and Zhi Fu Shi will come to the door and follow the prefect to handle the matter. The Prime Minister must take Zhang Fu as a warning! Don't let him go to jail! Zhang Fu died after being detained in prison for a few days. The government found out that he was cunning and had millions of illicit wealth. The king's power shocked the county, and the thieves scattered and settled on the borders of the county. Many powerful people were killed, tortured, injured and brought to justice. Wang Zun was dismissed from office because he killed too many people. Wang Zun was summoned to take up an official position, and he also served as a lieutenant in charge of transportation affairs under the General's Department of Protecting Qiang, escorting the transportation of military rations. However, the Qiang people rebelled, cutting off the transshipment route, and tens of thousands of soldiers besieged Wang Zun. Wang Zun rushed out with more than a thousand cavalry to break through the Qiang thieves. His merits were not reported to the emperor, but he was convicted of leaving his deployment without permission. At the time of the pardon order, he was dismissed from office and returned home. Xu Ming, the prefect of Zhuo County, recommended Wang Zun and believed that he should not live idle in the alleys for a long time. The emperor heard that the emperor was proclaimed king in South Vietnam and did not help the people of the world to eliminate the tyrannical forces. The general originally wanted to send troops to kill the emperor, but the emperor took pity on the people who had just finished their hard work and needed to rest and recuperate, so he sent me to grant the emperor the seal, divide the talisman letters, and exchange envoys. The king should go to the outskirts to welcome him, and to the north to proclaim his vassalship, but you actually want to use this newly-established country with unpopular hearts and unconsolidated political power to claim strength here. If the King of Han really hears about it, he will dig up and burn the graves of your ancestors, annihilate your clan, and send a lieutenant general to lead a hundred thousand people to attack Yue. The Yue people will kill the king and surrender to the Han. It will be easy to conquer. So Wei Tuo stood up in shock and apologized to Lu Jia: "I have lived among barbarians for a long time. It is really rude." So he asked Lu Jia: Who is better among me, Xiao He, Cao Shen, and Han Xin? Lu Mai said: The king is wiser than them. He asked again: Who is more worthy than the emperor? Lu Jia said: The emperor raised troops in Fengpei to attack the violent Qin, destroyed the powerful Chu army, brought benefits and eliminated harm to the people of the world, inherited the great cause of the five emperors and three kings, unified the world, and governed the country.
target: Lu Jia of Chu was a skilled orator who served as an envoy for Emperor Gaozu. He was sent to South Vietnam to grant Wei Tuo the king's seal. When Wei Tuo received him disrespectfully, Lu Jia warned him that the Han emperor could easily destroy him. Wei Tuo apologized and acknowledged Han's superiority. Lu Jia successfully secured South Vietnam's submission. Later, when Emperor Gaozu dismissed the value of studying the classics, Lu Jia argued that while one could conquer the world on horseback, one could not govern it that way. He wrote twelve essays explaining why Qin fell and Han succeeded, which became known as the "New Speeches." During Empress Dowager Lu's regency, Lu Jia retired but later advised Chancellor Chen Ping to ally with General Zhou Bo to counter the Lu family's conspiracy. His strategy helped preserve the Liu imperial house.

source: In this way, the relationship between the two people became closer, and Lu's conspiracy was further destroyed. Chen Ping gave Lu Jia a hundred slaves, fifty carriages and horses, and five million yuan to pay for meals and drinks. Lu Mai then used these properties to lobby the officials in the court, and his reputation grew. Until the Lu family was executed and Emperor Xiaowen was established as emperor, Lu Jia was very helpful. Emperor Xiaowen came to the throne and wanted to send someone as an envoy to South Vietnam. Prime Minister Chen Ping reported to the emperor that Lu Mai should be appointed as the Taizhong doctor and sent as an envoy to South Vietnam. Wei Tuo gave up his imperial title and agreed with the princes, which was in line with the court's wishes. These events are recorded in "The Biography of South Vietnam". Lu Jia finally died. Zhu Jian, a native of Chu, once served as the prime minister of Huainan King Yingbu. He fled because of a crime and later followed Yingbu again. When Ying Bu wanted to rebel, he asked Zhu Jian. Zhu Jian advised him not to rebel, but Ying Bu refused to listen and listened to his father Liang, so he rebelled. The Han Dynasty suppressed Ying Bu. Hearing that Sai Jian had discouraged Yun Hu from making it, he gave Gui Jian the title of Lili Jun and his family moved to Chang'an. Sai Jian is a eloquent and talented person, with a clean and upright character. His behavior is different from that of others, and he does not agree with others casually when interacting with others. Marquis Piyang behaved improperly and was favored by Empress Dowager Lu. He wanted to make friends with Zhu Jian, but Zhu Jian refused to see him. When Zhu Jian's mother passed away, she had no money to pay for the funeral because of poverty, so she borrowed money to buy mourning clothes and funeral utensils. Lu Jia had always been friendly with Ji Jian, so he went to see Piyang Hou and congratulated him: "Pingyuan Jun's mother is dead." Marquis Piyang said: Lord Pingyuan's mother is dead, why do you congratulate me? Lu Mai said: A few days ago, Junhou wanted to make friends with Guijian. Mr. Pingyuan insisted on the principle of righteousness and refused to see you because of his mother. Now that his mother is dead, if you really give generous gifts at the funeral, then he will become a good friend who will die for you. Marquis Piyang then presented him with a hundred gold pieces of clothing and quilt. Other princes and nobles also went to send a total of five hundred gold to support the funeral because of Lord Piyang. As time went by, some people slandered Piyanghou. Emperor Hui was furious and arrested Piyanghou and wanted to kill him. The Queen Mother felt very ashamed, but could not say it herself. Most of the ministers were deeply dissatisfied with the behavior of Marquis Piyang, so they all wanted to kill him. The Marquis of Piyang was afraid and anxious, so he sent someone to see Sai Jian. Sejian declined and said: Your case is at a critical moment and I dare not see you.
target: Zhu Jian of Chu served as prime minister to Yingbu, King of Huainan, and advised against rebellion. After Yingbu rebelled and was suppressed, Zhu Jian was rewarded. He was known for his integrity and refused to associate with the corrupt Marquis of Piyang, who was favored by Empress Dowager Lu. When Zhu Jian's mother died, Lu Jia advised the Marquis of Piyang to offer generous funeral gifts, which led to reconciliation. Later, when the Marquis of Piyang was imprisoned, Zhu Jian secretly instructed the emperor's favorite minister to plead for his release, saving his life. After Empress Dowager Lu's death, Zhu Jian's earlier advice helped protect the Marquis of Piyang from execution. During Emperor Xiaowen's reign, Zhu Jian was implicated in a case involving the Marquis of Piyang and committed suicide to protect his family.
