source: Not because the morals are weak, but because the strength is too weak. Now your Majesty raised troops from Feng and Pei, and recruited 3,000 soldiers. He used these people to sweep the Shuhan area, pacify the Three Qin Dynasties, and fought with Xiang Yu in Rongyang. There were seventy major battles and forty minor battles, causing the lives of all the people in the world. Moreover, the land of Qin is surrounded by mountains and rivers, and the terrain is difficult. If there is a sudden war, millions of troops can gather. With the old conditions, abundant resources and fertile land, it can become a natural treasury. Your Majesty entered Guanzhong and made it the capital of the country. Although there was war in Huashan, Qin's old land could still be preserved and occupied. If you fight with someone, you can't win completely without grabbing his throat and blowing his spine. Now that your majesty has entered Guanzhong to build the capital and pacify the old land of Qin, this is also strangling the throat of the world and striking its backbone. Emperor Gao asked the ministers, all of whom were from Shandong, and they all said that the Zhou Dynasty ruled for hundreds of years, while the Qin Dynasty only extended to the second generation, so it would be better to build the capital of Luoyang. Emperor Gaoti hesitated and could not decide where to make his capital. It was not until Zhang Liang, the Marquis of Liu, made it clear that he should enter Guanzhong, that he set off to the west to make Guanzhong his capital. So the emperor said: The first person who was determined to be in Qin was Lou Jing, and Lou was Liu. He gave Lou Jing the surname Liu, made him a doctor, and titled him Feng Chunjun. In the seventh year of the Han Dynasty, King Han Xin of Han rebelled, and Emperor Gao personally led his troops to attack him. When he arrived in Jinyang, he heard that Han Xin was planning to unite with the Xiongnu to attack the Han army. The emperor was furious and sent an envoy to the Xiongnu. The Xiongnu hid the strong men and fat cattle and horses, and only saw the old and weak people and very thin livestock. Ten batches of envoys came, and they all said that the Huns were easily defeated. The emperor sent Liu Jing to go to the Huns again. When he returned, he reported to the emperor: When two countries are hostile and fighting, they should show off their strengths. Now when I go to the Xiongnu, I only see thin livestock and old and weak people. They must have deliberately shown their shortcomings to lure us into being deceived and ambush surprise soldiers to defeat us. I think the Huns are unattackable. At this time, the Han soldiers had advanced northward and had crossed Gouzhu Mountain. More than 300,000 soldiers had been mobilized. The emperor was angry and scolded Liu Jing: "You are a slave of Qi!" I got the official position by talking nonsense, and now I want to stop me from sending troops with nonsense words. Put Liu Jing in chains and stay in Guangwu. So he went to Pingcheng. The Huns really came out with surprise troops and besieged Gaodi in Baideng. It took seven days to relieve the siege. Emperor Gao went to Guangwu and released Liu Jing, saying: "I don't accept your words, so I was besieged in Pingcheng." I have killed the ten groups of people who said they could attack the Huns. So Liu Jing was granted the title of Marquis of Guan Neihou with two cadres, and his title was to be on duty during the day.
target: Lou Jing of Qi advised Emperor Gaozu to establish the capital in Guanzhong rather than Luoyang, arguing that Qin's former territory had natural defenses and abundant resources. Despite opposition from ministers from Shandong, Zhang Liang supported this plan, and the emperor adopted it, granting Lou Jing the surname Liu and the title of Feng Chunjun. Later, when the emperor planned to attack the Xiongnu, Lou Jing warned that the Xiongnu were deliberately showing weakness to ambush the Han army. The emperor ignored this advice, was besieged at Baideng, and later released Lou Jing, rewarding him. Lou Jing then proposed a marriage alliance with the Xiongnu, suggesting the emperor send his eldest princess to marry the Chanyu. Although Empress Lu objected, a substitute princess was sent. Lou Jing also recommended relocating powerful clans from various states to Guanzhong to strengthen the region.

source: These people are just thieves, so why should they care? The county guards and lieutenants are hunting them now, so what is there to worry about? Qin II was very happy. Asked every Confucian scholar, some said they were rebels, and some said they were thieves. So Qin II ordered the censor to write down the people who made the remarks and hand them over to the judge for trial to punish them for their wrong remarks. All scholars who spoke of thieves were dismissed. He gave Shusun Tong twenty pieces of silk and a set of clothes, and he was called a doctor. After Shusun Tong came out, he returned to the academy. The Confucian scholars said: "Why do you talk so flatteringly?" Shusun Tong said: You don't know that I can hardly escape from the tiger's mouth. So he fled to Xue County, which had surrendered to Chu. Xiang Liang came to Xue County, and Shusun Tong followed him. Xiang Liang was defeated in Dingtao, and he followed King Huai again. King Huai became the Righteous Emperor and moved to Changsha County. Shusun Tong stayed behind to assist King Xiang. In the second year of the Han Dynasty, the King of Han led the troops of the five princes into Pengcheng, and Shusun Tong surrendered to the King of Han.
target: Shusun Tong of Xue served under Qin II, cleverly avoiding punishment by calling rebels mere thieves. He later served Xiang Liang, King Huai, and finally surrendered to the King of Han.

article_path: 汉书/传/郦陆朱刘叔孙传
source: What you are doing is not in line with the ancient ways, so we will not go. Go ahead and don't tarnish our character. Shusun Tong smiled and said: You are really pedantic and ignorant of worldly affairs. You do not understand the changes in the current situation. So he went west with the 30 people he had recruited, and together with Gaodi's close officials and Shusun Tong's disciples, a total of more than 100 people tied thatches in the wild to determine the ceremonial positions. After practicing for more than a month, Shusun Tong said: "Your Majesty, you can give it a try." After exercising the etiquette, the emperor said: I can do it. So he ordered all the ministers to practice, and the rituals were completed just in time for the beginning of October. In the seventh year of the Han Dynasty, Changle Palace was built, and all the princes and ministers came to worship in October. Etiquette: Before dawn, the visitor is responsible for the etiquette, and the pilgrims are brought into the palace one by one. The palace is equipped with chariots, garrison soldiers, and guards, as well as various weapons and flags. Paging trend, that is, rush to enter. Hundreds of guards lined the steps of His Highness. To the west stood the heroes, princes, generals, and military officials in order, facing east; to the east stood the civil servants and prime ministers, facing west. Daxing ordered to preside over the ceremony of going to court, set up nine stations of masters of ceremonies, and shouted loudly to attract the ministers into the palace. So the emperor came out of the house in a chariot, and hundreds of officials held halberds, calling for the clear way, and guided the princes and officials down to six hundred stone officials to come to the emperor in turn to congratulate him. Everyone below the princes and kings was frightened and respectful. After the worship, all the officials, big and small, prostrated themselves on the ground, and a banquet was held with strict etiquette. The waiters in the palace all bowed their heads and stood up one by one to wish the emperor a birthday. After nine drinks, the visitor said: The banquet is over. If the censor reports someone who violates etiquette, he will be taken away. During the whole process of worshiping and drinking, no one dared to make any noise or violate etiquette. So Emperor Gao said: Only now do I know the dignity of being an emperor! He worshiped his uncle Sun Tong as Fengchang and gave him five hundred catties of gold. Shusuntong then said to the emperor: These disciples, Confucian scholars, have been following me for a long time. They worked with me to formulate etiquette. I hope your majesty can grant them official titles. Emperor Gao named them all Lang. Shusun Tong came out and gave all the five hundred gold he had received to the Confucian scholars. The Confucian scholars said happily: Mr. Shusun is really a saint and understands the world today. In the ninth year of the Han Dynasty, Emperor Gao promoted his uncle Sun Tong to the title of Crown Prince and Tutor. In the twelfth year, Emperor Gao wanted to make King Zhao Ruyi the crown prince. Shusun Tong said: In the past, Duke Xiang of Jin deposed the crown prince and established Xi Qi instead because of Li Ji. The Jin Kingdom was in chaos for decades and was ridiculed by the world. Because the Qin Dynasty did not appoint Fusu as the crown prince early, Hu Hai used deception to win the throne and reduced the Qin Dynasty. This was witnessed by your Majesty personally.
target: Noticing the disorderly behavior of ministers at court, he offered to create court rituals. Despite criticism from conservative Confucian scholars, he adapted ancient and Qin rituals to create a practical system. After the completion of Changle Palace, the new rituals were implemented, impressing Emperor Gaozu, who remarked, "Now I know the dignity of being emperor." Shusun Tong was appointed Fengchang and rewarded with gold, which he distributed to his disciples. He later served as Crown Prince Tutor and successfully dissuaded Emperor Gaozu from replacing the crown prince. Under Emperor Xiaohui, he continued to formulate rituals and established the practice of offering fruits at ancestral temples.

source: Confucius said: If you use political decrees to induce them and punishments to rectify them, the people will only be temporarily exempted from their sins, but they will have no sense of shame; if you use morality to induce them and use rituals to rectify them, the people will not only have a sense of shame, but also have people's hearts subdued. Laozi said: Superior virtue is in line with nature and is truly virtuous; inferior virtue is created subjectively and is actually unvirtuous. The multiplicity of laws and regulations breeds cunning and deceit, so the number of thieves increases. This is really a wise and clear statement! Laws and regulations are tools of governance, not the source of good or bad governance. In the past, when the law was tight in the world, thieves became more and more numerous and developed to the extreme, causing the monarchs, ministers and people to avoid each other, resulting in the world being ruined and unable to be saved. At this time, local governance was in crisis. If tough and harsh measures were not used, how could the governance be maintained? Those who advocate morality adopt a relaxed approach. Therefore, Confucius said: When trying lawsuits, I am no different from others. I must completely eliminate the litigation events! Lao Tzu also said: It is in vain to ridicule a mediocre person who does not know the way. These are not lies. The rise of the Han Dynasty broke the square into a circle, returned to simplicity and truth, and the legal framework was extremely broad and sparse. However, the situation of officialdom is flourishing, banditry and chaos are not prevalent, and the people live and work in peace and contentment. From this point of view, the key to official governance is not the harshness of the law. When he was a high-ranking empress, the only cruel official was Hou Feng, who trampled on the clan and insulted the meritorious officials. After the Lu family was defeated, Hou Feng's family was eradicated. During the reign of Emperor Jing, Chao Cuo used sharp tactics to support his talents, and the Rebellion of the Seven Kingdoms was also caused by Chao Cuo, and finally Chao Cuo was killed. Later, Zhidu and Ningcheng appeared again. Zhidu was born in Dayang County, Hedong County. Serve Emperor Wen as a Langguan. Emperor Jing was the Zhonglang General at that time, and he dared to speak out to the emperor and rebuke the ministers' faults in person at the court. Zhidu once accompanied the emperor to Shanglin Garden. Jia Ji was in the toilet, and the wild boar also entered the toilet. The emperor looked at Zhidu, but Zhidu was unmoved. The emperor wanted to personally take the sword to rescue Maiji. Zhidu knelt down in front of the emperor and said: "We have lost a Jiajie and a new Maiji has come in. Is it possible that the world lacks people like Maiji?" Even if your Majesty doesn't care about yourself, how can you be worthy of the country and the Queen Mother? After hearing Zhidu's words, the emperor retreated, and the wild boar did not harm Maiji. When the Queen Mother heard about this, she rewarded Zhidu with one hundred catties of gold. The emperor also rewarded Zhidu with one hundred catties of gold. From then on, Zhidu was highly valued. There were more than 300 families in Jinan's Kun clan. They were powerful and committed all kinds of evil. The prefect of the county could not subdue them, so Emperor Jing appointed Zhidu as the prefect of Jinan. After Zhidu arrived, he immediately killed the chief culprit of the Shu clan, and the remaining members of other clans were so frightened that their thighs trembled. Zhidu served as the prefect for more than a year, but Jinan County did not pick up the troops. The prefects of more than ten nearby counties feared Zhidu as they feared the superior palace.
target: Confucius taught that governance through laws and punishments only temporarily prevents wrongdoing without instilling shame, while governance through morality and rituals creates both shame and willing compliance. Laozi similarly distinguished between superior virtue aligned with nature and inferior virtue that is subjectively created. The text observes that excessive laws breed cunning and increase thieves, noting that laws are merely tools of governance, not its source. During the Han Dynasty's rise, broad and sparse legal frameworks allowed officials to flourish and people to live peacefully, demonstrating that effective governance depends not on harsh laws. The text then chronicles several cruel officials. Zhidu served Emperors Wen and Jing, known for his bravery, integrity, and harsh enforcement. He once prevented Emperor Jing from risking his life to save a palace attendant from a wild boar. As governor of Jinan, he executed the chief culprit among powerful clans, causing such fear that the county became orderly. He declared his loyalty to duty over family.

source: However, Emperor Jing sent someone to Zhidu's home to appoint him as the governor of Yanmen. He did not have to go to the court to say goodbye, but took a shortcut to his post. He could take advantage of the situation and handle government affairs with full authority. The Huns were aware of Zhidu's integrity and all evacuated their border troops. After Zhidu's death, they did not dare to take a step near Yanmen. The Huns carved a puppet figure that looked exactly like Zhidu, and ordered the cavalry to gallop and shoot, but none of them could hit. They were so frightened by Zhidu.
target: The Huns feared him so much they carved his likeness for target practice but could never hit it.

source: Zhou Yafu became the prime minister, and then Yu became the prime minister. Everyone in the government praised him for being honest and fair. However, Zhou Yafu did not reuse him and said: I know that Yu's character and talent are extraordinary, but he is too harsh in upholding the law and cannot be entrusted with important tasks. During the reign of Emperor Wu, Tào Yu had accumulated achievements as a swordsman and pen official and was transferred to the imperial censor. The emperor thought he was talented and promoted him to the rank of doctor. He and Zhang Tang negotiated legal regulations together, and the laws he made were recognized, and officials, prime ministers, and supervisors began to teach the law. Zhao Yu was an honest and upright person. Since he entered the officialdom, he has not had a single guest in his house.
target: Despite Emperor Jing recognizing him as a loyal minister, Empress Dowager Dou had him executed for his role in Prince Linjiang's suicide.

source: And once someone is removed from office due to weakness and dereliction of duty, he will be discarded for life and never be used again. This kind of humiliation is much more serious than committing the crime of corruption and harboring. Please be careful and don’t neglect your duties! Yin Shang's four sons all became officials and became county guards, and the eldest son Yin Li became a Jingzhao Yin. They all respected majesty and had a reputation for being good at governance. Zan said: The recorded masters from Zhidu on down were all famous for their harshness and violence. However, Zhidu was upright, knew right from wrong, and understood the general picture. However, Zhang Tang flattered the monarch and was valued for his appearance and deeds. He often used clever words to stir up trouble and made the trend of flattery prevail in the country. Yu acted according to the law and strictly observed justice. Du Zhou was obedient to flattery, and it was important to speak less in everything. After Zhang Tang's death, the law was strict and troubled, and the country became increasingly chaotic and desolate. The nine ministers were busy rescuing and fighting the chaos, so they had no time to discuss matters other than the rule of law! From then until the reigns of Emperor Ai and Emperor Ping, there were many cruel officials, but it is impossible to count them. Here we only select the famous ones and see them in the records. Among them, those who are honest can serve as examples, while those who are dirty may have strategies and education, or may have the courage to punish traitors and thieves, and may also have literary talents and military strategies.
target: Ningcheng succeeded Zhidu as governor of Jinan, known for aggression and cruelty. After Zhidu's death, he became lieutenant and terrorized nobles. Under Emperor Wu, he was sentenced to shaving and iron collar, but escaped, became wealthy through land leasing, and wielded power greater than county governors. Zhou Yangyou was known for bending laws according to personal feelings, eradicating tyrants, and competing with superiors for power, eventually executed for his conflicts.

source: Since Ning Cheng and Zhou Yangyou, the world has become more and more unstable. The people use clever methods to resist the law, and the officials are mostly similar to Ning Cheng and Zhou Yangyou. Zhao Yu was a native of Yaxian County. As an assistant historian, he was appointed as the official of Zhongdu. Because of his integrity, he was appointed as the commander of the order and served the Taiwei Zhou Yafu. Zhou Yafu became the prime minister, and then Yu became the prime minister. Everyone in the government praised him for being honest and fair. However, Zhou Yafu did not reuse him and said: I know that Yu's character and talent are extraordinary, but he is too harsh in upholding the law and cannot be entrusted with important tasks. During the reign of Emperor Wu, Tào Yu had accumulated achievements as a swordsman and pen official and was transferred to the imperial censor. The emperor thought he was talented and promoted him to the rank of doctor. He and Zhang Tang negotiated legal regulations together, and the laws he made were recognized, and officials, prime ministers, and supervisors began to teach the law. Zhao Yu was an honest and upright person. Since he entered the officialdom, he has not had a single guest in his house. The ministers invited him to be a guest, but Yu always declined, saying that he would cut off all invitations from friends and guests and only wanted to be alone.
target: Zhao Yu served under Zhou Yafu, who recognized his integrity but considered him too harsh for important positions. Under Emperor Wu, he helped formulate legal regulations and became known for honesty, refusing all social invitations. Yi Zong rose from banditry to become an official through his sister's connection to the Empress Dowager. He governed with daring severity, eradicating powerful families in Hanoi.

source: Now that the Shuyue rebels have penetrated deep into the Han territory, General, can you lead troops to fight against the enemy and make up for your mistakes? After hearing this, Yang Pu was very frightened and replied: I am willing to die in battle to atone for my sins and make meritorious service! Later, he and Wang Wenshu defeated the Shuyue rebels together. He also attacked North Korea with General Xun Shen of the left, but was bound by Xun Shen. This story can be seen in "Chosun Biography". After returning to the court, Yang Pu was dismissed from his official position and became a commoner. He eventually fell ill and died. Xianxuan was born in Yang County. He served under the governor of Hedong as an assistant historian.
target: As governor of Dingxiang, he executed over 400 prisoners in one day. He was eventually executed for his actions.

source: So I wrote it down. In winter, Yang Ke had just presided over the complaint. Yi Zong thought it was an act of chaos, so he sent officials to capture the envoy sent by Yang Ke. When the emperor heard about this incident, he asked Du Shi to try it, and he was convicted of infringing and abolishing Shaoshu. Yi Zong was executed and his body was abandoned in the market. A year later, Zhang Tang also died. Wang Wenshu was from Yangling. When he was young, he killed people with vertebrae, buried them privately, and became a thief. Later, he broke away from the traitorous party and became the county pavilion chief. He was deposed several times. After being appointed to official positions several times, Wang Wenshu was promoted to the rank of Ting Wei Shi because of his ability in managing the prison. Under Zhang Tang, he was transferred to the post of censor, supervising the arrest of thieves and killing many people. Later, he gradually rose to the rank of Captain of Guangping. He chose more than a dozen brave heroes from the county to be his minions. He concealed their serious crimes and let them supervise the arrest of thieves. Wang Wenshu was very happy because he captured the people he wanted to arrest. Therefore, although this person has hundreds of sins, he has not been questioned or punished; but if he does not try his best to supervise the arrest and adopts an evasive attitude, he will be executed immediately and his clan will be exterminated. As a result, thieves from the Qi-Zhao border areas did not dare to approach Guangping, and the Guangping area began to be famous for not picking up people on the road. When the emperor heard about this, he transferred Wang Wenshu to be the prefect of Hanoi County. Wang Van Thu always lived in Quang Binh and was already aware of the home of gangsters and rapists in Ha Noi County. When he arrived in September, he ordered the county to prepare fifty private horses and set up post stations on the road from Hanoi to Chang'an. He also ordered the officials to use the method originally used in Guangping to arrest the powerful and traitorous people in the county. More than a thousand people were involved in each other and were guilty. Then he reported to the court, requesting that those who committed the most serious crimes should have their clan destroyed, those who had committed the minor crimes personally be put to death, and all their family possessions should be confiscated. Only two days after the memorial was sent, the news of the accurate memorial was received, and the execution was carried out according to the order, causing the blood of the murdered person to flow for more than ten miles.
target: Wang Wenshu began as a thief but became an official known for managing prisons. As governor of Guangping, he recruited brave men as informants, concealing their crimes while executing those who failed him. As governor of Hanoi, he arrested over a thousand people, executing the worst and confiscating property, with blood flowing for miles.

source: A few years later, all of his petty officials became rich thanks to the protection of powerful people. Wang Wenshu came back from the attack on Shuyue. When he discussed political affairs, he went against the emperor's will, so he was dismissed from office. At this time, the emperor just wanted to build the Tongtian Tower but lacked manpower. Wang Wenshu petitioned to call all the outstanding soldiers who were former lieutenants, and obtained tens of thousands of manpower in total. The emperor was very happy and appointed Wang Wenshu as the young master. Later, he was transferred to You Neishi, but his governance remained the same, and the number of cunning and evil people was reduced until they were completely banned. Later, he was dismissed from office because of his conviction. After his comeback, he served as right assistant and concurrently as lieutenant, and his conduct remained the same as before. More than a year later, when the imperial court sent troops to conquer Dawan, the emperor issued an edict to recruit powerful officials. Wang Wenshu hid his powerful official Hua Cheng, and someone reported that Wang Wenshu secretly accepted dirty money from soldiers and did other illegal things. The crime should be punished by the clan. Wang Wenshu could not bear this blow, so he committed suicide out of fear of the crime. At that time, Wang Wenshu's two younger brothers and his wife's entire family were also executed together as a clan for his crimes. Guang Luxun Xu Ziwei said: How sad! How sad! In ancient times, there was a plan to exterminate three tribes, but Wang Wenshu actually committed the crime of annihilating five tribes at the same time! After Wang Wenshu's death, his family property was worth thousands of gold. Yin Qi is from Chiping County, Dongjun. Officials with swords and pens were gradually promoted to censors. Working under Zhang Tang, Zhang Tang praised him many times for his integrity. Emperor Wu sent him to supervise thieves. He killed and eradicated thieves without fearing their fame and power.
target: He regretted that winter ended before he could eliminate all thieves. He became lieutenant but committed suicide when facing execution for his crimes, with his entire family executed.

source: During the reign of Shenjue, the Xiqiang rebelled. General Xu Yanshou, a powerful crossbow general, invited Yan Yannian to be a long history officer, joined the army and defeated the Xiqiang. After returning to the court, he was appointed as the governor of Zhuojun. At that time, the governors sent to Zhuojun were all incompetent. As a result, Bi Yebai and others from Zhuojun were able to ignore public laws and disturb the countryside. The powerful clans Xigao and Shugao became even more arrogant. source: Jun Buyi's courtesy name is Manqian, a native of Bohai County. Proficient in "Spring and Autumn", he served as county literary official. His words and deeds must follow etiquette standards, and he was famous in the state and county. In the last years of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, thieves and thieves appeared in droves across the country. Baoshengzhi was appointed as the Zhizhi envoy. He wore bright embroidered clothes and held a sharp axe. He went to various places to suppress thieves and supervise the administration of county and state officials. His law enforcement scope reached as far as the coast of Shubu. Those who disobey his orders will be punished with severe military laws, and his reputation shocked all states and counties. Baosheng had long heard that Jun Buyi was very virtuous, so after he inspected Bohai County, he sent his entourage to invite Jun Buyi to come and meet him. Jun Buyi wore a Jinxian crown on his head, a sword decorated with beautiful jade and wood carving patterns on his waist, a jade pendant such as a ring and block on his body, a wide robe and wide robes, and went to pay homage to Baosheng's residence in full attire. When they arrived at the gate of Baofu, the guard wanted Juan Buyi to take off his sword. Jun Buyi said, "The sword is a gentleman's weapon and equipment. It is used to protect one's body. It cannot be taken off casually." If you insist that I take off my sword before letting me enter the riot, then please allow me to take my leave now. The guard informed Baoshengzhi of the situation. Baoshengzhi opened the door and invited Jun Buyi into the house. Seeing Jun Buyi's serious face, confident demeanor and neat and solemn clothes, Baoshengzhi hurriedly left his seat and stood up to greet him with his shoes on. When the guests and hosts arrived and sat down in the hall, Jun Buyi straightened his waist and knelt down on the ground and said: I live in a remote coastal area and have heard of your reputation, Mr. Bao, for a long time, but I have never had the honor to meet and talk with you until today. Generally speaking, as an official, if you are too firm, you will easily suffer setbacks, and if you are too weak, you will easily neglect government affairs. Therefore, the best way is to exercise dignity while giving favors, so that you can make achievements and keep your position forever. Baoshengzhi knew that Jun Buyi was not an ordinary person, so he respectfully accepted his warning, received him with high etiquette, and asked him what measures and means should be adopted to govern under the current situation. The staff of the tyrant government were all outstanding talents selected from the officials of various states and counties. They listened to Jun Buyi's conversation and were all shocked and impressed. It wasn't until late at night that Jun Buyi left the house. So after the sudden victory, he recommended Buyi to the imperial court. The emperor summoned Buyi to the public transportation department and worshiped him as the governor of Qingzhou. After a long time, Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty passed away and Emperor Zhao of the Han Dynasty came to the throne. At this time, Liu Ze, the grandson of King Xiao of Qi, colluded with the heroes of the county and country to conspire to rebel. They planned to assassinate the governor of Qingzhou first. Jun Buyi discovered the conspiracy of Liu Ze and others in time and arrested them all. Liu Ze and others all confessed to the crime. Bu Juan was promoted to Jing Zhaoyin and was given millions of dollars.
target: Jun Buyi, a native of Bohai, was known for his strict adherence to etiquette and expertise in the "Spring and Autumn." He recommended to the emperor that Peng Xuan was proficient in classics, steady and prestigious, and could serve as a court official. So Peng Xuan entered the court as You Fufeng, and soon moved to Tingwei. Later, because the early Han Dynasty stipulated that people from various vassal kingdoms were not allowed to serve as officials in the capital, he became the prefect of Taiyuan County. A few years later, he entered the capital and served as Da Sinong, Guang Luxun, and General You. After Emperor Ai of Han came to the throne, he was appointed General Zuo. More than a year later, Emperor Ai of the Han Dynasty planned to appoint his relatives, Ding and Fu, to be in charge of the royal guards, so he wrote to Peng Xuan: Relevant departments have reported many times that people from the princely kingdoms cannot serve as royal guards. General, because you are from the kingdom, you are not suitable to be in charge of the army and hold a high position. I consider that General, you have the important task of being a general of the Han Dynasty, and your son has previously married the daughter of the King of Huaiyang. There is a marriage relationship between your family and the kingdom, but you are an official in Beijing. This is not in line with the national system. I asked Dr. Guanglu Man to reward you with fifty kilograms of gold and a four-horse carriage. You can return General Zuo's seal and ribbon and return to your hometown as the Marquis of Guannei. In the years after Peng Xuan was dismissed from office and returned to his hometown, Bao Xuan, the remonstrating doctor, wrote many times to recommend him. It happened that there was a solar eclipse on the first day of the first month of the first year of Yuanshou, and Bao Xuan recommended him again. Emperor Ai of the Han Dynasty summoned Peng Xuan to the court as Guanglu doctor, and was promoted to Yushi doctor, and later to Da Sikong, and was granted the title of Marquis of Changping. When Emperor Ai of the Han Dynasty passed away, Wang Mang, the lord of the new capital, became the Grand Sima and took over the power of the government. Peng Xuan wrote a letter saying: The three princes are like the three legs of a tripod, supporting the monarch together. If one of the legs is incompetent, there is a danger of overturning the delicious food in the tripod. I have little talent, am old, faint, frail and sick, and my memory is failing. I hope that I can be allowed to hand over the seals and ribbons of Da Sikong and Changping Marquis and return to my hometown to spend my remaining years. Wang Mang reported the matter to the Queen Mother, who issued a policy letter to Peng Xuan, saying: You have not been in charge of political affairs for a long time and have not yet established outstanding merits. However, due to old age and confusion, you are unable to assist the country and stabilize the country.
target: Peng Xuan, from Huaiyang, studied the "Book of Changes" and served as a general. Emperor Ai dismissed him due to his kingdom origins, but he was later recalled. After Emperor Ai’s death, Wang Mang took power, and Peng Xuan resigned, citing old age. Wang Mang, resenting his resignation, denied him customary gifts. Peng Xuan died in his fief, and his title was later abolished.

Praise: Jun Buyi participated in government affairs as a well-educated person, was not confused when encountering difficulties, had outstanding achievements, and started well and ended well. It is also advisable to retreat from the rapids to avoid humiliation and danger. Yu Dingguo's father and son sympathized with the widowers and understood the situation in prison, so they were competent ministers. Xue Guangde retained the glory of Xuanchao, Ping Dang had the sense of shame to retreat, and Peng Xuan resigned resolutely when he saw the dangerous situation. target: The text concludes with praise for these officials: Jun Buyi for his wisdom and achievements, Shu Guang for timely retirement, Yu Dingguo for his fairness, and Xue Guangde, Ping Dang, and Peng Xuan for their integrity, contrasting them with those who cling to power.

source: Huo Guang, courtesy name Zimeng, was the younger brother of Huo Qubing, the general of the Hussars. His father, Zhong Ru, was from Pingyang, Hedong Province. He served in the Pingyang Hou family as a county official and had an affair with his maid Wei Shaoer and gave birth to Huo Qubing. After Zhongru completed his errand, he returned home and married again and gave birth to Huo Guang. He broke off the relationship with Wei Shaoer and had no contact with him. After some time, the boy's younger sister Zifu became favored by Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty and was made the queen. Huo Qubing had a distinguished status and was favored by the emperor because he was the son of the queen's sister. After Huo Qubing grew up, he learned that his father was Huo Zhongru, but he never had time to visit him. It happened that Huo Qubing was appointed as a hussar general and went to attack the Xiongnu. He passed by Hedong. The governor of Hedong went to the outskirts of the city to greet him. He led the way with a bow and arrow on his back and rested at the reception area of ​​Hou Jiabao in Pingyang. Huo Qubing sent a small official to invite Huo Zhongru to meet him. Zhongru hurried over and greeted him respectfully. Huo Qubing stepped forward to greet him and bowed down. He knelt down and said, "Qubing didn't know that I was your flesh and blood." The middle child kowtowed to the ground and said, "This veteran can entrust his destiny to the general. This is God's help." Qubing bought a large number of fields, houses, and slaves for Zhongru and left. When returning to the army, Huo Qubing passed by Hedong again, so he took Huo Guang to Chang'an. Huo Guang was only ten years old at the time, so he appointed Huo Guang as Lang, and soon he was promoted to the minister of all Cao Cao. After Qu Bing's death, Huo Guang was granted the title of Guanglu, the Commander-in-Chief of the Fengcha. He accompanied the emperor as a chariot when traveling, and served around him in the palace. He had been in and out of the forbidden palace for more than 20 years. He had always been cautious and made no mistakes. He was very close and trusted by the emperor.
target: Huo Guang, courtesy name Zimeng, was the younger half-brother of the renowned general Huo Qubing. Their father Zhongru served as a county official in the Pingyang Hou family and had an affair with the maid Wei Shaoer, fathering Huo Qubing. After completing his duties, Zhongru returned home, married, and fathered Huo Guang, severing all ties with Wei Shaoer. When Huo Qubing later learned of his father's identity while serving as a hussar general attacking the Xiongnu, he visited Zhongru in Hedong, purchased lands and slaves for him, and took ten-year-old Huo Guang to Chang'an. Huo Guang was appointed as Lang and later promoted to various positions. After Huo Qubing's death, Huo Guang served as Guanglu and Commander-in-Chief, accompanying Emperor Wu for over twenty years with cautious conduct, earning the emperor's complete trust.

source: Huo Qubing sent a small official to invite Huo Zhongru to meet him. Zhongru hurried over and greeted him respectfully. Huo Qubing stepped forward to greet him and bowed down. He knelt down and said, "Qubing didn't know that I was your flesh and blood." The middle child kowtowed to the ground and said, "This veteran can entrust his destiny to the general. This is God's help." Qubing bought a large number of fields, houses, and slaves for Zhongru and left. When returning to the army, Huo Qubing passed by Hedong again, so he took Huo Guang to Chang'an. Huo Guang was only ten years old at the time, so he appointed Huo Guang as Lang, and soon he was promoted to the minister of all Cao Cao. After Qu Bing's death, Huo Guang was granted the title of Guanglu, the Commander-in-Chief of the Fengcha. He accompanied the emperor as a chariot when traveling, and served around him in the palace. He had been in and out of the forbidden palace for more than 20 years. He had always been cautious and made no mistakes. He was very close and trusted by the emperor. In the second year of Zhenghe, Prince Wei was framed and defeated by Jiang Chong. King Liu Dan of Yan and King Liu Xu of Guangling both made many mistakes. At this time, the emperor was old, and his beloved concubine Gou Yi and Zhao Jieyu gave birth to a boy. The emperor planned to pass the throne to him and ordered ministers to assist him. The emperor observed that among the ministers, only Huo Guang could take on the important task of assisting the country. The emperor then asked the court painter to draw a picture of Duke Zhou carrying King Cheng on his back to receive congratulations from the princes, and gave it to Huo Guang. In the spring of the second year of the Yuan Dynasty, the emperor traveled to Wuzha Palace and became very ill. Huo Guang asked in tears: If something happens to the emperor, who will succeed him? The emperor said: Don't you still understand the meaning of the painting I gave you last time? When you establish a young son as emperor, you should act like the Duke of Zhou assisting the king. Huo Guang kowtowed and said humbly: I am not as good as Jin Rixi. Jin Rixi also said: I am a foreigner, not as good as Huo Guang. The emperor then appointed Huo Guang as the Grand Sima General, Jin Rixi as the Chariot and Cavalry General, Shangguan Jie, the imperial servant, as the General of the Left, and Sang Hongyang, the captain of the Sosu Su Army, as the Imperial Censor. They all kowtowed before the bed in the emperor's bedroom and accepted their duties, accepting orders to assist the young monarch. The next day, Emperor Wu died, and the prince inherited the throne and was called Emperor Xiaozhao. The emperor was only eight years old, and Huo Guang made all political decisions. Before this, in the first year of Hou, the servant Shemang Heluo and his younger brother Hou Mangtong conspired to rebel. At that time, Huo Guang, Jin Rixi, Shangguan Jie and others killed these rebels, and their achievements were not recorded and rewarded. After Emperor Wu fell ill, he sealed the seal and said: After I die, I will open the seal and follow it.
target: As Emperor Wu aged and Prince Wei was defeated, the emperor chose his young son as heir and entrusted Huo Guang with assisting him. He gave Huo Guang a painting of Duke Zhou carrying King Cheng, symbolizing his expectations. When Emperor Wu fell ill at Wuzha Palace, he appointed Huo Guang as Grand Sima General, along with Jin Rixi, Shangguan Jie, and Sang Hongyang as co-regents. After Emperor Wu's death, the eight-year-old Emperor Zhao ascended the throne, with Huo Guang making all political decisions. Huo Guang was calm, thoughtful, and meticulous in his conduct, maintaining consistent positions when entering and leaving the palace gates.

source: Huo Guang wanted to seize the seal, but Lang Guan pressed his sword and said: My head can be obtained, but the seal cannot be obtained by you! Huo Guang admired Lang Guan's behavior. The next day, he went to Shao to raise the rank of the Langguan by two levels. Everyone applauded Huo Guang's behavior. Huo Guang and Shangguan Jie, the general of the left, were sons and daughters and had a close relationship. Huo Guang's eldest daughter married Shangguan Jie's son Shangguan An. Shangguan An had a daughter who was the same age as Emperor Zhao, so Shangguan Jie passed! Emperor Zhao's sister Eyi Gaizhu took the daughter of Shangxuanshi into the harem as Jieyu, and she was established as queen a few months later. The queen's father, Shangxuanzhou, was appointed as a hussar general and named Sanglehou. Huo Guang sometimes went out of the palace on vacation, and Shangguan Jie would come into the palace to handle political affairs on Huo Guang's behalf. After Shangguan Jie and his son became powerful, they were very grateful to the elder. The eldest princess has no moral integrity and gets close to Ding, a foreigner who dotes on Hewen. Shangguan Ji and Shangguan An planned to apply for the title of marquis on behalf of Ding, hoping to follow the country's previous practice of only marquises marrying princesses, but Huo Guang did not agree. They also asked for the position of Guanglu doctor for Ding foreigners in order to be summoned by Emperor Zhao, but they were rejected by Huo Guang again. The eldest princess was very resentful towards Huo Guang. Shangguan Jie and Shangguan An also felt ashamed because they had failed to obtain titles for Ding strangers several times. During the reign of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, Shangguan Jie was already among the nine ministers, and his official position was above Huo Guang. When Shangguan and his son were both generals, they had an important relationship with the queen in the palace. The queen was Shangguan An's biological daughter, and Huo Guang was just her grandfather. Instead, he took charge of the government alone. Therefore, Shangguan and his son competed with Huo Guang for power. King Liu Dan of Yan thought he was Emperor Zhao's brother, but he did not inherit the throne, so he often harbored resentment. In addition, Sang Hongyang, the imperial censor, suggested setting up a liquor monopoly and salt and iron official management system, which increased the country's wealth. Sang Hongyang took credit for it and planned to get official positions for his children, but failed, so he resented Huo Guang. So Eyi Gaizhu, Shangguan Jie, Shangguan An and Sang Hongyang conspired with the King of Yan Liu Dan, pretending to have someone write a letter on behalf of the King of Yan, saying: Huo Guang went out of the city to practice Lang Guan and Yu Lin. He set up a dignified manner on the road like an emperor when traveling, and also asked the eunuchs to prepare meals in advance. Also, Su Wu was sent as an envoy to the Huns, and was detained for twenty years without surrendering. After returning, he was only made a vassal state, while Yang Chang, the chief general of the general, had no merit, but became the captain of Sosu. Huo Guang also transferred in without authorization to increase the number of captains in his shogunate.
target: Huo Guang's daughter married Shangguan Jie's son Shangguan An, whose daughter became Emperor Zhao's empress. However, conflicts arose when Huo Guang refused to grant titles to Ding Wairen, a favorite of the Grand Princess Eyi Gaizhu. Shangguan Jie, his son, Sang Hongyang, and the Grand Princess conspired with King Liu Dan of Yan, sending a false letter accusing Huo Guang of arrogance and improper conduct. Emperor Zhao, only fourteen, saw through the deception, noting that the letter mentioned events that occurred only ten days prior, which King Yan could not have known. The conspirators then plotted to assassinate Huo Guang, but their scheme was discovered. Huo Guang executed Shangguan Jie, Shangguan An, Sang Hongyang, Ding Wairen, and their families, while King Yan and the Grand Princess committed suicide.

source: The emperor said: "The general arrived in Guangming, and the training of lieutenants was only a recent matter. It has only been ten days since the selection of lieutenants. How did King Yan know these things?" Besides, if a general wants to do something illegal, he doesn't need a lieutenant. At this time, Emperor Zhao was only fourteen years old. The minister and the ministers around him were surprised. The person who submitted the letter actually escaped, and the government began an urgent search. Shangguan Jie and others were frightened, so they told the emperor that this was just a trivial matter and not worth pursuing. The emperor did not listen. Later, whenever Shangguan Jie's party members spoke ill of Huo Guang, Emperor Zhao became angry and said: "The general is a loyal minister, entrusted by the late emperor to assist me. If anyone dares to slander him, he will be punished." From then on, Shangguan Jie and others did not dare to say bad things anymore, so they conspired to have the eldest princess prepare a banquet for Huo Guang, preparing to ambush soldiers to kill him, and then take the opportunity to depose Emperor Zhao and install King Yan as emperor. When the incident was discovered, Huo Guang executed Shangguan Jie, Shangguan An, Sang Hongyang, Ding Wairen and their families. King Yan and Lord Gai also committed suicide. Huo Guang's power shocked the whole country. After Emperor Zhao came of age, he formally appointed Huo Guang to be in power. By the 13th year of Emperor Zhao's reign, the people's lives were abundant and abundant, and all ethnic minorities from all over the world had surrendered. In the first year of Yuanping, Emperor Zhao died without an heir. Among the six sons of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, only King Liu Xu of Guangling is still alive. The ministers discussed the candidate to be appointed, and everyone advocated the establishment of King Guangling. King Guangling was originally not selected by the late emperor because of his immoral behavior. Huo Guang felt uneasy inside. A Lang official wrote: King Zhou deposed his uncle and established Wang Ji, King Wen abandoned Boyikao and established King Wu. As long as it is beneficial to the country, it is okay even to depose the eldest son and establish a younger son. King Guangling could not inherit the ancestral temple and the state. What he said coincided with Huo Guang's thoughts. Huo Guang showed this memorial to Prime Minister Yang Chang and others, and promoted the official to the prefect of Jiujiang. On the same day, according to the empress dowager's edict, he sent Shaofu Lecheng, Zongzheng Liu De, Guanglu doctor Bingji, and Zhonglang general Lihan to meet the Changyi king Liu He. Liu He was the grandson of Emperor Mowu and the son of King Ai of Changyi. After he arrived in the palace and ascended to the throne of God, he soon began to act lewdly. Huo Guang was worried and angry, so he went to ask his close confidant, Chief Farming Yannian, about the matter alone. Tian Yannian said: As the pillar of the country, since the general found that this person cannot be entrusted to the country, why not report it to the Queen Mother and choose another worthy person to make him emperor? Huo Guang said: I want to do this too. I wonder if there is any precedent for this in ancient times? Tian Yannian replied: When Yi Yin became the prime minister of the Yin Dynasty, he deposed Taijia to stabilize the country. Later generations praised his loyalty.
target: After Emperor Zhao died without an heir, the ministers initially considered King Liu Xu of Guangling, but Huo Guang opposed this due to the king's immoral character. Following a suggestion from a Lang official citing historical precedents, Huo Guang arranged for the installation of King Liu He of Changyi. However, Liu He soon began behaving lewdly and improperly. Huo Guang, troubled by this, consulted with Tian Yannian, who cited the precedent of Yi Yin deposing Taijia. Huo Guang gathered the ministers, and after Tian Yannian threatened those who hesitated with execution, they agreed to depose the king. Huo Guang reported to the Empress Dowager, who issued an edict. The ministers jointly impeached King Changyi for numerous offenses during his twenty-seven-day reign, including failing to observe mourning, engaging in debauchery, and issuing over 1,127 orders for various items. The Empress Dowager approved the deposition, and Huo Guang personally removed the imperial seal from King Changyi, who was sent back to his former residence.

source: Emperor Xiaowu's great-grandson was ill. Emperor Wu had Shaoling to raise and take care of him in Yeting. Now he is eighteen years old. He studied "Poetry", "The Analects of Confucius" and "The Classic of Filial Piety" as a teacher. He practiced frugality and was kind and loving. He could inherit the throne of Emperor Xiaozhao, serve his ancestors and rule the people. I risked my life to tell you. The Empress Dowager issued an edict: "It must be played accurately." Huo Guang sent Zongzheng and Liu De to his great-grandson's home, Shangguanli, to help him wash and bathe, and gave him the emperor's clothes. He asked the servant to take his great-grandson to Zongzheng's mansion in a light car to fast, and then went to Weiyang Palace to see the empress dowager. He was named Marquis of Yangwu. Soon Huo Guang held the emperor's seal and went to the Gaomiao to pay homage, becoming Emperor Xiaoxuan. The next year, the emperor issued an edict saying: It is common practice in ancient and modern times to praise those who are virtuous and reward those who have made great achievements. Huo Guang, the great general of Sima, guards the court with loyalty and integrity, promotes morality and shows kindness, preserves integrity and upholds benevolence and righteousness, so as to stabilize the ancestral temple. Seventeen thousand households in Hebei and Dongwuyang were granted to Huo Guang. Including his previous fiefdom, there were a total of 20,000 households. He was rewarded seven thousand catties of gold, sixty million in money, thirty thousand pieces of silk of various colors, one hundred and seventy slaves, two thousand horses, and a first-class residence.
target: Huo Guang then arranged for the installation of Emperor Wu's great-grandson, who was living among the people, as Emperor Xuan. For his services, Huo Guang received additional fiefdoms totaling 20,000 households, along with gold, money, silk, slaves, and horses.

source: He was rewarded seven thousand catties of gold, sixty million in money, thirty thousand pieces of silk of various colors, one hundred and seventy slaves, two thousand horses, and a first-class residence. From the time of Emperor Zhao, Huo Guang's son Huo Yu and Huo Guang's brother's grandson Huo Yun were already Zhonglang Generals. Huo Yun's younger brother Huo Shan served as Fengche Captain and Shizhong, and controlled the military power of Hu and Yue. Huo Guang's two sons-in-law are the guards of the East and West Palaces respectively. The sons-in-law and grandsons of Huo Guang's brothers are eligible to participate in court meetings, serve as Cao officials, cavalry captains, and receive official positions in the affairs. Factions and relatives were united and occupied the court in an intricate manner. Huo Guang had been the prime minister of the government since the Hou Yuan Dynasty. He did not return the government until the emperor ascended the throne. The emperor was humble and refused to accept it. He had to consult Huo Guang for instructions on all political matters before reporting them to the emperor. Every time Huo Guang went to court to see him, the emperor was humble and serious, and treated him with great respect and courtesy. Huo Guang was in power for twenty years. In the spring of the second year of Dijie, he became seriously ill. The emperor personally went to his home to see his condition and shed tears for him. Huo Guang wrote a letter to express his gratitude and said: I would like to use the three thousand property of my feudal land to enfeoff my brother's grandson, Fengche Captain Huo Shan, as a lord, in order to worship my brother Hussar General Huo Qubing. The emperor handed over the matter to the Prime Minister and Censor, and appointed Huo Guang's son Huo Yu as the right general on the same day. After Huo Guang passed away, the emperor and the empress dowager personally went to Huo Guang's mourning hall to express their condolences. Ren Xuan, the Taizhong doctor, and five imperial censors held the talisman to organize the funeral. The minister of Nakajikoku set up shogunate services on the cemetery. The emperor also gave money, silk and cotton, a hundred embroidered quilts, fifty boxes of clothes, gold and jade clothes, an inner coffin, an outer coffin, and a pair of yellow intestines, and fifteen pairs of fir wood coffins were buried with him. The secret weapons of Wenming made by Cambodian Garden are all in compliance with the emperor's specifications. Huo Guang's body was carried in a roller carriage, which was covered with yellow satin, and a feathered flag was placed on the left side of the shaft. Officers, light carriages, and soldiers from the five schools of the Northern Army were sent to Maoling to bury Huo Guang. He was given the title of Xuanchenghou.
target: His family members held numerous important positions throughout the court. Huo Guang remained in power for twenty years until his death, after which he was buried with great honors at Maoling and given the title Xuanchenghou.

source: Huo Shan said: The prime minister arbitrarily reduced the number of lambs, rabbits, and frogs offered to the ancestral temple. This can be used to convict him. They conspired to ask the Queen Mother to set up a banquet for Lord Boping, summon the prime minister and officials below Ping'enhou, and have Fan Mingyou and Deng Guanghan take these people out and behead them on the Queen Mother's order, taking the opportunity to depose the emperor and make Huo Yu the emperor. Before the agreed plan was implemented, Huo Yun was appointed as the prefect of Xuantu, and Ren Xuan, the Taizhong doctor, was appointed as the prefect of Daijun. Huo Shan also broke the law for copying the palace secretaries. Xian wrote a letter expressing his willingness to donate his mansion in the west of the city and a thousand horses to atone for Huo Shan's crime. Emperor Xuan only approved it in his memorial. Just when their plot was discovered, Huo Yun, Huo Shan, and Fan Mingyou committed suicide, and Xian, Huo Yu, Deng Guanghan and others were captured. Huo Yu was cut in half, and several of her daughters and brothers were executed. Only Empress Huo was deposed and imprisoned in Zhaotai. Thousands of families were implicated in the Star Doctor and were convicted and executed to exterminate their clans. Emperor Xuan then issued an edict saying: Not long ago, Shi Zhangshe, the commander of the Zhishi Office, instructed Li Jing, a wealthy family in Wei County, to reply to Guanyang Hou Huoyun and conspire to cause rebellion. Because of the general, I suppressed the matter and did not make it public, hoping that they could change Bai Xin. Now the great Sima Bo, Lu Hou Huo Yu, his mother, Xuancheng Hou's wife Xian, and their cousin's sons, Guanyang Hou Huoyun, Leping Hou Huoshan, and their sisters' sons-in-law, are conspiring to harm the people. Thanks to the blessing of the ancestors, they were discovered and captured in advance, and all of them were executed according to law. I am very sad about this matter. All those who were implicated by the Huo family, if the incident occurred before Bingshen and had not yet discovered that the reporting officer was in custody, will be pardoned. The man Zhang Zhang discovered the incident first and told Dong Zhong of Qimen. Dong Zhong reported it to Zuo Cao Yang, and Yang Pan reported it to Shizhong Jin Anshang. Yang Fan was summoned to state the situation, and later Zhang Zhang wrote a report. Shi Gao and Jin Anshang, the servants, suggested reporting the matter. If the Huo family was not allowed to enter the palace ban, the Huo family's conspiracy did not succeed. They were both equally meritorious.
target: After Huo Guang's death, his wife Xian and their sons Huo Yu, Huo Yun, and Huo Shan became increasingly arrogant and extravagant. Xian had previously poisoned Empress Xu to install her daughter as empress, a secret that Huo Guang had concealed. As Emperor Xuan gradually reduced the Huo family's power, they grew fearful and plotted rebellion, planning to depose the emperor and install Huo Yu. The conspiracy was discovered, leading to Huo Yun, Huo Shan, and Fan Mingyou committing suicide, while Xian, Huo Yu, and others were executed. The Huo clan was exterminated, and Empress Huo was deposed.

source: When Emperor Xuan first came to the throne, he went to visit the Gaomiao Temple. General Huo Guang was riding in a car with him. The emperor was very frightened, as if there were thorns in his back. Later, the chariot and cavalry general Zhang Anshi accompanied Huo Guang on the ride, and the emperor felt more comfortable and relaxed, feeling very safe and close. After Huo Guang's death, his clan was also executed. Therefore, there is a legend among the people: Those whose power shocks the monarch will not be tolerated. The Huo family's troubles began with accompanying people. When he became emperor, a hundred people were assigned to guard Huo Guang's tomb, and officials and soldiers performed sacrifices on time. In the second year of the Yuan Dynasty, Huo Yang, the great-grandson of Huo Guang's cousin, was granted the title of Marquis of Bolu and was granted food to a thousand households in the city. Jin Rixi, whose courtesy name was Uncle Weng, was originally the prince of King Xiutu of the Xiongnu. During the Yuanshou period of Emperor Wu, Hussar general Huo Qubing led troops to attack the western region of the Xiongnu and killed many people. They also captured the gold Buddha statue that King Xiutu used to worship the gods.
target: Jin Rixi, originally a Xiongnu prince, was captured as a slave after his father King Xiutu was killed.

source: At this time, Emperor Wu went to Linguang Palace, where Jin Rixi was lying in the palace to rest because of a minor illness. Mang Heluo, Mang Tong and their younger brother Mang Ancheng came out at night under the pretense of the emperor's order, killed the envoy together, and then launched an army to rebel. The next morning, Emperor Wu had not gotten up yet, so Mang Heluo had no excuse to enter the palace from outside. Jin Rixi was suddenly moved when he was going to the toilet, so he immediately went in and sat down in the noodle room. After a while, Mang He came in from the box with a dagger wrapped in his sleeves. When he saw Jin Rixi, his expression suddenly changed. He ran quickly towards the emperor's bed, trying to go in, but he encountered the dagger and stayed there for a while. Jin Rihui took the opportunity to hug Mang Heluo, and then shouted loudly: Mang Heluo has rebelled! Emperor Wu was frightened and stood up quickly. The people on his left and right drew their swords and wanted to kill Mang Heluo. Emperor Wu was afraid of accidentally hurting Jin Rixi, so he told his people not to kill him. Jin Richan grabbed Mang Heluo by the neck and threw him to His Highness. The guards then caught Mang Heluo and tied him up. All the rebels were thoroughly investigated and convicted. From then on, Jin Rixi became famous for his loyalty and filial piety. Jin Rixi has been keeping his eyes open for decades since he was by Emperor Wu's side. He never dared to get close to the maid given to him. Emperor Wu wanted to marry his daughter into the harem, but he refused. Jin Rixi was so loyal and cautious, and Emperor Wu felt that he was different even more. When Emperor Wu fell ill, he asked Huo Guang to assist the young monarch. Huo Guang recommended Jin Rixi, and Jin Rixi said: "I am a foreigner. If you do this, the Huns will despise the Han Dynasty." So he became Huo Guang's deputy. Huo Guang married his daughter to Jin Rixi's son Jinshang. Later, Emperor Wu sent an edict to confer Jin Rixi the title of Marquis of Shao for his contribution to the expedition against Mang Heluo. Jin Rixi refused to accept the title of Marquis because Emperor Zhao was young.
target: He served as a horse keeper but caught Emperor Wu's attention through his dignified bearing and honest answers. He became a trusted attendant, known for his loyalty and filial piety. He killed his own son for improper behavior with palace servants and later helped thwart a rebellion by Mang Heluo. When Emperor Wu appointed regents, Jin Rixi served as Huo Guang's deputy, refusing a marquisate due to Emperor Zhao's youth. His descendants continued serving the Han court for seven generations, maintaining a reputation for loyalty and filial piety.

source: Wei Xian, whose courtesy name is Changru, was born in Zou, State of Lu. His ancestor was Wei Meng, who originally lived in Pengcheng and was the Fu of King Yuan of Chu. He was also the Fu of King Yuan's son, King Yi, and his grandson, Liu Wu. Liu Wu was dissolute and disobedient, so Wei Meng wrote poems to ridicule and admonish him. Later, Wei Meng resigned from his official position, moved his family to Zoudi, and wrote another remonstrative poem. His admonition poem said: Our solemn and great ancestors founded the country from the time of Weishi, wearing fur clothes decorated with ax-shaped patterns and Zhu Fu decorated with "Ya" patterns, driving a chariot drawn by four male horses, with dragon pins on them. He was given the Tong Gong and was responsible for conquests; he pacified the people in remote areas, took charge of many states, and assisted the Shang Dynasty. Later, there was Dapeng, who also made outstanding achievements. By the time of the Zhou Dynasty, our Chu state had been among the princes for several generations and participated in alliances.
target: Wei Xian, courtesy name Changru, was from Zou in the State of Lu. His ancestor, Wei Meng, served as a tutor to King Yuan of Chu and his descendants. Because Liu Wu was dissolute, Wei Meng wrote poems to admonish him, then resigned and moved his family to Zoudi, where he wrote another remonstrative poem. This poem recounts the history of their lineage from the Shang Dynasty through the Zhou, the decline of Chu, and the rise of the Han Dynasty.

source: Wei Meng later died in Zoudi. Some people say that his descendants wrote this poem because they did good deeds and recalled the ambitions of their ancestors. It has been passed down for five generations from Wei Meng to Wei Xian. Wei Xian was a simple man with a pure heart and few desires. He devoted himself to learning. He was proficient in "Li" and "Shangshu" and taught "Poetry" to others. He was called the great Confucian of Zou Lu. Later, the imperial court recruited him as a doctor and appointed him as an official. He entered the palace to teach Emperor Zhao to study "Poetry", and was slowly promoted to Guanglu doctor Zhan Shi, and later to Dahonglu. Emperor Zhao died without an heir, so the general Huo Guang and the ministers honored him as Emperor Xiaoxuan. Emperor Xuan had just ascended the throne. Wei Xian was given the title of Marquis of Guannei and had a household to worship him because he participated in the plan to support Emperor Xuan, stabilize the country and stabilize the country. Moved to the Shaofu of Changxin Palace. Because Wei Xian was once the teacher of Emperor Zhao, he was very respected. In the third year of Benshi, Wei Xian replaced Cai Yi as prime minister and was granted the title of Marquis of Fuyang, with a settlement of 700 households.
target: It criticizes the current king for neglecting state affairs, indulging in pleasure, and surrounding himself with flatterers, warning him to learn from past examples. Wei Meng later died in Zoudi. It was passed down for five generations to Wei Xian. Wei Xian was a simple, pure-hearted man devoted to learning. He was proficient in the "Li" and "Shangshu," taught the "Poetry," and was called the great Confucian of Zou Lu. He was recruited as a doctor, taught Emperor Zhao the "Poetry," and was promoted to Guanglu doctor Zhan Shi and later Dahonglu. After Emperor Zhao died without an heir, Wei Xian was made Marquis of Guannei for his role in supporting Emperor Xuan. He became Shaofu of Changxin Palace and was highly respected. In the third year of Benshi, he became prime minister and was granted the title of Marquis of Fuyang.

source: Emperor Xuan had just ascended the throne. Wei Xian was given the title of Marquis of Guannei and had a household to worship him because he participated in the plan to support Emperor Xuan, stabilize the country and stabilize the country. Moved to the Shaofu of Changxin Palace. Because Wei Xian was once the teacher of Emperor Zhao, he was very respected. In the third year of Benshi, Wei Xian replaced Cai Yi as prime minister and was granted the title of Marquis of Fuyang, with a settlement of 700 households. At that time, Wei Xian was over 70 years old. He had been prime minister for five years and had been in Jiji for three years. He asked the court to resign because of his old age and illness. The court rewarded him with one hundred catties of gold, dismissed him and returned to his hometown, and also gave him a mansion. The resignation of the prime minister began with Wei Xian. Wei Xian died at the age of eighty-two, and the imperial court gave him the title of Jiehou. Wei Xian had four sons: the eldest son, Wei Fangshan, served as the magistrate of Gaodi County and died very early; the second son, Wei Hong, was promoted to the prefect of Shuhai; the third son, Wei Shun, stayed in Lu to guard the cemetery of Wei's ancestral hall; the youngest son, Wei Xuancheng, was promoted to the position of prime minister many times because of his proficiency in Confucian classics. Therefore, there is a proverb in Zoulu: It is better to leave a box full of gold to your son than to leave him a scripture. Wei Xuancheng, a young man, was appointed as a Langguan and a regular attendant on Sanqi due to his father's favor.
target: Over seventy, he served for five years before resigning due to illness, receiving gold and a mansion. His resignation began the practice of prime ministers retiring. He died at eighty-two and was given the title of Jiehou. Wei Xian had four sons. The eldest, Wei Fangshan, died early. The second, Wei Hong, became a prefect. The third, Wei Shun, guarded the ancestral cemetery. The youngest, Wei Xuancheng, became prime minister due to his knowledge of the classics. A proverb in Zoulu stated it was better to leave a son a classic than a box of gold.

source: Wei Xian had four sons: the eldest son, Wei Fangshan, served as the magistrate of Gaodi County and died very early; the second son, Wei Hong, was promoted to the prefect of Shuhai; the third son, Wei Shun, stayed in Lu to guard the cemetery of Wei's ancestral hall; the youngest son, Wei Xuancheng, was promoted to the position of prime minister many times because of his proficiency in Confucian classics. Therefore, there is a proverb in Zoulu: It is better to leave a box full of gold to your son than to leave him a scripture. Wei Xuancheng, a young man, was appointed as a Langguan and a regular attendant on Sanqi due to his father's favor. He was eager to learn when he was young and inherited his father's Confucianism. He was extremely humble and courteous to virtuous people. Sometimes when he went out and met people he knew on foot, he would always ask his attendants to get off the car and take them back as a normal thing. He treated people, including the poor and humble, with even greater respect, and his reputation spread far and wide. Because he was proficient in Confucian classics, he was promoted to the position of admonishing doctor and then moved to the rank of captain of Dahe County.
target: Wei Xuancheng was appointed as a Langguan due to his father's favor. He was eager to learn, humble, and respectful to all, earning a wide reputation. He was promoted to admonishing doctor and then captain of Dahe County.

source: Because he was proficient in Confucian classics, he was promoted to the position of admonishing doctor and then moved to the rank of captain of Dahe County. At the beginning, Xuancheng's elder brother Wei Hong was serving as Taichang Cheng, and his duties were to guard the ancestral temple and be in charge of the imperial tombs and gardens. Because of the complicated affairs, he committed many crimes. His father Wei Xian, because Wei Hong should be the heir of the Wei family in the future, was afraid that he would be deposed for committing crimes, so he ordered Wei Hong to resign from the official position of Taichang Cheng due to illness. However, Wei Hong was humble and refused to resign. When Wei Xian became seriously ill, Wei Hong was finally imprisoned for not being considerate in guarding the ancestral temple, and had not yet been convicted. The family members asked Wei Xian who should be the heir to the Wei family, but Wei Xian showed an expression of anger and hatred and refused to speak. So Wei Xian's disciple, Dr. Yi Qian, and others discussed with Wei Xian's clan members, pretending that it was Wei Xian's order, and asked the general manager of the Wei family to write a general order to establish Wei Xuan, the captain of Dahe County, as the successor of the Wei family. After Wei Xian's death, Xuancheng heard the bad news in his official position and heard that he should be the heir. Xuancheng knew that dismissal was not what his father Wei Xian had always meant, so he pretended to be insane, urinated and defecated in bed, talked nonsense, and laughed wildly. The imperial court summoned him to Chang'an. After the funeral, Wei Xuancheng was supposed to inherit his father's title, but Xuancheng pretended to be insane and ignored the imperial edict. Da Honglu wrote to the court, and the court issued documents to the prime minister and censor, asking them to investigate and handle the matter. Xuancheng always had a good reputation. Many scholar-bureaucrats believed that Xuancheng wanted to give up his title to his brother Wei Hong, so he pretended to be insane. Prime Minister Shi, who was in charge of the investigation, then wrote to Xuancheng, saying: The ancients must have a decent name when they resigned, so that their reputation can be passed down to future generations. Now you are just blindly destroying your appearance, suffering humiliation, pretending to be crazy, without any luster, and your benevolence and righteousness are hidden and not exposed. The name you used to give in is too humble. I have never been very clever, and the imperial court placed too much emphasis on me, making me the prime minister and deacon. I hope you can let me hear the good excuse you used. Otherwise, I'm afraid you will hurt Gao Gaoxing and I will become a villain. Wei Xuancheng's friend and minister Zhang also wrote to the court saying: When a wise monarch governs the country, he advocates courtesy, benevolence and righteousness. The Xuancheng court should treat him with courtesy and kindness, and should not wrong or wrong his good ambitions, so that he can feel at ease even though he is poor. The prime minister and censor finally impeached Xuancheng to the court because he was pretending to be ill. The imperial court issued an edict not to impeach Xuancheng, but sent someone to call him and worship him as an official. Xuancheng had no choice but to accept the title. Emperor Xuan admired his integrity and made Xuancheng the governor of Henan. He made his elder brother Wei Hong the captain of Taishan County and moved to the prefect of Donghai. A few years later, Xuancheng was recruited by the imperial court as a guard in Weiyang Palace and was promoted to Taichang. Because he had a good relationship with the original Pingtong Marquis Yang Tan, Yang Tan was killed and his comrades and friends were dismissed from their official positions. Later, because the princes accompanied them to worship at Emperor Xiaohui's temple and they should enter the temple in the morning, because it rained and formed puddles, they did not ride in a four-horse cart but rode to the ancestral temple. The officials in charge petitioned for impeachment, and several princes of the same generation as Wei Xuancheng were demoted to the rank of Guannei Marquis. Xuancheng was very sad because his father's title was reduced due to his mistakes. He sighed: "How can I have the face to preside over the sacrifices in the ancestral temple!" I wrote a poem to blame myself. The poem says: Our glorious and glorious ancestors began to be granted the title of marquis since Weishi, and were appointed to be called uncles, assisting the Yin Shang Dynasty to stabilize.
target: When Wei Xian was ill, he was angry that Wei Hong, who was supposed to be the heir, was imprisoned for a crime. Wei Xian's disciple and clan members, pretending it was his order, established Wei Xuancheng as the successor. Xuancheng knew this was not his father's wish, so he feigned insanity to avoid inheriting the title. The court investigated, and many believed he was trying to give the title to his brother. The prime minister and censor impeached him for feigning illness, but the emperor did not punish him and instead called him to serve. Xuancheng accepted the title. Emperor Xuan made him governor of Henan and his brother Wei Hong a captain. Xuancheng later became a guard in Weiyang Palace and was promoted to Taichang. Due to a mistake during a rainstorm when he rode instead of using a four-horse cart to the ancestral temple, he was demoted to the rank of Guannei Marquis. He was deeply saddened and wrote a poem blaming himself, lamenting his loss of title and vowing to be more careful.

source: Who said Huashan is high? I hope to be as high as it; who said practicing virtue is difficult? I hope I can achieve it through hard work. Oh, little me, I can never make such a mistake again; I ruined my good reputation by saying these sad words. Princes and kings everywhere should learn from me; their attire, chariots and chariots should be dignified and orderly, and their steps should be solemn and dignified. At the beginning, Huaiyang Xianwang, the son of Emperor Xuan's favorite concubine Zhang Jieyu, liked to handle state affairs and was familiar with the law. The emperor appreciated his talents and intended to make him his heir. However, because the prince was born in poverty and lost his mother early, he could not bear to depose the prince. After a long time, Emperor Xuan wanted to influence King Xian from the side and make him understand, so he wanted people who knew etiquette and resignation to assist him, so he summoned Wei Xuancheng and worshiped him as the lieutenant of Huaiyang. At this time, King Xian had not yet taken office in his own kingdom. Xuancheng accepted Shao's order and discussed the similarities and differences of the scriptures with the prince Taifu Xiao Wangzhi and the Confucian scholars who were responsible for the "Five Classics" in Shiquhe, and wrote an entry to inquire the emperor. After Emperor Yuan came to the throne, he appointed Xuancheng as Shaofu, promoted to Prince Taifu, and later became Yushi Dafu. During the Yongguang period, Wei Xuancheng replaced Yu Dingguo as prime minister. Wei Xuancheng was demoted for about ten years, and then took the official position of the prime minister where his father had been. He was also made a marquis in the original feudal country, and he was honored in the world.
target: Later, Emperor Xuan wanted someone to influence King Xian of Huaiyang, so he appointed Wei Xuancheng as the lieutenant of Huaiyang. After Emperor Yuan came to the throne, Xuancheng became Shaofu, Prince Taifu, and Yushi Dafu. During the Yongguang period, he replaced Yu Dingguo as prime minister, returning to the same position his father held.

source: Xuancheng wrote another poem in which he expressed the difficulty of getting up from mistakes and used it to admonish his descendants. The poem said: A solemn gentleman cultivates his own virtue by behaving dignifiedly. He treats etiquette and dress respectfully and is neat and tidy to serve as a model. Alas, I am a humble person, but my virtue is not as good as theirs. I was deprived of my title because I was careless in dress, carriage and carriage. The sage emperor has outstanding virtues; he did not abandon me in the end and let me rank among the nine ministers. Since I received such a favor from the emperor, I have been careful day and night, warning myself to exercise self-discipline and not to neglect my duties as an official.
target: He wrote another poem admonishing his descendants to be careful in their duties and dress.

source: Be cautious about important court affairs, be careful about dressing up for car and car battles, don't be ungraceful, and keep your fiefdom well. Don't look at me and imitate me, being careless and untidy like me; the restoration of my official position is a blessing from God. Oh, juniors, be careful. Don't tarnish your glorious ancestors and protect the Han Dynasty! Wei Xuancheng had been prime minister for seven years. He was not as good as his father Wei Xian in terms of ethics and stability, but surpassed his father in literary talent. Wei Xuancheng died in the third year of Jianzhao, and Mi was named Gonghou. At first, Wei Xian moved to Pingling during the reign of Emperor Zhao, and Wei Xuancheng moved to Duling. Xuancheng was very ill and was about to die.
