He sent a messenger to express his feelings to the court. He said: I can't bear the deep love between father and son but they are buried in two places. I hope the emperor can allow me to resign and go back to be buried with my father. The emperor agreed to his request. His son Wei Kuan, Marquis of Qing, inherited the title.
target: He served as prime minister for seven years, surpassing his father in literary talent but not in ethical stability. He died in the third year of Jianzhao and was named Gonghou. He requested to be buried with his father, which was granted. His descendants inherited his title.

source: Taishang and Xiaohui temples have become estranged due to estranged family relationships and should be demolished. The deity in the Taishang Emperor's Temple should be buried in the cemetery. Emperor Xiaohui should be Mu, and the deity should be moved to the Taizu Temple. No more mausoleums or gardens should be built. Their memorial was approved. The ministers who discussed the matter also believed that the poem "Qing Temple" said that the etiquette of worshiping the god does not require silence, but now once a month, the emperor's clothes are carried in a procession between the mausoleum and the temple. There are many carriages and horses, wind and rain, which does not meet the requirements of silence. "The Book of Rites" says: Don't perform too many sacrifices. Too many sacrifices are blasphemy, and blasphemy means disrespecting the ancestors. Therefore, the ancient ritual system should be restored, and sacrifices should be held in temples according to the four seasons. In addition, there is no need to build those mausoleums, gardens, or cities where sacrifices should be performed from time to time or once every few days. The emperor will no longer change. The next year, Wei Xuancheng wrote another letter saying: In ancient times, etiquette was formulated to distinguish the superior from the inferior. If the king's mother is not a direct descendant, she cannot be sacrificed in the temple with the former emperor. Then food should be offered in the mausoleum for sacrifice, and it will stop when the emperor dies. Your Majesty is very filial and upholds the will of God. You have established ancestral temples and ancestral temples, and formulated a system for destroying and abandoning sacrificial temples one after another. His memorial was approved. More than a year later, Wei Xuancheng died and Kuang Heng became prime minister. The emperor was lying ill in bed and dreamed that his ancestors had condemned him for destroying the temples of various feudal states. The emperor's younger brother, King Chu Xiao, also dreamed about this. The emperor went down to Shao and asked Kuang Heng what to do, and discussed the idea of ​​re-establishing sacrificial temples in various feudal states. Kuang Heng tried his best to dissuade him, thinking that this could not be done. The emperor's illness could not be cured for a long time. Kuang Heng was very scared and prayed in the temple of Emperor Gaozu, Emperor Xiaowen and Emperor Xiaowu: "The great-grandsons of future generations will inherit the great achievements of their ancestors and work hard day and night, not daring to enjoy themselves. They want to carry forward the legacy of their ancestors and show their great achievements." Therefore, every move and every move to welcome the Lord God must follow the scriptures of the ancient saints. In the past, officials in charge believed that the purpose of establishing ancestral temples in places where the emperor had visited was to win over the hearts of the people at home, not to honor ancestors and fathers. Now, relying on the gods of the ancestral temple, no one in the world dares not to surrender. Therefore, the ancestral temples should be built in the capital, and the emperor personally presides over the sacrifices. The temples in various feudal states can stop being built. The emperor respected the rituals of the past and respected the gods of his ancestors, so he appealed to his ancestors and did not dare to be disrespectful. Now the emperor was ill and could not recover for a long time. He also dreamed that his ancestors warned him about the destruction of the ancestral temple. King Chu's dream also had this meaning.
target: The text then discusses the system of ancestral temples. During Emperor Gaozu's reign, temples were built in various vassal states. Over time, many temples were established. During Emperor Yuan's reign, Gong Yu proposed destroying temples that did not conform to ancient rituals. After discussion, many temples were abolished. Later, due to the emperor's illness and dreams, some temples were restored, but the ancestral temples in vassal states were ultimately abandoned. After Emperor Yuan's death, Kuang Heng proposed further abolitions. During Emperor Ai's reign, a debate occurred about whether to destroy Emperor Xiaowu's temple. Some argued for its preservation due to his great achievements, while others argued for its destruction based on ritual. The emperor adopted the suggestion to preserve it. During Emperor Ping's reign, Wang Mang proposed destroying the Huangkao Temple and other gardens, which was approved. The historian Ban Biao noted that the Han dynasty's ancestral system was determined according to the times, and the plans of the Confucian scholars, particularly Liu Xin, were profound.

source: Han Xin was born in Huaiyin County. The family is poor and has no good character. He cannot be elected to be an official, and he cannot do business to make a living. He often lives in other people's homes and eats nothing. His mother passed away and was too poor to bury her, so he found a high, dry place with spacious surroundings as a cemetery so that tens of thousands of families could be placed next to the grave in the future. Han Xin once went to the countryside to eat at the pavilion chief's house in Nanchang. The pavilion chief's wife hated him so much that she got up very early to prepare the meal and put it on the bed to eat. When it was breakfast time, Han Xin went and no meal was prepared for him. Han Xin understood her intention and left her, never to interact with her again. Han Xin once went fishing in the city. An old woman was rinsing silk cotton wool. She took pity on him and gave him food. This continued for dozens of days until the rinsing was completed.
target: Han Xin, born in Huaiyin, was poor and unable to become an official or engage in trade. He often relied on others for food. After his mother died, he buried her on a high, spacious site, hoping for future grandeur. He once ate at a pavilion chief's home, but the chief's wife resented him and prepared meals early, leaving none for him at breakfast. Han Xin understood and left. While fishing, an old woman rinsing silk fed him for dozens of days.

source: Xiao He replied: How dare I run away? I am chasing those who run away. The king of Han asked: Who are you chasing? Xiao He replied: It's Han Xin. The King of Han scolded again: "There are dozens of generals who have escaped, but you have not pursued them; you only pursued Han Xin. This is a lie." Xiao He said: Those generals are easy to get, and outstanding talents like Han Xin can be said to be unparalleled in the world.
target: Grateful, he promised to repay her, but she scolded him, saying she pitied him, not expecting repayment.

source: Han Xin once went fishing in the city. An old woman was rinsing silk cotton wool. She took pity on him and gave him food. This continued for dozens of days until the rinsing was completed. Han Xin said gratefully to his old mother: I will definitely repay you heavily in the future. The old man was very angry after hearing this and said, "You are a man and can't support yourself. I gave you food out of pity for you, a young man. Do I want you to repay me?" A young man in Huaiyin City bullied Han Xin and said: Although you are tall and like to wear swords, you are actually very timid. He insulted Han Xin in public and said: If you are not afraid of death, stab me with a sword; if you are afraid of death, get under my crotch. So Han Xin stared at the young man carefully, then bent down and crawled under his crotch. People watching the excitement on the street laughed at Han Xin and thought he was cowardly. When Xiang Liang led his army across the Huai River to the north, Han Xin took his sword and went to him, and became an unknown soldier under Xiang Liang. After Xiang Liang failed, he returned to Xiang Yu, who made him a doctor. Han Xin repeatedly offered advice to Xiang Yu, but Xiang Yu did not adopt it. Liu Bang, the king of Han, entered Hanzhong, and Han Xin escaped from the Chu army and joined the king of Han. At the beginning, he was still unknown and worked as a granary management clerk. Later, he was sentenced to death for breaking the law. Thirteen of his accomplices were beheaded. When it was Han Xin's turn, Han Xin looked up and happened to see Teng Gong Xia Houying, so he asked: Doesn't the King of Han want to unify the world? Why kill the strong man? Teng Gong felt that Han Xin's words were unusual and he looked very powerful, so he did not kill him. After talking to Han Xin, he was very happy and reported his situation to the King of Han. The King of Han appointed Han Xin as the Commander-in-Chief of Su Su, but did not reuse him. Han Xin talked with Xiao He many times, and Xiao He appreciated his talent very much.
target: A young man in Huaiyin insulted Han Xin, daring him to fight or crawl under his crotch. Han Xin stared, then crawled through, enduring public ridicule. Han Xin joined Xiang Liang's army as a soldier, then served Xiang Yu as a郎中, offering advice that was ignored. He later defected to Liu Bang, King of Han, as a仓管员. Sentenced to death for a crime, he appealed to Teng Gong Xia Houying, who spared him after a conversation. Liu Bang made him a治粟都尉 but didn't value him. Han Xin fled when not promoted, but Xiao He chased him back. Xiao He convinced Liu Bang to formally appoint Han Xin as a大将, with a ceremony. Liu Bang asked Han Xin for strategies. Han Xin analyzed Xiang Yu's weaknesses—his inability to delegate, stinginess with rewards, and cruelty—contrasting Liu Bang's potential to win hearts by appointing capable men, rewarding merit, and respecting the people's wishes. He predicted easy conquest of the Three Qin states. Liu Bang followed his plan, marching east through Chencang to pacify the region.

source: Now that the king has sent troops to advance, the fiefdom of the Three Qin kings can be pacified as long as a document is passed down. So the King of Han was very happy, thinking that it was too late to get Han Xin, so he arranged the targets for the generals to attack according to Han Xin's strategy. The king of Han sent troops to march eastward through Chencang and pacified the Three Qin Dynasties. In the second year of the Han Dynasty, he led his troops out of Hanguguan and conquered the king of Wei and the king of Henan. The king of Han and Yin also surrendered. Then he united the troops of Qi and Tang to attack Pengcheng, the capital of Chu. The Han soldiers were defeated and returned in disarray. Bi Xin then sent troops to join forces with Mu Yingchang, and attacked the Chu army between the fortress and the fortress, and defeated the Chu army. Therefore, the Chu army could not advance westward. After the Han army was defeated in Pengcheng, Sima Xin, king of Sai, and Dong Yi, king of Zhai, escaped from the Han army and surrendered to the Chu army. Bianyou, Shengyu and Qu also rebelled against each other and made peace with each other. He sent Tai Qi to lobby Wei King Bao, but Wei Bao refused to listen, so he appointed Locust Xin as Zuo Prime Minister to attack Qu. Cross-examining Su: Can Qu not use Uncle Dan as a general? Li Sheng replied: The general is Yuan Zhi. The whole letter said: He is just a child. Then he marched to attack the grasshopper. The king of Wei deployed heavy troops in Zhayuan and blocked Linjin Pass. Hanzhi then set up additional suspects, deployed his boats, and pretended to cross the river from Zhuozhi. He also sent a concealed ambush force to cross the river from Xia Yang with wooden urns and basins of floating water to sneak attack Anyi. King Wei Bao of Wei was greatly frightened and hurriedly led his troops to attack Zhengzhi. He captured Wei Bao and put Mi down. After that, Han Xin sent someone to see the King of Han and said: I hope to increase the number of 30,000 troops. I request to take advantage of the victory and march north to conquer the two countries Yan and Zhao, attack Qi to the east, cut off Chu's grain routes to the south, and finally go west to join forces with the king in Rongyang. The King of Han agreed to give Han Xin 30,000 more troops, and sent Tan Dan and Han Zhi to attack Zhao Er and Ji Er to the north. He defeated the attacking army and captured Xia Yue alive in the hammer. After Kongcao captured Chongxiao and Zhuyou, the King of Han sent people to call back his elite troops and marched to Rongyang to resist the Chu army. Han Xin and Zhang Er led tens of thousands of troops and wanted to march eastward to capture Jingxing and attack Zhao. King Chu and Chen Yu, Lord of Cheng'an, heard that the Han army was about to attack Zhao, so they gathered a heavy army to guard Jingxingkou, claiming to have an army of 200,000.
target: In the second year of Han, Liu Bang conquered Wei and Henan, then attacked Pengcheng but was defeated. Han Xin later joined forces to defeat Chu troops. After Wei Bao rebelled, Han Xin, as左丞相, attacked Wei. He feigned a river crossing at Linjin while secretly crossing at Xiayang, capturing Wei Bao. Han Xin then requested 30,000 troops to conquer Yan, Zhao, and Qi. Liu Bang agreed, sending Zhang Er and others. Han Xin defeated Zhao at Jingxing, using a背水阵 (back-to-water formation) to inspire his troops to fight desperately. He captured King Zhao Xie and killed Chen Yu. Han Xin spared Li Zuoche, who advised against attacking Yan and Qi directly, suggesting instead to intimidate Yan into surrender and then approach Qi. Han Xin followed this, and Yan surrendered.

source: After Wu She left, Kuai Tong knew that the key to the final outcome of the world lay in Han Xin, and further persuaded Han Xin with the view that three parts of the world would make him the king. His words are recorded in "The Biography of Kuai Tong". Han Xin couldn't bear to betray the King of Han, and he believed that he had made great contributions and the King of Han would not seize his Qi State, so he refused to listen to Kuai Tong. The King of Han was defeated in Guling and adopted Zhang Liang's strategy, recruiting Han Xin to lead his troops to join forces at the foot of the country. After Xiang Yu's death, Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty used a surprise attack to seize Han Xin's military power, changed the title of King Han Xin of Qi to King of Chu, and made Xiapi his capital. When Han Xin arrived in Chudu, he summoned the floating mother who had given him food in the past and gave her a thousand gold coins. He went to the head of the Xiangxiang Pavilion and presented him with a hundred coins and said: You are a villain, and the good deeds you do have a beginning and an end. He also summoned the young man who had insulted him by asking him to crawl under his crotch, and appointed him as the lieutenant of Chu State. Han Xin said to the generals: This is a strong man. Can't I kill him when he insults me? But there was no reason to kill him, so I endured it, and that's how we achieved today's achievements.
target: Han Xin was later made King of Qi. After Xiang Yu's death, Liu Bang demoted him to King of Chu. Han Xin rewarded the old woman who fed him and the young man who humiliated him, making him a lieutenant. When Liu Bang suspected him of rebellion, Han Xin was captured and made Marquis of Huaiyin.

source: In the tenth year of the Han Dynasty, Chen Xi rebelled. Emperor Gao personally led troops to attack him, but Han Xin pretended to be ill and did not follow him. Secretly sent someone to Chen Xi's residence. Han Xin planned with his retainers and pretended to pass Shao's order at night to pardon the criminals and slaves in various government offices and prepare to send troops to attack Empress Lu and the prince. The arrangements are in place, waiting for Chen Xi's report. One of his retainers offended Han Xin, and Han Xin imprisoned him and prepared to kill him. The retainer's brother wrote a letter to Empress Lu reporting Han Xin's preparations for rebellion. Empress Lu wanted to summon Han Xin, but she was afraid that he would not submit, so she discussed with Xiao Xiangguo and sent someone pretending to be from the emperor, saying that Chen Zhu was dead and all the ministers were going to congratulate him. Xiangguo deceived Han Xin and said: Although you are sick, you should go to the palace to congratulate him. As soon as Han Xin entered the palace, Empress Lu asked the warriors to tie Han Xin up and behead him in the clock room of Changle Palace. When Han Xin was beheaded, he said: I did not adopt Kuai Tong's strategy, but was deceived by a woman. Isn't this God's will? So the three tribes of Han and Xin were killed. Emperor Gaozu returned from suppressing Chen Xi's rebellion and arrived in the capital. When he heard that Han Xin was dead, he was happy and pitiful, and asked: What did Han Xin say before he died?
target: He feigned illness, avoiding court. Later, he plotted with Chen Xi to rebel but was betrayed. Empress Lü and Xiao He tricked him into the palace, where he was executed, his clan exterminated. Before death, he regretted not following Kuai Tong's advice.

source: So the three tribes of Han and Xin were killed. Emperor Gaozu returned from suppressing Chen Xi's rebellion and arrived in the capital. When he heard that Han Xin was dead, he was happy and pitiful, and asked: What did Han Xin say before he died? Empress Lu repeated what Han Xin said. Emperor Gaozu said: This person is Kuai Tong, the lobbyist of Qi State. Summon Kuai Tong to cook him to death. After Kuai Tong arrived, he explained himself and was pardoned without being killed. This incident is recorded in "The Biography of Kuai Tong". Peng Yue, courtesy name Zhong, was born in Changyi County. He often fished in Ju Ye Ze and later became a bandit.
target: Peng Yue, from Changyi, was a fisherman and bandit. He led a group of youths, enforcing strict discipline.

source: A young man in Huaiyin City bullied Han Xin and said: Although you are tall and like to wear swords, you are actually very timid. He insulted Han Xin in public and said: If you are not afraid of death, stab me with a sword; if you are afraid of death, get under my crotch. So Han Xin stared at the young man carefully, then bent down and crawled under his crotch. People watching the excitement on the street laughed at Han Xin and thought he was cowardly. When Xiang Liang led his army across the Huai River to the north, Han Xin took his sword and went to him, and became an unknown soldier under Xiang Liang. After Xiang Liang failed, he returned to Xiang Yu, who made him a doctor. Han Xin repeatedly offered advice to Xiang Yu, but Xiang Yu did not adopt it. Liu Bang, the king of Han, entered Hanzhong, and Han Xin escaped from the Chu army and joined the king of Han. At the beginning, he was still unknown and worked as a granary management clerk.
target: He joined Liu Bang but later served Xiang Yu. After Xiang Yu's defeat, Liu Bang made him King of Liang. Accused of rebellion, he was captured, exiled, and killed by Empress Lü, his clan destroyed.

source: I asked him to come with me. At this time, Empress Lu asked Peng Yue's retainers to report him for another rebellion. After the emperor was informed by Tingwei, Peng Yue and his clan were killed. Ting Bu, a native of Liu County, originally had a surname of Ying. When he was young, a guest told him that he could become king after being tortured. When he reached his prime, he broke the law and was punished by Tao Bu. Tao Bu smiled happily and said, "Someone told me that after being punished, I would become king. Isn't that what it is?" Everyone who heard this laughed at him. Tingbu was sent to Lishan for hard labor for committing a crime. There were hundreds of thousands of prisoners in Lishan. Tinghu had contacts with the leaders and heroes among the prisoners, and finally led this group of people to escape to the Yangtze River and became a group of bandits. When Chen Sheng raised his troops, Qing Bu went to meet Wu Rui, the magistrate of Fan County. At that time, Jing Bu had thousands of troops. The county magistrate married his daughter to him. Zhang Han destroyed Chen Sheng and defeated Lu Chen's army. Yingbu led his troops north to attack the troops of the left and right captains of the Qin army. He defeated them at Qingbo and led his troops to advance. Yingbu heard that Xiang Liang had pacified Kuaiji, so he crossed the Huai River to the west and surrendered his troops to Xiang Liang. Xiang Liang attacked Jingju, Qinjia and other places to the west, and Yingbu's army was always the bravest. After Xiang Liang knew for sure that Chen She was dead, he supported King Huai of Chu and named him Dangyang Lord with a tattoo. Xiang Liang was defeated and died in battle. King Huai of Chu, Ying Bu and other princes and generals gathered in Pengcheng. At this time, the Qin army stepped up the siege of Tangguo, and Tangguo sent people to request King Huai of Chu for rescue many times. King Chu Huai sent Song Yi as the general, and Xiang Yu and Ying Bu were subordinate to him to go north to rescue the country. Xiang Ji killed Song Yi on the bank of the Zhang River and established himself as general. He sent Yingbu to cross the Zhang River first and attack the Qin army, winning many times. Xiang Ji led all his troops across the river and followed Ying Bu, defeating the Qin army and forcing Zhang Han and others to surrender. The Chu army often won battles and made the greatest contributions among the princes. The reason why the armies of the princes all obeyed and subordinated to the Chu army was because Yingbu repeatedly defeated the larger number with a smaller number. Xiang Ji led his army westward to Xin'an, and sent Yingbu and others to attack and bury alive Zhang Han's Qin soldiers of more than 200,000 men at night. When they arrived at Hangu Pass, they were unable to enter, so they sent Ying Bu and others to raid from a small road and defeat the troops guarding the pass before they were able to enter. When he arrived in Xianyang, Yingbu served as the forward. King Xiang conferred titles on various generals, and made Yingbu the King of Jiujiang, making six counties his capital. King Xiang honored King Huai of Chu as the Righteous Emperor and moved the capital to Changsha, but secretly asked King Yingbu of Jiujiang to kill the Righteous Emperor. Yingbu sent generals to chase him to Chen County and kill him. King Tian Rong of Qi rebelled against Chu. King Xiang went to attack Qi and fine-tuned his army to Jiujiang. Wang Yingbu of Jiujiang excused himself from illness and sent his generals with thousands of people to go.
target: Ying Bu, from Liu County, was a convict who escaped to become a bandit. He joined Xiang Liang, then Xiang Yu, who made him King of Jiujiang. He killed the Righteous Emperor for Xiang Yu. Later, Sui He persuaded him to defect to Liu Bang. Ying Bu was made King of Huainan. After Han Xin and Peng Yue's deaths, he feared for his life and rebelled. He was defeated and killed by the emperor's forces.

source: Chang'an is the original Xianyang. After Xiang Ji died, Lu Wan was asked to lead another army and attack Linjiang King Gongwei together with Liu Mai. After returning, he followed Emperor Gaozu to attack Zang Tu, King of Yan, and defeated the enemy and pacified those places. At that time, there were seven princes who were not named Liu and were crowned kings. The emperor wanted to make Lu Wan king, but the officials were dissatisfied and complained. When Zang Tu was captured, he issued a letter from Shao and ordered the ministers and princes to choose the meritorious minister among the ministers to be crowned King of Yan. The officials knew that the emperor wanted to make Lu Wan a king, and they all said: Lu Wan, the Taiwei Marquis of Chang'an, who often followed the emperor to bring peace to the world, and who made the most contributions, can be made king. The emperor appointed Lu Wan as King of Yan. Among the princes and kings, no one was as favored as King Yan. Six years after Lu Wan was granted the title of King of Yan, Chen Xi collapsed due to suspicion of his rebellion.
target: Lu Wan, from Fengyi, was a childhood friend of Liu Bang. He became King of Yan. Suspected of colluding with Chen Xi and the Xiongnu, he fled to the Xiongnu after Liu Bang's death, dying there.

source: After the death of Emperor Gaozu, Lu Wan led his men to flee into the Huns, who made him King of East Hulu. Lu Wan was bullied and plundered by the barbarians, and often thought of returning to the Han Dynasty. More than a year later, he died in the Huns. When he was the empress, Lu Wan's wife and son escaped from the Xiongnu and surrendered to the Han Dynasty. When the empress became ill and could not be received, they were asked to live in Yan's mansion and planned to hold a banquet to invite them. Empress Gao eventually passed away, and Lu Wan's wife also died of illness. During the reign of Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty, Lu Wan's grandson Lu Taren surrendered to the Han Dynasty as King Shuhu and was granted the title of Marquis of Evil Valley. It was passed down to his great-grandson that the feudal state was abolished due to crime. Wu Rui was the magistrate of Fanyang County during the Qin Dynasty. He was very popular among the people in the Jianghu area and was known as Fanjun. The world began to rebel against the Qin Dynasty, Yingbu surrendered to Wu Rui, and Wu Rui married his daughter to him. So he led the Yue people to raise troops to respond to the anti-Qin struggles in various places. Peigong attacked Nanyang County and encountered Wu Rui's general Mei Guo, so he and he attacked Xi County and Li County of Nanyang County. Both counties surrendered. When Xiang Yu divided the princes among the princes, Wu Rui led the Baiyue soldiers to cooperate with the princes and followed them into Guanzhong, so he made Wu Rui the king of Hengshan and established Zhu as his capital. His general Mei Guo had many merits and was granted the title of lord of 100,000 households. After Xiang Yu's death, the emperor followed him into Wuguan because of his merits in the plum pot. So he was grateful to Wu Rui and changed his title to King of Changsha. He established his capital in Linxiang. He died a year later and was named King Wen. Zicheng Wang Wuchen succeeded to the throne.
target: Wu Rui, a Qin magistrate, led Yue troops to support Liu Bang. Xiang Yu made him King of Hengshan, later Liu Bang made him King of Changsha. He died a year later, his kingdom passed down five generations before ending without an heir. The historian comments that among the eight non-Liu kings, only Wu Rui remained loyal, his kingdom lasting longest due to his virtue.

source: Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty had eight sons: Empress Lu begat Emperor Xiaohui, Lady Cao was the father of King Qiyouhui Liu Fei, Bo Ji was the father of Emperor Xiaowen, Lady Qi was the father of Zhaowu King Liu Ruyi, Gui Xun was the father of Huainan King Li Xingzhou, and other concubines were the children of Zhao Youwang Suqu, Zhao Gongwang Liu Yue, and Jixi King Liu Jian. Huainan Li Wang Xingzhou has his own biography. The mother of Liu Fei, King Hui of Qi, was Gaozu's mistress when he was a commoner. In the sixth year of Emperor Gaozu's reign, Liu Fei was made king, and he had more than seventy cities under his control. All the common people who could speak the language of Qi were given to the State of Qi. In the second year of Emperor Hui of the Han Dynasty, King Qi went to the capital to meet Emperor Hui. Emperor Hui held a banquet in front of Empress Dowager Lu to entertain King Qi. According to family etiquette, Emperor Hui invited his eldest brother, King Qi, to sit at the head of the table. Empress Dowager Lu was so furious that she had two glasses of poisoned wine poured in front of her, and asked King Qi to offer wine to celebrate his birthday. King Qi stood up, and Emperor Hui also stood up, wanting to celebrate his birthday with wine. The Queen Mother was frightened, so she stood up and knocked over the wine glass. King Qi felt strange and did not dare to drink anymore. He pretended to be drunk and left. Later, I found out that the wine wrapped in wine was poisonous. I was very worried and thought that I would not be able to leave Chang'an and return home. The historian said: The Queen Mother only gave birth to Emperor Hui and Princess Lu Yuan. Now there are more than seventy cities in your country, but the princess's food town is only a few cities. You might as well dedicate a county to the Queen Mother and use it as a place to increase the princess's food and fiefdom. In this way, the Queen Mother will definitely be happy, and the King will be free from disaster. Therefore, the King of Qi dedicated Chengyang County and honored Princess Lu Yuan as the Queen Mother. Queen Mother Lu happily agreed. So they held a banquet at Qi's residence in the capital, drank and had fun together, and sent King Qi back to his country. Thirteen years later, King Liu Fei of Qi died, and his eldest son Liu Xiang succeeded to the throne. Liu Ruyi, King of Zhao Yin, was established as King of Zhao in the ninth year of Emperor Gaozu's reign. Four years later, Gaozu died, and Empress Dowager Lu summoned King Zhao Ruyi to Chang'an to kill him. He had no sons and his country was extinct. Liu You, King of Zhao You, was established as King of Huaiyang in the eleventh year of Emperor Gaozu's reign. In the year when Zhao Yin King Liu Ruyi died, which was the first year of Emperor Hui of the Han Dynasty, he was granted the title of King of Zhao and reigned for fourteen years.
target: Emperor Gaozu of Han had eight sons from various consorts. Empress Lu bore Emperor Xiaohui; Lady Cao bore Liu Fei, King of Qi; Bo Ji bore Emperor Xiaowen; Lady Qi bore Liu Ruyi, King of Zhao; and other concubines bore Liu You, Liu Yue, and Liu Jian. Liu Fei, King Hui of Qi, was granted over seventy cities in the sixth year of Gaozu's reign. During Emperor Hui's reign, King Qi visited the capital. Emperor Hui honored him as eldest brother at a banquet, angering Empress Dowager Lu, who attempted to poison King Qi. After discovering the plot, King Qi dedicated Chengyang County to increase Princess Lu Yuan's fiefdom, appeasing the Empress Dowager and securing his safe return. Liu Fei died thirteen years later, succeeded by his son Liu Xiang.

source: If you are a king and starve to death, who will take pity on you? Mr. Lu violated the laws of nature. I could only ask heaven for revenge, so I died in confinement. The imperial court buried him in Chang'an with the courtesy of a commoner. After the death of Empress Dowager Lu, Emperor Wen of Han ascended the throne and established Liu Sui, the son of King You, as King of Zhao. The following year, the officials in charge asked the prince to be crowned king. Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty said: King Zhao You died in confinement. I pity him very much. His eldest son Liu Sui has been established as King of Zhao. Liu Sui's younger brother Liu Piqiang, Prince Zhu Xuhou Liu Zhang, son of King Qi Yaohui, and Shu Mouhou Liu Xingju all have meritorious services and can be established as kings. Therefore, Hejian County was taken from Zhao State and Liu Piqiang was established as King Wen of Hejian. Thirteen years later, Liu Piqiang died and his son Liu Fu, King Ai, succeeded him. Liu Fu died after one year as king. He had no sons and the feudal state was abolished. King Zhao Liu Sui was king for twenty-six years. When Emperor Mo Jing came to the throne, Chao Cuo thought that King Zhao was at fault and cut off the Changshan County of Zhao State. The princes were dissatisfied and Wu, Chu and other countries rebelled. Liu Sui also participated in the conspiracy and raised troops to attack the Han Dynasty. Zhao's Prime Minister Jiande and Internal History Wang Han advised him, but Liu Sui not only refused to listen, but also burned Jiande and Wang Han to death. He sent troops to garrison the western border of Zhao, hoping to wait for the troops of Wu and Chu to join up and then move westward. He also sent people north to contact the Xiongnu. The Han Dynasty sent Quzhou Hou Liji to attack Zhao. The King of Zhao garrisoned Handan and resisted the Han soldiers for seven months. Wu and Chu were defeated. When the Xiongnu heard about it, they refused to send troops to help. Shi! After defeating Manzhi, Xi led his troops back, joined forces with Li Zhou and others to attack Zhao, and diverted water to fill the city. After the city was broken, the Zhao royal family committed suicide in a tunnel and Zhao Li was deposed. Lian Kentong felt sorry for Zhao Moxiang and Nei Shi who died for insisting on respecting the imperial court, and named their sons as marquises. Liu Hui, the king of the Communist Party of Zhao. In the eleventh year of Emperor Gaozu's reign, after he executed Peng Yue, the king of Liang, he established Liu Hui as king of Liang. In the 16th year, Empress Dowager Lu killed King You of Zhao and moved Liu Hui to King Zhao. Liu Hui was unhappy. Empress Dowager Lu married Lu Chan's daughter to King Zhao and became the queen. The queen's attendants were all members of the Lu family. They monopolized power in the palace and secretly observed King Zhao. King Zhao could not do whatever he wanted. King Zhao had a beloved concubine who was poisoned to death by the queen with wine. King Zhao composed a song in four chapters and ordered the musicians to sing. King Zhao was overly sad and committed suicide six months later. After Empress Dowager Lu heard about it, she thought it was a woman who committed suicide instead of offering sacrifices to the ancestral temple, so she deposed her country and cut off her inheritance of the throne. Liu Jian, King of Yanling. In the eleventh year of Mo Gaozu's reign, King Lu Wan of Yan defected to the Huns. The following year, Liu Jian was granted the title of King of Yan. In the fifteenth year, Liu Jian died, and his son by a beautiful woman was killed by Dan Liqiu's men. The heirs were extinct and the country was abolished.
target: Liu Ruyi, King of Zhao, was killed by Empress Dowager Lu after Gaozu's death, leaving no heirs. Liu You became King of Zhao but was imprisoned and starved to death after his Lu-family queen falsely accused him of plotting rebellion. After Empress Dowager Lu's death, Emperor Wen established Liu Sui as King of Zhao. Liu Sui later joined the Wu-Chu rebellion, was besieged for seven months, and committed suicide after the city fell. Liu Hui was moved to Zhao against his wishes. His Lu-family queen poisoned his beloved concubine, causing him to compose a sorrowful song and commit suicide. Liu Jian, King of Yan, died, and his son was killed, extinguishing his line.

source: Liu Hui, the king of the Communist Party of Zhao. In the eleventh year of Emperor Gaozu's reign, after he executed Peng Yue, the king of Liang, he established Liu Hui as king of Liang. In the 16th year, Empress Dowager Lu killed King You of Zhao and moved Liu Hui to King Zhao. Liu Hui was unhappy. Empress Dowager Lu married Lu Chan's daughter to King Zhao and became the queen. The queen's attendants were all members of the Lu family. They monopolized power in the palace and secretly observed King Zhao. King Zhao could not do whatever he wanted. King Zhao had a beloved concubine who was poisoned to death by the queen with wine. King Zhao composed a song in four chapters and ordered the musicians to sing. King Zhao was overly sad and committed suicide six months later. After Empress Dowager Lu heard about it, she thought it was a woman who committed suicide instead of offering sacrifices to the ancestral temple, so she deposed her country and cut off her inheritance of the throne. Liu Jian, King of Yanling. In the eleventh year of Mo Gaozu's reign, King Lu Wan of Yan defected to the Huns. The following year, Liu Jian was granted the title of King of Yan. In the fifteenth year, Liu Jian died, and his son by a beautiful woman was killed by Dan Liqiu's men. The heirs were extinct and the country was abolished. Nine of the sons of King Hui of Qi Yao were established as kings: the prince Shengjin was the king of Qisei, the second son Xingtong was the king of Chengyangjing, Liu Xingri was the king of Ji Dongdou, Liu Laoyi was the king of Bian, Yan Jin was the king of Zhamu, Su Biguang was the king of Zamu, Xingtong was the king of Lancong, Xingsheng was the king of Zhuiyou, and Liu Xiongji was the king of bran. Liu Xiang, King Ai of Qi, succeeded to the throne in the sixth year of Emperor Hui of the Han Dynasty. The following year, Emperor Hui died, and Empress Dowager Lu came to rule. In the first year of Gaohou's reign, Lu Tai, the son of Queen Lu's brother, was granted the title of King of Lu, and the Jinan County of Naoqi was divided into his own state. The next year, Liu Zhang, the younger brother of King Ai, was summoned to the capital to guard the Han court. He was named Zhu Xuhou and married to him Lu Lu's daughter. Four years later, Liu Zhang's younger brother Liu Xingju was granted the title of Marquis of Cambodia, and both of them guarded the Han court in Chang'an. In the seventh year of Emperor Gao's reign, the Langye County of Qi was divided, and Liu Ze, the Marquis of Yingling, was granted the title of King of Langye. In the same year, King Zhao Liu You was imprisoned and died in the royal residence in the capital. Since the three kings of Zhao were deposed, Empress Gao selected three from the Lu family as kings and took over the power to handle affairs. Liu Zhang was twenty years old at the time and was very powerful. He was dissatisfied that Liu could not get his authority. He once went to the palace to serve the Empress Dowager Lu at a banquet, and the Empress Dowager Lu ordered Liu Zhang to be the drinking officer. Liu Zhang demanded: "I am a descendant of a military general. Please follow military laws and enforce the drinking order."
target: King Qi Yao's nine sons were established as kings. During Empress Dowager Lu's regency, Lu-family members were granted kingdoms from Qi's territory. Liu Zhang, a grandson of King Qi, served at court and openly defied the Lu family during a banquet, killing a drunken Lu relative under military drinking rules. After Empress Dowager Lu's death, the Lu family plotted rebellion. Liu Zhang secretly informed his brother King Qi, who raised troops. The Han generals killed the Lu family, and the ministers chose to make King Dai (Emperor Wen) emperor instead of King Qi, fearing the Qi queen's mother's family was too powerful.

source: His son Liu Yun succeeded to the throne as King Ai. Liu Yun died after one year on the throne. He had no sons. The country was exterminated and the territory was transferred to the Han Dynasty. During the reign of Emperor Cheng of the Han Dynasty, Liu Yun's brother Liu Li was made King of Chengyang. During the reign of Wang Mang, the feudal state was abolished. Liu Xingju, the king of Jibei, initially welcomed Emperor Wen to the official residence of Daiguo together with the ministers as Shu Mouhou. He said: "I have no merit in killing the Lu family. I request that I go to clean up the palace with my servant Teng Gong Xia Houying." So he brought out the young emperor appointed by the Lu family and welcomed Emperor Wen of Han into the palace to rule. At the beginning of the crusade against the Lu family, Zhu Xuhou and Liu Zhang made the greatest contribution. The ministers discussed and agreed to make Liu Zhang the king of all the territories of the Zhao State, and to make Liu Xingju the king of all the territories of the Liang State. After Emperor Wen ascended the throne, I heard that Song Xuhou and Dongmuhou had wanted to make King Qi emperor, so they deposed him and reduced the credit of the Lu family. In the second year, Emperor Wen made the princes kings, and then divided the two counties of Qi and made Liu Zhang and Liu Xingju the princes and kings. Liu Zhang and Xingju believed that they had lost their merit because of their dereliction of duty. More than a year later, Liu Zhang died. At that time, the Xiongnu invaded the border in large numbers, and the Han Dynasty sent a large number of troops. Prime Minister Guan Ying led the attack, and Emperor Wen personally went to Taiyuan to supervise the battle. Liu Xingju believed that the emperor wanted to personally attack the Xiongnu, so he launched an army to rebel. When Emperor Wen heard about it, he stopped his troops and returned to Chang'an. He sent General Chai Wu, the Marquis of Jipu, to defeat the rebels and capture the King of Jibei. The king of Jibei committed suicide and the country was abolished. Emperor Wen took pity on the King of Jibei for rebelling and destroying himself. In the second year, he made Liu Bojun, the seven sons of King Hui of Qi, and others into princes. In the fifteenth year of Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty, King Wen of Qi Liu Ze died without a son. But at that time, the descendants of King Qi Huihui still had King Chengyang. Emperor Wen pitied King Qi Hui because he had no legitimate son to succeed him, so he divided the Qi country into six, and the six sons of King Hui who were previously named princes were still alive. Established as kings: Yang Xuhou Liu Jianglu is the King of Qi Xiao, Anduhou Liu Zhi is the King of Jibei, Wuchenghou Liu Xian is the Miao King, Baishihou Liu Xiongqu is the Micellar King, Pingchang Hou Liu Yin is the Jiaoxi King, and Jiehou Liu Biguang is the Jinan King. In the sixteenth year of Emperor Wen's reign, six kings were made kings on the same day. In the eleventh year of the reign of the above-mentioned six kings, that is, the third year of Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty, Wu and Chu rebelled. The four kings of Miaojie, Jiaoxi, Lei!, and Jinan all responded by sending troops to fight against the Han. They wanted to invite King Qi to fight against the Han, but King Xiao of Qi was hesitant, so he held on to the city and refused to rebel.
target: Emperor Wen restored Qi's lost territories and granted titles to Liu Zhang and Liu Xingju. Liu Xingju later rebelled and committed suicide. Emperor Wen divided Qi into six kingdoms for King Qi Hui's sons. During Emperor Jing's reign, four of these kings joined the Wu-Chu rebellion. King Xiao of Qi initially hesitated, was besieged, but held out until Han forces arrived.

source: Later, when I heard that the King of Qi had conspired with the Three Kingdoms, he wanted to send troops to attack Qi. King Xiao of Qi became frightened and committed suicide by drinking poison. The four kings of Jiaodong, Jiaoxi, Jinan, and Miaochuan were all beheaded. Their feudal state was also abolished, leaving only the King of Jibei. When Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty heard the news of King Qi Xiao's suicide, he believed that King Qi had no intention of rebellion at first and had other plans because of coercion. This was not his crime. Emperor Jing went down to Shao and established Liu Shou, the crown prince of Prince Xiao, as King Qi Yi. King Yi died in the 23rd year of his reign, and his son King Li Liu Ciyuan succeeded him. King Qi Li's mother was Queen Mother Ji. The Queen Mother made her brother's daughter his queen, but King Qi did not love Queen Ji. The Empress Dowager Ji wanted to pamper the Ji family for generations, so she ordered her eldest daughter Ji Wengzhu to enter the palace, control the harem, and prevent the concubines in the harem from getting close to the King of Qi. She wanted the King of Qi to love Queen Ji exclusively. The king of Qi therefore committed adultery with his sister. There was a eunuch named Xu Jia in the state of Qi who entered the palace to serve the empress dowager of the Han Dynasty. The Queen Mother has a beloved daughter named Xiuchengjun. She is not born to the Liu family, and the Queen Mother loves her very much. Xiu Chengjun has a daughter named Mo, and the Queen Mother wants her to marry the princes. Xu Jia then requested to be sent as an envoy to the state of Qi, saying that he would definitely ask the king of Qi to write a letter requesting to marry E.
target: After learning the king had negotiated with rebels, he committed suicide. Emperor Jing pardoned him posthumously. Later, King Qi Li committed adultery with his sister. When Emperor Wu sent an investigator, the king committed suicide, leaving no heirs, and Qi was abolished. The remaining Qi territories eventually passed to the Han dynasty.

source: In the fifth year of Emperor Mo Xuan's reign, the governor of Qingzhou reported to Emperor Xuan that Liu Zhonggu had his Ai slaves commit adultery with his concubines and many of the maids who served him. He either slept with them or made them naked during the day, like animals having sex, and Zhonggu watched in person. When a child is born, he says: If he is in chaos and does not know his father, he will kill the child. Emperor Xuan handed the matter over to the prime minister and the imperial censor for discussion. The prime minister and the imperial censor reported that he was the king of the vassals in ancient times, and asked him to set up a concubine with the title of eight sons, with a salary rank of 600 dan, in order to allow him to have more children to respect his ancestors. However, Zhonggu behaves like an animal, messing up the relationship between monarch, ministers, and husband and wife, and violating human ethics. Please arrest him. The emperor then issued a letter to Shao and cut off the four counties under his jurisdiction. Died twenty-eight years later. His son Liu Shang, king of Kao, succeeded to the throne and died five years ago. His son, Xiao Wang Liu Heng, succeeded to the throne and died in thirty-one years. His son Liu Jiao, King Huai, succeeded to the throne and died in six years. His son Liu Yong succeeded to the throne, and by the time of Wang Mang, the feudal state was extinct. Zan said: The state of Qi under King Hui of Qi is the largest among the vassal states. source: Qi and Tang each sent fifty military chariots to help support Zhou Shi as king. Zhou Shi refused to accept it and sent people to Chen County to meet Wei Jiu. target: The histories of three prominent figures from the Six Kingdoms period: Wei Bao, Tian Dan, and Han Wangxin, detailing their rise, fall, and the fates of their descendants. Wei Bao, son of the Wei state, saw his brother Wei Jiu made king by Chen Sheng after the Qin collapse. Wei Jiu later surrendered to Qin to save his people and committed suicide. target: Zheng Dangshi proposed a canal from Chang'an to divert the Wei River, reducing transport time and irrigating farmland. Ancient people said: If a man does not cultivate, some will suffer from hunger; if a woman does not weave, some will suffer from cold. If there are seasons for producing materials, but there is no restraint in using them, then the materials will definitely be exhausted. In ancient times, the world was governed in a very detailed and comprehensive manner, so their savings were enough to rest assured. Nowadays, we are abandoning the roots and tending to the ends. There are many people who live on leisure, which is the greatest harm in the world. Excessive and extravagant customs are increasing day by day. This is the greatest harm in the world. Cruel and violent acts are carried out openly, and no one comes to stop them; the fate of the country is about to be overturned, and no one comes to save it. With fewer people producing and more people squandering, how can the world's wealth not be exhausted? The Han Dynasty has been established for nearly forty years, and the public and private accumulations are particularly worth mourning. If it doesn't rain when it's supposed to rain, the people will be afraid; if the age is bad and there is no income, then the official position and children will be sold. After hearing this, how can the emperor not be shocked when he faces such dangers in governing the world? There are years of famine in the world. This is God's arrangement. Dayu and Shang Tang have already suffered it.
target: After the Han Dynasty, the Qin's shortcomings continued. Princes revolted, people lost jobs, and famine struck, with grain costing 5,000 yuan per stone and cannibalism. Emperor Gaozu ordered people to sell children and move to Shu and Han. After peace, the emperor restricted frugality, reduced land rents to one-fifteenth, and taxed based on official salaries. Emperor Wen practiced frugality and encouraged agriculture. Jia Yi advised that production must exceed consumption, warning of poverty and unrest. He urged returning people to agriculture to build savings. Emperor Wen was moved and began farming himself. Chao Cuo further advised that wise kings ensure people have savings, citing Yao, Yu, and Tang's success. He noted that poverty leads to evil, and farmers work hard but suffer from taxes and merchants' exploitation. He proposed valuing grain over gold and jade, and using grain for rewards and punishments. Emperor Wen allowed people to send grain to the border for titles, reducing taxes. Over 70 years, the country prospered, with full granaries and surplus property. However, wealth led to pride and land annexation. Dong Zhongshu advised planting more wheat and reforming taxes and labor, but after his death, prices rose and cannibalism returned.

source: Some people cultivate the fields of wealthy people and pay five-tenths of the tax. Therefore, poor people often wear the clothes of cows and horses and eat the food of pigs and dogs. Coupled with the greedy and tyrannical officials who arbitrarily increased the punishment, the people were worried that they had no sustenance, so they fled to the mountains and forests and turned into thieves. Prisoners filled half of the roads, and the number of trial cases counted in the tens of millions a year. After the establishment of the Han Dynasty, the rules were not changed. Although the ancient well-field system is difficult to implement suddenly, it should be as close as possible to the ancient system, restricting people from owning land in private names, using it to supplement deficiencies and block the road to annexation. Let the profits from salt and iron return to the hands of the people. Free the slaves and abolish the authority to kill without permission. Reduce taxes and reduce corvee labor to ease the burden on the people. It can then be governed well. After Dong Zhongshu's death, things became more expensive, the world was depleted and empty, and people began to eat each other again. In the last years of Emperor Wu's reign, he felt regretful about his conquests, so he made Cheng Fu the Marquis of the Rich People. The order states: The most important thing now is to devote ourselves to agriculture. Ren Tangguo was appointed Captain of Sosu. Zhao Guo knew how to cultivate the fields, and he had three furrows per acre of land. Changing the position of the furrow every year, so it is called Daitian, is an ancient method. During the Hou Ji period, furrows were dug in the fields, and two people plowed them side by side, one foot wide and one foot deep, called a ridge, extending to the end of the acre.
target: Emperor Wu regretted his conquests and appointed Cheng Fu to promote agriculture. Zhao Guo introduced the Daitian method, with three furrows per acre, changing positions yearly. This method, using convenient tools, increased yields. Zhao Guo taught it widely, and it proved efficient. By Emperor Zhao's time, exiles returned, fields expanded, and savings grew.

source: He taught the family fields and the three auxiliary public fields, and also taught the border counties and Juyan City. After that, the people in the border cities, Hedong, Hongnong, Sanfu, and Taichang all thought that Daitian was convenient and they could get more grain with less effort. By the time of Emperor Zhao, the exiled people gradually returned to their hometowns. The opening of fields has increased, and there is a lot of savings. After Emperor Xuan came to the throne, most of the officials appointed were virtuous people. The people were content with their own country, and their annual income was abundant. The price of grain reached five yuan per stone, and farmers had little benefit. At that time, Geng Shouchang, the great minister of agriculture, was good at calculation and measurement, and could calculate the labor required for the project. He was favored by the emperor. During the Five Feng period, he reported: According to the old practice, four million dendrobium grains from Guandong were transported by water every year to supply the capital, and 60,000 soldiers were employed. The grains in Sanfu, Hongnong, Hedong, Shangdang and Taiyuan counties should be purchased to be enough to supply the capital, which can save more than half of the soldiers needed for water transportation in Guandong. He also asked for instructions to increase the sea rent three times, and the emperor followed his advice. Xiao Wang, the imperial censor, said: "It turns out that the Xu Gong family of the imperial censor's subordinates lives in Shulai. He said that the sea rent was increased in previous years and the fish would not come out." The elders all said that during the reign of Emperor Wu, the county magistrate personally fished, but no fish came out of the sea. Later, they returned it to the people, and the fish came out. Yin and Yang interact with each other, and things of the same kind correspond to each other. This is the case for all things. Now Geng Shouchang plans to purchase grain from the nearby water transport pass, build warehouses and ships, which will cost more than 200 million yuan. It involves the working people, fearing that a drought will occur and the people will suffer from it.
target: Emperor Xuan appointed virtuous officials, and grain prices fell to five yuan per stone. Geng Shouchang proposed purchasing grain from nearby counties to save on transport costs, building Changping warehouses to stabilize prices.

source: In the second year of Emperor Yuan's reign, there was a famine in Qi. A grain of rice cost more than 300 yuan per stone. Many people starved to death. People in Langxie County were cannibals. Most of the Confucian scholars in official positions said that Yantie Palace, Beijia Tianguan and Changpingcang could be dismissed, and they should not compete for interests with the people. The emperor listened to their opinions and dismissed Yantieguan, Beijiatianguan and Changpingcang. He also dismissed the palace guards of Jianzhang and Ganquan, Jiaodui, Qi San served as officials, reduced the number of forbidden gardens to provide for the poor, and reduced the number of guards in the princes' temples by half. He also reduced the number of soldiers in Guanzhong by 500 and transferred grain to help the poor. After that, due to insufficient funds, only Yantieguan was restored. When he became emperor, there was no war in the world and it could be said to be peaceful. However, the people's customs were extravagant and they did not consider saving and hoarding. In the second year of Yongshi, Liang State and Pingyuan County suffered from floods for consecutive years, and cannibalism occurred. The governor and county governor were dismissed from office for crimes. Emperor Ai ascended the throne, and Shi Dan assisted in political affairs. He suggested: In ancient times, wise kings always established well fields and then managed them to achieve peace. Emperor Xiaowen inherited the emptiness of the world after the collapse of the Zhou Dynasty and the violent wars of the Qin Dynasty, so he devoted himself to encouraging the people to engage in farming and mulberry farming, and set an example for the world with frugality. The people had just begun to enrich themselves, and there was no danger of annexation, so there were no restrictions on people's land and slaves. Nowadays, generations of peace have passed down, and the wealthy and officials have a lot of property, but the poor and weak are even poorer. When a gentleman engages in politics, it is valuable to keep the old laws without changing them, so it is difficult to make changes and innovations. However, the reason why there are reforms is because they are used to save emergencies. However, it is not a complete change and should be roughly restricted. The emperor conveyed his suggestions to his ministers. Prime Minister Kong Guang and Grand Sikong Hewu submitted a petition requesting that all princes, kings and princes receive privately owned land in the country. The land held by the princes in Chang'an, the princess in each county, and the land held by the princes and officials in Guannei in their private names should not exceed thirty hectares. The number of slaves for the princes and kings is two hundred, the number of slaves for the princes and princesses is one hundred, and the number of slaves for the princes and officials in Guan Nei is thirty. There is a three-year period, and any violation will be confiscated to the government. At that time, the price of slaves in the fields and houses was reduced, Ding and Fu were in power, and Dong Xian was high-ranking, which was not good for them. The emperor's order was postponed for the time being, but later it was stopped and not implemented. There are already many collections in the palaces, gardens, and treasury. Although the wealth of the people is not as good as that of Emperor Wen and Emperor Jing, the population is the largest in the world. After the death of Emperor Ping, Wang Mang became regent and he usurped the throne.
target: Emperor Yuan faced floods and famine, with cannibalism in Langxie. Confucian officials advised dismissing salt, iron, and Changping offices, which the emperor did, but later restored salt and iron due to insufficient funds. Emperor Cheng's reign was peaceful but extravagant, with floods causing cannibalism. Emperor Ai considered land and slave restrictions, but they were not implemented. Wang Mang usurped the throne, despised Han systems, and provoked the Xiongnu, leading to war. He renamed land and slaves, prohibited sales, and imposed harsh punishments, causing chaos. Droughts and famines led to cannibalism, with grain prices soaring. Wang Mang opened granaries but officials stole supplies, and many died. He lamented his rule until his death.

source: As for the uses of property, money, cloth and silk, their details are not recorded before the Xia and Yin Dynasties. Jiang Taigong established the method of currency circulation in the nine prefectures for the Zhou Dynasty: gold is one inch square and weighs one catty; coins are round and have square holes, and baht is used as the weight; cloth is two feet and two inches wide and is one piece, and four feet long is one piece. Therefore, currency is more precious than gold, sharper than a knife, smoother than spring water, more dispersed than cloth, and more able to gather than silk. After Jiang Taigong retreated to the feudal country, he implemented it in Qi. When Guan Zhong assisted Duke Huan of Qi, he established the standard of measuring weight. He said: There are years of famine and years of harvest, so grains are expensive and cheap; orders are slow and urgent, so goods are light and heavy. If the emperor does not govern, then the hoarding merchants will roam the market, and when the people cannot support themselves, they will raise the price to a hundred times the cost. Therefore, a country with ten thousand cars must have merchants worth ten thousand gold to buy them, and a country with a thousand cars must have merchants worth ten thousand gold. This is because the profits are hidden. If we consume what we produce, we will be able to meet our own expenses. However, if there are hungry people among the people, that is why the grain is hidden. When the people have plenty, they despise grain, so the monarch levies a low price; when the people have a shortage, they value grain, so the monarch distributes it at a high price. All low prices, high prices, collections, and distributions are all done at a certain time. Then supply and demand are adjusted, and prices will be stable. Adhere to the measures of regulating supply and demand and stabilizing prices, so that a town with a population of ten thousand households must have a collection of ten thousand bells, and a string of money tied with millions of strings; a town with a population of only ten thousand households must have a collection of thousands of bells, and a string of money tied with millions of strings. Farming is carried out in the spring, weeding is carried out in the summer, and the equipment and seeds must be abundant. Therefore, big merchants and hoarding merchants cannot use their power to rob the people. Duke Huan of Qi used the small state of Qi to unite the princes and promote his reputation as an overlord. More than a hundred years later, when King Jing of Zhou Dynasty came to the throne, he was worried that the money was too light and planned to cast large coins instead. Duke Shan Mu said: "This won't work." In ancient times, when disasters came from heaven, it was necessary to weigh property and currency to save the people.
target: The uses of property, money, cloth, and silk were not recorded before the Xia and Yin dynasties. Jiang Taigong established currency circulation for the Zhou Dynasty: gold was one inch square and weighed one catty; coins were round with square holes, using baht as weight; cloth was two feet two inches wide and four feet long per piece. Currency was considered more precious than gold, sharper than a knife, smoother than spring water, more dispersed than cloth, and more able to gather than silk. After Jiang Taigong retreated to Qi, he implemented this system. Guan Zhong assisted Duke Huan of Qi by establishing standards for measuring weight, noting that grain prices fluctuated with harvests and that goods varied in value based on demand. He warned that without governance, hoarding merchants would exploit the people, raising prices a hundredfold. A country with ten thousand cars needed merchants worth ten thousand gold to buy them, as profits were hidden. By consuming what was produced, expenses could be met, but hunger arose when grain was hoarded. The monarch should levy low prices when grain was abundant and distribute at high prices when scarce, adjusting supply and demand to stabilize prices. A town of ten thousand households should have a collection of ten thousand bells and millions of strings of money. Farming required abundant equipment and seeds in spring and summer, preventing big merchants from robbing the people. Duke Huan used Qi to unite the princes and become an overlord.

source: All low prices, high prices, collections, and distributions are all done at a certain time. Then supply and demand are adjusted, and prices will be stable. Adhere to the measures of regulating supply and demand and stabilizing prices, so that a town with a population of ten thousand households must have a collection of ten thousand bells, and a string of money tied with millions of strings; a town with a population of only ten thousand households must have a collection of thousands of bells, and a string of money tied with millions of strings. Farming is carried out in the spring, weeding is carried out in the summer, and the equipment and seeds must be abundant. Therefore, big merchants and hoarding merchants cannot use their power to rob the people. Duke Huan of Qi used the small state of Qi to unite the princes and promote his reputation as an overlord. More than a hundred years later, when King Jing of Zhou Dynasty came to the throne, he was worried that the money was too light and planned to cast large coins instead. Duke Shan Mu said: "This won't work." In ancient times, when disasters came from heaven, it was necessary to weigh property and currency to save the people. The people think that money is light, so we create heavy money for them to use. In this way, big money and small money go hand in hand with heavy money being the main one, and the people can get convenience. If heavy money cannot be used, make more light money for use, and do not abolish heavy money. Therefore, if the heavy money is insufficient, use light money to make up for it. Money and small money are mostly beneficial. Now that the king has abolished light money and created heavy money, the people have lost their wealth. How can they not be in want? If the people are in shortage, the king will have difficulty in spending money; if there is difficulty, he must collect more from the people; if the people cannot provide, they will flee. This is a way to separate the people. Moreover, exhausting the people's wealth to enrich the palace is like blocking the water source to stop the flow of water. It will not take a few days for the water to dry up. Please make your decision, Your Majesty. King Jing did not listen to his words, and finally made a large coin with "actual goods" engraved on it. The round edges and holes of the money had outlines, which were used to encourage farmers to make up for the shortage, and the people benefited. When the Qin State annexed the world, its currency was divided into two classes: gold was measured in yi, which was the first-class currency; copper coins were shaped like the money of the Zhou Dynasty, with the inscription "ban liang" on the front and a weight of half a liang. Pearls, jade, turtles, shells, silver and tin are used as decorations and treasures, not as currency, but they change at any time, and their weight has no rules. After the rise of the Han Dynasty, they thought that the Qin Dynasty coins were heavy and difficult to use, so they ordered the people to mint pod coins instead. The unit of gold returned to the weekly system of kilograms. Those who did not abide by the law and pursued profits used their own surplus to accumulate goods, so that the goods on the market accumulated in their own hands, causing prices to skyrocket. The price of rice reached ten thousand gold per stone, and a horse was worth one hundred gold. After the world was peaceful, Emperor Gaozu ordered merchants not to wear silk and ride in carriages, and increased taxes to frustrate them. During the reign of Emperor Xiaohui and Queen Gao, considering that the world had just stabilized, the laws on merchants were relaxed again, but the descendants of people in the market could not become officials. In the fifth year of Emperor Xiaowen's reign, because the money was more abundant and lighter, four baht coins were minted, with the characters "banliang" on the front. Abolish the law on stealing money and let the people mint it at will. Jia Yi remonstrated and said: The law allows the world to openly hire people to make coins with copper and tin. Anyone who dares to mix lead and iron to commit adultery will be punished by tattooing. But the situation with coining money is that if there is no doping, there will be no benefits; and the more subtle the doping, the more generous the benefits will be. Things can bring disaster, and laws can cause evil. Now the common people can mint money, and they mint it in hiding, intending to prevent their huge profits and cunning. Even if they are sentenced to tattoos every day, this situation cannot stop. Recently, the people have paid their share of the crime, with as many as a hundred people in one county. As for the officials who suspected it, many people were whipped and tortured and fled.
target: More than a hundred years later, King Jing of Zhou worried that money was too light and planned to cast large coins. Duke Shan Mu advised against it, arguing that when disasters came, property and currency should be weighed to save the people. If money was light, heavy money should be created for use, with both types circulating together. Abolishing light money for heavy money would cause the people to lose wealth, leading to shortages and flight. King Jing ignored this and made large coins with "actual goods" engraved, which benefited the people. When Qin annexed the world, currency was divided into two classes: gold measured in yi, and copper coins shaped like Zhou money with "ban liang" inscribed, weighing half a liang. Pearls, jade, turtles, shells, silver, and tin were decorations, not currency, and changed value arbitrarily. After the Han rose, they found Qin coins heavy and ordered pod coins instead, with gold returning to the weekly system of kilograms. Those who pursued profits hoarded goods, causing prices to skyrocket—rice reached ten thousand gold per stone, and a horse was worth one hundred gold. Emperor Gaozu ordered merchants not to wear silk or ride carriages and increased taxes to frustrate them. During Emperor Xiaohui and Queen Gao's reign, laws on merchants were relaxed, but their descendants could not become officials. In the fifth year of Emperor Xiaowen's reign, four baht coins were minted with "banliang" on the front, and the law on stealing money was abolished, allowing people to mint coins freely. Jia Yi remonstrated, arguing that coining money with copper and tin led to doping for profit, and even daily tattooing could not stop it. He noted that coins varied by county—some light, some heavy—causing confusion.

source: There is no place for coins formulated according to law. If officials are anxious, they should unify them, but it is too cumbersome and not powerful enough. If they are allowed to flow without punishment, then the coins will be extremely confusing if they are used differently in the market. If there is no way to deal with this situation, people will not know where to go! Nowadays, more and more people are giving up farming and mining copper. They put down their farm tools and use furnace charcoal to smelt money molds. The illegal money is increasing day by day, but the grain is not increasing. If kind people are tempted and go astray, and cautious people fall into punishment, the punishment will be very unfair. How can we ignore this! The country knows that the worries are like this, and the officials must have discussed that it is forbidden to mint money. Forbidding coining money is illegal and will cause great harm. If there is an order to prohibit the minting of coins, then the coins must be valuable; if they are valuable, the benefits will be great. Secretly minting coins is like a cloud, and the crime of abandoning the market is not enough to prohibit it. The evil has never been exhausted and the law has prohibited the collapse. This is caused by copper. Copper is scattered all over the world, so the harm it causes is great. Now great disasters can be avoided and seven kinds of blessings can be obtained. What are the seven blessings? If the emperor collects copper and prevents it from being scattered, then the people will not mint money and the crime of tattooing will not increase. This is one kind. There is not much fake money, and people do not doubt each other. This is the second type. People who mine copper ore to mint money return to farming. This is the third type. All copper is gathered in the emperor, and the emperor controls the weight by accumulating a lot of copper. If the coins are light, he will try to collect them. If the coins are heavy, he will try to distribute them. Money and things will definitely be balanced. This is the fourth. It is used to make weapons, and it is used to give to noble ministers. There are some restrictions. Its use can distinguish the noble from the humble. This is the fifth. It is used to monitor the market, adjust profits and losses, and collect surpluses. Then the government will be rich but the industrial and commercial people will be poor. This is the sixth type.
target: People abandoned farming to mine copper, increasing illegal money without increasing grain. He proposed collecting copper to prevent scattering, which would bring seven blessings: reducing tattooing crimes, eliminating fake money, returning miners to farming, balancing money and goods, distinguishing noble from humble, enriching the government while impoverishing merchants, and competing with the Xiongnu.

source: People who mine copper ore to mint money return to farming. This is the third type. All copper is gathered in the emperor, and the emperor controls the weight by accumulating a lot of copper. If the coins are light, he will try to collect them. If the coins are heavy, he will try to distribute them. Money and things will definitely be balanced. This is the fourth. It is used to make weapons, and it is used to give to noble ministers. There are some restrictions. Its use can distinguish the noble from the humble. This is the fifth. It is used to monitor the market, adjust profits and losses, and collect surpluses. Then the government will be rich but the industrial and commercial people will be poor. This is the sixth type. If we control our excess money and compete with the Xiongnu for its people, then the enemy will definitely surrender. This is the seventh way. Therefore, those who are good at ruling the world can turn disaster into happiness and failure into success. Now, the seven blessings have been suppressed for a long time and the great disaster has been allowed. I really feel sad for this. The emperor did not listen to him. At this time, Wu State relied on its status as a prince to mint coins in Shanhuo, and became richer than the emperor. Later, it finally became a rebellion. Deng Tong was a great official. Because he minted coins, his wealth exceeded that of the king.
target: The emperor did not listen. Wu State minted coins in Shanhuo, becoming richer than the emperor, and later rebelled. Deng Tong, a great official, minted coins and became wealthier than kings. Their money spread worldwide.

source: The number of wars increased day by day. Those who traveled far away took their luggage with them, and those who did not leave went to see each other off. Internal and external harassments were connected, and the people were in decline. They had to resort to deception to avoid criminal laws, and the loss of property caused shortages. Those who pay money can be replaced by official positions, and those who contribute money can be exempted from punishment. Elections are declining, integrity is ignored, force is used, and laws are strict. This is where the profit-seeking ministers began. After that, Wei Qing used tens of thousands of cavalry to attack the Xiongnu every year, and then captured the area south of Hetao and built Shuofang City.
target: During Emperor Wu's reign, wars with the Xiongnu and campaigns in the southwest and Guangdong drained resources.

source: The emperor called on the people who could provide slaves and maids to be exempted from taxes or labor for life, and those who were men could have their salaries increased. Accepting sheep to serve as Langguan began at this time. For the next four years, Wei Qing led more than 100,000 people to attack the Xiongnu every year. The reward for killing and capturing the enemy soldiers was more than 200,000 catties of gold. However, more than 100,000 soldiers and horses of the Han Dynasty died, and the cost of weapons, boring armor, and transportation of grain was not included. So Da Sinong reported that the usual money and taxes had been used up and were not enough to pay the soldiers. Relevant officials asked for instructions so that people could buy titles and use money in exchange for exemption or reduction of the criminal penalties that prohibited industrial and commercial people from serving as officials; they also asked for the establishment of a rewarded official position, called Wugongjue, with each level worth 170,000 yuan, and a total value of more than 300,000 gold.
target: The government used money to buy titles and exempt people from punishment, leading to official chaos.

source: The official career is complicated and there are many clues, so the official position will be chaotic. From the time when Gongsun Hong used the moral principles of the Spring and Autumn Annals to restrain his ministers and became the prime minister of the Han Dynasty, and when Zhang Tang judged lawsuits with harsh and stringent laws and became a court lieutenant, officials knew that others had committed crimes but did not report them. A year later, signs of conspiracy by the kings of Huainan, Hengshan, and Jiangdu were discovered. The ministers looked for Mansuo to review the case and pursue their accomplices. Tens of thousands of people were sentenced to death. The officials used more ruthless methods and the laws became stricter. At this time, scholars who respected the upright, virtuous, and literary were recruited, and some of them became ministers and officials. Gongsun Hong used his position as prime minister, covered himself with cloth quilts, and did not eat many kinds of dishes as an example for the world. However, it did not benefit the folk customs and was only slightly beneficial to utilitarianism. Another year passed, and the hussar general sent troops to attack the Huns again and won a great victory. King Hunxie led tens of thousands of people to surrender, so the Han Dynasty sent 30,000 chariots to meet them. After arriving, they were given rewards, including those who had meritorious service. A total of more than 10 billion was spent this year. More than ten years before this, the Yellow River burst and flooded the Liang and Chu regions. It had been in trouble several times, and the counties and counties next to the Yellow River built embankments to block the Yellow River breach, but it soon collapsed again, costing countless people.
target: Gongsun Hong, as prime minister, used moral principles to restrain ministers, while Zhang Tang used harsh laws. The Yellow River flooded, costing billions.

source: If it still wasn't enough, he called in rich people to borrow money. Still unable to save these people, they moved the poor to the west of Guan and supplemented them to Xinqin south of Shuofang. There were more than 700,000 people who relied on government supplies for food and clothing. For several years, money was lent to production and operations, and envoys were escorted in batches, connected by cars in front and back, spending hundreds of millions, leaving the government with a huge emptiness. Some wealthy merchants hoard goods and serve the poor, transporting them with hundreds of vehicles. Some of them live in the city and hoard goods, buying at low prices and selling at high prices. The monarchs of the feudal states bow their heads and rely on their supply. Smelting steel, casting utensils, and boiling salt, some accumulated wealth worth tens of thousands of gold, but without supporting the government's difficulties, the people became even more miserable. So the emperor discussed with the ministers to change the coins to supplement the expenses, in order to combat those who were arrogant and extravagant and occupied other people's property. At this time, there were white deer in the Imperial Garden and there was a lot of silver and tin in the Shaofu Palace.
